title: Israel election results: Netanyahu bloc wins 53 seats, opposition holds 48, Arab parties skyrocket
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc is currently expected to enter the Knesset with 53 seats, the Central Elections Committee (CEC) announced on Wednesday morning after almost five million votes were counted. Netanyahu's Likud is projected to enter with 26 seats, while United Torah Judaism, Shas, and Otzma Yehudit are expected to enter with seven seats, and the Religious Zionist Party is expected to enter with six seats, respectively. The opposition bloc, comprising Yashar, B'Yachad, Yisrael Beytenu, and the Democrats, is expected to enter the Knesset with 48 seats, according to data from the CEC.Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar is projected to enter the Knesset with 21 seats. B'Yachad, led by Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid, is expected to enter with 12 seats. Yair Golan's Democrats are expected to enter the Knesset with eight seats, and Avigdor Liberman's Yisrael Beytenu is expected to enter with seven.The latest results by the CEC put 19 seats in the Arab parties, with the Joint List having 12 seats and Ra'am having seven seats in the next Knesset.Could Israel be heading toward a unity gov't - or another election?The prospect of a unity government involving Netanyahu and Eisenkot has appeared unlikely, as Eisenkot has rejected serving under Netanyahu, including in a rotation government. Other opposition leaders have also ruled out joining a coalition led by the prime minister.Eisenkot has called for the leader of the largest party in the opposition bloc to become its candidate for prime minister, though no agreement on the arrangement has been announced within the bloc.The exit polls also raised the possibility of a minority government that could win a Knesset confidence vote without holding an absolute majority of 61 seats. However, opposition within the bloc to relying on Arab parties could complicate such an arrangement.The political deadlock could ultimately lead to another election, although the parties may still reach an agreement through coalition negotiations.Democrats, Arab parties call to form opposition governmentDemocrats' chairman Yair Golan said that the bloc led by Prime Minister Netanyahu lost the 2026 Knesset election, as the opposition bloc reached 65 seats when the Arab parties are included."Netanyahu lost. I know how to count to 120. Sixty-five is more than 55. That's how Israeli democracy works. Period," he said, calling on Wednesday morning for the inclusion of Arab parties in the government in the upcoming Knesset elections.He also said that if Netanyahu was considering forming a Zionist bloc, he should "subtract from his own bloc the 16 Knesset members from the non-Zionist Haredi parties.""We have a majority. We have responsibility. And we have an opportunity to form a government of change in partnership with Israel's Arab citizens. A government that will serve all Israeli citizens," Golan added.Joint List chairman Yousef Jabareen said on Wednesday that his party was ready to "pave the way for the ousting of the Netanyahu government.""Against a government of bloodshed, against a politics of supremacy, racism, and exclusion, we offer a completely different alternative," he posted on X/Twitter."The change comes through Jewish-Arab partnership, a true and equal partnership. No less than that, and no more than that," he added.Later, in an interview with Army Radio, Joint List faction chairman MK Ahmad Tibi (Hadash-Ta'al) hinted at his willingness to sit with the opposition.“The opposition bloc will be able to form a government if it has the courage. We are extending a hand and are ready to help," he said.Jerusalem Post Staff contributed to this report.

title: Effi Nave, Eitan Orenstein judicial probe transferred to Tel Aviv prosecutors for review
body: Police have completed their investigation into suspicions that former Israel Bar Association chairman Effi Nave helped advance Eitan Orenstein's appointment as president of the Tel Aviv District Court in exchange for moving another judge out of cases relevant to Nave's legal practice, police announced Wednesday.The evidence has been transferred to the Tel Aviv District Attorney's Office (Taxation and Economics), which supervised the investigation, for review and a decision on how to proceed. The announcement did not specify whether police recommended charges.This is a developing story.

title: Trump wants Ben-Gvir, Smotrich out of Israel's next government, US sources tell 'Post'
body: US President Donald Trump wants Israel's next government to exclude far-right ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, American sources told Walla on Wednesday.According to the sources, Trump believes settler violence is undermining his regional vision and complicating efforts to implement it.Trump's associates have been briefed on the election results, though the president himself has yet to comment.Trump on Iran war: 'Will end very quickly'Separately, Trump addressed the war with Iran on Wednesday, saying it could end whenever he decides."It will end very quickly, but we have to make sure it ends the right way," he said.According to Trump, ending the war requires "an absolute and unequivocal declaration that they will never have nuclear weapons."Trump described Iran as "the number one state sponsor of terrorism in the world."Exit polls, CEC data show political deadlockPrime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc is currently expected to enter the Knesset with 54 seats, the Central Elections Committee (CEC) announced on Wednesday morning after over four million votes were counted. Netanyahu's Likud is projected to enter with 27 seats, while United Torah Judaism, Shas, and Otzma Yehudit are expected to enter with seven seats, and the Religious Zionist Party is expected to enter with six seats, respectively.The opposition bloc, comprising Yashar, B'Yachad, Yisrael Beytenu, and the Democrats, is expected to enter the Knesset with 49 seats, according to data from the CEC.The Reservists' Party and People of Israel failed to cross the electoral threshold in the exit polls, while celebrations broke out at Likud headquarters following the publication of the results.Meanwhile, Amcha Yisrael chairman Ofer Winter, whose party failed to cross the electoral threshold in the exit polls, criticized Netanyahu.Sources close to Winter claimed that the prime minister had "drained our votes" and described the move as a "strategic mistake."Despite the change bloc's advantage, neither bloc reaches the 61 seats needed for a Knesset majority, leaving the possibility of forming a government unresolved.The election's preliminary results have left coalition negotiations uncertain, with neither Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposition parties appearing to have a clear path to a 61-seat majority. The exit polls also indicated that Arab parties could play a significant role in determining whether a government can be formed.Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit and Smotrich's Religious Zionist Party-Zehut alliance were projected to win approximately 13 seats combined, making them potentially important partners in any future Netanyahu-led coalition.The election projections remain preliminary, and the final distribution of Knesset seats will depend on the official vote count. Keshet Neev contributed to this report.

title: Copa del Rey matches postponed following Spain train collision
body: The Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) announced on Wednesday the postponement of 24 matches in the first round of the Copa del Rey “as a mark of respect and solidarity” with the victims of a high-speed train collision. “The entire Spanish football family stands united in grief over this tragedy and stands ready to assist the authorities in helping the victims of this devastating accident,” the RFEF said in a statement published on its website. “As a mark of respect and solidarity with all the victims of the tragic train accident that occurred on Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo, the RFEF has decided to suspend the 24 matches in the first round of the Copa del Rey originally scheduled for this afternoon and this evening.” The federation added that it will “provide further details in due course regarding the revised tournament schedule and the final kick-off times for the postponed matches”. The latest provisional figures from the Spanish authorities put the death toll at at least 31, with 80 injured, following the collision of two high-speed trains around 130 kilometres (80 miles) south of Madrid. The post Copa del Rey matches postponed following Spain train collision appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Susan Saint James, ‘Kate & Allie’ and ‘McMillan & Wife’ actor, dead at 80
body:
Susan Saint James , the Emmy-winning actor who starred in Kate & Allie and McMillan & Wife , has died at the age of 80.
Saint James died Monday of pancreatic cancer , her family announced.
“She never met a stranger,” her family said in a statement to People . “Every person she met became the most important person in the room at that moment, from a fellow board member to the clerk at the shoe store, who usually walked away knowing her entire life story.”
“Her defining act: weeks after losing her youngest son, Teddy, in the November 28, 2004 plane crash, she delivered his eulogy as a note to each of her other children and her husband, giving them words to heal,” the statement continued.
“Even in the deepest grief of her life, she put everyone else first. Days after the crash she sat with Tim Russert to thank the people who had reached out and to tell them the family was okay,” her family added.
Her family said that Saint James “brought the same fire and positivity to everything that followed, and never lost it.”
“She is survived by her husband, Dick Ebersol, her four children–Sunshine Lucas, Harmony Lucas, Charlie Ebersol and Willie Ebersol–her seven grandchildren; her sister, Mary Mercedes Dewey, as well as her beloved service dog, Lola,” the statement concluded.
At 20, Saint James moved to Los Angeles and landed a seven-year contract with Universal Studios. She made her television debut in the 1966 movie Fame Is the Name of the Game with Tony Franciosa.
She got another break when it became a series called The Name of the Game in 1968, with rotating lead characters played by Franciosa, Gene Barry and Robert Stack. Saint James provided the show continuity in her role as Peggy Maxwell, a research assistant who worked for all three men. She won an Emmy Award for the part in 1969.
She is best known as Sally McMillan, the wife of Rock Hudson’s San Francisco police commissioner Stewart McMillan, in the series McMillan & Wife from 1971 to 1976. She received three Emmy nominations for her role.
After leaving the series before its sixth and final season, Saint James turned to feature films.
She played opposite Peter Fonda in Outlaw Blues in 1977. She co-starred with George Hamilton in the 1979 vampire spoof Love at First Bite and joined Jessica Lange and Jane Curtin in the 1980 comedy heist How to Beat the High Cost of Living .
She also co-starred in the 1981 romantic comedy Carbon Copy , in which Denzel Washington made his movie debut.
Saint James went on to reunite with Curtin in the sitcom Kate & Allie , which aired from 1984 to 1989 and earned Saint James two Emmy nominations for her role of Kate.
The actor met her husband Dick Ebersol while guest hosting Saturday Night Live in 1981. He was the show’s then-executive producer and they married six weeks after meeting.
Ebersol and Saint James had three sons together, Charlie, Willie and Teddy.
Teddy died at the age of 14 in a 2004 private plane crash that also killed the pilot and flight attendant. Ebersol and Charlie survived the crash with serious injuries.
After news of Saint James’ passing spread, Curtin shared a statement with ABC News , reflecting on the actor’s life.
“We lost a decent person today. Susan St. James was a decent person who made Kate and Allie a joy,” Curtin began.
“She juggled a really full life from the Ed Sullivan theater in between working on stage and being the Mom on set. She worked tirelessly for organizations she believed in like the Special Olympics. All the while raising children and going through the horrors of losing a child,” she added.
“Susan was my friend and working with her brought such laughter, community and family to the stage at the Ed Sullivan theater. I’ll miss her,” Curtin’s statement concluded.

title: Fund judiciary adequately to protect judicial independence – Valentin Mensah
body: Governance specialist Valentin Kwasi Mensah has called for adequate funding and resources for Ghana’s judiciary, arguing that judicial independence cannot be guaranteed without the financial and material capacity to deliver justice. Speaking at a JoyNews public lecture on the theme “Even Judges Must Eat – An Outside-In Provocation,” Mr Mensah said judges could be independent in principle but struggle to perform their duties effectively if courts lacked adequate staff, functional computers and operational funds. “Even judges must eat captures an important truth. Judges and court workers need decent conditions, while courts need buildings, records, equipment and functioning systems. Independence requires the means to do the work,” he said. Mr Mensah noted that Ghana’s 1992 Constitution provides safeguards for judicial independence, including provisions under Article 127 on the independence of the judiciary and aspects of its financial administration. He also cited provisions concerning judicial administrative expenses, conditions of service and the release of funds, alongside the legal framework governing the administration and financing of the Judicial Service. However, he argued that constitutional safeguards must be matched by effective implementation and greater transparency in the allocation and use of public funds. “Citizens should be able to see what courts request, what Parliament approves, what is released and how the money is spent. Institutions receiving public funds must explain both their needs and their results,” he said. Mr Mensah referred to a 1988 study published by the Centre for the Independence of Judges and Lawyers, which distinguished between the freedom of judges to decide cases and the employment security and material conditions needed to sustain that freedom. He warned that constitutional protections could lose their practical value if inflation weakened the purchasing power of judicial salaries or if approved funding commitments were not met. His remarks highlighted the relationship between the financial security of judicial officers, the operational capacity of courts and the effective administration of justice. The lecture, organised by JoyNews in collaboration with professional bodies, brought together stakeholders to discuss the state of Ghana’s judiciary and reforms needed to improve the delivery of justice. Mr Mensah’s intervention focused on the need to ensure that courts have the personnel, equipment and funding required to function effectively, while maintaining accountability for the use of public resources.

title: Lockheed Martin Advances Joint Fires Capability by Redirecting In-flight GMRLS Rocket During US Army Test
body:
WHITE SANDS MISSILE RANGE, N.M., Oct. 28, 2026. In a program first, Lockheed Martin, in partnership with the US Army, successfully redirected an in-flight GMLRS rocket during a recent test at White Sands Missile Range.



During the flight test, the team launched GMLRS from a HIMARS launcher and then used the Strigo datalink and the Remote Interceptor Guidance-360 (RIG-360), integrated through internal Lockheed Martin funding, to update the rocket’s target while in flight. The GMLRS then successfully destroyed the moving target.

THE BIG PICTURE 

This capability demonstration marks a significant step toward expanding the capabilities for the Army's combat-proven GMLRS without fundamentally changing the missile by connecting existing sensors, launchers and targeting systems. It also gives commanders the opportunity to make adjustments from pre-programmed strikes, offering a flexible firing option if battlefield conditions change.

WHY IT MATTERS 

 	An Interconnected Battlefield: The successful live-fire event supports the Army's vision for networked precision fires by connecting sensors, launchers and targeting systems into a single integrated kill chain and provides soldiers with greater flexibility against dynamic threats.
 	Application for Future Precision Fires Munitions: The datalink package is directly applicable to other precision fires rockets and missiles including Extended Range GMLRS and Precision Strike Missile (PrSM), to extend networked fire across an array of munitions.

“By delivering this level of integration between Lockheed Martin products such as GMLRS, RIG-360 and Strigo, we’re giving our warfighters the confidence and capability to succeed in the most complex, real‑world scenarios,” said Randy Crites, Vice President, Lockheed Martin Advanced Programs. “Accelerating mission integration with trusted systems ensures faster, more effective outcomes on the modern battlefield and gives commanders the flexible options they need to respond to any threat.”

title: 2027: ADC alleges plot to shift January 16 election, warns Tinubu
body: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council has raised the alarm over an alleged plot to pressure the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) into shifting the January 16 presidential election, warning President Bola Tinubu against seeking to evade an electoral verdict. The council said it had received information that INEC Chairman Prof. Joash Amupitan would be summoned to the Presidential Villa and instructed to alter the election timetable, with just 80 days to the poll. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the council urged Tinubu to abandon any such move and called on Amupitan to reject any instruction to change the date and immediately make any such approach public. “The election date belongs to Nigerians. It must not be rewritten behind closed doors at the Villa,” the council said. It said Nigerians had endured three and a half years of soaring prices, shrinking incomes and relentless hardship, insisting that they must be allowed to judge the Tinubu administration at the ballot box on January 16. “A government that has made life this difficult for Nigerians must not be allowed to postpone its day of judgement,” it said. While acknowledging Ebola as a serious public health concern, the council said health professionals must be allowed to contain the disease, and INEC must take necessary steps to protect voters and election workers. It cited the position of the Director-General of the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) that there was currently no reason to postpone the election, warning against using the health emergency as a political justification for delay. The council also put INEC, domestic observers and international election monitors on notice, demanding that any proposal to alter the timetable be made openly, backed by published health evidence and subjected to public scrutiny. “The Presidency must not use a health emergency to escape an electoral verdict,” it said. The post 2027: ADC alleges plot to shift January 16 election, warns Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Lib Dems want six more frigates and new shipyards
body: Three more Type 31 frigates, three more Type 26 frigates and four new shipyards should be funded through defence bonds and delivered by the mid-2030s to counter the threat from Russia, according to the Liberal Democrats. The party published the proposal alongside polling it commissioned, which found that sixty per cent of people think the government is not doing enough to protect Britain’s critical infrastructure, including undersea cables, from Russian attack. James MacCleary, the Liberal Democrat defence spokesperson, said: “After years of the Conservative Party underinvesting in our military, we are now dangerously exposed and woefully unprepared. Russia is actively, and brazenly, testing the limits of our naval defence capabilities – but Labour has dragged its feet on investing properly in our defence. “We cannot afford to sit on our hands while Putin’s aggression intensifies and our national security weakens. We need a plan which gives confidence to British industry and allows our manufacturers to get on with delivering for Britain’s long-term security. “By investing now in six new warships and by expanding our ship-building capacity with four new British shipyards, we can regenerate our fleet, protect our vital underwater infrastructure, and ensure Britain has the defence capabilities we need to stand up to the Kremlin.” The party said it would raise the Digital Services Tax from two per cent to ten per cent and use part of the proceeds to cover crewing and maintenance. It acknowledged that no estimates exist for the in-service costs of either the Type 31 or the Type 26, despite parliamentary questions pressing the government for them, and extrapolated an assumed £20 million a year for each ship from 2018 estimates for the Type 23 and Type 45, giving £120 million a year for six ships in 2034/35 terms. On the threat, the party cited the Royal Navy spending twenty five per cent more time monitoring Russian vessels around British waters, a Russian warship firing warning shots at a yacht off the Isle of Wight in June, and a Russian attack submarine and two intelligence submarines loitering over critical undersea cables in the North Atlantic for a month in May. It also raised Russian escorts for sanctions-busting tankers passing through the Channel. The polling was carried out by Savanta, which interviewed 2,234 United Kingdom adults online between 29 May and 1 June this year, weighted to be representative by age, sex, region and social grade. Respondents were told that the head of the United Kingdom’s intelligence and security agency has warned of relentless attacks from Russia on critical infrastructure, and asked whether the government is doing enough to protect it. Five per cent said definitely, twenty two per cent probably, thirty nine per cent probably not and twenty one per cent definitely not, with fourteen per cent unsure. Concern ran highest among older respondents, at sixty seven per cent of those aged fifty five and over against fifty one per cent of those aged eighteen to thirty four. The Defence Committee reported last week that dramatic progress is needed in building up British forces and ships for the High North, and the Liberal Democrats argued that the Strategic Defence Review set a compelling vision for the hybrid Navy while the Defence Investment Plan failed to provide the resources to rebuild the fleet. The post Lib Dems want six more frigates and new shipyards first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Billionaire taxes, trans rights, abortion, voting rights: This year's biggest state votes
body: Statewide ballot measures are flying under the national radar — but some are drawing big spending. At least $400 million has been spent on TV ads for ballot initiatives, according to data from the ad-tracking firm AdImpact. The 145 ballot measures across 39 states include fights attracting the attention of future presidential candidates and millions from dark-money groups on both sides of the aisle. The focus of this year’s ballot measures reflect broader shifts in the political discourse. The number of abortion-related initiatives has dropped precipitously since 2022 as states have had time to determine their individual laws following the repeal of Roe v. Wade. At the same time, voters in five states will weigh in on ballot measures focusing on transgender issues, the most in history. Here are the most consequential ballot initiatives facing voters in November: California’s wealth tax By far the most expensive and most aggressively targeted ballot measure in November is California’s Prop 40, which if passed would levy a one-time 5% tax on the state’s billionaires. An eye-watering $92 million has been spent on TV ads debating the issue, mostly on the “No” side, although that pales in comparison to what the Silicon Valley tycoons opposing the initiative like tech investor Peter Thiel and Google co-founder Sergey Brin would be forced to pay should it pass. Leading progressive figures including Bernie Sanders and Ro Khanna are backing the “Yes” side. Caught in the middle is Gov. Gavin Newsom, a potential 2028 presidential candidate, who’s opposed the measure even as he’s tried to claim some populist credibility by proposing a national tax hike on billionaires. A Citrin-POLITICO poll earlier this month found the measure receiving 46% support, short of the majority needed to pass. Newsom and Brin are both backing another ballot measure, Prop 42, a separate question that would cancel out the Prop 40 wealth tax if it passes. If both pass, Prop 42 could still cancel out Prop 40 if it receives more votes. Redistricting wars continue Maryland Gov. Wes Moore is making himself the face of a constitutional amendment that, if it passes, would pave the way for the state legislature to draw new lines turning the state’s lone GOP House seat solidly blue. Moore, a potential presidential candidate in 2028, is taking a cue from Newsom, who passed a redistricting referendum last year that is likely to swing five House seats in favor of Democrats. Former President Barack Obama cut an ad for the “Yes” campaign this week. Missouri Democrats recently won a contentious legal battle that barred the GOP from using a new gerrymander to erase a Kansas City-area Democratic seat held by Rep. Emanuel Cleaver and allowed voters a referendum on whether that gerrymander will be used in future elections.. Now, voters get to choose what the state does going forward. The campaign pushing “No” on the referendum reported raising $6 million earlier this month, with big help from Democratic megadonors, including LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman and Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker. Transgender rights restrictions hit the ballot This year marks the first time multiple states have taken up ballot initiatives focusing on transgender issues. The six initiatives across Colorado, Missouri, Washington, Arizona and Nebraska help make up the most LGBTQ-related ballot measures in a year since the Supreme Court legalized same-sex marriage in 2015. Each of the measures asks voters to either ban transgender surgeries for minors or restrict access to girls sports for transgender girls. Abortion access measures in four states Measures in Nevada and Virginia would enshrine abortion access in those states’ constitutions, similar to measures that have passed over the last few years in Ohio, Michigan, Montana and other states. A measure in Idaho, which would override the state’s near-total ban, is a statutory change rather than a constitutional one, meaning the GOP-dominated state legislature could (and is expected to) vote to override it if it passes. Missouri has a social conservative combo: a proposition to overturn the abortion-rights constitutional amendment that voters approved in 2024 and reinstate a near-total ban on the procedure that would also prohibit gender transition surgeries for minors. Advocacy groups on both sides are pouring millions into the initiatives, with abortion rights groups spending $22.5 million and anti-abortion groups spending $8.7 million on TV ads, with most of that money being spent in Missouri. Voting on voting Over a dozen ballot measures will weigh election administration rules for future elections. In seven states,voters could approve requirements for valid ID to vote. Six states will give voters the chance to explicitly codify in state law that only U.S. citizens can vote in the state. Massachusetts voters will weigh in on whether to establish a top-two nonpartisan primary system, like California has, while Alaska voters will decide if the state will end its top-four primary and ranked-choice voting laws in favor of traditional party primaries and first-past-the-post vote counting.

title: Russia plans to establish transport hub on Africa's east coast — Deputy Foreign Minister
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Russia plans to set up a port transport and logistics hub on the east coast of Africa, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov announced at the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.
"In particular, we are discussing establishment of a Russian port transport and logistics hub on the east coast of Africa as part of the International North-South Transport Corridor," Ryabkov said. "Regarding projects to improve irrigation, water, and land use to enhance the resilience of agriculture and the food system in the Sahel region, as well as the development of scientific and technical cooperation - a high-level international conference was held in Addis Ababa in November 2025 at our initiative, bringing together experts from various ministries, government agencies, and the business community."

title: Court rules 2-1 against expanding Mandelblit testimony as judge queries investigative actions
body: Judge Moshe Bar-Am on Wednesday questioned how the court could disregard former attorney-general Avichai Mandelblit's testimony about unlawful investigative actions before the Jerusalem District Court ruled by a majority against allowing defense lawyers in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's trial to pursue that line of questioning.“How can we ignore the fact that the attorney-general comes here and testifies about unlawful actions?” Bar-Am asked prosecutor Yehudit Tirosh during arguments over the scope of Mandelblit's testimony.The intervention offered a glimpse of a judge's concerns about the evidence heard so far. But the three-judge panel ultimately ruled 2-1 to keep Mandelblit's questioning within the issue for which his testimony had been allowed: the approvals he gave for investigations into Netanyahu.Bar-Am said parts of Mandelblit's testimony appeared relevant to the defense's argument that investigative misconduct could justify canceling the indictment, warning that preventing further questions might leave a gap in the factual record.When Tirosh cautioned against opening the door to questioning prosecutors about their work, he replied: “Here, the door has already been opened. He testified, and we heard things that apparently require deeper examination.”Adjournment requested by Netanyahu lawyerThe panel comprises presiding Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman, Bar-Am, and Judge Oded Shaham. Following the ruling, Netanyahu's lawyer, Amit Hadad, requested an adjournment to adapt his planned questioning. The prosecution did not object, and the hearing ended after about two hours.Mandelblit was called as a defense witness to address whether police acted with the necessary authorization and whether their inquiries exceeded what he had approved. Under Basic Law: The Government, opening a criminal investigation into a sitting prime minister requires the attorney-general's consent.In his testimony so far, Mandelblit has maintained that he authorized the investigations, while acknowledging that some significant actions were taken without his approval. He has distinguished permission to investigate particular subjects from supervision of every police step, saying investigators were expected to consult him on major developments.Mandelblit said he ordered police to stop wiretapping Netanyahu confidant Natan Eshel after learning of the operation. He also criticized a tactic used against Nir Hefetz, Netanyahu's former media adviser who became a state witness: Investigators arranged an encounter with a woman close to Hefetz while he was in custody, signaling that they knew personal details about him. Mandelblit said he had not known of the tactic beforehand and considered it improper.On Monday, he acknowledged that questioning in Case 1000 went beyond the warning given to Netanyahu about the suspicions against him, and the warning in Case 2000 did not fit the allegations being investigated. The judges also pressed him on when approval to question Netanyahu as a suspect became a formal decision rather than an intention discussed among officials.Mandelblit has nevertheless defended the decision to prosecute, rejected suggestions that pressure dictated his decisions, and said he would be surprised if prosecutors deliberately concealed information from him. He has also disputed the defense's assertion that the Case 4000 bribery charge had collapsed and argued that investigative irregularities do not automatically require excluding evidence.Wednesday's dispute concerned the defense's attempt to question him more broadly about police and prosecution conduct between his authorization of the investigations and his decision to bring charges.Material information withheld from Mandelblit, says HadadHadad argued that material information had been withheld from Mandelblit, undermining the decision to prosecute. Jacques Chen, representing Shaul Elovitch and his wife, Iris, argued that investigative failures should have formed part of Mandelblit's assessment of whether bringing charges served the public interest.Tirosh opposed expanding the testimony into the prosecution's internal decision-making, arguing that alleged gaps in the investigative record should be addressed with investigators. Friedman-Feldman noted that Mandelblit had said he had not personally reviewed some material, including transcripts.Mandelblit's appearance placed his handling of the cases before the public during the final weeks of the election campaign. Netanyahu's defense requested his summons on September 17, seeking seven hearing dates between October 11 and October 22, with the last falling five days before the October 27 election. His testimony began on October 11.The court declined his request to postpone until November or December because of preparations for the academic year in his role as law faculty dean at the Academic College of Ramat Gan. His testimony has since extended beyond the original dates, with Wednesday's hearing taking place the day after the vote.The trial, which began in May 2020, concerns three cases. Case 1000 involves expensive gifts Netanyahu allegedly received from businessmen Arnon Milchan and James Packer, and actions he allegedly took to benefit Milchan. Case 2000 concerns discussions with Yedioth Aharonoth publisher Arnon Mozes about favorable coverage in exchange for steps against rival newspaper Israel Hayom.Case 4000 concerns allegations that Netanyahu advanced regulatory measures benefiting Bezeq's then-controlling shareholder, Elovitch, in exchange for intervention in Walla's coverage. Netanyahu faces fraud and breach of trust charges in all three cases, and bribery in Case 4000. He denies wrongdoing.The proceedings remain in the defense stage.Netanyahu completed his own testimony in June after 98 hearings, and the court is hearing other defense witnesses. Hearings moved to a five-day weekly schedule this month to accelerate the remaining evidence. The defense cases and closing arguments must still be completed before the judges deliver a verdict.

title: The Middle East’s New Rivalry Runs Through Central Asia
body: Eighty years after Winston Churchill described an Iron Curtain dividing Europe from Stettin to Trieste, another geopolitical rivalry is emerging across the Middle East, with the swing states of Central Asia and the South Caucasus poised to play a pivotal role. From Gwadar to the Golden Horn, the new Mecca Pact brings together Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey. From Pune in India to Piraeus in Greece, the proposed India–Middle East–Europe Economic Corridor, or IMEC, represents a different vision of regional integration, linking India, the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Israel, and Europe. At the heart of the struggle is the Turkey–Israel rivalry for regional leadership in the wake of the Iran war. But the contest will be shaped not only by the Middle East’s principal players, but also by countries on its periphery, particularly in the South Caucasus and Central Asia. When Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan walked out of a regional summit in Baku as Israeli President Isaac Herzog began speaking on October 15, he was accompanied by representatives of Iran, Pakistan, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, the Palestinian Authority, and others opposed to Israel’s actions in Gaza. But none of the five Central Asian leaders followed him. Kazakhstan’s President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev went further. On the sidelines of the summit, he held a bilateral meeting with Herzog, speaking about the “dynamic development” of Kazakhstan-Israel relations. The episode illustrated that the more Turkey plays the Israel card, the more difficult it becomes to maintain cohesion across the Turkic world. The Competition for Swing States At a Hudson Institute discussion in Washington on October 26, analysts examined competing regional alignments as the Middle East prepares for an era of reduced American engagement. Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, director of the Turkey Project at the Brookings Institution, said the Mecca Pact is “an early experiment” in managing a post-American region. “In the long run, whether it’s a Democratic or Republican administration, the notion of reducing U.S. footprint in the region is a very dominant theme, and you only have to look at the American public to see that,” she noted. Soner Çağaptay, director of the Turkish Research Program at the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, suggested the pact could best be understood through the countries it excludes, both beginning with the letter “I.” Israel and Iran are seen as “part of the regional problems, not the solutions,” he said, adding that the Mecca Pact envisions a broad coalition of countries establishing a new security architecture without either country at its center. India is the third “I,” said Chaim Martin, Israel’s minister of economic affairs to the United States. “That too is an ‘I’ that is specifically not in that pact,” he said. Israel views India as a key strategic partner, with both democracies navigating complex regional environments. Erdo g an’s Azerbaijan Problem Despite the ambitions of the Mecca Pact, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has received a reminder of the limits of bloc politics from one of his closest allies: Azerbaijan. Ankara and Baku describe themselves as “one nation, two states.” Turkey’s military support played a significant role in Azerbaijan’s victories over Armenia, while Azerbaijan remains indispensable to Turkey’s ambitions to become an energy and transportation hub connecting Central Asia and Europe. At the discussion, Michael Doran, Hudson’s director of the Center for Peace and Security in the Middle East, cited Zbigniew Brzezinski’s description of Azerbaijan as “the cork in the bottle” containing the riches of the Caspian Sea basin and Central Asia. Without access through Azerbaijan, Turkey’s ability to connect with Central Asia through the Middle Corridor, bypassing Russia and Iran, would be severely constrained. Yet Baku also maintains close security and economic relations with Israel, whose relationship with Turkey has deteriorated sharply. In recent weeks, tensions between Ankara and Baku have surfaced over Azerbaijan’s restrictions on headscarves in state schools. Erdogan’s adviser Oktay Saral publicly criticized the policy as “unacceptable,” provoking an angry response from Azerbaijan. With the Organization of Turkic States (OTS) summit scheduled for October 30, the dispute raised questions about whether Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev would attend. On October 25, Saral confirmed that he had left his position at Erdogan’s direction, clearing the way for reconciliation. Although Azerbaijan has traditionally been viewed as the junior partner in its relationship with Turkey, Aydıntaşbaş observed that Baku “is now actually calling the shots.” Kazakhstan: Israel’s Opening into the Turkic World A similar dynamic is emerging in Kazakhstan, where Israel has made significant diplomatic inroads. In November 2025, Kazakhstan became the first Central Asian country to join the Abraham Accords , the U.S.-sponsored framework originally established to promote normalization between Israel and Arab states. The relationship has deepened rapidly. In January, Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar visited Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan with a large business delegation, seeking cooperation in fields including agriculture, water management, cybersecurity, and advanced technology. In April, President Herzog visited Astana, where he and Tokayev discussed expanding cooperation. Then came the October 15 meeting between Tokayev and Herzog in Baku, even as Fidan led a diplomatic walkout during the Israeli president’s address. Kazakhstan’s relationship with Israel has an intriguing Washington dimension. Astana has long sought the repeal of the Jackson–Vanik amendment , a Cold War-era U.S. trade provision originally intended to pressure the Soviet Union to permit Jewish emigration. More than three decades after independence, Kazakhstan remains subject to the provision, although it receives normal trade treatment through a waiver mechanism. Ending its application remains an important diplomatic objective for Astana. By joining the Abraham Accords and strengthening ties with Israel, Kazakhstan may be able to build additional support in Washington for its efforts to secure permanent normal trade relations, a step that requires congressional action. For Israel, Kazakhstan offers a diplomatic foothold inside the Turkic world, complicating any assumption that Turkic solidarity automatically translates into support for Ankara’s positions. Th e C6 Alternative to Turkic Unity Erdogan’s decision to remove his adviser likely reflected concern that a prolonged rupture with Baku could encourage Azerbaijan to place greater emphasis on another regional grouping gaining momentum: the C5 plus Azerbaijan. In November 2025, Azerbaijan became a full participant in the consultative meetings of the five Central Asian states, creating what is increasingly described as the C6. The arrangement brings together Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Azerbaijan in a regional framework without Turkey. The developments demonstrate the limits of Turkish influence over Azerbaijan, Aydıntaşbaş said. While Aliyev will likely visit Ankara for the OTS summit, “this doesn’t mean there won’t be a residual effect,” she said. A renewed conflict in Iran or the pace of normalization with Armenia could reopen the wounds, she added. A New Balance of Power The Mecca Pact and IMEC may represent two competing visions for the Middle East. Yet the countries linking the Middle East to the Eurasian interior are demonstrating that the future regional order will not simply be determined by whichever bloc assembles the greatest number of powerful members. Eighty years after Churchill’s Iron Curtain speech, the swing states of Central Asia and the South Caucasus are determined to avoid being placed on one side of another dividing line. The emerging Middle Eastern rivalry is making them more important, not less independent. Ken Moriyasu moderated the Hudson Institute panel discussion on October 26, 2026, on which this article is based.

title: PhosAgro aims to double fertilizer shipments to Africa in 2026
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. PhosAgro increased its fertilizer shipments to Africa by 50% year-on-year in January-September and expects to double its total annual deliveries compared to 2025 levels, Sergey Pronin, the company’s First Deputy CEO, announced.
"In the first nine months of this year, we have already exceeded last year’s total shipment volume by 50%, having delivered over 1.3 million tonnes. By the end of 2026, we intend to double our shipments compared to the 2025 volume," Pronin told reporters at the Russia-Africa Forum.
He noted that last year, the company increased mineral fertilizer shipments to the African continent by one-third, with total exports reaching nearly 1 million tonnes - more than double the volume recorded in 2021.
South Africa, Ethiopia, and Mozambique became top three importers of PhosAgro's products on the continent. Overall, in the first half of 2026, the company accounted for 61% of the total volume of all types of Russian mineral fertilizers exported to Africa.
TASS is an official media partner of the third Russia-Africa Summit and the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.

title: CSOs identify stigma, poor facilities as barriers to HIV, TB, malaria treatment in Akwa Ibo
body:
Civil society organisations and health workers in Akwa Ibom State have identified stigma, cultural restrictions, inadequate health facilities and concerns about confidentiality as barriers limiting access to HIV, tuberculosis (TB) and malaria treatment.
They are calling for urgent government action to make healthcare more accessible to women and other vulnerable groups.
The stakeholders made the observations on Friday in Uyo at a one-day meeting to evaluate compliance with gender-responsive health policies in the state.
They called on the government to improve public awareness of available services, train health workers to treat patients without discrimination and equip primary healthcare centres to encourage service uptake.
They also called for consistent data collection to track HIV, TB and malaria cases and assess the implementation of policies designed to address gender-related inequalities in healthcare.
The meeting was organised by Lawyers Alert in partnership with Media Health and Rights Initiative of Nigeria (MHR) as part of efforts to strengthen accountability and promote gender-responsive policies in the state’s health sector.
Edidiong Enang, programme manager of Vitonia Lead Foundation, said cultural beliefs that discourage women from speaking up, economic hardship and institutional barriers continued to prevent women from accessing healthcare on equal terms.
“We have cultural barriers that people believe that women are not supposed to speak up,” she said, adding that women who lacked economic independence often experienced delays in seeking healthcare.
Ms Enang said some health facilities were not sufficiently gender-friendly, while stigma could discourage women from seeking services even when they were available.
She said the project had strengthened the capacity of participating civil society organisations to engage ministries, departments and agencies, as well as public officials responsible for policy decisions.
She called for sustained advocacy to ensure that government institutions addressed the barriers and included women in healthcare interventions.
Participants said the government needed to do more than establish policies and build model health facilities, stressing that primary healthcare centres must also be adequately equipped to provide accessible and reliable services.
They called on authorities to intensify public sensitisation about available healthcare services and train health workers to be more accommodating and maintain patients’ confidentiality.
The organisations also stressed the need for consistent data on HIV, TB and malaria to improve case tracking and measure the effectiveness of interventions.
However, health workers from primary healthcare facilities said malaria treatment in the state was free when testing confirmed the infection.
They explained that the state’s policy required patients to undergo testing before treatment, noting that not every fever was caused by malaria.
Ubong Ekpo, representing the state Ministry of Health, said the government had intensified efforts to identify tuberculosis cases, including through house-to-house testing in rural communities.
He also said that the state had three sexual assault referral centres at Ikot Ekpene General Hospital, Iquita Hospital in Oron and Immanuel Hospital in Eket.
Mr Ekpo said the Ministry of Health is working closely with the Ministry of Justice on relevant interventions.
Enobong Akpan, project manager of the Akwa Ibom State Agency for the Control of AIDS, said the state had domesticated several HIV-related policies but was yet to have the governor’s assent to an anti-stigma law passed by the State House of Assembly.
PREMIUM TIMES’ investigation had shown how this has caused avoidable deaths and increased infections in Akwa Ibom State.
Mr Akpan said the bill had been received by Governor Umo Eno and forwarded to the Ministry of Justice for review before assent.
He commended Lawyers Alert for providing technical support to the state, particularly in reviewing its HIV workplace policy.
According to him, Akwa Ibom has policies covering HIV prevention, workplace protection, care and treatment, prevention of mother-to-child transmission, and key and vulnerable populations.
He said the state reviewed its HIV workplace policy last year with support from Lawyers Alert and was planning to unveil the revised document.
On tuberculosis, Mr Akpan said the state had policies on care and treatment, including for multidrug-resistant TB, describing the care and treatment policy as functional.
The discussions at the meeting pointed to the gap between having policies in place and ensuring that vulnerable people can access services without discrimination.
Lawyers Alert and MHR launched their Gender Equality Fund project in Akwa Ibom in October 2024.
The two-and-a-half-year initiative, supported through the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria in partnership with GSK and ViiV Healthcare, is being implemented in Akwa Ibom and Benue states.
Tagged “Law, Rights and Community Empowerment for Social Change in TB, HIV and Malaria Response,” the project seeks to strengthen women-led organisations and equip women leaders to demand accountability and advocate policies that address gender-related barriers to healthcare.
The Uyo meeting brought together government officials, health workers and civil society organisations to assess the implementation of gender-responsive policies, identify gaps in service delivery and clarify the responsibilities of institutions, health facilities and communities.
Participants said the findings should guide advocacy and practical action to make healthcare services more inclusive and accountable.

title: Zelensky reveals what to expect as Ukraine, Russia head back to peace talks
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky, following an interview in Kyiv, Ukraine, on Oct. 18, 2026. (Olga Ivashchenko/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
A planned meeting between Ukraine, Russia, and the U.S. in Abu Dhabi will focus on de-escalating Russia's war, President Volodymyr Zelensky told reporters on Oct. 27, as Moscow seemingly agreed to resume talks with Kyiv after a pause of more than eight months.
Although Ukrainian officials do not expect the first round to produce a major breakthrough, Kyiv hopes the meeting will restart regular negotiations and deliver limited results.
"They had the impression the Russians are serious about the meeting in Abu Dhabi," Zelensky told reporters, referring to a call Norwegian and Finnish leaders held with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Oct. 27.
The planned meeting follows renewed U.S. efforts to bring the sides together, including visits by President Donald Trump's envoy to Kyiv and Moscow.
But even if the talks resume, major disagreements over territory and security guarantees are likely to remain obstacles to any potential settlement.
The latest push for a trilateral meeting began in early September, when Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner traveled to Kyiv and Moscow to seek progress toward ending Russia's war before the U.S. midterm elections.
The visits produced one tangible outcome: an agreement in principle to hold a meeting involving Ukraine, Russia , and the U.S.
Putin initially declined to meet with the Ukrainian side after the September trip, but the Kremlin signaled readiness to resume talks after Witkoff visited Moscow on Oct. 21.
Zelensky said the planned meeting should focus on immediate steps toward de-escalation.
"The agenda should cover the following issues: initial steps toward de-escalation, the main priorities for the Ukrainian side — particularly security priorities — and, more broadly, ending this war," Zelensky told reporters.
"We hope for a result regarding energy and at sea, an exchange of prisoners , and a discussion of the possible format for a trilateral meeting at the leaders' level."
The Ukrainian president added that Kyiv hopes the technical groups will agree on practical measures or make progress.
One senior Ukrainian official told the Kyiv Independent that the first meeting is unlikely to produce any results, arguing that the sides need to reestablish a shared understanding after such a long pause in negotiations.
Still, Kyiv hopes subsequent meetings will become regular and deliver at least limited gains each time. The official said that prisoner exchanges and sector-specific ceasefires , including one focused on energy infrastructure, are priorities.
A recent example of a limited ceasefire was the temporary truce in Oleshky, a city in Kherson Oblast that has been effectively blockaded by Russian forces. The truce was intended to address the humanitarian situation in the city.
A meeting between Putin and Zelensky remains a much more uncertain prospect. The two leaders have not met since 2019, and Moscow continues to insist that Zelensky travel to Russia for direct talks — a proposal Kyiv rejects.
During a phone call with Finland's president and Norway's prime minister on Oct. 27, Putin said Zelensky could come to Moscow. Ukraine views the proposal as a sign that the Russian leader is unwilling to meet Zelensky on mutually acceptable terms.
Trump, however, told reporters on Oct. 27 that a meeting between the two leaders could happen "soon."
Even if the planned talks resume, the sides will face the same disagreements that stalled previous negotiations, particularly over Donbas and the security arrangements that would accompany an end to the war.
The Kremlin has repeatedly rejected a ceasefire and demanded that Kyiv surrender the parts of Donbas that Russia has failed to capture militarily. The strategically important region in eastern Ukraine remains a central point of talks.
Ukraine, by contrast, has called for a ceasefire along the current front line.
In earlier negotiations, U.S. representatives proposed establishing a demilitarized zone in Donbas, an idea both sides initially supported. However, Putin insisted that Moscow should effectively control the territory, a position Kyiv rejected.
Zelensky said U.S. envoys have again raised the issue of Donbas in discussions with Ukrainian and Russian teams. Moscow continues to link the territorial question to the broader terms for ending the war, including security guarantees .
"Russia links the issue of territories to ending the war, security guarantees, and the possible forms those guarantees could take," Zelensky said.
He added that Ukraine's partners had avoided an in-depth discussion of territorial concessions because they understood Kyiv considers the issue a red line.
"Our partners couldn't go into the territorial issue in depth because they know it's a red line for us," Zelensky said. "This is an issue that can only be discussed by the leaders of the countries at war, and only at their level."
Zelensky said Ukraine had been prepared to discuss a buffer zone or demilitarized zone on both sides of the line of contact as a possible compromise.
But the dispute over control of the territory remains unresolved, leaving the planned meeting focused primarily on whether the sides can agree on immediate steps toward de-escalation rather than a settlement. At least for now.
Tim Zadorozhnyy is a reporter at the Kyiv Independent covering foreign policy, U.S.-Ukraine relations, and political developments across Europe and Russia. He studied International Relations and European Studies at Lazarski University and Coventry University. Tim began his journalism career in Odesa in 2022 as a reporter for a local television channel. He later spent a year and a half at the Belarusian independent media outlet NEXTA, first as a news anchor and later as a managing editor. He is fluent in English, Ukrainian, and Russian.

title: Rajnath Singh, Pete Hegseth review India-US defence framework at Cebu meeting
body:
By R Anil Kumar

Cebu, Philippines, Oct 28, 2026. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Wednesday, October 28, met US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth in Cebu, Philippines, to review progress under the 10-year India-US Defence Framework and explore ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation.



The meeting took place on the sidelines of the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus), being held on October 28-29.

“Had an excellent meeting with US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on the side-lines of the 13th ADMM-Plus. We reviewed the progress of our 10-year India-US Defence Framework, driving strategic convergence across military technology, information sharing, and co-production,” Singh said in a post on X.

He described the partnership as a cornerstone for a free, open and secure Indo-Pacific.

Hegseth said the two leaders marked the first anniversary of the framework and discussed further cooperation.

“Great meeting with Indian Minister of Defence Singh. We celebrated the one-year anniversary of the Framework for our Major Defense Partnership and explored ways to strengthen cooperation,” he said in a post on X.

Signed in 2025, the framework provides a unified vision and policy direction for deepening defence cooperation over ten years, according to the Ministry of Defence.

Singh, who is leading the Indian delegation, arrived in Cebu on Tuesday night. He received a ceremonial welcome at the airport, where Indian Ambassador to the Philippines Harsh Kumar Jain and Defence Attaché Captain ChandraKant Kothari were among those present.

The Defence Minister is scheduled to address the ADMM-Plus forum on regional and international security issues on Thursday. He is also holding bilateral meetings with counterparts from participating countries to review defence ties and explore stronger strategic partnerships.

ADMM-Plus brings together ASEAN member states and eight dialogue partners - India, the United States, China, Russia, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand to strengthen security and defence cooperation. The Philippines chairs the forum in 2026.

India, an ASEAN dialogue partner since 1992, is co-chairing the ADMM-Plus Experts Working Group on Counter-Terrorism with Malaysia for the 2024-2027 cycle.

title: UAE's Emirates Red Crescent provides Dh50 million in winter aid to Gaza
body: The Emirates Red Crescent is delivering Dh50 million ($13.6 million) worth of winter and medical aid to Palestinians in Gaza as temperatures drop across the Middle East. The relief effort includes clothes, blankets, food, tents, medicine and other essential supplies. It is focused on the most vulnerable groups, including children, the elderly and families facing acute hardship as winter conditions intensify across the territory. The assistance is being provided under the directives of President Sheikh Mohamed and the co-ordination of Sheikh Hamdan bin Zayed, Ruler’s Representative of Al Dhafra Region and Chairman of the ERC. The aid is part of the UAE's continuing efforts to support people in Gaza and meet the basic needs of affected families as winter approaches and is carried out in co-ordination with Operation Gallant Knight 3. The initiative is part of the UAE's long-standing relief efforts supporting the Palestinians. The ERC said the aid was designed to help ensure dignified living conditions amid what it described as exceptional circumstances in the territory. The organisation reaffirmed its continued commitment to the Palestinian people and its determination to strengthen relief operations in line with on-the-ground needs and humanitarian priorities. Last week, two UAE aid convoys carrying 260 tonnes of food supplies entered Gaza . The convoys, comprising 10 lorries, were sent under Operation Gallant Knight 3. Their arrival brought the total number of lorries that had entered Gaza under the operation to 14,594, collectively carrying 138,290 tonnes of humanitarian aid since the mission's launch. The latest Dh50 million package underscores the Emirate's continued focus on urgent needs, particularly as deteriorating weather conditions further put pressure on displaced families and overstretched humanitarian infrastructure across the strip. The UAE has been among the most active countries in delivering aid to Gaza, with Operation Gallant Knight 3 serving as the country's primary co-ordination framework for relief operations. Dubai Humanitarian has also launched a new air bridge to deliver winter relief to Gaza. The first flight, carrying essential humanitarian supplies including thermal blankets, was delivered with the help of Unicef. The air bridge involves flights operated by the Dubai Royal Air Wing using C-130 aircraft, each carrying approximately nine metric tonnes of humanitarian supplies. At least three more flights are scheduled in the coming days to deliver blankets for children and other vulnerable groups as families prepare for the approaching winter.

title: Russian Embassy in Spain conveys condolences over tragic train collision
body:
MADRID, October 28. /TASS/. The Russian Embassy in Madrid extended its deepest condolences on Wednesday to the families of those who died in the collision between two passenger trains in the province of Toledo (in the Castilla La Mancha Autonomous Community).
"We express our most sincere and deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives in the accident. We wish a speedy recovery to the injured," the Russian Embassy said in a statement on its Telegram channel.
Local television channel Antena 3 reported earlier on Wednesday that at least 50 people had been killed and 179 more had been injured in a collision between two high-speed passenger trains in Toledo Province in central Spain.
Spain’s ABC daily reported earlier in the day that at least 46 people were killed in the tragic accident, which occurred around 9:00 a.m. local time near the town of Urda in the Castilla La Mancha region. Two cars of one of the trains derailed.

title: Rajnath Singh, Japanese Counterpart Review Defence Ties, Explore Naval Cooperation
body:
By R Anil Kumar

Cebu, Philippines, Oct 28, 2026. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and his Japanese counterpart Shinjiro Koizumi on October 28, reviewed bilateral defence cooperation and explored ways to strengthen the India-Japan Special Strategic and Global Partnership during a meeting in Cebu, Philippines.



Meeting on the sidelines of the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus, the ministers welcomed progress in maritime security, air force exchanges and defence industry engagement since their previous meeting in August.

Maritime discussions covered strengthening mine countermeasure capabilities and exploring joint development in naval shipbuilding and design by combining Japan’s technological expertise with India’s production capabilities.

The ministers noted that engagements, including the Indian Navy Vice Chief’s visit to Japan, had helped advance discussions on cooperation suited to both countries’ strategic and operational needs.

They also reviewed efforts to strengthen ties between their air services following the first visit to India by Japan Air Self-Defense Force fighter aircraft for Exercise Veer Guardian 26. The Japanese air service’s Chief of Staff visited India in conjunction with the exercise.

Both sides welcomed the India-Japan Defence Industry Forum held at the Indian Embassy in Tokyo, which brought together approximately 40 companies from the two countries.

The ministers agreed to accelerate discussions on convening the fourth India-Japan Foreign and Defence Ministerial Meeting, known as the 2+2 dialogue, and a Defence Ministers’ Meeting in Tokyo later this year.

In a post on X, Singh described the talks as productive and said the two sides had reviewed ongoing cooperation and explored new avenues for strengthening their partnership.

“Our shared commitment remains vital for a free, open, and peaceful Indo-Pacific region,” he said.

title: Azov personnel strike over 100 Russian trains
body:
Personnel from the Azov unit of the National Guard of Ukraine (NGU) are striking enemy logistics, specifically fuel supply lines heading toward the front.

"Thanks to your donations and the work of the Come Back Alive foundation—which provided 440 Starlink Mini terminals—the Azov unit of the NGU has successfully struck more than 100 trains used for enemy logistics," the Azov press service reported.

It is noted that Azov drones systematically monitor rail traffic at stations in key supply hubs for the occupying forces in Donetsk region, including Volnovakha, Debaltseve, Yasynuvata, Yenakiyeve, and Dovzhansk.

"Disrupting fuel supply chains to the front line leads to ammunition shortages, weakened support for combat units, and failures in the maintenance of weaponry and equipment. The occupiers face an extremely difficult winter ahead. This cannot be fixed by deceitful statements or AI-generated special effects," the unit emphasized.

title: Iran economy faces 25% deeper contraction amid soaring inflation, major employment crisis
body: Iran's struggling economy could see as many as 1.4 million people leave the labor market by the end of the Iranian calendar year if the pattern of economic contraction continues, according to Seyed Malek Hosseini, deputy for entrepreneurship and employment in Iran's Cooperatives, Labor and Social Welfare Ministry.According to official figures Hosseini cited in an interview with the Iranian Labor News Agency earlier this week, about 700,000 jobs were lost during the war, though he acknowledged unofficial reports suggest the actual figure could be closer to two million.The economy and employment sector was hit by an Internet blackout lasting nearly three months, starting during the January protests earlier this year, which left many people unable to access the online platforms and services needed to run their businesses and carry out their work.Even if all 700,000 people whose job losses the government acknowledged applied for monthly unemployment benefits, the 16 million to 17 million tomans they would receive would be insufficient to cover basic living costs amid soaring inflation, Hosseini said.Year-on-year inflation reached 89.8% in September 2026, while the national consumer price index rose 4.2% from August to 729.8, the Statistical Center of Iran reported last month.The soaring cost of living has reportedly had fatal consequences. Two retired Iran Air employees had died after they could no longer afford treatment and medication, Iran Air Retirees Association chairman Jalal Hashemi told ILNA.Despite the regime's failure to increase retirement and welfare benefits, and amid weekly protests, Lebanon-based Hezbollah has reportedly received tens of millions of dollars from Iran to build up its military capabilities ahead of future wars with Israel, according to unnamed sources who spoke with Reuters earlier this week. This is in addition to $200 million reportedly provided last month to compensate the displaced.Chronic structural issues in labor marketHosseini said 54% of Iran's labor market was in the informal sector, a share that had grown further following the war. Many workers in this sector lack employment protections and insurance coverage, while others are unable to secure enough working hours or income to meet their basic needs, he said.“It shows that our labor market suffers from chronic structural problems,” Hosseini said. “Formal employment and extensive insurance coverage are products of a dynamic, capable economy that experiences high growth rates over long periods.”Citing a 20-year assessment, he said Iran's economy had recorded average annual growth of about 2.2% to 2.3% over the past two decades. Each percentage point of economic growth created about 170,000 jobs, while each percentage-point decline was associated with an average loss of a similar number of jobs, he added.BEFORE THE wars with Israel began, Iran had a working-age population of 65 million and a labor-force participation rate of 40%, Hosseini said, adding that more than one million jobs had already been lost, with the number of employed people falling from 24.7 million to about 23.5 million to 23.7 million by the end of this past March.“Official reports show that economic growth in the spring, compared with the same period in the previous year, was negative 10% excluding oil and negative 4.6% including oil,” he said. “Given the increased sanctions and the serious economic blockade, we expect the summer to follow the same trajectory.“Negative growth inevitably reduces employment. When consumers' purchasing power and demand for furniture, electronics, food, and other goods decline, businesses reduce production. Lower revenue then forces them to cut costs.“Businesses' resilience has been depleted. Since sanctions were reimposed in 2018 under US President Donald Trump's first administration, Iran has faced sanctions, COVID-19, high inflation, and three periods of conflict. Inflation, particularly in the cost of production inputs, has driven up expenses while reducing demand. Businesses have consequently had to scale down or leave the market entirely.”Further contractions expected in coming monthsNearly 740,000 people had left Iran's formal labor market following the 12-day war in June, Hosseini said. That figure does not include workers in the informal sector, who are not covered by the relevant employment insurance, he added.About 1.15 million people were removed from Iran's compulsory social-insurance rolls between March and August, although further analysis was needed to distinguish retirements, disabilities, and new registrations, Hosseini said.By the end of August, about 300,000 people had been added to the number of unemployment-benefit recipients and were receiving payments, he said.Many people who had lost their jobs had not yet applied for benefits, either because they hoped to return to their previous employment or because they wanted to preserve their eligibility for a more serious emergency, Hosseini said.US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Tuesday told Iran International the Iranian economy would contract an additional 25% by next March and recommended that Iranian civilians begin stocking up on gasoline.According to the Financial Times, Mohammad Reza Aref, Iran's first vice president, earlier this week began urging citizens to limit their use of subsidized gas to prepare for greater domestic demand in the winter. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has also called for citizens to cut the country's natural-gas consumption by 10%.With Iran's energy infrastructure significantly damaged by the war, caretaker Oil Minister Hamid Bovard discussed joint oil and gas projects with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Monday. A gas trade deal was “almost finalized,” Iran's semi-official Tasnim News Agency reported, adding that Russia was developing four major Iranian oil fields under contracts agreed by both sides.“My advice to the Iranian people would be: Don't pay your taxes because you're not going to get anything back from the government,” Bessent said, although taxes are often automatically deducted from employee pay.“We are seeing the regime go bankrupt,” he said. “So many of the people who are holding money outside of Iran do not want to send it back in.”Unsanctioned Iranians could provide information to the US Treasury under its whistleblower program and be rewarded up to 30% of recovered funds, Bessent said.

title: Ghana–New Zealand Chamber seeks tourism partnerships between the two countries
body: The Ghana-New Zealand Chamber of Commerce is exploring opportunities to strengthen tourism and business ties between Ghana and New Zealand by connecting tourism operators, guides and industry stakeholders in both countries. The Executive Director of the Ghana–New Zealand Chamber of Commerce, Mr Isaac Koumessina, said the initiative would create opportunities for both countries to share tourism experiences, promote their attractions and develop partnerships within the sector. Speaking on the sidelines of the recently concluded 2026 Inter Tourism Expo in Cape Coast, he said the Chamber was working to facilitate connections between Ghanaian tourism businesses and their counterparts in New Zealand. Mr Kumesina said the Chamber’s involvement in the sixth edition of the expo followed an agreement with the organisers to collaborate on promoting tourism and business opportunities. “When Inter Tourism Expo contacted us, it was an exciting opportunity for us to collaborate. We had an MoU signed, and then we decided that we have to support the Inter Tourism Expo, the sixth edition of the Tourism Expo,” he said. He disclosed that the Chamber had held discussions with the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA) on tourism and other sectors, including energy, as part of efforts to identify areas for cooperation. According to him, GIPA had also requested the organisation of an event to facilitate engagement with stakeholders in New Zealand and explore opportunities for linking tourism attractions in both countries. “Now, the GIPA also requested that we organise an event to get them into New Zealand. Then they can find out how many Ghanaians are in New Zealand, what are the tourism attraction areas in New Zealand, and how we can link both tourism attraction-related events between New Zealand and Ghana,” he said. Mr Kumesina said the proposed engagement would also provide an opportunity to connect tour operators and guides in Cape Coast with tourism agencies in New Zealand, enabling them to showcase local attractions and explore potential partnerships. He said stronger cooperation could help businesses in both countries benefit from tourism-related opportunities while expanding international exposure for Ghana’s tourism industry. The Chamber’s initiative comes as Ghana continues to explore ways to attract more international visitors and strengthen tourism’s contribution to economic development. Mr Kumesina also called for greater coordination among Ghana’s tourism agencies, citing New Zealand’s year-round tourism activities as a model Ghana could consider adopting to sustain visitor interest and create more business opportunities. He said stronger collaboration among tourism stakeholders, coupled with targeted promotion, could help position Ghana as a destination offering activities and experiences throughout the year.

title: Death toll in Spain’s passenger train collision reaches 64 — daily
body:
MADRID, October 28. /TASS/. The confirmed number of fatalities in a collision between two high-speed passenger trains in Toledo Province in central Spain has risen to 64, while up to 180 were injured, El Diario daily reported.
TASS has compiled the key details about the tragic accident.
- The accident took place at around 9:00 a.m. local time.
- According to Europa Press, two passenger trains collided near the town of Urda in the Castilla La Mancha region.
- El Pais daily reported later that the accident took place between two residential settlements in the Province of Toledo.
- Two cars of one of the trains derailed, according to reports.
- EFE news agency specified that the two trains involved in the collision were passenger trains.
- Up to 544 passengers were on board the trains in total before the collision.
- El·Pais daily reported that 197 passengers were booked for on the high-speed train operated by the railway company Renfe, while 147 more passengers, including an infant, were booked for taking a ride at the train operated by the Iryo company.
- Medics and fire and rescue teams are working at the scene of the accident.
- Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez confirmed that the emergency relief services are working at the scene of the tragedy.
- According to him, they are providing assistance to the victims and ensuring their safety in coordination with all relevant authorities.
- The reported number of fatalities in a collision between two high-speed passenger trains in Toledo Province in central Spain has risen to 64, El Diario daily reported.
- According to the daily, up to 50 injured people have been diagnosed with moderate injuries, while 15 more are in serious condition.
- Local television channel Antena 3 reported earlier in the day that at least 179 people were injured in the accident.
- The Spanish government considers human error to be one of the possible causes of the collision between two passenger trains, El Pais daily reported, citing its sources.
- According to the daily, the possible cause of the accident was human error by an Adif company operator (the operator of the railway network) due to a failure in the security system.
- The daily pointed out that the system is fully automated and train movements were initially halted due to a malfunction; however, switching to manual control could have led to the malfunction, ultimately causing the disaster.
- ABC claimed in turn, citing its sources, that an employee responsible for overseeing the safety system failed to issue an earlier warning about the dangerous proximity of the approaching trains.
- The Russian Embassy in Madrid stated that no Russian nationals were reported to sustain injuries in the tragic train collision in central Spain.
- Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said he was shocked by the news of the passenger train collision in the Province of Toledo.
- Sanchez pointed out that he was in permanent contact with Transport Minister Oscar Puente and the regional authorities.
- The Russian Embassy in Madrid told TASS that it had received no inquiries from Russian nationals regarding the railway disaster in the Spanish Province of Toledo.
- The Russian Embassy in Madrid extended its deepest condolences to the families of those who died in the collision between two passenger trains in the province of Toledo. "We express our most sincere and deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives in the accident. We wish a speedy recovery to the injured," the Russian Embassy said in a statement.

title: Russia builds highly efficient fishing fleet — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Russia is building high-capacity and high-performance ships for fish catching and processing directly at sea, President Vladimir Putin said.
"We have started building the fleet for fisheries. For catching and processing. These are such large plants for catching and processing of fish resources," the head of state said. "Some of our partners, for example, Indonesia, the President of Indonesia, showed high interest [in them]. Even the Soviet Union was not building such large ships for fish catching and processing. The vessels are modern and very efficient," the head of state said.

title: Russia imports five times more prosthetic arms and legs from Germany than before the war
body: Germany supplied Russia with prosthetic arms and legs, as well as artificial joints, worth 79 million euros in the first half of 2026, almost a third more than a year earlier, according to Eurostat data reviewed by Forbes Russia.
