Prosthetic arms and legs and related components accounted for 41.2 million euros of that total, while endoprostheses — artificial hip, knee, and other joint replacements — accounted for 37.8 million euros. Supplies of prosthetic arms and legs grew 5.4 times compared with 2021, while shipments of endoprostheses grew 6.1 times. Russia received prostheses and endoprostheses worth a total of 144.9 million euros from European Union countries in the first half of 2026, compared with 66.5 million euros during the same period in 2021. Russia’s prosthetics market is growing, but domestic production capacity is not keeping pace with demand, Forbes writes. People with disabilities received 152,661 prosthetic arms and legs from the state in 2024, more than in any of the previous 10 years, according to the Labor Ministry. Market participants say prosthetics are now being issued significantly faster and recipients have become significantly younger. Young people accounted for about 8% of those needing prosthetics before 2022, but their share had grown to 15–20% by 2025, according to Rostec, the Russian state defense conglomerate. Most are people who fought in the war with Ukraine and were wounded there. Younger patients need more complex, technologically advanced devices, but production of these prostheses in Russia has “historically developed somewhat more slowly,” experts say. As a result, Russian-made products account for about 80% of the prosthetics market by unit but only 30% by value, and imports account for up to 70% of the market for expensive, high-tech components. title: 2027: Kwankwaso joins TikTok, promises daily life content
body: By Adegboyega Adeleye The vice-presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, has joined TikTok, promising followers authentic information, latest updates and exclusive content about his daily life as he prepares for the 2027 general election alongside presidential candidate Peter Obi. Kwankwaso announced his arrival on the social media platform in a post on his X handle on Wednesday, urging Nigerians to follow his account and engage with his videos. “I am on TikTok! I encourage you all to follow me there for authentic information, the latest updates, and exclusive contents directly related to my daily life. “Nigeria will be OK. — RMK,” he wrote. In a video attached to the post, the former Kano State governor also welcomed users to his account and encouraged them to follow and share his content. “Hello TikTokers, welcome to our TikTok account. Turn on your notifications, follow us, share our video, thank you, and God bless you,” he said. Kwankwaso’s move comes as the NDC steps up preparations for the 2027 presidential election, in which he is expected to run alongside Obi on the party’s ticket. The two opposition figures formally joined the NDC in May after leaving the African Democratic Congress (ADC), following consultations over their political future and the party’s zoning arrangement. Obi was subsequently ratified as the NDC’s presidential candidate at its national convention on May 30, with Kwankwaso named as his running mate. The ticket brings together Obi’s political support base and Kwankwaso’s Kwankwasiyya movement, which has a strong presence in Kano and other parts of the North. The party recently unveiled its National Campaign Council ahead of the 2027 election, with its National Leader, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, named chairman and Obi appointed co-chairman. Kwankwaso was named co-vice-chairman, while Ibrahim Hussain Abdulkarim was appointed Director-General of the campaign council. The campaign council is expected to coordinate the party’s nationwide campaign activities and mobilisation ahead of the election. The post 2027: Kwankwaso joins TikTok, promises daily life content appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Drone strike cuts power to large parts of Khartoum
body: A drone strike on the Al-Markhiyat transformer station in Omdurman has disrupted electricity supplies across large parts of Sudan’s capital, Khartoum, worsening living conditions for residents already struggling with shortages of basic services. The station was hit early on Tuesday, 27 October, and taken out of service, according to the Ministry of Energy and Petroleum. The ministry said the facility sustained extensive damage and that technical teams were assessing the site to determine the repairs needed to restore electricity. The outages affected large parts of Khartoum and River Nile State, as well as areas in several other states, the ministry said. It did not give a specific timeline for restoring normal power supplies. Abdel-Gadir Al-Sheikh, a resident of Khartoum, told Radio Tamazuj that prolonged electricity and water shortages, fuel scarcity, bakery closures and the spread of mosquitoes had further worsened living conditions. He described the situation as extremely difficult, saying access to essential services had become increasingly challenging. He added that similar hardships were affecting people elsewhere in Sudan. Repeated attacks The strike followed drone attacks on electricity facilities in several states on Monday, 26 October. The Sudanese Electricity Company accused the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) of targeting power stations in Al-Jazirah, Sennar, Al-Qadarif and White Nile states. The affected facilities included Al-Junaid in Al-Jazirah State, Singa in Sennar State, Al-Hawata and Al-Faw in Al-Gedarif State, and Mashkour in White Nile State. The attacks damaged electrical equipment and disrupted power supplies, raising concerns about the stability of Sudan’s national electricity grid. Sudanese authorities also blamed the RSF for the attack on Al-Markhiyat. The United Nations has expressed concern over continued drone attacks in Sudan and damage to critical civilian infrastructure, including electricity facilities. Power cuts threaten essential services such as water supplies, healthcare and bakeries, adding to the hardships faced by civilians amid shortages and economic disruption. Sudan has been at war since April 2023, when fighting erupted between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the RSF following disagreements over the integration of the paramilitary group into the regular military. The conflict has killed tens of thousands of people, displaced millions and deepened hunger and the humanitarian crisis across the country, according to the United Nations and international estimates. The post Drone strike cuts power to large parts of Khartoum appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Binduri Naaba urges EPA to prosecute violators of Styrofoam ban
body: Binduri Naaba and Alhaji Akorlbila Agetwin Robert have called on the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) to prosecute individuals and businesses that violate Ghana’s impending ban on Styrofoam products, insisting that strict enforcement is essential to securing compliance. He described the ban on Styrofoam and single-use plastics as long overdue, citing the unacceptable levels of pollution across the country and the urgent need for decisive action to protect the environment. The traditional ruler made the call during a stakeholder engagement organised by the EPA in Bolgatanga in the Upper East Region on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, as part of an intensive campaign to sensitise the public to the forthcoming ban. While commending the John Dramani Mahama-led administration for the initiative, the Binduri Naaba urged the Authority to go beyond public education and ensure that offenders face the full force of the law once implementation begins. “As a traditional ruler, I am a custodian of the environment and therefore welcome the government’s proposed ban. I just want to add that prosecution must be part of the implementation, and all those who violate any aspect of the ban must be prosecuted,” he said. He added that consistent enforcement and prosecution would be critical to achieving full compliance, warning against an approach that raises public awareness without holding violators accountable. “That is the only way we can get full compliance with the ban,” he stressed. The Binduri Naaba’s appeal comes as the EPA steps up nationwide public education ahead of January 1, 2027, when the ban on Styrofoam products is scheduled to take effect. The Authority has launched an intensive, week-long awareness campaign across northern Ghana, visiting regional capitals, including Bolgatanga, to engage stakeholders and educate communities on the policy and its environmental implications. The campaign, led by EPA Chief Executive Officer, Professor Nana Ama Browne Klutse, seeks to deepen public understanding of the ban, encourage responsible consumer choices and secure voluntary compliance before enforcement begins. The EPA has given manufacturers, importers and distributors advance notice to prepare for the implementation deadline and stop stocking the prohibited products ahead of the ban. The Authority has also made it clear that the January 1, 2027, deadline will not be extended, signalling its determination to proceed with implementation as scheduled. The northern Ghana campaign follows similar public education exercises in Accra and Kumasi and is expected to culminate in a major durbar in Tamale. The closing activities are expected to include a public float, a quiz competition and a debate on the environmental implications of Styrofoam pollution and the importance of the impending ban. The EPA is using the engagements to mobilise traditional authorities, businesses, institutions and the general public behind the policy, as Ghana prepares to phase out the prohibited products. The Binduri Naaba’s call adds to the growing emphasis on enforcement as a critical component of the exercise, with the January deadline fast approaching.

title: With conflicts escalating worldwide, Security Council underscores need to protect women, girls, include them in peace negotiations
body:
By R Anil Kumar

New York/Bengaluru, Oct 27, 2026. The “ancient, universal power imbalance between women and men” remains “glaring” and demands urgent action, the Security Council heard today, as the 15-member organ opened its annual open debate on women, peace and security.



António Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations, addressed the theme of “Women, peace and security in the next quarter century: fulfilling the promise through implementation”, affirming that the story of crises confronting the world is one of power: “Who holds it — and who is denied it.”

Despite the legacy of Council resolution 1325 (2000), he said “the plague of gender inequality persists”, with women absent from negotiating tables, peacebuilders underfunded and “women and girls caught within the hell of conflict”, enduring “horrific acts of violence — including sexual violence”.

Noting “positive strides”, including over 110 countries adopting national action plans on women, peace and security, he called for a minimum target of one third for women’s participation in UN peace processes and gender parity across all senior leadership, Headquarters and Professional staff “for the first time in history”.

With the world facing the highest number of conflicts since the Second World War, the number of UN-verified cases of conflict-related sexual violence has sharply increased, reaching over 9,700 last year, with girls denied education and facing severe restrictions in Afghanistan, Mali, Yemen and Somalia.

Meanwhile, with global military expenditures skyrocketing to almost $2.9 trillion last year, foreign aid continues to plummet. Noting that women represented just 5 per cent of negotiators across 57 peace processes last year, he urged all States to live up to official development assistance (ODA) commitments. “Equality is not a dream,” he stressed. “It’s a decision.”

Exclusion of Women Not Accidental:

Sima Sami Bahous, Executive Director, United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women (UN-Women), said that, after 26 years of commitments, it is indefensible that nearly 80 per cent of active peace negotiations last year took place without a single woman at the table. “This exclusion is not accidental,” she said. “It reflects persistent institutional barriers, unequal power relations and deeply entrenched gender norms that continue to deny women their rightful place in shaping peace.” Not 1 of 13 ceasefire agreements reached in 2025 included substantive references to women and girls and not one prohibited sexual violence, she recalled.

Echoing the Secretary-General’s call for action, she urged that at least 15 per cent of ODA be earmarked to conflict-affected countries, specifically to advance gender equality. Further, impunity for crimes against women and girls must end, sanctioning and holding accountable those responsible. “The question now is whether we have the courage to share power,” she stressed.

Tamana Zaryab Paryani, human rights activist, said women in Afghanistan are forced out of public life as their rights are routinely violated, without access to mechanisms to hold violators accountable — a reality extending to the Occupied Palestinian Territory, Sudan, Myanmar and beyond. Gender justice and women’s rights must be integrated throughout the Council’s work, she stressed, and the targeting of women and marginalized groups should be treated as a threat to international peace and security. The international community must refuse to normalize these violations, she added, voicing alarm over several countries that have handed over diplomatic recognition to the Taliban. “Women’s rights must be the number one priority in any engagement with the Taliban,” she stressed, calling on the international community to define gender apartheid as a crime against humanity.

As the floor opened for debate, the representative of the United States recalled that the country is “the biggest single donor to the humanitarian system” and understands the imperative of protection assistance for women and girls in conflict and disaster settings — particularly victims of sexual violence. “It is after all the twenty-first century, we all deserve better,” she stressed, urging Member States “to match words with deeds”. She then called it “unacceptable” for Afghanistan to deny girls education, reversing decades of hard-won progress, further denouncing pervasive sexual violence in Haiti, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Sudan and South Sudan.

Conflict Prevention, Root Causes Must Be Central to Women, Peace and Security:

From an African perspective, Somalia’s delegate emphasized that “conflict prevention must be central to the women, peace and security agenda”, addressing the root causes that allow conflict to persist — “including prolonged occupation, political exclusion, discrimination and violations of human rights”. Liberia’s delegate said his country’s experience with conflict left it questioning “how women can help bring a war to an end yet still struggle for influence over the peace that follows”.

The representative of Nigeria noted women’s meaningful participation in mediation must become the norm rather than the exception, with “a seat at the negotiating table”, while national justice systems must hold perpetrators of conflict-related sexual violence accountable. “Survivors, including women and girls formerly held captive by terrorist groups, must have access to medical care, psychosocial assistance and economic opportunities to rebuild their lives,” he said. The representative of the Democratic Republic of the Congo called on the Council to systematically include a gender analysis in mandates, improve follow-up on women’s participation in peace processes, and strengthen oversight of commitments made by Member States. He further called for support to networks of female mediators, training programmes and mentorships.

Escalating Conflicts, Violence Demand Shift from Commitments to Implementation:

Georgios Gerapetritis, Minister for Foreign Affairs of Greece and Council President for October, affirmed the UN Sanctions Committees’ role as crucial in ensuring that sexual and gender-based violence is included as a standalone designation in all criteria against sanction regimes. Victims and survivors of conflict-related sexual violence must have safe and unhindered access to sexual and reproductive healthcare and psychosocial support. As conflicts and violence against women escalate, Bahrain’s delegate said shifting from commitments to actual implementation is critical. “The lesson is not in the multiplicity of decisions, but in the extent to which they are implemented and their impact on the lives of women and girls,” he said.

The Russian Federation’s delegate noted the country is a G20 leader in the proportion of women in leadership positions, calling the status of women globally a “litmus test” for broader trends. Condemning Ukraine as a country of harsh censorship and repression, she noted it has been five years since appointment of the presidential ombudsperson on children’s rights — reuniting parents of Ukrainian and Russian children who were separated because of the crisis.

However, Oleksandr Karasevych, State Secretary for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine, cited the recent Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) report documenting 892 cases of conflict-related sexual violence “perpetrated by representatives of the Russian Federation”, including 151 cases against women and 14 cases against girls. He stressed the report “confirmed that sexual violence was used as a method of torture and other forms of cruel inhuman or degrading treatment.”

Women, peace and security is ‘not a slogan’:

It is an operational imperative, said Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations Jean-Pierre Lacroix.

“When women participate, lead and shape decisions, peacekeeping is more effective and peace is more sustainable,” he said.

Women must sit at peace tables, meaningfully shape outcomes, Nigeria say:

To bridge the gap between commitment and implementation, Nigeria’s delegate said women's meaningful participation in mediation must become the norm rather than the exception.

“Women must have a seat at the negotiating table and a meaningful voice in shaping the outcomes,” he said, adding that predictable and sustainable financing must reach women-led organizations working in conflict-affected communities.

National justice systems, with appropriate international support, must hold perpetrators of conflict-related sexual violence accountable.

“Survivors, including women and girls formerly held captive by terrorist groups, must have access to medical care, psychosocial assistance and economic opportunities to rebuild their lives,” he said.

 ‘War is getting deadlier for women and girls’:

The battlefields have become more deadly for women and girls, according to major UN report

“War is getting deadlier for women and girls and the world is allowing it to happen,” UN Women Deputy Executive Director Nyaradzayi Gumbonzvanda told journalists at UN Headquarters in New York, presenting the UN Secretary-General’s annual report on women, peace and security.

“For them, war is not something they can scroll past. War is outside their door.”

Stronger international cooperation needed to investigate, prosecute conflict- related sexual violence, Ukraine says:

Oleksandr Karasevych, State Secretary for the Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Ukraine, emphasized the “particular importance for Ukraine” of ensuring accountability for war crimes and grave human rights violations committed by the Russian army against women and girls - including conflict-related sexual violence, “which continues to have serious consequences for survivors their families and affected communities”.

He cited the recent Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) report, which documented 892 cases of conflict related sexual violence perpetrated by representatives of the Russian Federation, including 151 cases against women and 14 cases against girls.

The report “confirmed that sexual violence was used as a method of torture and other forms of cruel inhuman or degrading treatment as well as a means of intimidation and coercion”.

The findings underscore the urgent need to strengthen international cooperation in investigating and prosecuting conflict related sexual violence and ensure that perpetrators are held accountable.

Women should be included in peace negotiations, appointed lead mediators, Somalia says

Somalia’s delegate, Abukar Dahir Osman, emphasized that “conflict prevention must be central to the women, peace and security agenda”, addressing the root causes that allow conflict to persist – “including prolonged occupation, political exclusion, discrimination and violations of human rights”.

Women should be included directly in negotiating delegations and appointed as lead mediators, he said.

As protection must be matched by accountability, he emphasized the plight of Palestinian women who continue to endure killing, injury, displacement, deprivation and trauma.

With nearly 1 million women and girls forced from their homes, the long-standing occupation on the Palestinian land must end.

title: Putin says only Russia has low-capacity NPPs already in operation
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Russia is the only country that has not only developed but also operates low-capacity floating nuclear power plants (NPPs), President Vladimir Putin said while viewing an exhibition on the sidelines of the Russia-Africa summit, adding that no other nation in the world, including those in the West, has managed to achieve anything of the kind.
"This is not just a development project. This plant is in operation. It is located in the Arctic zone in northern Russia, and since 2020 it has been working and generating energy," he said referring to the Akademik Lomonosov low-capacity floating nuclear power plant. "It is quite efficient: they are in demand in certain conditions," the Russian leader added.
"And our competitors, French, Japanese, American companies, all claim they are ready to develop small power plants. However, no one has practically done anything yet. In Russia, there is [the plant] that has been built and is operational. Nothing like it exists anywhere else in the world yet," he stated.

title: Rays stun Brewers with rally in 12th inning and force World Series Game 5
body:
Jonny DeLuca and pinch-hitter Ben Williamson singled home runs in a stunning 12th-inning rally, and the Tampa Bay Rays staved off World Series elimination with a 4-3 win over the Milwaukee Brewers that forced Game 5
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- Milwaukee was three outs from its first World Series title when Junior Caminero started the bottom of the 12th inning with a grounder to third. Thousands of Brewers fans who trekked to Tropicana Field to witness the long-awaited moment started to cheer.
Third baseman Joey Ortiz bounced the throw, and the ball glanced off first baseman Jake Bauers’ mitt for an error.
One of the most stunning rallies in World Series history started to unfold.
Liam Hicks, Jonny DeLuca, Chandler Simpson and pinch-hitter Ben Williamson followed with consecutive singles in a 15-pitch span against rookie Shane Drohan, and the Tampa Bay Rays staved off elimination Tuesday night with a 4-3 win that forced Game 5.
“Sometimes the game tests you. Sometimes the game makes you want to dig deep,” Brewers captain Christian Yelich said. “It’s all part of the journey, all part of the experience, and that’s part of our story.”
Milwaukee rookie Cooper Pratt hit a tiebreaking home run off Ian Seymour in the top of the 12th for a 3-2 lead, sending the Brewers sprinting out of the dugout in excitement as they sensed completing the first Series sweep since 2012.
Milwaukee's bullpen, led by seven outs from Aaron Ashby , had combined for seven straight scoreless innings, before Caminero reached against Antonio Senzatela.
“I've got to make that play," he said. “Just no excuse about it.”
Caminero appeared to hurt his left foot but stayed in the game. Brewers manager Pat Murphy brought in Drohan, a 27-year-old left-hander who had not pitched since a one-inning start in Game 4 of the National League Championship Series on Oct. 15.
With Pratt shifted toward second for the left-handed batter, Hicks hit an opposite-field grounder through the vacated shortstop hole and into left field as Caminero slid headfirst into third.
“For just regular D, that's right at Coop,” Drohan said of the defensive alignment.
Pinch-runner Cedric Mullins replaced Caminero before DeLuca, who had made sparkling catches to deny Yelich in the third and William Contreras in the fourth, hit a grounder past the mound as Drohan tried in vain to make a behind-the-back snag. The ball bounced into center as Mullins tied the score at 3.
Nick Fortes ran at second for the slower Hicks. After missing a bunt attempt and pulling back another while taking a called strike, Simpson lined a single into center, loading the bases.
Sal Frelick moved in from left to form a five-man infield, with three defenders on the left side and everyone playing in.
Williamson, who had been 1 for 15 in the postseason, batted for Victor Mesa Jr.
"It’s what you dream of as a player to be in that spot,” Williamson said.
On the game's 367th pitch, he hit a chopper that kicked up chalk from the foul line 7 feet from home plate. The ball bounded high over Bauers and onto the grass in short right field. Fortes sprinted across the plate with the winning run, then headed toward first to join his jumping teammates in foul territory.
“That was totally what I told him to do,” Rays manager Kevin Cash said, drawing laughs.
“Definitely hard. I’m human," he said softly. “I knew what I was walking into. I just didn’t do the job there.”
Tampa Bay became the fourth team in World Series history to avoid elimination with an extra-inning comeback, according to OptaSTATS, joining the 1912 Boston Red Sox, 1986 New York Mets and 2011 St. Louis Cardinals — who all went on to win titles.
“We've got a lot of fight in us. We’re never going to shy away," Simpson said. “We were going to keep fighting until the end — the last inning, the last out, the last play, the last pitch."
Game 5 in the best-of-seven matchup is Wednesday night at Tropicana Field, with NL Cy Young Award favorite Jacob Misiorowski scheduled to start for the Brewers. Cash said he hadn't decided on a starter yet.
Tampa Bay became just the fifth of 26 teams that fell behind 3-0 in the World Series to win Game 4. The previous four lost Game 5.
Of 43 teams to trail 3-0 in any best-of-seven postseason matchup, the only one that rebounded to win was the Boston Red Sox against the New York Yankees in the 2004 AL Championship Series.
“It just shows the resiliency of this group,” Williamson said. “We continue to fight, and that’s been the motto this series and this full season, is just fight.”
Caminero was replaced by Mullins at third base and hobbled off the field with an ailing left foot. But the All-Star slugger said he’ll definitely play Wednesday night.
“He’ll play tomorrow on one leg. I’ll make sure of it,” Cash said.
Tampa Bay ended an eight-game winning streak by the Brewers, who were bidding to become only the second team to sweep a League Championship Series and the World Series.
“I feel like today we’ve just been playing so free,” DeLuca said. “It’s a pretty cool position we’re in and it’s a special opportunity that we have."
David Hamilton also homered for the Brewers. Jackson Chourio had a single and double, improving to 10 for 20 in the Series.
“When you’re achieving something like this, it’s going to have its adversity,” Murphy said. “We had some things go our way yesterday. They had some things go their way today. That’s the way it is.”
Pratt, a 22-year-old who debuted in June, drove a slider into the left-field seats against Seymour to become the first rookie to hit a World Series extra-inning homer. His go-ahead hit sparked the Brewers to a 5-4 win in Game 2 after Seymour allowed Frelick’s tying home run.
“Nobody said this was going to be easy,” Pratt said.
Milwaukee fans in the crowd of 40,514, many waving yellow towels and some wearing cheeseheads, brought a Badger State feel to Tropicana Field.
Tampa Bay returned to its white home jerseys, a day after playing in Devil Rays throwbacks.
Simpson hit an RBI double off starter Dustin May in the second, but Milwaukee tied the score in the fourth against Griffin Jax when Frelick hit a two-out single and came around on Pratt's double.
Caminero singled leading off the bottom half to chase May and advanced on a groundout. DeLuca hit a hard grounder to Hamilton and Caminero twisted toward the grass to avoid the third baseman’s tag, then came home when Hamilton bounced his throw past Bauers for an error.
Hamilton, Milwaukee’s No. 9 hitter, drove an 0-2 fastball at the letters from Jax into the right-field seats for his second home run of the postseason — half his regular-season total and just his second since June 6.
Six scoreless innings followed before the late drama in a 4-hour, 20-minute game that ended at 12:28 a.m. with the first Series walk-off pinch hit in extra innings since Gene Larkin's single won Game 7 for Minnesota in 1991.
“You play Wiffle ball in the backyard with your friends and you’re dreaming of hitting a walk-off ball in the World Series,” Williamson said.

title: 80% of Ukrainians back strikes on Russian refineries even if US cuts support, poll shows
body:
The vast majority of Ukrainians want Kyiv to continue striking Russian refineries, even if the U.S. threatens to end or curb its support, according to a survey by the Kyiv International Institute of Sociology (KIIS) published on Oct. 28.
Some 80% of respondents back the continued strikes, even if Washington restricts intelligence sharing or Starlink operations. Only 11% said Ukraine should pause the attacks, despite Russia 's ongoing attacks on the Ukrainian energy grid and other civilian facilities.
U.S. President Donald Trump has urged Kyiv to stop attacking Russian refineries, a key source of revenue for Moscow's federal budget that helps fund its war against Ukraine.
As Washington ramped up pressure, Ukraine said it had faced a temporary pause in U.S. intelligence sharing on incoming Russian ballistic missiles, restrictions on Starlink operations , and delays in Patriot air defense missile shipments.
The U.S. administration has denied ordering any restrictions to pressure Kyiv.
Trump unilaterally declared an energy truce between Ukraine and Russia on Oct. 11. Kyiv then largely suspended strikes against Russian refineries for three days, President Volodymyr Zelensky said.
In the meantime, Russia has continued attacking Ukrainian energy facilities, driving fears about energy and heating outages as winter approaches.
According to the KIIS poll, 63% of Ukrainians are ready to endure the war as long as necessary, a rate that has remained largely stable since summer.
Some 76% of respondents supported continued armed resistance against Russia, even if Moscow's attacks in winter result in outages in electricity, heat, and sewage.
The survey was conducted between Oct. 16 and 25 through telephone interviews with 828 respondents living in the government-controlled territories.

title: Rosatom Says It’s in Advanced Talks to Supply Floating Nuclear Power Plants to African Countries
body:
Russia 's state nuclear corporation Rosatom could supply floating nuclear power plants to coastal African countries and is in advanced discussions with at least four nations, senior company executives said Wednesday at the Russia -Africa Summit.
Vladimir Aptekarev, deputy head of Rosatom's machine-building division, said that 38 of Africa's more than 50 countries have sufficient coastline to host a Russia n-made floating power unit.
At present, only one floating nuclear power plant is in operation globally, in Russia 's remote Chukotka region, dating from 2020. Floating plants use smaller reactors, are contained within a vessel which can be towed to a destination and require less infrastructure on land. They also make it possible to secure a new source of energy quickly and at a lower cost.
"As a first step, a floating nuclear power unit can serve as a good entry point, enabling a country both to address its energy needs and to join the nuclear club," said Aptekarev.
Rosatom is proposing implementing such projects under a power purchase agreement (PPA) model, with servicing and refuelling cycles carried out in Russia , allowing the unit to operate for up to 60 years.
"With this source of electricity, we are effectively addressing all the key issues and challenges facing the African continent," he said.
Rosatom is currently building Egypt's first nuclear power plant, El Dabaa, which will become the second nuclear power station on the African continent after South Africa's Koeberg plant, built using French technology in the mid-1980s. The project comprises four 1,200-MW power units with Russia n-designed VVER-1200 reactors.
Rosatom Chief Executive Alexei Likhachev told reporters the company is in advanced discussions on potential floating nuclear power plant projects with Egypt, Togo, Namibia and Tanzania.
The prospect of deploying floating nuclear power plants in Egypt could also gain momentum following a meeting between the presidents of Russia and Egypt scheduled for Wednesday, he said.
For international markets, Rosatom is offering floating power units with a capacity of 100 megawatts with RITM-200M reactors adapted for warm climates.
Rosatom has already reached an agreement with Indonesia on what it describes as the world's first export supplies of electricity generated by two floating nuclear power units with a combined capacity of 200 megawatts.

title: Kano Assembly Passes State Police Bill, Slashes Supplementary Budget By ₦266bn
body: The Kano State House of Assembly has passed a bill seeking amendments to the 1999 Constitution to pave the way for the establishment of a state police in Nigeria. The Assembly also approved the Kano State Supplementary Appropriation and Amendment Bill, 2026, reducing the proposed expenditure from ₦1.478 trillion to approximately ₦1.211 trillion. The two bills were passed during Tuesday’s plenary session presided over by the Speaker, Rt. Hon. Isma’il Falgore, following consideration by the Committee of the Whole and approval at the third reading. The proposed constitutional amendment seeks to provide a legal framework for state governments to establish and operate their own police services. During deliberations, lawmakers examined all 26 clauses of the bill before approving it. The move comes amid renewed national debate over decentralising policing, with growing calls for state police to address Nigeria’s persistent security challenges. The proposal is expected to form part of the broader constitutional review process aimed at restructuring the country’s security architecture and strengthening state governments’ capacity to tackle security threats. Meanwhile, lawmakers approved a downward review of the 2026 supplementary budget proposal submitted by Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf. The Assembly reduced the proposed expenditure from ₦1,477,829,666,130.71 to approximately ₦1.211 trillion, representing a cut of about ₦266.61 billion. The adjustment followed legislative scrutiny of the state’s supplementary spending requirements and proposed amendments to the 2026 appropriation framework. In a related development, the Assembly had earlier confirmed six commissioner nominees forwarded by Governor Yusuf for appointment to the state executive council. The nominees are Air Commodore Salisu Yusha’u (rtd.); Hon. Ibrahim Namadi; Professor Sani Lawan; Hon. Muktar Yakasai; Dr. Aminu Tsanyawa; and Hon. Idris Mustapha. title: Britain intends to continue fighting by proxy on foreign soil — Russian envoy to Vienna
body:
VIENNA, October 28. /TASS/. The British leadership intends to continue fighting by proxy on foreign soil, as evidenced by military medical drills conducted by the country’s Defense Ministry in October, Yulia Zhdanova, head of the Russian delegation to the Vienna talks on military security and arms control, said.
She recalled that in mid-October, the ministry organized a three-day command-post exercise for its medical command involving more than 100 representatives of the armed forces, the National Health Service and other agencies, as well as military personnel from the United States and Canada. "The goal was to test the ability to receive and treat large numbers of service members wounded outside the country on British territory," she said at a regular plenary meeting of the OSCE Forum for Security Cooperation in Vienna.
According to Zhdanova, participants practiced evacuating wounded personnel from combat zones, transporting them to rear hospitals and subsequently transferring them to Britain, as well as receiving and distributing large numbers of casualties, including among civilian hospitals. They also practiced coordinating transport services and government agencies, organizing medical evacuations with the participation of allies and using allied infrastructure. "Apparently, just as before, Britain intends to fight by proxy, and certainly not on its own territory," the diplomat concluded.

title: The “Rebuilding Borodianka” Charitable Foundation Was Presented in Borodianka
body:
On October 21, the official presentation of the charitable organization “Rebuilding Borodianka Charitable Foundation” took place at the Taras Shevchenko Palace of Culture in Borodianka.
The Foundation’s motto—“For the people, by the people, about the people”—reflects its main goal: to unite efforts for the reconstruction and development of the community.
During the event, the organization’s mission, main areas of activity, and strategic projects were presented. Special attention was given to supporting people in need, particularly the families of prisoners of war and defenders missing in action. The presentation provided an opportunity to outline a shared vision for Borodianka’s future and prospects for cooperation. Subscribe to our Telegram channel Lenta.UA—THE ONLY independent news source covering events in Ukraine and around the world
Speakers included Yevhen Kalensky, chairman of the “Rebuilding Borodianka” Charitable Foundation; Oleksandr Badrudinov, co-founder of the Foundation—head of PJSC “Regional Aviation Center” and the “Ukrainian Aviation Development Association,” as well as an organizer and coordinator of projects for the development of aviation infrastructure and defense technologies; Yevhen Burlyka, co-founder of the Foundation—a philanthropist and public figure; Yevhen Chechil, Chairman of the Board of JSC “Bank ‘Ukrainian Capital’”; Serhiy Belashov, ultimate beneficial owner of JSC “Bank ‘Ukrainian Capital’”; and Oleksandr Sakharuk, Mayor of Borodianka. Among the guests were also Jabrail Mirzoev—chairman of the “Caucasian Union” socio-political movement and a partner of the Foundation; and an active-duty military officer with the call sign “Tuman.”
“We’re not saying that we’re just getting started, because that’s usually how people talk about newly established foundations. We’re already up and running, and I’m confident that we’ll implement our first projects in collaboration with the Borodianka Town Council. I’d like to express my deep respect for Town Mayor Oleksandr Sakharuk, all the council members, residents, and our friends who are supporting us with their words, actions, and sincere dedication. “Our first projects will be aimed at preserving our heritage and, of course, at our future—our children. We want to work in a way that we won’t be ashamed in front of the people or our own families,” said Yevhen Kalensky, chairman of the “Restoration of Borodianka” Charitable Foundation.
“Today we have launched a very worthy cause—we presented the ‘Rebuilding Borodianka’ Charitable Foundation, which will work for the benefit of this community, one of the first to bear the brunt of Russian aggression,” said Oleksandr Badrudinov, co-founder of the Foundation.
“Ukrainian Capital Bank is pleased to join this worthy cause and support the work of the ‘Restoration of Borodianka’ Charitable Foundation. The stork depicted on the Foundation’s logo has always been associated by Ukrainians with high hopes for something good and new, with the birth of dreams. We are very pleased that the ‘Restoration of Borodianka’ Charitable Foundation invited us to join this cause,” said Yevhen Chechil, Chairman of the Board of JSC “Ukrainian Capital Bank.”
“Borodianka is a special town, as it served as a kind of frontline against the Russian Federation’s invasion. We, the people of Kyiv, must understand what Borodianka has done for all of us. Once again, I would like to express my deep gratitude to the Fund’s chairman, its co-founders, the community, and the town mayor,” said Yevhen Burlyka, a co-founder of the Fund.
“Today, I personally, as a shareholder of Ukrainian Capital Bank, took part in a charity event organized by the ‘Restoration of Borodianka’ Charitable Foundation. Among the cities and towns of the Kyiv region, Borodianka, Bucha, and Gostomel suffered the most from Russian aggression and the hostilities that took place in this region. The goal of this event is to raise funds for the top priority: the restoration of the children’s clinic and children’s hospital. This is exactly what the community needs today,” emphasized Serhiy Belashov, the ultimate beneficial owner of JSC “Bank ‘Ukrainian Capital.’”
“Today is, without exaggeration, a landmark event, because we are all united by a single goal—to help our citizens. And I am pleased that, together with the founders of this Fund, we will soon achieve a common goal that will affect every person and every settlement in our local community. After all, this is for the people and about the people,” noted Oleksandr Sakharuk, mayor of Borodianka.
“On the front lines, you do your job and hope that someday you’ll be remembered. After all, a person lives as long as they are remembered. Therefore, I bow low to you, community! May your resilience serve as an example to other active and true patriots,” said an active-duty soldier with the call sign “Tuman.”
The Foundation extends special thanks to Ukrainian Capital Bank for its partnership, support of the organization’s activities, and contribution to joint initiatives aimed at rebuilding the Borodianka community.
An important part of the event was the symbolic “Seeds of the Future” ceremony. The Foundation’s leadership, partners, and community representatives placed seeds into a commemorative capsule, symbolizing the rebirth, growth, and faith in Borodianka’s future.
The program was complemented by an exhibition of the First Regional Art Plein Air by Ukrainian artists, “Code of Resilience: From Ashes to Painting,” dedicated to Borodianka. The artists’ works reflect both the pain the community has endured and its aspiration for renewal.
Local performers Artem Semenov, Lyudmila Potapenko, and Yulia Kuvshinova provided the musical program for the event.
The “Rebuilding Borodianka” Charitable Foundation thanks all participants, partners, and donors for their support and willingness to contribute to the community’s reconstruction. “By the people, for the people, about the people”—this is the principle that unites the Foundation’s team and guides its work.

title: Police arrest 52-year-old man over 37 parcels of suspected Indian hemp in Tema
body: The Tema Regional Police Command has arrested a 52-year-old man, Ibrahim Saani, for allegedly possessing 37 parcels of substances suspected to be Indian hemp at New York, near Airport Junction. The arrest followed an intelligence-led operation conducted by a police team in the area at about 7 pm on Sunday, October 25, 2026. According to a statement signed by the Head of Public Affairs of the Tema Regional Police Command, ASP Dede Dzakpasu, officers retrieved a bag containing 37 parcels of compressed substances suspected to be Indian hemp and a crusher. The suspect was subsequently taken to the police station with the items retrieved for further investigation. Preliminary investigations suggest that Saani may have been involved in the distribution of suspected narcotic substances in New York and nearby communities. The police said intelligence gathered during their investigations indicated that the suspect allegedly pretended to be mentally unwell to conceal his suspected activities. The suspected substances will be sent for forensic examination to determine their nature and assist investigators in establishing whether other people were involved. The police have not disclosed whether any other suspects have been identified in connection with the case. The Tema Regional Police Command said Saani would be put before the court once investigations had been completed. “The suspect and his accomplices, if any, will be arraigned before the court as soon as investigations are completed,” the statement said. The outcome of the forensic examination is expected to help investigators establish the nature of the substances seized and determine the next steps in the case. The Command has cautioned the public against involvement in the possession, distribution and trafficking of illegal drugs. It also urged residents with credible information about suspected narcotics-related activities to report to their nearest police station.

title: Ukraine's fugitive ex-prosecutor general alleges conspiracy, anti-graft agencies hit back
body:
The National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU) and the Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor’s Office (SAPO) on Oct. 27 denied former Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko’s allegations that their officials were involved in a conspiracy against him.
Kravchenko remains on the run, despite not being officially charged.
The former prosecutor general broke a month-long silence after fleeing Ukraine to Austria amid a corruption scandal involving senior officials from the Prosecutor General's Office.
His statement came after two Ukrainian military intelligence (HUR) officers were detained in Austria in early October, Austrian newspaper Der Standard reported.
In a social media post, Kravchenko claimed the officers belonged to Artan, a special military intelligence unit. He said one of them had previously worked in NABU 's external surveillance unit and that Artan commander Viktor Torkotiuk had also allegedly been in Austria at the time.
Kravchenko said he learned in September that a group had allegedly been sent to carry out "unlawful acts of violence," claiming NABU and SAPO chiefs and the President's Office may have been behind it.
Kravchenko didn't elaborate on his sources, saying he "lacked reliable information on who had issued" the alleged order.
"The statement regarding NABU and SAPO's involvement in any of the events mentioned is untrue," the bureau told the Kyiv Independent, describing Kravchenko's statement as an attempt to "secure protection for himself in his country of residence."
Austria rarely extradites Ukrainian nationals to Ukraine, making it a potential refuge for former Ukrainian officials facing corruption charges at home. Several have sought shelter there, complicating Kyiv’s efforts to bring them back to face prosecution.
The President's Office and HUR haven't commented on the claims.
Kravchenko 's personal office was searched by the Anti-Corruption Bureau in early September as part of a sweeping corruption probe into an alleged racket protecting scam call centers, reportedly operated out of the Prosecutor General’s Office.
Within the investigation, a top prosecutor described as a "confidant" of Kravchenko was charged. Publicly revealed evidence hints at Kravchenko being implicated , and he submitted his resignation on Sept. 7.
Kravchenko left Ukraine on Sept. 14 and simultaneously approved charges against Semen Kryvonos, the head of the Anti-Corruption Bureau investigating him.
The charges were canceled by the Prosecutor General's Office late on Sept. 14, and Kravchenko was dismissed by parliament the next day.

title: 24 Sussex restoration campaign secures $5.7M as public appeal launches
body:
The campaign to restore 24 Sussex Drive has secured $5.7 million, with public donations now being accepted.
The Rideau Hall Foundation said Wednesday that more than 4,000 contributions have been made toward its $50-million fundraising goal.
RHF was tasked in June with leading a fundraising campaign to help cover the costs of restoring the derelict official residence of Canada’s prime ministers.
“As the official residence of Canada’s prime minister, 24 Sussex is part of the architecture of our democracy,” said Robert Prichard, chair of the RHF board of directors, in a news release.
“Renewing it is not simply about preserving history; it is about ensuring that our national institutions reflect the confidence and ambition of the country they represent.”
The fundraising campaign is one element of the federal plan announced by Prime Minister Mark Carney to restore 24 Sussex Drive through a national design-and-build competition.
Built in 1846, the 35-room residence has been vacant since 2015, when former prime minister Justin Trudeau chose to live at Rideau Cottage because of the building’s condition.
Inspections have found dead rodents and feces in the walls and attic, along with extensive water damage and electrical problems. Carney currently lives in Rideau Cottage, as Trudeau did.
Maintaining the vacant property is estimated to cost taxpayers approximately $150,000 annually. The National Capital Commission estimated in 2022 that restoring the residence would cost approximately $37 million. That estimate is now expected to be more than $100 million.
“There are very few opportunities for Canadians to contribute personally to a project of national significance that will still matter generations from now,” said Teresa Marques, president and CEO of RHF.
“The renewal of 24 Sussex is one of them. Whether through a leadership gift or a modest contribution, every donor is helping write the next chapter in the story of 24 Sussex.”
RHF also announced the Council for 24 Sussex group Wednesday. The group is made up of philanthropic volunteers who will use their networks to encourage contributions across Canada.
RHF said the council will grow as the campaign engages more volunteer leaders across the nation.
The winning proposal of the design-and-build competition is expected to be announced by Canada Day.

title: Russian seafood exports to China may exceed $4 bln in 2026 — Federal Agency for Fishery
body:
SHANGHAI, October 28. /TASS/. The value of seafood shipments from Russia to China could surpass $4 billion by the end of 2026, Sergey Mikheyev, a representative of the Russian Federal Agency for Fishery in China, told TASS.
"Between January and September 2026, Russia exported $3.32 billion worth of aquatic products to China, marking a 53.1% year-on-year increase," Mikheyev noted. "Furthermore, the full-year figure for 2025, which stood at $3.2 billion, has already been exceeded. If the current trend holds, exports could reach $4.1-$4.2 billion by the end of this year."
On October 28, the China Fisheries & Seafood Expo, the largest trade show for the fishing, seafood, and processing technology sectors, opened in the Chinese city of Qingdao. More than 60 Russian enterprises are participating in the event, occupying an exhibition space of over 1,600 square meters.
"Participation in this expo facilitates a direct dialogue between the two sides, which further helps secure mutually beneficial trading terms," Mikheyev said, commenting on the presence of Russian companies. "Such exhibitions are crucial for expanding the reach of domestic exporters, both within the Chinese market and into third countries."
A Chinese delegation - led by Ma Yuxian, a member of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference and former Vice Minister of Agriculture, alongside Sun Haiwen, Deputy Director of the Fisheries Bureau under the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs - visited the Russian pavilion. The delegation was welcomed by Kirill Kolonchin, Director of the Russian Federal Research Institute of Fisheries and Oceanography (VNIRO); Sergey Mikheyev, Federal Agency for Fishery’s representative in China; and Ivan Fetisov, CEO of Expo Solutions Group, the pavilion's organizer. The parties reviewed products from Russian enterprises and exchanged views on the prospects for future cooperation.
The Russian pavilion has been a fixture at the China Fisheries & Seafood Expo for 10 years, becoming an essential component of Russia’s presence in the Chinese market and a key tool for promoting domestic fishery products.
The China Fisheries & Seafood Expo is China's largest international exhibition for the fisheries, seafood, and related technology sectors, held annually in Qingdao. In 2025, the event hosted over 1,500 companies and welcomed 45,000 visitors from 139 countries. The Russian national pavilion has participated in the exhibition since 2016.

title: Russia–Africa Summit – Ghana must count the cost of a deeper partnership
body: As Moscow courts African governments with promises of trade, investment and security cooperation, Accra must guard against opaque deals, resource dependence and commercial relationships that leave the country carrying more risk than reward.Ghana’s growing economic engagement with Russia presents an opportunity, but one that demands considerably more scrutiny than diplomatic declarations of friendship and mutually beneficial cooperation might suggest. Recorded bilateral merchandise trade reached US$506.5 million in 2025, according to a compilation based on UN Comtrade data. Yet Ghana exported just US$44.9 million worth of goods to Russia, compared with imports of US$461.7 million, leaving a merchandise trade deficit of approximately US$416.8 million.The imbalance raises an uncomfortable question at the ongoing Russia–Africa Summit in Moscow on October 28 and 29: is Ghana building a relationship that will strengthen its productive capacity, or one that risks entrenching its position as a buyer of foreign goods while struggling to expand its own exports? Deeper trade is not necessarily better trade, and a growing number of bilateral agreements does not automatically translate into economic transformation. Without clear safeguards, Ghana could find itself importing more, exporting relatively little and assuming commercial or strategic obligations whose long-term costs exceed their immediate benefits.The summit should therefore be approached with commercial discipline, not diplomatic enthusiasm alone. An imbalance that demands attention Russia’s trade with Africa reportedly reached US$27.7 billion in 2025, according to figures attributed to the Russian Academy of Sciences’ Institute for African Studies. Moscow is seeking to expand its commercial footprint through agriculture, fertilisers, energy, mining, manufacturing and technology. For Ghana, there are legitimate opportunities in these areas. Reliable access to fertilisers and industrial inputs can support production, while investment in processing and manufacturing could help diversify exports and create employment. But the current structure of bilateral trade reveals a relationship in which Ghana’s export presence remains comparatively small.In the 2025 UN Comtrade-based compilation, Russian shipments to Ghana included approximately US$337 million in mineral fuels and oils and US$63 million in fertilisers. Ghana’s recorded exports were concentrated in oilseeds and other plant products, worth about US$33.5 million, cocoa products at US$6.2 million, and fats and oils at US$4.9 million. These imports may serve legitimate economic needs. The concern is whether Ghana can turn them into the basis for a more productive domestic economy, or whether the relationship will simply reinforce an existing dependence on imported goods.There is also a data question that policymakers should resolve. The Ghana News Agency reported in July that bilateral trade had risen from US$247 million in 2022 to more than US$800 million in 2024, citing the Russian ambassador. That figure differs from the 2025 customs-based compilation. The discrepancy may reflect different reporting methods or coverage, but it underlines the need for a consistent official series before the government makes ambitious claims about the relationship’s growth.A partnership cannot be evaluated properly when its underlying numbers are not readily reconciled. The danger of paying too much for strategic friendship Ghana should be particularly cautious where commercial agreements intersect with security assistance and strategic interests.In the Central African Republic and Sudan, investigations into companies linked to the Wagner Group have raised concerns about opaque gold and diamond operations and the relationship between Russian security networks and resource extraction. US authorities sanctioned several Wagner-linked entities over alleged illicit commercial activities, including gold dealings in the Central African Republic. Mali offers a different warning. Russian security assistance has expanded under the military-led government, yet the continued threat from armed groups and allegations of abuses by Russian-linked personnel have raised questions about the results delivered by the partnership.These cases do not establish that Ghana is negotiating similar arrangements. Nor do they mean that every Russian company or investment carries the same risks. They do, however, demonstrate why governments should not treat security assistance, commercial investment and diplomatic support as interchangeable benefits whose value can be assumed rather than measured. Where security and business interests overlap, governments must establish precisely what each party is providing, what it receives in return, and whether the terms serve the public interest.For Ghana, that means resisting any arrangement in which access to strategic assets, preferential concessions or long-term financial obligations is granted without transparent valuation, independent scrutiny and enforceable safeguards. The danger is not limited to outright corruption. A legally signed agreement can still be commercially disadvantageous if the state underestimates its fiscal obligations, overvalues the assistance received or fails to account for the opportunity cost of the resources committed. Sanctions and the cost of commercial exposure The geopolitical environment adds another layer of risk. Russia’s war against Ukraine and the sanctions imposed in response have complicated some transactions involving Russian counterparties. Depending on the parties and activities involved, businesses may face restrictions affecting payments, correspondent banking, shipping, insurance and access to particular markets.Ghanaian firms pursuing opportunities in Russia must therefore undertake careful due diligence on their counterparties, financing arrangements and contractual obligations. Transactions must comply with applicable sanctions and other legal requirements, while payment mechanisms should be demonstrably reliable. This is not an argument for excluding Russian businesses. It is an argument against assuming that every commercially attractive offer is necessarily executable or that the political relationship will shield Ghanaian companies from the consequences of a transaction that encounters legal or financial obstacles. The government should also avoid creating new dependencies in essential supplies. Russian fertilisers, fuel and other commodities can be useful components of Ghana’s import mix, but reliance on a narrow range of suppliers exposes domestic producers to geopolitical disruption, shipping difficulties and price volatility. Diversification is not a rejection of Russia. It is insurance against uncertainty. Investment must mean more than importing equipment The strongest argument for deeper relations with Russia would be the prospect of investment that expands Ghana’s domestic productive capacity. That is also where the government should be most demanding.Agriculture, agro-processing, fertiliser distribution and blending, energy infrastructure, manufacturing and technology offer potential areas of cooperation. But a shipment of machinery is not the same as the establishment of an industrial facility, and an investment memorandum is not evidence that capital has been committed. Proposed projects should be assessed against their financing costs, expected employment, local procurement, technology transfer, export potential and fiscal implications. Where public guarantees or other contingent liabilities are involved, those exposures should be disclosed and independently evaluated.Mining agreements require comparable scrutiny. The country should know who ultimately owns a concession, how production and exports will be verified, what taxes and royalties are due, and how environmental obligations will be enforced. These standards should apply to Russian investors just as they apply to companies from China, Europe, the United States or elsewhere. The objective is to secure investment on terms that benefit Ghana, not to confer special treatment on a foreign partner because of its geopolitical importance. The risk of confusing diplomacy with delivery The Moscow summit will generate declarations, meetings and potentially a package of agreements under the wider Russia–Africa Partnership Forum framework.But Ghana should resist the temptation to count signed documents as economic achievements before their substance has been established.Every significant agreement should have a clear implementing agency, financing arrangements, a realistic timetable and measurable targets. Progress should be reported publicly, with responsibility assigned for resolving delays or failures. The government should also assess what Ghana is committing in return. An agreement that attracts foreign investment but grants excessive tax concessions, weakens regulatory control or creates expensive future obligations may deliver less than its headline value suggests.The appropriate measure is the net economic benefit after financing costs, incentives, risks and public obligations have been considered. A more demanding partnership President John Dramani Mahama has said Ghana welcomes investment from all countries and seeks arrangements that deliver fair returns to both parties. That approach is consistent with a foreign policy that avoids exclusive geopolitical alignment.But non-alignment is most valuable when it gives a country the capacity to negotiate firmly with every partner. It loses practical meaning if the pursuit of diplomatic relationships takes precedence over commercial discipline or the protection of national interests. Ghana should therefore enter the Moscow summit with a clear set of priorities: better access for Ghanaian exports, productive investment rather than import dependence, transparent contracts, sustainable financing, technology transfer and safeguards against deceptive recruitment and other forms of exploitation.It should also insist on reliable data against which the results of the relationship can be judged. Without a consistent trade and investment baseline, it will be difficult to distinguish genuine progress from diplomatic optimism.Russia may offer useful markets, capital and expertise. But those opportunities must be evaluated against their actual returns, not the expectations surrounding them. The greatest danger is not that Ghana will engage Russia. It is that the country could deepen that engagement without adequately assessing what it stands to gain, what it may have to surrender and who will bear the cost if the promised benefits fail to materialise.The Moscow summit should be an opportunity to negotiate better terms, not a reason to suspend scrutiny. For Ghana, the test of partnership is not the scale of its diplomatic warmth but whether the relationship strengthens the economy, protects national interests and delivers measurable benefits to its citizens. >>>Ahmed Tahiru is a financial intelligence strategist, writer and advocate for financial literacy, startups, and SME growth. He is a financial strategist who believes in building businesses through systems, structures, and frameworks. He studies the startup ecosystem with a focus on creating scalable, high-impact ventures. title: Shelters in 76 educational institutions in Kyiv renovated over two years — Klitschko
body:
Over the past two years, renovation work on shelters in 76 educational institutions has been completed in Kyiv, with work currently underway at another 33, announced Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko.
"Nine new dual-purpose facilities (with a capacity of 4,781) have been built for educational institutions. This year, we plan to complete the construction of four more such facilities (with a capacity of 1,774)," Klitschko wrote on his Telegram channel on Wednesday.
In particular, a shelter at a school in the capital’s Solomyansky district recently underwent major renovations. As the mayor noted, the shelter previously lacked the conditions necessary for the educational process; it could only serve as a place to wait out air raid alerts.
"The renovation of the 600-square-meter shelter was completed by the start of the academic year, transforming it into a functional learning space. As a result, all 353 students at the school are now able to attend classes in person. The shelter has a capacity of 600 people and features 13 designated zones. It is equipped with an adequate number of desks, relaxation areas with soft beanbag chairs, and storage space for outerwear. A total of UAH 8 million from the city budget was allocated for the shelter's renovation. I also inspected the school’s cafeteria and gymnasium, which were renovated using city funds," he said.
Klitschko emphasized that the enemy continues to shell Kyiv, frequently targeting educational institutions.
"Ensuring the safety of our children and teachers during the educational process remains a priority for the capital. We are doing everything possible to enable children to attend school in person wherever safety conditions allow," the city’s mayor emphasized.
Currently, 55% of students in Kyiv are attending classes in person, 26.5% are following a hybrid model, 10.2% are studying remotely, and 8.3% are on an individual learning plan.

title: Israel’s economic outlook hinges on next government as shekel and stocks slide
body: Read the latest on Israel's election here Israel ’s next government will determine whether the country attracts fresh foreign investment and eases economic pressures, or faces deeper uncertainty over growth, public finances and its global standing. Israeli markets weakened on Wednesday after an inconclusive election result left the shape of the next government unclear. The shekel fell about 2 per cent against the dollar, its biggest intraday loss in two weeks and one of the steepest currency declines globally, reversing much of Tuesday’s gains. The benchmark Tel Aviv stock index, which was closed on Tuesday, fell about 3 per cent and was on track for its biggest decline since June. Shares of Bank Hapoalim fell about 4 per cent, while Phoenix Financial slumped more than 5 per cent. Israel’s economic outlook could diverge sharply depending on who forms the next government, with a right-wing coalition potentially deepening economic uncertainty and accelerating capital flight, while an opposition-led administration could help revive investor confidence, an economist tells The National . “If [Prime Minister Benjamin] Netanyahu succeeds to head the government again with a coalition of right-wing parties, then the uncertainty surrounding the economy will soar, resulting in a weaker shekel and GDP growth,” says Naser Mufrej, professor of finance and economics at the Arab American University in Ramallah. A Netanyahu-led coalition could also discourage investment in Israel’s high-tech sector and drive skilled workers and professionals abroad, further weighing on the economy, he adds. The prospect of wider boycotts and deeper international isolation could put more pressure on exports and foreign capital inflows, according to Mr Mufrej. “The credit rating of Israel will be reduced, thus raising the cost of financing,” he says. To get the economy back on track and ensure stability and financial strength, the new government will need a "comprehensive, bold economic emergency plan", says Vijay Valecha, chief investment officer at Century Financial. "The new government will need to tackle a series of challenges that have gripped the country over the past few years. Over three years of war, the country has suffered some structural damage such as high deficit within the country, rising defence budget, and high costs of living. Currently, Israel has debt approaching around 70 per cent of GDP and defence demands of around 200 billion shekels a year. "Despite these challenges, Israel remains supported by a diversified, resilient and high value-added economy and strong external finances against a high public debt/GDP ratio," he adds. By contrast, a government formed by opposition parties with the support of Arab parties could offer a more positive economic trajectory, he says. Such an outcome could generate renewed investor optimism, support steadier economic growth and strengthen the shekel and the Tel Aviv stock market, he adds. It could also help lower inflation , attract more foreign investment and boost trade, Mr Mufrej says. “The elections by themselves are not assumed to have any impact on the Israeli economy. What is important is who will form the government based on the results of the elections,” he says. Capital Economics made a similar point in a report this month, saying the Israeli election was unlikely to have a major effect on the country’s near-term growth outlook or fiscal trajectory, but could have significant implications for the economy over the medium term. The International Monetary Fund ’s July 2026 assessment projected Israel’s economy would grow by 3.5 per cent this year and 4.4 per cent in 2027. That was based on the assumption that regional ceasefires would largely hold. It warned that persistent geopolitical uncertainty, elevated defence spending and labour supply constraints would continue to weigh on the recovery. "Israel's economy has shown it can withstand considerable pressure, but managing one crisis after another is not the same as addressing the problems behind them," says Mr Valecha For investors, the next government’s success in reducing uncertainty and restoring international economic ties may determine whether this week’s market weakness persists or gives way to a recovery.

title: P.B. Rangarao assumes charge as Director (Operations), HAL
body:
Bengaluru, Oct 28, 2026. P.B. Rangarao has assumed charge as Director (Operations) of Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) today. Prior to this appointment, he served as Chief Executive Officer (Helicopter Complex) at HAL.



Rangarao joined HAL as a Design Trainee in 1995. Over his three-decade career with the company, he has held several key positions across functions, including Plant Maintenance, Advanced Light Helicopter (ALH) Manufacturing Shops, Cheetah/Chetak projects, outsourcing and planning. Before taking over as CEO (Helicopter Complex), he served as Executive Director, Helicopter Division.

During his tenure, Rangarao made significant contributions to strengthening HAL’s helicopter manufacturing capabilities. These include operationalising the new Helicopter Division at Tumakuru, paving the way for the production rollout of the first batch of Light Utility Helicopters (LUH), and commissioning the Limited Series Production (LSP) bases for the Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) for the Indian Army and Indian Air Force.

He was instrumental in concluding the contract for 25 Advanced Light Helicopter (ALH) Mk III helicopters for the Indian Army and signing the contract for 156 LCH Prachand helicopters for the Indian Army and Indian Air Force. Under his leadership, HAL re-established supply chains for Cheetah and Chetak helicopters following the closure of Airbus facilities in France, enhanced production capacity through public-private partnerships, addressed obsolescence challenges through focused indigenisation initiatives, and streamlined manufacturing processes to improve production efficiency of ALH components.

Rangarao holds a Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering from Regional Engineering College, Warangal, and a Post Graduate Diploma in Business Management from XIME, Bengaluru. He has also completed a Leadership Development Programme at the Indian Institute of Management (IIM), Ahmedabad.

title: De Beers diamond miner wants to cooperate more with Russia — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. De Beers diamond company wants to cooperate with Russia and Moscow welcomes such cooperation, President Vladimir Putin said at the third Russia-Africa summit.
