On the other part, they want more and more to cooperate with Russia because problems are created [for them] there, in the Western world, they endeavor to establish relations with Russia, with our company. We are for this, we only welcome such cooperation," Putin said.

title: Higher tariffs on Canadian imports would be ‘catastrophic,’ Honda exec says
body:
A pending increase in U.S. tariffs on steel and auto imports from Canada starting Jan. 1 would be “catastrophic” for the industry, Honda Motor’s head of public affairs said on Tuesday.
Automakers are closely watching talks between the U.S., Mexico and Canada, hoping the countries extend a longstanding trade deal. The three countries’ auto industries are tightly intertwined, and higher tariffs could raise costs and affect where companies such as Honda build new plants.
“We need that trilateral agreement to stay in place in order for the U.S. industry to be competitive. It’s integral to our success,” said Jennifer Thomas, senior vice president of corporate affairs for American Honda Motor Co, speaking at the Reuters Automotive USA conference in Detroit.
The auto industry has been grappling with tariffs since early 2025, when U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration placed varying tariff rates on imports from multiple countries , including Mexico and Canada.
“I am cautiously optimistic that cooler heads will prevail, and we will avoid that Jan. 1 doubling of the tariffs, because that really would be catastrophic just for the entire industry,” Thomas said.
The U.S. and Canada are working on a deal to ease U.S. tariffs on Canadian steel and autos, Reuters reported on Monday. Those talks are aimed at tariffs imposed under Section 232 of US trade law, including a tariff of up to 50 per cent on Canadian steel and a 25 per cent tariff on autos, with negotiators discussing potential relief from those duties.
Unlike trade deals with the EU, Japan or South Korea, the trade pact between Mexico, Canada and the U.S. has specific North American content requirements known as “rules of origin.”
In the negotiations with Mexico, the U.S. has demanded that all North American-built vehicles contain 50 per cent U.S.-specific content, a figure that would drive regional required content up to 82 per cent to qualify for U.S. benefits, sources familiar with the talks have said.
Vehicles assembled in Mexico and Canada would likely still be charged some level ⁠of tariffs, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer ​has said.
Thomas and other auto executives said that rules-of-origin requirements are not in place in other trade deals.
“Right now, North America is at an unfair disadvantage,” Thomas said.
In August, Honda said it may not build an eighth assembly plant in ​North America unless the trade deal between the three countries is extended.
“We are at capacity, and so we’re exploring all options. And at the end of the day, we’re going to continue to invest in the U.S.,” Thomas said.

title: UK defence spending target of 3 percent by 2030
body: The Chancellor has set a target date of 2030 for defence spending to reach three per cent of gross domestic product, and will set out at next year’s spending review how Britain meets its NATO commitment of three and a half per cent by 2035, according to the Budget statement. John Healey, who held the defence portfolio before moving to the Treasury, told the Commons: “At the spending review next year, I confirm that I will set out the details of how we will meet our NATO commitment to spend 3.5% of GDP on defence by 2035, with a target date for 3% in 2030.” On how it will be paid for, he said: “Today, I am getting work underway to get there in a fiscally sustainable way, that will include looking hard at public spending, as I have done today, to fund the defence investment plan. But I am also determined to use more innovative financing alongside the private sector and our international allies.” A new innovative defence finance task force will lead the work ahead of the spending review, the first of four measures announced. Treaty negotiations will begin on a multilateral defence mechanism, which Healey also called a bank, with Finland, Poland and the Netherlands, intended to boost defence investment and joint procurement across NATO allies. The government will seek the maximum private investment into the defence industrial base, including through public-private partnerships. And the National Wealth Fund and the British Business Bank will launch a new focus on defence, dual-use technology and sovereign capability, deploying up to £5 billion of investment and lending over the next four years. Healey said: “I will ensure this record defence investment works twice: once for our national security, and once for British jobs and British business. Places across all four nations: Barrow, Rosyth, Aldershot, Plymouth, Glascoed, and Belfast, reindustrialised and transformed.” On Ukraine, the Chancellor said he and the Prime Minister had called President Zelensky that morning to tell him what the Budget contained, and that the response was “you’ve made my day” . The package is £10 billion of additional economic and military support based on loans and export finance guarantees, together with urgent military funding for this winter. Healey said: “The whole house, the whole country, is united for Ukraine, and today we send a clear message to Moscow: Britain will stand with Ukraine for as long as it takes.” The Chancellor made the case personally, drawing on his own family: “I say this as Chancellor. I say this as former Defence Secretary. And I say this as a dad whose son is an army reservist, a reservist that came back four years ago from early training to say they had no kit and they had no bullets to fire. That’s the truth.” He said that for fourteen years Conservative governments had hollowed out and underfunded the armed forces, and that the defence budget this year is £14 billion higher than in the final year of the last government, which he described as the biggest increase in defence spending since the end of the Cold War. Britain signed up at the NATO summit in The Hague to three and a half per cent of gross domestic product on core defence by 2035, with a further one and a half per cent on defence-related resilience and infrastructure making up the alliance’s headline five per cent. Ministers had previously described three per cent as an ambition for the next Parliament, and attaching a target date of 2030 to it is firmer than the language used before. Industry witnesses told the Defence Committee this month that the Defence Investment Plan is not investable as it stands, that most defence technology firms report a declining market, and that the department’s small business office has four staff. The finance task force and the £5 billion through the National Wealth Fund and British Business Bank are the Treasury’s answer to that. The post UK defence spending target of 3 percent by 2030 first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Ukrainian forces deny Russian claims of capturing Barylivka in Sumy region
body:
The 8th Corps of the Ukrainian Air Assault Forces reported this in a Facebook post , according to Ukrinform.
"Barylivka in the Sumy region remains under the control of Ukraine's Defense Forces. The Russian claim that they have captured it is false. There have not even been any attempts to storm the village, and the 'decisive offensive operations' by the 41st Motor Rifle Regiment have taken place only on Telegram channels and in comments," the Ukrainian defenders said.
They noted that the reason for the enemy's activity is simple: with only a few days left until the end of October, the Russians needed to report the capture of Ukrainian settlements for the month.

title: MOD appoints its first Director General Innovation
body:
Anthony Reeves appointed as the first Director General Innovation, bringing extensive military, government and industry experience.
Role oversees 4,800 innovation experts and scientists and a £3.7 billion science, technology and innovation budget over the next four years to ensure the UK remains at the cutting edge of warfighting.
National Armaments Innovation harnesses UK ingenuity and boosts military technology, as part of a drive to turbocharge innovation.
After an external competition, Anthony will become the newest 3* senior civil servant within National Armaments, part of the organisation’s Executive Committee, and the Ministry of Defence’s first Director General (DG) Innovation.
Taking up the role this Autumn, Anthony will lead the newly designed National Armaments Innovation area, which includes some 4,800 experts and scientists working in the Defence Investment Unit (DIU), the Defence Science & Technology Laboratory (Dstl), the Defence Uncrewed Systems Centre (DUSC) and UK Defence Innovation (UKDI).
Anthony will oversee a ringfenced £1.6 billion defence innovation budget over the next four years, as well as supporting £2.1 billion investment in core science and technology.
He will play a pivotal role in accelerating the adoption of cutting-edge technologies, fostering collaboration with industry, academia and government departments, and embedding innovation as a core military capability.
Rupert Pearce, the National Armaments Director, said:
Anthony’s appointment marks a gear shift for UK Defence as we place innovation at the heart of the way we maintain war-fighting readiness, become an engine for economic growth and learn from the lessons of Ukraine to deter our adversaries.
As a leader, Tony brings a rare combination of frontline military experience, deep technical expertise and a proven track record of delivering transformation across Defence, government and industry.
His leadership will be instrumental as we strengthen Defence’s innovation ecosystem, accelerate the adoption of emerging technologies and deliver the capabilities our Armed Forces need, now and in the future.
Anthony joins National Armaments from Deloitte, where he led the UK and NATO Digital Defence section and was National Armaments Practice Head and Global AI Leader for Defence and Security.
He has worked extensively across UK Defence, NATO, AUKUS partners and defence industry organisations and his experience spans operational military service, national security, emerging technologies, AI and large-scale transformation programmes.
Commenting on his appointment, Tony said:
Innovation in Defence must be about mindset before toolset. I look forward to working with brilliant colleagues across Defence, industry, academia and our international partners to make innovation everyone’s business, bring new technologies into military service at pace, and deliver tangible growth for the UK.
Under Anthony’s leadership, National Armaments Innovation will identify, mature and exploit emerging capabilities, strengthen collaboration with industry, academia and allies, and help ensure the Armed Forces can access the technologies and capabilities needed to maintain operational advantage.
Anthony’s earlier career included responsibility for delivering critical communications, networks and information capabilities for military operations and specialist users, alongside operational deployments as an infantry officer in the British Army, which included Northern Ireland, Bosnia, Kosovo and Sierra Leone.
Before joining Deloitte in 2020, Anthony advised defence organisations on digital transformation and technology adoption at Microsoft, and led major defence and national security programmes within PA Consulting and Detica.
He is a regular speaker on defence innovation, digital transformation and artificial intelligence, and serves as a Board member of the AI Institute UK, and mentor to future leaders through King’s College London and the Common Mission Project.

title: Rosatom in talks with more than 40 African nations — CEO
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Rosatom is holding proactive negotiations with more than forty African countries in different areas of cooperation, CEO Alexey Likhachev said.
"If speaking exactly about presence of legal relations, then 29 countries. We have legally significant obligations in 29 countries out of 54 African sovereigns. The figure can be boldly increased to 40-42, where we have the active stage of talks. Interests are different, starting from exploration and production on deposits, uranium, rare-earth, and Centers of nuclear science and technologies. And nuclear power plants, certainly," he told reporters at the Russia-Africa summit.
Rosatom will start implementing five more small and large capacity nuclear power plant projects shortly, the chief executive added.

title: Russia building new radar close to the Polish border
body: Construction of a new radar facility in Kaliningrad has been under way for some time and forms part of wider Russian investment in military capability that Britain and NATO allies are monitoring, according to an answer given in Parliament. Gregory Campbell, the Democratic Unionist Party member for East Londonderry, asked whether the government would raise the construction of the radar at Gvardeysk, close to the Polish border, with NATO partners. Louise Sandher-Jones, the Minister for the Armed Forces, said: “The Government remains in close consultation with NATO Allies on developments that may affect the security environment in the Euro-Atlantic area, including monitoring and assessing Russia’s investment in its military capabilities. “Construction of the radar facility in Kaliningrad has been underway for some time and forms part of this wider investment. The UK and NATO Allies routinely monitor relevant Russian military developments and share information and assessments where appropriate. “NATO continues to maintain an effective deterrence and defence posture, including on its Eastern Flank.” Gvardeysk lies around thirty miles east of Kaliningrad city and has hosted Russian early warning radar infrastructure for years, including a Voronezh-DM site that watches across central and western Europe. The exclave has no land connection to the rest of Russia, hosts the headquarters of the Baltic Fleet at Baltiysk, and carries air defence and missile systems whose reach extends well into allied airspace. Kaliningrad borders Poland to the south and Lithuania to the north and east, and the stretch of frontier between them, the Suwalki gap, is the only land route between the Baltic states and the rest of the alliance. The post Russia building new radar close to the Polish border first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Jordan, Syria seek to reduce tensions following strike with joint security committee - analysis
body: Jordan and Syria are seeking to reduce tensions following Jordanian airstrikes against ISIS positions in southern Syria's Daraa province.According to Syria, the airstrikes on Monday killed seven civilians, including three children, and wounded three others. Jordan says it eliminated almost two dozen ISIS members.The incident has raised questions about the future of security cooperation between Amman and Damascus.Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani and Jordanian Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi agreed to establish a joint security committee to investigate the incident, Rudaw Media Network, a news channel in the autonomous Kurdistan Region of northern Iraq, reported. The committee is expected to meet within two days, the report said.“This committee will review all the details and facts surrounding the recent operations, follow up on their consequences, and develop mechanisms for field and intelligence coordination to counter terrorist threats,” the two countries said in a joint statement, Rudaw reported.Damascus condemned the airstrikes as a violation of Syrian sovereignty. Jordan said it had targeted ISIS positions posing an imminent threat, adding that more than 20 terrorists were killed and a terrorist hideout containing weapons was destroyed.Attack on Christians in Jordan sparks responseThe airstrikes followed a deadly attack on a Greek Orthodox church in Jordan's Karak governorate that killed nine people. Amman linked the attack to militants operating in southern Syria, although it has not publicly presented evidence establishing that connection.The Syrian Foreign Ministry said it had communicated this to Jordan with its “full reservation” regarding military operations carried out inside Syrian territory without prior coordination with Damascus, Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA), Syria's official news agency, reported Monday.“We express our deep regret over the deaths and injuries among residents of Daraa province as a result of this operation,” it said, according to the report.The ministry also said contacts with Jordan were continuing to establish the circumstances of the airstrikes and address their consequences while safeguarding Syrian sovereignty.Daraa Health Director Dr. Khaled al-Omian said civilians, including children and an elderly man, were among those killed or injured in strikes on several locations in the Daraa countryside, SANA reported. Daraa Governorate is a southern province of Syria on the Jordanian border.Daraa is key area where the Syrian revolution began in 2011. Syrian rebels later held this area, and Jordan helped support them.About a million Syrians fled to Jordan from 2011-2023. Many have returned. Jordanian clans and tribes in northern Jordan have ties with Syrians on the other side of the border.After the Assad regime fell, a border crossing reopened in southern Syria with Jordan. The strikes caused the border to close.The Syrian government on Tuesday said the Jordanian operation had taken place without prior notification or coordination, SANA reported. Damascus said it had launched comprehensive investigations into the incident, and that government agencies were assessing the needs of affected families and arranging humanitarian assistance.Jordan disputes this. The dispute is rare because, in general, Syria and Jordan have gotten along over the past year.Amman might have growing concern about a power vacuum in southern Syria. It is also concerned about drug smuggling from Syria.The latest Syrian statement also confirmed that Damascus had opened direct communication channels with Jordanian officials to examine the circumstances of the strikes. Damascus stressed the need for joint field and security coordination along the border to protect Syrian sovereignty and preserve stability in both countries.The Syrian response illustrates the challenges facing Damascus. Its government shares Jordan's concerns about ISIS and other cross-border threats, but it is also seeking to assert control over its territory and prevent neighboring countries from conducting unilateral operations.Incident threatens to undermine relationshipA joint statement issued Wednesday by the Syrian and Jordanian foreign ministries, reported by SANA, provided further evidence that both governments are seeking to prevent the incident from undermining their growing relationship.During a telephone conversation with Syria's foreign minister, Shaibani, Jordan's foreign minister, Safadi, reaffirmed Jordan's respect for Syrian sovereignty and territorial integrity. He emphasized that Amman views Syria's security and stability as an integral part of Jordan's own national security.Safadi said the Jordanian military operations had been based on intelligence gathered on the ground concerning imminent terrorist threats. He expressed regret over the civilian casualties, offered condolences to the Syrian people, and stressed that ISIS represents a common threat to both countries.The ministers also emphasized their commitment to strengthening bilateral relations and addressing disagreements through dialogue rather than allowing them to escalate.The diplomatic response shows that Amman recognizes the importance of working with Damascus rather than relying on military operations, such as bombing, without coordination.For Syria, the challenge is to demonstrate that it can deal with security threats in its territory. It will need to investigate whether ISIS cells are present.What comes next? The reopening of the Nasib border crossing on Wednesday, October 28, suggests both countries want to avoid a prolonged confrontation. Jordan and Syria have trade ties, and there will be work on border security and preventing the resurgence of ISIS.The civilian casualties in Daraa, however, are concerning. Syrians are angry. They feel they are being bombed and attacked with impunity.They may have directed some anger over Israeli raids in Jordan, because many in Daraa are also angry over Israel's raids in the border area. As such, the anger is boiling over about a sense that Syria is not more secure since the Assad regime fell.The current test will be whether the joint committee can investigate the incident, address Syrian concerns, and establish practical procedures for future counterterrorism operations.The broader question is whether Jordan and Syria can transform their improving diplomatic relationship into a sustainable security partnership, particularly as Damascus seeks to reassert control over southern Syria and Jordan faces continuing threats along its northern border.

title: 2027: ‘We’ll rig those who rig elections,’ Peter Obi talks tough
body: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has threatened to deal with those who rig elections in Nigeria, declaring that his administration would ensure electoral offenders face jail terms if he wins the 2027 presidential election. Obi spoke on Wednesday at an NDC town hall meeting in Nasarawa State, where he addressed party supporters on electoral integrity and the need to strengthen Nigeria’s electoral system. Responding to a question about election rigging, the former Anambra State governor said the party would not allow electoral manipulation to go unchallenged in the next general election. “You didn’t ask about what we are going to do if people rig election next year. Let me assure you, number one, this coming election, we will rig those who rig it,” Obi said. He added that, if elected president, he would ensure that election rigging became impossible under his watch by strengthening political parties and reforming the electoral process. “And let me assure you number two, if I’m elected the President of Nigeria, nobody will rig election in this country again because the first thing we need to do is to strengthen our parties, strengthen the process,” he said. Obi also called for stricter laws governing eligibility to contest elections, arguing that candidates should be required to demonstrate that they had attended primary and secondary school. “Our laws will be strict. For you to contest election, you must have attended a primary school, you must have attended a secondary school and it will be visible, it will be clear,” he said. He warned that anyone who forged academic certificates or falsely claimed to possess the required qualifications would face imprisonment. “If you didn’t attend any of them or forge your certificate, you go to jail,” Obi said. The NDC candidate extended the warning to officials of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and others involved in election administration, saying anyone found guilty of rigging elections under his government would be prosecuted. “Any INEC official, anybody who is involved with elections under my watch that rigs elections will go to jail,” he declared. Obi said his proposed approach would be anchored on the rule of law, insisting that no individual, regardless of position, should be exempt from accountability. “Under my watch, Nigeria must be a country that has a law, and both from the number one person to the last person must obey the rule of law,” he said. “Nobody must be above the law; nobody will behave rascally.” He said his political ambition was driven by a desire to change the country and build a system in which electoral rules were respected. “That’s why we are doing what we are doing. We want to change Nigeria. A new Nigeria is possible, and that new Nigeria will be OK,” Obi added. The post 2027: ‘We’ll rig those who rig elections,’ Peter Obi talks tough appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Russia building new drone launch site near Millerovo airfield in Rostov Oblast, HUR says
body:
Russia is building a new site for operating attack drones near Millerovo airfield, close to the Ukrainian border, Ukraine's military intelligence agency (HUR) said on Oct. 28, citing satellite imagery.
The airfield is located in the village of Dolotinka in Russia's Rostov Oblast , about 20 kilometers (12 miles) east of Ukraine's Luhansk Oblast .
According to HUR, the facility's design indicates it is intended for the preparation and launch of jet-powered attack drones, likely Geran-4 and Geran-5 models and their variants.
"The construction of the facility in the Rostov Region may be part of Russia's preparations to intensify its attacks on Ukrainian territory, particularly during the winter ," HUR said.
HUR estimated that once construction is complete, the site could accommodate up to 100 drone launches per day.
The site's actual operational tempo will depend on several factors, including supplies of ready-made drones, the availability of fuel and warheads, the number of trained drone crews, equipment readiness and the missions assigned by Russia, the statement read.
As of late August 2026, there were no significant signs of active construction at the site. Since then, launch positions and other infrastructure for drone operations have been established, HUR said.
The agency added that the rapid pace of construction may be attributed to the use of already-developed technical solutions.
Located just 3.5 kilometers (2.2 miles) from Millerovo airfield, the new site could benefit from the air defense systems already deployed to protect the airfield. Its operation could also be supported by the airfield's existing road network, utilities, logistics infrastructure and technical support systems, HUR said.
As Russia expands the drone launch site, it is also upgrading its range of jet-powered drones. The updated Geran-4 features additional autonomous navigation systems and a new warhead designed to target bridges and power transmission towers, according to the agency.
The new facility would expand Russia's network of drone launch sites, which currently numbers at least 12.
The Geran-4 and Geran-5 drones can strike targets at distances of up to 770 kilometers (nearly 480 miles) and 950 kilometers (590 miles), respectively, posing a threat not only to Ukraine but also to neighboring countries, HUR added.

title: Metinvest plans four months ahead, reviews market and production capacity monthly amid strikes – CFO
body:
Mining and metals group Metinvest plans four months ahead, reviewing market conditions and production capacity each month before drawing up cash flow forecasts and budgets, although circumstances can change dramatically even within that period, Chief Financial Officer Yulia Dankova said at the 24th Ukrainian CFO Forum in Kyiv.
Despite the uncertainty, Metinvest has retained annual business planning, preparing a plan for the following year each autumn. However, the process has changed to incorporate a baseline operating scenario, potential risks and contingency reserves for unexpected events.
Dankova said the situation could change significantly between planning cycles, with attacks, shutdowns of Black Sea ports, the introduction of EU steel import quotas and changes to national programs all affecting the business. The company selects the scenario it considers most likely and is prepared to defend, then identifies additional measures it could take even under an aggressive planning scenario. It subsequently tracks which contingency measures have been used, which risks have materialized and which unforeseen events, or "black swans," have emerged.
The company has also changed the assumptions underpinning its plans. Rather than forecasting when the war might end, it assesses practical operating conditions, including when Black Sea ports might reopen, the railway's capacity to transport cargo and whether its plants can operate.
Businesses must be prepared to revise plans continuously, Dankova said. The planning process helps management teams understand their objectives, assess different scenarios and choose economically and operationally sound decisions. For large corporations in particular, she said, the key is to quickly assess how a change in one factor affects the entire business.
Metinvest must therefore be able to reorganize operations quickly. If logistics are disrupted, cargo may need to be diverted from Black Sea ports to Poland and Romania. If raw material supplies are interrupted, the company must find alternative sources and recalculate production economics.
"Unfortunately, there was another strike on Oct 17. The plants are not operating. At the same time, we are already planning the next four-month cycle, which will include two months of next year, and preparing decisions within the selected scenario," Dankova said.
Metinvest reviews its scenarios whenever a significant event could affect operations, including a blockade of Black Sea ports or changes to EU export conditions under the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM).
Dankova said the company approved its business plan in December last year, only to learn in early January that Ukraine had not received an exemption from CBAM. Since the decision affected the plan, Metinvest immediately reviewed its operating scenarios.
The group uses dedicated platforms for sales and production planning and for consolidating plant cost data, while continuing to use Excel. Decisions are made locally or centrally depending on the circumstances and the scale of the problem. For example, if raw materials must be allocated among several plants, management needs to determine where they will deliver the greatest benefit.
Regular revisions of plans and decisions have become an integral part of Metinvest's operating model. Whereas sales, production and margin targets were previously set during the planning process, they are now reviewed by budget committees and at weekly operational meetings.
"This is adaptive management, which we use in crisis situations. And we have been living in such conditions since 2014," Dankova said.
She also stressed the importance of rapid information sharing and cooperation between departments. Decisions depend on teams understanding one another's needs, with working capital management requiring coordination with the commercial director and inventory and procurement management involving the operations director.
Metinvest is a vertically integrated mining and metals group with operations primarily in Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions. Its main shareholders are SCM Group, with a 71.24% stake, and Smart-Holding, with 23.76%. Metinvest Holding LLC is the group's managing company.

body:

After Elon Musk warned that “advertisers who post ads that are ugly, shrill, strident or overstate claims about their product will be barred from advertising” on X earlier this month, the platform now appears to be using a jarring animated arm that reaches across the screen to draw attention to the “promote” button while users are composing a post.
Many X users have seen and shared images of the unsettling promotional tool, including The Verge’s Tom Warren , but it doesn’t appear for everyone on the platform. The arm seems limited to verified users, or those with a paid subscription to X Premium. Reactions, unsurprisingly, have been less than positive. “I’ve never promoted a post and HATE this screen takeover,” said Sheel Mohnot , while Jesse Middleton likened it to a Halloween prank. “I wish I could explain how jarring this hand and animation was in the @X app. It was truly shocking, almost like a Halloween gag, but I’m pretty sure it was real.”

title: Highwaymen: How Cargo Theft Gangs Operate in Costa Rica
body: Highwaymen: How Cargo Theft Gangs Operate in Costa Rica PEÑAS BLANCAS, COSTA RICA – It was after midnight when we finally reached Peñas Blancas. We could not have timed it worse. The area is the primary border crossing for commercial truck drivers going north on the international highway between Costa Rica and Nicaragua. It is also a criminal hotspot—one of the worst places to sit, waiting in a truck, in Central America. We had been driving for over ten hours since departing from Paso Canoas on Costa Rica’s southern border with Panama, but now our headlights lit up the trailer in front of us as we approached the end of the two-kilometer line of semi-trucks waiting to pass into Nicaragua. “Two kilometers is nothing,” said Irvin Pérez, a Panamanian trucker who has been transporting cargo since 2017. “Sometimes it’s between 15 and 20 kilometers long and takes four days just to cross this border. They rob us while we wait.” The only drivers who can sleep easy in this line are those whose companies pay for private security teams to guard their trucks while they rest. Irvin was one of those fortunate drivers, and a security guard with a bulletproof vest and a 9mm pistol was sitting in the passenger seat. “Customs will reopen at 6 a.m.,” the guard said. “We’ll be outside the truck. Call us if you need anything.” Truck driver Irvin Perez drives along Route 2, a narrow highway in southern Costa Rica forming part of the Panamerican Highway system. Credit: Owen Alfonso A hot, humid breeze from the nearby jungle stirred the stagnant air in the cab as he opened the door and climbed outside to join three more guards protecting two other trucks in the line. The truckers I spoke with had similar stories about this border. Sometimes they only steal the truck’s outer accessories, such as hubcaps, or siphon gasoline. Sometimes they smash the truck’s windows to gain access to the cab, hold a pistol to the driver’s head or a machete to his throat, take his money, phone, and other valuables, and then leave him tied up in the back of the truck. Thieves even steal the barrier arms blocking the entrances to truck parking areas designed to prevent such robberies. But the border crossing at Peñas Blancas is only a small part of the growing insecurity within Costa Rica’s commercial transportation system. Irvin’s security detail was not only there to facilitate a safe border crossing into Nicaragua. They were there to guard against the greater threat of cargo theft, a thriving illicit business run by criminal groups specializing in highway robbery on Costa Rican roadways. The groups were just the start of a vast, illicit resale distribution chain stretching into informal markets around the country. Fact Box Gangs robbed at least 156 truckloads in 2025, making Costa Rica Central America’s leader in cargo theft Private security increases cost per container by up to 25% Gangs target trucks with high-value loads of between $100,000 and $500,000. Popular products include clothing, electronics, kitchen appliances, alcohol, and tires. Panama–Guatemala runs that once took three or four days can now take up to six as drivers avoid night travel Stolen goods are fenced in small markets, bodegas, and storefronts, where they sell for as little as half the normal retail price. Violent gangs and porous control behind Costa Rica cargo theft boom I flew to Panama City in early February 2026 after hearing criminal gangs were targeting trucks carrying goods from Panama’s Colon Free Trade Zone (Zona Libre de Colon – CFZ), Latin America’s largest tax-free shopping and trade area. Gangs have targeted trucks throughout Central America for years, especially in the northern countries like Guatemala, Honduras, and El Salvador, but in recent years Costa Rica has become an epicenter of cargo theft in the region. In 2025, gangs robbed at least 156 truckloads of merchandise—about three trucks per week. Through July 2026, there were 71 robberies, putting it on a pace similar to 2025. The Judicial Investigation Department (Organismo de Investigación Judicial – OIJ), Costa Rica’s version of the FBI, has been gathering data on cargo theft since 2016, when gangs robbed at least 121 trucks. Criminal groups target trucks that contain the most value, usually carrying between $100,000 and $500,000 worth of cargo, or those that contain popular resale items such as clothing, electronics, kitchen appliances, alcohol, or tires. Over the last decade gangs have robbed over 1,300 trucks along two primary transport corridors cutting through Costa Rica. I organized a ride-along on one of those corridors: a 520-kilometer mix of highways stretching the length of the country from Paso Canoas to Peñas Blancas. A freight forwarding company in the CFZ had connected me to the owner of a trucking company outside of David, Panama, who had a truck go missing in December 2025. He introduced me to Irvin, one of his drivers, who graciously agreed to give me a ride through the countryside. Truckers wait in the customs line near Penas Blancas on the Costa Rica-Nicaragua border: Credit: Owen Alfonso I met Irvin in his white and red truck near the customs checkpoint outside of Paso Canoas. I opened the door to be greeted by a broad-shouldered man wearing a gray polo shirt and a pair of sunglasses resting on top of his short, black hair. “Once security arrives, we’ll leave,” he said. That was supposed to be at 10 a.m. so we could avoid driving during the night when most of the robberies occur, but due to a paperwork infraction, it was after 2 p.m. by the time we hit the road. Crossing the border left our truck exposed. Cargo theft gangs have lookouts on the borders to tip off robbery teams with information about the truck and its contents. They also obtain information from customs systems. Gangs use Costa Rica’s cargo tracking system, the Information Technology for Customs Control (Tecnología de Información para Control Aduanero -TICA) to target trucks with specific goods and values. And they can identify targets by accessing an online system called the Single Central American Declaration (Declaración Única Centroamericana – DUCA). Once the information is entered, customs officials in every country through which that truck passes have access to the truck’s contents, the value of the load, the license plate, the registration number, and the driver’s name and passport credentials. The system is accessible to freight companies as well as customs officials, and while the information should be protected, it can be leaked to bad actors. “These gangs often have access to customs information. So, they already know which truck is carrying what. The system itself is vulnerable. Anyone who knows how to use the system can look up a truck’s license plate and see its cargo,” said Marjorie Lizano, the president of the Costa Rican Chamber of United Transporters (Cámara Costarricense de Transportistas Unitarios – CCTU). Lizano said there have been plans to transition to a new system, but it hasn’t been implemented yet. “For now, the current system remains quite porous,” she added. Two trucks traveling in convoy exit the Zurqui tunnel on Highway 32, which connects Limón with San José: Credit: Owen Alfonso The border itself is also porous. The only other checkpoint along the Inter-American Highway is 35 kilometers after Paso Canoas. It is often not manned during the night, and if it is raining, officers sometimes suspend operations altogether. The gangs know this. In 2025, a group commandeered a Panamanian truck from a rest area in Paso Canoas while the driver was sleeping. The thieves drove the truck straight past the Costa Rican customs checkpoint, which is located off the side of the highway, with no physical barrier preventing trucks from entering the country from Panama. The empty trailer was eventually recovered in Alajuela province, some 350kilometers from where it was stolen. From hijacking to fencing: the Costa Rica cargo theft chain From the Panama crossing, Irvin and I headed northwest along Highway 2. I sat on the bottom bunk of the sleeper cab. The 500-horsepower engine rumbled steadily under the high-pitched whirring sound blowing from the portable fan Irvin had strapped to the back of his seat. The jungle’s deep green foliage shook and swayed as we rumbled past. The warm air was thick, but a cool drizzle of rain kept the cab bearable. Our progress was tracked by the trucking company. Transporters have tried to mitigate the risk of robbery by installing GPS trackers on their trucks and trailers and by traveling in convoys during the day. But the gangs use jammers to block the signal and have split convoys by squeezing their vehicles in between the trucks or surrounding them with multiple vehicles. After the gangs stop them, they typically hold the driver at gunpoint and steal the rig. “There are gangs that travel in two to three cars,” explained Andrés Muñoz, the treasurer of Panama’s National Chamber of Freight Transport (Cámara Nacional de Transporte de Carga de Panamá – CANATRACA). “They box in the truck, restrain the driver, gag him, put him in the sleeper cab, and keep him there for a while. Then they move him to one of those three cars and drive him away and dump him while they take the trailer.” “They are professionals, not just amateurs who randomly show up, because the guy who takes the truck can drive just as well as, or even better than, the original driver,” Muñoz added. The trailers, if they are not recovered, can cost transporters up to $14,000. The merchandise generally disappears entirely, swallowed by a parallel, informal economy where the goods are resold. According to Yeric Vega Blanco, an officer with OIJ who is investigating the robberies, brokers sell the stolen goods to loosely controlled retail outlets, where they are then fenced in small markets, bodegas, and storefronts. “The main indicator is how low the price is,” Vega added. “Sometimes it is less than half price.” Tires that normally cost 50,000 colones (about $110 might be sold for 25,000; or 60-inch TVs sell for 100,000 colones when they are normally 350,000 to 400,000. In 2025, Costa Rica passed law 10736, increasing prison penalties for receiving high-value stolen merchandise. But the illicit resale market persists. Security needs drive rising freight costs Our 53-foot trailer carried agricultural goods that were commonly sold in Costa Rica, which is why we needed an armed security detail to join us, Irvin told me, gesturing and smirking at Josué, our security guard for the first leg of the journey. The increased security comes with a price. When a freight forwarding company hires a private security company, the cost to transport a container through Costa Rica can increase up to 25%, from $2,000 to $2,500 per trailer load. For transporters unable to spend the extra cash for security and unwilling to risk driving through the night, they lose valuable time. Routes from Panama to Guatemala that used to take three or four days now can take up to six when the drivers refuse to drive during the night. When a trailer is robbed, some freight forwarding companies pay out again to hire private investigators to track down the missing merchandise. Around 5 p.m., we stopped in front of a small single-lane bridge spanning the Coronado River. Cars crossed from the other side, and Irvin squirmed in his seat. “I hate stopping at bridges like this,” Irvin said under his breath, peering at his rearview mirrors. “If someone is trailing you, they can climb into your truck while you wait to let cars pass. I’m constantly checking my mirrors to see if the same car has been following me.” Truck robbery has become so normal in Costa Rica that it haunts life along its highway corridors. While our cab talk was often filled with jokes and laughter, the conversation was also punctuated with disturbing stories of shootouts and drivers being robbed, beaten, and discarded on the roadside. Josué told us about the two times he has faced off with hijackers. “I fired warning shots so they knew there was armed security, and they backed off,” he said. “But some of them carry assault rifles, and when you only have a 9mm pistol, at that point there is nothing you can do.” For those without protection, it’s far worse. Late one night at a David maintenance yard filled with semi-trucks in various stages of repair, I met Ovidio Martínez, who had just delivered a cargo shipment from Colón. He described to me how a gang had assaulted him and hijacked his rig in 2012. Martínez had been delivering a $560,000 load of Puma and Nike sneakers to a client in San José, the capital of Costa Rica, when a green Nissan Sentra blocked a roadway intersection, causing him to slow the speed of his truck to a near stop. A man walking on the side of the road jumped onto the truck, opened the driver door, and pointed a pistol in his face. Another man hopped out of the Sentra, opened the truck’s passenger door, and got in. They forced Martínez into the sleeper cab, tied him up with his shoelaces, and gagged him. Then they drove off. “I couldn’t see anything because they had me in the sleeper compartment, face down. At one point, the weight of my own body made me feel like I was suffocating.” Martínez told me. “The one sitting with me kept telling the driver he wanted to kill me, but the other one told him to leave me alone because I wasn’t resisting, and there was no need.” Martínez was lucky. After the criminals detached the trailer and tried to drive away, the driver collided with a motorcyclist on the road. In the scramble that followed, they abandoned the truck with him inside. Soon after, someone found him tied up in the cab and called the police. They later located the still fully-loaded trailer in a parking lot in a town 40 kilometers from where the gang assaulted Martínez. Frustrated police, defenseless drivers We drove into El Roble soon after 9 p.m. El Roble is near the Pacific Port of Caldera, a connection point for two major cargo transport corridors in Costa Rica: our northwesterly route to Nicaragua and the roughly 250-kilometer east-west route connecting Caldera to Limón, a major Caribbean port city and drug trafficking hub. It was in El Roble that hijackers murdered Panamanian driver Krevith Holbart Shaw Beitia in 2024, shooting him in the head during a robbery. Local Costa Rican truckers transporting goods between the two port areas are frequently targeted on the highway that runs through the rugged mountains of Braulio Carrillo National Park, where the peaks rise to nearly 3,000 meters and the cell phone service is sparse. The cloudy jungles between San José and Limón provide excellent cover to discard trailers and truck drivers. When a truck fails to arrive at its intended destination, this is one of the first areas that friends, colleagues, and police search. Trucks traverse Braulio Carrillo National Park, a hotspot for truck robbery due to the lack of cell phone service. Credit: Owen Alfonso The OIJ’s Vega has worked these robbery cases for years. He described the criminal groups behind them as agile and said that some were connected to more powerful networks involved in the drug trade. Vega was frustrated. The OIJ, he said, was spread too thin to deal with this issue, especially as officials were already scrambling to deal with the recent spike in organized crime violence. His frustrations are shared by the truckers, who feel defenseless. Transport companies have met with Costa Rican officials who have promised to put more resources towards quelling the problem, but organized cargo theft persists. “The government tells us, ‘Let’s see what happens, let’s see what solutions we can find,’” said Martínez, the trucker who was robbed in 2012. “But meanwhile, we continue living with the risk of being killed.” Faith in the transport sector is also waning. Some believe the trucking companies themselves might be complicit. “It stains your reputation badly,” said Martínez. “People start wondering whether the transport company might have been involved or whether it truly was just a robbery. And mistrust begins to grow between the commercial sector and the transport sector.” It is having an impact. Some clients have begun to transport their products via ocean-going vessels from the Colon Free Trade Zone directly to ports in Honduras and Guatemala to avoid Costa Rican highways, despite the slower travel times. From El Roble, Irvin and I spent the next few hours snaking our way towards the border, and soon we were sitting in the queue in Peñas Blancas. After our bodyguard began his rounds, we were able to grab a few hours of sleep in the cab’s bunk beds. Not long after first light, the line started moving again. Before we crossed, I said goodbye to Irvin. He later messaged me, letting me know he had passed safely into Nicaragua, but still had two more days of driving until he could deliver his cargo in Honduras. Then, he would finally head home. Drawing on the same field research and investigative networks behind this story, we offer tailored diagnostics, briefings, and route- or country-specific analysis and monitoring services. title: From windfall to wealth: how to make your money last
body: Receiving a financial windfall, whether through an inheritance, gift from family or prize winnings can fast-track major financial goals and responsibilities. However, without a clear plan, a sudden windfall can easily become a missed opportunity to building long lasting wealth. As more young people focus on financial independence and long-term wealth creation, young adults are encouraged to view a financial windfall not as spending money, but as a foundation for future financial security. Akweley Laryea, Head of Retail Banking at First National Bank shared that one of the biggest mistakes young adults make is treating a windfall as an opportunity to immediately upgrade their lifestyle. “Many young people dream of owning a home, driving a new car or travelling the world. While a financial windfall may make these goals achievable immediately, it is important to first define your financial goals. The decisions made in the first few months can have a significant impact on future financial wellbeing,” adds Akweley as she shares financial considerations to take into account: Don’t make major financial decisions immediately: Take time to develop a structured financial plan that considers your short, medium to long term financial needs so that you avoid unnecessary spending. Seek professional advice: we encourage young people to avoid making significant financial commitments for at least six to 12 months after receiving a windfall. This provides time to seek advice, gain a full understanding of their financial needs and make decisions that support long-term wealth creation rather than short-term gratification. Set clear financial goals: a financial windfall can create significant opportunities, but managing it wisely is important. Young adults should focus on setting clear financial goals, reducing costly debt, building an emergency fund and invest for long-term growth. Make informed decisions: young people are also encouraged to avoid rushing into business ventures or investment opportunities. It is advisable to rather take the time to understand these opportunities fully and obtain appropriate advice before committing funds. Don’t resign from your job: be cautious of viewing a windfall as a replacement for employment or career growth. A financial windfall should complement and not replace your career ambitions. Continuing to work, building skills and enhancing your earning potential remains one of the most effective ways to preserve and grow wealth over time. Giving a gift that creates wealth: Financial windfalls do not always arrive through inheritances or prize winnings. Increasingly, families are looking for meaningful ways to transfer wealth and create financial opportunities for loved ones during important milestones. What if those moments became opportunities to build wealth instead? This is where innovative solutions such as the FNB Investment Gift Card are changing the way people think about gifting. Instead of giving cash that may quickly be spent, families and friends can gift an investment that provides the recipient with an opportunity to start or grow their wealth journey. “Whether it is helping a young graduate take their first step into investing, contributing towards a child’s future, supporting newlyweds as they build their financial future, or celebrating a professional milestone, an investment gift has the potential to create value long after the occasion has passed”. By shifting from consumption-based gifting to investment-based gifting, families can play a meaningful role in building a stronger culture of saving and investing across generations. Akweley adds that families should proactively prepare younger beneficiaries for future inheritances. We often underestimate the responsibility that comes with inheriting money. Where possible, families should start conversations early and help younger beneficiaries understand the financial responsibilities that may come with managing large amounts of money. “Receiving a financial windfall is rare. For young people, it can be a powerful opportunity to build wealth, achieve financial freedom and create a stronger financial future, provided it is managed with patience, discipline and the right support,” concludes Akweley.

title: European Commission rules out resumption of Russian gas supplies to EU
body:
Russian gas supplies to the European Union and operation of the Nord Stream pipeline will not resume after the end of Russia's war against Ukraine, the European Commission said on Wednesday, responding to media reports that the United States and Russia are discussing a possible restoration of supplies.

European Commission chief spokesperson Paula Pinho said EU legislation ruled out a return to imports of Russian fossil fuels, including gas.

She said European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen had recently reiterated that energy sanctions imposed in response to Russia's war would remain in force until Russia ends the war. The EU was aware of the cost of dependence on Russian fossil fuels, which Moscow had used as a weapon, Pinho said, adding that the consequences of that dependence remained significant regardless of whether the war continued.

title: At least 64 people killed in Spain as 2 high-speed trains collide
body: URDA, Spain – Rescue workers in Spain on Wednesday, October 28, were scouring the wreckage for more bodies at the crash scene where at least 64 people were killed when two high-speed trains collided, in the second deadly railway accident in the country this year. Evacuated passengers streamed along a road near the scene, some splattered with blood or with their wounds bandaged, others wheeling suitcases and being given water by volunteers who said it had been donated from neighboring towns. Hundreds of ambulances, funeral home vans and helicopters were parked next to a train with several carriages sitting on an elevated section of track while twisted metal, broken panels and wreckage could be seen strewn across an embankment beneath the line where at least three carriages had plunged. Miguel, a passenger traveling with several colleagues in the rear car of one of the trains, described to COPE radio the moment of the accident. “We heard a massive roar, a truly enormous thud that went on for 10 seconds, as if the train were about to derail. Through the right-hand window, we could see a wrecked train,” he said. A person briefed on the disaster said a train operated by private consortium Iryo stopped near Toledo on orders from infrastructure manager ADIF due to a signal fault. A train operated by Renfe then struck the stationary train at high speed, causing several carriages of both trains to derail, the person said. Renfe said in a statement that after a being authorized to continue its journey, its train had crashed into the Iryo train that had remained stationary “for reasons we don’t know.” “The Renfe train continued on its way as instructed, and a collision occurred. The exact sequence of events, the traffic conditions and the circumstances of the impact will have to be established by the investigation,” Renfe said. There was no immediate response to a Reuters request for comment from Iryo or Adif. – Rappler.com

title: Licensed, not banned: what China’s new rules mean for the parts inside Russia’s Shahed-type drones
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); China’s updated drone export rules will cover the engines in Russia’s Geran attack drones, Russia’s version of Iran’s Shahed, Ukraine’s sanctions commissioner Vladyslav Vlasiuk said on 27 October. He cited a clarification from China’s Commerce Ministry, Ukrainska Pravda’s defense desk Oboronka reported . The license requirement takes effect on 18 November. Licensing itself isn’t new. China has required permits for some drone engines since September 2023. Even so, Chinese engines kept reaching Russian drone plants, some shipped as refrigeration units, Reuters reported. Russia’s jet-powered Gerans rely fully on Chinese turbojets, HUR deputy chief Vadym Skibitskyi has said . So the update’s value lies in enforcement, not in the list. Three agencies, one list Beijing issued the update in a joint announcement by the Commerce Ministry, the General Administration of Customs, and the Central Military Commission’s Equipment Development Department. Announcement No. 49 bars exports of listed drone items without a license, including specially designed autopilots and certain drone engines. China will approve applications that comply with the rules, a Commerce Ministry spokesperson added . Explore further China calls itself neutral—but its fiber ends up in the drones that hit Ukraine Vlasiuk said the core of Russia’s long-range strike drones has formally come under control. He named engines for Gerans, turbojets for their jet versions, autopilots, and jam-resistant navigation. The announcement lists anti-jam navigation as a technology, not as hardware. He called the step an opening for Ukraine because Beijing now formally takes responsibility for these categories. Kyiv will press for the rules to be applied to known suppliers of Russia’s arms industry and, with partners, track licenses, transit routes, and re-exports, he said. Permits, refusals, and FPV parts Licensing does not mean a ban, Vlasiuk stressed. Exporters China deems reliable can get general permits for up to three years, while the rules leave broad grounds for refusal. The new thresholds do not cover motors and speed controllers for FPV drones, batteries, cameras, or optical fiber, he added. The rules do cover brushless motors that meet all of these: at least 48 volts, at least 3 kW, a power density of at least 3 kW per kilogram, and no more than 3,000 rpm. Their speed controllers are covered too, Militarnyi reported . Russia could still obtain parts with Beijing’s approval, the outlet noted. Ukraine, without such close ties, could face delays, inspections, and higher costs. Read also Russia’s new jet Shaheds run on turbojets from one Chinese company. title: Road crashes drop by 9.4% following TraffiTech sensitisation – MTTD
body: The Director of Education, Research and Training at the Police Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD), ACP Alexander Kwaku Obeng, says road crashes reported across Ghana declined by 9.4% following intensified sensitisation and caution notices issued to motorists under the TraffiTech-GH pilot project. He said the police recorded 1,003 crashes in September this year, down from 1,108 during the same period in 2025. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Wednesday, ACP Obeng attributed the reduction to increased public awareness and messages sent to vehicle owners, alerting them to traffic offences captured by the system. “Within twenty days of September this year, when we enhanced sensitisation, gathering evidence and confronting vehicle owners with it with an embedded message, with GPS, MTTD sender ID sending messages saying ‘speed kills, reduce it now’ with your vehicle number, time and place of the offence,” he said. He explained that a comparison of crash data for September 2025 and September 2026 showed a change in driver behaviour. “If you compare the data of crashes from September last year (2025) with the same period this year, we have seen a significant change in behaviour of drivers,” he added. ACP Obeng said the number of vehicles involved in crashes also fell from 1,928 in September 2025 to 1,693 this year, representing a 12.19% reduction. The number of people injured in road crashes declined by 15.02%, from 1,405 to 1,194 over the same period. TraffiTech-GH is currently being piloted and has not yet been rolled out nationwide. Traffitech-GH is an automated system developed by the Ghana Police Service to enforce road traffic laws and regulations and improve road safety in the country. The system uses cameras and sensors to automatically take a picture and or video of vehicles that flout road traffic laws and regulations, such as speeding and running a red light

title: Poland, UK Sign 3-Year Defense Cooperation Plan
body:
A bilateral meeting between Poland’s deputy prime minister and defense minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz and the UK’s defense secretary Wes Streeting took place in Warsaw on Tuesday, Oct. 27, at which they signed a three-year defense plan.
The plan was built on the UK- Poland Security and Defense Partnership Treaty – the “ Northolt Treaty ” – which was signed in May by the then-British Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
According to Kosiniak-Kamysz, the main areas of cooperation will include new technologies, artificial intelligence, drones, anti-drone systems, modern deterrence measures, as well as traditional exercises to build capabilities, and cooperation under different scenarios.
This will also include collaboration in development of the next generation of air defense missiles which, according to the Polish announcement , will be based on its “Narew,” “Pilica,” and “Pilica+” programs.
It will also address the co-development of drone and counter-drone technologies in the face of increased Russian threats against civilian infrastructure and drone incursions across Europe, according to the UK’s minister.
Streeting said: “We hear very clearly what Poland experiences every day in the form of what some describe as hybrid threats from Russia – I prefer to describe it directly as state-sponsored terrorism – the daily mobilization of your forces and air defense in the face of drone intrusions.”
It also will build on the jont construction of modern warships including the Polish “Miecznik” (Swordfish) and the British Type 31 frigate programs, which are said to be on schedule. This will go hand-in-hand with increased naval activity in the Baltic Sea which, through exercises and regional coordination, will allow the two countries to protect vital lines of communication in the waterway
The agreement also sees cooperation on cyber security and resilience to help both countries protect defense-related and civilian networks from hostile threats.
The two men say there will also be closer links between their defense industries that will include closer defense procurement coordination with companies including MBDA UK, in the area of missiles with BAE Systems,and Poland’s PGZ working together in the production of large-caliber ammunition.
The plan sees continued UK and Polish participation in large-scale exercises such as Steadfast Defender, Polish Dragon, and Joint Warrior, which will ensure their forces retain the capability to fight future conflicts, including the use of counter-drone warfare, electronic warfare, and missile defense.
The ministers said both nations are fully committed to supporting Kyiv in the war against Russia. They will both provide contingents for November’s major “Coalition of the Wiling” exercise in Poland, which will see the deployment thousands of personnel earmarked for the Multinational Force Ukraine, intended to support the military training and post-war rebuilding of the war torn country.
The exercise was announced in August by French President Emmanuel Macron, the UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz.
Euro News reported that the meeting also saw discussions on Europe’s relations with the US, which Kosiniak-Kamysz said reached agreement on the need to strengthen and build up Europe’s defense capabilities without disengaging with Washington.
He said “Poland and the United Kingdom support strengthening this alliance [with the United States - ed.], the transatlantic alliance, because the United Kingdom is the best example – everything connected with the transatlantic alliance grew out of Britain. We are in favor of reinforcing it and building our own capabilities, of greater independence for Europe, but not independence from the United States.”

title: Carrick, Fernandes, hold peace talks after Bournemouth neglect
body: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes and head coach Michael Carrick have held private talks to resolve tensions ahead of the club’s Premier League clash with Chelsea on Saturday. The meeting followed Fernandes’ omission from the starting line-up in United’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday, after the Portuguese midfielder reportedly criticised Carrick’s tactics following a 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League. BBC Sport report that the pair met privately at United’s training ground on Tuesday to discuss their differences and clear the air before the team travels to Stamford Bridge. Fernandes, 32, remained an unused substitute against Bournemouth but could return to the starting line-up when United face Chelsea at 12:30 GMT on Saturday. Carrick, meanwhile, will remain in charge for the fixture despite mounting pressure over the team’s poor performances. The 45-year-old was widely expected to lose his job following the Bournemouth defeat, but United’s board has decided to give him another opportunity to turn the situation around. The club currently sit 16th in the Premier League table, having recorded just one victory in eight league matches this season. Despite the disappointing run, senior figures at Old Trafford reportedly believe Carrick should not bear the entire responsibility for the team’s struggles. The board is understood to consider the squad capable of qualifying for the Champions League and believes the players have failed to perform to their expected standard. In a further boost for Carrick, midfielder Kobbie Mainoo returned to training on Wednesday after spending a fortnight on the sidelines with an injury. However, uncertainty remains over Carrick’s long-term future, with United reportedly drawing up a shortlist of potential replacements. Former Newcastle United manager Eddie Howe and ex Germany and Bayern Munich head coach Julian Nagelsmann are among the names being considered. Saturday’s encounter with Chelsea could therefore prove significant for Carrick as he attempts to improve United’s results and restore confidence within the squad. The talks with Fernandes may also help ease tensions between the manager and his captain as United seek to recover from their latest setback. The post Carrick, Fernandes, hold peace talks after Bournemouth neglect appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Five killed in airstrike near El Geneina airport, West Darfur
body: Five people, including two women, have been killed in an airstrike near El Geneina Airport in Sudan’s West Darfur State, according to eyewitnesses and the state government. Khalil Hamid, secretary-general of the Rapid Support Forces (RSF)-aligned government in West Darfur, accused the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) of carrying out the attack using a drone on Monday, 26 October 2026. Eyewitnesses told Radio Tamazuj that the drone flew over El Geneina, the state capital, before launching an attack towards the airport. They said five people, including two women working on nearby farmland, were killed in the strike. Hamid said the drone fired three missiles during the attack, which he described as a strike on civilian objects. He said El Geneina Airport had been out of operation since fighting erupted between the SAF and the RSF in April 2023 and had not handled any air traffic since then. Sudan has been at war since April 2023, when fighting broke out between the army and the RSF. The RSF largely controls West Darfur, including El Geneina. Hamid described Monday’s incident as the third attack involving drones and Antonov aircraft targeting the airport since the conflict began. He condemned the attack and called for an end to strikes on civilian objects and the destruction of infrastructure. The SAF’s response to the allegations was not available at the time of publication. The post Five killed in airstrike near El Geneina airport, West Darfur appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: European Commission informed of Stubb and Støre’s plans to speak with Putin – spokesperson
body:
The European Commission was aware of the plans by Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre to hold a telephone conversation with Vladimir Putin, stated European Commission Chief Spokesperson Paula Pinho.
Pinho said during a briefing in Brussels on Wednesday, in response to questions from journalists, that they were informed before the conversation took place. It was held on a bilateral basis and followed up on a meeting that took place in Oslo last week, on October 20.
At the same time, she emphasized that the EU is united in its commitment not only to bring an end to this terrible war but also to achieve a just and lasting peace.
According to her, this is the position they are maintaining throughout the current negotiations, and it is important that they present a united front on this matter, regardless of the specific nature of the talks being held with President Putin. The chief spokesperson added that, unfortunately, President Putin himself shows little willingness to engage in such discussions.
She offered no assessment of this conversation.
At the same time, according to Pinho, she has no new information regarding the upcoming negotiations.
As reported, Ukrainian President Zelenskyy discussed with Stubb and Støre their conversation with Putin, thanking them for their active support of our diplomacy and the peace efforts undertaken jointly with all our partners. According to the Ukrainian president, the President of Finland and the Prime Minister of Norway conveyed to the Russian leader that concrete steps are required to de-escalate the situation regarding Ukraine’s energy sector and infrastructure. Furthermore, the discussion touched upon preparations for a trilateral meetingб involving Ukraine, the USA, and Russia, scheduled for November in Abu Dhabi (UAE) at the level of their respective teams.

title: Developing Africa’s hydropower potential directly linked to water conservation — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Developing Africa’s hydropower potential is directly linked to water conservation, Russian President Vladimir Putin announced at the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.
"The development of Africa’s hydropower potential - which is far from being fully tapped - is directly connected to water conservation. This year marks the 55th anniversary of commissioning the Aswan High Dam, one of the enduring symbols of high-tech cooperation between our country and the African continent," the Russian president said.
The head of state noted that the African Union has designated ensuring sustainable access to clean water as a key objective for this year.
"The African Union has identified securing sustainable access to clean water as a major priority for the current year. Russia is ready to share its unique, responsible water-management technologies to help efficiently and carefully manage water resources. This encompasses land reclamation, the design and construction of irrigation canals and hydraulic structures, digital water facility management, and the monitoring of irrigation networks and water loss zones," Putin said.
He added that Russia is ready to assist Africa in modernizing existing power plants.
"Another company of ours, RusHydro, is prepared to help our African friends design new facilities and modernize existing power plants, as well as develop modular, localized power generation to supply remote, isolated areas in Africa," he said.
TASS is an official media partner of the third Russia-Africa Summit and the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.

title: Ondo: Mob attacks police station over farmer’s killing
body: By Promise Adagba The Ondo State Police Command has arrested two suspects in connection with the murder of a farmer, Rasheed Hassan, in Ala, Akure North Local Government Area of the state, and rescued them from an angry mob attempting to lynch them. The police also arrested 14 persons over an attack on the Ala Divisional Police Headquarters and officers who intervened to rescue the suspects. The Command’s spokesperson, DSP Abayomi Jimoh, disclosed this during a press briefing on Wednesday, adding that two police officers sustained gunshot injuries during the incident. Hassan was reportedly murdered at General Camp in the Government Reserve area, with the incident reported to the police on October 24, 2026. Bayelsa: Cleric arrested over alleged defilement of two minors Rivers Rainbow Coalition retains Chinda, allocates 33 slots to APC, 15 to PDP Jimoh said police operatives, who visited the scene, recovered the victim’s body with deep cuts on his head and other parts of his body, while his belongings were reportedly missing. He said investigations commenced immediately to identify and apprehend those responsible for the killing. According to him, the Ala Youth President arrested the two suspects on October 26 and conveyed them to the police station, when an angry crowd confronted him, demanding that the suspects be handed over for extrajudicial killing. The youth president subsequently sought refuge at the Ala Divisional Police Headquarters with the suspects, but the mob pursued them and attacked the facility, throwing stones and other dangerous objects at the station. Jimoh said tactical and rescue teams were deployed to the area and successfully rescued the suspects at about 1:45 a.m. on October 27. However, the patrol team conveying the suspects to Akure came under attack, leaving two police officers with gunshot injuries allegedly caused by pellets fired from a pump-action firearm. The Commissioner of Police, CP Felix Ohagwu, condemned the incident, warning against attempts to take the law into one’s hands or obstruct lawful police operations. He assured residents that anyone found culpable would face the full weight of the law and urged community leaders and youth groups to discourage mob action and allow the criminal justice system to take its course.

title: 'This is America!' Waltz says as he and Cubans get into shouting match at UN
body:
Things got testy as the Cubans approached the podium as Waltz was speaking.
Tension between the U.S. and Cuba was on full display at the United Nations on Tuesday as the Trump administration's envoy to the body, Ambassador Mike Waltz, and Cuba's foreign minister engaged in a shouting match on the floor of the General Assembly.
During the U.N.'s annual debate on the U.S. blockade against Cuba, Waltz took the podium and began delivering a speech that was hotly critical of the Cuban regime.
Shortly after Waltz began his remarks, Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla and the rest of the Cuban delegation began challenging him from the audience -- shouting and gesturing as the president of the assembly banged his gavel and fruitlessly asked them to quiet down.
"I hope everyone, Mr. President, is listening to the delegation right now," Waltz said with a smile. "Imagine what happens when someone ask these questions in Havana, not in a room of ambassadors and cameras! Imagine what happens to those people if this is the intimidation and disruption that we see!"
Rodríguez Parrilla and Waltz traded more remarks, with Waltz declaring "This is America, this is the United Nations, this isn't your communist dictatorship. You can't silence me or you cannot silence my colleagues!
Rodríguez Parrilla, whose comments could not be clearly heard on a U.N. livestream of the meeting, approached the front of the hall.
Waltz yelled, "Mr. President, this individual needs to back away from this podium. He's not going to intimidate me in the United States of America! I'm the representative of the United States of America! Back up!"
At that point, the assembly president suspended the meeting. After recounting the U.N.'s rules for the event, the president then gave Rodríguez Parrilla a chance to issue a point of order on the condition he limit his grievances to procedure rather the substance of Waltz's remarks.
Rodríguez Parrilla returned to his seat and used the opportunity to speak to protest Waltz's claims, accusing him of "grossly lying."
Waltz finished his speech without major incident, ending by urging the chamber to vote against the resolution under consideration on Wednesday. Waltz finished his remarks without major incident -- urging the chamber to vote against the resolution under consideration on Wednesday.
Following the incident, Rodríguez Parrilla doubled down on X, writing that Waltz "with his arrogance and hubris, forgets that he is at the United Nations, not at the US National Security Council, nor in a Green Berets unit, nor in a Signal group, where he has repeatedly shown his incompetence and incapacity."
Waltz, a former Green Beret, came under scrutiny last year while serving as national security adviser for inadvertently inviting a journalist to a Signal chat with Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, Vice President JD Vance and other top national security officials discussing details of the strike on the Houthis in Yemen.
President Donald Trump nominated Waltz to the U.N. post at the same time he announced Secretary of State Marco Rubio would also serve as national security adviser.
