title: Russian business in Africa not involved in 'predatory exploitation' of resources — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Russian companies do not engage in the "predatory exploitation" of natural resources in Africa, but instead increase local processing of raw materials, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.
"One of the main areas of the Russia-Africa partnership has traditionally been the extraction and processing of mineral resources. This is a systemic, vital sector for many of the continent's economies, bringing real dividends and revenues into the budgets of African nations," the head of state noted. "And specialized Russian companies, which have a long and successful history of interaction, are continuing this work with African countries, continuing the implementation of a number of major projects," Putin said.
"At the same time, our business does not engage in the predatory, neo-colonial exploitation of natural and human resources but increases the processing of raw materials on-site, thereby creating new jobs and generating tax revenues across all levels of the budget systems of African nations," the Russian leader stressed.

title: Three people dead following multi-vehicle crash near Windsor: OPP
body:
Three people are dead following a multi-vehicle crash early Wednesday morning in a town just outside of Windsor.
Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) said its officers responded to the crash on County Road 22 in Lakeshore around 6:07 a.m.
The drivers of two vehicles involved in the crash were pronounced dead on scene; a passenger was taken to hospital where they were pronounced dead.
Police are assessing others for injuries. The OPP did not specify the amount of people or vehicles involved in the crash.
Anyone with information is asked to contact police.

title: NELFUND moves to stop students collecting loans while parents pay fees
body: …plans nationwide for re-education of students, institutions …400,000 students covered by the payment system pilot By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) has announced plans to clamp down on alleged double-dipping by students who benefit from its loan scheme while still relying on their parents to pay their school fees. The move, which signals a fresh effort to tighten accountability in the implementation of the Federal Government’s student loan programme, will also see parents provided with a mechanism to verify whether their children’s tuition fees have been paid through the scheme. Managing Director of NELFUND, Akintunde Sawyerr, disclosed this on Wednesday during a press briefing, where he said the fund had identified cases of students allegedly accessing loan support while continuing to place the burden of tuition payments on their parents. Describing the practice as unacceptable, Sawyerr said the fund was determined to end the situation and strengthen transparency in the administration of the scheme. “This comment is based on our recognition that there are so many students out there who are double-dipping. They are taking from the NELFUND and still stressing their parents,” he said. “We are going to put an end to that.” Under the proposed arrangement, parents would be able to confirm whether their children’s school fees had been paid through NELFUND without necessarily having access to the actual amount involved. Sawyerr said the initiative was intended to address concerns among parents who continued to shoulder the financial responsibilities of their children’s education despite the availability of government-backed loans. The development comes as the Federal Government intensifies efforts to expand access to tertiary education through the student loan programme, designed to ease financial barriers and prevent eligible students from being denied higher education because of their inability to pay institutional fees upfront. Under the arrangement, NELFUND provides loans for institutional charges, while upkeep allowances are processed separately to assist beneficiaries with their living expenses. However, the fund’s latest intervention suggests that ensuring students understand the payment process, alongside preventing potential abuse, has become a priority as the scheme expands. To address gaps in understanding and clarify the revised procedures, NELFUND will organise re-education workshops across the six geopolitical zones of the country. Sawyerr explained that the exercise would go beyond the fund’s routine public awareness campaigns, which primarily inform students about the availability of the loan scheme. According to him, the new engagements would focus on educating students, parents and tertiary institutions on how the payment system works and the changes introduced to improve its administration. “We can easily do a press release and say, ‘Hey, this is what we’re doing.’ But if we don’t educate the institutions, if we don’t educate the students, everybody will still be running behind,” he said. “This is not sensitisation. This is re-education of the stakeholders and the students as to the changes that we have made in their favour,” he added. The managing director said the workshops would help eliminate confusion. surrounding institutional payments, upkeep allowances and the documentation required by beneficiaries. He also indicated that journalists might be invited to some of the engagements to observe the exercise and help communicate the changes to a wider audience. Sawyerr urged the media to support the information campaign, noting that the regional workshops alone might not reach every student who needed clarification. Meanwhile, NELFUND’s Executive Director, Mustapha Iyal, provided further insight into the fund’s payment architecture, explaining that the system was designed to minimise intermediaries in the transfer of institutional fees. Iyal said the fund relied on students’ application identification numbers and wallet numbers for institutional payment processing rather than their conventional bank account numbers. “To be clear, we don’t use account numbers. We use their application ID and wallet number,” he said. He explained that institutional fees and upkeep allowances followed separate payment processes, with tuition payments handled through the fund’s institutional payment arrangement, while upkeep allowances were transferred to students’ personal bank accounts through external payment channels. According to him, NELFUND uses platforms such as NIBSS Instant Payments and Paystack to process upkeep payments because the fund is not a banking institution and cannot open bank accounts for beneficiaries. He said the involvement of external payment channels could sometimes lead to delays, depending on the financial institutions handling the transactions. Providing an update on the scale of the payment system, Iyal disclosed that the pilot phase covered about 400,000 students, with approximately 20,000 additional students recorded between the previous week and the week of the briefing. He added that the system processed transactions for nearly 5,000 students daily. “We are not talking about 20,000. No, we are talking about 400,000,” he said, emphasising the scale of the operation. Iyal further explained that the system employed a tokenised arrangement linked to each student’s application identification number, with a wallet attached to the application. He said the upkeep wallet operated separately from the mechanism used to process institutional payments, underscoring the distinction between money paid directly to schools and allowances transferred to students. The post NELFUND moves to stop students collecting loans while parents pay fees appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Tokayev Unveils $14 Billion Construction Plan in Kazakhstan State of the Nation Address
body: Kazakhstan plans to spend 6.5 trillion tenge (about $14.3 billion) from its National Fund on infrastructure projects by 2029 and eliminate its electricity shortage in the same period, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced in his annual State of the Nation Address on October 28. The president also outlined plans to accelerate nuclear power plant construction , expand transport routes between China and Europe, and establish a separate court for investors in the new city of Alatau. $14 Billion for Infrastructure Tokayev proposed declaring 2027 a year of large-scale construction and launching a nationwide program covering roads, airports, railway stations, and public facilities. The government is expected to allocate approximately 6.5 trillion tenge from the National Fund by the end of 2029, including 1.5 trillion tenge ($3.3 billion) for social projects in the remaining months of 2026 and the first two months of 2027. The program envisages building around 70 healthcare facilities and approximately 50 education, sports, and cultural facilities. Plans also include extending gas supplies and clean drinking water to underserved communities. Tokayev said public funding should help attract private investment rather than finance the entire program. The spending plans raise questions about the use of Kazakhstan’s accumulated oil revenues. The National Fund was established in part to protect the economy from fluctuations in commodity prices, but its resources are regularly used to meet budgetary needs. Tokayev said Kazakhstan must balance preserving financial reserves for future generations with investing in modern infrastructure. He argued that public spending should deliver economic and social returns. Kazakhstan Aims to Eliminate Electricity Deficit Tokayev acknowledged that Kazakhstan’s electricity production is insufficient to meet the needs of its growing economy, particularly as the country seeks to expand industry and build data centers . According to the national grid operator KEGOC , Kazakhstan generated 123.1 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity in 2025, while consuming 124.6 billion. The shortfall of approximately 1.5 billion kilowatt-hours was covered by net imports. The president set a target of achieving a sustained surplus of electricity production over domestic consumption by 2029. Tokayev criticized the longstanding practice of purchasing expensive electricity from neighboring countries during winter peaks in demand and subsequently returning electricity in summer at substantially lower prices. “That’s quite a simple little ‘business,’ and it’s been going on for decades,” Tokayev remarked. He also pointed to delays in bringing new generating capacity online in Turkestan, Kyzylorda, Almaty, and Ekibastuz, as well as a shortage of qualified energy specialists. To meet the 2029 target, Kazakhstan will need to build new power stations and modernize existing facilities. Tokayev called for further development of coal-fired generation alongside renewable energy, particularly solar power. Nuclear Power Plans Tokayev said construction of the Balkhash nuclear power plant could begin in 2027. He also proposed accelerating preparations for an agreement on the Moyynkum nuclear power plant. Russia’s state nuclear corporation Rosatom is leading the Balkhash project, while China National Nuclear Corporation has been selected as the main contractor for the second plant. However, the first reactor at Balkhash is not expected to begin operating until 2034, meaning Kazakhstan will have to address its immediate electricity shortage through other projects. Tokayev also proposed establishing a national strategic uranium reserve to ensure long-term supplies for the country’s planned nuclear power plants. “We need to start thinking now about how we will supply them with uranium, say, 50 years from now and beyond,” he said. Kazakhstan is the world’s largest producer of natural uranium , but its nuclear ambitions will also require foreign technology and trained specialists. Tokayev said Russian and Chinese companies had made proposals to establish manufacturing facilities and train Kazakh nuclear personnel. New Transport Routes Between China and Europe Tokayev also outlined plans to expand Kazakhstan’s role in transporting freight between China and Europe, including through the Trans-Caspian transport corridor , also known as the Middle Corridor, which diversifies freight links between Central Asia and Europe. The 272-kilometer Bakhty–Ayagoz railway in eastern Kazakhstan is scheduled to open in 2027. Construction began in December 2023, and the project includes a new border crossing with China at Bakhty–Tacheng. The line is expected to increase annual rail freight capacity between the two countries from approximately 28 million to 48 million metric tons. Another major project is the Aral–Caspian Highway , an approximately 800-kilometer road connecting Beineu in western Kazakhstan with Saksaulsk, near the Aral Sea. Construction began in August. Tokayev stated that the highway would shorten the overland freight route between China and Europe by approximately 1,000 kilometers and reduce delivery times by three days. These remain official projections, with the eventual savings dependent on the routes used by freight operators. “The vulnerability of maritime routes has increased the strategic importance of overland transport corridors. Kazakhstan must seize this historic opportunity to become a leading logistics hub in Eurasia in practice,” Tokayev said . He also called for the development of domestic logistics companies and new cargo handling facilities near major transport hubs, enabling Kazakhstan to earn more from the goods passing through its territory. A New Court for Investors in Alatau Tokayev also proposed establishing a separate judicial system in Alatau , a developing city near Almaty that already operates under a special legal regime intended to attract investment. Commercial disputes would be heard by an investment court modeled on English common law, while a separate civil court would deal with other matters arising under the city’s special legal arrangements. Kazakhstan already has an English common-law court at the Astana International Financial Centre (AIFC), which operates independently of the national judicial system. Alatau’s proposed courts would provide a similar framework specifically for businesses operating under the city’s legal regime. The government must submit amendments to the law governing Alatau to the Kurultai, Kazakhstan’s new unicameral parliament , by the end of January 2027. Tokayev also acknowledged shortcomings in government efforts to attract investment, saying that agencies lack coordination and investors do not receive sufficient support. He proposed giving the state-owned Baiterek holding company a greater role in coordinating investment projects. Higher Taxes for the Wealthy and a Minimum Wage Increase Another eye-catching element of the speech was Tokayev’s call for consideration of higher taxes on people with large fortunes, although he offered little on how this proposed system would work. Kurultai deputy Nikita Shatalov told journalists that discussions were focused on taxing high incomes rather than introducing a conventional luxury tax. The president also ordered an increase in the minimum monthly wage from 85,000 tenge ($185) to 110,000 tenge ($240), effective January 1, 2027. According to Tokayev, the measure will raise the incomes of approximately 1.8 million people. The program will test whether Kazakhstan can turn National Fund spending into lasting economic benefits without deepening its reliance on oil revenues to finance government expenditure.

title: ‘Taken Off the Street’: Russia’s Forced Mobilization Spreads to Siberia
body:
Omsk, one of Siberia’s three cities with more than 1 million residents, has emerged as a new hotspot for alleged forced mobilization, with residents accusing military recruiters of snatching men from the streets and forcing them to sign contracts to fight in Ukraine.
Residents have flooded the Sirius-55 military recruitment center’s page on 2GIS, a popular Russian mapping and business-directory app that allows users to post public reviews, with complaints, according to the Omsk Civic Association .
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“My father went out to the store and disappeared,” one user wrote. She said her 60-year-old father was quickly issued a second passport and taken to Yugra the following day. “There has been no word from him since.”
Another woman said her brother had traveled to Omsk with a work crew to earn money but disappeared. The recruitment center later called to tell her he had signed a military contract.
“They took him without documents or a phone,” she wrote.
Other reviewers alleged that recruiters ignored men’s age, medical conditions, and lack of identification documents. One woman, Natalia, accused staff of abducting men, beating them, and holding them illegally until they agreed to sign contracts.
Another user said two acquaintances had been taken from the street and denied contact with their families. Among those allegedly seized were sick men, people recovering from strokes, and individuals who had simply stepped out to buy groceries.
Two accounts described elderly men seized in the evening. In one case, relatives reportedly found a man beaten at the recruitment center and took him home.
The allegations could not be independently verified.
Reports of forced military recruitment have surged in September and October, both in number and geographical reach, lawyers told the independent Russian outlet Verstka .
Complaints have emerged from 33 Russian regions and occupied Crimea, Verstka reported, citing several human rights projects.
Police, members of Russia’s National Guard (Rosgvardiya), and military enlistment office staff are typically involved in the raids, according to the report.
Men are stopped on the streets, often under the pretext of minor offenses, and taken to enlistment offices or military units, where they are allegedly pressured through deception, coercion, or threats to sign contracts.
Some people who report to enlistment offices voluntarily after receiving summonses through the government services portal Gosuslugi have also allegedly been caught up in the practice.
During the spring and summer, such tactics were reported in several regions, particularly Penza Oblast. The alleged raids have since spread from the Republic of Karelia in northwestern Russia to Primorsky Krai in the Far East.
Moscow has also seen similar cases. In late October, men were reportedly targeted in street raids for both compulsory military service and contract recruitment, The Moscow Times reported on Tuesday, Oct. 27 .
The alleged raids in Omsk come amid a broader campaign to replenish Russian forces fighting in Ukraine, with independent Russian media reporting coercive recruitment, expanded eligibility for military service, and efforts to attract recruits from poorer regions.
In November 2025, the independent Russian news agency Important Stories (IS) reported that Russian recruiters were advertising military service to men with HIV, hepatitis, and tuberculosis in some regions, citing the independent outlets Important Stories and Liudi Baikala.
One recruiter reportedly told a journalist posing as a potential recruit that men with chronic illnesses faced a high likelihood of assignment to assault units.
Financial incentives have also come under pressure. According to IS, the enlistment bonuses have declined in several Russian regions, while Ukraine’s military intelligence agency (HUR) reported in October 2025 that recruitment offices in the Far Eastern Republic of Sakha (Yakutia) were falling short of Kremlin targets by around 40%.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Machar disputes Bol Mel’s claims over Nasir attack
body: Former South Sudan First Vice President Dr. Riek Machar on Wednesday denied ordering White Army leader Tor Gille Thoan to attack the military garrison in Nasir, Upper Nile State, in March 2025. Testifying during the 125th session of his trial, Machar, the fifth accused, disputed allegations he attributed to former Vice President Benjamin Bol Mel about his role in the violence. Machar said Bol Mel had claimed in a speech at the burial of Maj. Gen. David Majur Dak that Machar ordered Tor Gille Thoan to act after learning that boats transporting government troops could not reach Nasir. “I didn’t know the nature of those orders I gave to Tor. What I know is that barges were taking SSPDF soldiers to replace or relieve SSPDF soldiers in the Nasir garrison at Wec-Yar-Adiu,” Machar said. He said two committees comprising members from Nasir and Ulang had been formed to receive the soldiers and that the barges had not been attacked. “I told the two commissioners, the chiefs and youth leaders to tell the youths to go back to their villages in Nasir County on March 1, 2025,” he said. Machar said the young people left Nasir and Ulang that afternoon, adding that the two commissioners confirmed their departure to him the following day. He said he held a telephone conference with the commissioners, Upper Nile State Governor James Odhok and then Chief of Defence Forces Gen. Paul Nang Majok after gunboats could not proceed beyond Malual. “Since the barges could not move further than Malual, I proposed to Gen. Paul Nang Majok to hire six big boats to transport the SSPDF forces and their logistics to Wec-Yar-Adiu,” Machar said. He said Majok had agreed to pay $60,000 to hire the boats, as requested by their owners. “The commissioner of Ulang and the members of the committee had gone to where the gunboats got stuck. The commissioner met the first commander in the gunboat. The mission was called off without me being informed by Gen. Paul Nang Majok,” he said. Buffer zone Machar also rejected Bol Mel’s alleged claim that he had been asked to deploy Sudan People’s Liberation Army-in-Opposition (SPLA-IO) forces as a buffer between government troops and the White Army in Nasir. He said no such request had been made, pointing instead to clashes between South Sudan People’s Defence Forces (SSPDF) troops and local youth in Nasir in February 2024. According to Machar, SPLA-IO forces were deployed during those clashes to establish a buffer zone in Nasir town before withdrawing to their bases after relations between government forces and local youth improved. He also rejected allegations that he had refused to cooperate with the United Nations or misled the international body about the situation in Nasir. Machar said he had asked the UN to evacuate Gen. David Majur Dak and 26 soldiers from Nasir after young people captured Wec-Yar-Adiw. Peace agreement Machar also discussed the political tensions preceding the Nasir incident, including fighting between SPLA-IO and SSPDF forces in Western Bahr el Ghazal and Western Equatoria in January and February 2025. He said he initially viewed the fighting as a violation of the peace agreement but later concluded that the country was returning to war. He also linked the tensions to disagreements over the Tumaini Consensus, discussed during peace talks in Nairobi with opposition groups that had not signed the 2018 Revitalized Agreement on the Resolution of the Conflict in South Sudan (R-ARCSS). Machar argued that the proposed consensus risked undermining the 2018 peace agreement and South Sudan’s sovereignty. The court adjourned the session until Monday, November 2, 2026, when Machar is expected to continue his defence testimony. Charges and allegations Machar and seven co-defendants face charges including murder, conspiracy, terrorism, treason, destruction of public property and crimes against humanity. Machar is under house arrest, while the other defendants are being held at National Security Service facilities in Juba. The co-defendants are Puot Kang Chol, Mam Pal Dhuor, Gatwech Lam Puoch, Lt. Gen. Gabriel Duop Lam, Camilo Gatmai Kel, Mading Yak Riek and Dominic Gatgok Riek. Prosecutors allege that SPLA-IO forces allied with the White Army killed 257 SSPDF soldiers, including commander Gen. David Majur Dak, and destroyed or captured military equipment worth about $58 million during the March 2025 attack on the Nasir military garrison. The post Machar disputes Bol Mel’s claims over Nasir attack appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Ghana urged to adopt year-round tourism programme to attract more visitors
body: The Executive Director of the Ghana–New Zealand Chamber of Commerce, Mr Isaac Koumessina, has urged Ghana to adopt a year-round tourism programme similar to New Zealand’s to attract more international visitors and boost economic activity. He said Ghana’s tourism activities were often organised by different groups at different times, without sufficient coordination among the agencies responsible for promoting the sector. Speaking on the sidelines of the recently concluded 2026 Inter Tourism Expo in Cape Coast, Mr Koumessina said a coordinated approach involving the Ministry of Tourism, the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA) and other relevant agencies could ensure that visitors have activities to engage in throughout the year. “New Zealand always has a year-long tourism event going on. Every day there is something going on in the industry of tourism,” he said. “Ghana is limited. It’s either a group is organising something today, another group the next day, so there is no inter-agency related event such as tourism going on in Ghana,” he added. Mr Kumesina said Ghana could learn from New Zealand by developing a unified calendar of tourism events that would give visitors more reasons to explore the country, regardless of when they arrive. “What we’re looking at Ghana to learn from New Zealand is inter-agency linkage with tourism, with the Ministry of Tourism, the GTA, other tourism agencies coming together to organise a year-long event,” he said. He explained that such coordination would help ensure that whenever investors or tourists visit Ghana, there are activities and attractions available to showcase the country’s tourism potential. Mr Kumesina also highlighted the need to improve engagement with visitors after their trips, citing the potential to encourage repeat visits through targeted promotions and follow-up communication. Reflecting on the Year of Return initiative, he questioned whether Ghana had adequate data on visitors and effective systems for maintaining contact with them to promote future tourism activities. He said tourism also presented opportunities to address youth unemployment, urging the Youth Employment Agency to collaborate with tourism authorities to train young people as tour guides and equip them with skills to promote Ghana’s attractions through digital platforms. Mr Kumesina said sustained tourism activities and stronger institutional collaboration could help expand business opportunities and create jobs across different sectors of the economy.

title: Spot gas price in Europe surpasses $1,150 per 1,000 cubic meters first since December 2022
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. The spot price of gas on the exchange in Europe surpassed $1,150 per 1,000 cubic meters during Wednesday trading for the first time since December 2022, according to TASS calculations based on data from major trading hubs in Europe.
Specifically, day-ahead prices at the TTF hub reached $1,160 per 1,000 cubic meters, or 100.85 euros per MWh. Prices also surpassed the 100 euro per MWh mark for the first time in four years.
The price of November futures contracts at the TTF hub in the Netherlands has risen to around $1,142 per 1,000 cubic meters, or 99.25 euro per MWh, according to data from London's ICE exchange.

title: Religious, Media Leaders Mobilise Against Disinformation Ahead of 2027 Polls
body: Yemi Kosoko in Jos Religious leaders and media stakeholders have been urged to intensify efforts to combat misinformation, disinformation and Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI) in order to prevent religious tensions, communal crises and electoral violence ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 general election. The call was made at a two-day workshop organised by Alkalanci, a fact-checking and media literacy organisation, in collaboration with the Institute for Media and Digital Innovation (IMDIL), in Jos, Plateau State. The workshop, themed ‘Scaling Faith-Based Resilience Against Disinformation and FIMI,’ brought together Christian and Muslim leaders to build their capacity to identify false information, promote responsible communication and strengthen community resilience against information threats. Speaking at the opening session, Editor of Alkalanci, Alhassan Bala, warned that the proliferation of false information posed a serious threat to Nigeria’s security, social cohesion and democratic processes. He noted that the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) to create deceptive images, videos and audio recordings had made it increasingly difficult for citizens to distinguish authentic content from fabricated material. According to him, malicious actors could exploit such technologies to inflame religious and communal tensions, provoke violence and undermine public trust, particularly as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 elections. Bala urged religious leaders to exercise caution and verify information before sharing it with members of their congregations, stressing that responsible communication remains critical to safeguarding peace. “When in doubt, do not share,” he said, emphasising the need for verification before circulating information capable of misleading the public. Also speaking, Cyber and Hybrid Threats Programme Lead at the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office’s Integrated Security Fund (FCDO-ISF) West Africa, Oriola Odetoye, reaffirmed the United Kingdom’s commitment to supporting Nigeria in addressing foreign information manipulation and other hybrid threats. He explained that the intervention, implemented under the UK-Nigeria Security and Defence Partnership, is designed to strengthen Nigeria’s capacity to detect, respond to and counter information manipulation campaigns that could threaten national stability. Odetoye described religious and community leaders as critical stakeholders because of their influence in shaping public opinion and either preventing or escalating tensions within their communities. He disclosed that the programme would be expanded to Plateau, Kano, Adamawa and Benue States to complement ongoing federal-level efforts aimed at promoting peace and countering information-related security threats. Representing the Jama’atu Nasril Islam (JNI), Haruna Tanko cautioned against the deliberate spread of false information for political, religious or personal gain. He warned that misinformation could create unnecessary fear, deepen divisions and trigger avoidable crises, especially during election periods. Tanko called on both Muslims and Christians to uphold the values of truthfulness, peace and responsible communication while also advocating accountable leadership and improved governance. Similarly, Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), Plateau State Chapter, Rev. Dunka Gomwalk, urged religious leaders to strengthen interfaith dialogue and encourage their followers to verify information before sharing it. He warned that unverified social media posts and impulsive public comments could fuel religious tensions and undermine ongoing peacebuilding efforts. Gomwalk expressed optimism that the workshop would produce practical strategies and collaborative approaches through which faith communities could promote mutual coexistence. Kalanci’s Programme Manager, Bamas Victoria, highlighted the organisation’s ongoing efforts to strengthen community resilience through fact-checking training, media literacy initiatives and public awareness campaigns. She explained that the programme equips religious leaders, educators and other stakeholders with practical skills to recognise information manipulation, verify follow-up training sessions conducted in different locations have enabled participants to transfer knowledge to their communities, thereby expanding the reach of counter-disinformation efforts. She expressed confidence in sustained collaboration among religious leaders, civil platforms, and techniques for identifying propaganda and manipulative narratives. Organisers said the initiative aims to empower faith leaders to become stronger advocates for truth, peace and responsible information sharing as Nigeria prepares for another electoral cycle in 2027.

title: What are the main Palestinian Israeli parties and why are they doing so well?
body: With most votes counted in Israel's general election , one of the most striking stories is how well Israeli Arab parties have performed at the polls. As it stands, the Arab Joint List, which includes Hadash, Balad and Ta'al, alongside the Ra'am party led by Mansour Abbas, have won a record 18 of the Knesset's 120 seats. A government needs 61 seats for a majority. With a tight race between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party and his rival Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party, government formation cannot happen without a coalition. So which are the Palestinian Israeli parties and how did they influence the results? Arab Joint List The Arab Joint List is made up of three parties: Hadash, Ta'al and Balad. Hadash is a left-wing party, comprising Arab and Jewish Israelis , headed by Yousef Jabareen. Mr Jabareen is a lawyer who regularly goes to the Supreme Court with motions to defend Palestinian rights. He was first elected to the Knesset in 2015 and is also the head of the Arab Joint List. Hadash's other significant members include MP Ofer Cassif , a vocal critic of Mr Netanyahu and his war on Gaza, which he calls a genocide. Ta'al is an anti-Zionist, nationalist Arab Israeli party led by Ahmad Tibi. It is considered a secular movement that supports a two-state solution and an Israeli troop withdrawal. Mr Tibi, who has been in the Knesset since 1999, is from the mainly Arab city of Taibeh and was an adviser to late Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat, as well as a mediator between Israeli and the Palestine Liberation Organisation. His involvement in Israeli politics has been significant, including a spell as deputy speaker of the Knesset between 2006 and 2013. Balad, a left-wing secular party led by Sami Abu Shehadeh , is also in the alliance. Mr Abu Shehadeh was disqualified from running in the elections by Israel's Supreme Court, which upheld a decision by the Central Elections Committee earlier this month. The ban on Mr Abu Shehadeh's candidacy was linked to alleged extreme views and incitement of hatred against Israel. Balad, formed in 1996, is seen by Israeli commentators as far-left and the most extreme anti-Zionist party of the three. It believes Israel should not be an independent state, instead supporting a one-state solution. Ra'am, which used to be part of the Arab Joint List, is a religious Muslim party running separately and was on course for four seats. Its leader Mr Abbas, a dentist by profession, made history in 2021 as the first Palestinian-Israeli to become a minister in a government coalition. Unpopular among Palestinians in the occupied West Bank, Mr Abbas is seen by many as a "traitor" and a "normaliser" with Israel, focusing on local issues rather than the wider Palestinian cause. Why did the Arab parties do so well? Palestinian-Israelis are already celebrating their gains at the polls, with a large Arab voter turnout seen as having largely contributed. But why did Arab-Israeli voters decide to vote in elections that they had previously been known to boycott? Xavier Abu Eid, a political scientist and former PLO official, told The National this time was different. "For Palestinian citizens, it's an existential matter. Keeping the far-right in the government is being seen as keeping the prospects for a new Nakba," he said. Videos circulated in Arab communities, showing the elderly urging young people to vote. Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank asked those in Israel to try to make a difference. Violence against Palestinians and Israeli-Arabs has surged since the Hamas attacks and subsequent Israeli war on Gaza beginning in October 2023. "The amount of incitement against Palestinians went up, persecution against students and professors, doctors and nurses in Israel also went up, so the way they've been living in the past three years, shows that the only thing the government wants them to do is leave the country," Mr Abu Eid said. Many Palestinian Israelis see themselves as the likely next targets after attacks on Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank. Although the two main election rivals, Mr Netanyahu and Mr Eisenkot, are unlikely to enter a formal coalition with Arab parties - a development that would result in another election - analysts say that the Arab turnout has still been significant. "The Arabs are not going to be kingmakers, but they still have a huge achievement," said Danny Citrinowitz, a senior fellow at the Institute for National Security Studies. He believes that, with the feat of snapping up about 18 seats in the Knesset, Arab voters have reduced Mr Netanyahu's chances of forming a majority government. This could force Mr Netanyahu into a unity government, which would include members of the opposition, potentially pushing extreme figures such as Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich out of a future cabinet. "Not the outcome they [Arab voters] hoped for but their turnout prevented Netanyahu from having 61 seats. They prevented him from having a path unless it's a unity government," Mr Citrinowitz said. If the results of 18 seats of the Knesset's 120 seats for Arab politicians are final, representing 15 per cent of the total number of seats, the ratio of Arabs in the Knesset will be more reflective of the community's representation in Israeli society, which stands at 20 per cent. This would also break the current record of 15 seats for Arab parties in the Knesset, set during the 2020 elections.

title: Alex Eala advances to Toray Pan Pacific quarterfinals after besting Talia Gibson
body: MANILA, Philippines – Alex Eala pulled off a thrilling win over Australia’s Talia Gibson, 4-6, 6-2, 6-0, in the Toray Pan Pacific Open round of 16 match in Tokyo, Japan, on Wednesday, October 28. Eala had gotten off to a rough start after losing the first set to her World No. 38 opponent, 4-6. It had been smooth sailing in the succeeding sets, 6-2, 6-0, as she was able to contain Gibson by a large margin. “I think really staying in the match [and] never giving up,” Eala explained in a post-game interview when asked what the key to her victory was. “The first set was difficult, and I had my chances, so I knew that if I kept my concentration I would have more chances.” This is not the first time the two players went head-to-head. Eala and Gibson had previously played against each other at the IXXVII Open Generali Ciudad de Palma del Rio round of 16 in June 2023, and then in the ITF W25 Aldershot GB Pro Series round of 16 in August 2023. The Filipina won both matches. The Filipina tennis star will now face Diana Shnaider of Russia in the quarterfinals on Friday, October 30. Just before Eala made her Toray Pan Pacific Open debut, she had suffered a second-round exit at the hands of Shnaider at the Ningbo Open in China on October 22. – Rappler.com

title: 22 Financial institutions yet to begin data localisation — NITDA survey
body: By Juliet Umeh Twenty-two of 44 financial institutions surveyed are yet to begin implementing measures to comply with Nigeria’s data localisation requirements, with the January 1, 2027 deadline approaching. The findings were presented by Dr Muhammad Aminu Lawal, Special Assistant on Digital Transformation to the Director-General of the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA), Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi, at the Executive Regulatory Dialogue on National Cloud and Software Infrastructure (NSCI) Implementation and Data Localisation in Lagos. The dialogue, convened by NITDA and the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), brought together regulators, financial sector executives, banks, fintech operators and technology service providers. According to the survey, 26 institutions, representing 59 per cent of respondents, had completed the required actions or expected to complete them by the deadline. Fifteen said they were unlikely or very unlikely to finish on time, while three could not assess their readiness. The presentation summarised the findings by stating that “half are still planning; 22 of 44 have not started implementing.” It classified 59 per cent of the institutions as “on track” and 34 per cent as “at risk”. However, the presentation clarified that the responses were self-reported, anonymised and aggregated, stressing that they did not constitute a formal compliance assessment. The survey also showed that institutions had made more progress in identifying the data and systems covered by the requirements than in securing funding, engaging local providers or migrating systems. While 70 per cent had identified data or systems within the scope of the requirements, 52 per cent had mapped their hosting and administration arrangements. In contrast, only 25 per cent had secured board or executive approval and a budget, 23 per cent had contracted local providers, while 18 per cent had begun migration or remediation. “Mapping is done; budgets, contracts and migration lag,” Lawal said. Uncertainty surrounding the requirements was also identified as a major obstacle to implementation. The survey found that 64 per cent of institutions wanted a definition of “payment transaction data”, while 38 per cent sought clarification on what it means for data to be “stored and managed in Nigeria”. Twenty-nine institutions said they depended on further clarification to proceed with their preparations. The presentation identified a written clarification on the scope of the requirements as a priority, alongside clearer transition milestones, an exceptions process and guidance on existing contracts. It further showed that half of the institutions were proceeding on working assumptions while awaiting clarification, while 16 per cent said material work had been put on hold. Summarising the findings, the presentation said compliance was “within reach for about six in 10, not yet for the rest”, adding that “clarity is the critical path” for institutions preparing for the January 2027 deadline. The post 22 Financial institutions yet to begin data localisation — NITDA survey appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Court dismisses Nollywood actor’s N10bn damages suit against Wike’s aide, INEC
body:
The Federal High Court in Abuja on Wednesday dismissed a N10 billion rights suit filed by the Nollywood actor, Emeka Ike, against Lere Olayinka, spokesperson for FCT Minister Nyesom Wike, and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).
Judge Salim Ibrahim, in a judgement, upheld the preliminary objections of the respondents on the grounds that the suit was incompetent and improperly constituted.
Mr Ibrahim also held that suit lacked proof for its claims.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Mr Ike, who aspired to vie for the House of Representatives’ seat for AMAC/Bwari Federal Constituency, Abuja, for the 2027 general elections on the platform of Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), lost the bid in a primary poll.
Mr Olayinka, the FCT minister’s aide, through a post on X in May, allegedly mocked Mr Ike and leaked his confidential voter registration details on social media, in the aftermath of the actor’s loss.
The post allegedly showed details of Mr Ike’s voter registration transfer from Imo State to the nation’s capital.
Meanwhile, Mr Ike, through his lawyer L. T. Adeh sued Mr Olayinka and INEC in the suit marked: FHC/ABJ/CS/1272/2026.
He asked the court to declare that Mr Olayinka’s decision to publish his database on X without his approval “amounts to gross breach and violation of the applicant’s fundamental right to privacy and the protection of personal data.”
Mr Ike argued that Section 37 of the Nigerian constitution, Article 12 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, and Sections 24 & 39 of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 guaranteed his right to privacy and protection of personal data.
The actor asked the court to declare that INEC owed him and other voters a “statutory duty of care” to protect their private data against unauthorised access.
The applicant, therefore, prayed the court to award him N10 billion against Mr Olayinka and INEC as aggravated and general damages, to be paid jointly and severally for violating his fundamental right to privacy.
He sought a declaration that the press release by INEC dated 2 June, in reaction to the viral publication and circulation of his personal voter information and private data on social media by Mr Olayinka, amounted to a tacit admission of guilt and liability to him.
Mr Ike also sought an order directing Mr Olayinka to immediately retract and pull down the offensive post and publication on his social media X handle, @OlayinkaLere, containing screenshots of his personal voter information and private data.
He sought an order directing him to immediately tender an unreserved apology in writing for breach and violation of his fundamental right.
But responding in separate counter-affidavits, INEC and Mr Olayinka urged the court to dismiss the suit.
INEC stated that the subject of the post complained about by Mr Ike in the suit was neither classified, sensitive nor confidential information.
In the counter-affidavit sworn by Anthonia Makwe, an Assistant Director/Data Protection Officer in the Legal Drafting and Clearance Department, said that such information is displayed and published in accordance with the Electoral Act, 2026.
It stressed that the electoral body had the “statutorily and constitutional power to make available information of its voters to the general public without the consent of any registered voter.”
It said its statutory responsibility included the compilation, maintenance, display, publication, certification and management of the register of voters in accordance with the constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), the Electoral Act 2026, and the National Data Protection Act 2023.
It said what was alleged to be posted by Mr Olayinka on his X handle did not emanate from the commission.
“The 2nd respondent, as a data controller, has never breached its statutory duty of care, custody and protection of personal voter information and data, it owes the applicant and other Voters under its secured portal and restricted database, ” the commission also stated.
On his part, Mr Olayinka stated in his counter-affidavit he personally swore, Mr Ike’s suit was brought in bad faith.
He said the only information contained in the document he published was Mr Ike’s name and passport photograph, and that the information was already in the public domain.
He said contrary to Mr Ike’s claims, the information he published was not only in the public domain, it was also not accessed through any unlawful means.
Mr Olayinka stated that he did not owe the actor any duty of care and confidentiality and did not require his consent to publish his name and passport photograph that was already in the public domain.
He said Mr Ike, who brought himself to contest election into the House of Representatives, cannot be traumatised by the circulation of his name and passport photograph which he personally presented to the public when seeking to contest election, and as a Nollywood star.
He argued that information supplied in voter cards is not private data because by the provision of Section 19(1) of the Electoral Act, 2026, INEC is mandated to publish such information, not later than 90 days to the general elections.
He said contrary to Mr Ike’s deposition, the only information contained in the document published by him was his name and passport photograph.
He said the publication was done when Mr Ike led a team of hoodlums to INEC office to disrupt INEC’s activities immediately he declared his intention to contest the election.
According to him, the publication was to remind him of the recent change of his voter registration area.
He said it was to also draw the public’s attention to the statutory provision to avoid any breach of the law.
He said contrary to Mr Ike’s submission, the applicant who submitted his personal data and information to INEC and to the general public when he decided to contest could not feel unsafe and traumatised by the publication of his name and passport photograph.
Mr Olayinka said contrary to Mr Ike’s claim, INEC admitted in its press release that “there was no external breach of its CVR database, no hacking incident and no unauthorised external access to the commission’s ICT infrastructure.”
He argued that the purported injury suffered by Mr Ike was not caused by him who is not a data controller under the Nigerian Data Protection Act, 2023, and who does not owe him any obligation to safeguard his documents.
Mr Olayinka stated that the prayers in the suit, including N10 billion in damages, was in bad faith and “an indication that the applicant is a gold digger, who wants to reap where he did not sow.”
He insisted that he cannot pay damages for information that was already publicly accessible at the time of the publication.
He, therefore, urged the court to dismiss the suit in the interest of justice.

title: Rosatom to deal with nuclear energy sector development in Togo
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. The Russian state nuclear corporation Rosatom and the Ministry of Energy of Togo have signed a memorandum of cooperation in the field of the peaceful use of atomic energy on the sidelines of the Russia-Africa Summit.
"The signing of the memorandum opens a new chapter in Rosatom's relations with the Togolese Republic and lays the foundation for joint work across a wide spectrum of peaceful nuclear technologies. We are ready to offer our partners solutions in the fields of energy, healthcare, and agriculture. We will also facilitate professional training and nuclear infrastructure development. One of the promising areas of cooperation is the use of floating nuclear power units for reliable, low-carbon energy supply. For Togo, nuclear technologies can become a powerful driver of socioeconomic development and improve the people's quality of life," Rosatom CEO Alexey Likhachev said in a comment.
The memorandum provides for the creation of specialized working groups that will assess the potential for implementing practical projects in nuclear power and non-energy applications of nuclear technologies. The working groups will also determine the concrete steps of the parties toward human resource development in the peaceful atom sector and the promotion of a positive public attitude toward nuclear energy in Togo.

title: Zelenskyy visits Netherlands on Wednesday, government to allocate €1.2B in aid to Ukraine over three years – media
body:
President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy is visiting the Netherlands on Wednesday, where he will hold meetings with Prime Minister Rob Jetten and King Willem-Alexander, while the country's government will announce the allocation of €1.2 billion in non-military aid to Ukraine over the next three years, Dutch media report.
According to NOS, Prime Minister Jetten will receive Zelenskyy in the afternoon at Catshuis in The Hague. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defense Dilan Yeşilgöz and Minister of Foreign Affairs Tom Berendsen will also join the negotiations. Following the meeting, the Ukrainian president will speak with representatives of the Dutch and Ukrainian business communities, and in the early evening, he will have an audience with King Willem-Alexander at Huis ten Bosch Palace.
As BNR News notes, this is Zelenskyy's first visit to Catshuis under Jetten's premiership. The President of Ukraine last visited the Netherlands in December of last year, when the government was headed by Dick Schoof. In April, Zelenskyy and Jetten met in Middelburg, where the Ukrainian president was presented with the Four Freedoms Award.
"President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy is visiting the Netherlands today... The visit takes place on the day the government allocates new funds for the reconstruction of Ukraine. Over the next three years, the government will spend 1.2 billion euros on non-military aid to Ukraine," the outlet's report on Wednesday states.
The Dutch government stated that the aid package aims to meet Ukraine's most urgent needs, facilitate its recovery and reconstruction, and expand opportunities for Dutch companies. The main focus will be placed on supporting energy and water supply and developing business cooperation.
The largest share of specifically designated aid areas will be channeled toward energy support and involving Dutch business in Ukraine's reconstruction: €40 million is earmarked for the emergency repair of energy infrastructure, another €55 million for supplying energy equipment, €136 million to support partnerships with Ukrainian companies, and an additional €19.5 million for export credit insurance to reduce financial risks for Dutch enterprises operating with Ukraine.
"In addition, Minister Sjoerdsma and Ukrainian Minister of Economy Kravchenko will sign a letter of intent to contribute to President Zelensky's Industrial Ramstein Initiative worth €10 million. This initiative aims to restore and modernize the production capacity of Ukrainian companies, through the supply of (Dutch) machinery, equipment and other goods," emphasized the statement released on the website of the Dutch government on Wednesday.
The Netherlands will also continue supporting humanitarian projects, demining, the search for abducted Ukrainian children, and the restoration of cultural heritage. The package provides for the continuation of previously announced non-military aid commitments to Ukraine amounting to €878 million plus an additional €327 million, with a significant portion of the funds to be channeled through international financial institutions.
"Support for recovery and reconstruction cannot wait until a ceasefire. Ukraine needs us now. Militarily, but also socially and economically. No matter how well you do on the battlefield, energy systems, hospitals and food production must also keep running. Governments cannot do this alone, the role of companies is crucial in this," emphasized Minister for Foreign Trade and Development Cooperation Sjoerd Sjoerdsma.

title: Barcelona fined €602 over approach for Atlético Madrid’s Álvarez
body: Barcelona have been fined €602 by the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) following a complaint by Atlético Madrid over the Catalan club’s approach for Argentine striker Julián Álvarez. The sanction followed Atlético’s allegation that Barcelona contacted the forward, who remains under contract with the Madrid club until June 2030, without first notifying them in writing of their intention to negotiate a transfer. According to Reuters, the RFEF imposed the fine under Article 133 of its regulations, which covers minor breaches of regulatory obligations. Atlético had lodged complaints with both the Spanish federation and FIFA over Barcelona’s alleged approach. However, FIFA declined to consider the case, stating that it lacked jurisdiction. The disciplinary proceedings established that a conversation took place between Álvarez’s agent, Fernando Hidalgo, and Barcelona sporting director Deco on May 15, 2026, before Atlético received written communication on May 28. During the conversation, Hidalgo reportedly told Deco that Atlético would consider offers for the striker and indicated that he had permission to discuss a potential departure. However, the disciplinary committee said it could not establish that Atlético had authorised the agent to negotiate the player’s exit. The federation ultimately classified Barcelona’s conduct as a minor infringement rather than a serious offence, resulting in the €602 penalty. The club can appeal the decision. Álvarez’s potential move to Barcelona generated considerable tension between the two Spanish clubs during the summer transfer window after the Argentine expressed his desire to play for the Catalan side. The 26-year-old, who joined Atlético from Manchester City in 2024, has a contract running until 2030 and a reported release clause of €500m. His comments about wanting to fulfil his ambition of playing for Barcelona angered sections of Atlético’s supporters, who frequently booed him during matches this season. However, the striker recently sought to repair his relationship with the club’s fans after scoring the winning goal against Deportivo La Coruña on Saturday, his second consecutive match with a goal. Following the victory, Álvarez acknowledged that his earlier comments had upset supporters. “It was a mistake. I understand why the fans are angry. If I were a fan, I’d be angry too. Especially given how they’ve supported me since I arrived,” he said. The victory moved Atlético to within two points of LaLiga leaders Barcelona, while the reception Álvarez received after scoring suggested that relations with sections of the club’s supporters could be improving. Despite the controversy surrounding his future, Álvarez remains an Atlético player, with Barcelona’s pursuit ending in a financial penalty rather than a transfer. The post Barcelona fined €602 over approach for Atlético Madrid’s Álvarez appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Russian marketplace Ozon estimates losses from drone attacks on warehouses at over 30 billion rubles
body:
According to Ukrinform, Radio Liberty reported this, citing the marketplace’s financial statements.
The reported amount includes “Damage to goods held for sale, losses associated with the disposal and impairment of equipment, as well as other losses and expenses.”
Since August, 11 of the company’s warehouses have come under attack.
Ozon added that some of the risks associated with goods and other assets stored at the affected facilities were insured. The company is negotiating compensation for the losses with insurance companies.
However, the report noted that any insurance payouts, if received, may fall far short of the losses incurred.
Meanwhile, Ozon reported a net profit of 3.7 billion rubles for the July–September period, up 25% from the same period in 2025, according to the report.
Ozon previously announced that, effective October 13, it would discontinue insurance coverage for goods against large-scale damage, including damage caused by drone attacks. The program, provided to Ozon sellers by Ingosstrakh, was being discontinued because “conditions for covering certain risks in the insurance market have changed significantly,” the company said.
As previously reported, Russian marketplace Ozon offered sellers the option of storing their goods at its warehouses in Almaty and Astana, Kazakhstan.

title: Iran Says Samarkand Heritage Posts Targeted U.S.
body: Iran has said that posts by its embassies about Samarkand’s Persian heritage were directed at the United States. The explanation followed a diplomatic protest from Uzbekistan, which demanded the removal of posts describing the city’s architecture as part of Persian civilization. Esmaeil Baghaei, spokesperson for Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said on October 26 that Tehran attaches great importance to its relations with Uzbekistan and views their shared cultural heritage as a foundation of friendship between the two countries. “Some of our colleagues at certain embassies published their messages as an address to the American side,” Baghaei explained. In the reported remarks , Baghaei did not specifically address the architectural claims made in the embassy posts. The dispute followed U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s visit to Samarkand on October 19. Accompanied by Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of Uzbekistan’s Presidential Administration, he visited Registan Square , one of Central Asia’s best-known landmarks. Rubio spoke about Samarkand’s historical role in international trade and the region’s importance to relations with Washington. The posts appeared to be a response to a speech Rubio gave in Athens on October 7, in which he recalled the Persian destruction of the Acropolis in 480 BC and sharply criticized Iran’s current leadership. Following Rubio’s visit to Samarkand, Iranian embassies in several countries posted photographs and videos on X showing him in front of the city’s historic monuments, arguing that he was surrounded by the Persian cultural heritage he had attacked earlier that month. Iran’s embassy in Armenia wrote that the site visited by the U.S. secretary of state was part of Persian civilization and architecture . The Iranian diplomatic mission in Zimbabwe described Registan’s arches as a characteristic feature of Iranian-Islamic civilization. On October 23, Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs summoned Iranian Ambassador Mohammad Ali Eskandari and delivered a diplomatic note of protest. Tashkent regarded the posts as one-sided and politicized , saying the heritage of Samarkand and other historic Uzbek cities reflected centuries of cultural development and formed part of Uzbekistan’s history. By October 26, Iranian embassies in Armenia, Bulgaria, Zimbabwe, Finland, and China had removed the posts , according to Uzbek Foreign Ministry spokesperson Omonulla Fayziev. The dispute touched on the sensitive issue of competing claims to Central Asia’s cultural heritage. Samarkand was one of the centers of ancient Sogdiana and later belonged to states ruled by different dynasties. Persian language and culture played an important role in the city’s life for centuries. Samarkand also remains home to a substantial Tajik population, and Tajik, a variety of Persian , is still widely spoken, particularly in the historic center. The monuments around Registan Square, built between the 15th and 17th centuries , reflect the city’s history under different rulers and the influence of several cultural traditions. Since Uzbekistan’s independence in 1991, they have also become national symbols.

title: Putin says number of African students in Russia has increased 1.5-fold since 2020
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. The number of African students in Russia has risen by 50% since 2020, while the number of Russian scholarships for African students has nearly tripled, Russian President Vladimir Putin said.
"Education has traditionally been a key area of Russian-African partnership. Moreover, our cooperation in this area is developing through new technologies and improvements in quality," Putin said at the Russia-Africa summit.
"African student numbers in Russia have grown by 50% since 2020, while Russian government scholarships for African countries have nearly tripled. Russian universities now host a record 40,000 students from African countries. Russia has raised its scholarship quota to 5,500 places for the 2026-2027 academic year," he added.

title: Asenso-Boakye commends new TESCON coordinator over digital membership platform
body: Former Roads and Highways Minister Francis Asenso-Boakye has commended the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) newly appointed National TESCON Coordinator, Ebenezer Kojo Amoah, for introducing a digital application to connect members and alumni of the organisation nationwide. The application was presented to the Bantama MP during a courtesy visit by the NPP National Youth Organiser, Abanga Fuseni, and the newly appointed national TESCON leadership. The platform is designed to create a centralised database of TESCON members and alumni across the country, with the aim of improving communication, coordination and networking within the organisation. Mr Asenso-Boakye, TESCON’s founding president, expressed satisfaction with the initiative, particularly because it had been introduced within a relatively short period after Mr Amoah assumed office. He described the application as an encouraging demonstration of the innovation needed to reposition TESCON and strengthen its operations in an increasingly digital political environment. Mr Asenso-Boakye noted that TESCON had grown from just three universities at its inception about 26 years ago to more than 250 tertiary institutions nationwide, making modern systems for managing membership records and maintaining links with alumni increasingly important.

title: Russian doctors ready to keep helping Africa fight cholera and Ebola — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Russian doctors are ready to continue helping African countries in their fight against dangerous infections, including cholera and a new strain of the Ebola virus, President Vladimir Putin said at the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.
"A specialized program of assistance to African countries implemented by [Russia’s sanitary watchdog] Rospotrebnadzor is aimed at strengthening the Russian-African partnership in sanitary and epidemiological welfare and the fight against infectious diseases. For example, 15 mobile anti-epidemic laboratories were transferred to eight states, and about 450 specialized African specialists were trained thanks to it," the president said. "Since the program is effective, the Russian side decided to extend it until 2029. I would like to note that Russian doctors provided and continue to selflessly assist Africans in combating a variety of dangerous infections, including cholera and an outbreak of a new strain of Ebola in the spring."
Putin said that Russia is ready, as before, to help the continent in dealing with the consequences of emergencies, jointly promote a balanced agenda in the field of the environment and adaptation to climate change, and to strengthen sports ties, preventing the politicization of sports.
"We will continue to provide health protection assistance, localize the synthesis of Russian effective medicines and vaccines, create laboratories and diagnostic centers, implement and adapt digital medicine platforms to local specifics," he said.

title: More than 40 African nations receiving Russian fertilizers, grain — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. More than forty African countries are already receiving fertilizers and grain from Russia, President Vladimir Putin said at the Russia-Africa economic and humanitarian forum.
"I would like to note that Russia is one of the most reliable food security guarantors in the African continent. More than forty African nations are already receiving Russian fertilizers and grain," Putin said.
Russia is "ready to further expand the geography of supplies" of agricultural commodities to the African continent, the head of state added.

title: MASLOC disburses GH¢4m to about 200 market traders in Kumasi
body: More than 200 market women in Kumasi have received government support through the Microfinance and Small Loans Centre (MASLOC) to expand their businesses and create employment opportunities. The beneficiaries, who trade at major markets including Bantama, Kejetia, Kumasi Central Market and Racecourse, have pledged to repay the loans on schedule to enable other traders to benefit from the scheme. Speaking to Adom News, the Deputy Director in charge of Operations at MASLOC, Vivian Owusu Asante, disclosed that the centre had disbursed an initial tranche of GH¢4 million to about 200 traders in Kumasi. She stressed that the loans were provided without political considerations, insisting that MASLOC was established to support eligible Ghanaians who need financial assistance to grow their businesses. “We did not consider political affiliation before giving out the loans. MASLOC is a government institution established to support Ghanaians. Those who applied and qualified have received their loans, and we are still processing applications from others. Claims that MASLOC operates on political considerations are untrue,” she said. Madam Owusu Asante identified the low loan recovery rate under the previous administration as one of the major challenges confronting the centre, adding that efforts were underway to recover outstanding loans. “A lot of people took MASLOC loans but failed to repay them. We are working to recover the outstanding amounts. I am therefore urging all market women who have received the loans to repay them on schedule to enable other traders to benefit and expand their businesses,” she advised. The MASLOC team toured the various markets to present cheques to beneficiaries whose loan applications had been approved. Some of the beneficiaries who spoke to Adom News expressed gratitude to MASLOC, describing the loans as timely support that would help them strengthen their businesses. They also commended the centre for what they described as flexible loan terms and conditions, urging other traders to take advantage of the scheme. “Honestly, we thought the loans would not come because some of us support the NPP. Some of our friends suggested that people who did not belong to the party would not be prioritised. However, that has not been the case, and we have received our loans. Each of us received GH¢20,000,” a beneficiary said. The traders have assured MASLOC of their commitment to repaying the loans within the agreed period, expressing confidence that the financial support would help them expand their businesses and improve their livelihoods.

title: Action plan to be adopted following Russia-Africa summit — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. The Russia - Africa Partnership Forum Action Plan for 2027-2029 will be adopted following the Russia-Africa summit on October 29, Russian President Vladimir Putin said.
"Tomorrow, following the summit, the leaders intend to adopt the Russia - Africa Partnership Forum Action Plan for 2027-2029. This framework document will outline the primary direction for further comprehensive cooperation between Russia and African countries," he said at the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.
The implementation of the document will help further boost Russian-African ties, fostering the development of all countries "in the interest of well-being and prosperity of their peoples," Putin noted.
TASS is an information partner of the third Russia-Africa Summit and Economic and Humanitarian Forum.

title: US moves Patriot missile defense system from Texas to Israel ahead of possible Iran strike - report
body: The US military is moving a Patriot air and missile defense system from Texas to the Middle East as Washington and Israel prepare for a possible new round of heavy combat operations against Iran following the November 3 midterm elections, The Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday.The Patriot system, which includes radar equipment, an engagement control station, missile launchers, and interceptor missiles, is being deployed to strengthen American defenses amid preparations for a potential escalation.The US has also relocated troops from bases where they were considered vulnerable to Iranian attacks, officials familiar with the movements told the WSJ.Washington has reportedly warned several Gulf Arab countries to prepare for a short, intense military campaign against Iran following the midterm elections, according to people briefed on the conversations.Additionally, US forces have been replenishing their munitions stockpiles, while officials said bomber aircraft and fighter jets are being prepared for possible strikes.US military buildup ahead of possible Iran escalationAn additional aircraft carrier strike group and Marine Expeditionary Unit are also expected to join approximately 20 US warships operating in the Middle East in November, although some vessels could rotate out of the region.The reported preparations follow an earlier US decision to deploy a third aircraft carrier and additional Marines to the Middle East. A US official said on October 1 that the USS Theodore Roosevelt and additional Marine personnel were being sent to the region, expanding Washington's military options.The latest buildup comes as US President Donald Trump weighs further military action against Iran. According to the WSJ, Trump has not made a final decision on launching another campaign, although he is reportedly leaning toward strikes targeting Iranian infrastructure and nuclear facilities. A negotiated agreement remains a possibility.Iran has threatened to expand its retaliation if the US and Israel resume their attacks, including by targeting energy infrastructure, airports, and other civilian facilities across the Persian Gulf.Meanwhile, US intelligence warnings about Iranian plots against American officials and citizens have added to regional security concerns. A US official confirmed on Friday that Secretary of State Marco Rubio had received an intelligence memorandum warning that Iranian efforts to target Americans had intensified.Iran has also reportedly instructed Hezbollah to prepare for a possible renewed conflict. Two diplomatic sources said on October 15 that Tehran had warned the Lebanese terrorist group to increase its readiness in anticipation of further American military action.The timing, scope, and final decision on any renewed military campaign remain uncertain.

title: Taraba Killings: Senate Demands Security Crackdown As Death Toll Rises To 80
body: The Senate has called for an urgent security offensive in border communities across Taraba, Plateau and Bauchi States following the reported killing of about 80 people by armed bandits in Binnari, Karim Lamido Local Government Area of Taraba State. The lawmakers urged security agencies to establish additional security camps and intensify surveillance in the affected areas to prevent further attacks and protect vulnerable communities. The resolution followed a motion of urgent national importance moved by Senator Isa Shuaibu Lau during plenary on Wednesday. Lau expressed grave concern over the killings of innocent and defenceless civilians, warning that the persistent attacks had heightened fear, displaced residents and disrupted peaceful community life. He noted that the continued activities of armed bandits in rural communities undermined the government’s constitutional responsibility to protect lives and property. The Senate warned that failure to address the recurring attacks could lead to further loss of lives, destruction of property, displacement of residents and worsening humanitarian challenges. The lawmakers stressed that no community should be left at the mercy of armed criminal groups, calling for decisive action to restore security and protect residents. The Senate also urged the National Emergency Management Agency and the North-East Development Commission to urgently provide relief materials to communities affected by the attacks. The lawmakers observed a minute’s silence in honour of those killed in the incident. The death toll from the attack on Binnari community in Karim Lamido Local Government Area of Taraba State has risen from the initial figures reported by the police, with community accounts putting the number of fatalities at 50 in subsequent reports. The Senate has now cited about 80 deaths as it calls for an urgent security offensive in the border communities of Taraba, Plateau and Bauchi States. The attack on Binnari occurred on Friday, October 23, shortly after Jumu’ah prayers, with gunmen reportedly invading the community at about 3 p.m., firing sporadically and looting food items from shops and residential houses. The attackers also reportedly set shops and motorcycles ablaze, causing panic among residents. They were suspected to have crossed into Taraba from neighbouring Plateau State.
