title: Iraqi PM al-Zaidi arrives in Syria in landmark post-Assad summit on security, trade - analysis
body: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi arrived in Syria just before noon on Wednesday. It is the first visit to Syria of a high-level Iraqi delegation since the fall of the Assad regime in 2024.Iraqi state media reported on the visit but did not provide many details. Security and counterterrorism efforts were expected to be addressed during the talks.The visit marks a potential major turning point for Iraq and Syria, which are historically linked.The border between the countries is “completely” secure, Syrian President Ahmed Al-Sharaa said on Tuesday. Recent tensions between Syria and Jordan over a Jordanian airstrike against ISIS in Syria, however, indicated that there could be issues. According to Syria, Jordan killed several civilians.Sharaa is seeking to strengthen ties with Iraq, which highlights another important dimension of Damascus's regional diplomacy.Commerce between nations increases significantlySyria and Iraq have a historic opportunity to develop economic cooperation, strengthen state institutions, and coordinate regional security, Sharaa said in an interview with Iraq's Dijlah TV, Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA), Syria's official news agency, reported Wednesday.Syria's role as a trade corridor for Iraq is important, he said, citing the connections between Iraq's Faw Port and Syria's Mediterranean Port of Tartous.Sharaa also called for rebuilding oil pipelines connecting Iraq to Syria's Baniyas Port. Iraqi oil has been flowing to Syria due to the crisis with Iran.Sharaa said commercial traffic between the countries had increased significantly over the previous six or seven months, including more than 100,000 transit trucks and 40,000 import and export trucks, SANA reported.He also addressed Iraq's internal security challenges and expressed support for Zaidi's efforts to combat corruption and bring armed groups under state authority, the report said.Sharaa said the “decision of war and peace must remain in the hands of the state,” adding that competing military organizations undermine national institutions, SANA reported.He “spoke of his experience in Iraq, explaining he went there in 2003 out of solidarity and duty to defend Iraqis and confront the American occupation, without organizational, political, military or security affiliations,” the report said. “He said he entered prison around 2005, did not participate in the sectarian conflicts Iraq witnessed, and returned to Syria in 2011 after his release.”This is particularly interesting because Iraq considers the groups Sharaa worked with to be terrorists.The developments involving Syria, Jordan, and Iraq showcase Damascus's attempt to rebuild regional ties through trade and security cooperation. There are many challenges.Helpful for Israel?This matters for the wider region, including Israel. Iraq is home to Iranian-backed militias that threaten Israel. They used to also be in Syria before the fall of the Assad regime. As such, a secure Syria and Iraq, where militias cannot roam at will, helps Israel, Saudi Arabia, and Jordan.Syria and Iraq share a history that stretches from the Ottoman Empire to the rise of modern Arab nationalism, the Ba'ath Party, and the conflicts that followed the US invasion of Iraq in 2003. Their long border has repeatedly served as a corridor for trade, insurgencies, and regional power struggles.Both territories were part of the Ottoman Empire before its collapse during World War I. The Arab Revolt, led by Sharif Hussein of Mecca and his sons, helped lay the foundations for Hashemite ambitions in the region.King Faisal briefly ruled an Arab kingdom in Damascus before becoming king of Iraq in 1921. His brother Abdullah established the Hashemite monarchy in Transjordan. The family of Abdullah continues to rule Jordan.Syria and Iraq subsequently developed rival branches of the Ba'ath Party, which came to power in Damascus in 1963 and Baghdad in 1968. Although both regimes espoused Arab nationalism, their leaders became bitter rivals.The Hashemite rule ended brutally in Iraq due to these changes in power. During the era of the Arab-Israeli wars from 1948-1973, both Iraq and Syria sent forces to fight Israel.Sharaa's rise to power After the US invasion of Iraq in 2003, insurgents crossed from Syria into Iraq, using routes through the Middle Euphrates River Valley (MERV), particularly around Al-Bukamal and Al-Qaim. These same routes later became central to ISIS, which expanded across eastern Syria and western Iraq in 2013-2014, erasing the practical significance of the border as it seized territory.It seems that Sharaa was one of those who crossed into Iraq via this route. He was then detained in Iraq and sent to Camp Bucca after 2003.The flow along the river valley subsequently reversed as Iraqi Shi'ite militias entered Syria to support the Assad regime. The crossing between Al-Qaim and Al-Bukamal became an important part of Iran's network of regional supply routes. Militias moved into Al-Bukamal and moved weapons to Hezbollah.That all changed when Assad's regime fell, and Sharaa rose to power.Today, reports of oil moving by truck through the Syrian desert near Al-Tanf illustrate the continuing importance of these corridors. The routes that once carried insurgents, ISIS fighters, and militias also connect economies and communities.The geography of Syria and Iraq remains central to their security, commerce, and political future. In some ways, they are essentially one country, linked by the desert and the river.Nevertheless, part of Iraq is heavily Shi'ite and looks to Iran for influence, while part of Syria – in the hill country from Damascus to Homs and Hama and Aleppo, looks toward the Mediterranean historically.

title: Hanwha Defense USA acquires controlling stake in Philly Shipyard
body:
Hanwha Defense USA is acquiring a controlling stake in Hanwha Philly Shipyard, bringing the shipyard under its leadership and expanding its presence in the US shipbuilding and defense sectors.
The announcement follows HDUSA establishing a presence at the shipyard earlier this year to transition it into a dual-use yard for the US Navy and commercial customers.
Since Hanwha acquired the shipyard in December 2024, Hanwha Systems has held a 60% stake, with Hanwha Ocean holding the remaining 40%. In September, Hanwha Systems announced plans to sell its stake to Hanwha Defense USA Shipbuilding, an HDUSA-led joint venture with Hanwha FutureProof.
HDUSA President of US Shipbuilding RADM Tom Anderson (Ret. US Navy) will oversee all shipbuilding operations in the US.
“As Hanwha Defense USA continues to grow its multi-domain presence across the US, bringing the Philly Shipyard under HDUSA will further align our government and commercial shipbuilding efforts,” said HDUSA President and CEO Michael Coulter .
“We look forward to continuing to invest in our Philly Shipyard facilities and workforce in preparation for exciting work ahead.”
“Over the past two years Hanwha has made significant investments in the Philly Shipyard to contribute to the revitalization of the U.S. shipbuilding industry,” said HDUSA President of U.S. Shipbuilding Tom Anderson .
“Now we are positioning the shipyard to transition to dual-use, aligning shipyard operations, workforce, and customer relations in preparation to build for the U.S. Navy, other federal agencies, and commercial customers.”

title: Putin urges African nations to use national payment systems in settlements with Russia
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Russian President Vladimir Putin urged African countries to use national payment systems in settlements with Russia at the Russia-Africa economic and humanitarian forum.
"It is important to continue work on building up stable channels of mutual payments in national currencies. To expand the network of correspondent ties of Russian and African banks, facilitate mutual opening of their branches and make a transition to alternative mechanisms of payment information. Particularly with the use of the financial messages transmission system of the Bank of Russia and the Pan-African payment systems operating in countries of Africa and the African Union," Putin said.
This will significantly reduce transaction costs and protect payments from the politicized interference of unfriendly countries, and will also strengthen sovereignty of African nations, the Russian leader added.

title: Call for Applications: MWI’s 2026–27 Research Fellows Program
body:
The Modern War Institute at West Point is pleased to invite applications for our research fellows program. MWI research fellows are nonresident volunteers committed to expanding the boundaries of policy-relevant research related to the study of modern war. They contribute to MWI’s mission by expanding our ability to conduct rigorous research, amplify expert voices, and offer relevant programming. For 2027, West Point’s intellectual theme continues last year’s focus on the Indo-Pacific.
To ensure the United States and its allies are ready to deter conflict in the Indo-Pacific, MWI seeks fellows from a wide range of backgrounds, including military and national security professionals, analysts, and academics, from the United States as well as its allies and partners. A significant consideration in selecting fellows is not only the merits of applicants’ own research, but also how they complement each other and align with MWI’s functions of research , integration , and education .
Competitive applicants will have demonstrated an ability to carry out innovative and original research and to advance discussions centered on deterring near-term war in the Indo-Pacific. They should have a track record of academic research or practical expertise in fields related to one or more of the instruments of national power or joint functions. This program is open to individuals of any age, profession, and citizenship who are committed to the ideals of MWI and the US Army. However, we are particularly interested in developing mid-career professionals who seek an active and enduring relationship with MWI and West Point.
All positions are unpaid and accepted on a purely voluntary basis. Announcements of selections will occur at the end of January, and the cohort will serve a term that runs through December 31, 2027. Based on engagement and theme alignment, MWI will consider renewals for 2028.
Fellows will actively contribute to MWI through publications, podcasts, conference participation, and collaboration with other research fellows, senior fellows, and West Point faculty. Expectations include:
In addition, MWI creates opportunities to mentor fellows’ own research projects by facilitating relationships across MWI’s professional network. MWI will promote the independent work of its fellows. Fellows may have additional opportunities to publish articles, reviews, reports, or podcasts with MWI, as well as to participate in research trips or other MWI curriculum-enriching events with cadets.
Applicants should send a succinct CV, a published (or publishable) writing sample, and a one-page cover letter. The cover letter should include the following:
Please send all items in PDF format with “MWI Fellows Application” in the subject line to mwi@westpoint.edu no later than 5:00 p.m. EST on Sunday, December 1, 2026.
Please note that we are currently unable to reply to every application to confirm receipt, but applicants should expect to hear about acceptance decisions by the end of January 2027.

title: Cut tax, reduce deficit, grow economy. Can B.C. Conservatives do it all at once?
body:
With two-thirds of the seats in the next legislature, the B.C. Conservatives may have a resounding mandate to follow through on their election promises to cut taxes, reduce the deficit and grow the economy at 3.2 per cent — but some economists say the challenge will be doing it all at once.
Cutting tax and simultaneously fixing the budget “are contradictory,” said Werner Antweiler, a professor at the University of British Columbia.
And the surge in government spending behind the record $14-billion projected deficit is conversely a contributor to economic growth, said Marc Lee, senior economist with the Canadian Centre for Policy Alternatives.
Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson has promised the appointment of a panel to review the books before presenting his government’s first budget.
But instead of easy solutions, tough choices await about what to cut, said Jairo Yunis, policy director with the Business Council of B.C.
Yunis said public sector employment had grown by over 45 per cent since 2019 under the NDP, while private sector employment in the same time was up only about three per cent.
He said public sector cuts need to be a “big part of the conversation” in an extensive review of government spending, which should take lessons from former federal Liberal prime minister Jean Chrétien and his governments.
The review should question whether the province still needs certain programs, whether there is duplication and if they can be delivered differently.
“My point is to make choices based on priorities and outcomes,” he said.
He said the deficit could be halved as a result of the review, more discipline around the use of contingencies, economic growth and lower regulatory burdens. But it won’t be easy, he said.
“That is going to entail a lot of hard choices,” Yunis said.
The Conservatives promised to raise B.C.’s basic personal income tax exemption to $32,000, amounting to a $1,000 tax cut for most individual workers. As for the deficit, their platform pledged to bring it down with the help of growth it forecast to reach 3.2 per cent, well in excess of most predictions.
The party’s platform notably omitted detail on what might be cut to help make ends meet.
Antweiler agreed the Conservatives would need to shrink the public workforce.
But the government would also need to raise more revenue and it cannot cut taxes and fix the budget at the same time, he said.
Antweiler said voters have given Doerkson a mandate, but plans may need revising after the financial assessment, and nothing should be ruled out.
“There are things we cannot do right away, that may have to wait later until economic conditions improve actually enable us to do that,” he said. “There needs to be a small dose of austerity to fix what is quite obviously broken.”
He said the public service accounts for a “huge chunk of the expenditures,” but shrinking it can be tricky because it is heavily unionized, and Doerkson’s government can’t cut back on health care, education or public safety without compromising quality.
“Provincial governments have a limit how far they can go, because many of these expenditures are written in stone,” he said.
Shrinking the public service would have to be balanced in ways that make a difference in the budget, without triggering labour unrest, he said. “But shrink we must, because I don’t think there is any other avenue,” he said.
The Conservative platform foresees economic growth increasing to 3.2 per cent in 2029, raising an additional $2.62 billion without raising taxes.
Antweiler said the growth forecast was “lofty” and not realistic.
Lee at the Canadian Centre for Policy Alternatives said that while history showed the provincial economy could sometimes improve quickly, there was plenty of uncertainty.
“We don’t even know what is going to happen next week after the U.S. election,” he said. “If there is a major stock market crash, which seems incredibly likely in the next six months, that’s going to change the situation.”
Lee said the provincial economy ran on trade, housing and immigration, and government spending. But the trade engine was sputtering because of the trade war and the housing engine was completely dead, because of changes in immigration, he said.
“The B.C. budget has been contributing to B.C.’s economic growth,” Lee said. “If we didn’t have that budget deficit, we would probably be in a recession.”
He said that to reduce the deficit “you are going to need to increase tax or cut spending.”
Antweiler said he favoured an all-of-the-above approach, combining cuts with higher revenues from economic growth and more indirect forms of taxation.
He said the NDP government of outgoing Premier David Eby made a mistake by getting rid of the carbon tax, which blew a $2-billion hole in the budget.
He said the next finance minister should look at all options, including raising resource royalties, shifting taxation from income to consumption, and encouraging investment.
The Conservatives may need to “jump over their shadow” and break their tax promises, he said.
Yunis said B.C. has more of a spending problem than a revenue problem.
And British Columbia, he said, needed to improve its tax-competitiveness.
All three economists agreed that the new finance minister faced a difficult file.
“A new chapter needs to be turned now,” Antweiler said. “It’s not too late to turn the wheel around.”

title: We’re investigating Wontumi’s claim of an attempt to poison him – Prisons Service
body: The Ghana Prisons Service says it has launched investigations into the claim by convicted Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, that there has been an attempt by some prison inmates to poison him . According to the prison authorities, Wontumi did not report the supposed incident to the prison authorities, but notified his spokesperson, who in turn informed them. Speaking to Myjoyonline , Chief Public Relations Officer for the Ghana Prisons Service, CPS Abdul Latif, said the Service is investigating the matter. “It’s something that the spokesperson of Wontumi drew the attention of the Prison authorities to. But let me repeat that, it’s not a complaint coming from Wontumi himself directly to the Prison authorities. It’s something that the PRO has said. So, by that, we have also set up investigations to launch investigations into the matter, to find out first and foremost the truth in that matter. And if it has any truth, then we will know the steps to take to avoid that.” He also explained that incidents of attempted poisoning of prisoners aren’t common in Ghana, although they will still investigate the claim. “Let me state on record that I can’t even remember the last time we reported such an incident of inmates trying to poison fellow inmates or even officers. So, I can tell you that when this issue came up, we were a bit surprised. But because we are dealing with human beings, we took it and we are investigating it to find out the truth in it.” The Chief Public Relations Officer, however, noted that the former Ashanti Regional New Patriotic Party (NPP) Chairman, who is serving a 20-year jail term for permitting mining activities on his Samreboi mining concession without approval from the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, is safe. “But we can say that Wontumi is safe and there’s nothing to worry about when it comes to his security in the prison.” The prison official, however, denied claims by Wontumi’s spokesperson that some five prison inmates have been relocated from their cells following the alleged attempted poisoning incident. “No, I cannot confirm that”, CSP Latif said when Myjoyonline specifically asked him about that claim. CSP Latif also disputed claims that Wontumi was receiving special treatment in prison. “I think the Prisons are governed by rules and regulations, and those rules and regulations don’t segregate or discriminate between prisoner A and prisoner B. You understand? So, I can tell you that Wontumi is being subjected to the same rules and regulations that other prisoners are being subjected to. So, the claim that Wontumi is being given preferential treatment in prison is not true and cannot be true. Also, the prison is already overcrowded. We all know the situation in Nsawam.” A facility that’s supposed to hold about 851 inmates is now holding 3,000-plus inmates. So, I can tell you there’s no truth in that claim, and it’s something that perhaps is being put out there for attention.

Amazon used to blast out dozens of products onstage at annual hardware events. title: Nwoko: Okonjo-Iweala’s mother was women’s rights champion
body: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Chairman of the Senate Committee on Reparations and Repatriation, Senator Ned Nwoko (APC, Delta North), has commiserated with the Director-General of the World Trade Organisation (WTO), Dr Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, over the death of her mother, Professor Kamene Okonjo. In a condolence statement he personally signed, Nwoko described the deceased as a distinguished scholar, renowned sociologist and committed advocate for women’s rights and empowerment. He said her life was marked by intellectual excellence, compassion, service to humanity and an enduring commitment to the advancement of women and society. Nwoko said: “Professor Kamene Okonjo was a distinguished scholar, a renowned sociologist and a committed advocate for women’s rights and empowerment. Her remarkable life was defined by intellectual excellence, compassion, service to humanity and an enduring commitment to the advancement of women and society.” The senator, on behalf of his family and the people of Delta North Senatorial District, extended his condolences to Okonjo-Iweala, the Obi of Ogwashi-Uku, Obi Ifechukwude Anishi Okonjo II, and the entire Okonjo family. He described the late professor as the matriarch of the Okonjo royal family of Ogwashi-Uku, Delta State, who died at the age of 96. Nwoko noted that as the wife of the late Obi Professor Chukwuka Okonjo and mother of prominent individuals whose contributions had earned recognition locally and internationally, she left a legacy that transcended her immediate family. He said her contributions to scholarship, family life and women’s empowerment would remain a lasting part of her impact on society. “While her passing represents a profound loss to Ogwashi-Uku Kingdom, the Anioma nation and Nigeria as a whole, we must also celebrate a life of distinction, purpose and meaningful impact,” he said. The senator added that the values she upheld and the generations she inspired would continue to bear testimony to a life well lived. Extending his condolences particularly to Okonjo-Iweala, Nwoko said public achievements and positions could not diminish the pain of losing a mother. He prayed for God to grant the WTO chief, the Obi of Ogwashi-Uku, the Okonjo family and others mourning the deceased the strength and fortitude to bear the loss. He also prayed for the peaceful repose of the late professor’s soul, expressing hope that her legacy would continue to inspire generations. The post Nwoko: Okonjo-Iweala’s mother was women’s rights champion appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: BAE tests deck launcher that can reload at sea
body: BAE Systems has completed the first live firing of the Adaptable Deck Launcher, a missile launcher that bolts onto a ship’s deck and can be replenished at sea without the vessel returning to port, according to the company. The launcher was developed under a United States Department of War contract for the NATO Seasparrow Project Office. It uses the logistics and electronics suite of the Mk 41 vertical launching system already in service, which the company says gives it the reliability of that system at lower operating cost. Jason Casciotti, vice president of weapons systems at BAE Systems, said: “The successful demonstration of the Adaptable Deck Launcher is a major milestone in our commitment to enhancing the Navy’s combat effectiveness and readiness. The ADL complements the Mk 41 VLS, the foundation of naval missile integration, by providing a capability for rapid replenishment, using standard shipboard equipment and offering the fleet additional flexibility in how it sustains combat loads at sea.” Replenishment is where the real significance lies, I’d argue, because after a warship empties its vertical launch cells, it must go back to a port with the right facilities to reload them, which in a sustained campaign takes the ship off station for days or weeks. Royal Navy and United States Navy ships firing interceptors at Houthi drones and missiles in the Red Sea ran into exactly that constraint, and the United States Navy has spent several years working on ways to rearm cells while under way. The launcher is designed for anti-air defence and can go on aircraft carriers, amphibious ships and other surface combatants. BAE Systems said it is also optimised for uncrewed warfare, with compact configurations suited to medium uncrewed surface vessels, which is where a deck-mounted launcher has an obvious advantage over cells built into a hull. As mechanical design agent for the Mk 41 family, the company built the launcher to take Evolved SeaSparrow Missile Mk 25 quad-pack canisters, which hold four missiles in the space of one cell and provide defence against supersonic anti-ship missiles, aircraft and other aerial threats. The post BAE tests deck launcher that can reload at sea first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Bank of Canada hikes interest rates for the 1st time in 3 years
body:
The Bank of Canada hiked interest rates by 0.25 per cent on Wednesday to 2.5 per cent, marking the first change to its benchmark in a year and the first increase in three years.
Speaking to reporters Wednesday after the announcement, Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem ackowledged how raising rates will feel for Canadians and businesses, saying “look, we get it.”
“The best thing we can do is that we can get inflation down. We can prevent these higher energy prices from spreading to the prices of other goods and services. And by raising our policy rate today, that’s going to help lean against that pass-through, and it’s going to help get inflation back,” said Macklem.
“Yes, it’s not going to feel good immediately, but that’s how you get inflation back down, and that will feel good for Canadians and Canadian businesses.”
The move was widely expected by most economists as the central bank faces pressure to raise interest rates with the Iran war and other geopolitical conflicts resulting in higher prices for oil and gas, which is expected to lead to higher prices for goods and services beyond the gas pump.
Wednesday’s interest rate hike is what one economist sees as “an insurance policy” against inflation rising in the near future.
“Inflation pressures haven’t eased enough to reassure the Bank, and this move signals it is taking the supply shock seriously, even with the economy running well below full strength,” said principal economist Andrew DiCapua of the Business Data Lab and Canadian Chamber of Commerce in a statement.
“Its decision is predicated on stronger economic growth ahead, and that assumption will be tested, especially with the labour market still showing signs of slack.”
Consumer inflation was last measured at 3.1 per cent in September , and has been hovering around three per cent since April.
The Bank of Canada said in a statement it expects inflation to rise to about 3.5 per cent by the end of the year, as oil and gas prices push up the headline figure. When stripping away elevated gasoline prices, core measures of inflation have been closer to two per cent — the Bank’s target — but that is expected to change.
“Cost pressures are building, with high fuel prices raising the costs of production and transportation. Imported industrial and electronics input prices have also increased,” the Bank of Canada said in a statement.
“While businesses have mostly absorbed higher input costs so far, Bank surveys suggest cost pass-through will increase over the next year. Near-term household and business inflation expectations have risen, while longer-term inflation expectations remain well anchored.”
The Bank adds that its outlook for inflation is higher than its projections from July.
Financial markets and a Reuters poll of economists were betting that the central bank would deliver a quarter-point hike to its policy rate, the first increase in the key lending rate since July 2023.
“The Bank of Canada raised its overnight rate by 25bp to 2.50 per cent as widely expected today, as it looks to guard against the threat of elevated energy prices becoming a widespread inflationary problem,” said senior economist Andrew Grantham at CIBC in a statement.
The floor for borrowing rates set by the Bank of Canada was at 2.25 per cent since October 2025, when rates were cut from 2.5 per cent.
The Bank of Canada also released its updated forecasts for inflation and economic growth Wednesday, and said higher oil and gas prices are expected to continue accelerating inflation.
“With persistently elevated oil prices and refinery margins, inflation has risen in most countries,” said the Bank of Canada.
“The conflict in the Middle East is now in its eighth month and there is no clear path to resolution. The combination of higher-for-longer energy prices and increased pass-through adds to the persistence of inflation.”
The Bank of Canada said it expects the Canadian economy to grow in total by one per cent this year, and two per cent in 2027 and 2028 respectively, but stressed its forecast is “subject to considerable uncertainty,” especially because of trade tensions between Canada and the U.S.
The central bank also suggested in its statement that more hikes could be on the way.
“Looking ahead, governing council agreed we would take our decisions one meeting at a time. There could be a need to raise the policy rate further, but given the uncertainties, we will proceed carefully,” said the Bank of Canada.
Grantham says the Bank of Canada will likely proceed with caution, holding rates at 2.5 per cent at the December meeting, and hiking again in January by 0.25 per cent.
“We don’t expect that core measures of inflation will accelerate as much as the Bank fears, which should become more obvious early in 2027 and allow the Bank of Canada to then hold interest rates at 2.75 per cent throughout the remainder of next year,” said Grantham.
DiCapua said Wednesday’s hike is likely not part of a series of hikes, saying although inflation may be a risk the Bank needs to get ahead of, the economy is also sensitive to hikes right now.
“Financial conditions have already tightened, and while higher interest rates cannot fix a supply disruptions, they can further weaken demand,” said DiCapua.
“We expect the Bank to be patient from here. It has shown it is willing to act on inflation, but there are serious doubts about the economy’s ability to absorb meaningfully higher borrowing costs.”

title: Finlands defense minister talks NATO, Ukraine and fishing
body: Finland’s Defense Minister Antti Häkkänen visited New Zealand on Oct. 21 to discuss security issues with officials there. His travel agenda also included Australia and Japan, signaling the Northern European country’s interest in the region despite the geographical distance. “We are reinforcing our relations with partners in the Indo-Pacific region. In addition, we see plenty of opportunities to deepen defense materiel cooperation,” Häkkänen was quoted as saying in a statement released by the Finnish government ahead of the trip. He caught up with Defense News in Wellington for a brief interview. What NATO assets is Finland prepared to host? When we joined NATO we were prepared, nationally, to defend ourselves. As a NATO member our first responsibility is a strong, national defense with lots of European assets in the Navy, Air Force and also in space nowadays. We have established NATO’s northern Europe’s land headquarters in the Arctic area, on Finnish soil. So we are leading the land defense. What are your priorities for Finland’s defense? We have four pillars in our defense policy. The first one is that Finland, by itself, has to be always, always, ready to defend our own country. Second, is strong NATO in northern Europe. Now we have built NATO’s capabilities to operate in Arctic areas, so we are really happy to see that NATO’s evermore able to act in the north. Related Finland closes airspace, restricts maritime traffic near Russia over drone risk Finland’s military said it closed a section of Finnish airspace and restricted maritime traffic off the country’s southern coast near the Russian border. Third, is defense corporation with different countries. Some countries — for example the United States and European countries — are in operational planning on how to act together in crisis situations, so that’s the third pillar. Supporting NATO’s Article five. And the fourth pillar is comprehensive security. We have to have enough from our own country: energy, food, equipment from the defense industry. We have civil shelters for almost 5.5 million people [ editor’s note: much of Finland’s total population ], and the whole society has to be prepared to act in crisis mode. Every company has to plan how they can operate, even if war starts. We are developing and investing heavily in those pillars. The Finnish way to do things is cost-effective, high-quality and win-win. We are not just saying that Finland needs something, we’re also ready to provide our knowledge, our expertise. How do your NH90 operations compare with New Zealand’s? There were difficulties at the start. But now our special forces and our land forces are using the NH90 and they have been customized to Finnish needs, to our special environment. Our pilots are really satisfied and when they have compared NH90 to some other equipment that is now in the market, they think that this is still the best one. How is Finland supporting Ukraine ? Heavily, by all the political levels. We are heavy supporters of Ukrainian military from our stocks. We are giving a lot of money, because we see that if Ukraine doesn’t stop Russia, Russia’s hunger will grow for Europe and they will do something nasty. Supporting Ukraine is also supporting our own security and it shows all the other dictators around the world that democratic nations are united to support Ukraine and oppose violence against neighbors. That’s why we are really happy to see that New Zealand’s also [supporting] Ukraine. France has offered to extend its nuclear deterrent to Europe, what do you think of that proposal ? Let me be clear, NATO’s nuclear deterrence comes [from] U.S. weapon systems, that’s for sure, but France gives an additional, extra deterrence and that will create some strategic dilemmas for Putin. Related Macron opens door to deploying French nuclear forces to European allies The plan is a “major evolution” of France’s deterrence posture, the president said in a long-awaited speech at the Île Longue naval base in Brittany. What keeps you awake at night ? My kids! I have two small kids and I live at the eastern border, at the Russian border, so I’m cool. I fish there, in beautiful lakes, and I have my house there with my family, so I’m taking it easy, like everyone who lives [there]. That’s a strong border. We have always tried to have diplomatic relations with Russia, but throughout history, from Catherine the Great to Peter the Great, Russians have always been willing to use violence, against their own people, but also against their neighbors. That’s why Finland has been always pragmatic in defense and security, you have to always be ready. That’s why we are so cool and calm. There [are] a million reservists in Finland, everyone has had military training. We know that Russia is a threat, but we have to just do our stuff, be prepared to invest heavily, keep our friends close, get new friends globally and do stuff right —that’s the Finnish way to handle a difficult security situation. The Joint Expeditionary Force, is that proving useful? JEF is one of the most important defense operations for Finnish and northern Europe’s defense. We think that the most valuable part of JEF is that it can react fast; JEF has already operated, so there’s no need to wait for some kind of clear Article Five case. How can New Zealand’s forces support yours? Well, we are now having this dialogue between our partners … there’s different kinds of possibilities with different organizations. For example, today we discussed space capabilities, Finland has a lot of space companies and a lot of technological expertise, but New Zealand has different kinds of space capability, launching, for example. Also countering problems with undersea cables. Do you see Ukraine joining NATO? Maybe someday. Ukraine’s path is to the West, to their democratic alliances in Europe. But all the NATO countries have to approve it and U.S. and other countries have said no at this point. About a quarter of New Zealand’s defense force consists of women, do you know the percentage of women in Finland’s forces? It’s much smaller, but it’s rising. All the men are obliged to participate and it’s voluntary for women. The number of women are growing now because everyone in Finland wants to participate. Is everyone still happy in Finland? Yeah, we’re the happiest nation in the world, for nine years in a row. Even though there’s some challenges and dark clouds in the war in Europe, still people in Finland are quite cool. Russia is building new military infrastructure near our borders, so we have to do more for our security. But we can do it, it’s not a big problem. I’m optimistic. The Finnish mindset … it’s kind of a mixup of reason and optimism. You face the world as it is. You have to adapt, take your chances, find the possibilities in economy, security and do the best that you can do.

title: Onitsha traders petition IGP over alleged threats, demolition
body: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Traders operating under the Association of Modebeb Traders in Onitsha, Anambra State, have petitioned the Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, seeking a comprehensive investigation into alleged threats, intimidation and the demolition of commercial buildings amid a dispute over the leadership and ownership of a market plaza. The traders alleged that they had faced persistent harassment and threats for about two years, claiming that some individuals had allegedly used their connections with security agencies to intimidate members of the association. Speaking on behalf of the traders at a press briefing in Abuja on Tuesday, Chief Okey Muojekwu said the dispute had disrupted their businesses and left members concerned about their safety. He alleged that the plaza where they conducted their businesses was demolished in 2025, worsening the dispute and affecting traders’ livelihoods. According to him, four buildings, including properties at numbers 77 and 79, were demolished, affecting people who had invested in businesses at the location. Muojekwu also alleged that some individuals had altered or forged property documents to change the ownership name from Osumakan Model Ventures. He called on the relevant authorities to investigate the matter and establish the rightful ownership of the properties. He further alleged that police personnel, including officers attached to a special anti-narcotics command in Onitsha, had been used to intimidate traders. Muojekwu claimed that he was recently attacked by suspected thugs who allegedly stabbed him with a knife, but he escaped and reported the incident to the police. Expressing concern over what he described as the lack of effective action against those responsible, he said threats against members had continued. He also raised concerns over an alleged incident involving a man identified as Chris Okon, who was reportedly taken away alongside a woman after some individuals allegedly assaulted him at his residence. According to Muojekwu, the woman was detained from Friday until Monday or Tuesday before she was released. The traders appealed to the IGP to investigate the allegations, provide protection against further attacks and ensure that anyone found culpable was brought to justice. The Chairman of the market association, Tochukwu Umeh, said the dispute was also connected to disagreements over the removal of some market leaders by the Anambra State Government. Umeh alleged that some individuals had continued to occupy leadership positions despite the government’s decision to remove them. He argued that the government had no right to remove leaders elected by market members. He said the disagreement had contributed to the alleged harassment of traders and disrupted market activities, making the administration of the market difficult. Also speaking, a patron of the market, Onyeka Oguejiofor, alleged that some individuals had taken over shops without following due process and were attempting to force recognised leaders and traders out of their positions and businesses. He claimed that some traders had been removed from their positions or threatened with eviction without formal notice or communication. Oguejiofor further alleged that those involved had boasted of their connections with the police and their ability to act without consequences. He said the traders had reported the matter to the Commissioner of Police, the Police Public Relations Officer and the leadership of the relevant market association, but had yet to secure a lasting resolution. According to him, some individuals were arrested and detained for about a week before being released, after which they allegedly resumed the activities complained about. Oguejiofor added that the traders had approached state government officials responsible for trade and commerce, who reportedly urged compliance with the government’s decision on the removal of the affected leaders. He appealed to the police and relevant government authorities to intervene, investigate the allegations and ensure that traders could conduct their businesses without intimidation. The traders said they wanted a peaceful resolution of the dispute, protection of their rights and the opportunity to resume normal business activities. title: Africa holds boundless potential for development — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Africa offers immense opportunities for development, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.
"According to the African Development Bank, the continent’s economies are growing at an average rate of 4.2%, exceeding the global average. Moreover, 12 of the world’s 20 fastest-growing economies are located in Africa. The continent is remarkably diverse in its ethnic and religious composition, as well as its geography and climate. All these factors point to its enormous potential for accelerated development and sustainable economic growth," Putin noted.
He added that Africa is rightly described as the "continent of the future." According to United Nations projections, the continent is set to become the main driver of global population growth from 2030 onward.
"By 2050, Africa’s population is expected to exceed 2.5 billion, with young people under the age of 30 accounting for approximately 70% of the total," Putin concluded.

title: AFD, BoI Sign $30m Deal to Unlock Finance for Nigeria’s Creative Sector
body: Michael Olugbode in Abuja The French Development Agency (AFD) and the Bank of Industry (BoI) have signed a $30 million financing agreement to expand access to credit for Nigeria’s creative industry, with at least 90 per cent of the facility earmarked for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). The agreement, which includes a €500,000 technical assistance programme, is AFD’s first credit line dedicated to cultural and creative industries anywhere in the world, positioning Nigeria as the beneficiary of a financing initiative targeting one of the country’s emerging sources of jobs and economic diversification. The facility, signed in Abuja during the visit of AFD Chief Executive Officer, Christophe Lecourtier, is designed to improve access to finance for businesses in fashion, design, textiles, music, film and audiovisual production, video games and visual arts. Women-led and youth-led enterprises, as well as first-time borrowers, are among the priority beneficiaries of the programme, which seeks to address financing barriers that have constrained the growth of creative businesses. The initiative comes as Nigeria’s cultural and creative industries account for approximately five per cent of the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and provide livelihoods for more than 4.2 million people. Under the agreement, the BoI will deploy the credit facility to eligible businesses, while the technical assistance component will strengthen the bank’s capacity to finance the sector through staff training and the development of financial products tailored to the needs of creative enterprises. The programme targets the training of at least 70 per cent of relevant BoI staff, alongside the development of specialised financing products to better serve businesses whose needs may differ from those of conventional industrial enterprises. The agreement was signed by BoI Managing Director, Dr Olasupo Olusi, and Lecourtier, who represented AFD, reinforcing the longstanding partnership between the two institutions. Beyond expanding access to credit, the initiative is expected to promote financial inclusion, support skilled employment and strengthen the contribution of the creative economy to Nigeria’s sustainable and inclusive growth. Its focus on smaller businesses could prove particularly significant for entrepreneurs seeking to expand production, acquire equipment, develop new products or reach wider markets but who struggle to secure affordable financing. The facility also aligns with the Federal Government’s Destination 2030 ambition for the creative sector, as Nigeria seeks to diversify its economy and harness industries capable of generating employment and business opportunities for its growing population. The €500,000 technical assistance component is expected to complement the lending facility by improving BoI’s capacity to understand and meet the financing needs of creative businesses. For AFD, the agreement represents an expansion of its development financing partnership with Nigeria, while the BoI is expected to use the facility to support enterprise development, job creation and economic diversification. The two institutions said the programme would help remove financial and non-financial barriers to the development of Nigeria’s cultural and creative industries.

title: APC chair attacks Atiku over lack of projects in Plateau as VP
body: By Ayobami Okerinde The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Nentawe Yilwatda, has challenged former vice-president Atiku Abubakar to name one major project worth N10bn executed in Plateau State during his eight years in office. Yilwatda spoke on Wednesday at the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Jos, the Plateau State capital, while canvassing support for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general election. “Atiku was vice president for eight years. Show me one road or one thing that we had on the Plateau. Show me one N10 billion project on the Plateau within that period,” he said. “The best we can have in those days is a borehole, or they bring ‘Keke Napep’ for us. Today, the president is bringing major projects on the Plateau,” he added. Yilwatda listed a univeristy and the Federal Medical Centre among projects associated with Tinubu’s administration, adding that the president had addressed challenges in healthcare, education, infrastructure and security. He identified insecurity as the most pressing concern among Plateau residents and credited Tinubu with addressing the problem. “If you ask any Plateau man, ‘What is your problem?’ The number one problem is insecurity, and Mr President has addressed it,” Yilwatda said. Also speaking at the event, Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang urged residents to support Tinubu’s re-election, arguing that the president should be allowed to complete an eight-year tenure in line with the North-South power-sharing arrangement. “There’s no reason why we will change the power-sharing formula between the north and the south; we’ve agreed that the south can do eight years and the north will do eight years,” he said. “President Buhari did eight years for the north there; there is no reason why the south cannot do eight years. He added, “We must be promise keepers; therefore, we have every reason to stick with the president.” The governor urged Nigerians to exercise patience and allow Tinubu’s economic policies time to produce results, describing the president as a “good driver” and arguing that there was no need for a change in leadership. title: Zelensky: Ukraine’s Data Center Strikes ‘Hurt Russia More’
body:
Ukraine has found ways to counter Russia’s attacks on its digital infrastructure, President Volodymyr Zelensky said in an interview reported on Wednesday, Oct. 28, arguing that Ukrainian retaliatory strikes hurt Russia more because its systems are more centralized.
Speaking to The Sun, Zelensky contrasted the countries’ approaches to protecting communications networks and data centers, UATV reported .
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“Our retaliatory strikes are more painful for Russia, because everything there is more centralized,” he said.
Zelensky said Russia had repeatedly attacked Ukrainian data infrastructure and cyberspace, but Ukraine’s developed, decentralized networks had helped keep mobile communications and internet services functioning.
He also linked decentralization to Ukraine’s shortage of air defenses. Russia, he said, has substantial air defense resources and concentrates on protecting existing infrastructure, while Ukraine has dispersed systems to reduce their vulnerability.
That approach extends beyond data infrastructure, the president added.
Zelensky described Ukrainian strikes as a response to Russia’s campaign, saying Kyiv acted after Russian attacks against Ukraine.
The president’s comments follow weeks of Russian attacks on telecommunications infrastructure, including facilities whose operators have relied on backup sites to maintain services.
On Oct. 19, Datagroup said a Russian ballistic missile attack had destroyed its data center in Kyiv, leaving the equipment and infrastructure beyond repair.
The company reported no injuries among its employees and said it continued serving customers through backup facilities.
Datagroup had already reported damage to a data center on Sept. 25, when it said customer data had been preserved and services were continuing from reserve sites.
Other providers, including MiroHost and UTELS, also reported damage during Russian attacks in late September. Ukraine’s Ministry of Digital Transformation said earlier strikes had temporarily disrupted internet access for approximately 100,000 households in Kyiv and the surrounding region.
The disruptions show that continued nationwide connectivity has coexisted with serious damage and localized outages.
Russia has openly acknowledged targeting the facilities. On Oct. 16, Chief of the General Staff Valery Gerasimov told President Vladimir Putin that Russian forces were striking data centers alongside strategic bridges and railway infrastructure.
Ukraine’s response has included a series of drone attacks against data centers operated by Russian technology company Yandex.
On Oct. 8, drones struck the Sasovo facility , in Russia’s Ryazan region, triggering a fire. Yandex acknowledged an incident and said some services were temporarily unavailable, while users reported problems accessing its online storage and document platforms.
A day later, Yandex confirmed that another Ukrainian strike had disabled several modules at its data center in Kaluga. The company said it was assessing the damage and could not immediately say when the equipment would return to service.
Yandex’s infrastructure supports services used by both the company and outside clients, meaning disruptions can spread beyond its own consumer applications.
A third strike, on Oct. 11, hit a Yandex data center in Vladimir, bringing the number of targeted facilities to three in four days.
The attack disrupted more than 80 services and cloud infrastructure components. Yandex confirmed that operations at the Vladimir facility had been halted.
Affected systems included cloud computing, storage, databases, and artificial intelligence tools, alongside consumer products such as the Alice voice assistant, Yandex Music, and videoconferencing services.
Businesses using Yandex’s cloud infrastructure also experienced outages, illustrating how damage to a major processing hub can affect multiple platforms simultaneously.

title: Russia ready to share ideas in using public administration technology with Africa — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Russia has a robust public administration system based on modern technology and is prepared to share its expertise with interested African nations, President Vladimir Putin said at the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.
"Russia has significant experience in applying information technology to public administration. We would be happy to share our solutions and practices with interested African countries. I can tell you that we have truly excellent public administration systems built on modern technology," he said.
This improves the quality of governance, boosts state budget revenues, and ultimately enhances people's quality of life.
"As it has done in the past, Russia stands ready to assist the continent's nations in addressing the aftermath of emergency situations. We are prepared to work together to advance a balanced agenda focused on the environment and climate change adaptation, as well as to strengthen sporting ties - while ensuring that sports remain free from politicization," Putin stated.

title: Zelensky arrives in the Netherlands
body:
According to Ukrinform, the head of state announced his arrival on Facebook.
“We have arrived in the Netherlands with our team to meet with Prime Minister Rob Jetten. We are strengthening our partnership and working to better defend Ukraine. We will discuss defense and economic cooperation, strengthening Ukraine’s air defense, and new steps to support Ukraine,” Zelensky said upon arrival.
He also said the agenda included a meeting with representatives of Ukrainian and Dutch businesses, as well as an audience with King Willem-Alexander of the Netherlands.
As Ukrinform previously reported, the Netherlands announced today that it would provide Ukraine with €1.2 billion in aid over three years . The funds will go toward Ukraine’s reconstruction.

title: Putin Focused on Medieval History in Talks With Nordic Leaders
body:
Ukraine was aware that Norway and Finland were preparing to speak with Russian President Vladimir Putin and had been informed in advance about the purpose of the conversation, President Volodymyr Zelensky said.
He made the remarks while speaking with journalists, according to RBC-Ukraine .
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Zelensky said he spoke with Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Finnish President Alexander Stubb on Tuesday night, following a meeting in Oslo, shortly before their conversation with Putin.
“We discussed the topic. In principle, we had a briefing in Oslo on the topic of the upcoming planned trilateral meeting of the negotiating groups in November in Abu Dhabi,” he said.
“They wanted to discuss it with me and then with the leader of Russia. We talked to them then, but we didn’t come out with it publicly, because it was already night,” Zelensky added.
He said that Stubb and Støre spoke with Putin on Tuesday, with each side presenting its position. After the conversation, the Nordic leaders immediately called Zelensky to brief him on the details.
“In principle, they conveyed that there seems to be a feeling that the Russians are serious about the meeting in Abu Dhabi. The topics should be the following issues: The first de-escalation steps, the main priorities for the Ukrainian side – in particular security ones, and in general the end of this war,” Zelensky said.
According to Zelensky, the initiative came from Stubb and Støre. In a joint statement, the two leaders said they wanted to convey their positions to Putin directly regarding future negotiations aimed at ending Russia’s war against Ukraine.
Zelensky also pointed to their clarification that they were speaking on behalf of their own countries, rather than representing Europe as a whole. As Russia’s neighbors, he said, Norway and Finland have a particular interest in the discussions.
Zelensky said Norway and Finland should share the information with other Europeans and discuss the agenda with Ukraine, Europe, and the US.
“They want to play a bigger role,” he said, adding that while Norway is not an EU member, it is part of Europe more broadly.
Zelensky added that both countries view security guarantees for Ukraine and Russia as a major challenge because of their geographic proximity and their roles as European states and key Ukrainian partners.
“When there are security guarantees that Ukraine wants to discuss and security guarantees that Russia wants to discuss, they believe that this is also a serious challenge for them – both for Russia’s neighbors, for European countries, and for our serious partners,” Zelensky said.
He welcomed the initiative and said he supported the format of their communication with the Kremlin.
Zelensky also recalled the meeting between Putin and US President Donald Trump in Alaska, saying it had effectively ended Russia’s diplomatic isolation.
“It’s a fact: The ‘Russians’ were diplomatically isolated by a significant part of the world, and Alaska lifted this isolation,” he said.
Zelensky added that European contacts with Russia had taken place even before the Alaska meeting, although they were less public. He also pointed to communications involving national security advisers and intelligence services, as well as contacts with Turkey and countries in the Middle East.
“In addition to Europe, Turkey and the countries of the Middle East communicated. That is, this is happening,” he said, adding that Kyiv had learned about some other contacts only after they had taken place.
In contrast, Zelensky described the Norwegian and Finnish initiative as an open process involving advance discussions, a full briefing, and clear objectives.
“Finland and Norway show that they want to open another channel of communication so that Europe can receive information not only through the US and so that Russia can hear certain things directly,” Zelensky added.
Meanwhile, the Financial Times ( FT ) reported that Putin’s conversation with Støre and Stubb did not go as the Nordic leaders had expected.
According to the report cited by RBC-Ukraine, Putin devoted a substantial part of the discussion to his interpretation of medieval Slavic history.
The conversation was the Russian leader’s first contact with any of Ukraine’s European allies since he spoke with French President Emmanuel Macron in July.
However, Putin showed little urgency to address current issues, the FT reported, highlighting the challenges Europe faces in trying to influence future peace negotiations with Russia.
Stubb told Finnish media that the conversation had initially been scheduled to last less than 30 minutes but ultimately continued for an hour and a half.
Three sources familiar with the discussions told the FT that, rather than engaging in substantive debate about how to end the war, Putin spent considerable time discussing what the Kremlin calls the “root causes of the conflict.”
The sources also said the issue of an immediate ceasefire – which Ukraine has insisted upon – was barely raised. The Nordic leaders deliberately refrained from interrupting Putin’s historical digressions, seeking to assess how willing he was to engage in dialogue with Europe.
Previously, Putin also cited “the latest genetic research” to support his claim that Russians and Ukrainians are one people. He presented the argument through his own interpretation of Russia’s historical development and contemporary realities.

title: Sydney Family Calls for More Funding After Rare Ovarian Cancer Claims 30-Year-Old Jacinda Manettas
body: A Sydney family is calling for greater investment in rare ovarian cancer research after Jacinda Manettas died at just 30, following a three-and-a-half-year battle with an aggressive form of the disease. Jacinda during chemotherapy.. Jacinda celebrated her 30th birthday in early July, surrounded by family and friends. By the end of August, she had died from mucinous ovarian adenocarcinoma, a rare subtype of ovarian cancer that accounts for approximately 3 per cent of cases. Ovarian cancer patient Jacinda Manettas with her parents and brother Andrew. Her brother, Andrew Manettas, is determined to turn his family’s grief into action, pushing for greater research funding and better treatment options for patients diagnosed with the disease. A three-year battle with a rare cancer Jacinda’s cancer journey began in February 2023, when doctors discovered a cyst on her left ovary. Her left ovary was removed, and subsequent laboratory testing revealed the cyst was malignant. She underwent six rounds of chemotherapy, with initial tests showing no detectable traces of cancer. However, mucinous ovarian cancer can be particularly difficult to treat, with some tumours showing resistance to conventional chemotherapy. In January 2025, cancer was detected in Jacinda’s right ovary, which was also removed. She underwent further chemotherapy, but by March 2026, the disease had spread to her abdomen. A targeted antibody treatment initially showed promise before the cancer progressed again. In mid-August, Jacinda and her brother travelled to the United States to investigate further treatment options. They were encouraged to consider a clinical trial in Australia, but she never had the opportunity to begin it. After returning home, Jacinda suffered a stroke linked to complications from her cancer. She died four days later. Andrew said the family had been willing to pursue any treatment that might help his sister. He believes greater investment in research is essential to give future patients more options. Fundraising in Jacinda’s memory Jacinda’s love of poker has inspired a fundraising event in her honour. On November 7, Sydney venue The Pillars will host the Jacinda Royale , a poker night raising money for mucinous ovarian cancer research through the Peter MacCallum Cancer Foundation. The event aims to celebrate Jacinda’s life while supporting research that could improve treatment outcomes for other patients. Andrew said the fundraiser was a way to honour his sister through something she loved, while helping give others a better chance. Beyond community fundraising, he is also calling on policymakers to direct more resources towards research into rare cancers. For the family, the goal is to ensure Jacinda’s death helps drive progress towards better treatments and outcomes for others facing the same diagnosis.
