title: At least 64 dead, 80 injured in central Spain train crash
body:
Global Affairs Canada said Wednesday that six Canadians were injured in a high-speed train crash in central Spain that killed 68 people and injured dozens more.
One other Canadian is ‘unaccounted for,’ a spokesperson said.
In a statement on X , foreign affairs Minister Anita Anand said that consular officials were “in close contact with Spanish authorities to ensure that we have the most current information and that all Canadians affected receive the assistance they need.”
Earlier Wednesday, Prime Minister Mark Carney called the incident a “tragedy.”
“Our thoughts are with their families, the victims and their loved ones in the days and weeks ahead. And of course if there’s any assistance we can give, we will provide,” he said.
Carney extended his condolences to people in Spain and said Canada was working with local authorities.
The death toll rose to 68 on Wednesday morning, the Associated Press wrote, after it was initially reported that 30 people had died.
The regional president of Castilla La Mancha, Emiliano García-Page, said at least 80 people were injured as rescue workers continue to search in the wreckage for survivors and bodies.
It was the second major train accident in Spain this year.
Spain’s rail system operator ADIF said the crash occurred Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo. Rail service was suspended between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia.
The accident involved a train from Spain’s state-owned RENFE company and the private rail company IRYO.
Esther Padilla, spokeswoman for the Castilla La Mancha region, told state broadcaster TVE that the accident was between two high-speed trains carrying hundreds of passengers and heading in the same direction from the capital Madrid to Seville in southwestern Spain.
One ran into the tail of the other, which had stopped, knocking two of its cars off the track.
Spain’s Transport Minister Óscar Puente said that the accident was caused by what he called the “inexplicable” order from a central command center for Spain’s trains after a security system had failed.
He said the train engineers were not to blame.
Puente said that at 8:30 a.m. the security system on a stretch of 63 kilometres stopped working due to a computer malfunction, causing all trains on that stretch to stop. But the central command told the RENFE train to start running again without any speed restrictions, and it ended up colliding with the stopped IRYO train at 8:53 a.m.
Puente said that the train should never have been told to start moving again since there was still a “stop signal” active on that line. And if it had, at least it should have been told to go at reduced speed.
Puente said they were still studying information to see how fast the train was going, but it could have been at 200 kph for that stretch of the track.
“I am not attributing responsibility to anyone, I am just stating the facts,” Puente said.
The crash, which occurred in a flat stretch surrounded by fields in between the towns of Urda and Los Yébenes, left one car shredded into bits of metal and other material, scattering debris down a gravel slope.
Spanish Health Minister Mónica García told TVE that emergency workers were focusing on rescuing survivors and bodies from the two most damaged train cars. She said that the injured are being sent to different hospitals in the area.
“It was a high-speed impact, so we are expecting this to be a tragedy,” García said.
Padilla said that 397 passengers were in the RENFE train and 147 passengers in the IRYO train.
Trains from the same two companies were also involved in a deadly crash in January.
IRYO, an Italian-owned company, said in a statement that it has “activated its security protocols and is closely working with authorities.”
The mayor of the nearby town of Urda, Manuel Galán, told Spanish state broadcaster TVE that civil protection authorities had asked his town hall to prepare a sports pavilion to attend to injured passengers.
A military emergency brigade was deployed to help emergency services, firefighters and police.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez cancelled his agenda to focus on the crash. He wrote on X that he was “dismayed by the serious train accident in Toledo.”
“Emergency services are working on site to attend to the affected passengers,” wrote Sánchez, who faces a national election next month. “All my thoughts are with the victims and their families.”
Spain’s King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia said in a short statement on X that they were following news of the accident.
“We are deeply saddened and concerned by the train accident in Urda (Toledo),” the royal couple said. “We share in the grief of the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives, and we send our heartfelt support to the injured and all those affected.”
In January, 45 people died in southern Spain when a train jumped the track and hit an oncoming train. The crash was the deadliest in Spain since a 2013 crash that killed 80 people. The January incident shook confidence in the European country’s extensive high-speed rail service.
Over recent decades, Spain has invested heavily in high-speed rail — which the country’s railway union defines as rails for trains going 250 kph (155 mph) and over — turning it into a world leader.
Spain has laid some 3,900 kilometres (2,400 miles) of such tracks over more than three decades for its 49 million residents. Only China, with 45,000 kilometres (28,000 miles) for its 1.4 billion people, has more high-speed track, according to the International Union of Railways.
Spain only recently opened its rail network to private companies to compete with RENFE. Iryo started operating in Spain in 2022.

title: At least 11 Ukrainian cities are being prepared for 360 defense — underground sources
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Kiev is preparing at least 11 Ukrainian cities for 360-degree defense, including Dnepropetrovsk, Zaporozhye, Kharkov, and Kherson, a pro-Russian underground source told TASS.
"We’re talking primarily about the south and the east: Odessa, Nikolayev, Kherson, Zaporozhye, Dnepropetrovsk, Pavlograd," the source said. "At the same time, they are preparing Kiev and the Kiev Region, Kharkov, Sumy, Chernigov, and Volyn. The north is being attributed to a 'threat' from Belarus. Kharkov and Sumy are being fortified due to their [proximity] to the border with Russia."
In addition, he added, in the Zaporozhye and Dnepropetrovsk Regions, fortifications are being built around almost all cities, all the way to Orekhov and Volnyansk. Meanwhile, on the approaches to Odessa, trenches have long since been dug, and so-called "dragon’s teeth" and barbed wire have been installed.
At the same time, the pro-Russian underground sources noted that people are intentionally not being told which cities will be prepared for a circular defense, so as not to cause panic. "But our people are convinced that most of Ukraine’s remaining population is very tired of the Kiev regime’s senseless decisions. And the impasse in which the country now finds itself seems to many to be unsolvable due to the categorical stance of either Zelensky himself or his handlers," they said.
At the same time, the source added, Ukraine’s elites, on the contrary, advocate for the continuation of the conflict, which is precisely why fortifications are being erected around cities, while residents are assured that this is routine work.
Earlier, Vladimir Zelensky signed a decree on the construction of a belt of engineering barriers for the circular defense of Ukrainian cities. The text of the decree itself is available only for official use, details have not been published.

title: Everything announced at Amazon’s October 2026 hardware launch
body:
Amazon had plenty of new gadgets to share at its Echo hardware event this year, along with updates to the AI-powered Alexa Plus after it became available to everyone in the US in February. But the big news this year is screens: devices with big, beautiful ones, and those that lack them entirely.
There’s the Alexa Photo Frame, which Amazon devices chief Panos Panay describes as “the world’s smartest photo frame” and that doubles as a full Alexa speaker. There’s also the new Echo Time smart alarm clock, the screenless Echo Studio with Home Camera, a fully redesigned Echo Dot, and Amazon’s latest flagship smart display, the Echo Show 16, which comes with a whopping eight woofers and can run the full Fire TV experience by touch.
You can catch up on all our coverage below, including the six biggest announcements and our hands-on with the Echo Show 16 and Echo Time .
Three years ago, I wrote an obituary for the smart display . The category — smart speakers with touchscreens attached — was stuck with a few underpowered gadgets from Google and Amazon that tried to do too much and did too little well. Back then, I also laid out what they needed to do to improve . This month, Apple and Amazon launched new smart displays that check nearly every box on that list.
Based on my brief hands-on time with Apple’s first smart display, the $299 HomeView , and Amazon’s $499.99 Echo Show 16, a ground-up rebuild of its smart display line, these could finally turn the smart display into what it should have been all along: the family computer. Not a place to do homework or pay the bills, but a shared screen the whole household can use to check the calendar, see who’s at the door, and figure out what’s for dinner.
The Echo Time is cute, has great clock faces, and is designed for the bedroom — no cameras allowed. I’m hoping it will fill the Echo Dot-with-clock-shaped hole in my life , and its design is a fun throwback to the 2017 OG spot .
But $200?? Here’s my hands-on video and first impressions :
Watch my hands-on with Amazon’s newest smart display in this video, and catch my full first impressions here .
Amazon swapped its usual big fall hardware showcase this year for a series of smaller launches throughout October. So far this month, it has announced new Fire TV devices , colorful new Kindles , the Alexa Tablet Pro 12 , Ring’s first smart lock , new hardware from AI-wearable startup Bee , and new Blink 4K cameras .
Then this week, it hosted journalists at a small event in New York City’s financial district to showcase its new Echo hardware.
Amazon used to blast out dozens of products onstage at annual hardware events. If this October is any indication, the company has wisely changed its strategy to put more focus on each new product with its own launch. The latest round of launches focuses on Echo products, including speakers, smart displays, as well as a smart photo frame.
All products, save for the new Echo Show 16 (which might be the most interesting of the bunch), are available to buy today. This includes the Echo Dot , the Echo Studio with Home Camera , the Echo Time , and the Alexa Photo Frame . The Show 16 isn’t launching until December 16th, though you can preorder it now to save $100 off the cost.
Amazon has just taken the wraps off a bunch of new devices as part of a string of fall announcements . Today’s news focuses largely on new Echo speakers, with a few new smart home gadgets sprinkled in.
Here’s a roundup of all of the updates Amazon revealed on Wednesday.
Amazon’s smart home map interface that shows you where all your connected devices are has been overhauled with new graphics, features, and dynamic effects. The new Alexa Home Map is now an interactive 3D view of not just everything that’s inside your property, but what’s outside of it too — using compatible Ring cameras to provide a 360-degree view that animates cars and people moving nearby.
Even just visually speaking, it’s a considerable upgrade from the 2D map that was introduced to the Alexa app in 2023 . This new version looks similar to Samsung’s SmartThings Map View , and makes it easier to see exactly where all of your Echo devices, Ring and Blink cameras, Fire TV, lights, locks, thermostats, and other connected devices are located around your home.
Amazon just announced its newest smart alarm clock — the Echo Time . The baseball-sized smart speaker with a screen, the Time looks like an Echo Dot with Clock and an Echo Spot had a much bigger baby. It features a 3.2-inch touchscreen that prominently displays your choice of a huge selection of clockfaces and includes a sleep-sensing feature that promises to rouse you at just the right time in your sleep cycle to help you feel more rested. It costs $199.99 and is available to order now .
I spent some time with the Time at Amazon’s event in New York City and was impressed by several upgrades over the Spot, one of my favorite smart alarm clocks . The biggest is that you can set an alarm using the touchscreen, so you won’t wake your partner when you try to set one with your voice late at night.
Amazon’s latest Echo Show smart display is big, gorgeous, and eye-wateringly expensive. Announced today, the Echo Show 16 costs $499.99 (wall mount included) and is available to preorder now . There’s a Nanomatte display option for $569.99 , plus a $100 preorder discount ahead of its release later this year.
After spending time with the device at a small media event in New York City this week, I think the Echo Show 16 could be the versatile family hub Alexa users have been asking for. The sleek hardware brings with it a completely new software experience, including better smart home controls, a much-improved calendar interface, and a real photo frame option — all fully customizable.
Amazon is giving its premium smart speaker a camera. The new Echo Studio with Home Camera, announced today as part of Amazon’s big blast of announcements, has a built-in camera for monitoring a room while you’re away, showing things to Alexa, and, soon, to use with video calls on Fire TV devices. It’s an iteration on the revised Echo Studio announced last year, which had a brand-new design.
The Echo Studio with Home Camera also offers some audio updates. Amazon says a new feature called “Advanced Room Adaptation” will continuously tune sound to the space that the speaker is in. There’s also an “Adaptive Volume” feature that raises or lowers volume depending on where you are in a room so that “your music or audiobook maintains the same volume as you move about.”
Amazon’s screen-equipped smart speakers have long been able to display your family’s photos, but its new Alexa Photo Frame is purpose-built for that task. It’s designed to compete with other digital picture frames from companies like Aura , and Amazon’s incorporates a smart speaker with access to Alexa Plus’ capabilities through voice commands. However, unlike the Echo Show and Amazon’s other smart home hubs, the Alexa Photo Frame only ever displays your photos, and you’ll never be served an ad.
The Alexa Photo Frame is available starting today; it’s $199.99 for a black frame or $229 if you want to upgrade to a frame made from birch or walnut wood . It pulls images from Amazon Photos, which offers unlimited storage for Prime members, but otherwise the frame doesn’t require a subscription. The Amazon Photos app can back up photos from your Android or Apple devices and pull images from iCloud Photo, but importing from Google Photos isn’t supported yet.
A free daily digest of the news that matters most.

title: Reps Call For INEC Briefing On 2027 Election Readiness
body: The House of Representatives has passed a resolution for the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) chairman, Joash Amupitan, to, within the next seven legislative days, brief the House Committee on Electoral Matters on the Commission’s readiness for the 2027 General Elections and national election readiness. Amupitan is also expected to give updates on the Continuous Voter Registration, PVC management, election logistics, technology deployment, personnel training, electoral security, risk assessment strategies, and budget implementation. The resolution followed a motion sponsored by the minority whip and deputy minority leader of the House of Representatives, which initially proposed that the INEC chairman brief the entire House. The deputy speaker, however, opined that INEC had briefed the public in several fora on its preparations for the elections, hence no need for the House to invite the chairman to brief the general House. He proposed instead that the briefing be done at committee level. In preparation for the poll, INEC had approved and issued a revised timetable and schedule of activities for the general election. The Commission had earlier fixed Saturday, 20th February 2027 for the Presidential and National Assembly Elections and Saturday, 6th March 2027 for the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly Elections pursuant to the Electoral Act, 2022. However, following the repeal of the Electoral Act, 2022 and the enactment of the Electoral Act, 2026, which introduced adjustments to statutory timelines governing pre-election and electoral activities, the Commission has now reviewed and realigned the schedule to ensure full compliance with the new legal framework. Accordingly, the Commission noted that the Presidential and National Assembly Elections will now be held on Saturday, 16th January 2027, while the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly Elections will be held on Saturday, 6th February 2027. The post Reps Call For INEC Briefing On 2027 Election Readiness appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Army to buy heavy wheeled recovery vehicle for Boxer
body: The Army will procure a Heavy Wheeled Recovery Vehicle to recover Boxer in the field, the order remains at 623 vehicles with more than five hundred being built in Britain, and seventy two Boxer RCH artillery vehicles are being bought, according to an answer given in Parliament. Ben Obese-Jecty, the Conservative member for Huntingdon, asked how Boxer will be repaired in the field given that no repair and recovery variant has been ordered. Luke Pollard MP said: “Boxer is a world-class vehicle that will boost our soldiers in a variety of military missions and scenarios across the globe. As I said in Parliament on 19 October 2026, the programme is hugely successful, delivering important capability and national benefit. “The Army will absolutely have the ability to recover and support Boxer vehicles on the battlefield, such as through the Boxer support variants and the wider force, including the Heavy Wheeled Recovery Vehicle which we will procure. “There has been no change to our order of 623 Boxer vehicles, of which over 500 are being built here in the UK, and we are buying 72 Boxer RCH Artillery vehicles. “The work in Telford, Stockport and plenty of other locations across the country is backing more than 1,000 British jobs.” The commitment to buy the recovery vehicle firms up an answer given the day before, in which Pollard said the Flensburger Fahrzeugbau Gesellschaft armoured recovery module had been assessed for the role and rejected, the department concluding that a generic heavy wheeled recovery vehicle would offer greater utility and affordability across the force. He also set out that Boxers currently recover one another peer to peer, backed where needed by the Support Vehicle (Recovery) and the Challenger Armoured Repair and Recovery Vehicle. The RCH 155 is the wheeled self-propelled gun built on the Boxer drive module, pairing the artillery turret developed by Krauss-Maffei Wegmann with the vehicle already in British service. Seventy two of them will replace the AS90 in the close support artillery role. All 623 Mechanised Infantry Vehicle Boxers are being delivered to a common build standard, and ministers confirmed last week that a planned third batch is no longer being pursued through the Boxer programme, a decision that cannot be tied to a single date because it was taken as part of the work on the Defence Investment Plan. The post Army to buy heavy wheeled recovery vehicle for Boxer first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Edmonton experiences first major snowfall — just days before Halloween
body:
The ghosts, ghouls and goblins on some of Edmonton’s front lawns were made even spookier by the chilling sight of Old Man Winter.
The city, days before Halloween, woke up on Wednesday to its first significant snowfall.
Environment Canada forecasters said upwards of 15 centimetres of snow could fall through parts of central Alberta by Thursday morning.
The weather office has issued a number of special weather statements for the city and surrounding communities.
The snow was expected to have a significant effect on rush-hour traffic.
Officials have urged drivers to allow for extra travel time and prepare for fast-changing road conditions.

title: Russian Spy Satellites Helping Iran’s Allies Target Sites in Saudi Arabia – AP
body:
Russian satellites have consistently appeared in the skies above facilities in Saudi Arabia that Iranian-backed Houthis and Iraqi militia groups have struck with missiles and drones over the past several months, the Associated Press reported Tuesday.
Nawaf Obaid, founder of the Geneva-based firm AURORAH Geosignal Intelligence, told the news agency that he and his colleagues tracked 72 Russian military and government satellites between July and October, finding them orbiting above Saudi sites before and after they were attacked.
“What we found is a 100% match,” Obaid said.
The targeted facilities include Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline, which was forced to shut down immediately after it was attacked in September.
Another example is the Kind Fahd Air Base. When the base was attacked last month, an Italian fighter jet was struck while a nearby Saudi aircraft was left unscathed.
Obaid said the apparent precision of the strike on Kind Fahd suggests vital intelligence is being collected and transferred for Houthi and Iraqi militia targeting, given that the groups lack sophisticated reconnaissance capabilities on their own.
An official briefed on Saudi investigations into the recent attacks told AP that evidence showed Russian satellites were being used for targeting. A senior Houthi official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Iranian military advisers are directly providing the Russian reconnaissance information.
Moscow is one of Tehran’s closest partners and has repeatedly condemned the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran. In 2025, the two countries signed a strategic partnership agreement that includes provisions for countering shared threats.
American officials, including President Donald Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, have sought to minimize a growing number of reports that Russia is actively helping Iran target U.S. forces in the Middle East.
Trump claimed last week that Russia is “doing very little, if anything” to help Iran in the war. That came as President Vladimir Putin reiterated that Russia is ready to play a mediating role in ending the conflict.

title: Ethiopia expects to receive four S-400 air defense system batteries from Russia — PM
body:
NAIROBI, October 28. /TASS/. Addis Ababa expects to receive four S-400 air defense system batteries from Moscow, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali reported.
"Additionally, Ethiopia will receive four S-400 air defense system batteries," he wrote on his X page.
The prime minister's statement comes amid his participation in the 3rd Russia-Africa Summit, which is taking place in Moscow on October 28-29. Russia and Ethiopia have been developing military-industrial cooperation for many years. In July 2021, the two countries signed several agreements aimed at modernizing the Ethiopian army, transferring technologies, and training servicemen.

title: Ukraine secures $404.5 mln from Japan, World Bank for healthcare – PM
body:
Ukraine has attracted an additional $404.5 million from Japan and the World Bank under the THRIVE project to develop the healthcare system. The funds have already been received by the state budget, Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky said.

"Of this amount, $304.5 million was secured through financial support from the Japanese government, while another $100 million was provided in the form of a loan from the International Development Association," Koretsky wrote on Telegram.

The prime minister recalled that the THRIVE project aims to improve the efficiency of the Medical Guarantees Program and enhance the quality and accessibility of healthcare services.

According to him, Ukraine has received a total of $701.7 million under the project to date.

title: Four killed as truck rams into commercial bus in Lagos
body: Four people, including a commercial bus driver, have died, while 13 passengers sustained critical injuries after a truck rammed into a fully loaded bus on Alaro City Bridge in Epe, Lagos State, on Wednesday. Among the injured were market women reportedly travelling to a village market in the area. The identities of the deceased and injured victims could not be ascertained as of press time. However, emergency responders said the victims were evacuated to a mortuary and a public health facility in the area. The General Manager of the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA), Olalekan Bakare-Oki, disclosed in a statement on Wednesday that the crash occurred on the bridge inward T-Junction, Epe. He said preliminary accounts indicated that the truck rammed into the commercial bus while both vehicles were navigating the single-lane bridge, leaving several victims trapped in the wreckage. According to him, the collision killed four occupants of the commercial bus, including its driver, while 13 other passengers sustained critical injuries. “The truck driver also suffered severe injuries, including the loss of both legs, which became trapped in the wreckage following the impact,” he added. Bakare-Oki said LASTMA operatives, working alongside personnel of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), participated in the rescue and evacuation operations. “The four deceased victims were evacuated to a mortuary, while the Lagos State Ambulance Service transported the 13 injured passengers to a nearby medical facility for urgent treatment,” he said. Personnel of the Epe Police Division also provided security at the scene to facilitate rescue operations and protect emergency responders. The LASTMA general manager expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and wished the injured victims a speedy recovery. He urged motorists to exercise caution and comply with traffic regulations, particularly when driving on bridges, narrow roads and other sections with limited manoeuvring space. He added that LASTMA personnel implemented traffic management measures to ease congestion caused by the crash and restore the free flow of traffic along the affected corridor. Bakare-Oki reiterated the agency’s commitment to road safety and effective collaboration with other emergency response agencies. He urged motorists to maintain safe following distances, observe speed limits and avoid dangerous driving manoeuvres. He also warned that reckless driving on narrow bridges and other constricted roadways could result in fatal accidents.

title: Three Russian air defense assets hit over past 24 hours, General Staff says
body:
Ukrinform reports the development, citing the General Staff press service’s post on Telegram .
“On October 27 and overnight into October 28, units of Ukraine’s Defense Forces struck three enemy air defense assets on Russian territory, as well as a Russian military supply depot in temporarily occupied Donetsk region,” the post reads.
The targets included a Russian Tor-M2 surface-to-air missile system near Rzhava in Russia’s Kursk region; a radar station near Maloe Gorod’kovoe, also in Kursk region; an electronic warfare station near Semyachky in Russia’s Bryansk region; and a Russian military logistics depot near Valerianivka in Donetsk region.
The General Staff explained that each air defense system, radar, or electronic warfare station struck temporarily creates a gap in the enemy’s air defense network. The more such gaps there are, the greater the opportunities for Ukraine’s Defense Forces to deploy unmanned systems across all operational levels.
“Operations against key enemy military targets will continue until Russia’s armed aggression against Ukraine is completely halted,” the General Staff said.
As Ukrinform previously reported, Ukraine’s Defense Forces struck a drone launch site near Donetsk and Russian military depots on October 22 and overnight into October 23.

title: UK Set For Cautious Budget As Borrowing Costs Climb
body: Britain’s finance minister John Healey will unveil his first budget Wednesday, as he juggles commitments to defence spending and easing household bills with little financial room to manoeuvre. It could prove to be a tall order for Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s new administration as rising inflation and borrowing costs — largely a consequence of the US-Iran war — increase the government’s debt pile and heap pressure on businesses and individuals. “We can’t stop these shocks that hit Britain, but we can make Britain more resilient when they do,” Healey said in a statement released on the eve of the Labour government’s budget. “This budget is about getting through this difficult moment,” he said, adding that it would provide “breathing space” for households and “targeted support” for businesses. Burnham, who replaced Keir Starmer as prime minister in July, said Monday the latest annual tax and spending plans will set out how the government intends to finance the defence investment programme laid out by his predecessor. Healey is expected to delay until next year details of how Britain will meet NATO’s target of defence spending reaching 3.5 per cent of GDP by 2035. Healey resigned as defence minister under Starmer, accusing the Treasury of insufficient military funding. Labour had ruled out rises to income and capital gains tax, raising the prospect of spending cuts to balance the books, according to analysts. ‘Small-Scale’ Budget Healey, whose official title is chancellor of the exchequer, has also pledged to abide by the rules laid out by his predecessor Rachel Reeves, which state that day-to-day spending must balance with government tax receipts. The chancellor is expected to use a windfall tax on banks to fund a package of spending measures to help households manage rising energy bills. “This budget will largely be a stopgap that will tide the government over before a more significant policy overhaul in 2027,” said Alexander Harvey, UK economist at Oxford Economics. “The measures will be fairly small-scale ones to ease the cost of living, as well as other relatively low-cost policies,” he added. Some relatively low-cost relief measures have already been announced, including cuts to tariffs on more than 100 imported goods and an expansion of the parental pay regime. Further measures could include an extension of a freeze on fuel duty, more targeted help for the poorest households and an increase in the minimum wage, according to reports. Surging diesel costs at the pump helped push Britain’s annual inflation rate to 3.5 per cent in September, the highest rate for nearly a year. The government last week approved drilling in a North Sea gas field, claiming the move was aimed at boosting energy security rather than cutting bills. The budget will also include measures to reduce “pointless paperwork” to lower costs for businesses, according to Healey. A package of investment in artificial intelligence safety was announced by the Treasury over the weekend, amid growing global concerns over the cyber and biological risks posed by AI. Surging Borrowing Costs The government’s fiscal headroom of £23.6 billion ($31.4 billion) is expected to be slashed in an update given alongside the budget, as higher borrowing costs hike the state’s debt repayments. The Office for Budget Responsibility, an independent financial watchdog, will on Wednesday also publish its latest UK growth and inflation forecasts. Government bond yields around the world have struck multi-decade highs in recent weeks as wider inflation climbs largely because of energy prices soaring on wars in the Middle East and Ukraine. Rising inflation has cemented expectations that the Bank of England will hike its benchmark interest rate next month, further pressuring Britons holding loans, including mortgages. The post UK Set For Cautious Budget As Borrowing Costs Climb appeared first on Channels Television .

title: South-East: Abia records 460,011 new voters, only 21,528 collect PVCs
body: By Steve Oko, Anayo Okoli, Emmanuel Iheaka, Vincent Ujumadu, Jeff Agbodo and Chinedu Adonu With preparations for the 2027 general elections gathering momentum, the collection of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) has emerged as a major concern in the South-East, where the region accounts for the lowest share of Nigeria’s registered voters. While the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has reported progress in some states, the absence of updated figures in others has made it difficult to assess the overall level of PVC collection across the geopolitical zone. INEC statistics show that the South-East has 11,976,218 registered voters, representing 11.58 per cent of Nigeria’s national voter register of 103,428,715. The North-West leads with 25,083,411 registered voters, representing 24.25 per cent, followed by the South-West with 19,614,274, or 18.96 per cent. The North-Central has 16,965,787 registered voters, representing 16.41 per cent, while the South-South accounts for 15,823,550, or 15.30 per cent. The North-East has 13,965,475 registered voters, representing 13.51 per cent. The figures underscore the disparity in voter registration across the six geopolitical zones and the need for increased mobilisation in the South-East ahead of the 2027 elections. Investigations by Vanguard indicate that PVC distribution and collection in the region remain uneven, with some state offices yet to release updated statistics. Abia: Only 21,528 of 460,011 new registrants collect PVCs Only 21,528 of the additional voters registered in Abia State have collected their Permanent Voter Cards ahead of the 2027 general elections, INEC has said. The figure represents about 4.7 per cent of the 460,011 additional registrants, raising concerns about the pace of collection as preparations for the elections intensify. The Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Abia State, Professor Sylvia Agu, told Vanguard that the state had 2,620,151 registered voters for the 2027 elections, compared with 2,180,140 in 2023. The difference between the two figures represents an increase of 440,011 registered voters. Agu said 21,528 PVCs had been collected as of October 22, 2026, explaining that the cards had not all arrived in the state, as INEC was receiving them in batches. She said the commission expected more PVCs to arrive and commended newly registered voters for their enthusiasm in collecting their cards. The REC added that INEC had been sensitising residents on the importance of PVC collection and expressed optimism that the exercise would record significant success in the state. Imo, Ebonyi yet to release updated figures In Imo State, INEC is yet to release certified figures for registered voters and PVC collection as it continues to address issues arising from the display of the voters’ register. The Head of Voter Education and Publicity of INEC in the state, Mrs Emmanuella Ben-Opara, told Vanguard that the commission was reviewing complaints, including reports that some persons listed in the register were deceased. She said it would be premature to release final figures while the process was ongoing. “We still have more than two months to the election. You know we just displayed the voters’ register, and now we are dealing with issues arising from the register. Some people coming to say that some persons whose names are there are dead. So, we have to look at these things and address them,” she said. Ben-Opara, however, described the rate of PVC collection in the state as encouraging, although she declined to provide figures. “People are collecting their PVCs and the rate is encouraging, but I can’t give you the number now. It is a public document which we will make available when the process is completed,” she added. In Ebonyi State, INEC said it had commenced the distribution of PVCs to newly registered voters but did not provide figures on the number of cards collected or the updated voter register. The Head of Voter Education in the state, Mr Victor Okoh, said the commission’s Information and Communications Technology (ICT) department was still compiling the relevant data. He said the available figure for registered voters remained the 1,558,840 recorded in the register used for the 2023 general elections, pending the completion of the updated register. Okoh said the number of PVCs collected by newly registered voters would be determined after the ongoing distribution exercise had been concluded. “For the number of registered voters, what I can give you for now is the register used for the 2023 general elections, which stood at 1,558,840. The ICT department is still gathering the data for this year’s register, which will soon be ready,” he said. He urged eligible voters to take advantage of the ongoing exercise to collect their PVCs ahead of the 2027 elections. Anambra gets 5,720 BVAS, deploys 22,280 ad hoc staff INEC has procured 5,720 Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) machines and plans to deploy 22,280 ad hoc staff for the 2027 general elections in Anambra State. The REC in the state, Dr Elizabeth Agwu, disclosed this in Awka, saying the commission had also conducted an infrastructural audit and upgraded its technological facilities to ensure the smooth conduct of the polls. Agwu said INEC had intensified personnel training and improved its information and communications technology infrastructure as part of efforts to deliver credible elections. She warned political parties and candidates against attempting to induce electoral officials, stressing that anyone found culpable would be prosecuted. The REC also said electoral fraud and attempts to manipulate the process would not be tolerated. As part of measures to address electoral malpractices, Agwu said INEC had begun relocating offices operating within local government secretariats to alternative locations. She added that contracts had been awarded for the construction of storage facilities and other structures. Urging political parties to focus on issue-based campaigns, she said voters were more interested in candidates’ records and proposed policies than attempts to undermine the electoral process. “Showcase your political parties, tell the people what you want to do. The people are interested in what you have done before and what you will do for them in future. Don’t plan to scuttle the election because it’s not going to work,” she said. On voter registration, Agwu said about 2.844 million people had registered to vote in Anambra State. She said those who registered between January and July during the continuous voter registration exercise were expected to check the displayed registers and collect their PVCs at INEC headquarters or designated centres across the state. The collection exercise for that category of registrants ran from October 9 to 15, while those who registered after July were scheduled to begin collecting their PVCs on November 15. Enugu INEC officials unavailable for comment Efforts by Vanguard to obtain the reaction of INEC in Enugu State on PVC collection and other electoral issues were unsuccessful, as the REC, Dr Chukwuemeka Chukwu, and the Head of Voter Education were unavailable during a visit to the commission’s office. A receptionist declined to provide the officials’ contact details, insisting that the reporter submit a formal application to the REC for approval before any official could speak with him. Attempts to reach the REC and the Head of Voter Education for comments were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. South-East monarchs target 80% voter participation Meanwhile, traditional rulers in the South-East have set a target of between 60 and 80 per cent voter participation in the 2027 general elections, pledging to mobilise eligible voters across the region to collect their PVCs and exercise their civic rights. The Chairman of the South-East Traditional Rulers Council, HRM Eze Linus Nto Mbah, told Vanguard that traditional institutions were taking voter mobilisation seriously in a bid to reverse the low participation recorded in previous elections. Mbah said the monarchs had resolved to intensify grassroots sensitisation and encourage eligible voters, including Igbo people living outside the South-East, to participate in the elections. He disclosed that the traditional rulers had also agreed to discourage ceremonies and social engagements from January 3, 2027, until after the elections to enable people to focus on electoral participation. “We want to make sure that everybody participates, at least up to 60 or 80 per cent. We are spending resources on this,” Mbah said. He explained that increased participation would give the region a clearer picture of its voting strength and enable more eligible citizens to exercise their democratic rights. On PVC collection, the monarch said the exercise was still ongoing, adding that he would seek updated information on the collection rate. Mbah urged residents to obtain their PVCs and vote for candidates of their choice, stressing the importance of active participation in the democratic process. Igbo youths challenge INEC on PVC distribution The Coalition of South East Youth Leaders (COSEYL) has challenged INEC to ensure the timely distribution of PVCs and guarantee credible elections in the South-East in 2027. The group warned that no eligible voter in the zone should be disenfranchised by administrative delays, logistical failures or difficulties accessing PVCs. COSEYL President-General, Comrade Goodluck Ibem, told Vanguard that INEC must translate its assurances on electoral preparedness into verifiable results capable of inspiring public confidence. He urged the commission to improve PVC collection procedures, strengthen voter education, communicate clearly with the public and ensure the neutrality of electoral officials. “Our message to INEC is simple: Prepare thoroughly, communicate clearly, treat every voter fairly, and ensure that every vote is accurately counted,” the group said. COSEYL also urged INEC to strengthen electoral technology, establish effective channels for resolving complaints and engage youth organisations across the region in voter education and peaceful electoral participation. The group clarified that it was not demanding preferential treatment for the South-East but equal access to the electoral process and protection of every eligible citizen’s voting rights. It urged young people to collect their PVCs, verify their registration details, reject vote-buying and political violence, and make informed choices at the polls. “The time to address electoral challenges is before election day, not after the damage has been done,” COSEYL said, urging INEC to demonstrate its readiness through transparent and measurable action ahead of the 2027 general elections. The post South-East: Abia records 460,011 new voters, only 21,528 collect PVCs appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Niger Miners’ Saga: NSCDC death cell cleaned to destroy evidence, probe panel member says
body:
The cell of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps ( NSCDC ) where 33 suspected illegal miners died in Minna, Niger State, was allegedly washed, disinfected and renumbered in an attempt to destroy evidence, a member of the federal government’s investigation committee has said.
Deji Adeyanju, a lawyer and human rights activist who served on the 10-member Independent Investigation Committee, disclosed this in a post on his social media account on Wednesday, citing findings in the committee’s report.
“NSCDC Cell was washed clean, disinfected, renumbered in an attempt to destroy evidence after the death of 33 miners,” Mr Adeyanju wrote.
The allegation raises further questions about the handling of evidence following the deaths of suspected illegal miners in NSCDC custody in Minna in September.
The latest disclosure follows Mr Adeyanju’s earlier post announcing that the committee had submitted its report to the federal government and recommended prosecuting officers involved in the deaths for murder and other offences.
He also said the committee recommended a comprehensive overhaul of the NSCDC’s leadership, compensation for the victims’ families and the formalisation of artisanal mining.
On Wednesday, the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, said the committee had described the deaths as a preventable custodial tragedy caused by severe overcrowding, inadequate ventilation, prolonged exposure to extreme heat and dehydration.
In a statement on his official Facebook page, Mr Tunji-Ojo said the committee found that these conditions, not a disease outbreak, led to the deaths.
The minister added that the report had been transmitted to the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation for judicial action. He also warned that officers who attempted to conceal, disrupt, or destroy evidence would be held accountable.
The federal government constituted the independent committee on 19 September following President Bola Tinubu’s directive for a full and transparent investigation into the deaths.
The incident followed the arrest of suspected illegal miners during operations in Minna on 15 and 16 September. Niger State NSCDC Commandant Suberu Aniviye and 20 other officers were subsequently suspended in connection with the incident.
On 27 October, TheCable reported that the committee had identified asphyxiation, or the deprivation of adequate oxygen, as the cause of death. Committee chairman Jonathan Kure said investigators inspected the detention facility, conducted autopsies and collected witness statements and forensic evidence.
The minister’s subsequent statement attributed the deaths to conditions inside the cell and described the incident as preventable.
The allegation that the cell was cleaned, disinfected and renumbered has not been independently verified by PREMIUM TIMES. The committee’s full report and any official response from the NSCDC on the specific allegation were not immediately available.

title: Eleven of sixteen Protector drones now delivered
body: Sixteen Protector RG Mk1 air vehicles have been bought for the Royal Air Force and eleven have been delivered into service, with the remainder still in test and evaluation with the manufacturer, according to an answer given in Parliament. Ben Obese-Jecty, the Conservative member for Huntingdon, asked how many MQ-9B Protector RG-1 are in service with the RAF. Luke Pollard, the Minister of State for Defence, said: “Sixteen Protector RG Mk1 air vehicles have been purchased by the UK, eleven of which have been delivered into service, with others remaining in test and evaluation with the manufacturer.” Protector replaced the MQ-9A Reaper, which flew for two decades over Afghanistan, Iraq and Syria before being retired. The new aircraft is built to a NATO airworthiness standard with a detect and avoid system, lightning protection and de-icing, which allows it to fly in unsegregated British airspace alongside civil traffic without a block of sky being reserved for it. It carries Brimstone 3 missiles and Paveway IV bombs alongside electro-optical and infrared sensors. The fleet is based at RAF Waddington in Lincolnshire with 31 Squadron. Ministers confirmed last week that a Protector flying over the English Channel on 14 October was operating in support of defence aims and not, as the question had suggested, in support of the Home Office. The post Eleven of sixteen Protector drones now delivered first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Kano Assembly approves state police, reduces 2026 budget
body: The Kano State House of Assembly has approved a bill to enable the state government to establish its own police force. The House Majority Leader, Lawan Hussaini Dala, said the move followed the adoption of amendments made by the House of Representatives to facilitate the establishment of state police across the country. In a related development, the assembly has approved a proposal by Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf to reduce the state’s 2026 budget to reflect changes in its revenue projections. The state had initially approved a budget of N1.477 trillion for 2026. title: Three injured and one dead now reported in Kharkiv
body:
The number of wounded as a result of the Russian strike on Kharkiv's Osnovyansky district on Wednesday has risen to three, with one man killed, Head of the Regional Military Administration Oleh Synehubov reported.

"A 60-year-old man was killed... A 46-year-old, a 56-year-old, and a 41-year-old man with injuries of varying severity were hospitalized," Synehubov wrote on his Telegram channel.

title: No decision on Palantir role in targeting network
body: Palantir products are used across the defence digital and data ecosystem and that is expected to continue in some form, but no decisions have been taken on which parts of the Digital Targeting Web the company will provide, according to an answer given in Parliament. Ben Obese-Jecty, the Conservative member for Huntingdon, asked which element of the Digital Targeting Web will be provided by Palantir, referring to the strategic partnership announced in September last year. Luke Pollard, Minister of State for Defence, said: “Palantir products are currently used in the defence digital and data ecosystem, and this is expected to continue in some form. However, no decisions have been made on future consumption of Palantir products and services for the Digital Targeting Web. The process for industry to engage with the Digital Targeting Web is via the Challenge Book which runs a fully open and transparent assessment and selection process for potential candidate products.” The Digital Targeting Web is the programme intended to connect sensors, decision making and weapons across the services so that a target found by one platform can be engaged by another. Pollard told Parliament last week that the department intends to invest up to £1.8 billion in it over four years, with £266 million allocated for the current financial year, £352 million for 2027-28 and £1,213 million for the two years after, and that the profile is being refined in the planning round now under way. In a separate answer, Pollard said no assessment has yet been made of British integration with NATO’s Maven Smart System, which reached full technical operating capability in June, because work in the integration space is continuing. Maven Smart System is the alliance’s artificial intelligence targeting and decision support tool, built on technology from Palantir. The post No decision on Palantir role in targeting network first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Spain High-Speed Train Collision Kills 30
body:
A high-speed train collision south of Madrid killed 64 people and injured scores more on Wednesday, with the toll likely to rise, authorities said in one of Europe’s deadliest such disasters this century.
AFP reporters on the scene in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha saw one train embedded into another after the second such accident to strike Spain this year.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Some carriages were lying on their side in tangles of metal debris at the bottom of an embankment, while dozens of emergency services vehicles were racing to and from the site.
“We are speaking of approximately 64 (dead), but this is probably going to grow even more,” Castilla-La Mancha’s leader Emiliano Garcia-Page told reporters at the scene, raising a previous toll of 31.
A spokeswoman from the Castilla-La Mancha government told AFP that more than 100 people had been injured. Of them, 58 had been taken to hospital, with 15 in a critical condition.
Helicopters hovered above the site during a frantic search for survivors, while several black vans arrived from a funeral parlour.
State railway operator Renfe confirmed in a statement that the main high-speed line from Madrid to southern Spain had been suspended after one of its services suffered an accident with a train from private Spanish company Iryo.
Iryo said in a statement that its train, which was carrying 147 passengers and five staff including the driver, “was hit from behind” by the Renfe service.
A visibly shaken Manuel Ortiz, 49, who lives in the nearby village of Urda, around 130 kilometres (80 miles) south of Madrid, told AFP he had been transporting survivors all morning in his car.
Ortiz added that the passengers of the Iryo told him their train was stationary when the collision happened, describing a “horrific, horrible” scene that “smelled of an accident, of metal”.
The accident comes one month before Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who faced heavy criticism for this year’s first disaster, seeks to overturn unfavourable polls and extend his eight-year premiership in an early general election on November 29.
Sanchez’s office said he was heading to the scene. The premier had said on X that he was “shocked” by the accident and sent “my love, solidarity and support to all the victims and their families”.
Condolences flooded in from across Spain and Europe. The Spanish royal household said on X it was “shocked and concerned” by the accident, conveying its support to the victims, their loved ones and the emergency services.
An EU spokeswoman said the bloc was “ready to help Spain if needed”, while European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen said “Europe mourns” with the victims after the “devastating news”.
The Spanish football federation postponed 24 matches in the first round of the Copa del Rey “as a mark of respect and solidarity”.
Spain’s high-speed rail network has received huge investment in recent years, growing to become the world’s second-largest after China and a source of national pride.
But Wednesday’s accident comes after another collision between two high-speed trains outside the southern village of Adamuz in January left 46 dead, which raised major questions about safety on the country’s railways.
That crash was Spain’s deadliest train accident since 2013, when 80 people died after a train veered off a curved section of track outside the northwestern city of Santiago de Compostela.
Both of this year’s accidents happened on the line linking Madrid to the southern city of Seville.
The cause of the latest disaster, which happened on a straight stretch of track in sunny, dry conditions, was unknown. Five people wearing white overalls were examining the tracks and taking photographs, AFP saw.
One of the country’s busiest routes, it was Spain’s first high-speed line when it opened in 1992 to coincide with the Seville universal exposition.

title: The Download: dead startups fueling AI and interspecies communication
body: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models When Keelan Miskell began winding down his crypto startup, he didn’t think its data was worth much. But he’s since turned the company’s digital archives into tens of thousands of dollars, selling its codebase and workspace data. He’s part of a growing market in which companies that help shut down startups sell their data to AI labs. Demand has grown as training labs hit the limits of public and synthetic datasets, with buyers seeking real-world records to help train AI agents. But the sales raise legal and ethical questions. Read the full story on the AI labs buying up the remains of failed startups . —Matthew King Are we there yet? Interspecies communication Humans are far from the only species with a gift for gab, and our furry, feathered, and finned friends could have a lot to tell us. Decoding how animals communicate with one another could reveal the inner lives of other species—and give humans a window onto how they see the world. A growing arsenal of devices and advances in AI have made it easier to study their howls, squeaks, and clicks, but making sense of it all remains complex. Find out how close we are to interspecies communication . —Cassandra Willyard This story is part of “Are we there yet?” , our series that takes stock of six technologies that have long promised to change the world—and scores them on a progress meter. We’re exploring each one in The Download, so stay tuned, and subscribe to read the rest of the stories in our new Impossible issue . MIT Technology Review Narrated: what it would take to build a city on the moon The US and China are racing to build bases on the moon, with NASA hoping to establish a small lunar city by the end of the century. But the moon is a tremendously hostile place to set up camp. A sprawling lunar base must be safe for its inhabitants, protected from falling asteroids, endless cosmic radiation, razor-sharp lunar dust, and torturous temperature swings. It also must be somewhat self-sustaining. That will require autonomous robots, nuclear power, and a way to use the moon’s resources to keep the base operating. But the chief obstacle may be one of political will . This is our latest story to become an MIT Technology Review Narrated podcast, which we publish each week on Spotify and Apple Podcasts . Just navigate to MIT Technology Review Narrated on either platform, and follow us to get all our new content as it’s released. The must-reads I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology. 1 Hackers have disrupted the US Federal Election Commission’s website The FEC filing system went offline a week before the midterms.
