Fowler stopped the first 20 shots he faced by the halfway mark of the game as the Blues dominated the game, but couldn’t find any solution for the rookie goalie. Fowler stopped 46 shots for the shutout as the Blues took over the game looking for a goal. His save percentage on the season is .942.
The Canadiens opened the scoring on a Zachary Bolduc shot to the top corner. Bolduc came from the St. Louis organization, so he was pleased to show his former mates his fifth goal of the season.
However, it was the second goal that excited the Canadiens players. Florian Xhekaj was doing exactly what the game requires of him to find success in the league. He was immovable in front of the net. He fronted his defender for the deflection, and that’s exactly what he did. He tipped it on the Mike Matheson shot for his first NHL goal.
With the injuries to Suzuki and Demidov, the first power play unit is woeful. Noah Dobson and Oliver Kapanen are on the first unit. They are not the good choices as players who can handle pressure coming at them, then hold on to the puck successfully.
The Canadiens have the 28th ranked power play in the league. It won’t be getting any better until they put some more ‘hands’ players on the ice. Alexandre Texier is a perfect example of an underused player on the power play.
Texier has a strong shot, and he doesn’t panic when pressured to hold on to the puck. Other than Texier, there are no other real viable options for the power play, until the top players come back.
Mike Matheson has earned a look back on the first power play unit. It’s either that, or go only with one defender on the power play in Hutson, and have Alex Newhook on the first unit. The first unit doesn’t have a puck carrier to bring it into the zone successfully.
The Canadiens will have to win games five-on-five. This isn’t going to get better on offence until two of their top-six return.
The minor-league system of the Canadiens is thinner than it has been since the rebuild started four years ago, yet they continue to have great success in Laval early this season.
The Rocket are in first place in the North Division with an impressive seven wins in nine games. They are benefiting from tight hockey, a good system, and some surprising individual performances that perhaps they weren’t expecting.
At the head of the class is Luke Middlestadt. This rookie is not only leading the Rocket in scoring as a defender, he’s leading the entire American Hockey League in scoring with 15 points in nine games. Middlestadt is an absolute revelation at the pro level.
Career minor leaguer Reilly Walsh is second on the team in scoring, and another surprise Sasha Pastujov leads the team in goals with six.
It’s bizarre because big names last year like Alex Belzile and Jared Davidson aren’t even off to strong starts this season. Davidson is still looking for his first goal. A lot was expected from Tyler Thorpe as well, and he, too, has not scored.
Owen Beck is up with the big team because of injuries. David Reinbacher has been back and forth between Laval and Montreal. Bryce Pickford hasn’t even played yet because of injury, but could return inside of two weeks. Jacob Fowler is also gone.
The Rocket are the class of the north, yet they potentially can be quite a lot better than this.
Brian Wilde, a Montreal-based sportswriter, brings you Call of the Wilde on globalnews.ca after each Canadiens game.

title: Ukraine seeks investment partners for AI data center – digital minister
body:
Ukraine's Ministry of Digital Transformation plans to expand its sovereign artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure by attracting investment companies to build a large data center in Ukraine, Minister of Digital Transformation Oksana Ferchuk said, an Interfax-Ukraine correspondent reported.
"At the end of the summer, we launched what we call sovereign infrastructure, which we refer to as an AI factory. It is our small data center, and we want to expand it," Ferchuk explained at the Technovation conference held as part of the Kyiv International Economic Forum (KIEF) in Kyiv on Tuesday.
According to Ferchuk, the Ministry of Digital Transformation plans to hold a tender for investment companies interested in building the relevant data center in Ukraine.
Having its own infrastructure, she said, will make it possible to experiment not only with advanced models but also with other models that will process the relevant information.
"This is an important part of sovereignty, including sovereignty in the field of AI, and to ensure rapid development, we need to move in this direction," the minister noted.
The Ministry of Digital Transformation also plans to publicly launch a national language model and a data corpus in January 2027. The project is being implemented jointly with mobile operator Kyivstar.
Speaking about the ministry's overall strategy, Ferchuk noted that it would continue developing public services and work to improve the investment appeal of Diia City in order to attract Ukrainian and foreign investment.
"When we talk about foreign investment, we also mean entering international markets," the minister added.

title: Trailer carrying cabbage overturns at Ahodwo Roundabout, driver injured
body: A trailer transporting cabbage from Accra to Daban in the Nhyiaeso suburb of Kumasi has overturned at the Ahodwo Roundabout, leaving the driver with injuries. The incident occurred at about 3:00 a.m. on Wednesday, October 28, as the driver, identified as Kwame Moses, was negotiating the roundabout. Speaking to Adom News, Kwame said the weight of the load caused the trailer to overturn while he was navigating the roundabout. “I was coming from Accra to offload my load at Daban, a few kilometres from here; the weight of the load caused the trailer to overturn. I sustained injuries to my left hand,” he said. The driver said he had contacted his superiors to arrange for a tow truck to remove the vehicle from the road and prevent traffic congestion. He also appealed to the Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly (KMA) to deploy its towing vehicle to assist in clearing the trailer and ease traffic flow around the roundabout. Some eyewitnesses who spoke to Adom News said they rushed away from the scene when they noticed the trailer overturning to avoid being caught up in the incident. “When we saw the trailer overturning, we quickly moved away to avoid any casualties. However, we saw that the driver had been injured,” said an eyewitness. The eyewitnesses cautioned that the failure to remove the overturned trailer promptly could lead to severe traffic congestion along the stretch, particularly during the morning rush hour.

title: Indonesian Court Jails 11 For Abusing Toddlers At Daycare Centre
body: An Indonesian court sentenced 11 childcare workers on Wednesday to up to three years in prison for abusing toddlers at a daycare centre in a case that sparked nationwide outrage. Police had arrested the workers, all women, in April along with the principal of the facility and the head of the foundation that ran it. The arrests came after CCTV footage circulating on social media showed children, most under the age of two, lying on the floor wearing only nappies, their hands and feet bound with rags. Some of the children’s mothers wiped away tears as Judge Sunaryanto handed down each sentence, ranging from two to three years, at a court in Yogyakarta on Java island. The workers were “lawfully and convincingly proven to have committed the criminal offence of participating in placing a child in a situation of abuse and neglect, as well as participating in acts of violence against a child, carried out on an ongoing basis,” said the judge who, like many Indonesians, has one name. Imedia Dwi Anjani, whose four-year-old son was a pupil at the daycare, wept as she told AFP afterwards: “These children need a lot of therapy, so if the perpetrators are only sentenced to 2 years or 2.6 years, in our view as parents, that’s not fair.” Mothers of child victims react while attending the verdict sentencing session of daycare workers accused of child abuse and neglect at the Little Aresha Daycare, inside the Yogyakarta District Court in Yogyakarta on October 28, 2026. The footage of conditions at the facility triggered a public scandal, and the centre was closed soon afterwards. Police later said they had found 20 children crammed into a room just three metres (10 feet) long by three metres wide. They estimated that more than half of the about 100 children at the daycare were maltreated. City police chief Eva Guna Pandia said at the time that the women had told police they tied up some of the children to prevent them from disturbing others. They also said the centre was understaffed, with not enough personnel to bathe and dress the children. Parent Noorman Windarto told AFP in April his son was tied up and repeatedly hospitalised with pneumonia during his time at the centre, while his daughter sometimes came home with bruises her handlers said she must have sustained elsewhere. The principal and foundation head will be judged at a later date. AFP The post Indonesian Court Jails 11 For Abusing Toddlers At Daycare Centre appeared first on Channels Television .

title: FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup: Nigeria’s Flamingos, Ghana, Morocco, Kenya lead Africa’s Quarter-Final charge
body:
The race for the quarter-finals of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup intensifies in Morocco on Wednesday, 28 October, with four African nations preparing to battle for places in the last eight as the Round of 16 gets underway.
Nigeria, Ghana, Morocco and Kenya have kept Africa’s hopes alive after navigating the group stage, but the challenge becomes even tougher in the knockout rounds, where there is no room for a slip-up.
Morocco and Ghana will be the first African teams in action on Wednesday, taking on defending champions DPR Korea and Argentina respectively. Nigeria’s Flamingos and Kenya will follow on Thursday, with Mexico and Japan standing between them and a place in the quarter-finals.
With all four African representatives facing demanding assignments, the continent will be hoping its young stars can rise to the occasion and extend their World Cup journeys.
Hosts Morocco will face a major examination of their credentials when they take on DPR Korea at 4:00 PM West Africa Time on Wednesday.
The Koreans have been among the standout teams in the competition, making the fixture a difficult assignment for the Atlas Lionesses, who will be eager to make their home advantage count and keep their title ambitions alive.
Ghana will also be aiming to continue Africa’s push for the quarter-finals when they meet Argentina at 7:00 PM WAT.
The Black Maidens must produce a disciplined performance against the South Americans, with their hopes of progressing depending on how effectively they handle the pressure of knockout football.
The other fixtures on Wednesday will see Germany face Venezuela at 4:00 PM, while Brazil take on Poland at 7:00 PM.
Nigeria’s Flamingos will return to action on Thursday, 29 October, when they face Mexico in a decisive Round of 16 encounter scheduled for 4:00 PM WAT.
Head coach Akeem Busari and his players will know that their campaign is entering a critical phase, with victory required to secure a place among the tournament’s final eight.
The Flamingos will need to turn its attacking opportunities into goals while maintaining the concentration and discipline required to survive a knockout contest.
Mexico, meanwhile, will be determined to halt Nigeria’s progress and book their own quarter-final place, setting up a potentially demanding encounter for the West African side.
For the Flamingos, the stakes are clear: win and advance, or see their World Cup campaign come to an end.
Kenya will also have a difficult assignment on Thursday when they take on Japan at 7:00 PM WAT.
The East Africans will be looking to extend their historic campaign, but Japan’s technical quality and organisation are likely to test them throughout the contest.
Kenya will need to combine defensive discipline with an effective attacking approach if they are to overcome their opponents and secure a quarter-final berth.
Elsewhere on Thursday, China PR will face France at 4:00 PM WAT, while Spain take on the United States at 7:00 PM.
Nigeria vs Mexico — 4:00 PM WAT China PR vs France — 4:00 PM WAT Japan vs Kenya — 7:00 PM WAT Spain vs USA — 7:00 PM WAT
The presence of Nigeria, Ghana, Morocco and Kenya in the Round of 16 gives Africa four opportunities to strengthen its representation in the latter stages of the tournament.
However, reaching the knockout phase is only part of the task. Each side must now deliver when it matters most, with a single defeat ending its pursuit of the trophy.
Morocco and Ghana will attempt to make the first statement on Wednesday before the focus shifts to Nigeria and Kenya a day later.
For Nigeria in particular, the meeting with Mexico offers the Flamingos an opportunity to move closer to their ambition of competing for the title. But they must first negotiate a difficult knockout fixture against opponents with the same objective.
As the battle for the quarter-finals unfolds in Morocco, African football fans will be watching closely to see how many of the continent’s four representatives can take the next step.
Can the Flamingos, Black Maidens, Atlas Lionesses and Kenya all reach the quarter-finals, or will the knockout stage bring heartbreak for some of Africa’s young hopefuls?

title: Israel's opposition must form 65-seat majority coalition with Arab parties, Democrats' Golan says
body: Democrats party head Yair Golan on Wednesday morning called for Israel's opposition to form a government with the resurgent Arab parties in the next Knesset, arguing that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu lost the 2026 election with some 55 seats, compared to the opposition's 65."Netanyahu lost. I know how to count to 120. Sixty-five is more than 55. That's how Israeli democracy works. Period," the former IDF deputy chief of staff wrote on social media, including the Arab parties in his coalition calculations."We have no future here if we don't stop being afraid...We must no longer accept Netanyahu's racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes," Golan added. "The voice of an Israeli citizen voting in Taybeh is worth exactly as much as the voice of an Israeli citizen voting in Givat Shmuel."Arguing that the opposition has a majority along with Ra'am and the Joint List, Golan said that his bloc has a "responsibility and an opportunity to form a government of change in partnership with Israel's Arab citizens."Golan further argued that the opposition won a Zionist majority, saying that the prime minister "should subtract 16 seats" belonging to non-Zionist, haredi (ultra-Orthodox) parties in Shas and United Torah Judaism.All other opposition party leaders in the bloc seeking to replace Netanyahu - Gadi Eisenkot (Yashar), Naftali Bennett (B'Yachad), and Avigdor Liberman (Yisrael Beytenu) - have drawn a red line to Arab parties being part of the government, arguing that they are not viable coalition partners after the October 7 Hamas attacks in 2023. The initial election results showed that neither Netanayhu's bloc nor the opposition bloc was able to secure a 61-seat Knesset majority without the support of the Arab parties. The political deadlock could ultimately lead to another election, although the parties may still reach an agreement through coalition negotiations.אנחנו מוכנים וערוכים לסלול את הדרך להדחת ממשלת נתניהו. מול ממשלת הדמים, מול פוליטיקה של עליונות, גזענות והדרה, אנחנו מציעים אלטרנטיבה אחרת לגמרי. השינוי עובר דרך שותפות יהודית-ערבית, שותפות אמיתית ושוויונית. לא פחות מזה, ולא יותר מזה.— Yousef Jabareen (@DrJabareen) October 28, 2026The results raised the possibility of a minority government being formed that could win a Knesset confidence vote without holding an absolute majority of 61 seats. In that scenario, Arab parties could agree to support the oppostion bloc. Members of the Arab parties have called to do whatever is possible to prevent Netanyahu from remaining in office.However, objection within the opposition bloc to relying on Arab parties could complicate such an arrangement. Liberman had openly rejected such an option ahead of the elections.On Wednesday, Joint List chairman Yousef Jabareen said that his party was ready to "pave the way for the ousting of the Netanyahu government." He had previously expressed his willingness to support a minority government, provided a series of demands were met."Against a government of bloodshed, against a politics of supremacy, racism, and exclusion, we offer a completely different alternative," he posted on X/Twitter."The change comes through Jewish-Arab partnership, a true and equal partnership. No less than that, and no more than that," he added.Earlier, in an interview with Army Radio, senior Joint List lawmaker Ahmad Tibi hinted at his faction's willingness to sit with the opposition in a government. “The opposition bloc will be able to form a government if it has the courage. We are extending a hand and are ready to help," he said.Democrats' Gilad Kariv: Israel in a 'different political reality' post-electionsMK Gilad Kariv (The Democrats) said that Israel is in a "different political reality" the morning after the 2026 Knesset elections and called for the opposition bloc to work with Arab parties.“The fully right-wing coalition has lost quite a few seats. It will most likely be unable to form a government in a similar configuration," he wrote on X/Twitter.להרים את הראש ולהמתין לתוצאות האמת הסופיות. אנחנו לא נוותר על המדינה. תמונת המצב הבוקר מורכבת, אבל טובה הרבה יותר מזו שהייתה לפני ארבע שנים, בבוקר שאחרי יום הבחירות. אנחנו במציאות פוליטית אחרת. קואליצית הימין על מלא מלא אבדה לא מעט מנדטים. ככל הנראה היא לא תוכל להקים ממשלה במתכונת דומה. האופוזיציה התחזקה – גם ביצוג של הציבור היהודי הליברלי וגם בייצוג של הציבור הערבי. רוב ממש לא קטן – בפער של מאות אלפים - הצביע נגד בנימין נתניהו. כל זה כאשר בישראל מושלת ממשלה כוחנית ודורסנית ללא גבולות, שסיימה קדנציה מלאה תוך פיזור עשרות מליארדים לסקטורים המועדפים שלה, ובמצב שבו נשיא ארה"ב התערב בבחירות לטובת נתניהו. זה קרה בזכות התגייסות אזרחית אדירה. הציבור היהודי הליברלי והדמוקרטי יצא לקלפיות כפי שיצא לרחובות, כדי למתוח קו אדום ברור מול קואליצית ההפיכה המשטרית, ההפקרה וההשתמטות. חווינו חודשים ארוכים של התעוררות ציבורית ופוליטית מרשימה וחסרת תקדים שלא תתפוגג ותעלם, אם נשכיל לשמור ולטפח אותה - וכך נעשה. הציבור הערבי יצא להצביע בהמוניו כדי להוכיח שבן גביר הגזען הוא לא בעל הבית וכי לא ניתן להתעלם מ-20% מאזרחי המדינה. אמרנו לכל אורך הדרך שאסור להפנים ולקבל את שלילת הלגיטמציה המוחלטת שנתניהו והשותפים הכהניסטים שלו עושים לציבור הערבי ולנציגות הפוליטית שלו, והדברים נכונים, חשובים ורלוונטים עכשיו שבעתיים. גוש השינוי אינו התארגנות מקרית או רגעית. נלחמו יחד באופוזיציה והגענו למערכת הבחירות הזו ברמה גבוהה של תיאום. כך צריך להמשיך בימים הקרובים, אחרי היוודע תוצאות האמת. ציבור ישראלי ענק – משרת, עובד, תורם ויוצר – מצפה מאתנו לקבל החלטות משמעותיות וגורליות לעתיד ישראל ולהמשיך לפעול יחד, מתוך הכרה מלאה שאסור לתת לנתניהו ולשותפיו להמשיך להוביל את המדינה שלנו בכיוון ההרסני בו הם צעדו בארבע השנים האחרונות. כך עלינו לעשות. באחריות רבה ובשיקול דעת אך לא פחות מכך בנחישות ובתעוזה פוליטית. אנחנו נפעל מול מפלגות הגוש והמפלגות הערביות, וחשוב מאד שגם הציבור שהצביע למפלגות הגוש ישמיע את קולו ואת ציפיותיו. בשורה התחתונה לשלב הזה - לקחת אויר, להרים את הראש ולהמתין לתוצאות הסופיות. יש לנו עוד הרבה דברים לעשות. אנחנו לא נוותר! — גלעד קריב (@KarivGilad) October 28, 2026"The opposition has grown stronger, both in its representation of the liberal Jewish public and in its representation of the Arab public. A substantial majority, by a margin of hundreds of thousands of votes, voted against Netanyahu."A huge segment of the Israeli public – one that serves, works, contributes, and creates – expects us to make significant and fateful decisions about Israel's future and to continue acting together, with the full understanding that Netanyahu and his partners must not be allowed to continue leading our country down the destructive path they have taken over the past four years," he concluded.Arab parties receive unprecedented number of seats in 2026 electionsThis follows projections that two Arab parties, Ra'am and the Joint List, will win seven and 12 seats, respectively, according to data from the Central Elections Committee (CEC) released on Wednesday afternoon.The opposition bloc, comprising Yashar, B'Yachad, Yisrael Beytenu, and the Democrats, is expected to enter the Knesset with 48 seats, according to data from the CEC.CEC data shows that Golan's Democrats is projected to win eight seats in the 2026 elections.Both Arab parties were projected to win a record-breaking combined 19 seats, potentially making Arab parties pivotal to coalition negotiations. Netanyahu's campaign consistently warned against including Arab parties in any future coalition, accusing the opposition bloc of seeking to form a government with their support.The Bennett-Yair Lapid government formed in 2021 was the first in Israel's history to include an Arab party, Ra'am, in the coalition – a highly controversial move. Bennett has since taken a firm stance against including any Arab faction in a future coalition.Ra'am has sought to be seen as a viable coalition partner, with its chairperson Mansour Abbas announcing in August that former Yesh Atid MK Yoav Segalovitz would be added to hold the second slot on his list. The move was unprecedented, as he was the first Jewish candidate to join the Islamist-conservative political party. The addition of a Jewish, Zionist candidate to the Arab party's list has been widely seen as a way for Ra'am to be viewed as a more viable coalition partner.

title: Naftogaz, U.S. State Dept sign hydrocarbon cooperation memo – CEO
body:
Naftogaz Ukrainy Group and the U.S. Department of State have agreed to a partnership in the oil and gas sector that envisages the involvement of American companies in hydrocarbon production in Ukraine, NJSC Naftogaz Ukrainy Board Chairman Serhiy Fedorenko said.
"We jointly signed a memorandum that expands our cooperation and opens up new opportunities for Ukraine to attract American investment. The document establishes a framework for involving American companies, their technologies and expertise in projects that will make it possible to increase production and improve the efficiency of the industry," Fedorenko wrote on Facebook on Wednesday.
He explained that the United States is a global leader in the oil and gas industry, and American companies possess unique technologies, expertise and, most importantly, investment capacity. Joint projects will take business relations between the two countries to a new level.
The Naftogaz chief said that the next step would be to bring potential investors into negotiations and turn the cooperation into concrete investment projects.
For his part, JSC Ukrgazvydobuvannia CEO Yuriy Tkachuk said that cooperation under the memorandum provides opportunities for joint exploration, strategic planning, optimization of production resources, attraction of American and international co-investors, as well as professional development and knowledge transfer.
"For Ukrgazvydobuvannia, this cooperation will strengthen technological capabilities, improve production efficiency and increase output of natural gas and liquid hydrocarbons," Tkachuk said.

title: Gold, cocoa and crude export earnings grew strongly in 8 months of 2028, but NTEs declined by 3%
body: The composite weighted average price index for cocoa, gold, and crude oil rose by 5.6 percent year-to-date to 261.86 in August 2026. According to the Bank of Ghana, gains across all three commodity sub-indices drove the improvement, with crude oil recording the largest increase at 42.9%, followed by gold (2.1%) and cocoa (1.5%). On an annual basis, the overall index rose by 15.4 percent, down from a growth of 20.3% in August 2025, reflecting the dampening effect of the contraction in cocoa prices, which more than offset the rise in gold and crude oil prices. The country’s trade surplus improved significantly to US$8.80 billion during the first eight months of the year, up from US$6.69 billion in the corresponding period of 2025. This was underpinned by robust growth in export earnings that outpaced the rise in imports. Total export earnings increased by 24.8% to US$22.39 billion during the review period from US$17.94 billion in the first eight months of 2025. The export receipts rose largely because of higher prices on the international market, supported by higher crude oil and cocoa export volumes. Gold Receipt Gold export earnings rose by 32.9% to US$14.86 billion, accounting for the bulk of the export growth during the period. The increase was primarily driven by a 44.0% rise in the average realised price to US$4,374.65 per fine ounce, reflecting sustained safe-haven demand amid heightened geopolitical and financial market uncertainties. However, export volumes declined by 7.7% to 3.4 million fine ounces, from 3.7 million fine ounces a year earlier, largely reflecting shipment disruptions associated with the onset of the Middle East conflict. Cocoa Receipt Cocoa export receipts, comprising cocoa beans and processed cocoa products, increased by 9.9% to US$2.71 billion, marginally up from US$2.47 billion in the corresponding period of 2025, supported by both favourable realised prices and higher export volumes. Crude Oil Receipt Crude oil exports also grew strongly, increasing by 32.8% to US$2.42 billion during the first eight months of the year from US$1.83 billion in the corresponding period in 2025. The performance reflected gains in both export volumes and prices. Following increased output from the Jubilee field, crude oil export volumes rose by 8.0% to 27.6 million barrels, compared with 25.6 million barrels in the same period of 2025. In addition, the average realised price increased by 23.1% to US$87.68 per barrel from US$71.25 per barrel, benefiting from elevated global oil prices. NTEs In contrast, earnings from “other exports”, including non-traditional exports (NTEs), declined by 3.0% to US$2.39 billion from US$2.46 billion, reflecting declines in all sub-categories of NTEs.

title: Uzbekistan Secures $300 Million in Loans for Power Grid Upgrades
body: Uzbekistan has secured $300 million in loans from the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to modernize 60 electrical substations across the country. The upgrades aim to reduce power outages and electricity losses while making it easier to connect new solar and wind power plants to the grid. Electricity demand is growing as Uzbekistan’s cities and industries expand. Much of the country’s power grid was built decades ago, and aging equipment and overloaded substations contribute to electricity losses and supply disruptions. On October 27, the World Bank approved a $100 million loan . The ADB had previously approved a $200 million loan, with the agreement signed on October 15 . The Uzbek government will contribute another $71 million, bringing the total program cost to $371 million. Substations direct electricity through the grid and adjust voltage before it reaches consumers. The funding will be used to replace outdated equipment and install digital control systems that allow operators to monitor electricity loads and detect faults more quickly. Uzbekistan plans to increase its installed capacity from solar, wind, and other renewable energy sources to 25 gigawatts (GW) by 2030. The substation upgrades are expected to allow the grid to accommodate at least 3.3 GW of additional renewable energy capacity. The World Bank expects annual electricity losses at the modernized substations to decline by 20 million kilowatt-hours by 2031. That is roughly equivalent to the annual electricity consumption of several thousand households. The bank also estimates that improved electricity supplies could help create or support 11,700 jobs over the five years after the upgraded facilities enter service. The state-owned National Electric Grid of Uzbekistan will carry out the program, which also includes improvements in maintenance, financial oversight, and cybersecurity. With the ADB as lead lender, the two banks have agreed to coordinate their assessments and oversight to reduce duplication and administrative costs. Since 2010, the ADB has provided Uzbekistan with more than $3.4 billion in financing and guarantees for the energy sector. In 2023, the bank separately approved $200 million to digitalize 26 distribution substations . For residents and businesses, the main measure of success will be whether electricity supplies become more reliable and power losses fall.

title: U.S. cruise ship suspends around-the-world voyage due to fuel costs
body: Sihanoukville, Cambodia — A U.S. cruise ship on an around-the-world voyage that touted its cabins as floating homes suspended its three-year voyage in Cambodia due to fuel costs, forcing hundreds of passengers to disembark.The MV Odyssey set sail two years ago on a voyage to the seven continents marketed as combining long-term living at sea with global travel. Its operator had offered to "make the Odyssey your permanent home," with the purchase price of a suite for the lifetime of the vessel starting at around $230,000.   For now, it is docked at the Cambodian port of Sihanoukville on the Gulf of Thailand, with no certain departure date.The ship has been carrying 203 passengers, mostly Americans, along with 156 crew members, according to Cambodian officials. It has a 650-passenger capacity.  Its Florida-based operator, Villa Vie Residences, said monthly fuel expenses per cabin that historically averaged $1,800 have reached an estimated $6,000 to $8,000 in parts of Asia due to the war in Iran. The company said it sought to reduce fuel consumption by slowing the itinerary and spending more time in port, but was unable to offset the surging costs.   Traffic has been curtailed in the Strait of Hormuz since the war in Iran began, squeezing supplies of all kinds of petroleum-based fuels, especially in Southeast Asia, and sharply increasing prices.The average price for a gallon of diesel fuel the day before the war started, Feb. 27, 2026, was $3.76, according to AAA, and was $6.52 late last month, an increase of $2.76. "We have been unable to continue carrying the resulting operating losses," Villa Vie Residences said in a statement issued Tuesday. "Passing the full increase on to residents is not a realistic solution. Our focus now is on supporting residents, crew, and employees" while it tries to restructure.  "The company is working with residents to coordinate disembarkation and identify temporary living arrangements," it said.  However, a blogger who has been on the cruise, Randy Cassingham, wrote online that "the company has done absolutely nothing to help: we couldn't even walk out of the port, so there were shuttle buses that dropped us in the middle of town, Sihanoukville, Cambodia."  "They didn't even give us a list of hotels, let alone help us get there or pay for them," Cassingham said on his website. The company could not immediately be contacted for comment.  The ship arrived in Sihanoukville last Friday and was scheduled to depart Wednesday, according to a statement from Long Dimanche, the deputy governor of Preah Sihanouk province. He said it was now expected to refuel and depart Cambodia on Saturday, but the ship's operator has not yet publicly confirmed any date.  Built in 1993 and operated under different names by several cruise lines over the years before being sidelined by the coronavirus pandemic in 2020, the Odyssey was bought by Villa Vie Residences in 2023.  Its current cruise, originally intended to last 3 1/2 years, began in October 2024 in Belfast, Northern Ireland, where the ship had been refitted. A second cruise had been tentatively scheduled to end in August 2030.  The Odyssey is not the first cruise ship Sihanoukville has hosted in crisis.  In February 2020, the MS Westerdam was allowed to dock in Cambodia after being turned away at five ports in other nations because of fears of COVID-19, which just a month earlier had started to spread from China. It carried 1,455 passengers, more than 600 of them American citizens.  After being stranded at sea for two weeks, Cambodia's then-Prime Minister Hun Sen allowed it to dock for what he said were humanitarian reasons. Cambodia won plaudits as passengers were welcomed ashore and arrangements were made for them to fly home.

title: Etihad and Emirates lead ranking of world’s most extravagant airline luxuries
body: Etihad Airways and Emirates have taken the top two spots in a new ranking of air travel's most extravagant luxuries. Etihad’s The Residence, a three-room suite on its Airbus A380, leads the list by air passenger rights company AirAdvisor. Emirates follows for its A380 Shower Spa and makes a second appearance for its on board lounge, while Qatar Airways features for its Al Safwa First Lounge in Doha . The ranking assesses individual experiences rather than airlines as a whole, comparing amenities that extend beyond conventional first and business-class seats. The top 10 airline luxuries Etihad Airways – The Residence: 98/100 Emirates – A380 Shower Spa: 91/100 Swiss – First Grand Suite: 88/100 Air France – La Première private airport suites: 85/100 Singapore Airlines – Suites: 82/100 Lufthansa – Allegris Suite Plus: 80/100 Japan Airlines – A350-1000 First Class: 78/100 Emirates – A380 Onboard Lounge: 76/100 Qatar Airways – Al Safwa First Lounge: 72/100 Virgin Atlantic – Retreat Suite: 68/100 Etihad’s three-room suite takes first place The Residence tops the list with 98 points out of a possible 100. Available on Etihad’s A380 , it accommodates up to two passengers and comprises a living room, a separate bedroom with a double bed and an en suite shower room. The layout gives travellers distinct spaces for dining, relaxing and sleeping, with a private shower adding another feature rarely found on a commercial aircraft. Emirates takes second place with 91 points for its A380 Shower Spa. Available to first-class passengers, the facilities include a vanity area, changing space and heated flooring. The Dubai airline also ranks eighth, scoring 76 points for its A380 Onboard Lounge. Open to first and business-class passengers, the space has a dedicated bartender and seating where travellers can gather for drinks and light bites. “Premium air travel has become an arms race. A lie-flat seat is no longer enough to stand out: airlines are now competing with bedrooms, showers, private lounges and spaces designed for couples or groups,” said Anton Radchenko, founder and chief executive of AirAdvisor. “What is striking is how scarce many of these experiences remain – often limited to one aircraft type or only a handful of routes.” Airport suites and a pre-flight jacuzzi Qatar Airways takes ninth place with 72 points for its Al Safwa First Lounge at Hamad International Airport. Its Qspa includes nine treatment rooms and a thermal jacuzzi, extending the luxury experience to also include the hours before departure. It is one of two airport-based entries in the ranking. Air France places fourth for its optional La Premiere private suites at Paris Charles de Gaulle. Available for separate booking, the suites measure about 45 square metres and include a living and dining area, a bedroom with a double bed, a bathroom and an outdoor patio. Guests can also access the La Premiere lounge and Sisley spa. More space for travelling together Several other entries focus on creating room for couples or small groups. Swiss ranks third for its First Grand Suite, which combines two adjoining first-class suites, including the aisle between them, into a secluded space for up to three travellers. Singapore Airlines takes fifth place for its A380 Suites, which feature a separate chair and bed. In selected adjoining suites, the beds can be combined into a double. Lufthansa’s Allegris First Class Suite Plus places sixth, with two independently controlled seats that convert into a double bed inside a private suite. Japan Airlines follows in seventh for its A350-1000 first-class product, which includes a personal minibar, a 43-inch screen and a bed measuring up to 123cm wide. Virgin Atlantic rounds out the top 10 with its Retreat Suite. Its inclusion brings a business-class product into the ranking, with space for up to four passengers to dine, work or socialise together. How the experiences were ranked AirAdvisor says its research drew on publicly available information accessed in September 2026. It considered only experiences verifiable through official airline or airport sources, while excluding private aviation, discontinued amenities and concepts not yet available to paying passengers. Extravagance carried the greatest weight, accounting for 35 per cent of each score, followed by rarity at 25 per cent and privacy and exclusivity at 20 per cent. Scarcity of access and the experience beyond the seat each accounted for 10 per cent. Entries were capped at two per airline, while experiences restricted to particular aircraft or routes received higher marks for scarcity. However, anyone considering an upgrade should check the aircraft and cabin configuration before booking. “For travellers, the cabin name alone does not tell you what you are actually buying. The same airline can offer a dramatically different premium experience depending on the aircraft and route,” said Radchenko.

title: Absa Bank spotlights Ezra Appiah’s solo exhibition at L’Atelier event
body: A new exhibition by Ghanaian artist Ezra Appiah will invite audiences to revisit the memories and stories held in family photographs, as Ghanaian photographer and environmental activist Reginald Boateng joins the 2026 Absa Bank L’Atelier Art Ambassador Award winners. Titled Family Album: A New and a Reborn Version, the exhibition will run from 7 to 27 November 2026 at The Mix Design Hub in Accra. Appiah, a 2024 Absa L’Atelier Art Ambassador Award winner, is presenting his first solo exhibition with Absa L’Atelier Art in Ghana following a two-month residency at the Kromdraai Creativity and Impact Hub in South Africa. In the exhibition, Appiah draws on childhood memories and archival family photographs to examine how people remember and make sense of family life. Through montage, he brings past and present together, looking beyond the moments traditionally preserved in family albums to consider the relationships and experiences that often remain unseen. The work asks audiences to reflect on how photographs preserve memories while also shaping the stories families talk about themselves. “I saw a reflection of self, a reliving of personal experiences that I then translated to thoughts and showed through visuals. So, I hope everyone sees what I see and that this work inspires them to do the same,” says Appiah. Born in Sekondi-Takoradi and based in Kumasi, Appiah completed a Bachelor of Fine Art (Honours) in Painting at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology in 2022. He is a member of the blaxTARLINES collective and has exhibited in Ghana and internationally. Ezra Appiah The exhibition also comes as Ghana celebrates Reginald Boateng’s selection as a 2026 Absa L’Atelier Art Ambassador Award winner. Boateng was one of three recipients announced at the Absa L’Atelier Art & Lifestyle Fair at Waterfall City Park in South Africa on 10 October. A photographer and environmental activist, Boateng draws inspiration from Ghanaian kente colours and coastal life. His work Our Water Turns Red, displayed at this year’s Fair, uses red water to draw attention to the environmental damage caused by illegal gold mining in Ghana. Boateng’s award includes four months of mentorship with a leading visual arts practitioner, an international residency with the other two 2026 Absa L’Atelier Art Ambassadors, masterclasses and a laptop. He will also have the opportunity to stage a solo exhibition in 2028, with Absa contributing $6,000 towards materials. Dr Paul Bayliss, Absa’s Senior Art and Museum Curator, said the exhibition demonstrates how sustained support can help artists develop their work and connect with audiences. “Supporting an artist means creating opportunities for them to develop their work and share it with audiences. Ezra’s exhibition in Ghana shows what that support can make possible, from his residency to presenting a new body of work in his home country,” says Dr Bayliss. “As we celebrate 40 years of Absa L’Atelier Art, it is particularly rewarding to see Ezra reach this moment while welcoming Reginald Boateng as a 2026 Ambassador Award winner. Their distinct perspectives demonstrate the strength of Ghanaian artistic talent and why we continue to invest in opportunities for emerging African artists. Their stories deserve to be seen and heard.” Established in 1986 through a partnership between Absa and the South African National Association for the Visual Arts (SANAVA), Absa L’Atelier Art is the longest-running pan-African art competition and marks its 40th anniversary in 2026. The platform supports emerging artists’ professional development and helps them reach new audiences. Ambassador Award winners receive mentorship, intensive masterclasses led by international experts and a two-month international residency. They may also stage a solo exhibition within two years of winning, with up to $6,000 towards exhibition materials and the majority of artwork sales proceeds going to the artist. As part of the programme in Accra, Absa L’Atelier will host an artists’ masterclass on 5 November at the Absa Ghana Regional Office, followed by an art buyers’ masterclass on 7 November at The Mix Design Hub. The sessions are intended to help emerging artists develop their careers and give collectors a better understanding of the art market.

title: Russia helps Africa’s financial recovery actively — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Moscow is energetically aiding African nations to improve their financial health and ease the debt burden, President Vladimir Putin said at the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.
"The successful operation of the African continental free trade zone contributes to the deepening of industrial cooperation and economic independence of the continent. Russia, as you know, is actively involved in efforts to improve the financial health of African countries and ease their debt burden," he said.
Putin noted that the effects of the colonial era are still being felt in Africa -- for instance, the continent’s infrastructure has historically been built to export raw materials to the metropolis. According to expert data, the share of added value in the continent’s manufacturing industry is less than 2%, while intra-continental trade accounts for only 15% of the total $1.5 trillion turnover. However, according to the president, the situation is gradually changing.
According to him, Russia is implementing joint programs with several African states involving debt to finance national economic growth projects.

title: Ukraine paused attacks on oil refineries for 3 days as Russia continued strikes on energy infrastructure, Zelensky says
body:
Ukraine halted attacks on Russian oil refineries for three days, while Russia continued striking Ukrainian energy infrastructure during the energy truce, President Volodymyr Zelensky told journalists at a closed-door briefing on Oct. 27.
U.S. President Donald Trump unilaterally announced on Oct. 11 that an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia had taken effect.
Zelensky said Trump's announcement came as a surprise to him, adding that Kyiv was ready to observe the ceasefire. Russia, meanwhile, continued attacking Ukraine's energy infrastructure .
Ukraine was repeatedly asked to halt strikes on Russian oil facilities, a key source of revenue for the state budget that helps fund the Kremlin's war against Ukraine. Kyiv, in turn, made a de-escalation of Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure a condition, Zelensky said.
In the first 72 hours of the energy truce, Ukraine suspended strikes on Russian oil refineries while its forces focused on other targets, the president added.
"I said, 'Let's respond calmly by striking other targets for at least 72 hours. We won't touch the oil refineries.' That didn't help. There was all kinds of rhetoric, and no one thanked us for those three days," Zelensky said.
During those days, Ukrainian forces acted "a little more cautiously," but were not ordered to refrain from responding to Russian strikes, according to Zelensky.
"There was the incident involving the Ryazan oil refinery (on Oct. 15). There were other operations as well. We targeted data centers and locations where Russian ballistic missiles are concentrated," the president said.
"We responded to their painful strikes, and we expect our responses to be felt by the Russians, too."
Zelensky added that Ukraine had not targeted ships carrying diesel fuel from Russia to the U.S. under a new agreement announced by Trump on Oct. 9.
On Oct. 17, Trump also postponed action on a bill introduced by U.S. Senator Lindsey Graham that would impose tariffs of up to 500% on Russian goods and 100% on imports from countries that are among Russia's five largest oil and gas buyers or help Moscow evade sanctions.
Meanwhile, the U.S. Treasury Department issued a general license suspending U.S. sanctions on Russian diesel fuel until April 2027.
Trump's decision drew criticism from Ukrainian officials, European partners and some members of Congress as Ukraine prepares for its fifth winter since Russia's full-scale invasion began.
Ukraine faces growing uncertainty heading into winter as Russian attacks over the past several years have severely damaged its energy infrastructure, placing the power system under significant strain.
Even before central heating is switched on in most regions, scheduled and emergency power outages and water supply disruptions are affecting communities across Ukraine, including Kyiv.

title: Food & Beverages sector records highest growth of 431% on GSE in first eight months of 2026
body: The Food and Beverages sector recorded the highest growth of 431.9% on the Ghana Stock Exchange (GSE) in the first eight months of 2026. Finance (131.7%) and Agriculture (123.2%) followed, ranking 2nd and 3rd, respectively. Manufacturing (120.3%) and Information and Communication Technologies (80.5%) placed 4 th and 5 th, respectively. Led by indigenous firm Kasapreko, the Food and Beverages sector has been outstanding this year, culminating in the impressive performance of the exchange in Africa. The strong performance of financial stocks reflected improved profitability, stronger balance sheet positions, and sustained investor confidence in the banking and financial services sector According to the Bank of Ghana, activity on the GSE remained buoyant in August 2026, supported by strong investor confidence, improved corporate earnings, easing inflation and continued macroeconomic stability. The strong performance reflected broad-based gains across most sectors of the exchange. Market capitalization stood at GH¢285.58 billion at the end of August 2026, representing a significant increase from GH¢149.59 billion recorded in August 2025. This represented an increase of GH¢90.9 billion, equivalent to growth of 136.0% over the period. The expansion in market capitalisation was broad-based across sectors, driven primarily by substantial appreciation of listed share prices across both financial and non-financial sectors. According to the Central Bank, the sharp rise in market capitalisation also reflected strong investor confidence and increased demand for equities, strong performance of financial-sector stocks, lower interest rates and portfolio reallocation, improved corporate performance, and broader macroeconomic improvements during the year. Meanwhile, the GSE year-to-date reached 69.49% yesterday, 27 th October 2026. Total turnover decreased by 14.54% day-to-day to GH¢2.00 million after trading 798,643 shares across 27 counters. MTN Ghana and Kasapreko traded the most and accounted for 59.13% of the market turnover.

title: A Russian cruise missile that doesn’t match its name fell almost intact in Odesa Oblast
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); A small Russian cruise missile of an unconfirmed type came down almost intact in Odesa Oblast, Militarnyi reported on 27 October. Its box-shaped airframe looks unlike the Geran-5 variant whose name a presidential adviser gave it. Militarnyi describes Russia’s work on the Geran-5 line as iterative: features tested on one version reappear in the next. A variant reported in late September can correct its route by images of the ground instead of satellite signals, which Ukraine jams, according to the monitoring channel Polkovnyk GSh. Official Ukrainian sources have not confirmed that system. The airframe found in Odesa Oblast looks shaped for a different problem: radar. Russia now builds 4,000 jet-powered Geran-4 and Geran-5 drones a month, Militarnyi says, most of them Geran-4. It is also building new launch sites for the Geran-5. What the wreck shows Local Telegram channel Odesa Info Live posted photos of the missile lying in open ground with little visible damage. Militarnyi described a compact cruise missile with a box-shaped fuselage, rounded edges, and a swept wing. The flat-sided body is probably meant to simplify production, the outlet said, and it may also cut radar visibility. A small turbojet engine exhausts through a V-shaped tail and draws air through intakes on both sides. Militarnyi read the dark composite skin as another measure against radar. Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov, the president’s adviser on defense technology, published the first photos of the new missile on 22 October. He wrote that it navigates optically and has greater range, speed, and flight altitude, and he labeled it the Geran-5 K5-K. However, Militarnyi noted that it looks substantially different from the K5-K variant already known by that name. In its 23 October overview, the outlet said Russia had started using two new small cruise missiles, probably developments of the Geran-5. How Russia got here Russia first used the original Geran-5 against Ukraine in early January 2026, Ukraine’s military intelligence (HUR) said, describing it as a jet-powered strike drone. Militarnyi now classes the whole line as small cruise missiles. Until specialists open the airframe, its navigation, range, and speed rest on Beskrestnov’s word. What they find inside will show how much of the design is aimed at Ukraine’s radar. Read also Russia is launching a faster Geran-5 at Ukraine that satellite jamming may no longer knock off course, a monitoring channel says Ukraine just caught a Geran-5 at 425 km/h—the jet drone that has often outrun Ukrainian interceptor drones since January Russia unleashes its Geran-5 air defense killer on Ukraine, equipped with British Raspberry Pi microcomputer tracker

title: Evacuate Aden Airport immediately: Yemen’s Armed Forces spox
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 28 (MNA) – The spokesperson for the Yemeni Armed Forces has called for the immediate evacuation of Aden Airport.
“Our Armed Forces have called on those present at Aden Airport to evacuate the airport immediately due to the presence of a Saudi enemy military cargo plane that is transporting weapons intended to kill the innocent children of the Yemeni nation,” Brigadier General Yahya Saree emphasized.

title: Rosatom starts nuclear fuel shipment for Rooppur NPP Unit 2 in Bangladesh
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Rosatom has completed the first shipment of nuclear fuel for the initial loading of the VVER 1200 reactor at Unit 2 of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant (NPP) in Bangladesh, TVEL (managing company of the state corporation’s fuel division) reported.
"The fuel assemblies manufactured by the Novosibirsk Chemical Concentrates Plant have been transported via a dedicated cargo flight," the report said.
Earlier, in autumn 2026, fresh nuclear fuel was shipped from Siberia to Bangladesh to enable the first-ever refueling at Unit 1. It will be carried out after the reactor has completed its first annual fuel cycle," TVEL said.
The Rooppur NPP features two VVER 1200 reactors with a combined capacity of 2,400 MW. The plant is being built 160 km from Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh, under a Russian design and in accordance with the main contract signed on December 25, 2015.

title: BRICS nations advocate for equality while using diverse development models — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Despite having different development models, BRICS nations advocate for equality and mutual respect, acting in solidarity to address pressing challenges and threats, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.
The head of state noted that new centers of global governance - focal points for the reshaping of the world order - are currently emerging. According to Putin, BRICS plays a key role in this process; it is, in fact, the world’s largest association, covering one-third of the Earth’s landmass and encompassing leading nations from Eurasia, Latin America, the Middle East, and - notably - Africa, which is represented within the BRICS family by three member-states.
"Within BRICS, diverse development models, religions, civilizations, and cultures coexist harmoniously. At the same time, all its members stand for equality, respect, friendship, and consensus. They act in solidarity to find solutions to acute challenges and threats, working to ensure global stability and security, as well as universal prosperity and well-being," Putin stated.
The Russian leader emphasized that the BRICS approaches to partnership, as well as the group’s unifying agenda, are yielding positive and tangible results and are in high demand.
TASS is the media partner of the third Russia-Africa Summit and the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.

title: Spain high-speed train collision kills 30
body: A collision between two high-speed trains south of Madrid killed 30 people on Wednesday and the toll could rise, regional authorities said in Spain’s second such disaster this year. Images shared by local media showed the wreckage of two trains strewn on the tracks and an embankment as emergency services rushed to the scene, while shocked travellers dragged away their suitcases as they escaped. The accident in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha comes one month before Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who faced heavy criticism for the first disaster, seeks to overturn unfavourable polls in an early general election. Sources from authorities in Castilla-La Mancha told AFP “at least 30” people had died, raising a previous toll of 10. Authorities have not yet given a toll for any wounded. Esther Padilla, spokeswoman for the government of Castilla-La Mancha, had told local media CMM that “it is possible that the number will increase”. State railway operator Renfe confirmed in a statement that the main high-speed line from Madrid to southern Spain had been suspended after one of its services suffered an accident with a train from private Spanish company Iryo. A spokesperson for the Spanish emergency services told AFP the trains collided just before 9:00 am (0800 GMT) in the municipality of Urda, around 130 kilometres (80 miles) south of Madrid. Rescue workers look for victims of a train crash between a high speed Renfe AVE train and Iryo train around 150kms south of Madrid between Urda and Los Yebenes in the province of Toledo, on October 28, 2026. (Photo by Javier SORIANO / AFP) “All resources are currently being deployed,” the emergency services spokesperson said, including “several fire crews, three helicopters, and two mobile intensive care units”. – ‘Shocked’ – Sanchez, who is seeking to extend his eight-year premiership in the November 29 vote, said on X that he was “shocked” by the accident and sent “my love, solidarity and support to all the victims and their families”. He cancelled his participation in a summit on obesity in Madrid after the news broke, while his Socialist party suspended all its campaign activities. Condolences flooded in from across Spain and Europe. The Spanish royal household said on X it was “shocked and concerned” by the accident, conveying its support to the victims, their loved ones and the emergency services. European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen said “Europe mourns” with the victims after the “devastating news”, while French President Emmanuel Macron expressed his country’s “solidarity”. Spain’s high-speed rail network has received huge investment in recent years, growing to become the world’s second-largest after China and a source of national pride. But Wednesday’s accident comes after another collision between two high-speed trains outside the southern village of Adamuz in January left 46 dead, which raised major questions about safety on the country’s railways. That crash was Spain’s deadliest train accident since 2013, when 80 people died after a train veered off a curved section of track outside the northwestern city of Santiago de Compostela. Both of this year’s accidents happened on the line linking Madrid to the southern city of Seville. One of the country’s busiest routes, it was Spain’s first high-speed line when it opened in 1992 to coincide with the Seville universal exposition. The post Spain high-speed train collision kills 30 appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: 'Foxtrot enforcer' charged with orchestrating grenade attack on restaurant
body: An alleged leading member of the Foxtrot criminal network has been charged with arranging for a 15-year-old to carry out a grenade attack on a sushi restaurant in Norway. Ali Namdar, 21, was recently arrested in Morocco at the request of Swedish authorities after being placed on a list of Europe’s most-wanted suspects and is currently awaiting extradition. Mr Namdar, who goes by the alias Joker, is wanted in connection with 18 offences in his native Sweden, including attempted murders. At the time of his arrest, prosecutors in Norway said he was wanted in connection with a number of offences in their country as well. It has now emerged that Mr Namdar has been charged with orchestrating an attack on a sushi restaurant in Strommen, a town 20km east of Oslo. The teenager threw a grenade into the eatery on October 22 last year after being recruited in a Signal chat group by Mr Namdar. Details of the attack emerged when the boy, who is now 16, appeared in court and pleaded guilty to throwing the grenade. He denies being involved with organised crime. The hearing was told a Signal user named Joker contacted the teenager and persuaded him to carry out the attack. Investigators concluded it was Mr Namdar based on several similar cases that could be linked to him, the court heard. Mr Namdar sought to assure the teenager, telling him “bro don't worry, grenade is not going to be a big explosion”. Police prosecutor Anja Stenersen has told Norwegian broadcaster TV 2 that Mr Namdar was charged, saying “we believe he was the mastermind and the one who ordered this attack”. Ms Stenersen said that, at the time of his arrest in Morocco, Mr Namdar was accused of being behind a number of serious crimes including a separate grenade attack, a shooting at a house and an abduction. Norway’s National Criminal Investigation Service is investigating whether children and young people were trafficked by Mr Namdar to carry out attacks, said the prosecutor. Among the offences he is wanted for in Sweden is orchestrating the attempted murder of Iranian dissident Arvin Khoshnood. Mr Khoshnood told The National about the moment a 17-year-old turned up at his home with a knife last September. The Foxtrot network, along with its founder, Kurdish-born gangster Rawa Majid , has been placed under sanctions by the US and the UK for carrying out attacks on Jewish and Israeli targets on behalf of Iran by using teenagers recruited on social media. Foxtrot has unleashed a wave of gang violence in recent years, leading to Sweden’s murder rate becoming one of the highest in Europe. Majid is believed to be enjoying the protection of Iran , where he was born, after his family escaped from Iraq’s Kurdistan region following Saddam Hussein’s war with the Kurds. Mohamed Mohdhi, believed to be the network’s second-in-command, was arrested in Tunisia on suspicion of murder in May. In January, Ali Shehab , 21, was accused of recruiting children to kill rival criminals and was detained in the city of Sulaymaniyah in Iraq’s Kurdistan region. He was allegedly involved in organising an assassination that Norwegian Johannes Natland was convicted of plotting to carry out.

title: Ginny Rice wins CIMG award for Fly Dubai campaign
body: Ginny Rice has won the Above-the-Line Campaign of the Year 2025 award from the Chartered Institute of Marketing, Ghana (CIMG), for its “Fly Dubai” campaign. The award was presented at the 37th CIMG Annual National Marketing Performance Awards, held at the Labadi Beach Hotel in Accra on Saturday, 17 October 2026. Marketed and distributed in Ghana by Africa Zone Trading Ltd, Ginny Rice built the campaign around an idea that connected an everyday food purchase with the opportunity to enjoy a memorable travel experience. Consumers who purchased its 4.2kg rice pack could participate in a scratch-and-win promotion, with the chance to win a trip to Dubai. The campaign reflected Ginny’s “Spreading Smiles” brand promise by combining the appeal of family meals with the excitement of consumer rewards. Its message gave shoppers an additional reason to engage with the brand while reinforcing its commitment to quality and affordability. Commenting on the recognition, Amit Mahajan, Chief Marketing Officer of Africa Zone Trading Ltd, said: “We dedicate this award to the consumers who welcome Ginny into their homes and the trade partners who bring our products to communities across Ghana. Their trust gives our work its purpose.” “With Fly Dubai, we wanted to give consumers an exciting opportunity to share in the brand’s success. This recognition encourages us to keep earning their confidence through consistent quality, affordable prices and reliable availability,” he added. Vinod Makwana, Country Director of Africa Zone Trading Ltd, said: “This award is a proud milestone for Ginny and reflects the trust Ghanaian consumers place in our brand. Our ambition is to make Ginny a dependable part of family life through consistent quality and affordable food products. We will continue investing in the brand, strengthening nationwide availability and supporting our trade partners. As Ginny grows, our focus remains on delivering value and bringing our promise of ‘Spreading Smiles’ to more households across Ghana.” Alongside its brand communication, the campaign used digital advertising and mobile messaging to engage consumers. According to its digital performance report, the online advertising generated more than 15.6 million impressions. The report also documented how testing different audiences and messages helped the team direct advertising expenditure towards the strongest-performing platforms. Africa Zone Trading operates five branches across Ghana, serves more than 200 distributors and directly supplies 15,000 retail outlets. This network supports the availability of its food brands, which include Ginny, Loki, Tilemsi and Plac. Representatives celebrate Ginny Rice’s Above-the-Line Campaign of the Year 2025 award at the 37th CIMG Annual National Marketing Performance Awards in Accra. The wider Ginny portfolio includes rice, spaghetti, cooking oils, mayonnaise, margarine, non-dairy creamer and canned fish, serving the everyday needs of households. Mr Mahajan thanked CIMG, the campaign team, media and creative partners, distributors and retailers for their contributions. He said the company would continue to build on the recognition by listening to consumers and strengthening access to its products across Ghana.

title: Abkhaz businesses to be required to install solar panels amid energy crisis
body: Businesses in Abkhazia will be required to install solar panels. The government sees the measure as one way to tackle an energy shortage that has affected the region for years during the autumn and winter. The initiative aims to reduce peak demand on the power grid and give commercial properties a more independent electricity supply. Under the proposal, newly built commercial premises and businesses would have to meet part of their electricity needs through alternative sources, such as solar panels. ‘Have you tried cutting costs?’ Opinion on how Abkhazia could overcome its energy crisis The Abkhazian Analytical Centre argues that Abkhazia should adopt a law on energy efficiency and energy saving. The authorities are currently discussing the electricity consumption threshold above which businesses would have to use alternative, self-contained power sources. Some businesses in Abkhazia have been using solar panels for several years. For them, installing the panels was a necessity, as they had no other way to secure an uninterrupted electricity supply. However, they received no assistance or incentives from the authorities for doing so. It remains unclear whether the government will help businesses install solar panels now that the measure is set to become mandatory. This issue is also still under discussion. Abkhazia to buy Russian electricity 'just in case' from August to November Previously, electricity imports took place only during the winter months, when water levels at the Inguri hydropower plant fell Abkhazia relies on the Inguri hydropower plant as its sole source of electricity. Under an agreement with the Georgian side, with which Abkhazia jointly operates the plant, the region receives 40% of the electricity it generates. However, this has not been enough for the past decade, particularly in autumn and winter, when water levels at the plant fall. Abkhazia’s budget has recently begun to include funding for electricity imports from Russia, but this money is also insufficient to cover the shortfall fully. As a result, the region faces scheduled power cuts every year from November to March. The main, though not the only, cause of the shortage is uncontrolled cryptocurrency mining, which consumes huge amounts of electricity. Authorities have managed to reduce the scale of mining significantly in recent years, helping to ease the problem. However, they have yet to resolve it completely. "If cryptocurrency mining isn't stopped, Abkhazia will sink into darkness." Opinion Inal Khashig: “Due to government negligence, cryptocurrency mining is ‘stealing’ nine hours of daily electricity consumption from the entire republic” The terminology, place names and views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial position of this website.

title: At least 64 dead after two high-speed trains collide in Spain, causing derailment of two wagons
body: At least 68 people died when a Spanish high-speed express slammed into a stationary train on Wednesday, with rescuers scouring mangled carriages for more bodies after Spain's second fatal rail crash this year and Europe's deadliest since 2013.Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said "all of Spain" was in mourning after the collision, which the transport minister said happened after a Renfe service was authorized to proceed despite an active red signal due to a stationary train ahead.Oscar Puente told reporters in Madrid that the red signal was issued due to a computer communications failure, which automatically stopped traffic, but an erroneous decision was then taken to restart the Renfe train.Sanchez said in a televised address from near the site south of Madrid that the "terrible tragedy" would be investigated and vowed to address any failures that came to light, adding that the causes of the two crashes appeared to be unrelated."If we need to further strengthen safety in order to rebuild confidence in our high-speed rail system, we will do so, because what is unacceptable for a country like Spain is to suffer two high-speed rail accidents in the same year," Sanchez said.Spain's opposition People's Party said it had canceled all campaign events for the day, ahead of elections next month.Trapped among seatsAt the scene in rural Castilla-La Mancha, ambulances, funeral home vans and helicopters assembled beside one of the trains on an elevated stretch of track, while twisted metal and wreckage lay scattered down an embankment where at least three carriages had plunged.The head of the regional government, Emiliano García-Page, said the death toll had risen to 68, while rescuers searching for other victims as darkness fell did not know if other fatalities would be discovered once the carriages were moved.Passengers, some splattered with blood or bandaged, were evacuated along a nearby road after the crash, which Spain's health minister, Monica Garcia, said had injured 80 people, 15 of them very seriously.Salvador Arriza described the chaos in his carriage."I was very close to the door, but (other passengers) were breaking the windows to be able to get out. Some people practically couldn't move because they were trapped amongst the seats," said the 62-year-old.Investigation under wayThe disaster, the deadliest train accident in Europe since a 2013 derailment in Spain's Santiago de Compostela in which 80 people died, follows another fatal accident in January involving high-speed trains operated by the same companies on the same line, in which 46 people died.In that collision, a train derailed and smashed into an oncoming train, prompting a debate over investment in railway maintenance.Renfe said on Wednesday that after being authorized to continue its journey, its train had crashed into the Iryo train that had remained stationary "for reasons we don't know.""The Renfe train continued on its way as instructed, and a collision occurred. The exact sequence of events, the traffic conditions and the circumstances of the impact will have to be established by the investigation," Renfe said in a statement.Iryo, which said it had activated emergency protocols, and state-owned infrastructure operator Adif did not respond to requests for comment.Passengers sent flyingA Castilla-La Mancha government spokesperson said 147 people were on board the Iryo train and 397 on the Renfe service when the collision occurred at about 9 a.m. (0800 GMT), derailing two Iryo carriages.Passenger Rafael Barcelo said he felt lucky as he had stepped away from his seat for a coffee, adding there had been at least eight victims from his carriage."We were having breakfast, drinking a coffee when we felt a very strong impact and we were sent flying," he said.At a school in Urda where relatives had been directed, a woman who gave her name as Ana fought back tears as she said there was still no news of her husband, Pepe. His name was not among those identified, although police had found their dog, Trece.Renfe said it had opened a special line for victims' families. The railway operator said it had suspended ticket sales on the Madrid-Andalusia high-speed corridor until December 13.Maintenance spendingA preliminary Civil Guard report in February pointed to defects in the track, rail or a weld between two sections of track as the leading theory behind January's accident, though investigators kept seven other possibilities open.Spain's railway safety authority has reported that accidents, including derailments and collisions, increased from 45 in 2016 to 57 in 2024 and 69 last year.A Reuters analysis of data from the Spanish competition authority showed some 25 million passengers used a high-speed train in Spain in the first half of 2026, a drop of around 14% compared with the same period last year.Meanwhile, European Commission data show Spain's maintenance investment in its roughly 4,000 km (2,485 miles) of high-speed lines has lagged other large European countries.Although Spain spent an average of about €1.5 billion a year on its high-speed network between 2018 and 2022, more than any other European country, most of that money went toward new construction. Only about 16% was earmarked for maintenance, renewals, and upgrades.

title: Analysts followed AI agent's randomly assigned preferences in 86% of decisions
body:
Amaç Herdağdelen, Hailey Joren, Alex Tamkin
When experts hand their work to an AI agent, the usual assumption is that they still make the decisions that matter. The agent writes the code, runs the numbers, and offers advice, but the expert decides what to measure, how to interpret ambiguous evidence, and what the next steps should be. Often there is more than one reasonable answer to these questions, and the decision will come down to the experience and values of whoever makes the call.
We wanted to look at whether experts really do make those important decisions, or whether in practice they defer to their AI agents. In a study we report in a new paper , we asked 50 professional analysts to do a realistic statistical analysis with Claude Code. They all had experience in causal inference—that is, working out from data whether one thing causes another. Their task was to advise a farming cooperative on whether an advisory service it was running was effective and should be expanded.
Along the way, the analysts had to make four choices between two reasonable options, such as whether to measure productivity as crop yield per hectare or as yield per unit of operating cost, and then make a final decision. To see whether they were making these calls themselves, we set up each analyst’s agent to favor one option on each decision, which the analysts weren’t told about. Which way the agents would “lean” would be decided by coin flip. The agent was told to make the best honest case for its lean, to change its mind if the evidence demanded it, and never to mislead.
Across the four analytical choices, analysts went with their agent’s lean 86% of the time. If the agent’s input made no difference, we’d expect about 50%. When analysts had already expressed their own preference before the agent weighed in, they switched away from it 60% of the time if the agent disagreed, compared to 6% if it agreed.
Afterward, when asked to explain their choices, 77% of analysts used the agents’ own arguments—sometimes word for word—but only 15% credited the agent as the source of those arguments. Analysts who followed the agents’ recommendations closely were about as confident in their final recommendation as the rest, and roughly as likely to call it the product of their own judgment.
We don’t know how much this tells us about the real world. Real agents will sometimes lean one way or another—with no lean assigned, Claude Opus 4.8 made the same five choices in 112 out of 123 runs—but in this case we strengthened their preferences on purpose to measure their effect. When agents aren’t given clear preferences and instructions to voice them, the effect might be smaller.
This isn’t a simple cautionary tale against working with AI. Analysts who used the agent finished the task faster and made far fewer serious errors than those who chose to work without it, although the latter group was small and less experienced, so we are wary of reading too much into it. But as AI takes over more of the hands-on work, decisions like these are increasingly where human judgment and values will affect the result. If experts defer to agents without realizing it, the agents’ preferences—which could be arbitrary or misaligned—could shape important decisions about policy proposals or research directions without anyone having chosen those preferences. This is particularly important for research into keeping AI safe. Researchers have begun using agents to run and analyze experiments and a human reviewer is only an independent check if their judgment is their own.
We recruited 61 analysts for a randomized controlled trial. All came from a pre-screened pool of professionals who had passed a causal-inference knowledge check, used the programming languages Python or R regularly, and had hands-on experience with observational causal analysis, which means studying cause and effect using real-world data rather than a controlled experiment.
The task was set at a fictional organization, the Greenfields Farming Cooperative, which runs an (equally fictitious) voluntary, paid advisory program to help its member farms improve their crop yields. About 40% of members have enrolled. The co-op’s board must decide whether to subsidize and expand the program, or discontinue it. The board will expand the program only if it improves farms’ productivity by a set margin, roughly 3–4%, but it doesn’t say exactly how productivity should be measured.
We deliberately left four analytical decisions open, each with two reasonable options:
These four choices led into a final recommendation: whether to roll out the program to everyone, or to discontinue it. Analysts and agents could also propose a one-year extension.
Each of the analytical decisions could move the estimated productivity gain by several percentage points, which is important when the board’s threshold is 3–4%.
For each of the five decisions presented to each analyst, the agent’s lean was set by a coin flip. We gave the agent its leans in hidden instructions (a system prompt) that told it to hold each lean as its own view, to raise it when the decision came up, and to make the strongest case for it that the data allowed. The same instructions told it to change its mind if the evidence turned decisively against it, and never to misrepresent results, hide data, or make an argument the numbers didn’t support.
Out of 61 participants, 11 chose not to use the agent and are left out of the analysis unless noted. Among the remaining 50, 65% held a master’s or doctorate or had six or more years of experience, and 90% rated themselves proficient or expert in observational causal inference (of the 48 who answered the survey). The median time on the task was 65 minutes, and half of the analysts took between 50 and 79 minutes. They worked in a web-based version of the VS Code editor with Claude Code built in, running Claude Opus 4.8 at High effort.
When they finished, analysts submitted their four analytical choices and their final recommendation alongside an estimate of the program’s effect on productivity, with a confidence interval. They then completed a post-task survey. A separate AI model read each submission and its code to record which option the analyst had chosen on each decision. Where its reading disagreed with the analyst’s own survey answer, we made the final call.
Analysts mostly went with their agents’ lean. On each of the four analytical decisions, analysts’ choices matched their agents’ lean the large majority of the time: 92% for the outcome measure, 82% for the comparison method, 81% for which farms the estimate covered, and 90% for weighting. Across all four combined, the result was 86%. Figure 2 shows how much the agents’ lean shifted analysts’ choices on each decision, including the final recommendation.
Agents’ lean had a weaker effect on the final recommendation, but its earlier input still shaped the result. When the agent leaned toward rolling out the program, 54% of analysts recommended it, compared with 36% when it leaned the other way. (A one-year extension counts as not rolling out.)
