title: Stubb's call with Putin draws praise, criticism at home and abroad
body:
Critics are asking how much the government knew ahead of the 90-minute call.
Finnish President Alexander Stubb 's phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin this week has sparked reactions in Finland and Russia, among other places.
Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre jointly spoke with the Russian leader on Tuesday . Stubb and Støre met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo last week .
According to Stubb's office, the aim was to give Putin a direct message about upcoming negotiations in Abu Dhabi to help end Russia's war in Ukraine.
Some of the reactions in Finland came from Tuomas Forsberg , a geopolitics expert from the University of Tampere and Timo Soini , a co-founder of the Finns Party and former foreign minister.
They spoke about the significance of the leaders' call on Yle TV's discussion show A-studio on Tuesday evening — starting with the question of whether it was the right time for the conversation.
According to Forsberg, there had been discussions over the past year about the need for a call to the Kremlin, but the expectation was that Russia would offer a positive gesture that would provide a motive and opportunity for such a call.
This didn't happen. Instead, he said a round of US negotiations forced Europeans to jump in to relay their own — and Ukraine's — messages to Moscow.
The call has received a mixed reception outside of Finland. According to Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen , the call wasn't coordinated with other European countries. She told Danish public broadcaster DR that it's important for Europeans to remain united. Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson has also said he wasn't informed in advance about the call with Putin.
According to Støre, all of Finland's and Norway's allied countries received advance notice about the call with Putin. Stubb also claimed all the Nordic countries were informed beforehand.
According to Forsberg, once the process of arranging the call began, things advanced quickly.
"This naturally came together quickly once the process got moving. In that sense, it's difficult to agree with all European states on how to proceed. That might take too much time if you think a fire needs putting out," he said.
However, former foreign minister Timo Soini criticised what he characterised as the independent nature of the leaders' phone call. According to him, the matter should have been discussed in advance in Finland.
"Under the constitution, foreign policy is led by the president in cooperation with the government, without interruption. At what point did this cooperation happen, and who exactly was aware of it?" Soini said.
According to Soini, the call's talking points should have been formed together in advance, rather than Stubb speaking to Putin first and only afterwards explaining what was discussed.
"That's not any kind of policy-setting, to say 'I'll make the call, and once I've made it, I'll tell you what I talked about.'"
According to Stubb, the roughly ninety-minute call included topics such as limiting military operations particularly in regard to energy infrastructure, as well as matters related to food security.
The call laid the groundwork for a November meeting in Abu Dhabi involving Ukraine, the United States and Russia. Stubb said on Tuesday at a Nordic Council meeting that the meeting will also include European representation.
According to Stubb, the call with Putin was prepared in cooperation with Ukraine and the United States.
Zelensky thanked Stubb and Støre for the call on X that afternoon.
"Alex and Jonas made clear to the Russian leader that real action is needed to reduce attacks on our energy system and infrastructure," Zelensky said of the call.
According to a Kremlin statement, Stubb, Støre and Putin agreed to maintain phone contact in future as well.
Russian media has extensively covered the phone call between Stubb, Støre and Putin, largely drawing on official statements.
Newspaper Kommersant reported that Putin agreed with Stubb and Støre to continue direct contacts, with all parties welcoming the resumption of trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US in Abu Dhabi.
State broadcaster Vesti noted that Finland's president and Norway's PM participated as leaders of their own countries, not on Europe's behalf. Other outlets highlighted discussions on Baltic Sea stability and adherence to international maritime law.
Russian politicians largely welcomed the phone conversation.
Grigory Karasin , who chairs the Federation Council's international affairs committee, suggested that "common sense" was returning to European political thinking, though he emphasised that gestures need to be followed by concrete agreements.
Duma member Andrei Klimov said the call signalled that Europeans had realised nothing could be resolved without Russia, calling it a global power whose opinion must be considered. He suggested Finland and Norway were chosen as negotiators partly because they are Russia's neighbours.
Political researcher Nikolai Toropin tempered expectations, saying no major breakthrough had occurred, "but this is better than nothing."
Business paper Vedomosti reported that Putin accused EU and Nato countries of pursuing policies prolonging the war, as he emphasised that Russia's interests need to be considered in the conflict's resolution.
Russian outlets also revisited speculation that Stubb could become the EU's mediator in peace negotiations, citing reports from Germany's Berliner Zeitung and Politico. However, Russian media group RBK noted Putin previously said he'd prefer former German chancellor Gerhard Schröder as mediator.

title: Kazakhstan Records Sharp Increase in Transit Freight as Volumes Reach 36.3 Million Tons
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA – Transit freight volumes through Kazakhstan increased 5.6-fold over the past decade, rising from 6.5 million tons in 2015 to 36.3 million tons in 2025, according to the Bureau of National Statistics. The growth underscores Kazakhstan’s expanding role in transport links connecting China, Central Asia, Russia and Europe. Photo credit: energyprom.kz The increase accelerated in recent years, with transit freight volumes rising 70.8% in 2025 alone, adding 15.1 million tons. The figure exceeded 10 million tons for the first time in 2020, reaching 11.6 million tons, before climbing to 15.6 million tons in 2022 and 21.3 million tons in 2024. The upward trend continued in 2026. According to the government, 32.6 million tons of cargo passed through Kazakhstan in transit between January and September, up 13.1% compared with the same period last year. The government aims to increase annual transit freight volumes to 100 million tons by 2035. To support this goal, Kazakhstan is building new railway lines and modernizing existing sections of its transport network. However, official estimates for 2025 vary across government reports. While the Bureau of National Statistics recorded 36.3 million tons, a government report published on Oct. 15 put the figure at 39.1 million tons, representing an 18% annual increase. Railways and road transport drive transit growth Rail transport accounted for 18.7 million tons of transit freight in 2025, up from 13.3 million tons a year earlier. Another major category was vehicle combinations, including tractors with semi-trailers or trailers, which nearly tripled from 5.7 million tons in 2024 to 16.8 million tons in 2025. Together, these two categories accounted for the overwhelming majority of transit freight. Meanwhile, transit shipments of vehicles moving under their own power as commodities declined from 1.8 million tons to 745,900 tons. Other transport categories accounted for relatively small volumes. China remains a key source of transit freight Routes originating in China dominated Kazakhstan’s transit freight flows in 2025. The largest route by volume was China–Uzbekistan, which carried 6.5 million tons. An additional 4 million tons consisted of consolidated cargo from China bound for Kazakhstan and other countries. The China–Russia route ranked third, with 3 million tons. The top 10 routes also included Uzbekistan–Kazakhstan, China–Tajikistan, China–Belarus and Uzbekistan–China. The distribution highlights Kazakhstan’s role not only in freight transport between China and Europe but also in connections linking Central Asian countries with Russia and Iran. Industrial goods make up a significant share of cargo Industrial products accounted for a substantial share of transit freight through Kazakhstan in 2025. Cold-rolled iron and steel products topped the list, at 5.6 million tons. Motorcycles, mopeds and similar vehicles ranked second, with 2.2 million tons, followed by passenger cars at 619,200 tons. Other leading categories included certain polymers, at 482,400 tons, and automotive parts, at 478,200 tons. The top 10 product categories also included coated iron and steel products, vinyl chloride polymers, nitrogen and potassium fertilizers, and ceramic tiles. The figures indicate that Kazakhstan’s transit network carries both raw materials and finished goods, including vehicles and construction products. Total freight transport falls under revised methodology Beyond international transit, Kazakhstan’s transport sector handles domestic, export and import freight. The Bureau of National Statistics reported that all modes of transport carried 712.1 million tons of cargo between January and September 2026. This compares with 725.6 million tons in the same period of 2023, 782.4 million tons in 2024 and 853.5 million tons in 2025. The latest figure appears to represent a 16.6% year-on-year decline. However, the comparison is affected by a change in statistical methodology: the bureau excluded empty rail wagons from freight transport calculations for January–September 2026 and the corresponding period of 2025. When both periods are calculated using the same methodology, total freight transport instead increased by 0.9%. Road and urban electric transport carried the largest volume during the first nine months of 2026, at 270.4 million tons. Railways transported 248.5 million tons, compared with 339.4 million tons a year earlier. On a comparable methodological basis, rail freight transport fell by 1.4%. Pipelines transported 189.8 million tons, while maritime and coastal shipping carried 3 million tons. Inland waterways transported 265,000 tons, and air freight amounted to 20,000 tons. Freight revenue rises despite changes in volumes Revenue from freight, baggage and cargo-baggage transportation across all modes reached 4.5 trillion tenge (US$9.9 billion) between January and September 2026, increasing 5.3% year on year. Rail transport generated the largest share, with revenue rising from 1.7 trillion tenge (US$3.73 billion) to 1.8 trillion tenge (US$3.95 billion). Revenue from road and urban electric transport increased from 1.1 trillion tenge (US$2.41 billion) to 1.2 trillion tenge (US$2.63 billion). Pipeline transport revenue declined from 1.5 trillion (US$3.29 billion) to 1.4 trillion tenge (US$3.07 billion). Maritime and coastal transport generated 22.6 billion tenge (US$49.6 million), air transport 12.6 billion tenge (US$27.6 million), and inland water transport 1 billion tenge (US$2.2 million). Despite the overall increase in revenue, freight transportation’s share of total transport enterprise revenue gradually decreased, from 79% in January–September 2023 to 77.9% in the same period of 2026. The share varied considerably by mode. Freight accounted for 99.5% of revenue in maritime and coastal transport, 93.8% in rail transport, 76.1% in road and urban electric transport, and 52.4% in inland water transport. In aviation, where passenger services account for most revenue, freight contributed just 1.6%. As international freight flows expand, Kazakhstan has an opportunity to derive greater economic benefits from its geographic position. Beyond developing transport corridors, the country will need to expand supporting services, including logistics, warehousing, vehicle maintenance and repair. Strengthening this infrastructure could help domestic companies participate more actively in international supply chains, create jobs and increase the transport sector’s contribution to the national economy. The post Kazakhstan Records Sharp Increase in Transit Freight as Volumes Reach 36.3 Million Tons appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: Netherlands to provide Ukraine with €1.2B in non-military aid over three years
body:
Ukrinform reports this, citing the Dutch government website .
“The Dutch government will provide Ukraine with €1.2 billion in non-military assistance over the next three years. The package is aimed at meeting Ukraine’s most urgent needs, supporting its recovery and reconstruction, and expanding opportunities for Dutch businesses,” the statement said.
The main priorities will be supporting the energy and water supply sectors and assisting businesses. Minister for Foreign Trade and Development Cooperation Sjoerd Wiemer Sjoerdsma announced the package during a visit to Kyiv on Wednesday.
“Ukraine is facing intense Russian attacks, and an extremely difficult winter lies ahead. It is also crucial for our own security that we continue supporting Ukrainians in their resistance. That is why the government is taking another step,” he said.
The Netherlands will expedite the allocation of an additional €40 million to the Ukraine Energy Support Fund this year. The funding will be used for urgent repairs and the restoration of energy infrastructure.
Ukrainian energy and water infrastructure is increasingly being targeted by Russian air attacks, causing significant damage and destruction.
Dutch assistance will help repair damaged facilities, build up emergency stocks, and train specialized personnel in the energy and water supply sectors.
The Netherlands will also allocate €55 million to supply energy equipment and materials. Through the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO), Ukrainian partners will be able to obtain these products from Dutch companies.
Sjoerdsma is visiting Kyiv alongside VNO-NCW President Coen van Oostrom, representing the Confederation of Netherlands Industry and Employers (VNO-NCW). They will meet with Ukrainian government officials and Dutch companies operating in Ukraine to discuss strengthening business ties, expanding cooperation, and removing barriers to business activity.
The Dutch government is allocating funds to help businesses contribute more to Ukraine’s recovery and reconstruction while expanding their presence in the Ukrainian market. In particular, €136 million will go toward several programs, including the Ukraine Partnership Facility.
The government is also expanding export credit insurance to reduce financial risks for companies seeking to export goods to Ukraine. An additional €19.5 million will be allocated for this purpose, on top of the €60 million already earmarked.
“Support for recovery and reconstruction cannot wait for a ceasefire. Ukraine needs our assistance now—not only military support but also social and economic assistance. Regardless of how things develop on the battlefield, energy systems, hospitals, and food production must continue to operate. Governments cannot manage this alone, so the role of businesses is crucial. That is why it is good that we have come here together with VNO-NCW. Companies that get involved now are helping shape future partnerships, supply chains, and opportunities,” Sjoerdsma stressed.
VNO-NCW President Coen van Oostrom said he was impressed by how Ukraine had managed to keep its economy running under extremely difficult conditions.
“However, reconstruction is an enormous undertaking, and Dutch companies can play an important role. To make that happen, we need to work closely with the Ukrainian government and remove the obstacles businesses face. That is what I will be discussing today,” he said.
In addition, Sjoerdsma and Ukrainian Economy Minister Oleksandr Kravchenko will sign a letter of intent on a €10 million contribution to Industrial Ramstein, an initiative launched by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
The initiative aims to restore and modernize Ukrainian companies’ production capacity by supplying machinery, equipment, and other goods, including supplies from the Netherlands.
As reported, Chief of Defence (CHOD) of the Netherlands Armed Forces, General Onno Eichelsheim said that the war in Ukraine demonstrates how rapidly new technologies, including drones, are changing the nature of warfare.

title: Multipolar world is becoming real, this trend is irreversible — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Everyone is currently witnessing a multipolar world truly becoming a reality, this is an objective and irreversible trend, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.
As the Russian leader noted, this forum - along with its themes, the range of participants, and its free and open dialogue - fits well into global transformational processes, the scale and depth of which are so significant that they can hardly be overestimated.
"We are witnessing a multipolar world truly becoming a reality, and this trend is both objective and irreversible," Putin emphasized.

title: Ebola: Survivors can transmit virus through sex, but not sweat or saliva – WHO
body:
The World Health Organisation (WHO) has explained that Ebola survivors may transmit the virus through sexual intercourse if it persists in their semen after recovery. In contrast, survivors who have met the criteria for discharge from treatment are not expected to transmit the virus through sweat or saliva.
Patrick Otim, programme area manager for emergency response at the WHO Regional Office for Africa, explained this in a video answering questions about the virus.
Mr Otim said male survivors should receive counselling on safer sex practices and access to condoms after discharge from treatment centres. He said they should undergo regular semen testing until they obtain two consecutive negative results.
“Ebola virus after recovery and for patients with what we call a viral persistence can be transmitted through sexual intercourse,” he said.
He explained that the virus could remain in certain parts of the body after clinical recovery, posing a risk of transmission through infected semen.
The WHO recommends that male survivors practise safer sex for 12 months in the absence of a semen-testing programme. Where testing is available, they should undergo regular testing until two consecutive negative results are obtained.
Mr Otim said survivors who had recovered and been discharged from treatment centres could not transmit the virus through sweat or saliva because the virus would have been cleared from their blood.
He said patients were required to have two negative blood tests before discharge, adding that survivors who had met the discharge criteria could not transmit the virus through these fluids.
However, he warned that people who were still actively ill could transmit Ebola through sweat and other bodily fluids.
The explanation comes amid an ongoing Ebola outbreak involving the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Kenya .
Nigeria confirmed an imported case on 20 October. The patient, a 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman living in Abuja, was evacuated to Switzerland with her husband on 26 October.
Although the WHO said Nigeria had no active confirmed cases after the evacuation, health authorities continued monitoring contacts and implementing containment measures.
In the DRC, the outbreak has recorded 10,060 confirmed cases and 4,887 deaths, according to figures released on Tuesday by the country’s Ministry of Public Health.

title: Moscow not negotiating US companies’ return to Russian oil, gas projects — Novak
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Moscow is not currently negotiating the return of American companies, specifically Chevron and ExxonMobil, to Russian oil and gas projects, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told reporters.
"Our position has always remained the same: we are open to foreign partners, foreign investment, and whether or not they will return depends on them, in the first place. No such negotiations are currently taking place," he said on the sidelines of the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.
Novak said earlier that Russia and the US could begin cooperating on liquefied natural gas (LNG) projects in the Arctic, as well as on the development of mineral deposits.
TASS is an information partner of the third Russia-Africa Summit and Economic and Humanitarian Forum.

title: With AI writing the code, entrepreneurial thinking is now what counts most for newcomers at Anthropic
body:
Felix Rieseberg, an engineering manager at Anthropic, has scrapped the classic coding interview. He argues that AI makes the tests pointless and that ambitious young developers can use it to overtake more experienced colleagues.

Rieseberg, who has led development of Claude.ai and Claude Code Desktop at Anthropic, says there's no longer any reason to give candidates small programming tasks. Claude now handles them better than the candidates do, he says. In his view, handing someone a little React challenge makes as little sense today as quizzing them on Assembly.

On his teams, good test scores no longer predict who turns out to be a top developer. Instead, he's watching relatively new engineers overtake more experienced colleagues. "Hunger beats tenure," he says. Rieseberg aims his post at "junior" developers, though he deliberately redefines the term. He doesn't necessarily mean people just starting out. He means any engineer without social status, power, or a network inside their company.
Why newcomers spot the problems veterans stopped seeing
Rieseberg argues that newcomers have a structural advantage because they notice problems that long-time employees accepted as givens years ago. He points to organizational researcher James March, who wrote in 1991 that organizations depend on a steady stream of naive and uninformed newcomers. Stripe founder Patrick Collison has also explicitly urged new hires to flag anything that seems strange to them. Veterans, he noted, stopped noticing those friction points long ago.

Rieseberg cites his time at Notion as an example. He was asked to design an offline architecture that people inside the company considered impossible. The data model was too complex, and CEO Ivan Zhao would supposedly never accept the only workable solution. The technical hurdle was real, but the founder's resistance wasn't. Nobody had asked him, because everyone treated it as common knowledge.
Cheap execution weakens the old hierarchy
The core problem for newcomers, Rieseberg says, is that nobody in the company listens to them. Because execution used to be expensive, organizations were built so that a few decision-makers could approve or block ideas. You had to work your way up a rigid hierarchy before management trusted you to actually build something. AI changes that equation because execution is no longer expensive, Rieseberg writes.

His first piece of advice builds on a 2011 quote from Patrick McKenzie, who wrote that "engineers are hired to create business value, not to program things." Developers should understand what their company is really trying to achieve and attach themselves to the parts that make money. A useful starting point is knowing your manager's manager's goals.

From there, he suggests picking an ambitious idea that would dramatically advance those goals and building a working prototype over a weekend. That skips the usual cycle of product specs, approvals, and lobbying designers or product managers. The key is to focus on one good idea instead of hiding three good ones among 20 bad ones. Anyone who builds a prototype that includes a new programming language, a backend, and mobile apps all at once will fail. The prototype should get the idea across so clearly that leadership immediately sees both the opportunity and the right person to run with it.
Newcomers have the edge on empathy
Rieseberg distinguishes between two types of engineers. Newcomers working on user-facing products bring a natural empathy for outside users. Long-tenured colleagues at Slack or Notion had a hard time seeing things from an outside user's perspective. Engineers working on infrastructure or internal tools, on the other hand, benefit from not knowing why something is supposed to be impossible.

He backs this up with an example from his own company. Two Anthropic engineers who were relatively new at the time, Anthony Morris and Alice Zhao, built the graphical interface for Claude Code over a weekend. The first public version shipped about eight days later.

Rieseberg now looks for small prototypes in job applications that show taste, empathy, and principled thinking. The classic coding interview isn't coming back, he says.

On one hand, Rieseberg's advice reads as a message of empowerment. AI becomes an equalizer that lets newcomers get past gatekeepers who've gone blind to their own company's problems. On the other hand, it moves the bar for entry-level jobs away from diligence and craft toward entrepreneurial thinking, product sense, and taste. Most universities barely teach those skills, and companies have traditionally expected them from experienced product managers or founders.

The engineers he holds up as models also build prototypes on weekends without being asked. "Hunger beats tenure" sounds motivating, but it assumes a hustle mentality that not every new developer can bring to the job.

title: Ukraine, Romania discuss F-16, Patriot, HAWK ammunition supplies, joint drone production
body:
Minister of Defense of Ukraine Yevheniy Khmara, during a phone call with Romania's new Minister of National Defense Ștefan-Radu Oprea, discussed the supply of ammunition for F-16 aircraft and air defense systems, as well as joint drone production under the European SAFE program, the press service of the Ministry of Defense of Ukraine reported on Wednesday.
The parties also discussed Russian attacks on ports and vessels in the Black Sea, risks for both countries, and ways to counter them.
Special attention was paid to the supply of ammunition for F-16 aircraft needed for effective counteraction against jet-powered drones, as well as the training of Ukrainian pilots at the F-16 training center in Romania: "This support is important for Ukraine. The greater the number of trained pilots, the larger the fleet of aviation we can deploy and protect the Ukrainian sky. In particular, to shoot down jet drones."
According to him, the sides also discussed Ukraine's need for missiles for Patriot systems required to counter ballistic missiles, as well as ammunition to fight cruise missiles.
"Russia is intensifying its missile attacks; ballistics are one of the main threats. Therefore, we need missiles for Patriot so that our systems can protect people, civilian, and critical infrastructure. In addition, Ukraine needs ammunition to fight cruise missiles. We are talking about missiles for HAWK air defense systems and AIM-9 missiles," the Minister emphasized.
Another area of cooperation was the joint production of drones within the European SAFE program. "Ukraine has technologies and experience that can be useful to our partners, and we are ready to develop mutually beneficial cooperation," Khmara noted.
Khmara congratulated his Romanian counterpart on his appointment and thanked Romania for its aid to Ukraine, particularly for logistical support through its territory.

title: EU fears Russia-US contacts broader than Brussels expected — TV
body:
BRUSSELS, October 28. /TASS/. European officials fear that the contacts between Russia and the US are much broader than Brussels had anticipated, forcing the EU to explore options for participating in future talks on Ukraine, Euronews reported, citing sources.
According to the TV channel, Russia and the US could discuss new deals, particularly agreements related to Lukoil assets and natural LNG projects in the Arctic, as well as the relaunch of the Nord Stream pipelines. With this in mind, the Europeans are seeking a way to participate in the talks, Euronews emphasized.
On October 27, Russian President Vladimir Putin held a telephone conversation with Finnish leader Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store. The conversation took place at the request of Finland and Norway. The sides exchanged opinions on the Ukrainian conflict settlement issues. The leaders welcomed the agreement to resume trilateral talks between Russia, the US and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi during the first weeks of November. According to Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov, the substantial and detailed conversation lasted about one and a half hours. The three leaders agreed to continue engaging in direct telephone conversations. The Finnish presidential office noted that Stubb and Store "took the call as leaders of their respective countries and did not speak on the behalf of Europe as a whole."

title: Death Toll In Spain Train Collision Rises To 30
body: A high-speed train collision south of Madrid killed at least 30 people on Wednesday, regional authorities told AFP in an updated toll as Spain reeled from its second such disaster this year. The toll from government sources in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha comes after a collision between two high-speed trains in southern Spain in January resulted in the deaths of 46 people. The update comes after a regional government spokeswoman said the collision killed at least 10 people, warning the toll could rise. “The information we are receiving is not good at all. There are at least 10 dead and it is possible that the number will increase,” Esther Padilla, spokeswoman for the government of Castilla-La Mancha, told local media CMM. Local authorities said the crash resulted in injuries to numerous people. “Two trains have collided — there are people injured,” Manuel Galan, mayor of the town of Urda, told public broadcaster TVE. A spokesperson for the Spanish emergency services told AFP the trains collided just before 9:00 am (0800 GMT) but added it was too early to speak of injuries. “All resources are currently being deployed,” the spokesperson said, including “several fire crews, three helicopters, and two mobile intensive care units”. Rail infrastructure company ADIF also confirmed a collision had taken place, warning in a social media post that the high-speed rail line from Madrid to the south had been suspended. The post Death Toll In Spain Train Collision Rises To 30 appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Iran warns any Israeli-led attack would be ‘devastating’ for global markets
body: Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned on Wednesday that any Israeli-instigated attack in the Gulf region would have a “devastating impact” on global markets. “Devastating impact on int’l markets of any Israel-instigated military misadventure in Persian Gulf region remains major concern for both gas suppliers and consumers,” Araghchi said in a post on X. The United States and Israel have in recent days raised the prospect of renewed attacks on Iran in the Middle East war which began in February with strikes on the Islamic republic. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is seeking to form a new government after close elections, said on Wednesday he could work with US President Donald Trump to eliminate the “existential threat” posed by Iran. The post Iran warns any Israeli-led attack would be ‘devastating’ for global markets appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Trump Reaffirms Support for Kazakhstan Ahead of G20 Summit
body: United States President Donald Trump has reaffirmed his support for Kazakhstan’s independence and territorial integrity and said he looks forward to meeting President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev at the Group of Twenty (G20) summit in December. The remarks were made in a congratulatory message marking Kazakhstan’s Republic Day, published by Kazakhstan’s presidential office on October 27. “Our commitment to your country’s independence, sovereignty, and territorial integrity remains unshakeable,” Trump wrote. He also claimed that the U.S. was the first country to recognize Kazakhstan as an independent state in 1991. However, Kazakhstan’s embassy in Turkey identifies Turkey as the first country to recognize its independence, on December 16, 1991. The U.S. recognized Kazakhstan on December 25 . The U.S. president highlighted growing cooperation in international security and trade. He noted the role of American companies in Kazakhstan’s economy and expressed confidence in the future of bilateral relations. The summit will take place in Doral, near Miami , Florida. Kazakhstan is not a G20 member but has received an invitation from the U.S. Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs had reported preparations for Tokayev’s participation in the summit as early as August. At the time, Foreign Minister Yermek Kosherbayev discussed bilateral relations with U.S. Assistant Secretary of State for South and Central Asian Affairs Paul Kapur, including cooperation in energy, critical minerals, digital technologies, and transportation. In November 2025, Tokayev visited Washington, met with Trump, and attended the C5+1 summit , a forum bringing together the U.S. and the five Central Asian countries. During the visit, the two sides announced 29 agreements worth approximately $17 billion , covering sectors including mining, aviation, and technology. Kazakhstan celebrated Republic Day on October 25, with congratulatory messages from world leaders. This year marked the 36th anniversary of the adoption of Kazakhstan’s Declaration of State Sovereignty.

title: Russian troops liberate two communities in Ukraine operation over past day — top brass
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Russian troops liberated two communities in the Kharkov and Sumy Regions over the past 24 hours in the special military operation in Ukraine, Russia’s Defense Ministry reported.
"Battlegroup North units liberated the settlements of Alisovka in the Kharkov Region and Barilovka in the Sumy Region through active operations," the ministry said in a statement.
The Ukrainian army lost roughly 1,160 troops in battles with Russian forces in all the frontline areas over the past 24 hours, according to the latest data on the special military operation in Ukraine released by Russia’s Defense Ministry.
The latest figures show that the Ukrainian army lost over 195 troops and six motor vehicles in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup North, more than 240 troops and an armored combat vehicle in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup West and over 155 troops and two armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup South.
During the last 24-hour period, the Ukrainian army also lost over 335 troops and nine armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup Center, more than 215 troops and two armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup East and roughly 20 troops and a jamming station in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup Dnepr, the latest figures show.
Russia’s Battlegroup North inflicted more than 195 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed six enemy motor vehicles in its areas of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
During the last 24-hour period, Battlegroup North units "inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two mechanized brigades, a motorized infantry brigade and an assault regiment of the Ukrainian army in areas near the settlements of Izbitskoye, Stary Saltov, Bugayevka and Rubezhnoye in the Kharkov Region," the ministry said.
In the Sumy direction, Battlegroup North units struck formations of a mechanized brigade of the Ukrainian army and a territorial defense brigade in areas near the settlements of Luzhki and Sukhodol in the Sumy Region, it said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 195 personnel and six motor vehicles in the areas of responsibility of Russia’s Battlegroup North over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup West inflicts over 240 casualties on Ukrainian army in past day
Russia’s Battlegroup West inflicted more than 240 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed an enemy armored combat vehicle in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup West units improved their forward positions and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two mechanized brigades, an assault brigade of the Ukrainian army and two territorial defense brigades in areas near the settlements of Glushchenkovo, Studenok, Monachinovka and Smorodkovka in the Kharkov Region and Bogorodichnoye in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 240 personnel, an armored combat vehicle, 15 motor vehicles, two field artillery guns, a Grad multiple rocket launcher and six electronic warfare stations in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it said.
Russia’s Battlegroup South inflicted more than 155 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed two enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup South units improved their tactical position and inflicted losses on formations of a mechanized brigade, an air assault brigade of the Ukrainian army and a marine infantry brigade in areas near the settlements of Semyonovka, Slavyansk, Kamyshevakha and Kramatorsk in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 155 personnel, two armored combat vehicles, 31 motor vehicles and three artillery guns in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup Center inflicted more than 335 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed nine enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup Center units gained better lines and positions and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two mechanized brigades of the Ukrainian army, two marine infantry brigades and two National Guard brigades in areas near the settlements of Belozerskoye, Bokovoye, Kalinino, Shilovka and Viktorovka in the Donetsk People’s Republic, Ivanovka and Novopavlovka in the Dnepropetrovsk Region," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 335 personnel, nine armored combat vehicles, 10 motor vehicles and two electronic warfare stations in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup Center over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup East inflicted more than 215 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed two enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup East units advanced into the depth of the enemy’s defenses and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two air assault brigades, an assault regiment of the Ukrainian army and a marine infantry brigade in areas near the settlements of Berestovoye, Novoukrainka, Tersyanka and Sergeyevka in the Zaporozhye Region," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 215 personnel, two armored combat vehicles, seven motor vehicles and an artillery gun in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup Dnepr eliminated roughly 20 Ukrainian troops and destroyed an enemy jamming station in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup Dnepr units improved their forward positions and inflicted losses on formations of a mechanized brigade of the Ukrainian army and a territorial defense brigade in areas near the settlements of Orekhov and Preobrazhenka in the Zaporozhye Region," the ministry said.
"Up to 20 Ukrainian military personnel, five motor vehicles and an electronic warfare station were destroyed," it said.
Russian troops struck energy and transport infrastructure facilities used by the Ukrainian army and enemy deployment areas over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Operational/tactical aircraft, attack unmanned aerial vehicles, missile troops and artillery of the Russian groups of forces struck energy and transport infrastructure facilities used by the Ukrainian army, ammunition depots, workshops producing and sites storing unmanned aerial vehicles, and also temporary deployment areas of Ukrainian armed formations and foreign mercenaries in 142 locations," the ministry said.
Russian air defense forces intercepted and destroyed 617 Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and two Neptune missiles over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Air defense capabilities shot down two Neptune long-range missiles and 617 fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles," the ministry said.
Overall, the Russian Armed Forces have destroyed 674 Ukrainian combat aircraft, 284 helicopters, 273,040 unmanned aerial vehicles, 672 surface-to-air missile systems, 31,439 tanks and other armored combat vehicles, 1,794 multiple rocket launchers, 36,830 field artillery guns and mortars and 75,823 special military motor vehicles since the start of the special military operation, the ministry reported.

title: Ex-prosecutor general Kravchenko's statement bids for protection in country of residence – NABU
body:
The statement by former Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko claiming that Defense Ministry Main Intelligence Directorate (GUR) servicemen detained in Austria intended to commit violent acts against him is an attempt to secure protection in his country of residence, the National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine (NABU) emphasized.
"NABU and SAPO perceive the statement of the former Prosecutor General, who hastily left the territory of Ukraine following the implementation of NABU and SAPO's Operation 'Carthage,' as an attempt to secure protection for himself in his country of residence," NABU told Interfax-Ukraine on Wednesday.
The Bureau also emphasized that Kravchenko's statement regarding the alleged involvement of NABU and SAPO in any of the specified events does not correspond to reality.
Earlier, Kravchenko released a statement on his Telegram channel claiming that GUR servicemen from Artan unit recently detained in Austria were preparing illegal violent acts against him.
"As is known, two active-duty GUR servicemen from the so-called 'Artan' unit were detained. Their commander, Viktor Torkotiuk, was also in Austria at the time of his subordinates' detention. One of the detainees is a former NABU employee who worked in the operational surveillance unit," the former Prosecutor General wrote.
He claimed: "Back in September, I received information that a group of individuals had been sent after me to commit illegal violent acts against me." Kravchenko asserts he was informed at the time that "the leaders of NABU and SAP asked to send this group."
As reported, NABU and SAPO exposed five members of a criminal organization led by an official of the Prosecutor General's Office (Operation Carthage) who systematically received illicit gains for covering up a network of fraudulent call centers and laundered over UAH 42 million through real estate purchases, including apartments in the Carpathians, valuables, and placing funds in relatives' accounts.
Amid the scandal over possible involvement in Carthage case, Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko submitted a letter of resignation. President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy suspended him from office, and on September 15, the Verkhovna Rada approved Kravchenko's dismissal. In wiretap materials, key suspect Serhiy Kropyva, deputy head of the International Cooperation Department of the Prosecutor General's Office, appears as Kravchenko's confidant. In particular, according to the investigation, he coordinated household issues and renovation work at Kravchenko's house.
Kravchenko has not been formally served with a notice of suspicion to date.
At the same time, after writing his resignation letter on September 14, Kravchenko signed a notice of suspicion against NABU Director Semen Kryvonos. In response, NABU and SAPO stated that they viewed such actions as a continuation of a systematic attack on independent anti-corruption bodies. The Prosecutor General's Office reported on the evening of September 14 that no such suspicion existed.
Kravchenko, for his part, informed that he left the territory of Ukraine, citing an official business trip. According to unconfirmed reports, Kravchenko and his wife may be in Vienna, Austria, negotiating with local law firms regarding asylum.
Acting Prosecutor General Anton Kovalsky reported in October that an internal investigation into former Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko's departure abroad is ongoing, verifying the circumstances surrounding his trip authorization. Overall, eight individuals mentioned in the context of Operation Carthage have been dismissed from the prosecution service.

The Novolipetsk Metallurgical Plant (NLMK) is Russia’s only producer of electrical steel, Ukrainska Pravda reported in April 2025. title: Russia escalates AI-powered cyberattacks on Ukraine's public and private sectors – ministry
body:
Russia has intensified cyberattacks on Ukraine's public and commercial sectors using artificial intelligence (AI) tools that make attacks faster to prepare and carry out, Minister of Digital Transformation of Ukraine Oksana Ferchuk said.
"The enemy has realized that it cannot physically destroy digital infrastructure, so cyberattacks have now intensified not only against the public sector but also against the commercial sector. This has changed two fundamental things: attacks are now much faster, and preparations for them are also faster," Ferchuk said at the Technovation conference held as part of the Kyiv International Economic Forum (KIEF) in Kyiv on Tuesday.
According to her, Ukraine is studying ways to use AI tools to counter such attacks.
Among other measures, the government plans to invest in cybersecurity education and expand educational programs at academic institutions, particularly those covering work with artificial intelligence models.
In the public sector, the Ministry of Digital Transformation is urging its colleagues to complete the formation of cyber teams over the coming weeks. For businesses, the minister recommends first and foremost ensuring that they have a specialist or team responsible for the cybersecurity of their information systems.
Ferchuk advised large companies with numerous users and information systems to analyze which professional cybersecurity tools are being used in their businesses.
"In today's world, it is not enough simply to have a team of specialists. You need professional tools that are installed on every computer used by your employees and monitor the actual condition of each computer," the minister of digital transformation noted.
Earlier, in a blitz interview with Interfax-Ukraine, Dmytro Pakholchenko, director of the Cyber Protection Department of the Administration of the State Service of Special Communications and Information Protection of Ukraine, said that CERT-UA specialists had identified signs of possible AI use by malicious actors in January–September 2026 when preparing phishing messages, creating fake web pages and developing software code.
According to him, although there is no separate accounting category for AI-related incidents, the practical experience of the agency's specialists indicates that malicious actors are turning to AI tools significantly more often than they did last year.
Vitaliy Balashov, deputy minister of digital transformation for cybersecurity and cloud technologies, also mentioned the trend of malicious actors using AI in an interview with the agency.
In particular, he said that some cyberattacks detected by the specialized Security Operations Center unit of the state enterprise Diia may be carried out using AI, which can enhance the capabilities of both attackers and those countering their attacks. Such tools enable them to work faster, automate a large number of processes and increase the number of actions performed simultaneously.

title: Oleshky Truce Holds for 30 Hours as Kherson Falls Quiet
body:
The first 30 hours of the humanitarian ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky passed without incidents, Ukrainian Human Rights Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets said on Wednesday, Oct. 28, as neighboring Kherson experienced a rare respite from Russian attacks.
Lubinets announced the update in a Telegram post , crediting sustained communication between the Ukrainian and Russian negotiating teams.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“Thirty hours of silence in Oleshky without a single incident,” he wrote.
The ombudsman said he remained in contact with his Russian counterpart, Yana Lantratova, to coordinate implementation of the agreement.
He also thanked US First Lady Melania Trump and her team for their involvement in the humanitarian mission, describing her direct participation and coordination as important to the process.
The shared objective, Lubinets said, was to provide assistance to civilians in Oleshky and create conditions for those who needed to leave safely.
The lull was also reflected in local authorities’ morning reports.
Kherson regional governor Oleksandr Prokudin said no shelling or strikes on civilian and critical infrastructure had been recorded over the preceding day, Suspilne reported .
Four people sought medical assistance for injuries sustained in earlier Russian attacks. Five residents were evacuated from dangerous communities on the Ukrainian-controlled right bank.
Kherson military administration chief Yaroslav Shanko separately reported that the city’s community had experienced no Russian shelling or drone attacks during the reporting period.
Across the Dnipro River, in Ukrainian-held Kherson, residents described a sense of relief in a Suspilne report filmed on Tuesday, Oct. 27.
“I feel free,” said resident Sofiia, describing going to work and breathing more easily as people returned to the streets.
Halyna Kyrychenko, displaced from the Beryslav district, welcomed the calmer conditions but remained apprehensive.
“More people are walking around now, but the anxiety is still there,” she said.
Barista Marharyta noticed substantially more customers venturing outside and expressed hope that the mission would help people trapped in Oleshky.
The pause also changed conditions for emergency responders. By 1 p.m. on Tuesday, Oct. 27, ambulance services had received more than 40 requests for assistance, none involving injuries from shelling or drone attacks, according to emergency medical official Lina Bondareva.
Municipal workers used the lull to remove rubbish, board up windows, and repair roofs near the river. They continued wearing helmets and body armor and carrying drone detectors, municipal official Andrii Zaluzhnyi said.
The ceasefire began at 3 a.m. Kyiv time on Tuesday, Oct. 27 and is scheduled to remain in force until 10:59 p.m. on Nov. 1.
The humanitarian operation envisages clearing mines from access routes, delivering essential supplies, and enabling civilians to leave voluntarily.
Parliamentary faction leader David Arakhamia described the arrangement as the largest de-escalation since 2022, crediting Melania Trump’s initiative.
Ukraine’s Marine Corps also confirmed Russian compliance during the ceasefire’s opening hours and said Ukrainian Marines were monitoring developments on the ground.
Oleshky, on the Russian-occupied left bank of the Dnipro River opposite Kherson, has faced severe shortages of food, clean water, and medicine.
The White House estimates that 1,700-2,000 people remain in the city, including elderly residents and around 50 children, compared with a pre-invasion population of approximately 24,000.
The mission’s stated aim includes allowing residents to choose where they evacuate. President Volodymyr Zelensky has previously warned that Russian forces could manipulate demining arrangements to direct civilians toward Russia rather than Ukrainian-controlled territory.
Lubinets’ latest update confirmed that the ceasefire was holding, but did not announce completed evacuations or provide a tally of aid delivered.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Yle names Krista Taubert as new head of news and sports
body:
Taubert will begin working in the role from 1 November.
The Finnish Broadcasting Company Yle has appointed Krista Taubert as Director and Editor-in-Chief of the News and Sports unit.
"We promise to offer our audience a truthful and balanced picture of Finland and the world every day. We create the nation's greatest shared experiences and most lasting memories," Taubert said.
In the role, Taubert will be responsible for Yle's news, current affairs, sports, event and local content across all distribution channels, in all languages except Swedish or Sámi. The News and Sports division also includes Yle's news in English, Russian, Ukrainian, Somali, Arabic, and sign language.
She will take up the position on 1 November.
Her appointment was announced to staff on Wednesday morning by Yle CEO Marit af Björkesten .
"In the current state of the world, the importance of reliable information is greater than ever," af Björkesten remarked. "I am very pleased that we have such an experienced journalist and ambitious leader to take our news journalism into the future."
Taubert has served as acting Director and Editor-in-Chief since June, when her predecessor Panu Pokkinen became seriously ill while on holiday in Portugal. He died on 8 July after suffering a second cardiac arrest at home.

title: Russia draws up list of industrial facilities, solutions for protection — top official
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. The list of strategic and critically important social, transport, energy, trade, logistics, and IT infrastructure facilities, as well as the most significant industrial enterprises, has been compiled, First Deputy Prime Minister of Russia Denis Manturov said.
Threat models were developed in these areas, and standard protection solutions were prepared, he said during the government hour in the Federation Council.
"We at the government identify risks on a weekly basis and determine priority operational and medium-term tasks to ensure that enemy strikes do not undermine the stability of critical infrastructure and life support systems. We focus on the social, transport and energy sectors, trade and logistics, information infrastructure and, of course, the most important industrial enterprises. The list of strategic and critically important facilities was compiled in all these areas, threat models were formed, standard solutions for active and passive protection were developed, and resource reservation requirements were set," he said.
Manturov also said that active work is underway in all regions to create mobile fire groups and strengthen emergency recovery teams.
"Our main task is to ensure the safety of people and the resilience of the economy, while minimizing the impact of attacks on the daily lives of our citizens," he said.
Decisions on classifying the facilities as critical infrastructure are made by industry ministries, taking into account their importance, Manturov previously said in an interview with TASS.
Russian President Vladimir Putin earlier signed a decree allowing the government to introduce temporary management at critical infrastructure facilities whose owners have failed to ensure their safety or restore them in time.

title: Reliance’s Jio soars on market debut after Indian record $3.1bn IPO
body: Jio Platforms has bucked the poor track record of India’s biggest share sales, handing investors a rare bright spot amid a bruising equity sell-off as it began trading in Mumbai. Shares of billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s telecoms and digital services company jumped 27 per cent to 1,417.50 rupees ($14.90) at the close, after it raised a record $3.1 billion in India’s biggest initial public offering. The rally valued Jio at $137 billion, making it India’s second-most valuable listed company after parent Reliance Industries and lifting the Ambani empire past Tata Group as the country’s most valuable conglomerate. “It is a bumper listing and highly welcome in the current market situation,” said Shankar Sharma, founder of GQuant Investech. “Sometimes a big listing can alter the mood of the investing nation, and we all hope Jio does that to the Indian market.” In the build-up to the deal, led by Akash Ambani, the patriarch’s eldest son, executives pitched Jio as a full-throttle technology company rather than simply Reliance’s telecoms arm. Its valuation ultimately fell short of some earlier expectations as Indian stocks fell and global markets turned volatile. Still, strong demand for the offering had raised expectations of a robust start. The listing also marked a milestone for the next generation of the Ambani family, decades after Mukesh helped work on Reliance’s IPO at the age of 20. Four generations of the family took the stage for the bell-ringing ceremony in Mumbai, including matriarch Kokilaben Ambani, in a show of family unity. The ceremony was heavy on emotion and nostalgia. Akash told investors Jio would create value for the next 50 years, much as Reliance had over the previous five decades, while siblings Isha and Anant struck a similar note. Mukesh appeared visibly moved at several points, according to a video feed streamed on the National Stock Exchange of India’s YouTube channel. The listing has also shuffled the pecking order among India’s top business houses. Reliance Group has now become India’s most valuable conglomerate, with a combined market capitalisation of more than 30 trillion rupees. Shares of Reliance, which holds two-thirds of Jio, fell 3.2 per cent at the close, their steepest decline in more than five months. Jio’s strong start also defied the recent record of India’s biggest IPOs, which have often stumbled out of the gate. The four IPOs that raised at least $2 billion this decade posted a weighted-average decline of 9.9 per cent on their first day, with only one – the NSE last month – recording a gain on debut. The longer-term picture is hardly more encouraging. Each of India’s five biggest previous IPOs is now trading below its offer price, underscoring how blockbuster share sales have often struggled to reward investors. Hyundai Motor India, whose 279 billion-rupee IPO held the record before Jio’s, trades about 4 per cent below its offer price. The NSE, which raised about $2.4 billion last month, has also slipped below its issue price. Valuation picture Still, some analysts see Jio as better placed for longer-term gains. Nomura Financial Advisory and Securities (India) initiated coverage with a buy rating, citing its market leadership and the prospect of an improvement in free cash flow. Analysts, including Bineet Banka set a target price of 1,340 rupees. Risks remain. Jio depends on telecoms licences and spectrum, with delays in approvals, non-renewal of licences or difficulties acquiring additional spectrum threatening to weigh on the business, according to Religare Broking. Valuation is another concern. Jio’s market value is nearing that of US telecoms companies AT&T and Verizon Communications, despite it generating only a fraction of their revenue, while user revenue in India has barely grown over the past two decades, according to Anurag Singh, founder of Ansid Capital. “At 14 per cent annual growth, Jio could take 20 years to match AT&T’s revenue, a stark reminder that even great businesses can deliver poor returns when investors overpay,” he said. For now, investor optimism is being underpinned by extraordinary demand for the offering. The deal attracted more than $78 billion of bids and nearly 14 million applications. The premium is supported by Jio’s market leadership, improving monetisation and strong cash generation, according to Geojit Investments. “Jio’s expansion has helped accelerate digital adoption, which in turn has brought millions of Indians into the financial ecosystem, including the stock market,” said Raamdeo Agrawal, chairman and co-founder of Motilal Oswal Financial Services. “Jio’s growth potential remains significant.”

title: Give Us Our Severance Package, Protesting WRPC Support Staff Tell NNPCL
body: Sylvester Idowu in Warri The support staff of Warri Refining and Petrochemical Company (WRPC) have accused the Refinery Coordinator, Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, (NNPC) Limited, Mr. Bayo Adenrele, of working against President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and trying to instigate violence against the administration. The aggrieved workers claimed that Adenrele has stripped off royalties from host communities of WRPC, vowing that they can no longer tolerate the rubbishing of host communities. Chairman of the support staff of WRPC, Dafe Ighomitedo, who spoke to newsmen at the entrance of WRPC Tuesday, during the continued protest of the support staff, said NNPCL had been telling the workers lies, upon lies since 2015. Ighomitedo, stated: “This is the fourth week we have been here protesting for us to get our severance package, having the old contract expired 30th September. Unfortunately, it has been lies upon lies. We have been here since 2015 and this protest has been going on since 2015, but it always ends with deceit. “The two palaces hosting this company (WRPC) went to Abuja, where they made promises to give the workers proper welfare. They laid off people and give us peanuts, we that remained, we’re still hopeful that someday, something good will happen, but no way. They told the masses that they are taking care of us, saying they are paying us N90,000 to N150,000. No pension, no medical, no transport, we don’t even have access to the plant clinic, when we are sick, it is so demeaning. We can no longer take it. We have been here since 5th October, till now they have not responded. “The Refinery Coordinator (RC) for the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL), Bayo Adenrele, feels we are nobody and we have lost confidence in him. He has no integrity when it comes to the Support Staff of WRPC. “He is working against this present government of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. He is doing this to instigate violence against the president. We have been peaceful for so long. The community has been rubbished for too long and we can no longer take it. Bayo Adenrele has stripped the community of all royalties. This time around, it won’t be business as usual.” Ighomitedo demanded to have a meeting with the Executive Vice-President, Downstream at NNPC Limited, Dr. Mumuni Dagazau, insisting that he should come down to Warri to address the protesting workers. “We want to see the Executive Vice-President, Downstream at NNPC Limited, Dr. Mumuni Dagazau. He should come and address us, because the RC is rubbishing his office and staining the image of the Group Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL), Bashir Bayo Ojulari. RC is telling people that we are outsourced. We have our letters and document. We were employed directly. Our case is peculiar. The Acting MD right now was once a Support Staff that was later converted, but now nobody wants to convert us,” he said. One of the support staff, Akivie Kingsley, who spoke in the same vein, stated: “It has been promises and failed promises, what this people are owing us, is what I can’t even speak out. We are entitled to every welfare, but their promises have gotten to the point that we can no longer take it. “If we are going on leave, no leave allowance. We have people that are already dead; we have two corpses in the mortuary as we speak; we have marriages that are crashing because of lack of finance. Children are off school, because we cannot pay their school fees and the RC expects engineers like us, with vast experience, to keep working in this kind of environment, with N90,000 salary, it won’t work. We are done with this slave contract.” Another support staff of WRPC, who is a Lab Technician, Benjamin Iwuno, lamented that he had put in over 13yrs in WRPC, stressing that all his service years has been taken for granted, being paid peanuts and no health benefit. “How do you explain to the government that you have over 300 personnel working with you and none of them is pensionable? They can’t have access to basic healthcare. Some of my colleagues have died on duty, no compensation. “Can the N90,000 take somebody with family home? The management is telling us that we don’t mean anything to them. How is it possible that my boss will write my job as his appraisal and I get nothing in return? It is painful. I want my rightful benefit working in oil and gas company,” Iwuno said. For Harriet Charles, the story was not different, she wept while narrating her experience with the WRPC for the past 14 years. “I have been here for the past 14years, I wasn’t like this, if you get to my house now, I don’t have TV, because N90,000 cannot get me TV. My children are in school but cannot pay their school fees. I go begging sometimes, because the money they are paying me is so meagre, people think I earn plenty money because I work in a refinery, where is the money? “I have to buy soup from people selling soup to manage with my children. I have lost close friends working in the same department with me. I need my severance package, so I can be able to take care of my children. My house rent is due. We need this money, we are dying,” she added. The aggrieved workers carried banners with inscriptions such as ‘EVP Downstream, Dr. Mumuni Dangazaun, must act now’; ‘The RC, Engr. Bayo Adenrele, Has No Integrity’; ‘WRPC Support Staff were never outsourced, but employed directed by WRPC’ and ‘No EVP Downstream, No discussion.’

title: The West persists in attempts to sow division among our compatriots — Russian MFA
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Russian compatriots living abroad are witnessing firsthand attempts by Western adversaries to sow discord and undermine unity within their communities, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Andrey Rudenko has said.
"Our compatriots abroad, who often find themselves in a hostile environment, including in the information sphere, are acutely aware of efforts by our adversaries in the West - global elites, certain media outlets, and non-governmental organizations - to divide the compatriot community and fuel discord along ideological and religious lines, as well as over moral, ethical, and personal values and principles," Rudenko said at the World Thematic Conference of Russian Compatriots Living Abroad.
He stressed that, under these circumstances, "it is our collective duty to counter such attempts and the West’s aggressive actions aimed at provoking conflict by pursuing a policy of ‘divide and rule.’"
In this regard, Rudenko urged participants to draw inspiration from the words of Russian poet and diplomat Fyodor Tyutchev, who wrote in 1870: "Unity - as the oracle of our day proclaims - can perhaps be forged only with iron and blood; but we shall try to forge it with love - and then we shall see which proves more enduring.".

title: Russia discussing with partners extension of ISS operations until 2032 — deputy PM
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Russia is discussing with foreign partners the extension of the International Space Station (ISS) joint operations until 2032, First Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov said at a meeting of the Federation Council.
"Our manned space program, cross flights, and work on the International Space Station are proceeding as planned. We are currently discussing with our partners the extension of its operations until 2032," he said.
In July, Roscosmos CEO Dmitry Bakanov announced that Roscosmos and NASA had agreed to extend the ISS operations until 2030. He emphasized that even after the ISS ceases operations, space agencies will continue to coordinate and exchange technical information regarding their orbital stations. Meanwhile, the first module of the Russian Orbital Station (ROS) is projected to be deployed in 2028.

title: Ten days later, Git on macOS still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificates
body:
Apple was notified of the eMudhra incident on 17th October. As of 28th October, the developer tools Apple ships with macOS, including git, curl and python3, still trust the compromised certificates.
Worse, macOS 27.2, released on 26th October, did not fix the issue and undid the workaround that users had applied by hand, leaving them vulnerable again.
Meanwhile, dozens of other projects , many run by volunteers, shipped fixes days ago.
Anyone can intercept any HTTPS connection these tools make.
For git, that means clones and pulls from https:// remotes can deliver attacker-chosen code, pushes can be altered in transit, and your credentials, such as GitHub tokens, can be intercepted.
To check whether your git is affected, run:
A certificate error means your git is protected. If git lists a commit, your git is affected. Your connections to GitHub, or any other https:// git remote, can be intercepted and tampered with.
To see an attack end to end, run the command below in a temporary directory. It clones a repository from a test server impersonating GitHub. The -c option redirects github.com to our test server for this one command only. The server presents a github.com certificate issued by one of the compromised eMudhra intermediates.
A patched git will refuse with a certificate error. If the clone succeeds, you'll see a README.md starting with INTERCEPTED .
A real attacker would not need the extra option. Anyone on the network path between you and GitHub can redirect your traffic themselves.
You can replace the demo repository with any other, public or private. Keep the fake-user@ prefix. Without it, git would send your GitHub credentials to the test server. For example:
curl, python3 and the other tools Apple ships are affected in the same way. To check curl, run:
A certificate error means curl is protected.
Apple has already protected Safari and other apps built on its networking framework.
Apple needs to ship a fix for macOS developers as soon as possible, for example by removing the affected roots from /etc/ssl/cert.pem .
The affected roots can be removed by hand. The macOS workaround on the main page walks through the steps. Apple's guidance states that macOS updates may revert the fix, so developers need to repeat the checks above and the workaround after every update until Apple ships a fix.
Security teams should also consider whether macOS runners are used in their CI or other build infrastructure and evaluate the supply chain risk.

title: Russian forces step up assaults on Huliaipole axis, National Guard says
body:
National Guard spokesperson Ruslan Muzychuk reported the development during a televised broadcast, according to Ukrinform.
“We are seeing the highest number of combat engagements on the Pokrovsk axis. The enemy is also conducting intensive assaults on the Ocheretyne axis, in the area of Dobropillia. The Kostiantynivka axis is also seeing heavy fighting. In recent days, we have also observed an increase in enemy assault activity on the Huliaipole axis,” the spokesperson said.
According to Muzychuk, National Guard troops repelled 27 Russian assaults across the front line over the past 24 hours, 17 of them in the Donetsk region. The number of daily combat engagements has fallen to 150–200 this week, down from 300 or more in previous weeks.
Muzychuk also described Operation Veles, conducted on the Kupiansk axis, as a technologically sophisticated operation. He said its success was due to comprehensive planning, including logistics and the movement of troops through a gas pipeline.
More than 100 Russian troops were killed and another 30 captured during the operation, the spokesperson said.
The operation prevented Russian forces from using the pipeline to infiltrate the rear of Ukrainian defensive positions and expand their foothold near Kupiansk, he added.
Muzychuk added that, as drones increasingly dominate the battlefield, more combat activity is shifting underground. He said Russia’s attempts to use the gas pipeline had made it essential for Ukrainian defenders to seize the initiative.
“We had seen relevant videos and received reports indicating that the enemy was trying to use it for its own purposes. It was important for our troops to seize the initiative,” the spokesperson said.
