title: Methil yard wins second export order and hires sixty
body: Navantia UK has won a second new vessel export contract for its Methil yard in Fife and is recruiting sixty skilled workers, according to the company. The roles are for experienced welders and platers along with riggers, scaffolders and painters, and follow a first export order secured earlier this year and the completion at Methil of the Navantia UK Seahorse, the barge supporting delivery of the Fleet Solid Support programme for the Royal Fleet Auxiliary. The company recently announced a further £12 million for the site covering training facilities, machinery, infrastructure and new technology, taking total investment to £26.7 million since it acquired the yard in January 2025. The workforce has grown from 180 to 275 over that period, with 75 apprentices now in training. Steve Chisholm, general manager at Methil, said: “Winning another export contract shows the progress being made at Methil and the confidence customers are placing in the yard. “With Seahorse completed, new work coming in and investment going into the site, we are now recruiting more skilled people to help build the yard’s future workload.” Katherine Thorn, head of talent and culture at Navantia UK, said: “These are good skilled jobs, with the opportunity to work on significant programmes, develop long-term careers and contribute to the future of shipbuilding in Fife. “We are looking for experienced welders and platers who want to join a growing team at a yard with a proud industrial heritage and a stronger pipeline of work.” Rhea Wolfson, GMB Scotland secretary, said: “Under new ownership, this shipyard is going from strength to strength with new investment being reflected in orders and recruitment. “The importance of these skilled jobs and quality apprenticeships to the communities of Fife and Scotland’s industrial capability cannot be overstated.” The company put three of its tradesmen forward to describe the work. Allan Lister, a plater who started at the yard in 1985, said: “I’ve worked all over Britain, and the guys you worked with here, nine times out of ten, were better than anybody else.” Peter Ednie, who began as a burner in 1982, said: “I’ve cut steel over 300 millimetres thick.” Welder Willie Gibson, who also joined in 1982, said of the intake coming through: “We’ve got some really good apprentices.” Navantia UK said Methil is well placed to support the floating docks programme for His Majesty’s Naval Base Clyde, following the Chancellor’s announcement this month that the infrastructure will be built and delivered in British shipyards. Scottish Labour said last week that a shortage of trained welders in Scotland has meant Babcock using workers from overseas on the Type 31 frigate programme at Rosyth, a few miles along the same coast. The post Methil yard wins second export order and hires sixty first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Kyrgyzstan Sanctions Crackdown Targets Companies and Bank Accounts
body: Amid growing pressure from Western countries to crack down on the evasion of sanctions against Russia, Kyrgyzstan says 52 companies have ceased operations and another 57 are undergoing compulsory liquidation. State-owned banks have closed more than 240 accounts. Economy and Commerce Minister Bakyt Sydykov outlined the measures on October 27, saying the figures were current as of October 20. Sydykov, who is also the president’s special representative on sanctions policy , said Bishkek would continue cooperating with the European Union (EU). He also pledged continued engagement with the United Kingdom and the United States. He identified the A7 payment network and A7A5, a cryptocurrency designed to track the value of the Russian ruble, as major sources of concern for Western regulators. “Our position is unequivocal: the territory, jurisdiction, and banking and payment infrastructure of the Kyrgyz Republic must not be used for transactions intended to circumvent sanctions,” the minister said. In August 2025, the U.S. sanctioned A7 and a Kyrgyz company involved in issuing A7A5. On October 1, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced further measures against A7 , accusing it of disguising sanctioned transactions as legitimate commercial payments. The EU also expanded restrictions in July 2026 as part of its 21st sanctions package against Russia. The measures included transaction bans affecting a Kyrgyz bank and cryptocurrency operators. According to Sydykov, the financial regulator has revoked the licenses of several market participants linked to A7, while the government has approved the liquidation of several organizations. The overall figures for company and account closures are not limited to entities linked to A7 or A7A5. However, Sydykov did not identify the companies affected or specify how many were suspected of involvement in sanctions evasion. He also did not say when the closures began, making it difficult to assess the extent of the crackdown. The National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic is working with commercial banks to review procedures for identifying customers and the individuals who ultimately own or control the companies involved. The review also covers the purpose of payments. Particular attention is being paid to transfers through intermediaries and affiliated companies, as well as transactions inconsistent with a customer’s stated business activities. At an October 21 briefing , Sydykov reported that another 25 companies were under review and that international consulting firm Kroll was being brought in to assess sanctions compliance systems. Separate restrictions are being prepared for the cryptocurrency market. The National Agency for Virtual Assets and Blockchain Technologies is drafting a presidential decree to tighten sanctions compliance. The proposed measures include screening market participants against United Nations, EU, UK, and U.S. sanctions lists, as well as restricting transactions where there are legal grounds. The authorities are also developing a unified digital platform for licensing cryptocurrency companies and supervising their activities, including automated applicant screening. The system would also monitor transactions and analyze cryptocurrency wallets. Sydykov linked the ongoing reviews to the need to preserve access to international payments for Kyrgyz businesses and citizens and to safeguard their access to investment and capital markets. He urged entrepreneurs to check counterparties and companies’ ultimate beneficial owners before entering into transactions.

title: Qatari mediators present peace deal to Iran in mediation effort, official says
body: Qatari mediators presented Iran with a new draft deal on Sunday to end the war with the US and Israel, and Tehran is expected to send a response to the draft by the end of the week, an official briefed on the negotiations said on Wednesday.The new draft being considered by Iran sets a seven-day timeline addressing both Tehran's and Washington's concerns, laying out daily confidence-building steps that each side must take, the official said.The timeline could begin early next week, and several countries would act as guarantors of the deal, the official added.Qatar, along with Pakistan, has led mediation to end the war that the US and Israel launched in February. The conflict has disrupted global shipping and oil supplies and spilled over across other parts of the Middle East.There were concerns ahead of Sunday's meeting in Tehran that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, fighting for another term in a general election, could resume attacks on the Islamic Republic this week, the official briefed on the negotiations said.Trump threatens to resume strikes on IranOn Friday, US President Donald Trump repeated threats to strike Iran again, while Iranian security officials told Reuters Tehran had drawn up detailed plans to attack Gulf undersea cables if the US and Israel resumed attacks.Earlier mediation ​efforts helped produce an interim peace agreement in June, but the deal quickly unraveled.In recent weeks, Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have launched repeated attacks against Saudi Arabia, the world's largest crude exporter.

title: Winnipeg election 2026: Here’s what you should know
body:
Scott Gillingham has been re-elected as the mayor of Winnipeg.
Gillingham defeated 11 other candidates who were vying for his position in the Manitoba capital Wednesday. According to the city’s unofficial results, Gillingham received roughly 40 per cent of the vote, followed by former Progressive Conservative MLA Kevin Klein and political newcomer Noah Redden, each with around 20 per cent of the vote.
The mayoral projection came roughly 50 minutes after polls closed in the city.
Gillingham celebrated his win with supporters at the Birchwood Inn.
“I still believe our city’s best days are ahead of us. We’ve accomplished a lot over the last four years, but there’s still so much more that we need to do,” he said, speaking alongside his wife, Marla Gillingham.
Gillingham was first elected mayor in 2022 after serving two terms as a city councillor.
As mayor, Gillingham led city council through the reopening of the Portage Avenue and Main Street intersection to pedestrians, the start of upgrades at the North End Wastewater Treatment Plant and an overhaul of the Winnipeg Transit system.
While seeking re-election, he told voters he would address community safety, in part, by establishing the Winnipeg Community Crisis Response team as an alternative for 911 calls regarding mental health or addictions, specifically for when the caller does not pose a danger to themselves or others.
Gillingham also pledged to ensure the continuation of a joint project between the Winnipeg Police Service and community organizations to tackle open drug use in problem areas.
Speaking to people who did not vote for him, Gillingham said he could empathize with why they felt the city needed a change.
“I know that people are worried about crime in in their neighbourhoods, people struggling with homelessness and addiction, mental health,” Gillingham said, adding that he will work to resolve those concerns.
“Whether you voted for me or not, I want you to know I will be your mayor too. My door will be open. Your voice will matter.”
Speaking to supporters at his election night headquarters, Klein said he called Gillingham to offer his congratulations.
“It’s very hard to beat an incumbent,” Klein said, joined by his wife, Heather Klein.
“I see a bright future for Winnipeg. And I hope we can all work together to have that bright future for our children and our grandchildren,” he continued.
The former cabinet minister said he hopes some of his team’s ideas will resonate as Gillingham enters his second mayoral term.
Klein ended his speech by thanking the Winnipeggers who voted for him.
Councillors seeking re-election in Old Kildonan, St. James, Transcona and Mynarski were defeated. There will be nine new faces joining Winnipeg city council.
Loren Remillard, president and CEO of the Winnipeg Chamber of Commerce, said Wednesday’s results point to an appetite for change in the city.
“(Winnipeg residents) looked at council as a whole and recognized that there’s 16 people around that table that need to lead our city,” he told 680 CJOB.
“I think what citizens are really saying is ‘We want more than just the same people pitching tired, recycled, old ideas.’
“There’s an appetite for some pretty big swings because the problems facing our community, be it municipal, provincial or federal, these are big.”
