title: [Mind the Gap] In chaotic US midterm polls, Filams are running
body: It’s hard not to feel that this November 2026 US midterm elections is a déjà vu of cheating in Philippine elections. “Dinaya!” is usually the first word a losing candidate shouts in the Philippines: “I got cheated!” President Donald Trump seems to have taken this script to heart, casting a shadow over the forecasted “Blue Wave” that could flip Congress to Democratic control even before the first ballot is counted. Even if Trump’s unfounded claims of voter fraud are overwhelmed by a huge Democratic turnout, many fear that Republicans in Congress, out of loyalty to Trump, may try to block Democrats from assuming the majority. Echoing the “doomsday scenario” espoused by US Attorney General Todd Blanche — delaying the count or refusing to certify results if they favor Democrats — Trump has directed the Justice Department to block certification of the coming Senate election in Alaska if Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan loses by a narrow margin. The New York Times reported that the justice department cited flimsy concerns about confusion with another candidate whose name is similar to Sullivan’s. Their efforts to project a narrative of widespread noncitizen voting is also relentless, even using as bogeymen the 11 individuals the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) who were arrested in California on October 16 for allegedly illegally registering to vote. Election experts have raised questions as to whether the charges could be trusted to be accurate, citing similar accusations being disproved elsewhere in the country. ‘Dagdag-Bawas’ Remember when Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo called “Hello, Garci!” to pad her votes during the 2004 presidential election against the late Fernando Poe Jr.? Trump seems to have taken a page from that “Dagdag-Bawas” playbook by questioning voter registrations, challenging mail-in ballots and raising the possibility of hacking voting machines. “My thought was they could keep it in their back pocket to invalidate any election results they don’t like,” a former Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) official told ProPublica, which reported that DHS has asked CISA to “secretly acquire a voting machine and hack it.” With early voting underway, shaving off Democrat votes is in play, with software glitches delaying nearly 600,000 voter registrations in Texas. In Nashville, Tennessee, Dolly Parton’s sister, singer Stella Parton, claimed she had to correct her ballot multiple times, saying a voting machine repeatedly selected Republican gubernatorial candidate Marsha Blackburn when she tried to vote for Democrat Jerri Green. Guns, goons, gold While a seasoned “ trapo ” in the Philippines rolls a ₱1,000 note in a folded T-shirt to buy votes, Trump is dangling $5,000 to voters and billions in federal aid to farmers affected by tariffs if Republicans keep control of Congress. Must Read Three issues defining the 2026 US midterm elections While hired armed goons in the Philippines steal ballot boxes, Trump has threatened to send heavily-armed ICE agents and National Guard troops to polling places, raising fears of intimidation among immigrant and minority voters. Though we are hopefully far from the impunity of an “Ampatuan massacre,” the shocking, pre-dawn DHS raid on Representative Ilhan Omar’s home three weeks before election day smacks of the same tactic in eliminating his political enemies. FilAm candidates Amid this chaos, Filipino candidates running across statewide and local races find themselves navigating an American political system increasingly resembling tactics they thought they had left behind. This year’s crop includes California Attorney General Rob Bonta, seeking reelection; Assemblymember Jessica Caloza, fighting to retain her 52nd District seat; and Cerritos City Councilmember Mark Pulido, campaigning for the 67th Assembly District in the California state legislature. In Daly City, Councilmember Rod Daus-Magbual is running for reelection, joined by Tony Bayudan in what is often celebrated as the “Pinoy Capital” of the United States, where Filipinos make up a full third of the population. In Southern California, Artesia Councilmember Melissa Ramoso is defending her seat while Los Angeles City Controller Kenneth Mejia seeks a second term. The Filipino political footprint extends beyond California. In Nevada, Assemblymember Erica Mosca is seeking reelection. In New York, Assemblymember Steven Raga is running for State Senate in Queens, while Georgia State Representative Marvin Lim is running unopposed. Across the Pacific, Hawaii — the first state to elect a Filipino governor in US history with the landmark 1994 election of Benjamin Cayetano — has its own growing crop of FilAm candidates. State Senator Joy A. San Buenaventura is seeking reelection in Puna, joined by State House candidates including Tess Abalos, Travis Bumanglag, Danny Degracia, Diamond Garcia, Greggor Ilagan, Darius K. Kila, Rose Martinez and Julie Reyes Oda. Must Read 4 ways US foreign policy could change if Democrats win in November At the county level, Tyler Dos Santos-Tam is seeking another term on the Honolulu City Council, while Kauanoe Batangan and Addison Bulosan are running for county council seats on Maui and Kauai. It’s time for us to walk precincts, man phone banks and donate to our kababayan running for office. We immigrated to the United States to escape the feudal dynasties, vote-buying and the “Guns, Goons and Gold” of traditional Philippine politics. Now it’s time to push back and make sure those tactics don’t follow us here. So, don’t forget to vote. If voting in person, carefully review your selections before submitting your ballot to make sure the machine properly records your choice. If voting by mail, don’t wait until November 3 to mail your ballots to prevent the understaffed US Postal Service from throwing them away if they don’t get picked up on Election Day. In one of the most consequential elections in modern history, our mission this November is not only in supporting our kababayan to win — it is a front-line battle to make sure our votes are counted, and defend them if need be. – Rappler.com Oscar Quiambao is a former reporter for The Philippine Daily Inquirer who now lives in San Francisco .

title: Gulf countries can turn the Syrian refugee crisis into an engine of regional growth
body: The deadly Houthi attacks on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport earlier this month are just the latest reminder of how the war with Iran continues to destabilise the Middle East. The conflict has driven Gulf countries to accelerate efforts to diversify trade routes and deepen regional integration. However, amid the focus on immediate security threats, a longer-standing regional challenge demands renewed attention – the fate of millions of Syrian refugees in the Middle East. The Syrian refugee response now stands at an inflection point. The collapse of western humanitarian aid, the overthrow of Bashar Al Assad, the lifting of sanctions on Syria and the war with Iran have transformed the regional context. More than 3.8 million Syrians still live in neighbouring countries , and many face increasingly dire conditions. Yet, these overlapping crises also present an opportunity for the countries of the region to pioneer a more sustainable refugee strategy that reduces dependence on humanitarian aid while advancing their ambitions for regional economic integration. For 15 years, the western-led response to Syrian refugees in the Middle East struggled to move beyond emergency relief. Efforts by donor governments to promote economic inclusion stumbled in the face of domestic political opposition . Aid agencies became locked into an expensive model of supporting refugees without enabling them to become self-reliant. Over time, donor fatigue and aid shortfalls left Syrian refugees poorer. Even after more than a decade of aid operations costing tens of billions of dollars, 69 per cent of Syrian refugees in host communities in Jordan lived in poverty, according to a UN study last year – a record high. The enduring displacement of Syrians risks compounding the region’s instability. The fall of the Assad regime allowed some refugees to return to Syria, but enduring challenges prevent largescale return. Syria’s new government cannot provide basic services, housing is scarce , and living costs have sparked protests. At the same time, western humanitarian aid cuts are forcing refugees to choose between basic needs such as rent, medicine and education, while also cutting off host countries from a key source of revenue. Without the legal right to contribute to host countries’ economies, refugees are trapped in worsening conditions, and tensions with host communities are likely to increase. But other developments create new opportunities. The new Syrian government’s successful diplomacy secured the lifting of international sanctions, creating an opening for private sector activity and international investment in the country’s recovery. Then, the war with Iran shifted the geopolitics of the region, enhancing Syria’s value as a potential hub of regional connectivity and an alternative trade route to the Strait of Hormuz. Even though Gulf countries have increased their humanitarian budgets in recent years, global aid cuts still pose a major challenge. Therefore, the alternative strategy would be to prioritise refugee self-reliance. To achieve that, host governments must be encouraged to grant refugees key rights of economic inclusion, including labour rights, mobility rights as well as access to banks and other financial services. These reforms would not only allow Syrians to reduce their reliance on aid but would also allow them to advance the regional integration agenda. Gulf states have worked to mitigate their reliance on key maritime chokepoints by investing in land corridors through the Levant Syrian refugees are particularly well placed to contribute to this vision. Having spent years working and building networks across the region, many possess the skills, commercial relationships and knowledge of different markets needed to connect the Levant’s economies. Giving them opportunities to establish businesses, access finance and move across borders would help build the commercial networks underpinning Gulf-funded infrastructure projects. Those who eventually return to Syria could bring capital, expertise and connections that accelerate its recovery. This could prove to be advantageous for the Gulf states in various ways. Enabling Syrian refugees to participate in Gulf-backed investments across the Levant would help meet labour needs, stimulate local economies and strengthen the commercial networks connecting the region to Gulf markets. Gulf states have worked to mitigate their reliance on key maritime chokepoints by investing in land corridors through the Levant. Saudi Arabia’s recent transport agreements with Syria, alongside Emirati and Qatari investments in Syrian infrastructure, demonstrate the Levant’s economic importance to the Gulf. Refugee participation could transform these projects into engines of regional economic integration. Gulf states have a unique ability to convince Syria’s neighbours to enhance Syrians’ economic inclusion. They have significant political and economic leverage with host governments, and their relationships are not burdened by western colonial legacies. They can mobilise development finance, sovereign wealth funds and private companies to support longer-term interventions and strategies. Their expanding investments across the Levant provide opportunities to link refugee employment and entrepreneurship to commercially viable projects that generate returns and sustain livelihoods well beyond the lifespan of humanitarian aid. They also have recent experience transforming their own economies, which they can bring to bear in refugee-hosting states. They have embarked on ambitious plans to diversify away from oil revenues and to move away from state-centric economic models. These strategies have included supporting private sector growth, boosting entrepreneurship and creating jobs. Expanding opportunities for Syrians and host communities advances Gulf states’ own economic interests, while simultaneously boosting the economies of refugee-hosting states and promoting stability in the Levant. To achieve these wins, Arab governments could integrate refugee self-reliance into their regional economic strategy and make economic inclusion a condition of investments in refugee-hosting countries. They could finance vocational training linked to infrastructure projects, support Syrian-owned small businesses through access to credit, and facilitate commercial ties between refugee entrepreneurs and Gulf markets. In order to overcome host governments’ resistance to reforms that might disadvantage their own citizens or encourage refugees’ permanent presence, Gulf governments could link opportunities for Syrians to job creation for host communities. As Gulf states seek to build a more connected and resilient Middle East, a vital component would be to bring in millions of Syrian refugees who find themselves on the margins of the region’s economic transformation. Empowering them to contribute to that vision would turn one of the region’s most enduring crises into an opportunity to advance prosperity and stability.

title: Two high-speed trains collide in Spain
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 28 (MNA) – Two trains have collided near Toledo, Spain. A Renfe AVE high-speed train travelling from Madrid to Seville collided with an Iryo train travelling in the opposite direction.
Adif, the company responsible for managing railway infrastructure, has suspended traffic on the Madrid–Andalusia high-speed line.
According to El Pais, eyewitnesses reported numerous casualties. Two carriages derailed and fell down an embankment. No official information on casualties has been released so far.
Minutes before the accident, the Renfe train had slowed down because of traffic problems on the line.

title: Military deepens peace restoration in North as over 70 abductees rescued
body: The military high command has stepped up operations across all the theatres of operations in the Northern region of the country with a view to restoring its peace permanently, Daily Trust reports. This is just as its troops attached with various theatres rescued more than 70 abducted and kidnapped victims and arrested a wanted terrorist kingpin during the nationwide operations. The Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Olatubosun Oluyede, while reiterating his commitment to safe and peaceful environment in Northern Nigeria, declared that terrorists are being squeezed from all sides with sustained military offensives. Providing updates to Nigerians on how peace restoration efforts are being championed by General Oluyede across the country, the Director, Defence Media Operations, Major-General Michael Onoja, explained that the operations covered multiple theatres across the country. Troops rescued dozens of kidnapped victims, recovered weapons and ammunition, while also arresting suspected criminal collaborators and sustaining pressure on terrorist groups. Breakdown of where victims were rescued The Defence Chief particularly highlighted the rescue of 27 villagers in Gamji community, Katsina State, and 29 farmers in Mariga Local Government Area of Niger State, alongside the recovery of suspected ransom in Falgore Forest. Checks showed that in Katsina State, troops while responding to a distress call on October 16, engaged terrorists who had abducted 27 residents, comprising 15 men and 12 women, from Gamji community in Sabuwa Local Government Area. The troops reportedly overpowered the attackers, forcing them to flee and abandon the victims, who were subsequently handed over to the village head after profiling. Similarly, troops operating in Mariga Local Government Area of Niger State rescued 29 residents who fled into nearby bushes when terrorists on seven motorcycles attempted to abduct farmers at Magaji Mai Kadarko village. However, one resident was reportedly killed before the troops arrived. In another operation in Kano State, troops tracked kidnappers from Fanyabo village in Tudun Wada Local Government Area to Yan Taburmi in Falgore Forest, where they neutralised two suspects and rescued their victim. The troops recovered ₦10 million suspected to be ransom paid by the victim’s family and handed over the money and rescued the individual to the family in the presence of community leaders and police officials. The military also recorded a major arrest in Mokwa town, Niger State, where troops apprehended a wanted terrorist kingpin and his accomplice on October 18. Four mobile phones and an undisclosed amount of cash were recovered, while efforts continued to arrest other identified accomplices. Troops consolidate on successes recorded in Yobe, Borno, Adamawa In the North East geopolitical zone, particularly in Yobe and Borno, troops sustained offensive operations against terrorists across Borno and Yobe States, consolidating the gains of recent engagements. Following the terrorist attack on troops’ location at Mairari in Guzamala LGA of Borno State, troops conducted clearance operations from 16th to 18th October 2026. Major-General Onoja disclosed that the operations led to the capture of eight AK-47 rifles, two pump-action guns, 300 rounds of PKT ammunition, two rocket-propelled grenade bombs and chargers, a handheld radio and a motorcycle. On 18 October 2026, troops intercepted a resident of Monguno LGA who had escaped after being kidnapped alongside 11 others around Minati in Kukawa LGA on 17 October 2026. The senior military officer maintained that efforts are ongoing to rescue the remaining victims. Similarly, on 22 October 2026, troops intercepted an abductee who had escaped from Chikide Village on the Mandara Mountains along the Guduf-Bubayagwa axis in Gwoza LGA. The individual was subsequently handed over to the IDP Camp Office in Gwoza. Troops also recorded sustained surrenders and arrests during the period. On October 16, 2026, troops arrested suspected terrorist logistics suppliers and collaborators at Benisheikh Market in Kaga LGA of Borno State. The following day, a suspected terrorist, who claimed to have been recruited through a social media group in 2024, surrendered to local security groups at Buni Gari in Gujba LGA of Yobe State. On the same day, troops arrested suspected terrorist collaborators at Kanama in Yunusari LGA of Yobe State. Further arrests were made in Damboa on 19 October 2026. The suspects were reportedly supplying clothing materials for terrorists’ uniforms in the Maidaji and Multe camps. Between 16 and 22 October 2026, a total of 19 terrorist fighters and family members surrendered to, or were intercepted by, troops in Bama, Konduga, Mafa and Gwoza LGAs of Borno State. They cited hunger, hardship and violent clashes between rival terrorist factions as reasons for fleeing the terrorist camps. Specifically, on 22 October 2026, troops also arrested a female collaborator at Ngurusoye in Bama LGA of Borno State while she was escorting a woman to a terrorist enclave. More victims rescued as terrorists neutralised in Kaduna, Katsina, Zamfara Meanwhile, troops of the Joint Task Force North West, Operation FANSAN YAMMA, have neutralised 8 suspected armed terrorists and rescued 3 kidnapped victims in coordinated operations conducted in Katsina, Kaduna and Zamfara States. The operations also led to the recovery of an AK-47 rifle, 3 locally fabricated guns, 3 motorcycles, cutlasses and assorted charms from the terrorists. Major-General Onoja explained that troops of Sector one received a distress call on Saturday 24th October 2026, from farmers at Machika Dam, Sabuwa Local Government Area of Katsina State, reporting terrorist activities in the area. The troops promptly mobilised to the location and engaged the terrorists in a gun battle, resulting in the neutralisation of two terrorists, while others fled the area. In the course of the operation, troops also rescued one Mr Suleiman Umar, aged 42, who had been kidnapped by the terrorists. Further exploitation of the area led to the recovery of one AK-47 rifle with a magazine containing rounds of ammunition, as well as one motorcycle. In another incident on the same day, troops of Sector one, in conjunction with the Civilian Joint Task Force (CJTF), foiled a terrorist ambush along Ungwan Iya, Igabi Local Government Area of Kaduna State, neutralising 6 suspected terrorists. During the operation, the troops recovered three locally fabricated guns, 2 motorcycles, cutlasses and assorted charms. The incident occurred when the troops responded to a distress call reporting an attack by suspected armed terrorists at Ungwan Mallami village, during which the terrorists fled with two kidnapped victims. However, while trailing the terrorists, the troops came under attack but responded swiftly with superior firepower, resulting in the neutralisation of the terrorists, while others fled in disarray. Similarly, troops of Sector 2, rescued two kidnapped victims in Bagega, Anka Local Government Area of Zamfara State, on Sunday, 25 October 2026. The rescued victims were identified as Mr Shehu Chete, aged 40, and Mr Bugu Bedi, aged 25, both indigenes of Kebbi State. The troops, while conducting surveillance operations in the general area, observed the activities of suspected terrorists and swiftly responded with a fighting patrol. On sighting the troops, the terrorists fled the area, abandoning the 2 victims. The rescued victims were immediately evacuated to Bagega Clinic for medical attention before being moved to the military base for further assessment and subsequent reunion with their families. Troops are currently dominating the general areas through sustained patrols and search operations aimed at apprehending the terrorists, rescuing kidnapped victims and preventing further attacks towards ensuring the safety of residents. General Oluyede speaks Commending the troops for their performance, Oluyede said the operational gains reflected the military’s determination to deny terrorists and other criminal elements freedom of action. He commended troops across all theatres for their resilience and urged them to sustain the momentum while remaining disciplined and professional. The military chief cautioned that a cornered adversary remained dangerous, directing troops to uphold the rules of engagement, respect human rights and avoid complacency during operations. The CDS also commended other security agencies for their collaboration and appealed to traditional rulers, community leaders, youths and other stakeholders to provide timely information on security threats, reject mob action and refrain from offering safe haven to criminal elements. Oluyede, however, warned terrorist collaborators, logistics suppliers, recruiters and gunrunners that the Armed Forces of Nigeria would continue to pursue them wherever they might be hiding. The Defence Headquarters reaffirmed the military’s commitment to sustaining operations until peace and security are restored across the country.

title: AI agents hacked Anthropic, maker of arguably the most capable AI models for cyberdefense
body:
Cybersecurity startup Cathedral used AI agents to infiltrate Anthropic's internal systems through third-party business software, exploiting the AI lab's own bug bounty program to expose major vulnerabilities.
Cathedral reported its access to internal data and messaging systems in a draft report reviewed by The Washington Post. The startup, founded by former employees of DOGE, the U.S. government efficiency agency, sells AI-powered security tools to government agencies and businesses.
Cathedral's researchers got in through external admin and sales programs. According to their report, AI agents running advanced models found paths to meeting transcripts, salary data, job postings, and Slack messages in under twelve hours. Ad
Anthropic confirmed that the researchers accessed a limited set of sales, human resources, and IT systems, including contact information for some customers and partners along with basic user account data. Chats with Claude, source code, and model weights were never exposed, the company said. Anthropic shut down the affected access points the same day it found the breach, disabled the third-party programs until the issue was resolved, and notified U.S. federal authorities. Ad
Cathedral says the incident took less than twelve hours. Anthropic says the attempted attack stretched over several days. Only after days of probing Anthropic's own systems did the startup pivot to third-party software, according to Anthropic red teamer Logan Graham . There, Cathedral found two vulnerabilities but reported only one. Anthropic says it discovered and patched the second on its own.
Anthropic also accuses Cathedral of violating the bug bounty program's rules through incomplete disclosure. Graham added that targeting third-party providers and pulling data went beyond the program's safe harbor provisions, though he welcomed the discovery of the vulnerabilities. Cathedral maintains it followed standard security research practices. Ad
How much data was actually accessed is still disputed. Former OpenAI employee Will Depue has claimed that Anthropic is downplaying the incident, saying several sources he considers highly reliable told him Cathedral gained full admin access to the Slack workspace, could read every message, and could log into any user account.
Both the Anthropic and OpenAI labs stored all of their research secrets in Slack, Depue added, with admin API keys scattered across their systems. Jacob Coxon, an Anthropic employee who left the company in September 2026, had previously criticized Anthropic for running dangerous AI research on office software like Slack . Ad
Graham pushed back , saying Depue's sources were wrong. Citing the sensitivity of the matter, he declined to get into specifics but confirmed Depue's core concern: the industry now has to reinvent its security every year. Ad
Depue pressed for details about exactly which claims were false and called on Anthropic to disclose what Cathedral actually accessed. He also blamed the problem on the pace of the AI race, where executives prioritize speed over security.
Alex Stamos, chief security officer at the AI startup Cognition, which uses Anthropic's models, told the Washington Post that he considered the findings significant. He noted that integrated third-party apps are a major problem across the industry and that Anthropic could have done a better job securing its external services.
After months of warnings about AI-powered cyberattacks and its own accidental security incidents , Anthropic is now on the receiving end. AI agents are changing how cyberattacks work, and this breach shows how fast the shift is happening. It's also not just any breach, since Anthropic is likely the company best equipped to defend itself against AI-led attacks.
Graham used the moment to warn that attackers already run AI agents around the clock, specifically targeting external dependencies. Even models half a generation to a full generation behind the current frontier are capable enough for these attacks, he said, and future adversaries will inevitably have more powerful systems at their disposal.
Graham's answer is continuous in-house penetration testing and rebuilding software with formal verification , which AI now makes economically viable. "You probably want to red team yourself all the time. Current models are very creative," Graham wrote.
What he did not address is how Cathedral managed to penetrate this deeply despite Anthropic having access to what are arguably the world's most powerful AI models for cyberdefense.

title: Russian Commander Organized Widescale Fraud Based on Fake ‘Action’ Videos
body:
Konstantin Frolov, former head of a special operations group within Russia’s 83rd Separate Air Assault Brigade, was sentenced on Oct. 27 to 21 years in a maximum-security penal colony and stripped of his rank of lieutenant colonel, according to the Russian media channel Kommersant.
Frolov was arrested in June 2024 and was expected to accept a plea bargain in exchange for giving evidence against his superior officer, Col. Artem Gorodilov, but he retracted his confession and was subsequently charged in his own right.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The charges against him included illegal weapons trafficking, bribery, and fraud by way of claims for self-inflicted wounds for which he was found guilty.
Konstantin Frolov is the son of Oleg Frolov, former deputy director general for the Roscosmos state armaments program who was charged with large scale fraud in December 2023 .
Frolov, whose callsign was “Executioner,” brought together a group of more than 30 soldiers operating in the Ukrainian combat zone with the sole purpose of embezzling money and to build up their reputation as “heroes” of Putin’s “special military operation” – Moscow’s name for the war in Ukraine .
The plan involved staging and videoing scenes of combat – some of which were aired on Russian state TV – from which the group could obtain receive state awards for “heroism” and compensation for the “wounds” they received.
In February 2023, one channel reported on a “unique group of snipers” led by “Executioner,” who claimed to have been wounded seven times who, “out of honor,” declined to be withdrawn and continued to serve.
Some of the battlefield depictions included the December 2023 simulation of a Ukrainian artillery strike by detonating pre-prepared explosive charges near their vehicles and a fake drone attack in January 2024.
On more than one occasion, according to Russian military investigators Frolov and the gang members faked wounds inflicted during “combat.” They were said to have used anesthetics and scalpels, assisted by medics, to cut themselves on various parts of their bodies into which they implanted metal fragments to simulate wounds resulting from combat. On several occasions it was alleged that “Executioner” and others in the group shot each other at close range to support their claims.
Ironically Frolov’s worst injury was accidental. During the filming of one staged assault by the group in May 2024 he threw a grenade into a dugout which bounced out and exploded at his feet causing “non-life threatening” wounds.
Frolov was said to have set up the “Saturn-Tuman VP” and “Bison VP” groups through which they acquired new combat drones for “testing.”
Among the charges made against the Frolov group were the illegal acquisition of captured weapons and ammunition, which include heavy and light machine guns, assault rifles, sniper rifles, pistols, grenades, rocket-propelled grenade launchers, TNT explosive block and detonators.
Some of the weapons are believed to have made their way to criminal gangs or were used in the group’s simulations, while others were gifted to high-ranking officials and Moscow’s Patriot Park military-themed culture and recreation complex.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: AVAS 2026: Accra to drive Africa’s Tokenisation Agenda
body: Ghana will host the Africa Virtual Asset Summit (AVAS) on November 2–3, 2026, as the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Ghana, convenes regulators, policymakers and industry leaders to advance a trusted, inclusive and innovative virtual asset ecosystem across Africa. The summit, taking place at the Kempinski Hotel Gold Coast City, Accra, will be held under the theme, “Tokenisation: Africa’s Pathway Towards Building a Trusted, Inclusive and Innovative Virtual Asset Ecosystem.” At the heart of the gathering is the proposed Accra Declaration, a shared set of principles and recommendations intended to guide the responsible development of virtual assets and tokenisation across the continent. Tokenisation—the digital representation of assets—offers opportunities to unlock value in gold, real estate, cocoa, bonds and trade receivables, potentially widening access to investment and improving the way assets are owned, transferred and traded. Ghana is already exploring these opportunities through its regulatory sandbox, including applications involving gold and Treasury bills. AVAS 2026 aims to move the conversation beyond possibilities towards practical outcomes, including policy recommendations, stronger dialogue between regulators and market participants, and cross-border partnerships to support responsible innovation. The summit is expected to bring together securities regulators, central banks, finance ministries, financial intelligence units, stock exchanges, banks, asset managers, pension funds, insurers, virtual asset service providers, fintech companies, investors, legal practitioners, academics and development partners. Among the announced keynote speakers are Finance Minister Hon. Dr. Cassiel Ato Baah Forson; Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr. Johnson Pandit Asiama; SEC Director-General Dr. James Klutse Avedzi; Chief of Staff Hon. Julius Debrah; and Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Hon. Samuel Nartey George. The proposed Accra Declaration will be central to the summit’s ambition to establish common ground for responsible tokenisation, encourage cooperation among jurisdictions and support the development of credible virtual asset markets. As African economies explore new ways to mobilise capital and expand financial inclusion, AVAS 2026 will provide a platform for shaping the policies and partnerships needed to realise tokenisation’s potential. The event is presented with the involvement of the Securities and Exchange Commission, Ghana. Registration information is available at www.avas2026.com .

title: 2 Russian army deserters arrested while heading for Kyiv
body:
Two Russian deserters were arrested after fleeing their units and attempting to make their way to Kyiv dressed as civilians, Ukraine's State Security Service (SBU) said on Oct. 28.
Both men had been fighting with Russia's 291st Motorized Rifle Regiment in Donetsk Oblast when they left their positions and reached a village in the gray zone near the front line.
"There, they changed into civilian clothes found in an abandoned house, buried their military uniforms and standard-issue Russian army weapons on the premises, and set off on foot toward the district center," the SBU said in a statement .
"En route to the city, they flagged down a vehicle; the driver agreed to give them a ride to Dnipro, from where they intended to travel on to Kyiv."
Both were detained when trying to cross into Dnipropetrovsk Oblast and one "was found to be wearing a Russian military identification tag around his neck."
"According to available information, the Russians hoped to reach the capital — where one of them has relatives — and 'go underground,'" the SBU added.
According to the SBU investigation, one is originally a resident of the Russian-occupied city of Dovzhansk in Luhansk Oblast who had been fighting for Moscow since 2016 and has two prior convictions for murder.
He faces charges under Parts 1 and 2 of Article 111 of Ukraine's Criminal Code, which cover high treason committed under martial law, and Part 7 of Article 111-1, which concerns collaborationist activity.
The other is a Russian citizen who signed a contract to fight for Russia in exchange for being released from prison on a charge of murder. He is being held as a prisoner of war (POW).

title: Kiev receives 12 Patriot missiles per month from US, but fires more than 30, Zelensky says
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Vladimir Zelensky says that Ukraine receives an average of 12 Patriot missiles per month from the United States, but fired 35 in October alone.
"There are documents on US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s desk that he has signed. Maybe he thinks he’s signed everything, but that’s not the case. He signed off on a US package of 12 missiles. Fine. But this month I’ve fired 35. And the question concerns the 23 missiles that I obtained through other channels," the UNIAN news agency quotes Zelensky as saying.
He did not identify which countries provided the 23 missiles.
Earlier, Kiev had repeatedly reported a shortage of interceptor missiles for its air defense system. On October 15, CNN, citing sources, reported that Ukraine’s stockpile of Patriot missiles had been completely depleted. Later, Vladimir Zelensky criticized delays in the delivery of American interceptor missiles purchased with funding from European Union countries under the PURL (Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List) mechanism. He accused Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth of holding up the delivery of missiles for the Patriot and NASAMS air defense systems by a month.

title: Mercedes To Cut More Jobs As Chinese Competition Bites
body: Premium German carmaker Mercedes-Benz will restart a voluntary redundancy programme and is in discussion with unions over further cost-cuts, its chief executive Ola Kaellenius said Wednesday after the firm warned on full-year profits. “Germany accounts for roughly 15 percent of our sales, but two-thirds of our employees and structures are based here,” Kaellenius told reporters and investors on an earnings call to present third-quarter results. “To reduce our fixed costs further, we have decided to restart the severance programme in Germany in December,” he added, without giving a target number of job cuts. German carmakers have struggled with cutthroat competition and falling demand in China, the world’s largest car market, leading to painful adjustments at home. Mercedes-Benz on Tuesday became the third of the big three German carmakers — alongside Volkswagen and BMW — to have issued a profit warning for the year, citing difficulties in China. BMW aims to cut 8,000 jobs by the end of 2027 with its own voluntary redundancy programme, and the Volkswagen Group plans to have cut 120,000 jobs globally by the end of the decade across its brands, which include Porsche and Audi. Kaellenius said Mercedes-Benz could not give more detail since discussions were ongoing, adding that he was nevertheless pressing hard to get costs down. “We will continue with determination to adjust the structures of the company to fit the revenue position of the company,” he said. Labour costs in China, Hungary, Romania and the United States are all lower than in Germany, Kaellenius said, adding that “eastern Europe as a whole is open to any industrialist looking to expand”. Net profit for the third quarter rose almost 30 percent to 1.52 billion euros ($1.69 billion) even as overall sales declined 4.5 percent to 30.7 billion euros, largely the result of a collapse in China. But Kaellenius said the company could not afford to abandon the Chinese market despite an intense price war driven by over 100 competing carmakers. “If you’re a global car company like Mercedes, there’s not a play where you put China aside,” he said. AFP The post Mercedes To Cut More Jobs As Chinese Competition Bites appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Nearly 50 companies involved in producing Russia's Starlink alternative, 23 not under international sanctions, HUR says
body:
Forty-nine Russian and Belarusian companies are involved in developing Russia's low-Earth orbit satellite communications system, Rassvet, Ukraine's military intelligence (HUR) said on Oct. 28.
HUR published the list on its War&Sanctions portal , identifying companies involved in the production of satellites, ground infrastructure, and user terminals.
According to HUR, 23 of the 49 companies and institutions identified, including Roscosmos, remain unsanctioned by any country in the international sanctions coalition.
Since February, Russian Starlink terminals have been blocked , allowing only verified devices to connect. The Rassvet satellite network could provide Russian forces with their own satellite link for controlling drones over long distances.
The system is being developed primarily for military use, HUR said. Russia plans to integrate Rassvet terminals into command vehicles, including those used with the Iskander-M ballistic missile system.
The project is led by Bureau 1440, part of Russia's IKS Holding technology group. Russian state space agency Roscosmos and other aerospace companies are responsible for launch vehicles, satellite components, and orbital deployment, while Russia's Defense Ministry is involved in integrating the system into military communications infrastructure.
Bureau 1440 said it launched the first 16 satellites of its planned communications constellation on March 23 and a second batch on July 20.
HUR also identified bank VTB , one of the largest financial institutions in Russia, as one of the project's investors.
Rassvet's planned coverage is expected to focus primarily on Ukraine and Europe, HUR said, warning that the system could also support Russian hybrid operations against other countries.
"The companies involved (in the Rassvet production) must be included on all 'blacklists' — of countries, banks and businesses — with a complete ban on cooperation with them and real consequences for any breaches," HUR said .
Ukraine's officials were previously seeking U.S. sanctions to hinder Russia's development of the Rassvet satellite network.

title: 16 Suspects detained in major stolen drones scheme
body:
Acting Prosecutor General Anton Kovalskyi reported the development in a Facebook post, according to Ukrinform.
“Drones were stolen from military personnel, their markings were changed, and they were then sold back to the military as new. That is how the scheme uncovered by law enforcement operated. The results of a large-scale joint effort: 16 suspects, 25 documented incidents, and more than 600 drones seized,” Kovalskyi said.
According to Kovalskyi, the scheme was organized by a former serviceman who recruited military personnel, civilian intermediaries, and businesses. The group sought out service members willing to hand over drones belonging to military units in exchange for money. A dedicated Telegram channel was set up to facilitate the scheme.
The stolen military property is estimated to be worth approximately UAH 16 million, law enforcement officials said.
During searches, officers seized UAH 13 million, $400,000, gold, silver, jewelry, and 15 vehicles, in addition to the drones, Kovalskyi said. All 16 suspects have been remanded in custody, with bail available as an alternative preventive measure.
The investigation is being conducted by the State Bureau of Investigation, internal security units of the State Border Guard Service and the National Police, and the Security Service of Ukraine’s military counterintelligence. Investigators are working to establish the origins of the seized equipment and identify everyone involved in the scheme.
As reported, the Security Service of Ukraine, with the assistance of the head of the Luhansk Regional Military Administration, uncovered a scheme involving the misappropriation of public funds through government procurement.

title: Constitutional reform must deliver institutions that serve Ghanaians
body: A judge may be independent on paper and still struggle to deliver justice because a court lacks staff, reliable computers or funds to operate. A public institution may have impressive legal powers yet depend on political goodwill for appointments and resources. These contradictions should be central to Ghana’s constitutional reform debate. The question is practical: how do we build institutions that serve citizens fairly, whichever party governs? The judiciary provides a useful example. Courts interpret laws, settle disputes and check abuses of executive and legislative power. Their effectiveness affects everyone, from a trader pursuing an unpaid debt to a family contesting land ownership. When cases drag on, businesses lose money, relationships deteriorate and confidence in lawful solutions weakens. Independence needs resources “Even judges must eat” captures an important truth. Judges and court workers need decent conditions, while courts need buildings, records, equipment and functioning systems. Independence requires the means to do the work. Ghana’s Constitution already recognises this. Article 127 protects judicial independence, including financial administration. It charges judicial administrative expenses on the Consolidated Fund, protects conditions of service and requires quarterly releases of judicial funds. The Judicial Service Act, 2020, also provides for administration, funding, audit and reporting. The challenge is making these protections work. Citizens should be able to see what courts request, what Parliament approves, what is released and how the money is spent. Institutions receiving public funds must explain both their needs and their results. A 1988 study published by the Centre for the Independence of Judges and Lawyers makes a distinction that remains useful: freedom to decide cases must be supported by security in employment and material conditions. Constitutional promises lose value when inflation erodes salaries or funding commitments go unmet. Appointments must inspire confidence Under Article 144, Supreme Court appointments involve the President, Judicial Council, Council of State and Parliament. Sharing responsibility creates safeguards, but procedures must also inspire public confidence. In Ghana Bar Association and Others v Attorney-General and Others, decided in 2016, the Supreme Court confirmed that a Supreme Court appointment requires a Judicial Council recommendation, although the President need not appoint every recommended person. The Constitution Review Committee proposes more structured selection procedures. Government’s July 2026 Position Paper rejects the proposed constitutional changes to appointment processes, favouring existing arrangements. These differences deserve public debate. Published vacancies, clear criteria and transparent procedures would help citizens judge whether merit drives appointments. Britain’s Constitutional Reform Act 2005 established a Judicial Appointments Commission, operating from 2006 principally in England and Wales. Ghana need not copy it, but can learn from its emphasis on merit and good character. Protection must reach Circuit and District Courts too. Existing constitutional safeguards should be acknowledged, while staffing, working conditions and disciplinary procedures receive serious attention. Most citizens experience justice through these courts. Social pressure matters Political interference is only part of the problem. Public officials also face demands from relatives, friends, schoolmates, religious communities and party supporters. Requests for preferential treatment often arrive as appeals to loyalty or gratitude. My 2008 doctoral research at Oxford Brookes University examined cultural and institutional pressures through surveys and 35 interviews. Discussing approaches to judges on behalf of relatives, participant PA2 argued: “He should be cut off from such things so that when he goes he reads the case and gives objective judgements.” This illustrates perceived pressure from personal connections; it does not establish that all judges yield to it. Family solidarity is valuable. So are funerals, weddings and community celebrations. However, expectations of lavish spending and reciprocal favours can place pressure on public workers. Better salaries help, but cannot replace ethical boundaries. Articles 284 and 286 already address conflicts of interest and asset declarations. Enforcement matters. Public office should never become a means of financing social status or rewarding personal networks. Respect for authority should allow questioning. Community loyalty should coexist with impartiality. Our cultural strengths include investment in children’s education and mutual support; reform should build on these while challenging practices that undermine fairness. Technology should improve justice Digital reform deserves sustained investment. Electronic filing, searchable records, digital payments and reliable hearing schedules could reduce missing files, unnecessary journeys and opportunities for unofficial payments. Case management systems should record adjournments and their reasons, helping judges identify avoidable delays. Appropriate remote hearings could save time without weakening fair participation. Citizens should be able to track cases and obtain published judgments. Public reporting should show case age, vacancies, expenditure and performance. However, judges should not be pressured to sacrifice careful decisions merely to improve disposal figures. Technology also needs maintenance, training, cybersecurity and proper judicial control. People without internet access or digital skills must receive assistance. A computer system that excludes citizens cannot deliver accessible justice. Reform must also address political financing. When financial support for parties is treated as an investment to be repaid through appointments, contracts or access, public institutions become vulnerable to private interests. Transparent financing and credible scrutiny can help interrupt that cycle. A shared national responsibility Afrobarometer’s 2024 survey found that only 35% of Ghanaians trusted courts somewhat or a lot, compared with 57% in 2017. Such perceptions underline the need to rebuild confidence through visible fairness and accountability. Citizens, journalists and professional bodies have responsibilities too. They should scrutinise decisions, demand reliable information and challenge wrongdoing without assuming every unpopular judgment reflects corruption. Protecting legitimate authority and questioning its use are compatible democratic duties. The CRC’s recommendations emerged from nationwide consultation. Government’s position is an executive response, not the end of the conversation. Where proposals differ, citizens deserve clear explanations and genuine efforts to find agreement. Ghana needs transparent appointments, predictable funding, stronger oversight, effective ethical enforcement and technology that improves services. Some changes require constitutional amendment; others require legislation or implementation of safeguards already in place. It behoves all well-meaning Ghanaians to help secure agreement on necessary reforms and hold authorities accountable for delivery. Constitutional reform must become a shared national responsibility that survives changes of government. Institutions should belong to the Republic. Their authority must serve all citizens fairly, their resources must match their responsibilities, and their independence must be accompanied by accountability.

title: Ukrainian Parliament passes initial draft of 2027 budget with UAH 5.65 tn in receipts, UAH 7.7 tn in outlays
body:
The Verkhovna Rada adopted government bill No. 16000/P on the draft 2027 state budget at first reading, with a deficit of nearly UAH 1.7 trillion.
According to an Interfax-Ukraine correspondent, 239 members of parliament voted in favor of the decision at Wednesday's session, 25 voted against, including 19 members of the European Solidarity faction, and 26 abstained, including 17 members of the Batkivschyna faction.
"I thank the Members of Parliament for their collaborative work and for supporting the 2027 draft budget in the first reading. This budget takes into account the realities of a full-scale war and the state's key needs for the coming year. Above all, it ensures necessary funding for security and defense, the maintenance of financial stability, and the fulfillment of vital social commitments to the people," Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky wrote on Telegram following the adoption procedure.
Lawmakers supported a number of amendments to the document. These included instructing the government to consider the possibility of not revising the subsistence minimum used to determine eligibility for free meals in kindergartens; examining the possibility of directing dividends of Ukrainian Financial Housing Company (Ukrfinzhytlo) toward housing programs for Ukrainians; extending financial support to agricultural producers who have relocated from combat zones; increasing the volume of state guarantees for the production of weapons systems and air defense systems; equalizing retirement eligibility conditions for all categories of citizens; directing the remaining education subvention funds from 2026 toward urgent needs in the education sector; addressing housing for internally displaced persons (IDPs); preserving reverse grants to local governments; and allowing local governments to retain 64% of personal income tax (PIT) revenues.
An amendment banning payments under the National Cashback program, which supports domestic production, received 295 votes. A ban on allocating state budget funds to the program received 284 votes, exceeding the required minimum of 226 votes.
Other amendments were also approved. They concerned asking the government to consider increasing payments to IDPs; setting the salary of forensic experts at no less than 10 subsistence minimums; limiting the salaries of executives and supervisory board members at state-owned banks and enterprises; revising the subvention for payments for natural gas; removing an instruction to the government to transfer academies of sciences to the jurisdiction of the relevant ministries; instructing the government to examine the possibility of increasing military personnel's pay starting January 1, 2027; increasing salaries for employees of national libraries, with the government instructed to address the issue; and increasing expenditures on business insurance against military risks without specifying a particular amount.
Parliamentarians did not support a number of amendments to the document. In particular, Amendment No. 611, which would have prohibited transferring funds received under plea agreements to private funds and required that amounts exceeding the damages caused be directed to a special state budget fund for financial support for servicemembers of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, failed to secure enough votes.
Amendment No. 1003 also failed to receive sufficient support. It proposed imposing a salary cap of UAH 80,000 per month in 2027 for government officials, members of parliament, judges, prosecutors and National Bank of Ukraine employees. The restriction would not apply to individuals involved in Ukraine's defense.
The defense and security sector remains the main priority for public spending, with UAH 4.89 trillion allocated to it, accounting for approximately 66.8% of total expenditures and nearly 12% more than in 2026. In particular, UAH 1.73 trillion, or 35.7% of this amount, consists of resources from European partners for weapons and equipment. These funds will be accounted for in the special fund, with the possibility of contributions in kind.
The budget calculations are based on a macroeconomic forecast projecting real GDP growth of 1.3% and year-end inflation of 8%. The state budget's own revenues are estimated at UAH 3.2 trillion, up UAH 265.9 billion from the 2026 figures. The main increases are expected to come from value-added tax (VAT) revenues, up UAH 167.2 billion; personal income tax, up UAH 106 billion; and excise duties, up UAH 48.7 billion.
At the same time, more than UAH 131 billion in planned revenues depends on the adoption of legislative changes increasing the VAT rate by 1 percentage point and the excise duty on fuel by 4 percentage points. Another UAH 52.5 billion is projected on the assumption that the 50% tax on bank profits will be extended and a law on the taxation of digital platforms will be adopted. Approximately UAH 12 billion is expected from changes to the taxation of international parcels.
To cover its financing needs, the government plans to raise UAH 544.4 billion through the issuance of government domestic loan bonds, exceeding last year's plan by UAH 125 billion. The total external financing required to meet mandatory expenditures amounts to $52.6 billion. International partners have so far confirmed $20 billion, leaving a funding gap of $32.6 billion.
Among civilian expenditures, the proposed allocations include social protection (UAH 540.3 billion, up UAH 72.6 billion); debt servicing (UAH 474.1 billion, down UAH 39.1 billion); education (UAH 328.5 billion, up UAH 50.8 billion); and healthcare (UAH 292.5 billion, up UAH 35 billion).
A total of UAH 133.6 billion is earmarked for supporting regions and energy infrastructure, including UAH 60 billion for regional resilience plans, UAH 30.4 billion in grants to communities affected by the war, and UAH 18.2 billion to compensate for differences in utility tariffs.
According to Koretsky, the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine will review the Parliament's recommendations on the budget and prepare the draft for the second reading.
As reported, the government's draft 2027 state budget envisages revenues of UAH 5.65 trillion for next year, up UAH 452.1 billion, or 8.7%, from the 2026 plan. Total expenditures are proposed at UAH 7.27 trillion, exceeding the 2026 state budget figures by UAH 864.9 billion, or 13.5%.

title: Super El Niño: When the Sun Decides to Do Overtime
body: FACILITY FOCUS Kenny Akintola Nigerians are already battling NEPA, fuel prices, food prices and landlords who believe rent should increase every time you sneeze. Now, the weather may have another surprise for us. Please, what exactly have we done? Meet El Niño, a climate phenomenon making headlines around the world. Scientists are warning that the 2026–2027 event could become exceptionally strong. Before anybody starts buying generators to power their standing fans, let us understand what this could mean for Nigeria. El Niño occurs when parts of the Pacific Ocean become unusually warm, influencing weather patterns around the world. A strong event can affect temperatures and rainfall, increasing the risk of drought in some places and other weather extremes elsewhere. However, Nigeria’s exact experience remains uncertain, so there is no need to panic just yet. So, what could this mean for Nigerians? First, heat. Imagine Lagos traffic at 2 p.m., no breeze, your AC struggling like a civil servant waiting for promotion, and fuel prices looking at you with wickedness. Higher temperatures could make life even more uncomfortable, especially for outdoor workers, the elderly and vulnerable people. Then comes food. If rainfall becomes unfavourable in farming areas, crops could suffer, livestock may struggle for water, and food supplies could come under pressure. In Nigeria, where food prices already run faster than Usain Bolt, this is no laughing matter. Water and electricity could also come under pressure. Hotter weather can increase water demand, while unreliable power supply makes keeping homes, offices and essential equipment cool even more difficult. For those of us in facility management, this is a reminder that water storage, drainage, generator maintenance, ventilation and energy efficiency are not merely items on a checklist. They are essential to business continuity. What should we do and what should we avoid? Let us start with the basics. Drink enough water, avoid prolonged exposure to intense heat and check on elderly relatives and vulnerable neighbours. Farmers should follow local weather advisories and consider suitable drought-tolerant crops and water-saving methods. Households should fix leaking taps, store water safely and clear drainage channels before heavy rainfall. Businesses and estates should inspect roofs and drainage systems, service pumps and backup power equipment, and prepare for possible heat-related equipment failures. Above all, follow credible updates from the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet). Not every alarming WhatsApp voice note deserves to be treated like a presidential broadcast. And what should we avoid? Panic buying food and water until the sitting room becomes a warehouse. Wasting water. Ignoring weather warnings. Or forwarding messages claiming Nigeria will become a desert overnight. Climate science is serious business; fearmongering is not preparedness. Can we trust our government to act? My answer is simple: we should demand that it does. Nigeria already has a meteorological agency. The real test is whether its forecasts will translate into practical action. Federal and state governments must provide timely weather warnings, support farmers with useful climate information, prepare drainage systems, protect vulnerable communities and coordinate emergency responses. Local governments should not wait until floodwater enters people’s bedrooms before remembering that drainage exists. Governments should not wait for farmers to lose their harvest before discussing food security. Emergency agencies should not begin looking for equipment when the emergency has already arrived. Can our government do this? Absolutely. Will it do so effectively? That depends on planning, funding, coordination and accountability not press conferences alone. There is still room for hope. A strong El Niño does not automatically mean disaster for Nigeria. Its effects vary by region and season, and early preparation can reduce losses, protect livelihoods and save money. For individuals, preparation means staying informed and making sensible adjustments. For businesses, it means planning ahead. For government, it means acting on scientific warnings before a crisis becomes a national conversation. Nigeria has enough challenges without inviting avoidable ones. We may not be able to tell the sun to reduce its working hours, but we can prepare our homes, businesses and communities for whatever the weather brings. Because in this country, we already have enough hot situations. We do not need the weather adding another one. Till next time, stay hydrated and stay safe. *Kenny Akintola, Chief facility officer EXPRESS BUSINESS SUPPORT (EBS)

title: Visa card holders in Nigeria can now use Google Pay for fast, secure digital payments
body:
Visa, a world leader in digital payments applauds the launch of Google Pay by participating financial institutions in Nigeria, supported through Visa’s partnership with Google. Eligible Visa cardholders of participating financial institutions can now securely add their cards to Google Wallet and make fast, convenient, and secure payments across millions of contactless acceptance points and online merchants.
The launch by participating financial institutions marks another significant milestone in Nigeria’s digital payments journey, providing consumers with a simple and secure way to pay using their Android devices. By adding their eligible Visa cards to Google Wallet, users can tap to pay in stores, make purchases online, and enjoy a seamless payment experience across Google’s ecosystem.
Google Pay uses tokenization technology to help protect payment information. Instead of storing or sharing a customer’s card number during transactions, a unique digital token is used, providing an additional layer of security while maintaining a fast and convenient checkout experience.
As consumer demand for digital-first payment experiences continues to grow, the partnership between Visa and Google, working alongside Nigerian financial institutions, aims to support contactless payment adoption and provide Nigerians with more ways to pay securely wherever Visa contactless payments are accepted.
“At Visa, we are committed to advancing the future of payments by delivering innovative, secure, and seamless payment experiences for consumers across Nigeria and beyond.
“Through our partnership with Google, we are pleased to support our financial institution partners as they bring Google Pay to their cardholders, combining the security of Visa’s global payment network with the convenience consumers increasingly expect in a digital-first world. Helping more people pay with confidence using their mobile devices supports digital commerce, financial inclusion, and the continued growth of Nigeria’s digital economy,” said Andrew Uaboi , Vice President and Cluster Head, Visa West Africa.
“We are delighted to bring Google Wallet to Nigeria, a market at the forefront of financial innovation in Africa. Google Wallet makes everyday transactions faster and safer while removing the friction of carrying physical cards. By working alongside Nigeria’s leading financial institutions, we are expanding access to modern digital payment tools for millions of everyday consumers,” Olumide Balogun, Country Director, Google West Africa
Visa (NYSE: V) is a world leader in digital payments, facilitating transactions between consumers, sellers, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories. Our mission is to connect the world through the most innovative, convenient, reliable and secure payments network, enabling individuals, businesses and economies to thrive. We believe that economies that include everyone everywhere, uplift everyone everywhere and see access as foundational to the future of money movement. Learn more at Visa.com.

title: At least 64 killed in train collision on high-speed line in Spain
body:
The collision occurred near the towns of Mora, Orgaz and Urda.
LONDON -- At least 69 people were killed after two trains collided on Spain's Madrid-Seville high-speed line on Wednesday, officials said.
The collision occurred at around 8:30 a.m. local time at kilometer marker 118 near Urda. The crash involved a Renfe train and an Iryo train, both traveling from Madrid to Seville, Spain's Transport Ministry told ABC News.
The collision was also the second major train crash in Spain this year on the same high-speed train line, involving the same trains from the same rail operators. In January, two high-speed Iryo and Renfe trains collided near Adamuz in the province of Cordoba, killing 46 people. Authorities said one of the trains derailed and another train collided with the derailed cars.
The Spanish Interior Ministry said in a statement Thursday that six more victims were added to the death toll overnight, bringing the total number of people who perished in the crash to 74. The office of the president and the Transportation Ministry later revised that number downward to 69 dead.
During a news conference Wednesday, Spain's Transport Minister Óscar Puente called the crash "truly unbelievable." He said the preliminary investigation indicates the crash was caused by an "inexplicable" order by the rail controllers to allow one train to proceed despite a safety failure that halted a train on the tracks further ahead.
According to Puente, a computer failure led to the initial halt of six moving trains, including the two trains that subsequently collided.
"In the event of a system failure, the control center takes over," Puente said, adding it was the control center which decided to allow the trains to move again without any speed restrictions. That decision, Puente said, resulted in the Renfe train crashing into the Iryo train, which was stationary on the tracks further ahead.
In addition to those killed, at least 15 people were seriously injured and were taken to area hospitals, and more than 50 were hospitalized with lesser injuries, Emiliano Garcia-Page, president of the Castilla-La Mancha Region, said during a separate news conference on Wednesday.
Garcia-Page said 24 victims who were killed were found on the Renfe train and the remainder were on the Iryo train. He said search-and-rescue crews are using canines to comb through the wreckage looking for victims.
"All of Spain is mourning. We express our solidarity and deepest sympathy to the relatives of the victims," Garcia-Page said.
Garcia-Page continued, "The ministry is trying to determine the causes of this terrible tragedy and understand how and why it happened. We are going to get to the bottom of this. And if there was any negligence, it will come to light. If there were failures in the safety system, we will address them decisively."
The incident marked the deadliest high-speed train crash in Spain since 2013, when 80 people were killed and more than 170 were injured when a train traveling from Madrid to Ferrol derailed in Galicia in northwest Spain.
"We have suffered two terrible high-speed rail tragedies in a single year. Everything appears to indicate that the causes of both accidents are unrelated, but it is not for me to say," Garcia-Page said at Wednesday's news conference. "That is the role of the independent railway accident investigation commission."
He added, "If we need to further strengthen safety in order to restore confidence in our high-speed rail system, we will do so, because it is unacceptable for a country like Spain to suffer two high-speed rail accidents in the same year, as we have."
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, who traveled on Wednesday to the site of the crash, said in a social media statement that he is "shocked by the serious train accident in Toledo."
"We extend all our solidarity to the families of the victims and to the injured, to whom we wish a speedy recovery. Our main priority is the victims," Sánchez said.
The government of Spain announced on Wednesday that it has declared three days of official morning, from Thursday to Saturday, to honor those killed and injured in the crash.
"We'd like to convey to the families our condolences, our sorrow, our support and our affection at such a hard, difficult time," Spain's King Felipe VI said in a statement.
As part of the preliminary investigation of Wednesday's crash, authorities said the Renfe train probably struck the Iryo train from behind, causing two coaches to derail and plummet down an embankment.
The Iryo train was carrying 146 passengers, including one baby, while the Renfe train had 397 passengers, according to the transport ministry.
"It was a terrible crash. The carriage partially overturned. We saw carriages next to it completely wrecked," crash survivor Miguel Ángel Pérez told RTVE, the Spanish national radio and television public broadcasting network.
Ángel Pérez said he was riding with work colleagues in the last car of the Renfe train when the crash occurred. He said that prior to the crash train operators warned that the train was stopping due to "an overload on the track."
"Then it started moving again, and that's when we felt immense impact. We felt the train move, derail and we were tilted. It was a terrible few seconds," Ángel Pérez said.
An American tourist named Dire and his wife said they were headed to Andalusia and were also on the train that had stopped on the tracks before they felt "a huge crash."
"The train moved, things flew everywhere," Dire of Florida told the Spanish news station, Canal 24 Horas. "I looked out the window and saw that the train was completely destroyed. People were screaming, crying, covered in blood... I told my wife, 'We have to leave now,' because we were afraid the train would overturn."
Another passenger, Ana, told reporters that she was traveling on one of the trains with her sister and her dog when the crash occurred, according to Reuters.
"Suddenly, I only heard screams," Ana, who suffered injuries to her face and leg, told Reuters.
In the aftermath of the crash, Ana said passengers broke windows and that firefighters pulled her from the wreckage. "I was covered in blood," she said.
She described the horrific scene of seeing people dying in front of her.
"Some people were fine, and others were really bad. You could see them dying, and you could do nothing," said Ana, who added that she and her sister, who was also injured, were taken to a hospital by ambulance.
In a statement, Iryo said its service 6076, traveling from Madrid to Seville, was involved in the accident near Urda. The company said it had activated all emergency protocols and was working closely with authorities to manage the situation.
As a result of the crash, all Iryo services departing from Madrid-Puerta de Atocha and traveling along the Southern Corridor have been canceled. The company said it had no estimate for when service would resume.
Spain's Health Minister Monica Garcia said the government was mobilizing resources and coordinating with relevant institutions to respond to the crash.
“We are mobilizing all the resources at our disposal and coordinating with all the relevant institutions,” Garcia said. “I’m working with the regional government of Castilla-La Mancha to provide any resources it may need. My full support and gratitude go to the emergency personnel dispatched to the area."
The U.S. State Department confirms that several U.S. citizens were injured.
"The Department of State and the U.S. Embassy in Madrid are working closely with local authorities to assist Americans,” a department spokesperson said. "We extend our deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of all those affected.”
The department is asking Americans in need of assistance and those concerned about the safety of loved ones in Spain to get in contact. So far, it has not indicated that any U.S. citizens are among the dead.
