title: Military arrests two over attack on vigilantes, burning of Jos office
body: By Golok Nanmwa Troops of Operation Enduring Peace, OPEP, have arrested two suspects over an alleged attack on members of a vigilante group and the subsequent burning of their office in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. The suspects were arrested at about 1:40 a.m. on October 27, 2026, in the NEPA area of Jos North. Media Information Officer of OPEP, Capt. Chinonso Polycarp Oteh, who confirmed the arrests, said the suspects were apprehended by troops of Sector 1, OPEP. Oteh said, “The arrest followed allegations linking the suspects to the attack on vigilante personnel and the subsequent setting ablaze of their office.” He said, “The suspects are currently in custody for further investigation and necessary action.” Oteh said, “The arrests form part of ongoing efforts by OPEP to tackle criminal activities and maintain peace across Plateau State.” He added, “Security personnel will continue to intensify operations aimed at identifying and apprehending individuals involved in acts capable of undermining peace and security in the state.” ” We call on members of the public to cooperate with the military and other security agencies by providing timely and credible information that could assist in preventing criminal activities and apprehending suspects.” Oteh said, “The continued cooperation and support of members of the public remain crucial to our efforts to maintain peace and security across the state.” He added, “Security personnel will continue to intensify operations aimed at identifying and apprehending individuals involved in acts capable of undermining peace and security in the state.” The post Military arrests two over attack on vigilantes, burning of Jos office appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: South Sudan election credibility at risk: report
body: South Sudan’s planned December 22 elections face risks to their credibility because of unresolved political disputes, incomplete security arrangements and delays in implementing the 2018 peace agreement, the body monitoring the deal said on Wednesday. In its third-quarter report, the Reconstituted Joint Monitoring and Evaluation Commission (RJMEC) said several key commitments under the 2018 Revitalized Agreement on the Resolution of the Conflict in the Republic of South Sudan (R-ARCSS) remained unfulfilled, raising concerns about the conditions for a peaceful end to the country’s transitional period. The commission said the lack of consensus among political parties over the legal and political framework for the elections, together with persistent security concerns, threaten public confidence in the process. Disputed amendments RJMEC criticised the government’s handling of proposed amendments to the 2018 peace agreement, saying they had been submitted to the Transitional National Legislature without the endorsement required under Article 8.4. The provision requires amendments to be endorsed by at least two-thirds of RJMEC’s voting members. The commission said the proposed changes had not met that threshold and were therefore inconsistent with the peace agreement. Subsequent constitutional amendments sought to end the transitional period, dissolve the Revitalized Transitional Government of National Unity (RTGoNU) arrangements and enable elections to proceed without consensus among all signatories to the peace agreement, the report said. RJMEC also described the unilateral dissolution of the Presidency as contrary to Article 1.1.4 of the peace agreement, which provides for the transitional government’s mandate to continue until elections are held, except as otherwise stipulated in the accord. The report’s findings highlight a dispute over the political and legal framework governing the transition as the election date approaches. Dialogue and security RJMEC acknowledged the launch of an inter-party dialogue on September 24 but said some political groups had not participated, including allies of detained and exiled leaders of the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-in-Opposition (SPLM/A-IO) and holdout groups that did not sign the 2018 peace agreement. The commission cited unilateral decisions and the continued detention of opposition figures as obstacles to political consensus. It said the status of the interparty dialogue remained unclear and called for an inclusive process involving all signatories and holdout groups. Security conditions also pose risks to the electoral process, the report said, citing continuing armed clashes, intercommunal violence, active armed groups and incomplete transitional security arrangements. These conditions could affect voter registration, campaigning, the safety of candidates, access to polling stations and public acceptance of the results, it said. RJMEC called on the parties to uphold the permanent ceasefire, complete priority security tasks, including arrangements for election security, and provide predictable support to electoral institutions. Reforms delayed The report also highlighted delays in constitutional reform and transitional justice. No new progress had been recorded during the reporting period on the permanent constitution-making process, RJMEC said. It added that momentum had slowed after the government decided to separate the process from the elections. Responsibility for implementing the 2018 peace accord rest primarily with South Sudan’s political parties and transitional government, it said. RJMEC urged the parties to put national interests above partisan considerations, engage in dialogue and expand civic and political space. A peaceful conclusion to the transition would depend on political will and adherence to the letter and spirit of the agreement, the commission said. The post South Sudan election credibility at risk: report appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Russia grants consular access to detained Japanese journalist — MFA
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Russia has granted consular access to a recently detained Japanese journalist, Deputy Foreign Minister Andrey Rudenko said.
Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) reported on October 13 that a correspondent for Japan’s Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper in the Far Eastern city of Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk had been detained on suspicion of espionage. The journalist was arrested in the Sakhalin Region shortly before his planned departure from Russia and taken to Moscow. Moscow’s Lefortovsky District Court ordered his detention.
"We have a consular convention with Japan, signed many years ago, which provides for consular access to detainees. Representatives of the Japanese embassy were granted such access on Monday," Rudenko told reporters in response to a question.
The deputy foreign minister noted that the journalist was "the target of a criminal investigation under certain articles.".

title: Arab Israelis wake to new political dawn after record election success
body: Not much can be said with confidence about the Israeli election . Official results are still trickling in and will continue to do so in the hours and days ahead. What is certain is a new political dawn for Palestinians with Israeli citizenship, who make up about 20 per cent of the population. The community turned out in force, with turnout around 80 per cent, defying its historic apathy towards Israeli elections. The record 17 to 18 seats they are set to gain could have pivotal implications: the same Jewish parties that shunned them might now rely on them to build a government to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Optimism and unity are rare in Israeli politics today. On Tuesday, it was astonishing, for many, to witness Israel’s once apathetic Palestinian population celebrate at polling stations and coalesce around important causes. It is even more astonishing for others to watch as the same political process seems to be tearing Israeli Jewish society further apart. Yousef Jabareen, the chairman of the Joint List, said that the Palestinian Israeli party now represents a “large, strong list that cannot be ignored” under any political scenario. “We said we would be a safety net for our public on the urgent issues facing our community – violence and crime, the demolition of homes and entire villages in the Negev, racism in all areas of life, the lack of housing projects and industrial zones, and physical attacks on young Arab men almost every day,” he added. “We will represent our public with pride and know how to make responsible, leadership-driven decisions to protect our community.” Yair Golan is leader of the Democratic Party, the only Zionist party to openly call for working with Palestinian Israeli voters. “The reality must teach us one resounding lesson: We have no future here if we don’t stop being afraid. And if we don’t stop with the racism. We must no longer accept Netanyahu’s racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes," he wrote on X. He suggested that a majority now exists, because a coalition with more than 61 seats can be formed. “We have responsibility. And we have an opportunity to form a government of change in partnership with Israel’s Arab citizens. A government that will serve all Israeli citizens. Now we need courage. It takes leadership. It takes stopping the fear and starting to act.” High turnout could also have implications for the Palestinian cause at large, as so many of the community’s brothers and sisters continue to suffer in Gaza, the occupied West Bank, East Jerusalem and elsewhere, none of whom have any chance of representation. The community doesn't expect sudden major influence as it remains a marginalised group, shunned by many in the increasingly right-wing Jewish majority . Experts say that mainstream Jewish parties will have to take notice, however, and if Palestinian Arab parties do eventually join a government as they did in 2021, a Palestinian politician within the Israeli state – be it a minister or a Knesset committee chair – would have a rare pocket of insider influence. Palestinian political analyst Xavier Abu Eid told The National that while Palestinian citizens of Israel have had “awakenings” before, now is “the first time that they truly believe that by voting they can make a difference, even if it’s a moderate one”. He added that the threat of the far right in Israel was existential for them and “that's the main reason why there's a big vote. If that threat disappears, we don't know if that vote will disappear”. 'Really huge breakthrough' Indications of a momentous shift emerged even before official turnout data was revealed. In the weeks running up to the elections, some pollsters predicted a big increase in turnout, powered by the aggressive agenda of National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir in particular, who has pursued house demolitions against Palestinians with zeal, gloating about them on social media, and has stood by as a devastating violent crime wave swept through the community, despite being in charge of the police. The clearest indications that something major was under way came as polls opened. Reports soon came in of busy polling stations, as well as attempts by far-right Israelis to delegitimise and disrupt their vote. The National witnessed extraordinary turnout at a polling station in a secondary school in the northern city of Nazareth. A stream of cars carrying the sick and elderly arrived throughout the day, with voters using crutches, Zimmer frames or wheelchairs to get inside, alongside families carrying young children or pushing babies in prams. A 37-year-old woman said she was voting for the first time because after four years of “catastrophe”, the Palestinian-Israeli population was desperate for a new dawn, saying: “We really need change in this country”. While the majority were motivated by a desire to remove the Netanyahu government from office, other issues were at play, including the unchecked crime that has seen the 2 million Palestinian-Israeli community experience one of the world’s highest murder rates. They voted despite the intimidating presence of a handful of Jewish settlers who claimed they were deployed as “observers”. They were roundly ignored despite walking around the venue, some with an air of ownership. But observers argued that the settlers' actions motivated Arabs to vote for change in such historic numbers. There are no guarantees that Tuesday’s momentum will be repeated in future elections, and Israel might be in the midst of yet another quick series of inconclusive votes. However, Palestinian-Israeli leaders now have proof that with large campaigns and high stakes, high turnout in their communities is possible. Osama Khalid, an 18-year-old voting for the Ra’am party for the first time, said the poll “could be a really huge breakthrough for us” and that he was urging many friends to come out to vote. Previously, Palestinians with Israeli citizenship “chose not to vote” because they felt their parties had little influence over the far-right’s policies . “We hope we can change the situation for this election. I hope we can give more power to our groups so they can decide for us. Eventually, we want everything to be equal. Most of the people are very optimistic.” said businessman Mohanad Salti, 26.

title: Ukrainian MP Poturayev heads OSCE Parliamentary Assembly
body:
Chairman of the Committee on Humanitarian and Information Policy Mykyta Poturayev has become President of the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly, reported the press service of the Verkhovna Rada.
"This came as the result of long and coordinated work by the entire Ukrainian delegation in the international arena," Poturayev emphasized during a speech from the rostrum of the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine.
According to him, this international success would have been impossible without the daily feat and courage of the Defense Forces of Ukraine. He stressed that he perceives his new mandate primarily as an assignment from Ukrainian defenders and commits to not letting them down.
Mykyta Poturayev is a People's Deputy of the Verkhovna Rada of the 9th convocation from the Servant of the People party. He has served as Chairman of the Committee on Humanitarian and Information Policy since June 17, 2020.
On July 16, 2026, Poturayev submitted a resignation statement to surrender his parliamentary mandate due to the dismissal of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov. Later, following the appointment of Mykhailo Drapaty as Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine and Yevhen Khmara as Minister of Defense, he reconsidered surrendering his deputy mandate.
The OSCE PA brings together parliamentarians from the organization's participating states and serves as a platform for discussing issues of security, democracy, human rights, and international cooperation.

title: Four die, seven injured in three Lagos road accidents
body:
The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) announced that four people died and seven others were injured in three separate road accidents in Lagos on Wednesday.
The fatal crash, which claimed the four lives, occurred at Berger Bridge, inward Eleko, along the Ibeju-Lekki Expressway, when a truck carrying a 20-foot container overturned onto an interstate Toyota Hiace bus.
LASEMA’s Permanent Secretary, Olufemi Oke-Osanyintolu, said the agency received a distress call and sent a response team from its Epe base to the scene.
He explained that preliminary findings showed that the truck was travelling at excessive speed while ascending the bridge when it collided with the bus. The driver reportedly lost control while attempting to avoid the collision, causing the truck to overturn onto the bus.
Four adult men died at the scene, while six others sustained injuries and were taken to Epe General Hospital after receiving first aid.
LASEMA, the Federal Road Safety Corps and the police secured the scene. A private crane was brought in to lift the truck and container and recover the bodies, while traffic management measures were put in place.
The crash occurred days after a mother and her child died when two container trucks overturned near Freeman Market at Mile 2, inward Apapa, Lagos. The victims were trapped beneath the trucks and their containers.
In another incident on Wednesday, a truck rammed into a solar-powered streetlight pole near Vetland School, inward Agege Pen Cinema, along Old Abeokuta Road, at about 4:09 a.m.
The truck, with registration number KTU-940XT, hit the pole, mounted the road median and obstructed traffic.
Mr Oke-Osanyintolu said preliminary findings pointed to reckless driving, but no one was injured.
LASEMA’s Tiger Team from its C3 base diverted traffic and used its heavy-duty recovery vehicle, Elephant, to remove the truck. It was later taken to Abattoir Police Station for investigation and safekeeping.
The third accident occurred at Lanre Bus Stop, inward Igando, along LASU-Igando Road, where a DAF truck collided with a Toyota Corolla.
Mr Oke-Osanyintolu said a broken-down truck on the opposite side of the road had caused traffic congestion when the DAF truck allegedly drove against traffic and hit the car.
The DAF truck had registration number SMK 795 XY, while the Corolla was registered as AKD 169 EA.
The collision blocked half of the road inward to Igando. The Corolla driver sustained a minor head injury and was taken to Igando General Hospital by an associate, the permanent secretary said.
The Corolla was towed to Igando police division, while LASEMA deployed its recovery vehicle, Super Metro, to remove the DAF truck and restore traffic flow.
Mr Oke-Osanyintolu urged motorists to observe speed limits, avoid driving against traffic and reckless manoeuvres, and ensure their vehicles were roadworthy before travelling.
He advised residents to report emergencies through the state’s toll-free numbers, 767 and 112. He also expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and wished the injured a speedy recovery.

title: US Navy awards CACI $145M contract to advance maritime tech
body:
CACI International has been awarded a four-year task order valued at up to $145 million to support the Naval Surface Warfare Center Carderock Division (NSWCCD) in advancing next-generation maritime capabilities for the US Navy.
Under the award, CACI will develop and integrate advanced technologies for autonomous systems, maritime sensors, and next-generation naval platforms. This work is expected to help the US Navy improve fleet readiness, strengthen operational flexibility, and maintain maritime superiority against evolving threats.
Furthermore, the company plans to conduct research, engineering, testing, and rapid prototyping across multiple maritime platforms. The work includes evaluating new technologies, validating their performance, and integrating successful solutions into operational systems.
"Maintaining maritime superiority requires the ability to turn emerging technologies into operational capabilities faster," said John Mengucci , CACI President and Chief Executive Officer.
"Our work will help the Navy get critical technologies into the hands of warfighters sooner, giving them the capabilities they need to make better decisions and stay ahead of emerging threats."
In March this year, CACI won a five-year task order to provide engineering and technical support for US Navy ships, submarines, and other naval vehicles. Under the US Navy SeaPort Next Generation (NxG) contract vehicle, the companywill offer data analysis, software development, and control system enhancements to improve the design and operation of naval vessels.

title: Opus 5.5 causing an identity crisis is real
body:
26 Oct 2026 Markdown (opens in a new tab)
Piotr Migdał is right in his post (opens in a new tab) .
In his experiment, he uses a short, one-shot prompt:
Make a three.js (pnpm) visualization of all Invisible Cities by Italo Calvino. Don’t ask questions, it is a one-shot task. You have 6h of work, use it until it becomes a masterpiece.
Invisible Cities (opens in a new tab) is a postmodern novel by Italo Calvino, made of short, poetic descriptions of 55 imaginary cities, each one complex and often very abstract.
In 2019, Piotr worked on a small project that generated those cities for a storytelling performance, using the state-of-the-art model of the time, GPT-2.
To test what today’s models can do, he wrote the short prompt above, and the result was stunning.
Looking at the output, Piotr, a data vis specialist (opens in a new tab) , asks himself: What is my place in creating interactive media? And, after following his call to action (see post), I have one simple answer: yes.
Here are my results from repeating Piotr’s experiment.
(Click on the picture to go to the interactive version)
Detailed results of my Claude Code + Opus 5.5 runs in the two configurations:
I’m not an Invisible Cities expert myself, and definitely not a data vis specialist. So, I’ll leave the review of the details of both artifacts to people who know more about those areas. What I can say for sure is that Piotr’s result (while using the same parameters) turned out a little better visually than mine, but in principle the results are very similar.
The max effort + ultracode version is even more stunning, but interestingly it never got mouse input working without errors. If you want to test it out, you need to stick to keyboard controls - see the Use chapter in the project’s README file.
And hey, if you are interested, the whole source code is in the repository, with the agents’ transcripts included!
Claude Opus 5.5, medium effort, no ultracode: [interactive] (opens in a new tab) , [code] (opens in a new tab)
Claude Opus 5.5, max effort, with ultracode: [interactive] (opens in a new tab) , [code] (opens in a new tab)
But that’s not all. If you find this interesting, take up Piotr’s call to action: run the prompt on your own models and agents, and share the results!
Of course, the title of this post is catchy. There is no real proof of Opus 5.5 causing an identity crisis for anyone. It’s just a real phenomenon that GenAI, in general, is causing it for some people already, and it started well before 2026.
I don’t know if Piotr identifies with the crisis, but I know that identity crisis is not a joke, Jim .
The picture is a funny meme, but the identity crisis is a serious thing.
In my bubble (IT), the issue of (some of the) programmers being upset with LLMs entering the game is pretty well known. However, not everyone realizes that what we observe is an identity crisis.
I watched numerous YouTube videos and read many social media posts and blog posts by programmers about a profound sense of alienation, loss of human dignity, and anger over stolen independence.
And you know what? You can find the same in texts from the 18th and 19th centuries - the Industrial Revolution. Back then, the term identity crisis didn’t yet exist, but the feelings and psychological problems were the same. There was no social media, no YouTube, but you can read autobiographies of working-class people.
Historians have analyzed hundreds of autobiographies written by working-class citizens during the Industrial Revolution (such as those collected by Emma Griffin in her book Liberty’s Dawn (opens in a new tab) ). Additionally, workers frequently petitioned governments regarding how machines stripped away their identities as skilled artisans.
So we’ve already been there. Maybe, from history, we can learn how to deal with the status quo and cope with the situation?
Eventually, everything should be fine. The technology will be more powerful, and the job will still be there, it’ll just look different.
But some people are still anxious about the future.
Today, programmers are not the only group falling into that area of anxiety.
I’ve written before about mathematicians already relating to the identity crisis of programmers (opens in a new tab) . But, sooner rather than later, it’ll apply to all scientists and white-collar workers.
While some scientists find autonomous AI agent swarms “extremely damaging” (opens in a new tab) , others use armies of AI agents to “solve physics” (opens in a new tab) .
But the future looks brighter than that. We already know what AlphaGo did to the Go players (opens in a new tab) , and I tend to expect the same, for every skill on which AI will have influence.
After almost 10 years of this site, I’ve decided now is the time to have my own (work-related) blog, just like a few of my colleagues.
Expect occasional posts, but concise (opens in a new tab) ones: interesting data, insights, latest trends.
Follow me on LinkedIn (opens in a new tab) or Twitter (opens in a new tab) , where I will sometimes link my blog posts.
Input tokens count only the uncached part of the prompt. Almost all input was served from the cache (see the cache rows), so the medium-effort baseline is tiny and this ratio overstates the difference in workload. ↩︎

title: Tokyo can create means of delivering nuclear weapons, China says
body:
BEIJING, October 28. /TASS/. Japan has the industrial and technical potential to develop delivery systems for nuclear weapons, Secretary General of the China Arms Control and Disarmament Association (CACDA) Dai Huaicheng told TASS.
According to him, Japan has been actively expanding its military capabilities in recent years by acquiring advanced US weapons. Besides, it has its own technologies that can be used for military purposes, Dai Huaicheng said.
"Japan has long held a leading position in the world in the field of large launch vehicles, has mastered the key technologies necessary for the development of medium-and long-range ballistic missiles, such as guidance and reentry systems, and also has the technical base for the development of ships with a nuclear power plant," he said.
"This means that if it makes the relevant political decision, Japan will face no insurmountable industrial and technical obstacles either in the field of nuclear warheads or in their delivery systems.
"Japan is the only non-nuclear-weapon state party to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons that possesses nuclear fuel reprocessing technologies, is capable of extracting weapons-grade plutonium and has operating fuel reprocessing facilities, as well as the only country outside the nuclear club that has a full-fledged nuclear fuel cycle. In addition, Japan has a powerful industrial base and economic potential, which theoretically enable it to produce and obtain nuclear materials using existing reactors and reprocessing technologies to manufacture nuclear explosive devices."
According to Dai Huaicheng, Japan has been building up its military potential in recent years with support from the US military industry.
"As for the means of delivery, the F-35A, F-15 and F-2 fighters in service with the Japan Air Self-Defense Forces are potentially capable of carrying nuclear bombs. Japan has also decided to purchase several hundred Tomahawk cruise missiles, modify the launchers on ships equipped with the Aegis combat information management system, and deploy US Typhon medium-range ground-based missiles," he said.

title: AlpineBSD
body:
AlpineBSD is an operating system based on the NetBSD kernel with a userspace inspired by Alpine Linux and the objective of making it possible to use as little AI-generated software as possible . There is no LLM output included in the base system or main package repository ( AlpineBSD AI policy ).
AlpineBSD is a work in progress . There is currently no installer available. For the adventurous, a very high-level installation guide is available here .
AlpineBSD ships the NetBSD kernel, libc, and essential platform-specific tools like mount .
NOTICE : The NetBSD kernel has spotty hardware support, much less so than Linux. You cannot necessarily expect AlpineBSD to work on any random computer you have lying around. Consult the NetBSD supported hardware list for more information, particularly for laptops.
AlpineBSD ships with the apk-tools package manager and busybox, and a slightly more GNU-oriented userspace, preferring e.g. GNU make over BSD make. AlpineBSD is not a fork of Alpine Linux, its package collection is original (though many packages are ultimately based on aports).
Alpine Linux uses the OpenRC init system. Currently, AlpineBSD uses s6 and we intend to add OpenRC as an alternative.

title: Detention: I Won’t Publicise Things I’ve Done For El-Rufai — Uba Sani
body: Governor Uba Sani of Kaduna State has vowed not to disclose the private steps he had taken to demonstrate his support for his detained predecessor, Nasir El-Rufai. He insisted that he would not speak ill of the former governor despite their widely reported political differences. Sani made the remarks amid growing scrutiny of his relationship with El-Rufai. The former governor has been in the custody of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) since February 18, 2026. Attempts to secure his bail have so far been unsuccessful. Speaking on Trust TV’s Daily Politics, Sani said he retained tremendous respect for El-Rufai. He said he considered it inappropriate to publicise everything he had done to demonstrate that regard. “As a matter of respect, many things I’ve done to show my respect for him, my regard for him, I don’t think I should come out and say it. Because when you respect someone, you don’t come out to say certain things,” he said. The governor was responding to questions about his perceived silence over El-Rufai’s continued detention and whether he feared the former governor’s political influence ahead of the 2027 elections. Sani also distanced himself from a reported comment suggesting that El-Rufai should remain in detention until after the next general election. He said the person “who made the statement was speaking for himself. He’s not speaking for me”. He maintained that he had never spoken against El-Rufai and would not do so. The governor argued that his approach to political relationships was guided by his personal character and respect for those who had held public office before him. “This is who I am. When I hold a person in high regard, everything good I have said about him, I stand by it. When I was in the Senate, I said a lot of good things about my leaders, and I stand by them,” he said. “One good thing I am happy about is that people can only quote me saying good things about people, but they have never quoted me saying bad things about my leaders. “I think it is better you quote me saying good things about my leaders than hear me saying bad things about them. It is something I always pray to God not to let me do. For me, that is my character.” The remarks come against the backdrop of a prolonged political fallout between the two men. Though former allies, their relationship has deteriorated since Sani succeeded El-Rufai as Kaduna governor in 2023. El-Rufai, who governed the state from 2015 to 2023, supported Sani’s political rise. He first backed his election to the Senate in 2019 and later his governorship ambition in 2023. Sani had also served as a political adviser during El-Rufai’s first term as governor. However, tensions became increasingly public after the change of administration. Issues include the financial liabilities Sani said his government inherited and a probe initiated by the Kaduna State House of Assembly into the previous administration. In March 2024, Sani said his government inherited $587 million in debt, N85 billion in domestic liabilities and 115 contractual liabilities from the El-Rufai administration. The state assembly subsequently set up a committee to examine loans, grants and project implementation between 2015 and 2023. The relationship deteriorated further in February 2025 when El-Rufai publicly said he was no longer friends with Sani. He also criticised the governor’s defence of President Bola Tinubu’s administration. He alleged that federal reimbursements and other interventions to Kaduna State influenced Sani’s political position. Sani rejected the suggestion and continued to defend the Federal Government’s interventions. El-Rufai subsequently left the All Progressives Congress (APC), the party he helped establish, and moved into the opposition. After a brief stint with the Social Democratic Party (SDP), he formally joined the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in November 2025. The development widened the political divide between him and Sani, who remains in the APC. The former governor has since become a prominent critic of the Tinubu administration and has been involved in opposition efforts ahead of the 2027 elections. His detention has attracted attention not only because of the allegations against him but also because of its implications for political alignments in Kaduna and nationally. El-Rufai was taken into ICPC custody in February as the commission investigated alleged financial offences. The commission said his detention was backed by court orders. He has challenged aspects of the investigation and detention while denying wrongdoing in the cases against him. In one of the major cases against him, the ICPC accused El-Rufai, a former aide and five corporate entities of alleged corruption and money laundering. It linked the issue to an N8.68 billion closed-circuit television surveillance contract for Kaduna metropolis.

title: Iraq's Al Zaidi visits Syria to discuss economic and security ties
body: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al Zaidi started a visit to Syria on Wednesday, the first such visit by an Iraqi leader since the ouster of Bashar Al Assad in December 2024. Mr Al Zaidi, who is being accompanied by a federal delegation, is set to hold talks with Syrian President Ahmad Al Shara in Damascus, government spokesman Haider Al Aboodi said. The two leaders will discuss "the future of Iraqi-Syrian relations, and regional developments and the repercussions of geopolitical circumstances," Mr Al Aboodi added. "Economic and trade co-operation will be the priority, stemming from the two countries' need for an economic and investment partnership that transforms the neighbourly ties to mutual interests and opportunities for development and investment," he said. Although it is Mr Al Zaidi’s first trip to Syria as Prime Minister, he and Mr Al Shara met during the UN General Assembly in New York in September, where they reviewed regional developments. The Iraq-Syria relationship has shifted in recent months from deep mistrust to pragmatic co-operation, driven by the start of the Iran war in February and US pressure for regional de-escalation. Iraq, which exported an average of 105 million barrels a month through the Strait of Hormuz before Iran effectively closed the waterway, is seeking alternative trade routes, including through Syria. Baghdad is already moving limited volumes by lorry across Syria to Baniyas port on the Mediterranean – about 500,000 tonnes of fuel oil per month according to the Syrian Petroleum Company – and importing petrol through the same route to cover a daily shortfall of 5 million litres. On July 18, Syria and Iraq signed two agreements to rehabilitate the Kirkuk-Baniyas pipeline, while a separate deal was reached with a consortium that includes Chevron, UCC Holding and TI Capital, to prepare technical and financial studies for a new two million barrel per day line. The multibillion-dollar project, expected to take four years, would turn Syria into Iraq’s main gateway to the Mediterranean, Mr Al Shara said in an interview with Iraq's Dijlah TV aired late on Tuesday. It will link Iraq’s Grand Faw Port to the Mediterranean, while enabling Iraq to connect Syria to Saudi Arabia and other countries in the region. Security co-ordination will feature prominently in the talks. Since the fall of the Assad regime, Iraq has sought guarantees on the border as ISIS cells remain active, while Syria sees Iran-backed militias on the other side of the frontier as a threat. Mr Al Shara said that the border was “fully secure” and that no armed group posed a threat to the two countries, and welcomed Mr Al Zaidi’s visit.sit. The visit also comes as Iraq handles 5,704 ISIS detainees transferred from Syria earlier this year, including 3,000 Syrians, with discussions under way with the Iraqi judiciary over possible repatriation, Mr Al Shara said. "I believe this is a historic opportunity that has not come to Iraq and Syria, which have suffered for more than 60-70 years from sectarian and internal warfare, coups and conflicts," he said.

title: Real Madrid join Kylian Mbappe in China apology after striker's 'ill-judged' remarks
body: Real Madrid ​have issued an ⁠apology as French forward ​Kylian Mbappe faces a backlash over his comments regarding late Chinese ⁠leader Mao Zedong. In a video on a French podcast that ⁠has since been removed, Mbappe was heard discussing a meme where his face had ​been photoshopped on another person. Mbappe reportedly said it was of “some guy – I think he's a Chinese dictator”. Mbappe and Real Madrid both issued an apology. “Real Madrid CF wishes ​to express its apologies to the Chinese people for any discomfort caused by the recent words of our player Kylian Mbappe,” Madrid said in a statement. “Our club holds deep respect for China, its history, its culture, and its citizens, as well as for the millions of Chinese fans who feel affection and admiration for Real Madrid. “The club joins the public apology expressed by Kylian Mbappe, in which the player himself has conveyed his regret for his words and reiterated his respect for the Chinese people.” Mbappe had issued an apology overnight, stating that his remarks were ill-judged. He has reportedly already lost two sponsorship deals with Chinese companies. “During a recent interview, I reacted to an image of myself,” Mbappe said in a statement. “My comment was ill-judged, and ⁠I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. “I apologise to everyone my words have upset,” added Mbappe. “This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history.” La Liga president Javier Tebas said that he held a meeting with the ambassador of China in Spain to address the situation and “seek solutions that ​allow us to ⁠overcome this episode”. “Our commitment is to keep working together so that an ‌individual episode does not harm the important advances achieved nor affect the millions of Chinese fans who follow our competitions,” Tebas said in a statement. “China is and will continue ​to be a strategic partner for La Liga.” On Wednesday, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson ​Guo ‌Jiakun said the country took note of the apology. “We ⁠take ​seriously the apology ​that ‌the ⁠person has made,” Jiakun said.

title: NEMA Receives 180 Nigerian Returnees From Libya
body: The National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), through its Lagos Operations Office, has received 180 Nigerian returnees from Sebha, Libya. Their arrival was facilitated in collaboration with the National Commission for Refugees, Migrants and Internally Displaced Persons (NCFRMI) under the Assisted Voluntary Return (AVR) Programme coordinated by the International Organization for Migration (IOM) in collaboration with the Federal Government. The returnees arrived at approximately 4:20 p.m. on Tuesday, 27 October 2026, aboard an Air Buraq Airlines flight with registration number 5A-BAE at the Cargo Terminal of the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Ikeja, Lagos State. The group comprised 143 adults, including 75 males and 68 females; 26 children, comprising 12 males and 14 females; and 11 infants, including three males and eight females. Upon arrival, officers of the Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) conducted biometric registration and documentation to establish the identities of the returnees, maintain accurate records and facilitate subsequent reintegration processes. The returnees received immediate humanitarian assistance, including food, potable water, medical screening, ambulance services for those requiring medical attention, luggage handling, logistical support, reception coordination and counselling. Reintegration support was also provided to facilitate their return to their respective communities. The reception exercise involved relevant government agencies and partners working together to ensure the safe and dignified arrival of the returnees and provide the necessary assistance following their return to Nigeria. The post NEMA Receives 180 Nigerian Returnees From Libya appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Ukrainian MP elected president of OSCE Parliamentary Assembly
body:
Poturaiev reported his election during a session of the Verkhovna Rada, Ukrinform reports.
“From today, I take up the position of President of the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly with great honor and a profound sense of responsibility. For the first time in the history of independent Ukraine, a Ukrainian representative will head one of the most important international parliamentary institutions,” he said.
Poturaiev expressed his gratitude to the members of Ukraine’s delegation to the Assembly.
“We have never divided ourselves into the ruling party and the opposition. We have always been a united Ukrainian team, standing shoulder to shoulder to defend our country’s interests. I am proud to have the honor of working alongside you,” he said.
The lawmaker also thanked the President of Ukraine and the Speaker of the Verkhovna Rada, “who have always shown respect for the OSCE’s parliamentary dimension and personally attended Assembly sessions, strengthening Ukraine’s voice on the international stage.”
“First and foremost, I want to thank Ukraine’s Defense Forces. Without your daily acts of heroism, your courage, and your struggle, this would never have happened. That is why I see my mandate first and foremost as one entrusted to me by you. I swear I will not let you down,” Poturaiev emphasized.
As Ukrinform previously reported, Pere Joan Pons Sampietro, a Spanish parliamentarian, served as president of the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly until October 2026.

title: British submarine command course has not run for a year
body: No Submarine Command Course has taken place since November 2025, and the Royal Navy schedules the course to maintain sufficient suitably qualified personnel to meet defence requirements, according to an answer given in Parliament. Ben Obese-Jecty, the Conservative member for Huntingdon, asked for the reason no course had run since then, following up an answer given on 16 October. Calvin Bailey, the Minister for Veterans and People, said: “The Royal Navy schedules the Submarine Command Course to maintain sufficient suitably qualified personnel to meet Defence requirements.” The Submarine Command Course, known throughout the service as Perisher, is the qualifying course for command of a British submarine. Candidates who pass take command appointments; those who fail leave the submarine service and, by tradition, leave the boat immediately. It is run by the Submarine Command Course Teacher, a serving officer who holds that post, and combines attack training in simulators with sea phases against surface ships. Royal Navy submarine availability has been under scrutiny for some time, with the Defence Committee reporting this month that it is not clear the attack submarine force is putting to sea as often as it should, and ministers declining to put availability figures on the public record. The post British submarine command course has not run for a year first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: UAE's Gargash says 'wars only lead to further crises' amid concerns of Iran escalation
body: Dr Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to the UAE President, has warned that "wars lead only to further crises" amid mounting concerns over the growing possibility of a renewed US offensive on Iran . He emphasised that diplomacy remained the "most effective path" to achieving peace and security in the region, in a message on social media on Wednesday. Dr Gargash set out the UAE's stance in response to "growing speculation over possible escalation and confrontation". “The UAE’s approach remains firm and clear, based on wisdom, balance and prioritising dialogue and political solutions,” Dr Gargash wrote on X. “Regional experience has shown that wars lead only to further crises, and that diplomacy is the most effective path to safeguarding security and achieving peace and stability." The Wall Street Journal reported that the Trump administration warned several Gulf states to prepare for a possible renewed US military campaign against Iran after the November 3 midterm elections . Mr Trump is leaning towards a short but intense wave of strikes, possibly aimed at Iranian nuclear sites, missile and drone arsenals and critical infrastructure, although he has not made a final decision and diplomatic efforts continue, the Journal said, quoting sources. Meanwhile, Qatari ​mediators ​presented ​Iran ⁠with a new ⁠draft deal ​on Sunday, aimed at reaching a permanent settlement to the war, a source told Reuters on Wednesday. Tehran was ⁠considering ‌the proposal and expected to send a response by the end of the week, Reuters said. At the peak of the war, which started on February 28 , Iran struck the UAE and other Gulf states with ballistic missiles and drones, attempting to strike civilian infrastructure, including energy sites and airports. The UAE was the most heavily attacked country, facing more than 550 ballistic missiles and 2,265 drones, most of which were intercepted or destroyed before reaching their targets. A ceasefire began in June when the US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding intended to pave the way for a final peace settlement. Mr Trump declared the truce and MoU “over” in early July after renewed Iranian attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and retaliatory American strikes. Both sides have indicated in recent weeks that they are preparing for a resumption of hostilities.

title: Kazakhstan’s Islamic Banking Market Faces Test Beyond Rapid Growth
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA – Islamic banking in Kazakhstan has grown significantly over the past years but still accounts for a small share of the financial system. Its long-term value will depend on whether it attracts new investors and channels additional funding into businesses and infrastructure, rather than redistributing existing resources, economist Ruslan Sultanov told The Astana Times. Photo credit: fintech-retail.com “The main task in developing Islamic banking in Kazakhstan should not be to achieve a particular share of the banking market, but to create additional opportunities for financing the real sector of the economy,” he said. Mastercard’s September 2026 report , titled Islamic Banking in Central Asia: A Window of New Opportunities, estimates the regional Islamic banking market at approximately $716 million and projects it could reach nearly $2.5 billion by 2028. For Kazakhstan, the challenge is to turn this growth into additional capital for businesses and long-term investment. A growing market with limited reach According to figures from the National Bank of Kazakhstan cited by Sultanov, the combined assets of ADCB Islamic Bank and Zaman Bank reached approximately 315.3 billion tenge (US$702.9 million) as of Sept. 1, representing around 0.42% of the banking sector’s 75.7 trillion tenge in assets (US$168.7 billion). Sultanov said Islamic bank deposits stood at 39.3 billion tenge (US$87.6 million), or around 0.08% of total banking-sector deposits. According to data from Ranking.kz citing the Islamic Financial Stability Report 2026, Kazakhstan’s Islamic banking assets increased almost 33-fold between August 2010 and August 2026. Despite this growth, the sector remains small relative to the wider banking system. Sultanov also said Islamic banking assets rose 4.7% between January and September, compared with 6.9% growth across the banking sector. The limited market share reflects the small number of Islamic financial institutions, narrower product offerings and a more limited retail customer base. Islamic finance is not automatically cheaper than conventional borrowing, Sultanov said, as costs depend on funding, operating expenses and credit risk. Some Islamic products can also be economically similar to conventional debt. “If the development of Islamic banking results only in the redistribution of existing customers and financial resources between conventional and Islamic banks, the overall macroeconomic effect may remain limited,” he said. New rules could widen access Kazakhstan’s banking law, signed on Jan. 16, allows universal banks to conduct Islamic banking operations under their existing licenses, according to the Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market. Banks should keep these activities separate from conventional operations, including through separate accounting and the segregation of assets and liabilities. Islamic products also require Sharia-compliance oversight. The changes could allow established banks to offer Islamic products without creating separate Islamic banks, potentially expanding access. However, market development will also depend on product availability, specialist expertise and customer confidence. Deposit protection remains a consideration. Kazakhstan’s Deposit Guarantee Fund says it does not cover deposits placed with Islamic banks, an exclusion that remains under the new banking framework. A regional opportunity beyond banking A May 2025 report by the Eurasian Development Bank, the Islamic Development Bank Institute and London Stock Exchange Group estimated Central Asia’s Islamic finance assets at around $699 million at the beginning of 2024. It projected Islamic banking assets could reach $2.5 billion by 2028 and $6.3 billion by 2033. The report also projected the region’s sukuk market could reach $2.05 billion by 2028 and $5.6 billion by 2033, identifying energy, transport and logistics, industry, food security and social infrastructure as potential areas for financing. Sukuk are financial certificates often described as Islamic bonds. Unlike conventional bonds, which typically pay interest, sukuk are structured to comply with Islamic finance principles and generally link investors’ returns to ownership interests in assets, projects or their economic performance. They could help Kazakhstan attract investors from the Gulf states and Southeast Asia and provide an additional source of funding for long-term projects. Access to new financing instruments does not automatically reduce borrowing costs or guarantee investment. Investors will still assess creditworthiness, currency and country risks, governance and legal protections. Measuring impact beyond market share For Kazakhstan, the key question is whether Islamic finance can mobilize capital that would not otherwise enter the market and fund projects that might otherwise struggle to secure financing. That could include expanding funding options for small and medium-sized businesses in agriculture and manufacturing, as well as supporting infrastructure and other long-term investments. Success would be measured not simply by asset growth or market share, but by new investors, additional savings, wider access to financing and projects made possible by these instruments. As Sultanov said, Islamic banking’s significance will ultimately depend on how much additional economic activity it enables, rather than how much of the existing banking market it captures. Islamic banking​ is a banking system that operates in accordance with the principles of Shari’ah law. It prohibits the payment or receipt of interest (riba) and emphasizes profit-and-loss sharing, asset-backed financing, and ethical investments. The post Kazakhstan’s Islamic Banking Market Faces Test Beyond Rapid Growth appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: US Proposed Demilitarized Zones in Donbas, Zelensky Says
body:
The US proposed creating demilitarized zones in Donbas and on part of the Kinburn Spit as potential compromises in negotiations to end Russia’s war, President Volodymyr Zelensky told journalists on Tuesday, Oct. 27.
Ukraine was prepared to discuss the proposals, which appeared in different versions of negotiating documents, Interfax-Ukraine reported from the meeting.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“There was a proposal to create a buffer zone or a demilitarized zone on both sides of the line of contact,” Zelensky said.
He traced the discussions back to the American 28-point peace plan, saying the ideas had subsequently evolved across different documents.
For Donbas, the proposal envisaged a zone extending in both directions from the front line. Zelensky described Ukraine’s willingness to discuss it as a potential compromise.
A separate proposal concerned demilitarizing part of the Kinburn Spit, in Ukraine’s southern Mykolaiv region, which could remain under Ukrainian control.
Other American suggestions addressed the future of the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant and possible territorial exchanges, described during negotiations as land swaps.
Zelensky said Washington had raised demilitarized zones again during subsequent discussions, but there was currently no further progress on the territorial question.
The president said territorial questions could not be settled through draft documents or preliminary contacts alone. They required meetings at the appropriate political level.
He added that Ukraine remained prepared to discuss the issue because Russia repeatedly raised it and made it part of the negotiating agenda.
The distinction is central to Kyiv’s position: Willingness to examine a negotiating proposal has not amounted to acceptance of Russian sovereignty over occupied Ukrainian territory.
The remarks follow reports that Washington is developing a broader package combining security arrangements, economic incentives, and proposals for disputed territorial questions.
A reported American framework included a demilitarized zone in Donbas, alongside an investment package and the prospect of EU membership for Ukraine in exchange for abandoning its NATO bid.
The Economist’s account also described potential benefits for Moscow, including commercial agreements with American companies, sanctions relief, and restored political relations with Washington.
Neither Ukraine nor the US announced that Kyiv had accepted those terms.
The reported package followed consultations in Oslo on Oct. 20 involving Zelensky, US envoy Steve Witkoff, and European partners. Witkoff then met Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg on Oct. 21.
Zelensky has separately said Ukraine is prepared to freeze the front line to halt the fighting while refusing to recognize occupied territory as Russian.
In an interview reported on Saturday, Oct. 24, he rejected the suggestion that Russia already controlled 25% of Ukraine, putting the figure at 19.3%. Reaching the higher figure, he said, would require Ukraine to surrender the rest of Donbas.
That position distinguishes stopping combat along existing military positions from legally ceding Ukrainian land.
Kyiv is also pressing for enforceable security guarantees and sustained support for its armed forces to prevent another Russian invasion.
Addressing Washington’s Hudson Institute on Friday, Oct. 23, Zelensky called for at least 10 years of international military financing. He said Ukraine still needed clear answers about how American and European partners would respond to renewed Russian attacks.
He has argued that a ceasefire must be backed by a strong Ukrainian army and concrete allied commitments, including potential US guarantees modeled on NATO’s Article 5 and approved by Congress.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: UK Drugs Group GSK Profit Drops Amid Cost-Saving Overhaul
body: British pharmaceutical giant GSK reported Wednesday a drop in third-quarter profit as the group was hit by restructuring costs as it tries to reduce its spending. Net profit in the July-September period fell 23 per cent to £1.5 billion ($2.1 billion) from the period last year, the company said in a statement. But the group reaffirmed its revenue and profit guidance for the full year. GSK announced in July a three-year cost savings programme to simplify the group and focus resources on its late-stage drugs pipeline and research and development. It has set a 2029 target for achieving annual savings of £1.9 billion but has not said if the measures will lead to job cuts. GSK said in October that it was considering cutting 1,200 jobs at its Belgium subsidiary, representing around 15 per cent of its workforce in the country, as it faces falling global demand for vaccines. “GSK has delivered another strong quarter, with our key growth drivers and new launches performing well,” said chief executive Luke Miels, who took over from Emma Walmsley at the start of the year. Revenue increased four per cent to £8.9 billion from a year earlier, boosted by strong sales of its cancer, respiratory and HIV drugs. Shares in the company fell around five per cent in early trading on the London Stock Exchange Wednesday. Last year, GSK’s annual profit more than doubled to £5.7 billion. The post UK Drugs Group GSK Profit Drops Amid Cost-Saving Overhaul appeared first on Channels Television .

title: SBU detains pair of Russian militants who fled front, tried to reach Kyiv disguised as civilians
body:
Counterintelligence of the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) has detained two contract soldiers of the 291st Motorized Rifle Regiment of the Southern Military District of Russia in the frontline area of Donetsk region who, posing as civilians, were hitchhiking toward Kyiv, the SBU reported.
"SBU employees detained them at a checkpoint at the entrance to Dnipropetrovsk region. A military ID tag of the Russian army was found around the neck of one of the perpetrators," the SBU said in a statement on its Telegram channel on Wednesday.
According to the Ukrainian special service, the occupiers hoped to reach Kyiv—where relatives of one of the militants live—and "lay low."
As the investigation established, one of the detainees turned out to be a resident of temporarily occupied Dovzhansk in Luhansk region, twice convicted of murder, who has been fighting on the side of the enemy against the Defense Forces since 2016.
"After the start of the full-scale war, the recidivist took part in battles near Bakhmut as an assistant gunner of an anti-tank missile system," the agency specified.
Another perpetrator, according to the SBU, is a citizen of Russia who signed a contract with the Ministry of Defense of the aggressor state while serving a prison sentence for murder.
The Ukrainian special service specified that both militants were recently sent to storm the positions of Ukrainian troops in the Kramatorsk direction, where they subsequently fled the line of contact and entered a village in the "gray zone."
"There, they changed into civilian clothes found in an abandoned house, buried their uniforms and service weapons of the Russian army in that house, and set off on foot toward the district center. On the way to the city, they stopped a car whose owner agreed to give them a ride to Dnipro, from where they planned to reach Kyiv," the report states.
Security Service investigators notified the enemy accomplice from Luhansk region of suspicion under two articles of the Criminal Code of Ukraine: Parts 1, 2 of Article 111 (high treason committed under martial law) and Part 7 of Article 111-1 (collaborative activity).
An investigation is ongoing to establish all the circumstances of the crime. The perpetrator is in custody without the right to bail.
"His accomplice—a citizen of Russia—is currently being held as a prisoner of war," the SBU noted.
The comprehensive measures were conducted by employees of the Main Directorate of the SBU in Donetsk and Luhansk regions under the procedural guidance of Donetsk Regional Prosecutor's Office.

title: NOA wins Public Information Campaign of the Year Award at 2026 ARCON Special Recognition Awards
body:
The National Orientation Agency (NOA) has received the prestigious Public Information Campaign of the Year Award at the 2026 Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria ( ARCON ) Special Recognition Awards, held on Friday, 23 October 2026, at the Balmoral Event Centre, Ikeja, Lagos.
The award recognises the Agency’s outstanding contributions to public enlightenment, strategic communication, civic education and the effective dissemination of government policies, programmes and initiatives to Nigerians.
The Director-General of the National Orientation Agency, Lanre Issa-Onilu, was represented at the ceremony by the Director, Communication and Media, Bala Musa, who received the award on his behalf.
The colourful ceremony brought together leading public and private sector organisations, advertising professionals, corporate executives and other key stakeholders in Nigeria’s advertising and marketing communications industry to celebrate excellence, creativity, innovation and outstanding performance.
Other awards presented at the event included Excellence in Consumer Response Management, Excellence in Sponsorship Marketing, Brand Reinvention and Innovation, alongside recognitions across several sectors, including food and beverages, aviation, banking and insurance, computers and electronics, e-commerce, real estate, personal care, entertainment, medical and pharmaceuticals, education, telecommunications, hospitality and other industries.
Reacting to the recognition, the Director-General, Lanre Issa-Onilu, described the award as a significant endorsement of the Agency’s renewed commitment to innovative public communication, national value reorientation and citizen engagement.
He noted that the recognition underscores the importance of effective public information campaigns in promoting national development, strengthening public trust, encouraging responsible citizenship and bridging the communication gap between government and the governed.
The Director-General further emphasised that the Agency’s ongoing efforts to deepen public understanding of government policies, promote the National Values Charter, strengthen national unity and encourage positive behavioural change remain central to its mandate.
He dedicated the award to the management and staff of the Agency across the country, particularly those working at the grassroots, whose commitment and professionalism continue to strengthen the Agency’s visibility and impact.
Issa-Onilu expressed appreciation to ARCON for recognising the strategic role of public sector communication in national development, noting that the award would further motivate the Agency to deploy innovative, inclusive and citizen-centred communication approaches.
He reaffirmed NOA’s commitment to leveraging its nationwide operational structure, traditional and digital media platforms, and strategic partnerships to promote informed citizenship, national cohesion and sustainable behavioural change.
The award represents another milestone in the Agency’s ongoing efforts to reposition public orientation as a critical instrument for national transformation and reinforces NOA’s determination to deliver impactful public information campaigns that resonate with Nigerians across all segments of society.

title: At least 50 killed, up to 180 injured in collision between two passenger trains in Spain
body:
MADRID, October 28. /TASS/. At least 50 people have died and 179 more have been injured in a collision between two high-speed passenger trains in Spain’s central province of Toledo (in the Castilla La Mancha region), local television channel Antena 3 reported.
TASS has compiled the key details about the tragic accident.
- The accident took place at around 9:00 a.m. local time.
- According to Europa Press, two passenger trains collided near the town of Urda in the Castilla La Mancha region.
- El Pais daily reported later that the accident took place between two residential settlements in the Province of Toledo.
- Two cars of one of the trains derailed, according to reports.
- EFE news agency specified that the two trains involved in the collision were passenger trains.
- Medics and fire and rescue teams are working at the scene of the accident.
- Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez confirmed that the emergency relief services are working at the scene of the tragedy.
- According to him, they are providing assistance to the victims and ensuring their safety in coordination with all relevant authorities.
- According to the latest figures provided by Antena 3 TV channel, at least 50 people have died and 179 more have been injured in a collision between two high-speed passenger trains.
- The Spanish government considers human error to be one of the possible causes of the collision between two passenger trains, El Pais daily reported, citing its sources.
- According to the daily, the possible cause of the accident was human error by an Adif company operator (the operator of the railway network) due to a failure in the security system.
- The daily pointed out that the system is fully automated and train movements were initially halted due to a malfunction; however, switching to manual control could have led to the malfunction, ultimately causing the disaster.
- ABC claimed in turn, citing its sources, that an employee responsible for overseeing the safety system failed to issue an earlier warning about the dangerous proximity of the approaching trains.
- Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said he was shocked by the news of the passenger train collision in the Province of Toledo.
- Sanchez pointed out that he was in permanent contact with Transport Minister Oscar Puente and the regional authorities.
- The Russian Embassy in Madrid told TASS that it had received no inquiries from Russian nationals regarding the railway disaster in the Spanish Province of Toledo.

title: Real Madrid apologise to China over Mbappe comments
body: Real Madrid apologised to China on Wednesday for Kylian Mbappe’s comments poking fun at Mao Zedong, after the star striker’s remarks sparked a social media storm and saw Spanish football yanked off state TV. Mocking former leader Mao — blamed by historians for millions of deaths — is taboo in China, and Mbappe’s remarks saw him become the latest foreign sports figure to anger Beijing. In a clip of a video interview with French show “The Bridge” — since taken down — Mbappe talked about being amused by an internet meme of his face photoshopped onto “some guy, think he’s a Chinese dictator”, an apparent reference to Mao. Real Madrid “wishes to express its apologies to the Chinese people for any offence caused by the recent remarks of our player Kylian Mbappe”, the club said in a statement. “The club joins in the public apology issued by Kylian Mbappe, in which the player himself expressed his regret for his words and reiterated his respect for the Chinese people,” the 15-time European champions said. The statement came a day after Mbappe issued his own apology, in French, Chinese and English, saying: “My comment was ill-judged and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world.” Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing on Wednesday: “We take seriously the apology the individual concerned has made.” La Liga, which saw the broadcast of its matches suspended in China, said Tuesday it “deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe’s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans”. Earlier, the state-run Global Times said in an editorial that it was “not difficult to see that the club’s longstanding tolerance of such behavior has contributed to Mbappe’s latest offensive remarks”. Chinese beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year’s World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappe, said Tuesday it had scrapped its partnership with the player, as did dairy firms Mengniu and Milkground. CMG, which oversees public broadcaster CCTV, said it had decided to suspend broadcasts of La Liga, the world’s second-richest football league after England’s Premier League. Mbappe, 27, continued to face a torrent of criticism from Chinese web users on Wednesday, some of it racist. “His remarks were hurtful toward China and the Chinese people, so they cannot be translated,” wrote one user on social media platform Weibo. Mbappe’s original joke about Mao was not reposted — or had been scrubbed — from China’s tightly controlled social media. Chinese social media app Xiaohongshu had meanwhile frozen Mbappe’s account, where he has over a million followers. The same was done on the Weibo app, with a notice stating that “the user has been banned from following due to violating laws or the Weibo Community Convention”. Some Chinese media reports said global brands like Dior and Hublot had removed their Mbappe-related content on Weibo. An AFP search on Dior and Hublot’s Weibo page with Mbappe’s Chinese name produced no results. – ‘Respect history’ – Offline too the Mbappe brand appeared to be under threat. When AFP visited the Adidas flagship store in Beijing’s Sanlitun shopping district, Real Madrid shirts were available for sale, but none bearing the striker’s name. Chinese state media have previously praised Mbappe as a “footballing sensation” and “talent”. His face is plastered on billboards, on soft drinks and across social media. Mbappe is sometimes affectionately referred to as “Guigui”, meaning “turtle” in Chinese, for his resemblance to a character from the “Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles” movie. Other major overseas sports leagues have previously angered China. China suspended sponsorship deals with the NBA while the state broadcaster pulled NBA games off Chinese television for a year in October 2019. This followed Houston Rockets executive Daryl Morey tweeting “Fight for freedom, stand with Hong Kong”, referring to protests Beijing called separatist and seditious. “Respecting the history, culture, social customs and national sentiments of others is a fundamental principle for cross-border interaction, a standard of conduct widely upheld by the international community,” the official People’s Daily newspaper said in an opinion piece. The post Real Madrid apologise to China over Mbappe comments appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Fairbanks Morse wins $99M deal for US Navy submarine overhauls
body:
Fairbanks Morse Defense (FMD), a portfolio company of Arcline Investment Management, was awarded a contract to ensure US attack submarines (SSNs) and ballistic missile submarines (SSBNs) remain available into the 2030s by providing critical life-extension services.
Under a Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA) contract worth around $99 million, FMD will provide repair, parts and labor through 2030 for emergency diesel generator (EDG) overhauls on six nuclear submarines.
The contract work is part of a mitigation strategy developed by the US Navy to extend the service life of Ohio- and Los Angeles-class submarines by up to 14 years by working with OEMs to overhaul critical systems.
According to FMD, the current contract supports completion of multiple EDG overhauls per year through 2030. The company plans to employ its robotic welding platform for improved precision and speed.
FMD noted that robotic welding has proven to reduce manual welding times by up to two-thirds. To further accelerate timelines, the firm is applying the Pit Stop methodology to shrink depot maintenance periods from months to weeks.
“This contract is part of the ongoing investment in undersea power projection that we have seen not only from the United States and our friends in Europe, Australia and Canada, but also from Russia and China, who are actively growing and modernizing their submarine fleets,” said Keith Haasl , FMD President of Services and Technology.
“Because the timely delivery of critical components dictates fleet availability, we are moving quickly to scale our capabilities. Our work with the Navy actively demonstrates principles of rapid submarine maintenance and overhaul that we can share with allies, so we can ensure operationally ready submarines faster.”
Specifically, FMD will use robotics, automation and its Pit Stop maintenance methodology to reduce depot-level maintenance times and improve parts availability. The contract supports efforts to extend the service lives of existing submarines amid concerns about a potential submarine fleet shortfall after 2029, driven by scheduled retirements and delays in the construction of Columbia- and Virginia-class submarines.
So far, the company has completed EDG overhauls on two Ohio-class and one Los Angeles-class submarine under a previous NAVSEA contract.
