title: Plane reportedly carrying Bolsonaro stops briefly in Ecuador
body: The plane that Argentine authorities say is carrying defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro made a brief stop in Ecuador on Wednesday, AFP journalists saw. Argentina’s government said Bolsonaro boarded a private flight operated by the company Baires Fly S.A. bound for the city of Guayaquil, Ecuador, with his wife and two daughters after arriving in Argentina on Tuesday night, despite a court order banning his exit. According to data from the Flightradar24 website, the Baires Fly flight took off just after midnight (0300 GMT) on Wednesday from the Argentine town of Puerto Iguazu in the country’s northeast. That flight landed in Guayaquil shortly before 4:00 a.m. (0900 GMT) before taking off again, AFP journalists and Flightradar24 data confirmed. Bolsonaro’s final destination is unknown, but the US State Department said it would issue visas to the senator and his family. AFP The post Plane reportedly carrying Bolsonaro stops briefly in Ecuador appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ogun LG challenges Lagos boundary signpost on disputed Yakoyo–Ojodu Road
body:
The Chairman of Ifo Local Government Area of Ogun State, Idris Kusimo, has challenged the placement of a “Welcome to Lagos State” signpost along the disputed Yakoyo–Ojodu Road, asking the Lagos State Government to intervene in the boundary disagreement.
Mr Kusimo said the signpost could mislead residents and motorists about the territorial boundary between the two states, insisting that the affected location around Yakoyo in Isheri-Ojodu Ward falls within Ogun State.
In a statement issued on Tuesday, the council chairman urged Lagos Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu to address the matter and ensure that actions by officials of the state did not aggravate the disagreement.
“Ifo Local Government maintains that the location of the signposts raises concerns about the boundary between the two states and has challenged the claim implied by their placement,” the statement read.
Contacted by PREMIUM TIMES for comments on Wednesday, the Lagos State Commissioner for Information and Strategy, Gbenga Omotoso, acknowledged the installation of boundary signposts at various locations across the state but said he was unaware of the dispute over the site of the signpost along Yakoyo–Ojodu Road.
“I’m not aware of that. You should contact the ministry in charge,” he said.
But the Lagos State Government justified the signposts installation along the state’s boundaries in an X post on Tuesday. It said the installation followed the specifications of the state’s surveyor general.
“The initiative is aimed at providing clarity on ambiguities around boundary demarcations between communities and neighbouring States, and to prevent disputes that may arise from boundary encroachment,” the statement stated.
It also quoted the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy Affairs and Rural Development, Kikelomo Bolarinwa, as saying during the commencement of the exercise that the state government was committed to ensuring clear boundaries between communities and neighbouring states.
Mrs Bolarinwa, whose Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy Affairs and Rural Development, is championing the signpost installation exercise, said the initiative would ensure the boundaries were “properly indicated in line with the position of the Office of the Surveyor General.”
However, Mr Kusimo said the signpost’s placement had heightened concerns about the boundary around Yakoyo, particularly following the construction of a road in the area by the Ogun State Government under Governor Dapo Abiodun.
“The dispute follows the placement of signposts bearing the inscription, ‘Welcome to Lagos State,’ along a newly constructed road built by the Ogun State Governor,” he said.
The chairman maintained that the disputed location falls within his local government’s jurisdiction and accused Lagos State of repeatedly attempting to assert control over areas it considers part of Ogun State.
“Over the years, the Lagos State Government has made several attempts to encroach on the Ogun State part of the area, which has always brought about confusion and unrest for residents,” he said.
The council called for the boundary to be determined through official records, approved survey coordinates and other relevant government documents, arguing that an authoritative determination would help prevent further misunderstandings and protect residents’ interests.
“The matter underscores the importance of establishing the precise boundary through official records, approved survey coordinates and relevant government documentation to prevent misunderstandings and ensure respect for the territorial jurisdictions of both states,” Mr Kusimo said.
He urged both state governments to handle the matter cautiously to prevent tension in communities along their shared boundary.

title: Three Royal Navy Vanguard-class submarines at sea does not signal change in nuclear posture
body:
Three of the Royal Navy’s four Vanguard-class ballistic missile submarines are currently at sea, an unusual concentration of boats that has prompted speculation about a change in Britain’s nuclear posture. The available evidence instead points towards routine operational activity and, more positively, improving submarine availability after several years in which maintaining the deterrent has placed exceptional demands on boats and crews.
One submarine is always maintaining Continuous At-Sea Deterrent (CASD) patrol, carrying Trident II D5 ballistic missiles, a mission that has continued without interruption since 1969. A second is believed to be preparing to relieve the patrol boat, while the third is probably conducting sea trials or work-up activity.
At the time of writing, the boat that left to take up the deterrent patrol in April has been away for 199 days and can be expected home very soon. Another Vanguard-class boat was observed conducting short periods at sea during September before visiting the Coulport Explosives Handling Jetty and sailing again on 12 October. A third left Faslane two days later.
This pattern is consistent with the handover of the deterrent patrol overlapping with trials or training by the third available submarine. A relieving boat normally conducts work-up activity before taking over CASD, so having two Vanguard boats at sea simultaneously for a period around a handover is not in itself unusual. Both will be fully armed with an outfit of Trident missiles.
Having three at sea together is much rarer, but not unprecedented and last occurred in 2022. HMS Victorious, the fourth boat, is not part of the current activity. She is in 9 Dock at Devonport undergoing a £560M Deep Maintenance Period intended to extend her operational life into the 2030s.
The more significant aspect of the current movements is therefore likely to be the return of a third boat to the operational rotation. Vanguard availability has been poor in recent years and CASD has at times effectively depended on two submarines alternating patrols. This has contributed to increasingly lengthy deployments, including a record 205-day patrol completed in April this year. Every one of the previous nine patrols had exceeded five months. Restoring three boats to the rotation would give considerably more room for maintenance, training and crew recovery and could finally allow patrol lengths to begin falling towards more sustainable levels.
Several media reports have linked the three submarines being at sea with heightened international tensions and the first UK-French joint nuclear air exercise conducted last week. During Exercise Rummy, French Rafales simulated a nuclear strike over the Mediterranean while RAF Typhoons provided escort. No nuclear weapons were involved. There is no evidence that the Vanguard movements are connected with that exercise or represent nuclear signalling. Britain maintains CASD precisely so that its strategic deterrent is continuously deployed and does not normally have to be visibly surged to sea in response to a developing crisis. The four-boat force is primarily structured to guarantee that one SSBN can remain continuously on patrol while the others undergo preparation, training and maintenance.
The Government maintains deliberate ambiguity about the detailed readiness and loading of the deterrent, so it cannot be stated that additional Vanguard boats could never be used to increase readiness during a crisis. Three boats being at sea, however, does not mean that Britain suddenly has three nuclear deterrent patrols underway.
The weapons carried should also be treated carefully. Vanguard-class submarines have 16 missile tubes, but the UK no longer publishes the number of Trident missiles or nuclear warheads deployed aboard individual boats. Before this policy changed in 2021, the declared load had been no more than eight operational missiles and 40 warheads per submarine on patrol. Trident II D5 is capable of carrying multiple independently targetable re-entry vehicles, but the present British missile and warhead configuration is classified.
For the Submarine Service, the unusual sight of three Vanguard boats simultaneously at sea is therefore more likely to be encouraging than ominous. After years of strained availability and exceptionally long patrols, it suggests the RN may finally be getting a third submarine back into the regular CASD rotation.

title: Novatek ready to offer technologies, LNG to Africa
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Novatek is prepared to offer its technologies and LNG to Africa and is open to discussing specific projects, the company’s Deputy Chairman of the Management Board, Director for Advanced Projects Sergey Solovyev said.
"Novatek is ready to offer two things to its African partners: technology that is unique globally, and its own LNG to generate energy for decades to come. We are interested in a long-term partnership and are ready to work together to develop specific projects and locations," he said on the sidelines of the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.
In addition to shareholders’ funds, major joint projects in Africa may be financed through the World Bank and the African Development Bank, Solovyev added.
"We offer integrated projects for generating power and receiving LNG: a single facility instead of four construction sites, one hub for several countries," he noted.
TASS is an information partner of the third Russia-Africa Summit and Economic and Humanitarian Forum.

title: Japan Football Official Quits Over World Cup Row
body: The vice president of Japan’s football association quit on Wednesday saying the “series of responses” to controversies surrounding the World Cup did not align with his personal values. Takeshi Okada, who coached Japan at the World Cup in 1998 and again in 2010, stepped down a week after the head of Asian football said the region supported Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election as FIFA president. Asian Football Confederation (AFC) president Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa delivered the unequivocal backing at a meeting in Tokyo. It came weeks after the AFC had joined football bodies in Europe and North America in condemning Infantino over his plan to open FIFA’s premium competitions such as the World Cup to private investors. Infantino has faced calls to quit and lost the support of some associations in his bid to be re-elected to a fourth and final term. Okada, who is one of three Japan Football Association (JFA) vice presidents, said he was stepping down “entirely of my own volition”. “Throughout my career I have treasured the social value of sport based on my conviction that sport must be conducted with integrity,” he said. “However, with regard to the series of responses surrounding the recent FIFA World Cup, there is a significant gap between those responses and my own beliefs, and as a sportsman I cannot accept them.” Infantino, who apologised for the failed private investment project, has headed FIFA since 2016 and is running for re-election in March. Two months ago the AFC and Sheikh Salman signalled they could turn on Infantino. A joint letter with European body UEFA and CONCACAF, representing federations in North and Central America and the Caribbean, declared football “belongs to no individual”. Okada said his decision had been “reached after careful and repeated deliberation”. “Taking into account our relationship with the AFC and the impact on Japanese football, I do understand that there are practical reasons for aligning our stance with that of the AFC,” he said. AFP The post Japan Football Official Quits Over World Cup Row appeared first on Channels Television .

title: 4 in 10 Americans say personal finances worsening: Survey
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 28 (MNA) – Four in 10 Americans say their personal finances are deteriorating, according to a new poll released shortly before November’s midterm elections.
In the NPR/PBS Poll, 40 percent of people said their “personal family finances” have declined in the last 12 months, while 16 percent said the opposite.
Forty-one percent said their personal family finances have “stayed about the same” within the prior year. Less than 1 percent of poll respondents were not sure about the state of their personal family finances within the last year, while three percent didn’t give an answer.
The NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll was conducted two weeks out from Election Day, with the rise in cost of living being a major concern in this election cycle, THE Hill reported.
Democrats have campaigned on targeting the Trump administration’s tariffs and the war in Iran — two factors behind U.S. price hikes. Amid the Iran war, the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for the oil industry, has been closed.
The average price of a regular gallon of gas in the U.S. has risen from about $3.05 last year to about $4.27 as of Tuesday afternoon. The average price of a gallon of diesel has risen in the last year, sitting at about $6.35 as of Tuesday afternoon compared to its $3.66 a gallon price in 2025.
In the NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll, 52 percent of respondents said they would cast their ballot for a Democrat for their congressional district if the election occurred that day, while 42 percent said the same of a Republican.

title: 5 inmates reportedly transferred after alleged plot to poison Wontumi in Nsawam Prison – Aide
body: A senior aide to former New Patriotic Party (NPP) Ashanti Regional Chairman Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, says five inmates at Nsawam Prison have been transferred following an alleged plot to poison the politician. Dr Palgrave Boakye-Danquah disclosed the development on Adom FM Dwaso Nsem , explaining that the alleged plot came to light after someone reportedly overheard the inmates discussing plans to poison Mr Wontumi. He said Mr Wontumi informed him about the incident when they spoke about his health following a court appearance on Tuesday, October 27. Dr Boakye-Danquah also said he had visited the prison over the weekend on an errand for the incarcerated NPP stalwart’s lawyer, Samuel Atta Akyea. According to the aide, the person who allegedly overheard the conversation alerted Mr Wontumi, prompting concerns about his safety. “I contacted the officer in charge, and he confirmed it and assured me that investigations were ongoing. The officer said a committee has been set up to probe the incident,” Dr Boakye-Danquah said. He indicated that the five inmates had since been moved to a different cell, while investigations into the alleged plot continued. The aide did not disclose the identities of the inmates, saying they had not been made known to him. Despite the development, Dr Boakye-Danquah said Mr Wontumi remained calm and was not frightened by the alleged threat. “Chairman Wontumi is not frightened,” he said, recounting the politician’s response during their conversation. He expressed confidence that the alleged plot would not succeed, adding: “But we know the good God we serve will not let the plan of the evil one prevail.” Dr Boakye-Danquah further disclosed that he was visiting the Nsawam Prison on Wednesday morning to visit Mr Wontumi and follow up on his welfare. The disclosure comes as Mr Wontumi marks 100 days in prison.

title: Zelensky Seeks Managers to Fix Kyiv’s Winter Crisis, but No One Wants to Take the Job
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky says Kyiv is unprepared for winter and wants experienced managers to help tackle the capital’s infrastructure problems. But potential candidates are reluctant to take on the job, as the dispute over the city’s readiness and leadership intensifies.
Speaking to journalists on Monday , Zelensky said Kyiv had failed to fully implement its resilience plans, citing concerns over electricity and water supplies, critical infrastructure protection and bridges.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
He said he had nothing personal against Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko but argued that the capital needed stronger management to prepare for Russian attacks and the coming winter.
Zelensky pointed to Kharkiv as an example of cooperation between city and regional authorities, regardless of their political differences.
“We have one common enemy, one winter and one country,” he said.
The president said he had asked the prime minister to assemble a special team for Kyiv, bringing together experienced managers from business and government. Zelensky said he was ready to personally approach candidates proposed for the role.
But potential candidates have been reluctant to accept the responsibility, he said, citing the pressure involved and the likelihood of political criticism.
Those reportedly considered for the task include former Infrastructure Minister Oleksandr Kubrakov, former Prime Minister Volodymyr Groysman, former Security Service of Ukraine chief Vasyl Maliuk and former Zhytomyr Mayor Serhii Sukhomlyn.
Zelensky also argued that Klitschko should be contacting experienced managers himself to help resolve the capital’s problems, rather than waiting for the president to intervene.
Klitschko has accused the central government of exploiting concerns over Kyiv’s winter preparations and bomb shelters to undermine his elected administration and tighten its control over the capital.
Speaking to Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty on Oct. 20 , he alleged that officials were behind a protest demanding his resignation. He named no officials and provided no direct evidence linking the government to the demonstration.
“Everything is being done to establish a military administration, implement centralized control, create a hierarchical structure, and destroy local self-government,” Klitschko said.
Several hundred people gathered outside Kyiv’s city administration building on Oct. 17, demanding his resignation over winter preparations, shelter shortages and spending priorities. Protesters also criticized urban improvement projects during wartime.
Klitschko pushed back against criticism of the city’s shelter network, saying Kyiv had more than 4,000 shelters. He also said funds allocated for mobile shelters remained unused because district administrations had not submitted requests.

title: Putin spent a call with Finnish and Norwegian leaders lecturing them on Slavic history, FT reports
body: Russian President Vladimir Putin spent much of an October 27 phone call with Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre recounting the “medieval Slavic history,” the Financial Times reported, citing sources familiar with the conversation. The call was initially expected to last 30 minutes but instead ran for an hour and a half. Putin spent most of the call describing what the Kremlin considers the “initial reasons for the conflict” rather than discussing ways to end the Russia–Ukraine war, according to the Financial Times. The prospect of an immediate ceasefire came up only briefly, the outlet’s sources said. One of the sources said Stubb and Støre chose not to interrupt Putin, wanting to gauge how serious he was about pursuing dialogue with Europe. The conversation between Stubb, Støre, and Putin took place at the initiative of Western leaders. The Kremlin reported the day before that the Russian president had “assessed the current situation” in Ukraine, recalling the “root causes of the conflict,” and had also drawn attention to the “confrontational policy of EU and NATO countries, which is prolonging the fighting.” A source close to the Kremlin told Reuters that Putin told Stubb and Støre that Russia would not abandon its goal of seizing the entire territory of Donbas. The European leaders responded that a “just” peace was necessary. During conversations with Western politicians and journalists, Putin has repeatedly spent a long time recounting his version of the history of Russia and Ukraine. He did so, for example, in an interview with American journalist Tucker Carlson in 2024, and during a meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump in Alaska. At the end of October 2026, Putin, in an interview with Pavel Zarubin, a correspondent for the Russian state broadcasting company VGTRK, commenting on his meeting with Trump’s negotiators, said that Russia does not want to fight Ukraine. According to him, “the latest genetic research shows that this is one people — Russians and Ukrainians.” It is unclear what research he was referring to. title: Motorists’ behaviour improves following sensitisation on TraffiTech – ACP Alexander Obeng
body: The Director of Education, Research and Training at the Police Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD), Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Alexander Kwaku Obeng, says the introduction of the TraffiTech-GH initiative and the issuance of caution notices to drivers have contributed to improved road-use behaviour. He said the police had observed positive changes in driver conduct, supported by data gathered since the technology-driven traffic enforcement system was introduced in some parts of the country. “With this strategy of embedding some of these cameras in vehicles running our roads all over and having some that are tripod-mounted that are also able to move from one end to the other, we have seen a very positive impact on the behaviour of motorists in the first place,” he said on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Wednesday, October 28. He attributed the changes to increased awareness of the initiative and warnings issued to drivers, which he said had encouraged them to be more cautious on the roads. “Within twenty days of September this year, when we enhanced sensitisation, gathering evidence and confronting vehicle owners with it, with an embedded message with GPS, MTTD sender ID sending messages saying speed kills, reduce it now with your vehicle number, time and place of the offence; if you compare the data of crashes from September last year (2025) with the same period this year, we have seen a significant change in behaviour of drivers,” he disclosed. He backed the claims with the data, saying, “Crises reported to the Ghana Police Service across our twenty-five police regions in Ghana in the last year amounted to 1,108. Now we have recorded 1,003, a reduction of 9.4%.” “Vehicles that were involved in these crashes last year were 1,928, and we have seen a significant reduction of 12.19%; that is, 1,693. In terms of morbidity, we have seen last year’s record of 1,405 persons, both male and female, getting injured; we have seen a significant reduction of 15.02% to 1,194,” he added. Traffitech-GH is an automated system developed by the Ghana Police Service to enforce road traffic laws and regulations and improve road safety in the country. The system uses cameras and sensors to automatically take a picture and/or video of vehicles that flout road traffic laws and regulations, such as speeding and running a red light.

title: Evzones Bring Oxi Day Pride to Parliament House
body: CANBERRA, October 2026 — The Evzones of the Hellenic Presidential Guard visited Parliament House on Wednesday for an Oxi Day morning tea, during their first official visit to the national capital. The Greek Orthodox Community and Church of Canberra hosted the Evzones at Parliament House, while the Hellenic Club of Canberra sponsored the visit. Clergy, including His Grace Bishop Athenagoras, also attended. A large group of guests and clergy pose with the Evzones in Parliament House. Photo: Nick Bourdaniotis John Loukadellis, president of the Greek Orthodox Community and Church of Canberra, said the visit carried deep meaning. “For the Greek Australian community, this visit is not simply ceremonial,” Loukadellis said. “It is deeply emotional and profoundly symbolic.” Seeing the Evzones in Canberra is “a moment of immense pride” for Australians of Greek heritage, Loukadellis said. He added that it “brings our history to life” and strengthens the connection between generations. Loukadellis also paid tribute to Les Cook, the last surviving ANZAC of the Battle of Crete. Cook lived in Canberra and died earlier this year aged 103 . Guests and officers sign the guest book at Parliament House. Photo: Nick Bourdaniotis Evzones at Parliament House House of Representatives Speaker Milton Dick welcomed the Evzones to Parliament House. “More than 424,000 Australians claim Greek ancestry, and generations of Greek Australians have made outstanding contributions to our nation’s economic, cultural, civic, public and political life,” Dick said. Clare O’Neil, Minister for Housing, Homelessness and Cities and co-chair of the Parliamentary Friends of Greek Australians, lives in Oakleigh. She said the community “enriches the life of me and my family every single day” . Recalling 28 October 1940, O’Neil said: “That is the day that Greeks stood up and said no. Oxi. No to fascism.” The Evzones in the courtyard of Parliament House in Canberra. Photo: Nick Bourdaniotis Similarly, former Deputy Prime Minister Michael McCormack, Member for Riverina, has Greek heritage through his grandfather. “We love traditions here in Australia, but of course, nobody does tradition like the Greeks,” McCormack said. Video: Kosta Velanis Dr Monique Ryan MP and Senator Andrew McLachlan CSC attended, as did Ambassador of Greece Stavros Venizelos and High Commissioner of Cyprus Haralambos Kafkarides. In addition, the Hellenic Club of NSW, the Greek Community of Melbourne, PRONIA, Fronditha Care, The Hellenic Initiative Australia and Oakleigh Cannons FC sent representatives. John Loukadellis, president of the Greek Orthodox Community and Church of Canberra, speaks at Parliament House. Photo: Nick Bourdaniotis Oxi Day and the Battle of Crete Oxi Day marks 28 October 1940, when Greece rejected Fascist Italy’s ultimatum. Later, in 1941, about 34,000 Australians and New Zealanders fought alongside Greeks in Greece and on Crete. This year marks the 86th anniversary of Oxi Day and the 85th of the Battle of Crete. The Evzones, who guard the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier in Athens, are visiting Sydney and Canberra from 22 to 29 October. A speaker at the Oxi Day ceremony at Parliament House. Photo: Nick Bourdaniotis After leaving Parliament House, the Evzones laid a wreath at the Australian War Memorial on Wednesday afternoon. Then, at 6:30pm, the Guard is due to march into the Hellenic Club of Canberra in Woden. title: Billion-query-per-second lookup tables in C++
body:
A lot of software spends its time mapping strings to values. A web server must identify the HTTP method ( GET , POST , …). It must recognize header names. A URL parser must recognize the protocol ( http , https , ftp , …). A compiler must recognize keywords.
In C++, the default approach is to put the strings in a std::unordered_map .
It works. But notice something: the keys are known when you write the code. They never change. And yet we pay at runtime as if they could change at any time: we hash the whole string, we pick a bucket, we follow a pointer, we compare, maybe we walk a list.
A hash function maps keys to slots. When two keys land in the same slot, we have a collision, and we must deal with it. Collisions are what make hash tables complicated and slow.
If you know all of your keys ahead of time, you can construct a hash function designed for your keys, a function that never produces a collision. It is called a perfect hash function. The idea is old: the GNU gperf tool has been doing it since 1989. You give it a list of keywords, and it generates C code.
We follow the same design as gperf . The slot for a key is computed as follows.
We add the length of the key to a few small values taken from an association table ( asso ) indexed by the characters at a few selected positions. Usually, one or two positions are enough. The table size is a power of two, so the modulo is a single bitwise AND.
Consider the four HTTP methods GET , PUT , POST and DELETE . We use only the first character. Set asso['G'] = 0 , asso['P'] = 1 and asso['D'] = 0 . Then GET goes in slot 3 + 0 = 3, PUT goes in slot 3 + 1 = 4, POST goes in slot 4 + 1 = 5 and DELETE goes in slot 6 + 0 = 6. No collision.
To look up PUT , we compute the slot (4), and we compare PUT with the one key stored in slot 4. One hash, one comparison. If you look up PATCH , which is not in the set, you land in slot 5 + 1 = 6, you compare with DELETE , and you are done: not found. There is no probing, no chain to walk.
How do we find the association values? We sort the characters by how many keys they touch. We then take them one at a time and try 0, 1, 2, … until we find a value that does not cause a collision. We never revise a value once it is set. It is a greedy algorithm with bounded work. The bound matters because we do all of this at compile time, and C++ compilers limit how much work a constexpr function may do.
With our library , you write ordinary C++23. There is no external tool to run.
The map is a compile-time constant. The compiler searches for the perfect hash function when it compiles your code. At runtime, computing the hash can take as few as four instructions: load one byte of the key, load one byte from the association table, add the length, apply a mask.
Computing the hash is cheap. But we still need to check that the string we are looking up matches the key stored in the slot. And comparing strings can be expensive: the textbook approach is a loop over the bytes with a branch for each byte. You can easily end up with dozens of instructions and several branches, and the branches are hard to predict when the strings vary.
Instead, we treat the key as a vector. Our processors, whether ARM or x64, have 16-byte registers. So we load 16 bytes unconditionally, even if the key is only three bytes long. We then use a shuffle instruction ( tbl on ARM NEON) to zero the bytes past the end of the key. The stored keys are zero-padded at compile time. A single vector comparison handles the whole key. We go from about forty instructions and eight branches to five instructions and no branch.
But wait: is it safe to read 16 bytes when you only have three? Reading past the end of a buffer is fine as long as you do not cross into another memory page, and pages are at least 4 kilobytes. So we check whether the address is within 16 bytes of the end of its page. If it is, we take a slower path. Otherwise, we do the wide load. We traded several unpredictable branches for a single branch that is almost always taken the same way.
I ran the benchmarks on an Apple M3 Max with AppleClang 15. We look up the keys in random order and we report the time per lookup. Let us first consider the 20 standard HTTP header names.
We need about 1.3 ns per lookup, or about 5 cycles. The classic gperf needs 7.7 ns. Abseil’s flat_hash_map , an excellent hash table, needs 10.9 ns. And std::unordered_map needs 16.6 ns. We are thirteen times faster than the standard library.
It is not one lucky key set. Here are the results over several sets of keys, from 6 URL protocols to the 100 tickers of the S&P 100.
We stay between 1.2 ns and 2 ns per lookup. We are 3 to 6 times faster than gperf , and 7 to 13 times faster than std::unordered_map . Notice how gperf struggles with the JavaScript reserved words: there we are 17 times faster.
Why is std::unordered_map so much slower? The C++ standard essentially requires a chained hash table. A lookup hashes the whole string by calling a function, follows a pointer to a heap-allocated node and walks a list. Our lookup does a few loads and has no function call. The processor can retire over 8.6 instructions per cycle with our code, which is about as good as it gets on this chip, and it almost never mispredicts a branch.
On an Apple M4, with the URL protocols, we exceed one billion lookups per second.
If your keys are known at compile time, you should not pay for collision handling at runtime. A perfect hash function gets you down to one comparison. With some care, a lookup costs about five cycles. The library is a single header you can drop in your project: github.com/ConstexprCore/perfect_hash .
This is joint work with Francisco Geiman Thiesen (Microsoft). We presented it at P99 CONF 2026. You can watch the talk on YouTube .
The benchmark numbers and the plotting script are available.
Daniel Lemire, "Billion-query-per-second lookup tables in C++," in Daniel Lemire's blog , October 26, 2026, https://lemire.me/blog/2026/10/26/billion-query-per-second-lookup-tables-in-c/ . [BibTeX]
A computer science professor at the University of Quebec (TELUQ). View all posts by Daniel Lemire

title: Zelenskyy to visit Netherlands Wednesday, Dutch government to allocate EUR 1.2 bln to Ukraine over 3 years – media
body:
President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy will visit the Netherlands on Wednesday to hold meetings with Prime Minister Rob Jetten and King Willem-Alexander, while the country's government will announce the allocation of €1.2 billion in non-military aid to Ukraine over the next three years, Dutch media report.
According to NOS, Prime Minister Jetten will receive Zelenskyy in the afternoon at Catshuis in The Hague. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defense Dilan Yesilgöz and Minister of Foreign Affairs Tom Berendsen will also join the negotiations.
Following the meeting, the Ukrainian president will speak with representatives of Dutch and Ukrainian businesses, and in the early evening, he will visit King Willem-Alexander at Huis ten Bosch Palace.
As BNR News notes, this is Zelenskyy's first visit to Catshuis under Jetten's premiership. The Ukrainian president last visited the Netherlands in December of last year, when the government was headed by Dick Schoof. In April, Zelenskyy and Jetten met in Middelburg, where the Ukrainian president was awarded the Four Freedoms Award.
"Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is visiting the Netherlands today... The visit coincides with the day the government is allocating new funds for the reconstruction of Ukraine. Over the next three years, the government will spend 1.2 billion euros on non-military aid to Ukraine," the publication's report on Wednesday states.

title: Real Madrid Apologise To China Over Mbappe Comments
body: Spanish football giants, Real Madrid apologised to China on Wednesday for star striker Kylian Mbappe’s comments poking fun at Mao Zedong. “Real Madrid C.F. wishes to express its apologies to the Chinese people for any offense caused by the recent remarks of our player Kylian Mbappe,” read the club’s statement, which came 24 hours after the furore broke. Mbappe was dropped Tuesday by two major brands in China after a video circulated online in which the French football star apparently joked about former leader Mao Zedong. “Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments,” drinks giant Dongpeng said in a statement, adding that “with immediate effect we are terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappe”. Mengniu, China’s largest dairy producer, also cut ties with the Real Madrid and France forward. “With immediate effect our company is terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappe,” Mengniu said in a statement. “Mengniu firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people,” it added. The announcements came after a video emerged online with Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen was of his face photoshopped onto that of “some guy — I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao, one of several using the footballer’s face and other historical figures. The authenticity of the video could not immediately be verified by AFP Fact Check. “Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe” was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo. The 27-year-old Mbappe lost out to Harry Kane for the Ballon d’Or on Monday. The post Real Madrid Apologise To China Over Mbappe Comments appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Tinubu’s burden, Atiku’s opportunity: The road to 2027, By Adnan Mukhtar
body:
Even the governors and National Assembly candidates of the APC are doing their posters alone without attaching the picture of Tinubu to these. Go through the billboards in the North, and you’ll notice that attaching Tinubu’s picture to your poster will create enmity for you and make you unpopular.
Elections are not won by emotions but by fact. Political party candidates campaign to people on the basis of what they can offer, while the ones in power use the dividends of their leadership to people as their major tools of campaign, by telling the world what they have done in terms of development. The opposition looks at that, criticises where they have gone wrong and what they have not provided for the people as a crucial part of its campaign.
That’s constructive campaigning. The recent flag off of President Tinubu’s campaign in Kaduna on Saturday says a lot about the failure of the president to deliver good governance to Nigerians.
I expected to president to campaign on three or four areas where the North is left behind in his government, not to talk of the massive nepotism whereby his kinsmen are in charge of critical government agencies, while not treating Nigerians equally. I was expecting to see President Tinubu making adjustments to the sort of nepotism that took place during the administration of President Muhammadu Buhari; however things are getting only worse, with Nigerians and the north experiencing the worst ever nepotistic government ever since independence.
The president should have asked himself whether the North has recovered from the massive kidnapping enterprises which he inherited from Buhari. Are people with fertile land to farm still going to their various farms to do produce food for the country? This answer is a resounding ‘No,’ due to the insecurity in the North.
In Kaduna, a family was kidnapped and nearly killed before they were rescued. Nobody knows whether ransom was paid or not but the Kaduna State government claimed to have rescued them. Governor Uba Sani was even seen thanking the National Security Adviser for his efforts in the rescue mission. This is the situation that the North still finds itself under President Tinubu.
The second most important thing is economic instability. No one would believe that there is economic improvement in the country, when people are not able to have three square meals in a day, and when people are abandoning their cars for electric bikes.
This is one area in which Atiku has won the heart of the masses by promising to restore the fuel subsidy whose removal has had massive negative impact on the masses. People are living in hunger and abject poverty, one which I have witnessed at its most severe form since the return to democracy in 1999.
Tinubu seems to feel no regret over the hardship in the country, and is putting the blame on the opposition. This has provoked Nigerians the most.
Even the governors and National Assembly candidates of the APC are doing their posters alone without attaching the picture of Tinubu to these. Go through the billboards in the North, and you’ll notice that attaching Tinubu’s picture to your poster will create enmity for you and make you unpopular.
What Nigerians are after at the moment is for the person who will provide them with security, remove them from abject poverty, restore fuel subsidy, and provide them with a conducive environment that will create job opportunities for the unemployed.
Children can’t go to school because their parents cannot afford this, whilst the daily income, minimum wage and meagre salaries cannot cater for their needs.
As a politician, campaign for Tinubu and become unpopular. I have since realised that politicians at the forefront campaigning for Tinubu don’t care about the predicament of the North. Despite all the problems and challenges there, they tend to care for their pockets more, and not for Nigerians. This is most unpatriotic.
It’s sad that even when Tinubu decided to pick his campaign DG, he ended up with Senator Yari, who has a poor record of good governance. The only thing he knows how to do is sharing money to the people. There are even serious speculations that his source of wealth is associated to his record as a governor. He is said to have come into power not as a business man but ended his tenure as governor as one of the wealthiest persons in Nigeria.
When during a TV interview, the anchor Rufai Oseni asked after his track record as governor of Zamfara and the high rate of poverty when he led the state, he ended up beating around the bush in response.
Nigerians are feeling the pain deep in them and they will vote for Waziri Atiku Abubakar. They will give him a try because of the good plans he has for the country. He served this country as vice president with diligence, and he is one of the best and capacitated vice presidents that the country has so far produced, and not the spare tyre Kashim Shettima, who not only serves as Nigeria’s second citizen but as the number one praise singer of his principal.
Atiku will win massively for the aforementioned reasons. It’s the people who vote, not the elite who make noise on social media or television stations. Elections are won at the polling units and not on social media.
They will share the money, people will collect it and vote for the right person.
I refuse to make mention of other presidential candidates for one reason, many of them are working for the return of the president, especially the NDC. I trust Seyi Makinde of APM to be more serious as an opposition candidate than Peter Obi of the NDC and Rabiu Kwankwaso, who have appeared to be more concerned and critical of Waziri Atiku, rather than Tinubu who has inflicted hardship on Nigerians.
Adnan Mukhtar is a public affairs analyst, university lecturer and doctoral candidate at Bayero University, Kano.

title: Airbus and Air France-KLM finalize A350 component support joint venture
body:
Airbus and Air France-KLM have completed the creation of Alpha Component Solutions, a 50-50 joint venture providing component maintenance and support services for Airbus A350 operators worldwide.
The company starts operations with contracts covering more than 500 aircraft, according to Airbus. That is a significant figure compared with the 736 A350s in service worldwide at the end of September, although the manufacturer does not disclose how the contracts are distributed among operators.
Alpha Component Solutions combines A350 component support activities previously conducted separately by Airbus and Air France Industries KLM Engineering & Maintenance (AFI KLM E&M). Its services include component maintenance and repair, access to spare parts and management of component inventories.
The company is headquartered near Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport in Tremblay-en-France. Corporate filings show that Air France transferred A350 component activities conducted at Villeneuve-le-Roi, Charles de Gaulle and Orly, while Airbus contributed activities based in Blagnac, near Toulouse.
The new company is the result of a partnership first outlined more than three years ago. Airbus and Air France-KLM announced exclusive negotiations in September 2023, when they expected the joint venture to begin operations in the first half of 2024.
The process took considerably longer. Airbus and Air France-KLM signed the agreement establishing equal ownership of Alpha Component Solutions in December 2024, and the transaction was subsequently submitted to European competition authorities. The European Commission approved it in April 2026.
Follow Air Data News: WhatsApp | Instagram | LinkedIn | Twitter | Facebook
The transfer of the component activities to Alpha Component Solutions became effective on September 30, 2026.
The joint venture is structured as an independent business rather than an operation dedicated to the Air France-KLM fleet. Documents from the European Commission show that it has its own management and resources and is expected to generate most of its revenue from third-party customers.

title: Gazprom ready to cooperate with Africa on exploration, production of hydrocarbons
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Gazprom has established a complete technological cycle and is ready to cooperate with Africa in the exploration and production of hydrocarbons, their transportation, storage, processing, and power generation, Gazprom Deputy Chairman Vitaly Markelov said on the sidelines of the Russia-Africa Summit.
"We are prepared to consider joint projects in areas including exploration, prospecting, and production of hydrocarbons, transportation and storage of gas, gasification, expansion of gas consumption, power generation, oil and gas processing, and the development of infrastructure for natural gas as a motor fuel. Gazprom is open to dialogue and ready for mutually beneficial cooperation," he said.
Gazprom is also ready to offer large-, medium-, and small-scale LNG solutions to Africa, according to Markelov’s presentation. The company possesses its own gas liquefaction technologies, Gazprom MR and Gazprom DMR, with capacities ranging from 1.5 to 7 mln tons.
TASS is an information partner of the third Russia-Africa Summit and Economic and Humanitarian Forum.

title: More than 5,000 enter South Sudan from DR Congo amid Ebola outbreak
body: More than 5,000 people have crossed into South Sudan from neighbouring Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), reportedly fleeing an Ebola outbreak, the UN said on Tuesday. The arrivals entered Ibba County in Western Equatoria state between July and mid-October, according to figures from the International Organization for Migration (IOM), the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said. Nearly 380 of the arrivals are Congolese nationals, while the remainder are South Sudanese returning after seeking refuge in the DRC, OCHA said. During a visit last week to Nabanga Payam in Ibba County, OCHA and its partners found that most recent arrivals urgently needed medicines, nutritional supplies, food, kitchen utensils, sleeping mats, blankets and dignity kits for women and adolescent girls. The agencies also called for an Ebola isolation centre to be made operational to strengthen screening and disease surveillance at the Nabanga border crossing. Continued Ebola transmission in the DRC poses a risk of the disease spreading into South Sudan through cross-border movements, OCHA said. South Sudan’s Ministry of Health, National Public Health Institute and UN partners recently conducted a simulation exercise in Juba and in Yei and Yambio counties to test the country’s capacity to prevent, detect and respond to suspected Ebola cases. UN warns of rising violence Separately, the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) expressed concern about escalating violence in Tonj North and Tonj East counties in Warrap state, including an armed attack on Akop Payam early on Tuesday. The attack followed clashes on October 26 that left 72 people dead and 38 wounded, amid a cycle of retaliatory violence, UN Associate Spokesperson Daniela Gross de Almeida said during the UN noon briefing. UNMISS has deployed a six-day patrol in the area. Peacekeepers based in Warrap town are conducting patrols towards affected communities in coordination with local authorities, Daniela said. She said the mission is also engaging state and county authorities to help contain the violence and prevent further attacks. The post More than 5,000 enter South Sudan from DR Congo amid Ebola outbreak appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Three Killed By Storm In Southern India
body: Ferocious winds and torrential rain lashed India’s southeastern coast after a cyclone made landfall on Wednesday, killing at least three people before the storm weakened, officials said. Cyclone Arnab hit southeastern Andhra Pradesh state as a “very severe cyclonic storm”, with winds of 125-135 kilometres (77-84 miles) per hour and gusts reaching 150 kph in the early hours of Wednesday morning, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said. Torrential rain was recorded — as much as 30 centimetres (nearly 12 inches) in parts of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha states, IMD said, with the storm weakening into a “deep depression” throughout Wednesday afternoon. “Three people have lost their lives, and 31 homes have been damaged,” Narendra Singh Bundela, Inspector General of India’s National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) told reporters. National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) personnel gather near houses damaged by uprooted trees after cyclone Arnab’s landfall in Yanam, in India’s Puducherry on October 28, 2026. Photo by NOAH SEELAM / AFP Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu thanked officials who had “worked tirelessly throughout the night”. Around 50,000 people were told to move to safer areas in Andhra Pradesh and another 48,000 in neighbouring Odisha. “Our homes get flooded, and we have to stay in the water,” said Rajeshwari, 65, who gave only one name and had been taken to a government-run shelter near Kakinada. A man cycles through a water-logged street in Andhra Pradesh’s Kakinada on October 28, 2026, as cyclone Arnab makes landfall. Photo by NOAH SEELAM / AFP Overnight, gales battered trees and heavy rain lashed the port city of Kakinada, close to the heart of the storm, as powerful waves crashed ashore. Residents on Wednesday emerged onto flooded streets to what appeared to be limited damage in the city. ‘Safe indoors’ Emergency officials were also busy clearing uprooted trees and other debris from affected roads in the coastal region. “Thank God, there was not as much damage this time,” said businessman Hussain, 43, who uses one name. Sadiq, 40, a Kakinanda city resident, told AFP that the situation had become “very dangerous” on Tuesday night, but early warnings from authorities had helped people prepare. “Many people locked their houses and moved to safer places”, he said. Fishing community members arrive at a relief shelter during rainfall in Andhra Pradesh’s Kakinada on October 27, 2026 ahead of cyclone Arnab’s expected landfall. (Photo by Noah SEELAM / AFP) Cyclones, called hurricanes in the North Atlantic and typhoons in the Pacific, are a regular menace in the Bay of Bengal and northern Indian Ocean. The storm season, however, has been turbocharged by the El Nino weather phenomenon that has contributed to unprecedented warming. Neighbouring Sri Lanka and Nepal had also issued warnings. Nepal’s disaster authority warned that the storm would move inland towards the Himalayas, bringing heavy rainfall and “a high risk of heavy snowfall, snowstorms and avalanches”. Nepal is still recovering from a catastrophic August 26 flood triggered by a glacial mountain collapse, which killed more than 1,400 people and left over 5,000 missing. AFP The post Three Killed By Storm In Southern India appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Grossi, Orban candidacies for UN secretary-general post good for Russia — Likhachev
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. The UN secretary-general candidacies of former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban and IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi are highly appealing to Russia, Rosatom Director General Alexey Likhachev said.
"Both options, it seems to me, will be very attractive for Russia," Likhachev said in a comment to Life journalist Alexander Yunashev.
Yunashev recalled Likhachev's promise to drink Argentinian wine with Grossi if he won, and asked, referring to Orban: "Is the plum wine good too?" The Rosatom head replied with a laugh: "Yes, we have that experience."
Earlier, US media reported that Washington, Moscow and Beijing are considering Orban as a possible joint candidate to replace UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, whose mandate expires on December 31. The countries have not yet officially confirmed the initiative. Russian Presidential Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said that the presidents of Russia and the United States did not discuss Orban’s nomination during their last phone call.

title: Tenstorrent and Smallest.ai Partner to Bring Production-Grade Voice AI On-Prem
body:
Tenstorrent and Smallest.ai have partnered to deliver a production-grade, on-prem voice AI stack.
Tenstorrent, an AI compute company, and Smallest.ai, an AI research lab building real-time voice AI infrastructure, have partnered to deliver a production-grade, on-prem voice AI stack designed to reduce deployment costs while delivering the performance required for real-time voice applications. The joint solution runs Smallest.ai's Lightning V2 real-time text-to-speech model natively on Tenstorrent Galaxy™ Blackhole™ servers, unlocking enterprise-scale voice AI.
Deploying voice AI at scale has historically required companies to make tradeoffs between quality, cost, or control. Running Smallest.ai's Lightning V2 on Tenstorrent’s Blackhole architecture enables companies to run real-time voice agents entirely on-prem with full data sovereignty.
“There shouldn’t need to be a choice between performance and cost – Tenstorrent has built efficient and scalable compute that reduces the cost of existing workflows and makes entirely new workloads practical,” said Grant Jensen, Head of Software Partner Ecosystem at Tenstorrent.
“Tenstorrent’s architecture is fundamentally different from existing paradigms. Working with the NoC and larger SRAM, we unlocked 4x gains at a fraction of the cost of comparable GPU infrastructure , driving a structural shift in inference economics,” said Ranjith, Senior AI Inference Performance Engineer at Smallest.ai.
The joint solution supports high-volume, data-sensitive use cases across financial services, telecom, healthcare, and enterprise environments, enabling low-latency and highly concurrent workloads while giving organizations greater control over sensitive data and sovereign AI infrastructure.
Lightning V2 is available on Tenstorrent hardware today , with usage-based pricing and no upfront commitments.
Tenstorrent is an AI compute company led by CEO Jim Keller - architect of Apple A4/A5, AMD Zen, and Tesla's Full Self-Driving chip. The company builds RISC-V-based AI processors and systems for developers, enterprises, and sovereign infrastructure worldwide. In addition to servers and workstations, Tenstorrent licenses its TT-Ascalon RISC-V CPU and Tensix AI cores to chip designers including Samsung and LG. Backed by Bezos Expeditions, Samsung, LG Electronics, Hyundai Motor Group, Fidelity, and others, Tenstorrent has raised over $1B+ and operates from Santa Clara, Austin, Toronto, Belgrade, Tokyo, and Bangalore.
Smallest.ai is a foundational AI research lab building the next generation of real-time voice AI infrastructure for enterprises. The company develops speech recognition, speech generation, and speech-to-speech systems designed to enable natural, scalable AI conversations across customer service, healthcare, financial services, and other high-volume communication environments. Headquartered in San Francisco, Smallest.ai serves enterprises globally through its Voice 4.0 platform and proprietary AI models. The company is backed by Seligman Ventures, Sierra Ventures, 3one4 Capital, Better Capital, Upsparks Capital, Schema Ventures, Tiny VC, DeVC, Mission Street Capital, and other angel investors.

title: Five baobab trees destined for Georgia seized in South Africa
body: South Africa blocks shipment of baobabs to Georgia Authorities in the South African city of Durban have blocked the shipment of at least five baobab trees. The trees were reportedly destined for a landscaping project in Georgia . A criminal investigation into the case is now under way. According to Daily Maverick , officials discovered the baobabs at a warehouse in Durban owned by Africa Global Logistics (AGL), a subsidiary of Paris-based transport giant MSC Group . Bidzina Ivanishvili , Georgia’s informal ruler, is known for his passion for collecting rare trees and plants. His name has featured in several cases involving the import of exotic trees into the country. In 2022, an attempt to bring eight baobabs from Kenya to Georgia attracted international attention. However, all eight trees eventually dried up and died. Centuries old trees – the billionaire’s latest temptation How is Bidzina Ivanishvili changing the landscape? A Report from the Black Sea coast What happened According to South Africa’s Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE), those involved in exporting the trees failed to produce valid permits authorising their possession and removal from the country. The baobab is one of Africa’s most recognisable tree species and can live for up to 2,000 years. In South Africa, it is among 50 endemic tree species that receive special protection. Without the appropriate official permits, it is illegal to cut down, damage, move, possess, sell, transport or export these trees. The identities of the Georgian buyers and their representatives have not yet been disclosed. Candy Botha, AGL’s regional marketing manager, told Daily Maverick that the company had provided logistics services only. It was neither the owner of the cargo nor the exporter, and it did not hold the required permits. After learning that the trees were in Durban, Daily Maverick visited the AGL warehouse and photographed at least five baobabs. The trees lay on their sides on a paved surface. They appeared to have been left there in direct sunlight for two to three months. Asked about the trees’ legal status, the company said such matters fell outside its responsibilities as a logistics provider. AGL also refused to disclose the client’s identity or contact details, citing confidentiality. After Daily Maverick sent further questions to the DFFE, it emerged that no valid export licence had been issued for the trees. There was also no permit authorising their removal and relocation. According to available information, the baobabs came from the Waterberg District in Limpopo province. Based on photographs, Jeff Nichols, a specialist in endemic plants, suggested that the trees could be more than 50 years old if they had been taken from the wild. If they had instead been grown under artificial conditions with irrigation, he estimated their age at 20 to 30 years. The DFFE said the exporter applied for the required licence on 27 July 2026. The application covered the removal, possession, collection, transport, export and acquisition of five protected trees. However, the department rejected it on 31 July. “The application was rejected because a criminal investigation into the matter is under way. The department will not issue a licence retrospectively to legitimise actions that appear to have been unlawful,” the department said. On 8 August, the exporter appealed against the decision. The department said the appeal was currently under review by the official responsible for such matters. Asked whether the applicants had complied with the relevant regulations, the DFFE said they had failed to meet the requirements of the National Forests Act. According to the department, the trees came from the local municipality of Lephalale in Waterberg District, Limpopo province, and were intended for export to Georgia. The department has launched criminal proceedings in the case. Under the law, the offence carries a fine or a prison sentence of up to three years. The DFFE has not disclosed the names of those facing criminal proceedings, nor has it identified the owner of the trees or the exporter. The department explained that possessing, collecting, removing, transporting, exporting, buying or selling protected trees constitutes a Category 1 offence. The plan to transport the baobabs to Georgia has also raised concerns among environmentalists. Dr Sarah Venter, founder of the Baobab Foundation , said that although it was technically possible to uproot baobabs and transplant them elsewhere, the record of their survival in Georgia was discouraging. “Unfortunately, the survival rates of these trees in Georgia leave much to be desired,” Venter said. The oligarch’s hometown – the founding legend of the Georgian Dream Life in the hometown of Georgia’s richest, most powerful man The Kenyan case: eight baobabs transplanted to Georgia dried up and died The investigation currently under way in South Africa echoes an earlier attempt to transport baobabs from Kenya to Georgia, an incident that attracted international attention in 2022. On 24 October 2022, The Guardian reported that Kenyan farmers had sold baobabs growing on their land to a group led by Georgian national Giorgi Gvasalia. The plan involved uprooting eight trees and transporting them to Georgia. In November that year, Kenya’s Ministry of Environment suspended a foreign company’s licence to uproot baobabs, citing several violations. The ministry also instructed the Kenya Forest Service to stop the trees from being moved. The ministry said uprooting baobabs required the appropriate permit and a transparent process demonstrating how relocating the trees would benefit the public. It concluded that the established requirements had not been met in this case. In April 2023, the Environment Committee of Kenya’s National Assembly, the lower house of parliament, launched an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the export of baobabs from the Kilifi region to Georgia. The eight uprooted trees remained in that condition for almost two years and eventually died. According to Georgia’s Dendrological Park, workers had uprooted the trees in 2021, but various obstacles delayed their transport to Georgia until October 2023. They planted the baobabs in the ground on 8 November 2023. “These African giants spent almost two years uprooted, in natural conditions entirely unsuitable for them and without proper care. Unfortunately, the stress took its toll: six to seven months after they were planted in Georgia, all eight baobabs had died,” the park said. Investigators in South Africa must establish who owned the trees and who arranged their removal from the country, under what circumstances these protected plants were uprooted, and who bears responsibility for the attempt to transport them to Georgia. South Africa blocks shipment of baobabs to Georgia

title: U.S. Air Force plans $1 billion campus at Nellis to test F-47 sixth-generation fighter
body: An October 22 presolicitation notice seeks up to four qualified firms for the design-and-build project. The estimated cost includes construction, design, security and other expenses. The campus would include a nearly 117,000-square-foot building for flightline operations and maintenance, primarily on the base’s east side. Plans also call for a specialized systems-reprogramming laboratory, an aircraft apron with sunshades and a simulator facility covering almost 41,000 square feet. Other facilities are listed as potential subsequent work. Those include hangars for fuel-system maintenance, corrosion control of the stealth coating, weapons-load training and maintenance training. The proposed schedule allows about nine months for design and preconstruction after the initial award. Approximately 40 months of construction would follow, taking the project into March 2031. The notice follows the Air Force’s fiscal 2027 budget request for $730 million in F-47 hangars and support infrastructure. That proposal identified Nellis as the location for the aircraft’s operational testing. The Air Force selected Boeing to develop the F-47 in March 2025, with the aircraft intended to replace the F-22 in the 2030s. Expected capabilities include advanced stealth, data sharing, electronic warfare and the ability to direct semi-autonomous Collaborative Combat Aircraft. Former Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. David Allvin said in September 2025 that the first F-47 was under construction and would fly in 2028. According to the magazine, service officials have continued to support that schedule. Source: Air & Space Forces Magazine .

title: Tinubu Addressing Longstanding Challenges, Barau replies Osinbajo
body: The Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau I. Jibrin, says President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is taking steps to address longstanding challenges confronting the country. Barau said that while Osinbajo’s concerns, particularly those drawn from Afrobarometer surveys on Nigeria and other African countries, were valid, the government needs to improve communication with the people to highlight ongoing efforts to address the challenges. The Deputy President of the Senate made the remarks on Tuesday in Yola, Adamawa State, during a public lecture titled “Democracy and Development: Rethinking the Leadership Question,” organised to commemorate the 59th birthday of Adamawa State Governor, Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri. Osinbajo, who served as Vice-President under former President Muhammadu Buhari from 2015 to 2023, expressed concern in his lecture about the failure of democratic governance among citizens across Africa after almost three decades of uninterrupted democratic rule in several countries. Citing Afrobarometer surveys, the former Vice-President highlighted widespread dissatisfaction with democratic institutions, economic hardship, declining public confidence in government and diminishing youth participation in electoral politics. He noted that although 64 per cent of Africans preferred democracy to other forms of government, only 38 per cent were satisfied with the way democracy was working in their respective countries. Osinbajo also cited findings indicating that 59 per cent of Africans considered their national economies to be in bad shape, while 51 per cent said their economies had deteriorated. He further expressed concern over the rising cost of living, unemployment, inadequate access to healthcare and declining voter turnout, warning that persistent hardship could weaken public confidence in democracy, particularly among young people. Responding to the presentation, Barau described Osinbajo’s lecture as thought-provoking and intellectually stimulating, but said the gloomy picture painted by the surveys was being addressed and that the gaps were partly attributable to inadequate communication between governments and citizens. “I know he is a very good orator, a good public speaker and an intellectual to the core,” Barau said, adding that he had initially decided not to prepare a speech to avoid turning the birthday celebration into an occasion for speeches. “Having said that, I am compelled to make some comments on the paper. It is a very beautiful and thought-provoking paper. “What I want to say is this: one important reason for the gloomy picture portrayed by the surveys, particularly those conducted by Afrobarometer, is what the professor talked about and specifically observed: the issue of communication between the leaders and the led. There is no proper communication.” The Deputy President of the Senate maintained that governments at both the federal and state levels were taking steps to address the challenges identified by the former Vice-President, particularly in the areas of education, infrastructure and economic development. On education, Barau said the government was expanding access to education to address the challenges posed by Nigeria’s growing population and its large youth demographic. He noted that providing educational opportunities for children, particularly those from disadvantaged backgrounds, remained critical to addressing the country’s long-term development challenges. “Before now, it was very difficult for a child who did not have the means to go to school. Now, everyone, except a child who does not want to go to school, can go to school in Nigeria with the NELFUND introduced by this administration,” he said. Barau also stressed the importance of infrastructure development in driving economic prosperity, noting that roads, water supply and other essential facilities were necessary to improve living standards and stimulate economic activities. He cited ongoing road projects across the country, including the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, the Badagry-Sokoto Highway and several projects in the North-East and North-West, as evidence of the government’s efforts to address infrastructure deficits. “When we talk about economic prosperity, you cannot achieve it without a certain level of infrastructure, including road networks, water supply and other essential infrastructure. “This is what is happening currently in this country under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration. Roads are being constructed everywhere to propel the process of bringing economic prosperity. That is being done. It is a long journey, but it is being done. Yet, there is no proper communication,” he said.

title: MTN reaffirms commitment to driving Ghana’s digital infrastructure- Group CEO
body: MTN Group President and CEO, Ralph Mupita, has reaffirmed MTN’s commitment to supporting Ghana’s digital infrastructure and digital sovereignty. He made this known during a working visit to Ghana on Monday, October 26 2026, as MTN Ghana marks 30 years of operating in the country. “Ghana remains a material operation for the Group, and our confidence in the country’s long-term prospects is unchanged. Our commitment is to support the Government’s digital transformation through mobile broadband and financial networks that support and strengthen Ghana’s digital sovereignty and support Africa’s progress,” Mr. Mupita said. During the visit, Mr. Mupita engaged key government stakeholders on how MTN’s accelerated investment will advance financial inclusion, connectivity and a resilient digital economy. Mr. Mupita paid a courtesy call on the Vice President of the Republic, H.E. Prof. Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang. Discussions focused on digital financial inclusion and how mobile money and digital platforms can expand economic opportunity for Ghanaian women, including traders, farmers and small business owners. The delegation also met the Honourable Minister of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Hon. Samuel Nartey George. The meeting focused on accelerating home broadband, expanding fibre and the rollout of 5G to enhance the experience for customers as well as investments needed to enable Ghana’s digital infrastructure needs. The final call was on the Bank of Ghana, with the Governor, Dr. Johnson Pandit Asiama. Mr. Mupita commended the Bank’s work in consolidating macroeconomic stability and reaffirmed MTN’s commitment to a safe, well-governed and inclusive digital payments ecosystem. MTN will continue investing in Ghana across connectivity, fintech and digital infrastructure. Mr. Mupita was accompanied by MTN Ghana CEO, Stephen Blewett and MobileMoney Fintech Limited CEO, Shaibu Haruna.

title: Innovation in action: Jetour entrenches cutting-edge travel strategy
body: These days, car manufacturers across the board are creating products that can be described as innovative, but Jetour is leading the charge by redefining just what a vehicle can do. Using advanced artificial intelligence, cutting-edge energy technologies and immersive, on-the-road experiences, the brand is transforming the concept of a traditional car. ​“The future evolution of vehicles lies not only in improvements in power and performance, but also in co-ordinating intelligent interaction, energy applications and mobility services to turn vehicles into intelligent travel companions for users,” says Jetour International president Ke Chuandeng. Global showcase of innovation Between October 20 and 23, the brand hosted its flagship 2026 Jetour Global Technology Experience Day is Wuhu, Moganshan, and Xiazhu Lake. The event offered a glimpse into tomorrow, with state-of-the-art tech displays, all-terrain off-road experiences and meaningful ecological conservation initiatives under the brand's signature Travel+ philosophy. ​Since its founding in 2018, Jetour has centred its entire product ecosystem around real-world travel needs. From sleek urban commuters to rugged long-distance explorers, the brand’s diverse portfolio is built for every kind of journey. ​The numbers speak volumes. As of September 2026, Jetour’s cumulative global sales crossed an impressive 2.56 million vehicles. With a presence in more than 100 countries and regions, a devoted global following of more than 50 million, and more than 300 owners' clubs worldwide, Jetour is rapidly expanding its vibrant travel community. ​Power and water on demand ​At the heart of Jetour’s technological leap is the groundbreaking G700, fitted with the innovative Solair system. Designed for extreme off-road adventures and remote road trips, the solar component uses a flexible photovoltaic cover to generate up to 6 kWh of electricity daily, with a peak output of 640 watts stored directly in the vehicle's traction battery. ​Meanwhile, the AIR system gathers moisture from the atmosphere through externally mounted equipment, filtering, disinfecting and heating it into up to five litres of pure, drinkable water every day. It is a game-changer for outdoor enthusiasts tackling remote terrain. ​At Moganshan, media and guests also put the C-DM Super Hybrid, XWD intelligent 4WD and GAIA architecture to the test. Features like visual AI working alongside chassis sensors and the V2L external power supply proved invaluable in challenging landscapes, while the G700 Ark Edition dazzled with its water navigation capabilities during emergency navigation drills. ​More than just a drive ​Jetour’s vision extends far beyond traditional automotive engineering. Through high-profile partnerships with FIBA, football clubs and international marathons, the brand weaves itself directly into global sports and cultural communities. ​Environmental stewardship is equally central to the Travel+ ethos. From protecting crested ibis and Tibetan antelope in China to global conservation efforts safeguarding cheetahs, sea turtles, markhor, and harpy eagles, Jetour ensures that exploring the world goes hand in hand with preserving it. ​Backed by an expansive global research and development network spanning the Middle East, Europe, the Americas and ASEAN – alongside more than 2,000 sales and service outlets worldwide – Jetour’s T-Series light off-roaders and G-Series luxury off-roaders are ready to take drivers further than ever before. ​The road ahead is intelligent, sustainable, and thrilling – and with Jetour, the future of travel has officially arrived. This page was produced by The National in partnership with Jetour
