title: Israel's election reveals a democracy of contradictions - opinion
body: And the people have spoken - out of both sides of their mouths. Bibi lovers can rejoice! Despite most polls predicting his loss, his Likud emerged as the largest party in the exit polls. Bibi haters can rejoice! The opposition parties together may have earned as many as 70 seats, to the coalition's 50.Once again, yet another Israeli election pivoted around Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's indefatigable political sorcerer. It's remarkable. After his October 7th failures, most people expected him to resign or be hounded out of office.Netanyahu and Israel's political tribalismYet three years later, Israelis voted in “droves,” and he survived.  “Droves” is the trigger word Netanyahu used in 2015 to warn of mass Arab voting, before apologizing a week later. Now, having mainstreamed thugs and descended himself into divisive demagoguery, especially as he panicked, he's not likely to backpedal this outburst of bigotry.Netanyahu's endurance, even without a coalition victory, reflects Israel's political tribalism. Party membership is often a social, ethnic, and political statement, from right to left, which Netanyahu exploits with virtuosity.But to be fair, his resurgence is not just irrational. Many of the post-October 7 moves that made Netanyahu's brand toxic worldwide, even in America, are what resurrected his domestic political career. Even many Israelis who detest him understand that the grueling fight in Gaza against Hamas was a just war.They acknowledge that he ultimately brought home 168 live hostages and accounted for every murdered hostage, while presiding over a war that crushed Hamas, Hezbollah and Iran. The fact that, as the Iranians and Americans keep skirmishing, neither side wants the Israelis fighting shows that the precious asset lost on October 7, Israeli deterrence, has been restored. Anyone who predicts what governmental constellation will result has a better crystal ball than I have. But, once again, I am struck by three clashing perceptions: the buoyant democracy so many Israelis experienced on Tuesday; the racist oppressor Israel's obsessive critics in the West decided they saw; and the infuriatingly successful society Israel's enemies watched, yet again.Israel remains one part kaleidoscope, genuinely projecting different, ever-changing, and sometimes contradictory images. It's also one part Rorschach test, as people praise or curse the oversimplified, black-and-white Israel they imagine because the real Israel is so multi-dimensional and elusive.This Election Day was particularly magical, given all that we have endured since October 7. So many observers noted how special it was that we have a Jewish democracy where we can vote freely, after thousands of years of being oppressed by authoritarian regimes.Families picnicked and shopped, kids enjoyed the day off from school, and most voters, despite their constitutional Israeli excitability, waited patiently, appreciatively, in the impressively long voting lines, as 77.7 of eligible voters cast those old-fashioned paper ballots.The joy, the calm, even the anxiety building toward the 10 p.m. exit poll announcement, illustrated Israeli democracy's strength and sacredness. We awaited the people's verdict.Calm contrasted with chaos of Israeli politicsSuch restraint also contrasted with the chaos and belligerence of Israeli politics. It's the kind of contradiction every soldier, every reservist, experiences. With lots of time on their hands, they all know where everyone stands politically, religiously, ideologically. And with stakes so high, they aren't afraid to shout about their differences, occasionally.But when it's time to spring into action, these distinct, often-dissimilar, hotheads become a high-functioning unit. And when reservist kids are bar mitzvahed, or fellow soldiers get married, you can always recognize the army friends' table; while broadening the events' demographics, they outdance everyone on the dance floor.Obsessively anti-Semitic anti-Zionists cannot compute Israel's many warm, human, intimate, and wonderfully democratic moments. Instead, burying the lede, they will emphasize the bigoted rants of Bibi and Itamar Ben-Gvir, rather than the remarkable results of this election wherein Ben-Gvir's bigotry motivated many Arabs to vote.Arabs not only have the right to vote, but their incredibly high turnout in this fair, peaceful election means they might be the next kingmakers. Exit polls estimate that Arab MKs may constitute 14 percent of oppressive, apartheid Israel's next Knesset.Israel emerges stronger, more united despite Oct. 7Finally, one can only imagine what Iran's Ayatollahs and Revolutionary Guards, what Palestinian terrorists from Gaza to Judea and Samaria, and what the dwindling ranks of Hezbollah are thinking. They, and their bots, will tweet all kinds of anti-Zionist trash talk, which their Western dupes, and too many Jews worldwide, will echo or at least buy into a bit. But our enemies know better. “Darn,” they must be thinking, “foiled again.”Three years after the worst day in Israeli history, Israel has emerged stronger, more united despite all the noise, and even happier despite the trauma, still scoring high in all happiness indices. I kind of understand their blind hatred of us; nothing's more annoying than watching people you despise, and keep trying to destroy, bounce back from tragedy, live life to the fullest, and show the world what a successful society looks like, even with all its challenges.Now that the votes have been cast, we Israelis need a quality that's often in short supply these days: patience. The votes must be counted, and the counting should be finished by Friday. The inevitably excruciating negotiations have to begin. Then, if and when a new government emerges, and we escape electoral deadlock, every citizen should remember to be patriotic. Give the new government a chance to succeed, or fail, while respecting the democratic process on display so impressively this Tuesday, once again.The writer is a scholar of North American history at McGill University and a senior research fellow at the Jewish People Policy Institute.

title: “To serve and to protect beyond borders”: 22 NYPD Officers to embark on landmark humanitarian mission to Ghana
body: Twenty-two members of the New York City Police Department are set to trade their precincts for purpose this November, embarking on an eight-day humanitarian journey to Ghana under the banner of the African Law Enforcement Organization (ALEO), a mission that embodies compassion, service, and a steadfast commitment to humanity. The themed initiative, “To Serve and to Protect Beyond Borders,” aims to bring hope, smiles, and meaningful support to underprivileged children and vulnerable communities in selected parts of Ghana from November 10 to 18, 2026. A Mission Rooted in Service ALEO is a 501(c)(3) non-profit fraternal organization of active and retired law enforcement and security professionals, based in Jamaica, New York. Under the leadership of its President, Detective Chibuzo C. Amadi, the organization brings together members who share a common heritage and a dedication to public service — both in uniform and in the communities they come from. The Ghana mission marks a significant step in ALEO’s work, extending the organization’s commitment to service beyond policing and beyond the borders of New York City. It reflects the belief that the values at the core of law enforcement — protection, unity, and community responsibility — carry meaning wherever there are people in need. Strengthening International Ties In addition to its humanitarian activities, the delegation will engage with Ghanaian officials. The officers are scheduled to visit the Ghana Police Service Headquarters on November 10, the day of their arrival, fostering professional exchange and goodwill between law enforcement in the United States and Ghana. The delegation will also pay a courtesy call at Jubilee House, the seat of the Presidency. A Community-Driven Effort The mission was made possible in part through ALEO member and NYPD officer Mr. William Apau, popularly known as Ministerapau, founder of the Magho Foundation, who connected the organization with schools and an orphanage in Ghana that his foundation has previously supported. The humanitarian mission is organized by ALEO, with the Magho Foundation, Afro Pop, and Exotical Sponges supporting the initiative as sponsors. Kindness That Restores Dignity For many children facing difficult circumstances, such acts of kindness represent more than material assistance. They offer encouragement, restore dignity, and serve as reminders that they have not been forgotten. As preparations continue for the November visit, the mission carries a powerful message: true service knows no borders, and even the smallest act of kindness can make a lasting difference in someone’s life. About ALEO The African Law Enforcement Organization (ALEO) is a 501(c)(3) non-profit fraternal organization of active and retired law enforcement and security professionals based in Jamaica, New York, dedicated to public service, community engagement, and strengthening ties between law enforcement and the communities they serve.

title: China’s New Trimaran Submarine: 16 Missiles And An Unconventional Design
body: China is building more submarines, of more classes, than any other country. It has several brand-new ambitious design readying for series production and is forging ahead in the uncrewed space. But this unique trimaran design appears the strangest of them all. Somewhere in the Eastern Pacific, a snorkel mast skims the ocean’s surface, the only visible sign of a vessel lurking below. An encrypted signal arrives, carrying target data. The vessel rises, revealing a distinctive trimaran hull unlike that of any other navy’s submarine. This unique configuration provides greater stability on the surface. Moments later, two large hangars built into the central hull slide open, and 16 missile tubes rise into firing position. Nearly 1,500 km (930 miles) away, an enemy carrier battle group lies within range. This is no ordinary submarine; it is a vessel unlike any other in the world. The above scene illustrates how new submersible warship is expected to operate. Previously described as a Semi-Submersible Arsenal Ship, it has yet to receive an official designation or Western reporting name. The vessel is currently being tested in Huludao on the Bohai Sea. Originally built in the southern city of Guangzhou , it was ferried to the north of China via the port of Dalian earlier this year. Satellite image of the submersible trimaran at Dalian in Northern China, 12th May 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor. It is, for sure, a completely new category of warship. Fresh analysis suggests that it is best thought of as a submersible warship, which is uncrewed, and yet needs to come to the surface to launch its weapons. 16+ Missile Tubes The new submersible warship built by China likely has 16 strike-length missile tubes occupying much of its central hull. Currently we can be confident that there are at least 8 tubes, but more probably 16-18 in total assuming both hangars are identical. The tubes are arranged in two circular clusters which are stored horizontally in hangars. To launch the missiles the vessel will logically have to surface, the hangar doors opened and the missile tubes elevated into a vertical position. As is the case with secretive naval projects, vessel has not been reported or named in Chinese media. We do not have a clear official narrative on its role or status. The following observations come from what can be gleaned by open-source intelligence (OSINT), principally commercial satellite imagery. It is likely that the missile tubes carry anti-ship or land-attack missiles. We can infer that the exact type of missile chosen, and China has many suitable types, is one which is intended for surface rather than submerged launch. This leads to the hypersonic YJ-20 missiles normally associated with the Type-055 cruiser, being a contender. Unique Hull Form, and likely Uncrewed The vessel is clearly submersible but, as indicated by its prominent snorkel, is intended to run on diesels even when submerged. Its trimaran hull form, with outrigger hulls towards the stern, appears optimised for surface transit and stability on the surface. This latter factor may be a driver since the missile tubes, when erected, must make the vessel somewhat top heavy. The outriggers also sport ducted propellers (‘screws’), possibly of a pumpjet type. Logically the vessel will have a set of screws or water jets on the main body for the diesels, and electric screws on the outriggers. Dr. Rachel Pawling, Principal Consultant and K39 Consulting and lecturer in ship design, has calculated the vessel’s likely internal make-up. She estimates that the ship displaces around 900 tonnes fully submerged. Dr. Pawling notes that the weapons hangars take up so much volume, that the rest of the internal space must be extremely cramped. So much so, that it appears unlikely that there is space for a crew. Yet the vessel has an open navigation bridge on top of its fin (sail). The obvious explanation is that this is only for a human pilot during entering and exiting ports. Most large uncrewed vessels have some form of bridge like this to simplify port operations. Concept of Operations There has always been a blurred line between submersible warships and true submarines. There have been numerous designs designed to fight on the surface which can partly or fully submerge. Indeed until World War Two submarines were mostly surface vessels which could submerge. Dr. Pawling suggests that the new type is similar to Cold War Soviet cruise missile submarines like the Juliett Class . That was a diesel submarine which had to surface to launch its powerful anti-ship missiles. It could pop-up to attack high-value warships from unexpected directions. The main differences will be that modern missiles, such as the YJ-20 hypersonic missile, will have much longer ranges and be able to target both land and sea targets. This means that they will be dependent on external targeting. This makes this vessel a transporter and launcher, a small part in a larger distributed network. What is more, the Chinese vessel will carry far more weapons than the 4 SS-N-3 Shaddock carried by the Juliett Class. This vessel will remain subject to analysis and speculation. China appears in no hurry to explain it to the outside world, and there is much which remains unclear. The ports it has been observed in do not match those associated with either China’s large uncrewed surface vessel (USV) or uncrewed submarine (XLUUV) programs, suggesting that it is distinct from either program. The post China’s New Trimaran Submarine: 16 Missiles And An Unconventional Design appeared first on Naval News .

title: ADC to Tinubu: ‘Explain your campaign spokesperson’s claim that ministers paid for appointments’
body:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council has challenged President Bola Tinubu to respond to allegations attributed to a spokesperson associated with his campaign that some ministers paid to secure their appointments.
The council, in a statement signed by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, also called for an investigation by anti-corruption agencies into the allegations reportedly made by Alwan Hassan during a television appearance.
According to the ADC-PCC, Mr Hassan alleged that some ministers paid to obtain their positions and were now seeking to recover the money before concentrating on government business.
The council asked Mr Tinubu to clarify whether he was aware of the allegations, whether any investigation had been initiated and what action his administration intended to take.
It also challenged Mr Hassan to identify the ministers allegedly involved, disclose the amounts purportedly paid and name those who received the money.
“Public office is a responsibility, not a commercial transaction. Ministerial appointments must be guided by competence, integrity and a commitment to national service—not by financial inducements or expectations of private returns,” the statement said.
The council urged the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) and the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) to examine any evidence of payments connected to ministerial appointments.
It also asked the National Assembly to consider a public inquiry, including inviting Mr Hassan to explain his remarks and provide supporting evidence.
“The allegation, if established, would suggest that ministerial appointments were treated as private investments rather than positions of public trust,” the council said.
It argued that such payments, if proven, would raise concerns about whether ministers were serving the public interest or pursuing personal financial returns.
The ADC-PCC said the allegations warranted an explanation from the Presidency, particularly at a time when Nigerians were facing qeconomic hardship and insecurity.
It maintained that the demands for an investigation did not amount to a presumption of guilt.
Mr Hassan made the remarks on Thursday, 22 October, on ARISE Television’s Prime Time programme while defending President Tinubu’s direct control over government expenditure.
He alleged that some ministers paid billions of naira to secure appointments but subsequently maintained that the practice was not peculiar to the APC administration and had existed under previous governments. He did not identify any ministers or provide evidence of the alleged payments.
On 23 October, Atiku Abubakar challenged Mr Tinubu to identify those allegedly involved and explain who received the money. The ADC-PCC’s latest statement extends that demand to investigations by anti-corruption agencies and a possible National Assembly inquiry.

title: Zelensky: All forms of diplomacy must be used to defend Ukraine
body:
According to Ukrinform, citing the head of state’s Telegram channel, he made this statement in an interview with The Sun.
According to the President, “Telling the truth is one of our weapons. We must be open and clear. Not to play games with our partners. That’s my rule.”
“There is a lot of pressure on Ukraine right now, and, of course, I have to speak up. And I will do so, because it’s part of our defense strategy,” Zelensky noted.
He emphasized: “We’re not trying to be someone else. If I feel that there are dangerous threats to Ukraine, I must defend my country. And I’m doing everything I can, just like our soldiers on the battlefield and the people working for Ukraine. And as President, I must use all forms of diplomacy.”
As reported by Ukrinform, Zelensky stated that Europe must be involved in discussions on security guarantees for Ukraine and its post-war recovery, particularly given that European partners are financing arms deliveries to Ukraine and supporting its budget.

title: Nigerian govt begins $100m South-east gas pipeline project
body:
The Nigerian government has kicked off a $100 million gas distribution pipeline project to boost industrialisation, attract investment, and create jobs in the South-east.
The 400-kilometre pipeline was designed to connect gas resources to industrial and commercial centres across Enugu, Anambra, Imo, Abia and Ebonyi states.
The pipeline has about 150 potential customers identified, with projected demand of 254 million standard cubic feet of gas per day.
President Bola Tinubu announced this on Tuesday shortly after the investment agreement for the project was signed at the South-East Gas Infrastructure Investment and Project Development Ceremony held at Hotel Presidential, Enugu.
Mr Tinubu, represented by the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, said the project was being implemented through the South-east Development Commission ( SEDC ).
He described the project as a “strategic investment” that would connect the South-east’s natural gas resources to industries, strengthen manufacturing and unlock economic opportunities across the five states in the region.
“The South-east’s entrepreneurial spirit is one of Nigeria’s greatest economic assets. I have always believed that the prosperity of the South-east is inseparable from the prosperity of Nigeria,” Mr Tinubu said.
The president added that the project aligned with his administration’s commitment to building an integrated regional economy, stressing that gas infrastructure should support industrial development across state boundaries rather than serve isolated markets.
“That is the economic logic of regional integration,” he said.
He said the pipeline would benefit manufacturers in Aba, strengthen industrial clusters in Nnewi and Onitsha, attract productive enterprises to Enugu, expand agro-processing and manufacturing in Ebonyi and connect Imo’s gas resources to the wider regional economy.
Mr Tinubu, however, said the ambition extended beyond supplying existing factories to creating the conditions for new industries.
“It was issued to make possible factories that do not yet exist, industrial parks yet to be developed, and investments that have remained on the drawing board because reliable energy was unavailable,” he said.
He described the SEDC as an institution established to deliver measurable development outcomes, urging it to assess its performance by the investments it mobilised, infrastructure it enabled, opportunities it created and lives it improved.
“This is the model I expect from our development institutions: identify strategic economic opportunities, prepare credible projects, commit public resources responsibly and mobilise private capital at a scale government budgets alone cannot achieve,” he said.
The president praised the SEDC for committing $3 million to the gas project and establishing a framework to mobilise additional investments from state governments, institutions and private investors.
He said the project’s initial phase required approximately $100 million, describing the partnership between public institutions and private investors as essential to developing sustainable infrastructure.
“We are not investing in pipelines for their own sake. We are investing in the industries, businesses and jobs those pipelines will make possible,” the president said.
Mr Tinubu urged the commission and its partners to uphold commercial discipline, transparency, environmental responsibility, community engagement and the highest safety standards throughout the project’s implementation.
He said the ultimate objective was to translate the region’s natural resources into productive economic activity, employment and improved living standards.
“Let the gas beneath our soil power our industries. Let that energy become production. Let production become employment. Let employment become prosperity for our people,” he said.
The president urged the SEDC, state governments and project partners to establish clear implementation timelines, measurable milestones and regular progress reports, stressing that the project’s success would ultimately be measured by its ability to attract investments, revive industries, and create jobs.
Also speaking, Governor Peter Mbah of Enugu State commended Mr Tinubu for establishing the SEDC, describing the commission as the institutional vehicle needed to realise the South-east’s long-standing industrialisation aspirations.
“Tinubu loves the Igbo. The SEDC is a commission whose time has come.
“It was an idea conceived many decades ago, but it took President Tinubu to establish this long-awaited dream of industrialisation of the South-east,” Mr Mbah said.
He described the signing of the investment agreement as the commencement of the investment process, adding that the initiative would help realise the region’s aspiration for a common market and coordinated industrial development.
The governor said the project would create opportunities for young people to build their futures in the South-east rather than migrate to other parts of the country in search of jobs.
“We, the South-east governors, are committed to this. We will ensure that the right of way and EIA are given accelerated approval,” he said.
The SEDC Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Mark Okoye, said the commission had conducted technical, financial and legal due diligence before committing funds to the project, which received approval from its governing board.
Mr Okoye said the commission was targeting aggregate regional investment participation of up to $30 million, including its initial $3 million commitment, as part of efforts to mobilise the private capital required to advance the project.
He said the initiative aligned with the commission’s industrialisation programme and its commitment to developing infrastructure that would benefit the entire region.
A representative of GasSync, the project promoter, Callistus Mba, said the pipeline would connect gas resources close to the South-east to industrial users across the five states, reducing dependence on the expensive transportation of compressed natural gas and liquefied natural gas by road.
Mr Mba said the proposed network would originate from the Ohaji area of Imo State, run through Owerri and branch towards Aba in Abia State and Onitsha in Anambra State, with extensions to Enugu and Ebonyi.

title: GomSpace and HIMERA begin satellite tests for Ukraine’s independent communications network
body: The satellite launched on SpaceX’s Transporter-18 mission on 1 October 2026. The partners said testing was progressing according to plan and that the spacecraft would operate under Ukrainian control. “It is an opportunity to lay the foundation for an independent communications network for Ukraine,” said Misha Rudominski, HIMERA’s co-founder and chief executive officer. “We are starting by testing technologies in orbit, while our long-term goal is to develop capabilities that will strengthen the country’s strategic security and reduce dependence on external communications providers.” The project aims to give Ukraine more communications options and reduce its reliance on foreign technology. The partners said dependence on providers in other countries, including allies, creates strategic risks, particularly during wartime. “We are excited to work with HIMERA and accelerate this important initiative,” said Carsten Drachmann, GomSpace’s chief executive officer. “Our shared ambition is to strengthen Ukraine’s independent communications capabilities and support the country’s long-term security and economic development.” The longer-term plan is to deploy a satellite network providing coverage across Ukraine and complementing European networks. Localising production of satellites and ground communications terminals in Ukraine is a planned next step, intended to build domestic expertise and manufacturing capacity.

title: Thieves steal military drones, alter markings, sell them as new
body:
Law enforcement officers have exposed a criminal scheme organized by a former serviceman: the perpetrators stole drones from the military, altered the markings, and then resold the UAVs back to the army under the guise of new equipment, Acting Prosecutor General Anton Kovalsky reported.
"We have a large-scale result of joint work: 16 suspects, 25 established episodes, and over 600 seized unmanned aerial vehicles," Kovalsky posted on his Facebook page.
According to him, the scheme was organized by a former serviceman who enlisted military personnel, civilian intermediaries, and commercial enterprises into the illegal activity.
"They operated quite systematically. They looked for military personnel willing to hand over drones from military units for money. For this, they even created a separate Telegram channel. The acquired equipment was brought to a workshop in Dnipropetrovsk region. There, factory serial numbers were removed, markings and QR codes were changed. Afterward, through controlled enterprises, these same UAVs were resold to the military, but as new ones," the Acting Prosecutor General explained.
According to the report, to establish the scale of this scheme, law enforcement officers conducted over 100 searches across nine regions and Kyiv.
Of the more than 600 seized UAVs, over 200 have already been identified as property of military units, while the origin of the rest is being verified.
"The value of the stolen military property amounts to about UAH 16 million," Kovalsky emphasized.
As reported by the press service of the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine, following investigative actions, law enforcement officers seized over UAH 13 million, about $400,000, 700 g of gold and 9 kg of silver, jewelry, 15 vehicles, weapons and ammunition, as well as documentation and electronic media—18 mobile phones, 10 personal computers, and other computer equipment (including 3D printers).
According to the data, the group had likely been operating since at least December 2025. Its members set up a multi-level system for obtaining, disguising origin, and reselling military drones.
"Initially, through personal contacts, online announcements, and a specially created Telegram channel, they sought military personnel willing to illegally sell drones on the inventory of military units. Unmanned aerial vehicles of various types were illegally bought up at prices significantly lower than market rates. To conceal shortages, equipment could be written off in documents as lost during combat actions," the statement reads.
Next, the drones were delivered to specially equipped workshops where they were repaired, cleaned, repackaged, and had their identification marks altered.
Original serial numbers were removed from the frames, while QR codes and stickers were replaced. Afterward, previously used or misappropriated drones took on the appearance of new items. Contracts were executed through controlled enterprises for the delivery of such equipment to military units of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.
"Thus, drones that had already been purchased for defense needs and were in military units could be resold to the state using budget funds. The main base of the group, according to investigation materials, operated in Dnipropetrovsk region. Individual participants secured drone purchases in various regions, while others were responsible for repairs, changing identification marks, executing contracts, and distributing proceeds," the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine stated.
Six military units have already been identified to which drones with altered identification data could have been supplied.
The court chose detention with an alternative of bail as a measure of restraint for all 16 suspects.
The participants in the scheme are charged, depending on their roles, with misappropriation of military property under martial law and laundering of property obtained by crime (Part 4 of Article 410, Part 2 of Article 209 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine).
The pre-trial investigation is ongoing. Employees of the State Bureau of Investigation are verifying the full volume of illegally alienated military property, other possible distribution channels, and the involvement of military officials in the scheme. Particular attention is paid to establishing all military units to which previously misappropriated drones could have been re-supplied, and documenting the movement of budget funds.
The Acting Prosecutor General noted that these results are the outcome of extensive joint work by prosecutors, investigators of the State Bureau of Investigation, internal security units of the State Border Guard Service and the National Police of Ukraine, and military counterintelligence of the Security Service of Ukraine.
"Our task now is to establish the origin of all seized equipment and the full circle of participants in the scheme—from those who facilitated the theft of drones to those who organized their resale to the army," Kovalsky summarized.

title: Bayelsa: Cleric arrested over alleged defilement of two minors
body: Operatives of the Bayelsa State Police Command have arrested a 50-year-old pastor identified as Ambros Mark, for allegedly sexually abusing two underage girls aged 13 and 14 in Yenagoa, the state capital. The cleric was arrested on Saturday after an alarm was raised that he defiled the two victims who are members of his Church. Police Spokesman in Bayelsa State, DSP Musa Mohammed, who confirmed the arrest to Daily Trust on Wednesday, said investigation is ongoing on the matter, while the accused is in custody. The suspect is said to be the pastor of New Generation Pentecostal Church, located behind the Amarata area of Yenagoa. Oil revenue: PANDEF seeks 50% derivation for oil-producing states Dataphyte, BudgIT, CJID, others launch platform to monitor election results The 13-year-old girl, who is one of the victims, hails from Abia State, while the 14-year-old is from Ogbia Local Government Area of Bayelsa State. Daily Trust gathered that the case came to light after the 14-year-old girl reportedly objected to the alleged sexual advances and informed her father, a police officer attached to the Bayelsa State Police Command. The father subsequently reported the matter to the police division, leading to the pastor’s arrest. It was also alleged that attempts to resolve the matter through financial settlement failed after the parents of the 13-year-old girl reportedly declined to accept the arrangement. The incident has attracted condemnation from women’s rights advocates, who have called for a thorough investigation and the protection of the alleged victims. The Chairperson of the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA), Bayelsa State chapter, Dr. Boma Tonye Miebai, and the founder of the Do Foundation, Dr. Dise Ogbise Goddy Harry, confirmed the incident and condemned the alleged sexual abuse of the minors. The Do Foundation expressed shock over the allegations, describing the reported incident as disturbing and emphasising the need to protect children from sexual exploitation and abuse. Miebai said FIDA Bayelsa was actively following the case within its mandate to protect the rights and interests of the affected children. She called on the relevant authorities to conduct a comprehensive investigation and ensure that the matter was prosecuted in accordance with the law. She said, “We acknowledge the arrest of the alleged perpetrator and urge the relevant authorities to conduct a thorough investigation and ensure that the matter is diligently prosecuted in accordance with the law.” According to her, FIDA Bayelsa would continue to advocate for the safety, dignity and confidentiality of the children while ensuring that they have access to appropriate legal and psychosocial support. She stressed that the rights and best interests of the alleged victims must remain a priority throughout the legal process. Miebai stated, “We reiterate that no religious title or position places anyone above the law. Our children deserve protection, and alleged sexual offences against them must never be concealed or trivialised.” She reaffirmed the organisation’s commitment to ensuring that the children’s rights are upheld and that the appropriate legal process is followed. The police are expected to investigate the allegations and establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

title: Nuclear ambitions threaten Japan’s future, Chinese expert warns
body:
BEIJING, October 28. /TASS/. The nuclear ambitions of Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s current cabinet could put the future of more than 100 million Japanese citizens at risk, despite widespread public opposition to nuclear weapons, Secretary General of the China Arms Control and Disarmament Association (CACDA) Dai Huaicheng told TASS.
He noted that statements by some Japanese politicians calling for the country to acquire nuclear weapons ran counter to Tokyo’s commitments to peace, as well as the views of the Japanese public.
"Opinion polls conducted by Japanese media show that 60% of the population opposes the development of nuclear weapons, while 80% demand respect for the three non-nuclear principles. This clearly demonstrates the anti-nuclear stance of the majority of Japanese society. Open attempts by Japanese ruling circles to promote the ‘nuclear option’ are putting the future of more than 100 million Japanese people at risk," Dai stressed.
"No one should forget history or go against the will of the people. If Japan’s ruling circles persist in their nuclear delusions and continue to compound their mistakes, this will not only pose a major challenge to the post-war world order and the international system of nuclear non-proliferation, but also run counter to Japan’s peace commitments and the general opinion of the Japanese people, ultimately exacting an extremely high price," he added.
"The international community must call on Japan to deeply reflect on the history of [its] aggression [during World War II], completely break with militarism, finally abandon ambitions to acquire nuclear weapons, and faithfully fulfill its international non-proliferation commitments," the expert concluded.
Japan maintains three non-nuclear principles: not possessing, not producing and not permitting the introduction of nuclear weapons into its territory. Although the principles aren’t enshrined in laws, all Japanese prime ministers have so far reaffirmed commitment to them. Discussions of the issue have long been considered taboo, prompting some politicians to refer to the "fourth principle" of not discussing nuclear weapons and call for abandoning at least this unwritten rule.
After Sanae Takaichi took office as prime minister, the Japanese media reported that the approach to the three non-nuclear principles would be discussed as part of a planned review of the country’s national security strategy. Media outlets claimed that Takaichi was prepared to call for lifting at least the ban on bringing US nuclear weapons to Japan. However, the prime minister said she had not instructed officials to review the non-nuclear principles as part of discussions of a new version of the national security strategy.

title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Preparing for 2027 Board and Executive Conversations
body: Insight. Effective board and executive discussions begin with clear evidence, honest assessment, and well-defined strategic choices. As CEOs prepare for 2027, they must ensure that discussions about organizational performance and future direction are supported by credible information and a realistic understanding of risks and opportunities. The objective is not merely to present results. It is to create a shared understanding of the decisions, investments, and governance priorities required to move the organization forward. Key Strategies: Prepare a clear assessment of year-to-date performance against strategic objectives. Identify material risks, emerging opportunities, and unresolved challenges. Develop realistic strategic options for the year ahead. Clarify the decisions and guidance required from the board. Ensure that proposed priorities are supported by credible analysis and resource plans. CEO Leadership Actions. Prepare a concise and evidence-based assessment of the organization’s current position. Identify the most important strategic questions requiring board and executive attention. Ensure that proposed 2027 priorities are consistent with the organization’s risk appetite, capabilities, and financial position. Actionable Tip. Before your next board or executive strategy discussion, prepare a one-page brief covering performance, key risks, growth opportunities, proposed priorities, and decisions required. Why This Matters? Strong board and executive conversations improve strategic alignment and decision quality. When CEOs present a clear view of performance and future choices, they enable more productive oversight, better resource allocation, and stronger organizational readiness for 2027. About the Author. Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee.

title: NATO spots Russian submarine in the High North
body: A Russian Kilo class submarine has been observed in the High North by Standing NATO Maritime Group 1, according to NATO Maritime Command. The command said: “SPOTTED: A Russian Kilo-class submarine in the High North, observed by Standing NATO Maritime Group 1 (SNMG1). “Anti-submarine warfare is a team effort. Ships, submarines, aircraft and helicopters from across the Alliance work together every day to detect, track and, if necessary, counter any threat beneath the surface. Our posture is defensive, our readiness is credible, and our resolve is clear: to deter aggression and keep our one billion people across Europe and North America safe.” Standing NATO Maritime Group 1 is one of the alliance’s permanently available naval forces, drawing warships from member navies on rotation and operating principally in the North Atlantic and northern European waters. The Royal Navy contributes to it regularly and has commanded it in the past. The Kilo class is a diesel-electric attack submarine built in large numbers from the 1980s, and the improved Project 636.3 boats are quiet enough on batteries to have earned the nickname Black Hole from American analysts. Russia operates them in the Northern Fleet, the Baltic, the Black Sea and the Pacific, and the type carries torpedoes, mines and the Kalibr land attack cruise missile. The Defence Committee reported this month that Britain does not have what it needs in the High North, urging ministers to retain Type 23 frigates until the Type 26 arrives and questioning whether the Royal Navy’s attack submarines are putting to sea as often as they should. The committee also called for the return of under-ice submarine skills and warned that Britain sells its nuclear contribution to NATO short. HMS Prince of Wales is currently in the Arctic and North Atlantic on the second phase of Operation Firecrest with the Type 45 destroyer HMS Dauntless, carrying Merlin Mk2 anti-submarine helicopters among her air group, and RAF Poseidon maritime patrol aircraft operate over the northern approaches from Lossiemouth. NATO warships began the current High North deployment earlier in the year. The post NATO spots Russian submarine in the High North first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Why California's election results take longer than other states
body:
Alaska and Pennsylvania could also see election results later than other states.
While Election Day is on Nov. 3, at least some of California's midterm election results may not be projected until days or even weeks later.
Not only is there a plethora of ballots to count because California is the most populous state, with 23 million registered voters, but it also relies on a large number of mail-in ballots, with some not arriving until a week after voting ends.
According to the California secretary of state , "vote-by-mail ballots postmarked on or before Election Day and received within seven days after the election, as well as any provisional ballots cast, must still be counted."
Earlier this year, the Supreme Court upheld a Mississippi law allowing tabulation of late-arriving mail-in ballots so long as they were postmarked by Election Day. The decision was a loss for the Republican Party, which brought the case, and the Trump administration, which has pushed to override state election rules nationwide by imposing strict federal limits on voting by mail.
The Supreme Court last month also rejected the Trump administration's attempt to limit mail-in voting for now, keeping in place a lower court decision blocking the U.S. Postal Service from implementing new restrictions.
In addition to late-arriving mail ballots, the California secretary of state told ABC News that there is an arduous process of counting mail ballots and validating voters' signatures, as each envelope signature must match the signatures on file. County election officials have up to 30 days after the election to count ballots.
More than 89% of Californians that voted in the June 2 primary election did so by mail, according to California Secretary of State Shirley Weber. On July 10, Weber announced that the primary results were certified.
ABC News projected the two candidates advancing to the state's gubernatorial general election about one week after the primary election: Democrat Xavier Becerra was projected to advance on June 5, and Republican Steve Hilton was projected to advance on June 9.
California's long ballot-counting process often opens floodgates for criticism, with President Donald Trump frequently claiming without evidence that elections in the state are "rigged."
"In the end, they're not going to let you win it. They just won't let you win it because it's a rigged state," Trump said during a Newsmax interview earlier in October.
In his claims of election fraud, Trump has repeatedly referenced Republican Spencer Pratt's loss in the Los Angeles mayoral primary. While Pratt was initially in second place on primary night, he was eventually edged out by Democrat Nithya Raman once ballots were fully counted -- which can happen given the state's vote-counting process.
"Spencer Pratt was doing great. And at the end of the election, Election Day, his opponent was crying. Oh, she's lost so badly. She was crying. Then all of a sudden, like a week and a half later, you hear that she's surging. Nobody ever heard of her. You know, people that nobody ever heard of don't surge. The only time they surge is when they cheat," Trump claimed in early October.
The University of Florida's Election Lab has found that so far, 50% of mail ballots that have been accepted by the state of California are from registered Democrats and 29% are from registered Republicans, as of Oct. 25. The remaining 21% of ballots are from those with no party affiliation or registered with a minor party.
An October ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos poll found that among likely California voters who said they would probably or certainly vote -- or who already had -- 65% said they would vote by mail. Just 11% of California voters said they would vote in person at a polling place on Election Day.
The president has also railed against mail-in ballots for years, despite himself voting by mail twice during Florida elections this year. A White House spokesperson said that Trump has supported "commonsense exceptions" to allow Americans to use mail-in ballots, including for "illness, disability, military, or travel," but that he opposes universal voting by mail due to it being "highly susceptible to fraud."
An analysis from the Brookings Institution from November 2025 found that voter fraud is rare in voting by mail.
As the president blitzes the country ahead of the midterms, he has continued to sow doubt in mail-in voting while simultaneously encouraging Republicans to vote any way they can . Speaking to Newsmax earlier this month, Trump claimed without evidence that Democrats are sent multiple ballots and that Republicans sometimes do not receive a ballot at all.
"They send out millions and millions of ballots. Democrats get, in some cases seven, in some cases one, but in some cases they get much more than one. Republicans oftentimes don't get any, they have to call in for their ballot," Trump claimed.
Ahead of the general election, officials and state leaders have emphasized the security of California elections and mail ballots.
"Voting in California is secure, reliable, and part of California's tradition of encouraging participation in our democracy," Weber, the secretary of state, said earlier this month.
"Voting is safe, vote-by-mail is accessible to any and all who need it. And I encourage every Californian to make their voice heard this November," California Gov. Gavin Newsom also said in October.
California is not the only state where election results take an extended amount of time. Alaska, for instance, accepts some ballots up to 15 days after the election and certification cannot be done before then.
The Alaska Division of Elections says that the "process is intentionally slow and methodical so that accuracy is obtained."
Pennsylvania also prevents counties from opening ballots until 7 a.m. on Election Day, meaning early votes cannot be counted upon receipt.

title: Nine killed in renewed communal fighting in Bor County
body: At least nine people have been killed in renewed fighting between the Abang and Malual communities in Bor County, Jonglei State, on Monday, the caretaker county commissioner said. Bor County Commissioner Daniel Deng Panchol said seven of the dead were from the two communities, while the other two were from neighbouring communities. “Five were from Malual and two from Abang. The report indicated two other casualties from different communities: one lady from Gwala and a gentleman from Deer. The total number of deaths rose to nine,” Deng said. State and county authorities held a security meeting and imposed a curfew from 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. to contain the violence, he said. Deng added that anyone found carrying a gun in the affected area would be arrested. Joint security forces, including personnel from the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) and National Security Service, had been deployed to ease tensions, protect civilians and prevent further violence, he said. The government would also engage young people and elders from both communities to encourage restraint and promote peaceful coexistence, Deng added. The latest clashes stem from a longstanding territorial dispute between the Abang and Malual communities over the Malual-Chaat area. Tensions have remained high since late April, when fighting first broke out following the creation of a new administrative boma, deepening disagreements over local boundaries and administrative control. title: NLnet Publishes More Stringent Generative AI Policy
body:
NLnet has published a new version of its generative AI policy (version 2.0). The revised policy is more restrictive than prior versions, stemming from the foundation's practical experience with thousands of applications processed since the previous policy was published. Generative AI can no longer be used for writing proposals - with the noted exception of supporting accessibility needs. For project development the use of LLMs and diffusion models is confined to read-only usage. These limitations will drastically simplify and speed up evaluation of proposals and work delivered, and allow the foundation to spend more time on actual grantees.
Our new policy is first and foremost a pragmatic measure towards self-protection. Last year we left our processes open to moderate use of LLMs and similar deep-learning systems in case their use was clearly documented, but the result of this experiment has been underwhelming and overwhelming at the same time , says Michiel Leenaars, director of Strategy at NLnet foundation. We found ourselves having to process an avalanche of additional proposals lacking maturity and relevance. Upon closer inspection, proposals involving AI were on the whole of much lower quality than we are used to at NLnet - and at the same time very taxing and demotivating for our experts to wade through , says Leenaars.
We recognise there is plenty of potential for generative AI for a variety of use cases , Leenaars comments. We are not trying to make a more general point about quality, ethical consideration, or security, nor are we making decisions or recommendations for others on whether the use of agents will work for their use cases. It is just that for our particular domain of digital infrastructure and at this point in time, the actual yield turns out to not be worth the additional effort.

title: PDP Chairmen Allege Escalating Political Violence, Opposition Intimidation In Ebonyi
body: The Forum of Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) State Chairmen has raised an urgent alarm over an alleged wave of political violence, threats, abductions, targeted killings, and systematic attacks on opposition members across Ebonyi State. In a press statement issued by the forum Chairman and Imo State PDP Chairman, Austin Nwachukwu, called for immediate investigations by federal security authorities and heightened monitoring by international election observers ahead of the 2027 general elections. The group condemned what it described as a troubling and deliberate strategy to undermine democratic participation through unlawful detentions, property destruction, and severe restrictions on PDP leaders, candidates, and supporters. “Public authority must never be weaponized to intimidate one political party while facilitating another.” “A thriving democracy relies on equal protection under the law and open political participation,” the forum stated. Addressing the alleged escalating tension, the forum urged Ebonyi State Governor Francis Nwifuru, President Bola Tinubu, the Nigeria Police Force, the Department of State Services (DSS), and the Office of the National Security Adviser (NSA) to intervene swiftly to protect lives and restore public confidence. Specifically, the forum called on the Inspector-General of Police (IGP) to immediately set up an impartial investigative panel to probe reported attacks, threats, abductions, killings, armed robbery, and property destruction. It also called on the Department of State Services (DSS) to conduct an independent, comprehensive security assessment regarding political violence in the state, saying that President Tinubu should mandate impartial security interventions and guarantee equal protection for all citizens, regardless of political affiliation. Likewise, the group urged the international community to actively monitor the situation, calling on the United Nations (UN), African Union (AU), ECOWAS, diplomatic missions, and international human rights organisations to scrutinise human rights and democratic freedoms in Ebonyi. The forum documented a series of violent incidents and state-backed crackdowns which it said spanned mid-2026. It expressed concern over the police department’s response, labeling its handling of opposition complaints as “deeply unsatisfactory.” Furthermore, the group raised ethical questions regarding reported accommodation arrangements between the Ebonyi State Commissioner of Police and ReMeritona Hotel in Abakaliki, a facility allegedly owned by Governor Nwifuru. While acknowledging the arrangement does not automatically prove bias, the forum noted that “it raises severe ethical concerns and requires immediate clarification to preserve public confidence in police neutrality.” Additionally, the statement highlighted unequal access to public infrastructure, noting that while rival political factions are granted seamless access to public spaces, PDP gatherings face alleged systematic bans and state restrictions. Concluding its address, the forum urged Governor Nwifuru to publicly reject political violence, clarify his position on reported statements against the opposition, justify the legal grounds for sealing party assets, and cooperate with independent investigators. “All allegations must be thoroughly and impartially investigated. Anyone found culpable through credible evidence should face the full weight of the law, regardless of their political standing or official position,” the statement read. The forum praised the resilience of the PDP governorship candidate in Ebonyi State, Ifeanyi Chukwuma Odii, encouraging him and his supporters to maintain a peaceful, focused approach as they prepare for the 2027 general elections. In a swift response to the allegations, the Ebonyi State Police Command firmly dismissed claims of political bias or compromise. ​Speaking on behalf of the command, the Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), SP Joshua Ukandu, stated that under the leadership of Commissioner of Police Hope Okafor, the command maintains strict political neutrality and continues to respond promptly and professionally to all security threats across the state. The post PDP Chairmen Allege Escalating Political Violence, Opposition Intimidation In Ebonyi appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Tokayev Calls for AI-Driven Digital Economy, Technology Push Across Industry
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA — Kazakhstan must build a digital economy, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev said in his state-of-the-nation address on Oct. 28, calling for broader use of AI in industry and agriculture, modernized geological exploration and a shift from digital consumption to technology-driven production. Photo credit: Akorda. Tokayev said Kazakhstan had begun building infrastructure for its Digital Qazaqstan strategy, including launching two supercomputers, preparing to commission a third by the end of the year, and laying a fiber-optic trunk line across the Caspian Sea. Data centers are also under construction. However, he acknowledged that the country still had to demonstrate results in digitalization, with the process sometimes reduced to automating existing procedures or purchasing expensive software without a clear understanding of its practical benefits. “We must be realistic in assessing our capabilities and use the best that new technologies can offer for the well-being of our people,” Tokayev said. He said Kazakhstan had only begun commercializing AI, asset tokenization, blockchain technologies and digital platform ecosystems. The government must develop a program to apply digital technologies across the economy. “Our goal is to build a truly people-centered digital economy,” Tokayev said. From digital consumption to digital work Tokayev called for a shift in how people use digital technologies, noting that internet access should enable economic activity and employment rather than serve primarily as a space for consumption and entertainment. “In public consciousness, the internet should be perceived not only as a space for consumption and entertainment, but also as a virtual territory for creation and work,” he said. He said smartphones should become effective working tools rather than expensive distractions. The government is expected to establish a simplified legal regime for digital employment by the end of the year. Tokayev also stressed that access to digital opportunities should not depend on where people live. “Our citizens, whether living in rural areas or cities, must learn to use smartphones as tools for earning a legitimate income,” he said. To support this goal, the government should combine existing state business support measures with the capabilities of private marketplaces, banks, logistics companies and digital services. Beyond loans and subsidies, entrepreneurs need additional digital tools to produce and sell goods. Next year, the government and the business community should launch pilot digital development projects in several regions to help rural producers market their products, with successful practices subsequently expanded nationwide. Tokayev also called for fully realizing the potential of asset tokenization, or transferring assets into the digital environment. AI and the next phase of industrial development Tokayev linked digital transformation to a broader push for industrial and technological development, including the modernization of geological exploration and the management of critical minerals. He said Kazakhstan needed to fundamentally change its approach to geological exploration, saying that outdated methods would not deliver the desired results. “Today, we must recognize geology as a high-tech industry. It is extremely important for us to comprehensively study the country’s subsoil using advanced technologies and ensure transparency and accessibility of data. We should actively attract private investment in the search for and exploration of new deposits,” Tokayev said. He called for a national system to manage critical metal reserves, supported by mechanisms for long-term financing of mining projects. The government should also consider off-take contracts to guarantee demand for products made by domestic enterprises in the sector. Tokayev said Kazakhstan should consider establishing a national stockpile of nonferrous and rare earth metals and integrate the country into global production chains. He called on the government to build strategic partnerships with developed countries in this field. At the same time, he warned against uncoordinated industrial investment that could create unnecessary competition for existing domestic producers. Tokayev cited Qarmet, an operating metallurgical enterprise, and plans to establish similar facilities in three other regions as an example, questioning whether the market would be able to absorb their output. He said each region needed to identify its own priorities, while the government should strengthen coordination to prevent fragmented decisions and excessive dependence on a single industry or enterprise. Regional development should extend beyond core industries to encompass education, applied science, logistics, services, related manufacturing and technological entrepreneurship. “There is confidence that the People’s Construction initiative will help create such a system in every region or, in modern terms, an ecosystem,” Tokayev said. AI in agriculture Tokayev also called for accelerating agriculture’s technological modernization, including increasing domestic production of advanced tractors and combine harvesters. He cited a recent visit to Astana by NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang , who, according to Tokayev, said it was time to introduce AI technologies into Kazakhstan’s agriculture. “In my view, this is a very timely proposal. We must begin implementing it as soon as possible,” Tokayev said. According to him, adopting these technologies could strengthen Kazakhstan’s role in global food security. “If our country overcomes this threshold, then, undoubtedly, in the event of a global food shortage, or the threat of world hunger, Eurasia could become one of the key centers for supplying food to the world,” he said. Kazakhstan had extensive agricultural land near major water sources, and using these areas for irrigated farming could increase yields of traditional crops by 2 to 2.5 times. President Tokayev called for applying advanced water-saving and agrochemical technologies when developing new agricultural land, noting that the country’s performance in this area remained low. Digital tools should also be used to improve the accounting and management of water resources, enabling better-informed decisions when planning new industrial facilities. Tokayev called on the government to complete the National Water Resources Information System as soon as possible. 2027 as the year of nationwide construction drive Tokayev said Kazakhstan’s next stage of development should combine an AI-based digital economy with investment in physical infrastructure. He proposed declaring the coming year the Year of Nationwide Large-Scale Construction, building on the current Year of Digitalization and Artificial Intelligence. The initiative should include building and renovating civilian infrastructure in regional centers, districts and smaller settlements, including roads, airports, railway stations, health care facilities and rehabilitation centers for children with special needs. Tokayev also called for new creative centers, sports complexes, libraries and scientific centers across the regions, while maintaining housing construction as a priority. “Thus, our common, nationwide response to the approaching era of artificial intelligence is to build, and build again!” he said. Tokayev said the initiative was intended to improve living standards and create opportunities for future generations. “The Constitution defines improving the well-being of the people as a strategic priority of the state. I want to emphasize that all these initiatives are aimed at the benefit of the country and, above all, at securing the future of the younger generation,” he said. The post Tokayev Calls for AI-Driven Digital Economy, Technology Push Across Industry appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: Russian men of draft age could be denied passports for foreign travel if they lack military IDs
body: The absence of a military ID for a man of draft age could become grounds for refusing to accept documents for a foreign passport application, according to materials from Russia’s Interior Ministry reviewed by the Russian state news agency TASS. The materials list several grounds for refusing to accept foreign passport applications, including the absence of a military ID for an applicant of draft age. The TASS report, widely cited by other media outlets, gives no further details, and it remains unclear whether it describes a change to the current procedure for issuing foreign passports. The report also cites provisions governing domestic Russian passports that are already in effect. Human rights activists have repeatedly said that applicants, including those of draft age, need to present a military ID when applying for a foreign passport only if they already have one. The same applies to a certificate from the local draft office, they said. At Meduza, we are committed to transparency about our use of artificial intelligence in the newsroom. The story you’re reading was written by one of our living, breathing journalists and translated from Russian using an AI model configured to follow our strict editorial standards. This translation process is the result of extensive testing and refinements to ensure our English-language coverage is timely and accurate. A Meduza editor reviews every draft before publication. title: What Is Wrong With Us: A continent cannot be built forever in the future tense
body: Africa has never been short of promises, plans or podiums. What its 1.5 billion people need now is proof: lights that stay on, classrooms that teach, and commitments that outlive the ceremonies at which they were announced. By Ing. Prof. Douglas Boateng, Chartered Director UK | Chartered Engineer UK | Fellow, Institute of Directors UK | Fellow, Ghana Institution of Engineering | Governance, Industrialisation and Supply Chain Strategist | Founder, Boardroom Governance Summit | Founder and Scriber, NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) A Continent Fluent In The Language Of Tomorrow Africa’s more than 1.5 billion people have heard every promise a podium can produce. They have been promised industrialisation, jobs, affordable housing, reliable electricity, good schools and modern hospitals at election rallies, inaugurations, investment forums and continental summits. Some of those promises were kept, and others produced real if incomplete progress, but far too many remain suspended somewhere between an eloquent speech and a disappointing site visit. Meanwhile, the mother still walks for water, the graduate still searches for work, the entrepreneur still borrows at punishing rates, and the farmer still watches harvests rot for want of storage and roads. And then, another conference is announced, another declaration is drafted, another photograph is taken, and another round of applause fills the hall. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) offers a gentle rebuke: “A promise may inspire hope, but only action improves lives, for no hungry child has ever been fed by a beautifully written development agenda.” The problem is not that Africa plans too much, since planning is essential, but that announcing intentions has quietly become more rewarding, politically and commercially, than delivering outcomes. The Numbers That Should Keep Us Awake At Night The evidence is sobering. The United Nations’ 2024 Africa Sustainable Development Report found that fewer than 6 per cent of the 32 measurable Sustainable Development Goal targets on the continent were on track for 2030, and it warned that gaps in data meant even that verdict was incomplete. According to the most recent global energy tracking reports, roughly 565 million people in sub-Saharan Africa still lacked electricity in 2023, while UNESCO’s 2025 scorecard counted some 118 million African children, adolescents and young people out of school, each of them somebody’s child and somebody’s unrealised future. None of this erases the genuine gains Africa has made in telecommunications, financial inclusion, health and infrastructure, yet progress must never become a comfortable blanket under which complacency sleeps soundly. As NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) warns, “when promises multiply faster than opportunities, citizens stop counting speeches and start counting disappointments.” Ghana And The Tyranny Of The Four-Year Calendar Ghana offers a lesson familiar across the continent. Successive administrations have launched ambitious programmes in industry, infrastructure, education, agriculture and employment, and while some have delivered tangible results, others have stalled amid financing constraints, implementation difficulties or the simple misfortune of having been started by the wrong party. Why should every change of government plunge existing projects into uncertainty? Governments must of course retain the freedom to discard policies that do not work, but they should also possess the maturity to continue worthwhile initiatives regardless of whose name is on the original plaque. A nation’s institutional memory cannot be allowed to expire at every election, because the state belongs to generations rather than to political parties. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) puts it memorably: “a nation cannot build a fifty-year future if, every four years, it behaves as though history has just begun.” Ribbons Are Events, Electricity Is Development Nigeria, blessed with extraordinary human talent, entrepreneurial energy, natural resources and a vast domestic market, shows what Africans achieve when initiative meets opportunity, from its technology founders to its globally celebrated creative industries. Yet tens of millions of Nigerians still lack access to electricity, and many of those who are connected know the familiar roar of the private generator better than the hum of the national grid. Imagine the transformation if reliable power became routine rather than a competitive advantage. South Africa, an advanced industrial economy, learned through years of load shedding how neglected maintenance and weak institutional discipline can dim a nation, and it is now learning that sustained operational focus, new generating capacity and coordinated reform can gradually restore the lights. The lesson for both is identical: political announcements cannot replace engineering, public relations cannot repair a turbine, and no slogan has ever maintained a power station. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) observes that “cutting the ribbon on a power plant is an event; keeping the lights on is development,” and that “a government may announce transformation in an afternoon, but delivering it takes thousands of disciplined mornings.” Proof That Africa Can Deliver Fairness demands that we celebrate delivery where the evidence supports it. Rwanda’s 2023 to 2024 household survey recorded health insurance coverage of 85.3 per cent, Kenya’s mobile money revolution transformed how ordinary people save, send and borrow, Morocco has built substantial renewable energy and automotive manufacturing capabilities, and Botswana’s diamond governance remains a reference point for how institutions can turn mineral wealth into public value. The real question, then, is not whether Africa can deliver, but why proven approaches are so rarely adapted, financed and sustained elsewhere on the continent. The Promises Made Over Dinner Governments are not the only promise makers who deserve scrutiny. International corporations, investors, consultants and development partners arrive with generous commitments to local employment, technology transfer, skills development, responsible sourcing, environmental protection and supplier participation, and while many honour them admirably, others leave communities wondering whether those undertakings were ever intended to become measurable obligations. Africa must therefore move beyond ceremonial memoranda of understanding and ask harder questions with courteous persistence: how many permanent jobs were created, how many local suppliers became competitive, how many African engineers were trained to advanced levels, how much value was added locally, and how much knowledge remained after the foreign contractor flew home. With trade among African countries still accounting for only around 16 percent of the continent’s exports, according to UN Trade and Development, investment must strengthen Africa’s productive capacity rather than simply expand markets for imported finished goods. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) reminds us that “partnership should mean shared value creation, not merely shared photographs.” We Celebrate The Wrong Scoreboard Perhaps our deepest institutional habit is the celebration of inputs rather than outcomes. We proudly announce how much money was allocated, how many committees were formed, how many agreements were signed and how many delegations travelled, yet citizens are rarely told whether maternal mortality fell, whether children read better, whether journeys became shorter or whether young people found lasting work. A budget is not an achievement merely because it was approved, a policy is not a success merely because it was published, and a summit is not transformative merely because the hotel was fully booked. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) cautions that “a government that confuses expenditure with achievement may discover it has spent a fortune without purchasing progress.” From Ceremonies To A Culture Of Execution The remedy begins with a new discipline of delivery, in which every major public commitment carries defined outcomes, a responsible institution, realistic financing, published milestones and independent review, with progress visible to citizens through accessible public dashboards. Public procurement should reward competence and value for money, contracts should contain enforceable performance obligations, and ministers and chief executives alike should be assessed by measurable results rather than by the frequency of their television appearances. National programmes should be designed to survive political transitions, while continental ambitions such as Agenda 2063 and the African Continental Free Trade Area must be translated into experiences people can feel, from shorter border crossings to seamless payments and harmonised standards, because a trader should never need to read a treaty to discover whether integration is working. The Mirror Every Citizen Must Face Here lies the most uncomfortable question of all, for development cannot be delivered by governments alone. We cannot demand clean cities while emptying refuse into drains, demand accountable institutions while seeking favours that bypass the queue, demand excellent education while shrugging at examination malpractice, or demand industrialisation while dismissing competitive African products in favour of anything bearing a foreign label. This does not absolve leaders of their duties, but it reminds us that progress rests upon a social contract in which leaders deliver, businesses create responsible value, institutions uphold standards and citizens contribute. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) observes, with a knowing smile, that “the citizen who demands national transformation while protecting his own bad habits is asking the country to change on his behalf.” Receipts, Not Reassurances It is time to change what we applaud, honouring functioning hospitals rather than hospital promises, reliable electricity rather than power sector declarations, employable graduates rather than graduation statistics, and enduring institutions rather than personalities whose achievements vanish when they leave office. This is not a demand for miracles, since development requires time, money, competence and hard choices, but it is a demand for honesty, so that a credible leader can say, “this is what we promised, this is what we delivered, this is what remains unfinished, and this is how we will correct it.” One day every president, minister, chief executive and investor will leave office, the banners will come down and the photographs will become archives, and what remains will be the factories that operate, the hospitals that heal, the schools that educate and the institutions that endure for children not yet born. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) offers a final reflection: “a promise belongs to the moment it is made, but a fulfilled commitment belongs to generations.” Africa has heard enough about what will be done, and it is time to show what has been done, because a continent’s future cannot be built forever in the future tense. What, then, is wrong with us, and are we finally willing to fix it? ABOUT THE AUTHOR Ing. Professor Douglas Boateng is a pioneering international industrial, manufacturing, and production systems engineer, governance strategist, and Pan-African thought leader whose work continues to influence boardroom thinking, supply chain transformation, and industrialisation strategy across the continent and beyond. As Africa’s first appointed Professor Extraordinaire in Supply Chain Management, he has long championed the integration of procurement, value chain development, industrialisation and governance into national and continental development agendas. An International Chartered Director and Chartered Engineer, he has received numerous lifetime achievement awards and authored several authoritative books. He is the scribe of the globally acclaimed NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom). His work rests on the conviction that Africa’s transformation and the protection of its children will come through deliberate action, strong institutions and leaders willing to build for generations they will never meet. © 2026 Ing. title: How Dubai Fitness Challenge changed lives, from finding love to losing 50kg
body: What began in 2017 as an initiative encouraging Dubai residents to exercise for 30 minutes a day over 30 days has grown into one of the emirate's largest annual community events. Dubai Fitness Challenge returns for its 10th iteration from October 31 to November 29, bringing thousands of free activities and fitness experiences across the emirate. Under this year's theme, What's Your 30?, residents and visitors are once again being encouraged to embrace a more active lifestyle, with flagship events including Dubai Run , Dubai Ride, Dubai Yoga and Dubai Stand-Up Paddle . Launched by Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed , Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence, the initiative has recorded more than 16 million participants since its inception, bringing together people of different ages, nationalities and fitness levels. Beyond the numbers and large-scale events, the initiative has transformed lives. Here, three Dubai residents share, in their own words, how the city's fitness culture has touched their lives. Tania Lolla Kaddoura: 'I met my future husband at the finish line' When I arrived in Dubai from Serbia in September 2017, I was a stranger to the city, carrying a bag, a lot of dreams and the hope that this new chapter would bring new opportunities. I was already a physiotherapist, personal trainer and athlete, so when I heard about the first Dubai Fitness Challenge, I knew I wanted to be involved.
