title: Israeli artillery fire hits southern Lebanon towns
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 28 (MNA) – Israeli artillery shelling targeted several areas in southern Lebanon on Wednesday.
Israeli artillery shelling has targeted several areas in southern Lebanon this morning, Lebanon’s state-run National News Agency (NNA) reports.
The NNA said al-Mansouri, Majdal Zoun, and the surrounding valleys were all targeted, with several shells landing in the eastern neighbourhood of the village of Haddatha.
There are currently no reports of any injuries.

title: Mbappe apology taken ‘seriously’ after Mao remark, China says
body: China said Wednesday it took “seriously” an apology from Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe after comments he made poking fun at Mao Zedong sparked a social media storm and saw Spanish football yanked off state TV. Mocking former leader Mao — blamed by historians for millions of deaths — is taboo in China and the French player’s remarks saw him become the latest foreign sports figure to anger Beijing. In a clip of a video interview with French show The Bridge — since taken down — Mbappe talked about being amused by an internet meme of his face photoshopped onto “some guy, think he’s a Chinese dictator”, an apparent reference to Mao. “My comment was ill-judged and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone my words have upset,” the France captain said in a statement in French, Chinese and English on Tuesday. Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing on Wednesday: “We take seriously the apology the individual concerned has made.” La Liga, which saw the broadcast of its matches suspended in China, said it “deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe’s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans”. But that may not be the end of the matter. Chinese beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year’s World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappe, said Tuesday it had scrapped its partnership with the player, as did dairy firms Mengniu and Milkground. CMG, which oversees public broadcaster CCTV, said it had decided to suspend broadcasts of the world’s second-richest football league after England’s Premier League. Mbappe’s club also drew fire for not issuing any public apology, with “How much longer will arrogant Real Madrid keep playing ostrich” ranking fifth on search engine Baidu on Wednesday. Real “has neither criticised nor warned Mbappe over his conduct, let alone imposed any disciplinary measures”, the state-run Global Times said in an editorial. Mbappe, 27, continued to face a torrent of criticism from Chinese web users on Wednesday, some of it racist. “His remarks were hurtful toward China and the Chinese people, so they cannot be translated,” wrote one user on social media platform Weibo. Mbappe’s original joke about Mao was not reposted — or had been scrubbed — from China’s tightly controlled social media. Chinese social media app Xiaohongshu had meanwhile frozen Mbappe’s account, where he has over a million followers. The same was done on the Weibo app, with a notice stating that “the user has been banned from following due to violating laws or the Weibo Community Convention”. Some Chinese media reports said global brands like Dior and Hublot had removed their Mbappe-related content on Weibo. An AFP search on Dior and Hublot’s Weibo page with Mbappe’s Chinese name produced no results. – ‘Respect history’ – Offline too the Mbappe brand appeared to be under threat. When AFP visited the Adidas flagship store in Beijing’s Sanlitun shopping district, Real Madrid shirts were available for sale, but none bearing the striker’s name. Chinese state media have previously praised Mbappe as a “footballing sensation” and “talent”. His face is plastered on billboards, on soft drinks and across social media. Mbappe is sometimes affectionately referred to as “Guigui”, meaning “turtle” in Chinese, for his resemblance to a character from the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles movie. Other major overseas sports leagues have previously angered China. China suspended sponsorship deals with the NBA while the state broadcaster pulled NBA games off Chinese television for a year in October 2019. This followed Houston Rockets executive Daryl Morey tweeting “Fight for freedom, stand with Hong Kong”, referring to protests Beijing called separatist and seditious. “Respecting the history, culture, social customs and national sentiments of others is a fundamental principle for cross-border interaction, a standard of conduct widely upheld by the international community,” the official People’s Daily said in an opinion piece. title: Sultan of Sokoto to Honour Peter Igho as Kakakin Daular Usmaniyya
body: The Palace of His Eminence, the Sultan of Sokoto, has announced that the formal turbaning ceremony of Chief Peter Igho as Kakakin Daular Usmaniyya will take place on November 1, 2026. The prestigious traditional title was conferred on Chief Igho by His Eminence, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, on September 10, 2025, in recognition of his invaluable contributions to the development of the Sultanate Council, Sokoto State, and Nigeria in general. The ceremony is expected to be witnessed by prominent Nigerians from all walks of life, and across the country, serving to further cement cordial relations and national unity among the diverse peoples of Nigeria. Chief P Igho is a legendary Nigerian broadcaster, television producer and media icon. A former Executive Director at the Nigerian Television Authority (NTA), he is best known as the Producer/Director of timeless classics such as Cock Crow at Dawn and other pioneering programmes that defined Nigerian television. He is a recipient of numerous national and international awards for broadcasting excellence and has mentored generations of media professionals. Chief Igho, who hails from the Niger Delta, is also a respected cultural ambassador and community leader noted for his philanthropy and commitment to national integration. The Sokoto Caliphate, also known as Daular Usmaniyya, was founded in 1804 by the great Islamic scholar and reformer, Shehu Usman Dan Fodio. It remains one of the most significant empires in African history, renowned for its scholarship, administration, justice and promotion of Islamic values. At its peak, it was the largest state in West Africa. Today, the Sultanate Council, under the Sultan of Sokoto, remains the pre-eminent custodian of its heritage and a central institution for Islamic leadership, peacebuilding, and national cohesion in Nigeria.

title: Ampem Darkoa Ladies arrive in Egypt ahead of final replay against Edo Queens
body: Ghana Women’s Premier League champions, Ampem Darkoa Ladies, have arrived in Egypt ahead of the replay of their game against Edo Queens. Ampem Darkoa and Edo Queens will play the 30 minutes of extra time in the WAFU B Women’s Champions League qualifiers after their penalty shootout result was nullified. In a letter addressed to both clubs, CAF referenced the WAFU Zone B qualifying final played on 5 September 2026 and the subsequent decisions of the CAF Organising Committee for Women’s Football dated 26 September 2026 and the CAF Appeal Board dated 16 October 2026. According to CAF, the match will resume from the start of extra time with the score at 2-2, with two periods of 15 minutes to be played, followed by a penalty shoot-out if the score remains level. The Ghanaian side have arrived in Egypt for the encounter to be played in Cairo this week. The winner will stay in Egypt to participate in the main CAF Women’s Champions League tournament.

title: ‘Nigeria to Begin Mass Production of Military Munitions within One Year’
body: Linus Aleke in Abuja The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (rtd), has disclosed that Nigeria will commence large-scale local production of defence hardware next year for domestic use and export, particularly to other African countries. Speaking at the inaugural Africa International Defence Exhibition (AFRIDEX) in Lagos yesterday, the minister urged participants to seize the opportunity presented by the exhibition to invest in Nigeria’s defence sector. According to a statement issued by the Chief Information Officer of the Ministry of Defence, Dr. Queenet Iheoma-Hart, the minister said the side events scheduled to take place during the exhibition would strengthen bilateral and multilateral relations among defence establishments, government representatives, industry stakeholders, and other strategic partners. In his remarks, the Minister of State for Defence, Dr Bello Muhammad Matawalle, described AFRIDEX as a dynamic platform capable of achieving the objectives for which it was established. In their goodwill messages, the Lagos State Governor, represented by his Deputy, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, and the representative of the ECOWAS Commission, Mr. Birame Diop, expressed optimism that the gathering would provide an inclusive platform for African countries to expand and revitalise their defence sectors. Also, the Director-General of the Defence Industries Corporation of Nigeria (DICON), Major General B.I. Alaya, commended President Bola Tinubu for his continued support for DICON, and pledged to enhance its production capacity. Following the opening ceremony, the Minister of Defence inspected exhibition stands featuring displays from various countries and held an executive meeting with the United States Africa Command (AFRICOM). Dignitaries in attendance included the Chief of Defence Staff, serving and former Service Chiefs, the chairman of the National Assembly Committee on Defence, and representatives from more than 20 African countries.

title: Gov Eno To Sponsor 100 Youths For Agricultural Entrepreneurship Training
body: Akwa Ibom State Governor, Pastor Umo Eno, has offered to sponsor 100 youths in the state for agricultural entrepreneurship training at CSS Global Integrated Farms in Nasarawa State as part of efforts to promote youth empowerment and enterprise development. He made the offer on Tuesday during the ninth edition of the Ibom Ignite Conference held at Ibom Hall, Uyo. Governor Eno said the initiative would equip young people with practical agricultural skills and prepare them to take advantage of opportunities in the sector. He urged youths to embrace continuous learning, rethink their approaches to business and adapt to changing economic realities, noting that the ability to reinvent oneself was essential for sustained entrepreneurial success. According to him, the Ibom Ignite programme, which began in 2017, has helped participants explore new opportunities, develop entrepreneurial mindsets and improve their businesses. Governor Eno explained that his commitment to mentoring and empowering young people was driven by the need to equip them with entrepreneurial and leadership skills to enable them to make meaningful contributions to society. He also highlighted other youth development initiatives undertaken by his administration, including the training of 2,000 youths through the Ibom Leadership and Entrepreneurial Development Centre (Ibom-LED), with each participant receiving a start-up package of ₦750,000. Another 2,000 youths, he said, had received training at the Dakkada Skills Acquisition Centre, with start-up grants ranging from ₦500,000 to ₦1 million for each trainee. He added that the state was developing youth development centres across its 31 local government areas. Governor Eno encouraged participants to take advantage of the opportunities available through the conference and remain committed to developing their skills and building sustainable businesses. The training sponsorship was announced during the conference, which had the theme, “Reinvent, Rethink, Reimagine, Redesign and Become.” In his keynote address, Apostle Joshua Selman spoke on “The Courage to Become: Why Your Next Level Requires a New You,” highlighting the importance of awareness, access to relevant information, consistent action, courage and sacrifice in achieving personal growth. Also speaking, the Chief Executive Officer of CSS Global Integrated Farms, Professor John Kennedy Opara, identified passion, performance and the ability to recognise possibilities as important factors in entrepreneurial success. He drew from his experience in agricultural business to encourage young people to remain committed to their goals and not despise small beginnings. title: Youth Olympics: Nigeria names 19 athletes for Dakar 2026
body:
Nigeria will be represented by 19 athletes across six sports at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, with the country’s contingent putting finishing touches to its preparations ahead of the competition, which begins in Senegal on 31 October.
The National Sports Commission (NSC) said the team comprises 12 female and seven male athletes who will compete in athletics, boxing, road cycling, swimming, table tennis and beach volleyball.
The Games, scheduled to run until 13 November, will be the first Olympic sporting event to be hosted on African soil.
The fourth edition of the Summer Youth Olympic Games will take place across three host zones in Senegal: Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly, with young athletes from across the world expected to compete.
Athletics will have Nigeria’s largest contingent, with nine athletes comprising five women and four men.
Swimming will feature four athletes, split equally between women and men, while table tennis will have two representatives, one male and one female.
Nigeria will also field one female boxer, one female road cyclist and a two-athlete women’s beach volleyball team.
According to the NSC, the contingent is undergoing final preparations following a 21-day local camping programme that began on 9 October and is scheduled to end on 29 October.
The programme has included medical screening, anti-doping education, technical and tactical training, kit fitting, travel documentation and other preparations for the Games.
The opening ceremony is scheduled for 31 October at the Diamniadio Olympic Stadium. Competitions in table tennis and beach volleyball are also expected to begin that day.
The Youth Olympic Games will offer Nigeria’s emerging athletes an opportunity to gain international experience, compete against some of the world’s best young talents and prepare for future senior-level competitions, including the Olympic Games.
As the countdown continues, the NSC has urged the athletes to represent the country with distinction and translate their preparations into strong performances in Senegal.

title: No violations recorded since Alyoshki ceasefire establishment — human rights commissioner
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. There have been no ceasefire violations near Alyoshki in the Kherson Region since its establishment, Russian human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova reported.
"Over the 30 hours of the ceasefire, no incidents in Alyoshki have been recorded," she wrote on her Max channel.
She said that she is in constant contact with her Ukrainian counterpart Dmitry Lubinets, with whom they coordinate the implementation of the agreements together.
"I would like to thank US First Lady Melania Trump once again for supporting the humanitarian mission and helping the residents of Alyoshki. Her personal involvement is crucial to the entire process. A huge thank-you also goes to Melania Trump’s team for their significant efforts in coordinating," the ombudswoman wrote.
Lantratova emphasized that the goal of the humanitarian mission is to assist the residents of Alyoshki in the Kherson Region, and to ensure that anyone who wishes to leave the town can do so safely.
On October 23, the White House announced that Russia and Ukraine, with the assistance of Melania Trump, had reached an agreement on a ceasefire in the town of Alyoshki in the Kherson Region starting October 29. The two countries agreed to halt all hostilities in Alyoshki to facilitate the delivery of humanitarian aid and prepare for the evacuation of civilians through a designated safe corridor.
The Russian Defense Ministry reported earlier that Russian forces had ceased combat operations in the Kherson area at 4:00 a.m. Moscow time on October 27 and declared a ceasefire to prepare a humanitarian operation in Alyoshki. On October 23, Russian Armed Forces’ General Staff Chief and First Deputy Defense Minister Army General Valery Gerasimov that, to ensure the safety of civilians and the delivery of essential supplies, engineering reconnaissance would be conducted and measures would be taken to ensure the safe passage of the humanitarian convoy in Alyoshki.
According to the Russian Defense Ministry, the Kiev regime has been shelling roads leading to Alyoshki and extensively using drones to destroy vehicles for over two years. Ukrainian forces have also used unmanned aerial vehicles to lay mines along roads, preventing civilian evacuations and impeding the delivery of food, medicine, and other essential supplies to Alyoshki.

title: Nigerian newspapers review: Tinubu seeks $20.5bn, €1.04bn foreign loans to fund projects
body: In today’s Nigerian newspapers review programme, Today in the News, Vanguard leads with President Bola Tinubu writing to the Senate to seek approval for a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion to finance infrastructure and development projects nationwide. Another headline reports that the Federal Government and the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) agreed on a series of measures to ease the economic difficulties facing workers, including a ₦70,000 transport intervention and payment of 19 months’ arrears owed to health workers. Moving to another newspaper, The Guardian leads with Nigeria’s mounting debt burden coming under heightened scrutiny as President Tinubu seeks legislative approval for fresh external loans of $21.7 billion ($20.52 billion and €1.045 billion), amid rising debt refinancing and little to no savings to liquidate maturing obligations. The Punch reports that Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara asked his supporters to stop referring to him as their leader, declaring that following his reconciliation with his predecessor, Nyesom Wike, he is now a member of the Rainbow Coalition, with the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory as its leader. title: Knife attacker killed outside Israel's embassy to Serbia after guard attacked, Serbian police say
body: A guard at Israel's embassy in Belgrade, Serbia, was attacked by a knife-wielding assailant early on Wednesday morning, according to Serbian police.The attacker was killed at the site shortly after midnight.Serbia's Interior Minister Ivica Dacic said that police had increased the terror threat level to "Red," the highest possible grade, and increased their presence at vulnerable locations, according to the Associated Press."A minor, so far unidentified... rushed at an officer of the Gendarmerie shouting 'Allahu Akbar' and attacked him with two knives," said Dacic.The guard was lightly wounded.Belgrade prosecutors describe the attackIn a statement, the Belgrade-based Higher Public Prosecution Office said that an investigation showed that a black-clad unidentified individual opened the door of a guard house in front of the embassy and, armed with two knives, rushed at the policeman, identified only by the initials D.S."The unidentified person threw one knife in the direction of D.S., hitting him in the left cheek. After that, D.S. took out his service weapon and fired several shots at the attacker, killing him on the spot," it said, adding that the policeman's action was qualified as justified and in self-defense.The investigation was continuing, it said.Suspect on security services' radar prior to attack, ISIS links suspectedDacic noted that security services had been monitoring the suspect prior to the attack."Based on the information available to us so far, he was known as a supporter of the Islamic State. His Instagram profile featured a black flag and symbols associated with the organization," he said, according to the Associated Press.Dacic added that he visited the injured officer in the hospital alongside Police Director Gen. Dragan Vasiljevic, noting that the officer is in good condition and expected to be discharged for home care later today.This was the second attack at the Israeli embassy in Belgrade in two years. In June 2024, an assailant shot a Serbian police officer in the neck with a crossbow.Israel's Foreign Ministry noted that "there were no casualties among embassy staff, as the diplomatic mission was closed at that hour of the night."

title: Israeli military escalation in PG could impact intl. markets
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 28 (MNA) – Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi has said that the Israeli military escalation in the Persian Gulf region could impact the international markets to a great extent.
Iran’s top diplomat emphasized that energy security and global gas markets were discussed at the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) Summit, warning that any Israeli-instigated military escalation in the Persian Gulf could severely impact international markets.
He went on to say that Iran’s energy diplomacy advanced at GECF Summit, adding that discussions focused on the global gas markets and energy security.
The devastating impact on the international markets of any Israel-instigated military misadventure in the Persian Gulf region remains major concern for both gas suppliers and consumers.

title: Dangote Refinery’s IPO closes with investors from 120 countries
body: A Nigerian oil refinery owned by Africa’s richest man Aliko Dangote has closed the continent’s biggest initial public share offering, claiming to have raised funds from investors in 120 countries. The IPO for the Lagos-based Dangote Petroleum Refinery was initially due to close on October 13 but was extended by two weeks to allow more Africans to participate. The company did not disclose how much money was potentially raised by the offering, after saying its target was $1.6 billion. But Aliko Dangote said earlier this month that it had exceeded that goal by “more than three, four times”. “This is a historic achievement for Africa. It shows what is possible when we believe in our continent, work together and invest in our shared future,” he said in a statement late Tuesday. The massive refinery has a capacity of 700,000 barrels per day and aims to double its output to 1.4 million barrels per day, potentially making it the world’s largest refinery, surpassing the Jamnagar refinery in India. Investors from all 54 African countries and five other continents participated in the offering, the company said. “Investor applications spanning 120 countries demonstrate the extraordinary international interest in our business and the confidence that investors are placing in the future of this refinery,” Aliko Dangote said “The opportunity to own a stake in a major African industrial enterprise has reached investors across every African country and all six inhabited continents,” he added. In July, the refinery secured $2.5 billion in investment from private investors. Last month, the company broke ground on a planned $16 billion refinery on Kenya’s Lamu island, with a projected capacity of 700,000 barrels a day. Africa currently imports more than 70 percent of its refined fuel, according to an Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) report in April. The post Dangote Refinery’s IPO closes with investors from 120 countries appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Forum of PDP State Chairmen Condemns Escalating Political Violence in Ebonyi
body: Benjamin Nworie in Abakaliki The Forum of State Chairmen of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has demanded urgent action on the alleged escalating political violence in Ebonyi State. Briefing journalists in Abakaliki, the Chairman of the forum, Hon. Austin Nwachukwu, alleged that democracy is under siege in the state and therefore called for national and international scrutiny. The Forum expressed profound outrage over reports of escalating threats, attacks, abductions, killings, unlawful detention, and destruction of property targeting PDP leaders, candidates, executives, and supporters in the state. According to Nwachukwu, “The reported incidents, combined with restrictions on PDP activities and concerns about the impartiality of security agencies, raise serious questions about citizens’ safety, freedom of association, and the integrity of the political environment ahead of the 2027 general elections. “Political disagreement must never become a justification for violence, and no Nigerian should suffer intimidation for belonging to a political party. “The Forum is concerned by reports that on May 25, 2026, Governor Francis Nwifuru ordered the closure of the PDP state secretariat, which was reportedly cordoned off by more than 150 security personnel. The facility has allegedly remained sealed, preventing the PDP State Working Committee from accessing its offices.” He added: “On June 15, 2026, the governor reportedly threatened to ‘consume, destroy or kill’ any PDP member considered a threat to his re-election. On September 1, 2026, he directed his newly selected local government chairmen to deal mercilessly with the PDP members in their respective jurisdictions. “Following the governor’s directive, the Chairmen of Ohaukwu Local Government Area, Mr. Paul Ituma, and Onicha LGA, Mr. Ikechukwu Ogboffia, went ahead to warn of lamentable consequences for PDP members in their areas. “On October 15, 2026, the PDP State Woman Leader, Mrs. Chinyere Nwele, was arrested by operatives of the Ebonyi State Police Command under frivolous reasons. According to information available to this Forum, she has remained in detention to date.” The PDP leader continued: “On October 20, 2026, Jimo Guest House, owned by one of the PDP youth leaders, Jimo Abu, was sealed by state government agents. Mr Abu was abducted the following day and forced to renounce PDP membership and publicly declare support for Governor Nwifuru at gunpoint. “On October 22, 2026, a gang of youths alleged to be agents of the governor attacked security personnel at Amaezekwe village in Ezza South LGA, resulting in serious casualties. The circumstances require independent investigation. “The Forum has also received reports of the abduction and killing of Elder Onwe Obochi of Oshege village, Ohaukwu, following his attendance at a political meeting involving opposition members.” He further demanded that the allegations be thoroughly investigated so that anyone found responsible through credible evidence must face the appropriate legal consequences regardless of political affiliation or official position. The forum also demanded that the Inspector-General of Police establish an impartial investigative team to investigate the reported attacks, threats, abduction, killing, armed robbery, and destruction of property. “The Forum is concerned by allegations that Governor Nwifuru’s administration has afforded APGA and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) access to public spaces for political activities while restricting or threatening or sealing private venues of PDP gatherings. “We have also received allegations of a discreet political understanding between the governor and the NDC intended to secure support from the political camp associated with the NDC presidential candidate. “The Forum is further concerned that the governor’s reported political arrangements could undermine President Tinubu’s re-election prospects, particularly as the Ebonyi State PDP governorship candidate, Chief Dr. Ifeanyi Chukwuma Odii, has openly indicated his support for the re-election of President Tinubu. These allegations require verification. Nevertheless, they raise important questions about equal access to public facilities, the impartial use of state resources and the freedom of political parties to organise themselves,” the Forum said. Police, however, said search operations are ongoing to rescue the remaining four victims and apprehend the perpetrators.

title: Five Suspected Bandits Invade Kwara Community, Abduct Father, Son
body: Hammed Shittu in Ilorin About five suspected bandits have reportedly invaded an Oke Esi compound in Kajola community in Oke-Ero Local Government Area of Kwara State, and abducted a father and son. The affected victims, according to THISDAY checks, are Elder Bamidele Mathem and his son, Bamidele Ibukun Already, palpable tension has gripped the residents of Kajola town in the local government area due to the kidnapping of their residents. The two victims, it was gathered, were kidnapped on their way to the farm at Idofin Igbana, Iloffa, headquarters of the local government area. Sources close to the town told journalists in Ilorin yesterday that vigilantes, police and other security agencies in the area have been deployed into the bush to rescue the victims. Although no positive results have yet to manifest, sources close to the town said the residents have embarked on fervent prayers and fasting to ensure the safe return of the two victims. One of the residents of Kajola town, who spoke on the condition of anonymity with journalists yesterday, expressed deep concern over the continued attacks by suspected bandits in the area despite the recent establishment of a military formation at Omu-Aran in Irepodun LGA of the state. She said that the ugly development has prevented many of the people of the town going to their farms to meet economic means recently. She, therefore, appealed to the appropriate authorities to rise to the ugly development to ensure the safety of the residents and the people of Kwara South Senatorial District of the state. When contacted, a senior police officer with the Oke-Ero Local Government Area of the state, who sought anonymity, confirmed the abduction of the two victims on Tuesday. He said: “It is true that a father and son were abducted in the area on their way to the farm, but we are working round the clock with other security agencies in the area to ensure the rescue of the victims. Meanwhile, in a related operation, a joint team of police operatives, military troops, forest guards and vigilantes has rescued one kidnapped victim, Musa Mejindaji, unhurt after intensive bush-combing. It was gathered that operatives also recovered 11 expended AK-47 ammunition shells at the scene.

title: 2026 U-17 WWC: ‘Success shall be ours’ – Black Maidens assistant coach ahead of Argentina clash
body: Black Maidens assistant coach Bashiru-Deen Sumaila has expressed optimism that “success shall be ours” as Ghana prepare for their Round of 16 clash against Argentina in the U-17 Women’s World Cup. The Maidens advanced to the knockout stage following a 2-0 victory over Canada in their final group game, with substitutes Linda Achiaa and Christiana Ashiaku scoring the goals. The victory set up a tie against the South Americans, who topped Group A unbeaten. “We’ve watched Argentina, we had the time to have the girls watch whatever is supposed to be done, what they need to work around, and what we have to be very careful of,” Sumaila told Ghana FA media. “The girls are very poised and ready for the game. [It] is going to be a very good game, and we will win. We are going to give our best tomorrow, and success shall be ours.” The game is scheduled to kick off at 18:00 GMT in Rabat.

title: Police arrest man who allegedly lured, raped PoS operators
body:
The police in Enugu State say they have arrested a 30-year-old man, Chika Ugbor, over alleged serial rape, robbery and sextortion of women in the state.
The police spokesperson in the state, Daniel Ndukwe, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday.
Mr Ndukwe, a superintendent of police, said the suspect had been targeting female POS operators for rape, robbery and sextortion.
“Preliminary investigations indicate that he lured female POS operators to secluded locations under the pretext of conducting transactions, where he allegedly robbed and sexually assaulted them,” he said.
The spokesperson said the suspect equally allegedly used Facebook, posing as Franklin Umeh, to lure another victim and often recorded his victims’ nude videos.
“A phone recovered from him reportedly contains nude images and video clips of identified and unidentified victims,” he said.
Mr Ndukwe said one of his victims, a 20-year-old POS operator at Akwata Market in Enugu was allegedly lured to a bush behind St. Peter’s Church, Coal Camp at about 11:00 a.m. on 21 May this year where the suspect allegedly robbed her of N600,000 and raped her.
The spokesperson said the second victim, a 30-year-old POS operator at the same market, was allegedly lured to the same location at about 5:00 p.m. on 11 August and robbed of N120,000, after unsuccessful attempts to also rape her.
He narrated that the third victim, 21, was allegedly lured through Facebook by the suspect, posing as Franklin Umeh, to Old Park, Enugu, at about 11:30 a.m. on 4 October, before being taken to a bush around Udi Siding.
“He (the suspect) allegedly raped her, recorded her nude, and robbed her of N100,000 and her phone.
“He subsequently threatened to circulate the video unless she paid N200,000 and allegedly used her phone to contact some of her WhatsApp contacts,” the police spokesperson said.
Mr Ndukwe said investigations into the incidents were ongoing and that the suspect would be arraigned upon conclusion of the investigations.
“Other victims are urged to come forward and assist the investigation. Young women who have experienced cyberstalking or sextortion are also encouraged to report such incidents to the police for appropriate action,” he said.
The spokesperson said the Commissioner of Police in Enugu State, Bitrus Giwa, reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to protecting residents from sexual violence, robbery and other crimes.
He urged the public, particularly women and business operators, to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious activities to the police.
Nigeria, in 2015, enacted the Violence against Persons (Prohibition) Act, which outlawed all forms of violence against women and girls, including rape, female circumcision and forceful ejection.
Offenders, on conviction, face life imprisonment or minimum of 14-year jail term, depending on the age of the offender and type of violence committed.
Several persons have been convicted by various courts for rape.
An Ado-Ekiti High Court, in July 2022, sentenced a 49-year-old man, Dele Adeyanju, to four years’ imprisonment for raping an 11-year-old girl.
A Bauchi High Court, in 2017, sentenced two middle aged men to life in prison for raping a 40-year-old woman and plucking her eyes.

title: Rada reviews rejected 2027 budget amendments until 0300, to vote on 2 Wednesday
body:
The Verkhovna Rada considered rejected amendments by MPs to the draft state budget for 2027 until 3:00 AM on Wednesday, and during the session on Wednesday, October 28, will vote separately on two of them, reported MP Yaroslav Zheleznyak (Holos faction) on his Telegram channel.
According to him, the first of these (No. 611) concerns the allocation of funds from plea bargain agreements: they must be credited exclusively to the state budget or for compensation under a civil lawsuit, and funds exceeding the damage caused—to a special fund for the monetary allowance of Ukrainian Armed Forces servicemen. The amendment also instructs the government to verify the legality of agreements for 2022–2026 and submit a report to parliament by September 1, 2027.
The second amendment (No. 1003) provides for a restriction in 2027 on the maximum monthly salary of 80,000 UAH for employees of government authorities, local self-government, budgetary institutions, as well as MPs, judges, members of the High Council of Justice, the High Qualification Commission of Judges of Ukraine, prosecutors, and NBU employees (excluding positions involved in defense).
In addition, during Wednesday's session in the assembly hall, all amendments incorporated by the Budget Committee will be put to a confirmation vote, in particular proposal No. 1279 regarding an increase in servicemen's monetary allowances.
According to information on the Rada's Telegram channel, the document will be considered in the first reading as a basis. As Zheleznyak specified, the Rada will consider it in the second reading in November.
As reported, on October 27, the Verkhovna Rada Budget Committee approved Budget Conclusions for the draft state budget for 2027, which contain 90 summary proposals formed from 5,236 deputy amendments, and recommended that parliament adopt them as a basis and send the budget draft to the government for preparation for the second reading.
The government's draft state budget for 2027 provides for general fund revenues at the level of 5.65 trillion UAH (8.7% more compared to 2026) and expenditures amounting to 7.27 trillion UAH (an increase of 13.5%).

title: Russia conducts tests of SOVA autonomous navigation system for UAVs
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Russia’s SOVA (Comparative Optical Visual Authentication) autonomous navigation system, designed to ensure precise positioning of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) when GPS/GNSS signals and external communications are unavailable or jammed, has been successfully tested in the field, the Center for Unmanned Systems and Technologies (CUST) told TASS.
"The developer of the solution, VA Technologies, is a finalist in the third cohort of the CUST Special-and Dual-Use Projects Accelerator. The SOVA system is based on computer vision technology. During flight, the system compares images from an onboard camera with a satellite map of the terrain and determines the UAV’s location in real time. During testing, a drone equipped with the SOVA system completed a route that had no clear landmarks and included substantial differences between the satellite map and the actual terrain," the company said.
The CUST specified that the flight path was star-shaped. "The UAV, equipped with the autonomous navigation system, sequentially visited four waypoints and returned to its launch site. To make the task more challenging, satellite images from the spring of 2025 were used instead of an up-to-date map. Thus, the tests were conducted with a known discrepancy between the actual terrain and the map data used by the drone," the center noted.
According to the CUST, the most challenging section for the system was the stretch between the second and third waypoints. "The second waypoint on the satellite map was located over dark plowed land, while the actual terrain featured a light-colored field covered with stubble. With no landmarks to guide it, the UAV deviated from its course. However, upon reaching a tree line, the SOVA system promptly corrected its course and successfully reached the third waypoint," the company said.
VA Technologies, commenting on the situation, emphasized that such a scenario is not a failure but a standard operating condition for which the system was designed. "According to the developer, in the absence of GPS, SOVA is capable of increasing the UAV mission reliability rate to 99%," the CUST noted.

title: Ukrainians back retaliatory strikes on Russian refineries even if US halts aid, 80% say – KMIS
body:
More than three-quarters of Ukrainians support continuing the armed resistance against the Russian Federation despite Russian attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure during the winter, and an even larger majority favors retaliatory strikes on Russian oil refineries even if the U.S cuts off military aid to Ukraine as a result, according to a survey conducted between October 16 and 25 by the Kyiv International Institute of Sociology (KMIS).
Specifically, 76% of Ukrainians maintain that even if Russia attempts to target the energy sector in winter to leave people without electricity, heat, or sewage, Ukraine must still continue its armed resistance. Meanwhile, 15% believe that under such conditions, Ukraine should agree to any Russian demands, even if they look like capitulation. Another 9% were undecided.
KMIS notes that macroeconomic breakdowns show no significant regional differences, and figures remain virtually unchanged from August-September within the margin of error.
An even greater share of respondents—80%—expressed the view that strikes on Russian oil refineries should still be carried out even if the U.S stops or limits its assistance to Ukraine. Only 11% answered that such strikes should be halted, while 8% were undecided.
During the poll, 63% of Ukrainians stated they are ready to endure the war for as long as necessary, while 5% mentioned a timeframe of 1 year. Shorter periods (several months to half a year) were cited by 21%, with the remaining 11% undecided. KMIS noted no significant changes compared to results obtained on October 8–16.
Additionally, 62% of respondents expressed trust in current Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, while 35% do not trust him (a balance of +27%). The institute noted that trust in the president stood at 43% (with 52% distrust) on October 8–9, but rose to 57% trust (and 39% distrust) by October 10–16.
"Following October 9—that is, after the 'diesel deal'—Ukraine and Ukrainians found themselves under triple pressure: from the Russian enemy and its terror campaign of jet drones and ballistic missiles (accompanied by information warfare), from certain domestic actors (some of whom insist on de facto peace at any price, while others prioritize an uncompromising struggle against the government), and from our strategic partner, the U.S... Despite these pressures, Ukrainians maintain resilience in repelling the enemy: the majority are ready to endure the war as long as needed, insist that despite a potentially difficult winter Ukraine must not yield to Russian peace terms, and believe that even with the risk of losing US support, strikes on Russian oil refineries must continue," commented KMIS Executive Director Anton Hrushetskyi on the survey results.
He also noted that despite calls from certain public figures for Zelenskyy to step down, trust in him continues to grow.
"Ukrainian society has wisely mobilized for unity during this difficult period, but the Ukrainian authorities must also learn the right lessons and avoid euphoria from success, otherwise we will quickly return to a downward trend in trust... In any case, our data demonstrate that Ukrainians, despite everything, have the will to continue resistance until an acceptable outcome in the war is achieved," Hrushetskyi concluded.
The survey was conducted via telephone interviews (CATI) based on a random sample of mobile phone numbers in all government-controlled regions of Ukraine among 828 adult respondents. Under normal conditions, the formal statistical margin of error for such a sample (with a 0.95 probability and taking into account a design effect of 1.3) does not exceed 4.4% for indicators close to 50% and 1.9% for indicators close to 5%. Under wartime conditions, certain systematic deviations are added alongside the formal margin of error, but the results retain high representativeness.

title: What’s hindering us from progress in our power generation, transmission, and distribution segments?
body: Editor’s note: This content is sponsored by AboitizPower and was handled by BrandRap, the sales and marketing arm of Rappler. No member of the news and editorial team participated in the publishing of this piece. With high electricity prices, vulnerable infrastructure, and critical supply, it can be difficult for Filipinos to have an optimistic outlook not only for our energy industry’s future, but also even just for the present. Did you know that in the Visayas alone, there have been nearly 130 yellow and red alerts since January 2026? “Nagkakaroon tayo ng red and yellow alerts. Maraming kadahilahan. Maaaring kinapos ang supply, may mga planta na nasira, o kaya naman ay may mga planta na nasa construction nga pero na-delay din ang pasok,” said Atty. Francis Saturnino “Nino” Juan, chairperson and CEO of the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC). (We have red and yellow alerts. There are many reasons behind this. It may be from a lack of supply, broken power plants, or probably power plants that are under construction but got delayed in deployment.) Juan said this in the panel discussion “Energy for Progress: Strengthening the Vital Links of our Energy System”, where he was joined by Energy Secretary Sharon Garin and Prof. Rowaldo “Wali” Del Mundo, who is the associate dean of the College of Engineering in the University of the Philippines (UP) and the UP System’s vice president for development. Moderating them was Ruth Yu-Owen, the energy committee chairperson of the ECCP (European Chamber of Commerce). “Energy for Progress” is part of Rappler’s “Powering Up” roundtable discussion, done in partnership with Aboitiz Power Corporation and the ECCP. Critical monitoring There is a perfect fuel mix fit for the Philippines, according to Energy Secretary Garin, but notes that it is an “evolving formula” that contains a mix of renewable energy, as well as baseload (steady and more affordable, like coal) and mid-merit sources that can fill up the gaps left by variable and intermittent supply. “The technologies change faster than our policies, so we keep catching up. And now what we’ve done is do a super simulation to have some projections, get a super computer with super people from DOE and the rest of the industry so we can calculate what to expect in the next 10 years,” quipped Garin. There’s also a need to create new regulations and even revisit the Philippine Grid Code , Juan added, on account of new technologies coming into the grid. “Nakapaloob kasi din diyan ’yung [energy] reserve requirements natin, so tinitingnan kung ano na ba ’yung sufficient na reserve. Anong klase na ’yung reserve na dapat papasok? So ito ang mga sinosolusyunan natin ngayon.” (It also houses our [energy] reserve requirements, so we get to check what kind of reserve is sufficient. What kind of reserve should we integrate? So these are the things we are trying to solve right now.) Meanwhile, Del Mundo stressed the need to catch up on project delays, especially as demand for electricity continues to grow. It can be recalled that the Department of Energy has been calling out projects that failed to meet their development commitments. “Electricity supply interruptions send ripple effects to other sectors of the economy, and this ultimately leads to economic losses,” the Philippine Institute for Development Studies said. Making energy affordable In terms of alleviating the cost of power, Del Mundo also emphasized the importance of strategic procurement on the part of distribution utilities for both the short-term and the long-term, with the latter serving as more of a signal for power producers to build more future capacity. But even then, Del Mundo observed that there were long-term contracts that didn’t result in new capacity. Instead, these were crafted for existing power plants, making it uncertain that there is available capacity in the long run. Del Mundo said that there’s too much dependence on the existing power plants, suggesting the need for more alignment when it comes to procurement in the distribution sector. Empowering the innovative Filipino spirit During the first episode, Garin also highlighted Filipino innovation as a big anchor in building more energy capacity – like through agrivoltaics, or growing vegetables under solar panels, to balance out the demand of both for arable land. Some forms of makeshift solutions have also come out of the Philippines being a climate-vulnerable nation, like what Garin recalled during her visit to a location that experiences floods: The people raised the pole mount of the solar panels. The Philippines itself, as an archipelago, invites the need for innovation and exploration. “Because of this, very expensive [and weak] ang ating transmission[…] So kung ang ating power generation ay magiging embedded, ibig sabihin, distributed… Bawat island, may adequate supply[…] so yung ating interconnection ay hindi natin kailangan problemahin na, “Kailan natin i-u-pgrade [o] lalakihan?” Ibig sabihin, importanteng ma-interconnect natin para ma-hold lahat nung mga island together para sa stable na operation,” Del Mundo said. (Because of this, our transmission is very expensive and weak. So if our power generation will be embedded, meaning distributed… Each island, there’s an adequate supply, so we don’t need to stress about our interconnection in terms of, “When do we need to upgrade or expand?” This means it’s important to interconnect so the islands will be held together for a stable operation.) Improving and modernizing electric cooperatives Electric cooperatives should also be improved in terms of their capacity-building and infrastructure, Garin said. The far-flung areas served by these cooperatives shouldn’t be forgotten, the panel maintained, with Juan adding that the consumers’ best interest should always come first. For Del Mundo, an option could be combining multiple electric cooperatives into just one entity per region to produce scale and, ideally, improve overall performance and power rates. title: Russian online marketplace Ozon lost billions of rubles to Ukrainian drone strikes on its warehouses
body: Ozon estimated that drone attacks on 11 of its logistics centers cost it 30.1 billion rubles, according to the company’s financial report for the third quarter of 2026. The loss figure includes the cost of goods destroyed in the warehouses, damaged equipment, and what the report describes as “other losses and expenses.” The report says some of the company’s own risks were insured, and Ozon is continuing negotiations with insurance companies over possible compensation. Despite the losses from the strikes, Ozon’s net profit grew 25% in the third quarter, reaching 3.7 billion rubles. Revenue increased 1.6-fold to 421.2 billion rubles, and Ozon delivered 1.2 billion orders to customers over the same period, 76% more than a year earlier. Ukraine expanded its target list for strikes on Russian infrastructure in the summer of 2026, moving beyond oil refineries and defense plants to marketplace warehouses. Ukrainian drones attacked a warehouse belonging to Wildberries for the first time on July 18, and 36 of the company’s warehouse facilities came under attack over the next three months. Attacks on Ozon’s warehouses began on August 22. Ukraine’s armed forces shifted to digital infrastructure in October. From October 8–11, Ukraine carried out a series of strikes on three data centers belonging to Yandex. Ukrainian drones attacked a data processing center belonging to Sberbank on October 14, and a data center belonging to the Federal Tax Service on October 23. The strikes caused widespread disruptions to services at Yandex, Mail.ru, Ozon, MegaFon, VKontakte, and other companies.
