title: BRICS won’t be a magic wand for Ghana; corruption and irregularities in public finances pose a threat
body: The government of Ghana under President John Dramani Mahama has applied to join BRICS as a partner. The country’s Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa argues that the decision forms part of the government’s efforts to expand Ghana’s economic options and diversify its international partnerships. “The major highlight, which I am disclosing to the Ghanaian people for the first time, is that the Cabinet of President John Dramani Mahama has decided that Ghana will be joining BRICS,” he said. Ablakwa and many government officials express the view that Ghana’s membership of the bloc, which brings together major emerging economies, could provide the country with alternative economic and diplomatic partnerships. We believe that joining India in BRICS will give us economic options, will diversify our base and our partnerships, and will also allow us to have more cooperation within the Global South framework, as far as South-South engagements are concerned. This announcement by the Foreign Affairs Minister’s signalled Ghana’s intention to deepen its engagement with emerging economies as the government seeks to broaden the country’s international economic partnerships. BRICS comprises Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa and seeks to strengthen economic, political and diplomatic cooperation among its members. Therefore, partnering with BRICS may open new economic avenues for Ghana, including trade diversification, Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), and alternative development financing. Ghana already enjoys excellent relations with the BRICS member countries. Therefore, it will be joining natural allies in a bloc that arguably is the largest trading bloc today. But there are some concerns that need to be addressed. Ghana risks becoming a market for powerful BRICS economies and exposing its natural resources to further exploitation without a clear industrial strategy. While joining BRICS could expand Ghana’s trade and investment opportunities, the natural resource-rich West African country may end up benefiting less than industrial giants such as China, India, Brazil and Russia. BRICS brings together eleven major emerging markets and developing countries of the world: Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and United Arab Emirates. It will therefore serve as a useful platform for consultation and cooperation on contemporary issues having global, as well as regional significance, and issues of global political and economic governance. Concerns were also raised that this decision will affect Ghana’s relations with its traditional partner countries who have ideological differences with the BRICS member countries. However, Ghanaian authorities explain that the decision affirms Ghana’s policy of non-alignment, which enabled President Kwame Nkrumah, at the height of the Cold War, to navigate the terrain to secure the support of the United States to build the Akosombo Dam, while at the same time getting the then Soviet Union (Russia) to launch Africa’s pioneering atomic energy programme, the Ghana Nuclear Reactor Project (GNRP). Despite the optimism, the point ought to be made that joining BRICS will not be a magic wand for Ghana’s economic problems. Corruption There are several factors that will not include corruption. Corruption poses a grave threat to the stability, development, and integrity of Ghanaian society. It deprives the country of the needed development. To that end, if Ghana is to really benefit from joining BRICS, effort will have to be made to fight corruption. If expatriate investors come into the country as a result of BRICS membership, yet they are subjected to corruption practices in business registration and work permits, these businesses will eventually get frustrated and exit the country. Recently, the National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE) indicated that Ghana loses more than US$3 billion every year through corruption. According to the NCCE, the resources lost through corruption could instead be invested in infrastructure, job creation and essential services, where the demand for development remains high. This comment highlights the point that in order for BRICS membership to fully benefit Ghana, corruption will have to be addressed. It is for this reason also that the Office of the Special Prosecutor advocates the efficacy of investigations and prosecutions in curbing corruption. The OSP also recognises that transforming Ghana’s culture of corruption requires a comprehensive, large-scale prevention programme. The Office, as mandated by Section 2(c) of the Office of the Special Prosecutor Act, 2017 (Act 959), is dedicated to taking proactive measures to prevent corruption. Poor management of public finances The other threats to the benefits of BRICS are issues with irregularities in the public financial system in Ghana, as captured in the Auditor-General’s reports. Recently, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) highlighted GH₡5.2 billion in irregularities, with GH₡4.8 billion on tax infractions recorded in the 2025 audit report. The committee’s chair, Abena Osei-Asare, expressed concern about the recurrence of similar audit findings involving public institutions, and said such development gave a clear indication that MDAs were not learning their lessons. “If the same institution is cited repeatedly for the same control failure, then we are no longer dealing with just audit findings; we are dealing with a failure to learn,” she pointed out. The irregularities in the public finances have been prevalent and appear in the auditors’ general reports year in and year out. The issues seem unresolved because surcharges are unpaid. Abena Osei-Asare says a total of GH¢280.5 million in surcharges following audit reports remains unpaid. Information from the Audit Service showed that GH¢280.5 million in surcharges remained uncollected. About GH¢57.2 million had been collected through the Auditor-General’s recovery accounts since 2022, as of February 2026. Definitely, if issues in public finance management aren’t resolved, the benefits of BRICS will be an illusion to the government and the people of Ghana. Because the revenues that will accrue from the FDIs may not be properly accounted for by the state agencies. Stronger internal controls across public institutions to prevent financial irregularities and safeguard public funds will be key in ensuring the benefits of BRICS partnership are realised. Effective internal auditing was critical to ensuring that public resources were properly managed and channelled into development priorities under the government’s New Economy agenda. Geopolitical concerns Concerns are that Ghana’s attempt to join BRICS will affect Ghana’s relations with its traditional partner countries who have ideological differences with the BRICS member countries. The question is, is BRICS’s partnering status a means for a safe pragmatic stepping stone for a balanced foreign policy, diversifying the economy or just for a half-measure that lacks real decision-making power? Hence, will this move by Ghana damage its established sources of loans, grants/Aids from the Western Bloc/ International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank and access to Western Markets of the USA (especially AGOA) and the markets of the European Union for her products, which are needed by the thousands of Ghanaians, other Africans, and offspring of Africans in the Western Countries and Countries of their allies? There are also the Constitutional and Historical Questions, which Ghana needs to take note of in its attempt to join BRICS. Ghana needs to take note of Article 40 of the 1992 Constitution, which guides Ghana’s foreign policy to promote and protect national interests and Ghana’s historical non-alignment policy, which saw President Kwame Nkrumah’s historical playbook of non-alignment by balancing ties with the Western Bloc and the Eastern Bloc, which saw Ghana obtaining financial and technical support from the West, especially the USA, for projects like the Akosombo Dam and its early nuclear cooperation with the East. So, the real litmus test is: when Ghana is granted the Partner Status, can Ghana use the platform of the BRICS to transform its raw exports into localised industrial capacity without burning bridges with traditional Western financiers. About BRICS BRICS is an international organisation currently comprising ten countries: Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates. Its conceptual origins were articulated by Russian foreign minister Yevgeny Primakov in 1998, and can be traced to informal forums and dialogue groups such as RIC (Russia, India, and China) and IBSA (India, Brazil, and South Africa). BRIC was originally a term coined by British economist Jim O’Neill, and later championed by his employer Goldman Sachs in 2001, to designate a group of emerging markets. The bloc’s inaugural summit was held in 2009 and featured the founding countries of Brazil, Russia, India, and China; they adopted the acronym BRIC and formed an informal diplomatic group where their governments could meet annually at formal summits and coordinate multilateral policies. South Africa joined the organisation in September 2010, which was then renamed BRICS, and attended the third summit in 2011 as a full member. Iran, Egypt, Ethiopia, and the United Arab Emirates attended their first summit as member states in 2024 in Russia. Indonesia officially joined in early 2025, becoming the first Southeast Asian member. Saudi Arabia was invited to the Johannesburg summit, and it is considered part of the organisation, but has not publicly confirmed its membership. The term BRICS+ has been informally used to reflect new membership since 2024. Collectively, BRICS comprises more than a quarter of the global economy and nearly half the world’s population.

title: Zelensky pushes back against Musk, says Ukraine uses Starshield to defend itself
body:
Ukraine has used SpaceX's Starshield satellite systems only to defend itself against Russian forces on its own territory, not for attacks on Russian soil, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Oct. 27.
The comments come as a rebuff of SpaceX founder Elon Musk , who claimed Ukraine 's "military violated Starlink terms of service" by using the systems for offensive drone attacks.
Ukraine widely uses both commercial Starlink terminals and their militarized version, Starshield.
Starshield was temporarily speed-restricted to 160 kilometers per hour in Ukraine earlier this month, hampering Ukrainian drone interceptors' ability to down Russian jet-powered drones and disrupting other military operations.
"When Elon Musk said that we use Starshield against the Russians — yes, against the Russians, but on our own territory. This is not offensive; it's defensive," Zelensky told journalists at a press briefing.
"But the point is that we use it against Russian troops on our territory, not on Russian territory. They came here to kill," he said.
Musk alleged that Kyiv used commercial Starlink terminals for "offensive drone strikes to kill people," adding that the "loophole" has now been closed. However, he rejected responsibility for Starshield restrictions, saying the militarized terminals are controlled by the U.S. government.
Ukrainian officials have previously rejected Musk's claims about Kyiv violating Starlink's service terms. Presidential adviser Serhii "Flash" Beskrestnov said that the commercial Starlink has a speed restriction of 70-90 kilometers per hour and does not work on Russian territory.
Zelensky confirmed on Oct. 24 that both Starlink and Starshield are again working at full speed. Nobody has publicly claimed responsibility for the throttling of Starshield, though Trump administration officials have pointed fingers at Musk.
"Of course, civilians died while Starlink/Starshield were switched off," Zelensky said. "We're now shooting down about 90% of (Shahed-type drones). When the (latest wave of) attacks began, we were shooting down between 50% and 75–78%. Then that rate dropped back again."
The president revealed that Ukraine was just successfully testing its jet-powered Bars drone interceptors — 2,000 units of which were paid for by a European country — when the restrictions hit.
"So I really don't know who told SpaceX to do that," Zelensky said, suggesting it could either be Musk's personal decision or an instruction by a U.S. official. "I only know that, technically, SpaceX turns these systems on and off."
The Wall Street Journal reported on Oct. 23 that Trump had ordered the SpaceX CEO to lift the restrictions, while the U.S. president publicly claimed he had not spoken to Musk about the issue but might do so if the problems persisted.
The restrictions came amid deteriorating ties between the U.S. and Ukraine, with Trump easing sanctions pressure on Moscow while accusing Zelensky of not being interested in peace — despite Kyiv repeatedly backing various U.S.-backed ceasefire proposals, which were turned down by Russia.

title: Russia ready to establish joint ventures with Africa for fertilizer packaging — RAPU
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Russia is ready to expand its fertilizer supply footprint in Africa, establish joint ventures for fertilizer packaging and bagging, and share expertise in raw material extraction and processing, announced Andrey Guryev, head of the Russian Fertilizer Producers Association (RAPU).
According to Guryev, Russian products are currently available in 25 African countries. "We are ready to discuss terms for mutually beneficial cooperation with companies from the remaining 30 nations," he stated at the Russia-Africa Forum.
"The second area of cooperation is the creation of fertilizer bagging and packaging enterprises. Currently, most of our products are shipped in bulk. Packaging them into consumer containers will enable retail distribution," Guryev added. The third avenue of cooperation is scientific and technical. "We are ready to share our experience in the extraction and processing of mineral raw materials with African producers," the RAPU head said.
He added that Russia also aims to help train qualified personnel for Africa’s agricultural sector.
TASS is an official media partner of the third Russia-Africa Summit and the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.

title: If Canada picks the Gripen fighter, these local firms would help Saab deliver the jets
body: VICTORIA, British Columbia — Saab will collaborate with several of Canada’s top aerospace firms to build the Gripen fighter jet in Canada if the aircraft is selected by the Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government. Saab confirmed Oct. 27 that it has formed alliances with several firms to build, deliver and support the Gripen E advanced multi-role fighter, should the Canadian government purchase the plane. Canada had already committed to buying 88 Lockheed Martin F-35s but that is under review after U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to economically cripple the country and suggested it could be annexed to be the 51 st state. At this point Canada has paid for 16 F-35s. Two of the aircraft were transferred to Canada on Oct. 9 and Oct. 22, said Department of National Defence spokeswoman Andrée-Anne Poulin. Canadian Prime Minister Carney will decide whether the rest of the F-35s will be purchased but he has not indicated when he would announce his decision. In the meantime, the Canadian government is examining whether it should purchase the Gripen E, either as an alternative to the F-35 or to complement the U.S. fighter jets. Saab has responded by forming a teaming arrangement with Canadian firms CAE of Montreal, Quebec; IMP of Halifax, Nova Scotia; and Magellan Aerospace of Mississauga, Ontario. “Together with CAE, IMP and Magellan Aerospace we are prepared to establish a strong Canadian industrial ecosystem around Gripen that delivers operational effect, national sovereignty and lasting industrial and technological benefits,” Micael Johansson, President and CEO of Saab, said in a statement Oct. 27. Saab noted it has signed a teaming agreement with IMP to establish a new final assembly line, for the Gripen fighter in Canada, if Canada decides to acquire the aircraft. IMP will also be responsible for electrical assembly production and in-service support for Canada’s Gripens. Saab has also signed a new Memorandum of Understanding with Magellan Aerospace to provide local manufacturing of advanced aerostructures, composite structures and structural assemblies in Canada — again, if Canada decides to acquire the aircraft. Saab has previously signed a Memorandum of Understanding with CAE to deliver advanced fighter pilot and technician training, mission systems engineering and support/sustainment capabilities in Canada. Saab has already made significant inroads into the Canadian market. Carney announced May 27 that Canada will purchase six GlobalEye early warning and control aircraft from Saab as part of deal to not only boost Canadian military capabilities but energize domestic defense production. Carney said the proposed GlobalEye purchase is estimated to cost more than $5 billion CAN ($3.6 billion). GlobalEye is based on a Bombardier 6500 executive jet, an aircraft that is manufactured in Toronto. Carney said that at least one-third of the projected GlobalEye aircraft orders for various allies will be built in Canada. That is expected to be 40 aircraft over the next 15 years. On Sept. 25 the Canadian government announced it had worked out an agreement with Saab that will provide the framework for upcoming negotiations on the purchase of the six GlobalEyes. In announcing the agreement, Stephen Fuhr, Secretary of State for Defence Procurement, said Canada will be focusing on pursuing a partnership that supports “Canadian jobs, innovation, and long-term economic growth while ensuring we acquire capabilities from trusted partners when they are needed.”

title: Four die; seven injured in Lagos accidents
body: Four persons died and seven others sustained injuries in three separate road accidents in Lagos on Wednesday, the Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) has said. The ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌‌⁠​​‍​​‌​agency said the fatal accident occurred at Berger Bridge, inward Eleko, along the Ibeju-Lekki Expressway, involving an articulated truck conveying a 20-foot container and an interstate Toyota Hiace bus. LASEMA’s Permanent Secretary, Dr Olufemi Oke-Osanyintolu, confirmed the incidents in a statement made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Wednesday in Lagos. Oke-Osanyintolu said the agency received a distress call and immediately activated its response team from Epe Base to the scene. According to him, preliminary investigations revealed that the truck was ascending the bridge at excessive speed when it collided with the bus. He said the truck driver lost control while attempting to avoid the collision, causing the truck to overturn onto the bus. Oke-Osanyintolu said four adult males died at the scene, while six other adult males sustained varying degrees of injuries. He said LASEMA, alongside the Federal Road Safety Corps and the Nigeria Police Force, secured the scene and administered first aid to the injured. He said the injured persons were subsequently conveyed to Epe General Hospital for further medical attention, he said. Oke-Osanyintolu added that a private crane had been secured to recover the overturned truck and container and facilitate the safe extrication of the deceased. He said the recovery operation was ongoing, with traffic management measures deployed to ensure safety along the corridor. In a related development, he said LASEMA’s Tiger Team from C3 Base responded to a truck accident at about 4:09 a.m. near Vetland School, inward Agege Pen Cinema, along Old Abeokuta Road. He said the truck, with registration number KTU-940XT, rammed into a solar-powered streetlight pole before mounting the road median and obstructing traffic. He said that preliminary findings attributed the incident to reckless driving, although no casualty was recorded. Oke-Osanyintolu said the agency deployed traffic diversion measures and later recovered the truck using its heavy-duty equipment, Elephant. He said the truck was conveyed to Abattoir Police Station for further investigation and safekeeping. The permanent secretary also said LASEMA’s Beta Team from Igando Base responded to another accident at Lanre Bus Stop, inward Igando, along LASU-Igando Road. He said the accident involved a DAF truck, with registration number SMK 795 XY, and a Toyota Corolla, with registration number AKD 169 EA. According to him, a broken-down truck on the opposite side of the road had caused traffic congestion when the DAF truck, allegedly driving against traffic, collided with the Corolla. He said the collision obstructed half of the road inward in Igando, while the Corolla driver sustained a minor head injury. “The injured driver was taken to Igando General Hospital by an associate,” Oke-Osanyintolu said. He added that the Corolla had been towed to Igando Police Station, while LASEMA deployed its heavy-duty equipment, Super Metro, to recover the DAF truck and restore traffic flow. Oke-Osanyintolu said the recovery operation was ongoing. He urged motorists to observe speed limits, avoid driving against traffic and reckless manoeuvres, and ensure their vehicles were mechanically sound before embarking on any journey. He also advised residents to report emergencies through the state’s toll-free lines, 767 and 112. The permanent secretary commiserated with the families of the deceased and wished the injured persons a speedy recovery. (NAN) The post Four die; seven injured in Lagos accidents appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: IN BRIEF: Netanyahu’s future at stake as Israel votes amid high Arab turnout
body:
TEL AVIV, October 28. /TASS/. Israel’s Likud party, led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, is holding on to its lead in the October 27 parliamentary elections, with 57.3% of the vote counted, according to data released by the Central Elections Committee.
The Yashar party of Netanyahu’s main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, is in second place.
The Central Elections Committee is expected to announce preliminary results on October 29, with the final election outcome to be officially published no later than November 4.
TASS has compiled key details available so far.
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party is holding on to its lead in the elections, with 57.3% of the vote counted, according to data released by the Central Elections Committee.
- According to this data, Netanyahu’s party is projected to win 28 seats in the 120-seat parliament.
- His main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar opposition party, is in second place with 21 seats.
- Meanwhile, Netanyahu’s bloc of parties is currently projected to win a total of 55 seats, while the opposition is expected to secure 49.
- Arab parties are projected to win 16 seats, although neither Likud nor the opposition is prepared to form a coalition with them.
- According to exit polls, the Beyachad (Together) bloc, led by former prime ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid, ranks third with 14 seats.
- The center-left Democrats, led by Yair Golan, and the Arab Joint List, led by Yousef Jabareen, are expected to win ten seats each.
- Avigdor Lieberman’s party, Our Home Israel, which focuses on the interests of Israel's Russian-speaking community, is projected to win eight seats.
- The United Arab List (Ra’am), led by Mansour Abbas, and the far-right party Otzma Yehudit (Jewish Power), led by Itamar Ben-Gvir, are projected to receive seven seats each.
- The ultra-Orthodox parties Shas and United Torah Judaism, along with the far-right bloc comprising the Religious Zionist Party and Zehut, are each expected to win six seats.
- Other political forces are not expected to surpass the 3.25% electoral threshold.
- A total of 36 parties and alliances participated in the elections.
- A governing majority requires 61 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, but, according to exit polls, no political force is expected to reach that number.
- Parliamentary elections in Israel are held under a party-list system.
- A total of 7.3 mln Israeli citizens are eligible to vote.
- Voter turnout in the elections to the 26th Knesset was 77.7%, the highest level since 1999, Israel’s Channel 12 reported.
- United Arab List leader Mansour Abbas said that turnout in Arab-populated areas had reached 80%.
- He stressed that Arab voters had been more active than other voters.
- The Central Elections Committee is expected to announce preliminary results on October 29, with the final election outcome to be officially published no later than November 4.
- Once the final results are announced, President Isaac Herzog will begin consultations with representatives of the parties that have won seats in the Knesset before asking one of them to form a new government coalition.
- According to Amjad Shbeita, coordinator of the Joint List coalition of Arab parties, left-wing and democratic forces have a strong chance of unseating Benjamin Netanyahu’s government.
- Netanyahu previously claimed that opposition parties were trying "to steal the elections" from his bloc.
- Posts urging supporters to turn out in greater numbers appeared on Netanyahu’s X account approximately three times an hour, along with allegations that Arab parties were transporting thousands of their supporters to polling stations to secure more votes.
- As a rule, the leader of the party that wins the most seats in parliament becomes a candidate for the post of prime minister.
- However, the president may also task a politician whose party did not win the most seats with forming a cabinet, provided the party has a chance of forming a coalition.
- The first candidate for prime minister will have 28 days to form a government, with the possibility of a two-week extension.
- If the candidate fails, the president will assign the task to another lawmaker, who will have two weeks to form a cabinet, with no option for an extension.
- If no government can be formed with the support of at least 61 members of parliament, a new election will be called within 90 days.

title: Caleb International School Wins Bank’s N5m Young Innovation Challenge
body: James Sowole in Abeokuta Caleb British International School (CBIS), Abijo, Lagos, has officially emerged as the national champion at the Zenith Bank Future Innovators Challenge. The school was represented by a team of senior secondary students comrising Deborah Iweha, Makayla Inyere, Fife Alonge, and Okeke Janelle. The Caleb team defeated finalists from across Nigeria to secure the coveted first-place position at Zecathon 6.0. The team carted home the grand prize of Five Million Naira (₦5,000,000) for their groundbreaking project, ReLearn. The Future Innovators Challenge is Zenith Bank’s premier innovation contest dedicated to senior secondary schools. Run in partnership with Beyond Limits as part of the broader Zecathon 6.0 2026 innovation programme, the initiative provides African students early exposure to teamwork, problem-solving, and technology, offering a combined ₦10 million prize pool for the top three schools. The CBIS quartet impressed the national panel of judges with ReLearn, a student-built digital platform designed to give unused textbooks a second life. Developed after the team conducted independent research with parents, ReLearn targets the high cost of educational materials. Instead of allowing old textbooks to sit idle in homes after an academic session, the platform seamlessly redistributes them to students in need. Team member Deborah Iweha explained, “The platform helps families save money and ensures no child goes to school without the right set of books.” Adding to this, Fife Alonge noted that ReLearn actively bridges educational gaps by allowing children in underserved communities to access quality learning materials at a fraction of the market price. The project directly aligns with three United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): Quality Education (SDG 4), Reduced Inequalities (SDG 10), and Responsible Consumption (SDG 12). With the ₦5,000,000 prize money, the victorious team plans to scale the platform beyond CBIS to put thousands more textbooks into the hands of Nigerian students. The Director of the Caleb Group of Schools, Dr. Oladega Adebogun, expressed immense joy and pride in the students’ historic triumph, describing them as worthy ambassadors of the Caleb brand—which prioritizes excellent academic performance richly spiced with high moral tone. “This national success is a firm validation of our huge investment in modern, state-of-the-art ICT learning hubs, tech innovation labs, and world-class audiovisual laboratories,” Dr. Adebogun stated. He added that the feat is no surprise, as the Caleb Group of Schools—spanning Lekki, Magodo, and the Lagos Mainland—has consistently established itself as a citadel of academic excellence and a nurturing ground for tomorrow’s entrepreneurs. He further extended his deepest gratitude to the parents, management, and staff, emphasizing that the win was a collective triumph for the entire school community. This victory marks yet another milestone in a phenomenal year for the institution. Caleb Group of Schools recently produced best-in-the-world students at the British Council Recognition and Outstanding Learner Awards (BROCLA) 2026, where Akota-Chika Serena (CBIS Magodo) emerged Best-in-the-World in IGCSE English, and Adekimi Tolulope Israel (CBIS Lekki) secured Best-in-the-World in IGCSE Mathematics. The winning team expressed their profound gratitude to the school’s leadership, including Director Dr. Oladega Adebogun; Head of School, Ms. Colette O’Hehir; Principal, Mr. Kasimu Rabiu; and Deputy Principal, Mr. Oluwabunkumi Ogbowa. The students were heavily supported and coached by the mentors of the Caleb British International School Young Entrepreneurs Club, including Club Coordinator Mr. Israel Adewuyi, Mr. Gbadebo Clement, Mr. Adedayo Olaoluwa, Miss Uche Okeke, and Miss Awodiya Dorcas, alongside the school’s Head of Competition, Mr. Awoyemi Samuel.

title: Brent crude price tops $116 per barrel for 2nd time in Oct.
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 28 (MNA) – Brent crude oil prices has exceeded $116 per barrel for the second time in October amid the global economic impact of the US-Israeli imposed war on Iran.
Back on Oct. 23, oil prices continued to rise to above $114 bpd amid persistent concerns over disruptions to global energy markets as a result of continued US and Zionist regime aggression on Iran.
Brent crude briefly climbed to $114 a barrel. Around five months ago, in mid-May, the benchmark had risen above $114 and reached $112 a few days later. It had not returned to these price levels since then.

title: Tokayev Urges Higher Taxes on Wealthy, Calls on Banks to Boost Business Lending
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA – Kazakhstan should consider raising taxes on wealthy individuals, revise parts of its new Tax Code to address business concerns, and encourage banks to provide more long-term loans to businesses, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev said in his annual state-of-the-nation address on Oct. 28. Photo credit: Akorda. Tokayev outlined priorities for macroeconomic policy, including fighting inflation, improving public spending and increasing investment in the real economy. He stressed that economic policy should ultimately be measured by its impact on people’s prosperity and economic activity. “Our main goal is therefore to increase household incomes. To achieve this, we must first systematically combat inflation,” he said, describing inflation as “a silent enemy that steadily undermines the well-being of our citizens.” He called on the government and the National Bank to coordinate efforts to contain and reduce inflation, pursue balanced fiscal and tax policy, and create conditions for stronger production capacity and higher business productivity. Higher tax rate for wealthy individuals Tokayev also called for a discussion on introducing a higher tax rate for individuals with substantial wealth, framing the proposal as a matter of fairness rather than a restriction on private property. “I believe the time has come to discuss introducing a higher rate for those with substantial wealth,” he said. He stressed that the proposal would not involve restricting legally acquired assets, which he said would contradict the Constitution. Instead, he stressed that citizens should make a fair contribution to the country’s development in proportion to their means. “This is about a proportionate and fair contribution by every citizen to the development of our country. This is about fairness,” Tokayev said. The government and the Kurultai, Kazakhstan’s national legislature, are to examine the proposal and submit recommendations. The president also linked fair taxation to transparency and digitalization. He called for advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence, to improve tax collection, reduce the shadow economy and lower corruption risks. Banks urged to finance the real economy Tokayev said Kazakhstan’s financial system remained resilient, with bank assets exceeding 75 trillion tenge (US$164.6 billion) and deposits reaching a record 52 trillion tenge (US$114.1 billion). About 78% of deposits are held in the national currency, which he cited as evidence of the tenge’s growing value. The next priority, he said, is to channel these accumulated financial resources into the real economy. “The most important task now is to direct accumulated financial resources toward the development of the real sector of the economy,” Tokayev said. He called on the National Bank to play a more active role in initiatives supporting economic development while continuing to safeguard price and financial stability. President Tokayev also urged commercial banks to increase investment lending to businesses, describing it as their core responsibility. According to him, Kazakhstan’s demand for long-term financing exceeds the capacity of the state budget and development institutions. “Banks must take the most active part in investment lending to businesses. This is their main mission,” Tokayev said. He called for regulatory conditions that would encourage lending, including more effective management of excess liquidity in the banking system. He also proposed new mechanisms for long-term financing of key economic sectors involving banks, development institutions, international financial organizations and the Unified Accumulative Pension Fund. According to him, the forthcoming Capital Market Law should provide concrete mechanisms to mobilize additional financing and strengthen investment discipline. AI to help improve public spending Tokayev identified better budget management as another priority for long-term macroeconomic stability. The Budget Code adopted last year has improved the management of public funds and strengthened financial discipline, he said. However, government expenditure continues to grow, making better budget planning and oversight increasingly important. He proposed using artificial intelligence to identify unjustified or inefficient spending and called for the full digitalization of the state treasury system. The government should establish an automated system for managing public funds based on unified methods and standards, Tokayev said, adding that he expects concrete proposals from the government and the National Bank. Targeted changes to Tax Code Tokayev said Kazakhstan’s new Tax Code laid the foundation for a comprehensive overhaul of the tax system but acknowledged that implementing it created difficulties for businesses. Large-scale reforms inevitably reveal problems that are difficult to anticipate during drafting, he said, noting that companies were struggling to apply certain provisions. “The Tax Code is not dogma, nor is it sacred scripture, and it must not be detached from reality,” Tokayev said. “Our legislation has become so cumbersome and difficult to understand that it has turned into a real headache for entrepreneurs,” he added. He instructed the government to address contradictions, eliminate ambiguous interpretations and remove disproportionate burdens on entrepreneurs. Tokayev emphasized that the government must carefully consider the changes to avoid repeatedly changing the rules for entrepreneurs. The post Tokayev Urges Higher Taxes on Wealthy, Calls on Banks to Boost Business Lending appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: New Awujale Will Emerge Before May 2027, Says Dapo Abiodun
body: The Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has reassured the people of Ijebuland that a new Awujale will emerge before May 29, 2027, while projecting a major economic transformation for Ogun East Senatorial District through emerging oil exploration activities and the proposed Gateway Deep-Sea Port. The governor gave the assurances on Tuesday at the Ogun East Senatorial District stakeholders’ meeting in Ijebu-Ode, where he engaged representatives of various interest groups on traditional affairs, governance and the economic prospects of the district. On the succession process for the revered Awujale stool, the governor assured the people that his administration was committed to facilitating a smooth, peaceful and widely acceptable process leading to the emergence of a new monarch. He acknowledges the importance of the Awujale institution to the cultural heritage, identity and unity of Ijebuland, appealing to the people to remain calm and patient as the necessary processes were being concluded. The governor said his administration was giving the matter the attention it deserves, with a view to ensuring that the process was concluded peacefully and that the emergence of a new Awujale enjoys the acceptance and support of the people. He commended the people of Ijebuland for their continued support and cooperation with his administration, assuring them of his commitment to addressing issues of importance to the district and preserving peace and harmony across the state. He explained that the stakeholders’ meeting was organised to strengthen engagement between the government and the people, provide an opportunity for various groups to express their views and showcase the achievements of his administration over the past seven years. Turning to the economic prospects of Ogun East, the governor declared that the district was on the threshold of significant economic expansion, driven by emerging oil exploration activities and the proposed Gateway Deep-Sea Port in Ogun Waterside Local Government Area. He identified the discovery of crude oil around Eba Island and the deep-sea port project as strategic developments capable of transforming the economic landscape of the district, attracting fresh investments and creating employment opportunities for residents. The governor said the projects, alongside the proposed Blue Marine Special Economic Zone, would strengthen Ogun State’s position as a major destination for industrial investment, international trade and maritime business. “The Gateway Deep-Sea Port is expected to open new opportunities in shipping, logistics, manufacturing and related industries, while the associated industrial development is projected to stimulate economic activities across Ogun East and other parts of the state,” he said. Abiodun expressed optimism that the emerging investments would enhance the district’s commercial importance, expand opportunities for local businesses and create jobs for young people, while strengthening Ogun State’s contribution to Nigeria’s economic growth. He reiterated his administration’s commitment to infrastructure development, investment promotion and policies designed to improve the living conditions of residents, stressing the importance of cooperation among government institutions, traditional rulers, communities and the private sector in realising the state’s development aspirations. The governor also acknowledged the Federal Government’s support for critical infrastructure and development initiatives in Ogun State, expressing appreciation for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s cooperation with his administration. He called for continued collaboration between the state and federal governments, noting that such partnerships were important to advancing major projects and unlocking the economic potential of Ogun State. Representatives of various groups at the meeting, including market men and women, hunters, members of the Council of Baales and Olorituns, commended the governor for engaging grassroots stakeholders and providing a platform for them to discuss issues affecting their communities. They described the meeting as an opportunity to strengthen communication between the government and the people, noting that direct engagement was important to understanding local concerns and advancing development at the grassroots. The representatives also expressed support for the administration’s development initiatives and pledged to mobilise their members and supporters for the All Progressives Congress (APC) and its candidates in the forthcoming general elections. The post New Awujale Will Emerge Before May 2027, Says Dapo Abiodun appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Zelensky Wants Abu Dhabi Talks Before ‘New Yalta,’ Warns NATO Against Russian Demands
body:
Ukraine wants to meet with US and Russian delegations in Abu Dhabi before any proposed talks between Washington, Moscow and Beijing, President Volodymyr Zelensky said, warning that Russia could use renewed peace negotiations to seek concessions on NATO’s military presence in Europe.
Speaking to journalists on Monday , Zelensky said the agenda for a potential US-China-Russia meeting remained unclear but would likely include the Middle East and Russia’s war against Ukraine, RBC-Ukraine reported .
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“I really don’t want this to be ‘Yalta 2, 3, 4,’ when influence is being redistributed,” Zelensky said, referring to the 1945 Yalta Conference, where the leaders of the Soviet Union, United States and United Kingdom discussed the postwar order in Europe.
He argued that today’s fragmented, technologically advanced world was fundamentally different from the one that emerged after World War II, making a similar redistribution of power impossible.
“After Alaska, this would be Russia’s second major diplomatic advantage if things unfold as the Russians are currently suggesting, with their talk of a new ‘Yalta.’ I think Russia wants it more than anyone else,” Zelensky said.
He added that China had the least to gain from such a meeting.
“We would very much like our meeting in Abu Dhabi to take place before that,” he said.
Zelensky also warned NATO against accepting Russian demands to roll back the alliance’s military presence to its 1997 configuration while Moscow continues its war against Ukraine.
His remarks follow an Oct. 25 report by The Telegraph , which cited diplomatic sources as saying Moscow could use renewed peace talks to secure concessions on NATO enlargement and military deployments near Russia’s borders.
According to the report, a potential Russian demand could involve withdrawing NATO forces from Poland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania and Finland, all of which border Russia.
The reported demand has not been confirmed as an official Russian negotiating position, and there is no indication that a NATO rollback has formally been added to the talks’ agenda.
The Kremlin has nevertheless signaled that it wants a broader discussion of European security. Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Oct. 22 that future negotiations should address security guarantees for both Russia and Ukraine, as well as the “architecture of European security as a whole.”
Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov has also argued that European countries should be involved in negotiations to end the war.
Zelensky said on Monday, Oct. 27 , that Moscow’s security demands went beyond preventing Ukrainian attacks and amounted to an attempt to secure a separate agreement with NATO or the United States.
“They say: ‘If you want security guarantees for Ukraine, then we want them for Russia.’ We need to understand what Russia means by this. It is not simply about Ukraine refraining from striking Russia. For them, this is a much broader and more specific issue,” he said.
The president said discussions about broad security guarantees for Russia should wait until the terms for ending the war and Ukraine’s own security arrangements were clear.
“First, we need to resolve the issues related to this war, and only then seek answers to the questions Russia raises based on its own perceptions and expectations of security,” Zelensky said.
Russia’s push to change NATO’s military posture in Europe predates its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
In December 2021, Moscow presented the United States and NATO with draft security agreements that sought to halt further alliance enlargement, including Ukraine’s potential accession, and restrict military deployments in countries that joined NATO after May 1997.
NATO rejected Russia’s attempt to restrict its open-door policy, while saying it remained willing to discuss arms control and other security issues.
A return to NATO’s 1997 military configuration could have significant implications for the alliance’s eastern flank. Poland joined NATO in 1999, the Baltic states joined in 2004, and Finland became a member in 2023 following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Zelensky said Russia’s renewed demands could reshape the wider European security architecture. He suggested Moscow had raised similar issues in talks with then-US President Joe Biden before launching its full-scale invasion in February 2022.
He argued that NATO members should determine the alliance’s military posture themselves, without negotiating those arrangements with Russia, which is not a member.
“Any retreat, any rollback of security, is a weakness for the alliance,” he said.
The diplomatic maneuvering comes as Ukraine, Russia and the United States prepare to resume technical-level negotiations after a lengthy pause.
On Oct. 23 , Zelensky said the next round of talks was expected in the first half of November, with Abu Dhabi among the possible venues.
On Oct. 25 , Ushakov said Moscow was ready to resume negotiations after Russia’s Nov. 4 National Unity Day holiday, describing the next meeting as preliminary and exploratory.
The format and participants remain unsettled, including whether European representatives will take part in a broader discussion of continental security.
Kyiv has insisted that any settlement must include credible security guarantees for Ukraine and prevent Russia from using a pause in hostilities to prepare for another attack.

title: Most of Britan’s nuclear missile submarine fleet now at sea
body: Three of the Royal Navy’s four Vanguard class ballistic missile submarines are at sea at the same time, an arrangement naval sources described as unusual, according to reporting in The Times. One of the boats is understood to be conducting the deterrent patrol, carrying Trident II D5 missiles, which is the task the Royal Navy has maintained without a break since 1969. The other two are believed to have been on sea trials and preparing to take over the patrol. HMS Victorious, the fourth boat, is at Devonport undergoing maintenance and was not among those at sea. The Ministry of Defence declined to comment. Having three boats out at once is not a sign of extra capacity, though, as the Vanguard class was designed around a four boat cycle in which one submarine is on patrol, one is working up or recovering, one is in training or trials, and one is in deep maintenance, and the fourth hull is what keeps continuous at sea deterrence going as the submarines age. Running three at sea at the same time means the cycle has been compressed, and it is as consistent with pressure on availability as it is with a deliberate signal. The Times was told by a former senior naval source that the service had been operating in what submariners call 2BA, or two boat availability, for a prolonged period. In that condition only two of the four boats are available for operational tasking at any time, which leaves no margin, because a defect on the boat at sea has to be covered by a single relief. The strain is visible in how long the boats are staying out, Navy Lookout reported in March 2025 that a Vanguard class submarine had returned to the Clyde after 204 days , breaking a record set in 2023, and patrols of more than two hundred days have since been reported again. Deterrent patrols were historically planned around three months. Crews now routinely spend five months or more submerged with no contact with their families. Forces News reported last week, in an account of life aboard the boats , that Commander Roger Ireland, a retired submariner who served on the earlier Resolution class, described the length of modern Vanguard patrols as horrendous. Resolution boats carrying Polaris went out for around eight weeks at a time. Maintenance has been the other great difficulty, and HMS Vanguard emerged from a refit at Devonport in 2023 that took around seven and a half years against a planned three and a half, after an unscheduled nuclear refuelling pushed the cost from roughly £200 million towards £500 million, as this publication reported when she sailed . The four Vanguards entered service between 1993 and 1999 and were designed for around twenty five years each. All four are now beyond that, and they must hold the deterrent until the Dreadnought class arrives from the early 2030s. The Defence Investment Plan commits £63 billion over four years to the nuclear enterprise, covering Dreadnought, SSN-AUKUS attack submarines, a new sovereign warhead and the infrastructure behind them. The post Most of Britan’s nuclear missile submarine fleet now at sea first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: India – Indonesia Joint Special Forces Exercise
body:
New Delhi, Oct 27, 2026. The 11th edition of the India-Indonesia Joint Special Forces Exercise GARUDA SHAKTI has commenced at Banyuwangi, Indonesia. The exercise is being conducted from Oct 27 to Nov 6, 2026. The Indian contingent comprises troops from the Parachute Regiment (Special Forces), while the Indonesian contingent comprises personnel from the Indonesian Special Forces.



The exercise aims to strengthen mutual understanding, cooperation and interoperability between the Special Forces of the two nations. The training focuses on tactics, techniques and procedures for special operations in jungle environments, including obstacle crossing, combat marksmanship, mountaineering, air assault training and combat-hardening sessions. It also includes the exchange of expertise and information on weapons, equipment and operational practices.

The joint training will culminate with a validation exercise designed to simulate realistic operational scenarios and assess the endurance, coordination and combat readiness of both contingents.

The exercise will further strengthen defence cooperation and bilateral relations between India and Indonesia.

title: Japan seeks to develop nuclear capability — China Arms Control and Disarmament Association
body:
BEIJING, October 28. /TASS/. Japan is seeking to develop a nuclear capability, according to Dai Huaicheng, Secretary-General of the China Arms Control and Disarmament Association (CACDA).
"Since the current Japanese government took office, the country's right-wing forces have clearly demonstrated their ambitions to revive militarism, violate the 'three non-nuclear principles,' and pursue the creation of an indigenous nuclear arsenal - rapidly accelerating their progress along this misguided path. These statements are by no means isolated incidents; rather, they represent long-conceived, dangerous 'probing' steps that are part of a pre-planned strategy to 'gradually loosen restrictions in the nuclear sphere'," he stated.
Dai also noted that Japan’s current cabinet denies the country’s history of aggression during World War II, seeks to "whitewash the war crimes that were committed," and is actively pursuing remilitarization - all of which, he warned, "poses a serious threat to peace and stability in the region."
"As a non-nuclear-weapon state party to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons, Japan is bound under international law not to acquire, develop, possess, or proliferate nuclear weapons. There is no room for negotiation on this matter," Dai concluded.
Japan adheres to the Three Non-Nuclear Principles: not to possess, produce, or permit the introduction of nuclear weapons into its territory. Although these principles are not legally binding, successive Japanese prime ministers have reaffirmed their commitment to them. For decades, even discussing a possible revision was considered taboo. Some politicians have referred to an unwritten "fourth principle" - the prohibition on discussing the issue - and called for at least this constraint to be lifted.
Following Sanae Takaichi’s appointment as prime minister, media reports indicated that a review of Japan’s national security strategy would include discussions of the Three Non-Nuclear Principles. In particular, Takaichi was reported to be prepared to advocate lifting the ban on the introduction of US nuclear weapons into Japan.
Amid the reports, however, Takaichi stated that she had not instructed officials to revise the Three Non-Nuclear Principles as part of the deliberations on the updated national security strategy.

title: Sheikh Khaled holds talks with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney as economic partnership confirmed
body: Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed , Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, held high-level talks in Canada with Prime Minister Mark Carney as a major economic partnership between the nations was confirmed. The two men were on hand as the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (Cepa) was signed by Dr Thani al Zeyoudi, Minister of Foreign Trade and Maninder Sidhu, Canada’s Minister of International Trade. Sheikh Khaled said the Cepa - which was finalised in July - underlined the strength of bilateral relations and pledged that the UAE would continue to work with Canada to encourage private sector growth and innovation. The Cepa will seek to reduce trade barriers to goods, services and investment and will give Canadian companies better access to the UAE, which remains the largest market for Canada's exports to the Middle East, and could help attract capital into energy, mining, artificial intelligence and ports. It follows a $50 billion investment commitment made by the UAE government as part of Mr Carney's visit to the country in November. Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed - who concluded his visit on Wednesday - and Mr Carney had earlier held high-level talks in Ottawa as key deals were struck to bolster strategic ties across defence, diplomacy and renewable energy. The two countries set out plans to spur further collaboration in mining, logistics, energy and investment through sovereign wealth funds, Abu Dhabi Media Office reported on Wednesday. Emirati and Canadian companies have also come together to drive C$21.1 billion (US$15 billion) in trade under a major investment framework between the nations. Sheikh Khaled and Mr Carney explored efforts aimed at boosting long-standing relations during a meeting at Parliament Hill in Ottawa. The discussions - held as part of Sheikh Khaled's official visit to Canada - focused on efforts to bolster links in key sectors such as artificial intelligence, aviation, food security, infrastructure and logistics. The Abu Dhabi Crown Prince emphasised the UAE's commitment to establishing long-term partnerships with Canada in support of the development plans of the allies. The two sides assessed ways to advance co-operation between their business communities and encourage joint projects and investment. Sheikh Khaled and Mr Carney also exchanged views on a range of international and regional issues, stressing the need to encourage dialogue and diplomatic solutions to bring about peace and security both regionally and across the globe. Sheikh Khaled signed the Distinguished Visitors Book at Parliament Hill, expressing his pride in UAE-Canada relations and his hope that the trip would open up new opportunities. He also met with a number of young Emiratis studying in Canada and urged them to seize the opportunities for learning, research and training being made available to them. Sheikh Khaled had on Tuesday attended a dinner hosted by Mr Carney as part of the official visit. Mr Carney welcomed Sheikh Khaled and expressed hope that the visit would further strengthen friendship and co-operation between the UAE and Canada. Sheikh Khaled thanked Mr Carney for the warm welcome and generous hospitality extended to him and the accompanying delegation. Sheikh Khaled's visit came only weeks after President Sheikh Mohamed spoke by phone with Mr Carney to explore efforts to deepen partnerships, with a focus on the economy, investment and advanced technology.

title: Russian forces shoot down most Ukrainian UAVs using standard quadcopters — fighter
body:
MELITOPOL, October 28. /TASS/. Operators of Russian quadcopter drones are shooting down most enemy unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) over the Zaporozhye Region, an unmanned systems unit soldier of the 1430th Guards Motorized Rifle Regiment with the call sign Uragan told TASS.
"Behind the scenes, there’s a huge amount of work being done by our operators using our standard, favorite quadcopters, which shoot down the vast majority of drones during combat operations. In other words, a standard attack drone can easily be turned into an interceptor drone, and thanks to the operator’s experience and skills, everything is shot down perfectly: from the Mavic to Baba-Yaga UAVs, as well as attack drones," Uragan said.
He noted that quadcopter interceptor drones had proven their effectiveness practically from the very first days they were deployed as air defense systems.

title: Amnesty International, GYLA urge independent probe amid rising Georgian prison abuse claims
body: Violence in Georgian prisons International human rights organisation Amnesty International and the Georgian Young Lawyers’ Association (GYLA) issued a joint statement calling on the Georgian authorities to ensure an independent investigation into reports of torture and other forms of ill-treatment in prisons, as well as to establish effective mechanisms to prevent violence. According to the organisations, reports of torture and other forms of ill-treatment in Georgian penitentiary institutions have increased, including allegations of sexual violence, beatings and threats. The organisations also expressed serious concern about the risk of reprisals against prisoners who speak out about such abuse. In their joint statement, the organisations cited the cases of Giorgi Davitadze, Giorgi and Davit Peikrishvili, Lasha Chachanidze and other prisoners. The authors of the statement also noted that the authorities’ hasty denials, in the absence of proper investigations, raised serious questions. The organisations urged the authorities to “break the vicious cycle of impunity and establish an oversight mechanism capable of effectively and independently preventing violence”. 14 years in power: how experts assess Georgian Dream's rule Assessments differ sharply from those given just five years ago Giorgi Davitadze case and allegations of sexual violence On 2 October 2026, a recording of a court hearing emerged in the media in which prisoner Giorgi Davitadze alleged that he had been subjected to sexual violence by penitentiary service staff. According to him, on 21 December 2025, in a de-escalation room at Prison No. 6 in Rustavi, one of the officers inserted a finger into his anus. The Special Penitentiary Service rejected the allegations and released CCTV footage. The service said that a forced search had been carried out in accordance with established procedures after the prisoner refused to undergo a search and began insulting staff. The footage, which has no audio, shows several officers restraining Davitadze, placing him face down on a bed and positioning themselves behind him. As the officers partially obstruct the view of the prisoner, it is impossible to fully assess their actions. According to his lawyers, the penitentiary service released only a short excerpt from footage lasting approximately 20 minutes. A second camera was installed in the room, but prosecutors did not obtain its recording. According to the Public Defender’s Office, Davitadze’s lawyers reported the alleged abuse on 26 December 2025, and prosecutors launched an investigation on 29 December. Prosecutors say dozens of witnesses have been questioned, while Davitadze refused to undergo a forensic medical examination on 12 January 2026. His lawyers explained that the proposed examination was aimed solely at identifying physical injuries and did not involve investigating the alleged rape itself. Amnesty International and GYLA said the published footage did not clarify what had happened in the room. The human rights organisations stressed that, in cases involving allegations of sexual violence, the authorities were obliged to promptly arrange independent medical and psychological examinations. According to his defence team, Davitadze was repeatedly subjected to humiliation and threats: half of his hair was shaved off, the heating in his cell was deliberately switched off, and threats were made against him and his family members. On 13 October, his lawyers reported that two officers had verbally abused the prisoner and confiscated his television. According to representatives of the human rights organisations, the prison administration had not restricted access to Davitadze for the officers he accused of abuse. They demanded that the investigation examine not only the events of December but also all allegations of repeated threats and humiliation. Prisoner in Georgia accuses guards of sexual abuse. Penitentiary Service denies allegations The prisoner says he faced pressure after demanding forensic medical examinations. Alleged reprisals against prisoners The organisations also highlighted the cases of prisoners at Prison No. 6 in Rustavi who expressed solidarity with Davitadze. According to reports, after Davitadze’s allegations became public, some prisoners staged protests, including by making noise in their cells. They were reportedly subsequently subjected to beatings, placed in de-escalation cells (isolation cells) and transferred to other penitentiary institutions. On 5 October, the lawyer representing Lasha Chachanidze said prison officers had physically assaulted his client and four other prisoners in response to their protest. According to the lawyer, Chachanidze was beaten with batons on 2 October, with officers striking his arms and legs. Visible injuries were documented on his body when he was transferred to Prison No. 3 in Batumi. On 16 October, another prisoner, Beka Tsertsvadze, reported that prison officers had beaten and verbally abused him while transferring him to a de-escalation cell, after which he was moved to another facility. The Special Penitentiary Service rejected the allegations of beatings. The service said that placing at least four prisoners in de-escalation cells was a lawful security measure. According to the service, the measure was taken in response to attacks on prison staff on 2 and 4 October and was unrelated to the protests. The service also released video footage showing two incidents in which prisoners attacked prison officers. Amnesty International and GYLA noted that prison authorities were obliged to protect both staff and prisoners from violence. However, they stressed that alleged misconduct by prisoners did not justify the use of violence in retaliation. The use of force is permissible only when strictly necessary and must be proportionate to the situation. Furthermore, restrictive measures must not become a means of punishing prisoners who file complaints or express solidarity with others. The statement also cited an assessment by the European Committee for the Prevention of Torture (CPT). In a report published in February 2026, the committee expressed concern about the frequent and sometimes prolonged use of de-escalation cells in Georgian prisons. The CPT warned the authorities that, in practice, placing prisoners in such cells could amount to punishment. According to the committee, de-escalation cells should be used exclusively for prisoners who are agitated or displaying aggressive behaviour, for the shortest possible period and under medical supervision. Davit Peikrishvili beating case The case of Davit Peikrishvili has raised further concerns. On 20 October 2026, his lawyer, Paata Gogiashvili, reported that Peikrishvili had been repeatedly subjected to physical violence by fellow inmates at Gldani Prison No. 8 since 16 October. According to the lawyer, the prisoner had been diagnosed with four fractured ribs, injuries to his skull and facial bones, and numerous bruises across his body. On 19 October, Peikrishvili was transferred to hospital, where medical staff confirmed that he had sustained multiple injuries. On 19 October, the Special Penitentiary Service initially denied that Peikrishvili had been beaten. The following day, amid media reports and public criticism, the Justice Ministry announced the launch of a criminal investigation into his injuries. On 22 October, the Public Defender said that, according to Peikrishvili, prison officials had also participated in the beating. The Public Defender called on prosecutors to conduct an independent investigation. On 26 October, prosecutors told journalists that the case had been transferred from the Justice Ministry’s General Inspectorate to the investigative department of Georgia’s Prosecutor General’s Office. Prosecutors also recommended the suspension of Giorgi Pataridze, director-general of the Special Penitentiary Service under the Justice Ministry. Following the recommendation, Pataridze left his post, and a new head of the service was appointed. According to human rights organisations, the developments surrounding Peikrishvili’s case have once again highlighted problems with the effective investigation of allegations of torture and other forms of ill-treatment in Georgia, as well as holding those responsible to account. They linked these concerns, in particular, to reports of violence against protesters detained since 2024. Old enemies in same cell: crime boss beaten, codes and politics. What is happening in Georgia’s prisons? Well-known underworld figure Davit Peikrishvili was taken to hospital twice. His lawyer says it was a criminal feud and rules out a political motive, but other theories have emerged. Rights’ groups urge authorities to establish independent oversight mechanism Amnesty International and GYLA insist that all credible allegations of torture and other forms of ill-treatment must be subject to prompt, thorough, independent and impartial investigations. They argue that the authorities must ensure that all relevant evidence is collected, victims of alleged abuse are protected, and those against whom there is sufficient evidence are held accountable. The organisations also called on the authorities to review practices in penitentiary institutions, complaints procedures and mechanisms for protecting prisoners from ill-treatment. “ The Georgian authorities must break this vicious cycle of impunity by establishing an oversight mechanism genuinely capable of effectively and independently preventing violence, creating truly independent complaints procedures, and guaranteeing victims access to justice and compensation ,” the organisations said in their joint statement. title: Ukrainian drones strike Russia’s Tula region, reportedly sparking fire at chemical plant
body: Ukrainian drones struck the Tula region overnight on October 28. Governor Dmitry Milyaev said that “debris falling” in the city of Novomoskovsk damaged apartment buildings and private homes, as well as “infrastructure in the surrounding industrial zone.” Laboratories from the Tula region’s Ministry of Natural Resources and Rospotrebnadzor were sent to the city, though the governor did not say why. Ukrainian monitoring Telegram channels Exilenova+ and Supernova+ said the Azot chemical plant was hit in the attack. Ukraine has previously targeted the plant . Residents of Lipetsk reported hearing explosions overnight on October 28. Ukrainian Telegram channels said a fire broke out near the Novolipetsk Metallurgical Combine. Authorities did not comment on the reports. At Meduza, we are committed to transparency about our use of artificial intelligence in the newsroom.
