title: Zelensky: Abu Dhabi meeting depends on U.S. side
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky made this statement during a conversation with journalists, according to a Ukrinform correspondent.
“In my view, this meeting in Abu Dhabi depends on the U.S. side—much like the meeting in Brussels. The Russians confirmed it, and we confirmed it. In my view, today it no longer depends on the Russians or on us. Today, Abu Dhabi depends on the U.S. side. This is because everyone has said they view this format of the meeting positively. And for the United States, the main focus is the Middle East. Therefore, various developments, including possible political changes in some countries, will influence what unfolds in the Middle East,” Zelensky noted.
He suggested the possibility of an escalation in the Middle East.
“There could be an escalation there, and many people are talking about it. I think it will happen,” the President said.
As reported by Ukrinform, on October 20 in Oslo, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky held talks with U.S. Special Presidential Envoy Steve Witkoff, with the participation of Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gar Støre and Finnish President Alexander Stubb.
On October 21, Witkoff met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg, after which he stated that discussions on ending the Russian-Ukrainian war would continue in the format of trilateral talks at the technical level. These talks are expected to take place in the first half of November in Abu Dhabi.

title: How students were killed in accident involving Niger Gov’s convoy
body: At least four students and a driver attached to Government House, Minna, have been killed in an accident involving the convoy of Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago of Niger State. Daily Trust gathered that the accident occurred along Minna–Bida Road, on Monday morning. Sector Commander of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) in Niger, Aishat Sa’adu, confirmed the incident, but did not give details. The convoy was said to be returning to Minna after a condolence visit to the Etsu Nupe in Bida, over the death of Hajia Aisha, Sagin Nupe, when the accident occurred at Gidan Mongoro. It was unclear if the governor was in the convoy when the unfortunate incident occurred. Some of the deceased were identified as Nafisat Abubakar Aguye and Ibrahim Ado Bayero. They were said to be postgraduate students of the Federal University of Technology (FUT), Minna. The names of the two other students had not been disclosed as of the time of filing this report. Dauda Chukuba, the Director-General of Government House, sustained injuries in the accident and was reportedly taken to the IBB Specialist Hospital, Minna, for treatment. Commenting on the incident, Police Public Relations Officer in Niger, SP Wasiu Abiodun, said the accident was being investigated.

title: AI Emergency Alerts Are Coming. Humans Might Not Be Ready
body:
Earlier this month, after Hurricane Isaias made landfall on the Gulf Coast as a Category 3 hurricane, the emergency management expert Laura Myers got a call from a meteorologist in Alabama. Myers is director of the University of Alabama’s Center for Advanced Public Safety, and she talks to state and local emergency managers around her region all the time. The meteorologist told Myers that a local emergency manager had published a graphic showing where Isaias might threaten the Alabama coast with a “sting jet” of high winds.
The problem? The emergency manager had generated the graphic using an artificial intelligence chatbot, and it wasn’t accurate.
“That county emergency manager was trying to get his stakeholders to focus on the risk in that county, and so he had asked AI to help him,” she said. “It did what he wanted it to do, but it was not meteorologically accurate.”
Most emergency management agencies don’t permit employees to use generative AI, but Myers and most other emergency management experts agree that its usage is likely already pervasive at state and local disaster departments. There are hundreds of companies that are marketing AI tools to emergency managers for tasks like flood damage assessment and resource coordination, but public communication is one of the areas where government employees and startups have the most interest.
The reason? Most emergency managers aren’t very good at sending out alerts and quickly communicating about disasters with the public. That’s not because they’re emergency managers, but because they are human beings. They tend to write in jargon that non-experts might not understand, leave out information on the assumption that the public already knows it, and include irrelevant details that could distract people from what they actually do need to know.
“A lot of agencies are really limited in resources and the number of people that they have,” said Jeannette Sutton, a disaster researcher at the University of Albany who has created a comprehensive dashboard that provides templates for disaster alerts. “I think they recognize it as a priority, but they don't prioritize it until they realize they should have. They're just trying to get their job done without screwing something up.”
Emergency managers are the government officials who are in charge of disaster response and recovery. At the state and local level, It is these officials and their agencies, not the Federal Emergency Management Agency, that make up the first line of defense after an extreme weather event. As such, emergency managers often like to say that “trust is our currency,” and it’s in their communication with the public that they build and lose this trust.
As climate disasters become more frequent and widespread, there have been numerous examples of flawed human communication scrambling an emergency response. In 2016, for instance, adjacent counties in California issued a “voluntary evacuation” and a “mandatory evacuation” for the same wildfire. In Australia in 2019, officials warned about wildfires by using the phrase “Watch and Act,” which the government later said caused “significant confusion” because no one knew what it meant.
In some cases, inadequate communication can mean the difference between life and death. This happened in Montecito, California, after the 2017 Thomas Fire. A few weeks after the fire, a heavy rainstorm produced a deadly mudslide. The government of Santa Barbara County struggled to communicate the risk to residents still traumatized from the blaze and experiencing a phenomenon that Sutton calls “warning fatigue.” The county sent alerts to everyone in the “voluntary evacuation zone” for wildfires, telling residents to “stay alert to changing conditions and be prepared to leave immediately.” Most of those residents should have left immediately, but to many the evacuation notice was optional; others just didn’t want to evacuate for a second time in a month. The mudslide killed 23 people and injured more than 160 others.
Governments that put out bad warnings are apt to lose the public’s trust, said Sutton. “They're losing the opportunity to be that voice to help people to be safe.”
In theory, alerts are a perfect use case for artificial intelligence, and in particular for the generative AI systems that have developed at a dramatic pace over the past few years. FEMA provides training sessions for emergency managers to learn best practices for synthesizing and sending alerts, but many officials don’t remember all their training when an emergency arrives. A large language model is different. It can read hundreds of thousands of alerts in mere minutes, digest all the research on what works in similar scenarios, and then apply that to edit a human alert in seconds.
“If you’ve only sent one [alert] in your life, and that was 15 years ago, and you need to remember all your training, and you’re thinking ‘Hey, there's a chemical plume coming my way, the phone's ringing, the radio's blaring, I need help,’ the AI is probably gonna do a better job than you are,” said Rob Dale, a former meteorologist who now runs the emergency management department in Ingham County, Michigan.
Dale has already used AI to draft a few practice alerts behind the scenes, but he’s never had to send one out. Ingham County is a small county in central Michigan, and it’s immune from major weather events like hurricanes and fires. If such an event did happen, Dale said he would have no issue allowing a chatbot to draft his incident communication, but he’d still want control over sending the alert out.
Some experts believe the technology is already good enough to deploy. EM1, a startup that produces AI software for emergency managers, has used Sutton’s research to train a model that its executives say is already better than almost any human emergency manager. The company has tested this in-house model on a number of scenarios including wildfires and tsunamis. It can already match or exceed human capabilities on most benchmark tests.
Sutton gave Grist an example of how the software works: Grist provided her with a recent alert sent by a New Mexico county that was trying to warn residents about flooding on the San Juan River.
The original alert read, “Breeched banks. The water is rising. EVACUATE NOW. McGee Park open for people and pets, RV.” Sutton asked the EM1 model to evaluate and revise the alert. In a few seconds, it produced what she said is a far better alert, one that checks all the main boxes of disaster communication.
The new alert read: “San Juan County: Floodwater is rising near [location]. People in [evacuation area]: LEAVE NOW for higher ground. Do not walk or drive through floodwater. McGee Park is open for people and pets. Check [official update source] for updates.” The model identified and fixed several problems with the original text, which does not say who is sending the alert, name the specific location where flooding is happening, or clarify who needs to evacuate and give advice on how to do so safely. It misspells the word “breached,” and it doesn’t provide any guidance on where residents can seek further information.
EM1 has contracts with around a hundred government agencies and school districts, but none are using it to automate their extreme weather alerts just yet. For the moment, they’re only using it to workshop plans and internal preparations. Even so, all the experts interviewed for this story said they are certain that many emergency managers are already using chatbots to write messages, even if they won’t admit it. Sutton said that the emergency managers who take her alert training sessions often present her with high-quality alerts they have drafted in seconds using ChatGPT or Gemini.
“Official adoption is pretty low, but people are unofficially using it, absolutely,” said Sarah Miller, a professor of emergency management at Pierce College in Florida and a longtime instructor at the National Disaster Preparedness Training Center. “They're using their own personal accounts, or they're using free ones.”
It sounds like an easy trade-off: if AI is better and faster than humans, and the difference between a good alert and a bad alert can be life and death, we should be using AI for every heat wave and wildfire. Yet even researchers who are bullish on chatbot technology say that making the switch could backfire. Members of the public who are skeptical of AI or who don’t trust the government in the first place may spurn agencies that publish AI-generated graphics or social media posts. In Syracuse, New York, for instance, a union of public employees sued the local government for using an AI service to answer non-emergency 911 calls.
“We trust things that we perceive [are] authentic and care about us,” said Ginny Katz, the founder of HazAdapt, a consultancy that helps disaster officials figure out how to use technology. “AI-generated content does not feel authentic.” There’s also a risk that chatbots could allow emergency managers to send out more alerts, and faster, which could increase the risk of warning fatigue.
As is the case in other areas where AI is being deployed, disaster experts say that for the moment the software is only as capable as the person using it. A seasoned emergency manager might be able to speed up their communication with the public by having a chatbot draft a series of alerts, but an inexperienced one rushing to create an urgent alert won’t know how to evaluate the output of a model like ChatGPT or Claude.
Even though the technology is a ways off from being able to perform without a human expert in the loop, that hasn’t stopped many understaffed emergency management departments from using it. As for how the proliferation of AI-generated content is affecting public trust in government, experts say it’s too early to tell.
“If you had a human sending you a text message versus a computer sending you a text message, which one would you believe is being more accurate?” said Justin Snair, the founder of Preppr, another company that offers AI software to emergency managers.
The answer, he said, depends on the person receiving it.

title: BUA Cement donates ₦12m to families of eight Sokoto crash victims
body: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto BUA Cement has donated ₦12 million to the families of eight people killed in a road accident along the Kajiji–Tambuwal road in Sokoto State. The company provided ₦1.5 million to each of the bereaved families as financial assistance following the crash, which reportedly involved a commercial minibus conveying 13 passengers and a BUA Cement truck. Eight people, including a child, reportedly died in the accident. The company’s management visited the affected families in Tambuwal to deliver the assistance, accompanied by the District Head of Tambuwal, Alhaji Ahmad Dahiru, and the Chairman of Tambuwal Local Government Area, Hon. Abba Shehu Tambuwal. The donation was commended by the traditional ruler and the council chairman, who described the intervention as a significant demonstration of compassion and support for the bereaved families. The two leaders expressed appreciation to BUA Cement for providing financial assistance despite reports that the company’s truck was not responsible for the accident. They said the gesture demonstrated the importance of corporate social responsibility and urged other organisations to support communities affected by tragedies. The leaders also noted that although the financial assistance could not replace the lives lost, it could help ease some of the immediate financial difficulties confronting the families. They prayed for Allah to reward the company for its generosity, grant eternal rest to the deceased and give their families the strength and patience to bear their losses. The donation comes as the affected households grapple with the loss of their loved ones following the fatal crash. The intervention also highlighted the role of collaboration between businesses, traditional institutions and local government authorities in supporting families affected by emergencies and other tragedies. title: First Training Squadron of the Indian Navy arrives at Colombo, Sri Lanka
body:
New Delhi, Oct 27, 2026. The ships of the Indian Navy’s First Training Squadron (1TS) — INS Tir, INS Sujata and Indian Coast Guard Ship (ICGS) Sarathi — arrived at Colombo, Sri Lanka, on Oct 26, 2026. The ships were accorded a ceremonial welcome by the Sri Lanka Navy in the presence of a naval band, marking the commencement of the port call. The visit provides an opportunity for professional interaction between the two navies and engagement with sea trainees undergoing training with the First Training Squadron.



On arrival, Director General of Naval Training, and Commander, Eastern Naval Area, Sri Lanka Navy, interacted with the sea trainees onboard the ships. The interaction provided an opportunity to engage with the trainees and exchange perspectives on professional naval training.

During the port call, personnel from both navies will undertake a range of professional and training engagements, including cross-training visits and a Passage Exercise (PASSEX). These activities will provide opportunities for personnel to exchange professional knowledge and gain exposure to each other’s practices and procedures, while promoting mutual understanding and strengthening coordination between the two navies.



Community outreach activities and ship visits for the public will also be conducted during the port call. These engagements will provide opportunities for interaction with the local community and familiarisation with the Indian Navy’s ships and training activities.



The port call reflects the enduring maritime partnership between India and Sri Lanka and the continued commitment of both navies to professional engagement and cooperation. The visit also aligns with India’s vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions), emphasising mutual cooperation and collaborative efforts towards maritime security and regional prosperity.

title: Police Warn Against Planned Violent Protest In Edo
body: The Edo State Police Command has urged law-abiding citizens to go about their lawful business and refrain from actions capable of disrupting public peace, safety, law and order in the state. A statement by the Command’s Public Relations Officer, ASP Eno Ikoedem, on Tuesday, noted that the warning was necessitated after the Command received calls from several citizens drawing its attention to online posts from certain quarters calling for public protest. According to the statement, the Commissioner of Police, CP Patrick Daaor, acknowledged citizens’ right to peaceful protest; however, advised anyone with grievances to channel their complaint through appropriate and legitimate means instead of resorting to self-help that could truncate existing peace. He warned against violence, destruction of property, obstruction of public roads, and other acts capable of threatening public peace and order, as the Command will not tolerate any such unlawful acts from any individual or group of persons. The Command assured residents that adequate security measures are being put in place to protect lives and property. He urged the public to promptly report suspicious activities through the following channels: Police Emergency Control Room (Distress Lines): 08077773721, 08067551618, 08056776365, 08123827225, and 08037646272. Complaint Response Unit (CRU), Benin — Complaints Against Police Personnel: 08100389992 and 08150999335. title: Russian shelling of Donetsk region kills 2, wounds 3 in past day – official
body:
Two people were killed and three others were wounded as a result of Russian shelling of settlements in Donetsk region, with 24 attacks recorded over the past day, Head of the Donetsk Regional Military Administration Vadym Filashkin reported on Wednesday.

According to his data, two people were wounded in Sloviansk, Kramatorsk district, where multi-story residential buildings, cafes, shops, a church, a private house, and industrial premises were damaged.

In Novostepanivka of the Oleksandrivka territorial community, an administrative building was damaged; in Novobakhmetieve, a warehouse; and in Rozdolle, a private house.

One person was killed in Novodonetske, while another person was killed and one more was wounded in Iverske.

"In total, over the past day, the Russians shelled settlements in Donetsk region 24 times. 750 people, including 82 children, were evacuated from the frontline," Filashkin emphasized on his Telegram channel.

title: Ukrainian mobile operator Kyivstar acquires cloud provider GigaCloud for nearly $50 mln
body:
Kyivstar Group Ltd. (Nasdaq: KYIV), the parent company of Ukraine's largest telecommunications operator, Kyivstar, has announced the acquisition of GigaCloud, one of Ukraine's leading cloud infrastructure providers, for nearly UAH 2.28 billion (almost $50 million) to expand its cloud solutions capabilities for businesses.
"By combining these strengths with our telecommunications infrastructure, customer reach and investment capabilities, we will be able to help even more companies modernize their operations and develop a stronger technology business for the enterprise segment," Kyivstar Group Ltd. President Oleksandr Komarov was quoted as saying in a press release.
He added that the acquisition would help develop infrastructure that Ukraine will need over the long term.
The transaction is expected to close after the standard closing conditions for deals of this kind have been met. GigaCloud will continue operating as a separate business unit within Kyivstar Group Ltd., retaining its own brand and management team.
In particular, the company's founders are expected to continue running the business.
The agreement also provides for no changes to existing customer contracts, service levels or commercial terms.
"Together with Kyivstar Group Ltd., we will be able to accelerate infrastructure investment, expand our market presence and continue providing services at the level of quality our customers expect," GigaCloud CEO and co-founder Nazarii Kurochko said in the press release.
GigaCloud co-founder Anton Khvastunov, in turn, emphasized that the partnership would strengthen the company's ability to scale secure cloud services and enable it to continue contributing to Ukraine's digital development.
Kyivstar added that the investment would expand the operator's technological capabilities for the corporate sector, further strengthen its capabilities in sovereign cloud infrastructure and enable the development of artificial intelligence (AI)-based services tailored to the needs of Ukrainian businesses and government institutions.
Founded in 2016, GigaCloud currently serves more than 1,800 corporate customers. The company specializes in providing relevant services to businesses. Its clients include agricultural holding company Kernel, Naftogaz and others.
The mobile operator's press release specifies that, according to unaudited management accounts, GigaCloud generated approximately $14 million in revenue and $4.7 million in EBITDA in 2025, corresponding to an EBITDA margin of approximately 34%.
"The agreement is expected to have a positive impact on the development of Kyivstar Group Ltd. The transaction valuation takes into account GigaCloud's growth rate, expertise in cloud technologies, leading market position and the expected benefits of combining the businesses," Kyivstar said.
The transaction structure includes $41 million in acquisition consideration, up to $4 million in deferred debt obligations, approximately $3 million in payments tied to the achievement of agreed performance targets, and up to $2 million in compensation for capital expenditures (CAPEX), in accordance with the terms of the deal.
As reported in the summer of this year, the Antimonopoly Committee of Ukraine authorized Kyivstar Private Joint Stock Company to acquire control of GigaCloud LLC, the cloud provider operating under the GigaCloud brand.
In June 2025, the mobile operator launched its own cloud service for Ukrainian users, Kyivstar Cloud, which is available to small, medium-sized and large businesses, as well as public-sector organizations.
Kyivstar increased its revenue by 29.1% in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period in 2025, reaching UAH 28.9 billion, while revenue in U.S. dollar terms rose by 22.8% to $662 million. Kyivstar's net profit for the period increased by 36.1% compared with the first half of 2025, reaching UAH 7.1 billion, while net profit in U.S. dollar terms rose by 28.8% to $162 million.

title: President Tokayev Proposes SME Inspection Moratorium in State-of-Nation Address
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA — President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed a new three-year moratorium on inspections of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and called for a more systematic investment policy in his state-of-the-nation address on Oct. 28. Photo credit: Akorda. “Investment efficiency should be assessed by the number and quality of commissioned production facilities, as well as their actual contribution to the economy,” Tokayev said. He said priority should be given to projects involving deeper processing of products and higher labor productivity. “This is the main requirement,” he said. Tokayev also called for developing domestic production of construction materials, metal structures and engineering equipment needed for major infrastructure projects. He said these projects should form the foundation of the People’s Construction program. “It is unacceptable to use National Fund resources to finance imports,” Tokayev said. To give the economy fresh momentum, Kazakhstan should attract leading international companies with advanced technologies, expertise and access to global markets, including through cooperation with domestic companies, he said. Tokayev proposes three-year moratorium on SME inspections Tokayev proposed that the government and members of the Kurultai, Kazakhstan’s parliament, consider introducing a three-year moratorium on SME inspections starting Jan. 1, 2027. He said the proposal followed a mixed trend in enforcement. In the first half of the year, the number of violations by individual entrepreneurs fell by 34%, while the total amount of fines increased by nearly 11% and unscheduled inspections rose dozens of times. “Meanwhile, an analysis of business activity shows that businesses simply need not to be obstructed,” Tokayev said. He pointed to the 2020-2023 moratorium on inspections of micro and small businesses as an example of an effective measure, while stressing that the experience of the previous moratorium, including its positive and negative aspects, should be taken into account. Tokayev described the proposed measure as a strategic pause to reset the oversight system and transition to digital regulation. Small and medium-sized enterprises account for 40% of Kazakhstan’s gross domestic product, while their share of investment in fixed capital is approaching 70%, he said. More than one-third of entrepreneurs in the sector are engaged in trade, underscoring the need to diversify small businesses. The government must also develop a dedicated plan for medium-sized businesses, including mechanisms for long-term financing and technological modernization, as well as closer cooperation with large enterprises and opportunities for smaller companies to supply them with products. Tokayev called for improving SME access to procurement by government agencies and quasi-public companies. He suggested reserving part of procurement volumes for small and medium-sized enterprises and easing requirements for suppliers. “Most importantly, it is essential to ensure stable ‘rules of the game’ for entrepreneurs,” he said. Alatau to establish investment court Tokayev highlighted the importance of Alatau, the city planned as a center of accelerated development and an environment conducive to investment and entrepreneurship. He said effective justice was essential to maintaining the long-term attractiveness of any international jurisdiction and called for a judicial system in Alatau that would ensure high-quality justice. “An investment court based on the English common law model will hear commercial cases,” Tokayev said. A civil court would handle other matters related to the city’s special legal regime. The government is expected to submit amendments to the constitutional law on Alatau’s special legal regime to the Kurultai by the end of January 2027. Tokayev stressed that the Constitution would protect investors and entrepreneurs. “The investment interests of all respectable and honest entrepreneurs are guaranteed by the strongest and most reliable legal protection — the Constitution,” he said. Calls for fair competition Tokayev also called for further decriminalization of economic offenses and stronger safeguards for fair competition, particularly for SMEs. According to him, domestic producers, especially food manufacturers, sometimes faced deliberate obstacles. These included artificially lowering the prices of imported goods while restricting domestic products’ access to the local market. Tokayev described such practices as corruption and called for them to be stopped, warning that they weakened the competitiveness of domestic companies and products. He said protecting businesses was directly linked to strengthening the independence of the national economy. “It would not be an exaggeration to say that deliberately creating illegal obstacles for businesses is a crime against the state,” Tokayev said, calling for stronger mechanisms to support entrepreneurs, including through trade associations. The post President Tokayev Proposes SME Inspection Moratorium in State-of-Nation Address appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: Geopolitical shocks contribute to increasing food insecurity — senior diplomat
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. The Middle East conflict and other geopolitical shocks are contributing to the destabilization of food markets, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov said at the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.
"Unfortunately, geopolitical shocks, primarily the conflict in the Persian Gulf, are contributing to increasing food insecurity," he noted.
The senior diplomat pointed out that, as a result of the abovementioned conflict, "disruptions in food supply chains have taken place, leading to a decline in fertilizer supply on global markets and, consequently, a surge in prices." "Rising fuel prices, as well as increasing transport tariffs have led to inflation in the countries of the [African] continent," he pointed out. "Grain crops, animal feed, meat, and dairy products are becoming more expensive," Ryabkov stressed.
"Once again: this is a reminder to us all that it is necessary to not only put out the political and geopolitical fires, but also work together to achieve food sovereignty for the [African] continent," the deputy foreign minister concluded.

title: Two weeks before Starlink’s speed cap hit Ukraine’s drones, a Ukrainian test satellite went up on a SpaceX rocket
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); A test satellite for a future communications network under Ukrainian control is working in orbit, Ukraine’s Himera and Denmark’s GomSpace said on 27 October. The companies say it will work for Ukraine’s strategic security, and that the long-term aim is to rely less on foreign communications providers. Public launch records for the mission do not list a satellite by that name, though some of its objects are still unidentified. Ukraine fights Russia on satellite links it doesn’t control, and the announcement comes two weeks after it saw what depending on an outside provider can cost. The satellite, the companies say, went up on 1 October, before that trouble began. Overnight on 14 October, Starlink and its military version, Starshield, began dropping links on fast-moving terminals, and Ukrainian officials said the cap disrupted drone missions. On 24 October, 10 days after the cap began , Ukraine’s Defense Ministry reported speeds restored. Who ordered the cap remains contested. That same day, Elon Musk wrote that Ukraine’s military had violated Starlink’s terms of service and that “that loophole was closed last week,” a claim a Ukrainian presidential adviser disputed . What the companies say, and what launch records show Obria Nano flew on SpaceX’s Transporter-18 rideshare mission, the release said. Aalborg-based GomSpace built it on Himera’s order, Himera co-founder and CEO Misha Rudominski wrote on Facebook. He added that the team received the first signals the next day and that the satellite is now working. Its tests are meant to inform the design of the full Obria system, the release said. Explore further The Starlink hot potato: Musk points to Trump, Trump points to nobody, then credits Musk with the fix. The speed limit stays No satellite called Obria Nano appears on SpaceX’s published list for the mission, The Insider found . Public tracking catalogs show one Ukrainian satellite from that launch, named UASAT-Nano. Another 26 objects from the mission are still listed with placeholder names and no confirmed owner. The outlet said it is unclear whether the two names refer to one satellite. UASAT-Nano is the satellite network Stetman, another Ukrainian company, is building , and its founder said the network’s first test satellite would launch in October. In April, Stetman and GomSpace agreed to set up a joint venture called UASAT and planned a first launch for fall 2026. The Obria release does not mention Stetman or UASAT. Production in Ukraine is the stated next step Rudominski wrote that Himera’s next stage is to produce satellites and ground terminals in Ukraine. He called it important not only to use the technology but also to gradually build domestic expertise and manufacturing. “For us, this project is about more than launching a satellite. It is an opportunity to lay the foundation for an independent communications network for Ukraine,” Rudominski said in the release. In the long run, the network would cover all of Ukraine and complement European satellite networks, the release said. The network does not exist yet, and Himera has given no timeline. Explore further “Trump and Musk must be held accountable”: US senator warns Starlink network failing over Ukraine could cripple its shield against Russian missiles and drones Replacing Starlink will not be quick. Lance Hunter, a political scientist at Augusta University, told Time that Ukraine cannot quickly swap out such technology, since diversifying it “takes a lot of time. It takes a lot of resources.” Meanwhile, one Ukrainian interceptor-drone maker has begun rethinking its air-launched designs after the slowdown. title: Ukraine expects results from work on humanitarian unblocking of Oleshky within days – Zelenskyy
body:
Ukraine is working on the humanitarian unblocking of the temporarily occupied city of Oleshky in Kherson region and expects to see results within a few days, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated.
"I know how the evacuation to Ukraine can happen technically, but I don't know how it will actually happen. This is what our people, the military, and intelligence told me. And, of course, they have all the information on what to do and how to communicate with each other. Let's give it a few days and we will see the result," Zelenskyy said at a meeting with journalists on Tuesday, an Interfax-Ukraine agency correspondent reports.
According to him, U.S mediation is to play an important role in the process. The Ukrainian side asked to ensure the presence of American representatives and journalists, as it does not trust the Russian side.
"I don't know which side the people will choose. Of course, it's easier to leave Oleshky deeper into the temporarily occupied territory of Ukraine. But I also know that there are a large number of people who want to leave for the territory controlled by Ukraine," the President said.
As reported, a regime of silence in the area of the city of Oleshky in Kherson region was declared at 03:00 on October 27. It will last until 22:59 on November 1 as part of an initiative by U.S First Lady Melania Trump to unblock the city.

title: Dela Rosa again presses SC to reverse ruling on ICC arrest warrant
body: MANILA, Philippines – Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa has again pressed the Supreme Court to reverse its earlier ruling and stop the use of an International Criminal Court arrest warrant against him. In a manifestation on Tuesday, October 27, Israelito Torreon, dela Rosa’s lawyer, asked the SC to urgently rule on a pending motion for reconsideration they filed in June, seeking to reverse a May court decision that denied their plea for a temporary restraining order or a status quo ante order to stop the implementation of the ICC arrest warrant. A status quo ante order simply means a rewind or the court wants things returned to how they were before a disputed action happened, while it decides the case. Dela Rosa’s lawyer argued that the enforcement posture surrounding the senator had “escalated” while the motion remained unresolved. It cited supervening events, including the Department of the Interior and Local Government’s (DILG) declaration of the senator as “armed and dangerous” and the P50-million bounty offered for his arrest. “Taken together, these are not stray remarks of individual officials. They constitute an announced executive enforcement program: an official ‘armed and dangerous’ designation, a ₱50-million capture bounty from public funds, a dedicated task force, Special Action Force deployment, and express presidential support, all directed at the arrest of a sitting senator of the Republic for surrender to a foreign tribunal, while the legality of that very act is pending before this Honorable Court,” the manifestation reads. Voting 9-5-1, the SC previously denied Dela Rosa’s request for a TRO, saying he had “no clear and unmistakable right to be protected.” The tribunal also noted that the Senate had provided the lawmaker with protective custody, preventing his arrest and the implementation of the ICC warrant. “Hence, Senator Dela Rosa’s claimed invasion of his purported rights is more imagined than real,” the SC said. Dela Rosa’s camp said the recent pronouncements from the executive branch placed the senator’s right to life in “present and serious danger.” “No court has found Petitioner Dela Rosa to be armed and dangerous. In law enforcement practice, the designation signals to operating units that armed resistance should be anticipated, which is precisely the setting in which lethal force is most likely to be used,” it said. “Coupled with a bounty and a declaration abandoning restraint, the designation places Petitioner dela Rosa’s right to life under Article III, Section 1 of the Constitution in present and serious danger,” the lawyer added. ICC drug war case The ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I issued a warrant against Dela Rosa in November last year due to his role in former president Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war. He was Duterte’s first police chief who implemented the bloody anti-drug campaign which human rights organizations said took the lives of nearly 30,000 people. The ICC named him a co-perpetrator in the case . It added that those involved “controlled a structure of power” which enabled them to “direct and control the actions” of those who carried out drug war killings. In November, the ICC warrant was still sealed. It was only made public on May 11 , after Dela Rosa, following months of absence in the Senate, showed up to back Senator Alan Peter Cayetano’s election as Senate president. For three days, Dela Rosa sought refuge inside the Senate building until a shooting chaos, which was allegedly triggered by his mistah, Senate sergeant-at-arms Mao Aplasca , ensued on the night of May 13. Hours later, Dela Rosa escaped from the Senate at around 2:30 am. He was accompanied by his political ally, Senator Robin Padilla. Dela Rosa has since stayed out of public view. – with reports from Jairo Bolledo/Rappler.com

title: Polymathic AI and Princeton Researchers Release FlashMap, a Flow Map Drafter for 6.14x Faster LLM Decoding
body: Researchers from Polymathic AI, Princeton University, USC ISI, NYU and the Flatiron Institute have released FlashMap . FlashMap speculative decoding replaces the discrete diffusion drafter with a continuous flow map. It drafts a full 16-token block in 1 forward pass. Tokens in that block stay consistent with each other. On Qwen3-8B, the research team reports up to 6.14x lossless speedup on GSM8K. Drafter weights for Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-4B are on Hugging Face , with vLLM and SGLang plugins . TL;DR Size: 0.5B-parameter drafter (500M for Qwen3-8B, 475M for Qwen3-4B); drafts blocks of K = 16 tokens. Runs on: the same GPU as the target model. Paper speedups use 1 NVIDIA H200 NVL at concurrency 1, in bf16. Performance: fastest drafter tested on Qwen3-8B, about 7% above a retrained DFlash on average. Best: 6.14x speedup on GSM8K at temperature 0 (acceptance length 7.69 tokens). Worst: 2.28x speedup on Alpaca at temperature 1. On Qwen3-4B (temperature 0), it trails DFlash on 4 of 9 tasks. What is FlashMap? FlashMap is a speculative decoding drafter that maps Gaussian noise to a token block in 1 step. A small drafter proposes K tokens. The target model then checks all K in 1 parallel pass and keeps the longest matching prefix. Output stays exactly what the target would produce. Speed depends on 2 things. How many drafted tokens get accepted, and how cheaply they were drafted. EAGLE-3 drafts autoregressively, so cost grows with block length. DFlash drafts the full block in 1 pass with block diffusion. Why do diffusion drafters lose acceptance? DFlash predicts each slot in the block independently. The research team calls this the factorized approximation. Picture a continuation that is “new york” or “san diego” with equal odds. An independent drafter proposes “new diego” or “san york” half the time. The target rejects those at slot 2. FlashMap builds on Flow Map Language Models . Each noise sample maps to 1 full block. The noise picks the mode for every slot jointly. How does FlashMap work? The drafter is a 6-block diffusion transformer (DiT), with embedding dimension 2048 and 16 attention heads. It reads hidden states from target layers 1, 9, 17, 25 and 33. Embedding matrix and LM head are copied from the target and stay frozen. Training runs in 2 stages: Flow teacher: a continuous flow over one-hot token blocks, trained with cross-entropy. A time reparameterization handles Qwen3’s 151,936-token vocabulary. Flow map student: semigroup distillation turns the flow into a 2-time denoiser. It jumps from noise to data in 1 step. Both drafters train on 500K samples from Open-PerfectBlend . Total compute across all models and ablations was about 4,600 GPU hours on H200s. window.addEventListener("message",function(e){if(e.data&&e.data.fmxHeight){var f=document.getElementById("fmx-frame");if(f&&e.source===f.contentWindow)f.style.height=e.data.fmxHeight+"px";}}); How does FlashMap compare on benchmarks? The research team retrained EAGLE-3 and DFlash on the same data and settings. Tests cover 9 benchmarks across math, code and chat, at temperatures 0 and 1. Speed: 1-step FlashMap is the fastest drafter on every Qwen3-8B task, at both temperatures. Accuracy: 1-step FlashMap beats DFlash on acceptance length in 15 of 18 settings. It has about half the parameters. Chat gains are largest: at temperature 0, gains over DFlash are 5.5% on math, 11.1% on chat. 2-step mode: acceptance length beats DFlash in 18 of 18 settings, by 10% on average. EAGLE-3: at temperature 1, it has 9% higher acceptance length but runs 35% slower. A shuffle test checks whether drafts use real inter-token structure. At 2 steps, FlashMap recovers most of the joint-structure gain of a 16-step teacher. At 1 step, it keeps only a small fraction. Drafting 4 noise samples as a tree raised speedup by 11% on average. Comparison: FlashMap vs other speculative decoding drafters Feature FlashMap DFlash EAGLE-3 DSpark Drafting style Continuous flow map, 1 or 2 passes Block diffusion, 1 pass Autoregressive, tree Semi-autoregressive Inter-token dependencies Yes, joint over block No, per-slot independent Yes, sequential Yes, lightweight sequential module Drafter size (Qwen3-8B) 500M 1B 302M (retrained, per FlashMap paper ) Not disclosed Headline claim (own source) Up to 6.1x Up to 6.17x on Qwen3-8B Up to 6.5x 60 to 85% faster per user vs MTP-1 Avg speedup, Qwen3-8B, T=0 (matched, FlashMap paper ) 4.36x 4.07x 2.55x Not tested GSM8K speedup, T=0 (matched) 6.14x 5.77x 3.20x Not tested Weights license Apache-2.0 MIT Apache-2.0 (code) Not disclosed Serving Transformers, vLLM, SGLang Transformers, vLLM, SGLang SGLang and others DeepSeek-V4 serving Average speedups are computed by Marktechpost from Figure 1(c) of the FlashMap paper. Matched rows use the authors’ retrained baselines. How do you deploy FlashMap? The flashmap package needs only torch and transformers>=4.56 . Install it with uv pip install flashmap . A spec_generate call runs drafter and target together on 1 GPU. For serving, the project page gives 2 paths: vLLM 0.31: pass the drafter in --speculative-config with num_speculative_tokens set to 16. SGLang 0.5.20: use --speculative-algorithm DSPARK with the FlashMap draft path. Set num_steps=2 to trade some speed for higher acceptance. For sampling above temperature 0, vLLM needs "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic" . Key Takeaways FlashMap drafts 16 tokens jointly in 1 pass with a continuous flow map. Up to 6.14x lossless speedup on Qwen3-8B, using a 0.5B drafter. Faster than a retrained DFlash on all 9 Qwen3-8B benchmarks. 2-step mode keeps acceptance flat across the block. Weights are Apache-2.0, code is MIT, with vLLM and SGLang plugins. Check out the paper , project page , GitHub repo and model weights . title: Lagos Orders Residents To Get Health Insurance Latest By December 31
body: The Lagos State Government has launched the Lagos Private Health Plan (LPHP) Partnership and flagged off the enforcement of mandatory health insurance, with Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu announcing a grace period until December 31, 2026, for employers, workers and residents to secure appropriate coverage before enforcement commences on January 1, 2027. The launch, held at Lagos Continental Hotel, Victoria Island, also featured the unveiling of 21 participating Health Maintenance Organisations (HMOs), marking a major step in the state’s drive to expand health insurance coverage and protect residents from the financial burden of healthcare. Governor Sanwo-Olu said the initiative, anchored on Executive Order EO/BOS/01/2024 signed on July 16, 2024, was designed to ensure that access to healthcare would no longer depend solely on an individual’s ability to pay at the point of illness. Reaffirming the state’s commitment to the implementation of the State Health Insurance Scheme, Ilera Eko, the Governor said the scheme would create a more inclusive healthcare financing system for formal-sector employees, informal-sector workers and vulnerable residents. Explaining the rationale for the new plan, the Governor said the existing Ilera Eko scheme was designed primarily to support vulnerable populations and people working in the informal sector, necessitating a complementary arrangement for salaried workers and corporate organisations. He disclosed that actuarial analysis of approximately two million claims and enrolment records informed the development of the LPHP, which offers structured health insurance options for the formal sector. The Governor said the state had established implementation and enforcement mechanisms to ensure compliance, including a Lagos Private Health Plan Implementation Steering Committee and an Enforcement Task Force. He directed the relevant authorities to provide operational guidelines and support for enrolment before the end of the grace period, stressing that the objective was compliance rather than confrontation. “We want compliance, not unnecessary confrontation,” Sanwo-Olu said, urging employers and workers to use the transition period to select suitable plans and complete registration. He added that the initiative would strengthen healthcare financing by making payments to participating providers more predictable, improving service delivery and reducing pressure on public hospitals. The Governor also said part of the contributions would support the Lagos State Health Equity Fund and public healthcare infrastructure, helping extend coverage to residents unable to afford insurance. He assured stakeholders that the state would monitor HMOs’ performance, particularly prompt payment to providers, claims settlement and access to appropriate care. The State Commissioner for Health, Prof. Akin Abayomi, described the launch as a defining shift in the state’s healthcare financing system, arguing that out-of-pocket payments expose households to severe financial hardship. He explained that health insurance pools contributions from a broad population, spreading the cost of healthcare across individuals and reducing the risk of families exhausting their savings or falling into debt when illness occurs. Prof. Abayomi said mandatory participation was necessary to build a sufficiently large and diverse insurance pool, noting that voluntary schemes often struggle because healthier people may opt out until they need medical attention. He said the policy would promote solidarity, whereby the healthy support the sick, the young support the old, and those able to contribute help protect vulnerable residents. Outlining the expected benefits, the Commissioner said the LPHP would provide healthcare providers with more predictable income, encourage competition in service quality, ease patient congestion in public facilities, support vulnerable residents and expand the insurance market. Abayomi noted that Lagos was targeting an increase in insured residents from about two million to at least 10 million, while confirming that participating organisations were accredited by the National Health Insurance Authority. The Special Adviser to the Governor on Health, Dr Kemi Ogunyemi, said the Executive Order provided the legal framework for compulsory health insurance for residents and required public and private employers to provide coverage for their workers. She described the LPHP as an opportunity to expand choice by enabling individuals, families and employers to select from accredited health insurance plans suited to their needs. Dr. Ogunyemi stressed that the initiative was not intended to penalise HMOs or private healthcare providers but to bring stakeholders into a coordinated and regulated system. She said competition among participating providers could help improve affordability and service quality, adding that government, employers, insurers and healthcare facilities must work together to achieve universal health coverage. Chairman of the Governing Board of the Lagos State Health Management Agency (LASHMA), Dr Adebayo Adedewe, said the agency had sustained public sensitisation through radio, billboard and digital campaigns, as well as engagements with traditional rulers, market associations, transport unions and community leaders. He disclosed that funding for the Lagos State Health Equity Fund had increased from ₦1 billion to ₦3 billion to strengthen access to healthcare for vulnerable populations, with a target of enrolling 500,000 residents. The Permanent Secretary, Lagos State Ministry of Health, Dr Dayo Lajide, said the programme was critical in addressing the high financial burden of healthcare on Nigerian households. Citing the National Health Insurance Authority’s report that out-of-pocket payments accounted for 58 per cent of total health expenditure in Nigeria in 2024, she said the LPHP would build on Lagos’ existing insurance structure and help protect more families from financial hardship. Permanent Secretary, LASHMA, Dr Emmanuella Zamba, described the launch as a transition from policy development and stakeholder engagement to implementation. She thanked the Governor, the Ministry of Health, participating HMOs, healthcare providers and other partners, urging sustained collaboration to ensure that the new framework delivers accessible and reliable healthcare coverage. Representing Sterling Bank’s Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Abubakar Suleiman, the Vice President, Government Banking, Adewale Adebowale, said the bank was supporting the initiative as a technology and financial partner. He explained that the digital platform developed with Sterling Bank’s assistance would facilitate enrolment and enable employers to register their workers more efficiently, noting that effective partnerships were essential to translating policy into practical benefits. Also speaking, the National President of the Healthcare Providers Association of Nigeria, Dr Aipoh Augustine, commended the state for the consultations that preceded the launch but called for transparent implementation, timely reimbursement of healthcare providers, simplified payment procedures and fair accreditation processes. He said the programme’s success should be measured not only by the number of people enrolled but also by their ability to access appropriate treatment without financial distress. The National President of the Guild of Medical Directors, Dr Raymond Abiodun Kuti, said building public trust through transparency and accountability would be crucial to the scheme’s success. He urged the government to maintain effective engagement with private healthcare providers and address their concerns, while the immediate past President of the Health and Managed Care Association of Nigeria, Dr Leke Oshunniyi, said a well-functioning insurance system would help providers receive payment for services rendered while reducing the financial burden on patients. The Lagos Private Health Plan Partnership complements Ilera Eko by providing additional coverage options for formal-sector employees and corporate organisations within a coordinated state framework. The government said enrolment would be supported through a digital platform, while operational guidelines would specify applicable contributions, minimum benefit packages and the responsibilities of participating organisations. With the grace period ending on December 31, 2026, full enforcement of mandatory health insurance is scheduled to commence on January 1, 2027. The post Lagos Orders Residents To Get Health Insurance Latest By December 31 appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Hanwha Aerospace explores Lithuanian production roles for mobile air defence system
body: The memoranda of understanding cover vehicle integration with KMT, turret shell fabrication with Cosmos Construction and cable manufacturing with T&G Lithuania. Nortal will explore integrating the system’s command-and-control capabilities with NATO networks. “We see Lithuania as a long-term strategic partner and recognise the strong technological capabilities and potential of its defence industry,” said Robert (Sangwon) Park, senior vice president and head of Hanwha Aerospace’s Air Defence and Missile Launcher Systems Business. “We aim to build lasting industrial partnerships with Lithuanian companies, exploring opportunities in technology transfer, joint development and lifecycle support, while contributing to Lithuania’s ambition to become a regional hub for defence manufacturing and maintenance in the Baltic region.” The agreements identify potential industrial roles rather than confirmed production orders. Together, they cover work ranging from structural fabrication and vehicle integration to the connections needed for operation within NATO networks. The Wheeled Anti-Aircraft Gun, or WAAG, is designed to engage drones and other low-altitude aerial threats. It combines automated fire control, target tracking and 40mm ammunition in a mobile system that Hanwha describes as cost-efficient. Hanwha is also discussing its broader air defence portfolio, spanning short-, medium- and long-range capabilities. Its counter-drone approach combines radar and electro-optical sensors, command-and-control systems and multiple countermeasures, while long-range precision fires are another potential area for cooperation. The company has joined the Lithuanian Defence and Security Industries Association to support continued engagement with local businesses. It presented the partnerships at an industry day in Vilnius on 23 October, attended by more than 80 participants from approximately 30 Lithuanian companies. “Hanwha brings great experience and advanced technology,” said Vaidas Sabaliauskas, the association’s director. “We see great opportunities to work together in production, technology, research of new products.”

title: Israel election results: Netanyahu bloc drops to 54 seats as Arab parties rise to 18
body: With 93% of polling stations reporting and 85.6% of votes counted, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing and religious bloc stood at 53 projected seats, eight short of the 61 needed to form a government. The rival bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot held 48 seats, while the predominantly Arab parties had a combined 19, leaving neither main political camp with a parliamentary majority. The Central Elections Committee has completed counting ballots from all regular polling stations, with the results excluding double-envelope ballots, which are scheduled to be counted Wednesday evening. Those votes could still alter the final distribution of Knesset seats.   Netanyahu's Likud remained the largest party with 26 seats, followed by Eisenkot's Yashar! with 21. Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett's Beyachad and the Joint List were projected to win 12 seats each. The Democrats were projected to win eight seats, while Avigdor Liberman's Yisrael Beytenu, United Torah Judaism, Shas, Itamar Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit and Ra'am held seven seats each. The Religious Zionism-Zehut alliance was projected to win six seats. The counting of double-envelope ballots, including votes cast by soldiers and other eligible voters outside their assigned polling stations, could still change the distribution of seats. Political deadlock leaves caretaker government in power With neither Netanyahu's bloc nor the rival camp securing a parliamentary majority, Israel could remain under a caretaker government as coalition negotiations unfold. Under Israeli law, a caretaker government retains the same formal powers as a regular government, including the authority to authorize military action. However, it is expected to exercise restraint, particularly when making major decisions with potentially irreversible consequences. Any decision to go to war must be approved by the government or security cabinet, rather than by the prime minister alone. Operations Guardian of the Walls and Breaking Dawn serve as precedents for military action under caretaker governments. Despite the restrictions associated with caretaker status and concerns over irreversible decisions, the assessment is that a decision to launch military action, if necessary, would receive unanimous approval. Arab parties gain ground as leaders signal willingness to oust Netanyahu The strengthening of the Arab parties has become one of the most significant developments in the vote count. Joint List chairman Prof. Yousef Jabareen said Wednesday that his faction was prepared to use its growing parliamentary strength to help remove Netanyahu's government from power. "The Netanyahu and Ben-Gvir government has made the lives of every Arab citizen miserable," Jabareen said. "We will know how to leverage our political strength to advance the values we believe in. We will be prepared to pave the way for removing the Netanyahu, Ben-Gvir and Smotrich government and sending them home." Ra'am's rise from four to six projected seats earlier in the morning was driven partly by the arrival of results from Rahat, a predominantly Bedouin city in southern Israel where the party enjoys strong support. With 31 polling stations counted there, Ra'am received 83.6% of the vote, compared with 14.7% for the Joint List. In the Bedouin town of Kuseife, Ra'am received 86.6% of votes from five polling stations counted, while the Joint List received 9.9%. In Kafr Qasim, Ra'am led with 74.06%, compared with 22.9% for the Joint List. Small parties fight to cross the electoral threshold Beyond the battle between the main blocs, several smaller parties were struggling to secure enough votes to enter the next Knesset. In an earlier count, when 60.2% of votes had been processed, the Reservists-Economic party led by Yoaz Hendel and Yaron Zelekha was 19,803 votes short of the electoral threshold. Another party, Amcha Israel, led by former military officer Ofer Winter, was 54,888 votes below the threshold, making its chances of entering parliament increasingly remote. Ra'am, meanwhile, remained at six projected seats, while the Joint List rose to 13, bringing the Arab parties' combined representation to 19. The final distribution of seats could still change as additional results arrive. Golan calls for government backed by Arab parties Democrats chairman Yair Golan insisted Wednesday that Netanyahu had lost the election and urged the opposition to form a government with the support of Arab parties. "Netanyahu lost. I know how to count to 120. Sixty-five is more than 55. That's how Israeli democracy works. Period," Golan wrote on X, referring to the parliamentary balance at an earlier stage of the count. Golan criticized what he described as Netanyahu's attempt to distinguish between Jewish and Arab votes, arguing that the opposition should not exclude Arab citizens from the political process. "We have a majority, we have a responsibility, and we have an opportunity to establish a government of change in partnership with Israel's Arab citizens," he wrote. "Now we need courage. We need leadership. We need to stop being afraid and start acting." Golan declined to speak to reporters waiting outside his home in Rosh HaAyin. Trump seeks to keep Ben-Gvir out of next government, sources say U.S. President Donald Trump is closely monitoring the Israeli election through his aides, according to sources in his circle, who told ynet that the president does not want Netanyahu to include Ben-Gvir, and likely Bezalel Smotrich, in his next government. According to those sources, Washington views Ben-Gvir's participation as unacceptable, potentially complicating Netanyahu's efforts to preserve his existing right-wing coalition. The development raises the possibility of American pressure to establish a broader unity government, although no such arrangement has been agreed upon. Trump earlier shared a statement on Truth Social attributed to Irving C. Schwartz that credited the president's endorsement of Netanyahu with reversing the political momentum against him. The partial results showed Netanyahu's bloc ahead of its main rival, but its tally of 54 seats left it seven short of a majority, while Eisenkot's bloc and the Arab parties together accounted for 66 seats. The shekel weakened as the results emerged, reflecting uncertainty surrounding the country's political future. Special ballots could still change the results The IDF reported that 79.9% of military personnel had exercised their right to vote, an increase of 6.2% compared with the previous Knesset election. More than 890 military polling stations operated across Israel, including mobile stations deployed to military bases, units and combat zones. Many military ballots are counted under Israel's double-envelope system, which requires additional verification to prevent duplicate voting. Elad Naveh, head of the Central Elections Committee's control center, said more than half a million double-envelope ballots were expected, with counting scheduled to begin around midnight Wednesday and conclude Thursday evening. Naveh cautioned that it was too early to estimate their impact on the parliamentary seat distribution. Even after the additional votes are counted, the results will remain nearly final rather than fully certified, with further checks scheduled for next week. The committee also clarified that the absence of published results from several cities, including Kfar Saba, Ra'anana, Sakhnin and Kafr Qasim, did not mean ballots had not been counted locally. Instead, results from those polling stations had not yet been fully received and processed by the central committee's systems in Jerusalem. Eisenkot's early victory speech meets changing results The emerging results cast a different light on speeches delivered by the two main political rivals overnight. Eisenkot addressed supporters shortly after the television exit polls were released, declaring that Israelis had voted for political change and calling on Netanyahu to step down. "We have made history," Eisenkot told supporters. "The public chose change." He accused Netanyahu's coalition of losing the public's confidence, while supporters repeatedly chanted, "The next prime minister!" Netanyahu, meanwhile, addressed supporters at the International Convention Center in Jerusalem, celebrating Likud's emergence as the largest party and calling for cooperation among Israel's Zionist political forces. "The Zionist majority must come to its senses and unite. Only that way can we guarantee Israel's future," Netanyahu said. He also twice thanked his "loyal partners" in the outgoing coalition, signaling his intention to preserve those political relationships. With 70.7% of votes counted, the remaining ballots and the expected double-envelope count could still alter the allocation of seats. The growing representation of Arab parties has also intensified the debate over whether they could help facilitate an alternative government, although a parliamentary majority alone does not guarantee that the parties involved will agree to govern together.

title: Launch of Next Generation Offshore Patrol Vessel (Yard 1283, Srishti)
body:
New Delhi, Oct 27, 2026. Yard 1283 (Srishti), Next Generation Offshore Patrol Vessel (NGOPV), was launched at Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL), Goa on Oct 27, 2026 by Mrs. Sandeepa Sahay, in the presence of Vishvajit Sahay, Secretary (Defence Finance). The event reflected the rich traditions and ethos of the Indian Navy. Senior dignitaries from the Indian Navy, Ministry of Defence and GSL attended the occasion.



These indigenously designed and built ships will augment the existing OPVs/ NOPVs for multi domain operations, such as maritime surveillance, Search and Rescue, protection of offshore assets, Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) and anti-piracy missions. The construction of NGOPVs is concurrently being undertaken at two shipyards (GSL, Goa & GRSE, Kolkata).



These ships derive their names from India’s rich heritage, with this ship being named as ‘Srishti’, meaning ‘Creation’ or ‘Act of Creating’ in Sanskrit.



Speaking on the occasion, Vishvajit Sahay highlighted the Government’s emphasis on indigenisation and its multiplier effect on the economy, including its contribution to GDP growth and the development of the domestic industrial ecosystem. He lauded the three Services, particularly the Indian Navy, for taking the lead in this endeavour and congratulated GSL on its contribution towards realising the Government’s vision of self-reliance in defence manufacturing.



The launch marks yet another significant milestone in Indian Navy’s pursuit towards indigenous shipbuilding and is in consonance with Government of India’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India initiatives.

title: New Awujale will emerge before May 29, Abiodun assures Ijebuland
body: Governor Dapo Abiodun of Ogun has assured the people of Ijebuland that a new ‘Awujale’ will emerge before May 29. This is contained in a statement in Abeokuta on Wednesday by Abiodun’s Media Adviser, Mr Kayode Akinmade. Abiodun gave the assurance at the Ogun East Senatorial District stakeholders’ meeting in Ijebu-Ode, attended by representatives of various interest groups. The governor explained that his administration was committed to ensuring a peaceful, smooth and acceptable succession process, urging the people to remain calm and patient. “I acknowledge the importance of the Awujale institution to the cultural heritage, identity and unity of Ijebuland, our people should remain calm and patient as the necessary processes are being concluded. “Our administration is giving the matter the attention it deserves, with a view to ensuring that the process is concluded peacefully and the emergence of a new Awujale enjoyed the acceptance and support of the people,” he said. Abiodun said the meeting was organised to strengthen engagement with grassroots stakeholders, address community concerns and showcase his administration’s achievements over the past seven years. On economic development, he identified oil exploration around Eba Island and the proposed Gateway Deep-Sea Port in Ogun Waterside Local Government Area as major growth drivers. He added that the proposed Blue Marine Special Economic Zone would attract investments, create jobs and position Ogun state as a hub for maritime trade, manufacturing and logistics. The governor reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to infrastructure development and investment promotion, appreciating President Bola Tinubu’s support for critical projects and initiatives in the state. He urged continued cooperation to advance peace and development in the state. NAN reports that the Awujale stool became vacant in July 2025 following the passing of Oba Sikiru Adetona at 91 after a 65-year reign. The post New Awujale will emerge before May 29, Abiodun assures Ijebuland appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Iran's oil min. rebukes US treasury chief on fuel shortage
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 28 (MNA) – Iran’s caretake oil minister has lashed out at US Treasury secretary for making baseless claims on impending fuel shortages in Iran, telling him to instead focus on the skyrocketing energy costs burdening American citizens.
In a post on his X account, Hamid Bovard dismissed Scott Bessent’s recent psychological warfare campaign, which falsely claimed Iran would face severe gasoline shortages this winter and advised Iranians to stockpile fuel.
"Instead of advising Iranians to stock up on fuel, the US Treasury Secretary should worry about its price for his own people," Bovard wrote.
Highlighting the contrast in the two nations' current energy postures, Bovard noted that while Iran is actively advancing its strategic "gas diplomacy in Moscow" and securing new regional energy alliances, the United States is desperately scrambling to secure diesel.
"Bessent's audience for fuel stockpiling should be the American people, who have been paying the heavy price for Trump's adventurism for months," the minister added, pointing to the severe cost-of-living crisis and surging fuel prices inside the US driven by Washington's aggressive foreign policies.
The retort comes as Washington continues its campaign of economic terrorism against Tehran.
Despite decades of unilateral sanctions and hostile rhetoric, Iran continues to seamlessly expand its oil exports, boost domestic production, and forge robust energy partnerships, rendering American attempts to cripple its fuel and energy sectors ineffective.

title: Karim Zito sacked over inconsistent results and disunity among backroom staff – AshantiGold CEO
body: AshantiGold Chief Executive Officer Edward Kwasi Akuoko has attributed the dismissal of Karim Zito and his assistants to inconsistent results and disunity among the backroom staff. The Obuasi-based club announced the decision in a statement on October 27, relieving the former Asante Kotoko coach and his two assistants, Ernest Okyere and Robert Dabuo, of their duties following a consultative meeting of the Interim Management Committee. AshantiGold have made a mixed start to the 2026/27 Ghana Premier League campaign, recording three wins in their opening eight matches. They currently sit 11th on the league table with 11 points. “As a serious club, you always want to win,” Akuoko told Obaapa Radio. “I’m not a leader who always lowers expectations just because we are a newly promoted side. We are not saying we have to win the league at all costs, but we simply want consistent results. Our away performances have been poor. “The second reason is that, personally, I received reports that the technical team led by Karim Zito were not on good terms, and that could be affecting our results.” Zito joined AshantiGold in February 2026, 15 days after resigning from Kotoko, where he had been in charge. The former Dreams FC coach subsequently guided AshantiGold to promotion to the Ghana Premier League. Meanwhile, the club said that a caretaker coach would take charge of the team until a substantive head coach and technical director is appointed.

title: Petrol prices tipped to fall from Nov. 1 as diesel floor rises
body: Petrol prices could fall at the pump from November 1, 2026, while diesel prices may rise marginally after the National Petroleum Authority (NPA) adjusts its price floors. Market data obtained by JoyBusiness indicates that the petrol price floor has been reduced from GH¢16.09 to GH¢15.39 per litre for the November 1–15 pricing window. The diesel floor, however, has increased from GH¢17.09 to GH¢17.41 per litre. Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) could also see some relief, with its price floor declining from GH¢13.89 to GH¢13.73 per kilogram. These figures are price floors, not final retail prices. According to the NPA, they exclude premiums charged by International Oil Trading Companies, operating margins of Bulk Import, Distribution and Export Companies, and margins charged by Oil Marketing Companies and LPG Marketing Companies. The respective companies will determine those charges independently under the prescribed Petroleum Products Pricing Formula. Impact The adjustments could produce mixed price movements at the pumps during the next pricing window. Lower price floors could give marketers room to reduce petrol and LPG prices. However, final adjustments will depend on the premiums and margins individual companies apply. One major oil marketing company currently sells petrol at GH¢16.45 per litre and diesel at GH¢17.95 per litre. Some marketers could reduce prices, while others may leave them unchanged. The higher diesel floor also suggests upward pressure on its retail price. Although international crude oil prices have been rising, the cedi’s recent appreciation may help cushion some of the pressure on local fuel prices. Background and price quotes for October Petrol and diesel prices recorded marginal reductions at the pumps from October 16, 2026. LPG prices, however, were projected to rise by about 18.5% per kilogram. The Chamber of Oil Marketing Companies attributed the petrol and diesel reductions to movements in international refined product prices and government subsidy measures. In its report for that period, the Chamber said average crude oil prices rose 2.03% to US$126.73 per barrel amid renewed supply concerns. Refined petroleum products recorded mixed movements. International LPG prices rose 7.77%, while diesel and petrol prices fell 6.68% and 3.93%, respectively. Over the same assessment period, the cedi depreciated by 1.61% to GH¢11.8222 per US dollar, based on average bank rates between September 26 and October 11, 2026. The Chamber said the currency had lost more than 11% against the dollar since the start of the year, with seasonal import demand and higher energy costs contributing to the pressure. Despite those pressures, lower international petrol and diesel prices, together with the subsidy measures, supported modest reductions at the pumps during the October 16 pricing window.

title: Kyiv's housing market feels the chill as residents escape ahead of winter
body:
As temperatures are falling in Kyiv, so are rent prices, with residents leaving the capital to escape Russian bombardment and the prospect of a winter without heating and electricity.
Over the last two months, the number of long-term rentals listed on Kyiv's market shot up by 66%, Alona Babko, head of public relations at LUN, a leading real estate portal in Ukraine, told the Kyiv Independent.
The sharp rise in vacancies started in August, as Russia stepped up attacks on Kyiv , causing civilian casualties to increase. The trend has deepened with renewed strikes on energy facilities and fears that the capital will endure another winter without heating and electricity, prompting residents to pack their bags and look elsewhere.
With more housing options on the market, and the competition it brings, rental prices have been declining since July, falling by 6% in the last month to an average of 17,000 hryvnias ($377) per month for a one-bedroom apartment — the lowest in a year — Babko said.
"We’re now seeing a trend of more and more people vacating their apartments. A lot of people are moving to safer places. Some are going abroad, while others are choosing Ukraine’s western regions," Oleksandra, a realtor in Kyiv, told the Kyiv Independent.
"It’s not just individuals, either. Companies that had branches here are relocating them to places such as Lviv and Ivano-Frankivsk. Naturally, the people who work for those companies are moving there, too."
Oleksandra, as well as a landlord the Kyiv Independent spoke to for the story, declined to give their last names, citing security concerns that are not evident given the nature of the story. The request to remain anonymous may say more about the informal nature of Ukraine’s real estate sector.
Anna, a landlord who declined to provide her full name, hasn’t been able to rent out her empty apartment in central Kyiv for around a month. It used to only take her a week to find a new tenant, she told the Kyiv Independent.
Now, she is considering shaving $100 off her rent to attract renters, although she still hopes to find someone to pay the full price — $800.
Unsurprisingly, rents are cheapest in parts of the city that frequently suffer attacks — usually the industrial neighborhoods on the eastern side of the Dnipro River. With Russia continuously targeting warehouses, factories, and power plants in these districts, demand is dropping as some residents relocate to the western side of the city.
The recent Russian strikes on Kyiv’s bridges connecting the western and eastern banks have also alarmed residents, Olena Haydamakha, president of Ukraine’s Association of Realtors, told the Kyiv Independent. After the first wave of strikes in early October, her colleagues in western Ukraine were flooded with calls from anxious Kyivans.
"Most people said they wanted to secure an apartment in advance. If the situation deteriorated, they would then move to that apartment," she said.
While Kyiv’s rents fall, prices in cities in western Ukraine are soaring, Babko said. Currently, rents in Lviv, Uzhhorod, and Ivano-Frankivsk have surpassed those in Kyiv — historically the country’s most expensive city — even rivaling prices in EU capitals, drawing criticism on social media.
"I read the news about the hard winter, the problems with power and heating, and decided to see how much it costs to rent housing in other Ukrainian cities. I found a one-room apartment in Uzhhorod for $1,500 a month. So if you decide to leave the capital, you’ll have to pay three to five times more for housing?" one Facebook user from Vyshhorod, Kyiv Oblast, wrote on Oct. 11.
But many Kyivans can’t afford to move away because rents are so high in other regions or because they cannot leave their jobs and families.
With no choice but to remain in the city, or because they are reluctant to leave, many are relocating to apartments on lower floors that are safer from drone attacks and easier to access when elevators don’t work during power outages.
Some apartment owners are also installing equipment like gas stoves and battery storage systems to make life more comfortable for renters during blackouts. Anna said she wants to install a $3,000 backup power unit in her apartment to help attract renters.
In online groups for renters, many landlords advertise power units in their properties as part of the deal.
