LUN even launched an online map of Kyiv to show which housing units are best prepared for an energy crisis , covering information such as insulation work carried out and which services, if any, operate during power outages, including heating and water.
For now, most relocations from Kyiv are a temporary reaction to the coming winter, Babko said. When it comes to the property sales market, little has changed, indicating that residents aren’t yet willing to permanently give up their homes in the capital, she added.
Anna is optimistic that many people will continue to remain in Kyiv, even over the winter, where there are more job opportunities than in western Ukraine, and rents are cheaper.
"The city will continue to live, work, and function," she said.

title: Is a custom financial LLM a mirage? Lessons from BloombergGPT for IT leaders
body:
Home - Insights - Is a custom financial LLM a mirage? Lessons from BloombergGPT for IT leaders in UK financial services
By Dmitry Baraishuk, chief technology officer and partner at Belitsoft
This year, a senior Bloomberg executive admitted that BloombergGPT, the financial language model the company announced with much fanfare in 2023, isn’t actually used in any of its products at all. I think every IT leader in financial services should stop and ponder this fact.
For three years, this model was the proof behind a common assertion: serious financial AI requires its own LLM. I still hear that assertion from banks and fintechs, in the UK and elsewhere, about spending a budget they can’t afford on a model they won’t need. Does a financial firm really need to build one big custom model? I doubt it.
I’ve been managing software development teams for 20 years and know how often companies build complex products when a simpler solution could address their business needs. I had to find out what had happened. I went through Bloomberg’s releases, from the 2023 paper to this year’s disclosures, to understand what went wrong with the project, what happened and what the business is using instead.
In my opinion, the story below represents the most accessible learning in financial AI this year.
In March 2023, Bloomberg published a paper about BloombergGPT, its own large language model trained on financial data. The training set was built on Bloomberg’s extensive proprietary data, arguably the largest financial dataset to date. Bloomberg claimed that BloombergGPT significantly outperformed existing models on financial tasks.
“It was clearly a big investment. We decided it was worth it to start building our own model. I’m not sure we knew exactly at that time what it would be used for”, David Rosenberg said on the TWIML AI Podcast. At the time, Rosenberg led the Machine Learning Strategy team in the Office of the CTO at Bloomberg and was a co-author of BloombergGPT.
According to David Rosenberg, using an API like OpenAI’s wasn’t an option for Bloomberg: “We have data we don’t want to send out. So for internal and sensitive use, in-house models are preferable.” We will come back to this argument, because Bloomberg’s own position on it has since changed.
The core team consisted of approximately nine people. Bloomberg pre-purchased approximately 1.3 million GPU hours in the cloud at an agreed price of about $1 per hour and sized the model to fit this budget.
Hence, by my calculations , computing alone cost approximately $1.3m at the low end of cloud pricing. Add the salaries of nine machine learning specialists for the duration of the project, and the total investment comfortably runs into several million dollars.
Training required three attempts. In total, from the first attempt to the finished model took the better part of a year.
Just two months after the paper was published, general-purpose models accessible via API outperformed BloombergGPT on most of the financial tasks tested. Researchers from Queen’s University and J.P. Morgan AI Research found that ChatGPT performed better than BloombergGPT, which was specifically trained on financial data, on three of the five tasks where the two were compared, and GPT-4 beat it on all but one. On conversational question answering, ChatGPT outperformed BloombergGPT by more than 15 percentage points.
Since the paper’s publication, Bloomberg hasn’t provided any official updates on BloombergGPT. The model was never released, no public demo was available and pricing was never announced.
But then in February 2024, an executive fellow at Harvard Business School wrote a review : “I recently had the opportunity to try out BloombergGPT on the Bloomberg Professional service.” He wrote that BloombergGPT had disrupted the Bloomberg terminal with a new technology that was likely to replace the established one.
The review was widely circulated, and it seemed that despite the researchers’ scepticism, Bloomberg had implemented its model into its products, and customers were very happy. Bloomberg had its own model, and this came to be seen by many as the only way to create a financial LLM that would stand out from the crowd. This opinion persisted in the community until 2026.
However, in April 2026, Wayne Barlow, Bloomberg’s global head of terminal products, told A-Team Insight that BloombergGPT was a research model and is not actually used in any of its products.
So, Bloomberg trained its own large financial LLM with a core team of approximately nine people, but this specific model was never implemented into a product.
In fact, Bloomberg’s products are built on a combination of models. There are some commercial models, some openly available models and smaller models developed by the company’s own team. Different parts of the system have different models for solving certain problems. In some cases, speed matters most, and a smaller model is required. In other cases, it’s simply a question of which model is best suited to a particular task.
Shawn Edwards, Bloomberg’s CTO, confirmed this. He told Fortune that the system uses a variety of AI models, including some developed in-house by Bloomberg and others from leading AI model companies like Anthropic, and routes requests to the cheapest model capable of handling a given task.
This is where the security argument from 2023 comes back. Bloomberg no longer refuses external models outright. Instead, the most sensitive data is handled by its own in-house models, while everything else can go to a commercial one.
In other words, Bloomberg learnt to build one custom mega-model and then applied this knowledge to building smaller custom models for specific tasks, and only for those tasks where off-the-shelf models weren’t powerful enough. If a large commercial model performed a task at a higher cost than a cheaper model, the task was given to the cheaper one.
The direction was set early. As far back as 2023, David Rosenberg said on the TWIML AI Podcast: “We’re more interested now in smaller models. They’re easier to use: you can run inference on a single GPU.”
Both of the products below run on this combination of models, not on BloombergGPT.
In April 2025, Bloomberg launched Document Insights. Users ask questions in everyday language about a company document, such as a transcript of a financial results call, and receive links to the relevant sections in the original document.
In February 2026, Bloomberg’s AI-powered financial product, ASKB , started producing the data queries behind its answers. It allows traders to transfer results directly to Excel and Bloomberg’s analytics tools for further work.
The BloombergGPT model wasn’t included in any product, but the data was. In 2026, ASKB draws on hundreds of millions of company documents, such as transcripts of financial results calls, presentations and reports. Shawn Edwards told Fortune that the data is the hardest part: “You have to buy all those sources, do all the validation work, build benchmarks, and tokens aren’t cheap.”
As Barlow said, in 2026 the model itself isn’t used in any product. What Bloomberg gained from this investment is the experience of training a large model, a data pipeline and a team, which it now uses for smaller custom models.
“As for production use, we need to be very cautious. No one has really solved the hallucination problem yet. These language models can say wrong things, do strange things, so there needs to be a process around making them safe to use, either internally or, eventually, with clients”, David Rosenberg said on the TWIML AI Podcast.
As Edwards told Fortune, using AI to check AI can work in simple cases, but for everything else, human experts are needed. During development, Bloomberg engaged bond experts, equity analysts, market structure specialists and journalists to write the benchmark questions and evaluate entire workflows.
According to a Bloomberg press release, each ASKB response is accompanied by transparent attribution of the original sources and the underlying query for any data analysis, so users can verify the answer.
In 2026, evaluation is a core part of the work. Benchmarks are now developed by subject matter experts, not just the machine learning team.
Truewind, a US fintech start-up, relies on OpenAI models. The same applies to JPMorgan’s LLM Suite, rolled out in 2024, which uses OpenAI and Anthropic models. Goldman Sachs, a US multinational investment bank and financial services group, has built its GS AI Assistant to work with a range of models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google as well as publicly available models.
The biggest fintech firms in the UK have done likewise. Starling launched its Spending Intelligence system, powered by Google’s Gemini models, in June 2025, and Starling Assistant in March 2026 . Spending Intelligence analyses customer transactions within Starling’s own cloud environment and, in accordance with its agreement with Google, none of this data is used to train Gemini. Revolut, which rolled out its AI assistant AIR to 13 million customers in the UK in April 2026, declined to reveal its suppliers, but its head of machine learning, Nikolai Donets, explained the backend model pipeline supporting each generative product, where 9-12 metrics are checked by LLM judges and experts.
The closest British parallel to Bloomberg’s approach is Cleo, a London-based money management app with annual recurring revenue exceeding $300m. Its chat assistant is powered by a combination of commercial LLMs. But this year, Cleo trained a small proprietary model on its own conversation data to perform a single task: determining which agent should handle each message. It’s a miniature version of Bloomberg’s strategy: hand the core work to ready-made models and build a proprietary one only for a highly specialised segment where proprietary data provides an advantage.
At the same time, model providers have come to finance themselves. On May 5, 2026, Anthropic released ten prebuilt agent templates for the most labour-intensive work in financial services. Today Claude connects to dozens of market data providers, research platforms and financial companies internal systems.
And where a custom model is still needed, it no longer has to be big or built from scratch. Fin-R1, first released in 2025 and last updated in March 2026, is an openly available model fine-tuned for finance. It is a fraction of BloombergGPT’s size and, despite this, demonstrates competitive results across financial benchmarks.
The UK has a financial LLM of its own, but not one trained from scratch. Aveni, based in Edinburgh, launched FinLLM in May 2025. The model was developed exclusively for the UK financial services market and backed by an £11m Series A round, closed in July 2024 and led by Puma Private Equity, with Lloyds and Nationwide as investors and testing partners. Look what that means: over six months of work , building on the open-weight model Qwen 2.5 through continued pretraining, not training from scratch. In June 2026, Nationwide became the first organisation to deploy it in a live environment.
I didn’t find any UK fintech company that trained a large financial model from scratch.
Thomson Reuters looks like a clear counterexample. The company launched its own LLM, Thomson, in August 2026, and Computer Weekly said it spent some $40m on it. So does this prove the need for a financial company to have its own large-scale model? Let us have a look. Thomson Reuters didn’t create the model from scratch, but started from an open-source foundation model and trained it with proprietary content collected over decades. CoCounsel Legal “remains multi-model by design”, the company says : it applies Thomson “where it delivers the clearest advantage and other leading models elsewhere”. This is Bloomberg in 2026, not BloombergGPT in 2023. It is not a counterexample at all. Like Bloomberg, Thomson Reuters sells unique data. A bank or a regular fintech has far less of that.
I would say that a single large custom financial LLM is rather a mirage nowadays. One was trained by Bloomberg, which does not use this model in any of its products in 2026.
The small bespoke models for particular tasks and the off-the-shelf commercial models are not a mirage.
I would advise growing financial companies that plan to build their own products to consider Bloomberg’s experience.
Bloomberg trains small custom models only for specific tasks where off-the-shelf models aren’t powerful enough. Also, the company fine-tunes existing open-source models on its own financial content. For the tasks where commercial models, such as OpenAI, Google or Anthropic, perform better or cost less, the team integrates them. Eventually, Bloomberg’s ASKB product delegates each task to the cheapest model that can handle it, and the team configures task routing between these models based on latency and cost.
If you follow the same approach instead of training one big model, you can create your own AI-powered financial product, whether an internal assistant, a decision-making tool or a document processing system. The most sensitive data remains inside the company and is processed by custom models hosted on your server, while the remaining tasks are transferred to ready-made commercial models via their APIs.
Dmitry Baraishuk is a partner and chief technology officer at Belitsoft , a software engineering company serving fintech, healthcare and enterprise SaaS clients in the UK, US and Canada.
I love understanding strategy and innovation using the business model canvas tool so much that I decided to share my analysis by creating a website focused on this topic.

title: Zelensky Warns of Russia’s ‘Economic Marriage’ With US as Ukraine Feels ‘Home Alone’ Without Patriots
body:
Russia could offer the US an “economic marriage” built on energy and other economic deals, but it would likely come at a cost in the long run, President Volodymyr Zelensky said.
“I believe the ‘diesel deal’ opens the door for the Russians to take further similar steps,” Zelensky told journalists, as quoted by Ukrainian media .
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
He suggested that future agreements could involve fertilizers, gas, frozen assets, and the lifting of sanctions on specific individuals and entities.
He revealed that sanctions had already been lifted on Russian oligarchs close to Russian President Vladimir Putin.
“Russia understands that – unlike other nations – it possesses such natural resources, capabilities, reserves, and a centralized, vertical control over all of this, that it could genuinely propose a sort of ‘economic marriage’ to America – as unpleasant as that may sound,” Zelensky said.
However, he said that such an arrangement might not benefit Washington in the long run, even if it appeared advantageous initially.
“Every deal involving Russia contains some unpleasant element that isn’t immediately apparent – even if, in the short term, it might seem like there are benefits to be gained,” he said.
Zelensky warned that NATO should not agree to Russia’s demands for security guarantees while Moscow continues its war against Ukraine.
“If you want security guarantees for Ukraine, then we want them for Russia,” the Russian side has argued, according to Zelensky.
He said Moscow’s demands go far beyond assurances that Ukraine would not attack Russian territory, instead seeking a broader agreement with NATO or the US .
Zelensky added that Russia had raised similar demands before the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Moscow could again seek NATO’s withdrawal from certain territories or the removal of Alliance infrastructure, he said.
Such decisions, he stressed, rest with NATO member states – not Russia or Ukraine. Zelensky also warned that any rollback in security would signal weakness for the Alliance.
“One cannot discuss any global security guarantees for Russia while it remains unclear how – and on what basis – their war against Ukraine will end, and before we know what security guarantees Ukraine itself will have,” he said.
Zelensky added that the issue of the war must be resolved before Russia’s demands regarding the European and global security architecture can be addressed.
He also acknowledged that Washington had sent signals about a possible reduction in the number of US troops stationed in Europe.
Zelensky said the war in the Middle East had negatively affected military and financial support for Ukraine, including supplies of air defense missiles. He pointed to the situation around the Strait of Hormuz as one factor contributing to global energy pressures.
According to Zelensky, Ukraine received just 12 US missiles per month for its Patriot air defense systems throughout 2026.
He said the amount was far below Ukraine’s needs, as Russia launches approximately 150 ballistic missiles against the country each month.
Even if Ukraine received 150 US interceptor missiles a year, Zelensky said, it would still face a significant gap between available supplies and the demands of defending against Russian attacks.
Ukraine is working with partners to secure additional anti-ballistic missiles, but transfers of US-made interceptors require approval from US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, he added.
Zelensky said several issues had converged in Ukraine’s relations with Washington, including Starlink and Starshield, intelligence sharing, interceptor missile supplies, and agreements concerning Russian diesel .
“We understand where things are heading. It’s like the next installment of Home Alone. It is a challenge – a tough challenge,” he said.
The president also said Ukraine had provided assistance to Middle Eastern partners at their request, including support related to bases hosting American personnel in Saudi Arabia and the UAE. He added that ending the regional crisis was important for Ukraine, too.
Separately, Zelensky confirmed that Ukraine and the US had resumed intelligence sharing, thanking US President Donald Trump, military officials, and others who helped make the decision possible.
“We are grateful to our American partners – to everyone who made this happen: President Donald Trump, the military, and everyone else who helped,” Zelensky said.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Aselsan CEO says record $30.7 billion backlog makes capacity and deliveries the priority
body: The backlog rose by $7.5 billion from the previous quarter, while new export contracts increased 34% to $1.9 billion. Its book-to-bill ratio reached 4.4, which Akyol said signalled a substantial workload extending into future years. “Securing orders far above sales volume signals a robust and sustained workload in the years to come,” Akyol said. “Our primary responsibility moving forward is to convert this portfolio into timely deliveries, expanded production capacity, and sustained technological superiority.” The first phase of the Oğulbey Technology Base became operational during the period, following the start of construction in 2025. Aselsan also commissioned a Guided Ammunition Systems Production Centre and strengthened robotics and automation across air, naval and land defence manufacturing. Revenue reached TL 151.5 billion, up 28% in real terms from the first nine months of 2025. EBITDA increased 38% to TL 40.6 billion, and its margin widened by 190 basis points to 26.8%. “This improvement was driven by the effective use of Artificial Intelligence in our processes, the impact of digital transformation, and the growing share of higher value-added products in our portfolio,” Akyol said. “We are not only measuring growth by its volume, but by its quality.” Research and development expenditure rose 36% to $1.3 billion. Priorities include low-Earth-orbit satellites, quantum computing, underwater systems, high-power microwaves, microelectronics, smart ammunition and propulsion technologies. Akyol said the ASTRALINK project would extend Aselsan’s communications business into satellite services. The company presented its low-orbit satellite concept at the International Space Congress in Antalya. “Maintaining financial discipline while executing our investments remains one of our top priorities,” Akyol said. “We have invested nearly twice the amount of last year’s total capital expenditure within the first nine months of this year.” Operating cash flow reached TL 23 billion, while financing expenses fell 10.3% from the corresponding period of 2025. Financial liabilities represented 14% of total assets, and return on equity rose by 400 basis points to 16.6%. Akyol said rising defence budgets and greater emphasis on supply-chain security and technological sovereignty were increasing interest in Aselsan’s products. He described the company’s objective as becoming one of the world’s leading defence technology businesses. Go deeper: Aselsan .

title: Senior Russian diplomat describes Africa as one of key areas for BRICS development
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Africa is one of the key areas for the development of BRICS over the coming decades, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov said at the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.
"The African direction is not merely an important part of the agenda, but one of the primary vectors for the development of BRICS over the coming decades," he said.
"Relevant cooperation frameworks with African countries have been defined across a range of areas, such as the creation of an informal BRICS cooperation platform involving African diamond-producing nations. We are also moving toward the establishment of a BRICS grain exchange, a direct response to the continent’s needs, and are expanding Africa’s representation within the BRICS New Development Bank. In addition to South Africa, one of the bank’s founding members, Egypt and Algeria have also joined it in recent years," Ryabkov added.
"Further increase in the number of the New Development Bank’s shareholders by adding African nations could help to further diversify its portfolio of investment projects, including by extending into the agricultural sector," he noted.
BRICS was established in 2006, while South Africa joined its original members (Brazil, Russia, India, and China) in 2011. Egypt, Iran, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Ethiopia joined the group on January 1, 2024, followed by Indonesia on January 6, 2025. Moreover, since the beginning of last year, Belarus, Bolivia, Kazakhstan, Cuba, Malaysia, Thailand, Uganda, and Uzbekistan officially attained the status of its partners, with Nigeria having joined on January 17 and Vietnam on June 14.

title: Top 68 concerts and events coming to the UAE, from Jennifer Lopez to Mariah Carey
body: From pop and rock to stand-up comedy, ballet, opera and musicals, the UAE’s live events season is in full swing, with the months ahead offering a packed line-up across Abu Dhabi, Dubai and Sharjah. Mariah Carey will return to Abu Dhabi with her Christmas-time show in December, while Wasla Festival brings regional acts, including Marcel Khalife, Le Trio Joubran, TootArd and Fatima to Expo City Dubai in November. Najwa Karam will bring her greatest hits to Dubai’s Coca-Cola Arena, while Abu Dhabi Comedy Season has announced shows led by Palestinian-American star Mo Amer and US comic Aries Spears. Abu Dhabi Grand Prix weekend will feature Jennifer Lopez , with the pop star completing the after-race concert line-up at Etihad Live alongside Lewis Capaldi, Kings of Leon , Alex Warren, Imagine Dragons, The Chainsmokers and The Script. Looking ahead to 2027, Shah Rukh Khan curate the inaugural Unifyd festival at Etihad Live, with Arijit Singh, Karan Aujla and Sonu Nigam among the first artists announced. Here, we round up the concerts and live events still to come in the UAE. 1. The Fridge Concert Series Season 50 Special: October 27 at The Fridge Warehouse, Alserkal Avenue, Dubai The Fridge marks the 50th season of its concert series with a reunion night featuring former performers from across its 20-year history. The line-up is being kept under wraps, with collaborations and jam sessions planned for the limited-capacity show. Free; pre-registration required 2. Titize: A Venetian Dream: October 29 to 31 at Dubai Opera Venice is the inspiration for this show mixing circus, theatre, dance and live music. The 10-member cast use acrobatics, clowning and physical theatre to create a dreamlike version of Venice through its masks, waterways and carnival traditions. Shows at 2pm and 8pm; tickets from Dh275 3. Nass: October 30 at The Arts Centre at NYU Abu Dhabi French-Moroccan choreographer Fouad Boussouf brings together seven male dancers in a work connecting hip-hop movement with the ritual dimensions of North African music. The title takes inspiration from Moroccan group Nass El Ghiwane and draws parallels between their search for identity and the origins of hip-hop. Show starts 7.30pm; tickets from Dh52.50 4. Abdul Majeed Abdullah: October 31 at Coca-Cola Arena, Dubai Saudi singer Abdul Majeed Abdullah returns to Dubai with a catalogue spanning decades of Khaleeji and Arabic pop. Known for a distinctive vocal style that has helped shape Gulf music, his songs include Mn Mithlek , Tetnafasek Denyaay , Yabn Elawadem and Ghazal Ma Yensady . Show starts 9.30pm; tickets from Dh495 5. Riverdance: October 31 and November 1 at Etihad Arena, Abu Dhabi Riverdance returns to the UAE with a production marking the Irish dance show’s 30th anniversary. The staging retains Bill Whelan’s Grammy Award-winning score while introducing updated choreography, costumes, lighting, projection and motion graphics. Performance times vary; tickets from Dh215 6. Benjamin Clementine: November 1 at Dubai Opera British singer, pianist and composer Benjamin Clementine performs a programme combining experimental pop, contemporary classical music, jazz and poetry. His debut album, At Least for Now , won the Mercury Prize, while later recordings include I Tell a Fly and And I Have Been . Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh500 7. Jony: November 4 at Coca-Cola Arena, Dubai Russian-Azerbaijani singer Jony is a star Russian pop and built a following with songs including Kamin , Kometa and Ty Besposhchadna . Show starts 9pm; tickets from Dh295 8. Mo Amer: November 6 at Etihad Arena, Abu Dhabi Palestinian-American comedian Mo Amer performs as part of Abu Dhabi Comedy Season. Born in Kuwait to Palestinian parents and raised in the US, his comedy draws on displacement, immigration and life between cultures. Those experiences also shaped Mo , the semi-autobiographical Netflix series he created with Ramy Youssef, which won a Peabody Award in 2023. Show time and ticket prices to be announced 9. Maz Jobrani: November 7 at Etihad Arena, Abu Dhabi Iranian-American comedian Maz Jobrani returns to Abu Dhabi with material exploring immigrant experiences, cultural misunderstandings and family expectations. He previously performed at the inaugural Abu Dhabi Comedy Week in 2024 on a shared bill with Bassem Youssef. Show time and ticket prices to be announced 10. Ministry of Sound Classical: November 7 at Dubai Opera Club anthems are given an orchestral spin as Ministry of Sound Classical brings dance music into the concert hall. Conducted by David Mahoney, the show combines a full orchestra and vocalists with electronic music, lighting and visuals, drawing on tracks associated with decades of club culture. Show time and ticket prices to be announced 11. Abdelkader Secteur: November 8 at Emirates Theatre, Dubai Algerian comedian Abdelkader Secteur returns to Dubai with a stand-up show drawing on family life, cultural traditions and everyday situations. Known for storytelling rooted in North African humour, he follows a previous Dubai appearance last year. Show starts 7.30pm; tickets from Dh195 12. American Ballet Theatre: November 20 at Emirates Palace, Abu Dhabi Dubbed one of the world's greatest dance companies, the American Ballet Theatre will perform works including Frederick Ashton’s Birthday Offering , Jiri Kylian’s Nuages , Brady Farrar’s Trio Elegiaque and Paquita , staged by Natalia Makarova after Marius Petipa. Show starts 8pm, tickets from Dh125 13. Aries Spears: November 21 at Etihad Arena, Abu Dhabi American comedian Aries Spears brings more than three decades of stand-up, impressions and crowd work to Etihad Arena. A former Mad TV cast member, he is known for his celebrity impersonations that include Michael Jackson, Eddie Murphy and Shaquille O'Neal. Doors open 9pm; show starts 10pm; tickets from Dh120 14. Synthony x Faithless: November 21 at Bla Bla by McGettigan's, Dubai Synthony makes its Middle East debut with a full orchestra reworking electronic dance anthems through live instrumentation, vocals and visual production. The night will also feature Faithless Sound System, led by Sister Bliss, with tracks including Insomnia and We Come 1 . Doors open 6pm; tickets from Dh295 15. Trevor Noah: November 25-26 and November 28 and 29 at Dubai Opera Trevor Noah brings a new stand-up show to Dubai across four nights. The Emmy Award-winning South African comedian and former host of The Daily Show has released several Netflix specials, hosts the podcast What Now? with Trevor Noah and is the author of Born a Crime and Into the Uncut Grass . Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh295 16. Algarabia: November 26 at Emirates Palace, Abu Dhabi Algarabia presents a theatrical production blending flamenco with Arabic poetry, performed by musicians from Spain’s University of Navarra Symphony Orchestra alongside dancers and actors. The work follows the journey of an Arab girl drawn to ancient botanical theory and poetic tradition. Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh100 17. Bader Saleh: November 27 at The Hive, Dubai Saudi comedian Bader Saleh brings his Bliss of Ignorance stand-up show to Dubai. He rose to prominence through the YouTube series EyshElly and has since worked across television, online comedy and live performance. Show starts 9pm; tickets from Dh175 18. Hiba Tawaji and Ibrahim Maalouf: November 27 at Dubai Opera Hiba Tawaji and Ibrahim Maalouf will unite for a one-night performance at Dubai Opera, with the programme drawing on French musical heritage through a blend of chanson, jazz and contemporary composition. Tawaji’s emotive vocals and Maalouf’s genre-crossing trumpet work make this one of the more distinctive concert pairings on the calendar. Show starts 8.30pm; tickets from Dh355 19. Atif Aslam: November 27 at Coca-Cola Arena, Dubai Atif Aslam returns to Coca-Cola Arena after five consecutive years of sold-out Dubai concerts. The Pakistani singer’s programme will move between Bollywood songs, pop-rock and devotional music, with hits including Tajdar-e-Haram , Jeena Jeena , Pehli Nazar Mein , Dil Diyan Gallan and Aadat . Doors open 9pm; tickets from Dh350 20. Tarkan: November 27 at Etihad Arena, Abu Dhabi Known internationally for the global hit Simarik and a catalogue that has defined Turkish pop for more than two decades, Tarkan is making his Abu Dhabi debut is further proof of Turkish’s pop growing popularity in the region. Show starts 8.30pm; tickets from Dh295 21. Wasla Festival: November 28 at Jubilee Park, Expo City Dubai Lebanese composer and oud player Marcel Khalife headlines the return of Wasla Festival, alongside Palestinian ensemble Le Trio Joubran, Syrian duo TootArd and Emirati-Honduran singers Fatima . Starts 6pm; tickets from Dh350 22. Ramy Sabry: November 28 at Etihad Arena, Abu Dhabi Egyptian singer Ramy Sabry comes to Abu Dhabi with a catalogue of romantic Arabic pop and ballads. His songs include Lama Bywhashny , alongside a wider repertoire centred on love, memory and heartbreak. Doors open 7.30pm; show starts 9pm; tickets from Dh295 23. Artbat Present Upperground: November 28 at Ushuaia Dubai Harbour Experience Ukrainian electronic duo Artbat bring their Upperground event series to Dubai, joined by Miss Monique, R3hab and Italian DJ and producer 7 Skies. The show follows Artbat’s recent reworking of Gotye's Somebody That I Used to Know with David Guetta. Doors open 8pm; tickets from Dh150 24. Verdi’s Opera Gala: November 29 at Emirates Palace, Abu Dhabi Marking 125 years since Giuseppe Verdi’s death, this programme is led by soprano Maria Agresta and tenor Giorgio Berrugi, and includes selections from Nabucco , I Vespri Siciliani , Otello and La Traviata , alongside overtures and duets drawn from Verdi’s wider catalogue. Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh125 25. Ghostly Kisses: November 29 at Etihad Arena, Abu Dhabi Canadian singer-songwriter Margaux Sauve brings her Ghostly Kisses project to Abu Dhabi as part of her 2026 regional tour. Her music combines atmospheric pop, understated electronic production and intimate vocals, with songs including The City Holds My Heart . Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh215 26. Andrea Bocelli: December 2 at Etihad Arena, Abu Dhabi Italian tenor Andrea Bocelli brings his 30th Anniversary Romanza World Tour to Abu Dhabi as part of Yasalam Classics. The concert celebrates Romanza , the album that helped establish him internationally and includes songs such as Con te partiro and Vivo per lei . Doors open 6pm; tickets from Dh295 27. The Tsar's Bride by the Bolshoi Theatre: December 2 at Dubai Opera The Bolshoi Theatre begins its first official UAE tour with Rimsky-Korsakov's The Tsar's Bride . Set during the reign of Ivan the Terrible, the opera centres on Marfa, a young woman whose selection as the tsar's bride sets off jealousy, rivalry and political intrigue. Show time and ticket prices to be announced 28. Bolshoi Theatre Orchestra, December 3 The Bolshoi Theatre Orchestra takes centre stage for a symphonic concert on the second night of the company’s first official UAE tour. Showtime and ticket prices TBC 29. Lewis Capaldi and Kings of Leon: December 3 at Etihad Park, Abu Dhabi Lewis Capaldi and Kings of Leon will open the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix 2026 after-race concert series with separate sets at Etihad Park. Zara Larsson was initially on the bill but has been replaced by the American band. Capaldi returns to the capital following his Saadiyat Nights performance in January, bringing a catalogue that includes Someone You Loved , Before You Go and Forget Me . The occasion marks Kings of Leon's return to the Abu Dhabi F1 concerts, having made their Middle East concert debut at the inaugural Abu Dhabi Grand Prix in 2009. The show launches the four-night programme running alongside the race weekend at Yas Marina Circuit. Showtime yet to be announced; access exclusive to Abu Dhabi Grand Prix ticket holders 30. Jennifer Lopez and Alex Warren: December 4 at Etihad Live, Abu Dhabi Jennifer Lopez returns to Abu Dhabi for the second night of the Grand Prix after-race concert series, sharing the bill with US singer-songwriter Alex Warren. Lopez's catalogue includes If You Had My Love , Waiting for Tonight , Jenny from the Block and On the Floor . Warren makes his UAE debut after the international success of Ordinary . Access exclusive to Abu Dhabi Grand Prix ticket holders 31. Shimza: December 4 at 16/360, Yas Marina Circuit, Abu Dhabi South African DJ Shimza brings his percussion-heavy Afro-tech sound to 16/360 as Abu Dhabi Grand Prix weekend gets under way. Known for extended, hypnotic sets, he has performed across Europe and Africa and collaborated with fellow South African DJ Black Coffee. Access exclusive to selected 16/360 Grand Prix hospitality ticket holders; packages from Dh1,250 32. Mont Rouge and Moojo: December 4 at Bagatelle, W Abu Dhabi, Abu Dhabi Swiss duo Mont Rouge and French DJ Moojo share the Friday bill at Bagatelle's rooftop pop-up during Abu Dhabi Grand Prix weekend. Mont Rouge are known for their Afro-house version of Voyage Voyage , recorded with Francis Mercier and Coco, as well as their remix of Axwell and Sebastian Ingrosso's More Than You Know . Tables from Dh7,000 33. The Nutcracker by the Bolshoi Theatre: December 4 to 6 at Dubai Opera The Nutcracker has become a Dubai Opera tradition, and this year's production will feature the Bolshoi Theatre, with Tchaikovsky's ballet performed by the company's dancers and orchestra. Yuri Grigorovich's choreography follows Marie from a family Christmas celebration into a fantasy world of toys and magic, set to a score containing some of Tchaikovsky's best-known music. Show times and ticket prices to be announced 34. Anyma: December 4 at Yas Gateway Park, Abu Dhabi Italian-American DJ and producer Anyma will perform at Yas Gateway Park as part of the official Abu Dhabi Grand Prix after party concert series. Known for large-scale audiovisual shows and melodic techno, he brought his dazzling live production to the Pyramids of Giza in 2025 and has become one of electronic music’s most distinctive live acts through his work as a solo artist and as one half of Tale of Us. Abu Dhabi Grand Prix ticket holder presales begin on September 10, with general sales opening on September 11; show time and ticket prices to be announced 35. Imagine Dragons: December 5 at Etihad Live, Abu Dhabi Imagine Dragons will headline the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix after-race concert series on Saturday night. Fronted by Dan Reynolds, the US band are known for songs including Believer , Radioactive , Demons , Thunder and It’s Time . The group last performed in Abu Dhabi in 2023, when they sold out Etihad Arena. Showtime yet to be announced; access exclusive to Abu Dhabi Grand Prix ticket holders 36. CamelPhat: December 5 at 16/360, Yas Marina Circuit, Abu Dhabi British electronic duo CamelPhat take over the trackside 16/360 venue on the second night of its Grand Prix programme. Dave Whelan and Mike Di Scala broke through internationally with the Grammy-nominated Cola , while their catalogue also includes Panic Room with Au/Ra and Breathe with Cristoph and Jem Cooke. Access exclusive to selected 16/360 Grand Prix hospitality ticket holders; packages from Dh1,250 37. Gordo: December 5 at Bagatelle, W Abu Dhabi, Abu Dhabi DJ and producer Gordo, formerly known as Carnage, joins Bagatelle's race-weekend programme with his house-focused sound. He contributed to Drake's 2022 album Honestly, Nevermind and released his debut album Diamante in 2024, featuring collaborations with Drake and Maluma. Tables from Dh10,000 38. The Chainsmokers and The Script: December 6 at Etihad Live, Abu Dhabi The Chainsmokers and The Script will close the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix after-race concert series with separate sets on race day. Irish band The Script are known for songs including Breakeven , The Man Who Can’t Be Moved , For the First Time and Hall of Fame . US electronic duo The Chainsmokers bring a catalogue that includes Roses , Don’t Let Me Down , Closer , Paris and Something Just Like This . Showtime yet to be announced; access exclusive to Abu Dhabi Grand Prix ticket holders 39. Black Coffee: December 6 at 16/360, Yas Marina Circuit, Abu Dhabi Grammy-winning South African DJ Black Coffee closes the three-night 16/360 programme on race day with his blend of deep house, African percussion and soulful vocals. His album Subconsciously , featuring collaborations with Pharrell Williams and David Guetta, won the Grammy Award for Best Dance/Electronic Music Album. Access exclusive to selected 16/360 Grand Prix hospitality ticket holders; packages from Dh1,250 40. Carl Cox: December 6 at Bagatelle, W Abu Dhabi, Abu Dhabi British DJ Carl Cox closes Bagatelle's Grand Prix weekend programme. A pioneer of Britain's acid-house movement, he has spent more than four decades playing house and techno and held a 15-year residency at Space Ibiza. His links with motorsport extend beyond the weekend through Carl Cox Motorsport, which he founded in 2013. Tables from Dh10,000 41. Enrico Macias: December 10 at Dubai Opera More than six decades of chanson and Mediterranean music feature in Enrico Macias’s latest Dubai concert. The French-Algerian singer is known for Adieu mon pays , Les filles de mon pays and Enfants de tous pays . The concert is reportedly among his final international appearances. Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh295 42. Lisa Batiashvili and Giorgi Gigashvili: December 10 at The Arts Centre at NYU Abu Dhabi Georgian musicians Lisa Batiashvili and Giorgi Gigashvili will perform works by Beethoven, Bartok and Franck, alongside a contemporary piece by composer Josef Bardanashvili. Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh150 43. Minsoo Sohn: December 11 at The Arts Centre at NYU Abu Dhabi Pianist Minsoo Sohn will perform Book One of Bach’s Well-Tempered Clavier , presenting the 24 preludes and fugues that explore every major and minor key. The recital highlights both the intellectual depth and emotional breadth of the landmark work. Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh150 44. Sole DXB: December 11 to 13 at The Square, Nad Al Sheba, Dubai Sole DXB returns with three days of live music, DJ sets, fashion, art and street culture. The line-up includes British singer Lola Young, electronic duo Overmono, jungle producer Nia Archives, Malian musician Fatoumata Diawara, Matthew Herbert, Peter Cat Recording Co, Hajaj, Gia Fu, and Maii and Zeid. Runs from 4pm to 2.30am each day; three-day tickets from Dh495 45. Bamboo and Cup of Joe: December 11 at Dubai World Trade Centre, Dubai Filipino acts Bamboo and Cup of Joe share the stage for a night of OPM at Dubai World Trade Centre. Bamboo brings songs including Masaya , while Cup of Joe's catalogue includes Multo . Show starts 7pm; tickets from Dh129 46. Guy Manoukian: December 11 at Dubai Opera Guy Manoukian marks Dubai Opera's 10th anniversary by returning for his own milestone 10th performance at the venue, following nine sold-out shows. The Lebanese-Armenian pianist and composer blends original work with Arabic melodies and contemporary arrangements, with his repertoire also drawing on the music of Fairouz and Abdel Halim Hafez. Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh330 47. Mariah Carey: December 12 at Etihad Arena, Abu Dhabi Mariah Carey returns to Abu Dhabi with her Christmastime show, featuring festive songs including All I Want for Christmas Is You , Santa Baby and Christmas (Baby Please Come Home) alongside hits from her wider catalogue. The concert will be her second Abu Dhabi performance of the year, following her Saadiyat Nights show in February. Doors open 7pm; tickets from Dh249 48. Mahmut Orhan: December 12 at Ushuaia Dubai Harbour Experience, Dubai Turkish DJ and producer Mahmut Orhan returns to Dubai Harbour after performing there on New Year's Eve. His sound moves between deep house and indie dance, and he has performed at festivals including Coachella, Ultra Europe and Awakenings. Doors open 8pm; tickets from Dh150 49. Chicago the Musical: December 16 to 20 at Coca-Cola Arena, Dubai The Broadway production of Chicago comes to Coca-Cola Arena for eight performances over five days. Set during the Jazz Age, the musical follows nightclub performer Roxie Hart and vaudeville star Velma Kelly as they compete for public attention while awaiting trial for murder. The score includes All That Jazz , Cell Block Tango and Razzle Dazzle . Performance times vary; tickets from Dh49 50. Denis Matsuev: December 16 at Dubai Opera Russian pianist Denis Matsuev moves between classical repertoire and jazz in a concert titled Classics and Jazz . Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh350 51. Abracadabra: December 18 and 19 at Dubai Opera Gulf theatre comes to Dubai Opera with Abracadabra , an Arabic language suspense comedy about two struggling theatre groups trying to save their careers. Their plan to stage a new show inside an abandoned theatre is disrupted by strange events, unexpected twists and a series of comic situations. The production runs for about an hour and blends Gulf theatre, suspense and entertainment. Show times vary; tickets from Dh230. 52. Dopa World: December 18 to 20 at Jubilee Park, Expo City Dubai Dopa World is a three-day festival focused on young Arab music, culture and creative businesses. Saint Levant is the first announced artist, with the Palestinian-Algerian performer known for blending Arabic, English and French across songs including Very Few Friends and Deira . The remaining artists are yet to be announced. Doors open 4pm daily; tickets from Dh245 53. Dhafer Youssef: December 19 at The Arts Centre at NYU Abu Dhabi Oud maestro Dhafer Youssef will perform with his quintet, bridging sounds from the East and West through jazz, Arab and North African traditions, as well as European classical and electronic elements. He is expected to perform material from his latest album Shiraz , described as his most personal work to date. Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh150 54. Yassar Lemghari: December 25 at Emirates Theatre, Dubai Moroccan comedian Yassar Lemghari brings his Lamhayab show to Dubai, performed in Moroccan Darija. His stand-up draws on Moroccan culture and everyday life and follows a series of international performances. Doors open 8pm; show starts 8.30pm; tickets from Dh169 55. Rahat Fateh Ali Khan and Shah Zaman Ali Khan: December 26 at Coca-Cola Arena, Dubai Rahat Fateh Ali Khan returns to Coca-Cola Arena for his eighth appearance at the venue, joined by Shah Zaman Ali Khan. The concert brings together Qawwali, Sufi music and contemporary South Asian songs, with Shah Zaman continuing the musical tradition of the family into a new generation. Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh95 56. Katy Perry: December 31 at Atlantis, The Palm, Dubai Katy Perry returns to the UAE to headline the New Year's Eve gala at Atlantis The Palm, a year after closing the 2025 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. The American pop star brings a catalogue including Teenage Dream , Roar , Dark Horse and Firework . The black-tie gala also features a 30-piece live band, entertainment throughout the evening and a midnight fireworks display across Atlantis Dubai on Palm Jumeirah. Doors open 7pm; tickets from Dh6,500 for children and Dh8,500 for adults 57. Vessbroz: December 31 at Cavo, Ramee Dream Hotel, Dubai Vessbroz headline Cavo’s New Year’s Eve party with a set built around electronic house music and Middle East-inspired sounds. The line-up also includes Bazz Key, Qtee Rue, Taina and Hellfox. Doors open 10pm; tickets from Dh150. 58. Tony Ann: January 12, 2027, at Dubai Opera Canadian pianist and composer Tony Ann makes his Dubai debut with a programme blending contemporary piano and classical influences. Known for his viral #playthatword series and the Emotionally Blue, Orange and Red EP trilogy, Ann has also co-written The Chainsmokers tracks Sick Boy and Call You Mine . 59. Swan Lake on Ice: January 14 to 17, 2027, at Dubai Opera Tchaikovsky’s Swan Lake is reimagined on ice by the Imperial Ice Stars, with 24 skaters bringing together figure skating, ballet, aerial movement and theatrical choreography. The production follows the story of Odette, Prince Siegfried and Rothbart, with snowfall, fog, pyrotechnic effects and elaborate costumes adding to the staging. Show times vary by date; auditorium doors open 30 minutes before each performance; tickets from Dh300 60. Buena Vista Social Club Legacy Concert: January 24, 2027 at Dubai Opera Cuban music takes over Dubai Opera with a concert featuring Ibrahim Ferrer Jr, son of Buena Vista Social Club singer Ibrahim Ferrer, alongside veteran laud player Barbarito Torres Billed as Una Noche En La Habana , the show draws on son, bolero and other Cuban traditions associated with the musicians who brought Buena Vista Social Club to international audiences in the late 1990s. Show time and ticket prices to be announced 61. Tamaas Festival: January 29, 2027, at The Arts Centre at NYU Abu Dhabi Tamaas Festival returns with three acts moving between traditional forms and club-orientated production. Moroccan-Swiss musician Sami Galbi combines rai and chaabi with electronic music, while Nigerien guitarist Bombino performs Tuareg desert blues and rock. British collective Ibibio Sound Machine close the evening with West African rhythms, post-punk, disco and electronic music. Festival starts 7pm; free pass upon registration 62. Harry Potter Film Concert Series: February 5 to 6, 2027, at Etihad Arena, Abu Dhabi The UAE National Orchestra accompanies two Harry Potter films across consecutive nights. John Williams’ stirring score for Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban is performed on February 5, followed by Patrick Doyle’s music for Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire on February 6. Doors open 6.30pm; shows start 7.30pm; tickets from Dh120 63. Ramadaniyat – The Handover: February 17, 2027, at The Arts Centre at NYU Abu Dhabi Egyptian oud player Aly Eissa, Alexandrian violinist Ayman Asfour and Belgian-Norwegian keyboard player Jonas Cambien make their UAE debut as The Handover. The trio bring the ritual and folk music of rural Egypt into contact with free improvisation, psychedelic rock and electronic textures. Show starts 9.30pm; tickets from Dh52.50 64. The Phantom of the Opera: March 10 to 28, 2027 at Etihad Arena, Abu Dhabi Andrew Lloyd Webber's The Phantom of the Opera makes its Abu Dhabi debut with a three-week run at Etihad Arena. Based on Gaston Leroux's novel, the musical follows the masked phantom who lives beneath the Paris Opera House and becomes obsessed with soprano Christine Daae. The score includes The Music of the Night , All I Ask of You and the title song. The Abu Dhabi run comes during the musical's 40th anniversary year, following its West End premiere in 1986. Runs from March 10 to 28; tickets from Dh240 65. Unifyd: March 20, 2027 at Etihad Live, Abu Dhabi Arijit Singh, Karan Aujla and Sonu Nigam lead the inaugural Unifyd music festival curated by Bollywood star Shah Rukh Khan. The one-day event will feature more than 15 artists across several stages, spanning Hindi film music, Punjabi music and other strands of Indian culture. General sale opens October 20 at 10.30am through the District app; ticket prices to be announced 66. Tribute to Ziad Rahbani by Faraj Suleiman: March 26, 2027, at The Arts Centre at NYU Abu Dhabi Palestinian composer and pianist Faraj Suleiman returns with a programme dedicated to Lebanese composer, pianist and playwright Ziad Rahbani. Rather than reproducing the original recordings, Suleiman re-orchestrates and re-harmonises the material through contemporary piano, jazz and Arabic composition. Show starts 7.30pm; tickets from Dh78.75 67. A1 and Music Travel Love: April 17, 2027, at Coca-Cola Arena, Dubai British-Norwegian pop group A1 and Canadian duo Music Travel Love will share the stage for the first time in Dubai. A1 are known for hits including Everytime , Caught in the Middle and Like a Rose , while Music Travel Love, formed by twin brothers Bob and Clint Moffatt, are known for acoustic covers and originals including Nothing’s Gonna Change my Love for You . Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh295 68. Richard Marx: June 6, 2027 at Coca-Cola Arena, Dubai American singer-songwriter Richard Marx comes to Dubai with a catalogue spanning more than four decades. title: Conclusion of 33rd edition of Singapore-India Maritime Bilateral Exercise (SIMBEX-2026)
body:
New Delhi, Oct 27, 2026. The 33rd edition of the Singapore-India Maritime Bilateral Exercise (SIMBEX-2026), hosted by the Indian Navy at Visakhapatnam, concluded on 26 Oct 2026. The exercise further strengthened the longstanding maritime cooperation and operational engagement between the Indian Navy and the Republic of Singapore Navy (RSN).



As part of the bilateral engagement, Colonel Bertram Ang, Fleet Commander of the RSN, called on RAdm Vishal Bishnoi, Flag Officer Commanding Eastern Fleet, and exchanged professional views on strengthening maritime cooperation between the two countries. The meeting provided an opportunity to discuss matters of mutual interest.



SIMBEX-2026 was conducted in two phases. The Harbour Phase featured Subject Matter Expert Exchanges (SMEEs), cross-deck visits, professional interactions, sporting engagements and planning conferences, facilitating the exchange of operational knowledge and enhancing mutual understanding. The Sea Phase in the Bay of Bengal involved Maritime Interdiction Operations, Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW), Anti-Air Warfare and Anti-Surface Warfare drills, seamanship evolutions and cross-deck flying operations, enhancing coordination and interoperability between the participating forces.



The exercise witnessed the participation of RSN ship RSS Supreme, a Formidable-class stealth frigate with an embarked SH-70B helicopter. The Indian Navy was represented by the indigenously built stealth frigate INS Nilgiri, ASW corvette INS Kamorta and participating aviation assets, including P-8I and Dornier maritime patrol aircraft, Hawk Advanced Jet Trainers and MH-60R helicopters.



SIMBEX has served as an important platform for strengthening bilateral maritime cooperation, operational interoperability and professional engagement between India and Singapore. The exercise also demonstrated the commitment of both nations to enhancing maritime security and promoting stability in the Indian Ocean Region (IOR).

title: Generalissimo Suvorov nuclear-powered submarine test-launches Bulava ICBM
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. The Pacific Fleet’s strategic nuclear-powered missile submarine Generalissimo Suvorov has test-fired a Bulava intercontinental ballistic missile from a submerged position in the Sea of Okhotsk toward a test range in the Arkhangelsk Region, the Russian Defense Ministry reported.
"The crew of the Project 955A Borei-A class strategic nuclear-powered missile submarine Generalissimo Suvorov of the Pacific Fleet, in accordance with the combat training plan, test-fired a Bulava intercontinental ballistic missile aimed at the Chizha test range in the Arkhangelsk region," the ministry reported.
It noted that the missile launch was carried out from a submerged position in the Sea of Okhotsk in the Russian Far East.
The K-553 Generalissimo Suvorov is a fourth-generation Borei-A class nuclear-powered submarine (designed by the St. Petersburg-based Rubin Central Design Bureau for Marine Engineering). The sub features entirely new technical solutions, improved equipment, reduced physical fields, and enhanced protection. Its imported components have been replaced.
The submarine was laid down at the Sevmash Shipyard of the United Shipbuilding Corporation (USC) on December 26, 2014, and was commissioned into the Russian Navy in 2022. In October 2023, it completed its transfer from the Northern Fleet to the Pacific Fleet and arrived at its permanent base in Kamchatka. The primary armament of the Borei/Borei-A class strategic missile submarines includes 16 Bulava intercontinental ballistic missiles.

title: Africa to ensure its own food sovereignty in long term — Russian MFA
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Africa will be able to ensure its own food sovereignty in the future by reducing its reliance on external supplies and localizing production, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov said at the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.
"We proceed from the fact that in the long term Africa is certainly capable of providing itself with food. In this context, it becomes of paramount importance for African nations to achieve food sovereignty, meaning less reliance on external supplies by boosting crop yields, building up reserves, and localizing the production of finished food products," he said.
Moscow provides significant humanitarian assistance to Africa, Ryabkov noted. "Supplies of Russian agricultural products and food are often viewed by our friends in Africa as evidence of our country’s reliability and its readiness to support them during difficult times, and to do it selflessly," he said.

title: Yak-130M aircraft arsenal includes laser-guided precision weapons — Rostec
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. The arsenal of the Yak-130M combat training aircraft has been expanded to include laser-guided precision weapons, Russia’s state tech corporation Rostec reported.
"The modernized combat training aircraft of the United Aircraft Corporation (UAC) has gained the strike capability of a light attack aircraft. The aircraft’s arsenal has been expanded to include ‘smart’ munitions. Its new targeting systems, including the SOLT-130K pod with thermal imaging, television, and laser channels, enable the use of precision weapons in any weather conditions, day or night," the corporation noted.
Rostec emphasized that the aircraft’s primary armament consists of satellite-and laser-guided bombs. It also noted that despite its compact size, comparable to World War II-era fighter jets, the Yak-130M is capable of carrying a combat load of up to 2.5 tons. The weight of the guided bombs themselves can reach 500 kg.
The AI-222-25 nonafterburning turbojet engines, manufactured by the United Engine Corporation (UEC), enable the aircraft to carry such armament. They deliver powerful thrust at full capacity and are fuel-efficient. The aircraft’s digital automatic control and monitoring system ensures the propulsion system’s high reliability.

title: Teenager killed in attack on Israeli embassy in Serbia
body: A 16-year-old was shot dead after attacking a policeman outside the Israeli embassy in Belgrade, Serbia’s departing Interior Minister Ivica Dacic said, describing the incident as a terrorist act. The teenager, who has not yet been identified, appeared to have acted alone and attacked the officer guarding the embassy with two knives early on Wednesday, shouting “Allahu Akbar,” Mr Dacic said. The officer, who sustained a minor injury, killed the attacker in response, he added. Serbia has raised its security alert “to the highest level” after the attack, Dacic said. “Although the attacker’s identity has not been established, our services followed him and it’s known that he was a supporter of [ISIS],” Mr Dacic said, referring the attacker’s Instagram profile that featured a black flag and symbols of the terrorist group. In June 2024, another assailant used a crossbow to shoot a guard in the neck with an arrow outside the same embassy. Security guards at the embassy shot and killed the attacker in response. In the incident more than two years ago, officials described the assailant as a local man who embraced a hard-line interpretation of Islam. Authorities declared the attack an act of terrorism. The latest attack took place days after Serbia’s longtime President Aleksandar Vucic unexpectedly lost a general election to a leaderless, student-led movement in a major political upheaval for the Balkan country.

title: Kings of Leon replace Zara Larsson at Abu Dhabi F1 Grand Prix concert
body: Kings of Leon will return to the Abu Dhabi Formula One Grand Prix after-race concerts, replacing Swedish singer Zara Larsson on the opening night of the four-day series. The American rockers will co-headline the opening night with Scottish singer-songwriter Lewis Capaldi at Etihad Live on Thursday, December 3, as part of the concert series accompanying the season-ending race at Yas Marina Circuit. Organiser Ethara confirmed that Larsson, announced in February, is no longer able to perform. No reason was given for her withdrawal. Access to the after-race concerts is exclusive to Abu Dhabi Grand Prix ticket holders. The occasion marks Kings of Leon's return to the Abu Dhabi F1 concerts, having made their Middle East concert debut at the inaugural Abu Dhabi Grand Prix in 2009, a year after the release of their breakthrough fourth album, Only by the Night , which included the international hits Sex on Fire and Use Somebody . According to The National's report at the time , the band walked on stage to Mozart's Requiem before opening with Crawl . The concert was enthusiastically received, with the audience eager to hear the band's popular hits while also welcoming older material such as Molly's Chambers . The band returned to the UAE in 2014 for a concert at Atlantis, The Palm in Dubai, supporting their sixth album, Mechanical Bull . In its review, The National praised the band's tight musicianship during a 22-song set, particularly the blistering guitar work on Doesn't Matter and the furious rendition of Four Kicks . Their forthcoming Abu Dhabi appearance could also feature new material, coming shortly after the scheduled November 6 release of their 10th studio album, O My Beloved , their first entirely self-produced record. The 13-track album explores family, childhood memories and the band's early years, with a more acoustic-led sound heard on the lead single My Whole World . That direction reportedly emerged after frontman Caleb Followill broke his foot last year. During his recovery, he began writing songs on an acoustic guitar, prompting the band to abandon some of the electric guitar-driven material they had been developing. Comprising brothers Caleb, Nathan and Jared Followill and their cousin Matthew, Kings of Leon formed in Nashville in 1999 and released their debut album, Youth and Young Manhood , in 2003. They went on to win four Grammy Awards, including Record of the Year for Use Somebody in 2010. Capaldi, meanwhile, returns to the capital after a sold-out performance at Saadiyat Nights in January. Best known for songs including Someone You Loved and Before You Go , he was among the first artists announced for this year's F1 concerts. The announcement completes the four-night after-race concert line-up, with Jennifer Lopez and Alex Warren performing on December 4, Imagine Dragons on December 5, and The Chainsmokers and The Script closing the series on race day, December 6. The wider Grand Prix entertainment programme begins on December 2 with Andrea Bocelli at Etihad Arena. Other events include an official after-party with electronic musician Anyma and trackside DJ performances by Black Coffee, CamelPhat and Shimza, alongside club appearances across Yas Island.

title: FACT CHECK: Castro spoke about Rodrigo Duterte, not Marcos, in spliced drug-use clip
body: Claim: Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. admitted to using marijuana and abusing fentanyl because it felt like “cloud nine.” Rating: ALTERED Why we fact-checked this: A Facebook post by “Wilfredo Villacastel Orencejr,” published on October 24, carries the claim. Its caption reads, “Ay naku, Ante Claire binubuking mo na yung boss mo, Ante .” (Oh, Auntie Claire, you’re exposing your boss, auntie.) The video shows Castro speaking in a supposed interview, with a breaking news label overlaid on top. In the clip, Castro says, “Inamin mismo ni Pangulong Marcos Jr. na siya’y gumagamit ng marijuana, at inamin niya rin na ang paggamit niya ng fentanyl ay inabuso niya dahil masarap daw ang pakiramdam, cloud nine.” (President Marcos Jr. himself admitted that he uses marijuana, and he also admitted that he abused fentanyl because it supposedly felt good, cloud nine.) As of writing, the video has garnered over 709,000 views, 11,000 reactions, 1,300 comments, and 5,600 shares. The facts: Castro did not say Marcos used marijuana or abused fentanyl. The viral clip altered what she said during September 11 press briefing in New Delhi, where she was referring to former president Rodrigo Duterte. In the genuine clip, Castro was asked to respond to Vice President Sara Duterte’s accusation that Marcos was an “addict.” She said: “ Inamin mismo ni dating Pangulong Duterte, pangulo na siya, na siya’y gumagamit ng marijuana. At inamin niya rin na ang paggamit niya ng fentanyl ay inabuso niya dahil masarap daw ‘yung pakiramdam, ‘cloud nine’ ang feeling .” (Former president Duterte himself admitted, while already in office, that he used marijuana. He also admitted to abusing fentanyl because he enjoyed the feeling, describing it as being on “cloud nine.”) The viral clip replaces Duterte’s name with “ Pangulong Marcos Jr .” (President Marcos Jr.) and omits the phrase “ pangulo na siya ” (when he was already president). GMA News reported Castro’s original remarks, which match the Presidential Communications Office transcript and RTVM livestream on September 11. No credible report shows Marcos admitting to using marijuana or abusing fentanyl. Duterte’s original remarks: Duterte acknowledged using fentanyl in December 2016, saying he took it for a spinal injury from motorcycle accidents but had exceeded the prescribed dose. He denied being addicted, saying he used it only when prescribed. In a 2017 Davao City speech, he recalled using an entire fentanyl patch instead of cutting it into four pieces, saying it made him feel “on cloud nine,” the phrase Castro later repeated. He later told critics he had made up the fentanyl story. In 2018, Duterte said he used marijuana to stay awake during official functions, later calling the remark a joke . Both statements were made while he was president, as Castro said. Drug-use feud: Castro’s press briefing was a response to the Vice President’s accusation that Marcos was an “addict.” Duterte made the statement at her September 11 arraignment in Quezon City. The accusation against Marcos is not new. Senator Imee Marcos made a similar claim at a rally in November 2025, which Malacañang rejected , citing a negative drug test. Rappler also published a fact-check of a similar manipulated clip falsely attributing the remarks to Marcos, along with several other fact-checks debunking his alleged drug use: FACT CHECK: Marcos did not say cocaine use led to diverticulitis diagnosis FACT CHECK: Marcos not arrested over illegal drugs FACT CHECK: No proof cited in posts claiming ‘authenticated’ Marcos ‘polvoron’ video FACT CHECK: No Supreme Court-led raid, drug-related arrests in Malacañang – Cyril Bocar/Rappler.com Efren Cyril Bocar is a journalist from Llorente, Eastern Samar who graduated with a degree in English Language Studies at the Visayas State University. Cyril is also a graduate of the Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024. Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

title: Saab unveils new Sea Giraffe AMB D radar
body:
Saab has unveiled the Sea Giraffe Agile Multi Beam D (AMB D), a new naval radar designed to give maritime forces enhanced 3D surveillance and tracking of air and surface threats in increasingly contested environments.
The Sea Giraffe AMB D is a maritime 3D surveillance radar intended to detect, track, and classify air and surface targets, including aircraft, drones, missiles, and crewed or uncrewed vessels. It has a stated maximum range of 250 km against air targets and 50 km against surface targets.
The system provides target data intended to support early warning and decision-making in naval and multi-domain operations. It incorporates electronic counter-countermeasures designed to reduce the effect of jamming, and its modular, software-defined architecture is intended to allow integration with other naval systems and future upgrades.saab+1
Saab describes the radar as a C-band, multi-channel digital AESA system with simultaneous air and surface surveillance capabilities.
“Sea Giraffe AMB D takes a proven naval radar capability to the next level, combining increased performance with a low footprint and an architecture built for continuous development. It is designed to meet the demands of today’s naval forces while giving customers the flexibility to evolve with future threats,” said Carl-Johan Bergholm , head of Saab’s business area Surveillance.

title: Saab offers Canada third Gripen assembly line in bid to challenge F-35
body:
Saab is offering to establish a Gripen final assembly line in Canada as part of its attempt to secure a place in the country's future fighter fleet, just days after the Royal Canadian Air Force formally accepted its first two CF-35As.
The Swedish manufacturer said it plans to work with CAE, IMP Aerospace & Defence and Magellan Aerospace if Canada acquires the Gripen E, with production, final assembly, training and long-term support performed in the country.
The most significant part of the proposal is a new agreement with IMP to establish a Canadian final assembly line. The company would also produce electrical assemblies and provide in-service support for the Canadian fleet.
Magellan would manufacture aerostructures, composite structures and structural assemblies, while CAE would provide pilot and technician training, mission systems engineering and support.
Follow Air Data News: WhatsApp | Instagram | LinkedIn | Twitter | Facebook
If established, the Canadian facility would become the third final assembly line for the current Gripen E/F generation.
Saab builds the fighter at Linköping in Sweden, while Embraer recently began producing the aircraft at Gavião Peixoto in Brazil . The first Brazilian-built Gripen E made its maiden flight on October 6.
The industrial structure proposed by Saab is unusual considering the relatively modest production volume of the Gripen E/F.
There are currently 117 aircraft under firm order: 60 Gripen Es for Sweden, 36 Gripen E/Fs for Brazil, 17 for Colombia and four for Thailand.
Ukraine has also announced plans to acquire an initial batch of up to 20 Gripen E/Fs , but Saab said in May that negotiations were still underway and that it had not received an order.
A Canadian production line would therefore create a third final assembly location for a fighter that currently has little more than 100 firm orders worldwide.
Rather than concentrating production entirely in Sweden, Saab has made local manufacturing, technology transfer and industrial participation an important part of its international Gripen strategy.
Brazil is the most developed example. Embraer's Gavião Peixoto plant became the first Gripen final assembly facility outside Sweden, with Brazilian engineers and technicians participating in production and development under a technology-transfer program.
Saab and Embraer are also preparing the Brazilian operation to play a larger role in international production, with plans for additional aircraft to be manufactured there to serve potential export demand.
The Canadian proposal follows a similar model but goes further than simply assembling aircraft for the Royal Canadian Air Force.
IMP President David Gossen said the company sees an opportunity for the proposed facility to produce and support aircraft for other Gripen customers internationally, potentially making Canada another production center for the global program.
Canada selected the F-35A to replace its CF-188 Hornets and finalized an arrangement in 2022 for 88 aircraft. The government began reviewing the acquisition in March 2025, examining operational requirements, industrial benefits, strategic considerations and possible alternatives.
The first two Canadian aircraft were formally accepted this month at Luke Air Force Base in Arizona . They will remain in the United States for pilot and maintenance training, with the first CF-35As expected to arrive in Canada in 2028.
Canada remains committed to the initial 16 aircraft while the government considers how to proceed with the rest of the planned fleet.
That has left an opening for Saab to promote the Gripen as a potential component of a mixed fighter force, with domestic production becoming one of the central elements of its offer.
The industrial argument does not mean Canada currently lacks participation in the F-35 program. Canadian companies have supplied components and services to the multinational program for years, while facilities are also being prepared at Cold Lake and Bagotville to support the CF-35A fleet. Saab's proposal, however, would put final assembly of the fighter itself in Canada.

title: Niger Miners’ Deaths: Panel describes incident as preventable custodial tragedy
body:
The federal government has described the deaths of suspected illegal miners in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Niger State as a preventable custodial tragedy, blaming overcrowding, poor ventilation, extreme heat and dehydration.
The Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, stated this in a statement posted on his official Facebook page, following the submission of a report by a 10-member independent investigation committee set up to establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths.
Mr Tunji-Ojo said the committee found that the conditions inside the detention facility, rather than a disease outbreak, led to the fatalities.
“Thirty-three lives, including fourteen minors, were lost in what the Committee has established as a preventable custodial tragedy,” he said.
“The evidence points to severe overcrowding, inadequate ventilation, prolonged exposure to extreme heat and dehydration, and a systemic failure of duty of care within the detention facility. These conditions, rather than any disease outbreak, led to the fatalities.”
The minister said the report had been transmitted to the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation for immediate judicial action.
He added that officers who attempted to conceal, disrupt or destroy evidence would face suspension and accountability, while the government would undertake institutional reforms within the NSCDC.
Mr Tunji-Ojo also said supporting the bereaved families and survivors remained a priority.
The announcement follows a post by Deji Adeyanju, a member of the investigation committee, who said the panel had recommended prosecuting officers involved in the deaths for murder and other offences.
Mr Adeyanju also said the committee recommended a complete overhaul of the NSCDC leadership, compensation for the victims’ families and the formalisation of artisanal mining.
As PREMIUM TIMES reported on 28 October, Mr Adeyanju urged the federal government to act on the recommendations and file charges against officers found culpable.
The minister’s statement confirms that the report has been forwarded to the Attorney-General’s Office for further action.
However, he did not disclose whether the government had accepted the committee’s specific recommendation to prosecute officers for murder.
President Bola Tinubu directed a full investigation into the deaths, leading to the constitution of the 10-member committee on 19 September.
The committee was chaired by Jonathan Kure, a retired deputy director-general of the State Security Service, with Isa Hayatu Chiroma, a former director-general of the Nigerian Law School, serving as secretary.
The committee conducted five weeks of fieldwork, according to the minister, who commended its members for their work.
The incident followed the arrest of suspected illegal miners during operations in Minna on 15 and 16 September.
The detainees subsequently died in NSCDC custody, prompting public outrage and calls for accountability.
The Niger State NSCDC Commandant, Suberu Aniviye, and 20 other officers were suspended in connection with the incident.
On 27 October, TheCable reported that the committee had identified asphyxiation, or a lack of adequate oxygen, as the cause of death.
Its chairman, Mr Kure, said the panel had inspected the detention facility, conducted autopsies and collected witness statements and forensic evidence.
The minister’s latest statement provides further detail on the conditions the committee said led to the deaths, rejecting the earlier suggestion of a disease outbreak as the explanation.
The Attorney-General’s office is expected to consider the report for possible judicial action.
The government has not yet announced any charges arising from the investigation.
