title: A U.S. cruise ship ends voyage due to fuel costs and passengers lose their homes
body:
A US cruise ship MV. Odyssey docked at Sihanoukville Autonomous Port in Sihanoukville southern Cambodia, Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026. Heng Sinith/AP hide caption
SIHANOUKVILLE, Cambodia — A U.S. cruise ship on an around-the-world voyage that touted its cabins as floating homes suspended its three-year journey in Cambodia due to fuel costs, forcing hundreds of passengers to disembark.
The MV Odyssey set sail two years ago on a voyage to the seven continents marketed as combining long-term living at sea with global travel. Its operator had offered to "make the Odyssey your permanent home," with the purchase price of a suite for the lifetime of the vessel starting around $230,000.
For now, it is docked at the Cambodian port of Sihanoukville on the Gulf of Thailand, with no certain departure date.
The ship has been carrying 203 passengers, mostly Americans, along with 156 crew members, according to Cambodian officials. It has a 650-passenger capacity.
Its Florida-based operator, Villa Vie Residences, said monthly fuel expenses per cabin that historically averaged $1,800 have reached an estimated $6,000 to $8,000 in parts of Asia due to the war in Iran. The company said it sought to reduce fuel consumption by slowing the itinerary and spending more time in port, but was unable to offset the surging costs.
Traffic has been curtailed in the Strait of Hormuz since the war in Iran began, squeezing supplies of all kinds of petroleum-based fuels, especially in Southeast Asia, and sharply increasing prices.
"We have been unable to continue carrying the resulting operating losses," Villa Vie Residences said in a statement issued Tuesday. "Passing the full increase on to residents is not a realistic solution. Our focus now is on supporting residents, crew, and employees" while it tries to restructure.
"The company is working with residents to coordinate disembarkation and identify temporary living arrangements," it said.
Passengers, however, said they received no support and had to make their own arrangements after being given seven hours notice on Tuesday to disembark. Some were devastated and expressed hope a new company could rescue the venture so life at sea can continue.
Paul and Lynn Montoya, a retired couple from Wyoming, said they bought a window cabin and had expected to sail for years. They boarded the ship 17 months ago in Panama.
A couple passenger from a U.S. cruise ship, the MV Odyssey, Paul Montoya, left, stands for an interview with his wife, Lynn Motoya, at the Independence Hotel in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. Heng Sinith/AP hide caption
Paul praised the concept of residential cruising but said the shipowner lacked the expertise to make the business financially sustainable. While rising fuel costs had been cited publicly as the reason for the suspension, he said the company had already been struggling. Changes to itinerary, unreliable internet access and declining food quality had pushed many residents to leave the ship in recent months, he said.
Lynn said residents were repeatedly asked to contribute additional money for fuel and other expenses, including a fresh call to raise funds for fuel to get out of Cambodia. She said the crew members were also not paid.
"We were tired of every two to four weeks being asked for money for fuel, money for everything," she said. "We had hopes but they just kept sinking further and further into the hole through mismanagement."
The company could not immediately be contacted for comment.
Yet for some, even the financial and logistical turmoil couldn't outweigh the extraordinary experience of traveling the world and living at sea.
Carol Larson, 69, and her sister Crystal Lavering, 72, occupied separate cabins aboard the ship for 18 months. The siblings, from California, described the suspension as heartbreaking, and hoped the cruise would be resuscitated.
A sibling passenger from a U.S. cruise ship, the MV Odyssey, Carol Larson, 69, left, stands for an interview with her sister, Crystal Lavering, at the Independence Hotel in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. Heng Sinith/AP hide caption
"I hope there is a movement for the residents to buy the ship and I am hoping that goes through because it's a dream to live on the ship and I don't want it to end," Larson said.
Lavering said her health improved during her time on the ship, and that she didn't need to use a cane to walk anymore. "You come to this ship to live … it's just sad that it's all over."
Larson bought her cabin for $120,000, paid in installments, in addition to monthly maintenance fees, under a plan that had promised the possibility of living aboard for up to 15 years. She said she blamed U.S. President Donald Trump for the ship's woes as fuel costs spiked due to the Iran war, in addition to poor management. But she said she didn't regret her investment.
"Because it was a startup company, I believe that it was a risk. From the very first day, I said to myself that if it lasts a year, I can walk away and feel like I got my money's worth … I still feel that way. I feel blessed to have been part of the experiment of residential cruising," she said.
The ship arrived in Sihanoukville last Friday and was scheduled to depart Wednesday, according to a statement from Long Dimanche, the deputy governor of Preah Sihanouk province. He said it was now expected to refuel and depart Cambodia on Saturday, but the ship's operator has not yet publicly confirmed any date.
A U.S. cruise ship, the MV Odyssey, docks at the Sihanoukville Autonomous Port in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, late Wednesday evening, Oct. 28, 2026. Heng Sinith/AP hide caption
Built in 1993 and operated under different names by several cruise lines over the years before being becalmed by the coronavirus pandemic in 2020, the Odyssey was bought by Villa Vie Residences in 2023.
Its current cruise, originally intended to last 3 1/2 years, began in October 2024 in Belfast, Northern Ireland, where the ship had been refitted. A second cruise had been tentatively scheduled to end in August 2030.
The Odyssey is not the first cruise ship Sihanoukville has hosted in crisis.
In February 2020, the MS Westerdam was allowed to dock in Cambodia after being turned away at five ports in other nations because of fears of COVID-19, which just a month earlier had started to spread from China. It carried 1,455 passengers, more than 600 of them American citizens.
After being stranded at sea for two weeks, Cambodia's then-Prime Minister Hun Sen allowed it to dock for what he said were humanitarian reasons. Cambodia won plaudits as passengers were welcomed ashore and arrangements were made for them to fly home.

title: BAE to build thirty five thousand guidance kits a year
body: BAE Systems has signed a framework agreement running up to seven years with the United States Department of War to lift production of APKWS laser guidance kits to as many as thirty five thousand a year, according to the company. The kits turn unguided two point seven five inch rockets into precision guided munitions, and are in service with the United States Air Force, Army, Marine Corps and Navy. They are available to American allies and work in air-to-surface, surface-to-surface, surface-to-air and air-to-air engagements, including against drones. Tom Arseneault, president and chief executive of BAE Systems, Inc., said: “APKWS delivers proven, reliable and affordable precision at scale to counter evolving threats and ensure our warfighters maintain a decisive advantage. This agreement highlights the importance of sustained investment in critical munitions to strengthen readiness and equip forces for evolving operational needs.” Under the framework the company will increase production while negotiating a multi-year contract within it, which the company described as surge-ready support for evolving operational demands. BAE Systems said it has invested in manufacturing capacity, materials and expertise in line with the department’s Acquisition Transformation Strategy, and continues to develop upgrades, mission specific variants and new technologies. The kits are built at BAE Systems facilities in Hudson, New Hampshire and Austin, Texas. The company delivered its hundred thousandth APKWS kit earlier, and the system is the United States government’s only programme of record for guided seventy millimetre rockets. APKWS came to wider attention when American aircraft used the rockets against Houthi drones over the Red Sea, where a guidance kit costing a fraction of an air-to-air missile proved able to bring down one-way attack aircraft. The cost exchange problem that drove that use is the same one pushing European manufacturers towards cheaper interceptors. The post BAE to build thirty five thousand guidance kits a year first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Who’s 0xabadbabe and why? (2011)
body:
It is Friday after all, so I’ll offer this little glimpse as an example from what I do at work…
A while ago, I was working for a customer (who shall remain unnamed here, but let’s call it Intel ) doing system simulation software. I worked on this project for a year or so. I ran full x86 systems completely simulated. During that time I was chasing some nasty bugs in the simulated usb-disk device that caused my Windows boot to end up in a blue screen.
I struggled to figure out why Windows 7 would write 0xABADBABE to EHCI register index 0x1C – which is a reserved register – during boot some 10 milliseconds before the blue screen appears, and I was convinced that it was due to a flaw in the EHCI simulation code and thus was the first indication of the failure. If I didn’t have any simulated usb-disk inserted that write wouldn’t occur, and similarly that write would occur even if I inserted the usb-disk much later – like even after Windows 7 had started and I was passed the login screen.
An interesting exercise is to grep for this (little-endian so twist it around!) 32 bit pattern in a freshly installed windows 7 file system – I found it on no less than 16 places in a 20GB file system. This bgrep utility was handy for this.
To properly disassemble that code, I hacked up a quick bcut tool so that I could cut out a suitable piece of the 20GB file to pass to objdump, as objdump very inconveniently does not offer an option to skip an arbitrary amount from the beginning of a file! Also, as it is not really possible to easily tell on which byte x86 code starts at, I had to be able to fine-adjust the beginning of the cut so that objdump would show correctly (this is x86-64):
But then, reading that code never gave me enough clues to figure out why the offending MOV is made.
Thanks to a friend with a good eye and useful resources, I finally learned that Windows does this write on purpose to offer some kind of break-point for a debugger. It always does this (assuming a USB device or something is attached)!
A red herring as far as I’m concerned. Nothing to bother about, just MOV on! I simply made the simulation accept this.
Oh. You want to know what happened to the blue screen? It had nothing at all to do with the bad babe constant, but turned out to be because the ehci driver finds out that some USB data structs the controller fills in get pointers that point to memory outside of the area the driver has mapped for this purpose. In other words it was a really hard to track down bug in the simulated device.

title: ‘Netanyahu has lost’: Yair Golan calls for coalition with Arab parties
body: With about 60% of the votes counted and neither bloc holding a majority needed to form a government, Democrats chairman Yair Golan declared Wednesday morning that "Netanyahu has lost" and called for a coalition that includes Arab parties. Golan said nothing to reporters gathered outside his home but laid out his plan in a post on X. Shortly after 9 a.m., updated election results showed that with 60% of the ballots counted, Netanyahu's bloc had secured 56 seats and Eisenkot's bloc 48.   "Netanyahu has lost," Golan wrote on X. "I know how to count to 120 — 65 is more than 55. That's how Israeli democracy works. Period. The reality before us must teach us one resounding lesson: We have no future here unless we stop being afraid. And unless we put an end to racism. We can no longer accept Netanyahu's racist distinction between Jewish votes and Arab votes." Golan continued: "The vote of an Israeli citizen casting a ballot in Tira is worth exactly the same as that of an Israeli citizen voting in Givat Shmuel. Not less. Not approximately. Exactly. Anyone who tries to erase the votes of Arab citizens is surrendering to Netanyahu and giving up on Israel. "And now let's talk about Zionism. Netanyahu's bloc includes 16 lawmakers from non-Zionist ultra-Orthodox parties that promote mass draft evasion while our children are fighting and dying. "If Netanyahu insists on counting only a Zionist majority, he should first subtract the 16 lawmakers from the non-Zionist ultra-Orthodox parties in his own bloc. They have no right to lecture us on Zionism. "The change bloc has a Zionist majority: 49 to 39. The change bloc has an Israeli majority: 65 to 55. We have a majority. We have a responsibility. And we have an opportunity to form a government of change in partnership with Israel's Arab citizens. A government that will serve all Israeli citizens. "Now we need courage. We need leadership. We need to stop being afraid and start taking action. A government of change now!"   On Tuesday night, following the release of the exit polls, officials at Democrats Party headquarters repeatedly delivered the same message: "Netanyahu's bloc has collapsed." At the same time, they called for the formation of a government, even if it meant relying on outside support from Arab parties or bringing Ra'am, an Islamist Arab party, into the coalition and the next government. "The Israeli public fired Netanyahu and Likud on Tuesday," Golan said that night, urging members of the bloc to act. "We must make sure those dismissals take effect. We must establish a government of change as soon as possible." Golan has now broadened his appeal to include the Joint List, an alliance of Arab-majority parties. Golan also said Tuesday night: "The mandate we received from the public is a directive to rebuild the country. When given such a directive, we do not hesitate, allow egos to get in the way or leave room for political maneuvering. "Israel's citizens have taken their fate into their own hands. We are at a historic moment. Israel's security is at stake. Forming a new government is an urgent national security mission. Every day of delay could have serious consequences. "The responsibility to prevent Netanyahu from leading Israel into war for political reasons rests with us."

title: Injury in Lipetsk Region, damage in Tula Region, 531 UAVs: aftermath of Ukrainian attacks
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Air defense systems intercepted and destroyed 531 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions overnight, Russia’s Defense Ministry reported.
One person required medical attention in the Lipetsk Region.
Falling drone debris damaged apartment buildings, private houses and infrastructure in the industrial zone in the city of Novomoskovsk in the Tula Region.
TASS has summarized key details about the aftermath.
- On-duty air defense systems intercepted and destroyed 531 Ukrainian fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) over Russian regions between 8:00 p.m. Moscow time (5:00 p.m. GMT) on October 27 and 8:00 a.m. Moscow time (5:00 a.m. GMT) on October 28, the Defense Ministry reported.
- According to the ministry, drones were shot down over the Belgorod, Bryansk, Voronezh, Kaluga, Kursk, Lipetsk, Oryol, Rostov, Ryazan, Smolensk, Tambov, Tula and Moscow Regions.
- Air defense forces intercepted 45 Ukrainian UAVs over the Lipetsk Region, Governor Igor Artamonov reported on his Max channel.
- As many as 19 Ukrainian drones were destroyed over the Oryol Region overnight, Governor Andrey Klychkov said on Max.
- Air defense forces intercepted four Ukrainian UAVs over the Ryazan Region overnight, Governor Pavel Malkov wrote on his Max channel.
- One person required medical attention in the Lipetsk Region, Governor Igor Artamonov said on his Max channel.
- Falling UAV debris damaged apartment buildings, private houses and infrastructure in the nearby industrial zone in the city of Novomoskovsk in the Tula Region, Governor Dmitry Milyayev reported on his Max channel.
- According to the governor, emergency services have been sent to the scene.
- Information on casualties and damage is still being clarified.
- Laboratories from the Tula Region state institution "Priroda" and the regional department of Russia’s sanitary watchdog Rospotrebnadzor have been sent to Novomoskovsk.
- Two houses in the private sector caught fire in the Miloslavsky District of the Ryazan Region, Governor Pavel Malkov said on Max.
- Emergency services are operating at the scene.

title: Russia wants deal with NATO to reshape Europe's security order, Zelensky says
body:
Moscow wants a separate agreement with NATO or the U.S. that would effectively mean changing the security infrastructure of Europe and the world, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Oct. 27.
The Kremlin is repackaging these demands as "security guarantees" for itself amid ongoing negotiations to end the war in Ukraine , the president told journalists at a press briefing.
"This isn't the first time Russia has raised, in one form or another, the issue of security guarantees as they see them," Zelensky remarked, stressing that such discussions should only take place after the war in Ukraine ends.
During talks with the Biden administration shortly before launching its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Moscow demanded that NATO roll back its military blueprint in Europe to pre-1997 levels, effectively demanding that the alliance withdraw forces and infrastructure from some Central and Eastern European members.
Zelensky said he is unaware of the details but believes the Kremlin could once again demand that the alliance withdraw infrastructure from some of its member states.
"I believe that any retreat, any rollback in security terms, is a sign of weakness for the alliance," he said, stressing that such decisions should rest solely on NATO members.
"But we've also heard signals from the United States from a different angle, regarding the presence of American troops on European territory, possible reductions, and so on."
The Trump administration has been pushing Europe to take greater responsibility for its security and has publicly discussed a "review" of its military presence on the continent.
European capitals have acknowledged the need to ramp up defense spending, but have raised concerns that unexpected and unplanned withdrawal could open the door to Russian aggression.
Zelensky hinted that it was Washington's diesel deal with Russia that opened the door for further demands from Moscow, though "it's hard to predict what they might be."

title: Onion price jumps 900% to N300,000 in 6 months
body: By Cynthia Alo The price of a 120kg bag of onions jumped from N30,000 in April 2026, to about N300,000 in October representing a 900 percent increase in six months. National Onion Producers, Processors and Marketers Association of Nigeria (NOPPMAN) attributed the increase to inadequate storage facilities and fire outbreaks in warehouses in the North which contributed to post-harvest losses of more than 51 percent within the period. A Vanguard AgroBiz market survey shows that the price of a big sack of fresh onions at Mile 12 Lagos international market is N300,000, while the dried one is between N350,000 to N380,000 as of last week. In an interview with Vanguard AgroBiz, the National President of NOPPMAN, Aliyu Isah, said the price surge was not necessarily due to inadequate national production, but rather the loss of a significant proportion of harvested onions before the next production season. “It’s not that we did not produce enough for the country, but we lost more than 51% from April to October,” he said. Isah attributed the losses to poor storage facilities, fires that destroyed onions in local storage centres and the disruption caused by unsuitable seeds introduced into Nigeria during the 2024–2025 growing season. He said the seed, reportedly brought in from Algeria, was unsuitable for Nigeria’s farming system and caused substantial losses to farmers’ investments. According to him, the seed crisis alone resulted in losses estimated at nearly N100bn, while the sector needed government intervention to prevent the disruption from worsening into a supply shortage. He said government intervention was necessary when a crisis affected an agricultural subsector, warning that failure to address the underlying problems could deepen losses in subsequent seasons. Isah said the Ministry of Agriculture had discussed support for the onion subsector with the Bank of Agriculture and the Nigerian Agricultural Development Fund (NADF), regarding seed supply and farm inputs. He said the association had yet to receive the proposed intervention at the time of the interview, although discussions were ongoing. The support, he added, should help farmers restore production and prevent a repeat of the crisis. Looking ahead, Isah expects supplies from Sokoto to begin around November and December, followed by Aliero in Kebbi State from late December to January. The main harvest season is expected around March and April. He expressed optimism that the incoming harvest would ease prices, but said better storage facilities and timely government support were needed to reduce losses and prevent future shortages. title: West turns food, fertilizers into instrument of geopolitical blackmail — senior diplomat
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Western countries have turned food and fertilizers into tools of geopolitical and geoeconomic blackmail, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov said at the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.
"We are actively pursuing the launch of the Russia-Africa Agro-Industrial Alliance. It is probably still taking shape and has not yet been fully established. At a time when the West has turned food and fertilizers into instruments of geopolitical and geoeconomic blackmail, Russia sets no political conditions for cooperation in this area," he noted.
Ryabkov expressed confidence that "this will continue." "And the Russia-Africa Agro-Industrial Alliance will become an important element of the new global architecture," the senior diplomat emphasized.

title: General Staff: Russia has lost 1,583,350 troops in Ukraine since Feb. 24, 2022
body:
Russia has lost 1,583,350 troops in Ukraine since the beginning of its full-scale invasion on Feb. 24, 2022, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reported on Oct. 28.
The number includes 1,510 casualties that Russian forces suffered over the past day.
According to the report , Russia has also lost 12,448 tanks, 25,609 armored combat vehicles, 167,738 vehicles and fuel tanks, 51,674 artillery systems, 2,241 multiple-launch rocket systems, 1,727 air defense systems, 449 aircraft, 356 helicopters, 3,032 unmanned ground vehicles, 35 ships and boats, and two submarines.
Ukraine's General Staff has not revealed its own losses during the full-scale invasion, citing operational secrecy. Independent Western think-tank reports agree that the Russian casualties significantly surpass Ukraine's losses, with the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) estimating the ratio to be "roughly 2.5:1 or 2:1."
A January 2026 CSIS report said Ukraine has likely suffered between 500,000 and 600,000 casualties from February 2022 to December 2025, of which between 100,000 and 140,000 are thought to be killed in action.
While Ukrainian officials rarely disclose the figure, President Volodymyr Zelensky told France TV on Feb. 4 that at least 55,000 Ukrainian soldiers have been killed in action since the beginning of the full-scale war, in addition to significant numbers who are missing in action.
The intensity of Russian drone attacks and the fighting has made it extremely difficult for Ukraine to retrieve the bodies of fallen soldiers, which are needed for DNA confirmation.

title: Tokayev Pledges $14 Billion for Infrastructure, Sets 2029 Energy Surplus Target
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA – Kazakhstan will allocate 6.5 trillion tenge (US$14.3 billion) from the National Fund by the end of 2029 to modernize infrastructure nationwide, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev said in his annual state-of-the-nation address on Oct. 28. Photo credit: Akorda. Tokayev outlined a People’s Construction program to develop social, transport and engineering infrastructure, create jobs and stimulate economic growth. He described it as potentially the largest infrastructure project in the country’s history. “I am deeply convinced that this initiative will provide jobs for hundreds of thousands of people, and our entire nation, especially the younger generation, will benefit from it,” Tokayev said. He characterized the program as a nationwide effort to renew and rebuild civilian infrastructure, but warned that relying solely on state resources would be inappropriate for a project of this scale. “The logic behind the decisions being made is simple: state funds must become a guarantee for attracting private investment,” President Tokayev said. He also highlighted that Kazakhstan’s gold and foreign exchange reserves, along with the National Fund’s assets, have exceeded $130 billion. “The main goal and mission of the National Fund is to carefully preserve and increase the country’s wealth, as well as use it for the benefit of present and future generations,” Tokayev said, noting that the fund had contributed to the country’s financial stability over the years. Roads and air corridors: Kazakhstan’s logistics ambitions Tokayev said global logistics was undergoing a major transformation, with vulnerabilities in maritime routes increasing the strategic importance of land-based transport corridors. According to him, around 85% of freight transported from China to the European continent already passes through Kazakhstan. However, he warned that the country could not afford to remain a passive transit territory. “Being satisfied with the current favorable situation would condemn us to the role of a follower in the future,” Tokayev said. “We must already move toward becoming a full-fledged organizer of international freight flows.” He called for the development of domestic logistics operators, cargo consolidation and distribution centers, and new manufacturing facilities and commercial sites around transport hubs. Tokayev also instructed the government to complete the high-quality reconstruction of all road border crossing points next year. He described the condition of Kazakhstan’s roads as an urgent problem, criticizing central and local executive bodies for shifting responsibility and allowing the issue to remain unresolved. “I repeat: we need very high-quality roads,” he said. “Without quality roads and modern roadside service infrastructure, Kazakhstan cannot claim the status of a global transit corridor or a Eurasian transport and logistics hub,” Tokayev added. Tokayev also highlighted Kazakhstan’s strategic position along major air corridors connecting Europe and Asia, describing it as a significant competitive advantage that the country had yet to fully capitalize on. “For now, enormous revenues are literally flying past our country,” he said, criticizing the lack of tangible progress. He added that Kazakhstan needs to complete several key tasks to establish itself as a major Eurasian transport hub, with full digitalization of the transport sector among its priorities. “In the age of artificial intelligence, managing global transit flows with paper waybills is absurd,” Tokayev said. “And it is the shortest path to nowhere.” Sustainable electricity surplus Tokayev identified electricity supply as a decisive factor in national competitiveness and economic sovereignty, describing the current period as an “era of electricity.” Tokayev said the annual volume of 123 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity was critically insufficient for a country expanding its industrial, construction and agricultural sectors while pursuing economy-wide digitalization and the adoption of artificial intelligence, which would require the construction of data centers. He pointed to the country’s recurring electricity shortages, particularly during winter peak-demand periods, when Kazakhstan buys electricity from neighboring countries at high prices and sells it back in summer at much lower prices. “This simple ‘business’ has been going on for decades,” he said, questioning claims that the arrangement was normal practice in the energy sector. Tokayev also criticized delays in developing new generating capacity, citing the previously halted construction of the Balkhash thermal power plant and delays in bringing generating facilities online in Turkistan, Kyzylorda, Almaty and Ekibastuz. He set a strategic target of achieving a sustainable electricity surplus by 2029. Tokayev instructed the government to update Kazakhstan’s unified long-term energy balance through 2035. New nuclear power projects Tokayev also emphasized the strategic importance of nuclear energy, saying Kazakhstan had made the right decision by supporting the construction of a nuclear power plant in a nationwide referendum. Tokayev described a proposal to establish a state strategic uranium reserve as worthy of serious consideration, saying it could cover the needs of Kazakhstan’s nuclear power plants for the next century. “I believe it is possible and perhaps necessary to begin construction of the Balkhash nuclear power plant as early as next year and sign a comprehensive cooperation agreement to accelerate the start of construction of the Moyinkum nuclear power plant,” he said. He stressed that negotiations must be carefully prepared and aligned with Kazakhstan’s national interests. The post Tokayev Pledges $14 Billion for Infrastructure, Sets 2029 Energy Surplus Target appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: Russia’s Putin hails Iran's martyred Leader role in GECF
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 28 (MNA) – Russian President Vladimir Putin has praised the role played by the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei in establishment of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF).
In his remarks at the 8th Summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF), Russian President Vladimir Putin emphasized that Iran’s martyred Leader, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, played a significant role in the establishment of GECF.
President Putin also welcomed the remarks by Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian regarding the need for collective action by GECF member states against unilateral sanctions.
Putin called on member states to counter unilateral Western sanctions against energy-rich countries, which he said lead to unfair competition. The consequences of these sanctions not only affect gas consumers but also impact producers, he added.
He also pointed to the rising trend of global gas consumption, stating that by 2050, global demand for gas will reach 5.5 trillion cubic meters per year, and international supply will increase by about 1.5 times.
Putin criticized European sanctions against Russia, saying that by turning away from Russian energy resources, Europe is damaging its own industry and social sector.

title: Russian UAV attack on Pavlohrad wounds boy, 15 – regional administration
body:
A 15-year-old boy was wounded as a result of a Russian drone attack on Pavlohrad, Dnipropetrovsk region, on Wednesday morning, and is being taken to the hospital, reported Head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration Oleksandr Hanzha.

title: Flavio Bolsonaro on way to Ecuador from Argentina after fleeing Brazil
body: Defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro was on his way to Ecuador after fleeing Brazil, Argentina’s government said on Wednesday. Bolsonaro, who lost Brazil’s runoff election to Lula on Sunday, entered Argentina on Tuesday night before boarding a flight to Ecuador, the country’s National Directorate of Migration said on X. The 45-year-old entered Argentina “with valid travel documents and no legal impediment,” it added, despite a court order banning his exit. Bolsonaro, his wife and two daughters boarded “a private flight operated by the company Baires Fly S.A. bound for the city of Guayaquil, Ecuador,” the government agency said. According to data from the Flightradar24 website, the flight took off just after midnight (0300 GMT) on Wednesday from the Argentine town of Puerto Iguazu in the country’s northeast. Baires Fly did not immediately respond to AFP’s request for comment. US media citing anonymous sources had earlier reported that Bolsonaro had arrived in the United States on Tuesday. The US State Department said it would issue visas to Bolsonaro and his family but did not confirm their travel plans. Brazil’s Supreme Court banned Bolsonaro from leaving the country and ordered him to hand over his passports. He is under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering, and with his election loss is also set to lose parliamentary immunity. Bolsonaro has not acknowledged his electoral defeat, citing the decision to extend polling hours over transport difficulties that prevented some citizens from voting. AFP The post Flavio Bolsonaro on way to Ecuador from Argentina after fleeing Brazil appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Israel’s parliamentary election too close to call as Netanyahu seeks another term
body:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’ s right-wing bloc takes an early but marginal lead in the Israeli parliamentary election, with a third of the votes counted.
However, exit polls suggest Israel’s election hangs in the balance, as neither Mr Netanyahu nor Gadi Eisenkot can secure a clear parliamentary majority.
The two revised exit polls released so far showed Mr Netanyahu’s right-wing camp and his opponent Mr Eisenkot’s bloc tied at 51 seats. Israeli news outlets rely heavily on polls to predict elections.
The winning bloc needs at least 61 seats to form a majority government.
This election will determine whether Mr Netanyahu remains in power or Israel sees a change in leadership.
The election is a referendum on the country’s leadership after the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack, its subsequent wars, and the political and security decisions that have shaped Israel since then. The result could influence the direction of the war, relations with the Palestinians, Israel’s international standing and its domestic political future.
After polls showed a neck-and-neck race, Mr Netanyahu called for a strong right-wing government among the Zionist public and called for the formation of a “national right-wing government.”
He warned against forming one dependent on Arab parties. Arabs make up one-fifth of Israel’s population. Many of them also identify as Palestinians.
He recounted what he called his government’s military achievements and argued its work remained unfinished.
“Iran is weaker than ever; Israel is stronger than ever,” he said.
He also said Israel has a “unique opportunity” alongside President Donald Trump to “remove the Iranian threat once and for all.”
Meanwhile, the opposition has disputed the initial projection of 50 seats for Mr Netanyahu’s bloc, arguing that the prediction underestimated its support.
Mr Eisenko described the election as Israeli society’s response to the 7 October attacks and three years of war.
“People had not remained indifferent. They had come out to vote,” he said.
Mr Eisenkot said Israelis voted for “change” which he intends to introduce by forming “a government that represents the entire society.”
Meanwhile, Arab-led parties are also celebrating, with exit polls projecting they will win 19 seats. It will be the most they’ve ever held in parliament.
