title: Zelenskyy: temporary Starshield restriction stops operation of 2,000 'Bars' drone interceptors
body:
Ukraine received 2,000 Bars drone interceptors funded by a European country, and during testing, one of them destroyed a Russian Shahed, but Starshield restrictions halted the operation of these interceptors, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated.
"We found a European country. They paid for 2,000 units. I knew we had 2,000. I said: 'Let's test it. Maybe it can destroy targets.' They tested it, and it destroyed a Shahed. We were very happy. And then Starshield stopped working," Zelenskyy said at a meeting with journalists on Tuesday, an Interfax-Ukraine agency correspondent reports.
He noted that he does not know who exactly made the decision to turn off the system, which is technically turned on and off by SpaceX. Zelenskyy also explained that Ukraine uses Starshield against the Russian military on its own territory, rather than on the territory of the Russian Federation. In addition, the system is used primarily for logistics, in particular providing the military with food and water, as well as to counter "Shaheds" and jet-powered drones.
According to the President, Ukraine currently destroys about 90% of Russian Shaheds, whereas at the beginning of the attacks this figure was 50–75%, sometimes reaching 78%. Zelenskyy also stated that during the Starlink/Starshield disconnection, civilians died, although he emphasized that this happened for various reasons.
As reported, on the night of October 14, the Ukrainian military recorded restrictions on the operation of Starshield terminals – the military version of Starlink satellite communications. According to Interfax-Ukraine sources in the Ministry of Defense, terminals lost connection while moving at speeds exceeding a set threshold, which on various equipment was approximately 72–161 km/h. This complicated the tasks performed by drone interceptors and strike UAVs, as well as logistics, reconnaissance, and communications relay. The Ministry of Defense held consultations with the US, SpaceX, and NATO partners and checked backup communication channels.
On October 24, Ukrainian Defense Minister Yevhen Khmara reported that Ministry of Defense monitoring systems were recording the restoration of Starlink/Starshield speed capabilities.
"We are recording speeds of more than 400 km/h, the connection is stable. This is another example of how direct dialogue and the persistent position of the President of Ukraine at the highest level yield results. And this result is primarily important for our front, for the military, drone operations, logistics, and communications," Khmara commented in response to journalists' questions on Saturday.

title: Zelenskyy: Ukraine wants Abu Dhabi trilateral meeting before potential U.S-China-Russia summit
body:
Ukraine would like the tripartite meeting of the negotiating teams of Ukraine, the U.S, and Russia in Abu Dhabi to take place prior to a potential meeting between the US, China, and Russia, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated.
"We will see what kind of meeting this will be. We would very much like our meeting in Abu Dhabi to happen before that," Zelenskyy said at a meeting with journalists on Tuesday, an Interfax-Ukraine agency correspondent reports.
Commenting on the possible meeting of the leaders of the U.S, China, and Russia, the President noted that it will likely discuss the situation in the Middle East and the war in Ukraine.
At the same time, Zelenskyy expressed concern over the possibility of a redistribution of spheres of influence by analogy with the Yalta Conference.
"I really don't want this to be a 'Yalta – 2, 3, 4,' when there is a redistribution of influence. I would even say not influence, but opinions – that things can be redistributed this way. Today we have a different world, a fragmented world that is very different from the world of World War II, both before and after. A completely different technological world. Therefore, I think it is impossible to simply make such a redistribution between the three. Although Russia really wants to," the President emphasized.
In his opinion, such a meeting would be more beneficial to Russia than to China.
"I believe that after Alaska, this will be the second such diplomatic, serious advantage for Russia, if everything happens exactly as the Russians are now 'leaking' regarding their desires for a new 'Yalta,'" he said.
The President added that currently, holding the tripartite meeting in Abu Dhabi depends on the American side.
"The Russians have confirmed, we have confirmed. In my opinion, today this no longer depends on the Russians and not on us. Today Abu Dhabi depends on the American side," he noted.
According to him, all parties view the possibility of holding such a meeting positively, but the development of the situation in the Middle East is affecting U.S plans.
"There may be escalation there, and many are talking about it. I think there will be," the President believes.

title: Palisa turns down U.S ambassador post – Zelenskyy
body:
Former Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko, former Minister of Foreign Affairs Dmytro Kuleba, and Deputy Head of the Presidential Office Pavlo Palisa were considered as candidates for the post of Ukraine's Ambassador to the U.S, but the latter declined the offer, reported President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
"We discussed the candidacies of Yulia Svyrydenko, Dmytro Kuleba, and Pavlo Palisa, because he has an American education, speaks the language, there is a lot of work to be done specifically on military issues there, and Trump knows him. Palisa would have made a good ambassador, but he doesn't want it. He said: 'Send me to the front, return me to the brigade urgently. I will not leave Ukraine for anywhere.' We will continue consultations on this," Zelenskyy said at a meeting with journalists on Tuesday, an Interfax-Ukraine agency correspondent reports.
As reported, on August 3, Zelenskyy signed a decree dismissing Olha Stefanishyna from the post of Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Ukraine to the USA.
The respective decree No. 696/2026 was published on the president's website.
In a Facebook post, Stefanishyna reported that she had decided to resign her powers as Ambassador of Ukraine to the United States of America due to personal circumstances.

title: U.S requests postponement of Brussels meeting due to situation in Middle East – Zelenskyy
body:
The American side requested a change in the date of a meeting in Brussels involving U.S representatives, European Union leaders, and the NATO Secretary General due to the need for U.S representatives to be present in Washington amid the situation in the Middle East, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated.
"When the meeting in Brussels was being prepared, it concerned a format with the Americans, EU leaders, and the NATO Secretary General to discuss various issues and preparations for a trilateral meeting... But as I understand, there are issues in Washington regarding the Middle East, so our American partners asked us to change the date – so that their representatives could be in Washington at this time. We are waiting for new proposals regarding such a meeting with the American team," Zelenskyy said at a meeting with journalists on Tuesday, an Interfax-Ukraine agency correspondent reports.
On October 25, Zelenskyy reported that a meeting at the level of the President of Ukraine, the American side, the EU, and the NATO Secretary General was planned in Brussels for Tuesday or Wednesday of this week.
On October 26, Presidential Communications Advisor Dmytro Lytvyn reported that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's meeting in Brussels with EU, NATO, and U.S representatives was not yet confirmed due to a change in plans by the American side.

title: Zelenskyy: U.S proposes demilitarized zones in Donbas, Kinburn Spit
body:
Within negotiations on ending the war, the American side proposed various options for settling the territorial issue, including demilitarized zones and a buffer zone in Donbas, reported President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
"Starting as early as the '28-point plan,' there was one of the alternative proposals from the American side – demilitarized zones. After that, this was discussed in different ways across various documents. What will happen to the ZNPP? What will happen with certain territories that the Americans proposed addressing in a 'land swaps' format? Then there was the question regarding Donbas, where there was a proposal to create a buffer zone or a demilitarized zone on both sides of the line of contact," Zelenskyy said at a meeting with journalists on Tuesday, an Interfax-Ukraine agency correspondent reports.
According to him, the proposals also included the demilitarization of part of the Kinburn Spit, which could remain under Ukrainian control.
"As a compromise, we were ready to discuss this," the President noted.
He added that during the discussions, the American side raised the issue of demilitarized zones again, though there is currently no further progress on the territorial question.
"We are ready to discuss the issue of territories because the Russians constantly want to discuss it and make it part of the agenda. But this requires meetings at the appropriate level – this is not the kind of question that can supposedly be solved at the level of drafts, some preliminary talks, or anything of the sort," he said.

title: Netanyahu bloc leads after half of Israeli votes counted but no majority
body: The camp of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was ahead of his rival’s opposition bloc but still short of a majority on Wednesday after 50 percent of votes were counted in Israel’s pivotal general election. Voters turned out in the highest numbers in decades to give their verdict on Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister who has pushed the country sharply to the right and unleashed a wave of wars in response to Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack. Following the vote, both Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot vowed to form a government despite neither being projected to win a majority. After 51.8 percent of ballots were counted, Netanyahu’s bloc was shown to have 55 of the 120 seats in the parliament. Eisenkot’s opposition bloc had 49 seats and the Arab parties 16. The partial results are likely to change as more votes are counted. Exit polls had shown that Eisenkot, a former military chief and political novice, and his opposition bloc were neck-and-neck with Netanyahu’s hard-right camp, with both winning about 51 seats, well away from the threshold for a majority in parliament. The strongest gains came from Arab Israeli parties whose voters turned out in soaring numbers against Netanyahu, who has relentlessly warned that the minority would dilute the Jewish nationalist direction in which he has taken Israel. The partial results suggest that Eisenkot’s bloc would have enough seats for a majority if there was a coalition agreement with the Arab parties. But Eisenkot said during the campaign he would not govern with Israeli Arab lawmakers, echoing the position of Netanyahu, who has suggested a government relying on Arab votes would lack legitimacy. Arab lawmakers could also give Eisenkot support in parliamentary votes to maintain a minority government without joining a coalition. A lack of clear majority for either camp could mean weeks spent trying to cobble together coalitions, with possible new elections on the horizon if negotiations fail. A stalemate could in the immediate term benefit Netanyahu, who would remain caretaker prime minister until a new government is formed. Full results are expected by Thursday evening or Friday morning. Netanyahu, greeting cheering supporters at a Jerusalem convention centre after 3 am (0100 GMT) on Wednesday morning, called for a “strong government of the right” and said the “Jewish and Zionist majority must unite”. The 77-year-old prime minister, who has governed Israel on and off for nearly two decades, was unusually brief and did not directly claim victory. US President Donald Trump told reporters on Wednesday that his endorsement of Netanyahu had helped the premier “a lot”. – ‘Public voted for change’ – Speaking to supporters in Tel Aviv, 66-year-old Eisenkot issued a veiled warning to Netanyahu, who observers say could use a war to push for a unity government. “Netanyahu, don’t you dare use Israel’s security for your political needs,” Eisenkot said. He called Netanyahu “a caretaker prime minister, without a mandate or the people’s trust”. The vote came as Israel looks increasingly isolated on the world stage, driven by the war in Iran and the military campaign in Gaza, as well as soaring settlement construction and violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank. Eisenkot shares many of Netanyahu’s views on security and has backed the Gaza offensive that has reduced the territory to rubble. But he has vowed to create a more inclusive atmosphere inside Israel and to rein in violent West Bank settlers. After a turnout of nearly 78 percent, the highest since 1999, Eisenkot said it would be a mistake to hold a second election and vowed to work “swiftly” to form a government. “The public has voted for change,” he said. “A worthy leader would accept the people’s vote of no confidence and announce his retirement from political life today.” Exit polls had shown Israeli Arab lists projected to win 18 or 19 seats, a sharp gain. Arab Israelis, also known as Palestinian citizens of Israel, account for about 21 percent of the country’s population. The post Netanyahu bloc leads after half of Israeli votes counted but no majority appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Zelenskyy proposes PM assemble special management team for Kyiv
body:
President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy proposed that Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky form a special team of experienced managers and business representatives to develop solutions for Kyiv, discussing the possible involvement of Vasyl Maliuk, Oleksandr Kubrakov, and Volodymyr Groysman, among others.
"I asked the prime minister to assemble a special cabinet for Kyiv – business managers, strong people. I am personally ready to speak with whoever they name to me and ask them. Build such a cabinet and develop solutions. I will do what I can," Zelenskyy said at a meeting with journalists on Tuesday, an Interfax-Ukraine agency correspondent reports.
At the same time, he noted that Kyiv's resilience plans were not fully implemented, and the capital's critical infrastructure facilities are not fully protected.
"It would be wonderful if Kyiv could protect itself or at least prepare for dangers. But this did not work in any of the aspects. Now we can only go through these challenges together with all institutions," the president added.
According to him, daily work by various institutions is currently underway regarding the electricity and water supply situation in the capital, as well as the functioning of bridges. He emphasized that the protection of critical infrastructure must be ensured regardless of who formally owns a particular facility.
"Critical infrastructure facilities must be protected. They did not protect them to the end. Resilience plans were not fully completed," the president noted.
At the same time, Zelenskyy emphasized that he does not consider the situation in Kyiv to be a matter of political confrontation, but acknowledged the difficulty of interacting with the city authorities. According to him, when he discusses the possibility of strengthening the capital with managers, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko perceives it as an attempt to replace him.
"I would very much like the mayor to do everything himself. But he cannot do it alone. And working together is difficult," Zelenskyy said.
The president cited Kharkiv as an example, where, according to him, the head of the regional state administration and the mayor work together despite different political plans for the future. He noted that such interaction helps solve problems and maintain the situation in the city.
Zelenskyy also reported that he spoke with various managers about the possibility of heading the Kyiv administration or joining the work to strengthen the capital. According to him, he discussed this issue in particular with Vasyl Maliuk, Oleksandr Kubrakov, and Volodymyr Hroysman, as well as representatives of business and public administration, but no volunteers were found to join.
"I wanted to involve Maliuk in this group in the context of security issues. I also spoke with Kubrakov, Hroysman. Sukhomlyn refused – as soon as he heard about Kyiv," the head of state explained.
He emphasized that he has no personal claims against Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko, but the capital must be prepared for a difficult winter. According to Zelenskyy, despite the fact that massive Russian attacks started earlier than expected, this should not be a reason just to look for those to blame.
"He (Klitschko) should have called all these people himself and met with them, rather than me. During such a war, it doesn't matter whose bridge it is on paper. The main thing is that it stands and functions as one of the capital's most important logistical arteries," Zelenskyy said.

title: Zelenskyy: U.S supplies Ukraine with average of 12 Patriot missiles monthly in 2026
body:
Throughout 2026, the U.S has been supplying Ukraine with 12 interceptor missiles per month for Patriot systems due to the war in the Middle East, while Ukraine's need is about 150 missiles monthly for intercepting ballistic targets, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated.
"Throughout the entire year 2026, Ukraine has been receiving 12 missiles for Patriots per month from the U.S. As this year is already coming to an end, I can speak about this openly. All the more so since everyone has already understood this anyway – by the number of shootdowns, which, unfortunately, are few. Of course, my agreements with other countries influenced the number of missiles for Patriots that Ukraine had. But from America, we received 12 missiles per month. The reason is the Middle East. And imagine: you can count on 150 missiles per year from America, but you need to shoot down 150 ballistic missiles a month," Zelenskyy said at a meeting with journalists on Tuesday, an Interfax-Ukraine agency correspondent reports.
According to him, the reason for the reduction in American supplies is the war in the Middle East. He also noted that Ukraine seeks to obtain permission from the U.S for the supply of interceptor missiles by other countries with which Kyiv is negotiating their transfer.
"And therefore, when at some point a combination of various factors occurs: the Starlink/Starshield issue, intelligence, interceptor missiles against Russian ballistics, signatures, and a 'diesel deal' dropped in there as well, we understand where everything is heading. 'Home alone' – the next part. This is a challenge, a difficult challenge," the president noted.
He called the situation in the Middle East a "serious story" and noted that Kyiv provided assistance at the request of the American side, specifically regarding bases hosting U.S citizens in Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and other countries. He emphasized the importance of resolving the crisis in the region.

title: Trump claims endorsement of Netanyahu shifted momentum in Israel's election
body: US President Donald Trump took credit for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's performance during the election on Wednesday morning by claiming his endorsement shifted the election's momentum.Taking to Truth Social, the president quoted Irving C. Schwartz, who said, “When President Trump endorsed Bibi Netanyahu, the whole tide turned, and now, rather than a decisive defeat for a Great Prime Minister, it looks like a big come-from-behind stalemate, or even a WIN for Netanyahu."It all took place AFTER the Endorsement by President Trump, who only wants what is good for the Middle East, Israel, and the United States of America!”Trump: Netanyahu did better than expectedLater, on the tarmac by Air Force One, a reporter asked Trump about the election, to which he responded, "I heard the poll numbers were wrong... the exit polls; I heard he [Netanyahu] did very well. It was pretty close, but very well. When the endorsement went out, it helped him a lot."Trump concluded, "It's a little bit early, but I'm hearing in Israel, top people say, 'Wow! He did a lot better than people thought.' It's looking like maybe a stalemate or a win."

title: Goodbye, SPNEC: MVP rebrands Leviste’s solar firm, lines up P5-B deal
body: Manuel V. Pangilinan is giving Leandro Leviste’s old solar crown jewel quite the makeover. First, shed the SPNEC name. Next, bring in nearly P5 billion worth of other renewable energy businesses. And perhaps, pitch the shiny new thing to stock market investors all over again. SP New Energy Corporation (SPNEC) is now officially MGEN Renewables Inc., (MGENR) after securing Securities and Exchange Commission approval on Monday, October 26; its stock ticker is also set to change to MGENR. Officially, the renaming is part of the Meralco group’s broader rebranding strategy. Conveniently, it also removes a reminder of Solar Philippines , the controversial empire Leviste built before Pangilinan’s group took control . And there’s quite a history behind SPNEC. FROM SPNEC to MGENR. This Rappler diagram shows the ownership of the rebranded solar company as of September 1, 2026 and before the proposed share swap. Diagram by Raphael Reyes/Rappler. Leviste made his fortune assembling landholdings and securing solar development rights that attracted deep-pocketed investors, including Pangilinan himself. Industry sources that Rappler spoke with describe the young billionaire as a talented “flipper.” But getting the rights to build solar farms and actually getting them built are two different businesses. The Department of Energy (DOE) terminated 33 contracts tied to Leviste’s wider Solar Philippines group, covering around 11,400 megawatts of proposed capacity, and sought around P24 billion in financial obligations. His camp disputes the claims. While much of the P24-billion mess relates to Leviste’s other companies, SPNEC is dragged into this too. In a December 23, 2025 letter seen by Rappler, Energy Secretary Sharon Garin terminated the service contract for SPNEC’s 280-megawatt Santa Rosa Nueva Ecija 2 project and demanded P10.34 billion. The DOE cited missed work-program commitments, an unrenewed performance bond, and missing documents, including a feasibility study and proof of land rights. Most of the demand came from P12.38 billion in work-program commitments, less P2.04 billion credited for reported accomplishments. MGEN insists SPNEC is legally separate from Solar Philippines and not liable for the wider group’s P24 billion obligation. But it acknowledges that Santa Rosa belongs to SPNEC and says that it invoked force majeure over transmission delays and sought reconsideration. Separately, Leviste and his mother, Senator Loren Legarda, face graft and plunder complaints involving solar contracts awarded to Leviste-linked companies. Both deny wrongdoing. Leviste himself has kept his distance from his now Meralco-controlled company, resigning from the board in January and cashing out P3-billion worth of shares , leaving his holding company with an 11.51% stake. Must Read [Vantage Point] As Leandro Leviste cashes out of SPNEC, his private companies remain at the table New name, new MGENR So, what’s next for MGENR? On Tuesday, October 27, MGEN Renewables’ board approved a proposed P4.98-billion deal to take in stakes in five solar businesses from its controlling shareholder, MGEN Renewable Energy Inc., another Meralco subsidiary. The companies have interests in operating solar plants across Luzon: Greenergy for Global Inc. – 52.7-megawatt solar plant in Isabela Greentech Solar Energy Inc. – 19.8-megawatt solar plant in Nueva Ecija CACI Power Corporation – Linked to an 80.1-megawatt solar plant in Rizal Nuevo Solar Energy Corporation – 68.7-megawatt solar plant in Ilocos Norte PowerSource First Bulacan Solar Inc. – 55-megawatt solar plant in Bulacan Instead of paying cash, MGEN Renewables will issue around 3.1 billion new shares to its controlling shareholder. If completed, the share swap deal would strengthen Meralco’s control while further diluting Leviste and other investors. Then comes the more intriguing possibility, a “re-IPO” targeted for March 2027. Since Leviste already took SPNEC public in 2021, this would be another share offering in the now bigger company under Meralco’s control, rather than a second listing. Nothing has been finalized. This time, there’s more to show investors. Its P200-billion MTerra Solar project began commercial operations in August, while MGEN Renewables forecasts P774 million in profit for 2026, reversing a P4.1-billion loss in 2025. The group also plans to invest up to another P7.815 billion in Terra Solar, subject to lender and investor approvals. – Rappler.com Must Read Who comes after MVP? Pangilinan has successors in mind.

title: Senator questions Tinubu’s fresh loan request, use of previous borrowings
body:
Anambra Central senator, Victor Umeh, has questioned the federal government’s handling of previous loans, asking why contractors executing capital projects are still awaiting payment despite repeated borrowing approvals to fund projects.
Mr Umeh spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Tuesday in response to President Bola Tinubu ’s request for approval to borrow $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion.
He said the government has repeatedly framed borrowing as necessary to fund its budgets, yet it has failed to meet some of its financial obligations.
“The truth is that we have approved so much funds to be borrowed in the past, and on each occasion we’ve been told that this borrowing would be able to fund the budgets and these budgets have remained unfunded up till this day,” he said.
Mr Umeh, who represents Anambra Central Senatorial District in the Nigerian Senate, noted that three budgets were running concurrently, while contractors handling capital projects had yet to receive payments.
“So if you borrow to finance a budget and you are not able to finance that budget, where has the money gone to? That is the question on the lips of everybody,” he said.
He also said the latest borrowing request was likely to be approved, arguing that members of the ruling party would outnumber opposition lawmakers.
After reading the president’s letter on Tuesday, Mr Akpabio referred the request to the Senate Committees on Local and Foreign Debts and Appropriations for further scrutiny. He directed the committees to report back within one week.
The senate is expected to take a decision on the request based on the recommendations of the committees.
But no loan request from the Tinubu administration has been rejected by the senate. All loan requests have had smooth sailing at the senate with minimal scrutiny.
Mr Tinubu’s request for fresh borrowings was contained in a letter read by Senate President Godswill Akpabio during plenary on Tuesday.
The president’s letter sought approval to process external loans worth $20,517,755,901 and €1,045,083,643 under the 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan.
He explained that the funds would finance projects in infrastructure, agriculture, healthcare, education, water supply, security and employment generation, as well as financial management reforms.
According to the president, the projects were selected after technical and economic evaluations and are expected to contribute to the country’s socio-economic development.
He said the borrowing was necessary to address Nigeria’s infrastructure deficit and bridge the funding gap.
Mr Akpabio referred the request to the Senate committees on Local and Foreign Debts and Appropriations for consideration, directing them to report back within one week.
The latest request follows other borrowing approvals granted by the National Assembly under the Tinubu administration.
In May, lawmakers approved a $516.3 million loan from Deutsche Bank AG for the construction of the Sokoto–Badagry Superhighway.
The loan has a nine-year tenure, including a grace period of up to three years. Its interest rate is capped at the Secured Overnight Financing Rate plus 5.3 per cent annually. The facility is backed by insurance from the Islamic Corporation of Investment and Export Credit, the insurance arm of the Islamic Development Bank.
In March, the National Assembly approved a $6 billion external borrowing plan. The package included a $5 billion facility from First Abu Dhabi Bank to support the national budget and a $1 billion export finance facility arranged by Citibank for the rehabilitation of Tin Can Island Port and the Lagos Port Complex.
The latest request comes amid concerns over Nigeria’s rising public debt and the cost of servicing government obligations.
The government maintains that borrowing is needed to finance infrastructure and other development projects. But Mr Umeh has questioned whether previous loans have translated into the funding of approved budgets and the payment of contractors.

title: CBD COP17: Nigeria urges developed countries to fulfil $30bn annual biodiversity funding pledge
body:
Nigeria has urged developed countries to fulfil their commitment to mobilise at least $20 billion annually by 2025 and $30 billion annually by 2030 to enable developing countries to effectively implement biodiversity conservation initiatives.
The Minister of Environment, Balarebe Lawal , made the call while delivering Nigeria’s national statement during the high-level segment of the ongoing 17th Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD COP17) in Yerevan, Armenia.
“Excellencies, as Founding Chair of the Ministerial Alliance for Ambition on Nature Finance, Nigeria continues to champion the mobilisation of adequate and predictable resources for biodiversity. We call for the fulfilment of the commitment to mobilise at least US$20 billion annually by 2025 and US$30 billion annually by 2030 for developing countries,” Mr Lawal said.
He said Nigeria was pleased to join the global community to reaffirm its collective commitment to protecting biodiversity and securing a sustainable future for present and future generations.
“Nigeria reaffirms its unwavering commitment to the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework and our shared ambition to halt and reverse biodiversity loss by 2030,” he said.
Nigeria completed its revised National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025–2030 in June 2025 and submitted it to the CBD Secretariat.
The strategy provides a national roadmap for halting and reversing biodiversity loss during its six-year implementation period.
It aligns Nigeria’s conservation priorities with the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF) and establishes 23 national targets tailored to the country’s socioeconomic and environmental circumstances.
The targets cover critical sectors, including agriculture, forestry, infrastructure and ecosystem conservation.
The strategy also adopts a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach, integrating biodiversity conservation into government policies and development planning while encouraging the participation of stakeholders, including Indigenous Peoples and local communities.
It further emphasises private-sector accountability and environmental risk management, including efforts to help businesses assess and disclose their dependencies on nature.
Nigeria has projected an implementation budget of approximately $474 million over six years, highlighting the need to mobilise resources to address longstanding funding gaps.
Mr Lawal urged governments and delegates to translate their biodiversity commitments into concrete action supported by adequate financing, strong partnerships and measurable results.
He said Nigeria had continued to advance implementation since COP15, including validating its revised NBSAP in June 2025, with 23 national targets aligned with the global biodiversity framework.
He added that Nigeria had submitted its Seventh National Report to strengthen implementation, monitoring and accountability.
Mr Lawal said the country remained committed to the global 30-by-30 target of conserving at least 30 per cent of the world’s land and inland waters, as well as coastal and marine areas, by 2030.
He said Nigeria was pursuing this ambition through protected-area management, ecosystem restoration and marine conservation.
“Following the Federal Executive Council’s approval of the ratification of the BBNJ Agreement, we are advancing the necessary processes to strengthen our contribution to the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity beyond national jurisdiction,” he said.
The BBNJ Agreement, also known as the High Seas Treaty, provides a framework for conserving and sustainably using marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction.
Mr Lawal also said Nigeria was integrating biodiversity conservation, climate action and land restoration through the Global Environment Facility-supported Net Zero Nature Positive Project.
He stressed that effective biodiversity conservation must be inclusive and equitable, noting that Nigeria was promoting gender-responsive land governance, women’s access to land and natural resources, and their meaningful participation in environmental decision-making.
He added that the government remained committed to ensuring that women and vulnerable communities actively participated in and benefited from biodiversity conservation efforts.
Citing Decision 16/34 of the previous biodiversity conference, Mr Lawal advocated stronger collaboration between environment and finance ministers to integrate biodiversity considerations into national budgets, fiscal policies and development plans.
He said international financing commitments must be delivered through predictable, accessible and additional resources, complemented by domestic resource mobilisation, private-sector investment and reforms to harmful incentives.
He also highlighted the importance of technology transfer, capacity-building and institutional strengthening, particularly for developing countries.
Nigeria, he said, was calling for greater coordination among the three Rio Conventions on biodiversity, climate change and desertification to maximise available resources, minimise duplication and accelerate implementation.
“Mr President, COP17 must mark a decisive turning point—from commitments to delivery. Our global ambition must be matched by adequate financing, equitable access to the means of implementation, gender-responsive action and measurable progress,” he said.
Mr Lawal said Nigeria was ready to strengthen international partnerships and work with other parties to achieve the shared 2030 biodiversity goals and secure a nature-positive future for all.

title: 2027: Hamzat and Need to Sustain Lagos’ Development Map
body: As the All Progressives Congress prepares to unveil the manifesto of its governorship candidate, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, the contest presents an opportunity to consolidate Lagos’ development gains, deepen inclusive growth and respond to the aspirations of its rapidly expanding population, writes Wale Igbintade . Lagos has never been a state content to stand still. Its crowded roads, expanding neighbourhoods, bustling commercial districts and ambitious infrastructure projects tell the story of a city-state constantly negotiating the demands of growth. Yet beneath its reputation as Nigeria’s commercial powerhouse lies a continuing challenge: translating economic expansion into better living conditions for the millions who call it home. That challenge will occupy a central place in the political conversation ahead of the 2027 governorship election. For the All Progressives Congress (APC), which has governed the state since May, 1999, the election represents an opportunity to retain public confidence while responding to changing expectations. At the centre of the contest is the party’s governorship candidate, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, popularly known as KOH. His candidacy offers the APC an opportunity to build on its development record while presenting a renewed vision for a state whose economic importance continues to attract residents, investors and businesses from across Nigeria and beyond. The planned unveiling of Hamzat’s manifesto on Friday, October 30, is therefore more than a campaign milestone. It provides an opportunity to explain how the next administration intends to sustain Lagos’s development momentum, confront persistent urban challenges and ensure that economic growth benefits a broader section of the population. For Hamzat, the task is to demonstrate that experience can inspire fresh solutions and that the next phase of Lagos’ development can be more inclusive, responsive and sustainable. His experience within the state’s political and administrative structure provides a foundation for the APC’s case. However, its value will ultimately be judged by how effectively it translates into policies and programmes that improve residents’ daily lives. The next administration must preserve what has worked, address shortcomings and adapt government priorities to the pressures accompanying Lagos’ growth. This requires more than maintaining existing projects; it demands a clear understanding of the state’s changing needs and the determination to respond to them. Infrastructure will inevitably occupy a prominent place in that conversation. Roads, bridges, drainage systems and public facilities remain critical to economic productivity and residents’ quality of life. Improvements can reduce travel time, facilitate commerce, strengthen neighbourhood connections and support business expansion. Yet infrastructure must increasingly be measured by its practical impact. Residents want roads that remain usable, drainage systems that reduce flooding, public facilities that function efficiently and transport networks that make commuting less exhausting. In a city where congestion consumes working hours and imposes substantial costs on businesses, integrating road development with efficient public transportation will remain a major test of governance. Hamzat, if elected, would have an opportunity to advance a coordinated approach connecting transport planning with housing, commercial activity and urban development. Such integration would ensure that infrastructure projects serve a broader strategy for improving mobility, productivity and residents’ welfare rather than operating as isolated interventions. Housing presents an equally pressing challenge. Lagos continues to attract people seeking employment, education and business opportunities, placing considerable pressure on the availability and affordability of accommodation, particularly for low-and middle-income earners. For many residents, the challenge is not simply finding a home but securing accommodation within reasonable reach of workplaces and essential services. When affordable housing is concentrated far from employment centres, residents spend a disproportionate share of their incomes on transportation and lose valuable time commuting. Addressing this problem requires sustained investment, effective urban planning, collaboration with private developers and policies that recognise different income groups. It also demands adequate infrastructure in residential areas, including roads, drainage, water supply, schools and healthcare facilities. Placing affordable housing alongside transportation and social infrastructure would help make Lagos more accessible to the workers and families who sustain its economic life. The broader question is whether government policies can convert Lagos’ commercial dynamism into opportunities that extend beyond established businesses and better-positioned households. Sustainable economic growth requires residents to have a realistic chance of participating in its benefits. For the next administration, this means looking beyond aggregate economic indicators to consider household incomes, the cost of living, access to essential services and the prospects available to young people. Security is equally inseparable from development. Businesses require a safe environment to operate, investors need confidence that their assets will be protected, and residents must be able to work, travel and conduct their daily activities without undue fear. Effective security depends on cooperation among government institutions, law-enforcement agencies, communities and other stakeholders. It also requires attention to the social and economic conditions that can leave vulnerable communities susceptible to criminal activity. A comprehensive strategy would combine effective policing and intelligence with improved street lighting, responsible urban planning, community engagement and opportunities for young people. The objective should be to create an environment where security supports economic activity and strengthens public confidence in government. Beyond infrastructure, employment and security lies the broader question of inclusion. Lagos’ diversity is one of its greatest strengths, but the benefits of development are not always experienced equally across its communities. An inclusive agenda under Hamzat would require public services to reach communities according to their needs, vulnerable residents to receive adequate consideration in urban planning, and economic opportunities to extend beyond a narrow segment of society. Such an approach would strengthen the social foundations of development and build confidence in the state’s long-term direction. Environmental sustainability presents another major challenge. Lagos’ coastal geography, intense rainfall, dense population and rapid urbanisation make drainage, waste management, flood prevention and climate resilience essential components of effective governance. Environmental interventions are most effective when infrastructure is supported by public education, enforcement and responsible urban planning. Drainage channels must be maintained, waste collection systems must function efficiently, and construction and land use must account for their environmental consequences. The next administration would have an opportunity to integrate environmental protection with transport, housing and infrastructure policies, reducing the long-term costs of environmental damage while protecting communities and supporting economic activity. The APC’s manifesto will provide an important platform for explaining how it intends to address these interconnected challenges. Its value, however, will depend on the clarity of its priorities and the credibility of its proposed solutions. A strong manifesto should identify the problems the government intends to solve, explain the policies through which it will pursue those objectives and demonstrate how the necessary resources will be mobilised. It should also establish a realistic basis for assessing progress after the election. For voters, the essential questions concern feasibility and delivery. Which projects will receive priority? How will the administration finance its commitments? What role will the private sector play? How will public spending translate into measurable improvements in living conditions? These questions do not diminish the importance of an ambitious vision. Rather, they underline the need to connect that vision with sound planning, responsible resource management and effective implementation. Public confidence will also depend on how the next administration engages with residents. A city as diverse and complex as Lagos cannot be governed effectively through a one-size-fits-all approach. Consultation with communities, businesses, professional groups, labour organisations, young people and civil society can help the government understand the practical consequences of its policies and identify solutions that might otherwise be overlooked. Such engagement should continue beyond the campaign period. Regular communication about policy decisions, project implementation and public expenditure would enable residents to understand government priorities and assess whether commitments are being fulfilled. For Hamzat, this presents an opportunity to make accountability a defining feature of his proposed administration. It would mean retaining successful policies, improving those that have fallen short and remaining open to new ideas that deliver better results. This distinction is particularly important in a state where the demands of urban growth continually evolve. Lagos needs a government capable of advancing long-term development projects while responding to immediate pressures on households and businesses. The significance of the 2027 election also extends beyond the immediate contest for the governorship. Lagos remains a major economic centre whose policies influence investment, employment and commercial activity across Nigeria. The effectiveness of its next administration will therefore have implications beyond the state’s borders. For the APC, retaining public confidence requires demonstrating that its years in government have established foundations capable of supporting further progress. The party must show that its experience can be translated into practical solutions for a population whose expectations continue to rise. Hamzat’s candidacy gives the party an opportunity to make that case through his administrative experience and a forward-looking development programme. His challenge is to present a credible vision that acknowledges previous achievements while addressing needs that remain unmet. The manifesto unveiling on October 30 will be an important moment in that process. It will allow the APC to explain how it intends to approach the next phase of Lagos’s development and how Hamzat proposes to translate his candidacy into a programme of governance. Ultimately, the success of that vision will not be determined by campaign promises alone. It will depend on the administration’s ability to establish clear priorities, mobilise resources, implement policies efficiently and deliver improvements that residents can see and experience. Lagos has demonstrated considerable capacity for growth and reinvention. Its next chapter will require the same ambition, reinforced by responsive planning, wider participation and a sustained commitment to improving everyday life. For Hamzat, the 2027 election represents an opportunity to help shape a Lagos that is more productive, better connected, safer and more inclusive. If the APC translates its development agenda into a credible programme of practical solutions, his candidacy could help consolidate the state’s gains while opening new possibilities for its people. The ultimate measure of success will be whether residents find it easier to move around the city, secure affordable homes, access decent jobs, operate businesses, raise families and plan for the future with greater confidence. That is the promise Hamzat must seek to fulfil, and the standard against which the next chapter of Lagos’s development will be judged.

title: Silence regime holds in Oleshky for 30 hours without incident – Lubinets
body:
The regime of silence in Oleshky, Kherson region, has lasted for 30 hours without a single incident, reported Verkhovna Rada Commissioner for Human Rights Dmytro Lubinets, noting that the parties continue to coordinate the implementation of the reached agreements.
"This was made possible, among other things, thanks to constant communication between me and Commissioner for Human Rights in Russia Yana Lantratova. We are in contact and coordinating the implementation of the reached agreements," Lubinets wrote on his Telegram channel on Wednesday morning.
He also thanked First Lady of the United States Melania Trump for her personal attention to the humanitarian mission and assistance to the civilian population of Oleshky, as well as her team for consistent support, constant communication, and efforts made. "Her direct involvement and coordination of the parties' efforts are an important component of this process," the Ombudsman noted.
According to Lubinets, the common goal is to ensure aid for the civilian population of Oleshky and create conditions for the safe departure of those in need.
"We continue to work. The most important thing is people's lives and safety," he emphasized.
As reported, the regime of silence in the area of the city of Oleshky, Kherson region, was declared at 3:00 on October 27. It will last until 22:59 on November 1 within the initiative of U.S First Lady Melania Trump to unblock the city.

title: Meet Google DeepMind’s Genie 4: Real-Time World Model With Native Audio
body: Google DeepMind has released Genie 4 as a research preview for trusted testers. The Genie 4 world model generates explorable worlds from text and image prompts in real time. It also generates the soundscape: ambient noise, music and character dialogue. Users move with keyboard controls and steer events with plain-language prompts. The bigger change is architectural. A Gemini model now runs inside the simulation loop as a planner. That pattern is important for anyone building training environments for agents or robots. TL;DR Runs on: Google-hosted only (Project Genie web app, Gemini API early access). Performance: Photorealistic worlds with native audio and live text steering. Best: Scene consistency for up to 2 minutes, double Genie 3, per TechCrunch’s briefing . Worst: Sessions last a few minutes , and objects drift after repeated prompt edits. What is Genie 4? Genie 4 is a world model from Google DeepMind that simulates interactive environments frame by frame. It is not a video clip generator. Each frame responds to user input as it arrives. DeepMind states that the model is natively multimodal . Audio, music and dialogue are generated together with the visuals. It is DeepMind’s first real-time world model to generate audio natively. It succeeds Genie 3 , announced in August 2025. Genie 3 ran at 720p and 24 frames per second, with visual memory reaching back 1 minute. How does Genie 4 use Gemini? Genie 4 borrows from 2 parts of the Gemini family. Gemini Omni anchors the look and behavior of each world. Other Gemini models handle the reasoning that keeps a simulation coherent. The runtime loop works like this: Interpret: When you type a prompt, Gemini adapts it to fit the running scene. Plan: Gemini 3.8 Flash breaks a goal into a sequence of steps. Verify: It reviews incoming frames to confirm each step succeeded. Adapt: If the world shifts or you intervene, it revises the plan. Between user inputs, Gemini also steers the scene so the world keeps progressing. DeepMind team frames this as an early step toward hybrid world models . In that design, a language model handles structure and narrative, while Genie renders pixels and sound. What can you do inside a Genie 4 world? Steer with text : You can change the weather, move the camera or add a new person or object mid-session. Simulate physics and people : DeepMind cites aerodynamics and collisions. It calls human motion the biggest leap, with characters that react to their surroundings. Hear the world : Every world carries ambient audio. Characters can also hold conversations that react to your inputs in real time. Test robot tasks : In one research demo, Gemini 4 Argon split a checkers task into steps. Genie 4 received each step as a text caption and simulated Apptronik’s Apollo humanoid playing the game. How does Genie 4 compare with other world models? DeepMind released no benchmark tables for Genie 4. The comparison below uses only disclosed specs from each project’s own source. Feature Genie 4 Genie 3 Runway GWM Worlds 2 Skywork Matrix-Game 3.0 Released Oct 27, 2026 Aug 5, 2025 Sep 3, 2026 Mar 27, 2026 Parameters Not disclosed Not disclosed Not disclosed 5B (plus 2x14B MoE variant) Resolution / FPS Not disclosed 720p / 24 fps 720p / 24 fps 720p / up to 40 fps Native audio Yes, incl. dialogue Not reported Yes, 48 kHz, incl. speech Not reported Mid-session text control Yes, Gemini-mediated Yes, promptable world events Yes, timestamped text actions Keyboard and mouse actions LLM planner in loop Gemini 3.8 Flash No No (optional external harness) No Consistency A few minutes; 2 min per TechCrunch A few minutes; 1 min visual memory No preset length; memory imperfect Minute-long memory Hardware Google-hosted, not disclosed Google-hosted, not disclosed Runway-hosted, not disclosed 8 GPUs for DiT plus 1 for VAE Access / license Trusted testers; AI Ultra and API soon Project Genie (AI Ultra) Research preview, contact form MIT, open weights window.addEventListener("message",function(e){if(e.data&&e.data.g4xHeight){var f=document.getElementById("g4x-frame");if(f)f.style.height=e.data.g4xHeight+"px";}}); Who can use Genie 4, and when? Genie 4 is live for trusted testers today. According to DeepMind, it is expected to be available soon to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie . Early access partners of the Gemini API and Google AI Studio come next. All Genie 4 video and audio will carry SynthID watermarks. DeepMind states that it ran internal safety evaluations before the preview. Testers so far span creative industries, journalism, education, gaming and engineering. Reported uses include: Filmmakers running multiple live ‘takes’ for pre-visualization. Photojournalists turning a single archival photo into a grounded simulation. Game developers testing styles and mechanics before writing engine code. Enterprise partners generating zero-to-one simulation scenarios. What are Genie 4’s limitations? DeepMind lists several open problems on the Genie 4 model page : Visual details and object permanence drift in longer sessions, after complex prompt edits, or during navigation. Interaction is limited to a few minutes, not extended sessions. Real-world locations are not simulated with perfect accuracy. Legible text usually appears only when it is in the input description. Real-time audio accuracy and multi-agent interactions remain unsolved. Key Takeaways Genie 4 generates world, ambient audio and dialogue together, in real time. Gemini 3.8 Flash plans, checks frames and replans inside the loop. No parameters, resolution, frame rate or benchmarks were disclosed. Access starts with trusted testers, then AI Ultra and Gemini API partners. Drift and short sessions remain the main practical limits. Check out the Genie 4 announcement , the Genie 4 model page and the Project Genie waitlist . title: Five epic cup shocks after Arsenal’s League Cup humiliation
body: Arsenal suffered a stunning League Cup fourth-round defeat at fourth-tier Fleetwood on Tuesday. The Premier League champions lost 5-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in one of the greatest shocks in the history of English football. AFP Sport looks at five other epic cup upsets: Wrexham 2 Arsenal 1 (1992 FA Cup) The previous season 90 places had separated the two clubs in the English Football League, with Arsenal having claimed their second title in three seasons under manager George Graham. Alan Smith put the Gunners in front, but Mickey Thomas’s free-kick levelled matters with 10 minutes remaining and Steve Watkin astonishingly claimed a late winner. Chelsea 2 Bradford 4 (2015 FA Cup) Chelsea won the FA Cup five times between 2006 and 2018, but Jose Mourinho’s Blues were humbled by third tier Bradford at Stamford Bridge. The Premier League leaders went 2-0 up through Gary Cahill and Ramires. But Bradford stormed back and goals from Jon Stead, Filipe Morais, Andy Halliday and Mark Yeates left Chelsea in tatters. Hereford 2 Newcastle 1 (1972 FA Cup) The fourth-round tie that had everything: pitch invasions by Parka-clad fans and Ronnie Radford scoring one of the FA Cup’s greatest FA Cup goals. Malcolm Macdonald put Newcastle ahead eight minutes from time and it seemed as if there would be no fairytale for the non-league outfit. But Radford equalised with a screamer from 25 yards and Ricky George won it for Hereford in extra-time. Liverpool 0 Wimbledon 1 (1988 FA Cup) Wimbledon’s ‘Crazy Gang’ were given no chance to stop Liverpool from claiming a league and cup double in the final at Wembley. Wimbledon had been a third-tier side four years earlier and Liverpool had won the title by a margin of nine points. But Lawrie Sanchez headed home from Dennis Wise’s free-kick before Wimbledon keeper Dave Beasant saved John Aldridge’s penalty to seal the upset. Grimsby 2 Manchester United 2, Grimsby won 12-11 on penalties (2025 League Cup) United trailed 2-0 as Grimsby duo Charles Vernam and Tyrell Warren scored to expose the flaws in their supposedly superior opponents. Bryan Mbeumo and Harry Maguire managed to take the second-round tie into extra-time. But Grimsby won on penalties to leave then-United boss Ruben Amorim shell-shocked. AFP The post Five epic cup shocks after Arsenal’s League Cup humiliation appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: IDF kills Hamas commandos involved in Alexander Dancyg's October 7 kidnapping
body: The IDF announced that it had eliminated three members of Hamas' elite Nukhba force in separate airstrikes across the Gaza Strip last week, including an operative accused of participating in the October 7, 2023, abductions of Israeli civilians. Ahmed Muhammad Ahmed Baraka was eliminated Thursday in an airstrike in southern Gaza, according to the IDF. The military identified Baraka as a member of Hamas' Nukhba force, the elite unit that played a central role in the October 7 attacks on southern Israel.   According to the IDF, Baraka was among the Hamas terrorists who infiltrated Kibbutz Nir Oz, one of the communities hardest hit in the attack, and participated in the kidnapping of several Israeli civilians, including Alexander Dancyg, a Holocaust educator who was abducted from his home and later died in Hamas captivity. The IDF said Baraka also helped hold several Israeli hostages in southern Gaza during the war, including Nimrod Cohen, an Israeli soldier abducted on October 7. In a separate airstrike Friday in northern Gaza, Israeli forces eliminated two other Hamas operatives: Omar Awadallah, identified as a Nukhba platoon commander, and Moataz Mahmoud Mohammed Al-Nimr, also a member of the elite force. The IDF said all three men had been involved in planning attacks against Israeli troops and civilians, particularly in recent days, while working to rebuild Hamas' military capabilities. The army described their activities as violations of the ceasefire agreement and said the strikes were intended to eliminate threats posed by the operatives. Before carrying out the strikes, the IDF took measures to minimize harm to civilians, including the use of precision munitions and aerial surveillance. Israeli forces remain deployed in parts of Gaza under the terms of the ceasefire agreement. The IDF said its troops would continue operations against what it considers security threats.

title: Safeguards Against ‘Trojan Horses’ in EU Will ‘Bite Hard,’ Warns Enlargement Chief
body:
Safeguards introduced to rein in member states that do not adhere to the EU’s rules and values will “bite hard” to curb “Trojan horses” inside the bloc, Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos has told TVP World.
Kos said the EU had introduced the safeguards in light of its experience with Hungary’s former pro-Moscow leadership.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“If the new member states follow our rules, they will not even feel them,” she said. “But if they will go against them, then those safeguards will bite hard. So this is the main philosophy of these new safeguards.”
Kos was speaking after Sunday’s parliamentary election in Serbia —which has a history of balancing between Brussels and Moscow—was won by a political movement that grew out of widespread student-led protests against public-sector corruption.
In addition to problems with democratic fundamentals such as an independent judiciary, Serbia has been held back in its bid to join the EU by shortcomings in its “strategic alignment in the field of foreign and security policy,” Kos said.
She said if a candidate country is not strategically aligned with the European Union, “meaning being together in fighting Russia, especially in Russia’s war in Ukraine,” then it will be “very, very difficult for the country to advance,” in the accession process.
But Kos added that these issues can be addressed only when the new government has been formed in Belgrade.
The student movement that triumphed in Serbia’s parliamentary election has demands that tally with those of the EU, Kos said.
Describing the Serbian election result as “excellent,” Kos said the students’ demands—rule of law, democracy and free media, as well as fighting corruption—tally with “what we are demanding from Serbia in the accession process.”
“Serbia has been a candidate [for EU membership] for more than ten years, but... instead of advancing in the process, they were backsliding,” Kos said. “So this winning of the student list could be a new start for Serbia on the European path.”

title: My Endorsement Helped ‘A Lot’, Says Trump As Netanyahu Leads After 50% Of Votes Counted
body: US President Donald Trump said Wednesday that his endorsement of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in this week’s elections helped him “a lot”. “I think when the endorsement went out, it had helped him a lot,” Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One, referring to Netanyahu. The camp of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was ahead of the opposition on Wednesday after 50 percent of votes were counted in Israel’s pivotal general election, figures from the Central Elections Committee showed. After 50.1 percent of ballots were counted, Netanyahu’s bloc was projected to win 56 of the 120 seats in the parliament, compared with 49 for the opposition bloc and 15 for the Arab parties. The partial results are likely to change, and several exit polls showed the camps neck-and-neck without a majority. title: Zelensky: Ukraine receives average of just 12 Patriot missiles per month this year
body:
The head of state made this announcement during a conversation with journalists, according to a Ukrinform correspondent.
“The PURL program covers many different items: 20-millimeter rounds for the F-16, HIMARS, as well as Patriots and AIM. We buy a lot from the U.S. Europe paid, everything arrived, and everything was fine. But in some cases, especially with the Patriots, it’s a major challenge. Twelve missiles a month, on average—that’s what we’ll be getting in 2026,” Zelensky said.
The president noted that the search for interceptor missiles is something he works on every day.
“And when there’s a positive decision from one country or another, and they give me 5, 10, 20, or even just 2 missiles—I’m very grateful. I’m living in circumstances today where I constantly—every week—have to put together new packages, new missiles, new defenses. We need this every day—to save the lives of our people from Russian ballistic missiles. We need approval from the United States. That’s all,” the head of state remarked.
Regarding problems with the supply of interceptor missiles from the U.S. and other countries this month, Zelensky noted: “So, there are some documents right on Minister Hegset’s desk that he signed, and perhaps he thinks he signed everything, but that’s not the case. That’s because there’s a package from the United States containing 12 missiles, and he signed it. Great. But I’ve used 35 this month. And the question concerns the 23 that I found in other areas. When we spoke with President Trump in New York, I asked him, ‘Give me the winter package.’ I told him, ‘I need this package. Please approve this package now.” I specified the number of missiles and said that if you give them to me, we won’t strike any oil refineries. And he asked me where to get them. So I told him which countries have them. And he said they’ll do their best, but they need missiles because they don’t have very many themselves.”
As reported, in an interview with “TSN.Tyzhden,” Volodymyr Zelensky stated that progress is being made on the issue of providing Ukraine with missiles for the Patriot systems, but the process is moving very slowly. According to him, at the level of the U.S. Department of Defense, there are delays in the delivery of certain types of vital supplies to Ukraine.
In an i nterview with ABC News, the head of state said that over the past three months, Ukraine has received only 24 interceptor missiles for the Patriot systems from the U.S., although its needs are significantly greater.

title: Olympic Eagles begin U-23 AFCON Qualifier preparations in Ikenne
body:
Nigeria’s U-23 national team, the Olympic Eagles, have commenced preparations for next month’s U-23 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against the Democratic Republic of Congo, with 28 players participating in Tuesday’s opening training session in Ikenne, Ogun State.
The session took place at the Remo Stars Stadium under the supervision of head coach Eric Chelle, as the team began its build-up to the crucial qualifying fixtures.
However, Rangers International trio Chimobi Igwilo, Kenneth Igboke and Chibueze Oputa were excused from the session following their arrival from Algeria, where they featured for the Enugu-based club against MC Alger in the CAF Champions League.
The Olympic Eagles are currently based in Ijebu Ode, where they are staying at the AM2PM Hotel. The team will continue its training programme at the Remo Stars Stadium, which is also expected to stage the return leg of the qualifiers.
Despite the rainy weather on Tuesday evening, the players went through a light session designed to ease them into the preparations. The training began with stretching and muscle-relaxing exercises before progressing to ball work, passing drills and small-sided games.
The four goalkeepers in camp; Chinemerem Olughu, Clinton Andy, Ebenezer Harcourt and Michael Atata, initially worked separately under the supervision of goalkeeper trainer Olatunji Baruwa before the session continued.
The coaching crew has scheduled two training sessions for Wednesday at the same venue, with the first starting at 7:30am and the second at 5pm, as preparations gather momentum ahead of the qualifiers.
The squad list features players drawn from several Nigeria Premier Football League clubs and other domestic sides, with representatives from Rangers International, Rivers United, Sporting Lagos, Ikorodu City, Nasarawa United, Warri Wolves, Enyimba and Bendel Insurance, among others.

title: Scalable Vector Grief
body: What's the difference between Pro and DAST? Download the latest version of Burp Suite. Published: Tuesday, 27 October 2026 at 14:29 UTC Updated: Tuesday, 27 October 2026 at 14:29 UTC I tested eight popular SVG sanitizers and bypassed six of them. In this post, I'll show you how a response header can run JavaScript in Firefox even when the response body is completely harmless XML. I'll also show you how to get Safari to import a GIF as SVG and execute JavaScript from it. SVG is an image format that can contain scripts, event handlers, links, animations and even embedded HTML, so applications that accept SVG uploads usually run them through a sanitizer first. To see how well those sanitizers hold up, I tested the most popular SVG libraries according to ChatGPT: https://github.com/darylldoyle/svg-sanitizer https://github.com/Borewit/svg-sanitizer https://github.com/mattkrick/sanitize-svg https://github.com/alnorris/SVG-Sanitizer Library affected: mattkrick/sanitize-svg This library has so many bypasses that I'll only cover the interesting ones. My first finding was that you don't need to get HTML into an SVG. Switch the XML namespace on a single element to XHTML and the browser renders it as HTML directly inside the SVG. A with a JavaScript URL is all it takes: The same namespace trick works with iframes, which gives you srcdoc to play with: The library could also be bypassed with a plain old . It renders the SVG, which converts the element name to its camel-case form, foreignObject. It then hunts for the element with querySelectorAll('foreignobject') , which finds nothing, so the payload goes straight through: Even a nested SVG with an onload handler got through: This one didn't take much effort. The library let tags through untouched, so you could animate a link's href into a JavaScript URL: I bypassed the same library a second way using Kevin Mizu's trick , which uses to set a JavaScript URL in Safari: Libraries affected: bgalek/safe-svg, mattkrick/sanitize-svg, alnorris/SVG-Sanitizer Now things get more interesting. This is a pretty epic technique: you can get JavaScript execution from an XSLT stylesheet without needing a separate file. I was desperate to blog this one, because unfortunately the feature is deprecated and due for removal November 2026. The trick is to point an xml-stylesheet processing instruction at a data URL. Base64 is the most elegant way to encode the stylesheet, but URL encoding works too: Here's the stylesheet that gets base64 encoded: It matches the root of the document and outputs an HTML page containing a script that alerts document.domain, proving the code runs in the document's origin rather than a null origin. Put it all together and you get this: In the back of my mind was a trick Paulos Yibelo once told me about: Firefox lets you load external CSS files using a Link response header. I figured out that data URLs work there too, which got me thinking: if it works for CSS, could it work for XSLT too? You're damn right it can. First, I needed a version of the stylesheet that fits in a URL. This one has two layers. The outer stylesheet is URL encoded into a data URL. Inside it, XSLT's document() function loads a second data URL, URL encoded again, containing an XHTML with an onerror handler. The stylesheet copies that into a , where it fires. As a processing instruction, it looks like this: Here's the payload before encoding. I've left the Hackvertor tags in so you can see where each layer of URL encoding is applied: You can load and edit the full payload in Hackvertor . With the stylesheet ready, all that's left is to move it out of the document and into a Link header: The response body is a completely harmless bit of XML, yet this executes in Firefox! Libraries affected: cloudflare/svg-hush, jams2/py-svg-hush, bgalek/safe-svg To end this piece of research, here's another epic behaviour, this time in Safari. Firefox and Safari both let you use the element to reference same-origin files, but Safari goes a step further: it lets you import image files as SVG! Alas, you can't make a true SVG/image polyglot because SVG is a little too strict. However, if you can upload a GIF that contains the payload, it won't render when you open it in the browser, but it can still be imported with a element! That's all it takes to bypass all three libraries: I hope you enjoyed this post. I also exploited two popular applications that I can't name yet, but I'll update the post once I can. Both DOMPurify and darylldoyle/svg-sanitizer held up against everything in this post, which is quite impressive.

title: Russia launches over 10 strikes on Dnipropetrovsk region, damage reported
body:
Russian occupiers attacked Dnipropetrovsk region more than 10 times, damaging civilian infrastructure, reported Head of the Regional Military Administration Oleksandr Hanzha.

title: Europe struggles to top up gas storage at four-year high prices ahead of winter
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. In late October, European countries continue to inject small volumes of gas into underground storage facilities (UGS) ahead of the cold season, despite prices hitting a four-year high, according to TASS calculations based on data from Gas Infrastructure Europe (GIE).
Meanwhile, several countries have been net-withdrawing gas from European UGS facilities for the second consecutive week - with withdrawal volumes outstripping injections--signaling the gradual start of the heating season in the region.
To date, Europe has managed to inject only 75.5% of the gas volumes required for the upcoming winter, which amounts to 51 billion cubic meters.
As of October 26, European UGS facilities were 74.93% full, down from 82.9% a year earlier and 14.65 percentage points below the five-year average for this date. This remains the lowest level recorded for this date since monitoring began in 2011. EU storage facilities currently hold approximately 82.1 billion cubic meters of gas, which is 9.4 billion cubic meters less than last year and the lowest volume since 2013. Gazprom previously forecast that European gas inventories might fail to reach even the 75% mark, warning of a challenging autumn-winter season for the region.
Earlier TASS reported that Europe risks entering the heating season with record-low gas reserves. By the traditional start of the autumn-winter period, EU nations may only manage to fill their storage capacities to 70-75%, an all-time low for the start of a heating season.
Under European Commission regulations, EU member states must ensure their gas storage facilities are 90% full between October 1 and December 1 each year. A 10% flexibility margin is permitted under difficult filling conditions. Consequently, net injections into European storage facilities must reach at least 68 billion cubic meters to meet the requirement for the 2026-2027 autumn-winter season. However, hoping for a very mild winter, the European Commission is prepared to lower this threshold to 80% this year.

title: Shelling of Kharkiv region injures 14, including 4-year-old child, in past 24 hours
