title: Knife attack reported outside Israeli Embassy in Belgrade
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 28 (MNA) – Serbian police has reported that an unidentified attacker stabbed a guard with knives outside the Israeli Embassy in Belgrade before being shot dead.
Serbian police said on Wednesday that an unidentified assailant attacked a guard with knives outside the Israeli Embassy in Belgrade and was killed just after midnight.
Interior Minister Ivica Dacic said that police were treating the incident as a “terrorist attack” and had raised the terror threat to the highest level and stepped up police presence at key locations.
Dacic said that “a minor, so far unidentified … shouting Allahu Akbar, attacked the member of Gendarmerie and attacked him with two knives.” He added that the police officer “liquidated” the assailant in “self-defense” and was lightly wounded, according to ABC News.
Dacic said that Serbia's security agencies had been monitoring the attacker, who he said was a supporter of the Islamic State group. Dacic said that “he kept the black flag in support of the Islamic State on his Instagram” account.

title: ‘A very sad day’: Arteta despair as Arsenal stunned by Fleetwood
body: Mikel Arteta said Arsenal’s stunning League Cup defeat by fourth-tier Fleetwood was “a very sad day” as the Premier League champions suffered one of the most embarrassing results in their history. Arteta’s side crashed out 5-3 on penalties in an incredible fourth round upset after the tie finished 1-1 in normal time. Arsenal’s Bruno Guimaraes had his penalty saved by Jay Lynch in the shoot-out and Conor Haughey scored Fleetwood’s winner. Aaron Loupalo-Bi’s first-half goal had put Fleetwood ahead before Viktor Gyokeres equalised after the interval. Arsenal’s 16-year-old rising star Max Dowman was sent off for violent conduct in the closing stages. Arteta paid the price for prioritising Sunday’s Premier League trip to Liverpool as his decision to make nine changes backfired spectacularly. The Gunners boss conceded Arsenal could have no complaints, admitting it was a painful moment in his reign. “First of all, congratulations to Fleetwood for going through the next round. The manner that they have done it, and for us a very sad day,” Arteta said. “There is nothing to criticise the players for their attitude, their application. “The determination, you could see that was there from the start, even with 10 men. But we conceded a really poor goal to start with that gave them some momentum. “Obviously we have so much of the ball, so many chances, so many shots, and if you want the margins to be bigger than going to the penalties, you need to capitalise on that. And we didn’t. “It’s football, that’s the beauty of this competition. It’s a very sad day.” Arsenal had moved level on points with Premier League leaders Manchester City after a 2-0 victory over Everton on Saturday. But instead of extending their run of 11 wins from their 13 previous games, Arteta’s team returned to north London red-faced after a loss that ranks among the darkest days in the club’s glittering history. “Zero problem attitude-wise. Otherwise, I would be here absolutely fuming. I’m sad, I think we are all sad. We have a massive responsibility to carry this badge in the best possible way,” Arteta said. “You don’t capitalise, then you cannot go through to the next round. Unfortunately, we are out.” – ‘I just can’t believe it’ – Although it looked a harsh decision to send off Dowman for aiming a kick towards Harrison Neal, Arteta was unimpressed with the 16-year-old, giving him a stern word as the midfielder trudged off. “Something that we discussed already before the match,” Arteta said when asked what he told Dowman. “It’s difficult to see on the cameras like that, so I prefer to watch it back properly and then I can assess the situation.” Fleetwood made a mockery of the 84 places between the clubs in the English football system with a defiant display that stopped Arsenal establishing any momentum. Their refusal to be overawed by Arsenal’s star-power was a tribute to Fleetwood boss Matt Lawlor, who won the tactical battle with Arteta by sitting deep and attacking on the counter. “I just can’t believe it. The biggest night in the club’s history in terms of opposition coming to town and we’ve managed to beat the champions,” Lawlor said. “We’re not stupid enough and not egotistical enough that you think we’re going to out-play the best team in the country and the most organised team in the country. “So we had to ride our luck, we had to deny space, we had to deny options for them. And I think we did that really, really well in terms of the majority of the game.” While Lawlor was composed during the match, his emotions poured out in his tearful celebration as jubilant Fleetwood fans invaded the pitch after the winning penalty. “I’m just so glad that the lads have the feeling the way they are and took that performance into make that town, the club, everyone proud,” he said. The post ‘A very sad day’: Arteta despair as Arsenal stunned by Fleetwood appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Anti-drone net protects municipal bus from FPV drone strike in Zaporizhia – regional military administration
body:
In Zaporizhia, a Russian FPV drone attempted to attack a municipal bus on Tuesday evening, but became entangled in an anti-drone net and exploded, reported Head of Zaporizhia Regional Military Administration Mykhailo Semikin.

"The bus sustained minor damage. Most importantly, all passengers are safe and unharmed," he wrote on Telegram.

According to him, the attack occurred around 22:30.

"This is yet another proof of how important it is to protect our roads with anti-drone nets. We are continuing this work," Semikin added.

title: DARPA Tests Autonomous Combat Vehicles That Detect Targets Coordinate Battlefield Ops
body:
Four unmanned ground vehicles developed under the U.S. Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency’s (DARPA) Robotic Autonomy in Complex Environments with Resiliency (RACER) program demonstrated autonomous battlefield capabilities at Fort Knox’s St. Vith Range on October 15.
Two dozen military and government representatives witnessed the exercise.
The demonstration tested an end-to-end operation, from satellite imagery to tactical ground activity. An operator identified a simulated threat using satellite imagery and tasked the vehicles to investigate. The lead vehicle, carrying a drone, navigated the terrain using onboard sensors and detected a potential target. Two vehicles advanced to provide simulated cover, while the fourth moved forward. A simulated rocket struck a target approximately 300 yards away on an adjacent hill.
The drone could potentially inspect targets more closely or conduct strikes if equipped with munitions.
DARPA technical adviser Jason Gregory said the exercise marked the program’s first demonstration connecting satellite imagery directly to tactical ground operations.
The vehicles autonomously navigate, assess terrain, coordinate movements and detect targets. However, human operators retain authority over engagements. Detected targets are transmitted to an operator for approval before any attack.
RACER has spent approximately five years developing software for high-speed autonomous movement across complex off-road terrain, targeting speeds comparable to human drivers. The program combines vehicle platforms, sensors, drive-by-wire controls and autonomy software, drawing on three technology companies working on vehicle design, algorithms, autonomous intelligence and secure communications.
The modular vehicles can potentially carry weapons, drones and rockets, as well as support reconnaissance, logistics, food and ammunition delivery, and casualty evacuation. Their practical capabilities will depend on payload capacity, endurance and reliability, which the demonstration did not establish under combat conditions.
The test followed a request from U.S. European Command (EUCOM) to explore deploying robotic assets beyond the forward line of troops for early threat detection.

title: Nigerian extradited from Benin to US over alleged $100m tax fraud
body: A 43-year-old Nigerian, Akinade Adedeji Raheem, has been extradited from Benin to the United States to face federal charges over an alleged scheme involving more than $100 million in fraudulent tax refund claims using stolen identities. Raheem was arraigned in a US federal court following his extradition and ordered detained in the custody of the US Marshals Service pending further proceedings, according to the US Department of Justice. Prosecutors alleged that Raheem and his co-conspirators filed more than 300 fraudulent tax returns between 2018 and 2023, seeking over $100 million in refunds from the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). US Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg said the alleged operation involved hundreds of stolen identities and significant financial losses. “Raheem and his co-conspirators allegedly obtained hundreds of stolen identities, filed fraudulent tax returns using that information, and laundered the proceeds through prepaid debit cards and purchases of used cars that were shipped to Nigeria and other locations,” Hertzberg said. “The scope of the alleged fraud is staggering. Thanks to the dedication of the prosecution team and our law enforcement partners around the world, Raheem has been extradited to the United States,” he added. The indictment also named Abayomi Quadri Eletu, a resident of the United Kingdom and Nigeria, as an alleged co-conspirator. Eletu was indicted separately and arrested in the UK, where extradition proceedings are pending. According to court documents, the suspects allegedly obtained the personal information of American taxpayers and tax professionals, including names, addresses and Social Security numbers, to facilitate fraudulent claims. Investigators said the alleged scheme involved creating online IRS accounts to access private taxpayer information, filing false returns and directing refunds to prepaid debit cards linked to addresses controlled by the suspects. Prosecutors further alleged that Raheem, Eletu and others laundered some of the proceeds by purchasing money orders in amounts intended to avoid reporting requirements. The money was allegedly used to acquire used cars through auction platforms, some of which were shipped to Nigeria, as well as designer clothing and other items. Special Agent in Charge Christopher J. Altemus Jr. of the IRS Criminal Investigation Texas Field Office said the alleged scheme affected hundreds of taxpayers. “Raheem is an alleged co-conspirator in a nationwide identity theft scheme that victimised hundreds of taxpayers. The fraud also stole from the US Treasury, impacting programmes serving us all,” Altemus said. He added that authorities were working internationally to bring suspects in financial crimes to justice. “We are pursuing financial criminals to take back the stolen money and their freedom,” he said. Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration Special Agent-in-Charge Anthony Colello said the case demonstrated the commitment of investigators and prosecutors to tackling fraud. “The investigative efforts of the Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration (TIGTA) and its partners, along with the prosecutorial work of the US Attorney’s Office, demonstrate the commitment to pursuing, capturing, and prosecuting those who try to defraud the American people,” Colello said. According to the Justice Department, US federal agents sought to arrest Raheem at his residence in April 2026 but were unable to locate him. Investigators later discovered that he had booked a flight from Mexico City to Benin. Raheem arrived in Benin on April 15, 2026, and was arrested by local authorities pursuant to an INTERPOL Red Notice. Beninese authorities subsequently extradited him to the United States. The Justice Department described the extradition as only the second transfer of a suspect from Benin to the US in history. A federal grand jury in the Northern District of Georgia indicted Raheem on February 24, 2026, on charges including conspiracy to commit wire and mail fraud, conspiracy to commit money laundering, 14 counts of access device fraud and 14 counts of aggravated identity theft. If convicted, he faces maximum prison terms of 20 years for conspiracy to commit wire and mail fraud, 20 years for conspiracy to commit money laundering and 10 years for access device fraud. The aggravated identity theft charges carry a mandatory two-year sentence, according to the Justice Department. The case is being investigated by the IRS Criminal Investigation unit and TIGTA, with assistance from international law enforcement agencies and authorities in Benin and the United Kingdom. Assistant US Attorney Brian Pearce, alongside Senior Litigation Counsel Michael C. Boteler and Trial Attorney Michael Jones, is prosecuting the case. The Justice Department emphasised that the indictment contains allegations and that Raheem and other defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in court. The post Nigerian extradited from Benin to US over alleged $100m tax fraud appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Benue police rescue 29 kidnap victims, arrest 34 foreigners
body:
The Benue State Police Command says it rescued 29 kidnap victims and arrested 34 foreign nationals during security operations across the state in October.
The Commissioner of Police, Cletus Nwadiogbu, disclosed this on Tuesday while briefing journalists on the command’s operational achievements at its headquarters in Makurdi.
He attributed the rescues to intelligence-led operations and collaboration with other security agencies and community-based security groups.
Mr Nwadiogbu said four passengers abducted after gunmen attacked a commercial vehicle along the Uzer village axis of Ayilamo-Tse-Abi Road in Logo Local Government Area on 5 October were rescued in a joint operation involving the police, Operation Whirl Stroke, Benue State Civil Protection Guards and local hunters.
He said 17 farmers abducted from Tse-Acha and Tse-Wuam communities in Bamun village, Tombo District, Logo LGA, were rescued on 7 October.
The commissioner also said eight kidnap victims, including a Catholic priest, were rescued in Ohimini LGA following their abduction along the Ugbokolo-Ajegbe-Awume Road on 13 October.
PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that police announced the rescue of eight victims and the arrest of two suspects after the abduction along the road.
The police statement at the time did not confirm whether the rescued victims included Reverend Father John Inalegwu Otache, who was reported abducted on the same day.
Mr Nwadiogbu said the command arrested 34 foreign nationals in two separate operations during the month.
He said 16 Cameroonian nationals were arrested in Otukpo LGA on 9 October after they allegedly failed to produce the required travel documents.
On 22 October, operatives intercepted 18 Nigerien nationals at Orokam while they were reportedly travelling to Ikom in Cross River State.
The commissioner said the foreign nationals were taken into custody for investigation and verification of their immigration status, with the relevant authorities, including the Nigeria Immigration Service, to be involved.
He said investigations were ongoing to establish the circumstances of their entry into Nigeria and movements within the country.
The police commissioner also reported arrests in separate operations against suspected cultists and other suspected offenders in Naka, Makurdi, Aliade and Gwer East.
He said the command recovered seven locally fabricated firearms, 16 rounds of ammunition and cartridges, charms, mobile phones and ATM cards during the operations.
Mr Nwadiogbu further disclosed that a suspected bandit was killed during an encounter involving Operation Zenda personnel along Amaafu-Abaji Road in Katsina-Ala LGA on 2 October. A locally fabricated firearm was recovered during the operation.
In a separate case, the commissioner said police arrested a 60-year-old man over the alleged rape of a 10-year-old girl in Igumale, Ado LGA.
He said the incident was reported on 13 October and the victim was taken for medical examination and treatment. He added that investigations were ongoing and that the victim’s privacy and welfare would be protected.
Mr Nwadiogbu urged residents to provide credible information to security agencies, saying public cooperation was essential to preventing crime and protecting lives and property.

title: Over 80% Students Discharged, Govt Investigating Cause Of Bilharzia Drug Reactions — Health Commissioner
body: The Katsina State Government says the health condition of students affected by adverse reactions during a Bilharzia treatment and prevention exercise at Government Science Secondary School, Batagarawa, has significantly improved, with more than 80 percent already discharged and returned to school. The State Commissioner for Health, Hon. Musa Adamu Funtua, gave the assurance in an exclusive interview with Channels Television on Wednesday, stating that the situation had remained under control from the onset due to swift intervention by health authorities and what he described as God’s mercy. According to the commissioner, only eight students were still receiving medical attention as of Wednesday morning during his visit to Ahmadi Rimi Specialist Hospital, Katsina, adding that only one of them remained on intravenous treatment after doctors diagnosed him with malaria, rather than complications linked to the Bilharzia medication. “As Hausa people say, every child belongs to all of us. No one would deliberately do anything to harm a child,” Funtua said, stressing that the treatment exercise was a routine preventive health programme aimed at protecting children from Bilharzia. He explained that preliminary findings suggest there may have been a gap between breakfast and the administration of the medication, and noted that the government has already formed a committee to determine the exact cause of the incident. Edo State Commissioner for Health, Hon. Musa Adamu Funtua The commissioner said the exercise had been successfully conducted on the first day without any incident, while the reactions occurred during the second phase of the programme. He added that once the incident was reported, all affected students were immediately evacuated to hospitals for emergency medical care, a response he said helped stabilize the situation quickly. During his hospital visit, Funtua said he met with the school’s Vice Principal, medical personnel and parents, and also observed several students carrying on with normal activities, including returning from morning prayers and having breakfast. He reassured parents and residents that the government remained committed to the welfare of every child and pledged to implement recommendations from the ongoing investigation to prevent a recurrence. The incident involved no fewer than 64 students who developed symptoms including vomiting, abdominal discomfort and dizziness after receiving medication during a Bilharzia treatment campaign conducted by Primary Health Care authorities in collaboration with Batagarawa Local Government. The students were taken to Ahmadi Rimi Specialist Hospital and Turai Yar’Adua Maternal and Child Hospital for treatment, where medical officials confirmed they responded positively to care. The Medical Director of Ahmadi Rimi Specialist Hospital, Dr. Auwal Sani, had earlier disclosed that some students arrived unconscious but recovered following prompt medical intervention. He explained that the drugs were administered according to each student’s height to ensure the correct dosage. Also confirming the development, the Commissioner for Basic and Secondary Education, Yusuf Sulaiman Jibia, said all affected students had recovered, and arrangements had been made for their return to school. While investigations into the exact cause of the reactions continue, the Katsina State Government has assured residents that routine Bilharzia prevention programmes remain an important public health strategy and that lessons from the incident will be used to strengthen future interventions.
