title: FG moves to secure farms, attract investors
body: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federal Government has moved to address insecurity threatening agricultural investments, signing a partnership agreement to develop security arrangements for farms and attract investors to multibillion-dollar soybean and sugarcane projects in Yobe and Jigawa states. The Ministry of Finance Incorporated (MOFI), Integranium Holdings and Defence Agricultural Assets and Projects Development Company (DAPCO), supported by Defence Holding Company Limited, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in Abuja. Speaking at the signing ceremony, Dr Femi Ogunseinde, MOFI’s Executive Director, Investments, said: “We have a soybean initiative in Yobe, we have a sugarcane initiative in Jigawa—all large-scale, all multibillion-dollar projects. “Without having that security anchor to ensure that whatever comes from wherever to invest, the investments are safe, it becomes very difficult for us to do anything.” He said the partnership would provide a platform to approach prospective investors with security arrangements designed to protect their investments. Also speaking, the Managing Director of MOFI, Dr Armstrong Takang, said: “Nigeria needed to make better use of its land, water resources and people to produce sufficient food for households and industries, while generating additional supplies for export.” He said the partnership would focus on developing bankable agribusiness opportunities capable of attracting public and private investment. On his part, DAPCO Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Aliyu Abdulhameed, said: “The defence establishment’s role was to ensure that financing reached agricultural opportunities in rural areas under secure and properly structured arrangements.” He added that surrounding communities would be involved in projects established in their areas, while serving military personnel and veterans would also be considered. Ogunseinde said: “An estimated 30 million to 35 million hectares of land could be available for farming, providing considerable scope for expanding large-scale agricultural production.” He added that the partners had identified several opportunities and expected at least one project to break ground before year-end, although he did not identify the project or specify a commencement date. The Group Managing Director of Defence Holding Company Limited, Air Vice Marshal A.V. Ndache, said: “The memorandum of understanding signed by the institutions was a broad agreement covering agriculture, hospitality and other investment areas.” The post FG moves to secure farms, attract investors appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Prince William Praises Kazakhstan’s Success in Restoring Saiga Population
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA – Prince William has praised Kazakhstan’s efforts to restore its saiga population, highlighting the country’s conservation achievements during an appearance on the BBC’s The Graham Norton Show on Oct. 23. Prince William discusses Kazakhstan’s saiga recovery on The Graham Norton Show. Photo credit: The Graham Norton Show / So Television / BBC The Prince of Wales noted that saigas, which were once on the brink of extinction, have made a significant recovery, emphasizing the role of the Kazakh government in supporting conservation efforts. According to the Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources, Kazakhstan’s saiga population has grown from just 21,000 in 2003 to 4.689 million, according to the results of the spring 2026 census. The recovery has received international recognition. In 2024, Kazakhstan’s Altyn Dala Conservation Initiative won the Earthshot Prize, founded by Prince William, in the Protect and Restore Nature category. Established in 2005, the initiative is a long-term partnership involving Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources, the Association for the Conservation of Biodiversity of Kazakhstan and international conservation organizations. Its work focuses on restoring saiga populations, protecting their habitats and preserving the country’s steppe ecosystems. The initiative also participated in London Climate Action Week from June 23 to 27, joining international leaders and organizations to advance climate and nature solutions. Its representatives met with influential figures, including Prince William, during events such as Leading with Impact and Investing for Impact. Kazakhstan’s saiga recovery has become a prominent example of wildlife conservation, demonstrating the potential of sustained government support and partnerships between national and international conservation organizations. The post Prince William Praises Kazakhstan’s Success in Restoring Saiga Population appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: President Sheikh Mohamed establishes Zayed the Founder Day to honour Sheikh Zayed's enduring legacy
body: President Sheikh Mohamed has unveiled a new national day to celebrate the “life and legacy” of UAE Founding Father, the late Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan. The UAE leader said Zayed the Founder Day – which will be marked on January 7 – would pay homage to Sheikh Zayed's “vision, generosity and service to humanity”. Sheikh Mohamed said the annual occasion would serve as an opportunity to ensure Sheikh Zayed's values continue to play a crucial role in guiding the country's progress. “The UAE’s Founding Father, the late Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, forever remains in the hearts of the people of the UAE,” Sheikh Mohamed wrote on X. “As he led efforts to establish the Union, laid its foundations, and nurtured its development, his life and legacy were defined by his vision, generosity, and service to humanity. “Today, we declare 7 January as Zayed the Founder Day, a new annual national occasion dedicated to celebrating his enduring legacy, transforming wisdom into action, and ensuring these values continue to inspire our nation on its steadfast path of progress towards the future.” The UAE’s Founding Father, the late Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, forever remains in the hearts of the people of the UAE. As he led efforts to establish the Union, laid its foundations, and nurtured its development, his life and legacy were defined by his vision, generosity,… — محمد بن زايد (@MohamedBinZayed) October 28, 2026 Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid, Vice President and Ruler of Dubai, said the annual event would be a "celebration of our unity and solidarity". He described Sheikh Zayed as an "inspirer of generations" in a warm tribute shared on social media. Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed, Vice President, Deputy Prime Minister and Chairman of the Presidential Court, hailed the UAE's latest step to champion Sheikh Zayed's critical role in the birth of a nation. “The announcement by His Highness the President establishing Zayed the Founder Day renews the legacy of the Founding Father, Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan, and the values upon which our nation was built,” Sheikh Mansour wrote on X. “The greatest tribute to the late Sheikh Zayed is that his vision lives within us, and his values remain firmly rooted in generations to come.” In February, Sheikh Mansour approved the strategic plan of The Founder's Office, which is dedicated to honouring Sheikh Zayed's contributions to the Emirates. The strategy established a national framework to ensure the life, legacy, values and principles of Sheikh Zayed remain a "living source of inspiration for current and future generations", state news agency Wam reported at the time. The office will seek to provide a platform to shine a light on the achievements of the country's inaugural president, both in the Emirates and on the global stage. Unifying vision Sheikh Zayed served as the UAE's first president after uniting the emirates to form a new nation on December 2, 1971. He oversaw the country's rapid rise on the regional and global stage in the years that followed, proving hugely influential in the nation's transformation. He would become a familiar figure on the world stage until his death on the 19th day of Ramadan in 2004 , with his contributions still felt across the Emirates and beyond. Abu Dhabi's landmark Zayed National Museum – which opened to coincide with National Day celebrations last year – highlights how the UAE has sought to promote and preserve Sheikh Zayed's legacy. During Sheikh Zayed's time as Ruler of Abu Dhabi and UAE President, the country’s humanitarian and development aid reached more than Dh90 billion and 117 of the 193 countries represented in the UN, Wam reported. This generosity is reflected in the huge number of institutions and projects on every continent that honour Sheikh Zayed’s name.

title: Cooking gas supply rises 18% to 4.5m litres daily — NMDPRA
body: By Ediri Ejoh Domestic supply of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG), popularly known as cooking gas, rose by 17.78 per cent year-on-year, YoY, to 4.5 million litres per day in September 2026, from 3.7 million litres per day in September 2025. The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, NMDPRA, disclosed this in its latest data obtained by Vanguard. On a month-on-month, MoM, basis, supply increased by 33.33 per cent from 4.5 million litres per day in August 2026. Meanwhile, the price of cooking gas rose by 7.14 per cent to N1,400 per kg in October 2026, from N1,300 per kg in September. Reacting, former National President of the Nigerian Association of Liquefied Petroleum Gas Marketers, NALPGAM, Mr. Oladapo Olatunbosun, attributed the increase to improved local production but called for sustained investment and government support to prevent shortages. He said: “Local production has increased, which is the reason for the result. However, there is much to be done by both the government and stakeholders to drive the development required to harness the potential of LPG.” Olatunbosun urged the government to encourage indigenous operators and support major domestic producers, including Dangote Petroleum Refinery, to boost output and stabilise the energy market. “The government should continue to encourage indigenous operators, and they should see it as being a partner in bringing stability to energy,” he said. He also called for affordable supplies to surrounding communities, adding that increased investment in production and distribution would improve availability. “The market is wide and large, and the more we get people investing in the production and distribution of LPG, the more available the product will be,” he said. Similarly, National President of the Oil and Gas Services Providers Association of Nigeria, OGSPAN, Mazi Colman Obasi, described the supply growth as positive but stressed that consumers must benefit through improved access and affordability. “The growth in supply is a positive development because availability is fundamental to the expansion of LPG consumption. However, the real test is whether consumers are seeing improved access and more affordable prices,” he said. Obasi cautioned that increased supply would not automatically reduce retail prices, citing transportation, logistics, exchange-rate movements and other costs. He said efficient distribution was essential to ensure additional volumes reach consumers and encourage more households to switch to LPG. The post Cooking gas supply rises 18% to 4.5m litres daily — NMDPRA appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Egypt and Saudi Arabia look to contain regional crisis
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 28 (MNA) – The Egyptian Foreign Ministry has released a statement following a phone call between its foreign minister and his Saudi counterpart on Tuesday.
Badr Abdelatty and Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud discussed “efforts to contain” the current crisis in the West Asia region, with a focus on preventing escalation, the statement said.
Both countries also pledged to “continue close coordination”.

title: Air defenses neutralize 71 Russian drones overnight
body:
The Ukrainian Air Force said this in a Telegram post , Ukrinform reports.
According to the military, starting at 18:00 on Tuesday, October 27, Russia attacked Ukraine with an Iskander-M/S-400 ballistic missile launched from Taganrog and 88 attack UAVs, including Shahed-type drones (38 of them jet-powered), S8000 Banderol/Dan-T missiles, Gerberas, and Parodiya-type decoy drones. The attacks came from the directions of Oryol and Kursk in Russia and Hvardiiske in temporarily occupied Crimea.
The air attack was repelled by aircraft, anti-aircraft missile units, electronic warfare and unmanned systems units, and mobile fire groups of Ukraine's Defense Forces.
Preliminary data indicate that, as of 08:00 on Wednesday, October 28, air defenses had shot down or suppressed 71 drones.
Several attack UAVs remain in the air, with combat operations ongoing.
Impacts were recorded at eight locations, while debris from downed targets fell at two locations.

title: Winter speed limits take effect on Finnish roads this week
body:
Speed limits on main roads will generally be lowered to 80 km/h, though some limits will drop to 70.
Winter and darkness-related speed limits will take effect on Finland's main roads this week, according to the Finnish Transport Infrastructure Agency.
The agency said the main changeover day is Wednesday, though limits will be switched by Friday at the latest.
Speed limits on main roads will generally be lowered to 80 km/h, though on some road sections limits will drop to 70 km/h. On motorways, speed limits will go down to 100 km/h.
Decisions on winter restrictions are made by regional Centres for Economic Development, Transport and the Environment.
However, as in recent years, Fintraffic can raise variable speed limits on motorways to 120 km/h until the end of November. This measure requires that weather and road conditions, as well as the road-specific speed limit, allow it.
The switch to winter season speed limits comes at the end of October, as a large proportion of road traffic now occurs in darkness, following the end of daylight saving time last Sunday .

title: Capemay Properties launches Capemay Futures to equip young people with industry skills
body: Ghanaian real estate company, Capemay Properties, has launched Capemay Futures, an internship and youth development initiative aimed at bridging the gap between classroom learning and practical industry experience. The programme will expose high school and university students to career opportunities in real estate development, architecture, investment and finance, among other fields. Capemay Properties says the initiative is designed to equip young people with practical industry knowledge through professional mentorship, guided site visits, interactive learning sessions and practical assignments. The programme features two learning pathways: a High School Leadership Programme focused on industry exposure and transferable skills, and a University Internship Programme offering extended workplace learning opportunities. Project Lead for Capemay Futures and Head of Sales, Marketing and Asset Management at Capemay Properties, Belinda Boadu, said the initiative is intended to help young people gain a better understanding of the real estate industry and the range of career opportunities available within the sector. “At Capemay Properties, we have been running internship programmes for sometime and we have decided to formalize and structure our internship programme and that brought about the Capemay Futures initiative and we hope students from high school and universities can come on board and gain real experience from the real estate industry”, she said. Participants will have opportunities to explore luxury property sales, marketing, architecture and design, investment and finance, as well as property management, subject to available placements and programme requirements. Eligibility and application Head of Human Resources and Procurement at Capemay Properties, Naomi Fenteng, outlined the eligibility requirements for prospective applicants, explaining who can apply to benefit from the initiative. The programme is targeted at eligible high school and university students seeking practical exposure to complement their academic learning. Capemay Properties says Capemay Futures will also strengthen partnerships with educational institutions by providing a channel through which schools and universities can refer eligible students for consideration. The initiative seeks to connect academic learning with the practical demands of the real estate sector while helping young people develop relevant skills and make informed career decisions. Through the programme, the company aims to provide students with greater insight into the processes and professional expertise involved in real estate development and management.

title: PH spotlights South China Sea, ‘fragmenting world’ in ASEAN defense chiefs’ meeting
body: CEBU, Philippines — Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. told Southeast Asian defense chiefs, whose countries have widely varying ties with superpower China, that the bloc should “not allow differences to divide us from within.” “ASEAN [Association of Southeast Asian Nations] was founded on the belief that our strength lies in our diversity. We must therefore not allow our differences to divide us from within, and where such differences exist, including in the South China Sea, we shall settle them through peaceful and legal means,” said Teodoro, chairman of the ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting, to open the event on Wednesday, October 28. Regional security, as well as bloc cooperation over issues like disaster risk reduction, will be among the key issues defense officials are expected to tackle in meetings and sideline events from October 28 to 29 at the Mactan Expo in Lapu-Lapu City. Ministers, as well as working groups, are also expected to tackle protection of underwater critical infrastructure, cooperation for food and energy security, and preparedness for the super El Niño and its possible effects on security. Play Video ADMM and the ADMM-Plus is an annual gathering of defense ministers from Southeast Asia and “plus countries” or ADMM dialogue partners Australia, China, India, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, Russia, and the United States. It is the largest defense diplomacy gathering in ASEAN for the calendar year. Aside from all 11 defense chiefs from Southeast Asia, their counterparts for almost all plus countries, including US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Japan Defense Minister Koizumi Shinjiro, are participating in the meetings. Must Read Hegseth likely to face questions on US role in Indo-Pacific at ASEAN summit in Cebu As chair of ADMM, Teodoro will preside over all meetings, including two separate “informal meetings” with the US and Japan. China’s Dong Jun will not be attending ADMM+. Beijing will instead be represented by its defense attache assigned to the Chinese embassy in Manila. Cebu province has hosted several meetings under the Philippines’ chairmanship, including the first Foreign Ministers’ meeting, and the Summit in May. Tense PH-China ties “In a fragmenting world, our internal stability and intra-ASEAN unity are vital, perhaps even, in the future, existential. For it is only when we are united that we can effectively uphold ASEAN centrality and the principles that bind us, such as mutual respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, peaceful settlement of disputes, and the renunciation of the threat or use of force,” said Teodoro, in remarks that preceded a direct mention of the South China Sea. While disputes over and tensions in the critical waterway won’t be the center of discussions in Cebu, they certainly backdrop the Philippines’ chairmanship both of ASEAN and ADMM. Teodoro, among the loudest critics of Beijing in the Philippine government, is barred from entering and transacting in China over his statements against the Asian superpower. Just weeks before ADMM, China’s ambassador to Manila was criticized for saying the Philippines should be thankful that they do not use force in its disputes — a statement made in reaction to Teodoro’s assertion that it was Beijing who was causing trouble in the region. China claims almost all of the South China Sea, based on a supposed historical claim that a landmark 2016 Arbitral Award deemed invalid. Their claim overlaps with maritime claims and entitlements of several ASEAN members, including the Philippines. In the West Philippine Sea, an area that includes the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone, those overlapping claims have meant recurring confrontations between Chinese and Philippine maritime forces in some areas and features. Tensions in the South China Sea is a concern for ASEAN not only because several members are claimants. The waterway is where up to a third of global trade passes through. “ASEAN was founded on the belief that our strength lies in our diversity. We must therefore not allow our differences to divide us from within, and where such differences exist, including in the South China Sea, we shall settle them through peaceful and legal means,” said Teodoro. ADMM CHAIR. Philippines’ Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. waits for his counterparts’ arrival during the 20th ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM), Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026, in Cebu, central Philippines. US, Japan ties As chair of ADMM, it’s the Philippines who steers the agenda. It’s almost no surprise that in Cebu, the Philippines is hosting two “informal meetings” with treaty-ally United States and close partner Japan. Manila’s defense and security ties are deepest and most developed with Washington DC and Tokyo. The two countries are its staunchest partners in South China Sea issues and in its push to modernize the Philippine military. Manila is the first recipient of Japan’s Official Security Assistance (OSA). The US has allocated over $2.5 billion over five years in foreign military financing for the Philippines. Teodoro is also expected to host a quadrilateral meeting between Hegseth, Koizumi, and Australian Deputy Prime Minister and Defense Minister Richard Marles, a grouping known colloquially as the SQUAD. The Philippines’ defense engagements — both with traditional and new partners — is spurred, in no small way, by maritime tensions with China. In ASEAN, member states have varying degrees of closeness and cooperation with Beijing. It’s a difference that’s made cohesion a challenge, especially in a bloc that puts centrality and unanimity at the center of its decision-making and policy-making process. – Rappler.com

title: Knight Frank Nigeria to Host Second Golf Classic at Ikoyi Club 1938
body: Knight Frank Nigeria will host the second edition of the Knight Frank Golf Classic in Lagos on Thursday, October 29, 2026, at the Golf Section of Ikoyi Club 1938, bringing together a select gathering of clients, business leaders, associates and golf enthusiasts for a day of sporting excellence, relationship-building and celebration. The Golf Classic forms part of Knight Frank Nigeria’s ongoing commitment to nurturing enduring relationships with clients and partners through meaningful experiences beyond the workplace. Head of Marketing and Corporate Communications, Knight Frank Nigeria, Mr Lanre Sonubi, confirmed in a statement released to the media that Tatum Bank has been onboarded as a sponsor of this second edition of the tournament as tee off will start from 6:30am, while a reception and trophy presentation ceremony will commence from 2:00pm. The inaugural edition of the Knight Frank Golf Classic was held on June 20, 2025 at Ikoyi Club 1938 as part of the firm’s 60th anniversary celebrations in Nigeria. Building on that first event, Knight Frank plans to establish the Golf Classic as an annual fixture, creating a consistent platform for clients, associates and partners to connect through their shared interest in golf. Knight Frank Nigeria is a member of Knight Frank LLP, the leading independent global property consultancy, serving as our clients’ partners in property for over 128 years globally, and 60 years in Nigeria. Headquartered in London, Knight Frank has more than 20,000 people operating from 384 offices across 51 territories. The Group advises clients ranging from individual owners and buyers to major developers, investors and corporate tenants.

title: Tinubu: Why I Signed SEDC Bill Into Law
body: *Says South East region of enterprise President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has said that his decision to sign the South East Development Commission (SEDC), Bill into law was driven by his conviction that the prosperity of the South East region is inseparable from the prosperity of Nigeria. The President made the disclosure at the the South East Gas Pipeline Infrastructure Investment Ceremony in Enugu on Tuesday. It will be recalled that the President assented to the bill in July, 2024 Represented at the event by the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Okezie Kalu, President Tinubu said the Commission was created to provide sustained institutional attention to the region’s reconstruction, rehabilitation and long-term development. He said: “Our responsibility is to build upon that legacy. I have always believed that the prosperity of the South East is inseparable from the prosperity of Nigeria. When Aba’s industries thrive, when Nnewi’s factories expand, and when commerce flourishes in Onitsha, the entire Nigerian economy benefits. Nigeria cannot achieve its full economic potential while any region operates below its productive capacity. This conviction is central to our Renewed Hope Agenda. It informed my decision to assent to the legislation establishing the South East Development Commission in July 2024”. The President further said the SEDC was established to be an institution of delivery and not just another bureaucracy. “The Commission was established to provide sustained institutional attention to the region’s reconstruction, rehabilitation and long-term development. “I established the South East Development Commission to be an institution of delivery. We must measure its success by the investments it mobilises, the infrastructure it enables, the opportunities it creates, and the lives it improves”, he said. He commended the Chairman of the Commission, Dr. Emeka Wogu, the Board, and Management of the Commission led by its Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Mr. Mark Okoye, for advancing what he described as an important initiative, noting that the South East Vision 2050 process, supported by the Federal Government and the Governors of the region, provides an important foundation for coordinated development. President Tinubu also disclosed that he has approved the South East Investment Company, explaining that his administration is adopting a model that leverages public resources to unlock private capital. “We must use public resources strategically to unlock much larger pools of private investment. This is the model I expect from our development institutions: identify strategic economic opportunities, prepare credible projects, commit public resources responsibly and mobilise private capital at a scale government budgets alone cannot achieve,” he said. Reassuring the people of the South East, the President said his administration remains committed to delivering critical infrastructure that will drive trade and create jobs in the region. “My dear people of the South East, we recognise the importance of modern roads, rail connections, reliable energy and efficient access to markets. Our administration continues to advance critical transport infrastructure, including the Enugu–Onitsha and Enugu–Port Harcourt corridors, the supporting infrastructure around the Second Niger Bridge and the Eastern railway corridor. We know that much remains to be done. Our commitment is not simply to award contracts, but to deliver infrastructure that reduces costs, expands trade and creates jobs”, he said. The President added that the reforms introduced in the electricity sector are opening new opportunities for states and private investors to strengthen power supply in the region and across the country. Speaking on the gas infrastructure, President Tinubu said that the proposed South East Gas Distribution Pipeline Project will help develop a regional gas distribution network that will serve industrial and commercial users across the five eastern States. “But today, our attention is on another vital foundation of industrial competitiveness: Natural gas. Nigeria possesses substantial gas resources. Yet we must not measure those resources only by what lies beneath our soil. The true value of our gas is in the factories it powers, the jobs it creates and the prosperity it brings to our people. “With the Assa North–Ohaji South gas processing project in Imo State achieving first gas earlier this year, we have an important opportunity to connect domestic gas resources to productive industries. The proposed South East Gas Distribution Pipeline Project seeks to do precisely that. “It aims to develop a regional gas distribution network serving industrial and commercial users across Imo, Abia, Anambra, Enugu and Ebonyi States. “Consider what this could mean: More competitive manufacturing in Aba. Stronger industrial clusters in Nnewi and Onitsha. New investment and productive enterprises in Enugu. Greater opportunities for agro-processing and manufacturing in Ebonyi. A stronger connection between Imo’s gas resources and the wider regional economy. These are not five separate economies. They are parts of one interconnected economic region. “Gas infrastructure must therefore serve industries and markets, not stop at political boundaries. That is the economic logic of regional integration”, he said. President Tinubu also encouraged the governors from the South East region to sustain the spirit of cooperation amongst themselves, saying that the zone is a region of enterprise. He also charged the SEDC and its partners to produce tangible results that will impact the region positively, promising the government will always strive to create the enabling environment for businesses to thrive. “Your Excellencies, the Governors of the South East, I encourage you to sustain the spirit of cooperation that has brought us to this point. No single state can realise the full benefits of regional infrastructure on its own. “The Federal Government will continue to provide the enabling environment. But states, investors and the private sector must work together to convert these opportunities into productive investments. “To our investors, I say: the South East is a region of enterprise, talent and enormous industrial potential. Look beyond today’s ceremony. Examine the opportunities. Bring your capital, expertise, and long-term commitment. To our manufacturers and entrepreneurs, we recognise your resilience. Our responsibility is to create an environment in which your competitiveness depends less on endurance and more on productivity. “To the young people of the South East, this initiative is ultimately about your future. A future where your skills have value, your businesses can grow, and a lack of opportunity does not limit your ambitions. “I expect the South East Development Commission and its partners to move beyond today’s ceremony with a clear implementation plan, defined milestones and measurable results. “Let this project be remembered not for the agreements signed today, but for the factories it powers, the investments it attracts and the jobs it creates. For generations, the people of the South East have built successful businesses despite inadequate infrastructure. Our responsibility is to help build an economy in which they can succeed because of the infrastructure we provide”, the President assured.

title: Knife-wielding attacker shot dead outside Israeli Embassy in Belgrade
body: An unidentified attacker armed with two knives assaulted a Serbian police officer guarding the Israeli Embassy in Belgrade shortly after midnight Wednesday, before being shot dead by the officer, Serbian authorities said. Serbian Interior Minister Ivica Dacic said the assailant was believed to be a minor whose identity had not yet been established. According to Dacic, the attacker shouted "Allahu Akbar" before lunging at the officer with two knives. The officer returned fire, killing the assailant, and sustained minor injuries during the confrontation.   Dacic said Serbian police were treating the incident as a terrorist attack and had raised the country's terror threat level to its highest setting. Authorities also increased police deployments and tightened security at key locations following the attack.  The incident follows an earlier attack outside the same embassy in June 2024, when a man armed with a crossbow wounded a Serbian police officer guarding the diplomatic mission. The officer returned fire and killed the attacker. Serbian authorities also classified that incident as terrorism.

title: West suffers complete fiasco in its attempts to isolate Russia — diplomat
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. The West has made a fool of itself in its attempts to isolate Russia, suffering a complete fiasco in the process, Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said.
"Westerners are making fools of themselves. Their plans to isolate Russia have failed. They’re already arguing among themselves about who called whom," the diplomat noted during a Sputnik Radio broadcast, referring to the recent squabble in Europe over the telephone conversation between Russian President Vladimir Putin, Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store. "This so-called isolation of Russia is a complete fiasco for the West. It’s a caricature of their policy," she pointed out.
Zakharova also commented on Western officials’ attempts to dissuade African representatives from traveling to Moscow for the Russia-Africa summit. "The whole world is looking on with disdain at these efforts. They’re still running around, grabbing people by the sleeves and begging: 'Just don’t go,' " the spokeswoman said.

title: Athens and Thessaloniki Introduce Transport Changes for October 28
body: Greece is marking its October 28 national anniversary on Wednesday with extensive traffic restrictions, public transport changes and school parade cancellations, as severe weather threatens several regions with heavy rain, thunderstorms and possible hail. In Athens, authorities have introduced traffic measures around Syntagma Square, where the annual student parade is scheduled for 11:00. The Syntagma Metro station has closed from 08:00, while tram services are operating on shortened routes. In Thessaloniki, where the military parade is scheduled for 11:00 along Megalou Alexandrou Avenue, police have imposed extensive traffic and parking restrictions. Six Metro stations will close temporarily from 11:00. Meanwhile, authorities have cancelled student parades in Magnesia, the Northern Sporades, the Cyclades, the Dodecanese, parts of Evia and the Athens suburb of Agios Dimitrios, citing severe weather forecasts. Athens introduces traffic restrictions and transport changes Athens Traffic Police began implementing restrictions early on Wednesday because of the official religious service at the Metropolitan Cathedral and the student parade at Syntagma Square. From 06:00 until the completion of the service, authorities have suspended traffic along the entire length of Mitropoleos Street and on connecting streets up to the first parallel road. From 09:00 until the student parade ends, traffic restrictions cover Vasilissis Amalias Avenue, Panepistimiou Street, sections of Vasilissis Sofias Avenue, Syngrou Avenue between Athanasiou Diakou Street and Dionysiou Areopagitou Street, and Athanasiou Diakou Street. Restrictions also extend to connecting streets in the affected areas. Police have urged drivers to avoid Syntagma Square, Panepistimiou Street and surrounding central roads during the events. Authorities will restore traffic gradually after the parade. The Syntagma Metro station has closed from 08:00 following instructions from the Hellenic Police, according to the Athens Transport Company STASY. Trains will pass through the station without stopping for passengers. The station will reopen after the events end and police lift the restrictions. Tram services have also changed temporarily. Line 6, which normally runs between Pikrodafni and Syntagma, will terminate at Fix station from 08:00, operating between Pikrodafni and Fix in both directions. Line 7, which connects the Asklipieio Voula area with Akti Poseidonos, will terminate at SEF station from 09:00. Both changes will remain in place until the events finish and traffic conditions return to normal. All Athens public bus and trolleybus routes are operating on Sunday schedules because of the national public holiday. During local parades across Attica, some services may follow altered routes or use temporary stops. Passengers can call the Athens Urban Transport Organisation (OASA) information line on 11185 for travel updates. Athens anniversary programme The official programme includes the following events: 06:47: Ceremonial gun salutes from Lycabettus Hill and reveille performances by the Armed Forces and security services bands. 08:00: Official raising of the Greek flag on the Acropolis. 10:00: Official service at the Metropolitan Cathedral of Athens, led by Archbishop Ieronymos of Athens and All Greece. 10:40: Wreath-laying ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier by representatives of the authorities. 11:00: Student parade in front of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, featuring school groups, Scouts, Guides and people with disabilities. The Minister of Education, Religious Affairs and Sports is scheduled to attend the student parade. Thessaloniki imposes extensive traffic restrictions Thessaloniki has introduced extensive traffic and parking restrictions ahead of the military parade scheduled for 11:00 along Megalou Alexandrou Avenue. From 03:00 until the parade ends, parking and stopping are prohibited along Megalou Alexandrou Avenue, Grigoriou Papandreou Street between Megalou Alexandrou and Mitropolitou Kydonion, 30is Oktovriou Street, Pavlou Mela Street between White Tower Square and Tsimiski Street, G’ Septemvriou Street between Megalou Alexandrou and Stratou Avenue, Stratigou Napoleon Zerva Street, Ethnikis Amynis Street between Tsimiski Street and Nikis Avenue, and Gkyzi Street. The restriction on Agias Triados Street, between Megalou Alexandrou Avenue and Vasileos Georgiou Street, will remain in place until 15:00. Authorities will suspend all vehicle traffic on Megalou Alexandrou Avenue, Grigoriou Papandreou Street and 30is Oktovriou Street from 05:00 until the parade ends. Additional closures will begin at 07:00 on Markou Botsari, Karaiskaki, Kallidopoulou, 25is Martiou, Petrou Syndika, Paraskevopoulou, Chatzi, 28is Oktovriou between Vasilissis Olgas and Megalou Alexandrou avenues, Stratigou Kakavou, Pavlou Mela, Soulioti and Ethnikis Amynis streets. Police have also planned additional restrictions on sections of Kallidopoulou, Karaiskaki, Michail Psellou and Ifigeneias streets. They may introduce further closures on neighbouring roads depending on traffic conditions. Authorities have urged drivers to remove parked vehicles in advance and follow traffic officers’ instructions. Six Thessaloniki Metro stations to close The Thessaloniki Metro will temporarily close six stations from 11:00 following an order from the Hellenic Police. The affected stations are: New Railway Station Dimokratias Venizelou Agias Sofias Sintrivani Panepistimio Metro operator THEMA has said the network will return to full operation once police lift the restrictions. Traffic restrictions along the city’s waterfront and surrounding roads are also expected to affect bus routes serving the area. The Hellenic Police has additionally prohibited all outdoor public gatherings in central Thessaloniki from 09:00 to 21:00. The measure covers an area bounded by Nikis Avenue, Ethnikis Amynis, Agiou Dimitriou, Stelios Dragoumanos, Grigoriou Koloniasri, Agion Panton, Giannitson, Ioanni Kolletti, 26is Oktovriou, Karatasou and Navarchou Kountouriotou streets, as well as Nikis Avenue. Police cited public safety concerns and the need to prevent serious disruption to the city’s social and economic life, traffic and infrastructure. Severe weather forces school parade cancellations Regional and municipal authorities have cancelled student parades in several parts of Greece because forecasts warn of heavy rainfall, thunderstorms and possible hail. The cancellations include: Magnesia and the Northern Sporades: Thessaly Regional Governor Dimitris Kouretas has cancelled all student parades. Cyclades: Student parades have been cancelled across all regional units, including the participation of associations, organisations and clubs. Dodecanese: Authorities have cancelled student parades because of the increased risk of flooding. Evia: Cancellations cover Chalkida and the municipalities of Kymi-Aliveri, Mantoudi-Limni-Agia Anna, Dirfys-Messapia, Eretria and Skyros. Agios Dimitrios, Attica: Authorities have cancelled the scheduled anniversary parade. Zagora-Mouresi: Authorities have also cancelled the student parade because of forecasts of dangerous weather. In Chalkida, only the parade company of the Infantry School will march. Authorities had not finalised a decision on the military parade in Volos in the latest available announcements. They will decide according to how the weather develops. In Magnesia, the regional decision applies only to student parades. The relevant authorities will decide separately on other anniversary events. Red Code alert as storms threaten several regions The cancellations follow an emergency severe weather bulletin from the Hellenic National Meteorological Service, which forecasts locally heavy rain and thunderstorms on Wednesday. The most severe conditions, under a red warning, are expected in Thessaly, including Magnesia and Larissa, the Northern Sporades, Evia and the Dodecanese. Authorities also expect heavy rainfall and thunderstorms in the eastern Aegean islands, eastern Central Greece, Attica and the western and northern Cyclades, with orange warnings covering several of these areas. The forecast calls for severe conditions in Thessaly, the Sporades and Evia until late at night. The eastern Aegean islands and parts of eastern Central Greece may also experience storms into the evening, while the warnings for Attica and the western and northern Cyclades cover the morning hours. Localised hailstorms remain possible. Civil Protection has placed state services on heightened alert. Authorities have also activated the Red Code mobilisation status in Attica and parts of the Aegean because of the risk of dangerous weather and flooding. Authorities continue to monitor conditions and may announce further changes to anniversary events. People planning to attend or participate in parades should check announcements from their local municipalities, regional authorities and police, as arrangements may change depending on the severity of the weather. title: 2027: NDC campaign DG urges Atiku to join Obi-Kwankwaso
body: The Director-General of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Presidential Campaign Council, Ibrahim Abdulkarim, has urged former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and other opposition leaders to join the alliance backing Peter Obi and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Abdulkarim said the opposition needed to unite behind a common platform to improve its chances of defeating the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in the election. Speaking on Arise News, he said the coalition was already taking shape within the NDC, with Obi emerging as its presidential candidate and Kwankwaso agreeing to work with him. “The opposition has to come together for us to win. The opposition have already come together. Nobody said the coalition must happen on ADC. It can happen in NDC, and Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso has already dropped his ambition,” he said. Abdulkarim said Atiku and other opposition figures were welcome to join the alliance to broaden its national reach. “What we are asking for is for other people to join us, including former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, to join all of us, so at least we will have the spread that they think they can add,” he added. The NDC campaign chief also dismissed criticism of the party’s campaign structures, arguing that its organisation should not be compared with the Obidient movement and other support groups backing Obi. “How can you compare a party with a support group? We don’t have any problem. They’re all part of the NDC party. We have more than a thousand support groups like that,” he said. On concerns about electoral fraud, Abdulkarim urged Nigerians who feared their votes might not count to support the NDC, promising that the party had developed measures to protect votes during the 2027 elections. He said the party would campaign peacefully across the country and mobilise voters who had lost confidence in the electoral process. “We are going to do our campaign peacefully. We are going to go into every corner,” he said. Abdulkarim added that the party would reassure voters before the election that their votes would be protected. “I can promise anybody, anybody that feels he wants his vote to count, we have a very, very unique and serious programme that we have put in place,” he said. The post 2027: NDC campaign DG urges Atiku to join Obi-Kwankwaso appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Dr. Bawumia engages TUC leadership on youth employment, rising living costs and labour welfare
body: Former Vice President and NPP presidential candidate, Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia, has taken his broad-based stakeholder engagement to Organised Labour, meeting with the leadership of the Trades Union Congress (TUC) at the Hall of Trade Unions in Accra Tuesday. The meeting, held as part of Dr. Bawumia’s ongoing national consultations, brought together top executives of the TUC, the umbrella body representing thousands of Ghanaian workers across both the public and private sectors. Sources close to the meeting describe the atmosphere as cordial, frank and solution-oriented, with both sides demonstrating a commitment to addressing Ghana’s current labour concerns. At the centre of the discussions were bread-and-butter issues affecting workers, including the biting cost of living that has eroded disposable incomes, the long-standing demand for a sustainable living wage that goes beyond the minimum wage, and the growing anxiety over youth unemployment. Other critical matters raised were the need to reform and enhance the pensions regime to guarantee dignity in retirement, and the imperative of ensuring workplaces are truly inclusive for persons with disabilities. Beyond immediate welfare issues, the meeting also delved into strategic economic policy, with both sides exploring the idea of creating a resilient economy strong enough to absorb external shocks that affect exchange rates, inflation, commodity prices and supply chains. Dr. Bawumia, who has consistently advocated strong economic fundamentals to withstand global economic shocks, is said to have listened attentively to the concerns and proposals put forward by the TUC leaders, assuring them that their inputs would form part of his broader economic vision. The engagement with the TUC follows similar consultations Dr. Bawumia has held in recent weeks with traders, professional bodies, faith-based organisations, youth groups and private sector players, as he continues to gather diverse perspectives on building a more resilient and inclusive Ghanaian economy. Both sides are expected to hold follow-up meetings to drill down into concrete policy proposals.

title: Iran urges Qatar to abide by its mediation role in talks
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 28 (MNA) – The head of the Public Relations Department of the Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs has called on Qatar to adhere to its mediation role in the Iran-US talks.
In his reaction to the remarks of Director of the Media and Communication Department at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Qatar Ibrahim Al Hashemi regarding the visit of senior officials of Pakistan, Turkey and Saudi Arabia to Tehran, Head of the Public Relations Department of the Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs Mahmoud Maleki stated, “The quadrilateral meeting in Tehran is, in itself, a sign to Iran’s good faith and responsible approach toward the shared interests of the nations in the region.”
The Islamic Republic of Iran expects all regional states, including Qatar, to reciprocate this good faith in their own policies and approaches, he continued.
In addition, Iran expects neighboring Qatar, in adherence to the principle of good neighborliness, to strictly refrain from repeating certain action, specifically allowing aggressor parties to utilize their territory and facilities for the purpose of military aggression against Iran.
Referring to the constructive discussions held during the four-party meeting in Tehran, including Iran, Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia, Mahmoud Maleki advised the Qatari official to exercise greater caution in his public statements, given Qatar’s role in ongoing diplomatic processes.

title: Ebonyi Assembly unanimously backs state police bill
body: The Ebonyi House of Assembly on Tuesday unanimously approved a bill seeking to establish state police services, endorsing a constitutional amendment transmitted by the National Assembly. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that all 24 members voted in favour of the bill after extensive deliberations and consultations with their constituents. The proposed amendment seeks to alter the 1999 Constitution, as amended, to provide a legal framework for state police services while retaining the Nigeria Police Force at federal level. The Speaker, Moses Odunwa, said the unanimous decision demonstrated the assembly’s commitment to constitutional reforms aimed at strengthening the state’s security architecture. “This will also enhance access to criminal intelligence and protection of lives and properties,” Odunwa said. He described the demand for sub-national policing as a longstanding aspiration among Ebonyi residents. “The demand for a sub-national policing system has been an age-long clamour among Ebonyi people,” he said. Odunwa added that the state had formally presented its position in support of state police during a public hearing organised by the National Assembly on constitutional review. He said the bill’s passage reflected residents’ desire for a policing system closer to communities and more responsive to local security challenges. The Leader of the House, Kingsley Ikoro, said establishing state police would significantly increase manpower in the state’s security sector. Ikoro, who represents Afikpo North West under the All Progressives Congress (APC), said the proposed system would improve efforts to tackle crime at grassroots level. Other lawmakers, including Victor Nwoke (APC–Abakaliki North) and Oluchukwu Ezeali (APC–Afikpo North East), also stressed the importance of bringing policing closer to communities. They argued that decentralised policing could help address Nigeria’s security challenges by improving local responses to crime and criminal activities. Following the bill’s passage, Odunwa directed the Clerk of the House, Mrs Uche Edene, to formally transmit the assembly’s resolutions to the National Assembly. title: Aliyev discusses peace, external threats and ‘double standards’ at Baku forum
body: Aliyev’s speech at Baku Dialogue Forum Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev spoke at the opening of the 7th World Forum on Intercultural Dialogue in Baku on 27 October. In his speech , he addressed peace efforts with Armenia , the role of international organisations, Azerbaijan’s foreign policy and security. Aliyev said the country faced no internal threats, criticised “double standards” in international politics and proposed using Azerbaijan’s experience of transitioning from war to peace to help resolve other conflicts. The World Forum on Intercultural Dialogue brings together representatives of governments, international organisations and experts from different countries to discuss intercultural and interfaith dialogue. The forum was first held in Baku in 2011 as part of the Baku Process initiative launched by Azerbaijan in 2008. It was originally intended to take place every two years. After a break caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, the forum resumed in 2024. This year’s seventh edition takes place from 27 to 29 October under the theme “Dialogue for a Shared Future”. Fidan says 'everything is fine' in Baku, but relations remain strained Ankara seeks to ease tensions, while Baku stands firm: experts on strained relations between Turkey and Azerbaijan Intercultural dialogue and national unity Aliyev described Azerbaijan’s geographical position between Europe and Asia as an important factor in fostering intercultural ties. He said religious and ethnic tolerance, as well as traditions of multiculturalism, were among the foundations of the country’s stable development. The president said members of different ethnic and religious groups in Azerbaijan enjoyed equal constitutional rights and lived in an atmosphere of mutual understanding. According to him, the idea of Azerbaijani identity united different ethnic groups, and this unity had been evident even during the most difficult periods in the history of independent Azerbaijan. As an example, he cited the participation of members of different ethnic and religious groups in the Second Karabakh War. Aliyev recalled that October marked the 35th anniversary of the restoration of Azerbaijan’s independence. He stressed that, despite changes in political systems, the Azerbaijani people had managed to preserve their language, traditions and national identity. The president said the country’s achievements since independence were the result of the Azerbaijani people’s efforts and that its development had taken place without international assistance. Why Azerbaijan sees Talysh activism as security threat Kamal Isayev is serving an eight-and-a-half-year prison sentence, while concerns grow over Iqbal Abilov’s health in solitary confinement. “All potential threats come from beyond our borders” In the part of his speech devoted to security, Aliyev said Azerbaijani society demonstrated unity on all issues. In his assessment, the country faced no internal threats, while all potential risks came from abroad. “All potential threats come from beyond our borders,” the president said. He compared ideological risks to physical threats and stressed the need to remain vigilant to protect national identity, statehood, independence and the country’s way of life. However, Aliyev did not specify which countries or organisations might pose such threats. Azerbaijan vs Western media: Why were different reports labelled a single 'information campaign'? Four reports published in international media over the past five days have sparked a sharp reaction from Baku. Karabakh negotiations and military operations Aliyev said that restoring Azerbaijan’s territorial integrity had been the country’s main goal for most of its independence. The president criticised the years of negotiations over the Karabakh conflict, saying they had been aimed not at resolving the conflict but at freezing it. He justified Azerbaijan’s military actions by citing the right to self-defence under the UN Charter. According to the president, Azerbaijan restored its territorial integrity and sovereignty as a result of the 2020 war and the 2023 military operation, independently securing the implementation of UN Security Council resolutions adopted in 1993. Azerbaijan holds anti-Islamophobia conference while religious activists face persecution According to the Shi’a activist, around 300 religious activists are currently imprisoned in Azerbaijan Peace with Armenia and experience of ending war Speaking about relations with Armenia, Aliyev said that Azerbaijan had initiated peace efforts after the end of hostilities. According to him, the draft peace agreement initialled in the summer of 2025 had also been prepared by Baku. The president stressed that Azerbaijan had not sought a protracted war and had decided not to continue the confrontation after achieving its military objectives. He noted that the desire for revenge could make war endless. In Aliyev’s view, it was important not only to achieve victory but also to know when to stop and offer peace. The president suggested that parties involved in armed conflicts study Azerbaijan’s experience. He acknowledged that every conflict had its own characteristics but noted that ambition, aggression, the pursuit of superiority and a sense of impunity all played a role in their emergence. After Washington talks: Trump Route deal and diverging views — analysis from Baku At a trilateral meeting in Washington brokered by US President Donald Trump, a full peace deal was not reached, and the agreed route drew criticism from Russia and Iran. UN resolutions, sanctions and “double standards” Aliyev called for special attention to be paid to establishing a mechanism to ensure the implementation of UN Security Council decisions as part of discussions on UN reform. He criticised the failure to implement four resolutions on the Karabakh conflict for many years and the absence of sanctions against Armenia. The president recalled that numerous sanctions had been imposed on countries to Azerbaijan’s north and south, describing the different approach towards Armenia as an example of “double standards”. He accused Armenia of occupying around 20% of Azerbaijan’s territory, carrying out ethnic cleansing and destroying religious and historical monuments. According to him, one million Azerbaijanis had been forced to flee their homes, while 65 mosques had been destroyed in Karabakh. In criticising “double standards”, Aliyev addressed not only the international community’s response to wars. He also described attempts by other countries to dictate how Azerbaijan should live and what decisions it should make as unacceptable. The president said Azerbaijan did not interfere in the internal affairs of other countries and expected the same treatment in return. According to him, displays of disrespect towards Azerbaijan and attempts to impose outside demands on the country had always met with firm resistance and would continue to do so. Aliyev also noted that relations based on mutual respect could help reduce the number of international conflicts. Now ruling party leader indefinitely: Ilham Aliyev makes new tough foreign policy statements The president said Azerbaijan achieved its military victories without outside help. His remarks came amid criticism in Turkish media over Azerbaijan’s support for Israel Partnerships with US, China and Europe Speaking about foreign policy, the president described Azerbaijan as a pillar of stability in an unstable region. He attributed the country’s stronger international standing to its independent policies, economic potential and role in the energy and transport sectors. Aliyev highlighted strategic partnerships with China and the US, as well as strategic partnership agreements with ten EU member states. The president said Azerbaijan would host a summit of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation in 2027 and a summit of the European Political Community in 2028. He also recalled the summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia, held in Baku in October. According to him, Azerbaijan’s chairmanship of the organisation had been extended for another two years, and the country had been invited to become a full member of the Central Asian Consultative Format. Aliyev described these decisions as recognition of Azerbaijan’s growing role on the international stage. Azerbaijan's deputy prime minister visits Iran: what interests are bringing Baku and Tehran closer? At meetings in Tehran, Azerbaijan’s deputy prime minister discussed electricity supplies, border infrastructure and transport routes. External debt, energy and transport routes Turning to economic issues, Aliyev said Azerbaijan’s external debt stood at just over 5% of GDP. He highlighted energy exports and international transport links as factors strengthening the country’s position. In his view, Azerbaijan’s infrastructure and political ties, as well as its geographical location, played an important role in the development of international transport routes. The president stressed that developing international transport links required maintaining good relations not only with neighbouring countries but also with their neighbours. How rising food prices in Azerbaijan are affecting household budgets In Azerbaijan, families that spend a significant share of their budgets on food feel the impact of rising prices more acutely. Peace agreement initialled in Washington and region’s future Concluding his speech, Aliyev noted that both positive and negative developments had taken place around the world since the previous forum. He cited the outbreak of new wars in neighbouring regions as negative developments and the peace process with Armenia as a positive one. The president recalled that the text of a peace agreement had been initialled in Washington in August 2025, with the participation of Donald Trump . Aliyev stressed that, at that stage, the agreement had only been initialled, not signed. The US president had, however, signed a trilateral declaration as a witness. According to Aliyev, this process marked a new chapter for the South Caucasus.

title: Greek Art Helped Sustain National Morale During the Greco-Italian War
body: Greece’s artists played a vital role in sustaining national morale during the Greco-Italian War of 1940-41, using cartoons, posters, illustrated postcards and popular prints to inspire the public, rally support for the armed forces and strengthen the nation’s resolve beyond the battlefield. Historian and researcher Kostas Mamalakis told the Athens-Macedonian News Agency (AMNA) that the artistic output of the period drew on Greece’s longstanding tradition of historical imagery, which had already shaped popular consciousness before the war. At the time, Greek cafés commonly displayed maps of Greece, portraits of heroes from the 1821 War of Independence, paintings depicting battles from the Balkan Wars and, occasionally, portraits of political figures. Following the torpedoing of the Greek light cruiser Elli by an Italian submarine on 15 August 1940, Greece gradually moved towards war. Posters featuring Evzones, the legendary submarine Papanikolis, artillery batteries and other military subjects began appearing in cafés and other public spaces. When war broke out on 28 October 1940 and Greek forces began pushing back the Italian army, artists quickly adapted their work to reflect developments on the front. Cartoons and popular illustrations became tools of national mobilisation, ridiculing the enemy while encouraging public confidence in the Greek military. “The themes in cartoons followed events as soon as the first successes of the Greek Army were announced, particularly when the army began pursuing the Italians into Albanian territory,” Mamalakis said. Artists depicted an Evzone’s traditional shoe kicking back Italian armoured vehicles, a soldier’s fustanella chasing frightened Italian troops, and an inconsolable Benito Mussolini searching for the Acropolis through binoculars. Alongside newspaper cartoons and large posters, illustrated postcards circulated widely between the home front and the battlefield. They carried similar messages of courage, patriotism and reassurance to soldiers and their families. Postcards showed the Virgin Mary embracing and protecting a soldier, as well as sailors, airmen and infantrymen charging with bayonets fixed. Ships and aircraft also featured prominently. Mamalakis said the artistic output helped strengthen the nation’s psychological resilience, although wartime circumstances prevented it from receiving the recognition it deserved. “ We did not have time to celebrate the victorious outcome of this war because Germany attacked us immediately afterwards, followed by the country’s triple occupation by German, Italian and Bulgarian troops,” he said. As a result, Greece had little opportunity to assess the contribution of this art to awakening and encouraging a population enduring a struggle for survival and freedom. Much of the material has survived thanks to private collectors, their dedication and the painstaking work of historians and researchers. Exhibitions have periodically displayed works preserved in private collections, while publications have documented the painters and cartoonists whose creations appeared on posters, postcards, magazines and newspaper pages. Mamalakis described Greek art from 1940 not as a decorative luxury but as a necessity: a means of inspiring and strengthening a nation fighting for its survival and freedom. From newspaper cartoons to illustrated postcards, Greek artists turned ink and paper into a form of psychological resistance, helping sustain the spirit of a nation at war. title: Trump says he's ending restrictions on climate-warming methane from oil drilling
body:
President Donald Trump throws a hat into the crowd as he arrives at a campaign rally at Lubbock Memorial Civic Center, Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026, in Lubbock, Texas. Annie Rice/AP hide caption
BILLINGS, Mont. — President Donald Trump said Tuesday that his administration is "terminating" a Biden-era rule that aimed to cut planet-warming emissions of methane from oil and gas drilling.
Trump said during a campaign rally in Texas that the change would save companies and consumers billions of dollars and unlock 210 million barrels of oil. That's equivalent to about 10 days of U.S. petroleum consumption.
The move aims to encourage more domestic drilling as Trump faces criticism over high fuel prices amid the war in Iran.
Methane is responsible for about a third of planet-warming greenhouse gas emissions, scientists estimate.
FILE - A flare burns off methane and other hydrocarbons as oil pumpjacks operate in the Permian Basin in Midland, Texas, on Oct. 12, 2021. (AP Photo/David Goldman, File) David Goldman/AP hide caption
Cuts in methane emissions have emerged in recent years as a global priority to slow the rate of climate change. Oil and gas operations are the largest industrial source of methane, which is the main component in natural gas and far more potent to the atmosphere than carbon dioxide in the short term.
The invisible gas leaks from equipment and is released into the atmosphere or burned off as a waste product by oil drillers.
Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Lee Zeldin previewed the changes last month, saying they would eliminate the agency's "Super Emitter Program" that requires companies to investigate and repair major methane releases from oil and natural gas facilities. The agency would also set less restrictive standards for small oil and gas wells.
Trump said during Tuesday's rally in Lubbock for Texas Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton that Biden's plan "crushed the small operators" with crippling regulations.
"I'm officially terminating Biden's expensive and unnecessary methane regulations to save consumers and energy producers $45 billion in costs," Trump said.
The loosening of the emissions rule comes as Trump and Republicans in Congress have been methodically dismantling climate policies enacted under former President Joe Biden. That's included the revocation of a scientific finding that was central to U.S. action on greenhouse gas emissions, lower fuel economy standards for vehicles and a move to repeal emission restrictions for coal and natural gas power plants.
Environmental groups said the latest rollback will let companies continue polluting the atmosphere with gas that could be captured and provide energy to millions of households.
Environmental Defense Fund President Fred Krupp said it gives a "free pass" to companies at the expense of American consumers.
"EPA should be fighting this waste, not making it easier," he said.
Zeldin has said the methane rule would have cost $18 billion and was holding back the U.S. energy industry.
The Biden methane rule was announced by officials including former Vice President Kamala Harris during a 2023 U.N. climate conference in the United Arab Emirates.
Federal officials under Biden said it would prevent an estimated 58 million tons (52.6 million metric tonnes) of methane emissions by 2038 and reduce other pollutants that cause health problems.
By 2034, the rule was projected to yield $98 billion in benefits. That figure was derived by calculating the future "social costs" of greenhouse gas emissions on public health and the environment, an approach rejected by Trump's EPA.
While previous regulations focused only on new oil and gas wells in the U.S., the Biden rule regulated existing wells. Operators also would have needed to plug leaking methane from smaller wells that produce just 6% of the nation's oil and gas while accounting for up to half of all methane emissions from oil and gas fields.
The final rule was published in 2024. The EPA last year imposed an 18-month delay to give companies time to meet new inspection requirements and other provisions.
The rule was crafted to be coordinated with a methane fee, approved in the 2022 climate law. The fee program would have levied a "waste emissions charge" of as much as $1,500 per metric ton of methane on energy producers that exceed a certain level of methane emissions.
The fee marked the first time the U.S. government directly imposed a fee, or tax, on greenhouse gas emissions. Congress repealed it weeks after Trump took office.
Officials also tried to rein in methane from oil and gas under former President Barack Obama, but that effort was scaled back during Trump's first term.
