title: Why 5G remains out of reach for most Nigerians
body: …High cost of devices, coverage remains uneven …As smartphone market contracts 11% amid rising device prices …Africa’s budget smartphone shipments plunge 34% amid rising costs By Juliet Umeh Nigeria’s mobile market has shifted significantly towards newer network technologies over the past three years, but 5G remains out of reach for most consumers. High smartphone prices, uneven network coverage and rising infrastructure costs continue to limit adoption, despite growing demand for mobile data. In May 2023, 2G accounted for 58.36 percent of reported mobile connections, while 4G represented 25.06 percent and 5G just 0.12 percent. By August 2026, 4G had become the leading technology at 54.77 percent, while 2G fell to 36.05 percent. 5G increased to 4.92 percent. The data from the Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, show progress but underline how slowly the newest technology is reaching the wider population. Chief Technology Officer of NATCOM Development and Investment Limited, trading as NTEL, Kingsley Uwazie, said Nigerians had a strong appetite for data consumption, but the cost of accessing 5G remained a significant barrier. “The 5G ecosystem is in its maturity phase. It has been proven that there is an appetite. Nigerians have an appetite to consume data. But there is a barrier to acquiring the devices and using the technology,” he said. High cost of compatible devices Consumers need 5G-enabled smartphones to access the technology, but rising device prices are making upgrades increasingly difficult, particularly for low-income earners. Uwazie said 5G devices remained expensive despite subsidies offered by some operators. “5G, at the moment, is not a cheap technology to deploy or to own. The cost of 5G devices has been high,” he said. He cited MTN Nigeria and Airtel Nigeria as operators subsidising selected devices, adding that a phone available for about N50, 000 with a subsidy could cost more than N200, 000 without it. The affordability challenge has intensified as Nigeria’s smartphone market contracted by 11 percent in the second quarter of 2026, according to technology research firm Omdia. Rising memory-chip costs, partly linked to growing demand from artificial intelligence, AI, data centres, have increased pressure on manufacturers and consumers. Across Africa, shipments of smartphones priced below $100 fell by 34 percent year-on-year during the quarter. In Nigeria, a market assessment published by technology news platform Condia found that prices of selected Tecno, Infinix, Oppo and itel models increased between January and June 2026. The midpoint price of the itel S-Series Ultra rose from about N263, 500 to N316,400, while the Infinix Zero Series increased from approximately N550,000 to N637,500. Omdia warned in June that Nigerian smartphone prices could rise by another 15 to 30 percent through the remainder of 2026 if component costs continued increasing. These developments could discourage consumers from upgrading, slowing the growth of the 5G user base. Coverage remains uneven Even consumers who can afford compatible devices may struggle to access reliable 5G connections because coverage varies by location. MTN’s 2023 pilot announcement identified Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, Ibadan, Kano, Owerri and Maiduguri as intended launch cities, subject to coverage. Airtel began its rollout in Lagos, Ogun, Rivers and the Federal Capital Territory, focusing on selected locations. However, a rollout in a city or state does not guarantee availability in every neighbourhood. A December 2025 report based on Ookla analysis put Lagos’s average 5G coverage gap at 55.4 percent, meaning a compatible phone could not connect to 5G for more than half of the measured time. The gap was approximately 50 percent for MTN and 77 percent for Airtel. In Abuja, the average gap stood at 47.4 percent. These figures measure time-based access gaps, not the proportion of land without coverage, but they illustrate the difficulty consumers face in obtaining consistent service. High operating costs slow expansion Expanding 5G requires substantial investment in network infrastructure, electricity and transmission. Operators must determine whether the number of potential subscribers in an area can justify those costs. Uwazie estimated that operating a telecommunications site in Nigeria could cost between $2,000 and $3,000 monthly, compared with about $300 in China and $500 in India. He said the costs included power and transmission. “If you deploy 5G in areas where only two people have 5G-enabled phones, it means those two people can’t cater for the operating expenditure required to deploy 5G. The operating expenditure of running mobile networks in Nigeria is extremely high. It is a combination of both power and transmission, keeping that site up.” The limited number of compatible devices can, therefore, weaken the business case for expanding coverage, particularly in areas where operators expect low subscriber numbers. Digital inclusion at risk The challenge extends beyond 5G adoption to Nigeria’s broader digital inclusion ambitions. The GSMA’s smartphone adoption report found that only 27 percent of Nigeria’s population owned a smartphone in 2024, while the mobile internet usage gap remained close to 60 percent. The NCC said in April 2026 that it was exploring ways to make cheaper smartphones available. Nigeria was also selected for pilot initiatives coordinated by the GSMA’s Handset Affordability Coalition to expand access to affordable 4G smartphones. However, rising global component costs threaten to undermine these efforts. Affordable devices and reliable connectivity are essential for mobile banking, digital education, online commerce and employment opportunities. Expanding network coverage alone will not connect consumers who cannot afford internet-enabled phones. For 5G to reach more Nigerians, compatible devices must become cheaper, coverage must improve and operators must find sustainable ways to reduce deployment costs. Until these barriers are addressed, 5G will remain largely inaccessible to many consumers, with adoption concentrated among those who can afford compatible smartphones and live in well-served locations. The post Why 5G remains out of reach for most Nigerians appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Rays stun Brewers with 2-run rally in 12th inning and force World Series Game 5
body:
Tampa Bay Rays second baseman Ben Williamson connects for a game-winning RBI single off Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Shane Drohan during the 12th inning of Game 4 of baseball's World Series, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026, in St. Petersburg, Fla., between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays. Morry Gash/AP hide caption
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — Jonny DeLuca and pinch-hitter Ben Williamson singled home runs in a stunning 12th-inning rally, and the Tampa Bay Rays staved off World Series elimination with a 4-3 win over the Milwaukee Brewers on Tuesday night that forced Game 5.
Cooper Pratt hit a tiebreaking home run off Ian Seymour in the top of the 12th for his fourth hit of the game as Milwaukee neared a sweep and its first World Series title.
But the Rays, also seeking their first championship, rallied in the bottom half after a throwing error by third baseman Joey Ortiz on Junior Caminero's leadoff grounder against reliever Antonio Senzatela.
Liam Hicks singled off rookie left-hander Shane Drohan, who relieved in his first appearance since Oct. 15, and DeLuca's single to center drove in pinch-runner Cedric Mullins to tie the score at 3.
Chandler Simpson's single loaded the bases and Milwaukee employed a five-man infield with the infield in.
Williamson, who had been 1 for 15 in the postseason, batted for Victor Mesa Jr. and hit a chopper over first baseman Jake Bauers into right field.
"That was totally what I told him to do," Rays manager Kevin Cash said, drawing laughs.
"Pretty big swing. I've got to go back and recall everything that took place."
Tampa Bay Rays shortstop Jorge Mateo (9) and right fielder Victor Mesa Jr. (25) celebrate with Tampa Bay Rays second baseman Ben Williamson after his walk-off RBI single during the 12th inning of Game 4 of baseball's World Series, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026, in St. Petersburg, Fla., between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays. Chris O'Meara/AP hide caption
Tampa Bay became the fourth team in World Series history to avoid elimination with an extra-inning comeback, according to OptaSTATS. The first three all went on to win the championship (1912 Red Sox, 1986 Mets, 2011 Cardinals).
"We've got a lot of fight in us. We're never going to shy away," Simpson said. "We were going to keep fighting until the end — the last inning, the last out, the last play, the last pitch. We were going to keep fighting. That's what we did tonight."
Game 5 in the best-of-seven matchup is Wednesday night at Tropicana Field, with NL Cy Young Award favorite Jacob Misiorowski scheduled to start for the Brewers. Cash said he hadn't decided on a starter yet.
Tampa Bay became just the fifth of 26 teams that fell behind 3-0 in the World Series to win Game 4. The previous four lost Game 5.
Of 43 teams to trail 3-0 in any best-of-seven postseason matchup, the only one that rebounded to win was the Boston Red Sox against the New York Yankees in the 2004 American League Championship Series.
"It just shows the resiliency of this group," Williamson said. "We continue to fight, and that's been the motto this series and this full season, is just fight."
Caminero was replaced by Mullins at third base and hobbled off the field with an ailing left foot. But the All-Star slugger said he'll definitely play Wednesday night.
"He'll play tomorrow on one leg. I'll make sure of it," Cash said.
Tampa Bay ended an eight-game winning streak by the Brewers, who were bidding to become only the second team to sweep a League Championship Series and the World Series.
"If you want to win a championship, you've got to survive some hard things," Milwaukee captain Christian Yelich said. "Like I said earlier, it's supposed to be hard. It's supposed to test you. We understand that."
Tampa Bay Rays' Chandler Simpson celebrates during the 12th inning of Game 4 of baseball's World Series, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026, in St. Petersburg, Fla., between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays. Ashley Landis/AP hide caption
David Hamilton also homered for the Brewers. Jackson Chourio had a single and double, improving to 10 for 20 in the Series.
Pratt, a 22-year-old rookie whose go-ahead hit sparked the Brewers to a 5-4 win in Game 2, drove a slider into the left-field seats against Seymour. Pratt had tied the score at 1 with an RBI double in the second.
Milwaukee players bounded out of the dugout to greet Pratt, who debuted in June and became the first rookie to hit an extra-inning homer in the World Series.
"This kid responds to everything," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said.
Seymour also allowed Frelick's tying homer in Game 2.
Milwaukee fans in the crowd of 40,514, many waving yellow towels and some wearing cheeseheads, brought a Badger State feel to Tropicana Field.
Tampa Bay returned to its white home jerseys, a day after playing in Devil Rays throwbacks.
Simpson hit an RBI double off starter Dustin May in the second, but Milwaukee tied the score in the fourth against Griffin Jax when Frelick hit a two-out single and came around on Pratt's double.
Caminero singled leading off the bottom half to chase May and advanced on a groundout. DeLuca hit a hard grounder to Hamilton and Caminero twisted toward the grass to avoid the third baseman's tag, then came home when Hamilton bounced his throw past Bauers for an error.
Hamilton, Milwaukee's No. 9 hitter, drove an 0-2 fastball at the letters from Jax into the right-field seats for his second home run of the postseason — half his regular-season total and just his second since June 6.

title: Pentagon Plans Its Largest-Ever Homeland Base on Up to 250 000 Acres
body:
The U.S. Department of War is seeking locations for the Next Great American Base , a major joint force installation that could span 100,000 to 250,000 acres—roughly four times the size of the original District of Columbia.
Dale Marks, assistant secretary of war for energy, installations and environment, described nationwide interest as “exceptional” in an October 22 letter to governors and state adjutants general. He said responses reflected a commitment to supporting service members, strengthening national defense and enabling rapid global power projection.
Secretary of War Pete Hegseth announced the competition last month, saying the base would address increasingly complex, multidomain threats and could house up to 25,000 service members. He described it as a dynamic, self-sustaining power projection platform rather than a conventional government installation.
The proposed acreage range is a guideline, not a strict requirement. Marks said smaller or larger sites could be considered, provided they offer suitable land and infrastructure. Smaller proposals would receive full consideration if otherwise compelling, with mission suitability remaining the top priority.
All locations across the United States are eligible for consideration, including former military installations and land bordering existing bases. Governors representing the highest-scoring candidate sites are expected to present their proposals to War Department officials next spring.
The department has not yet announced a final location, construction timeline, total cost or detailed capabilities. All nominations will undergo competitive screening and evaluation.

title: ₦1bn Fundamental Rights Suit: Court Fixes Dec 2 For Judgement In El-Rufai’s Suit Against ICPC, Two Others
body: Justice Joyce Abdulmalik of the Federal High Court, Abuja, has fixed Dec. 2 for judgment in a N1 billion fundamental rights suit filed by former Governor of Kaduna State, Nasir El-Rufai, against the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and co-respondents. Justice Abdulmalik fixed the date after lawyers to the parties adopted their processes in the case. When the case was called, El-Rufai’s lawyer was not in court. Justice Abdulmalik then made an order deeming all the processes filed by the former governor adopted. Counsel for the ICPC, Abdul Mohammed (SAN), identified and adopted all their processes, urging the court to dismiss the suit in its entirety. The I-G’s lawyer, ACP Ezekiel Rimamsomte, and Maimuna Lami-Shiru, Director of Civil Litigation and Public Law, who represented the AGF, equally adopted their separate processes and prayed the court to dismiss the suit. While the proceeding was ongoing, Ubong Akpan, the ex-governor’s counsel, entered the courtroom and apologised for his lateness. When the lawyer sought the permission of the court to allow him adopt his court’s documents, he was informed by the judge that his processes had already been deemed adopted. Justice Abdulmalik consequently adjourned the matter until Dec. 2 for judgment. El-Rufai is demanding N1 billion in damages against ICPC, the Inspector-General of Police and the Attorney-General of the Federation. He filed the suit, alleging that operatives of the ICPC and the police violated his rights following the search of his Abuja house on 20 February. He prayed the court to declare that the invasion and search of his residence at House 12, Mambilla Street, Aso Drive, Abuja, on Feb. 19 at about 2 pm by the ICPC and I-G amounts to a gross violation of his fundamental rights. He said that it was a violation of the dignity of the human person, personal liberty, fair hearing, and privacy under Sections 34, 35, 36, and 37 of the Constitution.” He sought an order directing the 1st and 3rd respondents (ICPC and I-G) to forthwith return all items seized from the applicant’s premises during the unlawful search, together with a detailed inventory thereof. He also sought an order awarding the sum of N1,000,000,000.00 (One Billion Naira) as general, exemplary, and aggravated damages, among others. Responding, in its counter affidavit, the ICPC said it received a petition against El-Rufai and, acting on the petition, it commenced an investigation, leading to the search at his residence. It argued that its operatives acted under a valid search warrant issued on Feb. 18 and executed on Feb. 19 between 1:37 pm and 3:56 pm at 12 Mambilla Street, Asokoro, Abuja. The commission said its officials were accompanied by personnel of the Nigeria Police Force, and that the exercise was witnessed by El-Rufai’s wife, Hadiza El-Rufai, and his son, Mohammed El-Rufai. The ICPC, which urged the court to dismiss the suit, listed the items allegedly recovered from the residence. The I-G, also in his counter affidavit deposed to by Insp Ewa Anthony, argued that he had the statutory power to detect, arrest, investigate and prosecute offenders. He argued that the search carried out at El-Rufai’s residence was executed pursuant to a search warrant issued by a competent court of law. He disagreed with the ex-governor that the search warrant was invalid, insisting that it was a genuine court order. According to him, the applicant is trying to use the honourable court to shield him away from the security investigation and prosecution in the court of law. He, therefore, prayed the court to dismiss the suit in its entirety. The AGF, in his counter affidavit filed by Lami-Shiru, denied being privy to the facts of the alleged matter. He argued that the ICPC and I-G acted within their statutory functions. According to him, the items seized from the applicant (El-Rufai) by the 1st and 2nd respondents were seized to enable them to conclude the investigation on the applicant. He submitted that the suit was an abuse of court processes because the former governor had two pending suits on the same subject matter before the FCT High Court. The AGF, who argued that El-Rufai’s suit lacked merit as there are no legal and evidential justification to support all the claims and reliefs sought by him, prayed the court to dismiss it in its entirety. The post ₦1bn Fundamental Rights Suit: Court Fixes Dec 2 For Judgement In El-Rufai’s Suit Against ICPC, Two Others appeared first on Channels Television .

title: More than a slip: Dangers of falls in old age
body: By Sam Efararo Renowned nationalist, lawyer, statesman and first Premier of the old Western Region, Chief Obafemi Awolowo died in the bathroom of his Ikenne home on May 9, 1987. Although the exact circumstances of his death were never officially established, some have speculated that the 78-year-old elder statesman may have slipped while taking his bath. Whether or not that was the case, his death reminds us of a reality often overlooked in Nigeria: falls are a major health threat facing older adults. Studies from Spain, Italy and Brazil consistently show that between one-quarter and one-third of adults aged 70 years and above experience at least one fall each year. Nigerian studies have reported prevalence ranging from about 23 per cent to more than 40 per cent, depending on the community studied. Why do older people fall? Ageing can bring changes in balance, gait and muscle strength, making it easier to lose one’s footing. But falls are rarely caused by age alone. Arthritis, poor vision, dizziness, chronic pain and other medical conditions can increase the risk. So can environmental hazards such as slippery floors, poor lighting and uneven walkways. A study at Irrua Specialist Teaching Hospital, Edo State, identified several risk factors among participants, including smoking, chronic medication use, musculoskeletal pain, geriatric depression, environmental hazards, cognitive impairment and abnormal gait and balance. Researchers have also documented falls occurring during everyday activities such as bathing, lifting firewood, clearing farmland, climbing onto a motorcycle, crossing a drainage channel or pothole, standing in church or a bank, sitting down, lying down and simply walking. The environment matters greatly. One study found that older adults living in homes free of environmental hazards were about 2.5 times less likely to experience a fall than those living in hazardous environments. The consequences can go far beyond a bruise or cut. Falls can cause hip fractures, head injuries, prolonged hospitalisation, disability, loss of independence and premature death. Some older adults who survive serious falls never regain their previous level of mobility. There is also a psychological consequence. Fear of falling again can cause an older person to reduce physical activity. This may lead to muscle weakness, social isolation and an even greater risk of another fall. Preventing falls therefore requires more than telling older people to “be careful”. Family members, caregivers, communities and healthcare workers all have roles to play. Doctors should pay attention to conditions that can increase fall risk, including sudden drops in blood pressure when standing, gait and balance problems, vision disturbances, environmental hazards and episodes of loss of consciousness. Families can also make homes safer by clearing walkways, improving lighting, reducing slippery surfaces and ensuring that bathrooms and stairways have appropriate support. Older adults who experience dizziness, unsteadiness, new weakness or repeated falls should tell a healthcare professional rather than simply avoiding activity. Medication may need review, while problems with vision, hearing, balance or blood pressure may require attention. Staying physically active is also important. Appropriate walking, strength and balance exercises can help maintain muscle strength, coordination and confidence. For people who already have significant balance problems, exercise should be guided by an appropriate health professional. Nigeria has policies intended to improve the welfare of older persons, including the National Policy on Ageing and provisions of the National Health Act. But implementation remains a challenge, and fall prevention deserves greater attention as the country’s population ages. A fall is often treated as an accident. But for an older person, it can be the beginning of a long period of disability. That is why prevention deserves attention before the first fall occurs. Helping older Nigerians remain safely on their feet is also helping them remain independent, active and dignified. Takeaway Fall Prevention Tips Watch medications: Some medicines used for blood pressure, arthritis and insomnia can cause dizziness or a sudden drop in blood pressure. Report dizziness or unsteadiness to a healthcare professional so medicines can be reviewed where necessary. Make the environment safer: Clear walkways of clutter, loose rugs and extension cords. Pay particular attention to slippery bathroom floors. Improve lighting along dark corridors and staircases, and consider safety bars and handrails where appropriate. Wear suitable footwear: Avoid high heels, floppy slippers and shoes with slippery soles. Sturdy footwear with a secure fit and non-slip soles can provide better support. Check vision and hearing: Poor vision, cataracts, glaucoma and hearing problems can contribute to falls. Regular checks can help identify problems that need attention. Keep moving: Fear of falling should not automatically lead to inactivity. Walking, strength and balance exercises can help maintain muscle strength, coordination and confidence. Older people with significant balance problems should seek appropriate professional guidance before starting a new exercise programme. The post More than a slip: Dangers of falls in old age appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 28, 2026
body: The Nigerian Naira maintained relative stability against the United States Dollar across both official and parallel foreign exchange markets on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. Continued liquidity injections by the Central Bank of Nigeria and sustained foreign currency inflows from autonomous channels have helped cushion the local currency against aggressive market pressures. At the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, the Naira traded around 1,341.31 to 1,352.87 per Dollar. Spot market activity recorded moderate intra-day fluctuations as commercial banks and institutional buyers satisfied forex demand for import bills and capital remittances. The tight corridor underscores ongoing market clearing measures established under the refined operational framework of the central bank. In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, Bureau De Change operators and street currency traders in major hubs such as Lagos, Abuja, and Kano quoted buying rates near 1,375 Naira per Dollar and selling rates around 1,390 Naira per Dollar. This keeps the premium between the official window and the unauthorised market relatively narrow. Financial analysts attribute the steadying market conditions to disciplined monetary policy, steady national foreign exchange reserves hovering around key operational benchmarks, and balanced seasonal demand. Market participants expect trading volumes to remain steady over the near term as both official and informal windows absorb regular commercial order flows. title: Anti-Netanyahu bloc vows not to let chance to replace government slip away
body: As parties in the opposition bloc, the parties seeking to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government awaited the official results on Tuesday evening; a sharp, clear message was already emerging behind the scenes:This time, they do not intend to let the chance to unseat the government slip away. Sources in the bloc told Walla that after this campaign, and all the effort poured into it, there will be no second chances."All the stars aligned in this election campaign," the source told Walla. "After October 7, with the haredi issue that hurt the right-wing parties and shifted voters away from them, we managed to create a united bloc of people from the Right, the Center and the Left. Four tightly knit parties, with surplus-vote agreements, while the Right failed to get organized and wasted votes."Opposition activates 'all systems' of voter turnoutThe source said the bloc's unprecedented get-out-the-vote drive also obliges party leaders to seize the moment. "We brought people from abroad especially to vote; we made an enormous effort to reach maximum voter turnout; we activated all the systems. Now we need to form a government. Period."The bloc recognizes that building a coalition may require painful compromises, backing away from campaign pledges and even making deals with parties some of its leaders vowed never to join in government. This time, however, the sources said, there will be no patience for ego battles or for clinging to campaign promises."Whoever needs to break promises, let him break them; whoever needs to swallow his pride, let him swallow it. There's no choice. It's now or never," the source said. "Next time, the demographic changes, and especially the growth of the haredi population, may already make their mark. It's not certain we'll get an opportunity like this again."Despite the determination, the bloc knows everything hinges on the final results and whether it can form a parliamentary majority capable of replacing the government. Still, the message to party leaders on Tuesday evening was clear: If the numbers allow it, no one can afford to be the one who let the opportunity slip.

title: Should AI Decide Your Court Case? This Judge Says Yes
body:
In a few days, judge Geoffrey Vos will retire as Master of the Rolls, the most senior position in England’s civil justice system. As one of his final acts, he’s trying to stoke a debate about whether—and how—judges should be using artificial intelligence.
Under the latest guidance, judges in England are advised to confine their use of AI to administrative tasks, and Vos tells WIRED he uses Microsoft Copilot all the time to locate far-flung documents and summarize large bodies of text. But recently, he visited a court in Shenzhen, China, where civil disputes are already being decided by judges with heavy assistance from AI. Impressed by what he saw, Vos believes that courts across the globe should consider following.
That road is littered with pitfalls. Multiple lawyers have been caught citing case law hallucinated by AI, and in a first for the UK, somebody recently lost their license to practice in part because they misused the technology. Meanwhile, with chatbots as their legal counsel, litigants are flooding the courts with an unprecedented number of claims, some of them bogus.
Yet Vos remains convinced that AI will someday help resolve civil disputes more rapidly and in ways that cost far less. While complicated commercial disputes and sensitive family cases might require a human judge, he believes that personal injury claims, low-value professional negligence cases, and the like could easily be adjudicated by AI.
“What most people desperately want in civil disputes is resolution,” Vos tells WIRED. “The question is, where is the line to be drawn?”
Given his impending retirement, the debate for Vos is largely a philosophical one. But for everyone else in the profession—and for coders, cybersecurity experts, math professors, and a whole host of others—the rules are changing fast.
In October, WIRED met with Vos at his office at the Royal Courts of Justice, London. We discussed the ways that AI is spilling into the courts, the practical and ethical issues it raises, and how the justice system might adapt to serve a new generation raised alongside the technology.
This conversation has been edited for length and clarity.
WIRED: You’re just a few days away from retirement. How do you feel about leaving the post at this particular juncture, as AI begins to reshape how law is practiced and justice administered?
GEOFFREY VOS: When I started as a lawyer, we had foolscap paper, typists, and Tipp-Ex. We moved rapidly into word processors, faxes, and eventually computers.
Lawyers are conservative with a lowercase c. But that doesn’t mean that they should be backward-looking or retrogressive. It means they should be adopting change cautiously, with their eyes open.
The legal system is for the people of this country. You can’t be effective in providing access to justice if you’re not on the same technological wavelength. But it’s time to leave it to a new generation of leadership judges.
How have you built AI into your practice to date?
I don’t use it for writing judgments, but I use it for finding things out, navigating large quantities of material, and checking things. It saves me time. I have 11 meetings a day. I know there’s a document created years ago that’s relevant to my meeting—and Copilot finds it in seconds. I do that every day.
In law, isn’t the devil always in the details? Doesn’t confidence in the legal system depend on the understanding that a judge will review and consider every inch of every court submission?
I’m a little more cautious about using it to read papers for my cases, but that’s because I do the most important cases in the system.
People have confidence in our justice system because they believe that our judges have absolute integrity. In order not to lose that integrity, you have to explain how you’re adopting technology and achieve a broad consensus that it is appropriate.
How is AI spilling into the courts right now? Is it changing how litigants and legal professionals behave? What issues is it throwing up?
It’s changing everything remarkably quickly. We see a 10 percent rise in the number of county court cases started every year—and it looks as if this may increase. That’s because everybody who has a legal problem now puts it into Gemini, ChatGPT, or Claude. Ask it to create a particulars of claim, a case, a claim form—it can.
What proportion of these claims are based on sound legal principles, though? How often are people led by a chatbot to mistakenly believe they have a claim?
We don’t have the data. But I think it’s a mistake to assume that just because a claim is created by AI, it’s totally frivolous.
In a way it’s a good problem, because it shows there’s greater access to justice because of technology. One of the problems with justice in the past is that it’s only been available to rich people.
If people have a problem sufficient to bother ChatGPT, they probably genuinely think they have a claim. When you explore their problem in detail, you might find it is actually a bit different, but it may still be a legal problem and may still be reasonable for them to have wanted to bring it to attention.
People are not generally time wasters. They’re not generally trying to make trouble.
What about the opportunity for AI to fabricate evidence on which judges have previously been able to rely—images, video, voice recordings? Where does that leave the courts?
Often, judges have to decide whether a person is telling the truth. That is the most difficult thing to do, because humans are not bad at lying. But judges make these decisions every day. There’s absolutely no difference—in scale or qualitatively—in somebody producing a false image created by AI.
The only reason we’re all getting so excited about deepfakes is because they are so new. But actually, that is the stuff of judging.
But we’re talking about a whole category of evidence that’s now somewhat compromised. Doesn’t that affect a judge’s ability to decide whether somebody is lying?
It was always thus. We always had to decide whether wills were forged, because people used to do that. It’s exactly the same with voice recordings, and video. It’s just an extension of the type of false information that is produced to the court.
People will find out when they produce fake images to the court that they are committing perjury and they will go to prison, just as if they’d forged a will.
I think we need to be cautious about predicting disaster. I’m very optimistic.
You’ve previously described an “inevitable” future where simpler civil cases are adjudicated entirely by AI. Why are you confident that’s where we’re headed?
You need to find a way to deliver justice that is within the cultural grain. That doesn’t mean you just conduct all your cases on TikTok. But if you don’t understand that people are asking LLMs for the answer to almost every question under the sun, including legal questions, you’re likely to get it wrong when you try to devise a process fit for the 21st century.
It’s all about consensus. It will only be possible to ask people to accept algorithmic decision-making if they consent to the process in a particular case, or if society decides through legislation.
When people go to court and get an adverse outcome, even if they regard the outcome as idiosyncratic or even wrong, when it’s delivered in a human way, it can be accepted over time. With AI, we have to be careful; it may be less easy for people to accept an adverse machine-driven decision.
I very much want to see a very open, international discussion about how we should resolve disputes.
I suspect part of the reason people object to trial by AI is because we can’t know precisely how a model has arrived at a decision. What’s to be done about this problem of explainability?
I don’t think it’s about reasoning; it’s about outcomes. The AI can produce very plausible reasoning. You can’t see how it produced that reasoning, but you can see the reasoning it produced, and you can judge the plausibility.
I don’t think you’ll ever do away with human judges. There’s something almost biblical about the human judge; it’s in the human psyche to want to be judged by their fellow man. But that does not mean that in some situations people wouldn’t rather have a quick outcome—even if it’s not a human outcome.
Where would you draw the line?
I don’t think judges are yet in the position to say. It’s a question for society, politicians, and legislation to resolve. That debate is really important.
I think that custody and family cases are one of the areas where essentially human judgment is expected, even by the younger generation. In complex commercial cases, I think that’s also the case. But I think we will whittle away at how commercial cases are decided by using AI to collate information to make the decision-making process better and easier.
We will allow more people access to justice more cheaply and more quickly using technology. That will be an overall good for the economy and for the people we serve.

title: Agony of ostracized Ebonyi widow
body: …Claims the action aimed to deprive her and children of the late husband’s estate, family land …My life and the lives of my children are in grave danger, now a fugitive, she cries out A widow, Mrs. Njideka Ngwutu, from Nsokkara community in Ezza South Council of Ebonyi State, experienced the worst embarrassment of her life and indeed the height of encroachment into her fundamental rights, when a group of women from her community announced that she was from the community for allegedly questioning the change of the women’s meeting venue. She alleged that the leadership nd members of the Acharaukwu Development Union Women Wing (ADU) wrongfully accused her and ostracized her even without fair hearing and proper investigation. According to her, the punishment was initiated by notable personalities in her kindred to allegedly banish her and grab her late husband’s land and confiscate other estates belonging to the family. The widow has appealed to the Ministry of Women Affairs, the Governor’s wife, and other well meaning people across the country to urgently wade into matter and conduct a thorough investigate into her plights. In her letter of appeal, titled: “Urgent Petition against Extreme Harassment, Ostracization, and Attempted Forcible Eviction by the leadership and members of the Acharaukwu Development Union, Women Wing (ADU), in Ezza South Local Government Area”, the widow alleged that members of Umunaza kindred united against her because she was married from Achina Aguata Council of Anambra State and has no one to speak on her behalf because all the adult male children of her husband’s family had died of strange diseases. “I am originally from Achina, Aguata LGA of Anambra State, but was married into the Ngwuta Anyigor family of Acharaukwu Nsokkara in Ezza South LGA about 27 years ago. The union is blessed with three children. Tragically, my husband is deceased, just like his brothers, parents, and other prominent male relatives. Since the demise of my husband and his male relatives, nobody represents the family at kindred level that is why we have been maltreated. “I have been subjected to relentless torment by certain members of our kindred, Umunaza Kindred of Acharaukwu Nsokkara, who are hell-bent on dispossessing my family of the lands belonging to us. “My late husband had 2 brothers who got married and had children before the 3 brothers incidentally died under suspicious circumstances, leaving me and my co-wives as young widows with our young children behind. My parents in-law are also deceased, and so the entire Ngwuta Anyigor family was left in the hands of widows and young children. Before my mother-in-law died in 2016, my co-wives and their children had left the village owing to numerous spiritual attacks and unexplainable deaths in the family, leaving only my mother-in-law, myself, and my 3 children behind. “I had wanted to run away with my children from the village but I could not leave my mother in-law alone as she was old and needed care. I stayed behind and took care of her until she died and was buried. After her death, I realized that leaving the village with my children would mean that everyone in the family had run away and that would lead the family name, compound and legacy into extinction. I stayed back with my children, farmed on our lands and used the proceeds to train my children in school. As a result of my stay in the village, some of my husband’s nephews and nieces have returned and now live with me in the family compound,” she narrated. Mrs. Ngwuta, however, revealed that ever since she lost her husband and decided to stayed back with her children the husband’s nephews and nieces, some members of her late husband’s kindred, Umunaza, have been trying to forcefully take over her husband’s Estates and family lands and frustrate them out of the family compound. She expressed surprise that those at the forefront of the land-grabbing were close to her husband while he was alive. “Despite my vulnerability as a widow without adult male backing me in the family, I have consistently resisted these land-grabbing attempts. At the forefront of this oppression are some very close family members of my late husband, who share the same kindred with my late husband. When they attempted to forcefully take over my lands, I stood my ground, and the entire Acharaukwu community intervened, looked into the matter, and rightfully decided in my favour” Mrs. Ngwuta said, “Following their inability to take over the lands, these people have resorted to character assassination and blackmail.” “Sometime in 2024, two young girls from the same Acharaukwu Nsokkara came to my house around 9pm and begged me to agree that I had sold some cassava to them. I immediately suspected that I was being set up by the same people who had been trying to take me out of my family and I quickly refused and asked them to leave my house. Owing to my fear of being set up in more unsuspecting events, I made a conscious decision to stop attending public events or gatherings held at private residences. “This union conducts its meetings in each village from time to time, while the Annual General Meeting is held in August of every year. My own village is Effium, Acharaukwu Nsokkara, and the meeting is usually held at the Effium Playground. It is also worthy of note that as of 2024, I was the Secretary of the Effium Unit of the Union. Surprisingly, about 3 years ago, the then Chairlady of the Effium Unit of ADU Women Wing relocated the meetings from the public playground where such meetings were always traditionally held, directly to the compound of one of my late husband’s relatives. Understanding the clear danger this posed “to my safety and liberty, I protested and formally informed the association that I would not attend any meeting in anyone’s compound. I expressed my legitimate fear of being set up and subjected to jungle justice for crimes I did not commit” “Rather than understanding my plight as a fellow woman and a widow, the ADU Women Wing leadership became infuriated. They went as far as reporting me to the Catholic Church where I worship. In an attempt to make peace, the Catholic Women Organization (CWO) of my church mandated me to apologize to the ADU women. “In obedience to the CWO, I went with some members of the church to see the ADU women at Dr. Kelvin Nwankwo’s compound, but we were turned down at the gate, and Dr. Nwankwo specifically warned that they should not enter into his compound. I went back with the other church members, informed the CWO and the Priest of the church and have since then maintained my resolution not to attend such meeting in anyone’s compound” “They forcefully handed me a matchbox, indicating that I had been ostracized from the community. Furthermore, they passed the following draconian and illegal edicts against me: that I have been completely banned from fetching water from any of the community streams or boreholes, forbidden from interacting or associating with anyone in the community, and banned from entering the markets to buy or sell anything. “They (allegedly) expicitly threatened that I would be killed if I dared disobey their orders. It is abundantly clear that this women’s group is being sponsored and weaponized by some people in Acharaukwu Nsokkara whose aim is to frustrate, humiliate, and terrorize me into abandoning my late husband’s home so they can finally take over my family’s land” At the moment , “my life and the lives of my children are in grave danger. My three children, my husband’s nephews and nieces, have fled our home for fear of being harmed. I am currently living as a fugitive, sleeping in neighboring communities because it is no longer safe for me to sleep in my own marital home.” Mrs Ngwuta further alleged that one of her neighbours, Miss Rebecca Aleke, who visited her compound after she was ostracized, was later tortured and almost beaten to death for associating with her. Such action, she said, had left her traumatized and afraid of what may happen next. She is therefore calling on the wife of the Governor of Ebonyi State, Mrs. Uzoamaka Nwifuru, as her last resort to wade in and save her life and her home. “I also want Her Excellency to use her good office to promptly summon the leadership of the ADU Women Wing, Acharaukwu Nsokkara, to explain their justification for ostracizing a widow like me, denying me access to basic amenities, and issuing death threats against me”, Mrs. Ngwuta appealed. When contacted, President of the ADU Women’s Wing, Mrs. Leticia Ngele and Mrs. Eucheria Nwandende, confirmed that Mrs. Njideka Ngwuta was ostracized by the union, saying that Mrs. Ngwuta had always been at the forefront of carrying out barbaric act against other women who defaulted. However, the traditional ruler of Nsokkara Autonomous community, HRH Eze Festus Ifesinachi Okonkwo, and a major stakeholder from the Community, chief Celestine Ekechi, condemned the action of the women’s group, noting that such a barbaric act was never part of their culture. Okonkwo admitted that he was aware of the case but noted that all efforts to resolve it proved abortive, as even the letter of summons sent to the women was not honored. Meanwhile, Ezeogo Festus Okonkwo has disbanded the leadership of Acharaukwu Development Union (ADU) Women Wing for reprehensible action against the widow. Ezeogo Okonkwo, who has submitted the ban order to the office of the Honorable Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Matters, said the action of the women’s group contradicts Section 002 of the 2018 Ebonyi State Law Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP LAW) The Traditional Ruler who visibly frowned at the injustice meted out to the indigent widow, ordered that Mrs. Njideka Ngwuta should as a matter of urgency return to her matrimonial home and reunite with her children and loved ones. He warned that any further threat to her life shall be viewed seriously and visited with the full weight of the law of Ebonyi State and the Federal Republic of Nigeria. He emphasized that the barbaric act was against the culture, custom and traditions of Nsokkara and Ezza Ezekuna people noting he is very annoyed with the leadership of the women for bluntly and flagrantly refusing to honour his invitation when he got the wind of the matter. “The action, harassment and the inhuman treatment meted out against Mrs. Ngwuta is a violent act which has caused her physical and emotional trauma and is condemned in its entirety as it is an action perpetrated against her fundamental human rights and equally violates the provisions of Ebonyi State Violence Against Persons Prohibition No.002 of 2018 (VAPP LAW)”, he stressed, assuring that the palace has initiated an in-depth investigation to unravel the sponsors of the barbaric and heinous act in the community. The post Agony of ostracized Ebonyi widow appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Up to 650,000 special ballots could still turn Israel's election on its head
body: Hundreds of thousands of ballots cast outside voters' assigned polling stations could still affect the final outcome of Israel's general election, potentially shifting parliamentary seats between parties and altering the political balance. Unlike regular ballots, these votes undergo a separate verification process before being added to the nationwide count, meaning the first results may not fully reflect the final composition of the Knesset. These votes are known in Israel as double-envelope ballots, a system that allows eligible voters who cannot reach their assigned polling stations to vote elsewhere. They include soldiers, military reservists, diplomats, police officers, prison staff, hospital patients and displaced residents. Each voter places their anonymous ballot inside an envelope, which is then sealed inside a second envelope carrying identifying information. Election officials use the outer envelope to verify that the person has not voted twice before adding the anonymous ballot to the national count.   Because of the war and the large number of mobilized reservists and Israelis displaced from their homes, the Central Elections Committee prepared for an unprecedented number of double-envelope ballots. More than 460,000 were cast in the 2022 election, while advance estimates for this election ranged from 600,000 to 650,000. That volume represents roughly 15 Knesset seats' worth of votes, although those seats are not allocated separately. Instead, the ballots are added to the nationwide totals, potentially changing how seats are distributed among parties. Historically, these votes have tended to favor Zionist parties across the political spectrum, largely because soldiers make up a significant proportion of voters using the system. Ultra-Orthodox and Arab voters are considerably less represented in this group, meaning their parties' relative share of the overall vote can decline once the ballots are included. The effect is generally limited but can be significant enough to change the allocation of one or two seats. This means parties such as the ultra-Orthodox Shas and United Torah Judaism, as well as the predominantly Arab Joint List and the Islamist Ra'am party, could see their relative electoral strength change when the double-envelope ballots are incorporated. However, the outcome also depends on the remaining regular votes, the performance of other parties and the distribution of surplus votes. A similar shift occurred in the 2022 election. Before the double-envelope count, United Torah Judaism was projected to win eight seats and Avigdor Liberman's secular nationalist Yisrael Beytenu party five. Once the additional votes were included, United Torah Judaism fell to seven seats while Yisrael Beytenu rose to six. The shift illustrated how a relatively small change in the overall vote distribution can affect individual parties without necessarily changing the balance between political blocs. In that election, the number of votes required to secure one parliamentary seat under the allocation formula was approximately 36,227. The double-envelope ballots therefore represented the equivalent of roughly 12 to 13 seats. Likud received enough of those votes to represent approximately three seats, Yesh Atid around two, and Religious Zionism and Otzma Yehudit together nearly two. These figures illustrate the voting strength of different parties within the special count, rather than seats awarded directly from those ballots. The final allocation also depends on the electoral threshold and agreements between parties to combine surplus votes. The pattern was evident in the March 2021 election as well, when approximately 428,000 double-envelope ballots were counted. Their inclusion reduced Ra'am's representation to four seats and increased the left-wing Meretz party's total to six, without changing the balance between the main political blocs. The counting of double-envelope ballots requires additional checks and can continue after the regular vote count has been completed. Because the votes are incorporated into the national totals rather than counted as a separate electoral category, their impact may not become clear until the final stages of the process. In a closely contested election, even a small shift in parliamentary representation could have important implications for coalition negotiations. Until all ballots are verified and included, initial seat projections remain provisional, and parties could still gain or lose representation before the final results are announced. As of 1 p.m. Wednesday, 77.6% of valid ballots had been counted, with the balance between the political blocs shifting throughout Tuesday night and Wednesday morning. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc had fallen to 54 seats, while Gadi Eisenkot's bloc stood at 49 and the Arab parties held 17. The figures remain subject to change as the remaining ballots are counted, particularly once the double-envelope ballots are included. The IDF said Wednesday morning that voter turnout among military personnel reached 79.9%, an increase of 6.2 percentage points compared with the 2022 election. According to the military, more than 890 polling stations operated at bases and military units across Israel, beginning with voting last week and continuing through Election Day. About a quarter were mobile polling stations, deployed as part of an effort to ensure that service members could exercise their right to vote, including those stationed in combat zones. 'Until the votes are counted, we cannot know' Elad Naveh, head of the Central Elections Committee's control center, told ynet Wednesday morning that election officials were pleased with how voting had proceeded. "We are very tired but very satisfied. From our perspective, Election Day was very successful, both in terms of voter turnout and the incidents we dealt with," he said. "It was a quiet day. If we have reached a point where we are dealing with the weather that unexpectedly hit us Tuesday, then we are really in very good shape." Naveh said election officials were processing results from regular polling stations at regional centers, with approximately half already entered into the system. Despite the progress, he cautioned that it was too early to determine the impact of the double-envelope ballots. "Even if we have a very large number of double-envelope ballots, as we expect — more than half a million — their distribution is generally similar to the nationwide distribution. There are no significant deviations," he said. "At this stage, we cannot even provide a definitive seat count because, as far as we are concerned, until all polling stations have been entered into the system and the double-envelope ballots have been counted, we simply do not know. We do not yet have a final calculation of the votes required for each seat." Naveh explained that double-envelope ballots undergo several stages of verification before they can be counted. "First, they are cross-checked and verified to ensure that no one voted both at their assigned polling station and through a double envelope," he said. "Then the ballots are assigned to election committees and the outer envelopes are opened. All of this happens before the actual count." He said the final stage involves convening numerous polling station committees at the Knesset, made up of election officials and party representatives, to count the ballots. Naveh initially estimated that counting would begin around midnight Wednesday, but the committee later said the process was expected to begin Wednesday evening. He estimated that the double-envelope count would be completed Thursday evening, although the process could continue into Friday. Even then, he said, the results would be only "almost final" because additional verification procedures would still be required. "Why do I say almost? Because next week, on Sunday, Monday and Tuesday, as well as Friday, we will conduct an audit of polling stations," he said. "We will recount a sample of polling stations, stations where certain incidents occurred and those where discrepancies were found." "In the previous election, we recounted almost half of all polling stations," Naveh added. "We conduct checks upon checks upon checks to make sure the will of the voters is reflected in the results."

body:
