title: Ofala festival: From royal dancing to robust community enterprise
body: •As Obi of Onitsha warns S-East against electoral apathy •Says it will deepen political marginalisation of the region By Vincent Ujumadu The 2026 annual Ofala festival of Onitsha, Anambra State, has ended in the ancient kingdom with the usual assemblage of who is who from within and outside Nigeria. The magnificent Ime Obi arena was as expected filled to capacity by gaily dressed indigenes and their guests, as well as politicians from the various political parties, the clergy and security operatives. For effective crowd control during the Ofala, the popular Awka road from the Borromeo roundabout to the DMGS roundabout, was closed to traffic for most of the day and traffic diverted to other parts of the commercial city. The highlight of the day was the Royal dance of the Obi of Onitsha, Igwe Alfred Nnaemeka Achebe, accompanied by Ndi Ichie (cabinet chiefs). For over 500 years, the people of Onitsha have consistently shown resilience in showcasing their rich culture and tradition to the admiration of other kingdoms of the world. And for the last 15 years, communication giants, Globacom, has been part of the Ofala Onitsha and had helped to introduce some glamour into the festival. From 2025 when the theme of the celebration was “njiko na ntachi” (unity and resilience), to the 2026 theme which moved forward to “iga n’iru” (deliberate progress), the charge has always been that the people should use their craft to advance their communities and build a prosperous Onitsha Kingdom. At every Ofala, the people usually look forward to the Royal message delivered by the Obi of Onitsha. This year’s message was spectacular because, apart from speaking on the ‘State of the Nation’, which dwelt on the importance of free and fair election in 2027 and encouragement of the people of the South East to participate effectively in the election, the reigning Monarch, Igwe Alfred Nnaemeka Achebe, briefed his subjects on the Onitsha Advancement Foundation, OnAF, which came into existence five years ago, as well as other important areas affecting Onitsha. In the past one year, according to Igwe Achebe, the OnAF implementation committee approved some projects, including household farming, basic ICT training for women, one youth 2 skills programme, medical insurance, among others. In the Royal message, Igwe Achebe announced that all legal documentation and registration of the Onitsha Millennium Development Foundation, OMDF, have been completed and banking relationships established. So, Ofala Onitsha is not just about dancing, but also a forum to discuss the business and welfare of the people. Hear Igwe Achebe: “As at 31st August, 2026, total inflows of money stand at N291.78 million, comprising levies of N270.6 million, fines and penalties of N17.28 million and interest of 1% representing title ceremonies of over 24 months. This figure represents the amount paid into the Onitsha account. “Of this, N191.78 million has been reconciled and transferred to the account managed by the OMDF, while the balance of N100 million is undergoing reconciliation and will be transferred shortly. Investment activities have commenced in safe, secure and liquid money market infrastructure, and the Foundation has taken decisions to commence development activities”. According to him, going forward, the Foundation will be the sole repository for all Community funds, including the Ofala proceeds currently committed to ongoing capital projects at Ime Obi and Okwu Eze Umuezearoli and Okebunabo, adding that it will also be disbursed annually for the recurrent expenditure, such as Ime Obi maintenance and administration, vigilante security and OnAF. Beating his chest on the progress being made by Onitsha as a community, Igwe Achebe, who will be 25 years on the throne of Ezechima next year said: “The energy and commitment of our indigenes within and outside the homeland, including those abroad, are unrivaled. I am very proud that we are striving together at great sacrifice to our personal circumstances to leave Onitsha better than we inherited it. “We have a duty to nurture and grow our youths of today to grow and be ready to inherit the almost 600 legacy bequeathed by our predecessors. We are in a marathon, not a sprint. I therefore call on all indigenes, friends and associates of our community, not to relent in the sustained effort to take Onicha Ado ni’du to higher levels.” There are, however, areas which the Monarch wants his subjects to pay attention to in the next 12 months. They include assessment of the achievements and failures of OnAF @5; development of short, medium and long term priorities for Onitsha; engaging the large number of unemployed youths in the community, who have undergone training; finding solution to the alarming rate of substance abuse and drug addiction, as well as other social vices. He also said that in line with the Ohanaeze Ndigbo project, comprehensive census of victims of the Nigerian Civil War will be conducted with a view to creating a befitting memorial for them. He further announced that various communities would be engaged for enlightenment and sensitization programme to facilitate the adoption of the vault system for the interment of departed ones to manage limited land space. “The use of vaults for burial is an acceptable and universal method of interment, especially in environments with limited land space, such as Onitsha. In the circumstance, graves and soak away pits are competing with boreholes with the risk of percolation into water boreholes. “Between April 2024 and May 2026, about 851 bodies were buried in Inland town alone. This practice can no longer be sustained”, he stressed. Expectedly, the Onitsha Monarch did not shy way from the 2027 elections, as the Royal Father observed that the attention of the political class has increasingly turned to political positioning and away from governance. He called on the stakeholders to intensify their advocacy, mobilization and enlightenment for free and fair elections and also urged the political parties to abhor violence and engage in healthy, issue-based campaigns to enable the electorate make the right choice. He specifically charged the people of the South-East to turn out en masse for the 2027 general elections, warning that electoral apathy would only deepen the region’s political marginalization and weaken its capacity to influence decisions affecting its future According to him, with the 2027 general elections approaching, the people of the region could no longer afford to stay away from the electoral process while complaining about marginalisation and inadequate representation. “I call on the people of the South-East States to shake off their historical apathy towards elections. We cannot stay away from elections and turn around to complain of marginalization. In democracy, all votes count. Therefore, we must come out and vote for our candidates,” the Monarch said. He also called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to ensure free, fair and credible elections, stressing that the integrity of the electoral process was essential to strengthening public confidence in democracy. He appealed to the President to give urgent attention to the challenges confronting citizens, arguing that the issues transcended political, religious and ethnic considerations. According to him, the country’s leadership must focus on governance and practical solutions rather than political positioning, especially as the next general elections draw closer. The post Ofala festival: From royal dancing to robust community enterprise appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: After years of war, division, Israelis vote in record numbers to shape their future - editorial
body: Israelis have spent three years at war and in bitter argument at home. On Tuesday, they voted in unusually high numbers.That participation was strong from the start. By 2 p.m., turnout had reached 44.9%, with more than three million people having cast ballots. It was the highest turnout recorded at that hour since at least 1973. By 4 p.m., the figure had risen to 55.7%, with over four million cast.The message was already clear: Israelis want a say in what comes next. After everything the country had endured, that willingness to participate deserved celebration.This was the first national election since the October 7 massacre and the wars that followed. Israelis entered polling stations carrying memories of murdered relatives, fallen soldiers, hostage captivity, months of reserve duty, and displacement from their homes. They brought with them economic worries, bitter arguments over responsibility for the country's failures and achievements, and disagreements about what those experiences meant and who should lead the country through their consequences.The campaign had been intensely divisive. Parties had argued over October 7, Gaza, Iran, the courts, haredi (ultra-Orthodox) conscription, settlements, the economy, and the character of the state itself. Political leaders had accused one another of endangering the country. Voters had heard warnings that virtually every possible result could produce catastrophe.Millions of voters demonstrate the strength of Israeli democracyMillions responded by putting a slip of paper into an envelope. They made their own choices, in private, with the same right to participate as the people whose opinions had dominated the campaign. Citizens who rarely attended a demonstration or appeared on television had exactly the same ballot as cabinet ministers.Participation also mattered because an election gave people a way to turn their grievances into a decision. Public anger over security failures, the burden of military service, or the cost of living could find expression on a ballot. Each voter had an opportunity to reward a record, reject it, or support an alternative.That opportunity belonged equally to those who had defended the government and those who had demonstrated against it. Their willingness to use the same process was a reason for confidence in the country's ability to keep making difficult decisions together, even while its citizens remained so deeply divided.The queues at some polling stations were a visible expression of that determination. They also created practical difficulties, especially for elderly people and voters with disabilities. Election officials had a responsibility to keep the process accessible. The patience of voters, and the work of those administering the ballot, deserved recognition.The voters in those lines had chosen differing futures. A high turnout could offer encouragement to the public across the political spectrum, regardless of which party ultimately benefited. Broad participation brought more citizens into the decision about the next Knesset and gave more people a direct part in shaping the country's direction.Israelis from across society exercise their equal right to voteThat included Arab citizens, whose turnout attracted intense political attention during the day. Their participation was an expression of Israeli democracy. The same was true of haredim, settlers, secular Tel Avivians, residents of development towns, soldiers, and immigrants. Citizenship means having an equal ballot even when other citizens dislike how it is used.There were complaints on Tuesday about missing or damaged voting slips and other alleged irregularities. Those reports must be investigated seriously. Parties were entitled to identify problems and present evidence. Election authorities must provide the public with clear findings, and sweeping conclusions about the integrity of the vote require substantiation.The turnout itself gave the country something to appreciate. Even after years in which Israelis had repeatedly been told that the country was coming apart, citizens across its political and social divides participated in the same democratic process. They brought their disagreements into polling stations and entrusted their choices to the ballot.Democracy depends on citizens believing that their participation matters enough to show up. On Tuesday, millions of Israelis acted on that belief. Their reasons differed, as did their preferred leaders. Yet they participated in a common process for deciding their country's future. Whatever government eventually emerges from their votes, the scale of that participation deserves recognition. Israelis showed up. That was democracy in action.

title: Iran, Vietnam stress expanding coop. in state auditing
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 28 (MNA) – A delegation from the Supreme Audit Court of Iran met with the President of the Supreme Audit Court of Vietnam on the sidelines of an international summit in Hanoi.
A delegation from the Supreme Audit Court of the Islamic Republic of Iran met with Nguyen Huu Van, Auditor General of the State Audit Office of Vietnam on the sidelines of the international conference "Supreme Audit Institutions in a Changing World" in Hanoi.
During the meeting, the two sides discussed strengthening bilateral cooperation, developing technical and specialized interactions, and expanding the exchange of knowledge and experience between the two supreme audit institutions.
The meeting took place on the first day of the summit, as part of the bilateral consultations held between the heads and senior representatives of the supreme audit institutions of the participating countries. The summit is currently underway, attended by senior officials from supreme audit institutions representing various nations, including Egypt, India, China, Kazakhstan, the Republic of Azerbaijan, Pakistan, Brazil, Cambodia, Malaysia, Indonesia, Laos, Nepal, and Myanmar.

title: FACT CHECK: No report of Trump courtesy call on Sara; Marcos remains president
body: Claim: US President Donald Trump will make a courtesy call on Vice President Sara Duterte when he visits the Philippines next month, and Duterte will be the president by then. Rating: FALSE Why we fact-checked this: On October 22, Facebook user Rey Cano Salarda published a post that carries the claim. It is a text card on a green background that reads, “U.S PRES TRUMP WILL VISIT PHIL. NEXT MONTH COURTESY CALL TO VP SARA, SI VP SARA NA PALA ANG PRESIDENTE NEXT MONTH” (So VP Sara will already be President next month). As of writing, the post has 29,000 reactions, 2,200 comments, and 1,200 shares. The facts: There is no report, Palace statement, or White House announcement about a planned Trump courtesy call on Duterte. Trump’s planned visit will be for the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit, which is hosted by the Philippines. Also, Duterte will most likely not be replacing Marcos as the president next month. Marcos remains in office, and he has not resigned or been removed. Under Article VII, Section 8 of the Constitution , the Vice President takes over only if the President dies, becomes permanently disabled, is removed, or resigns. The Palace has dismissed as “delusional” claims from Duterte’s camp that the Vice President is ready to replace Marcos. Duterte is currently on trial before the Senate impeachment court. The trial resumes on November 9, when her defense team begins presenting its evidence on the remaining unexplained wealth article. The trial may or may not lead to her conviction and removal from office, not elevate her. (READ: Dropping 3 impeachment articles vs Sara, who benefits? ) Trump’s visit: Malacañang confirmed on October 14 that Trump will attend the ASEAN Summit and Related Summits in Manila. Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said that while it is confirmed, the rest of the details will not come from her. The summits run from November 16 to 18 at the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay City. The Philippines chairs ASEAN this year. Marcos declared those days as special non-working days in Metro Manila. The White House said Trump will take part in the summit on November 16 before heading to Shenzhen, China for the APEC summit. A US official said Marcos has been inviting Trump for some time. This will be his first visit to the Philippines since 2017 . At the summits, Trump will meet ASEAN leaders and other dialogue partners. The Department of Foreign Affairs expects leaders of China, Japan and South Korea to attend, along with UN Secretary-General António Guterres for the ASEAN-UN Summit. – Cyril Bocar/Rappler.com Efren Cyril Bocar is a journalist from Llorente, Eastern Samar who graduated with a degree in English Language Studies at the Visayas State University. Cyril is also a graduate of the Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024. Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

title: Arteta confronts teenage star Dowman after Arsenal stunned by fourth-tier Fleetwood
body: Mikel Arteta confronted 16-year-old Max Dowman after Arsenal's teenage star was sent off as the Premier League leaders suffered one of the biggest shocks in League Cup history against fourth-tier Fleetwood Town on Tuesday. Dowman saw red four minutes from time after an altercation with Fleetwood's Harrison Neal, leaving Arsenal with 10 men and their hopes of avoiding an embarrassing exit hanging by a thread. Fleetwood then completed the upset, beating Arsenal 5-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw to reach the quarter-finals, sparking wild scenes at the home of a side currently 18th in England's League Two. Arteta confronted Dowman as the teenager walked towards the tunnel, delivering a furious, arms-crossed lecture to the academy graduate as Fleetwood's players celebrated on the pitch. The remarkable result capped a night of drama, with Fleetwood recovering from Arsenal's second-half equaliser to force the tie into a shoot-out. Goalkeeper Ryan Lynch saved from Bruno Guimaraes before Conor Haughey sent Arsenal goalkeeper Illan Meslier the wrong way with the decisive penalty to send Fleetwood into the quarter-finals. The visitors had taken a surprise lead in the 21st minute when Aaron Loupalo-Bi shrugged off Arsenal defender Marli Salmon before firing a tight-angle effort beyond Meslier. The match had already been disrupted early on when play was stopped for more than eight minutes after a drone was spotted flying above the stadium. Arsenal responded after the interval and levelled four minutes into the second half. Ceadach O'Neill, making his senior debut, controlled a long ball from Piero Hincapie before delivering into the area, where Viktor Gyokeres converted from close range. But Arsenal's hopes of avoiding an embarrassing exit suffered another blow four minutes from time when Dowman was shown a straight red card following an altercation with Fleetwood's Neal near halfway. It was the second red card this month for the teenager, who was also dismissed while playing for England Under-19s during the last international break. Arteta later defended his reaction, saying he had specifically warned Dowman about keeping his composure. "When we prepared the context of the match, we were very clear on the things to respect, the things that emotionally we have to dominate. It was very clear," Arteta said. The Arsenal boss was reluctant to pass judgement on the incident itself, adding: "It's difficult to see on the cameras, so I prefer to watch it back properly and then I can assess the situation." Asked whether Dowman would learn from the experience, Arteta replied, "Yes, we all learn from everything." Arsenal pressed for a winner despite being reduced to 10 men, but Lynch produced a crucial late save to deny Ben White and force the tie into a shoot-out. Lynch then dived low to his left to palm away Guimaraes' penalty as Fleetwood went 4-3 ahead before Haughey completed the stunning victory. "Amazing for the club, the town. Honestly it means everything to everyone," Lynch told Sky Sports. Fleetwood had drawn inspiration from Grimsby Town's famous cup victory over Manchester United last season. "We took heart from Grimsby beating Man United last year. We kind of compared it," Lynch said. "The whole team throughout the game was magnificent. To beat the English champions – credit to these lads." Arsenal have won seven of their opening eight Premier League matches and are unbeaten in the Uefa Champions League. Fleetwood, by contrast, have won just once in their previous eight league games.

title: Abu Dhabi students help pack 10,000 winter relief kits to help needy Gazans
body: Community-spirited students in Abu Dhabi have joined a nationwide aid drive for Gaza after helping to pack 10,000 winter relief kits for needy civilians. Members of Mohamed bin Zayed University for Humanities turned out in force to prepare the aid packages, containing 70,000 items of clothing and heating supplies aimed at protecting embattled communities from plunging temperatures in the months ahead. The volunteer effort was organised by the Sheikh Saeed bin Zayed Al Nahyan Endowment and is in support of the UAE's humanitarian mission for the enclave. Hamoud Al Afari, director of UAE relief operations at the Operation Gallant Knight campaign, said the participation of the student community highlighted the values of solidarity and generosity instilled in the next generation. Mr Al Afari said the total amount of humanitarian aid delivered to the Gaza Strip since the outbreak of war in October 2023 has now exceeded 131,000 tonnes, with a value of $4.16 billion. UAE quest to help one million people The UAE launched its winter clothing initiative in September to provide warm clothing to one million people in the Gaza Strip braced for harsh living conditions during the colder weather. The strategy aims to provide a critical lifeline for civilians who remain in the grip of a humanitarian crisis. The sharp drop in temperatures in the months ahead is expected to exacerbate the severe challenges brought about by the prolonged conflict with Israel. Close to two million people in the Gaza Strip have been displaced due to the conflict, leaving them exposed to greater health risks during harsh weather. More than 74,000 Palestinians have been killed in Israel’s military campaign, according to Gaza health authorities. A US-backed ceasefire in October 2025 halted large-scale fighting in Gaza, but it has not ended Israeli strikes, and there has been little progress made towards a permanent peace. The Hamas-led attacks on October 7, 2023, killed 1,200 people in Israel and took about 250 hostage, according to Israeli tallies. Dubai Humanitarian launched a new air bridge to deliver winter relief to Gaza in October. The first flight, carrying essential humanitarian supplies including thermal blankets for Unicef, arrived in Al Arish, Egypt, before being transferred to Gaza. The initiative is being carried out under the directives of Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid , Vice President and Ruler of Dubai . The air bridge involves flights operated by the Dubai Royal Air Wing using C-130 aircraft, each carrying about nine tonnes of supplies. At least three more flights were scheduled to deliver blankets for children and other vulnerable groups as families prepare for the approaching winter. Serving up support The UAE began airlifting food aid to Gaza earlier this month under the Ahmed bin Rashid Humanitarian Bridge initiative. The initiative was named in honour of Sheikh Ahmed , brother of Sheikh Mohammed , who died on September 21, to recognise his generosity and philanthropic work. It brought together volunteers and community members and at Dubai World Trade Centre to prepare food the aid packages for families and children in Gaza.

title: Lockheed Martin to Add Air-Launched Hypersonic Missile to the American Arsenal of Freedom
body:
TROY, Ala., Oct. 27, 2026. Lockheed Martin has been awarded a $694M contract from the US Air Force for production of the Air-Launched Rapid Response Weapon (ARRW). The new capability brings sustained and maneuverable hypersonic capabilities to America's Arsenal of Freedom and is the culmination of years of developmental and test partnership between Lockheed Martin and the US Air Force.



THE BIG PICTURE

Integrated on the B-52, ARRW brings hypersonic strike capability that can be rapidly deployed to the US Air Force. Its production readiness makes it an essential asset for the military, providing a critical capability to counter emerging threats.

Earlier today, Lockheed Martin broke ground on an expansion of Building P-20 in Troy, Alabama, that will add 47,000 square feet of production space for ARRW. The expansion will triple the current facility's production space and generate new American jobs over the next four years, adding to the almost 4,000 Lockheed Martin employees in the state of Alabama. The world-class facility will prepare the workforce to build ARRW using advanced manufacturing, robotics and digital technologies.

WHY IT MATTERS

ARRW will travel at speeds greater than Mach 5, more than five times the speed of sound, to rapidly engage targets from significant standoff ranges.

ARRW is designed to operate in extreme environments through the use of advanced materials to manage extreme heat, an advanced technology package to maintain accuracy and lethality, and capability to overcome a wide range of defenses.

Lockheed Martin has already funded efforts, materials, and equipment required to start ARRW's production, underscoring the company's commitment to delivering this critical capability to the US Air Force at speed and scale.

EXPERT PERSPECTIVE

"The ARRW production contract award showcases Lockheed Martin's ability to develop and begin production on cutting-edge systems at unprecedented speed and scale," said Tim Cahill, president, Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control. "ARRW expands our weapon systems portfolio and launches a critical, high-precision, and sustained hypersonic capability that will enhance the US Air Force's strategic advantage across multiple domains."



ADDITIONAL CONTEXT

Lockheed Martin's $8-9 billion investment through 2030 to meet munitions demand is already delivering tangible results, including our $67 million investment for ARRW production facility expansion and equipment, prior to receiving government funding.

The company also continued research and development, ensuring long-term support and rapid delivery of the US Air Force's need for an air-launched hypersonic strike capability.

Lockheed Martin is the leader in hypersonic strike capabilities, leveraging more than 60 years of hypersonic strike experience to deliver game-changing capabilities in support of the US National Defense Strategy and security objectives of allied nations.

title: Air Astana Expands Winter Flights as Vietjet Offers Promotional Fares to Hanoi and Prague
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA – Air Astana has introduced its winter flight schedule, adding new international destinations and increasing frequencies on popular holiday routes, while Vietnamese carrier Vietjet is expanding its network and offering promotional fares from $135 on flights from Almaty to Hanoi and Prague. Photo credit: Shutterstock. Air Astana’s winter schedule, effective from Oct. 25 through March 27, 2027, includes new routes to Japan, Oman and Malaysia, alongside additional flights to popular destinations in Asia and the Middle East. The airline will launch regular flights between Almaty and Tokyo’s Narita Airport on Nov. 30, operating twice a week. Direct flights between Astana and Bangkok will begin on Dec. 11, with departures on Tuesdays and Fridays, complementing daily services from Almaty. Flights to Salalah, Oman, from Almaty and Astana began on Oct. 23. From Dec. 25 through March 27, 2027, Air Astana will also operate three weekly flights from Almaty to Langkawi, Malaysia. The airline is increasing frequencies on several established holiday routes. From late October, flights from Almaty to Malé in the Maldives will operate six times a week, with daily departures during peak periods around New Year and Nauryz. Services to Phu Quoc, Vietnam, will run five times a week from Almaty, increasing to daily flights in December, while Astana will have three weekly flights to the island. Flights from Almaty to Dubai will increase to 12 per week, while services from Astana will rise to 10 per week. Flights from Almaty to Phuket, Thailand, will increase to seven per week, rising to nine per week from early December. The airline will also continue services between Almaty and Shanghai and between Astana and Guangzhou. In 2026, the Air Astana Group added eight regular and charter destinations from Astana: Guangzhou, Bangkok, Larnaca, Dalaman, Batumi, Issyk-Kul, Salalah and Yining. Together with the seven routes launched in 2025, the group’s network from the capital has expanded to 32 destinations. Weekly international flights from Astana have increased from 99 to 116. “During the 2026–2027 winter season, Air Astana is expanding its international route network by launching flights to Tokyo, Oman and Langkawi. Increased frequencies to the Maldives, Phuket and Dubai will allow passengers to plan their winter holidays and festive travel more conveniently,” said Yerbolat Baisalykov, senior vice president for commercial planning and revenue management at Air Astana. Meanwhile, Vietjet is offering one-way Eco fares starting at $135, including taxes and fees, on flights between Almaty and Hanoi and between Almaty and Prague. The promotional fares are available for booking until 9 p.m. on Nov. 1 through the airline’s official website and mobile app. The offer applies to flights departing between Nov. 1 and March 31, 2027, according to the company’s press service. After launching flights between Almaty and Hanoi and between Almaty and Prague earlier in October, Vietjet is further expanding its Asian network. The airline will introduce flights between Hanoi and Tainan and resume services between Ho Chi Minh City and Chiang Mai. Both routes will operate four round-trip flights per week. Vietjet’s international network also includes services connecting Ho Chi Minh City with the Maldives, Cebu and Clark, as well as routes linking Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City with other destinations in Asia. The new services are expected to provide travelers from Kazakhstan with more options for exploring Northeast and Southeast Asia via Vietnam, while supporting tourism, trade and cultural exchange across the region. title: Nigerian govt approves N70,000 monthly transport allowance for workers
body:
The federal government has approved a ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance for public service workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, following a conciliation meeting with the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC).
The resolutions were contained in a statement signed by Annah Daniel, the head of press and public relations at the Ministry of Labour and Employment.
The approval was one of the resolutions reached at a meeting between government officials and the NLC leadership in Abuja on Tuesday, as both parties discussed workers’ welfare, the national minimum wage and outstanding allowances.
The government also approved the payment of peculiar allowance arrears, effective from 1 May 2026, in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November.
However, the parties failed to agree on the effective date for implementing the national minimum wage. They agreed that the Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee would be constituted and begin meetings immediately.
The resolutions were contained in a memorandum of understanding issued after the meeting, which was chaired by the Minister of Labour and Employment, Muhammad Dingyadi.
The NLC delegation was led by its president, Joe Ajaero.
The meeting followed an earlier conciliation session held on 22 October, convened by the Ministry of Labour and Employment to address disagreements between the government and organised labour.
Under the resolutions, the government also agreed to settle 19 months of outstanding allowances for health workers within three months, beginning in December 2026.
On tax relief for workers, the parties agreed that the matter would be referred to the NLC’s National Executive Council, as taxation is a statutory matter.
The meeting also considered the payment of hazard allowances to agricultural workers. The Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security has submitted the list of beneficiaries and the associated costs to the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission for verification.
The commission is expected to complete the verification within two weeks and issue an implementation template afterwards.
On the Consolidated Health Salary Structure (CONHESS), the commission is expected to update the cost implications within three weeks to enable the Presidential Committee on Salaries to decide on the proposed adjustment.
The meeting urged state and local governments to adopt the intervention measures. Labour unions were also encouraged to push for their implementation at their respective levels.
Both parties agreed to reconvene after one month to assess progress on the implementation of the resolutions.
The meeting was attended by the Director-General of Budget, Tanimu Yakubu; the Permanent Secretary of the Service Welfare Office in the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, Garba Abdul; and other government and labour representatives.

title: CDD-Ghana urges NDC to crack down on vote-buying
body: The Centre for Democratic Development Ghana (CDD-Ghana) has urged the National Democratic Congress (NDC) to introduce clear rules and stronger monitoring systems to address allegations of vote-buying in its internal elections. Programme Officer of CDD-Ghana, Vera Abena Addo, said the party needed to move beyond discussions about guidelines and demonstrate a commitment to tackling the practice before its forthcoming regional and national executive elections. She warned that incidents at the constituency level could set expectations for subsequent contests, potentially increasing pressure on candidates to offer money or gifts to delegates seeking to elect party executives. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, October 27, Ms Addo said the party should establish regulations governing its internal elections, even in the absence of specific laws addressing the conduct of such contests. “Even without the laws regulating the internal election, I think that the party needs to have some regulation,” she said. She expressed concern that the development of guidelines appeared to be taking too long, given the party’s electoral calendar. “I think it’s taking long, and I’m hoping that even before we move into the next level of elections [it would be implemented],” she said, referring to the regional and national polls that will follow the constituency contests. Concerns over future contests Ms Addo said allegations of vote-buying at the constituency level raised questions about what might happen when the party moved to elections involving regional and national delegates. “If at a constituency level we see this kind of activity happening, then how much more at the regional level?” she asked. She suggested that the distribution of money or gifts during constituency elections could create expectations among delegates contesting or participating in subsequent rounds of internal elections. “We expect that if we have given something at the constituency level, then they equally would want to expect something at the regional level and then at the national level,” she said. Ms Addo said the party needed to take the concerns seriously and act before the next stages of its internal electoral process. Referring to previous concerns about vote-buying, including the Ayawaso incident, she said she had expected concrete action rather than continued efforts to formulate guidelines. “From the incident at Ayawasu up to now, I would have thought that we could see some action taken, that it wouldn’t just be another—the guidelines, still parties still trying to get a guideline,” she said. Calls for stronger monitoring Ms Addo also called for a more structured approach to monitoring internal elections, saying the party should ensure that its field officers and monitoring committees had clear responsibilities and systems for reporting suspected breaches. Responding to comments by NDC National Deputy General Secretary Rashid Tanko, who referred to officers deployed to monitor the elections, she said the party’s monitoring arrangements needed to be sufficiently organised to establish what happened during the polls. She noted that CDD-Ghana’s assessment was partly dependent on media reports from areas its officers could not visit. Ms Addo said the party should therefore strengthen its own monitoring mechanisms to ensure that concerns about vote-buying were properly documented and investigated.

title: Video: Hero dog Martta saves neighbour from chilly fate
body:
"We're certainly proud of our dog for doing something like this. A great dog, a really great dog," her owner said.
Lapp Reindeer dog Martta lives in Kittilä, Finnish Lapland with her owners Pekka and Anu Nevalainen .
One day she caught their attention with an unusual bark.
For some reason, Martta really wanted to go outside, and took her owners with her.
Pekka and Anu followed Martta onto their neighbour's property and found him stuck in the cold water of a wastewater pit.
By then the man had completely run out of strength, and without help the icy water would likely have claimed his life.
The Nevalainens couldn't manage to lift the man out of the pit, but managed to keep him afloat until rescue services arrived. They struggled to hold onto their neighbour for around half an hour before help came.
Pekka said the worst part of the ordeal was knowing the man's likely fate if they lost their grip.
In recognition of her heroic instincts, Martta will receive the Hero Dog title from the Finnish Kennel Club, alongside seven other brave pups, at the Helsinki Dog Fair in December.
But Martta has already received rewards of ice cream and plenty of praise.
"We're certainly proud of our dog for doing something like this. A great dog, a really great dog," Pekka said.
Besides Martta, seven other dogs will also receive heroic awards in December. What unites the special canines is that at least one person likely owes their life to each of them.
The awards ceremony will take place on 13 December at the Dog Fair in Helsinki, where 14 other dogs will receive honourable mentions.

title: A guide to IFRS S1 and S2 sustainability implementation (4), By Innocent Okwuosa
body:
In a future amendment of the Sustainability Reporting Guideline (SRG Two), we will advocate for FRC to include Sustainability Practices Framework or Policy as an additional document to be submitted to it. Sustainability Practices should speak to a Sustainability Strategy to present an overall picture of how an entity is responding to or plans to respond to Sustainability Related Risks and Opportunities.
The implementation of IFRS S1 and S2 must not be approached strictly from a regulatory compliance perspective. Rather, it should lead to a change in a responsible business behaviour. For there to be this change, sustainability practices must be integrated and embedded in an entity’s operations. Today I want to provide more clarification and guidance on this.
One of the documents in the Financial Reporting Council’s (FRC) Phase Two implementation, requires an entity to identify all Sustainability Related Risks and Opportunities (SRROs) that could reasonably be expected to affect its prospect and carry out a materiality assessment of each identified SRRO. The materiality assessment enables the entity to zero in on those relevant SRROs for prioritisation. Materiality assessment is predicated on the likelihood/probability and magnitude of occurrence.
The magnitude of occurrence speaks directly to financial materiality i.e. SRRO’s effect on financial performance, position, cash flow, and access to or costs of capital. Prioritisation should be predicated on the SRROs with the highest financial effect, determined as likelihood/probability of occurrence multiplied by the magnitude. It is not my intention to go into the intricacies involved in this determination, but ultimately the entity would identify and prioritise the SRROs that could affect its prospect.
As such, the integration of sustainability begins with the entity identifying the sustainability practices that address the identified and materially assessed SRROs. Then, the entity must first update its Risk Register to include all the identified and materially assessed sustainability related risks. By doing this it would have acknowledged that they are part of the risks that it will now have to deal with and manage, going forward. If after Phase Two, an entity has not updated its Risk Register to include sustainability related risks, then there is outstanding work to be done. These form part of the risks to be integrated in the entity’s wider Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework. The ERM is a Phase Three document, and so it will be covered in future series.
Let us now focus on the sustainability practices to address the identified and materially assessed sustainability related risks. The implementation of IFRS S1 and S2 should embed sustainability practices within an entity’s operation, but this is not always the case, especially when implementation has been approached from a regulatory compliance perspective. The starting point in addressing the identified sustainability related risks is for the entity to come up with sustainability practices that will help manage these risks.
By instituting practices that address the SRRO, sustainability disclosures will now be about an entity’s sustainability practices. Such practices can be articulated in a document called its Sustainability Practices Framework or Policy. The implementation of IFRS S1 and S2 should result in the production of this Framework or Policy. Let us take the example of a brewery where the industry guidance shows that water is a sustainability risk facing that industry. Having identified and materially assessed this risk, then the question would be what practice the entity is putting in place to manage water. This would then form part of what is contained in the Sustainability Practices Framework or Policy.
Energy management is a material sustainability risk in the hotel business, hence the practices an entity in this industry puts in place to manage energy are part of its sustainability practices. In the financial sector, integration of ESG in credit analysis and investment management is a sustainability risk. What practices a financial institution has put in place to address this forms part of what is captured in its Sustainability Practices Framework or Policy. We can go on and on. You can now understand why identification and materiality assessment holds the key to the integration of sustainability practices in an entity’s operation.
The above explains why IFRS S2 requires the disclosure of certain industry specific metrics as a way of measuring performance on sustainability practices. That is why IFRS S2 will require an entity, for instance, in the food and beverage industry to disclose its energy management practices through metrics like (1) operational energy consumed, (2) percentage grid electricity, and (3) percentage renewable and water management practices through other metrics like (1) total water withdrawn, (2) total water consumed; percentage of each in regions with High or Extremely High Baseline Water Stress. Sustainability practices are what lead to reduction in energy and water consumption, thereby mitigating their impacts on the environment.
Evidence from the field shows that what I have stated above about a Sustainability Practices Framework or Policy is challenged, and I want to dwell a little bit on this. The first challenge stems from the fact that the FRC documentation does not require an entity to submit a Sustainability Practices Framework or Policy. Rather, what FRC requires in Phase Two is a Sustainability Disclosure Policy, and this is understandable since FRC’s focus is on reporting and disclosures, which are its mandate.
During implementation, some entities show that they have ESG or Sustainability Policy or Framework, and when one looks at these, one discovers that they are full of aspirational statements such as: “we believe the environment should be good for all,” “we will ensure we cause no damage to people and the environment and will work harmoniously with communities where we operate,” etc. In all, we see genuine intentions to evolve sustainability practices by these entities, but the missing link is evolving actual practices that address the identified and materially assessed sustainability-related risks, as opposed to just crafting aspirational statements.
Another challenge is that the existing ESG or Sustainability Framework or Policy serves different purposes and does not always mean the same thing from one entity to another. In one entity, it may contain those aspirational statements and embed the entity’s ERM and list of operational and conventional risks the entity is managing. In others, it tends towards a disclosure framework and risk governance structure. Thus, existing ESG or Sustainability Framework or Policy does not strictly address Sustainability Practices deployed to manage identified and materially assessed SRRO.
However, there are some entities in the financial sector that have done very well in articulating practices around how ESG has been integrated into their credit analysis following sustainable banking principles, but limitations still exist as these do not address financed emission, which is understandable. Similarly in other sectors, sustainability practices to manage sustainability risks are in place. In all, they do not always address all identified SRROs which IFRS S1 and S2 implementation will trigger.
Where the entity is now asked to produce the right Sustainability Practices Framework or Policy in line with the exigencies of IFRS S1 and S2 implementation, the challenge becomes the fact that it is not part of what FRC has specified, leaving it at the discretion of the entity to produce as an internal document. Yet, it is advisable for entities to still produce Sustainability Practices Frameworks or Policies, as if it is part of what should be submitted to FRC, even if they are internal documents, as these mark the beginning of embedding sustainability practices within the operation of the entities.
In a future amendment of the Sustainability Reporting Guideline (SRG Two), we will advocate for FRC to include Sustainability Practices Framework or Policy as an additional document to be submitted to it. Sustainability Practices should speak to a Sustainability Strategy to present an overall picture of how an entity is responding to or plans to respond to Sustainability Related Risks and Opportunities. In this lies the integration of sustainability practices into an entity’s operation and a change in business behaviour, since practices are bound to change behaviour.
Innocent Okwuosa is the immediate past chair, NIRC; the 59th president of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria, and an adjunct associate professor at Pan Atlantic University, Lekki, Lagos.

title: Latin America has vast potentials to expand coop. with Iran
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 28 (MNA) – Iran’s ambassador to Mexico has emphasized that Latin American countries have vast and extensive potentials and capacities to expand their relations with Iran in all areas.
Emphasizing the extensive potential of Latin American countries for expanding relations with Iran, the Iranian ambassador to Mexico stated that the affinity between the nations of this region and Iranian people presents a favorable opportunity for developing cooperation.
Speaking via a video link to the specialized seminar titled "Prospects for Cultural-Media Cooperation between Iran and Latin America"—organized by the Khayyam International Cultural-Media Foundation at the Tehran Municipality, the envoy highlighted the strategic importance of Latin America in Iran’s foreign policy.
He noted that the potential of this region, particularly in the realms of culture, media, and inter-nation communication, has not received the attention it deserves, and that further planning is required to effectively capitalize on these opportunities.
Pointing to the historical experience of Latin American nations in dealing with United States policies, he noted that some of these nations have suffered as a result of U.S. policies.
This very fact could provide a suitable foundation for mutual understanding and the expansion of relations with the Islamic Republic of Iran, he underlined.
Pointing to Mexico’s population of approximately 130 million and its economic potential, the Iranian ambassador emphasized the need to identify new markets for Iranian products, adding that items such as Iranian saffron could serve as an avenue for expanding exports to that country.

title: FG kicks off $100m Southeast gas pipeline project
body: …As SEDC seals deal with GasSync, commits $3m .. Tinubu says S’East must rise from potential to reality …Mbah, governors hail Tinubu, pledge support for 400km pipeline The Federal Government, through the South East Development Commission (SEDC) has kicked off a $100 million gas distribution pipeline project to boost industrialisation, attract investments and create jobs in the South East. The 400-kilometre pipeline, designed to connect gas resources to industrial and commercial centres across Enugu, Anambra, Imo, Abia and Ebonyi states, has about 150 potential customers identified, with projected demand of 254 million standard cubic feet of gas per day. The investment agreement for the project was signed on Tuesday at the South-East Gas Infrastructure Investment and Project Development Ceremony held at Hotel Presidential, Enugu, marking a significant step towards establishing a regional gas distribution network. Tinubu, represented by the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, described the project as a strategic investment that would connect the region’s natural gas resources to industries, strengthen manufacturing and unlock economic opportunities across the five states. “The Southeast’s entrepreneurial spirit is one of Nigeria’s greatest economic assets. I have always believed that the prosperity of the Southeast is inseparable from the prosperity of Nigeria,” the President said. He said the project aligned with his administration’s commitment to building an integrated regional economy, stressing that gas infrastructure should support industrial development across state boundaries rather than serve isolated markets. “Gas infrastructure must therefore serve industries and markets, not stop at political boundaries. That is the economic logic of regional integration,” he said. The President said the pipeline would benefit manufacturers in Aba, strengthen industrial clusters in Nnewi and Onitsha, attract productive enterprises to Enugu, expand agro-processing and manufacturing in Ebonyi and connect Imo’s gas resources to the wider regional economy. He, however, said the ambition extended beyond supplying existing factories to creating the conditions for new industries, industrial parks and investments that had stalled because of unreliable energy supply. “Our ambition is not simply to deliver gas to existing factories. It is to make possible factories that do not yet exist, industrial parks yet to be developed, and investments that have remained on the drawing board because reliable energy was unavailable,” Tinubu said. He described the South-East Development Commission (SEDC) as an institution established to deliver measurable development outcomes, urging it to assess its performance by the investments it mobilised, infrastructure it enabled, opportunities it created and lives it improved. The President said the South-East Vision 2050 development framework, supported by Vice-President Kashim Shettima and the governors of the region, provided a foundation for coordinated economic growth. He also cited his approval of the South-East Investment Company as part of efforts to attract private capital into strategic development projects, noting that governments could not finance every development ambition from public funds. “This is the model I expect from our development institutions: identify strategic economic opportunities, prepare credible projects, commit public resources responsibly and mobilise private capital at a scale government budgets alone cannot achieve,” he said. Tinubu commended the SEDC for committing $3 million to the gas project and establishing a framework to mobilise additional investments from state governments, institutions and private investors. He said the project’s initial phase required approximately $100 million, describing the partnership between public institutions and private investors as essential to developing sustainable infrastructure. “We are not investing in pipelines for their own sake. We are investing in the industries, businesses and jobs those pipelines will make possible,” the President said. He urged the commission and its partners to uphold commercial discipline, transparency, environmental responsibility, community engagement and the highest safety standards throughout the project’s implementation. “The true measure of government’s commitment is not what we promise, but what we deliver,” he said, expressing optimism that the investment would help create an industrial economy capable of competing in African and global markets. Tinubu said the ultimate objective was to translate the region’s natural resources into productive economic activity, employment and improved living standards. “Let the gas beneath our soil power our industries. Let that energy become production. Let production become employment. Let employment become prosperity for our people,” he said. The President urged the SEDC, state governments and project partners to establish clear implementation timelines, measurable milestones and regular progress reports, stressing that the project’s success would ultimately be measured by its ability to attract investments, revive industries, create jobs and improve the economic fortunes of people across the five Southeast states. Enugu State Governor, Dr. Peter Mbah, commended Tinubu for establishing the SEDC, describing the commission as the institutional vehicle needed to realise the Southeast’s longstanding industrialisation aspirations. “Tinubu loves the Igbo. The SEDC is a commission whose time has come. It was an idea conceived many decades ago, but it took President Tinubu to establish this long-awaited dream of industrialisation of the Southeast,” Mbah said. He described the signing of the investment agreement as the commencement of the investment process, adding that the initiative would help realise the region’s aspiration for a common market and coordinated industrial development. “What we have just signed here today is an investment agreement, meaning that investment has commenced,” he said. Mbah, who said he was excited that the project was advancing less than 13 months after he publicly advocated the idea, praised the commission for adopting an innovative financing model that brings governments and private investors together. He said the project would create opportunities for young people to build their futures in the Southeast rather than migrate to other parts of the country in search of jobs. “Before now, it was our young people running out of the region in search of greener pastures. But with what we have now, our young people can sit back and find their future here in the region. This is all thanks to President Tinubu,” he said. The governor assured the SEDC and its partners that the Southeast governors were committed to the pipeline project, promising to expedite right-of-way arrangements and environmental impact assessment approvals. “We, the Southeast governors, are committed to this. We will ensure that the right of way and EIA are given accelerated approval,” he said. Imo State Deputy Governor Lady Chinyere Ekomaru, who represented Governor Hope Uzodimma, commended Tinubu and the SEDC for initiating the project, noting that Imo’s substantial natural gas resources placed the state in a strategic position to benefit. She said the project was coming at an opportune time, particularly as companies were seeking to become offtakers of gas from the Assa North–Ohaji South development. Ekomaru urged residents to consider the Federal Government’s infrastructure investments in the Southeast in making their political choices ahead of the 2027 general elections. “A vote for APC is a direct vote for the continuation of this project. A bird in hand is worth more than 10 in the bush. Let’s reason wisely,” she said. Anambra State Deputy Governor Dr Onyekachukwu Ibezim, representing Governor Chukwuma Soludo, commended the commission but stressed that its success would ultimately be determined by its impact on the people. “We will clap for you when we begin to feel the impact of what you are doing,” he said. Ibezim noted that states across the region had gas resources that could support industrial growth if properly developed. He urged communities along the pipeline route to embrace the project and cooperate with its promoters. “I want to urge the communities through which the pipelines will pass to have a buy-in. We are strongly behind the commission,” he said, while commending the enthusiasm shown by industrialists at the event. Ebonyi State Deputy Governor Mrs Patricia Obila, representing Governor Francis Nwifuru, described energy as fundamental to industrial growth, lamenting that inadequate power supply had contributed to the decline of several enterprises in the region. “Energy is power. Its importance cannot be overemphasised. With it, factories will produce, the economy will blossom and employment will be great,” she said. Obila expressed the Ebonyi government’s readiness to support the project, promising to provide the necessary cooperation to facilitate its implementation and help moribund companies resume operations. “We will give you all the support needed to operate in Ebonyi to ensure that our moribund companies return back to operations,” she said. Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Regional Development, Dr Mary Ogbe, said the SEDC was developing initiatives capable of improving living standards across the Southeast. She assured the governors that the commission would complement their development efforts rather than compete with them, while urging investors to take advantage of the opportunities emerging from the project. Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of SEDC, Mark Okoye, said the commission had conducted technical, financial and legal due diligence before committing funds to the project, which received approval from its governing board. Okoye said the commission was targeting aggregate regional investment participation of up to $30 million, including its initial $3 million commitment, as part of efforts to mobilise the private capital required to advance the project. He said the initiative aligned with the commission’s industrialisation programme and its commitment to developing infrastructure that would benefit the entire region. Representing GasSync, the project promoter, Callistus Mba said the pipeline would connect gas resources close to the Southeast to industrial users across the five states, reducing dependence on the expensive transportation of compressed natural gas (CNG) and liquefied natural gas (LNG) by road. Mba said the proposed network would originate from the Ohaji area of Imo State, run through Owerri and branch towards Aba in Abia State and Onitsha in Anambra State, with extensions to Enugu and Ebonyi. He said the company planned to begin construction at two points simultaneously to accelerate delivery, following concerns raised by Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah that constructing the entire network sequentially from Imo could delay gas supply to other states. “We are going to start at Ohaji and Onitsha at the same time,” Mba said, explaining that the approach would allow construction towards Enugu and Ebonyi to progress alongside work on the Imo and Anambra sections. He said the company had identified about 150 prospective customers across the region and was engaging industries to secure demand for the gas, including manufacturing companies, power-generation facilities and agro-processing businesses. Mba cited Geometric Power in Abia State among the companies with which engagement was already underway. He added that the pipeline would support efforts to revive moribund industries in Enugu and develop agro-processing facilities in Ebonyi. On the project timeline, he said procurement activities had commenced, funding arrangements were advancing towards financial close, and preparations for engineering, procurement and construction were progressing. “We intend to start construction in the first quarter of 2027,” Mba said, projecting that the project would be ready for first gas delivery in the second quarter of 2028, subject to the completion of the necessary requirements. He identified regulatory approvals, right-of-way arrangements, community engagement and coordination among federal and state authorities as critical to meeting the schedule, urging the governors and relevant institutions to facilitate permits and work with host communities along the pipeline route. The post FG kicks off $100m Southeast gas pipeline project appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Tehran quadrilateral meeting paved way for regional dialogue
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 28 (MNA) – Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the quadripartite Tehran meeting created an opportunity to advance dialogue on regional peace and security and joint efforts against shared threats, with agreement to continue talks.
Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi said the recent Tehran meeting involving Iran, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey provided a valuable opportunity to advance dialogue on regional peace and security and joint efforts against threats and challenges. He described the agreement to continue consultations as a significant step.
In a message posted on Instagram, Araghchi said turning this opportunity into sustainable cooperation requires agreement on principles, trust-building, mutual respect for the sovereignty of states and practical commitments.
From the Islamic Republic of Iran's perspective, he said, sustainable security must be provided with the participation of regional countries and without the military presence and interference of extra-regional powers.
He said this approach is based on regional countries taking responsibility for determining their own destiny.
Countering the evil and aggression of the Zionist regime is, in the same framework, a fundamental necessity for defending the independence and sovereignty of states and preventing the expansion of war, Araghchi said, adding that Iran's neighbors are its priority.

title: European Central Bank Expected to Hold Interest Rates at 2.5%
body: The European Central Bank (ECB) is expected to keep its key deposit rate unchanged at 2.5% at its meeting on Thursday, 29 October 2026, as conflicting economic forces complicate the outlook for inflation and monetary policy across the eurozone. The ECB raised interest rates twice in 2026, by 25 basis points in June and another 25 basis points in September, in response to soaring energy prices triggered by the war in the Middle East and inflation exceeding its 2% target. The latest energy shock pushed eurozone inflation to 3.8% in September, up from 2.1% in February, when the United States and Israel began attacks on Iran. Energy prices drive inflation higher So far, higher energy costs have passed through to the prices of other goods and services to a limited extent. Energy prices rose by 18.9% year on year in September, compared with a 3.1% decline in February. Service prices increased by 3.5%, up from 3.3% over the same period. Core inflation, which excludes energy and food prices, edged up to 2.5% from 2.4%. However, economists expect core inflation to rise further as businesses gradually lose their ability to absorb higher energy costs without passing them on to consumers. Eurozone economy faces weaker demand The eurozone economy is in a different position from 2021–2022, when pandemic-related supply chain disruptions and the energy shock following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine coincided with expanding corporate profit margins. Households also held substantial savings accumulated during the pandemic, while government support measures boosted available income. These factors helped drive inflation into double digits. Today, economic demand is considerably weaker, limiting upward pressure on prices. The eurozone economy continues to grow, but at a much slower pace of around 1.2% in the second quarter of 2026. Business investment in artificial intelligence and exports of AI-related products account for a significant share of that growth. Europe’s green transition also supports economic resilience by reducing the impact of high natural gas prices on electricity costs. As a result, the latest inflationary wave is expected to prove considerably milder than the surge in 2021–2022. ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane has indicated that the central bank’s monetary policy response is also likely to be less aggressive. Markets anticipate further rate increases Money markets do not expect the ECB to change interest rates on Thursday, but they anticipate two to three additional increases over the next 12 months. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) expects at least one more increase before the end of 2026. However, the global bond sell-off has pushed yields significantly higher, including across Europe. Higher borrowing costs could weaken demand and reduce the need for further ECB rate increases. Analysts surveyed by Bloomberg expect the ECB to make one final increase, taking the deposit rate to 2.75% in December. Rising bond yields increase borrowing costs for large companies, discouraging them from using capital markets to finance investment projects. They also raise governments’ borrowing costs. ECB officials warn higher bond yields could slow growth In a speech in early October, Lane said September’s inflation figures did not indicate a broad-based and lasting increase in core inflation. He also warned that rising long-term bond yields would slow economic growth and limit the pass-through of higher energy costs more than the ECB had anticipated in September. ECB President Christine Lagarde delivered a similar message to the European Parliament late last month. “Although growth is resilient, long-term interest rates have increased significantly since our last meeting, which will slow growth and limit pass-through (of energy costs) more than anticipated in our September projections,” she said. The ECB therefore faces a delicate balancing act: containing renewed inflationary pressures without further weakening an already subdued eurozone economy.
