title: Bolsonaro arrives in Miami with family after fleeing Brazil
body:
RIO DE JANEIRO, October 28. /TASS/. Flavio Bolsonaro, who lost Brazil’s presidential election, has arrived in Miami with his family after fleeing the country, O Globo newspaper reported, citing sources.
According to the sources, Flavio Bolsonaro was met in Miami by his brother Eduardo Bolsonaro, who allegedly organized the escape in cooperation with US authorities.
The newspaper noted that the last person to contact Bolsonaro before his departure from the country was Rogerio Marinho, the former coordinator of his election campaign. Bolsonaro wrote that he needed to "clear his head" and stopped responding to messages at around 8:00 a.m. local time on Tuesday.
Earlier, CNN Brasil reported, citing sources, that Bolsonaro had fled Brazil despite a court-imposed travel ban. According to the broadcaster, the son of former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro traveled to the United States with his family. The Associated Press later added that the US administration had issued visas to Bolsonaro and his family.

title: Cenpower clears 600 tonnes of waste from Sega Beach
body: Cenpower Generation Ltd says it removed 600 tonnes of waste from Sega Beach during the fourth edition of its annual KIPP Clean Project, highlighting the scale of shoreline pollution. The exercise brought together employees, Kpone residents, the Kpone Katamanso Municipal Assembly, and waste management partners to clean the beach in the Tema Industrial enclave. Cenpower, which owns the Kpone Independent Power Plant (KIPP), launched the project in September 2023 to tackle coastal pollution, protect marine ecosystems and encourage responsible waste disposal. This year’s exercise involved Cenpower Operations (Cenops) and Excelior Solution Services, which supported shoreline cleaning, waste collection, sorting and safe disposal. Cenpower’s Chief Executive, Theophilus Sackey, said protecting the environment required collective action beyond individual businesses’ operations. He warned that waste dumped into the ocean could wash back onto beaches, creating recurring pollution problems for coastal communities. He called for clean-up exercises to be supported by responsible disposal practices and sustained public participation. The Director of Environmental Services at the Kpone Katamanso Municipal Assembly, Freeman George, commended Cenpower for maintaining the initiative. Speaking on behalf of the Municipal Chief Executive, he urged businesses, institutions, and residents to help keep the municipality clean. He stressed that lasting improvements would depend on changes in everyday waste disposal habits. He said environmental cleanliness should be a daily responsibility rather than an activity reserved for organised clean-up exercises. Community members welcomed the initiative and called for continued collaboration to prevent waste from accumulating along the shoreline. Cenops Plant Manager Darlington Ahuble said employee participation helped reinforce environmental awareness and responsible practices. He explained that environmental compliance and cleanliness formed part of the company’s operational responsibilities. He urged employees, partners and neighbouring communities to sustain those efforts beyond the annual exercise. Cenpower’s Director of Legal and Corporate Affairs, Elizabeth Akin-Taylor, also called for greater community involvement in coastal protection. She said local participation could strengthen ownership of environmental initiatives and encourage residents to prevent littering. According to her, the project’s value extended beyond the volume of waste collected. It also offered an opportunity to promote responsible environmental practices and strengthen cooperation among stakeholders. The initiative aligns with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 14, which focuses on conserving oceans, seas and marine resources.

title: ‘How my 5 children died in tricycle-tanker crash’
body: Mansur Muhammad, the father of five children who died after a water tanker rammed into a tricycle conveying them to school in Gombe metropolis, has recounted his final moments with the deceased. The accident occurred Tuesday morning near Kanady Academy, along APC Square in the state capital’s Government Reserved Area (GRA). The deceased were identified as Maryam Mansir Adamu and Usman Mansir Adamu, both Primary Five pupils of Jekadafari Primary School; Hauwau Mansir Adamu of Government Junior Secondary School (GJSS), Jekadafari; Aliyu Mansir Adamu of Government Day Secondary School (GDSS), Ahmadu Gombe; and Fatima Mansir Adamu, whose school was not specified. Three other children were injured in the crash and taken to the hospital for treatment. INEC promises inclusive polls, targets barriers against PWDs Bangkok’s debt debate: Can Africa secure fairer development finance? One of the surviving children, Umar Mansur, an SS1 student, said the tricycle was conveying them to school when it fell, after which the water tanker ran over them. Umar said he sustained an injury to his leg, while five of his siblings died in the accident. The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) Sector Commander in Gombe State, Samson Kaura, confirmed the incident, saying corps personnel arrived at the scene after the initial rescue operation. Kaura said FRSC officials later visited the hospital to ascertain the number of casualties. A source at the Specialist Hospital, Gombe, said the injured victims and the drivers involved in the accident were taken to the Federal Teaching Hospital, Gombe, for medical attention. The bodies of the five deceased children were deposited at the mortuary. Father speaks Speaking after the accident, Mansur said he received a telephone call barely 40 minutes after his children left home for school, informing him that they had been involved in an accident. He said he was asked to rush to the emergency unit of the Federal Teaching Hospital, Gombe, where some of the injured children had been taken. When he arrived at the hospital, he saw two of his children alive but could not find the other five. He later learnt that the bodies of the deceased children had been taken to the Specialist Hospital, Gombe. Mansur said one of the children had given his telephone number to the person who called to inform him about the accident. He said he rushed to the hospital, hoping to find all his children alive, but was devastated when he learnt that five of them had died. “The tricycle rider told me that the other children were at the Specialist Hospital. When I got there, I was directed to the mortuary, where I saw the bodies of my five children laid out in a row,” he said. Mansur said the sight was unbearable, adding that he was the only person allowed to see the bodies because his wives were considered too traumatised to be taken to the mortuary. He said he had been unwell that morning and had a fever, which prevented him from taking the children to school himself. His junior wife, who is the mother of three of the deceased children, therefore contacted a tricycle rider to convey them to school. The children, he recalled, had left home in good spirits, repeatedly telling him, “Abba, we are going to school.” “I kept responding, ‘May Allah grant you success.’ I never knew that was going to be the last time I would see them,” he said. He particularly remembered his son, Usman, who had complained that he did not have a pen to take to school. Mansur said he told the boy that he would not buy him an expensive pen because he frequently misplaced them. Instead, he gave him money to buy a cheaper one. “Usman said, ‘Abba, thank you.’ I did not know that I would never see him again,” he said. The father said the news of the accident nearly made him lose his breath. He added that he was still struggling to come to terms with the loss of five of his children in a single incident. Mansur, who has 12 children from two wives, said only seven remained following the tragedy. “Allah gave them to me, and He has taken them back. I am trying to accept it as a trial from Him,” he said. He added that the children suffered severe head injuries in the crash. Governor mourns victims Gombe State governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, expressed sadness over the deaths, describing the loss of five children from one family as devastating. In a statement issued by his Director-General of Press Affairs, Ismaila Uba Misilli, the governor extended his condolences to the bereaved family and the Jekadafari community. He also prayed for the speedy recovery of the three injured children. The governor urged motorists to obey traffic regulations, maintain safe speeds, avoid dangerous manoeuvres and ensure their vehicles were roadworthy. He also called on drivers to exercise extra caution when transporting schoolchildren. He prayed that Allah would grant the deceased Aljannatul Firdaus and give their family the strength to bear the loss. Meanwhile, relatives and sympathisers gathered at the family’s home in Jekadafari to offer condolences.

title: Agric ministry puts post-harvest loss at $10bn yearly
body: •As 14 of 17 federal silos fail •20% of grains, 70% of fruits, vegetables lost By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA — THE Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Abubakar Kyari, Tuesday, disclosed that Nigeria loses an estimated $10 billion annually to post-harvest losses. Kyari made this known as one of the panelists focusing on the topic ‘Productivity Revolution for Growth’ at the ongoing 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit (NES#32) organised by the Nigerian Economic Summit Group, NESG, in Abuja. He also said Nigeria loses between 15 and 20 per cent of its grains, including rice, maize and millet, while losses involving tomatoes, pepper, onions, fruits and vegetables could reach 60 to 70 per cent, depending on the season. He described the reduction of post-harvest losses as a low-hanging fruit in Nigeria’s food security drive, said the country could significantly improve food availability and farmers’ earnings by addressing weaknesses in storage, processing, transportation and market infrastructure. He stated: “We lose almost about $10 billion annually on post-harvest losses. “About 15 to 20 per cent on grains, and you can see grains that are hard, and you probably think we will not lose much of that, but we lose on grains, on cereal, rice, maize, and so on and so forth, millet. On fruits and vegetables, the minister warned that the scale of waste was considerably higher. “Tomato, pepper, onion, and other fruits and vegetables, we lose some of that as high as 60 to 70 per cent depending on the season”, Kyari said, attributing the vulnerability of tomatoes, in particular, to their short shelf life and the effects of hot weather. The Minister also lamented that 17 of the 33 silo complexes built by the Federal Government had been concessioned to private operators, but only three were performing. “The government had concessioned 17 out of the 33 silos that it had built over a period of time, but I’ll tell you that out of the 17, only three have performed. All the 14 are almost comatose for the past, I believe, since when it was concessioned”, he said. The minister attributed the problem partly to a disconnect between agricultural production centres and the location of storage facilities. According to him, some farming communities are situated more than 100 kilometres from major storage facilities, making it difficult and costly for farmers to transport their produce to the silos. He argued that the country’s storage strategy must be redesigned to reflect the geographical distribution of agricultural production rather than depend exclusively on large-scale facilities located far from farming communities. The minister’s position suggests that the challenge extends beyond the physical availability of silos to questions of accessibility, operational efficiency, commercial viability and the suitability of infrastructure to the needs of farmers. To address the shortcomings, he (Kyari) said the Federal Government was considering smaller, modern community silo systems that could be deployed closer to farming communities. He explained that the proposed facilities would draw inspiration from traditional grain-storage practices, while incorporating modern technology, ventilation and renewable energy. The facilities, he said, could be designed to accommodate capacities of 2,000, 3,000, 5,000 or 10,000 tonnes, depending on the productive capacity of the communities they serve. He said: “We need not only the huge silo systems, but we need community silo systems.” He noted that traditional grain-storage structures, known in Hausa as grumbu, offered a useful starting point for developing storage systems adapted to local conditions. He said the government was exploring modernised versions of such systems, equipped with appropriate ventilation and solar-powered infrastructure. “We have renewable energy that we must take advantage of because we have to have that in our budget”, he said. The proposed approach could reduce the distance farmers travel to store produce, improve access to preservation facilities and help prevent avoidable losses caused by inadequate storage. However, the effectiveness of the initiative will depend on implementation, maintenance, affordability and the ability of farmers and cooperatives to access the facilities when they need them. Beyond post-harvest losses, the Minister said the government’s approach to food security had evolved from its traditional emphasis on the availability, accessibility and affordability of food to include consumption of nutritious and diverse diets. He asserted that food security must be assessed not only by the volume of food produced or available in markets, but also by whether households can consume nutritious food capable of supporting healthy growth, particularly among children. The minister also disclosed that agriculture had assumed a higher level of national coordination, with the Presidential Food Systems Coordinating Unit bringing together relevant sectors, including agriculture, water resources, environment and health, to address interconnected food security and nutrition challenges. The approach recognises that food security is influenced by several factors, including agricultural productivity, water availability, environmental conditions, public health and nutrition. He also noted the fragmented structure of Nigerian agriculture as a major obstacle to improving productivity. He said between 85 and 90 per cent of Nigerian farmers were smallholders, with the average farm size standing at approximately 0.6 hectares, equivalent to 6,000 square metres. title: Iraq seeks joint meeting between Arab states, Iran
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 28 (MNA) – Iraq is consulting six Arab countries and Iran on convening a joint meeting to bolster regional security, the Foreign Ministry said, adding that Baghdad welcomes a meeting between Mecca coalition states and Iran.
Iraq's Foreign Ministry said it has held consultations with the six Arab states of the region and Iran to convene a joint meeting aimed at strengthening regional security.
The ministry said Baghdad welcomes a meeting between the member states of the Mecca Defense Alliance and Iran, as well as ongoing efforts to achieve peace in the region, according to Al-Mayadeen.
The Foreign Ministry also expressed Iraq's support for economic solidarity among regional countries.

title: Netanyahu bloc slips to 55 seats with nearly half the vote counted
body: With just over 41% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud leads with 28 seats, followed by Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar with 21 neither major political bloc is projected to secure a parliamentary majority.   Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party was projected to emerge as the largest faction in the next Kneset early Wednesday, as updated election tallies showed neither of the country's main political blocs securing enough seats to form a government. As of 6:02 a.m. Wednesday, 41.09% of votes had been counted, according to the Central Elections Committee. Based on the latest tallies, Likud was projected to win 28 seats in the 120-member Knesset, while Yashar, the party led by Netanyahu's chief political rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, was projected to secure 21. The predominantly Arab Joint List was projected to become the third-largest faction with 12 seats, followed by Beyachad with 11. United Torah Judaism and Yisrael Beytenu were each projected to win eight seats. The Democrats, the Religious Zionism-Zehut alliance, the far-right Otzma Yehudit party and the ultra-Orthodox Shas party were each projected to secure seven seats. Ra'am, an Islamist party representing Arab Israeli voters, was projected to win four seats. The updated figures put Netanyahu's right-wing and religious bloc at 57 seats, four short of the 61 required for a majority in the Knesset. The rival pro-change bloc was projected to secure 47 seats, while the Arab parties were projected to hold a combined 16 seats. The results leave both Netanyahu and Eisenkot facing significant obstacles to assembling a governing coalition, with the Arab parties potentially holding considerable influence over the next government's formation. The figures remain preliminary, with nearly 59% of ballots yet to be counted as of the latest update. Final seat allocations could change as counting continues, particularly for parties close to the 3.25% electoral threshold.  "Throughout the night, the official results will be updated regularly on the Central Elections Committee's website and interactive results map as vote counting, data processing and verification progress," the committee said. "The figures at this stage are partial and may change as counting and verification continue." Some exit poll results updated According to the updated Channel 12 News exit poll, Likud gained three seats to reach 27, bringing Netanyahu's bloc to 52 seats, compared with 49 for Eisenkot's bloc. The revised projection also shows the Joint List gaining two seats to reach 12, while Yashar! (21), the Democrats (9), Shas (7) and Yisrael Beytenu (7) each lost one seat. Some of Israel's major television channels have updated their exit poll results. The updated Kan 11 exit poll shows the two blocs tied, with 51 seats each for Netanyahu's bloc and Eisenkot's bloc. According to the revised projection, Likud gained two seats to reach 27, while Itamar Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit dropped one seat to six. The Democrats also lost one seat and now stand at nine. According to the updated Channel 13 News exit poll, Likud gained two seats to reach 27, while Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar! party dropped one seat to 22. United Torah Judaism also lost one seat, falling to six. The result is a 51-51 tie between the two blocs, with neither holding a majority. The Arab parties are projected to win a combined 18 seats. Results of first exit polls The first election exit polls released at 10 p.m. pointed to a narrow lead for the bloc seeking to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, but neither side is projected to win the 61 seats needed for a parliamentary majority. While Netanyahu's Likud emerges as the country's largest party, Arab parties are projected to make substantial gains, potentially complicating efforts to form the next government. According to Channel 12's exit poll, the bloc seeking political change wins 52 seats, compared with 50 for Netanyahu's bloc. The two Arab parties secure a combined 18 seats, leaving neither main bloc with an outright majority in the 120-seat Knesset. Channel 13 projected a slightly larger advantage for the change bloc, giving it 53 seats against 50 for Netanyahu's allies. The Arab parties receive 17 seats in that projection. The results represent a significant shift from the final pre-election opinion polls, which had consistently placed Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar! party ahead of Likud. Both exit polls instead put Netanyahu's party in first place, although the broader political balance remains narrowly tilted toward his opponents. The projections are based on surveys of voters and do not constitute official results. The allocation of seats could change as ballots are counted, particularly for parties close to the electoral threshold.   Channel 12: Likud leads with 24 seats, Yashar! follows with 22 Channel 12's exit poll projects Likud as the largest party in the 26th Knesset with 24 seats, followed closely by Eisenkot's Yashar! with 22. Naftali Bennett's Beyachad party is projected to win 12 seats, while the Joint List, an alliance of Arab political parties, reaches 11. The Democrats, led by Yair Golan, and Avigdor Liberman's Yisrael Beytenu each receive nine seats. The Islamist Ra'am party and the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism party are projected to win seven seats apiece.   Shas and the Religious Zionist Party-Zehut alliance each receive six seats. Together, the four main parties seeking to replace Netanyahu hold 52 seats, compared with 50 for the prime minister's political allies. The Joint List and Ra'am account for the remaining 18 seats. Channel 13: Opposition bloc grows to 53 seats Channel 13's exit poll presents a similar picture, although several parties receive different projections. Likud leads with 25 seats, followed by Yashar! with 23. Bennett's Beyachad party wins 14, while the Joint List receives 10 and the Democrats nine.   Yisrael Beytenu is projected to win seven seats, alongside Ra'am and United Torah Judaism, which also receive seven each. Shas and Religious Zionist Party-Zehut are allocated six seats apiece. The overall distribution leaves the change bloc with 53 seats, Netanyahu's bloc with 50 and the Arab parties with 17. Despite the differences between the two surveys, both point to the same central political challenge: neither main bloc has enough parliamentary seats to form a government independently. Arab parties emerge with 17 to 18 seats One of the most striking developments in the exit polls is the increased representation projected for Arab parties. Channel 12 gives the Joint List 11 seats and Ra'am seven, for a combined record total of 18. Channel 13 projects 10 seats for the Joint List and seven for Ra'am, bringing their combined representation to 17. That marks an increase from the final pre-election surveys, which projected 14 seats for the Arab parties on Channel 12 and 16 on Channel 13. The gains could have significant implications for the parliamentary balance. With the two main political blocs separated by just two or three seats, the Arab parties' positions may become an important factor in the political negotiations that follow. However, neither exit poll indicates an outright majority for the bloc seeking to replace Netanyahu, even as it holds a narrow advantage over his allies. Three parties fail to cross the electoral threshold Both exit polls also project that several smaller parties will fail to enter the Knesset. Former IDF general Ofer Winter's nationalist Amcha Yisrael party remains below the 3.25% electoral threshold, as does the Reservists-Economic Party led by former minister Yoaz Hendel and economist Yaron Zelekha. The Haredi Public party, which has attempted to attract ultra-Orthodox voters dissatisfied with the established religious parties, is also projected to fall short. Under Israel's electoral system, parties that fail to secure at least 3.25% of valid votes receive no parliamentary seats. Their votes are excluded from the allocation of seats among qualifying parties, potentially affecting the balance between competing political blocs. With record voter turnout, the absolute number of votes required to cross the threshold is higher than in previous elections. Final results could therefore change if parties finish particularly close to that mark. Record turnout, but the final result could take days The exit polls follow a day of historic voter participation. According to the Central Elections Committee, turnout had reached 74.3% by 8 p.m., the highest rate recorded at that hour since 1988. A total of 5,449,277 Israelis had voted by that point, out of 7,331,981 eligible voters. At the same hour in the November 2022 election, turnout stood at 66.3%. The final distribution of seats may remain uncertain for several days due to the large number of special double-envelope ballots, including votes cast by soldiers, diplomats, hospital patients and voters away from their registered polling stations. More than 650,000 such ballots are expected to require separate verification and counting. Central Elections Committee officials have warned that the process could continue until Friday morning. For parties hovering around the electoral threshold, those votes could be decisive, potentially changing not only their parliamentary representation but also the overall balance between political blocs. Even once the final results become available, Israel's next government will not necessarily be determined. President Isaac Herzog must consult the elected parliamentary factions before assigning a lawmaker the task of forming a coalition. With exit polls showing a divided Knesset and no immediate majority for either main bloc, the central political question remains unresolved: which combination of parties, if any, can secure enough parliamentary support to form Israel's next government?

title: Dmitriev believes proponents of military conflicts will be defeated
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Kirill Dmitriev, Russian presidential special representative for investment and economic cooperation with foreign countries and CEO of the Russian Direct Investment Fund (RDIF), expressed the view that proponents of military conflicts would be defeated.
"She (Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen - TASS) deserves to lose Greenland. Warmongers will lose. Dialogue will prevail," he wrote on X.
He made the remarks in response to criticism from Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, who said that Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store’s phone call with Vladimir Putin had not been coordinated with European allies.

title: Rivers Rainbow Coalition retains Chinda, allocates 33 slots to APC, 15 to PDP
body: The Nyesom Wike-led Rainbow Coalition in Rivers State has confirmed the governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Ogundu Kingsley Chinda, as its candidate, adding that it also shared other National Assembly and State House of Assembly positions between candidates of the APC and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). The PDP is to take the Rivers South-East senatorial district seat, which has Senator Olaka Johnson Nwogu as candidate, along with 14 other national and state assembly candidates for the general election. The Rainbow Coalition—which comprises several political parties in the state, including the PDP, APC, Labour Party (LP), and a faction of the Action Alliance (AA)—also adopted President Bola Ahmed Tinubu of the APC as its sole presidential candidate for the 2027 general election. Daily Trust reports that no candidate from the AA or Labour Party made the list of preferred candidates unveiled by the coalition, despite both parties being members of the alliance. Speaking at the official unveiling of the coalition’s candidates held at the Yakubu Gowon Stadium in Elekahia, Port Harcourt, the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, rallied political leaders and candidates across various parties in Rivers State behind President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. Wike said the event, which brought together Rivers State Governor Sir Siminalayi Fubara, political leaders, and candidates under the coalition’s platform, was designed to unite political interests in Rivers State around a common objective. He insisted that party differences should not prevent leaders from working together to advance the state’s interests and support Tinubu’s second-term ambition. He urged PDP members in Rivers, Kwara, Benue, Ondo, Ogun, and other states to rally behind the President. Wike maintained that the Rainbow Coalition offered a platform for politicians from different parties to work together in support of Tinubu and candidates endorsed by the alliance in Rivers State. Urging political stakeholders to avoid actions capable of reigniting tension, he added that the coalition remains committed to maintaining peace. The minister also expressed appreciation to Governor Fubara for personally attending the event and unveiling the candidates, describing the governor as a member of the coalition’s political family. Speaking before unveiling the candidates, Governor Fubara described the gathering as an opportunity to reunite political allies and work toward the development of Rivers State. Fubara acknowledged Wike’s role in his political journey, expressing appreciation for the support he received from the former governor and other leaders. He pledged to work toward victory for Tinubu and to ensure that political power remains within the bloc represented by the coalition. Speaking on behalf of candidates across the participating political parties, APC governorship candidate Kingsley Chinda said the coalition is seeking to move Rivers State away from divisive party politics toward a model of collective leadership.

title: INEC promises inclusive polls, targets barriers against PWDs
body: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has reiterated its determination to dismantle systemic and physical barriers that have disenfranchised or marginalised Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) at the grassroots before the 2027 general elections. The Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Kogi State, Dr. Shehu Wahab, disclosed this in Lokoja on Tuesday at a state-level sensitisation workshop on disability interventions for PWDs, electoral officers, and disability desk officers. Dr. Wahab stated that INEC remains firmly dedicated to the core democratic principle that elections must be free, fair, credible, and inclusive. He stressed that democracy thrives only when every eligible citizen, regardless of physical, sensory, or cognitive ability, has unfettered access to exercise their civic franchise. “Against this backdrop,” he said, “the commission is out to address real challenges and systematically dismantle those barriers faced by PWDs at the grassroots before the 2027 general election.” He noted that the workshop was specifically designed to bridge the gap between policy formulation at headquarters and practical implementation at the grassroots. “Today, we are not only reviewing INEC’s comprehensive Policy on Disability Inclusion and accessibility guidelines, but we are also focusing on the operational deployment and effective usage of assistive devices, such as magnifying glasses, Braille ballots, and PWD posters. “We recognise that the commission cannot achieve total inclusion in isolation. We deeply value our ongoing partnership with Organisations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs), civil society groups, and agencies like the National Orientation Agency (NOA). “Your feedback, advocacy, and collaborative spirit are vital in helping us identify blind spots, correct operational lapses, and build public trust,” he said. In his remarks, the state Chairman of the Joint National Association of Persons with Disabilities, Ibrahim Arome Daniel, noted that members have been suffering from the non-inclusive practices of the past, particularly those in the blind, deaf, and spinal cord injury clusters. Represented by the Secretary of the association, Ahmed Abdulkareem Onimisi, the chairman commended the inclusive posture of the current leadership of the commission, which is tailored to ensure members exercise their civic rights in the coming general elections. Meanwhile, the state Director of the National Orientation Agency (NOA), Ayedime Aleku, advised prospective voters to collect their PVCs at INEC offices located in the headquarters of the 21 local government areas. Aleku urged PWDs to speak openly at the workshop to enable the commission to resolve challenges or barriers preventing them from exercising their civic responsibility during the 2027 general election.

title: Tackle hardship now, Osinbajo charges leaders
body: Former Vice President, Professor Yemi Osinbajo, has charged African leaders to tackle the challenges of hardship, hunger, and economic emancipation facing their people. Professor Osinbajo gave the charge on Tuesday in Yola while delivering a public lecture titled “Democracy and Development: The Imperative of People-Centred Governance” as part of activities marking the 59th birthday of Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri of Adamawa State. Professor Osinbajo stressed that governance must go beyond occupying public office. In his view, leadership is most meaningful when it responds to the needs of the people, promotes accountability, strengthens unity, and creates opportunities for citizens to live better lives. He commended Governor Fintiri for his leadership and development efforts in Adamawa, noting that the governor’s profile and accomplishments had attracted attention beyond the state. According to him, the value of leadership is ultimately measured by its impact on people and the lasting contributions it makes to society. The Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin, who attended as the special guest of honour, spoke on the importance of effective communication between the government and the people. Jibrin observed that open communication helps build mutual understanding, strengthens public confidence, and allows citizens to better appreciate government policies and programmes. He commended Governor Fintiri’s efforts in developing Adamawa State’s infrastructure and urged residents to continue supporting initiatives that would move the state forward. Governor Fintiri expressed gratitude to Almighty Allah for the gift of life and the opportunity to serve the people of Adamawa State in different capacities. One of the significant announcements of the occasion was the governor’s plan to establish the Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri Foundation after leaving office. According to the governor, the foundation will sustain his commitment to helping the less privileged through scholarships and other forms of assistance for vulnerable members of society.

title: Vote-buying: NDC weighs rules to distinguish transport payments from electoral inducement
body: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) is weighing rules to determine when money given to delegates for transport becomes an electoral inducement. Former Tamale Central MP Inusah Fuseini says proposed constitutional changes must address payments that exceed reasonable travel costs, even when candidates describe them as transport support. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, he said the party needed clear standards for acceptable payments. “How much money can we say is appropriate in the circumstances? If somebody gives a delegate GH¢200, is it an inducement or what is it?” His comments follow reports of widespread alleged vote-buying during the NDC’s latest constituency executive elections. Mr Fuseini said declaring the purpose of a payment did not resolve the question. The amount could still exceed what a delegate reasonably needed for transportation. The committee reviewing the party’s constitution is examining how to handle such cases. It must also establish which party body can investigate complaints and impose sanctions. “So we need a framework.” Mr Fuseini said the committee had recognised the need for sanctions after acknowledging that inducement had occurred in the elections. But it found “there was no legal mechanism in our constitution to deal with that”. He explained that this gap could expose disciplinary decisions to challenges. The party needed rules that define misconduct and give its institutions authority to act. One option is to empower constituency councils of elders to handle cases locally. Another is referring offenders to the national headquarters, where the Functional Executive Committee would act. The party would further review the proposals before presenting them to a special congress for constitutional amendment. “So yes, it’s a work in progress.” Mr Fuseini also warned that the growing financial demands of politics were excluding women, young people and people with integrity. Some potential candidates lacked the resources to compete. Others were withdrawing from politics because of the sums involved. He said heavy spending also pressured politicians to recoup their money after winning office. “A politician is not an NGO, and so when people spend that amount of money, they expect to recoup that, and that fuels corruption on a national scale.”

title: US warns Gulf states of possible military action after November 3 — WSJ
body:
NEW YORK, October 28. /TASS/. The United States has warned several Persian Gulf countries of a possible "short, intense military campaign" against Iran following the November 3 midterm congressional elections, The Wall Street Journal (WSJ) reported, citing sources.
According to the report, the Pentagon has evacuated US military personnel from Middle Eastern bases where they could be at risk, US forces in the region are replenishing their ammunition stockpiles, and bombers and fighter jets are preparing to carry out strikes.
The Wall Street Journal reported that US President Donald Trump has not yet made a final decision on resuming military operations but is leaning toward launching a large-scale attack after the elections, potentially targeting Iranian infrastructure and nuclear facilities.
The US and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28. In June, Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding providing for an immediate cessation of hostilities on all fronts, including in Lebanon. However, on the night of July 8, the US resumed large-scale strikes against Iran, accusing Tehran of violating the terms of the agreements concerning the Strait of Hormuz. Approximately 25% of global oil trade and around 20% of global liquefied natural gas trade pass through the strait. The US administration subsequently effectively signaled an end to the use of large-scale military force against Iran and a shift toward attempting to economically strangle the country through sanctions.

title: Miners’ deaths: Panel recommends summary dismissal, prosecution of NSCDC officers, N1.4bn for victims
body: •Says overcrowding, heat stress, dehydration caused deaths •Rules out use of chemicals; as FG vows justice By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA—An independent ministerial committee has recommended summary dismissal, administrative sanctions and prosecution of some officers of the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps, NSCDC, over the deaths of 33 detainees in the custody of its Niger State command in Minna, along with N1.4 billion in compensation for victims and survivors. The committee’s chairman, Jonathan Kure, who presented the report to the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, in Abuja, yesterday, described the deaths as “entirely preventable.” Kure said the committee concluded that the incident was a preventable custodial tragedy, caused by severe overcrowding, unlawful and unsuitable detention conditions, failure of duty of care, disregard of repeated distress warnings, inadequate supervision, and wider systemic deficiencies. He said the evidence did not support claims that the deaths resulted from a disease outbreak. According to him, “available medical and forensic evidence instead indicated that the fatalities resulted from an environmental asphyxia, an acute respiratory failure caused by prolonged confinement in a severely overcrowded and poorly ventilated detention cell, aggravated by heat stress and dehydration.” The 65-page report, of which 46 pages form the main body, examined the arrest, detention, treatment and deaths of detainees between September 15 and 17, 2026. It was commissioned by the minister, following a presidential directive. The committee said the tragedy stemmed from enforcement operations against suspected illegal mining in and around Minna. No headquarter’s approval Kure said: “The operation was undertaken without an approved operational order, proper planning and consultation with relevant mining authorities, or involvement of the specialised Mining Marshals unit. National headquarters was not informed before the operation commenced,” he added. He said the raids led to the arrest of men, women and children, and that by the evening of September 16, 75 persons had been detained. He said after one release, 74 remained in custody overnight, with about 50 male detainees confined in a cell measuring about 20 square metres. The committee said the cell had “a solid metal door, inadequate airflow, no running water, poor lighting, and no functioning toilet.” It said food and drinking water were either unavailable or grossly inadequate, adding that adults and minors were held together. It found that the conditions breached constitutional safeguards, the Administration of Criminal Justice Act, the Child Rights Act and accepted international standards. The committee concluded that they “amounted to cruel, inhuman, and degrading treatment, and created an environment, in which fatalities became foreseeable and preventable.” Kure said signs of distress began shortly after 7pm on September 16 and continued through the night. “Detainees repeatedly banged on cell doors and walls, shouted for assistance, and pleaded for water,” he said. “These distress calls were heard by officers assigned to nearby duties,” he said. He said medical personnel had earlier raised concerns about poor ventilation and the risk of suffocation, but “were not acted upon.” Officers, he said, “failed to open the cell, decongest the facility, or arrange emergency intervention.” The deaths occurred inside the male cell between 8pm on September 16 and 7am on September 17, 2026. “By the time the cell was opened, many detainees had died,” Kure said. The committee authenticated 33 deaths, 14 of them minors, and identified 41 survivors, adding that the higher figures reported immediately after the incident “could not be reconciled with available records and identified victims.” Though some survivors alleged that an aerosol substance was sprayed into the cell before the deaths, Kure said the committee found no evidence to support this claim and concluded that the allegation remained unproven on the available evidence. The committee held individual officers responsible, stressing that the State Commandant, Suberu Siaka, authorised and supervised the operation without proper planning, approval or oversight, giving rise to overcrowding. It said the Head of the Investigation Unit, T. S. Sodiq, facilitated unlawful detention practices, ignored legal and medical concerns, and failed to act, despite direct awareness of the deteriorating conditions. SC Usman Ndamaka was accused of maintaining overcrowded conditions, instructing subordinates not to open the cell, failing to respond to emergency alerts, and taking part in the cleaning and alteration of the detention area before independent examination. The committee said ASC I Hassan Mohammed failed to open the cell, despite repeated distress signals and did not adequately escalate the emergency, while DSC Abubakar Dabang profiled the suspects into detention, including minors, and failed to protect their rights and properly document exhibits. It said DSC Musa Marafat unlawfully arrested and detained Emmanuel Emeka over a civil debt dispute unrelated to mining, contributing directly to his continued unlawful detention until his death. Beyond individual misconduct, it identified institutional weaknesses in the NSCDC, including “inadequate detention infrastructure, lack of effective custodial oversight, absence of CCTV monitoring systems, weak documentation practices, poor emergency medical capability, ineffective supervision, weak intelligence reporting arrangements, workforce imbalance, and chronic underfunding.” It said these deficiencies created an environment in which serious violations occurred and “would continue to occur without timely detention intervention.” Committee listed limitations. The detention register for 16th September 2026 was unavailable, 30 of the 33 deceased were buried before post-mortem examinations, and the detention area was cleaned, disinfected and altered before independent forensic investigators arrived. It nonetheless concluded that “sufficient evidence existed to establish the essential facts, causes, and responsibilities.” On accountability, the committee recommended “summary dismissal of officers found primarily responsible; prosecution for offences, including murder, criminal negligence, torture, and inhuman treatment where applicable; as well as investigation by anti-corruption agencies into allegations of extortion and exhibit mismanagement.” It also recommended administrative sanctions for officers whose failures contributed to the incident but “did not amount to primary culpability.” On compensation, the committee recommended N30 million for each of the 33 bereaved families and N10 million for each of the 41 survivors, totalling N1.4 billion. It also recommended educational support for dependents of the deceased, medical rehabilitation for survivors, psychological support for affected families, and a formal apology by the federal government. To prevent a recurrence, it recommended construction of standard detention facilities across all NSCDC commands, installation of closed-circuit television, CCTV, systems in custodial areas, an independent inspectorate and custodial oversight mechanism, enhanced custodial management and human rights training, among others. Kure appealed for political will to ensure the recommendations were brought to implementation.” FG vows justice Receiving the report, the Minister, Tunji-Ojo, said: “I want to assure you, nothing will be swept under the carpet.” He recalled that after the committee’s inauguration, he went to see President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, “and I never saw him more passionate about justice than that day. The era of setting up committees just to downplay tension is not now.’’ He said the 10-member committee was carefully chosen, adding that none of the members was appointee of government. He said there would be “a complete review” of the NSCDC, as the government had done in the Nigeria Immigration Service, and Correctional Service and the Fire Service. He said: “A single bad apple shouldn’t describe the apple tree. But, of course, of those that have goofed, there will be repercussions.” The minister said officers who concealed or doctored evidence must be suspended with immediate effect, pending internal investigation and other disciplinary action. “You cannot destroy evidence in a case where we lost 30-something people. That is wickedness,” he said. Tunji-Ojo said the report would be forwarded to the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice for judicial action where necessary. He added that the ministry would work with the NSCDC to ensure “that a body, an agency set up to protect Nigerians does not end up hurting Nigerians. “To the families of the deceased, we want to assure you, this government will never leave you alone. We will make sure justice is done to serve the memory of the lost ones.” The post Miners’ deaths: Panel recommends summary dismissal, prosecution of NSCDC officers, N1.4bn for victims appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Senanu questions NDC’s commitment to tackling vote-buying
body: Anti-corruption campaigner Edem Senanu has criticised the National Democratic Congress (NDC) leadership for what he considers an inadequate response to allegations of vote-buying during the party’s recent constituency executive elections, warning that the handling of the matter risks damaging the party’s image and ethical standing. He said the party should demonstrate accountability by committing to investigate credible allegations, rather than appearing to suggest that action would depend on evidence supplied by its own members. Mr Senanu made the comments on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, October 27, in reaction to remarks by the NDC National Deputy General Secretary, Rashid Tanko, on the controversy surrounding the internal elections. “I find [Rashid] Tanko’s response challenging and not demonstrating adequate leadership in terms of accountability,” he said. Mr Senanu argued that responsible party leadership should welcome evidence of possible wrongdoing from any source and take steps to establish the facts, irrespective of whether the information came from within or outside the party. He said the suggestion that the party needed evidence from its own people before being satisfied that vote-buying had occurred was troubling and could undermine efforts to address the practice. “That kind of implication, that trajectory does not carry us all along. We won’t get you the results you want,” he said. Timing of gifts raises questions Mr Senanu said the timing of the distribution of items, including television sets, during the constituency elections raised questions about the intentions behind the gifts. He explained that vote-buying involved the provision of an inducement by a political party, candidate or representative with the intention of securing the recipient’s vote. “In this context, you cannot tell me that these TVs and what have you were flying a month ago. They were happening at the exact time. So the intention of what they wanted to achieve is there,” he said. He maintained that whether candidates who distributed the items eventually won or lost was not the central issue. “Whether they won or not is not material,” he said. According to him, the timing of the alleged distribution was an important consideration in determining whether the items were intended to influence delegates’ choices. “The extent that these things were being given at that time tells us there was a clear intention to harvest votes,” he said. The claims, however, require proper investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the distribution of the items and whether they were intended to influence voting decisions. Calls for prompt investigation Mr Senanu said the absence of a sufficiently firm response from the party leadership, nearly 48 hours after the issue was raised, was worrying and risked conveying the impression that the allegations were not being treated with the seriousness they deserved. He said the party’s reputation could suffer even if the evidence did not come from its own members. “If it’s not your own people who are providing the evidence, but it’s available, it taints the image. It reduces the ethical standards of the party,” he said. He called on the leadership to adopt a more proactive approach by inviting anyone with relevant information to submit it and then initiating an investigation. “I would rather leadership say that we haven’t seen it, but please provide it. We will immediately ensure that we look into the matter,” he said. Mr Senanu said such a response would demonstrate a commitment to accountability and reassure members and the public that the party was prepared to confront allegations of wrongdoing within its ranks. “That’s the way that we demonstrate responsiveness and accountable leadership,” he added. He expressed concern that the passage of time without a clear response suggested the party might not fully appreciate the seriousness of the matter. “Forty-eight hours after, and we still haven’t seen, we haven’t heard. That is very worrying. It does not show a sensitivity to the fact that this is a very important issue, and it suggests that the party itself is not taking this as serious enough,” he said. Electoral integrity at stake The controversy has renewed attention on the role of money and gifts in internal party elections, where candidates compete for positions that influence party organisation and leadership. Mr Senanu’s argument is that the integrity of such contests must be protected regardless of whether the alleged inducements change the final outcome. A credible response, he said, requires party officials to examine the available evidence, explain their actions and demonstrate that rules on electoral conduct are taken seriously. The NDC’s handling of the allegations is therefore likely to be judged not only by the findings of any investigation but also by how promptly and transparently the party responds to concerns about its internal democratic processes.

title: Bolsonaro lands in US days after election defeat: Sources
body:
Incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva defeated Flavio Bolsonaro on Sunday.
Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, who is under investigation by authorities in Brazil, fled his country and landed in the U.S. Wednesday morning.
Bolsonaro landed at Miami-Opa Locka Executive airport in Florida shortly after 9 a.m. ET, accompanied by his family.
Images captured the plane touching down in South Florida and Bolsonaro, who was defeated by President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in Sunday's runoff election, coming off the jet.
The family was being shielded from photographers by umbrellas as they left the airport.
President Donald Trump's administration is issuing Bolsonaro and his family visas, a State Department official told ABC News.
On Tuesday, Brazilian authorities said they were unaware were investigating whether he fled to the U.S., according to authorities familiar with the investigation.
The former presidential candidate is under investigation over a sports betting case and for a probe into the production of a movie about his father, Jair Bolsonaro, who served as Brazil's president from 2019 to 2023, according to Brazilian authorities.
Bolsonaro released a statement Wednesday afternoon thanking Argentina's government and Trump for helping him leave Brazil.
He claimed, without any evidence, that there was fraud in Sunday's elections.
"Given the political weaponization of justice in Brazil, I brought my family to the United States, where we are safe," Bolsonaro said in a statement.
"I did not flee Brazil. I left Brazil -- left a state of exception -- so I could be the leader my people deserve," he added.
Trump was asked about the situation by reporters Wednesday and refused to say who he believed won Brazil's presidential election.
"But I know that we gave him a pass to come into the country, so we'll see," Trump told reporters on the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews Wednesday.
"But I won't get involved. It was a very strange election, that's for sure," he added.
When asked by reporters why he granted a visa to Bolsonaro and his family to come to the U.S., Trump said that he thought they had been "treated very unfairly" in Brazil. The president said Wednesday he had not spoken to the presidential candidate.

title: FG, NLC reach deal on N70,000 transport allowance, 19-month health workers’ arrears
body: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Federal Government and the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, have reached an agreement on a series of measures to ease the economic difficulties facing workers, including a ₦70,000 transport intervention and the payment of 19 months’ arrears owed health workers. The resolutions were reached at a conciliation meeting held at the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment yesterday, following an earlier meeting convened on October 22. The meetings were organised to address concerns raised by the NLC over the rising cost of living, the implementation of the National Minimum Wage, petroleum pump prices, workers’ welfare and outstanding allowances. The agreement was signed on behalf of the federal government by Dr. Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi, Minister of Labour and Employment; Timi Yakubu, Director-General, Budget; and Dr. Garba Abdul S. U., Permanent Secretary (SWO), Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, while NLC president, Joe Ajaero, and National Secretary, JNPSNC, Olowoyo Gbenga, stood for labour. Under the agreement, the federal government will provide a transport intervention of N70,000 across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026. The government also approved peculiar allowance with effect from May 1, 2026, while payment of the arrears is expected to begin in November and will be made in three equal monthly instalments. In addition, the 19 months’ outstanding allowances owed health workers is to be paid within three months, beginning in December 2026. The meeting also agreed that the Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee would be constituted to commence work immediately. However, the parties remained divided over the effective date for implementing the new minimum wage. On the issue of tax relief for workers, the meeting resolved that the matter would be referred to the National Executive Council, as taxation is a statutory issue. Meanwhile, the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security has submitted the list of beneficiaries and the cost implications of the proposed hazard allowance for agricultural officers to the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission for verification. The verification is expected to be completed within two weeks, after which the commission will issue an implementation template. Similarly, the NSIWC is expected to complete an updated assessment of the cost implications of the proposed CONHESS adjustment within three weeks. The assessment will enable the Presidential Committee on Salaries to take a decision on the matter. The federal government and NLC urged state and local governments to participate in the intervention process and implement the agreed measures. The parties also agreed to reconvene after one month to review the level of implementation of the resolutions. The post FG, NLC reach deal on N70,000 transport allowance, 19-month health workers’ arrears appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: US deploying additional Patriot air defense system to Israel — WSJ
body:
NEW YORK, October 28. /TASS/. The Pentagon is deploying an additional Patriot air defense system to Israel, The Wall Street Journal (WSJ) reported, citing sources.
According to the sources, the US military has decided to send the system from Texas to bolster Israel’s missile defenses. The newspaper also reported that an additional aircraft carrier strike group would arrive in the region next month, joining approximately 20 US warships already deployed in the Middle East.
