title: OWO 2026: The Or Foundation, Reggie Rockstone promote healthy living at Kantamanto
body: The Or Foundation, in collaboration with Ghanaian Hiplife legend Reggie Rockstone, has organised a four-kilometre health walk for traders at Kantamanto Market in Accra to promote physical fitness, encourage healthy lifestyles and raise awareness about preventive healthcare as part of activities to mark the fifth anniversary of the Obroni Wawu October (OWO) Festival. The exercise, held on Sunday, October 18, 2026, brought together market traders, particularly women, fashion enthusiasts and other members of the public to strengthen community bonds and highlight the economic opportunities associated with textile recycling and upcycling. According to a press release issued by The Or Foundation on Friday, October 23, 2026, the walk formed part of activities leading up to the main OWO Festival scheduled for Sunday, October 25, at Untamed Empire in Accra. The statement explained that the annual festival celebrated secondhand fashion, creativity, environmental sustainability and the contributions of thousands of traders, tailors, designers, transport operators and other workers whose livelihoods depended on Ghana’s circular fashion economy. According to the release, Mr Rockstone, the official ambassador for this year’s festival, told journalists after the walk that the exercise was intended not only to promote physical fitness but also to foster unity among traders and highlight the significant contribution of the secondhand clothing industry to Ghana’s economy. Mr Rockstone observed that the work undertaken by The Or Foundation and other players in the upcycling industry demonstrated how creativity and innovation could transform discarded clothing into commercially valuable products. He stressed that maximising the industry’s potential required substantial investment, technical expertise and stronger support from government, industry players and other stakeholders. The President of the Kantamanto Women’s Association commended The Or Foundation for organising the health walk and providing an opportunity for market women to prioritise their health. Beyond promoting healthy living, the statement indicated that the four-kilometre walk ended at an 80-stall demonstration site developed by The Or Foundation to showcase a proposed model for improving infrastructure and working conditions at Kantamanto Market. It explained that the facility, representing less than one per cent of the market, was designed by Ghanaian architect Nana Ayensua Amonoo of Unapparant using repurposed shipping containers on land entrusted to the project by the Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA). The project the statement said incorporates fire-resistant materials, wider aisles to facilitate the movement of carts carrying large bales of clothing, a solar-powered upcycling centre and waste-management infrastructure to improve safety, accessibility and environmental conditions. It noted that the design sought to reduce the risks associated with carrying heavy loads on the head, while its modular structure would allow for faster construction and minimise the displacement of traders during future redevelopment. It emphasised that the facility was intended to demonstrate the potential for safer and more sustainable market infrastructure rather than serve as a comprehensive redevelopment solution adding that over the past 12 months, The Or Foundation had engaged representatives of the Kantamanto Women’s Association, the Kantamanto Upcyclers’ Association and market leaders to gather feedback on the project. The statement estimated that extending a similar infrastructure model across the entire market could cost more than US$70 million, with the proposed investment to be mobilised through Globally Accountable Extended Producer Responsibility mechanisms, government-led special levies, public fundraising and private philanthropic support.

title: Dangote Refinery makes history as IPO attracts investors from 120 countries, all 54 African nations
body:
Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals has successfully concluded its landmark Initial Public Offering (IPO), attracting investor applications from 120 countries across all six inhabited continents, including every one of Africa’s 54 countries, in an unprecedented demonstration of the continent’s capacity to mobilise capital and broaden ownership of strategic industrial assets.
The historic offering, widely described as The People’s IPO, achieved 100 per cent geographical coverage of Africa, bringing together investors from across the continent and beyond in a transaction that could redefine the scale, accessibility and international reach of African capital markets.
More than a conventional fundraising exercise, the IPO has emerged as a landmark in financial inclusion, demonstrating how digital technology, coordinated financial institutions and innovative distribution channels can connect millions of potential investors to opportunities previously dominated by institutional and high-net-worth participants.
The transaction was supported by an extensive network of commercial banks, stockbroking firms, fintech platforms, capital market institutions and distribution partners, whose collaboration expanded access to the offer across national boundaries and created new pathways for retail participation.
For Dangote Industries Limited, the conclusion of the IPO marks a defining moment in its industrial journey, transforming the refinery’s ownership proposition from an investment driven by a single entrepreneurial vision into an opportunity for broader African participation. President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote , described the outcome as a powerful affirmation of African confidence, enterprise and the continent’s ability to mobilise its own resources for development.
“When we set out to build this refinery, many doubted that a project of this scale could be delivered by Africans. We proved that Africa could build it. Today, through this historic IPO, we have demonstrated something equally important: Africans are ready to own and participate in the prosperity created by their own industries.
“To have investor applications from all 54 African countries is deeply significant to me. It tells us that our people do not simply want to consume what Africa produces; they want to invest in it, own it and share in its future. This is the Africa we have always believed in,” he said.
“We did not undertake this IPO simply because we needed to raise capital. We wanted to open the doors of ownership, give ordinary Africans an opportunity to participate in an enterprise of global significance and establish a new culture of shared prosperity. The refinery was built in Africa, by African determination, and its future must create opportunities for Africans. Today, we have made history together. But the greater achievement will be the generation of African investors, entrepreneurs and industrialists that this transaction inspires.
“Our ambition is not merely to build successful businesses. It is to help build a prosperous, self-reliant Africa whose people are participants in its economic destiny. As we advance our expansion programme and Vision 2030 strategy, we remain committed to strengthening our operational performance, deepening our contribution to Africa’s energy security and building an enterprise that rewards the confidence placed in it”.
The IPO’s geographical reach is particularly significant for a continent where capital markets have historically been fragmented by national boundaries, differing regulatory environments and limited retail investor participation. By attracting applications from all 54 African countries, the transaction has demonstrated the potential for a more connected investment ecosystem in which Africans can participate in major industrial opportunities beyond their domestic markets.
The offering also highlights the growing importance of digital financial infrastructure in widening investment access. Through partnerships involving traditional financial institutions and technology-driven investment platforms, the transaction created multiple channels through which eligible investors could express interest and submit applications.
Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals, David Bird, said the international response reflected confidence in the refinery’s operating capabilities, industrial scale and long-term growth prospects.
“The successful conclusion of this IPO is a remarkable milestone for Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals. Investor applications spanning 120 countries demonstrate the extraordinary international interest in our business and the confidence that investors are placing in the future of this refinery. We have built one of the world’s most significant refining and petrochemical complexes, and our focus remains on translating that industrial scale into operational excellence, sustainable growth and long-term shareholder value,” he said.
“What makes this transaction particularly meaningful is the breadth of participation. The opportunity to own a stake in a major African industrial enterprise has reached investors across every African country and all six inhabited continents. That is a powerful endorsement of the refinery’s potential and of Africa’s growing relevance in global investment markets,” he added.
The refinery’s IPO opened on 14 September 2026, offering 4.1 billion ordinary shares at N525 per share, representing a proposed capital raise of approximately N2.15 trillion. Initially scheduled to close on 13 October, the offer was extended to 27 October following approval by the Securities and Exchange Commission, allowing additional time for investors across Africa and other international markets to participate. The extension reflected the Group’s stated ambition to prioritise the breadth of ownership alongside the financial objectives of the transaction.
Beyond the industrial significance of the refinery itself, the IPO has also established a model for collaboration across Africa’s financial services ecosystem. Its distribution network brought together institutions operating across banking, securities trading, financial technology and investor engagement, demonstrating how coordinated infrastructure can expand access to large-scale investment opportunities.
Group Chief Financial Officer, Dangote Industries Limited, Murat Erden, speaking on the execution and wider significance of the offering, said the transaction had established an important precedent for the continent’s capital markets.
“The Dangote Refinery People’s IPO represents much more than a landmark capital-raising exercise. It marks a defining moment in the evolution of African capital markets, demonstrating our continent’s ability to mobilise domestic savings, connect investors across borders and broaden ownership of strategic industrial assets.
“Reaching investors in 120 countries, including all 54 African nations, is an extraordinary achievement and a powerful testament to the growing investment appetite across our continent. By bringing together banks, capital market institutions, stockbrokers, fintech platforms and innovative digital distribution channels, we have demonstrated that African capital markets can transcend national boundaries and connect millions of people to investment opportunities previously beyond their reach,” he said.
“Importantly, this transaction is underpinned by exceptional industrial and financial fundamentals. With US$22.5 billion in revenue and US$5.52 billion in EBITDA in the first nine months of 2026, Dangote Refinery combines world-class industrial scale, strong profitability and significant long-term growth potential. Our greatest achievement is not simply the capital we mobilise, but the doors we open and the foundation we lay for future generations of African investors, entrepreneurs and businesses.
“We believe the People’s IPO will be remembered not only as a landmark transaction in African capital market history, but as a blueprint for a more inclusive, interconnected and globally competitive African financial ecosystem — one in which Africans increasingly finance, own and share in the prosperity created by their continent’s industrial transformation.”
The successful conclusion of the offer comes as Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals pursues an ambitious programme to expand its refining and petrochemical operations, strengthen its distribution network and support greater energy security across Africa. Located in Lagos, the refinery represents one of the continent’s largest private industrial investments and a major effort to reduce dependence on imported refined petroleum products while building domestic processing capacity.

title: Putin lectured Nordic leaders on Russian history during latest call, FT reports
body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin delivered a lengthy lecture on medieval Slavic history to the leaders of Norway and Finland during an Oct. 27 phone call, offering little mention of an immediate ceasefire despite renewed diplomatic efforts to end Moscow's war in Ukraine, the Financial Times (FT) reported.
According to three sources familiar with the call between Finnish President Alexander Stubb, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store, and the Russian president, Putin spent most of the 90-minute call to deliver a lengthy rant about Russian historical fixations.
The call , which was initially planned to last half an hour, comes ahead of trilateral peace talks expected in the Emirati capital of Abu Dhabi sometime in November between Ukraine, Russia, and the U.S.
Ukraine's calls for an immediate ceasefire were barely discussed during the phone call, the sources added. With one source telling FT that the leaders did not interrupt Putin's rant to gauge his seriousness on future dialogue with Europe.
The Russian leader has often invoked Ukrainian and Russian history to justify aggression against Ukraine, like during his interview with U.S. host Tucker Carlson in 2024.
Amid failed attempts at peace negotiations, Putin has repeatedly espoused his views on Russian history in conversations with world leaders. The Russian president reportedly gave a similar lecture to U.S. President Donald Trump during the August 2025 summit in Alaska, which reportedly included a lengthy lecture on medieval Rus princes , such as Rurik or Yaroslav the Wise, as well as the 17th-century Cossack leader Bohdan Khmelnytskyi .
While the exact details of the discussion remain unclear, Putin's cherry-picked historical narratives and outright distortions have been repeatedly disputed by Western historians as a means to justify Moscow's actions.
The two leaders' call with Putin follows an Oct. 20 meeting in Oslo with Ukrainian, European, and U.S. officials, but they stressed that in the Oct. 27 call, they "did not speak he behalf of Europe as a whole."
The two leaders discussed the call with President Volodymyr Zelensky afterward, who said: "I am grateful for the detailed briefing and for their active support for our diplomacy and the peace efforts we are pursuing together with all our partners."
The phone call between the Nordic leaders and Putin received mix reactions from fellow European leaders with Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen telling media that she was "skeptical" of the call and that it had not been coordinated with others.
Meanwhile a European Commission spokesperson reminded that "we have a shared interest in putting an end to this horrific war," in comments sent to the Kyiv Independent.
"On the EU side, we are adamantly committed not just to putting an end to the war but to achieve peace that will be just and sustainable. That is our aim and that is the stance we are defending in the ongoing talks," the spokesperson said.
A senior EU official told the Kyiv Independent to expect a round of talks in Europe before the expected Abu Dhabi meeting, after mixed messages from Kyiv had given the impression that there would be Brussels-based peace talks this week.

title: Smotrich vows Jewish settlements in Gaza as party defies election polls
body: Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich vowed early Wednesday that Jewish settlements would be established in the Gaza Strip, declaring that Israel would not reverse its settlement expansion in the West Bank or withdraw from territory it controls in Lebanon and Syria. His remarks came after exit polls by Israel's three major broadcasters — Channel 12, Channel 13 and public broadcaster Kan — projected that his far-right Religious Zionist Party had won six seats in the 120-member Knesset, a stronger showing than some preelection surveys had suggested.   During the campaign, the party had repeatedly struggled in polls to clear the electoral threshold of 3.25% of the national vote, the minimum required to enter parliament. Speaking to supporters at the Religious Zionist Party's election headquarters, Smotrich struck a defiant tone despite initial exit polls showing an advantage for the opposition's pro-change bloc. "We will not let them celebrate," Smotrich said. "They are celebrating because they think they will be able to reverse our settlement revolution in Judea and Samaria. I am telling them: They will not succeed. Jewish settlements will be established in Gaza." Judea and Samaria is the biblical name used by Israel for the West Bank, territory captured from Jordan in the 1967 Six-Day War. Most of the international community considers Israeli settlements there illegal under international law, a position Israel disputes. Israel withdrew its settlers and permanent military installations from Gaza in 2005, dismantling 21 Jewish settlements as part of a unilateral disengagement plan. Reestablishing civilian settlements in the Palestinian territory has since become a central demand of some far-right politicians. Smotrich also rejected the prospect of Israeli territorial withdrawals from Lebanon and Syria. "They are celebrating because they think, God forbid, that the State of Israel will retreat from Lebanon and the summit of Mount Hermon," he said. "We will not withdraw." Mount Hermon straddles the border region between Israel, Lebanon and Syria. Israel has maintained control of additional positions in the area following military operations in Syria, while its forces have also operated inside southern Lebanon. Smotrich blames wasted right-wing votes Smotrich also criticized rival right-wing political figures whose parties were projected to fall below the electoral threshold, implicitly targeting former IDF general Ofer Winter. Winter's Amcha Yisrael party failed to secure enough votes to enter the Knesset, according to the exit polls.   Smotrich did not mention Winter by name but blamed the uncertainty surrounding the election results on political rivals who had refused to unite with established parties. "Tonight, once again, it has become clear how right we were," Smotrich said. "The Arabs united. And, separately, our brothers on the left united. The only reason there is uncertainty is that irresponsible people threw votes into the trash." Under Israel's proportional representation system, votes cast for parties that fail to cross the electoral threshold do not translate into parliamentary seats, potentially weakening the broader political bloc to which those parties belong. "Despite those irresponsible people, our voters demonstrated maturity and responsibility," Smotrich said. "We hope to wake up in the morning to results much better than the exit polls." He urged right-wing voters and politicians to consolidate under the Religious Zionist Party rather than support smaller parties that might fail to enter parliament. "I call on all our friends and partners among the Israeli public: There is room for all of you in the Religious Zionist Party," he said. "We have had enough of parties that do not cross the electoral threshold. We are coming back together." A central figure in West Bank settlement expansion Smotrich has spent the past four years serving as both finance minister and a minister within the Defense Ministry, a dual role that has given him considerable influence over civilian affairs in the West Bank. During that period, he spearheaded measures to retroactively legalize numerous previously unauthorized settlement outposts and encouraged the establishment of agricultural farms across the territory. Those efforts form part of a broader strategy he outlined in 2017, known as his "Decisive Plan," which calls for consolidating Israeli control over the West Bank and rejecting the establishment of an independent Palestinian state. Smotrich became leader of the Religious Zionist Party in 2019, when it was still known as National Union-Tkuma. In the previous election, his party ran on a joint ticket with Otzma Yehudit, the far-right party led by Itamar Ben-Gvir. This time, after polls suggested the Religious Zionist Party might fail to enter the Knesset, Smotrich joined forces with former Likud lawmaker Moshe Feiglin and his Zehut party. Feiglin, a far-right libertarian politician, was placed second on the joint electoral list. He served as a Likud lawmaker more than a decade ago, previously challenged Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the party leadership and later unsuccessfully attempted to bring Zehut into parliament as an independent party. The alliance with Feiglin was intended to consolidate support among right-wing voters and prevent votes from being lost to parties that failed to meet the electoral threshold. With six seats projected in the exit polls, the Religious Zionist Party appears to have avoided that outcome, although its final representation will depend on the official vote count.

title: Tinubu seeks $20.5bn, €1.04bn foreign loans to fund projects
body: *Seeks Reps’ approval for ₦269.4bn promissory notes to settle FG’s debts *Senate refers 2026–2027 supplementary borrowing plan to debt committee By Henry Umoru, Luminous Jannamike & Gift Odekina ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has written the Senate, seeking an approval of a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion to finance infrastructure and development projects across the country. He also asked the National Assembly to approve establishment and expansion of the Federal Government’s Promissory Note Programme to settle outstanding verified liabilities totalling N269.44 billion. President Tinubu’s letter was addressed to President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio. Akpabio, who read the letter yesterday at plenary, said the request covered the 2026–2027 fiscal period, targeting critical sectors, including power, transportation, agriculture, healthcare, education, water supply and security. Tinubu, who noted that the proposed borrowing is necessary to bridge Nigeria’s infrastructure funding gap, sustain economic growth, generate employment and improve the living conditions of Nigerians, urged the National Assembly to give the plan urgent consideration and approval to facilitate the timely release of funds and implementation of the projects. In the letter, the president said the proposed external financing will support projects and programmes spanning virtually every sector of the economy. “The 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan cuts across all sectors, with specific emphasis on infrastructure, agriculture, health, education, water supply, growth, security and employment generation, as well as financial management reforms, amongst others,” he said. According to the letter, the proposed facilities cost $20,517,755,901 and €1,045,083,643. It explained that the projects had been selected after technical and economic assessments. “I want to emphasise that the projects and programmes included in the borrowing plan were selected based on thorough technical and economic evaluation, as well as their anticipated contribution to the socio-economic development of the country,” he said. The president, who explained that the proposed investments were expected to create employment opportunities, promote skills acquisition, encourage entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and strengthen food security, said: “These initiatives aim to generate employment, promote skills acquisition, foster entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and enhance food security, all of which improve the livelihood of the Nigerian child.” ‘Loan is for projects in 36 states and FCT’ He disclosed that most of the projects would be executed across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, stressing that the nationwide spread of the interventions would help address development needs across the federation. Tinubu added that the scale of Nigeria’s infrastructure deficit and the financial resources required to address it had made additional external borrowing necessary. “In light of the need for significant infrastructure investment in the country and the vast financial resources needed to address this gap, it has become essential to pursue broader external borrowings to close the financing shortfall,” he said. He identified power, transportation and healthcare among the critical sectors expected to benefit from the proposed financing. “These funds will primarily be directed towards critical infrastructure projects in various sectors, including power, transportation and healthcare, amongst others,” the president said. Tinubu maintained that prompt consideration of the request would enable the government meet its obligations to Nigerians through timely disbursement of funds and effective execution of the projects. He said: “Given the urgent nature of these needs and the importance of stabilising the country, it is crucial to seek the consideration and approval of the National Assembly leadership and the entire National Assembly for the 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan.” The President, who noted that legislative approval will enable government proceed with the proposed interventions, said: “This will enable the government to fulfil its obligations to the Nigerian people through timely disbursements and effective project implementation.” The President of the Senate, thereafter, referred the communication to the Senate Committee on Local and Foreign Debts for further legislative action, to report at plenary within one week. The committee is expected to examine the proposal, potentially in collaboration with the Senate Committee on Appropriations and other relevant committees. The letter, as presented to the Senate, did not provide a detailed project-by-project breakdown of the proposed facilities, the specific financing terms or the amount earmarked for each sector. The letter, titled “Federal Government 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plans, read: “ I write in reference to the above subjects and to submit the attached federal government 2026-2027 supplementary external borrowing plans for consideration and early approval of the National Assembly to ensure prompt implementation of our projects. “The 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan cuts across all sectors with specific emphasis on infrastructure, agriculture, health, education, water supply, growth, security, and employment generation, as well as financial management reforms, amongst others. “The total facility for the projects and programmes under the Borrowing Growing Plan is $20,517,000,000 and €1,045,083,643 respectively and the summary of the breakdown is attached to this presents. “So, distinguished colleagues, in light of the removal of the critical reforms of my administration, the need to accelerate growth of the national economy provides support for the External Borrowing Plan, which amounts to $20,517,755,901, and €1,045,083,643. “I want to emphasise that the projects and programmes included in the Borrowing Plan were selected based on thorough technical and economic evaluation, as well as their anticipated contribution to the socio-economic development of the country. “These initiatives aim to generate employment, promote skilled acquisition, foster entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and enhance food security, all of which improves the livelihood of the Nigerian child. “The majority of these projects and programs will be implemented across all the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. In light of the need for significant infrastructure investment in the country and the vast financial resources needed to address this gap, it has become essential to pursue broader external borrowings to close the financing shortfall. “These funds will primarily be directed towards critical infrastructure projects in various sectors, including power, transportation and healthcare, among others. “Given the urgent nature of these needs and the importance of stabilising the country, it is crucial to seek the consideration and approval of the National Assembly leadership and the entire National Assembly for the 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan. “This will enable the government fulfill its obligations to the Nigerian people through timely disbursements and effective project implementation. “This request will be looked at by the Committee on Local and Foreign Debts, probably in collaboration with the Preparation and Finance, but majorly by the Committee on Local and Foreign Debts. And you can report back in one week.” ₦269.4bn promissory notes Similarly, President Bola Tinubu asked the National Assembly to approve the establishment and expansion of the federal government’s Promissory Note Programme to settle outstanding verified liabilities totalling N269.44 billion. This was contained in a letter by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, Senator George Akume, which was read on the floor of the House at plenary in Abuja yesterday. The request is aimed at addressing outstanding contractual, project-related and other financial obligations owed various categories of creditors. In a letter dated August 18, 2026, and received by the Office of the Speaker on October 21, Akume said the liabilities amounted to N269,446,402,822.56, following a comprehensive review by relevant ministries, departments and agencies, MDAs. He said Tinubu had approved the proposal to establish and expand the programme as a mechanism for settling the verified obligations. According to the letter, the programme is designed to provide “a structured, transparent and fiscally responsible framework” for settling the outstanding debts, while ensuring that only verified and validated claims are admitted. The President is seeking legislative approval for the issuance of promissory notes worth N269.44 billion, or such other amount as may be approved by the National Assembly, to settle the liabilities contained in the accompanying schedule. The request also seeks approval for the inclusion of identified categories of liabilities and beneficiaries in the programme, subject to final verification, reconciliation and certification by the relevant government agencies. Tinubu further asked the National Assembly to authorise the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, in collaboration with the Debt Management Office and other relevant agencies, to take the necessary steps to implement the programme. Akume explained that the proposal was intended to mitigate the continued accumulation of interest, penalties and other financial costs associated with the outstanding obligations. He said the arrangement would also provide relief to affected creditors and strengthen confidence in the federal government’s commitment to honouring legitimate contractual and other obligations. The SGF noted that the federal government had previously used the Promissory Note Programme to settle inherited local debts and contractual obligations, following Federal Executive Council’s approval and subsequent National Assembly approval. He added that the proposed arrangement was expected to facilitate the orderly settlement of the liabilities without imposing an immediate and disproportionate cash-flow burden on the federal government. According to the letter, the programme will also support fiscal planning by spreading repayment obligations over an appropriate period, in line with prudent debt management principles. Akume urged the House to give the request urgent consideration, citing the magnitude and age of some of the outstanding liabilities and the possibility of further accumulation of interest and associated costs. He said early legislative approval would enable the Federal Government commence the necessary processes for issuing the promissory notes and bringing the affected liabilities to a close. The detailed schedule of the liabilities, including the relevant categories, beneficiaries, amounts and supporting documentation, was forwarded to the National Assembly for consideration. Vanguard News The post Tinubu seeks $20.5bn, €1.04bn foreign loans to fund projects appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Afrilition: Brazil’s valiant stride towards Pan-African excellence, By Adéwálé Àjàdí
body:
This win by Lula is another milestone towards the emerging African civilisation that Afrilition enlightens. A world of purposefully building Africa in the face of missteps and misdeeds, knowing where and what excellence looks like in spite of struggles. The face of Brazil in 2026 is 80-year-old President Luiz In á cio Lula da Silva, a metal worker with no university certificate and nine fingers. He plans to midwife Brazil, which means repairing injustice to the country ’ s majority, the Afro-Brazilians. This matters to all Africans who see African excellence as more than fantasy stories.. .
It was always going to be like this, our journey as African World envisaged in Afrilition . I remember my last working day in Manila, Philippines, during a retreat that my then-employers organised and a now-deceased opposition figure hosted. It was an evening that filled me with sadness as we watched what had happened to the Lula legacy in Brazil, after his successor was thwarted, and then his manufactured imprisonment. It was a memorable, sad evening because humanity seemed to have lost to brutality and treachery. To see the same Lula back in power a few years after seemed a miracle. He not only survived the attempt to criminalise him but came back as still a bulwark against the tyranny in his region and across the world. He remains a friend of Africa and Africans, and also a decolonising mind, even in his 70s.
There are no perfect people, but there are significant heads of countries who play the hands they are dealt for the improvement of the majority of their people, especially those at the bottom of the pyramid. A genuine and rare champion of progress for Afro-Brazilians in a system that is totally stacked against them. Brazil is the largest home of African descendants in the Americas and outside the African continent, and its effort includes being the last to end enslavement. Brazil is the home of the largest group of returnees from enslavement, whose influence and contribution after the Male insurrection dot the coast of West Africa with ornate verandas and families linked to Bahia to this day.
In the last few hours, Brazil moved more purposefully towards transformation, not just by electing Lula again and again, leading to his fourth term; this is largely because Brazil has become and is becoming a definitive part of the African world. There is no greater and more diverse part of the African diaspora than the country of Brazil. Outside Africa, it is home to the largest and most expressive breadth of retained African civilisation outside the geographic continent. It is more significant that even though Brazil became home to all of the forms of humiliation of the African people and continues to do its best to reduce their potential, damage their spirit, and vilify their expression of Africanness, they still stand.
This job of repair for the Brazilian majority is only the beginning. It certainly needs to include stopping Police brutality and prison reforms. The Afro-Brazilian majority can be the source of resilience for Brazil, and a powerful alternative, as the aging population and reduction in workforce hit in the next few decades.
In October, Lula’s record-breaking move from second in the first round ballot to winner in the second round was an unlikely but record-breaking fact. Yes, Afro-Brazilians had a lot to do with this. In the 2022 Census by the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE), it reported that people of African descent, mixed and unmixed heritage (or black), form the absolutely clear majority of the Brazilian population. It shifted the statistical and cultural centre away from the historically European or white majority status. This is now a mass Afro-Brazilian movement that encompasses the preto and pardo census classification. It is accompanied by an increased shift in ancestral pride and cultural valuation, and a sharp decrease in social stigma. Hence, the core of political and cultural Brazil as the majority of the country is Afro-Brazilian.
This, I think, is understood by President Lula, not just in the backroom data but also in his political priorities, from his commitments that include tackling systemic racism and racial inequality as a core pillar of governance, which has seen him create the Ministry of Racial Equality, while ensuring a 30 per cent of cabinet representation, civil service quotas, land rights, and repartitions of Quilombola Territories, among many other things. This job of repair for the Brazilian majority is only the beginning. It certainly needs to include stopping Police brutality and prison reforms. The Afro-Brazilian majority can be the source of resilience for Brazil, and a powerful alternative, as the aging population and reduction in workforce hit in the next few decades.
The demographic centre of the world will be Africa; as such it is an overwhelmingly Afro-Brazilian majority nation that should be a welcome partner and a cooperative part of a Pan-African civilisation, which can come fully into excellence. This means more than a simple geopolitical play but an immense alliance in economic abundance, reducing the demographic disadvantage of an aging workforce in Brazil.
The demographic centre of the world will be Africa; as such it is an overwhelmingly Afro-Brazilian majority nation that should be a welcome partner and a cooperative part of a Pan-African civilisation, which can come fully into excellence. This means more than a simple geopolitical play but an immense alliance in economic abundance, reducing the demographic disadvantage of an aging workforce in Brazil. It will be hard work, as we see hegemonic systems and classes across the world resort to genocide and war to protect their extractive gains. We must expect battles.
This win by Lula is another milestone towards the emerging African civilisation that Afrilition enlightens. A world of purposefully building Africa in the face of missteps and misdeeds, knowing where and what excellence looks like in spite of struggles. The face of Brazil in 2026 is 80-year-old President Luiz In á cio Lula da Silva, a metal worker with no university certificate and nine fingers. He plans to midwife Brazil, which means repairing injustice to the country ’ s majority, the Afro-Brazilians. This matters to all Africans who see African excellence as more than fantasy stories, as life work, and especially those who recognise it is Afrilition.
Adéwálé Àjàdí , a lawyer, creative consultant and leadership expert, is author of the newly released Afrilition: 21st Century African Manifesto , and Omoluwabi 2.0: A Code of Transformation in 21st Century Nigeria .

title: Court Freezes Five-Star Hotel Build on Milos Coast
body: A Piraeus appeals court has frozen work on the Pachaina hotel, a five-star seaside complex on Milos, until it rules on a challenge from two environmental groups. The Piraeus Court of Appeal granted a request from the Hellenic Society for Environment and Culture (ELLET) and the Milos Mountain and Sea Friends Group. This suspension is temporary and lasts only until the court decides the main appeal. In its ruling, the court said it acted “to prevent the creation of facts on the ground and further burden on the area from the execution of building permits” . What the Pachaina hotel permit allows Developer S Althaia received the permit for the Pachaina hotel in October 2025. It covers a five-star resort with 23 rooms, 46 beds and swimming pools. Under the plans, the complex would have 16 buildings with a total floor area of about 5,000 square metres. They would stand on a 4.95-hectare plot right beside the sea. According to the two groups, the Pachaina hotel plot has no frontage on a recognised road. Under planning law, land outside town plans needs that access before anyone can build on it. The groups also argue that the project would heavily alter the volcanic landscape of Milos . Its site lies inside a designated wildlife refuge. A similar road-access problem sits at the heart of another Milos case. This month, the National Transparency Authority found that the White Coast hotel should never have received a permit . Ministry sends 30 Milos permits back to the island Separately, the local ELLET committee on Milos asked the Environment Ministry months ago to check the legality of 30 building permits on the island. When the ministry gave no answer, the group sent an extrajudicial protest in June. Now the ministry has told ELLET that its environmental inspectors have no power to review building permits. Instead, it passed the request to the Milos planning office, which issued those same permits in the first place. On the White Coast case, owner V Tourism disputed the watchdog’s findings. The company said it applied the legally provided building ratio of 0.20, rather than 0.18, under transitional rules that covered the investment at the time. It added that officials had already examined the road-frontage question during the original licensing. V Tourism said it would use every legal right to protect its investment. For now, the Pachaina hotel joins a growing list of stalled projects on the island. In April, works also stopped on a five-star complex at Agios Konstantinos after appeals from the same two groups. Later that month, the government suspended building works in off-plan areas of Milos until the end of 2026. As a result, the fate of the Pachaina hotel now rests with the Piraeus court’s final ruling. title: US spent more than $47bn on Iran war, Pentagon data shows
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 28 (MNA) – The US military has spent more than $47bn on the war on Iran, more than 25 percent higher than the Pentagon’s estimate in July.
The US military has spent more than $47bn on the war on Iran, more than 25 percent higher than the Pentagon’s estimate in July, according to data obtained by Reuters.
The latest estimate includes more than $29bn to replace munitions used in the conflict, and more than $6bn to replace military equipment, including aircraft and drones lost during the war.
The figures mark a significant increase from Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s July estimate of $37.5bn.
Reuters reported that the estimate did not clearly account for the cost of repairing damage to US military bases caused by Iranian missile and drone attacks.

title: Oil prices rise after attack on Saudi Arabian refinery reignites supply concerns
body: Oil prices rose on Wednesday after an attack on a refinery in Saudi Arabia, the ​world’s biggest crude exporter, renewed concerns around the ‌risks to supply in the Middle East stemming from the conflict with Iran and its proxies. Brent crude futures rose $1.48, or 1.3%, to $115.36 a ​barrel as of 0140 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate ​crude rose $1.22, or 1.22%, to $101.12. Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said on Tuesday ⁠they had hit Saudi Arabia’s biggest oil refinery with ​a missile, intensifying their strikes against the world’s second-largest crude ​producer. Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the strike on the 550,000-barrel-per-day facility. Prices swung back after dropping nearly $2 on Tuesday as talks in the Middle East eased supply worries. That was despite data expected to show a rise in crude inventories ‌in ⁠the US. Crude oil stockpiles rose about 15,000 barrels in the week ended October 23, according to a Reuters poll of eight analysts. The OPEC+ oil-producing countries are expected to keep their ​December output targets steady on Sunday, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters, in line with market expectations. Production in most of the ​seven core ⁠OPEC+ members — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman — is below their output targets. Crude oil exports from Russia’s Baltic and Black Sea ports could fall next month as domestic refiners increase diesel output after a deal with Washington this month, traders said.

title: Jordan and Syria form joint security committee after deadly strikes
body: Jordan and Syria have agreed to form a joint security committee to examine the details and the repercussions of Jordanian strikes against ISIS , the two countries' foreign ministers have said. The Jordanian army on Tuesday said at least 20 ISIS members had been killed in strikes on Syria launched in “retaliation” for a deadly church attack in the kingdom last week that killed nine Christians. Syrian authorities said at least seven people, including three children, a woman and an elderly man, were killed in the strikes, which occurred late on Monday. Jordanian Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi told Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Al Shibani that ​Tuesday's ‌strikes ⁠were based on ​field intelligence ​and ‌aimed at “neutralising” ⁠confirmed threats and imminent attacks ⁠on Amman's security, while expressing “deep regret and sorrow” over civilian deaths. Mr Safadi offered condolences to the Syrian people and stressed that Jordan prioritised “the safety of Syrian civilians as it does its own”. Both officials reaffirmed the “deep historical” ties between Syria and Jordan . The joint statement said they emphasised the “importance of addressing any issues that could strain bilateral relations through frank and responsible dialogue, stressing that the security and future of the two countries are closely interconnected”. Jordan has been supportive of the Syrian government led by President Ahmad Al Shara since it came to power in December 2024 after toppling the former regime of Bashar Al Assad. Jordan's King Abdullah II and Mr Al Shara have agreed to strengthen co-operation, particularly on border security. Mr Al Shibani and Mr Safadi reiterated the close co-operation “to tackle common challenges, primarily combating terrorism and thwarting cross-border drug and arms smuggling through active institutional channels”. Syria also said it would restore passenger and commercial traffic through the Nassib border crossing with Jordan on Wednesday, after it was briefly closed in the wake of the Jordanian strikes. The ​Nassib ‌crossing ⁠is ​Jordan's only ​border ‌crossing ⁠with Syria open to ⁠passenger and commercial traffic.

title: Choriatiko Owner Allegedly Paid Mykonos Police Officer €300 a Month for Tip-Offs
body: The businessman behind Greek bakery chain To Choriatiko (Το Χωριάτικο) allegedly paid a police officer on Mykonos at least €300 a month for confidential information and advance warning of police checks, according to court documents reported by Kathimerini and Ta Nea. Angelos Giannakopoulos, whom police describe as the alleged leader of the network at the centre of the Choriatiko investigation, is said to have made the payments to a police sub-lieutenant serving on the island “from 2022 until at least October 2024”, Kathimerini reported, citing judicial documents in its possession. In return, the officer allegedly provided “information and official secrets”. According to Ta Nea, the information concerned upcoming inspections at businesses Giannakopoulos ran in Attica and on Mykonos. A €3,000 offer over a police transfer In a separate incident in September 2024, Giannakopoulos and another person allegedly offered €3,000 to a different police officer serving on Mykonos, in an effort to arrange a mutual transfer with the officer receiving the monthly payments, Ta Nea and Pagenews reported. According to the same reports, there is no indication that the officer accepted the money, and the transfer did not go ahead. Reports by MEGA, carried by Newsit, also point to 3 June 2024, when a planned inspection by the police Extortion Unit at a well-known Mykonos club managed by Giannakopoulos was allegedly leaked from inside the force. The officer who took part in the inspection recorded no violation. The sub-lieutenant was arrested in the summer of 2025. The trial, in which Giannakopoulos, a close associate who is among those arrested in the Choriatiko case and police officers are defendants, is due to begin on Friday, 30 October, according to Kathimerini. Pagenews reported that Giannakopoulos faces charges of bribing an official, jointly and repeatedly. Other officers under scrutiny Kathimerini also reported that investigators from the Organised Crime Directorate (DAOE) found that two serving police officers held regular phone conversations with the manager of a strip club on Syngrou Avenue linked to Giannakopoulos, allegedly warning him of upcoming checks. A police officer who previously headed a security unit on Rhodes, already suspended over a separate case, allegedly looked up the number plates of DAOE vehicles sent to Rhodes on the police’s internal Police On Line system and informed Giannakopoulos’s associates on the island. These officers are not named in the case file, and their role will be assessed during the main investigation, the newspaper said. Property and the money trail The 850-page case file, as summarised by Proto Thema, alleges that proceeds of the scheme were channelled into property in Greece and Dubai, high-value vehicles and purported severance payments to associates. Investigators are examining a €2.6 million payment involving a Cypriot company in July 2021, connected to a property transaction on Mykonos, as well as a €1.5 million transfer to a London-based company in August 2025. Seven Cyprus-based holding companies are under investigation. On Mykonos, Giannakopoulos acquired a 50 per cent stake in a company connected to the well-known Spilia restaurant at Agia Anna in autumn 2023, a deal that later led to a bitter dispute, Proto Thema reported. According to the case file, a criminal group later demanded that he accept €20 million for his stake and walk away. He reportedly refused. According to Pressing.gr, whenever he bought a business on Mykonos, he made sure to buy the building that housed it as well. Proto Thema reported that he had also bought a shop in Gialos, the island’s harbour area, with plans to open a takeaway cooked-food business. The scale of the case The case file names 149 alleged participants, 58 of whom were arrested, and more than 340 interconnected companies. Authorities have documented €95.56 million in outstanding tax and social security debts, including penalties and surcharges, Proto Thema reported. The allegations remain subject to judicial examination, and all those implicated are presumed innocent unless proven guilty. title: easyJet Adds Starlink Wi-Fi, but the Price Stays Secret
body: LONDON, October 2026 — An easyJet Starlink deal will bring Wi-Fi onboard the budget airline’s planes for the first time, with installation across its Airbus fleet starting in the first half of 2027. The airline said the satellite service will go on its A320, A320neo and A321neo aircraft , with the roll-out due to finish by early 2028. Under the easyJet Starlink plan, passengers will be able to stream, game and browse on their own devices. easyJet carries about 100 million passengers a year, and until now none of them could get online in the air. Chief executive Kenton Jarvis said the deal means the airline is “offering more of the options both business and leisure travellers want” . SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell said people will be able to “work, stream, or stay in touch without interruption” . Will easyJet Starlink Wi-Fi cost extra? However, the airline has not yet said whether passengers will have to pay. Asked by Business Traveller , easyJet said Starlink would manage access. Still, pricing details will follow once the first aircraft are fitted. easyJet added that, “as with the other extras we offer customers it will be entirely optional” . The easyJet Starlink deal marks a shift for the carrier. Jarvis told an earnings call in January that “the economics aren’t quite working for us” , Aviation Business News reported. Starlink initially required airlines to offer the service free. A newer model lets it manage access for some low-cost carriers, and Philippine budget airline Cebu Pacific plans to charge non-elite passengers. According to Business Traveller, the easyJet Starlink roll-out covers around 275 aircraft. The older A319s will miss out because the airline is phasing them out. What it means for flights to Greece Greece is a major market for easyJet. Its summer 2027 schedule offers more than 3.1 million seats on over 16,000 flights to the country. The airline will also launch two new routes next summer, linking Thessaloniki with London Luton and Rhodes with London Southend. For holidaymakers heading to the islands, easyJet Starlink Wi-Fi will offer flight status checks and local weather, transport and tourism information. The airline said the technology could eventually let passengers order from the inflight menu from their seats. More than 50 airlines and groups have signed up for Starlink. Qatar Airways already offers it to Australian passengers , and Wizz Air and airBaltic have also begun roll-outs. By comparison, Greece’s Aegean Airlines already offers Wi-Fi on its equipped aircraft. Access on European routes is free for Miles+Bonus members and Business Class passengers. Ryanair, Europe’s largest airline group, has so far rejected Starlink. Its chief executive Michael O’Leary also clashed publicly with Elon Musk in 2025. Founded by Greek Cypriot entrepreneur Sir Stelios Haji-Ioannou, easyJet is also in the middle of a £5.7 billion takeover by Apollo . The first easyJet Starlink aircraft should fly in the first half of 2027, with pricing to come. title: Insecurity driven by poverty – Peter Obi
body: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr. Peter Obi, has attributed the high level of insecurity in the country to widespread poverty. He vowed to fight poverty to reduce criminal activities across the country if given the mandate in the 2027 presidential election. The NDC presidential candidate disclosed this during a town hall meeting with stakeholders and supporters in Lokoja on Tuesday. He stated that citizens are hungry and insecure, driving some individuals into kidnapping and banditry as a desperate way out. He further stressed that the situation has become increasingly worrisome because public officers in positions of trust deliberately engage in graft and corrupt practices that divert public funds into personal interests. “An NDC-led government will fight poverty to reduce criminality. If you kidnap a person into the bush, we will follow you into the bush. We will not remain in our offices in Abuja issuing directives, but will enter the bush with you and settle matters with a heavy hand. “You cannot run away when there is trouble. I will stay and address it. An NDC government will bring down the cost of living so that the child of a nobody can become somebody without needing to know anybody,” he said. Obi highlighted that Kogi State is a tourist’s delight due to its historic position in both the pre-colonial and colonial eras. He stressed that the NDC would turn around the historical relics in the state to generate foreign exchange, create employment, and boost local income. He added that the natural endowments of Kogi and Plateau states are significant enough to attract leaders from within and outside the country to spend their holidays locally rather than traveling abroad. “If I am elected President of this country, I will not travel abroad for holidays. What people go outside the country to enjoy is right here. It only needs to be upgraded to international standards,” he said. Obi promised to visit every state to canvass for votes, emphasizing, “If you have the competence and energy to serve, come out and campaign—do not hide under any excuse.” The event attracted party stakeholders, loyalists, and supporters from across the three senatorial districts, including party candidates contesting in the general election.

title: Venezuela expects to rank fourth globally in natural gas reserves
body:
CARACAS, October 28. /TASS/. Venezuela expects to rank fourth in the world in natural gas reserves following an assessment of resources in its territorial waters and on its continental shelf, the country’s Hydrocarbons Minister Paula Henao said at the Gas Exporting Countries Forum in Moscow.
Henao noted that Venezuela currently "ranks ninth in the world in gas reserves and is projected to move into fourth place following an assessment of resources in its territorial waters and on its continental shelf." According to the country’s Hydrocarbons Ministry, the minister also announced that Venezuela had begun exporting gas.
During the summit, the minister emphasized the importance of international cooperation in mitigating the effects of climate change and addressing the sector’s challenges related to energy security, sustainable development, and energy accessibility. Henao proposed expanding cooperation among gas-exporting countries to strengthen their influence on the international market.

title: Judge to appoint special master in California voting case in setback to Trump admin
body:
The judge appeared skeptical of the DOJ's request for a restraining order.
The federal district judge overseeing the Justice Department's lawsuit asking California to segregate roughly 20,000 ballot belonging to individuals it claims are "likely" noncitizens appeared skeptical of the DOJ's efforts to seek emergency action just a week from the state's election.
U.S. District Judge David O. Carter said in court Tuesday he intends to appoint a special master to probe DOJ's process that led it to compile the list of alleged 20,000 likely non-citizens, dealing a setback to the Trump administration's attempt to quickly intervene in the election.
Judge Carter did not rule by the conclusion of the hearing on the DOJ request for a temporary restraining order against the state, though he appeared skeptical of the department's late-stage attempt to force what he described as a "monumental change" in California's ongoing administration of its election.
Carter told the parties he intends to issue some kind of ruling governing proceedings on the case moving forward by tomorrow.
Bill Essayli, a controversial Trump-installed leader of the U.S. Attorney's Office in the Central District of California, argued in the hearing that the administration was simply pushing for the state to be in compliance with federal law barring non-citizens from casting votes.
But state officials and other legal advocates opposing the DOJ lawsuit countered that the litigation violated longstanding Constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections -- and could have chaotic consequences for the state in tabulating final vote counts in the weeks ahead.
Notably in closing out the hearing, Judge Carter appeared to admonish the administration over its recent letters to state officials around California suggesting it could prosecute them if they are involved in tabulating ballots that could be from the list of alleged likely noncitizens.
"This court believes it would be wise that any threats to state and county elected employees cease immediately," Carter said. "Good night."
On Monday, a federal appeals court rejected a request from the DOJ to issue an order requiring California to set aside the 20,000 ballots from its list, kicking the back to the district court.
Earlier this month, the DOJ filed suit against California , accusing the state of failing to review the list of alleged noncitizens that the Trump administration claimed were sent mail-in ballots for next week's midterm election.
In court papers filed earlier last week, Los Angeles officials said a preliminary analysis of 200 of the names on the 20,000-person list, included a "high percentage" of individuals who say they were born in the U.S. and many more who have no voting history at all.

title: UK leader Burnham promises to fight anti-Muslim hatred after 'decade of division'
body: The UK government will soon appoint an anti-Muslim hostility adviser to avoid another “decade of division”, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said. Mr Burnham met British Muslim community leaders at Downing Street with Communities Secretary Angela Rayner, for the first time since he became leader. He acknowledged that Muslim communities across the UK had lived through “some of the worst examples of division”, including hatred online. A government adviser on Muslim affairs would be appointed shortly, he added. Akeela Ahmed , who was at the meeting and heads the watchdog British Muslim Trust, said the role was a “positive initiative” as the community faced “huge challenges”. “There is an awful lot to celebrate and build on in the British Muslim Community – there are huge successes in every field from community centres to global stars,” she told The National. “ But there are huge challenges too – anti-Muslim hate crime is rising, a mosque suffers an attack or racist incident every five days, and one in six of the wider population hold hostile views towards British Muslims. “These are issues that must be addressed and at BMT we look forward to working with a new government adviser in fighting back against the forces of division.” Mr Burnham has been under pressure to appoint an adviser since taking office this summer. A “special representative” on Muslim affairs was first promised by former prime minister Keir Starmer in March, when the government unveiled its definition of anti-Muslim hate and other measures to protect the community. The representative's role would be “to champion efforts across the UK to tackle hostility and hatred directed at Muslims and those perceived to be Muslim”, by engaging with communities, schools and other institutions. In September, veteran Labour MP Afzal Khan warned there was “a clear need for the anti-Muslim hostility tsar to be appointed” as he told the government to “get on with it”. Anti-Muslim hate crime has soared in recent years, largely due to growing far-right extremism. London has seen a six-fold increase in anti-Muslim hate incidents in the last five years, according to the British charity Tell Mama . Last year saw the highest number of annual reported incidents in London on record, at 1,909. The figure for the whole of 2026 is expected to be even higher, having already reached 1,031 by the end of June. The BMT, which is currently the government-backed watchdog, found that attacks on British mosques were becoming more severe, while lower level forms of harassment had decreased in the past year. Mr Burnham said he wanted young British Muslims to feel “that this is their country, this country is behind them, working to support them, opening up opportunity”. He also criticised the positions that opposition parties had taken towards Muslims as “completely unacceptable”. “Some of the language that they use about the community is unacceptable,” he added. The UK government will go ahead with its plans to commission a war memorial for hundreds of thousands of Muslim soldiers who died serving with the British Indian Army during the First and Second World Wars, Mr Burnham added. The project had been initiated by Mr Starmer, and is expected to cost almost £1 million ($1.33 million).

title: Tinubu Seeks $20.5bn, €1.04bn Loans, Atiku, ADC Raise the Alarm
body: • President cites infrastructure deficit, economic growth, security, agriculture, healthcare, education as priorities •Requests NASS approval for N269.4bn promissory notes to clear FG’s debts • Atiku alleges proposed borrowing may serve as campaign slush fund, demands project-by-project disclosure •ADC PCC says president mortgaging Nigeria’s future, warns of economic recolonisation • Senate refers supplementary borrowing plan to debt committee, gives one week to report Chuks Okocha, Sunday Aborisade and Juliet Akoje in Abuja President Bola Tinubu yesterday asked the National Assembly to approve a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion to finance projects and programmes across critical sectors of the economy, a move that has drawn criticism from former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and the African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC). While the President said the proposed facilities would address Nigeria’s infrastructure deficit, accelerate economic growth, generate employment and improve the living conditions of Nigerians, Atiku alleged that the borrowing request vindicated his earlier warning about a loan plan of up to $20 billion and raised concerns about the possible use of public funds for political purposes. The ADC-PCC, in a separate reaction, condemned the proposed borrowing, describing it as reckless, warning that excessive dependence on foreign loans could mortgage Nigeria’s future and set the stage for economic recolonisation. The controversy comes as President Tinubu has also sought the National Assembly’s approval for the establishment and expansion of the federal government’s Promissory Note Programme to settle outstanding verified liabilities amounting to N269.44 billon. Tinubu Seeks Approval for $20.5bn, €1.04bn External Loans Tinubu, in a letter read by Senate President Godswill Akpabio at plenary yesterday, urged the National Assembly to approve the supplementary external borrowing plan for 2026–2027 to enable the federal government to implement its projects and programmes without delay. He said the proposed borrowing plan covered infrastructure, agriculture, healthcare, education, water supply, security, employment generation and financial management reforms, among other sectors. Tinubu said, “The 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan cuts across all sectors, with specific emphasis on infrastructure, agriculture, health, education, water supply, growth, security and employment generation, as well as financial management reforms, amongst others.” Explaining the rationale for the request, the President said the need to sustain economic growth following the implementation of his administration’s reforms had made additional external financing necessary. “In light of the critical reforms of my administration, the need to accelerate growth of the national economy provides support for the External Borrowing Plan, which amounts to $20,517,755,901 and €1,045,083,643,” he said. He added that the projects and programmes covered by the plan had undergone technical and economic assessments to establish their potential contributions to national development. “I want to emphasise that the projects and programmes included in the Borrowing Plan were selected based on thorough technical and economic evaluation, as well as their anticipated contribution to the socio-economic development of the country,” Tinubu said. According to him, the proposed interventions are expected to stimulate economic activities, create jobs, promote skills acquisition, encourage entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and strengthen food security. “These initiatives aim to generate employment, promote skills acquisition, foster entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and enhance food security, all of which improve the livelihood of the Nigerian child,” he said. The President disclosed that most of the projects and programmes would be implemented across the 36 states of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory, underscoring the nationwide scope of the proposed investments. “The majority of these projects and programmes will be implemented across all the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory,” he said. Tinubu added that the scale of Nigeria’s infrastructure needs and the financial resources required to address them had made broader external borrowing necessary to bridge the funding gap. “In light of the need for significant infrastructure investment in the country and the vast financial resources needed to address this gap, it has become essential to pursue broader external borrowings to close the financing shortfall,” he said. He said the funds would be channeled primarily into critical infrastructure, particularly power, transportation and healthcare, while other sectors would also benefit from the proposed financing arrangement. “These funds will primarily be directed towards critical infrastructure projects in various sectors, including power, transportation and healthcare, amongst others,” the President said. Tinubu urged the Senate and the House of Representatives to give the proposal urgent consideration, arguing that prompt approval would facilitate timely disbursement and effective implementation of the projects. The President said, “Given the urgent nature of these needs and the importance of stabilising the country, it is crucial to seek the consideration and approval of the National Assembly leadership and the entire National Assembly for the 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan. “This will enable the government to fulfil its obligations to the Nigerian people through timely disbursements and effective project implementation.” He maintained that the proposed financing would support the implementation of development programmes and help address the country’s infrastructure funding shortfall. The letter, however, did not provide, in the material presented to the Senate, a project-by-project breakdown of the proposed facilities, the individual financing terms or the allocation of the funds among the beneficiary sectors. The proposed borrowing plan comes as the federal government seeks additional resources to finance infrastructure and development programmes amid competing demands on public finances. Its implementation will depend on the National Assembly’s consideration of the proposal and the details of the projects to be financed under the plan. Following the presentation of the letter, Akpabio referred the request to the Senate Committee on Local and Foreign Debts for consideration and directed it to report back to the chamber within one week. The committee is expected to undertake the initial legislative review of the proposal, with possible collaboration with the Senate Committee on Appropriations and other relevant committees. The request will require legislative scrutiny before the proposed external financing can proceed. Tinubu Seeks Approval for N269.4bn Promissory Notes to Clear FG Debts In a separate legislative request, Tinubu sought the National Assembly’s approval for the establishment and expansion of the federal government’s Promissory Note Programme to settle outstanding verified liabilities amounting to N269.44 billion. The request was conveyed in a letter from the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, which was read during plenary at the House of Representatives in Abuja yesterday. The proposed programme is intended to address outstanding contractual commitments, project-related debts and other financial obligations owed by the Federal Government to various categories of creditors. In the letter dated August 18, 2026, and received by the Office of the Speaker on October 21, Akume disclosed that the outstanding liabilities totaled N269,446,402,822.56, following a comprehensive review conducted by relevant ministries, departments and agencies of the Federal Government. He stated that Tinubu had approved the proposal to establish and expand the programme as a mechanism for settling the verified obligations. According to the letter, the initiative is intended to provide “a structured, transparent and fiscally responsible framework” for clearing the outstanding debts while ensuring that only claims that have been properly verified and validated are accommodated under the arrangement. The request also seeks legislative approval for the inclusion of the identified categories of liabilities and beneficiaries in the programme, subject to final verification, reconciliation and certification by the appropriate government agencies. Tinubu further requested that the National Assembly empower the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, working with the Debt Management Office and other relevant agencies, to take the necessary steps to implement the programme. Akume explained that the proposal was designed to reduce the continued accumulation of interest, penalties and other financial charges arising from the unpaid obligations. He added that the arrangement would provide relief to affected creditors and reinforce confidence in the federal government’s commitment to honouring legitimate contractual agreements and other financial responsibilities. The SGF noted that the Federal Government had previously deployed the Promissory Note Programme to settle inherited domestic debts and contractual obligations, following approval by the Federal Executive Council and subsequent authorisation by the National Assembly. He said the proposed arrangement was expected to enable the government settle the outstanding liabilities in an orderly manner without creating an immediate and disproportionate demand on its cash flow. According to the letter, the programme would also improve fiscal planning by allowing repayment obligations to be spread over an appropriate period, consistent with prudent debt management principles. Akume appealed to the House of Representatives to give the request urgent consideration, citing the substantial size of the outstanding liabilities, the length of time some of the debts had remained unpaid and the risk of further increases in interest and related costs. He said prompt legislative approval would allow the Federal Government to begin the necessary procedures for issuing the promissory notes and bringing the affected liabilities to a close. The detailed schedule of the outstanding obligations, containing the relevant categories, beneficiaries, amounts and supporting documents, was also forwarded to the National Assembly for consideration. Atiku Says Loan Request Vindicates His Warning Former Vice President and ADC presidential candidate, Atiku, said Tinubu’s request for approval to borrow $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion vindicates his October 12 warning about a loan plan of up to $20 billion. Atiku said the President’s failure to identify the specific projects the loans would fund raises serious concerns that borrowed public money could be channeled through the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway, now rerouted inland, to political campaigners and favoured contractors. In a statement issued by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku was quoted to have said: “On October 12, I warned Nigerians that President Tinubu was reportedly preparing to borrow up to $20 billion in connection with the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway. I asked him to confirm or deny the plan and publish the accounts. “He did neither. Today, he has asked the Senate to approve $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion in external loans. My warning has been vindicated. “The President has listed broad sectors but has not provided a project-by-project account of what this enormous borrowing will fund. Nigerians have not been given clear project details, costs, locations or contractors to scrutinise. “That silence is especially troubling given the highway’s inland rerouting. Nigerians have every right to ask whether it is becoming a pipeline for borrowed money to reach Tinubu’s campaigners and favoured contractors. “Barely 12 weeks before an election, how can the President ask lawmakers to saddle Nigerians with more than $20 billion and €1 billion in debt without identifying the projects and their costs? Is this a development plan for Nigerians or a campaign financing scheme dressed up as infrastructure? “You cannot continue taking frivolous loans on the eve of your departure from office. Let it be on record that one of the first responsibilities I will undertake as President is to scrutinise and investigate every kobo borrowed, especially loans taken in the final year of your tenure. Nigerians will ask questions, and we will find the answers by every lawful means. “I put local and international lenders on notice: any loan granted to this winding down administration must meet all constitutional, statutory and due process requirements. Upon assumption of office, I will scrutinise every such loan. Any borrowing found to have been obtained without proper authorisation or process will be challenged and will not be allowed to stand. “The National Assembly must not approve a single dollar until the President publishes every project, contract, cost, contractor, loan term and repayment obligation. No public money should be borrowed in the dark, and no lawmaker should sign a blank cheque against Nigeria’s future.” Atiku said the burden was on Tinubu to prove that the borrowing would serve the country, not his political interests. He urged lawmakers to publish the proposal and supporting documents and subject them to rigorous scrutiny before any decision. He added that families already struggling with a cost-of-living crisis should not be made to carry debts they did not approve. “The woman fighting to keep her business alive and the worker spending their income just to feed deserve to know where the money is going, who will benefit and who will pay,” he said. Atiku further said that Nigerians would have the opportunity at the ballot box to reject a government that borrows against their future while taking their sacrifices for granted. ADC-PCC Warns of Economic Recolonisation The ADC-PCC also condemned Tinubu’s request to the National Assembly for approval to borrow an additional $20 billion and £1 billion, describing the move as reckless, unconscionable and a dangerous step towards Nigeria’s economic recolonisation. In a statement by the Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC-PCC, Kola Ologbondiyan, the council expressed concern that the administration continued to pursue aggressive borrowing without providing Nigerians with a transparent and convincing account of how previous loans and savings from subsidy removal had been utilised. The ADC-PCC said the fresh borrowing request came at a time when Nigerians were still struggling with the devastating consequences of the administration’s economic policies, including soaring living costs, increased taxation and the removal of fuel subsidies, with millions of citizens facing worsening economic hardship. Ologbondiyan said it was alarming that the Tinubu administration was seeking additional foreign loans despite the enormous economic burden already imposed on Nigerians. “What exactly is President Tinubu borrowing all this money for?” he asked. He further queried: “Where are the roads, the electricity, the hospitals, the jobs and the critical infrastructure that should justify this relentless accumulation of debt?
