Nigerians deserve answers. “Where is the money saved from fuel subsidy removal? What happened to the previous loans? And why must the government return to the international credit market with another $20 billion and £1 billion when millions of Nigerians are struggling to survive?” Ologbondiyan said the development raised serious questions about the administration’s fiscal priorities, economic direction and commitment to accountability. According to him, “This is not a sustainable path to national development. It is a dangerous attempt to mortgage the future of Nigeria and generations yet unborn. A country cannot continue to accumulate foreign debt without a clear, measurable and transparent account of the benefits accruing to its citizens. “President Tinubu cannot continue to impose painful economic sacrifices on Nigerians, claim the benefits of subsidy removal and, at the same time, seek enormous additional loans without adequately explaining how the resources already available to his government have been spent.” The ADC-PCC argued that an economic strategy built primarily on borrowing and increased taxation, without corresponding improvements in productivity, infrastructure, employment and citizens’ welfare, risked pushing the country deeper into a debt trap. It warned that excessive dependence on foreign creditors could expose Nigeria to mounting debt-servicing obligations, constrain future governments’ policy choices and undermine the country’s economic sovereignty. The council further observed that the administration must demonstrate how the proposed borrowing would contribute to productive investment, economic growth and improved living standards rather than impose additional liabilities on future generations. “The sovereignty of Nigeria must not be compromised by fiscal recklessness. Our national assets, economic independence and the welfare of future generations must not become casualties of an endless borrowing spree,” Ologbondiyan said. The ADC-PCC therefore called on the National Assembly to subject the proposed borrowing to rigorous scrutiny and reject it unless the Federal Government provided compelling evidence of its necessity, sustainability and tangible benefits to the Nigerian people. It also demanded that Tinubu publish a comprehensive account of all domestic and foreign borrowing undertaken since May 29, 2023, alongside a detailed breakdown of the revenue realised from subsidy removal and how the funds had been applied. The council further called for full disclosure of the proposed loans’ purposes, interest rates, repayment periods, associated fees, conditionalities and any collateral or guarantees attached to the facilities. It insisted that Nigerians had a constitutional and democratic right to know the obligations being incurred in their name and the implications for the country’s fiscal future. “Nigeria cannot borrow its way out of poor economic management. Borrowing must be tied to clearly defined national priorities, transparent expenditure and measurable outcomes. Anything less is an injustice to the Nigerian people. “The National Assembly must not abdicate its oversight responsibilities. It must insist on accountability and ensure that no borrowing arrangement places the country’s future at unacceptable risk. “Nigerians must not be compelled to pay indefinitely for loans whose purposes, terms and benefits remain unclear. Our country must not mortgage its future through opaque and unsustainable borrowing,” the ADC-PCC stated.

title: Leadership Names Obaigbena, Rabiu Persons of Year 2026
body: • Cites businessmen’s contributions to innovation, job creation, others Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja Leadership Newspapers has named the Chairman of THISDAY Group and founder of Arise News, Prince Nduka Obaigbena, and the Chairman of BUA Group, Abdul Samad Rabiu, as its Persons of the Year 2026. The newspaper announced the recognition, while citing the businessmen’s contributions to institution-building, talent development, innovation, investment, job creation and philanthropy. According to Leadership, the duo are being honoured for “building influential institutions, nurturing talent, challenging convention, and breaking new ground” in their respective fields. Also yesterday, Leadership Newspapers presented the formal notification of Obaigbena as Person of the Year 2026 at the Ikoyi Offices of Arise News Channel in Lagos. Present at the event were: Ombudsman, Kayode Komolafe; Leadership Newspapers Vice Chairman & Editor in Chief, Azu Ishiekwene; Leadership Newspapers Chairman, Mrs Zainab Sam Nda Isaiah; THISDAY Managing Director, Eniola Bello and Arise News Director of Politics, Akin Osuntokun. Obaigbena was recognised for his contributions to Nigeria’s media industry, particularly his role in expanding the country’s media landscape and launching the Leekelee social media platform in February 2026. Rabiu, on his part, was recognised for BUA Group’s investments in manufacturing and local production, as well as its contributions to job creation, infrastructure development and shareholder value. The newspaper also highlighted the philanthropic activities of both businessmen, noting their contributions to strengthening confidence in Nigeria’s future. It described the recognition as an acknowledgement of their influence and impact on the country’s economic and social development. Earlier, the newspaper said Obaigbena had built influential media organisations, nurtured generations of journalists and expanded the reach of Nigerian and African media through investments spanning newspapers, magazines, television, fashion and digital platforms. It cited his founding of ThisWeek magazine in 1986 and THISDAY newspaper in 1995 as defining milestones in his career, noting that both publications introduced new approaches to journalism and newspaper production in Nigeria. Obaigbena founded ThisWeek at the age of 27, establishing a publication that covered politics, economics, international affairs, art and culture. The magazine also became a platform for talented journalists, many of whom went on to occupy prominent positions in the media industry and public life. His entry into newspaper publishing with THISDAY further expanded his influence, with the publication introducing innovations in presentation, editorial content and the commercial positioning of Nigerian newspapers. Leadership noted that THISDAY began operations without Obaigbena owning a printing press, while highlighting its adoption of colour production, the elevation of the back page as a platform for prominent columnists and the publication of the full table of daily transactions at the Nigerian Stock Exchange. Beyond newspaper publishing, Obaigbena, it said, extended his entrepreneurial interests into broadcasting, fashion and entertainment, establishing platforms designed to promote African talent and connect the continent’s creative industry with international audiences. These included ARISE Magazine, the THISDAY Music and Fashion Festivals, and ARISE Fashion Week, which provided platforms for Nigerian and other African creatives to showcase their work to wider audiences. In 2013, he launched ARISE News, an international television news platform with an African focus and global outlook, aimed at strengthening African perspectives in international news coverage. Leadership described the launch of LekeeLekee, a social media platform developed by ARISE Broadcast and THISDAY Media Group in February 2026, as another significant step in Obaigbena’s efforts to expand Africa’s presence in the digital media landscape. The newspaper said the platform had recorded more than 100,000 downloads within about six months, describing its launch as evidence of his continued interest in exploring new frontiers in media and technology. It added that Obaigbena’s career had been marked by a willingness to take risks, assemble exceptional talent and build institutions despite economic constraints, technological disruption and the challenges confronting traditional journalism. It noted that his media organisations had navigated changing governments, economic recessions and the pressures of digital transformation, while continuing to seek new ways of remaining commercially viable and relevant to society. Born on July 14, 1959, in Ibadan, Oyo State, Obaigbena attended Edo College, Benin City, before obtaining an honours degree in Creative Arts from the University of Benin. He began his media career in 1978 at the Nigerian Observer, where he developed his skills in writing, satire and cartooning. He subsequently became coordinating editor of The Dawn magazine and worked as a Special Section Representative for Newsweek. His professional experience also included work with Time magazine on special surveys and country sections covering Nigeria, Kenya, Morocco and Zimbabwe. Obaigbena also participated in public affairs, serving on a sub-committee of the Technical Committee on Privatisation and Commercialisation in 1990. He contested for a seat in the Senate in 1991 and became a member of the 1994 Constitutional Conference. His contributions to the media profession have earned him several honours and leadership responsibilities. He received the Fellowship of the Nigerian Guild of Editors in 1998 and served two terms as president of the Newspaper Proprietors’ Association of Nigeria (NPAN). He also chaired the Nigerian Press Organisation (NPO). In 2022, the federal government conferred on him the national honour of Commander of the Order of the Niger (CON). The following year, he received the Lifetime Achievement Award from the Diamond Awards for Media Excellence (DAME) in recognition of his contributions to journalism and society. Leadership said Obaigbena’s enduring significance lay in the institutions he had established, the conventions he had challenged and the opportunities he had created for successive generations of media professionals. It described him as an institution-builder whose career demonstrated that African media organisations could pursue global ambitions while retaining their roots and perspectives. The newspaper said his recognition reflected a career built on the conviction that ambitious ideas, supported by talent, execution and perseverance, could overcome the constraints often associated with operating in Nigeria’s media environment.

title: Mbah inaugurates 51-directorates strong Enugu APC Campaign Council, banks on scorecard
body:
Governor of Enugu State, Peter Mbah, on Tuesday, inaugurated the All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Council for Enugu State comprising 51 directorates. The governor dismissed the opposition as shallow and expressed strong confidence in a resounding victory for the APC in all the 2027 elections.
The Campaign Council which is chaired by Governor Mbah himself also has the Deputy Governor, Ifeanyi Ossai; Deputy National Chairman, APC (South); Speaker, Enugu State House of Assembly, Hon Uchenna Ugwu; Chairman of the party in the state, Dr Martin Chukwunweike; and the Secretary to the State Government, Prof Chidiebere Onyia as deputy and vice chairmen.
Headlined by an Advisory Council comprising several eminent personalities, the campaign council has Chief Charlie Mbah as the Director-General, while Dr Eric Oluedo serves as the Secretary-General.
Senator Osita Ngwu, Senator Ikeje Asogwa, and Senator Kelvin Chukwu are Coordinators of the Campaign Council in Enugu West, Enugu North, and Enugu East, respectively.
Speaking at the event, which took place at the International Conference Centre, Enugu, Governor Mbah said his administration had justified the mandate handed to him in 2023, while President Bola Tinubu’s bold reforms had greatly stabilised the macroeconomic indicators while also making funds available for the administration to embark on impactful projects across the state on a large scale.
He, therefore, urged party faithful to campaign hard on the administration’s achievements and be unapologetically APC in doing so, saying the opposition had nothing but propaganda to offer.
The governor said he was gearing up to campaign in each of the 68 Development Centres and also commission at least two projects in each of the 260 political wards in the state.
Mbah recalled that the 2026 Phillips Consulting State Performance Momentum Index ranked Enugu as the fastest-improving state, having recorded a Momentum Score of +1.15, the highest by any of the 33 states assessed.
He noted that, in terms of Ease of Doing Business, the state, under his leadership, had leaped from 36th out of 37 subnationals in 2023 to sixth position nationally in 2025, according to the Presidential Enabling Business Environment Council (PEBEC) report.
“So, you should be proud of Enugu. You should be unapologetically APC. I am really excited because we are going to go to all the 68 Development Centres. I will personally visit all the Development Centres. I will go to the markets with you.
“The people of Enugu cannot wait to see us. They are so excited. And as I go, I will also take time to go to every ward to commission both the Smart Green School and the Primary Healthcare Centre.
“As I go to every ward and Development Centre, I will commission all projects without exception, the Smart Green Schools and the Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres in all the wards where they are cutting the ribbon. And so, it is indeed my honour and privilege to formally inaugurate this APC Enugu State Campaign Council,” he stated.
Mbah, however, reminded them that all the achievements could not have been possible without the economic reforms and support of the President Bola Tinubu administration, which had, among other things, made more funds available to the states.
“We must also campaign hard for the President because it also took those bold and courageous policies of his to achieve what we accomplished in the last three years. You can have all this vision and conviction, but if you do not back it up with money, you cannot do anything. Therefore, we also need to recognise and acknowledge that,” he stated.
Mbah also listed several major infrastructural interventions by President Tinubu in the South East, and Enugu State in particular, noting that although the region gave him a marginal percentage of its votes in 2023, he had nevertheless shown good faith towards Ndigbo in terms of development projects, strategic appointments, among others.
The Deputy Governor, Ifeanyi Ossai; Speaker, Enugu State House of Assembly, Hon Uchenna Ugwu; Deputy National Chairman (South) of the APC, Dr Ben Nwoye; Senator Osita Ngwu, who spoke on behalf of all serving and aspiring National Assembly members; Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr Kingsley Udeh, SAN; Chairman of the party in the state, Dr Martin Chukwunweike; Commissioner for Children, Gender Affairs and Social Development, Mrs Ngozi Enih; and former Ambassador of Nigeria to Switzerland and Liechtenstein, Mrs Fidelia Njeze, charged the people to go all out for victory, enumerating the many achievements of the Mbah administration and the benefits of the Tinubu government to Enugu State.
In his remarks, the Director-General of the Campaign Organisation, Chief Charlie Mbah, while thanking the party leaders and faithful for the confidence reposed in him and his team, promised to lead a formidable campaign that would guarantee APC’s victory in the state.
“My commitment is to build an inclusive, organised, result-oriented and issues-based campaign that reaches every senatorial zone, local government area, ward, community, and polling unit across Enugu State,” he reassured.
Other members of the Council Composition include:
Deacon Okey Ogbodo, Dr Dan Shere, and Hon. S K E Udeh-Okoye are Deputy Campaign DGs for Enugu East Senatorial District, Enugu North Senatorial District, and Enugu West Senatorial District, respectively.
Steve Oruruo is the Campaign Spokesperson and Director of the Public Communication Committee, with Dr Austin Okolie as co-spokesperson and Dr Malachy Agbo as Secretary.
Mazi Uche Anichukwu and Dan Nwomeh, both drawn from the Governor’s media team, head the Directorate of New Media and Strategic Communication and the Directorate of Mainstream Media, respectively. DrCollins Ogbu is the Secretary of the former, while Dr. Reuben Onyishi is the Secretary of the latter.
Victor Udeh leads the Administration Directorate, while Dr Ben Nwoye and Uche Nwatu are the Director and Co-Director of the Fundraising Committee, respectively.
Former Chief of the Naval Staff, Vice Admiral Ikechukwu Ogalla (Rtd.), chairs the Security Directorate, while former Inspector-General of Police, Ogbono Onovo (Rtd.), is the Secretary.
The Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology is in charge of the Directorate of Government Appointees Coordination (Federal and State), with Prof Chidiebere Onyia as Secretary, while former Speaker of the Enugu State House of Assembly, Hon Eugene Odoh, heads Inter-Party Affairs.
APC State Woman Leader, Mrs Esther Edeh, is at the helm of the Women Mobilisation Directorate, with the APC South East Woman Leader, Dr Oby Ajih, as Co-Director and Commissioner for Children, Gender Affairs and Social Development, Mrs Ngozi Enih, as Secretary.
Senator Chuka Utazi heads the Directorate of Parliamentary Mobilisation, with former Deputy Minority Leader, Hon Toby Okechukwu, as Secretary, while Senator Ben Collins Ndu is the Director of Contact and Mobilisation, with Peter Okonkwo as Co-Director and Mrs Lovelyn Obioma Nweze appointed as Secretary.
Victor Udeh is the Director of the Directorate of Election Planning and Monitoring, which has the Political Adviser to the Governor, Chief Frank Anioma, as Secretary.
Commissioner for Culture and Tourism, Dame Ugochi Madueke, leads the Directorate of Welfare, which has Mrs Amaka Alinta as Secretary, while Dame Rita Mbah is the Director of Event Management, with Ifeoma Azike as Secretary.
Commissioner for Chieftaincy Affairs, Chief Charles Egumgbe, leads the Directorate of Monitoring, which has former Speaker of the Enugu State House of Assembly, Hon Edward Ubosi, as Secretary.
Uchenna Nwobodo is in charge of the Directorate of Works and Venue, with Christian Enebe as Secretary.
Hon USA Igweshi has returned to his 2023 role as Director of the Directorate of Support Groups, while Dr Chiedozie Nwafor will serve as Secretary.
The Town Unions Coordination Directorate is headed by Chief Arinze Ogbodo, while the secretariat will be manned by Hon Charles Chime.

title: IPO: Dangote Refinery Sets Record with Interest from 119 Nations, Faces Allocation Dilemma
body: • Landmark offer achieves 100% African participation, reaches all six continents • Aliko: Africa has shown it can finance, build and own its industrial future • Refinery to reap over $60m in annual gross operational benefits from AI deployment Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja The Initial Public Offering (IPO) of the Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals has attracted investors from 119 countries, setting up a potential allocation squeeze as demand from Nigerian, African and international investors may likely exceed the shares available for sale. The offer has secured between $1.5 billion and $1.6 billion in fully funded commitments from domestic and retail investors alone, effectively meeting its fundraising target before accounting for additional demand from overseas investors, according to a Bloomberg report citing people familiar with the transaction. The development underscores the scale of international interest in the equity offering by Africa’s largest refinery, valued at nearly $50 billion, and raises the prospect that some investors may not receive the allocations they seek. The company is expected to exercise an additional 30 per cent overallotment option, which could increase the total amount raised to approximately $2.1 billion and create room for more international investors. However, demand could still exceed the available shares even if the option is fully exercised, the report said. The IPO attracted applications from investors in all 54 African countries for the first time, while the total number of countries represented in the offering had reached 119 at the time of the report. The breadth of participation reflects efforts by Aliko Dangote, Africa’s richest man, to widen ownership of the refinery beyond Nigeria and encourage greater participation by African investors in the continent’s industrial assets. Dangote extended the closing date for applications by two weeks to October 27, allowing his team to engage investors across Africa and put structures in place to broaden participation beyond the Nigerian market. “We have more than reached our target,” Dangote said in Gaborone, Botswana, on October 14, adding that the refinery had attracted interest of “more than three times or four times what we are looking for.” The offer includes nominee structures involving Standard Bank Group for investors in Egypt and Ethiopia, as well as global depository receipts being sold through stock exchanges in Kenya and Botswana. The transaction is being closely watched as a test of the capacity of African capital markets to mobilise substantial domestic and regional funds for large-scale industrial projects without relying primarily on international financial centres such as London and New York. If demand significantly exceeds the shares available, Dangote could consider selling part of his personal stake to investors who fail to secure sufficient allocations through the IPO. However, people familiar with the process said no decision had been made on a secondary sale, which would depend on the final order book. The offering provides investors with an opportunity to take stakes in one of Africa’s most strategically significant industrial assets, whose scale has the potential to reshape petroleum product supply across Nigeria and the wider region. Beyond the equity offering, the refinery is also deploying advanced digital technology in an effort to improve operating efficiency and profitability, with industrial technology company Honeywell announcing the introduction of an artificial intelligence platform projected to generate more than $60 million in annual gross operational benefits at full capacity. The platform, known as Forge Plant Cognition, combines Honeywell’s industrial expertise with artificial intelligence and accelerated computing capabilities from NVIDIA and AI infrastructure from Dell Technologies. According to Honeywell, preliminary estimates indicate that the technology could deliver operational benefits exceeding $0.29 per barrel processed at the refinery. The company cautioned, however, that the projections are based on preliminary data and are not guaranteed. The system is designed to combine real-time operating data, engineering knowledge and physics-based models to help operators identify constraints, anticipate potential problems and improve plant performance. Unlike conventional AI applications that primarily analyse data and generate recommendations, Honeywell said the platform integrates industrial automation and process technology expertise with AI-driven analysis to support operational decisions. “Industrial plants are among the most complex operating environments in the world, with enormous potential to realise greater performance and value using digital technologies and connected solutions,” said President of Honeywell Technologies, Rajesh Gattupalli. The deployment is also expected to strengthen the capabilities of the refinery’s local engineering and operations teams, as Dangote Industries pursues a major expansion of its refining operations in Nigeria and elsewhere in Africa. In November 2025, Dangote Industries partnered with Honeywell to support plans to increase the Lagos refinery’s nameplate capacity from 650,000 barrels per day to 1.4 million barrels per day by 2028. The proposed expansion would more than double the facility’s original design capacity and increase its potential to supply petroleum products to Nigeria and international markets. The refinery’s processing capacity reached 700,000 barrels per day in June 2026, marking a further step towards the expansion target. Dangote’s engagement with Honeywell also extends beyond Nigeria. In September 2026, the industrial group selected the technology company to provide engineering services, licensing and equipment for its proposed 700,000-barrel-per-day refinery in Lamu County, Kenya. Separately, the refinery yesterday said that the IPO achieved 100 per cent geographical coverage of Africa, stressing that more than a conventional fundraising exercise, the offer has emerged as a landmark in financial inclusion, demonstrating how digital technology, coordinated financial institutions and innovative distribution channels can connect millions of potential investors to opportunities previously dominated by institutional and high-net-worth participants. It said the transaction was supported by an extensive network of commercial banks, stockbroking firms, fintech platforms, capital market institutions and distribution partners, whose collaboration expanded access to the offer across national boundaries and created new pathways for retail participation. President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, described the outcome as a powerful affirmation of African confidence, enterprise and the continent’s ability to mobilise its own resources for development. “When we set out to build this refinery, many doubted that a project of this scale could be delivered by Africans. We proved that Africa could build it. Today, through this historic IPO, we have demonstrated something equally important: Africans are ready to own and participate in the prosperity created by their own industries. “To have investor applications from all 54 African countries is deeply significant to me. It tells us that our people do not simply want to consume what Africa produces; they want to invest in it, own it and share in its future. This is the Africa we have always believed in,” he said. “We did not undertake this IPO simply because we needed to raise capital. We wanted to open the doors of ownership, give ordinary Africans an opportunity to participate in an enterprise of global significance and establish a new culture of shared prosperity. The refinery was built in Africa, by African determination, and its future must create opportunities for Africans. Today, we have made history together. “But the greater achievement will be the generation of African investors, entrepreneurs and industrialists that this transaction inspires. Our ambition is not merely to build successful businesses. It is to help build a prosperous, self-reliant Africa whose people are participants in its economic destiny. “As we advance our expansion programme and Vision 2030 strategy, we remain committed to strengthening our operational performance, deepening our contribution to Africa’s energy security and building an enterprise that rewards the confidence placed in it,” he stated. Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals, David Bird, said the international response reflected confidence in the refinery’s operating capabilities, industrial scale and long-term growth prospects. “The successful conclusion of this IPO is a remarkable milestone for Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals. Investor applications spanning 120 countries demonstrate the extraordinary international interest in our business and the confidence that investors are placing in the future of this refinery. “We have built one of the world’s most significant refining and petrochemical complexes, and our focus remains on translating that industrial scale into operational excellence, sustainable growth and long-term shareholder value,” he said. The refinery’s IPO opened on September 14, 2026, offering 4.1 billion ordinary shares at N525 per share, representing a proposed capital raise of approximately N2.15 trillion. Initially scheduled to close on October 13, the offer was extended to October 27 following approval by the Securities and Exchange Commission, allowing additional time for investors across Africa and other international markets to participate. Group Chief Financial Officer, Dangote Industries Limited, Murat Erden, speaking on the execution and wider significance of the offering, said the transaction had established an important precedent for the continent’s capital markets. “The Dangote Refinery People’s IPO represents much more than a landmark capital-raising exercise. It marks a defining moment in the evolution of African capital markets, demonstrating our continent’s ability to mobilise domestic savings, connect investors across borders and broaden ownership of strategic industrial assets. “Reaching investors in 120 countries, including all 54 African nations, is an extraordinary achievement and a powerful testament to the growing investment appetite across our continent. By bringing together banks, capital market institutions, stockbrokers, fintech platforms and innovative digital distribution channels, we have demonstrated that African capital markets can transcend national boundaries and connect millions of people to investment opportunities previously beyond their reach,” he said.

title: Dangote refinery IPO draws three times target demand, sources say
body: Nigeria’s $1.6 billion Dangote refinery initial ‌public offering has drawn about three times the total targeted orders, two people with knowledge of the situation said, underscoring strong demand for what has been billed as “The People’s IPO”. The share sale, which closes on Tuesday, has about 6.4 trillion naira ($4.78 billion) in orders from Nigerian retail and institutional investors, one person involved told Reuters. Aliko Dangote, the billionaire owner of the Lagos refinery, said the sale is targeting millions of ordinary Nigerians and Africans who can buy shares for as little as $4. The order book is expected to grow once subscriptions from investors in other African countries are included, one of the people said, adding that Dangote has received subscriptions from more than 2 million investors through digital channels so far. Given the demand, Dangote was expected to exercise a greenshoe option that would allow it to increase the offering size to as much as $2.1 billion, the person added. A ⁠Dangote spokesperson declined to comment on the demand and possibility of exercising the greenshoe option. The IPO comes as Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE has benefited from stronger margins, with higher crude oil prices linked to the Iran war lifting earnings. The refinery, which began commercial operations in early 2024, has steadily increased output and expanded exports, including shipments of jet fuel to Europe and other African markets, helping position Nigeria as a potential net exporter of refined petroleum products. Share allocation will begin ​next week ⁠ahead of the stock’s planned listing on the Nigerian Exchange later in November, the company’s IPO prospectus said. Built at a cost of about $20 billion, the refinery has transformed Nigeria’s fuel ⁠market since ​it began operating. It processes about 700,000 barrels of ​crude oil per day and aims to double capacity to 1.4 million barrels per day by 2029.

title: FG, WAHO Seek Regional Plan to Retain Health Workers, Tackle Japa Syndrome
body: Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja The federal government has canvassed stronger regional cooperation and practical measures to address migration of health workers and improve healthcare delivery across West Africa. The government’s position came just as the West African Health Organisation (WAHO) said that Africa accounts for 24 percent of global disease burden but only three percent of global health workforce. Quoting 2025 UK report, WAHO said that 85,000 to 90,000 Nigerian-trained doctors and nurses were registered in UK. The further organization projected that additional 4.2 million workers will be needed by 2030, Minister of State for Health, Dr. Adekunle Salako, while declaring open a meeting to review the regional work plan for motivation and retention of health workers in ECOWAS member countries said there are lans to grow the number of health workers in Africa. The meeting, organised by West African Health Organisation (WAHO), seeks to develop strategies for retaining skilled professionals, improving workforce planning and strengthening health systems across the sub-region. Salako, represented by Dr. Ovuoraye John, Director and Head of Department of Health Planning, Research and Statistics, said regional plan will complement continental initiative targeting two million community health workers across Africa by 2028. He said meeting coincided with 50th anniversary activities of West African College of Physicians and high-level African Union forum on community health workforce scheduled for Abuja from October 28 to 30. According to him, simultaneous meetings reflect growing recognition that health workforce challenge requires coordinated action at national, regional and continental levels. “We now know that we cannot do it alone in silos. We need every resource available to us as a country to get it right. The health workforce is the challenge that we are facing on our continent,” Salako said. He expressed satisfaction that three initiatives were taking place in Nigeria at same time, describing convergence as opportunity to align regional and continental priorities. On public health security, Salako urged participants to observe Nigeria’s Ebola prevention protocols, saying country had continued to allow public gatherings despite recording a confirmed case. He said no additional cases have been recorded since initial confirmation, with contact tracing expanded to 53 persons as of Sunday, all monitored and those at risk tested negative. He said index patient was recovering though evacuated to Switzerland earlier in day. Representative of West African College of Surgeons, Prof. Foluso Owoeye, said success of healthcare systems depends not only on infrastructure but on competence, motivation and availability of health workers. He described migration of health professionals, commonly called brain drain or japa, as major threat to sustainability and quality of healthcare in West Africa, warning those huge investments in training will have limited value if countries fail to create conditions for retention. He urged that work plans contain practical measures, measurable targets, realistic timelines and clear responsibilities, with stronger links between training and retention, including mentorship, research and career advancement. WAHO Director General, Prof. Palokinam Pitch, represented by Director of Public Health and Research, Prof. Joseph Olorunda, said Authority of Heads of State had directed that the document be completed to guide retention planning for next 5, 10, 15 and 20 years before presentation to Assembly of Health Ministers. Pitch said work had begun on harmonising training curricula, with 58 curricula developed to ease mobility of professionals across ECOWAS states. He said region needs long-term planning to address departure of professionals amid growing challenges including non-communicable diseases and climate change. WAHO said that Africa accounts for 24 percent of global disease burden but only three percent of health workforce, with projection of additional 4.2 million workers needed by 2030, while 2025 UK report showed 85,000 to 90,000 Nigerian-trained doctors and nurses registered in UK. The proposed framework is expected to promote improved remuneration, supportive working environment, career development and evidence-based staffing for underserved communities.

title: Fayemi Mourns Bishop Ajakaye’s Mother, Extols Her Legacy of Faith and Discipline
body: Gbenga Sodeinde in Ado-Ekiti A former governor of Ekiti State, Dr. Kayode Fayemi, has commiserated with the Catholic Bishop of Ekiti Diocese, Most Rev. Felix Femi Ajakaye, over the death of his mother, Mama Florence Funmilayo Ajakaye, describing her as a woman whose enduring values were reflected in the exemplary life and ministry of her son. In a condolence message dated October 26, 2026, Fayemi expressed deep sadness over the passing of the matriarch and extended his heartfelt sympathies to Bishop Ajakaye, the entire Ajakaye family, and the Catholic faithful in Ekiti State and beyond. The former governor noted that although the death of a mother creates an irreplaceable void, the memories of her love, sacrifices and moral upbringing would continue to serve as a source of strength and comfort for the bereaved family. Fayemi said the late Mama Ajakaye’s virtues could be seen in the life of the Catholic Bishop, whom he described as a model of faith, humility, discipline, selfless service and commitment to the physical and spiritual well-being of others. According to Fayemi, whose condolence message was conveyed on behalf of hmself, his wife, Bisi, and the entire Fayemi family, the bishop’s outstanding character and dedication to the service of God stood as a testament to the quality of upbringing and enduring values instilled in him by his late mother. “The character of a child often bears testimony to the life and values of the parent. The virtues you exemplify are a fitting testament to a mother whose life must have been marked by diligence, dedication, selflessness and an unwavering commitment to raising her children in the fear of God and in the enduring principles of integrity and discipline,” Fayemi stated. While praying God to grant Bishop Ajakaye, the Ajakaye family and all who mourn Mama Florence Funmilayo Ajakaye the strength to bear the painful loss, Fayemi also prayed for the peaceful repose of the deceased, saying her legacy of sacrifice, faith and virtue would continue to inspire generations.

title: Russia trip constructive, fruitful: Pezeshkian
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 28 (MNA) – President Masoud Pezeshkian said his two-day trip to Russia was constructive and fruitful, citing good understandings at the Gas Exporting Countries Forum summit and meetings with the Russian and Qatari leaders.
President Masoud Pezeshkian said his two-day trip to Russia was constructive and fruitful, with detailed and deep talks and interactions during the eighth Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) summit leading to favorable understandings.
In remarks before leaving Russia on Tuesday evening, Pezeshkian said the summit produced positive results and was constructive and fruitful.
He cited effective meetings and interactions with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Qatar's Emir on the sidelines of the summit.
Pezeshkian said understandings were reached in various fields, including agriculture, oil and gas, road construction, security issues and bilateral cooperation. He described the trip overall as very favorable and effective.

title: Yahaya Joins Osinbajo, Barau Four Govs at Gov Fintiri’s 59th Birthday Lecture in Yola
body: Segun Awofadeji in Gombe Gombe State Governor, Alhaji Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, yesterday, joined former Vice President Yemi Osinbajo, Deputy Senate President Barau Jibrin, Adamawa State Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri and their counterparts from Borno, Bauchi, Taraba and Plateau States at a special lecture organised to mark Fintiri’s 59th birthday. The event was attended by prominent political leaders, statesmen, traditional rulers, academics and other dignitaries to celebrate the Adamawa governor and reflect on issues of leadership, governance and national development. Osinbajo delivered the birthday lecture, titled, “Democracy and Development: The Imperative of People-Centred Governance” at the Banquet Hall of the Adamawa Government House. Ahead of the event, the Gombe governor had, in a goodwill message published in national newspapers, paid tribute to Fintiri, congratulating his Adamawa counterpart on the milestone and acknowledging his contributions to governance. “Today, we join your family, friends and well-wishers in celebrating a life defined by service, commitment and an enduring passion for the development and progress of Adamawa State, the Northeast and Nigeria at large. “We are profoundly grateful to Almighty Allah for the gift of your life, the wisdom He has bestowed upon you, and the compassion and sense of responsibility that continue to distinguish your leadership. “Over the years, we have been privileged to travel this path together, not only as colleagues, but as brothers united by a shared commitment to the growth, peace and prosperity of the Northeast”. Yahaya prayed Almighty Allah to continue to grant Fintiri good health, wisdom, strength and renewed energy to keep serving his people and contributing even more to the advancement of the North-East and Nigeria. Governor Inuwa Yahaya was accompanied to Yola by APC governorship candidate, Dr. Jamil Isyaku Gwamna; House of Assembly Member, Hon. Ali Baba Manu; President of Velocity Group, Aliyu Mohammed Combat; and Alhaji Mala Sheriff, among other officials and aides.

title: Tinubu: S’East Must Move to Realities, Gas Pipeline Will Boost Industrialisation in Zone
body: *Mbah: Inadequate energy supply, poor connectivity remain our major challenges Gideon Arinze in Enugu President Bola Tinubu has reaffirmed his commitment to industrialising the Southeast, declaring that the region must move beyond promises to tangible economic development. Tinubu spoke yesterday in Enugu at the launch of the Southeast Gas Distribution Pipeline Infrastructure Project, an initiative of the Southeast Development Commission (SEDC), through the Southeast Investment Company (SEIC). The project, launched in partnership with Gas Sync and NNPC Gas Marketing Limited (NNPC NGML), proposes a 400-kilometre pipeline network connecting the ANOH Gas Processing Plant in Imo State to major industrial and commercial centres across the five Southeast states. The pipeline is expected to improve energy access, attract investments and stimulate regional economic growth. Represented by the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Benjamin Kalu, the president said the project responded to the need for reliable energy infrastructure to support businesses and manufacturing in the region. He called on investors, industrialists and manufacturers to explore Southeast’s economic opportunities, noting that energy security remained a key commitment of his administration under the Renewed Hope Agenda. “Energy infrastructure will reduce costs, create jobs and expand opportunities. Nigeria has substantial gas resources, and the Southeast has its fair share, but we must use them to create jobs and prosperity for our people,” he said. Tinubu said manufacturers should not have to spend more on generating electricity than expanding their businesses, stressing the need for infrastructure that supports enterprise and industrial production. “The prosperity of the region is inseparable from the prosperity of the entire country. We cannot achieve our full economic potential when any region operates below its economic potential,” he said. In his address, Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah, said inadequate energy supply and poor connectivity had remained major challenges to industrial development in the Southeast. According to him, unreliable energy increases production costs, limits business expansion and weakens the competitiveness of enterprises across the region. Mbah said the proposed pipeline would provide opportunities for young people to build businesses and secure employment within the region rather than travel elsewhere in search of jobs. “Enugu State alone has more than 20 tertiary institutions graduating young people annually. Reliable energy would help them turn their ideas into viable enterprises. “Enugu alone has four gas fields that remain unexploited. This shows the massive opportunities we have, and we also have reserves in other states. We cannot wait to see the project become a reality,” Mbah said. The governor commended Tinubu for supporting the establishment of the SEDC, describing the commission as an important step towards addressing the region’s industrial development needs. Earlier, the Managing Director of the SEDC, Mark Okoye, said the commission was committed to promoting inclusive prosperity and creating economic development opportunities across the region. Okoye also proposed the establishment of a Southeast Oil and Gas Week to bring stakeholders together to discuss investment opportunities and challenges in the sector. The Deputy Governors of Ebonyi, Anambra and Imo States, Princess Patricia Onyemaechi, Dr Gilbert Ibezim and Chinyere Ihuoma, respectively, commended the SEDC for initiating the project. They pledged their states’ cooperation to ensure its successful implementation.

title: State Police: Presidency Tasks Private Sector To Develop Comprehensive Funding, Implementation Blueprint
body: Deji Elumoye in Abuja The Presidency has tasked organised private sector in the country to develop a comprehensive financing and implementation blueprint for the proposed state police system. It stated that businesses must take an active role in building the security institutions required to protect investments, create jobs and strengthen economic resilience. Chief of Staff to the President and Chairman of the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill, Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila, who gave the challenge, particularly charged the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG), chambers of commerce and business associations with producing practical proposals for financing, institutional management and accountable partnerships to support the decentralisation of policing. According to him, the private sector has a direct stake in the success of the reform because insecurity was already imposing enormous costs on businesses through disrupted supply chains, abandoned investments, postponed factory expansions and lost economic opportunities. Speaking during a plenary session on “Security, Stability and Economic Resilience” at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit in Abuja, Gbajabiamila said President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to establishing state police presented an opportunity for businesses to contribute directly to the development of security institutions capable of supporting sustainable economic growth. “I therefore ask the Nigerian Economic Summit Group to carry this engagement beyond our meeting. Bring forward a considered private sector contribution on financing and implementing state police, with practical proposals for accountable partnerships. “Take that work into the legislative process and into your engagement with state governments. For our part, we remain answerable for turning reform into protection that people can rely on,” he said. Gbajabiamila urged business leaders to engage governors and legislators on the proposed reform, drawing attention to the relationship between effective local policing, employment generation and investment decisions. He explained that the experience of businesses in managing institutions, controlling expenditure and assessing risks could strengthen the design and implementation of the new policing framework. According to him, the organised private sector should also provide evidence of security failures preventing otherwise viable investments from proceeding, enabling policymakers to determine where additional security capacity was most urgently required. “His words: “Your participation should also improve the substance of the reform. As the legislative process proceeds, examine the proposals for financing and oversight. “Bring your experience of managing institutions and controlling expenditure to that discussion. Help us understand the security failures that prevent viable projects from proceeding.” The Chief of Staff, however, cautioned that private sector involvement must be transparent and should never compromise the independence of police institutions. He said businesses could contribute expertise in communications infrastructure, equipment maintenance and financial planning, but insisted that such partnerships must operate within clearly defined legal and accountability frameworks. “Where businesses provide resources, those contributions need published accounts and independent scrutiny. “Public funding must remain dependable, and a donation must never purchase influence over an investigation or preferential treatment. The object is to strengthen a public service on which every citizen can rely,” he warned. Gbajabiamila explained that the administration was determined to establish financially sustainable state police institutions, insisting that states seeking to operate their own services must demonstrate the capacity to meet recurrent expenditure obligations. According to him, providing vehicles, uniforms and other equipment at the commencement of operations would be insufficient without sustainable arrangements for personnel salaries, professional training and operational maintenance. “Financial readiness is equally important. A state taking on policing must be able to sustain the service after the initial purchase of vehicles and uniforms. “Regular pay and continued training are essential to professional conduct. An institution that cannot meet its obligations to its officers becomes vulnerable to private patrons and unlawful demands on the public,” he cautioned. The Chief of Staff assured that federal policing would continue in states not yet financially or institutionally prepared to establish their own police services. Providing an update on the legislative process, Gbajabiamila confirmed that 24 State Houses of Assembly had approved the constitutional amendment providing for state police as at October 23, 2026 meeting the required two-thirds threshold. He disclosed that the Presidential Working Group had submitted the draft National Policing Bill and 29 consequential amendment bills to the Federal Ministry of Justice on October 19 for legislative review. According to him, after the review and the Working Group’s final consideration, the proposals would be presented to President Tinubu for approval before transmission to the National Assembly. He explained that the proposed framework would enable willing and capable states to assume greater responsibility for protecting their residents, while retaining a strong federal police institution to address interstate criminal activities and other specialised national security requirements. Gbajabiamila said the reform was intended to correct the structural imbalance under which state governments were responsible for responding to the consequences of insecurity without possessing corresponding authority to organise policing. “Bringing policing closer to the communities it serves can improve local intelligence and shorten the time between a call for help and an effective response,” he explained. Addressing concerns about the possible deployment of state police against political opponents, he assured Nigerians that the proposed legislation would contain enforceable safeguards, national professional standards and independent oversight mechanisms. “The concern that police powers could be used against political opponents or vulnerable communities is serious. Our answer is to place enforceable limits on those powers and provide remedies when they are abused. “A citizen’s entitlement to protection cannot depend on whom he supports or where she comes from,” the Chief of Staff declared. He said the framework had benefited from consultations with state governments, security institutions, members of the public and a Policy Advisory Committee drawn from the public and private sectors. Explaining why businesses should champion the reform, Gbajabiamila said insecurity affected investment decisions far beyond the immediate financial burden of hiring private security personnel. Said he: “The cost of the present arrangement is already in your accounts. You pay for additional security and disrupted deliveries. “You also bear losses that never appear as a separate charge: a factory expansion postponed, or a productive location excluded from your investment plans.” He argued that companies could not guarantee sustainable operations merely by securing their premises while surrounding communities remained unsafe. According to him: ‘A company can reinforce its perimeter. Its workers still have to travel home, and its suppliers still have to move through the surrounding communities. “Your long-term security depends on the strength of public institutions beyond your gates.” Turning to the administration’s wider security interventions, Gbajabiamila said President Tinubu had supported the modernisation of the Armed Forces through the induction of helicopters into Army Aviation and the restoration of more than 100 refurbished armoured fighting vehicles to active service. He recalled that the President commissioned three additional naval vessels in June to strengthen maritime security, noting that sustained operations against crude oil theft had contributed to improved oil production, foreign exchange earnings and government revenues. On food security, the Chief of Staff disclosed that the deployment of 10,000 Agro-Rangers across 19 states and the Federal Capital Territory was helping to integrate agricultural production with security protection. He explained that the administration recognised that investments in improved seedlings, agricultural credit and other support programmes would achieve little without guaranteeing farmers’ access to their land. “Improved seedlings and access to credit will achieve little on farmland that its owners are afraid to cultivate. Protection makes those agricultural interventions usable,” he said. Gbajabiamila also highlighted the Presidential Forest Guards Initiative, under which more than 7,000 personnel drawn from seven frontline states had completed training by December 2025 to support security operations in areas exploited by criminal groups. He disclosed that President Tinubu had directed the preparation of a National Threat Assessment and a rolling five-year Strategic Defence Operations Plan in August to improve coordination, align security spending with operational priorities and strengthen institutional accountability. Acknowledging that Nigerians continued to face threats of kidnapping and violent attacks despite government investments in security, he said the administration recognised that its achievements must ultimately be measured by the safety of citizens. “Nigerians living with the threat of abduction or attack are entitled to judge us by their own safety. We recognise the distance between an improvement in national capacity and dependable protection in every community.” The Chief of Staff further linked the administration’s security interventions with its economic reform programme, including fuel subsidy removal, foreign exchange restructuring and tax reforms. He acknowledged that the reforms had imposed considerable pressure on households and businesses but maintained that economic productivity and security were mutually dependent. “A government with inadequate revenues cannot sustain the institutions required to protect its citizens. An economy in which people cannot work safely cannot generate the revenues government needs. “We have therefore had to address both problems together, even as the costs of transition have placed considerable pressure on Nigerian households and businesses,” the Chief of Staff explained. Gbajabiamila urged investors to respond to improving security conditions by returning to communities where commercial activities had been disrupted, arguing that renewed investments would create employment, restore local supply chains and expand public revenues. He assured business leaders that the administration welcomed constructive criticism and practical recommendations, stressing that President Tinubu’s willingness to confront longstanding structural challenges required sustained cooperation from all stakeholders. “A farmer returning to his land and an employer reopening a business will be making decisions about their families’ futures. Our work together must give them sound reasons to proceed.”

title: CAN Blows Hot over Video Threatening to Attack Christians in Enugu, Jos on Sunday
body: Kuni Tyessi in Abuja Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) has petitioned the Department of State Services (DSS) and the Nigeria Police to immediately probe a viral video threatening coordinated attacks on Christians during Sunday worship in Enugu and Jos. In the disturbing footage, a young man is seen leading a group of boys in chants, vowing to attack Christian worshippers. Condemning the video, in a statement, CAN President, Archbishop Daniel Okoh, said the threat must not be treated as empty chant. Okoh warned that every Nigerian had the right to worship without fear of attack. CAN said it was particularly alarmed that children and young persons were deployed to issue the threats. “The possibility that young people are being exposed to or encouraged to embrace such hatred raises serious concerns that must not be ignored,” Okoh said. The apex Christian body tasked security agencies to establish the exact time and location where the video was recorded, unmask all those involved, and uncover who organised and bankrolled it. It demanded a security risk assessment and immediate protection for churches and Christian communities in Enugu, Jos, and other flashpoints. CAN acknowledged the reported disavowal of the video by the leadership of Jama’atu Izalatil Bid’ah Wa Iqamatis Sunnah, JIBWIS, but insisted a disclaimer was not enough. “The denial of responsibility by any organisation cannot replace an independent investigation into the identities of those involved, the origin of the video, and the circumstances surrounding the chants,” CAN stated. The association demanded that investigators determine whether the threats were sponsored or facilitated by any individual or group, and anyone found culpable must be prosecuted without favour. It also charged religious leaders to reject all teachings that incited hatred against other faiths, warning against indoctrinating young Nigerians to see fellow citizens as enemies on religious grounds. “Allowing such conduct to go unchallenged would send a dangerous message that threats against citizens on religious grounds can be made without consequence,” CAN warned.

title: INEC: Preliminary Voters Register Not Final, Suspicious Photos Under Review
body: Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) clarified that alleged AI-generated photographs found in the Preliminary Register of Voters were part of questionable records already flagged during the physical display exercise and were under review. INEC National Commissioner and Chairman Information and Voter Education Committee (IVEC), Mohammed Haruna, in a statement, yesterday, said the commission had noted public concerns circulating on social media about suspected AI-generated photos in the register published online. Haruna explained that the register published online on October 26, 2026 was the same preliminary register that was physically displayed at Registration Areas nationwide from October 9 to 15, 2026 as part of the Display, Claims and Objections exercise. Haruna said, “During the physical display, a number of questionable registration records were identified and flagged for further examination. “The commission commenced the process of reviewing these records and taking appropriate corrective action in accordance with established procedures.” He said the online publication represented the original preliminary register and does not reflect all ongoing data-cleanup activities. Haruna stressed that the preliminary register was not the final certified register. He stated that the Display, Claims and Objections exercise was specifically intended to facilitate public scrutiny, identify inaccuracies and irregularities, and enable corrections before certification. He added, “The commission is also examining the circumstances surrounding the suspicious photographs, including possible technical or procedural lapses, and will take appropriate action based on verified findings.” The electoral body said it appreciated citizens and stakeholders for their vigilance, saying such scrutiny helped improve the accuracy and integrity of the register. Haruna assured that INEC remained committed to completing verification, adjudication and data-cleanup processes ahead of the scheduled certification of the final Register of Voters on December 15, 2026. He said verified irregularities would be addressed through applicable procedures.

title: 2027: Bafarawa Gives Tinubu Condition for Northern Votes, Says Peace Key to Support
body: •Declares one month enough to change the security narrative in north Chuks Okocha in Abuja Former Governor of Sokoto State, Attahiru Bafarawa, has said he would vote for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general election if the president restores peace to the north. Bafarawa, who spoke with FRI, an online Hausa medium, said his only condition for voting Tinubu was for him to ensure peace and restore normalcy to Sokoto State and other parts of the north. “My only condition for allowing my vote to go to President Tinubu is for him to ensure peace and allow full normalcy to return to my area and other northern parts,” he said. He said time was no longer on Tinubu’s side, adding that the president has the resources and security apparatus needed to address insecurity in the region. “As a leader, who has power, money and security, three months or even one month is enough for him to change the insecurity narrative in the northern region,” he said. Bafarawa said he was not interested in campaign money but wanted the president to restore peace so that residents could return to their normal activities. He stated, “Look, as far as I am concerned, I don’t want anything in the name of campaign money. What I want is for President Tinubu to do everything he can to ensure peace and allow markets, schools, farming and other livelihood activities to return to our communities. I assure him that I will vote for him.” The former governor also stated that he had met Tinubu only once since he became president, adding that the encounter took place at a mosque. He alleged that a person whom Tinubu had asked to bring him to the presidency later refused to do so and blocked his phone numbers. Bafarawa, who said he was not a member of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), insisted that he would vote for anyone, including Tinubu, who restored peace to the north. He stated, “But it is unacceptable that today, our children cannot go to school. Doesn’t anybody who denies you education deny you life? Villagers cannot go to farms, and so many towns have been completely sacked. That is why, at this juncture, if Tinubu ensures peace, he is simply my candidate.” Commenting on the appointment of former Zamfara State Governor Abdulaziz Yari as Director-General of Tinubu’s campaign, despite persistent bandit attacks in his home state, Bafarawa defended the decision. He said Yari as an APC member was expected to respect his party’s decision, adding that the president who appointed him is someone he could not easily turn down. “So I don’t see anything wrong with Abdulaziz Yari accepting to be DG of the campaign for President Tinubu because he is doing a job he has been appointed to do. And don’t forget, it would be disrespectful for him to say no,” he said. Bafarawa added that Yari had consulted several people for advice before accepting the appointment and returned to seek further advice afterwards, saying this demonstrated Yari’s integrity.

title: Tinubu Decries Murder of Katsina Cleric, Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka, Instructs Probe
body: • African Centre seeks thorough investigation •Six killed in Gero attack as Mutfwang vows to track down perpetrators Deji Elumoye, Michael Olugbode in Abuja and Yemi Kosoko in Jos President Bola Tinubu has condemned the murder of a prominent Islamic preacher, Sheikh Yahaya Ibrahim Masussuka, and his friend, Adamu Abubakar, in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State. Unknown gunmen killed the duo in a drive-by shooting incident Monday evening. The president, who said he was “deeply saddened” by the news of the killing, in a release by his Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, described the act as heinous and an assault on the values of peace and sanctity of human life. Tinubu extended his heartfelt condolences to the families of the deceased, their followers, as well as the government and people of Katsina State, over the tragic loss. He directed the Nigeria Police and other security agencies to move swiftly, intensify efforts already underway by the Katsina State Police Command, and ensure that the perpetrators were tracked down, apprehended, and brought to justice. Tinubu prayed for the repose of the souls of the departed and for comfort for all those who mourn their death. African Centre for Security, Governance and Development called for an impartial investigation into the killing, warning that failure to bring the perpetrators to justice could heighten public fear and undermine confidence in the security agencies. The centre, in a statement issued in Abuja, condemned the killings, which reportedly occurred on Monday, October 26, and urged security agencies to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident, identify those responsible, and ensure their prosecution. It specifically called on the Inspector-General of Police, Katsina State Police Command, Department of State Services (DSS), and other relevant authorities to conduct a thorough and transparent investigation into the attack. The organisation described the killing as an unlawful act of violence, expressing condolences to the bereaved families and the people of Katsina State. It warned that attacks on religious leaders could threaten peaceful coexistence and deepen public anxiety, particularly if investigations failed to produce credible answers. The centre cautioned against speculation about the identities of the perpetrators or their motives, insisting that conclusions must be based on credible evidence and established through due process. It cited the killings of prominent Islamic scholars, including Sheikh Ja’afar Mahmud Adam in Kano in April 2007, Sheikh Umar Hamza Dan-Maishiyya in Sokoto in July 2007, and Sheikh Muhammad Auwal Albani Zaria in Kaduna State in February 2014, as reminders of the need to protect religious leaders and ensure accountability for violent crimes. Against the backdrop of preparations for the 2027 general election, the organisation urged security agencies to strengthen intelligence gathering, threat assessments, preventive policing, and community engagement to identify emerging security risks and forestall further attacks. It called on religious leaders, political actors, civil society organisations, and members of the public to remain calm, avoid spreading unverified information, and reject any attempt at retaliation. Mutfwang Vows to Track Down Perpetrators as Six Killed in Gero Attacks Amid renewed security concerns in Plateau State, Governor Caleb Mutfwang vowed to pursue the perpetrators of a deadly attack on Gero community in Jos South Local Government Area, where six residents were killed by armed assailants, according to police authorities. The governor gave the assurance yesterday during the swearing-in ceremony of newly appointed Special Advisers at the New Government House, Little Rayfield, Jos. Mutfwang expressed sadness over the Gero attack, describing it as disturbing and unfortunate. The attack, which occurred on Monday night in Gero community, claimed several lives and heightened concerns about security in parts of Plateau State. Reacting to the incident, Mutfwang urged communities across the state to remain vigilant and work closely with security agencies by providing timely and credible information that could help prevent future attacks. According to the governor, security operatives cannot be present in every location at all times and often rely on intelligence supplied by residents to respond effectively to emerging threats. He stated, “The security forces cannot be everywhere; they can only cover some places. If they get information, they will react, but sometimes the reaction comes late because by the time the information gets to them, it is impossible to have saved the situation. “This particular attack left some bits of evidence that we are trailing and, by the grace of God, we will continue to pursue these perpetrators of this dastardly act.” The governor revealed that the suspected leader of a previous deadly attack on Kombun District in Mangu Local Government Area had been arrested, stressing that his administration would continue to support the prosecution of individuals linked to violent crimes across the state. He maintained that security agencies had intensified operations against criminal elements in recent months and reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to ensuring that those responsible for violence face the full weight of the law. Plateau State Police Command confirmed that six persons were killed during the Gero attack, revising an earlier casualty figure of seven provided by community representatives. In a statement issued on Tuesday by Police Public Relations Officer, SP Alfred Alabo, the command said unidentified armed men invaded Gero community in the early hours of Tuesday and opened fire indiscriminately on residents. The statement said the Commissioner of Police in the state, CP Ayodeji Faniyan, immediately deployed mobile policemen and tactical teams led by the Deputy Commissioner of Police in charge of Operations to the area. According to the police, the operatives, working in collaboration with military personnel and Operation Rainbow, successfully dislodged the attackers, who fled into the surrounding hillside forest.

title: Obi Vows to Wage War on Corruption, Promises Nigerians Results from Day One
body: • Pledges emergency measures on security, agriculture, education, healthcare, electricity • Cleopas warns candidates against unfulfilled promis-es, says voters should reject party if it fails to deliver • Dickson describes new Abuja secretariat as party’s ‘Noah’s Ark’ • NDC appoints Soludo’s former ally to lead campaign in Anambra Sunday Aborisade in Abuja and David-Chyddy Eleke in Awka Presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, has vowed to wage an uncom-promising war against corruption and ensure trans-parent management of public resources. Obi declared that Nigerians would begin to see meas-urable improvements in governance from the first day of an NDC administration. Obi, who is contesting the January 16, 2027 presiden-tial election with former Kano State Governor, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, as his running mate, also promised emergency interventions in security, agriculture, edu-cation, healthcare, and electricity, insisting that Nige-ria can no longer afford leadership that blames previ-ous administrations for its failures. He made the commitments in Abuja at a dinner organ-ised to inaugurate the party’s National Presidential Campaign Council, present certificates of return to its candidates, and unveil its new national secretariat at 393 Etang Obuli Crescent, Jabi, Abuja. The former Anambra State governor said his admin-istration would prioritise problem-solving, accounta-bility, and measurable outcomes rather than political excuses. He said public officeholders must demonstrate how the country’s resources translated into improved living conditions. He declared, “The purpose of governance is to solve problems, not to blame people. Kwankwaso and I will not blame anybody. We will create that new Nigeria that is possible.” Obi accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of failing to translate increased government revenues and borrowing into commensurate improvements in Nigerians’ living conditions. He said the country needed leadership that would re-spond directly to the challenges confronting citizens, particularly insecurity, hunger, unemployment, pov-erty, and the rising cost of living. He said, “From my engagements all over Nigeria, Nige-rians are looking for new leadership. And we assure you that we will create that new leadership.” Obi made the fight against corruption a central pillar of his campaign, promising to ensure that public funds served the interests of Nigerians rather than being di-verted for private benefit. He stated that corruption had weakened public insti-tutions, undermined development spending, discour-aged productive investment, and contributed to the country’s persistent economic difficulties. Questioning the management of government revenues and borrowed funds under the Tinubu administration, he demanded greater transparency in public expendi-ture and challenged the federal government to ac-count for its spending and development projects. He said, “We must stop people from stealing public money. We must use public money for the public good. And that will be seen, it will be shown.” The NDC candidate insisted that public officials found culpable of corruption must be held accountable in accordance with the law. He also questioned the implementation of the 2023, 2024 and 2025 budgets, alleging that capital expendi-ture remains below 20 per cent and contractors are experiencing difficulties receiving payments for com-pleted projects. Obi challenged the federal government to provide Ni-gerians with a detailed account of its expenditure, pro-jects and achievements, stating that citizens deserve tangible improvements rather than repeated explana-tions of the country’s problems. He stated, “We don’t want you to hire us to tell you about our problem. It’s only in Nigeria that you hire people, and they start reminding you of what hap-pened in the past. “No, we don’t want you to hire us to tell you about our problem. We want you to hire us to improve from to-day.” On security, Obi promised a more direct presidential response to kidnapping, violent attacks, and other threats to life and property, insisting that the presi-dent must demonstrate leadership by visiting commu-nities affected by emergencies. He stated that the country’s security challenges re-quired urgent action and a leadership willing to en-gage directly with affected communities rather than remain distant from the realities confronting victims. “If they say there is a problem in Jos, he will go to Jos,” he said. Obi pledged to visit communities affected by insecurity in Plateau, Benue, Zamfara, Sokoto and Borno states, among others, and criticised what he described as ex-cessive foreign travel by the president. He maintained that Nigeria needed a leader who would devote greater attention to domestic challenges and demonstrate solidarity with citizens facing vio-lence, displacement, and economic hardship. The NDC candidate also promised emergency measures to revive agriculture, particularly in northern Nigeria, where insecurity had disrupted farming activi-ties and restricted access to productive land. He said restoring security in farming communities would enable farmers to return to their fields, increase food production, reduce dependence on imports, and strengthen the supply of raw materials to local indus-tries. “We have vast land in the north. When we secure the north, our farmers must go back and produce what we eat and what we use for our industries,” he said. He linked agricultural recovery to the broader task of tackling hunger, stabilising food prices, creating em-ployment, and moving the economy away from exces-sive dependence on consumption and borrowing. Obi also pledged emergency interventions in educa-tion, expressing concern over the number of Nigerian children outside the formal school system. He stated that the country could not achieve sustaina-ble development without investing in human capital and ensuring that children from disadvantaged back-grounds had access to quality education. Drawing on his experience as governor of Anambra State, he said education should serve as a pathway to opportunity, regardless of a person’s family back-ground or social connections. “We must create a society where a child of nobody will be somebody without knowing anybody,” he said. On healthcare, Obi renewed his promise to establish a functional primary healthcare centre in every ward within two years of assuming office. He said the proposed intervention would bring basic medical services closer to communities, improve ac-cess to treatment, and reduce preventable deaths. The former governor also pledged emergency measures to address persistent electricity shortages. He described reliable power supply as indispensable to industrial growth, job creation, and economic recov-ery. “We will declare emergency on generation, transmis-sion, and distribution,” he said. Obi said unreliable electricity had increased operating costs for businesses, burdened households, and con-strained the productive capacity of Nigerian industries. He called for the revival of manufacturing establish-ments across the country, citing the decline of indus-tries in Kano as an example of the economic conse-quences of inadequate infrastructure and weak indus-trial development. He said Nigeria must transition from an economy driv-en largely by consumption and borrowing to one built on production, investment and job creation. Small and medium-sized enterprises also featured prominently in Obi’s economic proposals, as he prom-ised improved access to credit, tax relief, and incen-tives to stimulate business growth. Citing figures indicating that Nigeria had more than 40 million small businesses, he said the sector remained constrained by limited access to bank financing, de-spite its importance to employment and economic ac-tivity. Obi said an NDC administration would work to ensure that more than 20 per cent of credit went to small businesses. He stated that expanding financing oppor-tunities would enable entrepreneurs to grow their op-erations and employ more Nigerians. He said, “We will put a mark to it. We will ensure that over 20 per cent of credits will go to small businesses. We will support them.” He also promised tax holidays and other incentives to support small businesses, while insisting that govern-ment policies must encourage production and enter-prise rather than impose burdens that stifle growth. The proposed measures, he said, would form part of a broader economic strategy to expand employment opportunities, strengthen local production and im-prove household incomes. Turning to the 2027 elections, Obi urged political ac-tors to respect the rights of opposition supporters and refrain from intimidating citizens engaged in lawful po-litical activities. He said political competition should centre on ideas, policies, and the credibility of candidates rather than harassment or the suppression of opposing voices. He stated, “Humility and civility are not weaknesses. It is a virtue. Good behaviour is not a weakness. It is a virtue.” The NDC presidential candidate also urged Nigerians to defend the integrity of the electoral process, insist-ing that the forthcoming election should provide citi-zens with an opportunity to determine their political future through the ballot. “The revolution that is coming is a revolution of the ballot,” he declared. He called for free, fair and credible elections, main-taining that electoral legitimacy remains fundamental to democratic governance and public confidence in political institutions.
