Earlier, NDC National Chairman, Senator Moses Cleo-pas, described the gathering as a significant milestone in the party’s preparations for the 2027 general elec-tion. Cleopas said it was driven by the determination to of-fer Nigerians a different approach to governance. He said the party had conducted its primaries within a short period and the dinner provided an opportunity for candidates, party leaders, and other stakeholders to strengthen their commitment to a common political agenda. He identified the inauguration of the National Presi-dential Campaign Council and the presentation of cer-tificates of return to candidates as major steps in the party’s preparations for the elections. Cleopas stated, “If we fail to bring water for you in two years, if we open our mouths to say, vote for us again, please, don’t vote for us. “We are going for a rescue mission; the hope of this country is in NDC.” National Leader of NDC, Senator Seriake Dickson, de-scribed the new national secretariat as their own “No-ah’s Ark”, presenting the facility as a unifying centre for the party as it prepares for the 2027 elections. Meanwhile, NDC appointed a former House of Repre-sentatives member, and erstwhile ally of Anambra State Governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, Hon. Ifeanyi Ibezi, as the state’s campaign coordinator for the party. Ibezi, who had been a strong ally of Soludo’s All Pro-gressives Grand Alliance (APGA), recently dumped the party at a highly attended rally, to join NDC. His appointment is seen as a move to use his populari-ty to drive votes for NDC and also put APGA in check, especially with Soludo’s growing resentment for Obi. Ibezi, who had immediately swung into action, called on Anambra residents to rally round Obi and give him a resounding victory, saying merely winning Obi’s home state, Anambra, is not enough. In a press statement yesterday, Ibezi said though the task was a daunting one, he and his team would move into the 326 political wards, markets, and town union meetings to speak to the people on the need for every Anambra vote to go to Obi and other NDC candidates. He stated, “Anambra occupies a peculiar place in this campaign. As the home state of our presidential can-didate, His Excellency, Mr. Peter Obi, the expectations are understandably high, and we must rise to meet them. “Our responsibility goes beyond securing victory; we must work to ensure that Anambra delivers a resound-ing mandate, reflected in the strength and number of valid votes cast for Mr. Peter Obi. “We must reach those who are undecided, those who feel left behind, those who have grown weary of the system, and those who have withdrawn from the elec-toral process because they no longer believe their votes can make a difference.” “We must listen to them, earn their confidence, and remind them that the future of our country is too im-portant to be surrendered to apathy. The work has be-gun, and there is no room for complacency.” Cleopas added, “We must take this campaign to the 21 LGAs, 326 Wards, 5,720 Polling Units, markets, church-es, and every household in Anambra State. “Our objective is clear: to mobilise the people, secure their participation, and translate their aspirations into votes at the polls. We must also ensure that every val-id vote counts and that the democratic process reflects the will of the people.”

title: Wike: Amaechi Unfit for National Leadership over N486bn Allegations
body: •Fubara declares FCT minister political leader •Chinda promises inclusive government Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has accused former Rivers State governor, Chibuike Amaechi, of presiding over questionable expenditures involving billions of naira. Wike declared that Nigerians would not entrust the country’s leadership to “political gamblers” ahead of the 2027 general election. Wike, who cited alleged expenditures and transactions involving approximately N486 billion at the exchange-rate equivalents he announced, challenged Amaechi to account for $10 million allegedly spent on mosquito fumigation, $39 million reportedly allocated to an uncompleted 1,000-bed Justice Karibi-Whyte Specialist Hospital, and $308 million from the sale of the Omoku gas turbine. The FCT minister made the allegations yesterday in Port Harcourt during the unveiling of candidates of the Rainbow Coalition, a political alliance of six parties backing President Bola Tinubu’s re-election and supporting candidates of All Progressives Congress (APC) in Rivers State. Wike stated that the allegations against Amaechi, whom he accused of failing to account for public funds during his tenure as governor from 2007 to 2015, allegedly raised serious questions about his suitability for higher political office. He also criticised the prospect of Amaechi serving as vice presidential candidate to former Vice President Atiku Abubakar under African Democratic Congress (ADC), insisting that the combination would be unacceptable to Nigerians. “As bad as the Atiku ticket is, attaching Rotimi Amaechi as a vice president worsens it. It is important to show your report card,” Wike said. Recalling Amaechi’s administration, the minister alleged that $10 million, which he valued at N14 billion, was spent on mosquito fumigation in Rivers State despite the continued prevalence of mosquito bites and malaria. “He paid $10 million. $10 million today is N14 billion. N14 billion for malaria not to bite you. Rotimi Amaechi, we are still having mosquito bites,” he said. Wike further alleged that $39 million, equivalent to N53 billion at the figures he cited, was spent on the proposed Justice Karibi-Whyte Specialist Hospital after the existing teaching hospital was pulled down, but that no foundation had been laid for the replacement facility. “Ask Rotimi Amaechi, what is the foundation of the Justice Karibi-Whyte Specialist Hospital? Is there any foundation? Have they laid any foundation? No. $39 million gone. N53 billion gone,” he alleged. On the Omoku gas turbine, Wike claimed that the facility was sold in December 2014 for $308 million, which he valued at no less than N419 billion, but that only $308,000 remained when he assumed office in May 2015. He said, “I came in on May 29, 2015. Six months after, what he left was $308,000. From $308 million to $308,000. Ask him, where is the $308 million that he sold?” The minister also claimed that a judicial panel of inquiry established during his administration indicted Amaechi over the transactions, adding that the former governor challenged the findings in court and lost at the State High Court, Court of Appeal and Supreme Court. Wike said the Rainbow Coalition was designed to unite politicians across party lines in support of Tinubu’s re-election rather than create divisions or political instability. “I have said, and let me reiterate, that the Rainbow Coalition means no harm, but to bring people of all the various political parties together to support Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. He insisted that members of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) across the country should support Tinubu, claiming that the party’s recognised national leadership was aligned with the coalition’s position. Wike specifically urged PDP members in Imo, Kwara, Gombe, Zamfara and Ogun states, among others, to support the president in 2027. He also dismissed the existence of any other politically viable party in Rivers State, declaring that the coalition represented a united front ahead of the next general election. Wike announced that the coalition would hold its flag-off rally on November 7 at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium, Igwuruta, Rivers State, while expressing confidence that the turnout would surpass that of yesterday’s event. Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, urged his supporters to stop referring to him as the political leader of the state, and openly recognised Wike as the leader of the coalition. “Going forward, this issue of my leader, my leader, my leader, I want it resolved here and now. I am no more the leader. My Oga, the General Overseer, GO, is our leader,” Fubara said. The governor expressed gratitude to Wike, acknowledging his role in his emergence as governor and pledging to work towards the coalition’s victory in the 2027 elections. He also reaffirmed his support for Tinubu, whom he credited with standing by him during difficult moments. Fubara unveiled Kingsley Chinda as the APC governorship candidate under the Rainbow Coalition, alongside other candidates representing the alliance’s participating parties. In his acceptance speech, after receiving the party’s flag from the governor, Chinda promised an inclusive administration that would accommodate different political parties, religious groups and ethnic communities if elected. “We are no longer divided on party lines. We are no longer playing the politics of the winner-takes-it-all,” he said. He pledged that the coalition would remain intact beyond the elections, with members participating in governance and prioritising the interests of Rivers residents. “Our number one candidate in the Rainbow Coalition is President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” Chinda declared.

title: NYSC, UNN Disowned Ex-minister Uche Nnaji’s Certificates, ICPC Witness Tells Court
body: An investigator with the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), Yakubu Ibrahim, on Monday, told a Federal High Court in Abuja that both the University of Nigeria (UNN) and the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) disowned the degree and discharge certificates presented by former Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Uche Nnaji, to the Senate for his ministerial screening in 2023. The witness, Superintendent of Police, Yakubu Ibrahim, testified as the first prosecution witness in the trial of Nnaji, who is facing a six-count charge marked FHC/ABJ/CR/389/2026, bordering on alleged corruption, fraud, conferring corrupt advantage and providing false information through the alleged presentation of forged university degree and national service certificates. The investigator, who was led in evidence by the prosecution counsel, J. A. Mumini (SAN), said he was part of the ICPC team that investigated two petitions against the defendant. The witness said his team was assigned to investigate the matter after the commission received two separate petitions alleging certificate forgery against Nnaji. He said the Chairman of the Special Task Force directed an investigation, prompting the commission to request relevant documents from the National Assembly, the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), University of Nigeria, Nsukka and the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC). He told the court that the team wrote to UNN to authenticate the Bachelor of Science certificate in Microbiology/Biochemistry allegedly submitted by Nnaji to the Senate. According to him, the university responded that it did not issue the certificate to the governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Enugu for the 2027 election. The witness added that the team also contacted the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) over a discharge certificate 15th May 1986, but the NYSC equally disowned it, maintaining that it did not issue any such certificate to the ex-minister. Ibrahim further told the court that UNN supplied the investigators with the defendant’s academic records, including a notice of withdrawal issued over his failure to obtain the required grade in a course. When shown copies of the correspondence between the ICPC and the two institutions, the witness identified the documents, following which the prosecution sought to tender them in evidence. Defence counsel, Wole Olanipekun (SAN), said he would allow the documents to be admitted at that stage but reserve his objection until later. On the steps taken to interview the defendant, Ibrahim said the head of his section issued an invitation, but investigators could not locate his address. He said a copy of the invitation, dated May 5, 2026, was subsequently sent to the defendant’s email address and WhatsApp number. According to the witness, after Nnaji failed to honour the invitation, the ICPC liaised with the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to effect his arrest on July 1. He added that the defendant was questioned and made statements dated July 1 and 2. During cross-examination by Olanipekun, the witness admitted that he did not visit UNN during the investigation and did not know the faculty to which the defendant had been admitted. He however said members of the investigating team interviewed the university’s Registrar. Asked whether the team established where the alleged certificates were forged, Ibrahim said he did not know. He also said the defendant made no comment on the allegations when questioned by investigators. On whether the team investigated where Nnaji undertook his national service, the witness said it did not because the NYSC had stated that it did not issue the certificate. “The NYSC said the certificate was not issued by it, which was why we didn’t inquire where he served,” he told the court. The witness also confirmed seeing a notice of withdrawal supplied by UNN. When asked to identify it, he identified the document, marked Exhibit C, dated November 7, 1984. He said the university explained in its letter the policy governing the grades required for the award of a certificate saying if one failed four times, the person was not qualified. Ibrahim said Nnaji failed at two stages and did not write the examination at the third stage for medical reasons. “The witness said, “the defendant went ahead to write the supplementary examination for which he did not register.” Ibrahim further testified that UNN confirmed that the BSc certificate in Microbiology and Biochemistry attributed to the defendant was not issued by the university. Olanipekun suggested that a subsequent letter dated March 18, 1985, rescinded the earlier withdrawal notice. Ibrahim agreed, adding that the withdrawal notice related to a course in General Microbiology. The witness also told the court that investigators did not establish the number of years a student studying Microbiology was expected to spend at the university. At the conclusion of cross-examination, the prosecution did not re-examine the witness, following which Justice Joyce Abdulmalik discharged him and adjourned further hearing until November 3. Meanwhile, it is recalled that Nnaji, who resigned as minister following the certificates forgery scandal did not include the controversial degree certificate in his Independent National Electoral Commissioner (INEC) filing ahead of the 2027 election in which he flies the flag of the PDP.

title: 300 Owners of Demolished Property in Asaba Send S.O.S to Gov Oborevwori
body: • Say about a dozen affected persons have died Omon-Julius Onabu in Asaba More than 300 people whose buildings were reportedly demolished in Asaba within the Delta State Capital Territory, have appealed to Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to intervene in a protracted land dispute between Parkview Estates and Dennis Osadebay University (DOU). The property owners, under the aegis of Parkview Estates, Anwai, claimed their buildings were demolished on May 14, 2024, allegedly by the Delta State Taskforce on Recovery of Government Lands while legal proceedings were pending, and as well an alleged court injunction restraining further action on the land. Speaking with newsmen after proceedings at the High Court, Asaba, the Chairman of Parkview Estates, Chief Charles Ogbobe, described the demolition as “simply devastating.” He lamented that the demolition exercise destroyed “valuable investments worth millions of naira, rendered families homeless and caused severe emotional and financial hardship.” Ogbobe said the disputed land, located in Musa Camp in Anwai, later renamed Ugbomanta by the Asagba of Asaba – was legitimately acquired from the Isieke community, which he said possesses documents establishing ownership. He underscored the point that the dispute stemmed from competing claims between the community and the state-owned university, noting that the land was originally leased to one Reverend Prior, a colonial administrator, in 1953 for a period of 50 years, a lease which expired in 2003. “We never disputed the government’s right to own land, but we asked them to provide evidence of ownership,” Ogbobe noted. He lamented that between 12 and 13 persons affected by the demolition have died since the exercise due to untold hardship and emotional distress. According to Ogbobe, the High Court has directed both parties to produce survey plans delineating the boundaries of the disputed property. Also speaking, the Vice-Chairman of the Parkview Estates, Mr. Samuel Onuwa David, alleged that the demolition was carried out before the expiration of the seven-day notice issued to occupants, despite efforts by residents to obtain an injunction. David, who revealed that he lost a private school, a residential building and four buildings belonging to his relatives, noted that available documents show the lease to the university expired in 1991. “We are appealing to the state governor, as a father, to come to our aid. Let him compensate us for the houses that were demolished and give us back our land,” he wept. Another affected property owner, Mr. Christian Nwaolisa, said that he returned from the northern part of Nigeria with the intention of settling down in his home state only to lose his building and residence, despite obtaining a Certificate of Occupancy and building approval before development. On his part, Mr. Chuks Okei said that he acquired his land directly from the community, conducted a survey and obtained government building approval before commencing construction in 2020, spending about three years to develop the property before it was demolished. The affected residents, therefore, urged Governor Oborevwori to investigate the circumstances surrounding the dispute and resultant demolition and ensure justice that is duly served.

title: Panel Recommends N1.4bn Compensation over 37 Miners Suffocated in NSCDC Custody
body: Michael Olugbode in Abuja A federal government investigative panel has found that 37 suspected illegal miners who died in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Niger State died from asphyxiation, recommending N1.4 billion in compensation for affected families and survivors. The panel also recommended the summary dismissal of the Niger State NSCDC Commandant and other officers found to have been directly involved in the incident, describing the deaths as avoidable and calling for measures to prevent recurrence. The chairman of the 10-member independent investigative committee, Jonathan Kure, a retired Deputy Director-General of the Department of State Services, disclosed the findings on Tuesday while presenting the panel’s report to the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, in Abuja. The recommendations followed investigations into the deaths of 37 suspected illegal miners who died on September 17, 2026, while being detained by the NSCDC in Minna, the Niger State capital. The victims were among dozens of people arrested during anti-illegal mining operations in the M.I. Wushishi and Lukoto areas of the state. According to reports on the panel’s findings, the committee recommended N1.4 billion in compensation for the families of 33 deceased victims and 44 survivors affected by the incident. The panel also called for the dismissal of the state commandant and officers whose involvement in the arrests, detention and circumstances surrounding the deaths was established. Fourteen of the deceased were reportedly minors, raising further concerns about the treatment of young people detained during the operation. The federal government constituted the independent committee following public outrage over the deaths and President Bola Tinubu’s directive for a comprehensive, transparent and unhindered investigation. The committee was mandated to establish the circumstances surrounding the arrests and detention, determine the cause of death, identify possible negligence or misconduct and recommend appropriate sanctions and compensation. The incident had earlier triggered protests in Minna, with residents and relatives of the deceased demanding answers over how so many detainees could die while in government custody. Initial accounts from the authorities suggested a possible disease outbreak, while survivors subsequently described overcrowded and poorly ventilated detention conditions. Some survivors also alleged that an unidentified substance was sprayed into the cell before detainees began experiencing breathing difficulties and other unusual symptoms. Those accounts raised questions about the conditions in which the suspects were held and whether security personnel responded adequately to their distress. The allegations, however, required independent verification, including forensic examinations, before responsibility for the deaths could be conclusively established. In September, the Minister of Interior announced the suspension of the Niger State NSCDC Commandant and 20 other officers pending the outcome of the investigation. The committee subsequently inspected the detention facility, visited relevant locations, conducted autopsies and obtained statements from NSCDC personnel, survivors, relatives of the deceased and other witnesses. It also reviewed documentary and forensic evidence as part of efforts to reconstruct the events leading to the deaths. Before the submission of its final report, the panel had identified institutional weaknesses, alleged overzealousness among personnel and inadequate training as issues requiring attention. The committee had sought additional time to complete its work, citing the volume of evidence and the need to obtain and review medical and forensic reports while allowing persons implicated in the incident to respond. The latest findings and recommendations now place the responsibility on the relevant authorities to determine and implement appropriate disciplinary measures, address compensation for affected families and survivors, and strengthen safeguards against deaths in custody. Receiving the report, Tunji-Ojo pledged that the federal government would implement the committee’s recommendations to ensure justice for the victims and prevent a recurrence. The minister also directed the NSCDC leadership to suspend officers allegedly involved in cleaning the detention facility in an attempt to destroy evidence, according to reports on the presentation of the panel’s findings. The circumstances surrounding the deaths have renewed concerns about accountability within Nigeria’s security agencies and the protection of the rights of people held in detention. The implementation of the panel’s recommendations, particularly the proposed compensation, disciplinary sanctions and institutional reforms, will be a key test of the government’s commitment to accountability in the case.

title: Duke: Floating Naira Without Local Production is Impoverishing Nigerians
body: Ayodeji Ake Former Cross River State governor and presidential candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Donald Duke, has said that floating the naira without strengthening local industries and domestic production is worsening the economic hardship faced by Nigerians. Duke, who spoke with journalists in Abuja on Tuesday, attributed Nigeria’s economic difficulties to excessive dependence on imported goods, rising fuel costs, high interest rates and government spending. He argued that the country needed deliberate policies to manage the value of the naira while developing local industries, creating jobs and reducing dependence on foreign goods. “No country floats its currency. The currency is your economic worth. It is like floating your value. As a human being, what is your worth? Are you going to float your worth? You manage your worth. You manage your currency,” he said. The former governor maintained that Nigeria should determine a realistic exchange rate and implement policies to achieve it, rather than allow currency depreciation to worsen the cost of living. He said strengthening domestic production would reduce demand for foreign exchange, create employment and improve economic stability. “As long as you continue importing, you’re creating jobs overseas,” Duke said, urging the government to identify goods that could be manufactured locally. He also expressed concern over Nigeria’s balance of trade, stressing the need to improve exports, reduce unnecessary imports and attract foreign investment. Duke criticised the Central Bank of Nigeria’s high interest rate regime, arguing that expensive borrowing was discouraging businesses from accessing funds for investment and expansion. He said monetary and fiscal policies needed better coordination to address inflation and support productive activities. According to him, fuel prices significantly influence inflation because transportation costs affect the prices of goods and services across the country. “But interest rates don’t cause inflation. The price of your fuel causes inflation. The high cost of your fuel causes inflation because everything moves through transportation,” he said. Duke added that prevailing interest rates made borrowing difficult for businesses, potentially limiting their ability to expand operations and create jobs. The former governor also faulted government spending on imported goods, including vehicles, saying public institutions should prioritise locally manufactured products where possible. “The second thing is the unbridled spending by the governments. If you go to government establishments, literally everything is imported. Vehicles, everything is imported,” he said. Duke argued that patronising locally produced goods would conserve foreign exchange, strengthen domestic industries and generate employment. He urged the government to direct expenditure towards initiatives that would stimulate local production and reduce pressure on the naira. On governance, Duke said greater attention should be paid to the competence of political leaders and their appointees rather than age. “Age doesn’t affect your brain,” he said. He criticised appointments driven primarily by political considerations, arguing that effective governance required individuals selected for their ability to deliver results. “A lot of the appointments are based on politics and not on governance,” he said. Duke also expressed enthusiasm about the presidential candidates, specifically mentioning Adewole Adebayo of the Social Democratic Party and Peter Obi of the National Democratic Congress. He said he looked forward to substantive presidential debates where candidates could explain their programmes and proposed solutions to Nigeria’s challenges.

title: Nasarawa Guber: Ex-IG, Adamu Pledges to Prioritise Security as Ethnic Group Endorses Him
body: Igbawase Ukumba in Lafia Former Inspector General of Police and gubernatorial candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Nasarawa State, Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, has said his aspiration to govern Nasarawa State in 2027 is driven by the desire to uplift the common man. Adamu stated this Yesterday in Doma, while responding to his endorsement as the preferred governorship candidate by the Alago ethnic nationality for the 2027 election. The endorsement was announced during a rally organised by the Alago Support Group for IGP Adamu. The former police boss first thanked God for the success recorded so far in his political journey, saying no success would have been possible without divine intervention. He expressed appreciation to the Alago Support Group for the support and for agreeing to include them in his campaign, noting that the people have shown they will vote for him and, God willing, he will win the election. “Because yesterday, the people gathered and the progressives as a whole came out and endorsed our candidate for governor. Also, the major tribe that is prominent here endorsed our candidate. We are grateful for the strong assurance they gave us that we will not face any hardship on election day,” he said. Adamu said his decision to contest is for the common people who are suffering under the present situation, where mothers, children and youths are neglected while government focuses on things that do not concern their lives. “Our coming out for this election is for the common people. We came out for the common man, to see that the common man does not suffer the way they are suffering now,” he stated. He promised to prioritize the lives of the people if elected, with focus on quality education, quality healthcare and security. “We will put people’s lives first, to see that education with quality is given to our people, health with quality our people have obtained, and the issue of security, we will see that everyone will find peace, so that people can return to their homes to sleep without any fear,” Adamu said. He also raised alarm over alleged vote-buying and collection of Permanent Voter Cards, PVCs, from women to stop them from voting. “Those who don’t have people following them are collecting cards in the hands of women, they are buying so as to stop them from coming out to vote. Therefore, anyone who collected a card, let them go and collect their card. Everyone should not agree to sell their card, and everyone should come out on election day with their card,” he urged. Earlier in his address, the Leader of the Conveners, Danjuma Joseph, said the historic movement was conceived when they resolved that Alago could not remain on the sidelines while the future of Nasarawa State is being shaped. Joseph said after thorough political and moral interrogation, they found in him a man of proven integrity, impeccable track record and uncommon patriotism who served Nigeria meritoriously to the pinnacle of his career. He noted that Adamu is not a stranger to Alago land, as he shares deep historical and blood affinity with the people, having schooled with many prominent sons and daughters of Alago in Obi, and having maternal ties with Alago. “We have resolved that we will no longer be onlookers or fence-sitters while the political destiny of our dear state is being decided. The time to participate, to take a stand and to take our destiny in our own hands is now,” Joseph declared. He said there should be no acrimony over who Alago should support, citing Section 40 of the 1999 Constitution which guarantees freedom of association, and stressed that their constitutional and political choice remains IGP Adamu. He added that the current political era is that of ‘Rainbow Coalition’, where one can remain in his party and still support any candidate of his choice, hence their action is not exceptional but a political alliance for the good of Alago and Nasarawa State. “Your Excellency, this programme today is organised on the sacred sand of Alago ancestral land, in the name of Alago and in the interest of Alago. It is a political covenant, a bond of trust between you and Alago nation. By the grace of God, when you ascend as Governor, do not forget Alago people,” he told Adamu. Joseph said the group will traverse all Alago electoral wards in Nasarawa South and extend mobilisation to Nasarawa North and West Senatorial Districts to deliver Adamu.

title: PANDEF Demands 50% Oil Derivation, Rejects 13% Allocation
body: • Forum sets up technical committee to work with works ministry on Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway •Seeks abolition of onshore/offshore dichotomy Sunday Aborisade in Abuja Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF) has demanded an increase in the minimum derivation allocation to oil-producing states from 13 per cent to 50 per cent, insisting the current arrangement is inadequate to address the environmental devastation and development challenges confronting communities in the Niger Delta. The socio-political organisation also called on the federal government; Revenue Mobilisation, Allocation and Fiscal Commission (RMAFC); and the National Assembly to urgently abolish the onshore/offshore dichotomy in revenue allocation. It said coastal communities suffered the consequences of offshore petroleum operations, irrespective of where the oil and gas resources were located. The demands were contained in a communiqué issued yesterday in Abuja at the end of a meeting of PANDEF’s Board of Trustees and National Executive Committee, attended by former governors, former ministers, traditional rulers, political leaders, and other stakeholders representing the six South-south states of Akwa Ibom, Bayelsa, Cross River, Delta, Edo, and Rivers. The communiqué, read by PANDEF’s National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, said the existing derivation arrangement had remained unchanged for more than two decades, despite the enormous environmental, ecological and developmental burdens borne by oil-producing communities. Citing Section 162(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the forum said the provision for a minimum of 13 per cent derivation had failed to adequately address the consequences of oil and gas exploration and production in the region. The communique said, “The meeting calls for an increase in the derivation allocation from the current minimum of 13 per cent to a minimum of 50 per cent, to enable oil-producing communities and states to address the longstanding developmental deficits, environmental damage, health hazards and social and economic consequences of oil and gas exploration and production.” PANDEF maintained that the increased allocation was necessary to enable the oil-producing states to confront the cumulative effects of decades of petroleum exploration, including pollution, damaged ecosystems, deteriorating livelihoods and inadequate infrastructure. The forum also urged the National Assembly, in collaboration with the federal government and RMAFC, to initiate the necessary legislative and constitutional measures to end the onshore/offshore dichotomy. It stated that offshore oil and gas operations were conducted within the maritime environment and fishing grounds upon which coastal communities depended for their livelihoods. It said, “Consequently, oil spills and other incidents arising from offshore petroleum activities can have devastating effects on marine ecosystems, fishing activities and the economic well-being of coastal populations, irrespective of whether the affected resources are located onshore or offshore.” On infrastructure, PANDEF announced the establishment of a high-level technical committee to work with the Federal Ministry of Works on the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, which it described as a strategic project with far-reaching implications for the economic integration and development of Nigeria’s coastal communities. The forum welcomed the federal government’s decision to retain the original broad alignment of the 750-kilometre highway as a distinct legacy infrastructure project following the reported reconsideration of an earlier proposal to integrate the route into the East-West Road. It said the coastal highway had a long historical background predating Nigeria’s independence and had featured prominently in national discussions on connectivity and economic development across the Niger Delta. According to the communiqué, previous design work undertaken by the Oil Minerals Producing Areas Development Commission (OMPADEC) and the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), alongside the expertise of professionals from the region, could assist the works ministry in advancing the project. The communique stated, “The meeting also noted that relevant design work had since been undertaken by OMPADEC and the NDDC, which, along with relevant professionals from the area, could assist the Federal Ministry of Works in advancing the project alongside the East-West Road and the other dilapidated roads in the area. “PANDEF therefore decided to set up a high-level technical committee to assist the Federal Ministry of Works for the road project.” The organisation insisted that the accelerated and successful completion of the highway was non-negotiable, citing its potential to improve connectivity among coastal states, stimulate trade and investment, strengthen national integration, and unlock opportunities in the blue and marine economy. It also called for the establishment of appropriate north-south rail connections to link the region with the rest of the country. On environmental restoration, PANDEF said communities across the Niger Delta continued to suffer the consequences of more than six decades of oil and gas exploration, calling for urgent intervention in Nembe Creek in Bayelsa State, Odidi in Delta State, and Kula in Rivers State. It demanded adequate, sustained, and transparent funding for the Ogoni clean-up programme and urged the federal government to develop a comprehensive framework for extending environmental remediation to other affected communities. The forum challenged presidential candidates in the 2027 general election to demonstrate their commitment to environmental justice by presenting practical, measurable, and time-bound plans for cleaning up and restoring polluted communities. On maritime infrastructure, PANDEF commended President Bola Tinubu’s decision to modernise and upgrade the ports of Warri, Port Harcourt, and Calabar. It also welcomed approvals for proposed deep-sea ports at Ibom in Akwa Ibom State, Bonny in Rivers State, and Agge in Bayelsa State. The organisation, however, urged the federal government to establish a sustainable financing framework for the projects comparable to arrangements adopted for major port infrastructure around the Lagos corridor. It said the strategic location of the South-south ports could strengthen trade with East, Central and Southern Africa, improve access to the Indian Ocean, and enable Nigeria to benefit more fully from the African Continental Free Trade Area. On economic diversification, PANDEF called for accelerated investment in gas infrastructure, power generation, mini-liquefied natural gas facilities, liquefied petroleum gas and compressed natural gas hubs, petrochemicals and other gas-based industries. The forum stated that the Niger Delta held more than 209 trillion standard cubic feet of natural gas reserves, stressing that their development could promote industrialisation, improve electricity supply, create jobs and stimulate economic growth. It also urged the federal government to revive plans for modular refineries through appropriate funding, licensing, technical support and environmental compliance frameworks. According to PANDEF, properly regulated modular refineries would complement existing and proposed large-scale refining facilities, reduce dependence on imported petroleum products, support local enterprise, and generate employment. The meeting called on the federal and state governments to establish a coordinated agricultural development programme focusing on palm oil, rice, cassava, vegetables and other crops suited to the region’s ecological conditions. It identified improved seedlings, mechanisation, irrigation, rural roads, storage facilities, agro-processing, affordable financing and reliable markets as essential to transforming agriculture into a major pillar of the Niger Delta’s economy. PANDEF also disclosed plans to explore a regional investment fund to pool resources from individuals, businesses, and institutions for investments in critical economic sectors, enterprise development, infrastructure, and job creation. Reviewing its first decade of existence, the forum highlighted its advocacy efforts, including the establishment of the South-South Development Commission, the commencement of activities at the Nigerian Maritime University, Okerenkoko, and the upgrading of the Maritime Academy of Nigeria, Oron. It also commended its leadership’s contributions to the restoration of peace in Rivers State and its continuing efforts to resolve the dispute over oil wells between Akwa Ibom and Cross River states. As Nigeria approaches the 2027 general election, PANDEF urged residents of the South-south to exercise their civic responsibilities peacefully and vote according to their conscience. It called on political leaders and public officeholders from the Niger Delta, particularly those serving at the federal level, to demonstrate greater commitment to the region’s collective interests. The communiqué stated, “The forum reaffirmed that the development of the Niger Delta is inseparable from the development of Nigeria and urged all relevant authorities to translate policy commitments and announced projects into tangible outcomes for the country.”

title: N61.45bn Debt: UBA Seeks Jail for Nine Over WEMPCO Factory
body: • Bank alleges respondents used thugs to prevent receiver from taking control of Ogun factory Wale Igbintade United Bank for Africa (UBA) Plc has asked the Federal High Court in Lagos to commit nine individuals linked to Western Metal Products Company (WEMPCO) to prison for allegedly disobeying a court order appointing a receiver-manager over assets of the industrial conglomerate. The application is the latest development in the bank’s efforts to recover N61.45 billion allegedly owed by WEMPCO and its associated companies, amid claims that the respondents prevented the court-appointed receiver from taking control of the group’s factory in Magboro/Ibafo, Ogun State. In a committal notice published on Tuesday, October 27, pursuant to a court order permitting service by newspaper, UBA accused the respondents of “wilful, deliberate and orchestrated disobedience” of an April 2 order. The bank is asking the court to commit them to prison until they comply with the order. Those named in the application are Lewis Shui Noor Tung, Phillip Shui Che Tung, Alhaji M.A. Ola Yusuf, Tung Lawrence Blake, Alli Aare Hadji Tokunbo, Paul Shui Po Tung, Robert Tung, CL Ip and Taiwo Alli. Their addresses are listed as 18 Wempco Road, Ogba, Ikeja, Lagos. Alli is the managing director of Nigerian Enamelware Company Plc, which is listed on the Nigerian Exchange and is among the 17 defendant companies in the proceedings. Robert Tung also sits on the company’s board. The allegations have yet to be tested in court, while WEMPCO’s response was not immediately available. The dispute stems from an April 2 order by Justice Akintayo Aluko of the Federal High Court, Lagos, freezing up to N61,445,695,993.76 in funds linked to WEMPCO and associated defendants across 27 banks and fintech platforms. The judge also appointed Romeo Ese Michael as receiver-manager over assets not already pledged under a 2019 credit agreement. Under the order, banks and fintech operators, including Moniepoint, OPay and Kuda, were directed to disclose and preserve balances belonging to the defendants. The receiver-manager’s powers also extend to two Wärtsilä power generators belonging to the defendants, wherever they may be found. In an affidavit supporting its committal application, UBA alleged that the respondents frustrated the receiver’s efforts to take control of the Magboro/Ibafo factory after court bailiffs had handed it over to him. According to the bank, the respondents brought in thugs, broke the receiver’s locks and threatened his staff with “serious injury”. UBA further alleged that the respondents continued to operate the business and divert its funds despite the court order. The bank maintained that the factory had remained under the respondents’ control since the alleged incident, preventing the receiver from effectively exercising his court-sanctioned powers. The court papers also detail unsuccessful attempts by the parties to negotiate a settlement of the underlying debt dispute. On June 22, WEMPCO’s lawyers at SimmonsCooper Partners, led by Senior Advocate of Nigeria Dapo Akinosun, wrote to UBA seeking an urgent meeting to discuss a possible resolution. They proposed an interim standstill arrangement, a joint reconciliation of the accounts and a structured repayment framework. UBA’s lawyer, Senior Advocate of Nigeria Temilolu Adamolekun, responded the following day, questioning the proposal in view of what the bank described as the respondents’ resort to physical force and self-help. Adamolekun questioned how a company allegedly “deploying physical violence on ground and resorting to self-help” could simultaneously seek negotiations, but agreed to meet its representatives. The parties met at UBA’s Marina head office in Lagos on June 26 and agreed to conduct a joint inspection of the Magboro facility on July 2. UBA alleged, however, that WEMPCO and its lawyers failed to attend the inspection and had since “gone incommunicado”. The bank said the failed inspection and the respondents’ alleged continued control of the factory had further complicated efforts to enforce the court order and recover the outstanding debt. Other defendants in the underlying proceedings include Lagos Oriental Hotel Limited, United Rolling Mills Limited, Wempco Steel Mill Company and Prime Nigeria Tiles Company, among other WEMPCO-linked entities. WEMPCO was founded by K.F. Tung, who first arrived in Nigeria in 1967. The committal application seeks to compel compliance with the April 2 order as UBA pursues recovery of the N61.45 billion debt. The court has yet to determine the allegations or grant the request to commit the nine respondents to prison.

title: PTDF Extends Partnership with 24 UK Varsities, Seeks Fee Cut, End to Visa Rejections
body: • Nearly 15,000 Nigerians sponsored for studies at home, abroad •British High Commissioner promises collaboration Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja The Petroleum Technology Development Fund (PTDF) has expanded its academic collaboration with universities in the UK to 24, including Robert Gordon, Strathclyde, Portsmouth, Aberdeen, Newcastle, Birmingham, Glasgow, Leicester, Liverpool and Manchester. Also, the organisation has called on the British government to reduce tuition fees for Nigerian scholarship beneficiaries and address visa rejections affecting students seeking postgraduate education in the UK. Executive Secretary of PTDF, Prof. Shehu Aliyu, made the disclosure yesterday during a high-level strategic bilateral meeting with the British High Commissioner to Nigeria, Pete Vowles, at the General Shehu Musa Yar’Adua University of Geological Sciences and Engineering Technology (UGSET) in Kaduna. Aliyu said the cost of education in Britain, compared with other European countries, and difficulties encountered by some scholars in securing visas were among the challenges confronting the Fund’s overseas scholarship programme. The PTDF chief also called for a framework to monitor Nigerian scholars studying in Britain, with support from the British government and their host universities, to strengthen oversight and cooperation throughout their academic programmes. He said the concerns needed to be addressed even as the Fund sought to deepen its longstanding educational relationship with the UK and expand opportunities for Nigerian students to acquire advanced technical knowledge. He explained that PTDF’s mandate rested on three integrated pillars: human capital development, institutional capacity building, and research and development. The Fund’s strategic priorities, he said, included employment-oriented programmes, the development of a knowledge-driven economy, reducing capital flight by expanding training within Nigeria, positioning the country as an exporter of skilled energy professionals, and integrating digital technologies and artificial intelligence into its programmes. “The strategic bond between Nigeria and the United Kingdom has yielded immense results in human capital development over the decades. Today, by breathing full life into the General Shehu Musa Yaradua University of Geological Sciences and Engineering Technology in Kaduna, we have an unprecedented opportunity to leave a lasting legacy for future generations of energy professionals across Africa. “I would like to take this opportunity to highlight several challenges we are facing with our UK partners for the High Commissioner’s attention. These include high tuition fees compared to other European countries and visa rejections. We also hope to develop a plan to monitor our scholars in the UK, with support from the UK government and the hosting university,” he stressed. He disclosed that the Fund had sponsored nearly 15,000 Nigerians for undergraduate and postgraduate education in Nigeria and abroad through its Overseas Scholarship Scheme and In-Country Scholarship Scheme. As of July 2026, the organisation stated that 1,571 scholars were studying across 15 countries and more than 120 partner institutions, while demand for PTDF scholarships continued to increase significantly. Aliyu said the growing demand made it necessary for the Fund to explore ways of expanding access to internationally recognised qualifications without relying excessively on expensive overseas training. To achieve this, Aliyu pointed out that PTDF introduced the split-site PhD programme, which allows scholars to undertake part of their doctoral studies in Nigeria and the remainder at partner universities in the United Kingdom. The arrangement, he explained, was designed to reduce the cost of overseas education, strengthen local institutions and retain technical expertise within the country while maintaining international academic standards. “This model reduces the cost of overseas education, strengthens local institutions and ensures internationally recognised qualifications,” he said. He described the Kaduna university as a strategic investment intended to bridge the gap between academic theory and practical industry solutions, with a mandate extending beyond Nigeria to the wider West African sub-region and the Gulf of Guinea. Aliyu, however, said the availability of infrastructure alone would not be sufficient to achieve the university’s objectives without sustained academic, technical and institutional collaboration with international partners. “The administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s goal is to transition the University from a physical asset into a thriving, world-class institution of learning, applied research, and energy innovation,” he said. “And we believe the United Kingdom is our natural partner in achieving this ambition,” he explained. Responding, the UK envoy, Vowles, acknowledged the challenges raised by PTDF and pledged to convey the concerns about tuition fees and visa rejections to the relevant authorities in Britain. Vowles said his visit to Kaduna was important because of the city’s significance to Nigeria and the strategic value of the partnership between PTDF and British universities. He thanked the Fund for its continued investment in the British university sector, describing the Kaduna institution’s ambition to become a world-class postgraduate education and research centre serving the wider region as particularly encouraging. “It is clear from your presentation, from conversations, your efforts to create a world-class postgraduate education institution. It is your learning and your commitment to working with international partners,” he said. The High Commissioner said Britain remained committed to providing quality education through its partnership with PTDF and supporting the development of talented Nigerian scholars. He highlighted measures already taken to improve the scholarship process, particularly the recognition of PTDF as a government-approved sponsor, which he said should help streamline visa applications. He assured Aliyu of Britain’s continued commitment to engaging with the Fund and finding ways for Nigerian scholars to access quality education at British institutions. Vowles added that the relationship offered opportunities for both countries to learn from one another, strengthen their understanding and make better use of their natural resources through sustained academic and technical cooperation.

title: Tinubu Seeks Law to Bring Nigerians Convicted Abroad Home to Serve Jail Terms
body: • Transmits amendment bill to Senate, seeks framework for prisoner transfers under bilateral agreements • Senate orders probe of travel agencies over suspected human trafficking networks in Libya Sunday Aborisade in Abuja President Bola Tinubu has asked the senate to amend the law governing the transfer of convicted offenders, seeking to empower Nigeria to enter into agreements with foreign governments to enable eligible Nigerians convicted abroad to serve their prison sentences at home. The proposed legislation, known as Transfer of Convicted Offenders Enactment and Enforcement Amendment Bill 2026, seeks to amend the Transfer of Convicted Offenders Enactment and Enforcement Act, Cap 216, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004. Tinubu transmitted the bill to Senate in a letter read by Senate President Godswill Akpabio during plenary on Tuesday. The president explained the proposed amendment would provide a legal framework for Nigeria to enter into agreements with other countries for the transfer of convicted offenders, while also enabling the country to honour similar requests from foreign governments under mutually agreed conditions. In the letter, Tinubu said the bill sought to give effect to agreements between Nigeria and other countries on the transfer of convicted persons. He stated, “The Transfer of Convicted Offenders Enactment and Enforcement Amendment Bill 2026 seeks to amend the Transfer of Convicted Offenders Enactment and Enforcement Act, Act Cap 216, Laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 2004, to give effect to the provisions of any scheme or agreement for the transfer of convicted offenders between the Federal Government of Nigeria and the government of any other country.” The president explained that the proposed amendment would empower him to extend the application of the law to countries with which Nigeria had entered into relevant agreements through an order published in the Federal Gazette. According to him, the provision would facilitate the implementation of prisoner-transfer arrangements, particularly with countries outside the Commonwealth. After reading the president’s letter, Akpabio referred the bill to Senate Committee on Rules and Business for further legislative consideration. The proposed amendment comes amid several high-profile cases involving Nigerians convicted by foreign courts, including former public officials and political figures. Among them is former Delta State Governor James Ibori, who was sentenced to 13 years’ imprisonment in the United Kingdom in 2012 after pleading guilty to money-laundering offences. He was released in 2016. Former Deputy Senate President Ike Ekweremadu was sentenced to nine years and eight months’ imprisonment in the UK in 2023 over his role in an organ-trafficking conspiracy involving a young man. Similarly, Abidemi Rufai, a former aide to Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun, was sentenced to five years’ imprisonment in the United States in 2022 for wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. Nigeria and the United Kingdom already have a prisoner-transfer arrangement that allows eligible prisoners to serve their sentences in their home countries, subject to applicable legal requirements and the agreement of both governments. The proposed amendment seeks to strengthen the domestic legal framework for implementing similar arrangements with countries outside the Commonwealth. However, the proposed legislation would not automatically entitle every Nigerian convicted abroad to return home to serve a sentence. Any transfer would depend on the terms of the relevant agreement, the eligibility of the prisoner and the applicable legal conditions. Meanwhile, Senate directed a comprehensive investigation into suspected human-trafficking networks and travel agencies allegedly connected to the trafficking, exploitation and abuse of Nigerians in Libya. The resolution followed the adoption of a report on the urgent need to protect Nigerians from trafficking, slavery and other human rights abuses in the North African country. Presenting the report on behalf of the joint committees on Diaspora, Judiciary, Foreign Affairs and Special Duties, Senator Anthony Yaro, representing Gombe South, said the committees had consulted relevant stakeholders, received memoranda, and examined the circumstances surrounding the abuses before making their recommendations. He said the recommendations were designed to strengthen Nigeria’s institutional response to human trafficking, improve the protection of victims and disrupt criminal networks responsible for exploiting vulnerable Nigerians. The motion for the consideration and adoption of the report received the support of Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central. In its resolutions, Senate called for stronger enforcement of existing anti-trafficking laws, increased funding for the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP) and other relevant agencies, and a comprehensive investigation into suspected trafficking networks and their associated travel agencies. The lawmakers also called for the establishment of a national reintegration and protection programme for returning victims of trafficking. They recommended that the National Commission for Refugees, Migrants and Internally Displaced Persons coordinate the programme in collaboration with NAPTIP and other relevant institutions to ensure that returning victims received appropriate protection and support. Senate urged the federal government to intensify diplomatic engagement with Libya through bilateral and multilateral channels to combat trafficking and promote safe and legal migration. Contributing to the debate, Senator Neda Imasuen, representing Edo South, said the country’s major challenge was not the absence of laws against human trafficking but the failure to enforce existing legislation effectively and hold offenders accountable. Imasuen’s position underscored concerns about the gap between Nigeria’s legal framework and the effective prosecution of individuals and networks involved in trafficking and exploitation. In his remarks, Akpabio called for stronger deterrent measures against perpetrators of serious crimes, stating that laws must carry sufficient consequences to discourage criminal conduct. Recalling his tenure as Governor of Akwa Ibom State, the senate president said he had signed an anti-kidnapping law prescribing the death penalty and the forfeiture of property where a kidnapped victim was found. He also advocated a strict Know-Your-Tenant policy, stating that landlords should be able to provide information about their tenants when crimes were committed. Akpabio warned that landlords who failed to provide relevant information could face questions over their possible complicity in criminal activities. As part of its resolutions, Senate directed NAPTIP to work with the Nigeria Police, Nigeria Immigration Service, Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, and Ministry of Foreign Affairs to investigate identified travel agencies. The agencies are expected to interrogate their directors, officers and agents to establish the extent of their involvement, if any, in recruitment networks, financial transactions and travel arrangements connected to the trafficking and exploitation of Nigerians abroad. The investigation is expected to help identify the individuals and organisations facilitating the movement of victims, expose the financial channels sustaining trafficking operations and strengthen measures to prevent further exploitation. The senate’s resolutions also placed renewed emphasis on victim protection, the reintegration of returning Nigerians and diplomatic cooperation with Libya, alongside stronger law enforcement against suspected traffickers.

title: NRS, BPP Move to Reform Procurement System, Seek Better Value for Public Spending
body: • Adedeji aims to replicate tax reform success in procurement to cut waste, boost confidence in tax spending James Emejo in Abuja The Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) and the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP), yesterday strengthened their collaboration to reform the country’s public procurement framework, with a focus on improving value for money, reducing administrative bottlenecks and strengthening the economic returns on government expenditure. Executive Chairman of NRS, Dr. Zacch Adedeji, said the engagement with the procurement regulator would help align the ongoing review of the Public Procurement Act with the operational realities of government institutions, ensuring that reforms deliver tangible benefits to the economy. Speaking when he hosted the Director General of BPP, Dr. Adebowale Adedokun, and their respective technical teams at the Revenue House in Abuja, Adedeji stressed the importance of making public spending more effective, noting that visible results from government expenditure could strengthen citizens’ confidence in the tax system and encourage voluntary compliance. He said the engagement provided an opportunity for both institutions to exchange ideas on proposed amendments to the procurement law and identify practical challenges that should be addressed in the reform process. Adedeji, who acknowledged the BPP’s support for the NRS team in navigating procurement procedures, said closer collaboration would help the revenue service avoid administrative pitfalls while ensuring that projects were executed efficiently and in accordance with the law. He also invited the procurement regulator to consider the specific operational challenges confronting the NRS in the ongoing review of the legal framework, emphasising that the outcome should benefit public institutions across the country. Technical team lead/Group Director, Support Services, NRS, Mr. Kunle Ogidi, while briefing the meeting, said the BPP had provided guidance and capacity-building support to the service, helping officials understand procurement requirements and manage the complexities associated with project execution. The team lead said the engagement was particularly important as the BPP worked towards reforming the Public Procurement Act, adding that closer consultations would enable the proposed changes to accommodate the practical needs of institutions responsible for delivering public services. He said the NRS considered the meeting an opportunity to contribute operational insights to the review process and strengthen cooperation between both agencies. Adedeji however, stated that the connection between tax collection and public procurement was critical to building confidence in government. According to him, citizens are more likely to appreciate their tax obligations when they can see that public funds are being deployed effectively to deliver infrastructure and other essential services. He maintained that demonstrating the benefits of public expenditure could serve as an important incentive for taxpayers to comply with their obligations, thereby supporting revenue generation and the government’s capacity to finance development. The NRS chairman Adedeji, reiterated the need for both agencies to sustain their partnership, stressing that efficient public spending could reinforce public confidence in government and its revenue mobilisation efforts. He said the visible impact of expenditure was important to encouraging taxpayers to recognise the benefits of paying taxes, adding that improved collaboration between revenue collection and procurement institutions would support better economic outcomes. In his remarks, Adedokun said the BPP was seeking a fundamental shift from a uniform procurement model to a sector-based approach that would reflect the different requirements of projects and services. He explained that applying identical procurement criteria to dissimilar sectors could undermine efficiency, adding that construction, healthcare and other specialised activities required approaches tailored to their distinct operational demands. The BPP director general said the proposed reforms would be supported by stronger professional capacity, technology and improved contractor classification, enabling procuring entities to identify qualified service providers and apply appropriate standards. He called for the NRS’s support in strengthening the national database of contractors and businesses participating in public procurement, noting that broader coverage could improve transparency, support compliance and enhance government revenue generation. Adedokun also clarified that procurement decisions should not be driven solely by the lowest bid, but by the overall value delivered to the public. He said the objective was to secure value for money and ensure that public contracts produced the intended results, even where the cheapest offer was not necessarily the most suitable option. According to him, a technology-driven procurement system, supported by reliable contractor data and appropriate categorisation, would reduce cumbersome processes and improve the efficiency of public contracting. Adedokun said the BPP had submitted recommendations on the proposed amendments to the National Assembly and expressed the agency’s readiness to continue engaging stakeholders to ensure that the revised framework addressed existing challenges. He added that the bureau was pursuing measures to strengthen its institutional capacity and expand its operational presence across the 36 states, while encouraging greater collaboration with government agencies. The BPP chief said effective procurement was central to national development, given its implications for project delivery, job creation, infrastructure provision and the efficient use of public resources. He urged public officials to comply with established procedures, warning that adherence to due process remained essential to protecting them and the institutions they served from procurement-related violations. Both institutions expressed commitment to continued engagement on the procurement reform process, with the aim of improving transparency, strengthening accountability and ensuring that public funds deliver greater value to Nigerians.

title: In Bid to Boost Food Security, Curb Insecurity in Farming Areas, MOFI Partners DAPCO, Military-linked Institutions
body: Ndubuisi Francis in Abuja Ministry of Finance Incorporated (MOFI), the investment arm of the federal government, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Defence Agricultural Assets and Projects Development Company (DAPCO) and other military-linked investment institutions to provide security for large-scale agricultural investments as part of overall efforts to restore investor confidence in farming parts of the country affected by insecurity. The MoU, which involves MOFI, Integranium Holdings, and DAPCO, supported by Defence Holding Company Limited, seeks to create a framework that combines investment mobilisation with security and project management. It is expected to help unlock, among other agriculture projects, multi-billion-dollar soybean and sugarcane projects in Yobe and Jigawa states, where security concerns has made it difficult to attract the capital needed to develop them. On the side-lines of the agreement signing ceremony in Abuja, Tuesday, MOFI’s Executive Director, Investments, who is responsible for the Integranium investment framework, Dr. Femi Ogunseinde, said the partnership would allow the institutions to return to prospective investors with a security arrangement that is fashioned to protect their investments. According to Ogunseinde, security has constituted one of the major obstacles preventing domestic and international investors from committing funds to large-scale agricultural projects in Nigeria. He said, “We have a soybean initiative in Yobe, we have a sugarcane initiative in Jigawa—all large-scale, all multi-billion-dollar projects. “Without having that security anchor to ensure that whatever comes from wherever to invest, the investments are safe, it becomes very difficult for us to do anything.” He submitted that attracting investors had been difficult without assurances that their money and agricultural operations would be secured. He stated that the new partnership would provide a platform through which the government and its partners could approach prospective investors and demonstrate that arrangements were being developed to address their security concerns. Ogunseinde disclosed that the initiative was intended to attract substantial private sector and international financing into agricultural production, rather than depend solely on public funds. He said an estimated 30 million to 35 million hectares of farming land could be available, providing considerable scope for expanding large-scale agricultural production. He explained that the partnership would help create a platform for investors interested in developing that potential, including offshore companies and financiers. According to him, the intention is to achieve economies of scale by bringing together land, capital, agricultural expertise and the security arrangements needed to support commercial farming. Ogunseinde hinted at the possibility of attracting investments worth between $1 billion and $2 billion from the initiative. The agreement is expected to cover risk management, security planning, and project management, with DAPCO working alongside MOFI and its investment partners to develop and implement agricultural projects. Although he made no reference to a particular project or provided any clue on the commencement date, Ogunseinde said the partners had already identified several opportunities and expected at least one project for ground breaking before the end of the year. Group Managing Director of Defence Holding Company Limited, Air Vice Marshal (AVM) Anthony Victor Ndache, disclosed that the MoU signed by the institutions was a broad agreement covering agriculture, hospitality and other investment areas. Ndache added that more detailed agreements would be developed for the individual projects as the partnership progresses. He said the initiative was intended to benefit Nigeria by improving national productivity, stating that the President Bola Tinubu administration prioritises food security. In his remarks, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of DAPCO, Aliyu Abdulhameed, said the defence establishment’s role was to ensure that financing reached agricultural opportunities in rural areas under secure and properly structured arrangements. Abdulhameed stated that agricultural investments often took place far from major urban centres, making security a critical factor for investors’ consideration. He said the partnership would enable the institutions to combine their respective strengths to develop agricultural projects across the country. Managing Director of MOFI, Dr. Armstrong Takang, said Nigeria needed to make better use of its land, water resources and people to produce sufficient food for households and industries, while generating additional supplies for export. Takang said the agricultural initiative was also expected to help address food inflation by increasing the volume of food produced locally. The partnership, he stressed, would focus on developing bankable agribusiness opportunities capable of attracting funding from both public and private investors. The projects are expected to support large-scale agricultural operators and encourage more investment across the farming value chain. Takang also said the initiative could create additional demand for fertiliser supplied through MOFI’s holdings and produced by Nigerian companies. He cited the PFI NPK, the Fertiliser Aggregation Company, as one of the businesses that could benefit from an expanded market for agricultural inputs. According to him, increased agricultural activity could create a larger market for fertiliser and help improve soil productivity, culminating in higher food yield. Among others, the initiative is equally expected to extend economic opportunities to communities around the farms, as surrounding communities would be involved in projects established in their areas, allowing the benefits of investment to spread beyond the immediate farm operations. Serving military personnel and veterans would be among the groups the partnership intends to incorporate into agricultural projects. The partners also plan to use technology, innovation and improved farming skills to increase productivity and make better use of available land. The MoU was signed in Abuja, Tuesday, and the partners were expected to assess each project, considering its financial viability, investment potential, due diligence requirements and value for money before proceeding. Specific production targets, the number of hectares to be cultivated under the programme, the number of jobs expected to be created or the total funding required will be unveiled as the initiative progresses. The MoU establishes the broad framework for cooperation, while individual projects will have to undergo further assessment and structuring before their implementation.

title: End to US, Israel mischief crucial for regional security
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 28 (MNA) – Iran's foreign minister told his Jordanian counterpart that restoring regional security requires stopping US aggression and containing Israeli expansionism, during a phone call on Tuesday.
Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi and Jordanian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi exchanged views on regional developments in a phone call on Tuesday.
Araghchi outlined Iran's positions on regional developments and stressed the need for serious action by Islamic countries and the world to confront the continuation of genocide and expansionism by the Zionist regime.
He recalled the devastating consequences of US and Israeli military aggression against Iran for the region and the world, saying that restoring security to the region requires an end to US aggressive and interventionist actions and curbing the Zionist regime's expansionism and warmongering.
Araghchi also condemned a terrorist attack on a church in southern Jordan and expressed condolences to the families of the victims.
The two foreign ministers stressed the importance of using diplomacy and continuing political consultations to protect regional peace and stability.

title: Nigeria’s president seeks parliament approval for about $21.7bn borrowing
body: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to approve a supplementary external borrowing plan worth $20.52 billion and €1.05 billion ($1.17 billion) for 2026-2027 to fund infrastructure and other projects. In a letter to lawmakers, Tinubu said the plan would support projects across sectors, including infrastructure, agriculture, healthcare, education, water supply, security, employment generation, and financial management reforms aimed at accelerating economic growth. “I submit the ​attached Federal Government 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing ‌Plan ⁠for consideration and early approval of the National Assembly to ensure prompt implementation of our projects,” ​Tinubu said. Tinubu ​said ⁠external funding was needed to bridge a financing gap ​created by the country’s ​substantial ⁠infrastructure needs. The borrowing request will require National Assembly ⁠approval before the government can proceed with the proposed financing programme.

title: Ukraine's 'shoot the archer' strategy is far from a silver bullet
body:
Kyiv wants US and European support to get at Russian launchers before they fire. History and current realities tell us that is harder than leaders think.
The story of the Ukraine war is one of “wonder weapons” and their failure to deliver.
First it was HIMARS . Then the Abrams tank . Then F-16s . Then ATACMS . Over and over, Kyiv and its backers have issued urgent demands for a new weapon or capability billed as the key to turning the tide of the war in Ukraine’s favor. Each time, after protesting, the U.S. chose to give in. And each time, the promised silver bullet failed to solve Kyiv’s battlefield challenges.
Now, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky and his champions in the U.S. Congress are back with their next request: the intelligence, targeting support , and weapons to find and destroy Russian ballistic missile launchers inside of Russia . As in previous instances, the plan is described as foolproof, an “ easy ” fix for Ukraine’s air defense challenge, and nearly costless for American taxpayers.
But this new proposal is none of these things. Not only will the plan fail to protect Ukraine’s cities, but it will take another step toward a direct U.S.-Russia war while leaving the U.S. homeland exposed in future conflicts. The Trump administration should dismiss the latest Ukrainian appeal as counter to American interests.
The motives behind Kyiv’s “ shoot the archer” strategy are easy to understand . Facing the coming winter with few of the Patriot air defense interceptors that it needs to protect against Russian ballistic missile attacks, Ukraine hopes it can use strikes of its own to disable Russia’s launchers pre-emptively.
The approach is not novel. The Trump administration has adopted the same strategy in its recent campaigns in the Middle East , first against the Houthis and then against Iran , seeking to remove the ability of each adversary to fire missiles at U.S. bases, partners, and commercial ships. Similarly, during the first Gulf War, the U.S. military exerted considerable effort searching for scud missile launchers in the desert to prevent Iraqi attacks on U.S. forces and regional neighbors.
In each of these cases, even with far superior conventional military capabilities and advanced intelligence and weapons, U.S. efforts were much less successful than anticipated or advertised. During the 1991 Gulf War, for example, the U.S. operation involved 1,500 sorties but resulted in few — if any — confirmed successful hits on Iraqi scud missile launchers. The Pentagon instead turned to special forces personnel who roamed the desert looking for the launchers. The U.S. failure to suppress Iranian missile fire has been just as stark. Despite over 10,000 American sorties, Iran still retains 50% of its missile launchers according to some reports, many now hidden underground.
Should Ukraine decide to go after ballistic missile launchers inside of Russia, its challenges would be different from those the U.S. faced in the Middle East. To launch Iskander and other ballistic missiles, Russia relies on mobile systems positioned in regions close to Ukraine, concealed in dense forests, tree lines, or even in old industrial buildings and warehouses. In addition to being hidden, the launchers can travel at fast speeds and across off-road terrain, allowing Russian soldiers to use “shoot-and-scoot” tactics and making it harder for Ukraine to identify and target launchers before their location changes — especially at night, when many Ukrainian operations will occur.
Kyiv has requested from the United States several types of support for its campaign against Russian missile launchers. Its top priority is permission to use Starlink over Russian territory . This capability would, in theory, allow Ukraine to more easily destroy the Russian launchers responsible for ballistic missile attacks by providing targeting, command and control, and counter-electronic warfare support to facilitate Ukrainian drone operations inside Russian territory.
