title: Melania Trump Brokers Russia-Ukraine Ceasefire in Oleshky
body: US First Lady Melania Trump has announced a localised ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky in southern Ukraine’s Kherson region, with the agreement set to begin on 29 October to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and preparations for civilian evacuations. The White House said both countries had agreed to temporarily halt all military activity in the city to enable aid to reach residents and establish a designated safe passage for civilians wishing to leave. Oleshky has been caught in fighting since Russian forces seized the city during the full-scale invasion in 2022. Former residents told AFP last month that people who remained faced severe food shortages, lacked medicine and struggled to leave. In a statement, Trump described the situation as dire, saying the remaining population consisted mainly of elderly residents who urgently needed medical care, medicine, food and clean water. She also cited limited electricity, mined roads and continuing military attacks. Trump said she believed humanitarian assistance and the evacuation of elderly residents would have been impossible without her intervention. White House outlines Trump’s role in ceasefire According to the White House, Trump first learned about conditions in Oleshky during a private discussion at her Fostering the Future Together event in New York during the 81st United Nations General Assembly. She said she and her representative immediately used a communication channel established with Russia and Ukraine during six previous reunifications involving 34 children. Both countries assigned teams to coordinate the arrangements, including demining, and worked on the process continuously, she said. The White House said Trump and her representative subsequently worked directly with Russian and Ukrainian leaders to establish the terms of the localised ceasefire. It described her role as an “Exclusive Intermediary”, saying she initiated discussions and helped align both sides on the agreement’s objectives, technical procedures, timing and terms. Civilian assistance and evacuation plans Trump said civilian representatives from Russia and Ukraine would visit residents in their homes to assess their needs. Residents who wish to leave will receive coordinated assistance and transport to their preferred destination. Trump said some may choose Russia, while others may prefer Ukraine. She also said she had secured the participation of an impartial American media organisation to accompany and document Russian and Ukrainian teams on the ground throughout the process. According to Trump, the organisation’s presence would help ensure authorities respect each family’s wishes. The ceasefire is intended to create a temporary window for humanitarian assistance and civilian evacuation in a city where residents have faced prolonged hardship. The effectiveness of the arrangement will depend on its implementation on the ground and the ability of aid and evacuation teams to operate safely. title: US military spending on Iran conflict reaches $47 bln — The Hill
body:
WASHINGTON, October 28. /TASS/. US spending on its military operation against Iran has reached $47 bln, The Hill reported, citing estimates submitted to Congress by the US Central Command (CENTCOM).
According to the newspaper, the figures were recorded as of October 16. Thus, total US spending on the military operation against Iran has increased by more than $3 bln since early September. As of September 3, CENTCOM had reported that the conflict with Iran had cost $43.6 bln.
The US and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28. In June, Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding providing for an immediate cessation of hostilities on all fronts, including in Lebanon. However, overnight on July 8, the US resumed large-scale strikes against Iran, accusing Tehran of violating the terms of the agreements reached concerning the Strait of Hormuz. Approximately 25% of global oil trade and around 20% of global liquefied natural gas trade pass through the strait. Subsequently, the US administration effectively signaled an end to the use of large-scale military force against Iran and a shift toward attempts to economically strangle the country through sanctions.

title: Former Miss Switzerland accuses Donald Trump of rape
body: Donald Trump has been accused of rape by a model and former Miss Switzerland in a report produced by the Democratic Party. Beatrice Keul, who shortly before the 2024 election claimed the president had groped her in November 1993, has now alleged that Mr Trump also raped her during that incident. The report, released Monday, detailed an investigation by US House Democrats into Mr Trump’s alleged connections to Jeffrey Epstein’s crimes. The White House denied the report’s allegations, with a spokesman describing the claims as “a desperate attempt by crazed Democrats to distract Americans from the surging Republican momentum driven by President Trump ’s historic achievements”. Beatrice Keul’s account is detailed in a House Democrats’ report examining the president’s alleged ties to Jeffrey Epstein During interviews with Democratic committee staffers “over several weeks”, Ms Keul said she met Mr Trump when she was 24 at a press event for a pageant at New York’s Plaza Hotel, which he owned at the time. According to Ms Keul, Mr Trump allegedly promised that he would arrange a visa for her and said he could ensure that she got accepted into New York University (NYU). “I will take care of you,” he told her, according to the claims in the report. After Mr Trump stepped away from their conversation, Ms Keul said she was immediately approached by Epstein, who described himself as “Don’s best friend” and invited her to a party at Mar-a-Lago. “We organise many parties with Don,” Epstein apparently told her. Mr Trump says that he ended his friendship with Epstein long before there were suspicions of any criminal wrongdoing and has repeatedly described him as a “creep” whom he kicked out of his Mar-a-Lago club. According to Ms Keul, Epstein introduced himself as ‘Don’s best friend’ Credit: Getty Images/Davidoff Studios Photography According to the Democrats’ report, a representative for Mr Trump later allegedly invited Ms Keul to meet the future president upstairs at the Plaza Hotel. “Upon entering, Trump reportedly grabbed Keul from behind and forcibly raped her; in the process, tearing her dress and causing bleeding and bruising on multiple parts of her body,” the report claimed. “Keul described the rape as ‘brutal,’” the report added. Following the alleged assault, Ms Keul claimed that Mr Trump “sat her on the edge of the bed, repeated his promises to arrange for a visa and NYU admission, and made her promise she would keep quiet, saying, ‘[T]he show must go on.’” In Ms Keul’s original claims in October 2024, she accused Mr Trump of groping her at the Plaza Hotel in 1993. “He kissed me on the lips and on the neck. He tried to lift my dress. He was grabbing and touching my body everywhere he could,” she told The Daily Mail. But she said things did not go further. “I tried everything I could. Finally, I said ‘let’s talk first’ or something like that, then he slowed down,” she said. The 6ft 1in ex-model suggested it was her size that “saved her” from the alleged attack from escalating. The newspaper also reported that a longtime friend said Ms Keul “first told him her story of Trump’s unwanted sexual advances 20 years ago, and that her telling of the incident has not changed in the intervening years.” Allegations dismissed as ‘fake’ At the time, Karoline Leavitt, then press secretary to Mr Trump, described the allegations as “fake”. A White House spokesman said Mr Trump had been “fully exonerated of anything related to Epstein.” “This ‘report’ is nothing more than a desperate attempt by crazed Democrats to distract Americans from the surging Republican momentum driven by President Trump’s historic achievements,” they said. The newly released report summarises the accounts of four other women who have accused Mr Trump of rape or sexual assault. It also claims that Mr Trump, Epstein and others used the pageant at the Plaza Hotel as a “‘hunting ground’ to prey on vulnerable young women and girls.” “Five women have directly accused Trump of rape or sexual assault in Epstein’s company or presence; others have indicated that Epstein or Maxwell attempted to traffic them to Trump,” Jamie Raskin, the committee’s ranking member, said in a statement alongside the release of the report. “Trump’s Justice Department appears to be covering up these crimes to protect the President,” he added. The report landed just a week before the US midterm elections . Mr Trump’s handling of the Epstein files – along with inflation and rising energy prices caused by his war with Iran – has hamstrung Republican candidates even though the US president is not on the ballot.

title: Dozens of Former Airmen Are Running in the ’26 Midterms
body: More than three dozen former Airmen are running for Congress, including Democrats, Republicans, third-party and independent candidates, Air & Space Forces Magazine has found. The diverse group includes both former officers and enlisted members whose service spanned the Active, Guard, and Reserve components. They include sitting members as well as newcomers to politics. Meanwhile, some of Congress’ highest-profile veterans are departing the legislature. They include Rep. Don Bacon (R-Neb.), a retired brigadier general who has been deeply involved in legislation affecting his former service. Among the issues Bacon championed: recapitalizing Air National Guard fighter squadrons, rethinking pass-through funding in the Air Force budget, and a 2050 force design . Bacon’s district includes Offutt Air Force Base, Neb., home to U.S. Strategic Command. Bacon is the highest-ranking among 15 Air Force veterans in the current Congress, and not the only one leaving. Also retiring are Rep. Vern Buchanan (R-Fla.) and Rep. Barry Loudermilk (R-Ga.). Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-S.C.), a “total force Airmen” who served in all three components, died unexpected in July. Even so, the number of former Airmen in Congress could grow come January, depending on how the election turns out. A crop of new candidates either favored to win election or seen as competitive in their House races include: Chris McGowan (R-Iowa), heavily favored in his race, served in the Air Force and Iowa Air National Guard. Having attended Undergraduate Pilot Training, he reclassified as an intelligence officer, according to his official bio. Jace Yarborough (R-Texas), also heavily favored, has served on Active Duty and remains in the Air Force Reserve. A lawyer, he touts his legal work challenging the military over past “vaccine mandates, religious discrimination, taxpayer-funded abortion travel, and woke diversity, equity, and inclusion policies.” David Flippo (R-Nev.), slightly favored in his race, is a retired USAF lieutenant colonel and former maintenance and logistics officer. His official bio touts his work establishing “three combat bases in Iraq.,” Having said in the past that he received a Bronze Star for valor, he later apologized noting he received a Bronze Star without the valor device. Carlos De La Cruz (R-Texas), is competing in a race handicapped by pollsters as a toss-up. He served 20 years in the Air Force as a Military Working Dog handler and an intelligence professional, deploying multiple times to the Middle East. Rebecca Bennett (D-N.J.), is locked in a tight race. The former U.S. Navy helicopter pilot now serves in the Air National Guard. Eric Conroy (R-Ohio), is seen as a slight underdog in his race. The U.S. Air Force Academy grad , he is a former intelligence officer who worked with Special Operations units and later served in the CIA. Kristina Knickerbocker (D-Ohio) is also seen as a slight underdog. The Air Force major, a nurse who has served both on Active-Duty and in the Reserve, is running to represent the district that includes Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio. Combined with House incumbents running in safe seats and Senators not up for reelection this cycle, these Congressional newcomers could raise the number of former blue-suiters in the Capitol. Among them, former F-22 pilot Rep. August Pfluger is the lone fighter pilot. In September, at AFA’s Air, Space & Cyber conference, Pfluger called for more “wingmen” to join him as legislators. “I am the only fifth-generation pilot in Congress,” Pfluger said. “I need some wingmen to come join me. … God bless my Navy SEAL friends, and they are dear friends, but we’ve got a lot of them in Congress. What we don’t have is a lot of air and space expertise.” Pfluger, facing little challenge, could be up for a leadership position in the Republican conference, depending on how the election goes, according to Punchbowl News. Another Air Force vet whose leadership position could be affected by the larger midterm results is Sen. Roger Wicker (R-Miss.) The former Air Force JAG officer chairs the Senate Armed Services Committee, but would become the ranking member if Democrats win the Senate. title: Saudi’s biggest oil refinery hit with missile, say Yemen’s Houthis
body: DUBAI, UAE – Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said on Tuesday, October 27, they had hit Saudi Arabia’s Ras Tanura oil refinery, the ⁠biggest in the kingdom, with a ballistic missile. Intensifying hostilities between Yemen and Saudi Arabia have further disrupted oil supplies and heightened the risk of a wider regional conflict , eight months since the Iran war began. The Houthis also said they had attacked Saudi military aircraft and repelled an advance by Saudi-backed forces near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, an important Red Sea shipping route. The Houthis’ military spokesperson, Yahya Saree, said the strike on the Ras Tanura refinery had caused a fire at the complex, which also includes a shipping terminal and is located on the Gulf, west of the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the strike. Ras Tanura, which has a capacity of 550,000 barrels per day, was shut for a period in the early months of the Iran war as a precautionary measure. Nearly all Saudi Arabia’s oil exports flow through two main ports: Ras Tanura in the Gulf and Yanbu on the Red Sea, both of which the Houthis have attacked in the past. Bloomberg News cited a person familiar with the matter as saying Saudi Arabia had contained a fire near Ras Tanura’s terminal. Airstrikes The ​Houthis said they had attacked two military transport jets at Najran Airport and an airbase in Khamis Mushait. They also said they attacked the Saudi defense ministry building in Riyadh, and Abha airport. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation of the attacks. On Tuesday afternoon, civil defense authorities briefly issued an air raid alert in the Saudi capital Riyadh. Falling debris from the interception of two ballistic missiles over Riyadh caused material damage to a building, a construction site and a vehicle, the Saudi Civil Defense said later on Tuesday. The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis in support of Yemen’s internationally recognized government said it had intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis towards Riyadh. The Houthis said they had repelled an advance by forces they described as Saudi-backed from the southern approaches to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces earlier this month pushed the Houthis out of coastal areas they had seized in September, loosening the group’s grip on a vital Red Sea oil route. Houthi-affiliated Al Masirah TV reported Saudi strikes on the Yemeni city of Mocha. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation. The fighting has shattered a 2022 UN-brokered truce between the coalition and the Houthis, who control the Yemeni capital Sanaa. On Monday, October 26, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iranian officials in Tehran to try to reduce regional tensions. Parliament in Egypt, which has said it is considering joining the three countries in a mutual defense pact, authorized Egypt’s military on Monday to help defend Saudi Arabia if asked. – Rappler.com

title: AI will bring in universal income and everyone will get wealthier, Oracle's Larry Ellison says
body: The widespread roll-out of artificial intelligence will eventually lead to universal income and will make "everyone wealthier", the executive chairman and chief technology officer of Oracle said on Tuesday. The ubiquitous use of robots across different industries and sectors will enable people to be more productive, Larry Ellison said in a wide-ranging discussion at the Oracle AI World event in Las Vegas. "We decided to get better tools, and we're going to build better systems ... The tools make people much better, makes us much more productive," he said. Highlighting examples of robotic surgeons and autopilot on planes, Mr Ellison said the tech will replace some jobs but also reduce costs. With the government taxing "everything we produce ... we need to change from taxing human labour to taxing value-added tax returns", he said. "A lot of companies have value-added tax. So when the robots add value, all the value that the robots add is cash, and we can have universal product income." While it will take more than a decade to come about, "eventually, robots will do more and more work that we don't want to do - but they're adding value". "We are on track [to get] healthier and wealthier because of AI - and with the right taxation systems and the right computer systems - all of that is critical," Mr Ellison said. While the concept of AI eventually creating a system of universal income has been touted in the past, it has not gained universal acceptance. In a report in May, the International Labour Organisation stressed that universal basic income funded by the government is not the answer to the impact of AI on the labour market. The report by the UN body disputed claims by tech chief executives that AI will devastate labour markets catastrophically and that the productivity gains it generates will make such transfers noninflationary. "Both claims are empirically weak, and the second does not follow from the first even if the first were true," it said. For universal basic income to work, AI needs to expand supply in the sectors in which people will spend the new income, it said. The composition of productivity gains "does not support this". "The state can increase the number printed on every cheque. Whether the goods and services that determine real welfare, housing, health, quality food, care, are available in sufficient quantity at stable prices depends on supply-side conditions that AI improves only partially and unevenly," the report added. Cancer cure The impact of AI on the healthcare sector in particular is expected to be extremely significant, Mr Ellison said. "AI's great gift to the world will be ... [that] most cancers will be gone in five years, and certainly 10 years," he said. And cures won't be only for the very wealthy. An increase in the number of clinical trials and the quicker development of drugs supported by AI will make them reach markets faster, he explained "We think drug discovery is going to go through a golden age. But that's only half the problem. You get the drugs. You next have to get the drugs where you distribute them in such volume that the prices come down," Mr Ellison added. Some of the current innovations on the healthcare side also enable earlier diagnoses. For instance, with an "AI-enabled metagenomic test, we can do a much better job of diagnosing and catching sepsis early before it kills you very fast in the hospital", he said. DNA tests will also help providers detect cancer early on, while also distinguishing any false positives to ensure early treatment and better therapeutic care. When the quality of care goes up globally, "the overall cost per patient goes down dramatically", he added.

title: China’s families are now supporting more old people than kids
body: Families in China are now supporting more elderly people than children, the government has said. Official data released last week show that the ratio of China’s dependent elderly people to the working-age population rose to 23% last year, overtaking the figure for children, which stood at 22%. The numbers are closely watched for signs of how China’s shrinking workforce will affect both the world’s second-largest economy and global growth. The latest figures mark a significant milestone as China grapples with an ageing population that could affect families, pensions and healthcare spending, analysts say. China has prepared for a growing proportion of elderly people in recent years, while urging younger generations to marry and couples to have more children . The latest data from China’s National Bureau of Statistics show that more than 223 million people in China are aged 65 and above, accounting for nearly 16% of the country’s total population. At the same time, about 213 million children are aged 14 and under. No official commentary accompanied the statistics. But the Chinese state-controlled news outlet Global Times wrote that the nation’s “entry into a moderately ageing society” results from a mix of factors, including the “size of past birth cohorts” and longer life expectancy. The shift could add strain on pension, healthcare, and long-term care systems, while also creating opportunities in the so-called silver economy that caters to older consumers, the newspaper said. “It reflects a historical trend in demographic development rather than a short-term phenomenon,” one researcher told the Global Times. The demographic shift is “symbolic” and could mean more public spending shifts from families and schools to pensions and healthcare, said Professor Stuart Gietel-Basten of The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. It may also challenge the country’s ambitions, as it could limit economic growth and people’s spending power, said National University of Singapore sociology lecturer Mu Zheng. Birth rates in China have been falling for years now China’s ageing population has been driven by a mix of factors, including rapid urbanisation and the effects of the controversial one-child policy , which was in place from 1980 to the end of 2015. The strategy, designed to keep China’s rapid population growth under control, is estimated by the country’s government to have prevented about 400 million births since it began, though this number has been contested. The policy played a key role in shrinking the population, meaning fewer younger people to support a growing number of elderly relatives, Mu said. But despite easing restrictions on family size, Beijing has struggled to persuade couples to have more children, with birth rates hitting historic lows. Other contributing factors include changing gender roles, rising living costs and higher education levels that have put pressure on fertility rates, Mu said. Beijing also made further support for older people part of its five-year economic blueprint, announced earlier this year. Financial support for pensioners has become an increasingly large part of Chinese government spending. By the end of 2025, more than 53 million elderly people were receiving senior citizen allowances and subsidies, according to official figures. The Global Times noted that many people entering old age who were born between the 1950s and the 1970s generally have higher incomes than previous generations, stronger purchasing power, and are healthier. The dependency ratio is widely used to measure ageing populations, but some experts have questioned it, arguing its scope is too limited. Gietel-Basten said using the statistics risks “taking agency away” from older people, many of whom he says have been misrepresented as dependants. It also fails to account for improvements in healthcare, he added.

title: Ukrainian forces launch 13 attacks on DPR settlements in past day
body:
DONETSK, October 28. /TASS/. Ukrainian forces carried out 13 attacks on populated areas of the Donetsk People’s Republic (DPR) over the past 24 hours, killing two people, the department for documenting Ukrainian war crimes under the DPR head and government’s administration reported.
"A total of 13 armed attacks by Ukrainian formations were recorded, with reports received of two civilians killed and four injured," the department said in a statement.
The department added that Ukrainian attacks had damaged residential buildings, trucks, passenger vehicles, and a civilian infrastructure facility.

title: PM Koretskyi orders faster repairs to Kyiv’s Southern Bridge
body:
Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi emphasized this in a Telegram post , Ukrinform reports.
“The Southern Bridge and the metro were hit. According to the Air Force, the enemy used up to 16 ballistic missiles. I was already in contact with the city administration this morning. I instructed the Ministry of Infrastructure to speed up the work to restore the bridge as quickly as possible. The government is providing the necessary assistance with the restoration. People need to be able to travel freely from one side of the river to the other. The other bridges remain operational, but the traffic load on them has increased,” the statement said.
Koretskyi urged local authorities to monitor passenger traffic and, if necessary, provide additional surface transport to metro stations that remain operational and to the urban rail service.
“People must be able to get to work and back home normally while the bridge is being repaired,” the Prime Minister stressed.
He reported that Russia had launched a large-scale attack on Ukraine overnight using missiles and attack drones. Kyiv bore the brunt of the assault, while 10 other regions also came under attack. One person was killed and at least 16 were injured.
As reported by Ukrinform, Russian forces attacked Kyiv with ballistic missiles, damaging medical facilities, a school, the Southern Bridge, a metro station, a university dormitory and an apartment building.

title: Egypt court fines journalist Lina Attalah and orders news site’s closure
body: The editor-in-chief of the independent Egyptian news outlet Mada Masr was detained for several hours after a court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website and ordered its closure, her lawyers say. Mada Masr said Lina Attalah was released after she paid the 3m Egyptian pounds ($53,500; £40,100) fine also handed down by the New Cairo Misdemeanours Court. It was the maximum possible penalty for the charge, which she had rejected. Amnesty International said the verdict represented “a crushing blow to press freedom”. It comes only weeks after six journalists working for the independent fact-checking platform Matsda2sh were charged with belonging to the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood. Egypt is among the top jailers of journalists globally, with 25 currently behind bars, according to the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ). President Abdul Fattah el-Sisi has overseen what human rights groups say is an unprecedented crackdown on dissent since he led the military’s overthrow of his predecessor, Muslim Brotherhood leader Mohammed Morsi, in 2013. Tens of thousands of people have been detained, mainly Brotherhood officials and supporters, but also leading secular and liberal activists, media workers and academics. The CPJ said Mada Masr, founded in 2013, was a vital source of critical reporting in Egypt and had long faced pressure from authorities over its journalism. The site had repeatedly sought an operating licence from the Supreme Media Regulatory Council (SMRC) since a new media law was passed in 2018, but its applications were either rejected or left unanswered, the media watchdog added. Amnesty International said Lina Attalah had also faced “years of harassment and intimidation”, including six criminal investigations over Mada Masr’s reporting. Last week, prosecutors summoned her for questioning over allegations that she published “false news” and operated a website without a licence. Mada Masr’s lawyer said the investigation included a recent report the website published about a wave of protests in prisons across the country, as well as a letter from the SMRC on its legal status. Attalah was released on bail and later referred to trial before the New Cairo Misdemeanours Court on the charge of operating a website without a licence. During Tuesday’s hearing, Judge Mohammed Mubarak ordered the courtroom to be cleared of everyone except Attalah, her eight-person defence team, and Hossam Bahgat, head of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights (EIPR), an independent human rights group. Bahgat told AFP that security personnel then filed in before the judge announced the court was denying several procedural requests made by the defence and appointing its own lawyer for Attalah. “In a move that astonished all those present, the judge recorded in the official court minutes that the court had appointed a lawyer from the Lawyers’ Syndicate to represent the defence,” he said. “Lina herself spoke up to object to this lawyer being appointed to represent her, which the judge refused to record in the court minutes. “In an even more shocking turn, the judge proceeded to dictate motions on behalf of this lawyer – who had not uttered a single word – and entered them into the official record,” he added. The judge then announced the fine for Attalah and ordered Mada Masr’s closure “amid shouts and protests from the defence”, before she was detained, according to Bahgat. On Tuesday evening, Mada Masr said it had paid the full fine to the court and that Attalah was released after several hours in custody. “During the release procedures, Attalah learned of a one-year prison sentence issued against her in absentia in 2024, on charges of publishing false news and managing an unlicensed website,” it added. “Her lawyers took steps to challenge the ruling, with a hearing in a retrial of the case scheduled for 11 November.” Amnesty International warned that the court’s verdict marked “a dark day for independent journalism” in Egypt and demanded that it be overturned. “This draconian ruling is the culmination of years of relentless harassment and unjust proceedings designed to shut down one of the country’s last remaining independent media voices,” said the group’s senior director for regional impact, Yasmine Ahmed. “Lina Attalah should never have been prosecuted for exercising her right to freedom of expression and doing her journalistic job.” CPJ Regional Director Sara Qudah said: “If Egypt can put in custody one of its most respected editors and shut down her newsroom, no independent journalist in the country is safe. Attalah must be released immediately, and Mada Masr must be allowed to keep reporting.”

title: Jordan Strikes Southern Syria After Deadly Attack on Greek Orthodox Church
body: Jordan has carried out airstrikes in southern Syria in retaliation for last Friday’s attack on St George’s Greek Orthodox Church in Karak, which killed nine people. Amman says the strikes killed Islamic State militants. Damascus says the dead were civilians, among them three children. The Royal Jordanian Air Force hit targets on Monday evening, 26 October. The Jordanian Armed Forces said in a post on X that fighter jets had destroyed “a number of terrorist sites in southeastern Syria”. It said the operation “resulted in the killing and wounding of many elements of the terrorist organizations and the destruction of a number of their vehicles”. The military also said it had acted in coordination with Damascus, according to Al Jazeera . Amman says 20 militants killed On Tuesday, Jordanian Government Communication Minister Mohammad al-Momani said the strikes killed about 20 Islamic State fighters. He also acknowledged that civilians had died. According to France 24 , al-Momani said the operation was based on intelligence about “confirmed threats and planned terrorist acts against Jordan”, and he expressed regret over the civilian casualties. He also sought to protect relations with Damascus. “Jordan holds great respect for the Syrian state and its brotherly people,” he said, adding that cooperation between the two countries against terrorism and weapons and drug smuggling was ongoing. Damascus says children among the dead Syria’s civil defence service said four sites in rural Daraa and Suwayda provinces were hit. Its crews recovered seven bodies. Five of the dead were from one family: a man, a woman and three children. They were killed when a strike hit a tent in the village of al-Taff, in the Lajat area of Daraa province. Three other family members, including a child, were wounded. An 80-year-old man was killed on a farm near Nassib, and a 60-year-old man died when a home was hit in northern Suwayda. A fourth strike hit a house in Muzayrib, with no casualties reported. Syria’s Foreign Ministry condemned the strikes as “an unacceptable violation and breach of Syrian airspace without any prior coordination”. It called them “a blatant violation of the principles of good-neighbourliness and Syrian national sovereignty”. Syria also closed the Nassib crossing, the only passenger and commercial border crossing between the two countries, the BBC reported . The attack on St George’s The strikes followed the shooting on Friday, 23 October. Three gunmen opened fire on mourners at a funeral at St George’s Greek Orthodox Church in the village of Hmoud, in Karak governorate, about 90 kilometres south of Amman. Nine people were killed and dozens were wounded. On Monday, Jordanian security forces arrested two brothers and their brother-in-law after a shootout at an abandoned house in Karak governorate. All three were wounded. Jordan’s interior minister said the attackers were all Jordanians. Al Jazeera reported that the Islamic State group has claimed responsibility for the church attack. Orthodox community mourns The Greek Orthodox Patriarchate of Jerusalem, which oversees the Orthodox Church in Jordan, condemned what it called a “vile, cowardly, and bloody act”. In its statement of 23 October , it said Christians would not be driven from the land. “If the intent behind this message is to uproot us from our Holy Land and displace us, it will only serve to strengthen our attachment to it and deepen our roots within it.” On Sunday, 25 October, Patriarch Theophilos III led the funeral of eight of the victims at St George’s, which was attended by thousands of people. He later visited the wounded at the Prince Ali bin Al-Hussein Military Hospital and the Italian Hospital. The BBC named the eight as Dr Maher Zureiqat, Ihab al-Halsa, Dr Fadi al-Halsa, Dr Khaled al-Halsa, Dr Asim al-Burqan, Alaa al-Masarwa, Marwan Khaitan and Mazen al-Qassous. The ninth victim, Dr Mohammad al-Qassous, was buried near Amman on Monday after a funeral service led by the Patriarch, Orthodox Times reported . Christians make up about 300,000 of Jordan’s 11.5 million people. Read more: Jordan Church Attack: Jerusalem Patriarchate Vows Christians Will Stay and Jordan Arrests Suspects Over Deadly Attack on Greek Orthodox Church . title: EU Commission Strengthens Border Protection With 30,000 More Personnel
body: The European Commission has proposed strengthening the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, Frontex, by expanding its personnel, increasing its role in returns and introducing rapid-response mechanisms to help EU member states protect the bloc’s external borders and manage emergencies. The proposed reforms aim to improve Frontex’s operational capacity, allowing the agency to respond more quickly and effectively by pooling resources, improving coordination and providing member states with additional operational support. The Commission proposes gradually increasing Frontex’s Standing Corps to a total of 30,000 personnel. The plan includes a new European Border and Returns Reserve comprising 17,000 personnel who could deploy wherever needs arise, complementing Frontex staff and personnel seconded by member states. The agency would also gain easier access to modern equipment and technology. It could participate in joint procurement procedures with member states and act as a central purchasing body for digital tools and artificial intelligence technologies. Frontex to take a greater role in returns Under the proposal, Frontex would play a more active role in planning and coordinating return operations across the EU, with the aim of improving efficiency and reducing costs. The Commission proposes establishing a dedicated Returns Coordination Centre to support every stage of the process, from voluntary return to reintegration. Frontex could also provide technical and operational assistance to non-EU countries organising and carrying out return operations between third countries. Such assistance would require the agreement of the countries concerned and compliance with fundamental rights and international standards. New monitoring centre and rapid-response force The proposed reforms would establish an Online Monitoring and Response Centre to identify emerging developments and threats at the EU’s external borders at an early stage. The centre would monitor publicly accessible social media content to help detect potential risks. The Commission also proposes creating a Rapid Response Force capable of deploying to external borders at very short notice to address crises and emergencies. Member states would face new reporting obligations during crises. They would have to report incidents with a significant impact on the EU’s external borders through the EUROSUR information-sharing network within 24 hours. EU proposes digitalisation of return procedures The Commission has also proposed a new regulation to digitalise return, readmission and reintegration procedures across the EU. The initiative aims to simplify and accelerate administrative processes, reduce workloads and improve the collection and exchange of data. The proposals will now go to the European Parliament and the Council of the European Union, which must reach agreement on the new rules before they can proceed. title: IERPP demands full account of 24-hour economy spending
body: The Institute of Economic Research and Public Policy (IERPP) is demanding that the government publish a comprehensive financing and implementation report on the 24-Hour Economy programme, detailing funds disbursed, expenditure incurred and projects completed. The institute’s Executive Director, Prof. Isaac Boadi, says the government must account for its financial commitments and demonstrate measurable results from the flagship programme. Speaking at a news conference in Accra on Tuesday, October 27, he questioned the difference between the GH¢90 million allocation in the detailed expenditure tables of the 2026 Budget and the GH¢110 million cited in the Budget Speech. “The Budget does not even agree with itself,” Prof. Boadi said. The detailed expenditure tables allocate GH¢70 million for goods and services and GH¢20 million for capital expenditure under the 24H+ Economy line, bringing the total to GH¢90 million. The Budget Speech, however, states that GH¢110 million has been allocated for the programme. Prof. Boadi is calling on the government to reconcile the figures and disclose the actual amounts released and spent, as well as the results achieved. “An allocation is not a release, and a release is not expenditure,” he said. IERPP is also demanding a comprehensive account of the programme’s financing and implementation to enable the public to track how resources are being used and assess progress. The Ministry of Finance previously described the GH¢110 million as a facilitating allocation, rather than the full funding for the programme, with additional financing expected from private investors and development partners. However, the explanation does not, on its own, resolve the difference between the two figures in the budget documents. The institute is urging the government to make the relevant financial and implementation information public to strengthen transparency and accountability.

title: Dutch zookeeper dies after being mauled by leopard
body: An experienced keeper at a Dutch zoo has died days after being mauled in a leopard enclosure, the safari park has confirmed. The woman, who had worked at Beekse Bergen park for 40 years, was caring for two Persian leopards in an indoor facility when she was attacked on Saturday. She sustained injuries to her head and neck and had emergency surgery, but the park confirmed her death on Tuesday. An independent investigation will be launched into the incident, it added in a statement. Announcing her death, Beekse Bergen, in the south of the Netherlands, said the keeper began her career there at 17 and worked there on and off for four decades. “Her passing has deeply affected us all, and our hearts go out to her family, friends, and loved ones. At this moment, our primary focus is on supporting her family and her colleagues,” the statement added. Staff usually keep the two leopards away, but brought them inside because of bad weather. It is not clear exactly what happened in the enclosure because there are no CCTV cameras inside. Local news website NL Times reported that despite her injuries, she managed to alert colleagues via her walkie-talkie. She was then taken to hospital in a helicopter in a critical condition. A park spokesperson told Omroep Brabant, a local media outlet, that the leopards were behaving naturally and they would not be euthanised. “They are, and remain, predators.” Beekse Bergen said it would create a memorial where guests and staff could share their condolences.

title: Israeli Exit Polls Show No Clear Winner as Arab Parties Make Gains
body: Israeli election exit polls suggest no clear winner, with former military chief Gadi Eisenkot’s bloc narrowly ahead of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc, while Arab parties record gains amid a strong turnout push in Arab communities. Mahdi Kabaha, a 29-year-old lawyer from the predominantly Arab northern town of Umm al-Fahm, campaigned to encourage Arab citizens to vote. He described the election night as historic, saying Arab society had demonstrated its presence and its right to influence political decisions. Arab citizens account for about one-fifth of Israel’s electorate, but just over half voted in the previous election, according to the report. Kabaha said some Arab voters had previously avoided elections because they did not want to legitimise Israeli institutions. He urged the community to use its electoral influence to change the government and remove far-right ministers, including Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich. Crime in Arab communities and what Kabaha described as insufficient policing were among the main issues driving voters’ concerns. Kabaha argued that political differences between Democratic Party leader Yair Golan and Ben-Gvir demonstrated why participation mattered. He contrasted their positions on Palestinian displacement and a possible two-state solution, saying voters had a choice between competing approaches to the conflict. The exit polls indicate gains for Arab parties, although the final distribution of seats and the formation of a governing coalition will depend on the official results. title: 3 Winnipeg Blue Bombers voted finalists for CFL Awards
body:
At least three members of the Winnipeg Blue Bombers are up for CFL awards this season.
The CFL announced the finalists for the first three of their year-end awards and a Bombers player is nominated for all three.
Bombers running back Brady Oliveira, offensive lineman Jarell Broxton, and defensive back Major Williams were all voted finalists.
Oliveira is one of three finalists for the Most Outstanding Canadian Award, which he has already won twice before. Oliveira just captured his third career rushing title with 1,493 yards. He also scored eight touchdowns, while moving past Jon Cornish into third place on the CFL’s all-time rushing list by a Canadian.
Oliveira was named the Bombers most outstanding player and top Canadian for the fourth straight season and previously won the Most Outstanding Canadian Award in 2023 and 2024.
Montreal Alouettes receiver Tyson Philpot and BC Lions quarterback Nathan Rourke are the other two finalists. Rourke won the award last year.
Broxton is a finalist for the Most Outstanding Offensive Lineman Award in his first season in Winnipeg after being the Lions top offensive lineman for the last three seasons. He started 17 of 18 games at right tackle and helped Oliveira win the rushing title.
The Alouettes’ Nick Callender and Pier-Olivier Lestage are also nominated for the award.
Williams is a finalist for the Most Outstanding Rookie Award after starting all 18 games in his first CFL season. He led the Bombers with three interceptions, while ranking second in defensive tackles with 77.
Williams is nominated against Toronto Argonauts receiver Tyler Kahmann and Lions linebacker Parker McKenna.
The CFL altered the awards process this season and now have three finalists from across the league, instead of just one finalist from each division.
The three finalists for the Most Outstanding Player Award, Most Outstanding Special Teams Player Award, and Most Outstanding Defensive Player Award will be announced on Wednesday.
Instead of the traditional CFL Awards ceremony during Grey Cup week, the winners will be honoured through surprise presentations during the post-season.

title: Trade between Russia, Libya continues to grow — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Trade between Russia and Libya continues to develop despite the challenging international political and economic environment, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at a meeting with Chairman of Libya’s Presidential Council Mohamed al-Menfi.
"Despite the difficult situation in international politics and the economy, bilateral trade continues to develop. The first meeting of the co-chairs of the joint intergovernmental commission took place in Moscow in April. We are, of course, interested in resuming its full-fledged activities as soon as possible," the Russian leader said.
Putin noted that Libya is a longstanding partner of Russia in North Africa, with 2025 marking the 70th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations. "Cooperation on multilateral platforms, particularly within the Gas Exporting Countries Forum, at the Moscow summit in which we both participated, as well as within OPEC+, enables us to jointly develop measures to ensure global energy security," the president added.
He also said he looked forward to productive and meaningful cooperation between Russia and Libya at the third Russia-Africa Summit, which begins on Wednesday.

title: HelloGitHub 第 127 期
body:
HelloGitHub shares interesting, beginner-friendly open-source projects from GitHub, updated every month on the 28th . Discover fun beginner projects, open-source books, practical tutorials, and enterprise-grade projects, helping you quickly experience and become interested in the charm of open source.
Watch a Flock of Birds Fly in Your Terminal.This terminal flock animation tool is written in C and simulates flocking with the Boids algorithm. It draws birds in the terminal using Braille dots and supports 3D mode, eagle hunting, birds spelling out text to show a clock, and a screensaver mode.
Run 100B+ Parameter Models Without a GPU.This is a mixture-of-experts inference engine written in pure C, with zero dependencies and no GPU required. It keeps only the parts the model needs on every run in memory, and reads the remaining expert weights from disk on demand. With as little as 8GB of RAM, it can run open-source large models such as GLM, Kimi, DeepSeek, and Qwen, and provides OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs. It works on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
Turning the Linux Desktop into a Desk.This project is a Wayland-based Linux desktop environment, with the entire room rendered using ray tracing. The desktop is a wooden desk, windows are sheets of paper; when minimized, they fold up like letters, and when closed, they are crumpled into paper balls and tossed away.
A Drag-and-Drop File Format Converter.This is an offline file format converter built in C#. It supports over 200 formats, including images, PDF, Office documents, ebooks, audio/video, archives, and CAD. To use it, just hold Ctrl and drag a file—a format ring appears next to the cursor; drop the file on the target format to convert. Files are never uploaded, and it works on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
Use Screenshots to Tell AI How to Modify the UI.This screenshot annotation tool for AI-assisted coding turns specific UI changes into JSON that AI can read directly. It supports hover-based element detection, point and box annotations, dragging components to adjust layouts, pausing videos for frame-by-frame annotation, plus OCR and long screenshots—all processed locally.
An Encrypted File System Written in Go.This project is a file encryption tool built on Go and FUSE. It mounts an encrypted directory as a readable and writable plaintext directory, encrypting file contents and file names separately. The resulting encrypted directory can be stored in cloud drives like Dropbox or incrementally synced via rsync.
One-Click Model Switching for AI Coding Assistants.This is a Go-based model management tool for AI coding assistants that lets Claude Code use Kimi and Codex use DeepSeek. It uses a local gateway to convert between OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini API formats, supports multiple coding assistants and model providers, and can share subscriptions with other assistants, automatically switching accounts when quotas run out.
A Terminal Email Client for Sending and Receiving Emails.A terminal email client built with Go and Bubble Tea that lets you send and receive emails via commands, with support for multiple accounts, Markdown email composition, and a plugin marketplace.
Self-Hosted Passwordless Identity Authentication Service.This project is an OIDC and OAuth 2.0 identity authentication service built in Go, with support for Passkeys instead of passwords. Users do not need to remember passwords—they can simply plug in a hardware key such as a YubiKey to log in.
An Open-Source GIS Platform That Runs in the Browser.This project is a geographic information system built with TypeScript for visualizing, browsing, and analyzing geospatial data while keeping data local. It includes over 1,000 analysis tools that run in the browser via WebAssembly, covering terrain, hydrology, LiDAR, and remote sensing analysis. It can run in the browser, on desktop, mobile, and in Jupyter Notebook, and also provides planetary basemaps such as the Moon and Mars.
Self-Hosted All-in-One Online Toolbox.A React-based collection of online tools for everyday tasks such as images, audio/video, PDF, text, date/time, math, and data processing, with all files processed locally in the browser. It offers image resizing and format conversion, video trimming, PDF splitting and merging, time zone conversion, JSON manipulation, and more.
Fitness Tracking App Where You Own Your Data.A self-hostable fitness and weight tracking app with no subscriptions, ads, or telemetry, deployable with a single Docker command. It includes over 5,000 exercises with animated demonstrations, supports weekly workout scheduling, guided workouts, rest timers between sets, automatic personal best detection, and muscle heatmaps to see training volume by body part. You can also import data from apps like Strong and Hevy, and it offers iPhone, Apple Watch, and Android versions.
A Cloud Computer That Runs in the Browser.This is a desktop operating system that runs in the browser, bringing files, apps, and games together in one place for access anytime, anywhere. It includes built-in apps such as Notepad, Voice Recorder, Spreadsheet, and Camera, and offers developers capabilities including AI, cloud storage, a key-value database, and Serverless Workers. Web apps and games you build can be published to its app store.
One Word, One Picture: An IELTS Vocabulary Learning Tool.This is a free, open-source web app for IELTS vocabulary learning. It runs right in your browser and requires no sign-up. It includes over 7,000 core IELTS words, each with an original illustration, two original example sentences, and both British and American pronunciations. Reviews are scheduled using the FSRS algorithm, and every word you master lights up a star on a 3D vocabulary star map.
Give Your TV an Apple TV-Style Home Screen.This open-source Android TV launcher is inspired by tvOS. It has no ads or recommendation feeds and launches automatically on startup. It works on Chinese TV brands such as Xiaomi, TCL, and Skyworth, as well as TV boxes and projectors. It supports organizing apps, creating folders, hiding system apps, and sorting apps via your phone by scanning a QR code. No root required, and you can restore your original launcher anytime.
Using CarPlay on Android Devices.This is a CarPlay app that runs on Android head units. Once installed on the head unit, it enables wired or wireless CarPlay. It supports Wi-Fi Direct and in-car hotspots, can project navigation turn arrows, distances, and street names onto the HUD, and lets you adjust icon size, resolution, and frame rate. It supports Android 7.0 and above and a Simplified Chinese interface.
Play Steam Games on Android Phones.This app brings SteamOS to Android, letting you run the Steam client on Android devices with Adreno GPUs. It supports running Windows games, installing Linux apps, and signing in to GOG, Epic, and Amazon game stores.
Generating Anki Decks with Python.This Python library generates Anki decks and supports custom note fields, card templates, and CSS styles, along with images and audio. After you modify the content and regenerate the deck, re-importing it will overwrite existing cards with the same names—ideal for batch-creating cards from word lists, question banks, and other data sources.
Making Comics Fit E-Ink Screens.A conversion tool that optimizes comic display for e-ink readers like Kindle and Kobo. It converts images, CBZ, PDF, and other files into e-books, scaling and cropping page margins according to device resolution.
A Faster Math Animation Engine.This project is a 3D math animation engine compatible with the Manim Community API. It uses GPU rendering and is 90x faster than the community edition. It supports AI coding assistants like Claude Code and Codex in writing animations directly, and can run in the browser via WebGPU or export MP4 videos.
Automating Windows Desktop Apps with Python.This is a Python library for Windows GUI automation that can simulate mouse and keyboard actions on windows, dialogs, and controls, and read text data from the UI. It supports two backends: Win32 API and MS UI Automation. It can locate elements by text attributes such as window titles and control names. With just a few lines of code, you can open menus, click buttons, type text, and more. It is suitable for automated testing and repetitive tasks in desktop software.
Writing High-Performance GPU Operators in Python.This is a domain-specific language designed for writing high-performance GPU/CPU/NPU operators. Built on top of the TVM compiler, it lets developers achieve highly optimized implementations of operators such as GEMM and FlashAttention without hand-writing low-level code. It supports multiple hardware backends, including NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, Apple Metal, and Huawei Ascend, and comes with built-in auto-tuning and debugging visualization tools, plus example operators for large models such as DeepSeek MLA.
Open-Source ESP32 Emulator.This is an ESP32 emulator written in Rust that lets you run unmodified real firmware on your computer or in a browser without a development board. It fully emulates the boot process from the bootloader to FreeRTOS, and can also emulate peripherals such as display, touch, LED, audio, camera, and WiFi, with support for chips including ESP32-S3, C3, C6, and P4.
Minimalist HTTP File-Sharing Server.A command-line tool written in Rust that shares files and directories over HTTP with just a single binary. It supports username/password authentication, file uploads, folder downloads as archives, search by name, QR code access, TLS, and WebDAV. It can also render README.md files like GitHub, offers light and dark themes, and is ideal for scenarios such as temporary file sharing.
NVIDIA's Open-Source Security Sandbox for AI Agents.A secure runtime purpose-built for autonomous AI agents, letting them read and write files, install packages, and call APIs without free rein over your data, keys, or network. Each agent runs in an isolated sandbox, with kernel-level, policy-driven controls over file access, system calls, and network connections. Real credentials are injected only when a request goes to an approved address.
Drawing Technical Concepts as Animated Mechanical Diagrams.An illustration skill for AI coding assistants that turns abstract technical concepts into realistic, movable mechanical devices, rendered as polished isometric interactive illustrations—for example, depicting a cache hit as a lock cylinder that only turns when every pin is aligned. It supports SVG, SVG + WebGL shaders, and 3D, and can export to HTML pages, SVG files, or React components.
Rewrite AI Instructions in Simplified English.This project is based on the Simplified Technical English standard from the aerospace industry. It rewrites ambiguous, verbose English into sentences that won't be misread, then feeds them to AI agents. It checks each sentence for passive voice, complex tenses, multiple instructions in one sentence, long sentences, and marketing adjectives, without losing any facts or conditions from the original.
Let AI Create Design-Forward Diagrams.This is a diagram design skill built for AI coding assistants that generates HTML+SVG files you can open directly in the browser. It supports 45 diagram types, including architecture diagrams, flowcharts, sequence diagrams, Gantt charts, and Sankey diagrams. It can automatically extract brand colors and fonts from websites, redraw existing diagrams from Mermaid, draw.io, and Excalidraw in a consistent style, and export them as PNG or SVG.
Make AI-Designed Interfaces More Tasteful.A front-end design skill for AI coding assistants, extended from Anthropic's official frontend-design skill to help AI avoid cookie-cutter interfaces—such as using Inter everywhere, purple-to-blue gradients, and cards nested inside cards. It provides 24 design commands like polish, audit, and critique, plus 62 deterministic detection rules, and supports Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, and other tools.
A macOS Tool That Hangs Screenshots at the Top of Your Screen.A compact macOS screenshot organizer that hangs each screenshot like laundry on a line at the top of your screen. Move your cursor to the menu bar and the line slides down; move away and it automatically tucks itself back, keeping your desktop free from screenshot clutter. Click to copy, press and hold to annotate, drag into an app to send directly, drag to the Trash to delete, and it even supports screen recording and trimming.
A Cross-Platform Xcode Alternative.A cross-platform Xcode alternative written in Swift that lets you build iOS apps with SwiftPM on Linux, Windows, and macOS and deploy them to physical devices. It supports creating projects, building and running apps, signing and installing apps, and managing devices, and it also lets you work with Apple developer services from the command line.
Google's Open-Source AI Phone Automation Tool.This is an AI-powered Android automation tool: just describe a task in natural language, and the AI will automatically operate a phone or emulator to complete cross-app testing workflows and everyday tasks. It includes a built-in MCP server that lets AI coding assistants such as Claude Code and Codex directly control the phone and collect logs and screenshots, and it supports multimodal models including Gemini, Claude, and GPT-4o.
DeepSeek's Open-Source Large Model Inference Framework.This project is the high-performance inference framework used for DeepSeek's large-scale online services, providing core capabilities for offline inference and large-scale deployment. It integrates self-developed optimized operators such as FlashMLA, DeepGEMM, and DeepEP, and supports attention data parallelism, MoE expert parallelism, asynchronous scheduling, deterministic sampling, and structured output. It can run on NVIDIA and Huawei Ascend NPUs.
Google's Open-Source Self-Evolving Agent Framework.This framework enables AI agents to self-improve on unfamiliar tasks without changing model weights. It proposes task-specific modifications—such as adjusting system prompts, memory, skills, sub-agents, and plugins—then runs real trials to compare results, and finally captures the lessons learned for future tasks.
Animate Any 3D Character with One Sentence.This project can generate motions for 3D models with different skeletal structures. Given a rigged 3D model and a text description, it can generate the corresponding motion in real time without retraining for each skeleton. It works with a variety of skeletal structures, including humanoids, quadrupeds, birds, marine creatures, insects, and mechanical rigs.
Open-Source Local AI Voice Studio.This is a fully local voice cloning and dubbing tool that serves as an open-source alternative to ElevenLabs and supports 600+ languages. It integrates multiple speech synthesis and recognition engines such as CosyVoice, IndexTTS, GPT-SoVITS, and WhisperX, with features including voice design, video dubbing, vocal separation, transcription, and audiobook production.
Building Open-Source Alternatives to Commercial Software from Scratch.This is an open-source project initiated by the Puter team, aiming to rebuild free, open-source alternatives to commercial software from scratch. It currently offers over 50 apps, including alternatives to Excel, PowerPoint, Photoshop, AutoCAD, Zoom, and Slack, as well as small games like chess and Sudoku—most of which can be used directly in the browser.
A Cyberpunk-Style Periodic Table.An interactive periodic table of chemical elements that runs in the browser with a dark cyberpunk aesthetic. It covers atomic number, electron configuration, isotopes, and valence data for all 118 elements. You can switch heatmaps based on properties such as atomic radius, electronegativity, and melting point, click any element to drag and rotate a 3D atomic model, explore its electron shell structure, and use a bilingual Chinese/English interface.
Unlocking the Compute Power of RTX 30 Series GPUs.This is a Linux kernel module that unlocks the FP16/BF16 instruction issue rate of NVIDIA RTX 30 series consumer GPUs to the level of their professional counterparts, significantly boosting matrix operation throughput. For example, the BF16 compute performance of the RTX 3090 Ti can increase from 87.5 to 157.4 TFLOPS, and large model prefill speed improves by 14%–36%. It performs the unlock before the official NVIDIA driver loads, requiring no driver modifications and no need to reapply patches after each driver update.
Open-Source Mobile Robot Navigation Framework.This is an autonomous robot navigation framework that provides perception, localization, path planning, motion control, and obstacle avoidance, with behavior trees orchestrating modular services. Beyond basic navigation, it also supports waypoint cruising, target following, and full-coverage navigation tasks.
A Minimalist Local Image Compression Tool.This is a local processing tool for images and animated images. It supports batch compression, drag-to-compare quality, format conversion, resizing, and watermarking. It automatically compares candidate outputs such as JPEG, WebP, and PNG, then selects the smaller file. It offers desktop apps for Windows, macOS, and Linux, and can also be used in the browser or via Docker. All images are processed locally on your machine. The desktop version also supports folder monitoring, automatic clipboard optimization, and MCP integration.
A Cost-Effective Guide to Life.A practical guide to trading less money, time, and energy for more years of life and greater financial security. It covers longevity and disease prevention, first aid, saving and money management, legal red lines, unemployment assistance, medical and social insurance, dating, marriage, and childbearing, and compliance for entrepreneurs.

title: El Niño and Your Health: What Nigerians Must Do Before the Heat Peaks
body: You do not need a weather bulletin to know that nights have been challenging lately. Still, the bulletins are worth reading. Recently, the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) recorded 41°C in Nguru, Yobe State, and 34°C in Lagos. In May, the agency issued a heat stress alert, with temperatures of between 40 and 45°C expected in some northern states. It also warned that dust in the air could raise the risk of meningitis. The label “Super El Niño” is a media creation, not an official category. The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) says El Niño is firmly established and rapidly strengthening. It forecasts a seasonal average Pacific temperature anomaly of about 3.7°C above normal for October to December, peaking around December. That would be the highest since observations began. The previous record was 2.6°C. The WMO also says this event could be among the strongest since at least 1950. Now, consider the mortality figures. Researchers at the University of Chicago’s Climate Impact Lab combined seasonal temperature forecasts with research on how heat affects death rates. They estimate 451,000 additional heat deaths worldwide by February 2027. Nigeria accounts for 31,400 of them. This makes it the country most likely to record the highest heat mortality worldwide. These are extra deaths compared with the average for the same months from 1996 to 2025. The period runs from September 2026 to February 2027. It is a projection, not a body count, and it can change depending on what we do. The truth is that many heat deaths go unnoticed. A man with high blood pressure has a stroke after a day in a tin-roofed workshop. A grandmother with weak kidneys becomes dehydrated and does not recover. A baby in an airless room develops a fever. The record will name the failing organ, and the weather often goes unmentioned. That is why heat-related deaths are so easily missed. Rainfall is the other concern. For this season, the Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWS NET), which monitors food security, reports that cumulative rainfall deficits have been recorded across the Sahel. This includes parts of south-western, north-western and north-eastern Nigeria. The same report cites some of the most severe deficits in the north-east. Dry spells of more than eight consecutive days occurred in several Sahel areas between late August and 20 September. Late rains are unlikely to make up the full shortfall. A later FEWS NET report describes the deficits in north-eastern Nigeria as moderate. A rainfall deficit is not the same as a declared drought. Yet, the trend points in one direction. NiMet’s February forecast warned of prolonged dry spells and a severe August break in some parts of the country. That forecast assumed a mostly neutral climate pattern, and the Pacific has since changed. A senior NiMet meteorologist, Musa Tanko, expects the effects to be worse in the north. Rainfall could fall there and dry spells could lengthen, and he expects heat stress to peak between March and May 2027. He also cautions that some places may see long dry spells and sudden heavy rain in the same season. The WMO adds that its seasonal signals do not replace local forecasts. Now, a poor harvest affects people far from the farm. Wells and streams run low, and people drink from whatever source is available. That is how dry weather leads to diarrhoea, cholera and malnutrition. Food prices then rise, and children are the first to eat less. So who is most at risk? The researchers point to people over 65, children under five, people with chronic conditions, and outdoor workers such as farmers who have no way of cooling down. I would add pregnant women, whose bodies are already working harder. Poverty widens the gap. The same researchers note that more than 60% of Nigerians were estimated to live below the national poverty line in 2025. About 87.3 million Nigerians have no access to electricity. For many families, a good fan is unaffordable. The government has a clear job here. It must issue heat warnings in plain language, keep clinics stocked and protect water supplies. We should demand all of it. However, a radio warning will not remind your father to drink water, and a policy paper will not cool a child’s room. Those tasks are our responsibility. Drink water regularly, not only when you are thirsty. You are already behind if your urine is dark. Keep sleeping rooms ventilated. Wet a cloth and cool a child’s face and neck. Never leave anyone in a parked car, even for five minutes. Move heavy work to the early morning or the evening. If you must work in the afternoon, rest in the shade every hour. Employers and foremen share this duty. Give breaks. Provide water. Do not push people through the hottest hours. You must know the danger signs. Confusion, heavy drowsiness, hot dry skin, vomiting or fainting may mean heatstroke. That is an emergency. Move the person into shade and remove excess clothing. Cool the skin with wet cloths and fanning, and rush the person to the hospital. Do not force fluids on someone who is not fully awake. If you take medicine for blood pressure, diabetes, epilepsy or kidney problems, speak to a pharmacist or doctor this week. Some tablets make you pass more urine, which can worsen dehydration in the heat. Do not stop any medicine on your own. Stock for a few weeks in case the roads or the pharmacy become difficult to reach. Water safety matters more as supplies shrink. Boil or treat what you drink. Keep storage containers covered. Wash your hands with soap. If a child has watery stools, start oral rehydration salts immediately. Take reports of cholera or meningitis near you seriously, and seek care early. Then think about the people around you. Who lives alone on your street? Which elderly neighbour has no fan? Which relative in the north depends on a borehole that may soon run low? A phone call, a sachet of oral rehydration salts or a bottle of treated water can make a real difference to how that person copes. Nothing we do will cool the Pacific. However, the projected toll is not fixed. The final count will depend on what households, employers and officials do in the coming months. A neighbour checked on, a worker given shade and a child given water in time all lower that number. Ojenagbon, a health communication expert and certified management trainer, lives in Lagos.

title: Lockheed Martin CEO says F-22 upgrades will deliver ‘fifth generation plus’ capability
body: Speaking during Lockheed Martin’s third-quarter earnings call on October 22, Taiclet identified F-22 modernization as one of three priorities for increasing air combat power at the most efficient cost. He said the work was underway at Skunk Works in conjunction with the U.S. military. “One is modernizing the F-22, especially with sensors, distributed aperture system, data links, and beyond line of sight capabilities that the original F-22 did not have,” Taiclet said. “That will take the F-22 to a fifth generation plus type of capability.” Taiclet did not provide a fielding schedule, contract value or detailed performance specifications. He also did not identify the individual systems being installed. The company is drawing on technology from across its divisions for the upgrades, Taiclet said. As an example, he cited the introduction of a sensor developed by Lockheed Martin’s Missiles and Fire Control business into the F-22. That work reflects a broader change in the company’s engineering approach, he said, with teams examining how existing aircraft, sensors and networks can be combined to improve military missions. Lockheed Martin aims to introduce incremental mission improvements every three to six months, although Taiclet did not give that timetable for the F-22 effort. The other elements of the company’s air combat strategy are further F-35 development and Vectis, an autonomous aircraft being funded internally ahead of formal customer requirements. Taiclet said Lockheed Martin’s experience with the F-22 and F-35 helped it anticipate how crewed fighters would connect with autonomous aircraft. Lockheed Martin has increased its investment in Vectis to build five aircraft, with flight demonstrations scheduled for 2027. Taiclet identified air-to-air combat and strike as its intended missions and said the design was informed by expectations of future requirements for range, payload and survivability. For the F-35, Taiclet said the company wants to incorporate sixth-generation technologies to deliver 80% of the capability of a newly designed sixth-generation fighter at half the cost. He presented the three efforts as a combined approach to increasing the combat power available to the United States and its allies.

title: King Charles acknowledges ‘suffering of the past’ as Caribbean tour begins
body: King Charles has arrived in the Bahamas for a nine-day Caribbean tour, the first time he has visited the region as monarch. The King, wearing sunglasses and a grey suit, was given a ceremonial welcome at the airport before attending a youth rally. Prior to the trip, Buckingham Palace said the King would not shy away from “colonial legacy” and the impact of the slave trade during the visit but, in line with the UK government’s position, he will not apologise for Britain’s role in the slave trade or offer reparations. Appearing at his first engagement, he told young people it is “only right” to “acknowledge the great suffering and injustices of the past”. Upon arriving on the island, he met the island’s Governor General, Dame Cynthia A. Pratt and its Prime Minister, Philip Edward, before speaking with members of the Royal Bahamas Defence Force as he inspected a guard of honour on the runway. The King was then met with cheers as he arrived for his first engagement at a youth rally at Clifford Park, where he attended the island’s independence celebrations as Prince of Wales in 1973. During his speech, the King acknowledged his 50-year commitment to fighting climate change and highlighted the challenges faced by low-lying Caribbean islands, saying, “our world cries out for healing”. He went on to call on the young people at the rally to “take up the sacred task to play your part” as “in years to come, this will surely be the measure of every person – how they answered the call to care for planet earth – the source of our life, our prosperity and our security”. The King spoke with young people as he attended his first engagement of the trip Buckingham Palace said opportunities for the King to reflect on the legacy of the slave trade will be built into his schedule in all three countries with visits planned to memorials and other places of reflection and remembrance. A palace spokesperson told the BBC that the King’s programme on the tour “will primarily focus on shining a light on the many modern partnerships and opportunities for the future”, specifically those “having a transformative effect on the region”. For the King, the spokesperson added, the “tour is both a new journey and also the continuance of a lifelong one, in which he has sought to engage, understand and educate about the most shameful aspects of our past”. The palace said the King will reflect those themes through the nine-day visit. The visit has been planned alongside the governments of the Bahamas, Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda, with an emphasis on honouring the past while also looking ahead to ambition and possibility for future generations. The King will move to Guyana later this week, where his engagements will focus on the environment and biodiversity. He will then visit Antigua and Barbuda, where Queen Camilla will join him for the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) and his keynote speech as leader of the Commonwealth. CHOGM is a biennial summit which brings together leaders of 56 Commonwealth countries to address shared challenges and advance cooperation.
