I would love to play at this age – I want to congratulate her.” While the straight-set scoreline will embolden the critics, Williams did make Tagger – a rising talent who is predicted to have a bright future at the very top – work hard. However, the teenager proved far too good. The 2025 French Open girls’ champion was superb on serve – dropping just seven service points and not facing a break point – while handling Williams’ pace and crushing groundstrokes off both wings. Tagger broke her illustrious opponent’s serve twice – for 1-0 and 5-2 leads – in two almost identical sets. At times, Williams was able to use her powerful serve to get out of trouble – fighting off 12 of 16 break points – and the veteran’s trademark competitive spirit never wavered. But it was another example of how far behind the rest of the tour she now is.

title: Transcorp Group Delivers N111.4bn PBT in Nine Months of 2026
body: Kayode Tokede Transnational Corporation Plc, yesterday announced its unaudited nine months ended September 30, 2026 result and accounts with profit before tax at N111.4 billion from N124.5 billion reported in nine months ended September 30, 2025. The Group declared revenue of N357.4 billion from N412.4 billion in corresponding period amid lower power evacuation at Transcorp Power Plc, as industry-wide transmission and gas supply constraints limited output during the period. The nine months 2026 performance across the portfolio underscored the quality of the group’s operating businesses. Transcorp Power Plc grew shareholders’ funds by 8.9per cent to N199.8 billion and increased cash and cash equivalents more than four-fold to N10.3 billion. Transcorp Hotels Plc grew Profit After Tax by five per cent to N15.5 billion, expanded its net profit margin to 22.3 per cent and reduced net finance cost by 36 per cent, while its total assets rose by 29 per cent to N206.8 billion. The group’s hospitality portfolio, Transcorp Hotels Plc, maintained its position as Nigeria’s foremost hospitality destination, attracting business leaders, dignitaries and international visitors through its iconic 670-room Transcorp Hilton Abuja and the 5,000-capacity Transcorp Centre, the country’s largest multipurpose event venue. Commenting, the President/GCEO, Transnational Corporation, Owen Omogiafo, in a statement said “Our performance reflects the strength of our diversified portfolio and our ability to sustain strong profitability and expand margins in a challenging operating environment. “We continue to work closely with stakeholders to address industry-wide constraints and improve electricity delivery, while leveraging our hospitality investments to strengthen Nigeria’s position as a destination for business, tourism and major events. “Across our businesses, we remain focused on unlocking opportunities for growth, deepening our contribution to Nigeria’s economy and delivering on our purpose to improve lives and transform Africa.” Group Chief Finance Officer, Transnational Corporation Plc, Festus Izevbizua, said; “Our nine-month performance underscores the strength and resilience of the Group’s underlying businesses. Year-on-year revenue was impacted by power evacuation constraints arising from vandalisation of transmission and gas infrastructure. “Notwithstanding this, the Group expanded its profit-before-tax margin to 31.2per cent, from 30.2per cent in the prior period, a direct result of deliberate cost optimisation and operational efficiency across our businesses. “Our financial position also strengthened considerably over the period. Total assets grew by 13per cent to N1.13 trillion, driven by improved receivables, investments in financial assets and stronger cash generation. “Total equity rose by 9.7per cent to N387.8 billion, reinforcing the Group’s robust capital base, while cash and cash equivalents more than doubled to N45.9 billion from N21.9 billion at December 2025, enhancing liquidity and providing greater financial flexibility to pursue strategic priorities.” He added, “Transcorp Group remains focused on advancing strategic opportunities across its power, hospitality and energy businesses, leveraging its diversified portfolio and financial strength to support long-term growth and sustainable shareholder value.”

title: Where Are The Aircraft Carriers?: October 27, 2026
body: The Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group (ARG) tied up in Yokosuka, Japan , on Monday, a week after the Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group departed from the same base to participate in exercise Keen Sword 27. Both are reportedly destined for the Middle East, two U.S. officials confirmed to Fox News , which would place three CSGs and two ARGs in the U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) area of responsibility (AOR) sometime in November, unless a group leaves before their arrival. More than 10 guided-missile destroyers are also operating independently in the region, as the U.S. beefs up force posture ahead of the possibility of renewed hostilities against the Iranian regime. Meanwhile, on the other side of the world, the USS Ronald Reagan remotely controlled an MQ-25A Stingray tanker drone thousands of miles away for the first time, and the Navy announced that USS Abraham Lincoln , which just returned from a historic deployment, will conduct a homeport shift to Bremerton, Washington. Here’s TWZ’s weekly carrier tracker monitoring America’s flattop fleet, including deployed CSGs and ARGs, using publicly available open-source information. Check out our last report here . A high-resolution graphic depicting the locations of U.S. Navy carriers and deployed ARGs. TWZ/IAN ELLIS-JONES Where Is The USS Theodore Roosevelt ? Surrounded by allied warships , the USS Theodore Roosevelt steamed through the Philippine Sea last week as large-scale combined exercise Keen Sword 27 got underway. Roosevelt and guided-missile cruiser USS Chosin departed Commander, Fleet Activities Yokosuka, on October 19 following a three-day port call. Roosevelt deployed on September 27 and was the first non-resident American carrier to pull into the vital naval port in over four years. U.S. Navy, Japanese, Australian, Canadian, and French warships steam together during Exercise Keen Sword 27. U.S. Navy photo Three American warships are participating in the exercise, a Navy official confirmed to TWZ . The third participant, Pearl Harbor-based guided-missile destroyer USS Decatur , another element of the five-ship strike group, also called port in Yokosuka and transited out of Tokyo Bay on October 26. Australian, Canadian, and French warships joined the exercise alongside the U.S. and Japan in a large show of force. Keen Sword 27 runs through October 29, but it’s unclear if Roosevelt and her escorts will remain until the conclusion before heading toward the Middle East via the Strait of Malacca. More than 45,000 Japan Self-Defense Forces personnel and 11,000 U.S. service members are participating . An F/A-18E Super Hornet launches off the flight deck of USS Theodore Roosevelt. U.S. Navy photo F/A-18 Super Hornets and F-35Cs launched from Roosevelt and airbases in Japan to complete a simulated strike against a target in the East Sea/Sea of Japan, which also included land-based launchers, an exercise spokesperson told Stars and Stripes . Japanese destroyers JS Kongo and JS Maya assumed the red team role. The precise location and munitions employed were not disclosed. The Theodore Roosevelt CSG, which a different Navy official confirmed also includes USS Paul Hamilton and USS Carl M. Levin , will arrive in the Middle East, Fox News reported last week. Both destroyers are disaggregated from the rest of the group. Hamilton , the last ship to deploy, left San Diego on October 10 and most recently pulled out of Pearl Harbor last week. Levin , the first ship to deploy, is already operating in the CENTCOM AOR , based on public images posted on the military’s content platform, DVIDS. If the CSG and ARG, which also includes amphibious transport docks USS Anchorage and USS John P. Murtha , arrive in the Middle East before the other two carriers on station, USS George H.W. Bush and USS George Washington , and big-deck amphibious assault ship USS Boxer , depart, that would add roughly 10,000 sailors and Marines to CENTCOM’s arsenal, the most significant force posture in the region since the war began. However, the overlap can only be maintained for a limited time given normal rotation schedules. Amphibious assault ship USS Makin Island pulls in to Commander, Fleet Activities, Yokosuka. U.S. Navy photo Acting Secretary of the Navy (SECNAV), Hung Cao, said during a panel at the Association of the United States Army (AUSA) convention that “the Teddy Roosevelt carrier strike group just deployed on October 8 with a medium sized unmanned surface vessel (MUSV). This is the first carrier strike group to ever deploy with a large size unmanned surface vessel.” However, despite multiple requests to comment, the Navy has not confirmed to TWZ that MUSV Seahawk (2) is assigned to the strike group. Seahawk was 10 nautical miles north of Guam, publicly available Automatic Identification System (AIS) data on MarineTraffic showed, as of publication. The USS Ronald Reagan Controlled A Tanker Drone Thousands Of Miles Away Providing a glimpse of the future, the USS Ronald Reagan used her brand-new Unmanned Air Warfare Center (UAWC) to operate an MQ-25A Stingray tanker drone at a Boeing facility in Illinois. “In a historic U.S. naval aviation event, an aircraft carrier connected to, and controlled, an unmanned aerial refueler MQ-25A Stingray more than 2,100 miles away,” the Navy said in a press release . The first painted MQ‑25A Stingray sits on the ramp outside Boeing’s dedicated MQ‑25 production facility in Mascoutah, Illinois. Unmanned Carrier Aviation (PMA-2 The UAWC, installed during Reagan’s recently completed 15-month maintenance availability, used its MD-5C ground control station to link beyond line-of-sight with the drone while the flattop was underway in the eastern Pacific Ocean. “The MQ-25A Stingray’s carrier-based refueling capabilities enable F/A-18 Super Hornets to fly farther and longer,” the Acting SECNAV said. “The integration of this unmanned aerial refueler demonstrates the transformational change our manned and unmanned asset integration provides the Fleet.” The test took place during a preliminary sea trial, part of a “series of build-up exercises designed to validate procedures, networks and interfaces,” reads the release. Capt. Daniel Fucito, program manager of the Navy’s Unmanned Carrier Aviation Program Office (PMA-268), said, “We have redefined naval power projection. This first-ever underway connection between a carrier-based UAWC and an MQ-25A aircraft proves that the Carrier Air Wing of tomorrow is a reality today.” USS Ronald Reagan (CVN 76) steams through the Pacific Ocean in October. U.S. Navy photo Reagan is the second Nimitz class carrier equipped with the UAWC. The MQ-25A will eventually take the role held by the F/A-18E/F Super Hornets that are tasked with fueling carrier-based aircraft, freeing up aircraft to take on higher-end combat roles. Reagan moored at Kilo Pier at Naval Air Station North Island in San Diego on October 27 after finishing Fleet Replacement Squadron and Carrier Qualifications. What’s Next For The USS Abraham Lincoln ? The USS Abraham Lincoln recently returned from a record-setting deployment. The carrier arrived back home on October 8 after being at sea for 321 days, less than a week short of the longest carrier deployment in the post-Vietnam era. The Navy has confirmed what TWZ was the first to report: the Lincoln will complete a homeport shift to Bremerton, Washington, to undergo an overhaul following a grueling deployment that left the carrier looking worse for wear. The release did not disclose the length of the availability, but Reagan was out of commission for more than a year, and was not previously involved in combat operations. U.S. Navy sailors aboard USS Abraham Lincoln conduct maintenance. U.S. Navy photo “The carrier repeatedly demonstrated unmatched multi-theater combat lethality and safeguarded critical sea lanes across the Indo-Pacific and Middle Eastern theaters. Home port shifts are part of the Navy’s continued commitment to the strategic dispersal of ships,” a statement released from Commander, Naval Air Forces reads. The move is a permanent change of station for the crew and their families. Where Is The Rest Of The Fleet? The two carriers enforcing the ongoing blockade of Iranian ports and coastal cities, USS George H.W. Bush and USS George Washington , have both been dark on AIS since arriving in the Middle East. The former is 210 days into her deployment and recently arrived back in CENTCOM after a five-day port call in Phuket, Thailand. The latter, forward-deployed out of Yokosuka, Japan, was spotted on DVIDS conducting flight operations on October 24. USS Nimitz , homeported in Norfolk, welcomed the public with tours during Naval Station Norfolk’s Fleet Fest over the weekend, and got underway again for training on October 27. The 51-year-old carrier is scheduled to be deactivated in Spring 2027. USS Dwight D. Eisenhower, also based at NS Norfolk, left port for work ups on October 24. Also on the east coast, USS John C. Stennis has been undergoing maintenance since 2021. The RCOH was expected to be completed and the carrier redelivered in October 2026, according to budget documents, but it’s unclear if that timeline will hold. However, USS Harry S. Truman recently moved to begin an RCOH, suggesting Stennis is nearing completion. On the other side of the country, USS Carl Vinson is in port in San Diego. Vinson returned on September 4 after a 25-day underway for a Final Evaluation Period and Tailored Ship’s Training Availability. The future USS John F. Kennedy was operating in the Atlantic Ocean launching a T-45C Goshawk training aircraft and EA-18G Growler, both attached to the “Salty Dogs” of Air Test and Evaluation Squadron (VX) 23, on October 25. T-45C Goshawk and EA-18G Growler on the future USS JFK. U.S. Navy photo Future USS John F. Kennedy conducts flight operations. U.S. Navy photo The Big Deck Fleet At A Glance Overall, three U.S. carriers are deployed, three are working up in various states of readiness, three are in maintenance availabilities, one is post-deployment, one is being used primarily for training before deactivation, and another will be delivered in 2027. Two amphibious ready groups are deployed, one is forward-deployed, three are working up or in port, and three are in maintenance. Note: Positions are general approximations. Non-deployed LHA/LHD amphibious warships are not shown. Contact the author: ian@twz.com or @ianellisjones The post Where Are The Aircraft Carriers?: October 27, 2026 appeared first on TWZ .

title: RISS Rewards Winning Public School with N1m in STEM Contest
body: Funmi Ogundare Community Senior High School, Wasimi, has emerged overall champion in an inter-school Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) competition, organised by Redeemer’s International Secondary School (RISS), Maryland, Lagos, with a N1 million grant to upgrade its facilities. The winning school’s student representatives will also receive N250,000 each, while Mende Senior High School, which came second, will receive N150,000 per student. Army Cantonment Senior Secondary School, which finished third, will receive N100,000 per student. The competition was organised as part of activities marking RISS’s 30th anniversary to promote educational development and support public schools across the state. Speaking at the grand finale recently, the Principal of RISS, Mrs Feyisara Osinupebi, noted that the initiative was designed to celebrate the school’s three decades of academic excellence by contributing to the development of under-resourced learning environments within its host community. Osinupebi explained that the school would assess the needs of Community Senior High School, Wasimi, before committing the grant to upgrading its facilities. She added that the students from the top three schools would receive their respective cash prizes, while teachers who prepared them for the competition would also receive tokens of appreciation. The Lagos State Commissioner for Basic and Secondary Education, Mr Tolani Alli-Balogun, who was represented at the event, commended RISS for extending its corporate social responsibility efforts to pupils in public schools. He urged other private educational institutions to adopt similar initiatives to strengthen collaboration between public and private schools and improve educational outcomes. The Head of the Organising Committee and Head of Science Department at RISS, Mr Francis Victor, said the competition was organised in collaboration with the Lagos State Ministry of Education to ensure academic rigour, transparency and fairness. According to him, the competition was conducted through a digital, paperless platform, eliminating the use of pen and paper. “We asked ourselves how best to give back to our community to mark 30 years of impact. We secured statutory approval from the state education ministry, targeted state-owned schools within our local catchment, and deployed a seamless, technology-driven platform without pen and paper,” he said. Victor disclosed that 26 schools were invited, while 16 public schools participated in the competition, which featured three elimination stages. The contest was subsequently narrowed to six schools, then four, before the top three finalists emerged. He said Promasidor and the RISS Parents Association supported the competition, adding that the public school pupils’ performance showed their capacity to excel when given appropriate digital tools and opportunities. The English Language teacher who led the winning school’s contingent, Mr Kehinde Kuje, attributed the victory to the school’s teachers and their commitment to keeping students academically prepared. He said the students maintained their composure despite receiving information about the competition at short notice. “It was the collective effort of every teacher at Community Senior High School, Wasimi. We drill our students consistently to ensure they are exam-ready at all times, even when memos arrive late. This victory proves that dedication in public education will never be in vain,” Kuje said. One of the winning students, Adeniyi-Yisa Aduragbemi, who studies science, attributed the school’s success to persistent research at the library and urged other public school pupils to remain disciplined in their studies. His teammate, Muhammad Abubakar, thanked their teachers for providing the training and support that enabled them to excel in the digital competition.

title: Hegseth likely to face questions on US role in Indo-Pacific at ASEAN summit in Cebu
body: MANILA, Philippines – US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is likely to face questions about Washington’s commitment to the Indo-Pacific region when he meets Southeast Asian counterparts in the Philippines on Wednesday, October 28. As the Iran war strains US military readiness and tension rises with China , the Pentagon said Hegseth’s attendance at the gathering in Cebu would reaffirm Washington’s commitment to “peace through strength” in the Pacific. Analysts said Southeast Asian nations could use meetings with Hegseth on the sidelines to seek clarity about the endgame in Iran, US expectations from allies and partners, and how the conflict’s demands square with commitments to the Indo-Pacific. “They will want to seek answers from the United States regarding certainty towards alliances and partnerships,” said Collin Koh, a security scholar at Singapore’s S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies. “And of course, the bigger elephant in the room is how does that juxtapose with US commitment to the Indo-Pacific or Western Pacific theater.” Economies grappling with Iran war impact Southeast Asian economies are grappling with the effects of Iran war , while tension between host the Philippines and Beijing add another source of friction to a forum meant to promote dialogue and practical cooperation on security. The Iran war, launched by US and Israeli strikes on February 28, has disrupted shipping and oil markets, exposing Southeast Asia’s vulnerability to imported-fuel shocks and pushing energy security higher on ASEAN’s agenda. Greg Poling, director of the Asia Maritime Transparency Initiative, said Hegseth would get an opportunity at the gathering to tackle aspects regarding China, the disputed South China Sea and Washington’s commitments to its treaty allies. “Most will want reassurance about US commitment to the region, despite the political turmoil in Washington and the weakening of both US capabilities and readiness by the war in Iran.” The topic is critical for the Philippines, a US treaty ally whose ties with Beijing have soured amid repeated confrontations in the disputed South China Sea, Chinese sanctions and, more recently, a summoning of the Chinese ambassador. China’s defense attaché in the Philippines will attend the meeting, its defense ministry said on Tuesday, October 27. Days before the meeting, set for October 28 and 29, the Philippine military said it monitored and shadowed China’s Liaoning aircraft carrier group as it passed through waters off the southern Philippines toward the Celebes Sea. Stronger signals were more likely to figure in talks among like-minded partners, added Poling. Such partners include the Squad, a grouping of the United States, Japan, Australia and the Philippines, whose defense chiefs are set to meet on October 28. Eventual chairman’s statement seen as restrained However, the eventual chairman’s statement was likely to be more restrained than talks behind closed doors and would employ familiar ASEAN language, said Koh. Manila’s position as ASEAN chair while embroiled in a dispute with China was “particularly sensitive”, he added. Poling said the Philippines had to balance “aspirational cooperation” on issues such as energy connectivity, the digital economy and coast guard cooperation against rising tension with China and stalled progress on a South China Sea code of conduct. “For the Philippines, the whole ASEAN chair year has been a difficult balance,” added Poling, who is also a fellow with the Southeast Asia Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies. “I’d expect tactical cooperation on the ADMM workstreams … but no strategic alignment on the South China Sea or other thorny issues,” he said, referring to the bloc’s effort to tackle issues such as maritime security and counter-terrorism. – Rappler.com

title: Alberta UCP officials, candidates must now sign pro-Canada pledge form
body:
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith says those looking to join her United Conservative Party board at next month’s annual general meeting must now sign a declaration vowing not to advocate for separation.
And she says anyone who wants to run for the party in next year’s election will also have to affirm pro-Canada views. Existing board members will also be expected to honour the pledge.
Smith says the issue is clear and unequivocal. “We’re not an independence party,” she told reporters Tuesday when asked about the pledge form now circulating online.
“There’s lots of range for people to able to advocate on policy — but just not that.”
Smith says Albertans voted resoundingly in last week’s referendum that they want Alberta to stay in Canada, and she says her party must respect that.
“The whole point of a political party is to faithfully represent your constituents,” Smith said.
“And if the constituents have told us they want us to go in a certain (pro-Canada) direction, to have credibility as a candidate you’re going to have to abide by what Albertans told us.”
She says they have a number of board positions to fill, and still have about two-thirds of candidates yet to be named ahead of the October 2027 election.
The move comes as Smith works to rein in separatists in her party ahead of next year’s general election.
Smith has warned that the issue could fracture her party and open the door to an NDP win in 2027.

title: NSE Inducts 800 ATBU Graduates, Tasks them on Integrity, National Development
body: Segun Awofadeji in Bauchi The Nigerian Society of Engineers (NSE), Bauchi State Branch, has urged 800 newly inducted graduate engineers from Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University (ATBU), Bauchi, to uphold professional ethics, embrace continuous learning, and help address Nigeria’s infrastructure and development challenges. The Chairman of the NSE Bauchi Branch, Shehu Wakili, gave the charge during the 4th induction ceremony of graduate members of the society at the university on Saturday, describing the occasion as a significant milestone in the young engineers’ professional careers. Wakili, speaking on behalf of NSE President Alimasuya Rabiu and the Society’s National Executive Council, congratulated the inductees on their admission to the professional body, describing their membership as the start of a new phase of responsibility and service. He noted that the induction went beyond the presentation of certificates, stressing that it marked the transition from academic training to professional practice, where engineers would be expected to apply their knowledge responsibly and adhere to established standards. Wakili said, “Engineering is a profession that directly affects human lives, public safety and national development, making integrity and competence indispensable qualities for every practitioner. “The bridge you will design, someone’s father will drive on it. The building you will supervise, someone’s children will sleep inside it. The power system you will operate, a hospital depends on it. Therefore, failure is not an option.” The NSE branch chairman emphasised that engineers must recognise the far-reaching consequences of their professional decisions, particularly in the design, construction and maintenance of infrastructure and essential services. He urged the newly inducted members to place public safety and professional responsibility above personal financial interests, warning them against compromising standards for profit. Wakili specifically warned against substandard construction materials, unprofessional practices, and shortcuts that can undermine the quality and safety of engineering projects. He maintained that engineers must protect the integrity of their profession by ensuring that every project entrusted to them meets the required technical and ethical standards. The chairman also encouraged the inductees to remain committed to professional development, noting that obtaining a Bachelor of Engineering degree was only the beginning of a lifelong learning process. He observed that technological advancements are rapidly transforming the engineering profession, with developments in artificial intelligence, renewable energy and smart-grid systems creating new opportunities and demands for practitioners. Wakili therefore urged young engineers to pursue postgraduate qualifications, acquire relevant technical skills, and work toward registration with the Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria (COREN). The chairman also assured them that the NSE Bauchi Branch would provide opportunities for professional training, mentorship and networking to help them develop their competence and remain abreast of emerging trends in the field. He further challenged the inductees to contribute meaningfully to national development by applying their expertise to Nigeria’s persistent challenges in electricity supply, road infrastructure, water provision and security-related technological needs. According to him, the country requires engineers who can develop practical solutions to its problems, create employment opportunities and support sustainable economic growth. In his keynote address, Prof. S.Y. Umar, a Geotechnical Engineering lecturer in the Department of Civil Engineering, ATBU, encouraged the new members to become job creators rather than depend solely on available employment opportunities, adding that their technical knowledge and innovative ideas could contribute to industrial growth and improved public services. Umar, also the institution’s dean of Student Affairs, acknowledged the contributions of the university management, lecturers, and parents to the training and development of the graduates. He thanked the parents for their sacrifices and lecturers for imparting the knowledge and skills required to prepare the young engineers for professional practice. He also urged the inductees to uphold the dignity of the Nigerian Society of Engineers, maintain high ethical standards and serve as worthy ambassadors of the university.

title: Chrisland High School, Lekki, Wins Double Championship in Science Olympiad
body: Funmi Ogundare Chrisland High School, Lekki, has emerged as national champion in junior and senior secondary school categories of the 2026 Science Olympiad Nigeria, defeating nine other schools in each category at the national competition held recently at Anchor University, Ayobo, Lagos. The school got recognition for the feat at the Science Olympiad Nigeria 2026 National Championship honours and awards ceremony, held at its Lekki campus. The school’s Division B and C teams won top honours after representing Lagos State at the national championship, underscoring the importance of practical science education in developing students’ critical thinking, problem-solving and innovation skills. Speaking at the ceremony, the National Director of Science Olympiad Nigeria and STEM Ambassador, UK, Adewumi Odunnaike, attributed the achievement to preparation, persistence and a commitment to learning. “Behind every award is preparation that the audience may never see, a difficult question revisited, an idea tested, a mistake corrected, and the patience to try again,” he said. He urged students to stay curious, approach scientific challenges with integrity, and apply their knowledge to solve societal problems, including unreliable electricity, poor water quality, waste management, and the safety of everyday technology. He said the skills acquired through scientific learning would prepare them for future roles as scientists, engineers, innovators and problem-solvers. The national director commended the school’s management, parents and coaches for their contributions to the students’ preparation and success. He also called on professional bodies, engineering practitioners, companies, foundations and alumni to partner with Science Olympiad Nigeria to expand opportunities for young people to participate in science and technology programmes. He noted that “such partnerships could provide learning materials, scientific equipment, laboratory access, practical workshops, coaching, mentorship and financial support for tournament participation”. He urged prospective partners to work with the programme through clearly defined initiatives that identify beneficiaries, specify required resources and provide mechanisms for tracking progress and the use of support. In his welcome address, the Principal of Chrisland High School, Lekki, Dr Kolawole Cole Bewaji, described the double championship as a significant milestone for the school and evidence of the value of education that encourages students to apply classroom knowledge to real-life challenges. He congratulated the students for making their parents, teachers and the wider Chrisland Schools community proud, while appreciating the support of the school’s management, parents, teachers and coaches. Bewaji said academic excellence should not be measured solely by examination results, noting that competitions such as the Science Olympiad allow students to demonstrate their ability to think critically, solve problems and innovate. “Grades measure knowledge, but competitions like this reveal how students apply that knowledge, think critically, solve problems and innovate,” he said. He stressed that science remained central to advancements in medicine, technology, agriculture and national development, adding that schools must prepare young people not only to use future inventions but also to create them. Speaking on the ceremony’s theme, ‘Innovate Now’, the principal encouraged the students to remain curious, ask questions and develop solutions to everyday problems. “The future does not belong merely to those who memorise answers, but to those courageous enough to ask questions and develop solutions,” he said. He urged them to regard the awards as motivation for greater accomplishments rather than the end of their journey.

title: BAOSA Commits Resources to Rehabilitate Labs, Install Solar Lighting
body: Oluchi Chibuzor The Baptist Academy Old Students’ Association (BAOSA) has unveiled seven legacy projects at its alma mater, committing resources to rehabilitate laboratories, improve campus security and restore the school’s green environment as the institution marked its 171st Founder’s Day. The projects, undertaken by different sets of old students, include the renovation of the Physics and Chemistry laboratories, rehabilitation of the Home Economics and Agricultural Science laboratories, installation of solar lighting across the school premises and inauguration of the BAOSA Garden. The association also unveiled a redesigned school badge and performed the groundbreaking ceremony for a proposed lecture theatre, medical clinic and preparation room. BAOSA Global President, Olumide Ajomale, said “the interventions were aimed at addressing infrastructure deficiencies, improving the learning environment and preserving the institution’s heritage. The renovation of the laboratories was necessary after years of inadequate maintenance, as the installation of solar lights will improve security and visibility within the premises, particularly during power outages.” Ajomale said the landscaping and tree-planting initiative was also designed to restore the greenery that once characterised the school and promote environmental consciousness among students. “When we were in school, this was a massive green land,” he said, urging students to appreciate nature and understand the importance of protecting the environment. He stressed that the association’s commitment to the school extends beyond physical infrastructure to include scholarships, mentoring, skills development and character formation. He disclosed that the association had awarded prizes and scholarships worth millions of naira through its annual activities, supporting students with disabilities and those from financially disadvantaged backgrounds. According to him, BAOSA also sponsors initiatives to strengthen students’ public-speaking and debating abilities, including the ‘Have Your Say’ debate competition organised by BAOSA, UK. “Our intervention goes beyond money. It goes beyond the physical infrastructure. It’s wholesome, and we’re proud to be able to do this,” Ajomale said. He stated that the association is determined to preserve the school’s 171-year history and ensure that its legacy continues to inspire future generations. As part of the heritage preservation effort, he disclosed that the school’s heritage room would be developed further with historical documents, graduation programmes and other memorabilia documenting the institution’s evolution and the achievements of its alumni. He also highlighted the BAOSA Order of Excellence, established to recognise former students whose academic accomplishments, professional achievements, leadership and service to society reflect the institution’s ideals. Ajomale said the initiative would expose current students to the achievements of distinguished alumni and encourage them to pursue excellence. The President of the Lagos East Baptist Conference, Rev. Matthew Olawale Awujoola, who represented the President of the Nigerian Baptist Convention, Rev. David Olusola Idowu, commended the alumni for investing in their former school. He said sustained alumni involvement could help bridge infrastructure gaps, strengthen academic development and provide students with role models. “If we have this replicated all across the land through our schools by our old students, I am very sure that education will greatly increase in Nigeria,” Awujoola said. The cleric expressed optimism that the investments would significantly improve Baptist Academy over the next decade and urged students to uphold the values exemplified by the association. The school Principal, Mr. Solomon Ajagunmo, said the projects would help improve teaching and learning. He assured the alumni that the management would maintain the facilities and protect the investments. Zonal Administrator of Baptist Mission Schools, Lagos Zone, Mrs. Titilayo Amune, described alumni interventions as critical to restoring the standards associated with established schools. According to her, contributions from old students went beyond buildings and equipment to include scholarships, mentoring and other forms of educational support that might otherwise be difficult to provide. Amune said such initiatives could instill a culture of generosity and responsibility in younger students, encouraging them to support future generations when they become successful.

title: University of Ibadan to Inaugurate Olapegba As VC Nov 2
body: The new Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ibadan, Prof. Peter Olamakinde Olapegba, will be inaugurated on November 2, 2026, at the University’s famous Trenchard Hall, where Emeritus Prof. Akin Akande will preside, while the outgoing VC, Prof. K.O. Adebowale, will be the chief host. The inauguration lecture titled ‘The African University in a New World Order, The Imperative of Knowledge Sovereignty and Relevance’ would be delivered by Prof. Akin Ogundiran of Northwestern University, Everyton, Illinois, USA. Until his appointment, Olapegba was the Deputy Vice-Chancellor, Administration. His research has led to the development of culturally relevant and globally accepted scales to measure constructs in social psychology, contributing to both theoretical foundations and practical applications. He has published extensively, with over 130 scholarly works, including books, chapters, monographs, journal articles, and creative pieces. His work has addressed critical issues like HIV/AIDS, sexual behaviour, domestic violence, and quality of life, providing models for behavioural change and attitudinal improvement. The professor of Applied Social Psychology is a fellow of the Nigerian Psychological Association, the Society for Peace Studies and Practice, and the Centre for Peace and Conflict Studies. Meanwhile, Ilutitun Osoro Community in Ondo, where Olapegba had part of his early primary education, has sent its felicitation and congratulations to the new VC. The paramount Ruler of the community, Oba Ernest Adeoye Idepefo, said in a statement that the community was delighted that the then small boy who accompanied his father to the community as a teacher is now the new vice-chancellor of the prestigious University of Ibadan. He prayed for a successful tenure full of landmark achievements for the new VC.

title: Eisenkot warns in victory speech: 'Netanyahu, don't you dare use Israel's security for your political purposes'
body: Yashar! chairman Gadi Eisenkot declared in a speech overnight at his party's headquarters in Tel Aviv: "We made history. I stand before you deeply moved. This morning, the people of Israel went to the polls in a referendum on the leadership that will guide Israel in the coming years. Tonight, we received our answer: The public voted for change. The coalition responsible for the failures has lost the people's trust. Israeli voters voted against Benjamin Netanyahu continuing as prime minister of Israel." Eisenkot stressed that the official results were still pending, but added: "We can already say that Netanyahu finds himself tonight facing a larger, stronger Zionist, statesmanlike majority. A clear majority among the general public, as well as among those who serve and work. A worthy leader would accept the people's vote of no confidence and announce his retirement from political life today."   "With voter turnout this high, it would be a mistake to hold another election. It is our duty, my personal duty, to do everything possible to fulfill the will of the people," he continued, as supporters chanted, "The next prime minister!" Eisenkot added: "Millions of Israelis are fed up with the culture of lies, fed up with failures, fed up with division and incitement. To the millions who voted today in favor of universal military service and new leadership, I want to promise you this: I will do everything in my power to establish a Zionist government committed to military service. My intention, and that of the Yashar! team, is to represent all Israelis." "When I founded Yashar!, it was still a party polling in the single digits. This was the vision I had in mind. We established a party that has earned the trust of people on the right, left and center, a party offering a credible alternative government. "I will work with my partners for change to ensure that the people's decision and wishes are translated into the swift establishment of a stable Zionist government that serves all Israeli citizens. That is the imperative of the hour and what is needed to unite the people. "It will be a government that upholds the principles I have presented throughout this journey: recognition of the State of Israel as Jewish and democratic, commitment to the values of the Declaration of Independence, commitment to passing a universal military service law and commitment to dismantling Hamas!" Eisenkot continued: "We will change Israel's national priorities and put the country back on track. We will bring unifying, responsible leadership and will not seek to defeat one side or another. Because we are one people, one nation that deserves a government that respects and recognizes all its members. "The challenges ahead are enormous, in security, the economy and issues that go to the very heart of our society. Israel needs stable and responsible leadership." The Yashar! chairman also warned against actions Netanyahu might take before the possible formation of a new government. "Tonight, I want to address all the heads of Israel's security agencies and public service: Netanyahu is the head of a caretaker government without a mandate of public confidence. Remember that you serve the state and the interests of Israel's citizens alone. Stand firm against any attempt to challenge you. You have my unequivocal backing. "Netanyahu, don't you dare use Israel's security for your political purposes. "And to all Israeli citizens, I say this now: I can promise you that the era of draft evasion, failures and lies is over. The era of 'us versus them' is over."

title: Netanyahu calls for right-wing government, warns against reliance on Arab parties
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called for a strong right-wing government and warned against forming one dependent on Arab parties early Wednesday, telling activists and journalists at Likud's election headquarters in Jerusalem to await the final count after exit polls left the outcome unresolved.“The Likud is the largest party in Israel,” Netanyahu said. He also claimed that the right-wing bloc held a decisive majority among the Jewish and Zionist public and those who supported the Jewish state.Data from the Central Elections Committee on Wednesday around noon showed Netanyahu's coaltion bloc leading with 54 seats; Likud had 27. Updated exit polls on Tuesday from Kan and Channel 13 put Netanyahu's bloc and the four-party opposition grouping at 51 seats each, with the Arab parties on 18. Channel 12 put Netanyahu's bloc at 52, the opposition grouping at 49 and the Arab parties at 19.“We must establish a strong, right-wing, national government,” Netanyahu said.He warned against establishing a government reliant on what he called anti-Zionist Arab parties, accusing them of opposing Israel's existence and attacking its soldiers. He challenged politicians advocating an alliance of those who serve in the military over the possibility of cooperating with those parties.His remarks placed the question of reliance on Arab parties at the center of the uncertain coalition arithmetic, even as he urged supporters to wait for the actual results.Netanyahu recounts government's military achievements, unfinished workSpeaking to party activists after a night of chants of “Only Bibi!”, Netanyahu recounted what he presented as his government's military achievements and argued that its work remained unfinished.“Iran is weaker than ever; Israel is stronger than ever,” he said.He described an opportunity to work with US President Donald Trump to remove the Iranian threat, while warning that the danger would persist as long as the current regime remained in power.Netanyahu's call for patience followed similar messages from Likud MK Amit Halevi and supporters The Jerusalem Post interviewed throughout the night.Halevi disputed the initial projection of 50 seats for Netanyahu's bloc, arguing that it understated its support and would not be the final outcome.He described the election as Israeli society's response to the October 7 attacks and three years of war. People had not remained indifferent, he told the Post. They had come out to vote.Halevi also pointed to the projected strength of the Arab parties. His objection to their political influence, he said, concerned what he characterized as their radical ideology, rather than ethnicity.He warned that an attempt by Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot to form a government reliant on figures Halevi described as radical advisers to Yasser Arafat would fail.Inside the hall, classic Israeli songs played in Mizrahi renditions. Journalists, activists, party members and sitting MKs filled the venue, surrounded by Likud's blue and white and campaign posters.When Meir Cohen, a longtime Likud member, was asked how Netanyahu would navigate the uncertainty and assemble a government, the answer was simple.“I trust Bibi,” he told the Post.Cohen traced his connection to Likud to his birth in 1973, saying Menachem Begin had been his sandak, holding him during his brit milah, the Jewish ritual circumcision.He expressed distrust of the initial projections from the three main broadcasters and credited Netanyahu with strengthening Israel's military power and standing abroad.“He will protect us. He will continue to protect us,” Cohen said.For supporter Tomer Shlomi Mishkaf Lavan, the evening was about the country's future and the need to bring Israelis together.This ship called the State of Israel to safe harbor'“We are fighting for the future of the State of Israel,” he told the Post, calling for a strong leader who would unite the country.He returned repeatedly to the divisions between Israelis, describing angry exchanges, burning tires and blocked roads over the past four years. He wanted quiet, an end to the protests and a different atmosphere between people.“We need mutual responsibility. We need people to love one another,” he said.Asked what being at Likud headquarters meant to him personally, he again spoke about overcoming divisions.“I came here to express my opinion. My opinion is unity,” he said.He wanted Netanyahu to mend the country's rifts and guide “this ship called the State of Israel to safe harbor.”Another supporter, who told the Post he had worked for the movement for decades, urged patience with the projections and questioned whether they fairly reflected support for Netanyahu.Throughout the night, questions about seats and coalition partners repeatedly brought the conversation back to the prime minister himself.“I trust Bibi,” Cohen said.

title: Pizza Fan Owner Remanded in Custody as Grigoris Chief Weighs Rescue Bid
body: Pizza Fan founder and owner Konstantinos Antaras has been remanded in custody pending trial, as talks emerge over a possible buyer for the troubled pizza chain and its roughly 2,500 workers. Antaras, whom authorities allege led a criminal organisation behind a €25 million tax-evasion scheme, was ordered detained on Tuesday, 27 October, after testifying for about two hours before Athens’ 32nd regular investigating magistrate, To Vima reported. Dimitris Iliopoulos, described by prosecutors as his second-in-command, was placed under house arrest with an electronic tag. According to Ta Nea, 18 of the 23 defendants had testified by Tuesday evening. Apart from Antaras and Iliopoulos, the other 16 were released under restrictive conditions, in some cases with bail of up to €6,000. The first five had been released earlier, with bail of up to €5,000. The last five defendants were expected to finish testifying in the early hours of Wednesday. “Tax offences, not a criminal organisation” Antaras denied the criminal organisation charge before the magistrate, according to Proto Thema and To Vima. “I deny the charge. All the acts concern tax offences and in no way a criminal organisation,” he reportedly said. “It is unfair to call a group of people who have built a successful business a criminal organisation. It employs more than 2,500 people, pays €36 million a year in wages and €15 million in VAT and taxes, while tens of millions go to suppliers.” He also reportedly admitted knowing that franchise operators were illegally using the so-called “kerasma” (“treat”) function, but argued that the central ordering system allowed their revenue to be checked. Iliopoulos reportedly told the magistrate he knew of the practice but had opposed it. His lawyer, Stavros Georgopoulos, said Antaras consents to the immediate release of the seized and frozen funds to the state to settle any tax liability. A second lawyer, Michalis Markoulakos, said the case referral cites €35 million in unpaid taxes, but the charge itself concerns €1.8 million, which, he said, relates to franchisees rather than Antaras. A possible buyer Vlassis Georgatos, head of VG Holding, whose businesses include the Grigoris chain and Air Canteen, has been approached by Antaras’s side about a possible takeover, Newmoney reported. No agreement or binding offer has been announced. “We have to see if and what can be saved, otherwise what would you take?” Georgatos said, according to Pagenews. Pagenews also reported that at least three businesspeople from the food-service sector have been sounded out, and that one of them declined. The chain has about 110 stores, more than 80 franchisees, estimated network sales above €100 million a year and about 2,500 employees, according to Newmoney. Union representative Giorgos Stefanakis said workers were told, after meeting a company legal representative, that the chain would not reopen under its current ownership, Newmoney reported. Workers left in limbo In Thessaloniki, dozens of Pizza Fan workers protested outside the Ministry of Macedonia and Thrace. Seven local stores have closed, leaving more than 150 employees uncertain about their future, To Vima reported. Deputy Labour Minister Kostas Karagounis told ERTnews that employment contracts remain active and that there has been no order to close the business. “The company must pay employees’ wages, social security contributions and its other obligations. Payroll is due at the end of the month,” he said. According to labour ministry officials cited by Net24, the government is also considering suspending contracts and paying affected workers a special-purpose allowance of €534, which would require a dedicated legislative provision. The defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty. title: FUTO Unveils TETFund-funded SciDial Platform to Bridge Science Communication Gaps
body: Amby Uneze in Owerri The Federal University of Technology, Owerri (FUTO) has presented findings from a multi-state study on science communication in Nigeria and launched SciDial, a digital platform designed to make research findings more accessible and to connect researchers with industry, government and the public. The Science Communication research model study, funded by the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) under its National Research Fund, examined barriers to effective science communication. The project, titled ‘Strategies to Overcome the Challenges of Science Communication in Nigeria: Towards Domesticating Science for Societal Benefits (SciComm FUTO)’, was anchored at the Africa Centre of Excellence in Future Energies and Electrochemical Systems (ACE-FUELS) of FUTO. The presentation held at Rockview Hotels in Owerri and drew more than 200 participants from academia, industry, government, research organisations, the media, civil society and the general public. Principal investigator, Dr. Kanayo Lucy Oguzie highlighted a fundamental disconnect between how researchers share their findings and how potential users seek information. Fieldwork surveyed 2,208 people across four states and eight local government areas, comprising 1,266 members of the public and 942 academics. Key patterns emerged: researchers are willing to communicate but rely heavily on academic channels such as journal publications and scientific conferences; the public is willing to use research but rarely seeks it out in those venues; and industry engages with research, though not widely enough to close the gap. Specific figures showed that 75-91 per cent of respondents were willing to use research findings, while 77-99 per cent considered outreach to the public, industry and government important. Yet 21-49 per cent never or rarely look for research findings. Regular contact with fellow academics ranged from 44-76 per cent, dropping to 32-61 per cent with industry and 23-53 per cent with government. Researchers preferred social media (40-61 per cent) and video (34-62 per cent), while 65-91 per cent relied on journals and 60-72 per cent on conferences; only 16-23 per cent used television. Between 26-37 per cent found research hard to access and 25-37 per cent found it unclear. Only 51-65 per cent considered scientific language simple enough, and 84-93 per cent wanted communication training. “The problem is not a lack of interest in research,” Oguzie said, “it is a mismatch between the channels researchers use and the channels potential users rely on. Valuable findings can go unused even when researchers are willing to share them and others are willing to apply them.” Dr. Ikechukwu Ayogu, one of the co-investigators, demonstrated SciDial, moving the project from diagnosis to a practical tool. Professor Emeka Oguzie, Centre Leader of ACE-FUELS, Founder and Scientific Adviser of SciDial, and former Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Research, Development and Innovation) of FUTO, led a strategic stakeholder engagement session. He linked the initiative to his Research 7.x framework, which holds that research should deliver measurable value beyond publication – for knowledge, capacity, innovation, enterprise, policy, society and national competitiveness. “Research that ends at publication has done only half its job,” Oguzie said. “Under Research 7.x, we judge research by the value it creates for industry, government and communities. SciDial is where that value begins to travel.” Mrs. Esther Ukachukwu, member of the TETFund Board of Trustees representing the South-East, commended the team for focusing on translating scientific knowledge into practical benefits. She noted that the greatest value of research is realised when it improves lives, strengthens industries, influences policy and contributes to national development, and urged stakeholders to take ownership of the outcomes. Dr. L.M Faruk, Director of Research, Innovation and Information Technology at the National Universities Commission (NUC), described the initiative as a step towards bridging the gap between universities and society. He stressed that universities must actively engage industry and society rather than wait to be sought out, and pledged the commission’s continued support. Chief Sylvester Obinna, Vice- President of the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN), highlighted SciDial’s relevance to manufacturers seeking expertise, presenting technical challenges and exploring research-based solutions. The Vice-Chancellor of FUTO, Professor Ikechukwu Dozie, was represented by Dr. Innocent Arukalam, acting Dean of the School of Engineering and Engineering Technology. Representatives of the University of Agriculture and Environmental Sciences, Umuagwo, and Claretian University of Nigeria, Nekede, also attended. The workshop marks the start of SciDial’s operational phase. The team plans to expand researcher participation, gather stakeholder feedback, refine the platform and strengthen institutional partnerships, with the broader goal of improving the visibility, accessibility and practical use of Nigerian research.

title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1707: UN commission finds Russia’s strikes on Ukraine’s power grid are crimes against humanity
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Exclusives “Our future cannot be the subject of agreements between Trump and Putin”: Ukraine supporters protest US policy on Russia in Europe, US, and Australia . Pro-Ukraine demonstrations took place in more than 10 cities as protesters condemned US moves to ease sanctions on Russia and pressure Kyiv to make concessions while Moscow’s war continues. Military Ukraine intercepts nearly 60% of Russia’s Geran-4 jet drones, General Staff says, as Kyiv races to counter evolving threat . Ukraine’s interception rate reaches 80% during some attacks, as F-16s, Mirage jets, mobile fire groups, and interceptor drones help counter Russia’s jet-powered attacks. He drove a taxi in Jakarta and once worked in the US. Russia trained him as a machine gunner for a week and a half, then sent him into his first and last battle . Ukraine’s military intelligence says Russian recruiters reached the Indonesian through his job search and moved him from a contract signing near Moscow to the front in a matter of weeks. Russia tries to drag a village north of Kupiansk into no-man’s-land after its losses in Ukraine’s underground operation . Ukraine’s military describes Russian troops trying to keep a path open toward the city through Radkivka, a village on its northern edge, while fighting for neighboring Holubivka goes on. Ukraine says it hit drone hangars at Crimea’s Hvardiiske. Now an OSINT channel spots 20+ bermed shelters there . Dnipro Osint says the base fires Shahed-type drones from vehicles on its runway, and the airfield kept turning up on Ukraine’s launch lists in October. Two weeks after a Russian supply base burned in Luhansk’s Khrustalnyi, Ukrainian drones came back for an ammo depot . The city in occupied eastern Ukraine has served Russia’s army as a rear logistics hub since early in the full-scale war. Ukraine plans to rebuild its air force on NATO’s model by 2035. Its Air Force already knows which fighter it wants next, and why . Ukraine’s F-16s face thousands of Russian targets a month, many of them worn jets bought secondhand. For the third time this year, Ukrainian drones hit Russia’s rocket-fuel rubber plant in Samara Oblast. This time they reach the raw-material shop feeding it . OSINT channels recorded fires at the same butyl-rubber shops in April and September. Intelligence and technology Germany’s Helsing promises jet-drone-hunting missiles at under $100,000 a shot—its CEO doesn’t expect them on the market before 2027 . One contract is signed. Ukraine’s own jet-drone interceptors, meanwhile, aren’t due in needed numbers before late November. Ukraine says it has finished its part of FREYJA, Europe’s joint anti-ballistic project. Partners’ work is still underway . Zelenskyy told ABC News on 23 October that Ukraine got only 24 US Patriot interceptors from the US in three months. Postal service Nova Post says it has already shot down Russian Shahed drones, as Ukrainian businesses take air defense into their own hands . The company says its air defense project is operational as Russia increasingly targets Ukrainian infrastructure, while other businesses weigh the costs and benefits of protecting their facilities themselves. Ukrainian intelligence says Russia’s missile makers use gear from seven countries—and the Chinese machines run on European, Japanese, and Taiwanese parts . Ukrainian intelligence listed 30 foreign-made items at Russian arms plants on 26 October, 17 of them made outside China. A 4-watt video link passed Ukraine’s state tests, its maker says, and could stretch STING interceptors’ radius from 20 km to 30 km . The 30 km figure is Wild Hornets’ own estimate, first given in August, and assumes good line of sight. Testers checked three drone types. Captured Russians say there is one place on Kupiansk front they will not go: “Orion” safety corridor . Ukrainian robot unit says it built that corridor, and runs supply and evacuation through it with almost no losses. Ukrainian intelligence: Russia can probably add 10–15 Su-34 bombers a year, but no new Tu-95s or Tu-22M3s . Ukraine’s military intelligence also listed Russian jets destroyed or critically damaged in 2026, including two Tu-95MS bombers hit at Engels. International Finland and Norway leaders make rare direct call to Putin, breaking with the West’s diplomatic isolation of the Russian leader to influence Ukraine peace talks . The Nordic leaders called for de-escalation ahead of November peace talks, with Zelenskyy saying they pressed Putin over attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure. The Kremlin reiterated that any settlement must account for Russia’s demands. Ukraine’s last two EU negotiation blocks stay shut as Hungary’s new government keeps Orbán’s veto . Budapest unblocked half of the remaining negotiations after Ukraine changed its minority-language rules, then said no to the rest. The Trump administration is backing Orbán, who blocked a €90 billion EU loan to Ukraine, for UN secretary-general and is counting on support from Moscow and Beijing, WSJ says . Orbán indicated that he was willing to consider the nomination but did not want to enter the race without being confident he could win, according to the WSJ’s editorial board. Ukraine’s Zelenskyy welcomes Student List’s win in Serbia and says Kyiv is “ready to keep increasing cooperation” . The party itself plan to end the trade that brought Ukraine €800 million in ammunition. 17 public broadcasters mapped Russia’s hybrid war on Europe. Germany: four dots . One point on the map may stand for several incidents of the same type nearby or in quick succession. Humanitarian and social impact Russia replaces Ukrainians with Russian settlers in occupied Kherson Oblast; only 10–20% of pre-war population remains, Ukraine says . Russia is forcing Ukrainians from their homes while offering Russian teachers and medical workers financial incentives to settle in occupied Kherson Oblast, Ukraine’s military intelligence says. Oleshky ceasefire expands beyond occupied town as truce holds without reported violations . The expanded ceasefire zone aims to secure humanitarian convoys to Russian-occupied Oleshky, where residents face shortages of food and medicine. Russia strikes publishing house warehouse in Kharkiv on Ukrainian Language Day, adding to a campaign against Ukrainian literature and culture . The publisher is assessing losses after the attack disrupted its planned 5 November releases, as repeated Russian strikes destroy books and damage Ukraine’s publishing industry. Guns fall silent around Russian-occupied Oleshky so its starving residents can get aid, but Russia’s guarantees remain secret . Ukraine’s ombudsman says both sides are keeping to the deal, while the US first lady’s adviser says Newsmax will send reporters to watch whether residents can leave freely. Russian ballistic missiles hit a Kyiv university campus, then return before dawn for the Southern Bridge again . Two waves hit the capital hours apart, reaching students in their dormitory in the evening and the bridge carrying its green metro line before sunrise. Sixteen Ukrainian doctors who work near fighting went through three Western trauma programs in one week. American surgeons led drills . On the front line, drones and shrapnel often tear through several parts of a soldier’s body at once. Political and legal developments Russian court jails IT company director for 13 years over crypto donations after Binance shared his data, rights group says . The man had lived in Bulgaria for about 10 years before flying to Moscow on business last year, where he was detained at the airport for allegedly using obscene language. UN commission finds Russia’s grid strikes are crimes against humanity, citing last winter at minus 21°C. Now they’re intensifying . The commission concluded the strikes followed a state policy to deprive civilians of power and cause suffering, and noted that Russian authorities had openly announced further attacks and referred to a plan to carry them out. title: BIF, ALTFIN Select Five Nigerian Businesses for Asset Support Programme
