title: 'Netanyahu has lost': Bennett declares victory despite change bloc falling short of Knesset majority
body: Naftali Bennett had hoped to return as prime minister, but according to television exit polls the anti-Netanyahu bloc remains short of the 61 seats needed for a majority, Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar! party has emerged as the larger force, and Bennett's Beyachad party is projected to win just 12 to 13 seats. Bennett did not comment for two hours after the exit polls were released, finally appearing at his party's headquarters in Tel Aviv well after midnight to deliver a speech.  "People of Israel, hold your heads high! The alliance of those who serve has defeated the alliance of draft dodgers," Bennett declared. "The people of Israel have risen and spoken: Netanyahu has lost, and the October 7 government is going home! The draft-dodging coalition has collapsed from 68 seats to 50."   Bennett stressed that the official results must still be awaited and announced that talks between the leaders of the anti-Netanyahu bloc were already underway. "We will patiently await the actual results, because a great deal can still change. But already, we, the leaders of the bloc seeking change, are talking and coordinating. We will do everything, without ego, to establish a Zionist government built on an alliance of those who serve, a government of people who get things done, that will run the country responsibly and serve all the people of Israel!" Bennett then addressed the public directly. "My brothers and sisters, the greatest love of my life is my love for my people. For you. There is no other people like us in the world. We are a nation of fighters, a strong people who never give up. Hold your heads high. We will never give up on our country." He promised to bring the spirit of his meetings with citizens throughout the campaign into the country's leadership. "Leadership that listens to the people's pain and embraces them. That is exactly the spirit we will bring from the grassroots gatherings across the country to the Israeli parliament, to the leadership of the state." Bennett also addressed the war and its consequences, pledging: "We will make sure that the enormous price the people of Israel paid in this difficult war was not in vain. We will be united at home and strong against our enemies abroad." He thanked his wife, Gilat, and his family, as well as his political partner Yair Lapid, whom he described as "a leader, an Israeli patriot and a true friend." Toward the end of his speech, Bennett thanked campaign staff, activists and volunteers. "In all my years in politics, I have never seen anything like this. You worked day and night, with creativity, determination and an enormous love for this people," he said. "There has never been a campaign like this in the history of the State of Israel," he added, concluding with a call to action: "And now, let's get to work. We have a country to fix! Am Yisrael Chai!" Bennett arrived at party headquarters alongside Lapid, the No. 2 candidate on his list, who had declared minutes after the exit polls were published: "Don't let anyone confuse you. Netanyahu's bloc has suffered a crushing defeat. This is a complete collapse, and the public has told them to go home." Bennett and Lapid, who both served as prime minister during the previous change government, joined forces in April with the establishment of the Beyachad party. Until then, Lapid had headed Yesh Atid, the party he founded in 2013. Bennett returned to politics after taking a break following the end of his tenure as prime minister and amid widespread criticism from the right over his alliance with parties from the opposing political bloc, particularly Mansour Abbas' Ra'am party. The first political partnership between Bennett and Lapid came after the 2013 election, when they formed what became known as the "brothers' alliance" within Netanyahu's government, in which both served. When Beyachad was established six months ago, Bennett appeared to be Netanyahu's main challenger for the premiership. But following the formation of Eisenkot's party, Beyachad slipped to become the third-largest party in the polls. Over the past month, however, the polling trend had begun to shift.

title: Russian Strike Hits Kharkiv Apartment Building, Injures 5 Including 4-Year-Old Boy
body:
Russian forces struck a residential apartment building in Ukraine’s northeastern city of Kharkiv late Tuesday, Oct. 27, injuring at least five people, including a four-year-old boy, Ukrainian officials reported.
Kharkiv Mayor Ihor Terekhov reported on Telegram that the strike hit an apartment building in the city’s Osnovianskyi district, leaving residents trapped inside.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Earlier, the mayor had reported an attack on the district at approximately 10:40 p.m. local time.
“An apartment building has been hit. According to available information, there are people trapped inside,” Terekhov said.
In a subsequent Telegram update at 11:45 p.m., he confirmed that the number of people injured had risen to four.
Kharkiv regional authorities identified the injured as two women, aged 32 and 65, a 56-year-old man and a four-year-old boy. Three were hospitalized, according to local reporting citing the regional administration.
According to the Kharkiv Regional Military Administration, the attack sparked fires in a two-story industrial building, a two-story apartment building and a single-story residential house.
A private home and a vehicle were also damaged, while emergency services worked at the scene.
According to a State Emergency Service (DSNS) report published at 6:23 a.m., the number of people injured in Kharkiv has risen to five.
“Five people were injured, including a 4-year-old child, as a result of a Russian drone strike,” the report said.
Overnight, Russian forces struck the city’s Osnovianskyi district with a jet-powered drone, triggering a massive fire that spread across 2,500 square meters and engulfed an apartment building, a private house, outbuildings, and an industrial facility. Several high-rise buildings, garages, and vehicles were also damaged.
Amid the risk of follow-up strikes, emergency responders and other services are continuing to deal with the aftermath.
The latest strike followed another deadly attack on Kharkiv on Monday, Oct. 26, when Russian forces struck the Novobavarskyi district.
Two people were killed and four injured, according to Terekhov. Apartment buildings, private homes and vehicles were also damaged.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Russia replaces Ukrainians with Russian settlers in occupied Kherson Oblast; only 10–20% of pre-war population remains, Ukraine says
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukraine’s military intelligence estimates that only 10–20% of the prewar population may remain in the Russian-occupied left bank of Kherson Oblast, accusing Moscow of forcing Ukrainians from their homes while relocating Russian citizens to the area. Russia’s efforts to displace Ukrainians and bring Russian citizens into occupied Kherson Oblast are part of Moscow’s broader campaign to consolidate control over occupied territory, impose Russian institutions, and erode Ukrainian national identity. Similar practices have been documented in other occupied Ukrainian territories, including the resettlement of Russians into homes in Mariupol and efforts to replace Ukrainian education with Russian curricula. The Main Intelligence Directorate of Ukraine’s Defense Ministry (HUR) said Russia was creating intolerable living conditions for Ukrainian residents and unlawfully seizing private property to displace them. The agency said Moscow was simultaneously using financial incentives to recruit Russian teachers, doctors, and other professionals to work in occupied areas. Russia brings in Russian workers as Ukrainians are pushed out Before Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, around 500,000 people lived on the left bank of Kherson Oblast, according to HUR. The agency estimates that only 10–20% of that population may remain. Moscow is using state-backed recruitment programs, including “Zemsky Teacher,” “Zemsky Doctor,” “Zemsky Feldsher,” “Zemsky Cultural Worker,” and “Zemsky Coach,” to attract Russian citizens to occupied Ukrainian territory, HUR said. Under these programs, Russian teachers and doctors who agree to work in occupied areas are offered one-time payments of 2 million rubles, while junior medical staff can receive 1 million rubles. The incentives also include higher salaries and other benefits, with contracts lasting at least five years. HUR said hundreds of Russian teachers and doctors had already been brought to occupied Ukrainian territories from regions across Russia, including Krasnodar, Khabarovsk, Stavropol, and Perm Krais, as well as Rostov, Kursk, and Leningrad oblasts. According to Ukrainian intelligence, Russian medical personnel are needed primarily to serve occupying forces, while Russian teachers are being brought in to undermine Ukrainian children’s national identity. Ukraine accuses Russia of war crimes and genocidal practices HUR said Russia’s efforts to displace Ukrainian residents and bring in Russian citizens bore signs of war crimes and genocidal practices against the Ukrainian population. The agency’s allegations concern both the coercive removal of Ukrainians from occupied territory and the replacement of local residents with people brought from Russia. Ukrainian authorities say these policies are part of Moscow’s broader effort to consolidate control over occupied Ukrainian land and impose Russian identity and institutions. Kherson Oblast faces displacement, attacks, and a humanitarian crisis Russian forces occupied much of Kherson Oblast in the early months of the full-scale invasion in 2022. Ukrainian forces liberated the oblast’s right-bank areas, including the regional capital, in November that year, but Russia continues to occupy the left bank of the Dnipro River. Russian forces regularly attack Ukrainian-controlled areas of Kherson Oblast with artillery and drones, killing and injuring civilians. Ukrainians have described repeated drone attacks on civilians as a “ human safari .” In May 2025, a UN commission of inquiry concluded that Russian forces’ repeated drone attacks on civilians along the Dnipro’s right bank amounted to crimes against humanity of murder. The occupied town of Oleshky, on the left bank, has also faced severe shortages of food, medicine, and medical care amid restrictions on movement and continued fighting. Explore further Thousands are starving in occupied Oleshky. People have no food, no way out, and Russian forces bomb incoming aid Russia’s occupation has also exposed residents of Kherson Oblast to major humanitarian disasters. The destruction of the Kakhovka Dam in June 2023 flooded settlements along the Dnipro, including Russian-occupied communities on the left bank, damaging homes and forcing residents to flee. Russian forces’ restrictions on access and evacuation further endangered civilians in the affected areas. While Russia occupies the left bank of Kherson Oblast, its forces continue to target civilians on the Ukrainian-controlled right bank. Across the oblast, residents face the consequences of Russia’s invasion, from forced displacement and property seizures under occupation to deadly drone and artillery attacks. title: DOJ fails to get indictment against ex-Trump aide Cassidy Hutchinson: Sources
body:
The Justice Department had sought charges of lying to Congress.
A federal grand jury in Washington, D.C., has refused to indict former Trump White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson on charges of lying to Congress over her testimony before the House Select Committee that investigated the Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the U.S. Capitol, sources familiar with the matter confirmed to ABC News.
The failed indictment is the latest setback for the Justice Department in its support of what critics call a campaign of retribution by President Donald Trump, who has long accused Hutchinson of lying to the committee regarding his actions surrounding the Capitol assault.
Republicans have long sought to undercut Hutchinson's testimony regarding a story she said had been relayed to her secondhand about President Trump lunging for the steering wheel of his presidential limo following his speech on the Ellipse on Jan. 6.
Trump has vehemently denied the account and other White House employees did not corroborate the specific detail about Trump lunging.
The Washington Post first reported that a grand jury refused to indict Hutchinson.
Former special counsel Jack Smith, who indicted President Trump for his efforts to overturn his 2020 election loss, has said he opted not to treat Hutchinson as a material witness after determining much of her testimony was based on hearsay. Trump pleaded not guilty to all charges related to Jan. 6 and Smith's case against him was ultimately dismissed .
Hutchinson has maintained that she stands by her testimony. She could not immediately be reached for comment on Tuesday.
A Justice Department spokesperson also did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

title: Gender Ministry steps in to support students in alleged Obuasi SHTS sex abuse case
body: The Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, has met some students affected by the alleged sexual abuse at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), assuring them of the government’s support as investigations into the case continue. The engagement was intended to give the students an opportunity to express their concerns and enable the ministry to assess their needs while measures are put in place to protect their welfare, safety and dignity. Dr Lartey said the students required sensitive and coordinated support, with particular attention to their privacy and emotional well-being as the relevant authorities pursue the allegations. She also stressed the need to shield them from stigma, victimisation and further distress during the process. The Ministry said it would continue to work with the Ghana Education Service (GES), social welfare officers, health professionals and other relevant stakeholders to ensure that the students received appropriate assistance. Support for students and families The meeting forms part of a broader intervention by the ministry following allegations of sexual abuse involving students at Obuasi SHTS. As part of the response, an advance team comprising officers from the Department of Social Welfare, the Domestic Violence Secretariat and the Department of Children has been deployed to engage the affected students and their families. The team is expected to assess their circumstances, identify their support needs and coordinate appropriate interventions. The approach is intended to ensure that assistance is tailored to the needs of the students, while protecting them from unnecessary exposure and the pressures that can accompany cases of alleged sexual abuse. The ministry said it remained committed to working with the relevant institutions to uphold children’s rights, support the affected students and strengthen measures to make schools safe places for learning and development. The engagement comes as the allegations against the school continue to draw public attention, placing renewed focus on student protection, institutional accountability and the need for appropriate support for those affected. Authorities are expected to continue their investigations into the allegations. The students’ welfare and privacy remain important considerations as the process unfolds.

title: Oshawa man given life sentence for 2024 double murder of upstairs neighbour and her ex-husband
body:
Mark Gordon sat quietly in the prisoner’s box of a packed courtroom in Oshawa Tuesday as a judge sentenced the 33-year-old to two concurrent life sentences with no eligibility for parole for 21 years for the fatal shootings of a Bowmanville teacher and her ex-husband, a former Oshawa Generals hockey player.
Gordon pleaded guilty to two counts of second-degree murder in September 2025 admitting that on July 13, 2024, he fired multiple shots at 42-year-old Patrick Montgomery in front of the home where he lived on Glenforest Street in Oshawa, as Patrick’s 12-year-old son watched on.
According to the facts, around noon that day, Gordon drove down the street, approached the house where Patrick lived and knocked on the door. The son recognized Gordon as the man who lived in the basement unit at his mother’s address.
Montgomery went outside and the two spoke in the driveway for roughly 15 minutes before the son looked outside to see Gordon pointing a handgun at his father. The boy heard his father say “please don’t” before Gordon fired several shots at his father. Patrick was shot nine times including four times to the back.
“As he left, he looked at (the boy) who put his hands up, believing he was going to be shot,” the facts state.
Gordon then got into his pick-up truck and drove 400 metres down Glenforest Street to where 42-year-old Andrieana Montgomery, Patrick’s ex-wife and the mother of their two children, rented the upstairs unit of a home.
Gordon exited his truck and began firing at Andrieana, who was standing at the sink washing dishes while looking out of the front window of the home. He fired six shots from outside and then entered the residence and fired a further three shots. Andrieana was shot four times including once in the head.
Gordon, rented the basement unit under Andrieana’s main floor unit, where he lived with his partner and their young son. The two did not have an amicable relationship.
In the months preceding July 13, 2024, they argued with one another about noise coming from each other’s unit. During one such argument in the winter of 2023, Gordon told Andrieana that he had a gun.
He was, in fact, the lawful owner of a Glock 17 gen 5 semi-automatic 9 mm handgun and some rifles. He stored the firearms in a metal safe in the unit. He had a valid possession and acquisition license for the firearms.
Andrieana felt threatened when Gordon advised he had a gun. She complained to their shared landlord about the excessive noise coming from the basement unit and advised him of her concern that Gordon had a firearm. Andriena, who lived with her two sons, aged 10 and 12, told her children, family members and friends about the conflict with Gordon and that he possessed a firearm.
The facts state that Andriena told her children, who lived with her, that Gordon was not nice and not to trust him and she was afraid of him.
On May 8, 2024, Andrieana contacted the City of Oshawa and reported that the basement of the house did not meet the legal requirements for a basement suite. The City of Oshawa contacted the landlord about the violations and provided options for addressing the issue.
The landlord decided to evict Gordon, who lived with his girlfriend and her three-year-son son in the basement unit. Gordon was served with a notice of eviction on July 12, 2024.
The following day, he shot the Montgomerys in what Madam Justice Michelle Fuerst called an extremely violent attack saying Gordon knew he was leaving two children without parents when he shot them both.
“The callousness of his decision to act as he did in the face of that knowledge is immense,” Fuerst told the court.
According to a pre-sentence report, Gordon said as the relationship between him and his upstairs neighbour continued to deteriorate, his perspective in his own words was that Andrieana Montgomery was ‘bullying him” and his “disliked being bullied.”
He also told the author of the pre-sentence report that the eviction notice was the catalyst for the murders, it was the “last straw for him.”
Gordon was arrested at the scene on July 13, 2024 and has been in custody ever since. He apologized in court saying that he was wrong for what he did and that he is the sole person to blame and that he regrets everything.
The judge found it extremely aggravating that Gordon fired shots at victims who were completely defenceless and that Patrick was executed in front of his son.
“The sheer terror experienced by the child is highlighted by the fact that when Mr. Gordon looked at him, (he) reacted by putting up his hands, believing that he was next,” said Fuerst.
The judge called the shootings brutal in nature and said Gordon had multiple opportunities to stop himself. “Even Mr. Montgomery’s words, ‘Please don’t’, had no effect on him,” Fuerst told court.
She found that Gordon’s moral blameworthiness was high. “His perceptions about Ms. Montgomery fueled an extreme and unjustifiable over-reaction to the news of his family’s pending eviction,” Fuerst said.
The judge found it mitigating that after the shootings, Gordon left the handgun in plain sight in his apartment, waited outside for police to arrive and immediately admitted to the first officer who attended that he was the person who shot the victims.
“He did not get rid of the firearms, flee the area or take any steps to conceal his responsibility for the murders,” Fuerst told court. She also said it was relevant that Gordon pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and that he is a first-time offender
Assistant crown prosecutors Gregory Black and Kylie Buker sought a parole ineligibility period of 23 years whereas defence lawyer Daisy Bygrave suggested 15-18 years.
Fuerst said 23 years would give insufficient weight to Gordon’s guilty plea and status as a first-time offender and found 15-18 years would fail to give appropriate aggravating features in this case.

title: UN commission warns of ‘constitutional coup’ in South Sudan
body: South Sudan’s 2018 peace deal is being systematically dismantled in what a United Nations human rights commission described on Tuesday as a “constitutional coup”, warning that President Salva Kiir’s concentration of power risks renewed conflict ahead of elections scheduled for December. The UN Commission on Human Rights in South Sudan called on member states and regional and international partners to take urgent action to prevent renewed conflict and secure lasting peace, irrespective of the electoral timetable. The commission warned that the political settlement established in 2018 to prevent another war is being undermined, putting civilians and the country’s fragile transition at grave risk. “A negotiated settlement has been displaced under cover of elections. This amounts to a constitutional coup through legislative reforms: the unilateral dismantling of the inclusive power-sharing settlement and concentration of all authority in the President,” Yasmin Sooka, chair of the commission, told the UN General Assembly’s Third Committee. South Sudanese people have a fundamental right to choose their leaders, but they must be able to do so freely and without fear, Sooka said, adding that elections cannot justify abandoning safeguards under the 2018 Revitalised Agreement on the Resolution of the Conflict in South Sudan (R-ARCSS). These include inclusive governance, free political competition and participation, power-sharing and institutional oversight. “The international community must look beyond 22 December. Whether elections take place or not, South Sudan will still need an inclusive political settlement, protection for civilians and institutions capable of preventing further violence,” Sooka said. “Expressions of concern have not deterred those driving this crisis. Member States must attach consequences to violations and measurable commitments to diplomacy,” she added. Power concentration The commission said that, following unilateral constitutional and electoral amendments, Kiir dissolved the transitional government, the national parliament and state legislatures on September 22, removed the first vice-president and other vice-presidents, and appointed a caretaker administration answerable only to him. Kiir is overseeing an election in which he is expected to be the ruling party’s candidate, while First Vice-President Riek Machar remains detained and on trial, and his party and other opposition actors remain excluded from the electoral process. The commission’s warning comes as South Sudan prepares for elections scheduled for December 22, amid concerns about the erosion of the power-sharing arrangements established by the peace agreement. “South Sudan’s biggest political challenge is not whether a vote takes place on a particular date; rather, what the country most needs is a credible political process that addresses unresolved grievances, manages political differences peacefully, and commands general confidence of citizens,” commissioner Barney Afako told the General Assembly. “But the current political trajectory eschews inclusion and promotes exclusion, and risks engendering disaffection and destruction,” he said. South Sudan’s short history showed the consequences of exclusionary politics and governance, Afako said, calling for dialogue, a ceasefire and implementation of the peace agreement’s core provisions. Risk of renewed war The commission warned that ongoing fighting, tens of thousands of fighters remaining outside a unified command, and persistent impunity are increasing the risk of renewed conflict. It raised particular concern about aerial bombardments and ground offensives in Upper Nile and Jonglei states, attacks on civilian infrastructure, conflict-related sexual violence and the recruitment of children by armed actors. Civilians continue to bear the consequences, with displaced communities struggling to access protection and essential services, it said. The commission urged the African Union to take concrete steps towards establishing the Hybrid Court for South Sudan, alongside support for credible domestic justice processes, evidence preservation and witness protection. It also called on member states to address the resources sustaining the conflict, including arms transfers, conflict financing and the diversion of public revenue, through targeted and evidence-based action. “Impunity is not only entrenched in South Sudan; it is rewarded. Serious violations continue without effective accountability, while individuals implicated in them continue to occupy senior military and political positions,” commissioner Carlos Castresana Fernández said. Corruption and the diversion of public resources deprived people of essential services and weakened the institutions needed to protect them, he said. “Sustainable peace requires political agreements, credible accountability, functioning justice institutions and transparent management of public resources. The Hybrid Court must be established, and concrete steps must be taken now to ensure that those responsible for serious crimes can be held to account,” he added. Call for action The commission called for the activation of a joint African Union, Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) and UN task force requested by the AU C5 Plus Summit on September 29. It said the task force should have a clear mandate, timelines, public benchmarks and coordinated political backing to restore inclusive governance under the peace agreement. The commission also called for an immediate cessation of hostilities, an end to unlawful attacks against civilians and safe, unimpeded humanitarian access. It urged member states to ensure that the UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) had the resources and freedom of movement necessary to protect civilians, strengthen early warning and support reconciliation. It called for sustained humanitarian assistance, survivor services and independent human rights monitoring, warning that reducing these capacities as risks increased would leave civilians more exposed. The commission further urged member states to insist on independently assessed electoral safeguards, civic freedoms, credible voter registration, participation by refugees and internally displaced people, and impartial mechanisms for resolving electoral disputes. International support should advance these safeguards rather than confer legitimacy on their removal, it said. The commission called on the General Assembly, the African Union, IGAD and the United Nations to work together to restore inclusive political dialogue, protect civilians, sustain humanitarian assistance and advance accountability. “South Sudan’s people cannot afford another cycle of warnings followed by inaction. Member States and regional partners must act together, with urgency and determination, to keep the path to sustainable peace open,” Sooka said, warning that the opportunity to prevent wider atrocities was narrowing. The commission’s independent members are in New York from October 26 to 30 to engage with member states, regional partners, civil society and other stakeholders on matters related to South Sudan. The Commission on Human Rights in South Sudan is an independent body mandated by the UN Human Rights Council. It was first established in March 2016 and has been renewed annually since. Its commissioners are appointed by the president of the UN Human Rights Council, are not UN staff and do not receive salaries for their work. They are supported by a secretariat based in Juba. The post UN commission warns of ‘constitutional coup’ in South Sudan appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: The data center boom has an upside: innovation for the US grid
body:
The AI boom has led to a gargantuan surge in energy demand across the country. Critics say this upswell in connections is enacting a stress test on America’s aging grid infrastructure. Worries abound that, in the short term, the energy crunch could lead to surging electrical bills and, in the long term, may eventually lead to outages or other technical problems.
At TechCrunch Disrupt earlier this month, industry insiders tempered much of this criticism with optimism about how the flood of new energy connections could actually be opening the door for grid modernization. Apoorv Bhargava, founder and CEO of WeaveGrid, Tim Heidel, CEO of Veir, and Kristin Eberhard, VP of policy at Rewiring America, said that though the grid faces new challenges, there are also plenty of new opportunities as well.
“It’s a very different electric grid, right?” said Bhargava. “We’re dealing with a ton of new variables, including renewable energy. We’re dealing with a ton of new load in the form of electric vehicles and data centers and heat pumps, and the ability to manage and orchestrate is fundamentally what utilities are now grappling with.”
While all of those new connections are driving an ever larger amount of stress to the grid, Bhargava’s company hopes to provide the kind of load orchestration and management that helps utilities maximize the potential of the current system. WeaveGrid’s software can help organizations efficiently deploy energy while also optimizing connections to reduce utility payers’ bills, the founder said.
Heidel, on the other hand, runs a company that is working to build out and expand the physical infrastructure of the grid, while also making it run much more efficiently. Veir sells superconductive power lines that promise to transfer energy at a much more efficient rate than traditional ones. Veir’s cables can carry power five times farther than traditional cables while also requiring 20 times less space, the company has said . Earlier this month the startup raised $110 million in a Series C funding round.
“The scale of the investment in AI infrastructure is driving a tremendous amount of innovation,” said Heidel. “There’s a ton of new technologies that are coming off the shelves and starting to get to scale that, pulled together, can actually really make sure that data centers are the best community neighbors and citizens they can possibly be.”
He added: “I think that we really need to look at ways that we can really adopt all of that as fast as possible to ease this next stage of growth.”
Eberhard, whose organization advocates for household electrification , also said that while the surge in data center energy demand has spurred a new urgency to the modernization cause, it has also created an environment where industries are ready to try new things.
“I feel like this era of AI and load growth is a very improv era,” Eberhard said. “There’s a lot of yes-and-ing going on. So yes, we need more transmission lines. Yes, we need more centralized power plants, and we also need to make sure that we’re taking advantage of all this other stuff that we had previously been leaving on the table when we didn’t have this urgency of the AI demand.”

title: Navantia launches Spanish Navy’s second F110 frigate four months ahead of schedule
body: The frigate entered the water with installation and assembly work substantially further advanced than is usual at launch, according to Navantia. The company followed the same approach with the first vessel, Bonifaz, which is undergoing systems installation and start-up before sea trials scheduled for 2027. Work is progressing on four ships in the series, with five blocks of the third frigate, F113, already on the slipway. Initial construction of F114 is under way at Ferrol’s new Digital Block Factory. The F110 frigates are designed to counter air, surface and submarine threats, operate alongside other naval units and support civilian authorities in maritime security missions. Their design also allows additional capabilities to be incorporated without fundamentally redesigning the platform. Digital technology is central to the programme’s approach to operations and maintenance. A digital twin, developed by Navantia with the Spanish Navy and the Directorate-General for Armament and Materiel, will provide a virtual replica of the vessel to support decisions using data from onboard sensors. The system draws on the Internet of Things, cloud computing and machine learning to help optimise operation and maintenance. It is complemented by the Integrated Services System, developed with the navy and the University of Vigo, which connects sensors installed in the ship’s lighting infrastructure. Navantia said the digital twin and sensor network would help improve safety, reduce crew requirements and incorporate unmanned vehicles into operations. Its SCOMBA combat system will process information from sensors, radars and weapons in real time. An integrated mast is designed to optimise use of the electromagnetic spectrum and reduce the frigate’s radar signature. Navantia is also supplying the Integrated Platform Control System, engines and other equipment manufactured at its facilities in the Bay of Cádiz and Cartagena. Spanish suppliers account for 65% of the programme’s content, alongside technology provided by international partners. Navantia said the programme involves approximately 500 companies across Spain and supports around 9,000 jobs over more than a decade. “The frigate ‘Roger de Lauria’, like its predecessor ‘Bonifaz’, faithfully reflects Spain’s commitment to innovation and technological sovereignty,” said Admiral Antonio Piñeiro, Chief of Staff of the Spanish Navy. “Each vessel in this series creates highly skilled jobs, promotes R&D&I and strengthens the Spanish naval industry’s international leadership.”

title: Here’s why the iPhone Duo’s hinge could be cracking the screen
body:
Within hours of the iPhone Duo launch last Friday, people reported that the inner screen on some brand new foldable phones was already broken. The issue was similar across many photos shared on social media: some kind of issue or crack would appear in the middle of the screen above the hinge, with lines appearing on the right side of the display. On Monday, Apple acknowledged an “issue” and said it’s replacing damaged units, without going into much detail about how many broken phones have been reported so far.
So what’s actually going on?
Shahram Mokhtari, the lead teardown technician at iFixit, has actually taken apart the iPhone Duo and has a pretty good idea about the potential cause, telling The Verge that it’s due to an issue along the hinge, where a series of gears, springs, and joints work together to let the device close flat, while also trying to avoid creating a deeper crease by giving that screen space to bend more gently inside while it’s closed.
[Image: The iPhone Duo’s hinge. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/iPhone-Duo_223b.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
At the troublesome spot, it appears that the flexible inner screen is pushing up against a part of the hinge. That inner screen is already “extremely sensitive,” he says — if you took a pick or a sharp tool and poked at the edges of the screen, “you’re going to break that screen.” If you look at the pictures of damaged Duos on social media, there’s often a black spot where the damage is focused on the display, and that’s where the metal is hitting the screen, Mokhtari says.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/iphone-duo-demo-v0-99e59a9by7xh1.jpeg.webp?quality=90&strip=all]
You can see a visual representation of what Mokhtari is talking about in iFixit’s written and video Duo teardowns, which reveal where the hinge transitions, as the center hinge support makes space for a crossing flex cable, creating several edges that could ultimately be the culprit. The damage iFixit has been seeing is at a point where the center support bar might not always drop down far enough while the screen folds, possibly creating a stress “hot spot” between the flat bar and the bent screen inside a closed iPhone Duo.
[Media: https://youtu.be/WOVIjFnivJA?si=-7pDu5QBnjn2IWVK&t=846]
At least one user with a broken Duo screen said they “felt something around the internal hinge” while showing it to a friend, kept opening it, and heard an “audible crack,” with the screen breaking. YouTuber CuriousHagi, who covered a Duo with dirt as part of a strenuous durability test, captured something similar on video, and the screen break appears in a similar spot. In a teardown video, CuriousHagi found that a part of the hinge that connects to the central bar had snapped.
[Media: https://youtu.be/wtP7Q9Io90I?si=xOyzakiNb5gU4Qe1&t=67]
Apple says the issue affects a “small number” of Duo units, and Mokhtari says that “In terms of numbers, we don’t know. Apple definitely has all the data here. And I suspect they know more than they’re telling us as well.” But he notes that because foldable screens are so delicate, a “certain number” of them will fail, as will a number of the hinges because they’re also “extremely complicated and delicate.” And while Apple isn’t recalling the Duos, “If three months from now, we’re still seeing the same kind of failure, then it’s a more widespread problem, and that might lead to a recall,” Mokhtari says.
Mokhtari points out that since this is the first generation of the iPhone Duo, it’s the first time Apple’s engineers are getting data on the hinge, and he says that “I guarantee you” Apple will redesign what’s at fault here for its next-generation foldable. He also notes that, generally speaking, “the phones do seem to be in people’s hands and people are using them, and they’re not running into any issues whatsoever.”

title: Peskov clarifies ceasefire zone extending beyond Alyoshki
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. The ceasefire arrangement around the city of Alyoshki in the Kherson Region was agreed upon from the outset, Russian Presidential Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said in response to a TASS question.
He was commenting on reports concerning a statement by US First Lady Melania Trump that the ceasefire zone had been expanded beyond the city of Alyoshki.
"Well, this has been discussed [before]. People have been talking about it for two days now," Peskov said. When asked whether the original agreement covered an area larger than the city of Alyoshki itself, he replied, "Of course. Read all the statements [on Alyoshki] carefully," the Kremlin spokesman stressed.
On October 23, the White House announced that Russia and Ukraine, with the assistance of Melania Trump, had reached an agreement on a ceasefire in the city of Alyoshki in the Kherson Region starting October 29. The two countries agreed to halt all hostilities in Alyoshki to facilitate the delivery of humanitarian aid and prepare for the evacuation of civilians through a designated safe corridor.

title: Man City players can block out ‘noise’ of away fans – Maresca
body: Manchester City suffered their first Premier League defeat of the season at a boisterous Aston Villa on Saturday, amid persistent reminders of their financial charges. “You know what you are,” echoed around Villa Park, with the chant including the word “cheating” after City’s guilty verdict over breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules. While it has been business as usual around the club as they await any sanctions and the outcome of their appeal, midfielder Elliot Anderson seemed to let the mask slip when asked whether his side would face a hostile Villa crowd. “Yes, probably,” the England international told TNT Sports prior to the game. “Everywhere we go we get it.” Liverpool fans made their feelings known during City’s trip to Anfield, while the Midlands visit was just City’s second away game since the independent commission announced its decision. Those in the travelling party have been given a clear flavour of what lies ahead for the rest of the season and, with players openly speaking about taking flak, the antagonism seems hard to block out. But manager Enzo Maresca remained steadfast in his belief that the two recent away performances showed the players will not be affected by recent events. “We played Liverpool away, Villa away, and the players showed that they don’t care about noise,” Maresca told BBC Sport. “They play the game, they are focused on the game and are doing the right things. “We are focused on our job and the players are focused on what they can do on the pitch. I think at Liverpool and Villa away, they showed they can focus on what they can control. “We don’t give too much attention to what we can find when we go away; we just focus on how we can try to do our best and try to win games.” Defender Marc Guehi said last week it can be “very easy to listen to the noise” and to be “affected by everything going on”, but everyone is “just focusing on the football”. The centre-back, though, found things tricky on the field against Villa, giving away the ball for the opening goal and receiving a yellow card for hauling down goalscorer Nicolas Jackson before being taken off at half-time. Maresca said he was “completely happy” with Guehi, whom he described as a “top guy”, and that when he or goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma make mistakes, it is “recognised”. The City faithful have countered the hostile atmosphere with their own self-deprecating “gallows humour”, hitting back at chants with “we know what we are” and “City’s going down with a billion in the bank”. Back-to-back home games against Brighton , in the Carabao Cup and Premier League, should provide some respite this week. Maresca’s men then head to RB Leipzig in the Champions League before travelling to Nottingham Forest in the league on 7 November. Supporters at the City Ground know all about being on the receiving end of Premier League sanctions, after being docked four points in 2024 for breaching financial rules. Forest fans, though, are unlikely to show much sympathy for City’s situation.

title: Republicans wanted Rubio on the stump. Trump coaxed him there.
body: Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday came as close to the campaign trail as he’s been all year. And even then, he tried to stay just offshore. Rubio appeared with President Donald Trump in Corpus Christi, Texas, as he rallied alongside an oil tanker carrying Venezuelan crude. The visit helped spotlight a proud White House accomplishment — toppling the Venezuelan dictator Nicolás Maduro and opening the country’s energy supply — in a political battleground state. The unexpected nature of Rubio’s presence, after the president coaxed him up on stage during the rally, is likely enough to shield the nation’s top diplomat from allegations that he is interfering in the midterm campaign. The former Florida senator has kept a careful distance from partisan politics, even as colleagues like Attorney General Todd Blanche have defied longstanding norms against some administration officials engaging in electioneering. “It's an honor to work for the greatest country in the world, for the greatest president in the history of the United States of America,” Rubio said in brief remarks from the stage. “We love you, Texas.” A White House official, who like others in this article was granted anonymity to share details of the trip, said that Rubio was backstage during the rally when the president brought him up and that he was only there in his capacity as national security adviser, not to stump ahead of the midterms. While Rubio, who was not expected to speak at the event, has maintained the tradition of secretaries of State not campaigning, Republicans have been clamoring for the potential 2028 presidential hopeful to do so, seeing him as one of the party’s strongest messengers in a bruising midterm cycle in which they have been desperate for any additional help. One GOP official in a state with a key Senate race, granted anonymity to share private conversations, said that they asked for Rubio to attend a recent political event but were told the secretary of State wasn't doing political events given his role as chief diplomatic officer. “Rubio is Trump’s best asset, and they know they are in a dog fight to win in Texas,” said Bill Cortese, a GOP operative who has advised Rep. Elise Stefanik (R-N.Y.). Even if Rubio had not come up on stage, “news of Rubio simply being in the state could potentially boost the GOP’s chances in places that they need it.” Plus, the secretary of State had another good reason for being there: Rubio was one of the central architects of the administration’s Venezuela strategy and has been a leading figure in managing the country’s political transition and economic arrangements with the U.S. in the wake of Maduro’s ouster. “It’s his win and his deal,” a Trump administration official added about Rubio and the Venezuela link. Asked why Rubio accompanied Trump on the Texas trip, the White House referred to one of Trump’s Truth Social posts from August in which he credited Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth for negotiating the oil deal with Venezuela. A State Department spokesperson noted Rubio’s role as national security adviser and said that he “needs time with the president on all kinds of issues. The president will be on the go, so being on the plane with him gives him a chance to talk to him about these items.” The secretary of State notably skipped the Republican National Committee’s midterm convention in Dallas last month, opting instead to go on a diplomatic trip to Colombia. “Marco loves campaigns and politics and he cares desperately about making sure that the House and Senate remain in Republican hands, but I think he also realizes that part of being secretary of State is you don’t engage in overt political activity,” said a person close to Rubio. In Trump’s first term, Secretary of State Mike Pompeo broke with tradition and made a handful of public appearances that directly or indirectly appeared campaign related, including delivering remarks to the Republican National Convention in 2020. On a practical level, most secretaries of State travel overseas so much that it’s hard to spare time for campaigns. But Rubio travels more infrequently than his predecessors, in part because of his national security adviser role, which keeps him at the White House. And Rubio also has a more nontraditional role even as secretary of State, focusing most of his energy on Latin America while the president’s special envoys, including Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, have handled negotiations to try to end the wars in Iran, Ukraine and Gaza. Yet the Texas visit — in which Trump sought to link one of his signature foreign policy accomplishments with efforts to reduce prices — came as a relief to the Republicans who believe Rubio is one of the party’s most trusted messengers on the economy and have for months wanted to see him on the trail. Results from The POLITICO Poll suggest Rubio can be a useful surrogate on the campaign trail. Across three polls this month, Republican midterm voters consistently selected Rubio as their third-highest choice to hit the campaign trail to help their party, behind Trump and Vice President JD Vance but ahead of Texas Sen. Ted Cruz, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and others. Support for Rubio on the campaign trail is also fairly steady across Trump’s 2024 coalition, with only an 8-point gap between the MAGA base (31%) and non-MAGA Trump voters (23%) saying the secretary of State would help Republicans if he campaigned. Meanwhile, MAGA loyalists were significantly more likely than non-MAGA Trump voters to support Trump and Vance hitting the trail. Notably, Rubio also generates less negative backlash than other figures. Democrats widely support the impeachment of Trump, Vance, Kennedy and others. But support for impeaching Rubio is lower than the other figures, pushing overall public opinion against impeachment. “Marco Rubio is Republicans’ most valuable asset in this difficult environment. While he has broad support from the MAGA base, he also appeals to centrist voters and obviously to critical Hispanic voters. It makes sense that they would find a way to activate him,” said former Florida Rep. Carlos Curbelo. Kimberly Leonard, Alex Gangitano and Seb Wride, chief pollster at PF Global, contributed to this report.

title: Eisenkot declares victory as bloc takes lead over Netanyahu's, despite election deadlock
body: Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot on Tuesday night issued a statement at press time declaring victory, saying the preliminary voting results could give him the first right to form a government to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.He had not yet spoken publicly about his plans, with coordination taking place behind the scenes with the leaders of the other parties in his bloc.How did Eisenkot perform in initial exit polls?Data from the Central Election Committee (CEC) showed his opposition bloc at 49 seats. Eisenkot's party, Yashar, is projected to enter the Knesset with 22 seats, according to the CEC. Channel 12 television exit polls showed his political bloc trailing the Netanyahu bloc 49-52, while Channels 11 and 13 projected the opposition bloc tying Netanyahu's bloc at 51 seats each. Exit polls from Channels 11, 12, and 13 projected Eisenkot's Yashar party to win 21-22 seats.Channel 13's television exit polls projected Netanyahu's bloc would tie with the opposition bloc, with both parties earning 51 seats.Eisenkot headquarters erupted into cheers when they heard the initial results of the balance of the blocs, even as there were a few seconds of nervousness when they saw that Netanyahu had the largest party.תוצאות המדגם הראשוניות מצביעות על אי אמון מוחלט בנתניהו וממשלת השבעה באוקטובר, של הרוב הציוני ושל רוב אזרחי ישראל. אם אלו התוצאות הסופיות זהו נצחון לרוב הממלכתי-ציוני בישראל. אפעל באופן מיידי למימוש הכרעת העם, להחלפת ממשלת נתניהו ולהקמת ממשלת גיוס ציונית, בהקדם האפשרי.— Gadi Eisenkot - גדי איזנקוט (@gadi_eisenkot) October 27, 2026In Israel's political system, the largest bloc usually gets the first right to try to form a government, and also can likely take control over the Knesset pending formation of a government.However, Eisenkot's slow-walking a public appearance showed the sensitivity of the challenges ahead of him, including the need to convince his coalition partners, most notably Avigdor Liberman, to accept a government or minority support from Israeli-Arab parties, which Liberman had refused during the campaign.Some commentators said Liberman might reconsider due to the high voter turnout, but the Yisrael Beytenu party leader is notoriously determined to stick to certain principles.Eisenkot faces difficulty forming government as Arab parties soarEarlier Tuesday, Eisenkot was hoping to have an even larger victory, but even then, due to the size of the Israeli-Arab parties, which are not specifically affiliated with a bloc, Eisenkot was not expected to be able to easily form the next government even if he won more votes than the Netanyahu right-wing bloc.Eisenkot's campaign on Tuesday started early in the morning at Ofakim and Nir Oz of the Gaza Strip corridor, calling attention to the failures of the past government in preventing Hamas's October 7 invasion.Eisenkot then traveled further north to Ashdod, with other stops along the way, before he was due to vote in Herzliya at 1:45 p.m. and eventually make it to his election-night headquarters at the National Sports Complex in Tel Aviv.Already by late morning, Yashar had filed complaints with the Israeli Election Commission complaining of alleged systematic vandalism and destruction of ballots carrying the parties' names at various voting sites.Eisenkot's largest support comes from voters who blame Netanyahu for October 7 or who blame him and his bloc for failing to draft the haredi sector into the IDF even after over 1,000 Israeli soldiers died in recent years.Yashar officials react to exit pollsEisenkot said the public had voted for change and against Benjamin Netanyahu continuing as prime minister, as he pledged to work to form a government committed to military service.“We made history,” Eisenkot said in a speech at the party's headquarters in Tel Aviv following the publication of exit polls. “We made history. This morning, the people of Israel went to a referendum on the leadership that would lead Israel in the coming years. Tonight, we received an answer: The public has decided in favor of change. The coalition of failures has lost the people's trust, and the Israeli public voted against Netanyahu continuing to serve as prime minister.” Eisenkot said the “era of draft evasion, failure, and lies” was over, adding that the results should be seen as a victory for the entire country rather than one political camp over another.He also addressed the heads of Israel's security establishment, describing Netanyahu as a caretaker prime minister “without a mandate or public trust.” Eisenkot urged security officials to serve the state and the interests of Israeli citizens, telling them they had his backing against any attempt to challenge them.“Netanyahu, do not dare use Israel's security for your political needs,” Eisenkot said.

title: Netanyahu or Eisenkot? Israel's election leaves Herzog with an impossible choice - comment
body: As the first exit polls emerged on Tuesday night, showing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud as the largest party but Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc holding more seats overall, one wonders what must be going through President Isaac Herzog's mind.After all, Herzog will soon have to decide which of the two men gets the first chance to form Israel's next government, a decision that could prove particularly complicated given the apparent divisions emerging from the ballot box.Initial projections from Kan and Channel 13 gave Likud 25 seats, compared with 23 for Eisenkot's Yashar party, while placing the opposition bloc on 53 seats against Netanyahu's 50. Neither side, however, appears to have the 61 seats necessary to command a Knesset majority.Under Israeli law, the president must consult the Knesset factions before deciding who gets the task of forming a government. Netanyahu will undoubtedly point to Likud's position as the largest individual party, while Eisenkot has an equally compelling argument in the game of parliamentary arithmetic, pointing to his larger bloc and the bigger chance of forming a government - particularly if the parties opposed to Netanyahu can agree on a common candidate.The question of how Eisenkot might assemble a coalition remains unanswered. Few of the parties have declared a willingness to sit with the Arab parties, who are projected to receive a record-high 18 mandates, except for Yair Golan's Democrats. Herzog knows how this game works well, having led the Labor Party and served as opposition leader before assuming the presidency in 2021. He will also be very aware of the political tensions that have characterized much of his presidency, and the criticism that could follow whichever decision he ultimately makes. We should remember these are only exit polls, and the final results may still change, particularly with several smaller parties hovering around the electoral threshold. Nevertheless, the president may soon face the most difficult decision of his tenure, as two political leaders with competing claims to the premiership seek his approval to begin assembling Israel's next government.Will he go with the long-time leader of Israel, the perceived protector who has led Israel in a multi-front war against its enemies? Or against the potential leader of the largest bloc, at a time when millions of Israelis have taken to the polls and demanded change. Whichever candidate Herzog eventually chooses, millions of Israelis will almost certainly be convinced the other should have had the first opportunity.

title: Arsenal loses to 4th-tier Fleetwood on penalties in English League Cup stunner
body: Fleetwood Town pulled off one of the biggest upsets in Carabao Cup history, beating Premier League champions Arsenal in an astounding penalty shootout to reach the quarter-finals. Mikel Arteta’s side were shell-shocked when Aaron Loupalo-Bi gave the hosts, ranked 84 places below the Gunners in the football pyramid, an unexpected lead in the 21st minute. Viktor Gyokeres pulled the visitors level after the break, but a wasteful Arsenal side could not put the game to bed, and they were reduced to 10 men in the 86th minute when teenage starlet Max Dowman kicked out after a hefty tackle by Harrison Neal. Jay Lynch made two sublime saves to stop Ben White and Martin Odegaard right at the death, sending the game to a penalty shootout. And the Fleetwood goalkeeper pulled off more heroics, stopping Bruno Guimaraes’ spot kick, before Conor Haughey sparked scenes of ecstasy at Highbury Stadium by converting the winning penalty. Fans flooded onto the pitch, players swore in their post-match interviews, while manager Matt Lawlor was reduced to tears during the emphatic celebrations. Fleetwood will learn their quarter-final opponents when the draw takes place after Chelsea’s game against Liverpool on Wednesday. Arsenal analysis: Wasteful Premier League champions left dumbstruck Arsenal were welcomed by flames and fireworks, but the game had barely got going before referee Michael Salisbury stopped play after spotting a drone flying above Highbury Stadium. The match restarted eight minutes later, after the players were briefly instructed to leave the pitch, and Arsenal were soon caught off guard when Loupalo-Bi rolled Marli Salmon and slotted past Illan Meslier. Despite countless chances and dominating possession, Arteta’s side trailed at the break, much to the delight of the raucous home crowd. But the Fleetwood’s elation did not last long as Gyokeres scrambled in the six-yard box to poke home an equaliser four minutes into the second half. Introduced at half-time, captain Martin Odegaard injected urgency into the team, but they still lacked a clinical edge, with only one goal to show for 26 shots and 59 touches inside the Fleetwood box. Their evening in the north west went from bad to worse when 16-year-old Dowman saw red after kicking out at Neal, then faced Arteta’s wrath as he headed down the tunnel. Meslier, making his debut for the Gunners, failed to get close to any of the Cod Army’s penalty kicks, while a lacklustre strike from Guimaraes sealed the Gunners’ fate. Fleetwood analysis: League Two minnows defy the odds With Fleetwood languishing in 18th in the English fourth division, Arteta made nine changes from Saturday’s win over Everton – opting for a blend of youthful talent and Premier League non-starters. Making just his second senior appearance for Arsenal, Salmon lacked the physicality to hold off Loupalo-Bi before the Fulham loanee jabbed the ball through Meslier’s legs, and the 17-year-old defender was hauled off at half-time. Fleetwood’s defenders, meanwhile, gave everything to keep Arsenal at bay, with Rhys Bennett, Conor Haughey and Shaun Rooney all throwing themselves in front of every shot as they weathered wave upon wave of relentless pressure. The home fans – perhaps expecting Arsenal to open the floodgates at some stage – took delight in their side’s ability to hold on for so long , and chants of “champions of England, you’re having a laugh” echoed around Highbury Stadium. Ultimately, it came down to conviction. Ronan Coughlan, Neal, Will Davies, Andy Cannon and Haughey each slammed their penalties emphatically past Meslier, showing a fearlessness that stood in stark contrast to Arsenal’s timid overall performance.

title: Vassilios Tsiavaliaris was the first fallen Soldier of the 1940 Greco-Italian War
body: Vassilios Tsiavaliaris was the first Greek soldier to fall in the Greco-Italian War. Italian military forces launched their first attack at about 5:00 AM on October 28, 1940. They struck at the Greek-Albanian border in the Pindos Mountains. He was 28 years old then. He came from a village near Trikala. Who was Vassilios Tsiavaliaris? Vassilios Tsiavaliaris was a 28-year-old Greek soldier. When the attack came, he stood guard inside the 21st outpost on Golio height. The outpost lay next to the village of Pyrsogianni. His life began in 1912 in the village of Pialeia, in Trikala. The village lies at the foot of Mount Koziakas. His parents were Giannis and Agoro. He was the fourth of their five children. Later, he completed his military service with the 5th Infantry Regiment in 1933–1934. As tension with Italy grew, the army recalled him on 22 July 1940. Then, in early September 1940, he took up a front-line post near Eptachori. There, he served in the Pindus Detachment under Colonel Konstantinos Davakis. Men from Trikala and Karditsa made up most of this unit. The first Greek soldier killed on 28 October 1940 The attacking force far outnumbered the Greek soldiers. Sadly, it overran them. Vassilios Tsiavaliaris fell before dawn, struck by mortar fire. Later, a fellow villager, Christos Apostolou Giannios, described his death. The shell hit him in the forehead, above the eye. He was holding a light machine gun when it struck. Tsiavaliaris was the father of three children. His children were George, Nikos and a daughter, Alexandra. George Papavassiliou is a school counsellor in Trikala, the region where the soldier came from. According to him, the soldier’s last words before he died were: “My children! My children will be lost…” (in Greek, «πάνε τα παιδούλια μου»). How Pialeia remembers him A marble plaque honours Vassilios Tsiavaliaris as “the hero who first fell for the homeland”. It gives the time as 5 a.m. on 28 October 1940. It also names the place: the Greek-Albanian border. However, the plaque spells his surname “Tsavaliaris”. This variant also appears in English. Later, in 2000, the University of Athens erected a statue of him in Pialeia. Every year, the village also holds a memorial event in his honour. This event is the “Tsiavaliareia”, as Kathimerini reported . OXI Day Story Shortly after 3:00 a.m. on October 28, 1940, the Italian ambassador reached the Greek prime minister’s residence. His name was Emanuele Grazzi. He demanded that Greece let Italian forces occupy “strategic locations” in the country. In effect, he was asking for Greece’s surrender. However, Prime Minister Ioannis Metaxas refused. Greeks remember his answer as one single word — Oxi — No. In fact, he replied in French: “Alors, c’est la guerre” (“Then it is war”). A few hours later, Italian forces invaded Greece. They expected that it would quickly fall. Instead, the Greek resistance forced Hitler to change his plans. News of Greece’s victory flooded the radio airwaves. It also covered the front pages of newspapers around the globe. A grateful world celebrated. After all, no one expected such a small nation to derail the seemingly unstoppable Axis forces. Churchill, Roosevelt and Greek bravery People often repeat many quotations by various leaders on OXI Day . This quote about Greek bravery during WWII is probably the most famous of the lot. Many sources also credit it to Winston Churchill: “Hence, we will not say that Greeks fight like heroes, but that heroes fight like Greeks!” Less circulated, however, is the eloquent praise from American President Franklin Delano Roosevelt. He bestowed it upon Greece and her people. Roosevelt’s letter of 29 October 1942 Here is the full text of Roosevelt’s “ Letter Praising the Heroism of the Greeks ”. It went to the Greek Ambassador in Washington, Cimon P. Diamantopoulos. Roosevelt sent it on October 29, 1942: My dear Mr. Ambassador: On the early morning of October 28, 1940, the Fascist aggressors handed an ultimatum to Greece. The challenge was hurled back without a moment’s hesitation. This was what might have been expected from a gallant and courageous people devoted to their homeland. You commemorate tonight the second anniversary of the beginning of the total resistance of the Greek people to totalitarian warfare. More significant, even, than the initial reply to the challenge is the fact that Greece has continued to fight, with every means at its command. When the Greek mainland was overrun, the resistance was carried on from the islands. When the islands fell, resistance continued from Africa, from the seas, from anywhere the aggressor could be met. To those who prefer to compromise, to follow a course of expediency, or to appease, or to count the cost, I say that Greece has set the example which every one of us must follow until the despoilers of freedom everywhere have been brought to their just doom. Very sincerely yours, Franklin D. title: Captain Xhaka allowed to play for Switzerland again
body: Granit Xhaka and Breel Embolo will both be allowed to play for Switzerland again next month following an investigation into forged Covid-19 vaccination certificates obtained by the pair. Switzerland captain Xhaka missed Nations League matches against Scotland, North Macedonia and Slovenia during the October international break after admitting he acquired a fake certificate that let him travel and compete in 2022. Striker Embolo, 29, was also dropped from the Switzerland squad in September for the same reason. The Swiss Football Association (SFV) confirmed on Tuesday that 34-year-old Sunderland midfielder Xhaka and Embolo will both be available for manager Murat Yakin to include in November’s fixtures against Slovenia and Scotland. National team director Pierluigi Tami said: “We considered this from various perspectives. The specific circumstances of both cases, the concluded legal proceedings, and the sporting consequences already implemented all factored into the decision. “We are convinced that a return to the national team in November is responsible and the right thing to do.” Both Xhaka and Embolo were fined 150,000 Swiss francs (£136,000) , suspended for two years provided no further offences are committed. Xhaka, who took responsibility for his actions, has not been stripped of the captaincy. However, the SFV said in its statement that the team’s coach, Yakin, will make the final decision on the captaincy and announce his squad on 5 November. Switzerland are top of Group E heading into their final two Nations League fixtures against Slovenia and Scotland on 13 and 16 November.

title: Israel Election: Four Scenarios as Opposition Edges Netanyahu but Falls Short of Majority
body:
Israelis went to the polls in the highest turnout for decades on Tuesday, with initial exit polls showing a slight edge but no majority for the opposition, meaning the next government will be formed by whoever can cobble together a coalition.
The country’s main pollsters projected the opposition bloc, led by ex-army chief Gadi Eisenkot, to win 52 or 53 seats, and Netanyahu’s bloc to win 50.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Israeli Arab lists made strong gains, with exit polls showing them winning 17 or 18 seats between them.
The parties will immediately begin negotiations to try to reach a 61-seat majority in the 120-member Knesset, but the path forward is far from clear.
President Isaac Herzog will name a candidate who has the best chance to form a government – not necessarily the party with the most seats, which the initial exit polls showed to be Netanyahu’s Likud.
The Arab Israeli parties, particularly Raam, have voiced openness to working with Eisenkot’s bloc, but the camp has kept them at arm’s length, perceiving their support as a liability during the campaign.
For Netanyahu’s bloc, however, there is no obvious place to pick up more seats after some smaller right-wing parties failed to meet the vote threshold for entering parliament.
Coalition negotiations can be arduous, with parties insisting on parochial interests, and can produce unstable governments.
Following the previous election in November 2022, it took Benjamin Netanyahu 58 days to form his government.
If no bloc manages to secure 61 seats, a candidate could attempt to govern without a majority but rather through support on an ad hoc basis from other lawmakers.
In this scenario, lawmakers from the Arab Israeli parties -- whose community makes up 20 percent of the population and generally identifies as Palestinian -- could play a critical role.
Raam, led by Mansour Abbas, has been a kingmaker in the past, having been the first Arab party to join an Israeli government in a short-lived 2021-2022 coalition led by Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid.
Another Arab movement, the Joint List, has said it would be unlikely to join a coalition government outright, but has offered to provide a “safety net” for any one that ousts Netanyahu from power.
Political commentator Tal Elovitz said especially high Arab turnout “indicates a strong desire for partnership”.
Eisenkot has not publicly even entertained the possibility, and Netanyahu in his campaign relentlessly told Jewish voters that a vote for the opposition could bring Arabs into government.
“Bottom line, at the moment it appears there is a possibility of forming a minority government headed by Eisenkot, but this could still shift depending on the final results,” Elovitz said.
Considering Israel’s extreme polarization, a national unity government would appear fanciful, but it could theoretically create a less extreme government.
Israeli commentators have often mused on the possibility of a national unity government in which Netanyahu would jettison his provocative far-right allies as well as ultra-Orthodox parties and team up with Eisenkot, who shares Netanyahu’s views on many security issues.
Such a grand coalition would also exclude Arab parties.
A poll published on October 16 found that 55 percent of Israelis would prefer a national unity government over new elections if the vote did not produce a clear majority.
This scenario has a recent precedent. In 2020, Netanyahu and Benny Gantz, like Eisenkot a retired general appealing to the center, reached a power-sharing agreement after three elections in less than a year.
The agreement stipulated a rotation of the prime ministership, but the partnership fell apart after a year, triggering another election.
A unity government in the present situation would face strong opposition from both sides, particularly the opposition bloc, which has built its campaign around ousting Netanyahu, casting him as unfit to lead.
If no candidate manages to form a government, Israel will have to return to the polls.
The country held four elections between April 2019 and March 2021 due to the inability of politicians to forge a lasting coalition.
The candidate designated by the president will, in principle, have 28 days to form a coalition, with a possible 14-day extension, although there are other procedural ways to prevent an immediate calling of new elections.

title: Feast Day of the Protection of the Theotokos, Agia Skepi
body: On October 28, the Greek Orthodox Church commemorates the Feast Day of the Protection of the Theotokos. She is the Mother of God and Ever-Virgin Mary. In Greece, Agia Skepi on Oxi Day is a double celebration. On that day, the Church honours the Holy Protection of the Theotokos. At the same time, the nation marks its historic “No” of 1940. The vision of Saint Andrew at Vlachernae The feast of the Holy Protection of the Mother of God comes from a vision of the holy Father Andrew. He saw it during a Vigil in the Church of Vlachernae in Constantinople. This church held several relics of the Mother of God. They included her veil and part of her Cincture (Sash) . At the Fourth Hour of the night, while deep in prayer, the Saint lifted up his eyes to heaven. Then he beheld the Holy Mother of God watching over the faithful. She was covering them with her holy Veil. Epiphanius, the disciple of Saint Andrew, also proved worthy to see this wonder (miracle). In turn, he confirmed the truth of the vision. The Veil above the worshippers The Saint then hastened to the altar. There he opened the coffer containing the Precious Veil of the Queen of the world. Standing in front of the Royal Doors, he then extended it above the worshippers. Upheld by an invisible power, the holy Veil hung in the air. In fact, it was large enough to cover the entire congregation. Then, amid a sheltering burst of Light, the Mother of God went up into Heaven and out of sight. She left the Christian faithful the Holy Veil as a pledge of Her loving protection. Many times the Mother of God gave clear evidence of her protection of the Imperial City. She did the same, by analogy, for the entire Holy Church of Christ, the New Jerusalem. Indeed, everywhere and at every moment, the Sovereign Lady of the world casts her Veil mystically over Christians. She prays and intercedes with her Son and Lord for the salvation of the world. The Mother of God, Protectress of the faithful The Holy Orthodox Church has always glorified the Most Holy Mother of God. It honours her as the Protectress and Defender of the Christian people. Through her intercessions (prayers), the Church entreats God’s loving-kindness towards us sinners. Indeed, times without number, she has clearly shown her aid. Individuals and whole peoples have received it, both in peace and in war. It has reached monastic deserts and crowded cities alike. “…She was clad in gold-encrusted purple and shone with an unspeakable radiance, surrounded by the Holy Apostles, Saints, Martyrs, and holy virgins. Seeing the vision, Saint Andrew gestured towards it and asked Epiphanius, ‘Do you see how the Queen and Lady of all is praying for the whole world?’ Epiphanius replied, ‘Yes, Father; I see it and stand in dread.’” Because of this wonderful miracle of the Theotokos, we keep a yearly feast of gratitude. Greeks celebrate it as Agia Skepi on Oxi Day. We implore our Lady never to cease sheltering us and the world in her mighty and holy prayers. The icon of the Holy Protection The holy icon of the Holy Protection depicts the feast. The Theotokos stands above the faithful Christians, draped with a veil. She holds her arms open in prayer. Angels also stand on both sides of her. In most icons, Saint Andrew and his disciple Epiphanius appear in the lower right. Saint Epiphanius wears a tunic under his cloak and seems astonished at the miraculous appearance. Saint Andrew, however, wears only a cloak. Below the Theotokos stands a figure holding an open scroll. This is Saint Romanos the Melodist, the famous hymnographer. His scroll carries the text of the Kontakion of the Nativity, in honour of the Mother of God. Saint Romanos also has his own feast on October 1st. His choir is with him, as are the Emperor Leo the Wise, the Empress and the Patriarch of Constantinople. Why Greece celebrates Agia Skepi on Oxi Day Most of the Orthodox Christian world celebrates the Holy Protection, or Agia Skepi, of the Theotokos on October 1st. This follows ancient Orthodox Tradition. Greeks, however, celebrate the Feast Day of the Agia Skepi (Holy Protection) on October 28th. They do so as a special holiday. In this way, they invite the secular government of Greece (Hellas) to honour the Mother of God. The reason is her loving protection of the Greek Nation during World War II. From Byzantium to 1952 Tradition places the vision at Vlachernae in the 10th century. This was during the reign of Emperor Leo VI the Wise (886–912). Later, the Church established the feast on October 1st to honour this great miracle. People sometimes confuse the Protection with an earlier deliverance of the city. In 626 A.D., the Avars (nomads from the Eurasian steppe) besieged Constantinople with their Persian and Slav allies. However, the miraculous intervention of the Theotokos saved the city. The Church gives thanks for that deliverance through the Akathist Hymn . The faithful chant this hymn during Great Lent. Greeks celebrated the feast on October 1st until 21st October 1952. On that date, the Holy Synod (Council) of the Church of Greece approved a joint celebration. From then on, Greece would celebrate a dual feast: the Holy Protection and the national holiday of ‘ Oxi’ (‘No’) Day . Oxi Day commemorates the day when Greece said NO to the Axis powers, fascism and nazism. The renowned Athonite hymnographer, the monk Gerasimos Mikragiannanitis, wrote the hymns for the new feast. Since then, Agia Skepi on Oxi Day has been both a church feast and a national celebration. Pokrov in the Slavic Orthodox churches Greeks keep Agia Skepi on Oxi Day. However, the Slavic Orthodox Churches still keep the feast on October 1st. They follow the Julian calendar, so on the civil calendar that date falls on October 14th. The faithful in Russia, Ukraine and Belarus especially love this feast, known as Pokrov. There, it ranks among the most important feasts of the Church year after Pascha and the Twelve Great Feasts.
