title: Eisenkot and Netanyahu have reason to celebrate, but Israel does not, yet - comment
body: If there are two clear winners from Tuesday's election, at least according to the exit polls, they are Gadi Eisenkot and Benjamin Netanyahu.The former IDF chief of staff began this campaign with his party polling in the single digits. If the projections hold, the ended it as the clear head of the bloc seeking to oust Benjamin Netanyahu.That is no small achievement, and it sends a clear message to Naftali Bennett and Avigdor Liberman: It is time to set aside their plans to force Eisenkot into a rotation agreement that would make one of them prime minister first. The opposition camp has spoken, and the voters have chosen Eisenkot. The others need to respect that decision, and if the opposition is to form a government, Eisenkot should lead it.Netanyahu also pulled off an impressive win. Based on the projections, he is close to 27 seats, almost nine more than what the final polls said he would get. He couldn't increase his bloc, which is at about 50, but he led the Likud to an impressive accomplishment: ending, despite everything, as the largest party in the Knesset.But while Eisenkot and Netanyahu scored personal accomplishments, the question is whether the Israeli people have won. That will take time to know.The exit polls point to a problem that has long been known throughout the campaign: Neither camp has a decisive 61-seat majority, and neither has a clear path to forming a coalition. That leaves us with a simple but unavoidable conclusion. For Israel to form a government in the coming weeks, someone will have to break a campaign promise.It could be Eisenkot deciding to form a government with the support of Ra'am, the Arab party led by Mansour Abbas. It could be Bennett, Liberman or even Eisenkot deciding to cross the partisan line and join a government with Netanyahu.That is why the coming days will be so consequential. Because if no one is willing to compromise, Israel could find itself barreling straight toward another election. And after everything this country has endured in recent years, that would be a gamble we simply cannot afford.Another conclusion from the exit polls is worth noting: a decisive majority of Israelis oppose Netanyahu and want to see him out of office. Based on projections, approximately 70 seats went to parties, Jewish and Arab, committed to ousting Netanyahu.That does not mean all 70 support Eisenkot or that they can necessarily sit together in one government. But it does mean that Netanyahu and his coalition have lost the support of a majority of the electorate.And this brings us to another disturbing feature of this election – the Arab turnout and the results that they brought, either 17 or 18 seats. That is unprecedented, despite the campaign that the Likud led in which it warned that Arab citizens were voting in large numbers. The message was unmistakable: high Arab turnout was presented not as a celebration of Israeli democracy but as a threat to Israel's future.We have become so accustomed to this rhetoric that we barely notice it anymore. But we should.Imagine an American politician warning next week that too many Jews were turning out to vote in Michigan. People would be outraged, and rightly so. Why, then, do we accept similar rhetoric about Arab citizens in Israel?Arab Israelis are citizens of this country. They have the same right to vote as Jewish Israelis. It is one of the founding principles of the state, enshrined in the Declaration of Independence, a document this government has too often tried to cast aside.Are there legitimate reasons to debate whether Arab political parties should be included in the next government? Yes. But portraying high voter turnout among Arab citizens as a threat to Israel's future is something entirely different.The real question now is whether the politicians elected on Tuesday will be able to translate the results into a functioning government.Even if the exit polls show a decisive majority against Netanyahu, he will not simply step aside. He will hope that Eisenkot, Bennett and Liberman fail to agree on a path forward, fail to agree to sit with the Arabs, and if that happens, he will then have an opening to try to bring one of those parties into his camp.But that will not be simple. Any party considering joining Netanyahu will come with demands. It will almost certainly refuse to let him take the first turn as prime minister in a rotation agreement; it will demand a state commission of inquiry be established into the failures of October 7, and it will need a real solution to the ultra-Orthodox draft crisis that has torn Israel apart.Can Netanyahu agree to all of that? Probably notFor Eisenkot and his potential partners, time will be critical, and they will need to move fast if they want to form a government – whether with Arab parties or a minority government. Netanyahu will not sit quietly while they negotiate and he will try to recruit defectors and prevent the establishment of a coalition before it can even take shape.There is also the looming possibility of another attack against Iran, potentially right after the American midterm elections next week. A new war could give Netanyahu an opening to try to force a national unity government.In the coming days, we will find out the final results of the vote. Such a high turnout shows us just how concerned Israelis are for the future of their country.The voters have done their part. Now the politicians need to do theirs.

title: Israeli exit polls show deadlock, setback for Netanyahu
body: JERUSALEM, Israel – Israel’s wartime election appeared deadlocked on Tuesday, October 27, exit polls showed, a potential setback for veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu if the projections hold, with neither side having a clear path to power but rival Gadi Eisenkot’s larger bloc potentially giving him the first chance to form a government. The stalemate could yet work in Netanyahu’s favor, allowing the prime minister to remain in power in a caretaker capacity while parties try to forge a governing coalition. Turnout was 77.7%, Israel’s Central Elections Committee said, the highest in more than two decades and around 7 percentage points higher than in the previous election in 2022. Must Read Fastest turnout in 45 years as Israelis pass wartime judgment on Netanyahu Israel’s three major networks updated their exit polls, giving Eisenkot’s bloc a two-seat edge over Netanyahu’s Likud-led camp, at 52-50, respectively. The remaining 18 seats were allocated to unaligned Arab parties in the exit polls. But Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, has all but ruled out forming a government with them, complicating his path to a majority despite his bloc’s lead. Some Israeli media outlets, including pro-Netanyahu Channel 14, projected a far stronger showing for Netanyahu and his parties, saying they would collectively win 60 seats. Final results could take days, and Israel’s fragmented political system leaves smaller parties potential kingmakers. No single party has ever won 61 seats outright in the 120-seat Knesset, making coalitions the norm. It was the first election since the Hamas-led attacks of October 7, 2023, and the ensuing wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. Anti-Netanyahu boost While there was no clear outcome, the strength of the anti-Netanyahu opposition was evident in the exit polls. Current opposition head Yair Lapid said in a statement: “Don’t let anyone confuse you: the Netanyahu bloc has suffered a crushing defeat. This is a total collapse and the public has told them to go home.” Eisenkot, 66, a hawkish former military chief who lost a son and two nephews in the Gaza war, emerged as Netanyahu’s strongest challenger, stressing his security credentials while positioning himself as a centrist domestically. He entered politics only four years ago and joined Netanyahu’s war cabinet after the 2023 Hamas attack, but quit eight months later, criticizing the prime minister’s leadership. Eisenkot offers a break with Netanyahu’s leadership and far-right allies, but not with the hawkish security views that have hardened since the 2023 Hamas attack: He opposes Palestinian statehood and says Hamas’ military wing must be destroyed or dismantled. The headquarters of the Joint List, an alliance of several Arab parties, burst into whistles and applause when exit polls were released at the close of voting, on a historic night for turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel. “We refuse the occupation and racism, and we will remain here,” said Faten Gattas, a candidate in the Joint List, in a speech at the alliance’s headquarters in Nazareth. Candidates hope that high Arab voter participation would allow them to play a decisive role in preventing Netanyahu’s coalition – the most far-right in Israel’s history – from returning to power. A record turnout Long lines had formed outside polling stations as voters turned out in huge numbers, grappling with the trauma of Israel’s deadliest day, when Hamas killed 1,200 people and took 251 hostage, and the wars with the Palestinian militant group, Lebanon’s Hezbollah and Iran that followed. While Netanyahu was criticized for the country’s biggest security failure, he argued that he made Israel and the world safer by assassinating top leaders from those groups and Iran. The policies of Netanyahu’s right-wing coalition have been divisive at home and deepened Israel’s international isolation, but he has portrayed himself as the leader with the mettle to face down Israel’s foes. Netanyahu, 77, has served as prime minister for nearly 19 of the past 30 years and has repeatedly survived political crises. His opponents have managed to wrest the premiership from him only once since 2009, after four inconclusive elections in two years. Eighteen months later, he was back. He entered the election facing longstanding corruption charges, which he denies, and criticism over intelligence failures that allowed Hamas-led militants to carry out their attack. Netanyahu’s nationalist brand of politics is deeply entrenched, and Israel’s fragmented system makes it difficult for an array of opponents to force out his coalition of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties. Netanyahu had urged supporters to come out to vote to balance high turnout among his opponents on the left and Arab Israelis. “You all need to stream to the polls,” he said. “This is a fateful moment.” Netanyahu campaigned on an endorsement from US President Donald Trump, his ally in the war against Iran , who has said they should “finish the job.” – Rappler.com

title: Incumbent mayors, premiers losing jobs a result of Canadians not ‘getting ahead’
body:
Cities and provinces across Canada have seen political change in recent months as frustrations over affordability and quality of life has meant incumbents being shown the door.
Multiple Ontario cities said goodbye to short and long-time mayors and councillors on Monday. A few days earlier, British Columbia ousted its NDP government and premier David Eby, following the trend of incumbent losses after several B.C. mayors were voted out of office. Those changes all came in a month that started with Quebec’s CAQ government losing every seat in the provincial election.
The back-to-back changes were a result of Canadians facing continued strain over tariffs from the U.S. administration, wavering inflation and uncertainty when affordability will get better, political experts said.
“If we think about the national mood right now in Canada … I think a lot of Canadians don’t feel like they’re getting ahead,” said Lewis Krashinsky, a political scientist and William Lyon Mackenzie King postdoctoral fellow at Harvard University. “Voters can be fickle.”
He said that when voters don’t feel like they’re getting ahead, they look for people they believe can bring new ideas.
Richard Johnston, professor emeritus of political science at the University of British Columbia, said the power of incumbency has decreased over decades. Previously, some provincial governments have served for decades such as the Progressive Conservatives in New Brunswick for 17 years, or the Alberta PCs for 43. The average length of a government now sits at about 10 years.
Incumbents have also faced multiple issues in recent months, with Johnston saying the handling of COVID-19, supply chain and inflation, and President Donald Trump’s tariffs have meant Canadians are feeling worse off.
As a result, people are pointing the finger at politicians in city hall or the provincial legislatures and punishing them for it.
“In general, this has been a decade of sort of institutional failure, I think that’s actually unfair, but that’s how voters perceive it,” Johnston said. “There’s a sense in which governments of almost any stripe seem to have dropped the ball or they’re overwhelmed by forces beyond their control.”
But Krashinsky, originally from Toronto, added that voters can choose someone new for a number of reasons including anger.
“Perhaps that’s out of a sense of anger, resentment towards a political candidate who’s been in there for so many years; perhaps it’s a sense of optimism with what the new candidate could bring in,” said Krashinsky. “Perhaps it is a sense of just needing a better option; it’s a sense of almost desperation that we’ve tried this path over and over again, and we haven’t gotten ahead.”
Long-time incumbency ended for several mayors in Ontario Oct. 26.
Gord Krantz, Canada’s longest-serving, lost his first election since becoming mayor of Milton in 1980. Further south, Sarnia’s Mike Bradley ended his 38-year run in the mayor’s seat defeated by newcomer Carrie McEachran.
It wasn’t long-time incumbents who lost either. One-term mayors in B.C. including Port Moody’s Meghan Lahti and New Westminster’s Patrick Johnstone, and Mississauga’s Carolyn Parrish and Hamilton’s Andrea Horwath in Ontario also lost.
Hamish Telford, associate political science professor at the University of the Fraser Valley in B.C., said those short-term mayors were the victims of the public disappointed in their own choices within the previous four years.
“It’s frustration with lack of progress on core issues as a generality,” he said. “People look over the past four years and say, ‘my life or my city hasn’t improved like you promised it would,’ and obviously, they come to the conclusion that the direction that the mayor set was not the right one.”
Not all incumbents are losing though, with Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow, Brampton Mayor Patrick Brown and several B.C. mayors still keeping their jobs.
Krashinsky said the reasons can range from a mixture of relatability to there not being a strong enough opposition candidate to give voters another strong choice.
“Affinity for a candidate that you know and recognize and trust someone perhaps that you’ve met,” he said. “Being able to have that personal touch that you can be established really over time I think can really help these incumbents.”
Yet Telford added even likeability won’t help if voters are losing respect for the judgment of longer-serving incumbents creating that need for change.
“The winds of change of change blow every decade in Canada and that’s what we’re seeing lately,” Telford said.
— with files from Global News’ Aaron D’Andrea and Amy Judd

title: Fleetwood-Arsenal halted for eight minutes because of drone
body: Arsenal’s match against Fleetwood Town in the last 16 of the Carabao Cup was delayed for more than eight minutes after a drone flew over the stadium during play. Referee Michael Salisbury stopped play with 1 minute and 40 seconds on the clock after spotting the drone flying above the pitch as Arsenal waited to take a free-kick at Highbury Stadium. The referee halted play to speak with management and staff on both benches, while police also investigated. The match got back under way with 10 minutes on the clock. A commentator for Sky later said police had located the drone operator. Players passed the ball around as they tried to stay warm during the delay, while supporters inside the stadium booed. After speaking to the managers and captains, the referee signalled for the players to come to the touchline, as play could not resume. However, just as the players were about to leave the pitch, the drone flew away and play resumed. The drone then dropped to the ground in a local housing estate. Commentating on the match on 5 Live, Ian Dennis said: “What a shame this has happened. This is the most high-profile game in the club’s history. In terms of the profile and the revenue, it’s so lucrative.” Seven minutes of stoppage time were added to the end of the first half because of the delay. Guidance from the Football Association on the action to be taken in such circumstances says: “Upon the sighting of a drone above a football pitch or stadium, the referee should stop the game and advise both team captains and managers that play will not continue until the drone has passed, or left the vicinity of the players and spectators.” The guidance adds that if the drone does not leave, both teams should be advised to return to their changing rooms. It also recommends that, when possible, teams seek advice from the home team’s safety officer. The BBC has approached the English Football League (EFL) for comment.

title: Greek-American Peter Sellis Takes Over Product at Musk’s X
body: Greek-American tech executive Peter Sellis has joined X to lead product, taking over from Nikita Bier at Elon Musk’s social media platform after a career at Snap, Discord and Microsoft. Peter Sellis announces on X that he is joining the platform to lead product. Photo: Peter Sellis/X Sellis announced the move in a post on X on Monday. “I’m joining the team at @X to lead Product,” he wrote. He also said he is “a huge believer” in the mission of Musk’s SpaceX. According to The Verge , Sellis replaces Bier after his one-year stint in the role. Bier announced in August that he would step down, Business Today reported. However, he will stay on for a time as an adviser. Musk also thanked him publicly on X. “Thanks for helping make this platform much better! You will be missed,” he wrote. Who is Peter Sellis? Peter Sellis has spent more than 15 years building consumer apps. He was head of product at the streaming company Ustream from 2009 to 2012. After that, Sellis worked at the venture studio Science Inc. In 2015, he joined Snap, where he spent seven years and rose to vice president of product. According to Business Today, he built the revenue product team that grew into a business worth more than US$4 billion. Later, he became senior vice president of product at Discord. Before joining X, he served briefly as a corporate vice president at Microsoft AI. What Peter Sellis plans for X In his post, Sellis said X is “the best way to find out what’s happening in the world right now and talk about it” . He said his goal is to speed up the platform’s recent momentum for users and businesses. In addition, he wants to make the product “beautiful and useful” . Still, X has not yet said what his appointment will mean for users, Business Today noted. Finally, Sellis ended with a joke for his new audience. “I’m sure the replies will be measured and magnanimous,” he wrote. By Tuesday, the post had drawn more than two million views and over 2,500 replies. Musk’s wider tech empire has been busy too. For instance, Musk’s Grok AI released its first ‘Odyssey’ episode , and Musk has also shared Marco Rubio’s Pnyx speech with his followers. The move comes weeks after Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis headed to Silicon Valley to court tech investment for Greece. In short, Sellis now holds one of the most visible product jobs in tech, at the helm of X . title: Azov fighter sentenced to 29 years by Russia returns from captivity
body:
Maksym Kozytskyi, head of the Lviv Regional Military Administration, announced this on Telegram , according to Ukrinform.
“More wonderful news for the Lviv region. During the latest prisoner exchange, Taras Zvarychuk, a resident of Drohobych who defended Ukraine as part of the Azov Regiment, returned home,” the post reads.
According to the Drohobych City Council, Zvarychuk was born in that city on May 11, 1994.
It is noted that he was among the first volunteers to stand up for his homeland immediately after the Revolution of Dignity and defended his homeland as part of the Azov Regiment.
According to the city council, Zvarychuk was taken prisoner on May 16, 2022. The Russians sentenced him to 25 years in prison, later increasing the term to 29 years—allegedly for terrorism.
“Taras tried for a long time to defend the truth and filed an appeal, but to no avail,” city council officials said.
For a long time, he was held in pretrial detention centers in Rostov, Samara, and later in Novosibirsk.
“Thanks to the soldier’s persistent efforts, he was freed from captivity and returned to his homeland. He is now undergoing rehabilitation along with other soldiers who have been returned home from captivity. His parents and two brothers are awaiting the hero’s return,” the city council added.
As reported by Ukrinform, on October 23, 270 Ukrainians returned from Russian captivity as a result of an exchange.
Illustrative photo: Volodymyr Zelensky / Telegram

title: Former Grand Slam winner Wawrinka ends tennis career
body: Stan Wawrinka bid farewell to tennis as he brought the curtain down on a decorated 24-year career following a first-round exit at the Basel Open on Tuesday. The 41-year-old Swiss announced earlier in the season that his last tournament as a professional would be the ATP 500-level event in his home country and a 7-5, 7-6 (7/2) defeat by Czech Jiri Lehecka brought an end to the career of the three-time major champion. Former world number three Wawrinka, along with Andy Murray, was the only player to win multiple Grand Slams in a period dominated by Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic. He bested Nadal to win his first Grand Slam at the Australian Open in 2014, before beating Djokovic in the French Open final the following season and then again in the US Open title-match in 2016. Alongside his compatriot Federer, the Lausanne native won the Davis Cup for Switzerland and claimed gold in the doubles at the 2008 Beijing Olympics. On court in Basel, Wawrinka’s every point won, as well as several trademark booming one-handed backhands, was greeted by wild cheers from the partisan home crowd. But Lehecka got his nose in front with a break of serve in the 11th game and sealed the opening set with an ace as he held to love. A tight second set rumbled towards a tie-break, but it was just a step too far for Wawrinka as his 21st-ranked opponent took firm control to seal the breaker and the match. The post Former Grand Slam winner Wawrinka ends tennis career appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Arab parties Ra'am, Joint List soar to 19 seats amid high turnout, election polling data show
body: With about 85% of the vote counted as of Wednesday afternoon, the Central Elections Committee's official results released Wednesday projected Israel's two main Arab parties, Ra'am and the Joint List, to win seven and 12 seats, respectively. This is a slight increase from early-night projections, which predicted a combined 16-18 seats. The current projections would give the two parties a combined 19 seats in the 120-member Knesset, up from ten combined seats in the outgoing parliament. The Joint List, led by Dr. Yousef Jabareen, comprises Hadash, Jabareen's left-wing Arab-Jewish communist party; Ta'al, a secular Arab nationalist party led by MK Ahmad Tibi; and Balad, a left-wing Palestinian nationalist party led by Sami Abu Shehadeh. With 12 seats, the Joint List is on course to be the fourth-largest party in the Knesset. MK Mansour Abbas's Ra'am party and the Joint List are unlikely to join a governing coalition, as parties allied with Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud, most notably the parties headed by Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, as well as Naftali Bennett and Avigdor Liberman in the opposition, have ruled out including Arab parties in a government. However, Ra'am or the Joint List could still play a role in determining whether either bloc can secure the 61 seats needed for a Knesset majority, including by supporting a government from outside the coalition.The Arab Israeli turnout at this election was significantly higher than in previous years, according to the Central Elections Committee. The unrecognized Bedouin village of Atuana, for example, registered the highest turnout in the country by early noon, at 64%, and two other villages placed second and fourth, at 47.9% and 47.8% respectively.Arab Israeli vote under scrutinyThe Arab Israeli vote in Israel on Tuesday drew significant attention, with Likud's election integrity headquarters claiming that it had received 620 reports of unusual incidents and suspected irregularities at polling stations in the Arab sector, collected through a network of over 1,500 representatives across the country. About one-third of the reports concern the recording of voters' personal information and the transmission of information outside polling stations. Some 66 reports concern irregularities involving ballot papers and envelopes, 26 involve difficulties verifying voters' identities and exercising polling station committee members' authority, and 17  concern violence and threats.The remaining reports involve staffing deficiencies, election campaigning, and documentation issues.“We categorically reject attempts by elements within the police to link Ra'am to the compromising of electoral integrity,” the Ra'am party said in response to the incident. “The activists were arrested at their homes hours before the polls opened, not in the vicinity of polling stations or voters.“These are baseless arrests intended to undermine Ra'am and suppress voter turnout within Arab society, as part of [National Security Minister Itamar] Ben-Gvir's political exploitation of Israel Police.”'We want to replace the current gov't in almost every way,' Ra'am chairman Abbas says "This is a historic day," Joint List chairman Prof. Yousef Jabareen said on Tuesday night amid election exit polls indicating that Arab voters had turned out in unexpectedly large numbers. "The public has spoken," Jabareen said. "The blood-stained government must go. We have proven that we are a political force that cannot be ignored, and that a future cannot be built here without our voice.""Arab society has reacted to this government's policy," Ra'am chairman Mansour Abbas told Israel's Channel 12 on Tuesday night as late-stage exit polls for the 2026 elections came in. "We want to replace it in almost every possible way," he added. Abbas hoped the final results would let the opposition bloc and Ra'am reach 61 seats together, but said, "With the numbers we have now, there is no government."Keshet Neev contributed to this report.

title: Barcelona fined £503 over approach for Alvarez
body: Barcelona have been fined €602 (£503) after Atletico Madrid complained about contact the club made with striker Julian Alvarez. Atletico accused La Liga rivals Barcelona of approaching Argentina international Alvarez without first notifying them in writing. The 26-year-old remained at Atletico and has a contract which runs until June 2030. The Spanish football association issued the fine. Atletico also complained to FIFA, but football’s governing body declared it had no jurisdiction over the case. Alvarez has frequently been booed by his own supporters this season, but some gave him a standing ovation after he scored the winning goal against Deportivo La Coruna on Saturday. After that victory, which put Diego Simeone’s side within two points of leaders Barcelona, Alvarez took the opportunity to apologise to Atletico fans. Referring to an interview he gave during the summer in which he said he wanted to “fulfil his dream” of playing for Barcelona, Alvarez said: “It was a mistake. I understand why the fans are angry. “If I were a fan, I’d be angry too. Especially given how they’ve supported me since I arrived.” Alvarez joined Atletico Madrid from Manchester City on a six-year deal in August 2024, worth up to £81.5m. After scoring 36 goals in 103 appearances for City, he has scored 51 goals in 115 games for Atletico.

title: Finland and Norway leaders make rare direct call to Putin, breaking with the West’s diplomatic isolation of the Russian leader to influence Ukraine peace talks
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre spoke by phone with Russian President Vladimir Putin on 27 October, urging him to de-escalate Russia’s war against Ukraine and resume negotiations. The roughly 90-minute call was coordinated with Kyiv and came ahead of planned trilateral talks between Ukrainian, US, and Russian officials in Abu Dhabi in November. The initiative marks a rare direct contact between Western European leaders and Putin since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022. The Nordic leaders are reportedly seeking to influence peace efforts increasingly shaped by US President Donald Trump, amid concerns in Europe that Washington is shifting toward Moscow’s position and sidelining Ukraine’s European partners. Stubb and Støre said they discussed Russia’s war against Ukraine, upcoming negotiations, and security in Europe. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the two leaders had urged Putin to take concrete steps toward de-escalation, particularly regarding attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure. Zelenskyy says leaders urged energy de-escalation After the call, Zelenskyy said he had spoken with Stubb and Støre to receive a detailed briefing. He thanked them for supporting Ukraine’s diplomatic efforts and said they had clearly told the Russian leader that real de-escalation steps were needed regarding Ukraine’s energy sector and infrastructure. Zelenskyy also said the leaders discussed preparations for a trilateral meeting planned for November involving Ukrainian, US, and Russian negotiating teams. In a joint statement , Stubb and Støre said the call followed their 20 October meeting in Oslo and was held in consultation with Ukraine. They emphasized that Finland and Norway, which both share borders with Russia, would continue their longstanding support for Ukraine. “The discussion was frank and substantive,” Stubb said, adding that the war’s outcome would directly affect Nordic and broader European security. Støre stressed the war’s enormous human and material costs and said the leaders had emphasized the importance of de-escalation. Presidents Volodymyr Zelenskyy (R) of Ukraine and Alexander Stubb (L) of Finland after signing the security agreement. Kyiv, 3 April 2024. Screenshot: Telegram/Zelenskyy Official Moscow gives no sign of changing its position The Kremlin’s account of the call offered no indication that Putin was prepared to soften his demands, according to Reuters. It said a just and lasting peace was possible only if Russia’s “legitimate interests” were fully taken into account, while blaming EU and NATO policies for prolonging the fighting. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov dismissed the call as offering nothing new on the conflict and accused European countries of seeking a role in negotiations. A source close to the Kremlin told Reuters that Putin had said the war must end while taking “the realities on the ground” into account. The source interpreted this as meaning Moscow would not compromise on its goal of capturing the entire Donbas region. Russia has continued its attacks on Ukraine while demanding territorial concessions. Kyiv, meanwhile, has called for meaningful de-escalation and a settlement that preserves Ukraine’s sovereignty and security. Nordic initiative draws criticism from European partners The call comes as European governments seek a greater role in peace efforts led by Trump. Western European leaders have largely avoided direct contact with Putin since the invasion, hoping to isolate Moscow, but concerns have grown that Europe is being sidelined in negotiations. Stubb said Ukraine had sought to open a new channel of communication and that Europe could no longer remain a bystander to peace efforts. He said the initiative had been discussed with Western allies. However, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen criticized the move, saying she saw no signs that Russia wanted peace and arguing that Europe should act together rather than pursue separate initiatives, according to Reuters. Reuters added that Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said other European leaders had not been informed of the talks and expressed low expectations for the conversation. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk also urged caution. Stubb and Støre stressed that they had acted as leaders of Finland and Norway, not on behalf of Europe as a whole. They said their countries would continue supporting Ukraine while pursuing diplomatic efforts to end the war. title: Liberman's Yisrael Beytenu projected to win seven seats in next Knesset, election data predicts
body: Yisrael Beytenu, led by Avigdor Liberman, was expected to win seven seats in 2026 Israeli Elections, according to official results released by the Central Elections Committee on Wednesday.Yisrael Beytenu has campaigned as part of the opposition to the ruling coalition led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Polling from Israeli national broadcaster KAN 11, as well as Channels 12 and 13, put the party at about eight seats.Liberman urged voters throughout the day to keep voting and to remove the “October massacre government,” referring to the current government that was in charge on October 7, 2023, when Hamas attacked.“Put a note in the box today, and you'll get public transportation on Shabbat starting tomorrow,” he wrote on X/Twitter. “Oust the government of the October 7 massacre and the draft dodgers!”Polls closed at 10 p.m. after a day that saw high turnout in the morning and scattered showers of rain in the afternoon.Yisrael Beytenu has generally polled between seven and 10 seats since August 2026. The polling data was also generally consistent.What does Yisrael Beytenu stand for?Over the last decade and a half, Yisrael Beytenu has drawn support from a diverse group of people across Israel. Originally popular with immigrants from the former Soviet Union countries and their descendants in the early 2000s, it has drawn support from many groups in the last elections. For instance, on October 20, former National Security Council head and longtime Likud politician Tzachi Hanegbi said he would vote for Liberman in the October 27 election.In early October, a report said Liberman had suggested handing over Palestinian areas to Jordan. He also slammed Netanyahu for fearmongering about Iran before the October 27 elections. He has rejected relying on the support of Arab parties to form a coalition in the Knesset. He has also warned that the US could recognize a Palestinian state in coming years.Yisrael Beytenu was founded in 1999 by Avigdor Liberman, who was a Likud activist in the 1990s and Director-General of the Prime Minister's Office when Benjamin Netanyahu was Prime Minister in the 1990s. He resigned due to concerns about concessions to the Palestinians.As head of Yisrael Beytenu, he left the party to join a coalition with the National Union in the early 2000s and became a minister. The party rose to 15 seats in 2009 and then ran with Likud in 2013. Liberman became Defense Minister from 2016 to 2018. He resigned over what he saw as appeasement of Hamas.  The results of the election on October 27 will have major implications for the coalition negotiations. Exit polls are preliminary projections, and the final seat distribution will depend on the official vote count.

title: ‘A government of paralysis’: Ben-Gvir rejects unity with Eisenkot after election setback
body: He had hoped to win a double-digit number of Knesset seats, but the exit polls suggested he had fallen well short. National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit party was projected to win six seats in the exit polls published by Channels 12 and 13, while Kan 11 gave it seven. Netanyahu's entire political bloc, meanwhile, was projected to fall from 64 seats to 50. Ben-Gvir did not immediately respond to the exit polls, arriving at his party's headquarters in Modi'in shortly before midnight, where he warned against forming a unity government with Gadi Eisenkot. Addressing party activists, Ben-Gvir said: "Tonight, we are marking another chapter in the development of Otzma Yehudit. I remember that two Knesset terms ago, this party barely existed on the political map. After that, we fought for a single seat, and tonight, for the first time, an independent party running on its own has won the support of hundreds of thousands of citizens."   "The night is still young. We believe and hope that we are close to forming a right-wing government, with God's help," he added. Ben-Gvir went on to praise the policies he had advanced during his time in office. "In any case, we are proud of our path, of the reforms we promised the public and delivered. I am proud that last time I promised to pass a law imposing the death penalty on terrorists, and we delivered," he said. "I heard some people saying that the Arabs didn't like the demolition of homes in the Negev. I'm proud that we demolished 10,000 illegal homes in the Negev," he continued. Turning to Palestinian security prisoners, Ben-Gvir said: "I can already hear the hopes of the terrorists in prison, hoping that their summer camps will return. We will continue fighting to make sure those hopes are not realized. We didn't enter politics to apologize for our principles." Later in his speech, Ben-Gvir attacked the possibility of forming a unity government with Yashar! party chairman Gadi Eisenkot. "Unfortunately, tonight I'm hearing that some people are talking about a unity government with Eisenkot," he said. "That's exactly the scenario I warned against, the one our friends in Likud made a point of denying and saying wasn't true. And now, just two minutes after the exit polls were published, we're hearing people talking about a unity government with Eisenkot. That would be a government of paralysis." As a teenager, Ben-Gvir was active in the Kach movement founded by Rabbi Meir Kahane. He was first elected to the Knesset in 2021 after a series of unsuccessful attempts, running on a joint electoral list with Bezalel Smotrich's Religious Zionism party. The two parties also ran together in the previous election. Following that election, Ben-Gvir was appointed national security minister. During his tenure, the number of murders in Israel's Arab communities surged to unprecedented levels. Upon taking office, he moved to expand the number of civilians permitted to carry firearms and repeatedly intervened in police affairs. Among other things, he sought to promote the arrest of protesters blocking roads, blocked the promotion of police officers and attempted to remove Tel Aviv District Police Commander Ami Eshed from his post. In this election, Ben-Gvir ran independently, without joining forces with other parties.

title: This Serbian Truck Carries A Truly Massive Mortar
body: Serbia has released the first footage of its TSMB M-25 heavy self-propelled mortar in action, revealing an unusual artillery system that puts a massive 203mm weapon on a comparatively light, six-wheeled truck. The system is designed to hurl projectiles weighing around 220 pounds at targets up to approximately seven-and-a-half miles away, bringing super-heavy firepower to a platform that looks surprisingly modest for the job. The Serbian Ministry of Defense published the brief footage in a larger video montage, seen immediately below, but has not disclosed when or where the firing tests took place or what they demonstrated. Regardless, the M-25’s configuration alone makes it stand out. A TSMB M-25 heavy self-propelled mortar in a firing position. Serbian Ministry of Defense/screencap The Teški Samohodni Minobacač (TSMB, translated as heavy self-propelled mortar) M-25 was developed by Serbia’s state-owned Military Technical Institute and first appeared publicly at the Partner 2025 defense exhibition in Belgrade. Its design lineage stretches back to the Yugoslav M-65 155mm howitzer, itself a licensed copy of the widely used American M114 , first introduced in World War II. Artillerymen of the 24th Infantry Division, U.S. Army, fire 155mm howitzers in the Korean War. Public Domain The M-25 takes that heritage in a different direction, with a 203mm barrel measuring 24 calibers in length and an automated loading mechanism for mortar projectiles. The mortar barrel has an elevation range from 0° to 75°, and the barrel must return to 0° in elevation for the next round to be loaded from the muzzle end. The standard 203mm mortar bomb weighs around 220 pounds, including approximately 60 pounds of explosive material. This results in a claimed destruction radius of around 250 feet, using impact fuzing. The system is intended to fire both high-explosive and concrete-piercing ammunition, making it particularly suited to attacking hardened positions and fortifications. Developers have also provided for rocket-assisted projectiles to extend its range and precision guidance kits to improve the accuracy of compatible rounds. The weapon is mounted on a FAP 2026 three-axle truck in a 6×6 configuration, a general-purpose off-road type made by Serbian vehicle manufacturer Fabrika automobila Priboj. This platform provides a range of 500 miles and a top speed of 50 miles per hour on the road. The vehicle has an armored cab for a crew of four, while its fire-control suite includes an inertial navigation system, a ballistic computer, communications equipment, and a dedicated gunner’s computer. The same truck has also been adapted to mount a 152mm gun/howitzer, under the name NORA B-39 . The NORA B-39 mounts a 152mm gun/howitzer on the same FAP 2026 three-axle truck chassis. Serbian Ministry of Defense The wheeled chassis is the defining feature of the M-25. While a weapon of this size would normally be either towed or mounted on a large tracked vehicle, Serbia has opted for a lighter truck-based arrangement. This offers advantages in road mobility and makes the system easier to move between firing positions, using “shoot and scoot” tactics. A general-purpose truck is cheaper to acquire and operate, and easier to maintain. It can also be more easily transported by air, although out-of-area operations are not generally on the Serbian Armed Forces’ agenda. However, its cross-country performance and overall survivability will be reduced compared to a tracked chassis. TSMB M-25 heavy self-propelled mortar firing a round. Serbian Ministry of Defense/screencap The M-25 is intended to deliver heavy fire against targets such as bunkers and other fortified positions, then relocate before an opponent can respond. Its relatively short stated range compared with many modern 155mm howitzers makes it a specialized system rather than a direct replacement for conventional long-range artillery. Its appeal lies instead in combining a very large projectile with a comparatively compact and mobile platform. Mortars have a long and grim history in the Balkans, particularly during the wars that accompanied the breakup of Yugoslavia in the 1990s. The steep trajectories of mortar rounds made them useful in the region’s mountainous terrain and in fighting around fortified positions and during sieges, while their ability to deliver indirect fire meant crews could engage targets without a direct line of sight. A visitor looks at infantry mortars at an exhibition of Serbia’s armed forces in Nis, southern Serbia, on February 14, 2024. Photo by SASA DJORDJEVIC / AFP SASA DJORDJEVIC As far as we know, the M-25 is the only 203mm mortar in current development and/or production. There are a few larger mortars on mobile platforms, notably Russia’s 2S4 Tyulpan , a 240mm self-propelled mortar, but this is on a significantly bigger tracked chassis. At approximately 19 metric tons, the M-25 is substantially lighter than the 2S4 Tyulpan, which weighs around 27.5 metric tons. Its tracked platform reflects a very different approach to moving super-heavy mortar firepower around the battlefield. The Tyulpan can deliver a 300-pound standard mortar round to a range of around six miles, or up to 11 miles away when using rocket-assisted rounds. A Belarusian-operated 2S4 Tyulpan (nearest camera) during joint maneuvers with the Russian military. Russian Ministry of Defense Russian artillerymen fire a 2S4 Tyulpan during a live-fire exercise. Russian Ministry of Defense Serbia claims the M-25 has a rate of fire of up to three rounds per minute, thanks to the automated loading mechanism. In contrast, the Tyulpan can hurl a maximum of one round every 62 seconds. Indeed, its sluggish rate of fire is one of the reasons that saw it fall from more widespread Russian use. There are still important unknowns. The newly released footage does not establish whether the advertised firing rate was achieved, how the weapon performs under sustained fire, or whether the system has entered operational service. Serbia has shown the M-25 at an exhibition and now in live-fire footage, but detailed test results have not been made public. Still, the concept is striking: a high-mobility wheeled truck carrying a 203mm mortar is a distinctly different take on super-heavy firepower, but one that might just find a niche in the Balkan environment. Contact the author: thomas@thewarzone.com The post This Serbian Truck Carries A Truly Massive Mortar appeared first on TWZ .

title: Yair Golan's Democrats projected to win eight Knesset seats in 2026
body: The Democrats, led by former deputy IDF chief of staff Yair Golan, were expected to win eight seats in the 2026 Israeli Elections, according to official results released by the Central Elections Committee on Wednesday.The party gained four seats in the 120-member Knesset compared with its current representation.Golan's party entered election night projected to secure between eight and ten seats in the 26th Knesset, according to final pre-election polling published ahead of the vote.Final surveys broadcast by Channel 12, as well as polls by Maariv and The Jerusalem Post, all projected 10 seats for Golan's slate. Channel 11 and 13 both projected the Democrats to win 9 seats.Throughout the campaign, Golan positioned the party around a platform of “fundamental change.” A key component of its agenda focused on what it alleged was safeguarding Israeli democracy, with Golan promising legislation to bar politicians under criminal indictment from serving as prime minister or cabinet ministers, while fully backing the judiciary and Attorney-General Gali Baharav-Miara against government attempts to undermine them.On domestic policy, the party advocated for the separation of religion and state, including the introduction of civil marriage and protecting the right of businesses to operate on Shabbat. The Democrats also targeted National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir over his handling of the rising crime wave in Arab communities and voiced firm opposition to military draft exemptions for Haredi men.Golan's Democrats oppose West Bank annexation, back demilitarized Palestinian stateOn security and diplomacy, Golan rejected Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's strategy of repeated military rounds in favor of pursuing a broader regional accord that would divide the land and establish a demilitarized Palestinian state. The party platform explicitly opposed West Bank annexation, called for a complete halt to state funding for illegal outposts, and pledged to strip Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich of his civil administration powers in the West Bank to return authoritative control to the IDF. Golan ruled out joining any coalition led by Benjamin Netanyahu or sitting alongside Smotrich, Ben-Gvir, or the ultra-Orthodox parties. However, unlike other opposition leaders, Golan openly backed sitting with Arab parties, such as Ra'am, in a future governing coalition, describing their participation as a natural and necessary component of Israeli democracy.Formed in July 2024 through a merger of the Labor Party and Meretz, The Democrats was established as a unified liberal-democratic Zionist framework to consolidate the Israeli left and prevent a repeat of the 2022 election, when splintered left-wing votes left Meretz below the 3.25% electoral threshold. The party selected its primary slate in July, placing incumbent lawmakers Naama Lazimi, Gilad Kariv, and Efrat Rayten behind Golan.Democrats chairman reacts to exit pollsDemocrats party chairman Maj.-Gen. (res.) Yair Golan declared that the Israeli public had “fired Netanyahu and the Likud” on Tuesday night, as he urged opposition leaders to form a new government as quickly as possible. Speaking at the party's election-night event, Golan said voters had rejected a government of “draft evasion, corruption, and extreme nationalism,” adding that Israel's security was at stake and delays in forming a government could have serious consequences. “From tonight, Israel can breathe. Starting tomorrow, we begin rebuilding,” he said.Jerusalem Post Staff contributed to this report.

title: Russia, Equatorial Guinea have significant potential to boost mutual supplies — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Russia and Equatorial Guinea have significant potential to increase mutual supplies of products in demand and implement joint investment projects, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at a meeting with Equatorial Guinean President Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo.
"I would also like to note that our countries have significant potential both to increase mutual supplies of products in demand and to implement promising investment projects, primarily in the energy and mining sectors," the Russian leader said.
Putin noted that trade and economic cooperation between the two countries is currently "lagging somewhat behind." "There has even been a certain decline. We hope that the establishment of an intergovernmental commission will help improve the situation," the president added.
At the same time, Putin said that positive results have been achieved in bilateral cultural and humanitarian cooperation. "Every year, we allocate federal budget funds to provide scholarships for 75 of your citizens to study at Russian universities. This year, we also held two competitive selection programs for advanced training of Equatorial Guinean civil servants at the Russian Presidential Academy of National Economy and Public Administration and St. Petersburg State University. The group in St. Petersburg completed its training just yesterday. In total, more than 1,000 specialists have been trained in our country over the years," he said.
Putin also noted that a Russian cultural center has been operating in Malabo since 2025.

title: First Boeing 737 built in Everett rolls out as new MAX production line comes alive
body:
For the first time, a Boeing 737 has rolled out of a final assembly line outside Renton, Washington. The aircraft, a 737 MAX 10 destined for WestJet, left Boeing's new North Line in Everett on Monday, October 26.
The milestone comes nearly four months after Boeing loaded the first aircraft into the new line, which occupies part of the company's massive Everett complex previously used for 787 production.
According to the Seattle Times, employees gathered for an internal celebration before the aircraft was moved out of the factory at around 2 p.m. Eight 737 MAX aircraft are now progressing through the North Line, with another MAX 10 for WestJet following the first aircraft.
The rollout does not mean the first Everett-built MAX 10 is ready for delivery. The aircraft was assembled while certification of the variant was still underway and must undergo modifications to incorporate the final certified configuration.
Those changes include work associated with the engine anti-ice system and an enhanced angle-of-attack sensor. After initial checks in Everett, the aircraft is expected to be moved to another Boeing facility for the modifications before it can be delivered to WestJet.
The Federal Aviation Administration also still needs to approve the Everett North Line for production deliveries. Certification of the 737 MAX 10 itself, completed on October 20, and approval of the new manufacturing line are separate processes.
Boeing began loading the first 737 into the Everett line on July 6, creating a second final assembly site for a family historically associated with Renton.
The North Line occupies space formerly used by the 787 program before Boeing consolidated Dreamliner final assembly in North Charleston, South Carolina. Boeing subsequently prepared the Everett building for 737 production as it sought additional capacity for the MAX.
Renton remains the main production center for the 737, but Everett is expected to become increasingly important as Boeing raises output.
The manufacturer is currently working toward a stable production rate of 47 737s per month. Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg said on Tuesday that the company now expects to fully stabilize at that level in 2027, with wing production among the factors limiting the pace of the increase.
The Everett line is expected initially to contribute about five aircraft per month. Its additional capacity will be needed as Boeing moves toward the next production target of 52 737s per month.
The timing gives the new factory a particularly important role for the MAX 10. The largest member of the 737 MAX family received FAA certification last week after years of delays, allowing Boeing to prepare customer aircraft for delivery.
WestJet is one of the customers awaiting the variant. The Canadian carrier has MAX 10s on order as part of a broader Boeing 737 MAX fleet that already includes the MAX 8.
The first Everett-built aircraft still has another regulatory milestone ahead of it: Boeing cannot deliver a 737 assembled on the North Line until the FAA adds the Everett operation to the company's approved production system.

title: Brazil’s Flavio Bolsonaro flees to US after election loss
body: Defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro left Brazil and is traveling to the United States despite a court order banning him from exiting the country, US media reported Tuesday. The son of jailed ex-leader Jair Bolsonaro lost elections to incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on Sunday and refused to concede defeat. The right-wing senator on Monday said a Supreme Court justice had ordered him to hand over his passports. Bolsonaro is under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering, and with his election loss is also set to lose his parliamentary immunity. The 45-year-old was heading to Florida, CNN reported Tuesday, citing an anonymous official source. Other US media confirmed he was heading to the country. The US State Department said Tuesday that it would issue visas to Bolsonaro and his family, without confirming his travel plans. A police source told AFP that the senator’s Brazilian and diplomatic passports had been canceled, adding that “there is no formal record of Flavio Bolsonaro leaving the country.” But he has held Italian nationality since 2023, according to an Italian parliamentary document seen by AFP. Bolsonaro’s campaign manager Rogerio Marinho expressed shock over reports that the defeated candidate had fled Brazil. “We still don’t have any news about his whereabouts,” he told reporters in Brasilia on Tuesday. “I received a text message from him this morning, where he said he would let some time pass today and then would talk with us, and that was it,” Marinho said. “That was the only communication we had.” – Scare tactic – Flavio Bolsonaro said Monday that the ban on his exit from Brazil amounted to a scare tactic. “I never had any intention of leaving the country. I will surrender my passports and defend myself against this travesty,” he said in the video posted on Instagram. US President Donald Trump, a close ally of Jair Bolsonaro, on Monday said Brazil’s elections were “rigged” following the defeat of Bolsonaro junior. Flavio’s brother Eduardo, a US-based former lawmaker, maintains close ties with the White House. Last week, he told a US podcast that Flavio Bolsonaro should leave Brazil in the event of electoral defeat, given the active probes into his activities. In his Monday statement, Lula’s challenger also said he would lead the opposition to the leftist government. Following Lula’s victory with 51.8 percent of the vote, Bolsonaro said he would seek to annul the result, citing the decision to extend polling hours over transportation difficulties that prevented some citizens from voting. Lula had requested the extension, as had Bolsonaro over bad weather in parts of the country. – In his father’s footsteps – All bets were on a Bolsonaro win after he came out on top in the first round of elections earlier this month. He campaigned on a pledge to liberate his father, who is under house arrest for coup-plotting after his own electoral loss to Lula in 2022. Jair Bolsonaro never conceded defeat and left the country on the eve of his rival’s inauguration, only returning to Brazil three months later. Separately on Tuesday, the Supreme Court ordered police to investigate alleged foreign funding of Flavio Bolsonaro’s campaign and other interference from abroad such as social media “manipulation.” Lula’s campaign complained about interference in the election by Meta, the parent company of WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram, claiming “algorithmic manipulation.” Meta denies taking any actions to favor one side in the election, but previously said that some of Lula’s campaign ads had been mistakenly deactivated due to technical errors. The post Brazil’s Flavio Bolsonaro flees to US after election loss appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ben-Gvir to win 6-7 seats as Smotrich's RZP takes 6, election exit polls project
body: National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit party was expected to win seven seats in the next Knesset, according to results published by the Central Election Committee (CEC) on Wednesday morning.The Religious Zionist Party-Zehut (RZP), led by Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, was projected to win six seats, bringing the two far-right parties' combined total to around 13 seats.Both parties are firmly part of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc. Their combined projected total would represent a decrease from the 14 seats they won in the 2022 election, when they ran on a joint ticket.Ben-Gvir campaigned on a security-focused platform and added former Likud MK Tally Gotliv to his party's slate, while RZP ran in a technical bloc with Zehut, led by Moshe Feiglin, to help the joint slate clear the electoral threshold.Feiglin is now projected to return to the Knesset for the first time since 2015.Responding to the exit poll projections released Tuesday night, Smotrich vowed that he would "not let the Arabs celebrate" after polls projected a strong showing for Ra'am and the Joint List."You are celebrating because you think you can stop the Judea and Samaria revolution," Smotrich told his supporters at his party's headquarters in Jerusalem. "We will not let you stop [it]."'Terrible mistake': Ben-Gvir rejects possibility of serving in Unity governmentBen-Gvir responded to exit polls projecting his party would win six seats on Tuesday night, saying the evening was "still young. “Regardless of the final results, we are very proud of our path, and especially of the major reforms that we promised the public, and we worked to realize them,” he said.Ben-Gvir added that reports of a possible unity government with Gadi Eisenkot were “exactly the scenario we warned against,” calling it a “terrible mistake.”Arab Israelis should not celebrate the results of the election exit polls, Religious Zionist Party chairman Bezalel Smotrich said early Wednesday morning, claiming they were celebrating because “they think they will succeed in stopping the revolution in Judea and Samaria.""We will not allow you to stop [it]," he added.

title: Alexander brothers each sentenced to 30 years in prison for sex trafficking case
body: Three brothers – two of them wealthy real-estate moguls – were sentenced to 30 years each in prison for drugging and raping dozens of women over decades. Tal Alexander, 40, and twins Oren and Alon Alexander, 39, were found guilty in March of using their wealth and social status to lure women to parties and luxury homes, where they sexually assaulted them. “Your conduct was monstrous,” said Judge Valerie Caproni before sentencing them. “Your crimes wreaked havoc on their lives.” On Tuesday morning, the court in New York heard from 12 victims, including one who did not testify during the trial. One by one, they spoke of the psychological trauma they endured after the Alexander brothers raped them, and their desire for the shame they had felt to instead fall on the defendants. Many asked the judge to impose the maximum sentence of life in prison for each brother. Maya Miller told the court that after Tal Alexander raped her in 2014, she lost all sense of safety. “I carry a quiet funeral within me for the person I might’ve become if this never happened to me,” she said. Another victim, using the pseudonym Isa Brooks, said that after being raped by Tal and Alon Alexander when she was 16, she lost the ability to trust herself. “I had no idea the danger I was in till it was too late,” she said. Another woman said that when she planned to come forward about being raped, Tal Alexander threatened her, saying he knew where her sister worked. Prosecutor Elizabeth Espinosa said the brothers deserved the maximum punishment for their crimes, saying facts “paint a truly devastating picture”. “For years, they honed their methods of luring women with the promise of luxury,” she said, adding that they were “completely unmoved by the path of suffering they left behind them.” During the women’s speeches, the three Alexander brothers showed little emotion. They stared ahead or conferred with their lawyers, who said they advised their clients not to look at the victims so the court couldn’t misinterpret it. Attorneys for the brothers pushed for sentences of 15 years, arguing that they had become devoted fathers whose families would suffer in their absence. The three men all addressed the court, continuing to profess their innocence. “We had a work-hard, play-hard mentality,” Tal Alexander said, adding he saw how his behavior “hurt people’s feelings”. But their statements did not assuage Caproni, who chastised them for refusing to admit their crimes. “How can someone who never acknowledged the wrongs they did be rehabilitated?” she asked. At the end of the hearing, she sentenced them each to 30 years in prison for certain crimes. She also sentenced each to 20 years in prison for additional crimes, but said the men would serve the sentences concurrently. Prosecutor Elizabeth Espinosa addresses the court and argues for a life sentence during the sentencing of real estate brokers Oren and Tal Alexander and their brother Alon During the five-week trial, 11 women – several said they were minors at the time of the assaults – testified that the brothers gave them gifts and flew them places including Aspen and the Bahamas where they fed them drugs before raping them. Prosecutors said the brothers’ pattern of abusive behaviour began in high school, though the trial involved crimes starting in 2008. They said the three slipped drugs into women’s drinks, and “physically restrained and held down their victims during the rapes and sexual assaults and ignored screams and explicit requests to stop”. Lawyers for the brothers argued the sex was consensual and that they were womanisers, but not abusers. Two of the brothers, Tal and Oren, became wealthy selling luxury properties in New York and Miami. They worked for American real estate giant Douglas Elliman, with clients including Lindsay Lohan, Kim Kardashian and Kanye West. In 2022, they founded their own New York-based firm called Official. Alon worked at the family’s private security firm, Kent Security. As they heard their sentences, the brothers stared straight ahead.

title: Odysseas Athanasiou: ‘Ellinikon Is My Child’ as He Leaves LAMDA
body: Odysseas Athanasiou told journalists on Monday that he feels Ellinikon is his own child, as he explained why he is leaving LAMDA Development after 18 years as chief executive. He spoke hours after the company named Evi Kostaki as his successor. Athanasiou leaves on 31 December 2026. Kostaki, a former finance chief at Swiss banking group Julius Baer, takes over on 1 January 2027. Visibly moved, the 21-year LAMDA veteran wanted to explain in person what the company had achieved. He also set out what comes next, and why. Why Odysseas Athanasiou is leaving now According to Odysseas Athanasiou, the decision dates back to September 2025. That month, he told Spyros Latsis and his son Alex he wanted to leave within 12 to 15 months. Together, they agreed he would stay until new management was in place. Key works at the old Athens airport site also had to be under way. Since his youth, he has wanted to build something of his own. Yet the project kept postponing that plan, as Athanasiou told reporters: “Ellinikon became a life mission. I gave it everything, and I will help wherever I am needed. My plan to do something of my own was extended because of it. I said I would wait until 2027, and my contribution, as I see it, is now complete.” Odysseas Athanasiou, LAMDA Development chief executive In a symbolic gesture, Odysseas Athanasiou plans to move to Ellinikon himself in March 2027. He compared this moment to leaving for an MBA in the United States at 22. Back then, he felt the start of some dreams, but also uncertainty. “That is how I feel now, because Ellinikon is my child,” he said. Optimism, delays and one wrong call Odysseas Athanasiou admitted that the project has not kept to its original timelines. Delays and higher building costs played a part. So did the pandemic, supply chain problems, wars and labour shortages. In his view, he had been too optimistic about the schedule, and some decisions perhaps came late. Without that optimism, though, he might never have taken the project on. “So optimism was both good and bad,” he said. Asked about his best and worst calls, he named his push to bid for Ellinikon as by far the right one. The mistake was not creating an in-house construction unit at LAMDA sooner. When he became chief executive in March 2009, the financial crisis was hitting Greece. At that point, the group’s net asset value stood at about €400 million. Today, Lamda Development manages a portfolio of around €5 billion, with a net asset value of about €1.5 billion. Its staff has grown from about 180 to more than 700. Even so, its recent results show the strain the giant investment places on earnings. What Ellinikon faces in the next 10 months For Odysseas Athanasiou, the biggest challenge ahead is running a brand-new city. Within 10 months, the coastal front should have 120 occupied condo apartments and at least 15 working villas. A marina should be operating, with the first shops beside it. Traffic will test the new district too. LAMDA has sent the government studies and proposals for a metro extension and better traffic lights. It has offered to fund studies to turn Vouliagmenis Avenue into an expressway. Turning to open issues, Odysseas Athanasiou believes LAMDA has a good chance of sealing its deal with ION Group, possibly before Christmas. First unveiled in August 2025 at €450 million, that investment would bring a research and innovation hub to Ellinikon. Talks with neighbouring mayors and fellow coastal investors are now on a good path, he said. Those investors include Achilleas Konstantakopoulos and Giorgos Prokopiou. He defended the 200-metre Riviera Tower , which has divided opinion over its looks. In his view, the Ellinikon tower brings something new to the modern image of Greece. A next venture in building and technology Odysseas Athanasiou, who has worked since he was 18, is not retiring. Instead, he wants his next venture to combine construction and technology with a clear social footprint. Ideally, it would ease the housing problem or make the city greener. At the same time, he will keep ties with the Latsis family. From 1 January 2027, he joins Consolidated Lamda Holdings (CLH), the main shareholder’s company. As an adviser, he will focus on relations with institutions and state authorities. Other business figures have approached him, he admitted, but his answer to the Restis group is no. He also dismissed talk that the Latsis family is leaving Ellinikon. Odysseas Athanasiou praised the shipping and banking heir for taking a huge business risk while Greece was going bankrupt. Latsis also endured years of criticism. “His moral stature is enormous,” he said. Asked for advice for Kostaki, he said he would tell her what he told himself: listen to everyone. Finally, his proudest achievement is people stopping him in the street to say LAMDA has built a place that belongs to society . title: Israel Election: Exit Polls Put Netanyahu’s Likud First but No Bloc Wins a Majority
body: Exit polls from Israel’s general election show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud as the largest party. However, the bloc of parties opposed to him is narrowly ahead, and neither side is on track for a majority in the 120-seat Knesset. The figures are projections, not official results. Israelis voted on Tuesday, 27 October, for the 26th Knesset. It was the first national election since the Hamas-led attack of 7 October 2023. What the exit polls show The three main broadcasters, Kan 11, Channel 12 and Channel 13, all projected Likud to win 24 to 25 seats. Former army chief Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party was second on 21 to 23 seats. Former prime minister Naftali Bennett’s B’Yachad was projected to win between 12 and 14. After updates through the night, all three networks put Netanyahu’s bloc on 50 seats and the anti-Netanyahu bloc led by Eisenkot on 52, The Times of Israel reported . Arab-led parties were projected to win 18 seats, which would be a record. Channel 13’s first projection had given the opposition bloc 53 seats. Channel 14, which NBC News described as strongly pro-Netanyahu, was the outlier. It gave the prime minister’s bloc 60 seats and Eisenkot’s 43. A coalition needs 61 seats to govern. No party has ever won an outright majority in Israel. Official results must be published within eight days of the vote, by 4 November. Record turnout Turnout was exceptionally high. Israel’s Central Elections Committee said 31.5 per cent of voters had cast ballots by midday, the highest at that hour since 1977. That was the year Likud first won power. By 8pm, turnout had reached 74.3 per cent, compared with 66 per cent at the same point in 2022. The Times of Israel reported a near-final figure of 77.7 per cent at 10pm, the highest at that hour since 1999. Rival camps react Eisenkot said the early figures showed “a complete lack of confidence in Netanyahu and the October 7 government”. He added: “If these are the final results, this is a victory for Israel’s mainstream Zionist majority.” Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar, of Likud, said “the left’s celebration is premature”. He wrote on X: “One thing is reasonably clear: Likud is the biggest party in Israel.” The campaign was bitter. During the day, Netanyahu sent voters a recorded message accusing the left and Arab parties of trying to “steal the election”, Haaretz reported . The Guardian reported that the election committee rejected the claim and said it had seen no evidence of systematic tampering. The committee also refused requests to keep polling stations open past 10pm. What happens next The result points to weeks of coalition negotiations. Once official results are published, President Isaac Herzog will choose a member of the Knesset to try to form a government. This is usually the leader of the largest party, but it can be whoever is considered most likely to succeed. If no one can form a coalition, Israel could face another election. The Guardian reported that the Arab-led parties could become kingmakers, although both Netanyahu and Eisenkot have ruled out governing with them, according to NBC News. Like all surveys, exit polls can be wrong, and counting is continuing.
