title: Anduril Industries and Qualcomm launch BlueChip to rebuild U.S. computer manufacturing
body: The laptop is the first product in BlueChip, a new hardware line intended to build a U.S. supplier base and the capacity to manufacture complete computers at scale. Qualcomm will supply its Snapdragon X Series platform, providing general-purpose processing, graphics and on-device artificial intelligence. Anduril plans to manufacture the laptops in the United States, with circuit board assembly planned for its Arsenal-1 facility in Ohio. It is qualifying suppliers and developing domestic production capabilities for enclosures, battery components and other hardware ahead of planned availability in 2027. U.S. and allied-country suppliers account for more than 90% of the prototypes’ component procurement cost, according to Anduril. The company plans to expand American sourcing in stages, with a fully domestic supply chain as its long-term goal. The engineering work reflects the limits of the existing U.S. supply base, with the laptop being designed around materials and manufacturing capabilities available domestically. That includes an enclosure suited to U.S. machining, metals that American industry can produce at scale, battery and power systems adapted to existing U.S. battery technology, and a bonding process for American-made display glass. Anduril said dependence on foreign computer manufacturers leaves access to essential hardware vulnerable to conflict and overseas supply disruptions. While the United States has invested billions of dollars in semiconductor production, the company said complete computers also require circuit boards, displays, batteries and other components still largely made abroad. BlueChip is intended to serve first responders and public safety organizations alongside defense and government customers. Anduril said the supplier relationships, designs and production processes developed for the laptop would support further products in the range.

title: Arab voter turnout would have been lower had there been any other outgoing government - analysis
body: Throughout this campaign and into its final hours, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sounded the same alarm he has sounded throughout his political career: Arab citizens are flooding the polls and endangering his rule. For once, the outgoing prime minister was telling the truth. Arab Israelis are voting today in numbers not seen in decades, and they may well bring his reign to an end.The last time this happened was 1999. In one of Israel's few direct elections for prime minister, Arab voters turned out in large numbers to back Ehud Barak almost unanimously, helping oust Netanyahu for the first time and opening the door of the prime minister's office to Barak, Israel's last left-wing prime minister.Sixteen months later, in October 2000, police under Barak's government opened fire on Arab demonstrators protesting Ariel Sharon's visit to the Temple Mount, Al-Aqsa Mosque. Twelve Israeli citizens were shot and killed. The Or Commission of Inquiry later confirmed what every Arab Israeli had already known: There were grave failures in how the police and the state treat Arab citizens. It surprised no one that no police officer was ever charged.October 2000 became an open wound in Arab Israeli collective memory and a reason to keep a distance from the Israeli mainstream. That memory has kept many Arab citizens home in every election since.This time is different.Netanyahu's coalition has abandoned, betrayed Arab citizensThe memory of October 2000 has not faded, but it has been overtaken by the reality of the past four years, under a government that has done far more than neglect Arab citizens.Israel's outgoing coalition, the most radical in the country's history, not only tried to import the reality of the West Bank across the Green Line and into Israel proper. It also taught Israel's two million Arab citizens that a bad situation can always get worse if they accept their own political marginalization.This government left Arab communities at the mercy of criminal gangs, living amid anarchy and state absence, with little urgency from those responsible for public safety. Meanwhile, its mouthpieces in the media spewed relentless incitement against Arab citizens: doctors, journalists, elected officials, bus drivers, ordinary people. Without that, Arab turnout today might well have continued its decades-long decline. Instead, the government that did the most to push Arab citizens out of Israeli politics may be the one that brought them back.The easy reading of this historic turnout is that Arab citizens rallied behind their parties. That reading is wrong. The Arab Israeli political establishment is widely seen as a closed, exclusionary club: outdated, ineffective, and recycling the same faces and the same speeches. Some Arab citizens voted for Jewish-led parties today. Many who voted for Arab lists did so without enthusiasm.They came out of a sense of citizenship and shared responsibility, just as they did in October 2023, when they stood shoulder-to-shoulder with Jewish Israelis in the country's lowest, most painful moment. Then and now, they showed that they belong to this state, that they are willing to carry its burdens and share its fate, and that they will not be written out of it. For a community so often accused of standing apart, and even branded an enemy within, today's turnout declares the opposite. It is a cry from below, from people who have spent four years under the most far-right government in Israel's history.Arab citizens, Israel's 'kingmakers' In 2021, the only government to unseat Netanyahu in over a decade came to power because Ra'am, an Arab party, provided its majority. It was the first Arab party ever to join an Israeli coalition. The opposition took power on that basis and then spent years acting as though it should apologize for it.In this campaign, its leading figures refused even to say they would govern with an Arab-Israeli partner.Arab citizens know they are once again the kingmakers. They have put aside their doubts and shown up to defend a democracy that has not always defended them. Voting in such numbers while carrying the memory of October 2000 is an act of extraordinary trust, and trust given twice is not guaranteed a third time.The opposition need not embrace every Arab politician or every platform. But before coalition talks begin, it must say plainly that at least one Arab party is a legitimate partner in government.Anything less sends two million citizens a message they have heard before: Your vote counts when it is useful, but your voice has no place in shaping this country.The hand has been extended. The Jewish-majority opposition can take it, and with it lead Israel toward a different future.Or it can confirm everything October 2000 taught Israel's Arab citizens and hand the outgoing coalition the deadlock it desperately needs to stay in power.The choice is the opposition's alone. Will Israel be a democracy among the nations, where every vote counts? Or will it keep sliding toward an isolated, undemocratic, and racist ethnocracy?

title: Shas, UTJ projected to win 14 seats in next Knesset, CEC says after 4.8 million votes counted
body: Israel's two main haredi (ultra-Orthodox) parties, Shas and United Torah Judaism (UTJ), are expected to enter the next Knesset with 14 seats combined, according to results published by the Central Election Committee on Wednesday.Both parties are expected to get seven seats, after almost five million votes were counted by the CEC. UTJ received 6% of the votes, and Shas has 5.5%, according to the latest published data.The results would mark Shas's worst electoral performance in 27 years. Its leader, Arye Deri, did not address his supporters at the party's election headquarters in Jerusalem following the publication of exit polls on Tuesday night.Both Shas and UTJ are part of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's political bloc, and their combined seat total could prove crucial in determining whether he can secure the 61 seats needed for a Knesset majority.Neither party has committed to joining only a Netanyahu-led coalition, and Shas's spiritual leader has indicated that he would be open to joining a government led by prime ministerial candidate Gadi Eisenkot. This challenges the assumption that a vote for Shas necessarily translates into support for a Netanyahu-led government.The military draft was a major issue in the election, with the ultra-Orthodox parties facing pressure over their opposition to mandatory enlistment for yeshiva students. The next government's approach to haredi conscription is expected to be a key point in coalition negotiations.'Perhaps we will join': Haredi parties won't rule out working with EisenkotThe ultra-Orthodox parties have not ruled out cooperating with Yashar party chairman Gadi Eisenkot, N12 reported on Wednesday morning."If Eisenkot has any sense, he will form a government and not fill the [ministerial positions] that are important to us," source in the Shas party told N12.""If there is a reasonable conscription law, perhaps we will join later,” the source added.Eisenkot has previously said that he would not include haredi parties in his coalition, saying they did not meet his criteria for joining the government.

title: Israel election night: What did Israeli polls indicate after ending of voting?
body: No clear winner emerged in Israel's election, according to exit polls published by Channels 11, 12, and 13 on Tuesday night; all showed both Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc and the opposition bloc seeking to replace him falling short of a 61-seat Knesset majority.However, by Wednesday morning, some polls showed Netanyahu's bloc with a clear lead.Notably, the exit polls have differed from final results in previous elections, and the official results will be determined after ballots are counted.On Tuesday, the opposition bloc was projected to win 49-51 seats, compared with 51-52 for Netanyahu's bloc.On Wednesday morning, the opposition bloc had fallen to 48-19 across all three channels, and Netanyahu's bloc was projected to win 53-57 mandates. Channels 13 and 11 exit polls on Tuesday projected a tie at 51 seats each for Netanyahu's bloc and the opposition bloc, while Channel 12 projected Netanyahu's bloc to receive 52 seats.On Wednesday, Channels 11 and 12 projected Netanyahu's bloc to land 56 seats, and Channel 13 projected 55.Tuesday polling predicted Likud would win 27 seats, with Yashar projected to win 21-22 seats. Neither side appeared to have a clear path to forming a coalition, though the opposition bloc declared victory shortly after the exit polls were released. These numbers were largely unchanged on Wednesday morning, with Likud projected at 27-28 seats, and Yashar winning 21 mandates across all three polls. The Joint List and Ra'am were projected to win a record-breaking combined 18-19 seats, potentially making Arab parties pivotal to coalition negotiations. However, opposition leaders have largely ruled out forming a government with the Arab parties, barring the Democrats' Yair Golan. This number was reduced slightly on Wednesday morning, with the upper end of the range, 19, remaining the same, and the lower end dropping to 16. The final voter turnout number came out as  77.7% when polls closed at 10:00 p.m., according to the Central Elections Committee (CEC), up by 7.1% from the 2022 election.The small right-wing parties hovering near the electoral threshold, Ofer Winter's People of Israel and Yoaz Hendel's The Reservists-Economic party, were both projected to fall short of the required 3.25% threshold, potentially further complicating efforts by Netanyahu's bloc to secure a majority.Could Israel be heading toward a unity gov't - or another election?The prospect of a unity government involving Netanyahu and Eisenkot has appeared unlikely, as Eisenkot has rejected serving under Netanyahu, including in a rotation government. Other opposition leaders have also ruled out joining a coalition led by the prime minister.Eisenkot has called for the leader of the largest party in the opposition bloc to become its candidate for prime minister, though no agreement on the arrangement has been announced within the bloc.The exit polls also raised the possibility of a minority government that could win a Knesset confidence vote without holding an absolute majority of 61 seats. However, opposition within the bloc to relying on Arab parties could complicate such an arrangement.The political deadlock could ultimately lead to another election, although the parties may still reach an agreement through coalition negotiations.Opposition leaders declare exit poll results a victory for blocEisenkot and other opposition leaders declared the initial Tuesday exit poll results a victory for their bloc, saying Netanyahu's camp had been defeated.The Yashar party leader later gave a speech at the party headquarters in Tel Aviv, saying the country had voted against Netanyahu's government and that holding another election would be a mistake.Eisenkot also addressed the heads of Israel's security establishment, urging them not to allow Netanyahu to use national security for political gain. He warned against the prime minister issuing a potential attack due to the election results.“The prime minister is now a caretaker prime minister. Stand firm against any attempt to challenge you. You have my clear backing,” Eisenkot said.“Netanyahu, do not dare use security for political purposes,” he added.Earlier, following the release of the initial exit poll results, Eisenkot said they indicated “a complete lack of confidence in Netanyahu and his October 7 government among the Zionist majority and the majority of Israeli citizens.”“If these are the final results, they represent a victory for Israel's national-minded, Zionist majority,” he added.“I will act immediately to implement the people's decision, replace the Netanyahu government, and establish a Zionist government committed to military conscription as soon as possible,” Eisenkot said.Opposition leader Yair Lapid also declared Netanyahu's bloc defeated.“Don't let anyone confuse you: The Netanyahu bloc has suffered a crushing defeat. This is a total collapse, and the public has told them to go home,” he stated.Democrats party chairman Yair Golan said the results presented an opportunity to establish a new government.“The public has spoken. It has fired the Netanyahu government. We have been given a historic opportunity to establish a genuine government of change in Israel, and we have no intention of giving it up,” Golan said.“We are ready to work with all our partners, bridge the gaps, and take responsibility,” he added.Politicians in Netanyahu's bloc urged him to wait until later results were given. Ben-Gvir warned against a unity government with Eisenkot, calling it "a terrible mistake."If Eisenkot were to become prime minister, he would oust Netanyahu, whose right-wing government was in power during the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attacks and went on to serve its full term. Netanyahu is Israel's longest-serving prime minister, having held the office for more than 19 years in total.Following the October 7 massacre and the ensuing war, the opposition bloc has called for Netanyahu to be held accountable for the attacks, arguing that he should no longer serve as prime minister and calling for a state commission of inquiry to be established.Jerusalem Post Staff contributed to this report.

title: Vladimir Putin starts work at Russia-Africa Summit
body:
MOSCOW, October 28. /TASS/. Russian President Vladimir Putin is beginning an extensive series of events as part of the Russia-Africa Summit.
Wednesday’s agenda includes participation in the third Russia-Africa Economic Summit and Humanitarian Forum, a meeting with the heads of major regional organizations, and a formal reception hosted by the Russian president.
As Presidential Aide Yury Ushakov previously reported, 48 of Africa’s 54 countries will participate in this year’s summit, including 22 represented at the level of heads of state. The current chairperson of the African Union, President of Burundi Evariste Ndayishimiye, will co-chair various events alongside Putin.
The theme of the Economic and Humanitarian Forum is "Developing Mutually Beneficial Cooperation and Unlocking the Potential of Every African Country Together." The Russian president will also participate in its first plenary session.
According to Ushakov, Putin will assess the state of trade and economic relations between Russia and African countries in his address. Particular priority will be given to sovereign development on an equal footing, as well as ensuring African countries’ equitable access to resources, fertilizers, and modern technologies.
Following the plenary session, Putin will tour an exhibition at Gostiny Dvor together with African leaders. The exhibition will have a practical focus. In addition to showcasing ongoing Russian-African projects, it will highlight Russia’s advanced technologies and innovations that Moscow is prepared to share with its partners on the continent.
However, Wednesday’s events will extend well beyond the forum’s plenary session. The Russian president will receive representatives of Africa’s largest regional organizations who have arrived in Moscow at St. Andrew’s Hall, the most ceremonial and prestigious hall of the Grand Kremlin Palace.
The traditional meeting is expected to bring together representatives of the African Union, the African Continental Free Trade Area, the East African Community, the Intergovernmental Authority on Development, the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa, the Southern African Development Community, the Economic Community of Central African States, the Economic Community of West African States, the Arab Maghreb Union, and the African Export-Import Bank.
A formal reception hosted by the Russian president is also expected. As is customary, Putin will hold the event in the very heart of the Kremlin, the Faceted Chamber. Dating back to the Soviet era, such formal dinners have traditionally underscored the highest status of these meetings and the particularly warm relations with the countries represented by the distinguished guests.
The series of bilateral meetings that Putin began the previous day will also continue. On Tuesday, Moscow hosted a summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum. After holding multilateral discussions with his counterparts, Putin met separately with several of them, namely Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Emir of Qatar Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, President of the Republic of Mozambique Daniel Francisco Chapo, President of Equatorial Guinea Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo, and Chairman of Libya’s Presidential Council Mohamed al-Menfi.
The program will continue over the following two days. In particular, plenary sessions of the Russia-Africa Summit and further bilateral meetings are expected.
The Russia-Africa Summit is being held for the third time and for the first time in Moscow. St. Petersburg hosted the previous summit in the summer of 2023, while the inaugural summit took place in Sochi in the fall of 2019.

title: FG Approves Six-Month ₦70,000 Transport Support For Workers
body: The Federal Government has approved a ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, following a conciliation meeting with the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC). The agreement was reached at a meeting convened by the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment in Abuja on Tuesday, October 27, to address issues raised by organised labour. Under the agreement, the government also approved the payment of peculiar allowance arrears, effective from May 1, 2026, with payments scheduled to begin in November in three equal monthly instalments. The parties, however, failed to agree on the effective date for implementing the national minimum wage, although they agreed that the Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee would be constituted and begin meeting immediately. The resolutions were contained in a press statement issued by the Ministry of Labour and Employment after the meeting, which was chaired by the Minister, Dr Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi, with NLC President Joe Ajaero leading the labour delegation. On the transport intervention, the statement said the Federal Government “will pay a transport intervention of Seventy Thousand Naira (₦70,000) across all levels for a period of six (6) months, commencing from November 2026.” On peculiar allowances, the government approved payments with effect from May 1, 2026, with the arrears to be paid in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. A conciliation meeting between the FG and the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC). X/@LabourMinNG The statement also addressed outstanding allowances for health workers, stating that “Nineteen (19) months arrears of allowances for health workers will be redeemed within three (3) months with effect from December 2026.” On hazard allowances for agricultural workers, the ministry said the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security had submitted the list of beneficiaries and the cost implications to the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission (NSIWC) for verification. The verification is expected to be completed within two weeks, after which the commission will issue an implementation template. The parties also discussed the Consolidated Health Salary Structure (CONHESS) adjustment. According to the statement, NSIWC promised to complete the update of the cost implications within three weeks to enable the Presidential Committee on Salaries to decide on the adjustment. On tax relief for workers, the statement said the issue would be taken to the National Executive Council because taxation is a statutory matter. The meeting followed an earlier conciliation session held on October 22 and came after discussions on issues raised by the NLC’s Central Working Committee and National Executive Council. The government and labour representatives agreed to reconvene after one month to assess the level of implementation of the resolutions. The meeting also called on state and local governments to participate in the intervention process and urged unions to push for implementation at their respective levels. The post FG Approves Six-Month ₦70,000 Transport Support For Workers appeared first on Channels Television .

title: One dead, 14 injured in Akuse–Akosombo highway crash
body: One person has died, and 14 others have sustained serious injuries in a collision involving a Toyota Hiace and a Peugeot saloon car on the Akuse–Akosombo Highway in the Eastern Region. The crash occurred at Trey Court on Monday, October 26, prompting a response from the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) after its Kpong Fire Station received a distress call at 2:50 p.m. A six-member rescue team was dispatched two minutes later and arrived at the scene at 3 p.m., where it found the two vehicles had collided side-on. The GNFS said the collision left 14 people seriously injured, while a male victim died. The deceased was conveyed to St. Martin de Porres Hospital for preservation, while the injured were taken to the same facility for medical treatment. The vehicles involved were a Toyota Hiace with registration number GE 6558-25 and a Peugeot saloon car with registration number GT 5463-11. The cause of the collision had not been established as of Tuesday, October 27, according to a statement issued by the GNFS Public Relations Officer for the Eastern Region. The incident adds to concerns about road safety, particularly the risk of serious injuries and fatalities when vehicles collide on highways. Investigations are expected to establish the circumstances that led to the crash.

title: People of Israel, Reservists-Economic Party, Haredi Public all projected to fall short of threshold
body: Three new parties that entered Israel's 2026 election campaign polling near the electoral threshold failed to secure seats in the Knesset, according to official results published by the Central Elections Committee (CEC) on Wednesday.People of Israel, led by former IDF Brig.-Gen. Ofer Winter, the Reservists-Economic Party, led by former communications minister Yoaz Hendel and economist Yaron Zelekha, and Haredi Public, led by Moti Leitner, were all projected to fall short of the 3.25% electoral threshold required to be allocated any seats in the Knesset.The Reservists-Economic Party received 2.63% of the vote, with 127,844 valid votes counted as of 15 p.m. Wednesday. People of Israel received 1.61% with 78,377 votes counted. Haredi Public received 0.20% of the vote with 9,502 eligible votes counted thus far.People of Israel campaigned on a right-wing security platform, advocating tougher action against Hamas while also supporting greater ultra-Orthodox participation in military service.Winter declared his party to be part of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc but challenged the prime minister on several issues during the election campaign and repeatedly called for new faces in Israel's parliament.Despite challenging the establishment, new parties projected to fall short of KnessetThe Reservists-Economic Party campaigned on expanding military service to include more ultra-Orthodox Israelis and addressing Israel's economic challenges. Hendel did not commit to joining either political bloc, instead calling for a broad Zionist government to be formed following the election.Haredi Public sought to offer an alternative to the established ultra-Orthodox parties, Shas and United Torah Judaism, with a focus on representing the haredi (ultra-Orthodox) public.The parties' failure to clear the threshold could affect the distribution of Knesset seats among the parties that qualify, as votes cast for parties that fall short are not included in the allocation of seats.The exit polls are preliminary projections. The final outcome will depend on the official vote count and the allocation of Knesset seats.People of Israel officials: Winter's campaign did not cost Netanyahu's bloc seatsOfficials from Ofer Winter's People of Israel party said, following an initial analysis of the exit poll results, that the seat distribution would have shifted against the right-wing bloc if Winter had withdrawn from the race.They claimed that Yoaz Hendel and Yaron Zelekha would have passed the electoral threshold, adding four seats to the left-wing bloc.The officials also argued that the vast majority of votes cast for Winter came from voters outside the governing coalition, dismissing claims that the party had wasted votes as “absurd.”

title: Ecobank Group profit before tax hits US$737 million for first nine months of 2026
body: Ecobank Group has reported continued growth in its financial results for the first nine months of 2026, despite an operating environment characterised by inflationary pressures, foreign exchange volatility and slower economic activity in parts of Africa. The Group reported profit before tax of US$737 million, up 12% year-on-year, while net revenue increased 12% to US$2.0 billion. Growth was supported by a continued focus on operational efficiency, customer deposit mobilisation, technology investments and disciplined execution of the Group’s Growth, Transformation and Returns (GTR) strategy. Ecobank continued to strengthen its balance sheet, with customer deposits growing to US$27.5 billion while maintaining a strong liquidity and capital position. The Group’s cost-to-income ratio improved to 47.8%, ahead of its target range of 48% to 50%, reflecting ongoing efficiency initiatives across the business. Performance was supported by Ecobank’s diversified business model and geographic footprint. Central, Eastern and Southern Africa (CESA) delivered a 20% increase in profit before tax, while Anglophone West Africa (AWA) recorded 10% growth, offsetting softer results in Francophone West Africa (UEMOA) and Nigeria. These results demonstrate the resilience of the group’s franchise across multiple markets. The Group also continued to benefit from balanced contributions from its corporate and investment banking and commercial and consumer banking businesses. Ecobank’s payments and digital businesses remained important growth drivers. Payment revenue increased by 9%, supported by sustained investment in technology platforms and digital capabilities designed to enhance customer experience and expand financial inclusion across Africa. Key highlights Net revenue increased 12% year-on-year to US$2 billion, while profit before tax increased 12% year-on-year to US$737 million, demonstrating strong business momentum despite macroeconomic and geopolitical headwinds. Operational efficiency continued to improve, with the cost-to-income ratio reaching 47.8%, ahead of the Group’s 2026 target range. Customer deposits increased 14% year-on-year to US$27.5 billion, demonstrating strong customer confidence and the strength of Ecobank’s deposit franchise. Performance remained broadly diversified across regions and businesses, with CESA increasing profit before tax by 20% and AWA by 10%, complemented by contributions from both corporate and investment banking and commercial and consumer banking. Group CEO on financial performance According to Group CEO Jeremy Awori, “We achieved a profit before tax of $737 million, an increase of 12% year-on-year, and a return on tangible equity of 24.9%. Net revenue also grew by 12%, reaching $2.0 billion.” He added that “Our Growth, Transformation, and Returns strategy is clearly reflected in our efficiency and franchise performance. He also stated that the Group’s cost-to-income ratio was 47.8%, ahead of its 2026 target range of 48% to 50%. Customer deposits rose 14% to $27.5 billion, with current and savings accounts accounting for 85% of the total. “This reflects the confidence and trust our customers have in us and in using us for their day-to-day banking. This growth has helped mitigate margin pressure from the rate-easing cycle in our markets, lifting net interest income by 12%. Payment revenue also rose 9%, supported by our continued investment in technology and digital platforms. The strength of our diversified business model was evident as profit before tax increased by 20% in Central Eastern and Southern Africa (CESA) and by 10% in Anglophone West Africa (AWA), offsetting softer results in Francophone West Africa (UEMOA) and Nigeria,” he explained. Awori added, “Our non-performing loan (NPL) ratio remained broadly stable during the quarter at 7.5%, which is within our 2026 target range of 6% to 8%, reflecting continued discipline in portfolio and risk management.” In conclusion, Awori remarked, “Energy prices, inflation, and foreign exchange volatility are real risks as we move through the remainder of the year. However, our strong deposit base, liquidity and capital position, combined with our new products and propositions, position us well to drive further growth while maintaining a disciplined approach to risk. We remain on track to meet our 2026 targets. I want to thank the Ecobank team for their dedication to serving our customers every day.” Continued momentum beyond financial performance During the quarter, Ecobank continued to strengthen its international presence through the opening of its new Beijing Representative Office premises and the signing of a protocol with the Chinese Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS). The Group also concluded its Ecobank@40 celebrations with a US$2.6 billion commitment aimed at supporting women-owned businesses and agriculture across Africa. Ecobank’s leadership was further recognised at the Global Finance Awards during the World Bank and IMF Meetings, where the Group received prestigious distinctions, including Best Bank in Africa 2026 and World’s Best Frontier Markets Bank 2026. These achievements underscore Ecobank’s continued commitment to innovation, customer service and sustainable growth across the continent.

title: Liberman calls for revolt within Likud, predicts better election results
body: Yisrael Beytenu chairman Avigdor Liberman remained silent for 90 minutes after the release of Tuesday night's exit polls before delivering a speech at his party's election headquarters, where he declined to commit to his next political moves. "I apologize for arriving late. I had to stop by my doctor's office for surgery to lengthen my fuse," Liberman joked, suggesting that patience would be needed before the final results became clear. He said he was not convinced the exit polls accurately reflected the election outcome, pointing out that votes equivalent to roughly 15 Knesset seats were still to be counted from special double-envelope ballots. "I assume we'll only see the actual results early Friday morning or sometime Friday morning," he explained.   According to the exit polls published by Kan 11, Channel 12 and Channel 13, the bloc seeking to replace Netanyahu holds a slight advantage over the prime minister's bloc, although Likud remains the largest party. Yisrael Beytenu is projected to win seven to eight seats. Liberman argued that the double-envelope ballots, which include votes cast by soldiers and other voters using special voting arrangements, would reduce the relative strength of the Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties. "That means it's very important to be patient," Liberman said. "By Friday, we'll know much more, and we'll be able to talk about a much better and more optimistic picture than the one we're seeing today." Liberman described the election as a difficult campaign. "We competed under unreasonable conditions as a liberal right-wing party, facing an impossible reality," he said. "If we've achieved a reasonably good result, it's thanks to each and every one of you sitting here." He accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of having "behaved today like the head of a criminal organization, crossing every red line." Liberman also referred to WhatsApp services being disabled and text messages being sent, adding that he would not elaborate. He stopped short of committing to his party's next steps in the effort to form a government. "We'll wait for the actual results and then consult," he said. Liberman went on to attack Channel 14 and Netanyahu supporters, whom he accused of inciting against him. "We will establish a Zionist coalition and put an end to the incitement," he declared. "It's important to form a government committed to the values of the Zionist movement. We will build an exemplary movement, a model for others to follow." He then issued a direct call for rebellion within Likud, urging party members and lawmakers to turn against Netanyahu. "I received dozens of phone calls from Likud members," Liberman said. "This man must leave the stage, and anyone loyal to the path of Herzl, Trumpeldor and Jabotinsky must get rid of him. Raise the banner of revolt within Likud." Addressing Likud Central Committee members, local party activists and Knesset lawmakers, Liberman added: "What you say privately, behind closed doors, it's time to say publicly. It's time to tell the truth, not just in closed rooms." He continued: "This man has destroyed the national camp and is destroying everything good. That's the key to preserving the national camp, rather than leaving it in the hands of a bunch of opportunists protecting their privileges." The Yisrael Beytenu chairman left the stage to the sounds of the song "You Won't Defeat Me," accompanied by applause. Liberman founded Yisrael Beytenu in 1999 and has led it ever since, for 27 years. Apart from serving as prime minister, he has held virtually every senior government position, including defense minister, foreign minister and finance minister. At its peak, Yisrael Beytenu won 15 Knesset seats in 2009. Since then, when running independently, the party has failed to reach double digits. In the previous election, it secured six seats. For many years, the overwhelming majority of Yisrael Beytenu lawmakers were immigrants from the former Soviet Union. This time, however, only Yulia Malinovsky joins Liberman among the party's senior figures from that background. Liberman placed Rafi Ben Shitrit, the former mayor of Beit She'an whose son was killed on October 7, 2023, second on the party's electoral list.

title: Meet LEANN: An Open-Source Vector Index that Shrinks a 60M-Chunk RAG Index from 201 GB to 6 GB
body: UC Berkeley’s Sky Computing Lab built LEANN , an open-source vector index that stores almost no embeddings. The LEANN vector index recomputes embeddings at query time instead of saving them to disk. The repo benchmark shows a 60 million chunk Wikipedia index dropping from 201 GB to 6 GB. The research paper won the Best Research Paper award at MLSys 2026 . So, it brings semantic search and RAG over personal data, on a laptop. TL;DR Size: 6 GB for 60M chunks ( repo ); 4 GB in the paper’s 76 GB Wikipedia setup. Default embedder: Contriever (110M params). It is an index, not an LLM, so no context length applies. Runs on: laptops and workstations. The paper tested an RTX 4090 box with 32 GB RAM and an M1 Ultra Mac. A CPU-only Linux install exists, with no published CPU latency. Performance: matches HNSW downstream accuracy at 90% recall, using under 5% of raw-data storage. Best: 25.5% NQ accuracy, identical to HNSW, using 4 GB instead of 188 GB. Worst: HotpotQA retrieval takes 44.80 s on the Mac, 50.1% of total pipeline time. What is LEANN? LEANN is a low-storage approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) index built on top of FAISS . It targets one problem: vector indexes are often bigger than the data they index. The research paper shows a 76 GB corpus needs 173 GB of embeddings plus a 15 GB HNSW graph. That more than doubles the raw data. LEANN keeps a pruned graph, drops the full vectors, and rebuilds them on demand. The code is MIT licensed and installs with uv pip install leann . How does LEANN recompute embeddings without stalling search? Graph indexes like HNSW visit only a small set of nodes per query. LEANN exploits that. It stores the graph plus a compact product quantization (PQ) table. At query time, it re-embeds only nodes on the search path. 3 techniques keep this practical: Two-level search: cheap PQ distances rank neighbors first. Only top candidates get exact recomputation. Dynamic batching: candidates from several hops are grouped, for example 64 at once, for GPU efficiency. High-degree preserving pruning: most nodes keep few edges, while the top 2% “hub” nodes keep more. In ablations, two-level search gives an average 1.4x speedup. Adding batching raises it to 1.8x. Embedding recomputation still accounts for about 76% of query latency. (function(){var f=document.getElementById('mtp-leann-frame');window.addEventListener('message',function(e){if(e.source===f.contentWindow&&e.data&&e.data.mtpLeannH){f.style.height=e.data.mtpLeannH+'px';}});})(); How does LEANN perform on benchmarks? The research team tested NQ, TriviaQA, GPQA and HotpotQA against a 60M-passage RPJ-Wiki datastore. Latency is measured at 90% Recall@3. All figures below are self-reported in the research paper . On NQ, with Qwen3-4B on an RTX 4090, LEANN and HNSW both reach 25.5% downstream accuracy. LEANN uses 4 GB of storage. HNSW uses 188 GB. BM25 scores 18.3%, and PQ compression scores 17.9%. The cost is search time. LEANN retrieval takes 2.48 s on NQ, versus 0.05 s for HNSW. Generation takes about 20 s, so end-to-end latency rises from 20.95 s to 23.34 s. Across datasets on the RTX 4090, LEANN retrieval ranges from 1.12 s (GPQA) to 7.12 s (HotpotQA). The IVF-based recomputation baseline, inspired by EdgeRAG , is up to 200x slower. LEANN improves exact match by up to 11.8% over BM25. The GitHub repo reports similar savings on personal data. 400K chat messages shrink from 1.8 GB to 64 MB. 38K browser entries shrink from 130 MB to 6.4 MB. LEANN vs other vector indexes Feature LEANN HNSW (FAISS) DiskANN IVF-Recompute (EdgeRAG-style) PQ compression Approach Pruned graph, recompute on demand Graph plus all vectors in RAM Graph and vectors on SSD, PQ in RAM IVF clusters, recompute on demand Compressed vectors plus graph Storage, 76 GB corpus 4 GB 188 GB 270 GB Below 5% of raw data 20 GB NQ retrieval at 90% recall (RTX 4090) 2.48 s 0.05 s 0.03 s 307.61 s Fails to reach 90% HotpotQA retrieval at 90% recall (RTX 4090) 7.12 s 0.05 s 0.11 s 429.46 s Fails to reach 90% NQ downstream accuracy (Qwen3-4B) 25.5% 25.5% Not disclosed Not disclosed 17.9% Fits 32 GB RAM workstation Yes No (OOM) Yes Yes Yes License MIT MIT MIT Not disclosed Varies by implementation Storage, latency and accuracy figures come from the LEANN paper v2 , Tables 1 and 2 and Section 7.2 (self-reported). License and design rows link to each project’s own source. Where can developers use LEANN? The repo ships ready apps for documents, Apple Mail, Chrome history, WeChat, iMessage, and ChatGPT or Claude exports. MCP readers pull live data from Slack and Twitter bookmarks. LEANN also runs as a semantic search MCP server for Claude Code . On 30 SWE-Bench Pro tasks from ContextBench, the team reports 24.2% initial relevant-code recall versus 11.4% for BM25. The agent also used 8.4% fewer tokens. HNSW is the default backend, with DiskANN for faster search. Generation works with Ollama, Hugging Face, Anthropic, or any OpenAI-compatible API. It supports Ubuntu, Arch, WSL, macOS and Windows. Some apps, like Apple Mail search, are macOS only. Key Takeaways LEANN stores a pruned graph and recomputes embeddings at query time. 60M chunks: 201 GB down to 6 GB in the repo benchmark. Matches HNSW accuracy (25.5% on NQ) at 90% recall. Search costs seconds: 2.48 s vs 0.05 s for HNSW on NQ. MIT licensed and an MLSys 2026 Best Research Paper. Check out the Paper , GitHub Repo and PyPI package . title: Kwesi Yankah: ‘Awengaa’ teacher on the loose as women march in protest
body: Two years ago, my sleep was disturbed by news of child rapists on the prowl disguised as customary rites. Here they come again this time in partisan costume. Listen to an excerpt from my write-up, 2024, on ‘Awengaa:’ We were careful those days in Duakwa not to be shamed and mocked as ‘Awengaa.’ A thirty-year-old man who had ‘slept’ with an underage girl; he was Awengaa. A forty-year-old having his way with a class four girl; they tagged him ‘Awengaa.’ He had grey hair, and the girl was only eight: Awengaa. So young girls took to their heels when they saw him from afar: ‘they say if you cross his red line, hmmmm.’ Little girls would giggle and scamper off. In cases where the victim was really a baby, the idiom carried a literal meaning: Awengaa: ‘a predator of crying babies.’ Paedophile! “It was a virtual taboo, a serious cultural breach. If caught, the offender would be paraded in the streets, gong gong, with songs of shame and boos trailing: ‘Waware ne ba, Akwasi,’ the song stigmatising the bad man. ‘He has slept with a girl young enough to be his daughter.’ The publicity was to caution the innocent one who might mistakenly make an Awengaa’s home a temporary day care: ‘Look after my girl-child until I return from the farm.’ Times have changed. The notorious Awengaa this time may be Your beloved Teacher Mensah;’ worse still, Master Mensah himself: the Big Boss among the Teachers. In Ogyakromian lingo, the Big man ‘himself himself;’ the alpha and omega! The school’s ultimate role model caught pants down! So then it could no longer be said of Master: ‘Suffer the children to come unto Master, for they shall be safe.’Master is no longer a safe refuge! No longer a Head Master, but a Bad Master. Under his care, he could give the kids a bad touch when nobody is watching, or lure them to a secret site and defile them. Not in those days; not Teacher Biney, not Teacher Ansah. Whether in primary or high school, the pattern gets worse and worse: mmɔndaa at school—rape, defilement, having your way with little school girls. The situation gets uglier when higher school authorities summon an Awengaa for sanctions. Hear the authorities’ sanctions for child rape: ‘Ladies and gentlemen, as punishment for this serious offence, we have decided to transfer Awengaa to another school… this time to a village without electricity!’ Here, the announced penalty is indeed a certificate of merit: a handshake meant to help Awengaa spread the virus in darkness! Other times, Awengaa himself, once caught and suspended, may decide to leave the classroom voluntarily and go to the safe haven of politics, where no one checks backgrounds. If he has failed as a custodian of underage girls, he may be a great Party ‘Chaaarman!’ Elsewhere, a concerned local community upset by the soft penalty may take a landmark decision: ‘Henceforth, all authorities that give any Awengaa a slap on the wrist, instead of a harsh penalty, shall be declared as suspects themselves. They are all Awengaa…. Awengaa sɔɔɔn: Monkye wɔn! So why wasn’t the long delay after the Obuasi scandal surprising? Remember the calendar of events. April 2025: suspicion that the new Headmaster was indeed a Bad Master; February 2026: a formal petition about him is sent to authorities.March: multiple reports about him; July/August: concerned old students petition authorities; August: students go on a rampage on campus and attack the ‘Bad Master.’ Education Ministry launches an Inquiry; on 14 October, Obuasi Awengaa is suspended…and an eternal CID probe begins. By the end of October, the everlasting probe continues with no end in sight. Since 2025, Awengaa has allegedly defiled several girls, hiding beneath his zip a total of 19 victims. Pɔr pɔr pɔr pɔr19; enough for a Guinness Book of Awengaa, or a Ballon d’Or! Surprisingly, Ghana, your beloved country, is mute, arms folded! No word on the investigations, not even an invite like, ‘Bad Master, please see the police.’ Madam Lydia Donkor, Head of CID. We haven’t seen your ‘red eyes’ yet. Where is your magic that swiftly brought down Salomey from Techiman while investigating ‘Ghana Jollof ‘? Remember, that lady, Salomey, had three kids but found herself painfully separated from them by 370 kilometres. Despite the distance, the arrest was swift. What then slows down the arrest of a suspected paedophile? Auntie Lydia, Salomey’s youngest child was only five years. You yourself are a mother of twins. That lady was in remand for a month without her kids; and kids without mummy for a month. In the case of the rape victims in Obuasi, while they and their families reel in pain, the predator is comfortably at rest, not on remand, nor on bail, nor in jail, nor in court. Is the state pampering a paedophile? Auntie Lydia, Aww! Asɛm yi yɛ yaw! The rape victims could be the future of your own twin girls or anybody’s daughters desperately crying for swift justice. Yet your outfit is not in a hurry, and eyebrows are raised. So then, our verdict. The education authorities who have been spectators for 16 months, pampering a suspected paedophile: A case to answer. Director CID, seeing no evil, hearing no evil; Mother of twin girls, there is a case to answer. Venue? The bar of public opinion. Then this bombshell that belittles all else. The case of an apolitical activist who, on camera, plays down the rape case in a blatant self-confession. Hear his words: ‘Why are we behaving as if it is not normal to rape? How many of you have never raped a woman?” Those were the words of a ruling-party communicator. So far, no denial, no condemnation; no distancing. The loud silence simply means, ‘Say it Loud, Brother! Rape is normal.’ It’s quite clear this frightening rape case has taken a political turn. The suspect being a party activist, a guilty verdict may give his party the dreaded name: Awengaa People’s Party. The Opposition may be waiting to justify the name change, so they’ll keep pussyfooting until Harmattan winds blow the case away. If the Awengaa suspect is proven innocent, Tweaaa, I will join the all-night Miracle service. Are we sacrificing our kids’ future for political power? Oh my God! Where are the Mrs Mary Grants of yesteryear? Our beloved Jane Naana? The majority women’s caucus? We need words from within that call the Reset team to order, and simply plead: ‘JM, please don’t let down your children.’ The last time I heard from the Ministry of Gender and Children’s Protection, the Minister on TV was speaking English in the future tense! And Haruna, the Minister for Education: English grammar in the future tense. The Vice Presidency? English grammar in the future tense. Happily, I hear the bells ringing for a peaceful demo this week. The red eyes of women activists seek Justice for our kids In the meantime, please keep our girl kids off the streets. Awengaa Teacher is still at large. ******* The writer can be contacted via email at kyankah@ashesi.edu.gh

title: ‘I have a duty to serve Nigeria, and I will’ — Adesina tells Tinubu
body:
Former President of the African Development Bank (AfDB), Akinwumi Adesina, has declared his readiness to serve Nigeria in any capacity, saying he has a duty and responsibility to contribute to the country’s development.
Mr Adesina made the declaration on Tuesday after meeting President Bola Tinubu at the Presidential Villa in Abuja, where he briefed the president on his 10-year tenure at the continental development finance institution.
“I’m fully able to help Nigeria in any capacity. I’ve always had that. You know, my heart is always at home,” he told journalists after the meeting.
Asked what role he could play, Mr Adesina said he would help in any capacity the president considered appropriate, but stressed he was not seeking a government appointment.
“I’m not looking for a job. I’m not looking for anything. I’m just here to help. It’s my country. I have a duty, an obligation, and a responsibility to do so, and I will,” he said.
There was no announcement of a specific role or appointment for the former AfDB president following the meeting.
Mr Adesina, an agricultural economist, served as Nigeria’s minister of agriculture and rural development from 2011 to 2015 under former President Goodluck Jonathan before becoming the first Nigerian to lead the AfDB.
He was elected president of the bank in May 2015 and re-elected for a second five-year term in August 2020. His tenure ended in 2025.
As agriculture minister, he championed reforms to the distribution of subsidised farm inputs, including an electronic-wallet system that let farmers receive support for seeds and fertiliser via mobile phones.
The AfDB said the programme reached 15 million farmers within its first four years. The initiative was intended to improve access to agricultural inputs while reducing the role of intermediaries in their distribution.
At the AfDB, Mr Adesina oversaw the institution’s development agenda, which included expanding electricity access, improving food security, industrialising African economies, promoting regional integration and improving living standards.
During his leadership, the bank’s general capital increased from $93 billion to $208 billion in 2019, following a decision by its shareholders, the largest capital increase in the institution’s history at the time.
At the meeting, Mr Adesina said the AfDB provided about $7 billion in financing to Nigeria between 2015 and 2025.
He compared this with the $11.1 billion in cumulative financing the bank had provided to Nigeria since it began operations in the country in 1971.
“Within 10 years, we were able to do 63 per cent, literally, of that,” he said, adding that President Tinubu was pleased with the bank’s support to Nigeria during his tenure.
Mr Adesina said he used the meeting to commend the president for his economic reforms, particularly the removal of the petrol subsidy and the harmonisation of the foreign exchange windows.
He described the measures as difficult but said they were beginning to produce results.
He cited increased foreign exchange availability, the return of portfolio investors and a downward trend in inflation as signs of progress. However, he acknowledged that prices remained high for Nigerians.
He also pointed to improved assessments of Nigeria by some international rating agencies, saying the country’s outlook had shifted towards stable or positive assessments.
The comments come amid ongoing debate over the impact of the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms, including higher fuel costs after the removal of the petrol subsidy and changes to the foreign exchange market.
Although the government has defended the measures as necessary to stabilise the economy, the higher cost of living has continued to put pressure on households and businesses.
Mr Adesina said stabilising the economy was only the beginning, arguing that Nigeria must now focus on structural transformation, economic growth and prosperity.
He said President Tinubu recognised the need to move beyond macroeconomic reforms and address the broader challenge of transforming the economy.
“I told the president, I’m back at home, here to help and ready to help. It’s my country. I love my country, and I’m ready to help,” he said.
His offer comes after a decade leading one of Africa’s major development finance institutions, a period during which the bank financed projects and programmes across sectors including agriculture, energy, transport and infrastructure.
Mr Adesina’s meeting with the president also gave him an opportunity to formally brief the president on the completion of his two terms and the achievements recorded during his leadership of the bank.
He said he was honoured to have been received by the president and was pleased with the report he presented.
While Mr Adesina did not specify how he might contribute to Nigeria’s development, he said he was prepared to do so whenever the president believed his experience could be useful.
“It’s my country. I have a duty, an obligation, and a responsibility to do so, and I will,” he said.

title: Pentagon to Give Startup Stoke Space $150M Loan for New Launch Pad
body: The Pentagon plans to issue a $150 million loan to Stoke Space Technologies, an emerging space launch provider, to help it expand its footprint at Cape Canaveral Space Force Base, Fla. The Defense Department announced the plan Oct. 26. The loan, managed by DOD’s Office of Strategic Capital, is contingent on Stoke clearing various financial, legal, and technical requirements. “The proposed loan from OSC, alongside private capital, would support the buildout of the company’s second launchpad at its existing launch complex at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station,” the Pentagon said in a statement. “The OSC commitment to Stoke Space more broadly supports the expansion of U.S. launch capacity, which is required to meet the rising demand for commercial and national security space launch by the United States Space Force.” The Pentagon established OSC in 2022 to help connect firms developing critical defense technology with private capital. The loan agreement with Stoke is one of several conditional deals OSC has announced this month alone. On Oct. 8, it revealed a plan to issue a $1.5 billion loan to Wolfspeed, Inc. to build advanced semiconductor components and materials, and on Oct. 17, it signed a conditional commitment with Antheia, Inc., to scale its biomanufacturing efforts. Stoke’s first launch pad, located at the Cape’s Space Launch Complex-14, is slated to host the debut flight of its Nova rocket in “the first part of 2027,” according to the company’s current schedule. That vehicle is a pathfinder for the firm’s future Nova Block 2 rocket—a fully reusable rocket designed to deliver 15 metric tons to low-Earth orbit. The first stage of Stoke Space’s Nova rocket moves through final integration. (Stoke Space) Stoke plans to fly multiple Nova missions in 2027 and 2028 to fuel its plans for Block 2, which it expects will log its first flight in 2029. The company announced in September that it had raised $1 billion in private capital to accelerate development of its Nova line. The firm hasn’t disclosed when it expects to break ground on the second facility, and a Stoke spokesperson did not respond to questions about those plans or the OSC deal. In September, it said it has started construction of a new payload processing facility that can service both the first Nova iteration, which it calls Pathfinder, and the Block 2 version. The company has also started work on the offshore platform that will recover both rockets after launch. While Nova has yet to lift off, the Space Force in 2025 tapped the company to compete for missions under its National Security Space Launch Phase 3 Lane 1 contract , which the service uses to fly smaller payloads with less stringent requirements. To be eligible for Lane 1 flights, firms must have flown their rockets at least once; at the time, Stoke projected Nova would launch by 2026. Space Force officials are eager for new rockets to enter the market amid broader market concerns about a forthcoming launch bottleneck as SpaceX pursues plans to retire its Falcon 9 workhorse and rely on its Starship super heavy rocket to fly mostly internal Starlink missions. Asked during an Oct. 21 media briefing about the service’s concerns about SpaceX’s new business model, Col. Eric Zarynisky, portfolio acquisition executive for space access, said the Space Force has regular conversations with current and potential NSSL providers about their business plans. “I’m seeing a lot of growth in those new providers, and being able to use those to support the customers that we see coming on in the national security space launch side,” he said. “We’re talking to all of the providers . . . about their future plans and then talking to them about where we see our manifest going. It is an ongoing conversation.” The post Pentagon to Give Startup Stoke Space $150M Loan for New Launch Pad appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .

title: The E-commerce revolution Ghana built for itself
body: How Instagram, TikTok, WhatsApp, MoMo and a network of dispatch riders are quietly building a uniquely Ghanaian kind of trust. There is a version of e-commerce we’ve all been taught to recognise. A polished website. A clean catalogue. An “Add to Cart” button. Card details are typed in carefully. A confirmation email. A branded van at your door a day or two later. It works. It’s efficient. It’s also a very particular idea of what digital commerce is supposed to look like, and it’s not, for the most part, the one Ghana is actually living. Spend an afternoon on Instagram or WhatsApp in Accra or Kumasi and you’ll see something else entirely. A young woman posts a video of a seamstress putting the finishing touches on an emerald-green dress, filmed on a phone, in a small studio, with the sound of a fan somewhere in the background. Someone comments: “How much?” Within minutes, the conversation slides into WhatsApp, the way conversations here always do. A voice note confirms the size. A MoMo number is sent. Payment goes through, and a screenshot comes back like a handshake. A dispatch rider is called, jumps on a motorbike, and threads through traffic to make the delivery. The parcel arrives. There was no shopping cart. No API. No checkout page. And yet two people who will probably never meet have just completed a fully digital transaction, built entirely on tools they already trusted before any of this had a name. Scroll over to TikTok and you’ll find a version that’s even more precise about it. Live selling videos run through racks of clothes, item by item, and the comments beneath them have developed a shorthand of their own. W for “want,” the first person to comment claims it. P for “pass,” move to the next item. D for “done,” the item has been sold and screenshotted as proof. Shopify is barely used here. TikTok’s own shopping tools aren’t available in the region. And yet, out of nothing but comment sections and common sense, an entire claims-and-fulfilment protocol assembled itself, understood instantly by everyone in the comments, taught to no one, written down nowhere. For years we’ve measured Ghana’s e-commerce progress against models built somewhere else: how many big marketplaces, how many saved cards, where is our Amazon. But maybe the revolution already happened, and we simply called it social media. Ghanaians didn’t wait for a perfect e-commerce ecosystem to arrive. Sellers just stitched together the platforms and habits already woven into daily life. Instagram and TikTok became the storefront. WhatsApp became the sales desk, the same app carrying family group chats and “good morning” messages now carrying enquiries, in the same warm register. MoMo became the checkout, borrowing the trust people already extend when sending a cousin transport money. The screenshot became the receipt. And thousands of independent riders became a logistics network nobody had to design. This matters because traditional e-commerce can be an expensive door to walk through: a website, hosting, payment integration, inventory software, professional photography, advertising, fulfilment- all before a business starts to look “proper.” Social commerce removes almost all of that. A baker can test a new product this afternoon and be taking orders by evening. A tailor working from a small room can reach customers well beyond his neighbourhood. Someone with nothing but a phone and something worth selling can simply begin. None of it works, though, without trust, and nobody handed these sellers a framework for that. They built their own, out of instinct and experience. Some ask for full payment upfront, especially on custom orders, because they’ve been let down before and need to protect what it costs to prepare one. Some buyers won’t pay until the item is in front of them, a quiet standoff one commentator recently described as buyers and sellers “playing chicken” with payment timing. Often the two meet in the middle: the customer covers the rider’s fee first, so that whoever changes their mind, the rider, who’s done nothing but agree to carry a parcel across town, isn’t the one left out of pocket. None of this came from a strategy document. It evolved through experience, and it’s worth resisting the urge to file it away as mere informality. Every one of those small workarounds is actually telling us something. A seller manually matching MoMo alerts against customer screenshots is pointing at a reconciliation problem worth solving. A buyer who insists on payment on delivery is showing us exactly where trust runs out. A stalled order because no rider was available is a logistics gap with a name. The appetite for digital money is already proven at a scale that’s hard to overstate. The Bank of Ghana reported that mobile money transactions reached GH¢4.54 trillion in 2025, up 50.8% on the year before. Ghanaians don’t need convincing that money can move digitally. They already send it, receive it and settle bills with it every day. So the right question probably isn’t: How do we get Ghanaians to adopt e-commerce? It’s how we make the e-commerce they’re already practising a little safer, a little easier, a little more able to hold their trust. That distinction points somewhere specific. The opportunity probably isn’t one giant marketplace trying to own the whole journey from discovery to delivery. It’s the quieter infrastructure that connects what people are already using: a lightweight escrow layer on top of MoMo, so a buyer’s payment is held until delivery is confirmed. The seller knows the funds are real; the buyer knows the money is safe. A WhatsApp sale that can trigger a delivery request automatically, with the nearest rider, a fair fee and live tracking attached without anyone having to think about it. And perhaps the quietest opportunity of all is reputation. A tailor or baker or skincare seller can build hundreds of successful transactions through WhatsApp and MoMo and still be invisible to the formal financial system: no history a bank would recognise, no file a lender could open. But those transactions already tell a story of consistent sales, repeat customers, a fulfilment record built one satisfied customer at a time. Give that story a form anyone can verify, and a small business someone built from a bedroom studio suddenly has something more valuable than a following. It has a track record. And a track record can become access to capital it would otherwise never see. Other markets built their e-commerce around a website, a cart, a card and a courier. Ghana is building something that runs on discovery, conversation, mobile money, hard-won trust and delivery, and the difference isn’t a lesser version of the same idea. One system tries to remove the human being from the transaction. The other depends on them. The voice note matters. The W, the P, the D, the seller sending a photo before dispatch: these aren’t inefficiencies waiting to be automated away. In many cases, they’re the very things making a stranger feel safe enough to send money to another stranger. The task now isn’t to replace any of that. It’s to make it a little sturdier without taking away what makes it feel human in the first place. Across Accra and Kumasi and every town between them, inside Instagram DMs and WhatsApp voice notes and TikTok comment sections and a phone call to a dispatch rider, millions of small transactions are already happening, carried by people who worked out how to trust each other before anyone built them a platform for it. The e-commerce revolution isn’t coming to Ghana. It’s already here, running on relationships. The technology just needs to catch up to it. By: Raphael Beinamwin/Business Unit Director, rfgPHD Ghana Limited. This piece grew out of a LinkedIn conversation started by Efuwa Quansah, COO at Ostec, on the ingenuity of Ghana’s informal commerce.

title: Trump Administration Weighs Lifting Sanctions on Kremlin’s Investment Fund – NYT
body:
The Trump administration is considering lifting sanctions on the Russian Direct Investment Fund (RDIF), on which the former Biden administration imposed sanctions in the early days of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Russian officials pushed for the move during discussions on RDIF’s role in Russian diesel exports to the US, The New York Times reported on Tuesday, Oct. 27, citing people familiar with the matter. An unnamed US official confirmed to the newspaper that the US Treasury Department was reviewing the fund’s application for delisting through its standard procedures.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“While officially a sovereign wealth fund, RDIF is widely considered a slush fund for President Vladimir Putin and is emblematic of Russia’s broader kleptocracy,” the Treasury said under the former Biden administration.
By contrast, the US official told NYT that the current review was a part of an effort to improve bilateral relations between Moscow and Washington, with the fund’s chief executive, Kirill Dmitriev, praised as a “helpful envoy” in ending the war.
RDIF was initially created in 2011, by the order of former Russian President Dmitry Medvedev and then-Prime Minister, current Russian President Vladimir Putin.
The request is linked to the diesel arrangement that Trump abruptly struck with Putin on Oct. 9, at the same time the Ukrainian delegation was in Miami , hoping to reach a breakthrough in Russia’s war.
Shortly after the deal’s announcement, the US Treasury Department authorized the sale and import of Russian diesel fuel through April 7, 2027.
The move came only three weeks after Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act into law on Sept. 18, appearing to completely disregard the bill intended to target Russia’s energy and defense industries, as well as networks close to Putin.
According to NYT, RDIF offered to handle transactions between Russian sellers and American buyers, while at the same time pushing for its removal from the sanctions list. To be delisted, RDIF would have to prove that the reasons for its original designation no longer apply.
Russian officials said three diesel tankers have sailed for the US this month, while Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said on Oct. 23 that RDIF had provided significant support for the shipments.
Some of the fuel left Russia before any US buyer had paid for it, people familiar with the matter told NYT.
Ship-tracking firms Kpler and TankerTrackers.com showed that one tanker, the Agioi Fanendes, departed the port of Primorsk on Oct. 23 and is expected in the US on Nov. 7.
It has since changed its listed destination from New York to “for orders,” meaning it has no discharge instructions yet.
Eric Green, who oversaw Russia policy at the National Security Council under former President Joe Biden, told the NYT that lifting the sanctions would signal that Washington was abandoning its earlier position of keeping economic pressure on Moscow until a peace settlement was reached in Ukraine.
Meanwhile, Dmitriev has become Moscow’s main economic channel to Trump’s team, working directly with senior US envoys Steve Witkoff and Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner.
On Oct. 21, Witkoff publicly confirmed that Washington and Moscow are discussing future economic and trade cooperation, alongside negotiations to end the war.
He also revealed that the US Treasury Department is working directly with Dmitriev.
On that same day, Moscow revealed that Russia and the US are discussing the future of sanctioned Russian oil giant Lukoil’s overseas assets , valued at approximately $22 billion.
The US also proposed restoring Russian gas supplies to Europe, including reviving the Nord Stream pipeline system, The Economist reported on Oct. 22.
Earlier on Tuesday, Le Monde reported that the Kremlin is courting Trump and his inner circle with economic deals, including those in energy, civil aviation, rare earth metals and artificial intelligence (AI), without first agreeing to a ceasefire.
According to the same report, Witkoff presented Ukrainian negotiators in Florida on Oct. 9 with a postwar “regional prosperity plan,” which envisaged fully restoring Russian oil and gas supplies to Europe through Ukrainian territory.
The diesel agreement triggered weeks of severe diplomatic tensions between Kyiv and Washington.
Around the same time, Trump claimed it was time for Ukraine to get a new president, while, days later, restrictions on Starshield, the military version of the Starlink satellite network, disrupted Ukrainian drone operations.
Elon Musk claimed such limits were ultimately decided by Trump, not his company; a claim the US president denied.
On Oct. 14, in an interview with British broadcaster Piers Morgan, President Volodymyr Zelensky described Trump’s diesel deal as a victory for Putin, warning that Moscow was exploiting Washington’s decisions to pressure Ukraine into concessions.
Around the time, Zelensky also suggested that Russia was offering Washington potential business ventures and economic projects to influence its decisions.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Russian forces strike apartment building in Kharkiv, casualties reported
body:
Kharkiv Mayor Ihor Terekhov said this on Telegram , Ukrinform reports.
“An enemy strike has been recorded in Kharkiv’s Osnovianskyi district. The consequences are being assessed,” the statement said.
Later, Terekhov reported that an apartment building had been hit. According to preliminary information, people are trapped inside.
“There is preliminary information about casualties – their number and condition are being clarified,” the mayor added .
As the mayor reported , as of 23:10, two people were known to have been injured, one of them a four-year-old boy.
