title: Bank of America kindly asks that you don’t share your banking password with your AI assistant
body:
Financial giant Bank of America is reminding customers to bank safely by kindly not sharing your banking credentials with your AI agent.
In an email blast to customers titled “Protecting your finances in the Al World,” Bank of America urged customers to never share their username and password with another person or an outside service, “including an Al-enabled tool or agent that offers to act on your behalf.”
You can practically sense the frustration in the person sending the email. Still, customers are increasingly handing over their log-ins as personal AI assistants grow more popular . Sharing your banking username and password with an AI assistant runs the risk that it could do something with your finances without your knowledge, or that your bank thinks someone’s raiding your account and locks you out of it. Worse, a security flaw in the AI assistant could result in it leaking your banking credentials elsewhere, giving financially motivated hackers a way into your bank account.
This latest warning comes as banks are still exploring how AI agents fit into the financial world but are reportedly grappling with unauthorized agents accessing their customers’ money . As we discussed onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt , banks, payment providers, and processors are still trying to figure out how to allow customers access to their bank accounts using AI tools, such as for agentic payments, which allow people to set agents to autonomously buy things at the best price or the right time.
A spokesperson for Bank of America confirmed the authenticity of the bank’s email that was posted to social media . But heed the bank’s warning, for if things go wrong, it’s on you. Account agreements at most banks hold customers responsible for anyone they give their log-in to. “If you do share your credentials,” its email reads, “keep in mind that you’re responsible for activity resulting from that access.”

title: Israel election turnout hits 77.7%, highest in 25 years, as exit polls show 52-50 split
body: Israel recorded its highest election turnout in 25 years on Tuesday, with 77.7% of eligible voters casting ballots by the official 10 p.m. closing time, according to the Central Elections Committee. Meanwhile, updated television exit polls showed a remarkably consistent picture: 52 seats for the bloc seeking to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, 50 for his political allies and 18 for the Arab parties. A total of 5,695,682 Israelis had voted by 10 p.m., an increase of approximately 7.1 percentage points compared with the same stage of the previous election in 2022. It was the highest turnout recorded at poll-closing time since 2001.   The figure is not yet final. Voters who arrived at their polling stations before 10 p.m. were permitted to cast their ballots even after the official closing time, meaning the total is expected to rise further. The high turnout was reflected across the country, with particularly strong participation in several Arab and ultra-Orthodox communities. In two small communities in the Arava region, Paran and Shaharut, the reported turnout reached 100%. Where Israelis voted: The major cities Among Israel's larger cities, Modi'in-Maccabim-Re'ut recorded one of the highest turnout rates at 79.2%, followed by Bnei Brak at 77%, Kfar Saba at 74.7%, Petah Tikva at 73% and Rehovot at 72.9%. Rishon LeZion and Herzliya each recorded 71.3%, followed by Ramat Gan at 71.2%, Ra'anana at 70.8% and Lod at 70.6%. Turnout in Jerusalem reached 65.9%, compared with 65.4% in Tel Aviv-Jaffa and 61.6% in Haifa, Israel's three largest cities. In other major population centers, turnout stood at 69% in Holon, 68.7% in Ashkelon, 68.5% in Hadera, 67.8% in Ashdod and Beit Shemesh, and 65.8% in Be'er Sheva. Netanya recorded 60.2%, while Bat Yam had one of the lowest turnout rates among the major cities listed, at 55.3%. Arab communities report strong turnout Turnout was particularly high in several Arab communities, with Sakhnin reaching 86.8% and Kafr Qasim recording 84.9%. In the southern Bedouin city of Rahat, turnout reached 82%, while Kuseife recorded 81.2% and Hura 79.1%.   Tayibe registered 79%, Shefa-'Amr 75.9%, Umm al-Fahm 75.7% and Nazareth 72.2%. The figures came as the updated exit polls projected a combined 18 seats for the Joint List and Ra'am, giving the Arab parties a potentially important role in the parliamentary balance. Ultra-Orthodox communities also see high participation High turnout was also recorded in several ultra-Orthodox communities. Rekhasim led the group with 86.9%, followed by Elad at 84% and Modi'in Illit at 83.1%. Beitar Illit recorded 80%, while turnout reached 77% in Bnei Brak and 75.1% in Emmanuel. These figures come as the main ultra-Orthodox parties, Shas and United Torah Judaism, remain part of the projected parliamentary bloc supporting Netanyahu. Updated exit polls converge on 52-50 split The latest exit poll updates from Kan 11, Channel 12 and Channel 13 all give the bloc seeking to replace Netanyahu 52 seats, compared with 50 for the prime minister's allies. The Arab parties are projected to hold the remaining 18 seats in the 120-member Knesset. The new projections represent a slight setback for former IDF chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot's change bloc compared with the initial exit polls, which had given it 53 seats in some surveys. In Channel 13's updated poll, Naftali Bennett's Beyahad party dropped from 14 to 13 seats, while the Joint List increased from 10 to 11. The change brought the anti-Netanyahu bloc down to 52 seats, with Netanyahu's bloc remaining at 50. Channel 13 projects Likud as the largest party with 25 seats, followed by Eisenkot's Yashar! with 23. Bennett's Beyahad receives 13, the Joint List 11 and the Democrats nine. Yisrael Beiteinu, Ra'am and United Torah Judaism each receive seven seats, while Otzma Yehudit, Shas and the Religious Zionism-Zehut alliance each receive six. Kan 11's updated exit poll also shows Beyahad dropping to 13 seats and the Joint List rising to 11, producing the same overall distribution of 52 seats for the change bloc, 50 for Netanyahu's bloc and 18 for the Arab parties. Channel 12's update showed a different movement within the change bloc: the Democrats rose to 10 seats, while Avigdor Lieberman's Yisrael Beiteinu fell to eight. Its overall bloc projection remained unchanged at 52 seats for Netanyahu's opponents against 50 for his supporters. The updated Channel 12 poll continues to show Likud leading with 24 seats, followed by Yashar! with 22 and Beyahad with 12. The Joint List receives 11 seats. High turnout, but no clear parliamentary majority Despite the unusually high voter participation and the narrow lead for Netanyahu's opponents, the updated exit polls still do not point to a clear parliamentary majority for either main political bloc. The change bloc's 52 projected seats leave it nine short of the 61 needed for an outright majority. Netanyahu's 50-seat bloc is 11 seats short. The Arab parties' projected 18 seats could therefore play an important role in determining the next government, although disagreements among the parties seeking to replace Netanyahu remain an obstacle to forming a coalition. The final outcome will also depend on the official count, including special double-envelope ballots cast by soldiers and other eligible voters whose votes require separate verification. The unexpectedly high turnout could also affect parties close to the 3.25% electoral threshold, with Ofer Winter's Amcha Yisrael, the joint party led by Yoaz Hendel and Yaron Zelekha, and the Haredi Public Party all projected to fall short in the exit polls. For now, election night has produced a clear result in one respect: voter participation has reached a level not seen in a quarter-century. Whether that translates into a decisive political outcome remains unresolved.

title: ‘I will forever miss you’ – Toluwanisings’ wife breaks down in tears at night of tributes
body:
Akanbi Elizabeth could not hold back her tears as she mourned her late husband, gospel singer Olayemi “Toluwanisings” Bolaji, at a night of tributes in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Tuesday.
The widow broke down as she addressed mourners who gathered at Hall of Grace, Jogor Centre, in Oyo State to honour the late singer. Family members, colleagues, friends and associates attended the event to pay their respects to the “Kabiyesi Olorun Ayo” crooner.
Overcome with grief, Elizabeth spoke of the pain of losing her husband and asked him to continue looking after her and their children despite his death.
Toluwanisings and his wife got married in September 2021 and had two daughters.
“Toluwanisings, my dear husband. I will forever miss you. Please do not forget your children and me,” she said.
Several gospel artistes and actors attended the tribute night, including Adeyinka Alaseyori, Esther Igbekele, Laolu Gbenjo, Akintayo Akinwande, Bidemi Olaoba, Peterson Okopi, Sarah Apekeola and Bimbo Oshin.
The artistes paid tribute through worship, songs and emotional reflections, celebrating the late singer’s life and musical legacy.
Toluwanisings died on 15 October after he slumped at his residence in Ibadan, Oyo State.
PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that his death sparked controversy over his burial, with his family yet to settle on whether to bury him in a cemetery, at his residence or in his hometown.
The family insisted that burial arrangements must remain on hold until the authorities establish the circumstances surrounding his death.
They demanded a transparent, impartial investigation, warning they would not tolerate any attempt to compromise the process. The family also called on the government, community leaders and security agencies to prevent interference.
The family said they would continue to bear the mortuary costs until investigators uncovered the cause of death.
They also alleged possible foul play, citing what they described as an absence of visible mourning by the singer’s wife, workers and others at his residence when seven family members visited.
These claims remain allegations and, based on the information provided, have not been independently established.

title: F-16 Jets to Add Startup Castelion’s Hypersonic ‘Blackbeard’ Missile
body: The Air Force has awarded Castelion, a venture capital-backed defense startup founded in 2022, a contract to integrate its hypersonic Blackbeard missile onto the F-16 Fighting Falcon. The announcement, which came from the company via social media on Oct. 26, marks a major advancement in the Air Force’s work on hypersonic munitions. Neither the Air Force Research Laboratory, which awarded the contract, nor Castelion immediately responded to a request for comment. The same day, the service awarded a $694 million contract to Lockheed Martin, a longtime defense prime, to begin production of the hypersonic Air-Launched Rapid Response Weapon, Air & Space Forces Magazine reported . The Blackbeard missile has drawn strong interest across the Pentagon, with the Navy pushing to field the rocket-powered, boost-glide strike weapon with a nearly 500-mile strike range on the sea service’s F/A-18 Super Hornet. Castelion has been awarded a contract modification to its existing work with the Air Force Research Laboratory to begin Blackbeard integration activities with the F-16. We are grateful to the Air Force for their trust. Aim High. pic.twitter.com/UerIcDG6Jx — Castelion (@Castelion) October 26, 2026 Navy Development The Navy’s Air Test and Evaluation Squadron 23 used the Super Hornet to conduct carriage and separation tests of Blackbeard on Sept. 18 at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Md., which validated the weapon’s compatibility and flightworthiness on the aircraft. The service selected Blackbeard as the winner in its Multimission Affordable Capacity Effector program, which shifted it to a program of record under framework contract orders of up to $200 million. The company won a $105 million contract to integrate the missile on the F/A-18 Super Hornet in April . The MACE initiative sought an affordable hypersonic missile about the size of an AIM-120 AMRAAM air-to-air missile. In June, the service awarded the company its first production contract, worth $23.4 million, for 50 early operational capability pre-production prototype Blackbeard missiles. Subsequent delivery orders from the Navy aim to speed up Blackbeard pre-production prototypes to EOC status and field the low-cost hypersonic weapon. Coming soon to a theater near you…BLACKBEARD! @USPACOM @CENTCOM @PAEAviation pic.twitter.com/KgBtIqdf8I — NAVAIR (@NAVAIRNews) September 25, 2026 USAF Spending and Development For its part, the Air Force has spent nearly $21 million to date on Blackbeard research and development, and AFRL added $16.4 million in a September contract modification for the missile. Those dollars cover development through June 2028 under current spending and contractual agreements. The USAF contract modification also pursues compatibility with the F-35A. While the F-35 is the services’ main fifth-generation tactical fighter, the F-16, like the Navy’s workhorse Super Hornet, are workhorse fourth-gen fighters that can carry more munitions without worrying about compromising stealthy characteristics. The Air Force has more than 600 F-16s in the fleet and recently moved forward with plans to upgrade the decades-old software system for those crucial aircraft, Air & Space Forces Magazine previously reported . Screenshot from Castelion The Big Picture The Air Force now has a three-pronged approach to hypersonic munitions. These include Castelion’s Blackbeard, an air-to-air missile; the Lockheed Martin AGM-183A ARRW, a strategic strike-focused, exquisite, long-range hypersonic missile; and the Raytheon/Northrop Grumman Hypersonic Attack Cruise Missile, a cruise missile option to strike ground or maritime targets. ARRW successfully completed booster and All-Up-Round tests and is poised to add terminal seeker and data-link integration for moving-target tracking in its Increment 2 tests. The strategic strike missile is envisioned for the B-52 Stratofortress and B-1B Lancer. The AHM-4A HACM is built for internal or external carriage and geared for both fighter and bomber use to add high-volume magazine depth to the fleet. The missile achieved milestone flight tests over an undisclosed Australian range in late September, Air & Space Forces Magazine reported. Initial operational delivery of HACMs is slated for 2027. Additionally, AFRL recently posted a request for white papers on developing a more advanced hypersonic rocket engine for its current and future munitions dubbed the Rotating Detonation Rocket Engine. If successful, the more affordable, mass-produced engine could extend ranges, increase speed, and up the payload for future hypersonic, Air & Space Forces Magazine reported . The post F-16 Jets to Add Startup Castelion’s Hypersonic ‘Blackbeard’ Missile appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .

title: S.A. evacuation: Minority blocked Ablakwa from appearing before Foreign Affairs Committee – Okoe Vanderpuije
body: The Chairman of Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Alfred Oko Vanderpuije, has accused the Minority of preventing Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa from appearing before the committee to explain expenditure on the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa. He said the Minority had insisted on receiving documents relating to the GH¢49.72 million evacuation expenditure before the minister could be invited to brief the committee, but failed to return to the committee with questions after the information was provided. Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story on Tuesday, October 27, Mr Vanderpuije said the committee had initially agreed to postpone the minister’s appearance to allow the Minority to examine the requested documents. “Yes, the Minority said they will not sit to listen to the minister. They want to receive the information first. So we respected that. We postponed the meeting,” he said. Mr Vanderpuije was responding to questions about the Minority’s continued demand for Mr Ablakwa’s resignation and its threat to initiate a censure motion against him over alleged discrepancies in the evacuation expenditure. Read also: Minority demands Ablakwa’s resignation or dismissal over SA evacuation payments He said he had expected the Minority to return to the committee after reviewing the documents and identify specific issues that required clarification from the minister, who, he said, was willing to appear. “As chair of the committee, I was expecting that when the minister has provided the information, and they have looked at it, if they have any problems, they would have come back to me and say, look, we have the information, we’ve looked at it, but we need the minister to come and explain certain things to us,” he said. According to him, the Minority’s failure to follow that process denied both sides of the committee the opportunity to question the minister and examine the expenditure together. He also criticised the Deputy Ranking Member of the committee for going public with allegations against the minister before the committee had completed its work. Mr Vanderpuije said he considered that approach unprofessional, arguing that the committee should have been allowed to hear the minister’s explanations and establish whether there were errors in the records. “He should have allowed the process of the committee to continue, so that we would have all had the opportunity, both sides, Majority and Minority, to have the minister there,” he said. The committee chairman said the Majority had also examined the information provided and had not found the discrepancies being alleged by the Minority. “So we, the Majority, also have to look at the information and we came back and we said, look, all what you are saying, we have not seen it,” he said. He added that the minister had agreed for the documents and expenditure records to be referred to the Auditor-General for examination, arguing that the findings should guide further discussions on the matter. “The Auditor-General will look at it and the Auditor-General will come back and tell all of Ghana what he found,” Mr Vanderpuije said. He maintained that the referral to the Auditor-General was consistent with calls for an independent examination of the expenditure, dismissing the Minority’s demand for the minister to resign before the process had been completed. Mr Vanderpuije questioned why the Minority had escalated its demands when the relevant investigative bodies had not yet presented their findings. “Independent bodies like the Attorney-General have not come to give us what they have found. Now you are jumping the gun and saying that the minister should resign,” he said. Read also: South Africa evacuation expenditure ‘smacks of a grand scheme of corruption’ – Abu Jinapor The dispute follows allegations by the Minority that GH¢16.4 million of the GH¢49.72 million reportedly spent on evacuating 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa remains unaccounted for. The Minority has called for an investigation by an independent, internationally reputable auditing and accounting firm and insists that Mr Ablakwa should resign pending the outcome of the investigation. The minister has rejected the allegations, maintaining that the expenditure has been accounted for and agreeing to have the records examined by the Auditor-General.

title: Ryanair Closes Thessaloniki Base, Cuts Flights and Relocates Aircraft
body: Ryanair has begun closing its base at Thessaloniki’s Macedonia Airport, relocating its three stationed aircraft to other European bases and sharply reducing flights and destinations for the winter season. The move also affects around 200 pilots and cabin crew, some of whom have transferred to other bases while others face unemployment. The Irish low-cost airline began implementing its decision in recent days, following its announcement last May. The first aircraft has already departed for Turin to reinforce Ryanair’s base there, while the other two will move to Stockholm and Tirana. The closure does not mean Ryanair will stop operating flights to and from Thessaloniki. However, the airline will serve around ten fewer destinations and reduce weekly frequencies on several remaining routes. Flight times may also become less convenient because Ryanair will no longer station aircraft overnight at Macedonia Airport to launch early-morning services. Ryanair’s winter flight schedule from Thessaloniki Ryanair’s winter timetable is gradually taking effect. The airline plans to operate the following services from Thessaloniki: London: Four flights per week. Rome: Two flights per week, down from four or five, on Mondays and Fridays. Milan Bergamo: Two flights per week, down from four or five, on Mondays and Saturdays. Paphos: Five flights per week, with no services on Tuesdays or Wednesdays. Vienna: Three flights per week, down from five, on Thursdays, Saturdays and Sundays. Brussels Charleroi: Two flights per week, down from three or four, on Mondays and Saturdays. Krakow: Three flights per week, down from five, on Mondays, Fridays and Sundays. Budapest: Four flights per week, down from five, on Mondays, Thursdays, Fridays and Sundays. Bucharest: Two flights per week, down from three, on Mondays and Fridays. Malta: Two flights per week, on Mondays and Saturdays. Bratislava: Two flights per week, down from four or five, on Mondays and Fridays. Karlsruhe: Two flights per week, on Fridays and Sundays. Nuremberg: Two flights per week, down from five, on Fridays and Saturdays. Memmingen: Two flights per week, down from four, on Fridays and Sundays. Paris Beauvais: Two flights per week, on Fridays and Sundays. Other airlines have taken over some routes that Ryanair has dropped from Thessaloniki. However, they generally offer fewer flights on those routes, while ticket prices are comparatively higher, according to the report. Dispute with Fraport over airport charges Ryanair has blamed the closure on what it describes as excessive and uncompetitive charges imposed by Fraport, the operator of Macedonia Airport. The airline argues that the fees make operations particularly unattractive during winter, when passenger traffic falls. The dispute intensified after the Greek government reduced the passenger departure tax from €12 to €3 — a €9 cut per departing passenger. Fraport then increased its own charges from €7.35 to €17.52, a rise of €10.17. It also raised the airport security fee from €2.94 to €3.39. The report argues that these increases more than offset the reduction in the state tax, meaning passengers did not benefit from the tax cut. Fraport, meanwhile, has reportedly presented Ryanair’s decision as a pressure tactic intended to secure commercial advantages, describing the closure threat as consistent with the airline’s usual approach. The dispute leaves Thessaloniki with fewer Ryanair services for the winter, while the future position of some of the airline’s local employees remains uncertain. title: Oleshky ceasefire expands beyond occupied town as truce holds without reported violations

The expansion is intended to facilitate aid deliveries to civilians trapped under Russian occupation. Ukraine and Russia are observing a localized ceasefire to enable a humanitarian mission to reach Oleshky, where residents have faced months of shortages of food, medicine, and medical care under Russian occupation. Trump said the ceasefire took effect at 04:00 Moscow time on 27 October, two days ahead of the original schedule, to protect civilians and facilitate the delivery of critical humanitarian aid. Russia’s chief of General Staff, Valery Gerasimov, had confirmed the arrangement, she said. He added that he remained in constant contact with his Russian counterpart, Yana Lantratova. THE CEASEFIRE HAS COMMENCED The ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia took effect at 4:00am Moscow time on October 27, 2026. Timing was accelerated two days ahead of schedule to protect the safety of civilians and to facilitate the delivery of critical humanitarian aid. The… — First Lady Melania Trump (@FLOTUS) October 27, 2026 Road to Oleshky must be cleared before aid can arrive Lubinets said the ceasefire began at 03:00 Kyiv time and would remain in effect until 22:59 Kyiv time on 1 November. He reported no violations since it began and said Russian forces had made no attempts to advance. The next steps are to clear mines from the road to Oleshky and deliver humanitarian supplies. Representatives of Ukraine, Russia, and the United States will be present once the route is cleared and the aid arrives, Lubinets said in an interview with Ukrainian broadcaster 1+1. He added that everyone who wants to leave for Ukrainian-controlled territory would be able to do so and that assistance would be provided to everyone who needs it. The Financial Times earlier reported , citing sources familiar with the negotiations, that residents who agree to leave Russian-occupied Oleshky during the ceasefire would first be transported to occupied Crimea or Russia before being allowed to return to Ukrainian-controlled territory. Humanitarian mission follows months of efforts Oleshky has been under Russian occupation since 2022. The town has been cut off for months, with shortages of food, medicine, and medical care worsening. The White House announced on 23 October that Melania Trump had secured a localized ceasefire originally scheduled to begin on 29 October. Russia subsequently announced a ceasefire on the Kherson axis from 27 October, with preparations to secure a route for a humanitarian convoy. Explore further Ceasefire planned for occupied Oleshky as residents face starvation and blocked escape routes, White House announces Lubinets said efforts to address the humanitarian crisis in Oleshky began in late February 2026, but progress accelerated in September following Melania Trump’s involvement. The expanded ceasefire area is intended to facilitate the humanitarian operation, but the route must still be cleared and supplies delivered before the mission can reach residents. The new boundaries of the ceasefire area have not been specified publicly. title: Who’s really in charge at Anthropic after the IPO?
body:
Anthropic was founded in 2021 to ensure humanity can control AI and benefit from it in the long-term. As the frontier lab approaches its initial public offering, however, there’s one class of humanity that is being shut out of control: anyone who buys its stock on public markets.
Complex structures that allow founders like Elon Musk or Mark Zuckerberg to control their public companies without owning most of them are nothing new in Silicon Valley. But Anthropic’s obsession with AI safety has resulted in a truly baroque style of corporate governance that will leave common shareholders with little say over most major decisions at the AI company, including who sits on its board.
First, Anthropic is a public benefit company — a for-profit corporation legally allowed to weigh a public mission alongside profit — with the goal of promoting AI safety. That status protects the board’s ability to make decisions about AI safety that aren’t driven entirely by shareholder value without being sued by angry investors.
Right now, the board is chaired by Anthropic president Daniela Amodei and includes CEO Dario Amodei (her brother), Netflix cofounder Reed Hastings, former Microsoft and GM CFO Christopher Liddell, Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan, and Spark Capital partner Yasmin Razavi. There is one vacancy on the board.
Second, Anthropic has allocated significant control of its board to a Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT), an independent panel meant to keep the company focused on mission to benefit humanity. The trust owns a class of stock that gives it the ability to elect and remove a majority of the company’s board, known as Class T directors. The LTBT is chaired by Neil Shah, a global health expert who was managing director at GiveWell, a nonprofit that ranks charities, and includes former Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke, national security expert Richard Fontaine, and Harvard physicist Christopher Stubbs. There is one vacancy on the LTBT right now. The existing members will themselves choose who fills it.
Third, Anthropic’s seven founders also jointly own a special class of stock that gives a majority of them 50.1% of shareholder voting power, allowing them to elect three members of the board of directors. If, for whatever reason, there’s no majority among the founders, only then are their shares voted in proportion with holders of common stock.
Finally, the board can put a check on the LTBT. When the LTBT nominates a “Specified” one of its four directors, or removes that director without cause (that is, without alleging misconduct), the board’s nominating committee can decline to approve the move and throw the decision to the company’s employees for a vote.
The dynamics of such a complex structure are hard to predict. We’ve already seen one notable instance where a similar structure was essentially overthrown: OpenAI’s so-called blip, when OpenAI’s board briefly fired CEO Sam Altman over concerns that he was not being candid with them. Thanks to the loyalty of the company’s employees to Altman, the board backed down, reinstated him, and a new governance structure was put in place. Anthropic’s structure seems to formalize that kind of employee power.
At Anthropic, cracks in the founders’ unified front could lead to common shareholders having more say than expected, while employees can overrule the LTBT on board seats if they back the board over the assembled luminaries.
The founders’ control won’t last forever: Ten years after the IPO, the founders can choose to end their control of the company, or their control will end automatically when fewer than three of them remain. At that point, the LTBT will continue until 85% of common shareholders vote to end it, or it decides to step down with approval from the board.
If and when neither special class of shareholder exists any more — hopefully not because of an AI-driven catastrophe — common shareholders finally get control.

title: Alberta government to end DEI public sector hiring
body:
Alberta is looking to end public sector hiring practices aimed at diversity, equity and inclusion.
A government bill tabled Tuesday, if passed, would prohibit a number of public bodies from using DEI policies to make hiring decisions.
Premier Danielle Smith said hiring needs to be based on merit and qualifications so that everyone has a fair chance at getting jobs.
“Albertans expect public institutions to hire and promote the best qualified people and ensure that everyone has a fair opportunity to succeed based on their skills, experience and qualifications,” Smith told reporters in Edmonton.
“These changes will help to ensure that fairness is at the heart of hiring.”
The bill covers public agencies, Crown corporations, post-secondary schools, school boards and municipalities. However, government officials said provincial employees are already hired based on merit.
The officials also said the change could apply to non-profit agencies receiving government grants, but that would be determined through future regulations.
They said there would be some exceptions to the prohibition but didn’t provide examples.
The proposed legislation would further prohibit public bodies from having mandatory DEI training for staff, except when necessary for the job. Other mandatory training would be required to be “ideologically neutral” and focus on job duties and skills.
The bill, tabled by Justice Minister Mickey Amery, specifically targets the Alberta Human Rights Act.
The government said it’s changing a section of the act that allows for policies and programs aiming to uplift those who may be disadvantaged because of their race, disability, gender or gender expression, sexual orientation, religious beliefs, age or other personal circumstance, including marital status.
Officials said hiring and promotion practices would continue to be subject to other protections or provisions under the act.
Opposition NDP member Kathleen Ganley said the NDP hasn’t heard any concerns about DEI hiring practices, leaving her to think the changes are more aimed at distracting from issues that are far bigger priorities for Albertans, like affordability and health care.
“This is a solution in want of a problem,” Ganley said.
Sandra Azocar, the president of the Alberta Union of Provincial Employees, agreed with Ganley, saying public sector employers already hire the best candidates.
Azocar, whose union represents nearly 100,000 workers that are mostly in the public sector, said she believes Smith is trying to appease the “extreme factions” within her party.
It’s not the first time Smith’s United Conservative Party government has cracked down on DEI policies.
Last year, it passed legislation prohibiting professional regulatory bodies, including the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Alberta, from making members undergo training around diversity initiatives.
That legislation also limits what behaviour regulatory bodies can police their members on. The government said at the time that it was inspired by Ontario psychologist and social media personality Jordan Peterson, who was sanctioned by his province’s professional regulator for controversial public statements.
Amery’s bill also aims to make changes to other provincial laws, including added penalties for the distribution or threat of distribution of digitally altered intimate images without consent.
While the issue is mainly a federal Criminal Code matter, Alberta has laws that allow residents to take civil court action.
The bill aims to capture other types of content, including audio recordings, livestreams and images created using artificial intelligence.
The government said those who violate the law could face fines up to $10,000, imprisonment for up to two years, or both. It also said the bill would allow the courts to give community service sentences.
Ganley said the NDP supported these change but said the government’s choice to tie the bill to ending DEI hiring practices was “inappropriate.”
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 27, 2026.

title: Apple unveils MacBook Pro with up to 24 hours of battery life
body:
NEW YORK, October 28. /TASS/. Apple has unveiled a new MacBook Pro laptop powered by the M6 chip, offering up to 24 hours of battery life on a single charge, according to a company press release.
According to Apple, the M6 chip enables the MacBook Pro to process artificial intelligence workloads 25% faster and handle graphics-intensive tasks more efficiently than its predecessor. In addition, the new chip allows the device to charge to 50% in just 30 minutes.
Sales are officially scheduled to begin on November 6. The new laptop will have a starting price of $1,999.

title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m at New York auction
body: The mounted skeleton of a newly identified dinosaur once mistaken for a young Tyrannosaurus rex has sold at auction for a colossal $47.3m (£35.5m). Nicknamed Jodi, the roughly 10-foot-tall (3m) skeleton was auctioned by Sotheby’s in New York. The sale comes a year after researchers confirmed that the skeleton belongs to a distinct genus. The Late Cretaceous carnivore was expected to fetch at least $9m when it went under the hammer on Tuesday. The auction follows Sotheby’s sale of a Tyrannosaurus rex, dubbed Gus, for a record $50.1m in July. The sale has reignited debate in the scientific community over whether dinosaur remains should be sold privately or displayed publicly. Sotheby’s described Jodi as an “excellent exhibition-ready” skeleton with about 191 fossil-bone elements and a “beautifully preserved, virtually complete skull”. The auction house added that the Nanotyrannus is “one of only three such skeletons known to science”. Sotheby’s said the specimen is the first to come to market since US researchers confirmed the genus’s existence last October. Sotheby’s has not disclosed the identity of the buyer, who won after a thrilling 12-minute auction between six interested parties. It becomes the second-most valuable dinosaur fossil ever sold, behind Gus. The third-most valuable was a Stegosaurus named Apex, which Sotheby’s sold in July 2024 for $44.6m. Megan Jacobs, a palaeontologist at the University of Portsmouth, told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme on Tuesday that Nanotyrannus “was for a very long time believed to be sort of a teenager of T. rex”. “But it’s a lot smaller and its a lot more gracile. So it’s very sort-of sleek, slender, [with] blade-like teeth for slicing through meat,” Jacobs said. Tyrannosaurus rex and Nanotyrannus lived alongside one another during the same geological period approximately 67 million years ago. Jodi was initially exhibited as a juvenile T. rex at London’s Frieze Masters international art fair in October 2023, before scientists classified the Nanotyrannus genus. Rancher Jodi Pierson discovered the skeleton on her land in Montana, in the Hell Creek Formation, a heavily studied geological site. Commercial palaeontologist Clayton Phipps later excavated it. Phipps also discovered the famous “Duelling Dinosaurs” fossil. That specimen, showing the remains of a Nanotyrannus and Triceratops apparently in combat, was found eight miles (13km) from Jodi in 2006. The “Duelling Dinosaurs” discovery became crucial to the research published by Lindsay Zanno and James Napoli that classified Nanotyrannus as separate from T. rex. Their paper ended decades of debate over whether the dinosaurs were distinct. The auction of Jodi comes as some scientists warn that auctions could herald a new era in fossil collecting by the ultra-rich. Researchers told the BBC after the sale of Gus that such remains should be exhibited in public spaces where they can be more freely studied. Prof Steve Brusatte, a palaeontologist at the University of Edinburgh and consultant on the Jurassic Park films, told BBC World Service’s What in the World programme in July that the T. rex’s auction was “concerning”. “I don’t know of any museum or university that can afford a price tag like that,” he said. “Imagine if the Mona Lisa was just owned by a super-wealthy person and it wasn’t on display and people couldn’t see it, couldn’t enjoy it.” He said at the time he hoped such a sale wouldn’t become a trend, adding that it could adversely affect scientific research and public education. Responding to Tuesday’s auction, Brusatte called it “harrowing” that Jodi could disappear from public view. “We’ve really just found out that Nanotyrannus is real, and now one of the best skeletons is about to be sold to the highest bidder, and it’s harrowing to think it could disappear into the vaults of a collector rather than displayed in a museum where it can wow and inspire kids and families and the public at large,” he told the BBC. But Jacobs told the Today programme on Tuesday that the debate had two sides, and that a lot of time, effort, and money went into excavating the specimens. “I don’t begrudge the people involved for wanting to sell it for such a large amount of money,” she said. “Although it’s a scary prospect, actually a lot of them have ended up in the public eye… these things without a doubt will end up in a museum at some point.”

title: Greece Cancels 28 October Parades in Magnesia, Sporades and Lamia
body: Greece has cancelled student parades for the 28 October national anniversary in Magnesia, the Northern Sporades and Lamia ahead of forecast severe weather, while authorities in Naxos and the Small Cyclades plan to proceed with celebrations, subject to local conditions. The expected deterioration in the weather has prompted regional and municipal authorities to revise anniversary programmes, prioritising the safety of students, teachers, families and spectators. Student parades cancelled in Magnesia and the Northern Sporades Thessaly Regional Governor Dimitris Kouretas has cancelled all student parades across Magnesia and the Northern Sporades because of forecast dangerous weather conditions. The decision, published on the Greek government’s Diavgeia transparency portal, aims to prevent risks to the lives and physical safety of participants and spectators. The cancellation applies exclusively to student parades. The relevant authorities will decide whether to hold other anniversary events according to the prevailing weather conditions. Thessaly’s Civil Protection Directorate must immediately notify the relevant education directorates, municipalities, police authorities and other agencies. Education officials will then inform schools, students and their parents or guardians. The military parade in Volos remains under consideration, with authorities expected to make a decision on Tuesday based on the weather forecast. Lamia cancels student parade but retains religious service Authorities in the Fthiotida regional unit have also cancelled the student parade in Lamia because of the anticipated severe weather. The cancellation covers students from primary and secondary schools, as well as other civilian parade contingents. Officials cited the risk of heavy rainfall disrupting the gathering and movement of participants. Fthiotida Deputy Regional Governor Ilias Sanidas, working with Civil Protection services, prioritised the safety of children, teachers and their families. However, the wider anniversary programme will continue. The official religious service will take place as scheduled at the Metropolitan Church of the Annunciation of the Virgin Mary, led by Metropolitan Symeon of Fthiotida and attended by local officials. Unless authorities announce a further change, the military parade and the participation of security forces are also expected to proceed. Fthiotida remains under heightened Red Code civil protection alert until Thursday, 29 October, because of the dangerous weather conditions. Naxos and the Small Cyclades plan to proceed In contrast, the Municipality of Naxos and the Small Cyclades intends to hold its 28 October parades as scheduled, despite a decision by South Aegean Deputy Regional Governor George Leontaritis to cancel student parades across the Cyclades regional unit because of forecasts of severe weather. Naxos and Small Cyclades Mayor Dimitris Lianos announced the municipality’s position during a special accountability meeting of the municipal council. The municipality will remain in contact with school principals to monitor conditions in each area. If severe weather affects a particular location, officials may cancel the parade there. Authorities will base their decisions on the safety of students and everyone taking part in the anniversary celebrations. Student parades cancelled in the Dodecanese and Agios Dimitrios The South Aegean Region has also cancelled all student parades for the 28 October anniversary across the Dodecanese. Civil Protection Coordinator Minas Papadakis announced the decision because of the increased risk of flooding. In Attica, Agios Dimitrios Mayor Stelios Mamalakis has cancelled the local parade. The religious service at the Church of Saint Dimitrios will nevertheless take place as planned. Flag bearers from each school must attend at the scheduled time of 10:00 a.m. Authorities across Greece are adjusting anniversary events according to local forecasts, with some cancelling student parades as a precaution while others retain the programme but reserve the option to make changes if conditions worsen. title: ‘Show courage, sit with Ra'am’: Israel's Democrats push to replace Netanyahu
body: While Yachad party leader Naftali Bennett and Yisrael Beytenu chairman Avigdor Liberman remained silent in the hour following the release of Tuesday evening's exit polls, senior Democrats lawmaker Naama Lazimi said at the party's election headquarters: "From the very beginning, we said we need to sit with Ra'am." "It's up to us to show political courage and leadership. The public has spoken, 70 to 50," she said. "The Israeli public has fired Netanyahu. It has fired the government of abandonment, draft evasion and plunder. Now it's up to us to be brave and do everything we can to bring this country healing, stability and calm."     Even before Election Day, the Democrats were the only party in the bloc seeking to replace Netanyahu to publicly support forming a government with Arab parties, particularly Mansour Abbas's Islamist Ra'am party. Earlier Tuesday evening, Democrats chairman Yair Golan responded to the exit polls in a post on X, saying: "The public has spoken. It has fired the Netanyahu government." "We have been given a historic opportunity to establish a genuine government of change in Israel, and we have no intention of giving it up," Golan wrote. "We represent an enormous segment of the public that has fought in the streets for four years, joined the party and gone out to persuade voters. We will do everything to ensure that such a government is formed." He added: "We are ready to work with all our partners, bridge the differences and take responsibility. The public has spoken. Now it's our turn to do the work." At the party's election headquarters, lawmaker Efrat Rayten told ynet: "Netanyahu's government has collapsed. Netanyahu's bloc has fallen to a low of 50 seats and has lost its majority in Israel." "The State of Israel has shown him a red card and told him: You're going home. As far as we're concerned, that's absolutely clear," she said. Rayten added: "As early as tomorrow, we need to get to work, take the reins in the Knesset and examine how to establish a new government that will safeguard Israel's security." According to most exit polls, Arab parties are projected to secure an impressive 17 to 18 seats in the 120-member Knesset, with Ra'am projected to win seven seats in each poll. It therefore remains unclear whether even a partnership with Mansour Abbas's party would give the bloc seeking to replace Netanyahu the 61 seats needed for a parliamentary majority in the 26th Knesset.

title: First Israeli Election Exit Polls Show Narrow Edge For Opposition
body: The first exit polls from Israel’s elections showed the opposition bloc with a slight edge over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp as voting ended Tuesday, but still shy of an outright majority in the 120-seat Knesset. The country’s main pollsters — Channels 11, 12 and 13 — projected the opposition bloc to win 52 or 53 seats, and Netanyahu’s bloc to win 50, although his Likud would be the largest single party in the parliament, with 24 or 25 seats. Israeli Arab parties also made gains after their voter base turned out in high numbers. The exit polls showed the two Arab-majority groupings, Raam and the Joint List, winning 17 or 18 seats between them. In the last election, Likud had walked away with 32 seats, enabling it to cobble together a coalition with smaller far-right parties after Netanyahu’s traditional allies balked at the corruption cases the premier was facing. This time around, those mainstream right-wing parties, by and large, vowed to work with main challenger Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party — projected to nab 21 to 23 seats — to form an opposition coalition capable of unseating Netanyahu. A volunteer stands behind a banner for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party at a polling station in Jerusalem on October 27, 2026, on the day of Israel’s legislative election. Photo by Jewel SAMAD / AFP) “The initial exit poll results indicate a complete lack of confidence in Netanyahu and the October 7 government,” Eisenkot said. Israel’s current opposition chief Yair Lapid said Netanyahu’s bloc had suffered a “crushing defeat”, while left-wing leader Yair Golan said the public had “fired the Netanyahu government”. While Raam and the Joint List do not belong to the opposition bloc, they have expressed openness to supporting it. Tuesday’s poll was marked by high turnout, with many voters saying they saw it as pivotal for the country’s future. The following is a party-by-party breakdown of the projected seat count in the first exit polls: Pro-Netanyahu camp Likud, right-wing, led by Benjamin Netanyahu: 24 or 25 Otzma Yehudit, far-right, led by Itamar Ben Gvir: 6 or 7 United Torah Judaism, Ashkenazi ultra-Orthodox, led by Yaakov Asher: 6 or 7 Shas, Sephardic ultra-Orthodox, led by Aryeh Deri: 6 to 8 Religious Zionism, far-right, led by Bezalel Smotrich: 6 Opposition camp Yashar, centrist, led by Gadi Eisenkot: 21 to 23 Beyahad, centre-right, led by Naftali Bennett: 12 to 14 The Democrats, left-wing, led by Yair Golan: 9 or 10 Yisrael Beiteinu, secular right, led by Avigdor Lieberman: 7 to 9 Arab parties Raam, moderate Islamist, led by Mansour Abbas: 7 Joint List, far-left, led by Yousef Jabareen: 10 or 11 The post First Israeli Election Exit Polls Show Narrow Edge For Opposition appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Police rescue 29 kidnap victims, arrest 34 foreigners in Benue – Official
body:
The Police Command in Benue says it has rescued 29 kidnapped victims, arrested 48 suspects, including 34 foreign nationals, and recovered seven locally fabricated firearms.
The Commissioner of Police, Cletus Nwadiogbu, disclosed this on Tuesday in Makurdi while briefing journalists on the command’s operational achievements in October.
He said the 34 foreign nationals comprised 16 Cameroonians arrested in Otukpo on 9 October over concerns about their travel documents and immigration status, and 18 Nigeriens intercepted at Orokam on 22 October while travelling to Ikom, Cross River.
Mr Nwadiogbu said the suspects were being investigated, adding that the Nigeria Immigration Service would help verify their status and determine appropriate action under the law.
He said the command also killed a suspected bandit and recovered 16 rounds of ammunition and cartridges.
On kidnapping, the commissioner said four passengers abducted after gunmen attacked a commercial vehicle along the Uzer axis of Ayilamo–Tse-Abi Road in Logo Local Government Area on 5 October were rescued.
He said the driver was killed, while the passengers were rescued through a joint operation involving the police, Operation Whirl Stroke, Benue State Civil Protection Guards and local hunters.
Mr Nwadiogbu added that 17 farmers abducted from Tse-Acha and Tse-Wuam communities in Bamun Village, Logo, were rescued on 7 October through a joint operation involving security personnel and local vigilantes.
He said eight kidnapped victims, including a Reverend Father, were also rescued in Ohimini Local Government Area following their abduction along Ugbokolo–Ajegbe–Awume Road on 13 October.
According to him, two victims were rescued on 16 October, while the remaining six were freed on 18 October.
He said the victims were taken to the Federal University of Health Sciences Teaching Hospital, Otukpo, for medical examination and treatment, while two suspects were arrested in connection with the abduction.
The commissioner also disclosed that the command was investigating cases of child abuse, homicide, cult-related violence and defilement.
He said a suspect, Hemen Wuese, was arrested over the alleged abuse of two children in Injorov Village, Turan, Kwande Local Government Area, on 5 October.
According to him, the children were allegedly subjected to severe physical abuse over an accusation involving N14,500, resulting in the death of one of them.
He said the surviving child was rescued and was in stable condition, while the deceased child’s body was deposited for autopsy.
Mr Nwadiogbu further said three suspects were arrested following an alleged cult-related attack on a resident along Maiduguri Street, Wadata, Makurdi, on Oct. 14.
He said the victim was taken to the Federal Medical Centre, Apir, but later died, adding that investigations were ongoing to establish the suspects’ individual roles.
He also disclosed that a 60-year-old man was arrested over the alleged defilement of a 10-year-old girl in Igumale, Ado Local Government Area.
The commissioner said the victim was taken for medical examination and treatment, while investigations continued.
On other security operations, Nwadiogbu said a suspected bandit was neutralised on 2 October during an encounter with Operation Zenda Joint Task Force personnel along Amaafu–Abaji Road in Katsina-Ala.
He said a locally fabricated firearm was recovered, while other suspected members of the group fled.
The commissioner urged residents to remain vigilant and provide credible information to security agencies to help prevent crime, identify threats and rescue victims.
He reaffirmed the command’s commitment to protecting lives and property and ensuring that offenders were brought to justice through lawful means.

title: Turkish Opposition Accuses Erdogan of Losing Ground to Greece
body: Turkish opposition leader Özgür Özel has accused President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s government of letting Greece gain the upper hand over Turkey in the Aegean, the Eastern Mediterranean and the skies. Speaking to his party’s provincial chairs in Ankara on Tuesday, Özel argued that foreign policy mistakes had left Turkey isolated. He pointed to Greece’s maritime deal with Egypt, its newer fighter jets and Turkey’s exclusion from European defence funds. Özgür Özel founded the New Party in July, after a court removed him as CHP leader. His new party is now the main opposition in Turkey’s parliament. Libya deal fails to win friends First, Özel said Turkey valued its maritime memorandum with Libya, but the deal alone could not protect Turkish rights in the Eastern Mediterranean. In his view, Ankara’s broken ties with Cairo made things worse. “The agreement Egypt signed with Greece is accepted by everyone, while our agreement with Libya is criticised, condemned and not accepted by insolent Europeans,” he said. Greece and its allies have rejected the Turkey-Libya deal as illegal , Greek City Times reported. Özel also mocked Erdogan for ending up “waiting at Sisi’s door” . He also criticised Turkey’s exclusion from SAFE, the European Union’s €150 billion defence fund. In fact, Turkey sends F-16s to help protect Baltic airspace, Özel noted. Likewise, he warned that the EU had left Turkey out of its “Made in Europe” rules. Nor has the bloc updated its customs union with Ankara. As a result, the Turkish car industry faces a “crushing blow” , he said. “They are treating Turkey as if it were China,” Özgür Özel told the meeting. Özgür Özel turns to F-35s and Fidan Turning to Washington, Özel said Turkey had bought 250 Boeing aircraft and paid high prices for gas. It also offered rare earths to win favour with US President Donald Trump. Yet US sanctions on Turkey remain in place. By contrast, Trump lifted the arms embargo on the Republic of Cyprus, which Özel called “South Cyprus”. Washington sold F-35s to Greece and Israel, along with the most modern F-16s, he said. Turkey, however, lost its place in the F-35 program. Özgür Özel also mocked Turkey’s Russian S-400 air defence systems. Turkey has switched them on only once, for a test, and they now sit in a hangar, he said. Finally, Özel turned on Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, whom he called “the TikToker Mr Hakan”. He accused Fidan of telling a Greek newspaper that extending Greek territorial waters to 12 miles is no casus belli. The Latin term means a cause for war. Turkey’s position, Özel said, rejects any extension beyond six miles. Turning to Fidan’s past as intelligence chief, he added: “Such ignorance is only possible with bad intent.” Similarly, he argued that Fidan’s request for notice of cable surveys , rather than a permit, had weakened Ankara. Since then, Greece has rejected even notification, Özgür Özel said. Later on Tuesday, Turkey’s Foreign Ministry denied that Fidan had given an interview to a Greek newspaper. The ministry also insisted that Turkey’s positions on the Aegean and the Eastern Mediterranean remain unchanged, Turkish media reported. title: U.S. Intel Confirms This Is China’s Secret Spaceplane (Updated)
body: The U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) has confirmed that an image that has been circulating online for years does indeed show an experimental Chinese reusable spaceplane in orbit. A newly released higher-resolution copy of the image underscores that the design is nearly a dead ringer for the X-37B miniature space shuttles now operated by the U.S. Space Force . DIA included the higher-resolution image of the Chinese spaceplane in a new unclassified report on global security challenges outside of the Earth’s atmosphere, which was released yesterday . A satellite belonging to Maxar Technologies (now Vantor) captured the image, but when exactly remains unclear. It does have a 2024 copyright date. The image shows a miniature space shuttle-like design with small wings and twin vertical tails. It also has upward-opening doors above a central payload bay. There is also an extension at the tail end with solar panels seen deployed on either side. There are what look to be side-by-side ventral bays, which are likely for the main gear in a tricycle landing gear configuration. Overall, the core design is extremely similar to that of the U.S. X-37B , which also features tricycle landing gear and can also be fitted with an extended payload module at the tail. One major difference is that the wings on the Chinese design have a much longer chord compared to the X-37B. A side-by-side comparison of the on-orbit shot of the experimental Chinese reusable spaceplane (at left) and a U.S. X-37B fitted with an extended payload module being prepared for launch (at right). Vantor/U.S. Space Force Another look at an X-37B, seen here sitting on its tricycle landing gear after returning from a mission in space. USAF The X-37B used on the OTV-6 mission on the flight line at the Kennedy Space Center after its return to Earth on November 12, 2022. USAF “A key capability for reusable space activities are spaceplanes like this PRC [People’s Republic of China] Spaceplane captured by Maxar. Spaceplanes can launch into orbit to place objects in space or even test them and return to earth [sic],” reads the caption to the picture in DIA’s report. As noted, the basic fact of the existence of this image is not new. U.S. Space Force Col. John Patrick, then head of U.S. Space Forces-Korea (SPACEFOR-KOR), included a much lower-resolution version in a presentation at the Open Space Forum in South Korea in 2024. It was also not immediately clear at that time whether or not the picture simply showed an X-37B. TWZ had reached out at the time to the U.S. Space Force and Maxar for more information, and both had declined to comment. Two X-37Bs were built, and they have been sent on eight orbital missions, in total, since 2010. The Orbital Test Vehicle 8 (OTV-8) mission was launched on August 22, 2025. X-37B in orbit photographed by ground-based telescopes？ pic.twitter.com/YPj8I4cQmZ — 笑脸男人 (@lfx160219) November 8, 2024 China is understood to have conducted four separate orbital spaceplane missions using the same experimental vehicle since 2020. Three of those missions had concluded before Col. Patrick gave his presentation. The most recent launch occurred on February 7 of this year, and the vehicle has not yet returned, at least as far as we are aware. On the third mission, which lasted from December 14, 2023, to September 6, 2024, the Chinese spaceplane was observed releasing multiple smaller objects into orbit. What those payloads may have been remains unknown, but they could have been released from the main payload bay, which is seen open in the on-orbit image. The bay could have opened without any subsequent release of objects on either of the two prior missions, as well. As an aside, the spaceplane appears to have released at least one more object earlier this year in the course of its latest mission. A secretive airbase in the northwest end of China, sporting one of the longest runways in the world at 16,400 feet, looks to be where the spaceplane has landed after missions. The facility, which has been expanded massively in recent years , is now loosely akin to America’s top-secret proving ground at Area 51 , and has been the site of other advanced aviation test efforts . DIA’s report also says that “China has two primary spaceplane models: the Shenlong and Tengyun,” but does not specify which one is seen in the image. The name Shenlong has been commonly used to refer to the spaceplane China has been experimenting with to date. Images said to show a prototype or test article of this design slung underneath an H-6 bomber for testing purposes had emerged in 2007. Images that emerged in 2007 of a reusable spaceplane prototype, or a related test article, referred to as Shenlong, underneath an H-6 bomber. Chinese internet The state-run China Aerospace Science and Industry Corporation (CASIC) unveiled the Tengyun design in 2016 as part of a so-called two-stage-to-orbit system that uses a mothership aircraft flying within the atmosphere as part of the launch method rather than a traditional space launch rocket. As of 2020, CASIC was aiming for a live test of Tengyun in 2025 , but it is not immediately clear whether or not that occurred. Images showing wind tunnel testing of a Chinese two-stage-to-orbit concept. Chinese internet There have been other spaceplane developments in China in recent years. This includes designs from the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC) and Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC) subsidiary Chengdu. The design from Chengdu is called Haolong and has been in development officially as an option for resupplying the country’s Tiangong space station . They seem not only got a model but also a full-scale prototype. HaoLong-1 cargo spaceplane https://t.co/VI1Yoh3sRj pic.twitter.com/Dthfd1gi1v — CNSPACE (@CNSpaceflight) November 11, 2024 In general, “spaceplanes are … reusable and feature enhanced maneuverability, making them more suitable for certain missions than traditional satellites,” DIA’s report notes. TWZ has highlighted in the past how reusable space shuttle-like vehicles offer ideal platforms for rapidly deploying small satellites and any other payloads into orbit. In this way, they can be critical assets for space-based experimentation, as well as operational activities. This could include intelligence gathering , and even on-orbit attacks , areas of clear interest to the Chinese government . As we often mention in the context of the X-37B , spaceplanes also have distinct advantages when it comes to rendezvousing with and maneuvering very close to other objects in space. They can execute course changes and other maneuvers in ways that traditional satellites cannot. All of this only underscores their potential as weapon systems , as well as for gathering intelligence. The fact that a Maxar (now Vantor) satellite took an on-orbit picture – a service the company is known to offer – of a Chinese spaceplane further highlights the kind of cat-and-mouse games that are increasingly emerging in space. The general risks posed by these kinds of activities were recently thrust into the public eye by the unprecedentedly close shadowing of a commercial radar imaging satellite tied to Ukraine by another satellite belonging to Russia. China has been making massive investments, in general, in new space-based intelligence and other capabilities in recent years. Chinese space developments have now also extended into reusable space launch rocket boosters . Space launch company LandSpace became the first in China to achieve a successful recovery of a reusable space launch rocket booster on land in August. That followed CASC’s successful recovery of a reusable space launch rocket booster at sea using a specially configured ship the month before. In general, “access to space traditionally requires expendable spacecraft: single-use launch vehicles, satellites, and one-time use capsules designed to maximize performance. Reliance on expendable vehicles has made access to space expensive and exclusive,” DIA’s report explains. “Reusable technologies, while even more difficult and expensive to develop and build, stand to greatly reduce the cost of spaceflight by recovering, refurbishing, and reusing rocket stages, fairings, and capsules.” Chinese spaceplanes, one of which we have not definitively gotten a view of in orbit, look set to become an increasingly important part of this growing ecosystem. Update: 6:32 PM ET – Vantor has now provided an additional copy of the image of the Chinese spaceplane, elements of which look to be redacted, and some additional details. The company has confirmed it was taken on May 28, 2024, by the WorldView-3 satellite at a range of just under 56 miles (90 kilometers). “There is a separate satellite docked to the aft section of the vehicle whose structure and solar arrays are visible,” Vantor also told us. “The spacecraft’s payload bay doors are visibly open.” Contact the author: joe@twz.com The post U.S. Intel Confirms This Is China’s Secret Spaceplane (Updated) appeared first on TWZ .

title: We’re not behind waving of Russian flags during 2024 protests in Nigeria – Russia Foreign Minister
body: Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov has dismissed insinuations that the Russian government sponsored some Nigerian youths who waved Russian flags during the 2024 #EndBadGovernance protests. Lavrov, who spoke in Moscow on the sidelines of the Third Russia-Africa Summit, in response to a question by the News Agency of Nigeria, said Russia had no hand in the action and distanced Moscow from any attempt to undermine Nigeria’s sovereignty. According to him, Russia and Nigeria enjoy a robust relationship dating back to the Soviet Union. He said those who wore Russian flags did so in their personal capacity and that it did not translate into official support from Russia. “Anyone, who donned the Russian flag, did so in his or her personal capacity. It does not mean that Russia was in support of this kind of action. “A lot of citizens sympathetic to Palestinians wave Palestinian flags to express solidarity. It does not mean the Palestinian government is behind them,” Lavrov said. The News Agency of Nigeria(NAN), recalls that the nationwide #EndBadGovernance protests took place from Aug. 1 to Aug. 10, 2024, with the protesters citing high cost of living and economic hardship for their action. NAN also recalls that during the protests, some groups of protesters, mostly youths and minors in Kano, Kaduna, Zamfara and Abuja, were seen waving Russian flags and chanting slogans calling for military intervention. The action, which the Federal Government described as treasonable and a threat to Nigeria’s sovereignty, led to the arrest of scores of protesters and some tailors who were allegedly sewing the flags. The Russian Embassy in Abuja had, at the time, also denied any involvement. Lavrov said the robust relationship between Nigeria and Russia had seen an increase in scholarships awarded to Nigerians, reaching a peak of 220 in 2026. He recalled that in 2024, he met with his Nigerian counterpart in Abuja who warmly received him, and cemented the bilateral ties between the two countries. On defence pacts with some countries in the Sahel, Lavrov said Russia was helping to eliminate security threats in the region, adding that Moscow was aware that some Western capitals were using Ukrainian mercenaries to sabotage the efforts, as they did in Libya, in a bid to undermine regional stability. Commenting on the recent diesel supply agreement with the United States, the foreign minister said it was purely a business decision and would not affect the interest of its allies. “The diesel agreement with the U.S. is purely a business decision by two world leaders who are concerned by the rising cost of energy,” he said. The post We’re not behind waving of Russian flags during 2024 protests in Nigeria – Russia Foreign Minister appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Turkey Forms New Marine Brigade as Greece Tests New Drone Systems
body: Turkey has established a new marine brigade in Iskenderun as Greece and Turkey pursue parallel programmes to develop unmanned military systems, highlighting the growing focus on drones, electronic warfare and amphibious capabilities in the Eastern Mediterranean. The developments come as both countries test new military technologies and adapt their armed forces to changing operational requirements. Turkey’s latest move follows the creation of a unified Amphibious Army Corps, which, according to the report, has tripled the number of its relevant brigades. Greek Navy tests unmanned systems The Hellenic Navy completed its small-scale technical exercise, UVEX 2/26, on Thursday, 22 October. The exercise took place in the Saronic Gulf and the southern Evian Gulf naval area, marking another step in Greece’s efforts to test and integrate innovative unmanned systems into naval operations. Observers from France, Italy and Cyprus watched the exercise, which brought together Greece’s defence innovation ecosystem, including ELKAK and KETAK, and domestic industry. The Hellenic Navy tested unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), unmanned surface vessels (USVs) and unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs) under realistic conditions. The scenarios included drone swarms designed to overwhelm opposing defences, the use of loitering munitions and measures to protect critical underwater infrastructure and ports. The electronic warfare trials also produced encouraging results for Greek military planners, according to the report. Participants successfully tested systems designed to detect and jam hostile drones through telemetry and satellite transmissions, examining vulnerabilities in the operation of these systems. Turkey expands its amphibious forces Turkey conducted its own unmanned-systems naval exercise, TURNAs-2026, in the Gulf of Antalya from 19 to 27 October. The exercise tested interoperability between military personnel and autonomous platforms. On Tuesday, 27 October, Turkey’s political and military leadership, led by Defence Minister Yaşar Güler, attended a ceremony in Iskenderun to present the military colours to the newly established 2nd Amphibious Marine Brigade. The development reflects a broader reorganisation of Turkey’s military forces. The report says Ankara has established a unified Amphibious Army Corps and tripled its relevant brigades. The new brigade’s location in Iskenderun places the unit on Turkey’s eastern Mediterranean coast, in a position relevant to its amphibious operations in the region and around Cyprus. During his address, Güler also presented Turkey as an influential international actor, referring to recent military agreements with countries in the Gulf and Asia, including the Mecca Agreement and the Bedir Memorandum. He also criticised Nicosia over what he described as the isolation of Turkish Cypriots. Greece outlines its defence strategy under Agenda 2030 Greek Defence Minister Nikos Dendias set out Athens’ response to regional security challenges and technological change in his order of the day for Greece’s 28 October national anniversary. Dendias linked the historic “Ochi” of 1940 to the modern need for Greece to defend its national sovereignty independently. “International law is the foundation of international relations, but the implementation and protection of the rights arising from it require a credible deterrence capability,” Dendias said. He added that revisionist practices, attempts to impose faits accomplis through military force and rapid technological advances made the adaptation of the armed forces a national duty. Greece is pursuing this transformation through its Agenda 2030 defence reform programme, which includes: A new force structure and long-term defence procurement planning. The integration of autonomous systems and emerging technologies, including the proposed Achilles Shield air-defence and anti-drone system. Stronger cyber defence capabilities and the reorganisation of the military reserve. Development of Greece’s domestic defence innovation sector, demonstrated through exercises such as UVEX 2/26. Athens has emphasised technological development, modernisation and deterrence as central elements of its response to the evolving security environment in the Aegean and Eastern Mediterranean. The developments in both countries illustrate how unmanned platforms, electronic warfare and force restructuring are becoming increasingly important to military planning across the region.
