title: High voter turnout leaves small parties below electoral threshold | This is who missed out
body: High voter turnout in Israel's 2026 election left little room for smaller parties, all of which fell below the electoral threshold, according to television exit polls. Three parties stood out in recent weeks: Amcha Yisrael, the Reservists-Economic Party and the Haredi Public Party. The first two had hovered around the electoral threshold in the latest polls, while the third generated momentum on social media that, according to the exit polls, failed to translate into votes. Amcha Yisrael Among the smaller parties, the collapse of former IDF brigadier general Ofer Winter's Amcha Yisrael party was particularly striking. The party initially polled in the single digits in Knesset seats following its launch, but slipped toward the electoral threshold in recent surveys as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu intensified his attacks against it. According to all television exit polls, it has now failed to cross the threshold.   Winter, who commanded the Givati Brigade during Operation Protective Edge in 2014, retired from the IDF in December 2024 with the rank of brigadier general. About a year and a half after leaving the military, he announced the establishment of Amcha Yisrael, naming pro-Israel advocacy activist Yoseph Haddad as his No. 2 candidate. Netanyahu waged an aggressive campaign against Winter in an effort to pressure him to withdraw from the race, amid polls suggesting he was at risk of failing to cross the electoral threshold. But Winter, who had announced at the beginning of his campaign that he would recommend Netanyahu for prime minister, refused to drop out. His decision appears to have cost Netanyahu's bloc tens of thousands of votes. Sources close to Winter told ynet Tuesday evening that he had spent recent days crisscrossing the country, persuading voters, making phone calls, joining family WhatsApp groups and fighting for every vote against the odds while facing what they described as an "insane campaign" against him.   They argued that had Winter not entered the race, Yoaz Hendel and Yaron Zelekha would certainly have crossed the electoral threshold, giving the anti-Netanyahu bloc another four seats. "We fought until the very end despite Netanyahu and his allies' violent, disgraceful and ugly campaign," a party source said. "We have a solid base of voters," the source added, claiming that more than 100,000 people had voted for the party. Amcha Yisrael officials insisted that Netanyahu had made the strategic mistake, arguing that his effort to draw votes away from their party had cost his own bloc valuable Knesset seats. "We could have won today," a party source claimed. "But the unhinged campaign by Netanyahu and Smotrich, who talked about Judaizing the Galilee and the Bedouins in the Negev, drove Arab voters to the polls in huge numbers instead of keeping them at home." Looking ahead, party officials maintain that Amcha Yisrael has established a solid voter base. They suggest that, much like Itamar Ben-Gvir, who ran unsuccessfully several times before gaining substantial electoral support, the party could return in the next election and attract more votes. The Reservists-Economic Party Yoaz Hendel and Yaron Zelekha, who joined forces on a single electoral list under the Reservists-Economic Party banner, also failed to cross the electoral threshold, according to the exit polls. Hendel and Zelekha explored several possible political alliances before ultimately joining forces. In some of the final preelection polls, their list appeared to gain momentum, reaching the equivalent of four Knesset seats. But when voters went to the polls, the exit surveys indicated that Israelis had opted for larger parties.   Hendel, who served as communications minister in the previous change government and, about 15 years ago, headed Netanyahu's National Information Directorate, established the Reservists Party last year. In July, he announced a joint run with Hili Tropper's party, but after Tropper joined Gadi Eisenkot, Hendel aligned himself with Zelekha's Economic Party. During the Swords of Iron war, Hendel was called up for reserve duty, participated in combat operations in Gaza and established a new battalion made up of former special forces soldiers who had passed the age of mandatory reserve service. Hendel previously belonged to Moshe "Bogie" Ya'alon's Telem party, which later joined Benny Gantz's Blue and White alliance. He was also a member of Derech Eretz alongside Zvi Hauser and New Hope under Gideon Sa'ar, and signed a merger agreement to establish the Zionist Spirit alliance headed by Ayelet Shaked. Economist Yaron Zelekha, ranked second on the list, served as the Finance Ministry's accountant general from 2003 to 2007. He ran independently in the previous two elections, receiving less than 1% of the vote each time and failing to cross the electoral threshold. Third on the list was Einat Wilf, who served in the Knesset from 2010 to 2013 as a member of the Labor Party and later Ehud Barak's Independence faction. Hendel said Tuesday evening that he was counting on the double-envelope ballots, which include votes cast by soldiers. "By the end of the week, we'll know the results from IDF polling stations," he said. "We experienced incredible momentum. Let's see the actual results. In any case, we fought very, very hard. We're fighters, we work hard, and we'll fulfill our ambitions for the State of Israel and the Jewish people. Nobody here is giving up. That's the first thing." Hendel also thanked Winter for what he described as the "difficult road" he had traveled.   The Haredi Public Party The third party that appears to have attracted some support but failed to cross the electoral threshold is the Haredi Public Party, led by Moti Leitner. Netanyahu also campaigned against the party in an effort to pressure it to withdraw from the race. Leitner sought to offer ultra-Orthodox voters an alternative to parties that support sweeping exemptions from military service and oppose the inclusion of core curriculum subjects in religious schools. While Israel's established ultra-Orthodox parties, Shas and United Torah Judaism, have pushed for military service exemptions, restrictions on core curriculum studies and the allocation of welfare funding, Leitner presented a more pragmatic ideological approach. Throughout the campaign, he claimed that support for his party was growing among younger members of the ultra-Orthodox community. According to the exit polls, however, that support ultimately proved insufficient to carry the party across the electoral threshold.

title: ‘We want to help Armenia find markets beyond Russia’, says Dutch foreign minister
body: The Netherlands to support Armenian entrepreneurs “The Netherlands wants to help Armenian businesses, including flower growers, find alternative markets for their products outside Russia ,” Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen said in Yerevan. At a joint news conference with his Armenian counterpart, Ararat Mirzoyan, he stressed that Russia’s economic restrictions were creating difficulties for Armenian businesses, particularly in the flower-growing sector. “We welcome the opportunities that the EU’s autonomous trade measures offer Armenia . We hope Armenia will make full use of this opportunity. The Netherlands will continue to support efforts to diversify Armenia’s economy,” he said. On 24 September, the Council of the EU gave final approval to a regulation introducing autonomous trade measures for Armenian goods. The regulation removes import duties on around 80% of Armenia’s exports to the EU. The preferential trade regime will remain in force for two years. Russian-led EAEU bloc warns Armenia of possible ‘serious blows’ to its economy How Armenia is reacting to export restrictions on Russia: farmers’ views and official statistics Preferential regime for Armenian exports to EU in response to Russian restrictions Dutch foreign minister offers help in finding missing persons The Dutch foreign minister welcomed the steps Armenia and Azerbaijan have taken over the past year as part of the peace process. “For peace to take hold in this region, it is crucial that the process culminates in the signing of a peace agreement. We fully support you,” he stressed. Berendsen announces initiative for both Armenia and Azerbaijan The initiative will provide funding to help establish the fate of people missing on both sides. “It is vital to build bridges of trust and make this an integral part of the peace process. The Netherlands stands ready to provide financial support and, where possible, assistance in other forms.” Armenian Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan thanked his Dutch counterpart for the initiative. “The issue of missing persons is extremely sensitive and important for both Armenia and Azerbaijan. In my view, the involvement and contribution of third parties such as the Netherlands in this area will be welcomed by everyone.” Asked by journalists about Armenian prisoners held in Baku, the Dutch foreign minister did not give a direct answer. He reiterated that his country supports the establishment of lasting peace between Armenia and Azerbaijan. He noted that the process would require the resolution of both “simple and difficult issues”. Rights activist Siranush Sahakyan: ‘Lives of all Armenians held in Baku are in danger’ Siranush Sahakyan, who represents Armenian prisoners at the ECHR, discusses their trials in Azerbaijan and conditions in detention. ‘There may be a political motive’: Armenian foreign minister on plans to expel Armenia from the EAEU Journalists asked Armenia’s foreign minister for his views on a document recently prepared by the Eurasian Intergovernmental Council concerning the possible expulsion of Armenia from the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU). The document itself states that the charter of the Russian-led economic bloc contains no mechanism for terminating a country’s membership at the decision of the other members. This means that Armenia itself would have to decide to change its membership status. However, the council’s experts, who prepared the document, cite the Vienna Convention to support their argument that Armenia’s membership could be suspended. The convention allows other states to terminate a country’s participation in a multilateral treaty if it commits a material breach. “For such a scenario to become possible, a partner — the one whose actions the others are unhappy with and whom they want to expel or suspend — would have to breach its obligations within the organisation. The other four partners could then say: ‘You are breaking our rules, dear fifth friend. Thank you and goodbye.’ But Armenia has breached nothing and has no intention of doing so,” Ararat Mirzoyan explained, commenting on the convention’s provisions. He stressed that Armenia had fulfilled its commitments in good faith and expected its EAEU partners to do the same. The minister believes Armenia’s EAEU partners have tried to find legal grounds for expelling the country, but he rejects their arguments. “We all understand that there is a political motive here, possibly even a political instruction to lawyers to find a legal justification for a political decision.” Experts in Armenia have linked the actions of its EAEU partners to the country’s efforts to diversify its international ties and move closer to the European Union. Mirzoyan said Yerevan would make its decisions based on its own national interests and sovereign rights, which were not up for negotiation. At the same time, Armenia would continue constructive co-operation with its partners in the bloc. Alongside Russia, the EAEU includes Belarus, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan. Armenia–Netherlands bilateral co-operation Ararat Mirzoyan praised the Netherlands for supporting democratic reforms in Armenia and efforts to deepen relations between Armenia and the EU. He said the two sides discussed the situation in the South Caucasus and the wider region during a one-to-one meeting and subsequent expanded talks. They also reviewed their bilateral agenda, with a particular focus on economic co-operation. The talks paid special attention to implementing the priorities set out in the Joint Declaration on Strategic Partnership, which the two countries signed in March 2025. “Political dialogue is at a very high level. It is active and effective. We can also see economic co-operation gradually developing, with the figures growing. However, we recognise that significant potential remains untapped,” the minister said. He added that the two countries planned to deepen co-operation in several areas, including healthcare, infrastructure, agriculture and floriculture. On the latter, he said that “our flower-producing companies have already established ties with world-renowned Dutch firms”. Meanwhile, the Centre for the Promotion of Imports from developing countries (CBI) has launched a year-long programme in Armenia. The initiative aims to help 21 Armenian producers of dried fruit and nuts develop their export potential and enter markets in the Netherlands and other EU countries. Armenia begins shift from Russia towards EU – but finish line remains distant JAMnews reviewed the latest developments and spoke to analysts with opposing views. Residents of Armenia also shared their opinions on how they believe the country should shape its future. The Netherlands to support Armenian entrepreneurs

title: Thessaloniki Marks 100th Anniversary of Military Medical School
body: Greece’s Aristotle University of Thessaloniki and the Hellenic Army Academy of Corps Officers (SSAS) marked a century of cooperation at an anniversary event, with university rector Professor Kyriakos Anastasiadis highlighting the strong ties between the institutions and the importance of combining higher education with national service. During the ceremony marking 100 years since the establishment of the Military Medical School, Aristotle University honoured Chief of the Hellenic National Defence General Staff General Dimitrios Choupis, while SSAS awarded former Aristotle University rector Anastasios Manthos. A shared history spanning a century Anastasiadis said the anniversary offered an opportunity to recognise a partnership that had developed over time, supporting the scientific training of military personnel while strengthening the university’s academic community. “Today, we celebrate a century of the Military Medical School and Aristotle University moving forward together. This is no coincidence. We share the same lecture halls and the same commitment to our homeland and its values,” he said. The rector noted that Aristotle University’s establishment in 1925 and the founding of the Military Medical School in 1926 reflected the same national need: investment in knowledge, science and the country’s human resources. He also recalled the military school’s re-establishment in Thessaloniki in 1946 and the integration of its students into Aristotle University’s academic life from 1947. The military school’s presence in Thessaloniki helped develop the university’s medical faculty, increasing student numbers and highlighting the need for greater investment in facilities, personnel and resources to educate military doctors. As the university established new academic departments, the school expanded its educational scope to train military officers in additional disciplines. Its renaming as the Hellenic Army Academy of Corps Officers in 1970 reflected this broader mission, which came to include law, economics, psychology and information technology alongside health sciences. “The two institutions did not simply follow parallel paths. They developed together. This shared journey represents one of the most successful examples of combining higher education with a national mission,” Anastasiadis said. Knowledge, integrity and duty as shared values The rector stressed that university education plays an essential role in preparing officers in specialist corps, describing scientific training as an integral part of their mission rather than an additional skill. He said the state’s decision to link military training with university education had stood the test of time. SSAS students study at Aristotle University, using the same lecture theatres, laboratories and university clinics and participating in the same academic life. “The military uniform and the academic gown do not represent two different worlds. They represent two different expressions of the same mission: service to people and to the homeland,” he said, expressing pride in the institutions’ longstanding cooperation. Their shared history has fostered a community built on knowledge, mutual respect and trust. SSAS graduates have returned to Aristotle University as distinguished professors, while university academics have helped train generations of military officers. Anastasiadis said SSAS brought together three important traditions: science, virtue and duty. “Knowledge without judgement can become dangerous. Power without values can become destructive. And technology without ethics does not lead to progress,” he said. Technology and the quality of human resources Addressing SSAS students, Anastasiadis said they had chosen not merely a profession but a mission carrying greater responsibility towards their country and society. “Most people your age choose a profession. You have chosen a mission,” he said. He noted that future officers would face a rapidly changing environment in which artificial intelligence, biotechnology, cybersecurity, hybrid threats and emerging technologies were transforming defence, security and healthcare. In this environment, he argued, a country’s strength would increasingly depend not only on its weapons systems but also on the quality and education of its people and their ability to generate knowledge, innovate and adapt. He pointed to Ukraine as an example, saying that despite four years of war and intense pressure from an adversary with superior technological and numerical resources, Ukrainians had developed systems that were becoming models for some of the world’s most advanced armed forces. The rector added that major institutions justified their historical legacy not only by preserving it but also by adapting their work to the needs of each era. New opportunities for cooperation in the next century Looking ahead, Anastasiadis said the centenary provided an opportunity to deepen cooperation between Aristotle University and SSAS while respecting each institution’s distinct role. He identified further opportunities for collaboration in education, research, innovation and lifelong learning, with the aim of connecting scientific knowledge more closely with practical applications and the needs of society and the country. “A hundred years ago, some people had the courage to bring us together, and history proved them right. Today, we must go further than they did,” he said. He called for new collaborative initiatives, greater investment in research and innovation, upgraded educational programmes and expanded international partnerships. Anastasiadis pledged to continue strengthening the relationship, with both institutions maintaining their shared commitment to science and national service. “A country’s real strength lies not only in its military power, its social mobility or the growth of its economy. It lies in its people,” he said. He concluded that Aristotle University and SSAS continued to share a mission rooted in knowledge, integrity, responsibility and service to the homeland. “These are the values the Hellenic Army Academy of Corps Officers has served for a century. These are the values Aristotle University has served for a century. And these are precisely the values we owe to our ancestors and our descendants,” he said, congratulating SSAS on its centenary. title: DIA Releases Clearest Image of China’s Reusable Spaceplane with Service Module Attached
body: The DIA report reviews the three missions flown between 2020 and 2023, highlighting reported rendezvous and proximity operations during the second and third flights, before China launched the spacecraft again in February 2026. The U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) has released a new image of China’s secretive reusable spaceplane, captured by a Maxar Technologies spacecraft in 2024. Published in the DIA’s “Challenges to Security in Space” report on Oct. 26, 2026, the photo provides a rare view of the spacecraft in orbit with its service module attached. China’s reusable experimental spacecraft has flown four orbital missions since September 2020, launched aboard Long March 2F rockets. The first mission lasted two days; the second, launched in August 2022, remained in orbit for 276 days; and the third, launched in December 2023, lasted 268 days. A fourth mission began in February 2026. Before the release of the Maxar image, public imagery was limited to grainy ground-based telescope observations and computer-generated illustrations with Chinese markings. Space tracking forums in early 2023 observed the Chinese spacecraft connecting with another object multiple times, but no image existed at the time. The Maxar image used in the DIA report is dated to 2024, when the spacecraft launched in December 2023 was still in orbit during its third mission. The timing is therefore consistent with the photograph depicting the vehicle during that flight, although the exact date of capture has not been publicly disclosed. Behold: The US Defense Intelligence Agency has released a report on challenges to security in space, including an NEI image of China’s spaceplane from Maxar, taken in 2024. https://t.co/F3msSwoFph — Andrew Jones (@AJ_FI) October 27, 2026 The report identifies two Chinese space models, Shenlong and Tengyun, but it is not known which of those is in the image. The Chinese spacecraft is often compared with the U.S. Space Force’s X-37B because both are uncrewed reusable orbital vehicles designed to return to Earth. However, the Chinese vehicle’s design, payload, and mission objectives remain largely undisclosed. Tracking data indicate that it has deployed objects and performed rendezvous and proximity operations, but these observations do not establish the spacecraft’s intended military role. The spaceplane appears in the DIA’s broader assessment of space-related capabilities and threats, whose goal is to cover the capabilities of strategic rivals. “The updated report details the space defense and military goals, including strategies, plans and intentions, of China, Russia and the emerging space powers of Iran and North Korea,” says the press release . The Long March 2F/T launch vehicle, similar to the one used to carry the Chinese reusable spaceplane, lifting off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center. | Source: Xinhua Chinese spacecraft The image provides a view of the underside of China’s reusable spaceplane, with its service module attached and solar arrays deployed. The module is understood to provide electrical power and propulsion during the orbital mission before separating from the spaceplane ahead of reentry, similarly to the X-37B’s service module. The image also appears to show the spacecraft’s payload-bay doors, although the precise configuration and function of the visible features have not been publicly detailed. Among the possibilities are systems like robotic arms, small satellites or specimens for in-orbit testing. Now then — this could be something exceptional. The rumours are that inside this exceptional payload fairing atop a CZ-2F is a CASC spaceplane, launching from Jiuquan Friday. Source: 俊了个锅 via 林晓弈。 https://t.co/qs6VRfzQoP https://t.co/ZPnpwAIfyO — Andrew Jones (@AJ_FI) September 3, 2020 Beijing launched its first ever reusable spaceplane prototype on Sep. 4, 2020 aboard a Long March 2F carrier rocket from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwestern China’s Gobi desert. The spacecraft remained in orbit for two days before returning to Earth. Although Chinese authorities did not initially disclose the landing site in detail, open-source analysis of satellite imagery associated the landing with a runway near the Lop Nur nuclear test site in northwestern China. Since its launch on 4 August 2022, we observed multiple large maneuvers raising the object’s altitude — as well as repeated deployments, formation flying, and docking of a sub-satellite Object J (NORAD ID 54218). https://t.co/ORVgSXYKmJ — LeoLabs (@LeoLabs_Space) May 8, 2023 The second launch of the space plane took place on Aug. 4, 2022, this time spending 276 days in orbit until May 8, 2023. According to the DIA, the vehicle appeared to “maneuver with a companion satellite and conduct station-keeping at around 1 km separation.” “At one point, the two objects appeared within 100 meters of one another. The spaceplane and satellite possibly rendezvoused before the satellite was re-released,” the DIA report said. This event tested our object tracking and maneuver detection and characterization capabilities, proving that we can provide critical intelligence on the behaviors and activities of objects in #LEO thanks to our continuous, real-time operations. https://t.co/WDP06ffBSv — LeoLabs (@LeoLabs_Space) May 8, 2023 On May 8, 2023, commercial space-tracking company LeoLabs reported that its observations indicated repeated deployments, formation flying, and apparent docking or capture operations involving ‘Object J’: “Since its launch on 4 August 2022, we observed multiple large maneuvers raising the object’s altitude – as well as repeated deployments, formation flying, and docking of a sub-satellite Object J (NORAD ID 54218). We’ve determined that the Test Spacecraft2 has propulsive capability and engaged in proximity operations with Object J, including what appeared to be at least two and possibly three capture/docking operations.” China launched the spacecraft on its third orbital mission on Dec. 14, 2023. It remained in orbit for 268 days, returning on Sept. 6, 2024, according to the DIA report. The U.S. Space Force’s X-37B Orbital Test Vehicle Mission Seven successfully landed at Vandenberg Space Force Base, Calif., March 7, 2025. | Source: U.S. Space Force courtesy photo During that flight, the spacecraft again “released and interacted with an object,”according to the DIA. Considering that the Maxar image was captured in 2024, we can presume the vehicle was photographed during this third mission. Although this was not covered by the report, the spacecraft’s fourth mission began in February 2026. Orbital-tracking data analyzed by astronomer Jonathan McDowell indicated that the vehicle released and subsequently recaptured the same object, whose precise identity and purpose remain unknown, with similar operations reportedly repeated later in the flight. then executed a rerendezvous with the subsat on Sep 10 and a recapture on Sep 13. This analysis is based on USSF GP data. USSF also cataloged an additional object 24J on about Sep 10, but with no orbit data; I think this was a mistake and is a duplicate of object 24H. — Jonathan McDowell (@planet4589) September 23, 2026 Future and purpose The spacecraft’s proximity operations have raised questions about potential counterspace applications, with some theories assigning more exotic kinetic ‘anti-satellite’ capabilities to the Chinese spacecraft. While there is no evidence yet the vehicle is designed as a kinetic anti-satellite weapon, and the spaceplane’s intended mission remains undisclosed, space is becoming a contested domain. The observed rendezvous and capture capabilities can support satellite inspection and servicing, but could also enable interference with other spacecraft. The spacecraft’s potential military applications remain uncertain. While there is no public evidence confirming that the vehicle carries military payloads, such a platform could be used for space-based reconnaissance, intelligence-gathering, and monitoring of other space objects, as well as kinetic missions possibly involving the use of directed energy weapons, offensive weapons or electronic warfare. A machine translation of a Xinhua report of the Aug. 5, 2022 launch said: “The test spacecraft will be in orbit for a period of time before returning to the scheduled landing site in China, during which reusable and in-orbit service technology verification will be carried out as planned to provide technical support for the peaceful use of space.”

title: Mbappé sorry for ‘ill-judged’ Mao remark after backlash in China
body: Kylian Mbappé has apologised for “ill-judged” comments about late Chinese leader Mao Zedong, which led several Chinese brands to drop him. Mbappé reportedly told the French talk show The Bridge about the meme “that makes me laugh the most, it’s the one where there’s a video of a guy, I think it’s a Chinese dictator…” He then laughs as the clip cuts to a meme showing his face superimposed on an image resembling Mao. The meme is part of a running joke about the Real Madrid forward being called a “dictator” because of his huge influence in football. “My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world,” Mbappé said in a statement. “I apologise to everyone my words have upset.” Spain’s La Liga also apologised, saying it “deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappé’s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans”. The joke did not go down well in China, where Mao is revered by the Communist Party, despite his chaotic and often violent rule that left millions dead. A few people came out in his support on Chinese social media, but that’s rare given China’s tightly controlled internet, where people are expected to toe the party and government line on sensitive topics. Few topics are as sensitive as Mao, which may explain why brands were so quick to terminate partnerships with a global sports star like Mbappé. The show’s YouTube channel doesn’t have the original video, and it’s unclear when the interview, hosted by Real Madrid’s Aurélien Tchouaméni, first aired. In clips circulating online, Mbappé does not name Mao. He says he “uses [the meme] with friends all the time”. The furore appeared to kick off Monday night after Chinese football forum Dongqiudi drew attention to the comments in a statement, calling them “inappropriate” and saying they “hurt the feelings of Chinese people”. Screengrabs of the clip and meme have since spread quickly on Chinese social media, with people echoing this sentiment and even calling for a boycott of both the French striker and his club, Real Madrid. But some have blurred the meme itself as well as the part of the comment they found offensive, when Mbappe refers to “a Chinese dictator”. Dongqiudi said in its statement that it was “unable to translate” his comments because they were “offensive to China and the Chinese people”. Many people are therefore also wondering what exactly Mbappe said and have responded to the angry posts and comments with questions, wanting to know more. Weibo users are recirculating the clip by blurring the meme and redacting references to Mao What is the reaction in China? Chinese fans have been criticising Mbappé – who is popular in China and has huge brand endorsements – of “profiting from the Chinese market yet making remarks that offend the Chinese public”. “International public figures, in particular, should show greater respect and sensitivity, as national sentiment must never be taken lightly,” reads another comment on Weibo. As online anger grew louder, Chinese brands began cutting ties, though they did not explicitly refer to the video. The country’s largest dairy producer, Mengniu, said it “firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people”. Drinks giant Dongpeng issued a similar statement: “Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments.” According to state-owned newspaper The Global Times, state broadcaster CCTV’s news apps will not feature content related to the French striker. Chinese media reported on Tuesday that CCTV will also stop showing La Liga matches. Real Madrid is one of 20 clubs in the Spanish football league and is the most decorated team, with 36 league titles. China’s foreign ministry has also weighed in, with spokesperson Lin Jian saying: “We have noted the relevant reports. Words and deeds that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with opposition from all sectors of Chinese society.” Mbappé has a significant commercial presence in China China is a major market for international sports stars and homegrown brands have signed multimillion-dollar endorsement contracts with Mbappé, Norwegian striker Erling Haaland, and NBA player Stephen Curry. By 14:00 local time on Tuesday, five of the top 10 trending topics on Weibo centred on Mbappé, with the hashtag “multiple brands terminate partnerships with Mbappé” topping the list. “Don’t ever come to China,” read one of Weibo’s top comments. Why is Mao a sensitive topic? Mao founded the People’s Republic of China in 1949 and ruled through the tumultuous 1960s and 1970s. His attempt at rapid industrialisation, the Great Leap Forward, led to a famine that killed tens of millions. Then came the Cultural Revolution: a violent purge of anyone seen as a threat to Communism, which included Chinese intellectuals, landowners, artists and often rivals within the Party. His death in 1976 ushered in a new era for China, as it began to open its doors to the global economy. Even as the country moved away from Mao’s rule, the party continued to hail him as a national icon whose legacy was beyond reproach. So jokes or memes about Mao are seen not just as an insult to the party but also to its closely guarded narrative about the country’s past. Mbappé has said some of the memes “reveal a lack of political and human awareness” It’s unclear when the Mbappé meme involving Mao began, but his nickname, “the dictator”, has made the striker the subject of many memes and jokes online. Mbappé is widely regarded as one of the world’s best footballers and has wielded significant influence at the clubs he has played for. His extraordinary speed, goalscoring ability, and worldwide popularity have made him a global icon, attracting millions of fans, major sponsorship deals, and media attention, with his influence extending into fashion, culture, and business. In 2024, he sued a French influencer and kebab shop owner for using his name in the description of one of the shop’s sandwiches, leading to more jokes about the nickname. France teammate Ousmane Dembele jumped on the trend during the 2026 World Cup, calling Mbappé Mobut – a reference to Mobutu Sese Seko, the dictator who ruled the Democratic Republic of Congo, formerly Zaire, for three decades. In a September interview with France Football, Mbappé acknowledged the light-heartedness behind many of these memes, but said they “sometimes reveal a lack of political and human awareness among people”. “There’s a side that’s a bit less funny, because we know the damage people like that have caused throughout history,” he said. “Being compared to people who murder others, or who have made millions upon millions of people miserable… I don’t think I’ve done that in my life.”

title: NCGC guarantees N64.13bn loans to businesses, individuals
body:
The National Credit Guarantee Company (NCGC) has supported N64.13 billion in loans to businesses and individuals since it began operations, expanding access to finance for Nigerians lacking conventional collateral.
The ‌‌‍‌‍⁠⁠‍‌‌‍⁠‌‍‍‍‌Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NCGC, Bonaventure Okhaimo, disclosed this on Tuesday at a news conference on the company’s performance and implementation of its mandate at the State House, Abuja.
He said the company had deployed N30.19 billion in credit guarantees to support the loans, enabling financial institutions to finance viable businesses and individuals they might otherwise reject because of inadequate collateral.
“Our value proposition is simple. We provide partial guarantees that de-risk lending, expand the supply of credit and catalyse economic growth,” Mr Okhaimo said.
He explained that NCGC does not lend directly but partners with financial institutions to share lending risks, providing guarantee coverage of up to 60 per cent under its standard framework.
“This allows lenders to say yes to borrowers they would otherwise turn away, often with less collateral and on better terms,” he said.
Mr Okhaimo said the company had reached 174,495 borrowers across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory as of 21 October, through partnerships with 19 financial institutions.
He said women accounted for 42.7 per cent of the beneficiaries, while 22,616 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) had accessed formal financing for the first time.
The NCGC boss said the interventions had supported an estimated 914,791 jobs, comprising 175,481 direct jobs and 739,310 indirect jobs associated with the businesses.
He added that the company recorded 7,731 beneficiaries under youth empowerment, noting that it intended to expand access to credit for young Nigerians.
To improve financing for women-owned businesses, Mr Okhaimo said the company introduced GuaranteeHer, a gender-responsive credit guarantee initiative launched on July 29, and formally unveiled to stakeholders in Lagos on Sept. 3.
He said the initiative targeted more than N100 billion in lending over five years, with at least 20,000 women-owned enterprises expected to benefit and generate more than 150,000 jobs.
“Rather than create yet another product, we strengthen the programmes women already know, so lenders can offer lower interest rates, less collateral and longer tenors,” he said.
Mr Okhaimo explained that GuaranteeHer provided coverage of up to 70 per cent of eligible loan exposure, compared with the standard 60 per cent, with a maximum guarantee obligation of N50 million per borrower.
He said the company had also introduced its Credit Advantage Series to help MSMEs improve financial literacy, understand credit requirements and strengthen their capacity to access and manage loans.
As part of the programme, he said NCGC was collaborating with the Nigeria Revenue Service on a virtual engagement scheduled for Wednesday to help businesses understand their tax obligations and requirements for participating in the formal economy.
The company commenced operations with N100 billion in capital, contributed equally by the Bank of Industry, Ministry of Finance Incorporated, Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority, and Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation (CREDICORP).
Established on 29 May, 2025, with President Bola Tinubu’s approval, NCGC obtained its operating licence from the Central Bank of Nigeria on 9 August, 2025, and operates under the oversight of the Federal Ministry of Finance.
Mr Okhaimo said the capital base could support a guarantee portfolio of up to N1 trillion under the company’s leverage framework, enabling it to mobilise additional financing for businesses and individuals.
“Our goal is clear: no viable Nigerian business should be denied credit simply because it lacks collateral,” he said. (NAN)

title: South Africa evacuation expenditure ‘smacks of a grand scheme of corruption’ – Abu Jinapor
body: The Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abdulai Jinapor, has accused the Foreign Affairs Ministry of failing to adequately account for expenditure on the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa, describing the entire exercise as a “grand scheme of corruption to siphon public funds”. According to him, the discrepancies surrounding the GH¢49.72 million evacuation expenditure raise serious concerns about possible misappropriation of public funds, fraud and corruption, warranting an independent investigation into the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Speaking on JoyFM’s Top Story on Tuesday, October 27, Mr Jinapor said the Minority believes GH¢16.4 million remains unaccounted for and has renewed its demand for Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa to resign pending an independent audit. “The point is that the totality of this whole South Africa evacuation accounted in expenditure smacks of a grand scheme of corruption to siphon public funds and in that case the minister should take ultimate responsibility,” he said. Mr Jinapor said the concerns go beyond questions about whether the expenditure was adequately documented, pointing to alleged duplicate entries, discrepancies in payment records and cases where individuals reportedly signed for allowances they did not receive in full or at all. Read also: Minority demands Ablakwa’s resignation or dismissal over SA evacuation payments He also cited expenditure records without supporting receipts and questions surrounding the chartered flights used during the evacuation. “We have consistently maintained that some 16.4 million Ghana cedis is unaccounted for,” he said. According to him, the Minority’s concerns have been reinforced by the Multimedia Group’s JoyNews Research documentary aired on Monday, October 26, which examined discrepancies in documents provided by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The Research investigation reported apparent discrepancies in payment records, including questionable signatures, as part of its examination of how the GH¢49.72 million expenditure was accounted for. Mr Jinapor further questioned why documents subsequently provided to Joy FM differed from those supplied to the Minority and Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee following a request under the Right to Information Act, 2019 (Act 989). He alleged that some of the documents appeared to have been prepared to address gaps in the Ministry’s account of the exercise. “Subsequent to that, Joy FM was given documentation which was not within the contours of the documents which were provided to the Minority, which was provided to the Foreign Affairs Committee,” he said. “And these documents, even when examined, it’s established clearly that these documents were conjured to kind of plug holes into the whole case which has been established.” He argued that the differences in the records, alongside the other alleged irregularities, made an independent investigation necessary to establish how the public funds were spent. The Minority is therefore calling for an investigation by an independent, internationally reputable auditing and accounting firm. Mr Jinapor said the Foreign Affairs Minister should step aside while the investigation is conducted, arguing that his continued stay in office could undermine confidence in the process. The Minority’s demands follow the controversy over the GH¢49,721,786 reportedly spent on evacuating 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa between May 27 and September 4, 2026, amid renewed xenophobic attacks. The expenditure, according to figures presented by Mr Ablakwa, comprised GH¢38.84 million for chartered flights, commercial tickets, ground transportation, feeding, accommodation and medical care; GH¢10.8 million for reintegration and transport allowances; and GH¢84,274 for repatriating the remains of two Ghanaian nationals and related autopsy costs. Read also: VIDEO: Ablakwa details GH¢49.7m SA evacuation spending, rejects Minority’s claims of unaccounted funds The Minister has rejected the Minority’s allegations, insisting that all the funds have been accounted for. He has also requested an independent audit of evacuation exercises undertaken by successive governments since 2017. The disputed expenditure and supporting documentation remain subject to further scrutiny, with the Minority insisting that an independent audit is necessary to establish whether any public funds were misappropriated.

title: Boeing Bullish on Defense Sector After Fighter Wins, Shunning Fixed-Price Deals
body: Fresh off Boeing’s victory in the competition to build the Navy’s sixth-generation F/A-XX fighter , CEO Kelly Ortberg on Oct. 27 expressed confidence that the darkest days of the company’s beleaguered defense sector are in the past. A year ago, Boeing expected its Defense, Space, and Security division to see revenue growth in the low single digits, Ortberg told investors in an earnings call. Now, the company is projecting defense revenue growth in at least the mid-single digits or higher. Ortberg pointed to Boeing’s Sept. 29 win of both the $20 billion F/A-XX contract and a $2.38 billion Air Force contract for 22 more F-15EX Eagle II fighters as examples of the tailwinds boosting Boeing’s defense portfolio. The F/A-XX win followed the Air Force’s March 2025 selection of Boeing to build its F-47, putting both the U.S. military’s sixth-generation fighter programs in its portfolio. In the first three quarters of 2026, Boeing’s defense sector brought in $23 billion in revenue, with earnings of $710 million. That’s up from $19.8 billion in revenue and $379 million in earnings a year earlier. Ortberg also said the company’s decision to swear off risky contracts—such as the fixed-price contract for Boeing’s KC-46 Pegasus program, which has lost the company billions—has helped put its defense sector back on course. “The important part is, all these programs are also being underwritten with the right contract type,” Ortberg said. “So not only are we booking more orders, we’re booking more orders that won’t result in some of the challenges we’ve had.” The F-47 contract is a cost-plus deal, Ortberg said. He declined to identify what type of contract Boeing signed for F/A-XX, but said it is “an appropriate contract type.” In 2022, Boeing put executive Ted Colbert in charge of its defense sector, who pledged to not agree to further fixed-price contracts with the Pentagon. A few months into the job, Colbert told reporters in London that Boeing had passed on competing for the Air Force’s Survivable Airborne Operations Center, or SAOC, in part because it would have required agreeing to fixed-price elements in the contract. Colbert also said fighters remained an important part of the company’s business, even though the firm then had not landed a contract to create an entirely new fighter in years. Later in 2022, Colbert reorganized Boeing’s defense sector in an effort to stop it from bleeding revenue and fix persistent quality problems. Two years later, Boeing Defense appeared increasingly troubled. Financial losses piled up, and the company fired Colbert in September 2024. Labor troubles between Boeing and its machinists led to a massive strike in 2024, and a smaller one a year later, further complicating the firm’s outlook and slowing its F-15EX delivery pace. But this year, Ortberg said he saw more reasons for optimism. Boeing’s T-7 Red Hawk trainer for the Air Force and MQ-25 Stingray for the Navy both achieved their Milestone C approvals and moved into low-rate initial production this year as well, which Ortberg said was a positive sign for the company. “We’re not done with the development programs until we’re done,” Ortberg said, adding that the defense team is “doing a really good job of finding win-win scenarios with our customers to get these projects moved forward.” “So the outlook is strong, our products are in strong demand, and the budget supports additional growth,” Ortberg said. “I think our defense portfolio is a little bit of a sleeper.” The post Boeing Bullish on Defense Sector After Fighter Wins, Shunning Fixed-Price Deals appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .

title: Arab voter turnout surges past 2022 figures as haredi strongholds lag behind
body: Voter turnout in several Arab-majority cities had already surpassed the final figures recorded in the 2022 Knesset election by 6 p.m. on Tuesday, while predominantly haredi (ultra-Orthodox) cities remained below their previous election totals, according to election-day turnout figures, as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned that high Arab participation could affect the election's outcome.In Umm al-Fahm, turnout reached 56.1% by 6 p.m., compared with a final turnout of 51.33% in 2022, an increase of 4.77 percentage points, with several hours of voting remaining.A similar trend emerged in Kafr Qasim, where turnout reached 73.9%, surpassing the 70.31% recorded in 2022. In Nazareth, 58.4% of eligible voters had cast their ballots, compared with 55.75% in the previous election.The largest increase among the four Arab-majority cities examined was recorded in Rahat, where turnout reached 72.2% by 6 p.m., compared with 59.54% in 2022, a difference of 12.66 percentage points.Netanyahu warns of high Arab turnout, calls on right-wing votersThe figures prompted concern among right-wing leaders, with Netanyahu and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich coordinating efforts to increase turnout among their supporters amid what they described as concerning Arab voter participation.“This is an emergency call! The future of our Jewish state is at stake,” Netanyahu wrote on X on Tuesday.“Get out and vote Likud now! Higher-than-usual turnout in the Arab sector compared with low turnout among right-wing voters. We must wake up – we cannot stay home. Go out and vote Likud and get as many people out as possible!”In a separate appeal, Netanyahu warned that high turnout among Arab voters could influence the election's outcome, urging right-wing supporters to head to polling stations.Haredi strongholds remain below 2022 turnoutMeanwhile, several predominantly Haredi cities recorded turnout figures that remained substantially below their final 2022 totals.In Bnei Brak, 64.3% of eligible voters had cast their ballots by 6 p.m., compared with 77.27% in 2022, a gap of 12.97 percentage points.Elad recorded a turnout of 71.2%, compared with 85.77% in the previous election, while Modi'in Illit stood at 69.8%, compared with 84.51% in 2022.Jerusalem, which has a substantial haredi population alongside other communities, recorded turnout of 66.7%, already exceeding its final 2022 figure of 63.37%.Shas chairman Arye Deri also expressed concern over turnout among Arab and left-wing voters, warning of efforts to unseat the current government.“Tens of thousands of people came from abroad to vote, to topple the Torah rule,” Deri said.Civil rights groups warn of voting disruptions in Arab communitiesThe high turnout figures came despite reports of possible disruptions at polling stations in Arab communities, prompting appeals to the Central Elections Committee.The Association for Civil Rights in Israel (ACRI) warned Tuesday that voting could be deliberately obstructed in several Arab towns, citing unusually slow processing of voters and lengthy queues.The organization appealed to CEC Chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg to dispatch inspectors to affected polling stations, warning that the delays could prevent voters from exercising their democratic rights.Reports of delays emerged from Rahat, Tel Sheva, Laqiya, Segev Shalom, Kafr Kara, Tamra, Tira, and several other Arab localities.In Segev Shalom, police and Border Police personnel reportedly prevented voters from entering a polling station compound, despite relatively few voters being inside, leaving approximately 200 people waiting outside.Separately, the Adalah Legal Center for Arab Minority Rights in Israel appealed to the CEC over reports that Arabic-language ballot slips were missing from several polling stations, demanding that the slips be supplied urgently.The reported disruptions have not been established as deliberate interference.The contrasting turnout figures highlight the importance of voter participation in Tuesday's election, although the final picture will only become clear after polling stations close.While Arab-majority cities have already surpassed their 2022 turnout levels, haredi strongholds still have several hours to narrow the gap. The figures do not establish how voters cast their ballots or whether the turnout patterns will translate into changes in Knesset representation.

title: Ex-wife of Zimbabwe’s vice-president freed after collapse of attempted murder case
body: The former wife of Zimbabwe’s vice-president has been freed from remand after seven years while on trial for his attempted murder. Marry Mubaiwa was charged in 2019, after her then husband Gen Constantino Chiwenga accused her of trying to impede his medical treatment in South Africa. Ordering her release, a magistrate said Mubaiwa had suffered mental, physical and financial prejudice during the trial, state-owned daily the Herald said. The ruling was made after the state asked for the trial to be postponed by a month in order to engage witnesses. Her lawyer described the ruling as a victory that had come too late, because her client’s rights had been violated by the delay in the trial. Speaking outside court in the capital Harare on Tuesday, the lawyer added that if the state moved for a new trial, they would deal with it when it happened. Mubaiwa was accused of attempting to kill Chiwenga, while he was in hospital in Pretoria. The vice-president then went to China for four months of treatment. Mubaiwa was remanded in custody and denied bail. According to the New Zimbabwe news website, Mubaiwa celebrated her release outside court, and said justice had been achieved and that she was proud of her lawyer. In 2017, Chiwenga played a key role in overthrowing then President Robert Mugabe.

title: Greek President Praises Metro Museum as a Masterpiece
body: Greek President Konstantinos Tasoulas described Thessaloniki’s Thessalonikeon Mitropolis Museum , which showcases archaeological finds from excavations for the Thessaloniki Metro, as a masterpiece during his visit on Tuesday, praising both its exhibits and the transformation of its historic site. Culture Minister Lina Mendoni and Tania Protopsalti, deputy head of the Thessaloniki City Antiquities Ephorate, welcomed Tasoulas and guided him through the museum. The institution occupies the preserved A3 barracks building within Pavlos Melas Metropolitan Park. On the museum’s ground floor, Tasoulas viewed antiquities unearthed during excavations outside Thessaloniki’s historic walls. These finds came from the New Railway Station, Dimokratias, Sintrivani, University and Fleming metro stations, as well as the Pylaia depot. On the upper floor, he viewed finds from excavations at Venizelou and Agia Sofia stations, both located within the city’s historic walls. After the tour, Tasoulas praised the museum for combining its archaeological treasures with the transformation of the former Pavlos Melas military camp, which the armed forces had no longer needed for decades. “If one compares what this former Pavlos Melas military camp used to look like with what it has become today, one understands that a masterpiece contains many, hundreds, thousands of smaller masterpieces — the finds unearthed during the Metro works,” he said. Tasoulas said the exhibits reveal Thessaloniki’s successive historical periods, including its Hellenistic, Roman, Byzantine and Ottoman eras. The archaeological discoveries, he added, help visitors understand the defining characteristics of each period. The president urged people not to miss the opportunity to visit the museum and experience the city’s history through its exhibits. He said the collection celebrates Greek civilisation and demonstrates Greece’s modern determination to protect its past. “By protecting its past, our country looks towards its future prospects with greater optimism,” Tasoulas said. Also attending the tour were Metropolitan Barnabas of Neapolis and Stavroupolis, Central Union of Municipalities of Greece (KEDE) president and Ampelokipoi-Menemeni Mayor Lazaros Kyrizoglou, and Pavlos Melas Mayor Dimitris Aslanidis, among others. title: Trump to ban the term AI 'in all relevant documents'
body: US President Donald Trump is angry that more people are not joining his move to rebrand artificial intelligence as super intelligence . On Tuesday, Mr Trump criticised The Wall Street Journal , which, along with almost everyone else has kept calling the technology artificial intelligence, or AI for short. "When will The Wall Street Journal start calling artificial intelligence (AI), a very bad and inaccurate name, SI (super intelligence), the name which virtually everyone else is using, or soon will be," he posted on social media. Mr Trump said his administration would soon "be officially banning the term 'AI/artificial intelligence,' in all relevant documents". Last month, as polls showed US residents have an increasingly negative view of AI due to fears of job losses , data centres and environmental concerns, Mr Trump signed an executive order that sought to force the US federal government to use the phrase "super intelligence". Several US agencies responded and promised to begin using SI instead of AI, but most technology companies, experts, analysts, media outlets and governments outside the US have kept using the term AI. During an event in Washington organised by the White House in early October, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang kept correcting himself while mentioning AI. “As you know we want to advance AI – I'm sorry, I mean SI. I'm going to get good at this,” he said. In recent weeks, the International Monetary Fund also told Reuters that it would not be changing what it calls AI, despite requests from the White House. Semantic origin and confusion AI research, which stretches back decades, already has a long list of established phrases. Shortly after Mr Trump initially announced the name several months ago, technology experts said the phrase “ AI super intelligence ” was already widely used. Those involved in its research often use the term when referring to the hypothetical idea that technology can perform highly advanced cognitive functions and develop reasoning skills that will pass those of humans. But Mr Trump's rebranding attempt has had some support. Neil Chilson , who was chief technologist for the Federal Trade Commission during the first Trump administration and now leads AI policy at the Abundance Institute, said he also had disdain for the phrase “artificial intelligence”. Mr Chilson highlighted an obituary written for computer scientist John McCarthy, who died in 2011. “McCarthy’s influence began at Dartmouth, where he coined the term 'artificial intelligence' while planning the first conference in the field, held in 1956, though he later wished he had named the field differently – 'computational intelligence' would have been more apt, if less alluring,” the obituary read. Mr Chilson posted on X: “The scientist who coined the term 'artificial intelligence' also regretted the term, but unlike Trump he didn't have the rizz to just up and change it.”

Those involved in its research often use the term when referring to the hypothetical idea that technology can perform highly advanced cognitive functions and develop reasoning skills that will pass those of humans. But Mr Trump's rebranding attempt has had some support. Neil Chilson , who was chief technologist for the Federal Trade Commission during the first Trump administration and now leads AI policy at the Abundance Institute, said he also had disdain for the phrase “artificial intelligence”. Mr Chilson highlighted an obituary written for computer scientist John McCarthy, who died in 2011. “McCarthy’s influence began at Dartmouth, where he coined the term 'artificial intelligence' while planning the first conference in the field, held in 1956, though he later wished he had named the field differently – 'computational intelligence' would have been more apt, if less alluring,” the obituary read. Mr Chilson posted on X: “The scientist who coined the term 'artificial intelligence' also regretted the term, but unlike Trump he didn't have the rizz to just up and change it.”

title: Dangote Refinery IPO Attracts Investors From 120 Countries, All 54 African Nations
body: Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals says its initial public offering (IPO) attracted investor applications from 120 countries, including all 54 African nations, following the close of the offer on Tuesday. The company described the outcome as a milestone for African capital markets, saying the offer brought together investors across all six inhabited continents and opened up ownership of a major industrial asset to a wider pool of participants. In a statement, President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, said the response demonstrated Africans’ willingness to invest in industries built on the continent and share in their growth. “To have investor applications from all 54 African countries is deeply significant to me. It shows our people don’t just want to consume what Africa produces; they want to invest in it, own it, and share in its future. This is the Africa we have always believed in,” he said. Dangote said the public offer was intended not only to raise capital but also to broaden participation in the refinery’s ownership. “We did not undertake this IPO simply because we needed to raise capital. We wanted to open the doors of ownership, give ordinary Africans an opportunity to participate in an enterprise of global significance and establish a new culture of shared prosperity,” he said. He added that the company would continue to pursue its expansion programme and Vision 2030 strategy, with a focus on operational performance and Africa’s energy security. Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals, David Bird, said the international response reflected confidence in the refinery’s scale, operating capabilities and long-term prospects. “The successful conclusion of this IPO is a remarkable milestone for Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals. Investor applications from 120 countries demonstrate extraordinary international interest in our business and the confidence investors place in this refinery’s future,” Bird said. He said the refinery would focus on translating its industrial capacity into operational excellence, sustainable growth and long-term shareholder value. The offer opened on September 14, with 4.1 billion ordinary shares priced at ₦525 each, representing a proposed capital raise of approximately ₦2.15 trillion. Originally scheduled to close on October 13, the offer was extended to October 27 following approval by the Securities and Exchange Commission, giving investors additional time to participate. According to the company, the offer was supported by commercial banks, stockbroking firms, fintech platforms, capital market institutions and other distribution partners. Their involvement provided multiple channels for eligible investors to submit applications. Dangote Industries Limited Group Chief Financial Officer, Murat Erden, said the transaction demonstrated the potential for African financial institutions and digital platforms to connect investors across national borders. “The Dangote Refinery People’s IPO represents much more than a landmark capital-raising exercise. It marks a defining moment in the evolution of African capital markets, demonstrating our continent’s ability to mobilise domestic savings, connect investors across borders and broaden ownership of strategic industrial assets,” he said. Erden also highlighted the refinery’s financial performance, stating that it recorded $22.5 billion in revenue and $5.52 billion in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) in the first nine months of 2026. He said the company believed the offer could serve as a model for wider retail participation and greater integration of African capital markets. The IPO comes as the refinery pursues plans to expand its refining and petrochemical operations, strengthen its distribution network and contribute to energy security across Africa. Located in Lagos, the refinery is one of Africa’s largest private industrial investments, established to increase domestic processing capacity and reduce reliance on imported refined petroleum products. The post Dangote Refinery IPO Attracts Investors From 120 Countries, All 54 African Nations appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Australia beefs up public/private defences for cyber threats
body: The Australian Government is working with public and private sector organisations to strengthen their cyber resilience as the Australian Signals Directorate’s (ASD) Annual Cyber Threat Report for 2025-26 highlights the need for continued vigilance against malicious state actors and cybercriminals targeting Australian networks. The Annual Cyber Threat Report recognises that artificial intelligence (AI) has been the defining force in the cyber threat landscape over the past year, allowing malicious actors to identify vulnerabilities faster and exploit them at unprecedented scale, speed and sophistication to conduct espionage, steal money and disrupt systems. The rapid adoption of AI has brought new and evolving security risks, including those stemming from the unintended actions of AI agents and model testing. Since the Second World War, no technology has carried greater potential to boost our sovereign capabilities, strengthen our national security and build our economic resilience. In this environment, the likelihood of cyber incidents has increased substantially and Australian organisations need to take action accordingly. It is vital that businesses prepare for service disruptions from a cyber incident. Protecting Australia’s critical infrastructure and essential services starts with strengthening cyber resilience, addressing vulnerabilities quickly and embedding strong cyber security practices before incidents occur. We are asking all entities to lower thresholds for reporting to ASD and to prioritise security over service availability. Key findings from the 2025-26 Annual Cyber Threat Report include: ASD notified entities of potential malicious cyber activity more than 4,400 times, up almost 80%, including mass notifications to over 2,100 entities. ASD responded to more than 1,500 cyber security incidents, up more than 20% from 2024-25 and 36% over the past five years. ASD received over 82,000 cybercrime reports, an average of one report every six minutes. ASD answered over 37,500 calls to the Australian Cyber Security Hotline, equating to around 102 calls per day. ASD published 76 alerts, advisories and publications on cyber.gov.au, including a range of joint products with international partners The report also highlights the growing impact of cybercrime on Australians and Australian organisations. ASD’s Australian Protective Domain Name System processed more than 220 billion queries and blocked access to more than 564 million malicious domains during the reporting period. The average self-reported cost of cybercrime was $33,000 for individuals and $93,500 for businesses. The Annual Cyber Threat Report reinforces the importance of government and industry partnerships in combatting cyber threats through intelligence sharing, combining the insights and capabilities of both to block and counter evolving threats. It calls on organisations to take five essential cyber security actions: log all cyber events, replace legacy technology, manage supply chain risks, strengthen AI preparedness and prepare now for quantum computing that may compromise current encryption. ASD’s Cyber Security Partnership Program grew to over 149,500 partners and the Cyber Threat Intelligence Sharing network shared over one million indicators of compromise with hundreds of Australian partners. A collective understanding of the threats improves cyber defences for the whole nation. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Defence Richard Marles said: “ASD’s Annual Cyber Threat Report reflects the fact that Australia continues to face a challenging strategic environment with AI accelerating the scale, speed and complexity of cyber threats. AI is reshaping the online landscape, enabling cybercriminals and state-sponsored actors to launch faster, more sophisticated and scalable attacks. To stay ahead, Australians must enhance their cyber defences while harnessing AI’s benefits. The Annual Cyber Threat Report reinforces that government and industry must continue to work together to strengthen our collective cyber resilience and safeguard our critical digital infrastructure.” Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Cyber Security Tony Burke said: “Cyber security has never been more important – being under attack is certain, constant and ever present. To keep people safe, we’re positioning Australia to respond to the evolving threats and opportunities presented by emerging technologies. That starts with protecting critical infrastructure and government systems, securing technology at its source and enabling people as our strongest defence to become Australia’s ‘human firewall’.” For Editorial Inquiries Contact: Editor Kym Bergmann at kym.bergmann@venturamedia.net For Advertising Inquiries Contact: Group Sales Director Simon Hadfield at simon.hadfield@venturamedia.net

title: ‎Investigator defends methods in Tano Nnimire mining trial
body: A police investigator has told an Accra High Court that he inherited an incomplete docket in the alleged illegal mining case involving Bernard Antwi Boasiako and Akonta Mining Company Limited.‎ ‎ ‎Detective Chief Inspector Akpo Glover said he studied the docket before continuing the investigations and did not alter any part of the inherited records.‎ ‎ ‎He was testifying under cross-examination in the ongoing trial of Boasiako, a former Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), and Akonta Mining Company Limited. ‎ ‎ ‎Detective Chief Inspector Glover, who has 17 years of policing experience, rejected the suggestion that his understanding of the case was based on “second-hand information”.‎ ‎ ‎”My understanding of this case is as a result of various methods of investigation the police conducted. They include interviews with witnesses, visits to crime scenes, drone surveillance and review of documents,” he said. ‎ ‎ ‎The investigator said two prosecution witnesses had stated in their caution statements that Akonta Mining erected barriers and side poles in the Tano Nnimire Forest to prevent people, including Forestry Commission officials, from entering the reserve.‎ ‎ ‎He said his investigations implicated Boasiako and Akonta Mining in the alleged illegal mining activities.‎ ‎ ‎Detective Chief Inspector Glover also disputed a suggestion by defence counsel, Mr Samuel Atta Akyea, that letters written to the Western Regional Security Council over alleged illegal mining on Boasiako’s concession demonstrated opposition to illegal mining by those involved.‎ ‎ ‎He maintained that agents of Boasiako and Akonta Mining had acted in their own interests in the Tano Nnimire Forest.‎‎ ‎ ‎The investigator recalled that the letter to the Western Regional Security Council was dated June 2021.‎ ‎ ‎The court adjourned the case to October 27, 2026.‎ ‎Boasiako and Akonta Mining face charges over alleged mining operations without a licence in the Tano Nnimire Forest Reserve in the Western Region.‎ ‎ ‎The prosecution alleged that the accused persons felled about 300 merchantable trees in the reserve and erected structures without written permission from the Forestry Commission.‎ ‎ ‎Boasiako, a 50-year-old entrepreneur, has denied the charges. ‎He is serving a 20-year prison sentence for a similar offence. ‎

title: Southwest flood damage estimates are hundreds of millions for New Mexico alone
body:
An aerial view of a flooded area in Shiprock, New Mexico. Navajo Nation Police Department hide caption
Intense rainstorms linked to a very active El Niño-driven Pacific hurricane season have left thousands of people in the Four Corners states displaced or facing massive cleanups from flooding.
The adjoining states of Colorado, New Mexico, Utah and Arizona all saw substantial flooding last week, and damage assessments are just starting to trickle in from cities, towns and some of the most remote territory in the continental U.S.
The northern New Mexico city of Farmington was hit particularly hard after torrential rains fell on the San Juan mountains in Colorado, sending floodwaters down the San Juan River that passes through Farmington on its way to Lake Powell on the Utah-Arizona border.
Small towns all along the river, from Pagosa Springs, Colorado, to Bloomfield, New Mexico and Bluff, Utah all saw historic flooding and are now assessing recovery challenges.
About 46,000 people live in Farmington, long a center for coal, oil and natural gas production. It's also an important hub for the northeast side of the Navajo reservation, which sprawls across three states.
Farmington residents started getting evacuation notices on their phones as early as Wednesday night.
"My sister was notified on Thursday that she had to get out," said Connie Gooch, who has lived in Farmington for more than 65 years.
Gooch's sister owns a house in a suburban neighborhood near the San Juan River.
"Every year she goes through this," Gooch said. "The river starts rising, and she starts making sandbags to put around. But this year it was so fast she didn't have time to do that."
An aerial view of a flooded area in Farmington, NM. San Juan County Office of Emergency Management hide caption
According to National Weather Service data from a river gauge in Farmington , the San Juan grew 13 times larger in just 36 hours, late last week.
In the wee hours of Thursday morning, the river was about 3.5 feet high. By Friday, it was 14 feet high, flooding neighborhoods across the city, and possibly setting a record for the highest water ever recorded in the city.
This even after the Navajo Reservoir upstream from Farmington was able to mostly contain water rushing down from the mountains. But downstream of the reservoir, flood surges into the city came from two normally dry tributaries, Gobernador Canyon and Cañon Largo.
"This is a catastrophic flood of historic proportions," said Devon Neeley, San Juan County's public information officer.
"This river got wider than we have ever seen it in our lifetimes."
An aerial image of the Shiprock Bridge spanning over a flooding San Juan River. Navajo Nation Police Department hide caption
Similar reports are coming in from the other side of the San Juan mountains in Colorado.
"It's nothing like most of us have seen before," said Tyler Schmidt, captain of the fire and rescue team in the small town of South Fork, Colo. on the banks of the Rio Grande. "We had several neighborhoods that were under two to three feet of water."
Colorado Public Radio's Dan Boyce reports that responders' immediate priorities are lifting final evacuation orders as waters recede. Damaged bridges need to be assessed. Well water all down the Rio Grande's path in the San Luis valley needs to be tested.
Other drinking water impacts from the storm include sewage spills from flooded treatment plants in Sedona, Arizona and other locations. KNAU reports extensive damage on the Hopi reservation.
The Hopi reservation is surrounded by the Navajo reservation, where there have also been reports of rescues, washed out roads and flooding of historic proportions.
San Juan County, New Mexico's Neeley said fire crews, police officers, National Guard troops, and even out-of-state swift water teams rescued between 200 and 300 county residents.
"We have pulled people out of vehicles stuck in running washes. We have pulled people by helicopter off of rooftops," Neeley said. "We have used not only high-clearance vehicles from the National Guard, but amphibious vehicles because the water is so high. It's been a lot."
A person walks along the edge of a flooded road in Shiprock, New Mexico. Navajo Nation Police Deparment hide caption
By Sunday, the rain had eased, river levels were falling, and some residents started returning home to assess flood damage.
Connie Gooch delivered tarps and other materials to her sister's house.
"The river was up four feet in her house," she said.
She found a neighborhood full of people moving furniture out of their homes and piling demolition debris in their front yards.
"There were trucks and cars all over the place," Gooch said. "There was a guy in front of me carrying a loaded trailer full of sheet rock that they'd chipped out of somebody's house."
But officials want the thousands of evacuated residents to stay out for now.
"The public is anxious to get back in; we recognize that, we're sympathetic to that," said San Juan County Fire Chief David Vega at a public briefing Sunday. "Now that the swift water component is out of the way, that exposes a whole new set of hazards for us," Vega added.
Public officials are concerned about hazards like raw sewage and damaged gas lines, live power lines, and the floodwater itself.
"The water is not healthy," Vega said. "Stay out of the water. Gas, diesel, pesticides, fertilizer, these are not things that you want on your clothes."
A flooded road east of Northern Edge Navajo Casino on N36 in Shiprock, New Mexico. Navajo Nation Police Deparment hide caption
New Mexico Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham visited San Juan County on Monday.
Grisham said that the damage to infrastructure alone could cost hundreds of millions of dollars.
"I hope we're only spending 30 to 40 million (dollars)," Lujan Grisham said, responding to recovery cost estimates from San Juan County manager Mike Stark.
"We think this could be closer to between 200 and 300 million (dollars)," Lujan Grisham said. "The environmental issues and the road issues and infrastructure issues alone, really are expensive."
Monday night, Governor Lujan Grisham released an announcement , stating that the federal government has "partially granted" New Mexico's request for an emergency declaration in response to the regional flooding. Yesterday, Lujan-Grisham signed executive orders making $8.25 million more in state funding available for flood response.
