title: Sokoto Assembly okays establishment of state police
body:
The Sokoto State House of Assembly has unanimously adopted the Sixth Alteration Bill seeking to provide a constitutional framework for the establishment of state police services in Nigeria.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the adoption followed a motion moved by the Deputy Majority Leader of the House, Mustapha Abdullahi (APC-Sokoto South II), during plenary in Sokoto on Tuesday.
Presenting the bill, Mr Abdullahi said it sought to amend the Nigerian Constitution to establish state police services while retaining the Nigeria Police Force as the federal police service.
He said the bill was transmitted by the federal executive, considered by the Senate on 24 June and the House of Representatives on 23 July, and presented to the Sokoto Assembly on 22 September.
According to him, the proposed framework will delineate the responsibilities of federal and state police services to ensure effective policing and address security challenges across the country.
He explained that the federal police would handle interstate and international crimes, terrorism, cybercrime, border security, policing of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) and protection of federal assets.
“Conversely, state police services would be responsible for law enforcement, maintenance of public order and safety, protection of lives and property, and investigation of local crimes.
“Therefore, the federal police and state police will function side-by-side in every state,” Mr Abdullahi said.
The lawmaker added that the federal police could intervene in state policing matters at the request of a state governor or where there was a breakdown of law and order that the state police could not contain.
He said the head of a state police service would be known as the State Commander of Police and appointed by the governor on the recommendation of the National Police Council, subject to confirmation by the State House of Assembly.
Mr Abdullahi further explained that the bill proposed the establishment of a State Police Service Commission as an executive body responsible for the appointment, promotion and discipline of state police personnel, except the state commander.
On funding, the lawmaker said the proposed framework would provide for the State Police Service Commission to receive funds directly from the state’s Consolidated Revenue Fund to ensure financial autonomy.
He added that the Nigeria Police Force would continue to operate in every state until the state’s police service commenced operations.
Mr Abdullahi cited Section 9(2) of the Nigerian Constitution, which provides that a constitutional alteration must be approved by resolutions of the houses of assembly of not less than two-thirds of all the states.
Contributing to the debate, several lawmakers supported the bill, describing state policing as a necessary measure to address the security challenges confronting states across the country.
The Speaker, Tukur Bala, who presided over the plenary, subsequently put the motion to a voice vote, and the lawmakers unanimously adopted it.

title: War update: 178 clashes on front line, Pokrovsk sector remains hottest
body:
As reported by Ukrinform, this was stated in a report by the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine on the situation as of 22:00 on Tuesday, October 26.
“A total of 178 combat clashes have taken place since the beginning of the day. The enemy launched one missile strike and 46 airstrikes, dropping 171 guided aerial bombs. In addition, they used 5,942 kamikaze drones to strike targets and carried out 1,563 shelling attacks on settlements and the positions of our troops,” the report said.
In the Northern Slobozhanshchyna and Kursk sectors, Russian forces carried out 27 attacks on the positions of Ukrainian troops and settlements, one of them using multiple rocket launchers.
In the Southern Slobozhanshchyna sector, the enemy attacked Ukrainian positions five times toward the settlements of Okhrimivka and Mala Vovcha. Two of these attacks are still ongoing.
In the Kupiansk sector, Russian forces made three attempts to improve their positions, conducting assault operations toward Radkivka. Fighting is ongoing.
Four attempts by Russian forces to advance were repelled in the Lyman sector, toward Nove, Stavky, and Lyman.
In the Sloviansk sector, Ukraine’s Defense Forces stopped two attempts by Russian troops to advance near Yampil and toward Orikhuvatka.
In the Kramatorsk sector, Russian forces launched one assault toward Malynivka.
In the Kostiantynivka sector, Ukrainian Forces repelled 13 Russian assaults near Kostiantynivka as well as toward Raiske and Pavlivka. One enemy assault is ongoing.
Russian forces launched 24 attacks in the Pokrovsk sector. They attempted to advance near Sofiivka, Vilne, Vodianske, Vasylivka, and Molodetske, as well as toward Toretske, Kucheriv Yar, Dobropillia, Hannivka, Novohryshyne, Hulive, and Serhiivka. One combat clash is ongoing.
According to preliminary estimates, 23 Russian troops were killed and eight wounded in the sector today. Ukrainian forces destroyed five vehicles and one piece of special equipment. Three vehicles, one electronic warfare system, one UAV command post and 39 enemy shelters were damaged. A total of 173 unmanned aerial vehicles of various types were destroyed or suppressed.
In the Oleksandrivka sector, Russian forces did not conduct any assault operations.
In the Huliaipole sector , Ukraine’s Defense Forces repelled 16 enemy attacks toward Ternuvate, Dolynka, Hirke, Charivne and Yehorivka. Fighting is ongoing.
Russian forces conducted no assault operations in the Orikhiv and Dnipro River sectors.
No significant changes in the situation were reported in other sectors of the front.
As reported by Ukrinform, the Vivaldi operation by the Ukrainian Defense Forces pushed Russian troops back and liberated significant areas north of Lyman, but the threat to the Sloviansk-Kramatorsk agglomeration still remains.

title: Australia names National Armaments Director
body: The Australian Government has appointed Kellie Parker to the role of National Armaments Director. Parker will be responsible for leading the new Defence Delivery Agency when established on 1 July 2027, with responsibility for delivering acquisition and sustainment projects. Parker has over 20 years’ experience spanning operational leadership, complex asset development and major transformation across the iron ore and aluminium mining areas. Most recently she was Chief Executive, Australia at Rio Tinto, responsible for delivering a multi-billion-dollar portfolio of projects with thousands of Australian suppliers. This extensive experience will support closer collaboration with Australian defence industry and more expedient delivery of capability for the Australian Defence Force (ADF) with stronger commercial discipline. Her significant experience leading a large organisation, managing complex matters in a high‑accountability environment, and delivering operational outcomes will also be invaluable in her role as the National Armaments Director. As a statutory appointment, Parker will be appointed as National Armaments Director Designate from 9 November 2026 until the establishment of the Defence Delivery Agency from 1 July 2027. Nadine Williams, who has been Interim National Armaments Director and instrumental in delivering this ambitious reform, will remain in the role until Ms Parker commences on 9 November. Ms Williams’ leadership has been invaluable and we thank her for her time and dedication during this time. Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles said: “I congratulate Ms Parker on her successful appointment to this role. Her significant experience in leadership, transformation and delivering operational outcomes will serve her well as she takes on this important responsibility. I thank Ms Nadine Williams for her leadership, advice and management of one of the most significant reforms in the Defence portfolio in decades, and helping to deliver the foundations to ensure its success.” Minister for Defence Industry Pat Conroy said: “The Albanese Government has been clear about its ambitions for reform of Defence’s capability acquisition process. Kellie has had a distinguished career in the private sector over several decades, and her appointment matches our ambitions to deliver increasingly complex defence projects at speed and scale. This appointment is about bolstering timely, cost-efficient and accountable delivery of capabilities, and getting better bang for buck for the record investment the Albanese Government is making in defence.” Parker said: “I’m excited and honoured to be appointed as the first National Armaments Director during a time of reform and transformation across Defence. I look forward to being part of the team responsible for delivering outcomes that support the Australian Defence Force through the acquisition and sustainment of capabilities, systems and platforms. An important focus will be working closely with businesses and organisations across Australia to support a home-grown Defence industrial base.” For Editorial Inquiries Contact: Editor Kym Bergmann at kym.bergmann@venturamedia.net For Advertising Inquiries Contact: Group Sales Director Simon Hadfield at simon.hadfield@venturamedia.net

title: Lockheed Martin closes Ultra Maritime acquisition
body: Lockheed Martin announced it has completed its acquisition of Ultra Maritime, a global defence company specialising in advanced undersea warfare and anti-submarine warfare (ASW) capabilities for allied naval forces. The company develops and delivers mission-critical systems including sonar technologies, sonobuoys, torpedo defense systems, radar solutions, electronic warfare and autonomous maritime sensing platforms. “Securing the undersea domain starts with giving sailors the tools and confidence to find, track and deter threats that put ships and crews at risk,” said Stephanie C. Hill, president, Rotary and Mission Systems at Lockheed Martin. “This is more than an acquisition – it’s a commitment to unite the best of our technology, capability and people to meet our partners’ urgent and growing demand for undersea warfare capability worldwide.” Ultra Maritime’s international footprint and portfolio of ASW products for allied customers, such as its sonobuoys, towed sonar arrays and hull mounted sonar product lines, will complement and expand Lockheed Martin’s ability to offer sonar solutions across next-gen maritime platforms. The Ultra Maritime business is aligned under the Lockheed Martin Rotary and Mission Systems business area. title: French Research Vessel Arrives for Greece-Cyprus Power Cable
body: A French-flagged research vessel, the Abeille Marengo, arrived at the port of Heraklion on Tuesday morning ahead of undersea surveys for the installation of high-voltage direct-current cables linking Crete and Cyprus through the Great Sea Interconnector project. The vessel arrived from Italy and remains on standby pending the official issuance of a NAVTEX notice specifying the maritime area where the planned operations will take place. Greek Navy to receive 72 hours’ notice before surveys The notification process for the relevant military and naval authorities will play an important role before the surveys begin. According to the relevant request, the Abeille Marengo must notify the Hellenic Navy’s Hydrographic Service, Submarine Command and Naval Aviation Command at least 72 hours before starting operations. It must also provide updates daily throughout the surveys. The notifications will include precise coordinates, descriptions of the planned work, required safety distances and any other information necessary to conduct the surveys safely. The document also calls for notifications to local port authorities and passing vessels. Other ships must maintain a safety distance of at least one nautical mile from the research vessels. According to information available, Coast Guard vessels and Hellenic Navy units are expected to maintain a discreet presence in the area to monitor and safeguard the operations. How the undersea surveys will work Italy’s Next Geosolutions Europe SpA will conduct the surveys. The company belongs to the Marnavi shipping group and specialises in geophysical and geotechnical investigations for offshore energy infrastructure. France’s Nexans, which has undertaken the construction and installation of the Crete-Cyprus electricity cable, commissioned the work. The surveys will follow the planned cable route between the coastal area of Korakia in the Heraklion regional unit and Cyprus. Their main objective is to map the seabed in detail and record its geological and morphological characteristics. The findings will help engineers select the most suitable route for safely laying and protecting the power cables. The survey team will use specialised equipment, including a multibeam echosounder, side-scan sonar, a magnetometer and underwater video systems. The programme also includes geotechnical sampling at depths of up to 700 metres below sea level, as well as penetration tests and seabed drilling. The main technical challenges stem from the great depths of the eastern Mediterranean, steep underwater slopes and complex seabed formations. Special authorisation for French-flagged vessel Authorities at the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and the Hellenic Coast Guard sought additional, exceptional approval to use the French-flagged Abeille Marengo. The relevant document states that authorities considered the vessel necessary because of the surveys’ demanding technical requirements and the lack of suitable Greek-flagged vessels available during the period. Built in Norway in 2009, the Abeille Marengo measures 73.2 metres in length and carries specialised equipment for offshore operations. title: Elbit Systems wins APAC deal for airborne ISTAR and training
body: Elbit Systems announced it was awarded contracts in an aggregate value of approximately $200 million from a country in Asia-Pacific for the supply of airborne Intelligence, Surveillance, Target Acquisition and Reconnaissance (“ISTAR”) and training solutions. The contracts will be performed over a period of up to five years. Under the contracts, Elbit Systems will supply the SPECTRO 12 multispectral Intelligence, Surveillance, Reconnaissance (“ISR”) and targeting payload for integration on helicopters. The SPECTRO 12 is the latest addition to Elbit Systems’ SPECTRO family of airborne ISR and targeting payloads, introducing a compact multispectral payload designed for platforms with strict size, weight and power constraints. The SPECTRO 12 combines high-resolution multispectral sensing, precision targeting technologies, including a Laser designator, and AI-powered image processing, enabling long-range target detection, identification, tracking and engagement performance in complex operational environments and adverse weather conditions. The contracts further include follow-on support and upgrade services for airborne live training systems installed on aircraft and used in live virtual constructive and virtual combat training scenarios. The systems support realistic air-to-air and air-to-ground training, including real-time combat simulation, weapon scoring and mission debriefing capabilities, contributing to enhanced pilot readiness and training effectiveness. In addition, under the contracts Elbit Systems will supply advanced Head-Up Display (HUD) systems. The HUD systems feature high-resolution display technologies, enhanced video capabilities and low power consumption, supporting day and night operations across a range of airborne platforms. Bezhalel (Butzi) Machlis, President and CEO of Elbit Systems, said: “Elbit Systems’ airborne solutions combine advanced technologies with extensive operational experience across a wide range of mission environments. We are proud to provide our customers with innovative capabilities that enhance mission effectiveness, situational awareness and operational readiness across a broad spectrum of airborne missions.” For Editorial Inquiries Contact: Editor Kym Bergmann at kym.bergmann@venturamedia.net For Advertising Inquiries Contact: Group Sales Director Simon Hadfield at simon.hadfield@venturamedia.net

title: Russia not behind waving of Russian flags during 2024 protests in Nigeria — Lavrov
body:
Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov has dismissed insinuations that the Russian government sponsored some Nigerian youths who waved Russian flags during the 2024 #EndBadGovernance protests.
Mr Lavrov, who spoke in Moscow on the sidelines of the Third Russia-Africa Summit, in response to a question by the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) , said Russia had no hand in the action and distanced Moscow from any attempt to undermine Nigeria’s sovereignty.
According to him, Russia and Nigeria enjoy a robust relationship dating back to the days of the old Soviet Union.
He said those who donned Russian flags did so in their personal capacity and that it did not translate to official support by Russia.
“Anyone who donned the Russian flag did so in his or her personal capacity. It does not mean that Russia was in support of this kind of action.
“A lot of citizens sympathetic to Palestinians wave Palestinian flags to express solidarity. It does not mean the Palestinian government is behind them,” Mr Lavrov said.
The News Agency of Nigeria(NAN) recalls that the nationwide #EndBadGovernance protests took place from 1 to 10 August 2024, with the protesters citing high cost of living and economic hardship for their action.
NAN also recalls that during the protests, some groups of protesters, mostly youths and minors in Kano, Kaduna, Zamfara and Abuja, were seen waving Russian flags and chanting slogans calling for military intervention.
The action, which the federal government described as treasonable and a threat to Nigeria’s sovereignty, led to the arrest of scores of protesters and some tailors who were allegedly sewing the flags.
The Russian Embassy in Abuja had, at the time, also denied any involvement.
Mr Lavrov said the robust relationship between Nigeria and Russia had seen an increase in scholarships awarded to Nigerians, reaching a peak of 220 in 2026.
He recalled that in 2024, he met with his Nigerian counterpart in Abuja, who warmly received him, and cemented the bilateral ties between the two countries.
On defence pacts with some countries in the Sahel, Mr Lavrov said Russia was helping to eliminate security threats in the region, adding that Moscow was aware that some Western capitals were using Ukrainian mercenaries to sabotage the efforts, as they did in Libya, in a bid to undermine regional stability.
Commenting on the recent diesel supply agreement with the United States, the foreign minister said it was purely a business decision and would not affect the interests of its allies.
“The diesel agreement with the U.S. is purely a business decision by two world leaders who are concerned by the rising cost of energy,” he said.

title: Greece Leads International Declaration on Women in Conflict
body: Greece joined 72 countries and the European Union in reaffirming their commitment to protecting women and girls in armed conflicts and ensuring women participate meaningfully in peace processes, in a joint declaration delivered by Greek Foreign Minister George Gerapetritis on 27 October during the UN Security Council’s open debate on the Women, Peace and Security agenda. Greece, alongside Colombia, Denmark, France, Latvia, Liberia, Panama and the United Kingdom, also belongs to the Security Council members that have endorsed the Shared Commitments on Women, Peace and Security. “We call for the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women, and for women to take leadership roles in peace processes and decision-making at all levels,” the joint statement said. The signatories backed the UN Secretary-General’s call for women to make up at least one-third of participants in UN-led or co-led peace processes. They called for women to participate meaningfully as negotiators, mediators and peacebuilders. They also stressed the need to integrate the Women, Peace and Security agenda into all peace operations, including during transitional periods and mission withdrawals. They called for the continued presence and retention of women’s protection advisers and gender advisers throughout these processes. The declaration placed particular emphasis on protecting the human rights and fundamental freedoms of all women and girls in full compliance with international law, including international humanitarian law and international human rights law. Recognising the particular impact of armed conflict on women and girls, the signatories urged all parties involved to take effective measures to protect them. “We condemn all violations and abuses of the human rights of women and girls and remain committed to ending impunity by ensuring accountability for all perpetrators,” the statement said. To support accountability, the signatories backed the development of targeted criteria for inclusion on UN sanctions lists. They also recognised the important work of the International Criminal Court and welcomed the establishment earlier this year of a network to prosecute conflict-related sexual violence. The participating countries and the EU condemned in the strongest terms all incidents of conflict-related sexual violence, as well as every form of sexual and gender-based violence. They called for comprehensive, life-saving assistance for victims and survivors, including sexual and reproductive health services and psychosocial support. The declaration also recognised the essential work of civil society, including women human rights defenders, journalists and peace activists. The signatories pledged to protect them against reprisals, threats and all forms of intimidation intended to silence their voices. The statement called for predictable, adequate and sustained funding for the Women, Peace and Security agenda, both across the UN system and through official development assistance provided by individual donors. It also encouraged all UN member states to adopt dedicated National Action Plans, backed by sufficient resources and effective implementation. On emerging technologies, including generative artificial intelligence, the signatories stressed that these tools should empower women rather than expose them to abuse. They rejected the misuse of technology to target women, including those in leadership positions, and to spread hate speech. The declaration concluded with a message to women and girls suffering from the consequences of war: “You are not alone.” “As member states, we remain committed to turning the pledges of the Women, Peace and Security agenda into concrete action to protect and improve the position of all women and girls,” the statement said. The joint declaration included Colombia, Denmark, France, Latvia, Liberia, Panama, the United Kingdom, Greece, Afghanistan, Albania, Andorra, Armenia, Australia, Austria, Bangladesh, Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Brazil, Bulgaria, Canada, Chile, Costa Rica, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Finland, Georgia, Germany, Guatemala, Guyana, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malaysia, Maldives, Malta, Mexico, Monaco, Mongolia, Montenegro, Morocco, Myanmar, Namibia, the Netherlands, North Macedonia, Norway, Poland, Portugal, the Republic of Korea, the Republic of Moldova, Romania, San Marino, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, South Africa, Spain, the State of Palestine, Sweden, Switzerland, Timor-Leste, Ukraine, the United Arab Emirates and Uruguay, as well as the European Union. title: ‘This isn’t the final certified copy’, INEC reacts to alleged AI-generated photographs on voters’ register
body: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has reacted to reports of AI-Generated images on the published voters’ register. In the preliminary register that the commission published after the outcry over alleged violation of the Electoral Act, there were entries from a polling unit in Etsako West Local Government Area of Edo State, which had photographs suspected to be generated by AI. This has fueled speculations online, with many doubting the credibility of the process. But in a statement on Tuesday, Mohammed Haruna, Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee, clarified that the published list is not the final one. “The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has noted public concerns and reports circulating on social media regarding suspected AI-generated photographs appearing in the Preliminary Register of Voters recently published on its website.” “The Commission wishes to clarify that the register published online on 26 October 2026 is the same preliminary register physically displayed at Registration Areas (RAs) nationwide from 9th to 15th October 2026 as part of the Display, Claims and Objections exercise. “During the physical display, a number of questionable registration records were identified and flagged for further examination. The Commission commenced the process of reviewing these records and taking appropriate corrective action in accordance with established procedures. “The online publication represents the original preliminary register and does not reflect all ongoing data-cleanup activities. It is important to emphasize that the preliminary register is not the final certified register. The Display, Claims and Objections exercise is specifically intended to facilitate public scrutiny, identify inaccuracies and irregularities, and enable appropriate corrections before certification. “The Commission is also examining the circumstances surrounding the suspicious photographs, including possible technical or procedural lapses, and will take appropriate action based on verified findings. “The Commission appreciates the vigilance of citizens and stakeholders who have brought these concerns to public attention. Such scrutiny contributes to the process of improving the accuracy and integrity of the register. “INEC remains committed to completing the necessary verification, adjudication, and data-cleanup processes ahead of the scheduled certification of the final Register of Voters on 15th December 2026. The Commission assures Nigerians that verified irregularities will be addressed through the applicable procedures and that further updates will be provided as the review progresses.”

title: Australian space power start-up MP Space secures A$23 million in seed funding
body: Sydney-based space power technology company MP Space has closed a $23 million (US$16 million) seed round led by Blackbird, with Seraphim Space making its first-ever investment in an Australian company. The fundraising, one of the largest seed rounds for an Australian technology company, will enable MP Space to scale local manufacturing, expand its range of power-system platforms, and grow its Australian engineering team. The investment highlights the strategic importance of the Federal Government’s Statement on Space, which sets out the national focus areas: Trusted Space Services, Spaceflight Ecosystem, Space Platforms, Microgravity Ecosystem and Exploration Technologies. MP Space’s power infrastructure underpins each of the five areas, supplying the reliable, fit-for-purpose power every satellite, launch vehicle and lunar mission depends on to operate. The scale of the seed round reinforces the increased confidence investors have in Australia in the wake of the Federal Government releasing the strategic agenda for the space industry. The round was led by Blackbird, with participation from Systemiq Capital, Seraphim Space, Speedinvest and MFV Partners, bringing together Australian and international investors to support MP Space’s next phase of growth. Founded in January 2024 by former Tesla engineers Jay Manley (CEO) and Sam Paterson (CCO), MP Space has already been designed into several space services and missions, totalling more than 500 spacecraft, with its hardware set to fly in orbit for the first time in Q4 2026. MP Space has been a resident of the NSW Government-backed National Defence and Aerospace Hub (formerly National Space Industry Hub) at Cicada Innovations for over two years, presenting at Cicada x Tech23 in Sydney on 9 September 2026 alongside this year’s cohort of Australian deep-tech ventures. Jay Manley, CEO and Co-Founder, MP Space said: “Our thesis is simple: the next generation of spacecraft will need a lot more power, and the space industry needs better ways to generate, store and manage it. We’ve seen enormous advances in power electronics, software and energy storage through electric vehicles, grid-scale energy and home batteries. MP Space is bringing that same advanced technology to spacecraft power systems, designed from the outset to be manufactured reliably and at scale. This raise reflects the customer demand we’re already seeing and gives us the capital to accelerate. Over the next 12 months, our focus is expanding manufacturing capacity, scaling the team and delivering power systems for the next generation of spacecraft and constellations.” Samantha Wong, Partner at Blackbird said: “At Blackbird, our investment conviction starts with the founding team. Jay and Sam have gone from solar racecar clubs at uni to industry-leading capability in scalable battery system design, having built Tesla’s Powerwall from electrons to a $10 billion businessline. The same energy management evolution will happen in space and we believe MP Space has a shot at revolutionising this fast-growing industry. In less than two years, MP Space has already delivered a software-defined battery, with one of the highest gravimetric energy densities of any space battery, and will gain flight heritage this month. They are moving with speed and precision in a market that has explosive potential. As space unlocks more use cases, MP Space is well-placed to seize the opportunity with an indisputable hardware advantage and deep software capabilities. It’s an Aussie business redefining the global standard. These are the types of businesses we are proud to back.” Lucas Bishop, Vice President at Seraphim Space said: “We’re excited to back Jay Manley, Sam Paterson and the broader MP Space team as they build the next generation of spacecraft power systems. Drawing on their experience scaling some of the world’s most demanding energy and power hardware programmes at Tesla, the team is exceptionally well placed to address two fundamental challenges facing the space industry. Power is a fundamental constraint on spacecraft capability, and we are seeing power requirements scale rapidly across almost every mission type. More available power directly enables more capable payloads, greater onboard processing and, ultimately, more ambitious missions. Separately, the industry lacks proven, independent suppliers capable of delivering critical hardware reliably and at scale. This has made vertical integration a necessity rather than a choice for spacecraft manufacturers. By replacing bespoke, high-cost and low-volume systems with reliable, cost-effective and off-the-shelf power hardware, MP Space can help reverse this historical over-reliance on vertical integration. We believe this positions MP Space to become a foundational supplier to the next generation of spacecraft, and we’re delighted to support the team on that journey.” For Editorial Inquiries Contact: Editor Kym Bergmann at kym.bergmann@venturamedia.net For Advertising Inquiries Contact: Group Sales Director Simon Hadfield at simon.hadfield@venturamedia.net

title: Tompolo says Tinubu needs another term to consolidate reforms, presents 30 vehicles for mobilisation
body:
Ahead of the 2027 presidential election, Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election, saying the president means well for Nigeria and deserves another four years to consolidate his administration’s reforms.
Tompolo spoke on Tuesday at the inauguration of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Imo State, where he donated 30 vehicles to support grassroots mobilisation for Mr Tinubu’s re-election.
Represented by the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services Limited, Kestin Pondi, Tompolo said the vehicles and other resources were provided to support Governor Hope Uzodimma and the movement’s campaign activities across the state.
He described President Tinubu as a courageous leader who prioritises Nigeria’s interests by embarking on economic reforms from the beginning of his administration in May 2023.
“Our president, President Bola Tinubu, is a very courageous man; a man who puts Nigeria first; a man who loves Nigeria more than he loves himself; a man who loves Nigeria more than the office that he is vying for.
“When he came into office, he did not do the normal calculations that politicians usually do. He came in and said that he wants to reform Nigeria,” Tompolo said.
Relaying Tompolo’s message, Mr Pondi said: “Your Excellency, we have come with vehicles. We have come with resources. These vehicles you have seen, there are 30 of them. We brought them to Imo State to support you in your cause to re-elect President Bola Tinubu.”
He said the movement would work with the governor and other political leaders to take the president’s campaign to households and communities across the state.
Mr Pondi added that the newly inaugurated chapter would be available to support campaign activities whenever required.
“Your Excellency, the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Imo State is at your beck and call. Anytime you need them, call them. Give them instructions. Tell them how you want them to campaign,” he said.
Speaking at the event, Governor Uzodimma commended Tompolo for providing resources to support the campaign, describing the movement as an important partner in efforts to secure another term for the President.
The governor, who is the secretary of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, said his assessment of the Tinubu administration’s performance had convinced him that the president should be given another term to complete his programmes.
“When we preach the Gospel about the All Progressives Congress government of President Bola Tinubu, we started, we were not many. But as the days go by, the efforts and activities of the government begin to trickle in. Nigerians begin to see the man called Bola Tinubu in his true colours,” he said.
He acknowledged that the administration had made progress but still had outstanding tasks to accomplish, adding that continuity would enable President Tinubu to complete his work.
“We have assessed the achievements of President Bola Tinubu, and we have seen the good things he brought. We have also seen so many things he is also yet to do.
“And we decided to lead the crusade that will enable him to complete his good work. We have taken that decision,” Mr Uzodimma said.
He described Tompolo as a man whose contributions and resources had helped advance the campaign for the president’s re-election.
Mr Uzodimma also praised the door-to-door strategy, saying it would enable campaigners to communicate the achievements of the Renewed Hope Agenda directly to Nigerians.
“We are partners in progress. We work with you. We do the work. We elect the president,” he said.
Earlier, the National Coordinator of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Sunday Asuku, urged Nigerians to remain patient with the administration, arguing that the economic difficulties associated with its reforms would give way to long-term benefits.
Mr Asuku said President Tinubu had laid a foundation for economic development over the past three and a half years and should be allowed four more years to build on it.
“The message we must tell today is simple and short. Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has sent us to make you understand that things might be rough, but Nigeria is on the right trajectory,” he said.
He maintained that economic reforms often bring temporary difficulties but argued they were necessary to achieve lasting prosperity.
“Where there is reform, we are expected to go through some pains. But it is a pain that guarantees long-term prosperity, and we can get through for sure,” Mr Asuku said.
He also challenged opposition politicians to explain their records in public office, urging Nigerians to examine their past performances before making electoral decisions.
He called on voters to turn out en masse on 16 January 2027 to vote for President Tinubu, adding that the movement would take its message from door to door, town to town and community to community.
In his remarks, Imo State APC Chairman, Austine Onyedebelu, highlighted the federal government’s economic reforms and the state government’s infrastructure projects, urging party members to take the campaign directly to residents.
He cited the removal of the petrol subsidy, foreign exchange reforms, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund and the increase in the national minimum wage to N70,000 as measures introduced by the Tinubu administration.

title: Liquid AI Releases LFM3: 6 Open-Weight 2B-Class Multimodal Models
body: Liquid AI has released LFM3 , its new generation of Liquid Foundation Models. Liquid AI LFM3 is a family of 6 open-weight, 2B-class models built on one shared backbone. The family covers text, vision, audio, omni and decision tasks. Every model can be fine-tuned on a single GPU. Developers can then deploy on phones, laptops, private servers or the cloud. TL;DR Size: LFM3-1.7B has 1.73B parameters and a 256K context window . LFM3-VL-2B has 1.92B and 128K. LFM3-Omni-2B has 2.2B. Runs on: about 1 GB of memory at 4-bit, so phones and laptops. GGUF, MLX, ONNX, FP8 and NVFP4 checkpoints ship. Performance: LFM3-1.7B averages 49.37 across 29 benchmarks, above Qwen3.5-9B at 47.24 (Liquid’s own eval). Best: IFEval 96.66, and AutomationBench 41.29 vs 15.10 for Qwen3.5-9B. Worst: Humanity’s Last Exam (no tools) 7.17, and RULER 128K 65.56 vs 87.11 for Qwen3.5-9B. What is Liquid AI LFM3? LFM3 is a multimodal model family from Liquid AI that branches 6 models from 1 base. All of them start from LFM3-1.7B-Base . The release includes: LFM3-1.7B: a text model for local agents, post-trained for harnesses like Hermes Agent, Pi and OpenClaw. LFM3-VL-2B: the first LFM vision model with video input, sampled at 2 fps. LFM3-Audio-2B: speech in and out across 18 languages, with tool calling. LFM3-Omni-2B: vision, audio and language in one model, answering in text or speech. d1-2B and d1-Omni-2B: decision models that answer many questions in 1 forward pass. How does the tri-hybrid architecture work? The backbone mixes 3 operators across 24 layers . There are 13 gated short convolutions, 5 sliding-window attention layers and 6 global attention layers. The SWA window is 256 tokens. Convolution kernels grew from 3 to 7. Liquid AI team found this mix with its hardware-in-the-loop architecture search. LFM2 was tuned on 1 phone and 1 laptop. LFM3 was tuned across 14 device and backend combinations. These include a Raspberry Pi 5 and the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU. Other changes include head-wise sigmoid gates on attention, partial RoPE on global layers and sandwich norm. The base model saw 22T tokens. The last 3.5T tokens were agent-heavy mid-training, which also extended context to 256K. Post-training ran in 4 stages. SFT on 1.75T tokens came first, then mixed RL. Next, 6 specialist teachers were distilled into 1 model, followed by agentic RL. How does LFM3-1.7B perform on benchmarks? Liquid AI reports that LFM3-1.7B beats LFM2.5-2.6B with 35% fewer parameters. The bigger story is the agent results. On WebArena-Verified it scores 38.42, against 28.94 for Qwen3.5-9B. On BFCL V4 it scores 71.39, against 62.83. Size still wins on knowledge and agentic coding. GPQA Diamond is 63.37, versus 80.40 for Qwen3.5-9B. SWE-bench Verified is 43.40, versus 51.20. Search narrows the gap: Humanity’s Last Exam rises from 7.17 to 13.90 with tools. window.addEventListener("message",function(e){if(e.data&&e.data.mtpLfm3H){var f=document.getElementById("mtp-lfm3-frame");if(f)f.style.height=e.data.mtpLfm3H+"px";}}); How do LFM3-1.7B and its rivals compare? Feature LFM3-1.7B MiniCPM5-2B Qwen3.5-4B Gemma 4 E4B Parameters 1.73B 2.52B 4B LM (5B on Hub with vision) 4.5B effective (8B with embeddings) Architecture Conv + SWA + global attention Standard Llama transformer Gated DeltaNet + gated attention Sliding window + global attention Context 256K 131,072 262,144 128K Input modalities Text Text Text, image, video Text, image, audio License LFM Open License v1.0 ($10M revenue threshold) Apache 2.0 Apache 2.0 Apache 2.0 BFCL V4 (Liquid eval) 71.39 62.65 55.12 48.25 WebArena-Verified (Liquid eval) 38.42 9.11 21.92 17.06 SWE-bench Verified (Liquid eval) 43.40 34.80 41.20 0.50 GPQA Diamond (Liquid eval) 63.37 65.15 75.76 57.88 GPQA Diamond (vendor-reported) 63.37 70.2 76.2 58.6 RULER 128K (Liquid eval) 65.56 37.96 84.63 18.82 Liquid 29-benchmark average 49.37 39.19 39.27 31.74 Sources: Liquid LFM3 model card , MiniCPM5-2B card , Qwen3.5-4B card , Gemma 4 E4B card , LFM license . What about vision, audio, omni and decision models? LFM3-VL-2B averages 71.4 across 62 vision benchmarks. Gemma 4 12B scores 71.7 on the same suite. It leads that comparison on visual grounding (77.3) and GUI understanding (83.1). Video (61.2) and agentic tasks (42.5) still trail larger API models. LFM3-Audio-2B reaches 6.2 English WER and a 3.8 UTMOSv2 TTS score. LFM3-Omni-2B scores 70.1 on Daily-Omni, against 61.3 for Qwen2.5-Omni-7B. d1-2B replaces d1-3B with a third fewer parameters. It improves Decision Bench from 83.6 to 85.2. How can developers deploy LFM3? Weights are on Hugging Face , the Liquid AI Playground and the Liquid API. The docs list GGUF, MLX and ONNX for the text and vision models. Runtimes include llama.cpp, MLX, vLLM, SGLang, Ollama and Transformers. On-device, Liquid AI measured llama.cpp at Q4_0 with 32K context. A full 128K context needs 1.6 GB of KV cache. Qwen3.5-4B needs 4.3 GB. On 1 NVIDIA B300 with SGLang, LFM3-1.7B produces 3.6B tokens per day at 1,024 concurrent requests. Liquid AI also showed specialization. A few hours of SFT and GRPO on 1 A100 lifted wind-turbine defect classification to 67%. Key Takeaways 6 open-weight 2B-class models share 1 tri-hybrid backbone. LFM3-1.7B fits in about 1 GB at 4-bit with 256K context. It beats Qwen3.5-9B on BFCL V4, WebArena-Verified and AutomationBench. Knowledge and agentic coding remain clear weak spots. title: HELLENiQ ENERGY Opens Greece’s First 100 MW Battery Storage Project
body: HELLENiQ ENERGY has brought its first large-scale battery energy storage project into operation at its Thessaloniki industrial facilities, investing approximately €50 million in a 100-megawatt (MW) system with a storage capacity of 200 megawatt-hours (MWh). Developed through HELLENiQ Renewables, the project marks the group’s entry into large-scale electricity storage. It is the first project of its size developed in Greece and ranks among the largest battery storage systems in southeastern Europe. The installation addresses a key challenge facing the expansion of renewable energy: how to use electricity generated by solar and wind farms when the power system needs it. By storing surplus energy, the system can help reduce renewable generation curtailment and create additional capacity for new renewable energy projects. The facility will complete at least one full charging and discharging cycle each day, storing more than 200 MWh of electricity. It will also provide flexibility and balancing services to support grid stability and strengthen energy security. 56 battery arrays across a 100-acre site The project occupies approximately 100 stremmata (10 hectares) and comprises three storage stations and 56 arrays of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries with liquid-cooling systems. The installation also includes the necessary control, protection and monitoring infrastructure. To connect the facility to Greece’s national electricity transmission system, the company built a new 33/150-kilovolt (kV) step-up substation and an underground high-voltage transmission line approximately five kilometres long, linking the site to the Thessaloniki Extra High Voltage Centre. The project secured selection through the Regulatory Authority for Waste, Energy and Water (RAAEY)’s first competitive procedure for energy storage systems. The company implemented it through Greece’s Greece 2.0 National Recovery and Resilience Plan, with funding from the European Union’s NextGenerationEU programme. HELLENiQ Renewables expands its storage portfolio The investment forms part of HELLENiQ ENERGY’s broader strategy to expand its electricity and renewable energy businesses. HELLENiQ Renewables’ renewable energy and storage development portfolio now exceeds 6 gigawatts (GW), including more than 1 GW of storage projects across Greece, Romania, Cyprus and Bulgaria. Sotiris Kapellos, CEO of HELLENiQ Renewables, said sustained investment in Greece and southeastern Europe had helped the company build a portfolio exceeding 6 GW, with more than 700 MW already operational. He described electricity storage as critical infrastructure for the future energy system, explaining that batteries provide the flexibility needed to integrate more renewable energy, reduce wasted green electricity and improve reliability, security and cost efficiency. Kapellos said the Thessaloniki battery energy storage system (BESS) represented an important step towards a more reliable and sustainable energy system, supporting the long-term provision of cleaner and more affordable electricity for consumers. George Alexopoulos, deputy CEO of HELLENiQ ENERGY, also highlighted the importance of storing renewable electricity. He said storage improves the use of renewable generation, strengthens grid reliability and supports greater energy security and access to sustainable, affordable energy. Alexopoulos added that the completion of the company’s first storage project marked another important step in its strategy to establish a strong electricity and renewables business alongside its existing energy operations. Second battery project planned for Florina HELLENiQ ENERGY expects to complete its second battery storage project in Florina in the coming period. The facility will have a power rating of 50 MW and a storage capacity of 200 MWh. The group aims to operate renewable energy projects with a combined capacity of 1.5 GW by 2028 and more than 2 GW by 2030. title: U.S. Air Force tests XQ-67A mission systems and data links for dispersed combat operations [VIDEO]
body: Conducted under the Demonstration of ACP Performance and Effectiveness, or Demon APE, project, the flight combined onboard hardware testing with live, virtual and constructive simulations. The Air Force said the demonstration showed how uncrewed platforms could be managed across distributed theaters using resilient, layered command and control. “By pairing AFRL’s rapid prototyping with ACC’s operational test units, the Air Force is shortening the timeline between concept and warfighter capability,” said Col. Matthew Caspers, DAF Deputy Technology Executive Officer for Air. The project brings together the Air Force Research Laboratory and Air Combat Command to accelerate development and delivery in support of National Defense Strategy priorities. The XQ-67A demonstrated the integration of sensors, mission computers, and power and thermal management hardware designed to work together in demanding combat environments. The flight also incorporated beyond-line-of-sight communications, supporting the management of uncrewed aircraft across dispersed operating areas. “This proved that AFRL’s autonomous architectures, aligned with Autonomy and Agile Mission Suite Government Reference Architectures, can reliably process and relay combat-relevant data in real-world scenarios,” said Trenton White, an aerospace engineer in AFRL’s Air Warfare directorate. The ability to process and share that information is part of the effort to give commanders deeper situational awareness. The Air Force described investment in platforms such as the XQ-67A as a means of extending the operational reach of crewed fighters. It also aims to add affordable operational mass to the fleet while limiting human aircrews’ exposure to risk.

title: The Greatest to Blade Runner 2099: 12 of the best TV shows to watch this November
body: From a drama about Muhammad Ali’s early years to Amy Poehler’s latest sitcom and a Blade Runner small-screen spin-off – these are the best series to watch and stream. 1. The Gilded Age The fourth season of Julian Fellowes’ addictive period drama picks up soon after the previous season ended and answers some burning, melodramatic questions. Will the nouveau riche George Russell (Morgan Spector), having moved out of their ostentatious mansion, go home to his manipulative social-climbing wife, Bertha (Carrie Coon)? Will the pedigreed Agnes van Rhijn (Christine Baranski) topple Bertha from the top of the social ladder? She’s certainly going to try. Subplots swirl around them as Peggy (Denée Benton) tries to maintain her career as a writer while dealing with her intrusive mother-in-law-to-be (Phylicia Rashad), while Marian (Louisa Jacobson) and Larry’s (Harry Richardson) on-and-off romance gets especially thorny. Last season’s ratings were among the show’s highest, so there may even be an appetite for the upcoming Voices of the Gilded Age: The Christmas Album , featuring songs from the Broadway-veteran cast. If you’ve ever wanted to hear Baranski sing We Need a Little Christmas or Brian Stokes Mitchell do It’s the Most Wonderful Time of the Year, here you go. The Gilded Age premieres 1 November on HBO in the US and 2 November on Sky Atlantic in the UK 2. The Greatest Muhammad Ali was one of the greatest boxers of all time and has also been one of the most often depicted on screen, from Will Smith in the 2001 film Ali to documentaries by Antoine Fuqua and Ken Burns. This dramatic series sets itself apart by focusing on his childhood and the early years of his career, when he was still known as Cassius Clay, in a story that moves from his boyhood in the Jim Crow South to the 1960 Olympics, through to the 1964 fight that made him the world champion. Newcomer Jaalen Best plays Ali in the show, which has the cooperation of the Ali family and counts his widow, Lonnie Ali, and Michael B Jordan as executive producers. “The Greatest is [about] his pathway to growth, at home with his brother and his parents. It’s a granular deep dive into Muhammad’s life,” Lonnie Ali told Esquire . Meanwhile the series’ creator, Ben Watkins (showrunner of the Alex Cross series), teased that despite its family ties, the details on screen “aren’t always flattering”. The Greatest premieres 4 November on Prime Video internationally 3. Stick For some reason, middle-aged former golf champions trying to make a comeback are a mini-trend in sitcoms. Will Ferrell’s character set out to do it as the title character in the tongue-in-cheek Netflix series Hawk. And in the second season of Apple TV’s Stick, a comedy that leans toward the heartwarming, Owen Wilson’s character – Pryce Cahill, known as Stick – attempts to come out of retirement too. The cast has always been this show’s biggest draw, and that is enhanced this season with Rhea Seehorn of Pluribus and Better Call Saul in a supporting role as Stick’s new coach. Timothy Olyphant returns as his former rival, who nudges him to try to become the oldest player ever to win the US Open tournament, with Judy Greer as Stick’s ex-wife and Marc Maron as his friend and caddie, Mitts. Apparently the burgeoning television golf world requires cringe-making nicknames. Stick premieres 4 November on Apple TV internationally 4. Black Doves Keira Knightley and Ben Whishaw return in the second season of this thoroughly improbable but always entertaining action-espionage series. Knightley plays Helen Webb, whose husband (Andrew Buchan) is about to become the UK’s prime minister – a situation that is not great for him because she has been leaking information for a decade to the shadowy Black Doves organisation, set on undermining governments around the world. Whishaw plays her best friend, Sam, a hitman who helps her get out of the scrapes while getting into some himself. In the new season, Helen’s Black Doves handler, Mrs Reed, played by Sarah Lancashire, seems to go missing, although Lancashire herself remains a major part of the show. Marital drama plays out in the background of the shootouts and power plays. The new PM might not be fit to govern since he hasn’t noticed his wife spying right under his nose. Or maybe she’s just that clever. The series creator, Joe Barton, captured its droll tone when calling the characters “our murderous little spy family”. Black Doves premieres 5 November on Netflix internationally (Credit: Channel 4) 5. It Gets Worse Leo Reich, who broke through with his HBO stand-up comedy special Literally Who Cares? in 2023, created and stars in this acerbic series about three Gen Z university friends struggling through their early 20s, characters Reich has described as “self-involved and quite objectionable”. He plays the self-absorbed Ethan, supported by his parents. His best friends are by-the-rules Abi (Emily Fairn) and would-be writer Sam (Olivia Gray). It’s a sign of Reich’s rising star that he has enticed some big names to join in. Andrew Scott appears in an episode, Lena Dunham has a cameo as Abi’s boss and the series’ unlikely narrator is the novelist Zadie Smith. The show is not just another Friends knockoff. It was a hit at the recent London Film Festival, with the Financial Times calling it “a witty Gen Z sex comedy” and the Guardian describing the series as “profound and properly funny” and Reich as “the future of TV comedy”. It Gets Worse is currently on Channel 4 in the UK and premieres 6 November on Paramount+ in the US 6. Rivals It has been months since the first half of this scathingly funny show’s second season dropped, but finally we’re back in the fictional Cotswold county of Rutshire, beloved from Jilly Cooper’s bonkbuster novels. It’s a place where cheating, in business and relationships, is just a way of life for its mix of mischievous, mean-spirited and occasionally good-hearted characters. Tony Baddingham, the tycoon played with devilish glee by David Tennant, is more sinister than ever, and unlikely to soften in the aftermath of a tragedy. His rival, Declan O’Hara (Aidan Turner), is ever more desperate to keep his career and marriage intact, which his wife is making more difficult on both counts. And their daughter Taggie (Bella Maclean) must decide whether to give into her love for the playboy Rupert Campbell-Black (Alex Hassell) or do the sensible thing and run for the hills. In the new episodes, Lady Monica Baddingham’s glamorous younger sister turns up. So does a legendary Argentinian polo player. They should fit right in. Rivals premieres 11 November on Hulu in the US and Disney+ in the UK 7. The Good Daughter Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy – either one could be the good daughter in this thriller about murder, justice and family dynamics. They play sisters from the fictional smalltown of Pikeville, Georgia, who survived a violent home invasion when they were girls. Byrne is Samantha, a patent lawyer who moved to New York. Fahy is Charlotte, who stayed in town and became a defence lawyer like their father (Brendan Gleeson). The sisters have been estranged for a decade, but when Charlotte witnesses a murder that recalls the attack in their childhood, the tension and mysteries ramp up and Samantha is called home. The Good Daughter – not to be confused with those other recent suspense series The Better Sister and The Girlfriend – is written by Karin Slaughter, based on her 2017 bestselling novel, and explores the traumatic effects of violence. “We’re all exposed to trauma all the time,” Fahy told Vanity Fair , adding, “It’s really important to show people navigating their trauma and coming out on the other side.” The Good Daughter premieres 12 November on Peacock in the US and Sky Atlantic in the UK 8. 12 12 12 Two commanding, high-profile actors star in this heist series. Jamie Dornan plays Paul Galvin, a criminal who tries to leave his old life but is forced back in as part of an $800m (£599m) theft from a Zurich bank. Anthony Mackie is Jack Strickland, a disgraced FBI agent on his trail, whose character handily explains the series’ title in the trailer . “FBI principles of crime say a high asset robbery is 12 months in planning, 12 hours in execution. A bank robber who’s not caught within 12 days is not caught at all,” he says. The show mingles those three timelines as the cat-and-mouse game takes the men across Europe – with spectacular settings on dark streets, at sea and against snowy landscapes – en route to their inevitable face-to-face. 12 12 12 premieres 13 November on Apple TV internationally 9. Blue Lights This fourth season of the exhilarating police series set in Belfast keeps things fresh by returning to a much-loved character from the past. Mo McIntyre, whose mother, Tina, runs the family crime ring, finally goes on trial for orchestrating the attack that killed Gerry Cliff (Richard Dornan), devastating his police colleagues, in season one. That storyline becomes a touching opportunity to look back at Gerry’s romance with his wife, Sandra (beautifully played by Andi Osho), a sergeant who worked alongside him in Blackthorn Station. Apart from the trial, the team of regular characters grapples with anti-immigrant protests that turn violent. And all the while, higher-ups are threatening to shut down Blackthorn for inefficiency. As always, the show deftly puts crime-fighting against the backdrop of lingering political divisions going back to the Troubles, while mixing in personal stories. The Guardian , in its review of this season, rightly called it “TV’s most thrilling cop show”. Blue Lights is currently on BBC iPlayer in the UK and premieres 12 November on Britbox in the US 10. The Altruists Another day, another drama about a tech-adjacent mogul. This time it’s the saga of Sam Bankman-Fried, coming in the wake of those about Mark Zuckerberg ( The Social Reckoning ), Elizabeth Holmes ( You Can See Everything ) or Sam Altman ( Artificial ). Anthony Boyle ( House of Guinness ) plays Bankman-Fried, who founded the cryptocurrency exchange FTX, which fell apart in 2022. Convicted of fraud, conspiracy and money-laundering, he is currently in prison. (He is appealing his conviction and has formally requested a presidential pardon .) Julia Garner, who played a different fraudster in Inventing Anna , is Bankman-Fried’s colleague and sometime girlfriend, Caroline Ellison, who pleaded guilty to wire fraud. The series was created by Graham Moore, who won an Oscar for his screenplay of The Imitation Game, and who has an unusual, to say the least, take on the convicted criminals. In his view, Moore has said , Bankman-Fried and Ellison started as “deeply committed altruists,” out to change the financial world for everyone’s benefit, then “with the very best of intentions talked each other and themselves into committing a number of terrible crimes”. The Altruists premieres 19 November on Netflix internationally 11. Dig Amy Poehler and Hugh Laurie play archaeologists on a dig in Greece, a setting Poehler has said is ideal for comedy. “A dig is a really funny place,” she told TV Insider . “It’s part summer camp, part mysterious uncovering of relics.” Laurie goes back to his wry comic roots as professor Neville Wycombe, who runs the archaeological program, and Poehler is Elise, the dedicated, serious head of a team of women. They arrive for the summer only to find themselves in an international muddle when they discover a priceless artifact. Geraldine Viswanathan and Antonia Thomas are members of Elise’s team, with Fina Strazza as Wycombe’s guileless in-over-her-head assistant. Poehler created the show with Mike Schur, a creator of her previous series, Parks and Recreation, one of television’s best sitcoms. Schur is a master of smart, low-key character-driven comedies including The Good Place, so whatever madcap adventures the archaeologists land in, the show promises to be slyly funny. Dig premieres 23 November on Peacock in the US 12. Blade Runner 2099 Michelle Yeoh stars in this series that takes the Blade Runner franchise racing toward everyone’s worst fears about artificial intelligence. In Ridley Scott’s classic film Blade Runner and Denis Villeneuve’s sequel, Blade Runner 2049, humans hunted down replicants. Now the robots have taken over and replicants are hunting down humans. Yeoh plays Olwen, a replicant on the Los Angeles police force. Hunter Schafer is Cora, who is actually a human masquerading as a replicant, so she can worm her way into the LA police as a way of protecting her brother. The series’ showrunner, Silka Luisa, told Empire magazine, “Everyone, globally, has been very aware of this palpable fear of the end of our species. Climate change, pandemics.” The series, she said, considers: “What would the world look like when it’s no longer ours?” Well, Cora is partnered with Olwen, who happens to be days from reaching the end of her lifespan, so while the world may be different, the old trope of an about-to-retire-cop paired with a rookie obviously lives on. Blade Runner 2099 premieres 25 November on Prime Video internationally

title: Afenifere Sets Up Committee For Fasoranti’s Burial, Warns Against Succession Talks
body: The pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere, has constituted a committee to plan the funeral of its late national leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, who died at the age of 100. The decision was taken on Tuesday at a meeting of the organisation’s National Executive Committee held at the residence of the deceased in Akure, the Ondo State capital. The meeting also extended condolences to the family and reaffirmed Afenifere’s commitment to preserving the values and ideals that defined the late elder statesman’s life. The Chairman of the National Executive Committee, the Olu of Ilu-Abo, Oba Olu Falae, said the committee would work with the family’s burial committee and the government committee to ensure a befitting burial for Fasoranti. Oba Falae said the committee would comprise Afenifere members and representatives of other groups that had previously met at Ogbo in Ogun State, adding that its membership would be expanded. The committee members include Oba Olu Falae, Oba Oladipo Olaitan, Bashorun Sehinde Arogbofa, Senator Femi Okurounmu, Senator Kofo Akerele-Bucknor, Chief Supo Shonibare, Archbishop Ayo Ladigbolu, Chief Tola Mobulurin, Otunba Dr Samuel Ibikunle, Chief Korede Duyile, Chief Femi Aluko and Dr Segun Mimiko. Others are Otunba Gbenga Daniel, Dr Gbola Adetunji, Hon. Wale Oshun, Otunba Iyiola Omisore, Chief Pekun Awobona, Engr. Bayo Adenekan, Chief Lekan Alabi, Abagun Kole Omololu, Dr Akin Onigbinde, SAN, Prof. Akin Onigbinde, Chief Dare Babarinsa, Dr David Atte and Chief Ayo Abereoran. The list also includes Hon. Lanre Omisore, Chief Sola Ebiseni, Otunba Deji Wellington, Mrs Nike Olujembola, Mrs Oluwatoyin Falade, Comrade Jare Ajayi, Arc. Goke Omigbodun and Chief Ademola Folarin. The organisation cautioned against discussions about who would succeed Fasoranti, describing such conversations as premature and contrary to Yoruba cultural values. According to Oba Falae, the immediate priority is to give the late leader a befitting burial, after which a credible successor would emerge to lead the organisation. He said the meeting stressed the need for unity among the groups involved in the funeral arrangements, adding that succession discussions should not distract from efforts to honour the deceased. Speaking on behalf of the family, Pa Fasoranti’s younger sister, Olori Rachel Falae, described him as a quiet, disciplined and trustworthy leader whose integrity earned him the respect of the people of Akure. She said her late brother demonstrated remarkable dedication while combining his responsibilities as a local government chairman and school principal. On the funeral arrangements, Olori Falae said the family expected representatives of Afenifere, members of the Akure community and the church to participate in the ceremonies. The post Afenifere Sets Up Committee For Fasoranti’s Burial, Warns Against Succession Talks appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Gold Fields Health outreach screens 735 people, refers 21 suspected breast cancer cases
body: A health outreach programme organised by the Gold Fields Ghana Foundation and its partners has provided screening and general healthcare services to 735 people in Samahu and Abekoase in the Western Region, with 21 suspected breast cancer cases referred for further assessment. The fourth-quarter (Q4) Health Engagement and Access Link (HEAL) Programme, held on October 17, 2026, enabled 185 women to undergo breast cancer screening as part of activities marking Breast Cancer Awareness Month. It was organised under the theme “ Every Story is Unique, Every Journey Matters ” in partnership with the Rotary Club of Tarkwa, Unilever Ghana and Diagnostic Centre Limited (DCL). Speaking at the programme, Dr Magdalene D. Bakari, Lead Specialist for Health Services at Gold Fields Ghana Limited, stressed the importance of bringing healthcare closer to communities and encouraging people to seek medical attention early. She urged women to prioritise regular check-ups and seek professional advice whenever they notice unusual changes in their bodies. Beyond breast cancer screening, residents benefited from general medical consultations, blood pressure and blood sugar tests, eye and dental screenings, ear, nose and throat assessments, lung function tests, X-rays and ultrasound services. Free medication, health counselling and referrals for further care were also provided where necessary. The Executive Secretary of the Gold Fields Ghana Foundation, Abdel-Razak Yakubu, said the Foundation’s health outreach initiatives form part of efforts to improve access to essential healthcare in its host communities. The programme also provided National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) registration, renewal and card replacement services to 937 community members, helping them access health insurance services. With an estimated cost of GH¢606,964, the outreach reflects efforts by the Foundation and its partners to promote preventive healthcare, improve access to screening, and encourage the early detection of diseases.

title: Alexander brothers sentenced to 30 years in federal sex trafficking case
body:
The jury found Alon, Oren and Tal Alexander guilty on all counts.
The Alexander brothers were each sentenced to 30 years in prison on Tuesday, after being found guilty on all counts in their federal sex trafficking trial in New York City.
The former real estate titans, Oren and Alon Alexander, 39-year-old twins, along with their brother, Tal Alexander, 40, were accused by prosecutors of a "decade-long sex trafficking and sexual abuse scheme."
The three brothers will have to participate in sex offender treatment programs in prison, the judge said. In addition to their prison terms, the brothers were each sentenced to 10 years of supervised release.
Oren and Alon Alexander were also ordered to pay $300,000 each in fines, and Tal Alexander was ordered to pay $350,000 in fines, as well as restitution, which will be determined by attorneys from both sides. Oren Alexander, who was also convicted of sexually exploiting a minor by distributing homemade child sex abuse material of a 17-year-old girl in 2009, was ordered to pay an additional $50,000 immediately.
Assistant U.S. Attorney Elizabeth Espinosa asked the judge for the maximum sentence -- life in prison -- for all three brothers, arguing that the government does not believe one is more culpable than the others in what prosecutors called an "immense" sex trafficking scheme.
"They spent years designing, executing, and perfecting their playbook of luring victims with promises of luxury, drugging victims so they could not resist, and then forcibly raping them," prosecutors wrote in a sentencing memorandum filed ahead of Tuesday's hearing. "The defendants carried out their playbook time and time again, drugging, raping, and assaulting dozens of victims. Over 70 women came forward with harrowing accounts of assault that stripped them of their dignity and autonomy."
Defense attorneys argued that the brothers should serve lighter sentences -- 15 years, the minimum for sex trafficking -- while maintaining their innocence.
"At no time did Alon, Oren or Tal rape or sexually assault another person. At no time did Alon, Oren or Tal entice, harbor, or maintain a woman to have commercial sex. At no time did Alon, Oren or Tal administer a drug or other substance to a woman against her will or without her knowledge. At no time did Oren intentionally make or distribute child pornography," defense attorneys wrote in their sentencing memorandum on behalf of the three brothers. "They are innocent of these charges, and they show honor and respect to our system of justice by vowing to fight for their innocence with all of their power for as long as is required, confident in the notion that one day they will be free to live out their lives with their children and families."
The brothers' friends and family members also submitted letters to Judge Valerie Caproni asking for leniency, describing their character and dedication to family.
The brothers addressed the court prior to learning their sentences during Tuesday's hearing in Manhattan, continuing to claim that they never sexually assaulted or drugged anybody.
Judge Caproni admonished the brothers for continuing to maintain their innocence.
"You did not have to stand up and say you’ve never raped anyone," Caproni said while handing down their sentences. "That's a lie and you know it."
A dozen women delivered victim impact statements during Tuesday's hearing, including six who testified during the federal trial.
Prosecutors thanked those who came forward in the case "to ensure that the defendants can no longer harm others."
"The defendants preyed on women and young girls, using drugs and violence to incapacitate them so they could rape them. The defendants did this for years --inflicting unspeakable harm on so many young women. And, for years, the defendants used their careers and social status to conceal the danger they posed," U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald said in a statement. "Today's sentence makes clear that this craven, sinister conduct is extraordinarily serious and will be met with serious punishment."
Throughout the five-week trial , 11 women testified that they were sexually assaulted by one or more of the brothers. At least eight of the women claimed they were drugged by one of the Alexanders.
The brothers denied sexually assaulting anyone or running a sex trafficking conspiracy, as prosecutors have charged. They pleaded not guilty. A spokesperson for the Alexander family called the verdict "deeply disappointing."
"We believe there are substantial problems with the evidence and the way this case was presented," the spokesperson, Juda S. Engelmayer, said in a statement following the jury's verdict in March. "The legal process does not end here. We will continue fighting every day until justice is done and the three brothers regain their freedom."
Oren and Tal Alexander gained notoriety in New York's luxury real estate market through their company, Alexander Group, and have been under federal investigation alongside Alon since late 2024.
They have been accused of luring women to nightclubs and parties, then drugging and sexually assaulting them.
In his closing statement during the spring trial, federal prosecutor Andrew Jones said there is "crushing evidence" that the brothers "masqueraded as party boys when really they were predators" who committed an "array of federal sex offenses."
Jones recounted the graphic accounts of the alleged victims and said the wealthy brothers had a "playbook" of luring women with exclusive parties, yachts and luxury travel so they could assault them.
During closing arguments, defense attorney Howard Srebnick conceded the brothers could be "obnoxious" and their conduct "inappropriate," but he told the jury, "Nobody was being assaulted, nobody had been trafficked."
