Choose a market, edit your brief, and click Find candidate pages . Three neighbourhoods mean three valyu.search() calls, requesting up to five results each. The SDK handles transport and may retry rate-limited requests. Returned results can overlap, and usage charges apply. Check current Search API pricing rather than assuming a fixed cost per app session. The app stores results in the current Streamlit session. Editing the review table or downloading the JSON doesn't make another search request. Clicking the search button starts a new search and replaces the current review, so download your work first if you want to keep it. London walkthrough: is £500 per week within a £2,200 budget? Choose London , enter your preferred neighbourhoods, and set a £2,200 monthly base-rent ceiling. Keep King's Cross and your cat's requirements in Other needs to check . That field stays visible during review; this version doesn't turn it into an automated commute or pet-policy filter. Open a candidate's source page. Check that you're looking at a particular flat rather than a search-results page or a room advertisement. Suppose the individual listing advertises £500 per week . This is an illustrative calculation, not a live rental offer. Monthly equivalent = weekly rent × 52 ÷ 12 = £500 × 52 ÷ 12 = £2,166.67 That is within the example base-rent limit. £500 × 4 = £2,000 would understate the monthly equivalent. In the review table, enter 500 under base rent and choose week . Before checking Fits brief , inspect the bedroom count, move-in date and lease, confirm the cat policy, and check the journey from the actual address using TfL's journey planner . “Near a station” isn't a door-to-door journey time. Include walking, transfers and the time you actually need to travel. Next action: if the flat fits, use the original listing to enquire about a viewing. If the cat policy is unclear, put the question in Notes and leave the fit confirmation unchecked until you have an answer. Outcome: the shortlist contains a source-linked candidate with a comparable rent and your review notes, rather than an attractive photograph you can't find again. San Francisco walkthrough: is the advertised rent the base rent? Switch to San Francisco and start a new search with a $3,200 monthly base-rent limit. Investigate the example areas or substitute your own. Keep your Embarcadero commute and pet-policy requirements visible in the brief. For a candidate building, open the actual unit and lease terms. A “starting at” price on a building page may refer to a different floor plan or unit. Consider this hypothetical offer: Monthly base rent: $3,200 Lease term: 12 months Concession: One month free Effective monthly average: $3,200 × 11 ÷ 12 = $2,933.33 The effective average is lower, but the base rent remains $3,200 . The payment schedule depends on the offer's terms. Enter the base rent in this tool, keep the concession in Notes, and separately check additional charges and any conditions attached to the offer. Compare like with like: monthly base rent in the same currency. Keep concessions, bills and other charges separate. Check the trip from the actual address with SFMTA's trip planner . Confirm that the advertised unit is available for your move-in date before checking Availability checked . Next action: contact the advertiser with the unit identifier, target move-in date and any outstanding questions about the lease or pet charges. Outcome: you can compare the unit against other candidates without quietly comparing one property's base rent to another property's promotional average. What belongs in the apartment shortlist? A useful apartment shortlist includes the source link, comparable rent, availability check and unresolved questions. In this app, a row enters the reviewed shortlist only when its normalized base rent is within the saved budget and all three review confirmations are checked. Field What to keep Source Original URL and returned source text Rent Advertised amount, currency and payment period Monthly comparison Weekly rent converted with 52 ÷ 12 , or the stated monthly amount Whole-unit check Confirmed for the specific listing, not inferred from the query Availability What you checked for the intended move-in date Fit Bedrooms, lease, commute and other requirements Notes Questions, concession terms, extra costs, and when and where you checked Discovery timestamp When the search result was retrieved, separate from source publication date Download research and review (JSON) saves all candidate pages, your edits, search receipts and the reviewed shortlist. Notes and confirmations are your review record; they aren't certifications from a rental platform. What should you add next? Choose the next feature based on the part of apartment hunting that still wastes your time: Too many broad pages? Add structured extraction for individual listing pages. Preserve the supporting text for each field and leave missing details unknown. Valyu Contents can help read known URLs where extraction is available. Seeing the same property on different websites? Add property-level matching using the full address and unit identifier. Keep uncertain matches separate. Commute is the deciding factor? Integrate a routing service and evaluate the actual address at a specified travel time. This example only records the requirement for manual review. Want to check again tomorrow? Persist the results and schedule another search. A newly discovered URL is a new search result, not necessarily a newly listed or newly available home. Search coverage can be incomplete, and some pages won't expose usable listing text. If reliable, comprehensive inventory is a product requirement, evaluate authorized listing feeds or partnerships alongside web discovery. Verification note: The supplied code uses the released Valyu Python SDK and was checked with synthetic SDK responses. Its serialized search requests were validated against the published contract with network transport mocked. The London and San Francisco budgets and offers are illustrative; this tutorial does not include a live, authenticated rental search or establish coverage of the selected websites. Frequently asked questions Can I build an apartment finder using a search API? Yes. Use a search API to discover public rental pages from a brief, keep their URLs and source text, then review individual listings. Numeric budget enforcement, price normalization and shortlist rules belong in your application. Search retrieval alone doesn't confirm availability or every rental requirement. Can the same rental search tool work in London and San Francisco? Yes. Separate the retrieval and review logic from market-specific settings. This example changes the country code, currency, rental vocabulary, source domains and neighbourhoods while reusing the same application. It compares candidates within each market; it doesn't convert GBP to USD. Does Search API return structured apartment inventory? This example uses web search results, not a dedicated property-inventory dataset. Results include source URLs and extracted content, and can describe individual listings, buildings or area pages. The app keeps those as candidate pages until you review a specific rental. How do I convert weekly rent to monthly rent? For a monthly comparison, multiply the weekly rent by 52 and divide by 12. For example, £500 per week is approximately £2,166.67 per month. Keep the original advertised payment period and check the listing's contractual rent; the conversion is a comparison calculation. Does a recent search result mean an apartment is still available? No. Retrieval time, publication date and availability are different facts. Open the original listing and confirm the unit and move-in date with the advertiser. The app leaves availability unchecked until you review it. Build something you would use during your own apartment search Start with one city, a few neighbourhoods and the requirements you actually care about. Use Search API to find candidate pages. Keep the source links. Put weekly and monthly rents on the same basis. Record the questions that still need answers. The useful end product is a shortlist that helps you decide which advertiser to contact next . Get a key at platform.valyu.ai , then follow the Search API quickstart to adapt the queries to your rental market. What's the detail you always end up checking manually when looking for a place: the commute, pet policy, bills, or something else?

title: Deploy your app to a VPS with Docker, Nginx, and SSL
body: Update VPS We will need a Debian/Ubuntu VPS. First, let's connect to our server. ssh root@server-ip-address # E.g., ssh root@1.2.3.4 And update the system. apt update && apt -y upgrade SSH-key login Now let's create a separate deploy user to run our app (using the root superuser is not the best idea). adduser deploy usermod -aG sudo deploy A more secure way to log in to a server is using an SSH key. Let's create one on the "local" machine. cd ~/.ssh ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f vps-key And copy it to the server (use brew install ssh-copy-id to install ssh-copy-id on Mac). ssh-copy-id -i vps-key deploy@server-ip-address Check that we can log in with the SSH key. ssh -i ~/.ssh/vps-key deploy@server-ip-address Next, let's disable root and password login. Open the config file: sudo nano /etc/ssh/sshd_config And set: PermitRootLogin no PasswordAuthentication no Save the config file and restart the service. sudo systemctl restart ssh Turn on Firewall (UFW) Only allow SSH, HTTP, and HTTPS. sudo apt -y install ufw sudo ufw default deny incoming sudo ufw default allow outgoing sudo ufw allow OpenSSH sudo ufw allow 80/tcp sudo ufw allow 443/tcp sudo ufw enable sudo ufw status Install Docker Use official Docker docs . Add the deploy user to the docker group. sudo usermod -aG docker $USER newgrp docker docker version Create App Docker Image Before we can run our app with Docker on the server, we need to "pack" it into a Docker image. Go to your project folder on your local machine, and create a Dockerfile . Search for a Dockerfile for your language/framework. For example, a Node.js app Dockerfile could look something like this . # syntax=docker/dockerfile:1 # Comments are provided throughout this file to help you get started. # If you need more help, visit the Dockerfile reference guide at # https://docs.docker.com/go/dockerfile-reference/ # This Dockerfile uses Docker Hardened Images (DHI) for enhanced security. # For more information, see https://docs.docker.com/dhi/ # Builder stage: install all dependencies and compile TypeScript. FROM dhi.io/node:24-alpine3.23-dev AS builder WORKDIR /app # Install dependencies as a separate step to take advantage of Docker's # caching. Leverage a cache mount to /root/.npm to speed up subsequent # builds. Leverage a bind mount to package.json to avoid having to copy # it into this layer. RUN --mount = type = cache,target = /root/.npm \ --mount = type = bind ,source = package.json,target = package.json \ npm install # Once you create a package-lock.json by running npm install locally, switch to npm ci and bind both files: # RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.npm \ # --mount=type=bind,source=package.json,target=package.json \ # --mount=type=bind,source=package-lock.json,target=package-lock.json \ # npm ci # Copy the source code into the container and compile TypeScript. COPY . . RUN npm run build # Deps stage: install production dependencies only. FROM dhi.io/node:24-alpine3.23-dev AS deps WORKDIR /app RUN --mount = type = cache,target = /root/.npm \ --mount = type = bind ,source = package.json,target = package.json \ npm install --omit = dev # Once you create a package-lock.json by running npm install locally, switch to npm ci and bind both files: # RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.npm \ # --mount=type=bind,source=package.json,target=package.json \ # --mount=type=bind,source=package-lock.json,target=package-lock.json \ # npm ci --omit=dev # Runner stage: minimal runtime image with compiled app and production deps. FROM dhi.io/node:24-alpine3.23 AS runner ENV PATH=/app/node_modules/.bin:$PATH WORKDIR /app COPY --from=deps --chown=node:node /app/node_modules ./node_modules COPY --from=builder --chown=node:node /app/dist ./dist # Expose the port that the application listens on. EXPOSE 3000 # Run the application. CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"] Now check that Docker is installed on your local machine, and build the app Docker image. docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 -t my-app:latest Notice the --platform linux/amd64 flag since we are building for our Linux server. GitHub Container Registry Great, we just created our app Docker image on our local machine. But how will we "copy" it to the server? With Docker, we can push and pull images to the "image registry". Let's use GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io). Create a GitHub token to be able to push Docker images to ghcr.io Log in to github.com . Click on the "Profile Icon" (the top right corner) -> select Settings . Then Credentials (on the left side) -> Personal access tokens (classic) (on the right side) Create a new token with: write:packages - push images read:packages - pull images delete:packages - optional Login to ghcr.io echo "your-github-token" | docker login ghcr.io -u your-github-username --password-stdin ⚠️ Change your-github-token and your-github-username to real values. Rebuild the Image We need to rebuild the app image using the proper image name. docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 -t ghcr.io/your-github-username/your-app-name:latest . ⚠️ Change your-github-username and your-app-name to real values. Push the Image docker push --all-tags ghcr.io/your-github-user-name/your-app-name Pull the Image on the VPS Log in to the server. ssh -i ~/.ssh/vps-key deploy@server-ip-address ` Log in to ghcr.io . echo "your-github-token" | docker login ghcr.io -u your-github-username --password-stdin docker pull ghcr.io/geshela/gesheru_bot:latest ⚠️ Change your-github-username and your-app-name to real values. Run the App docker run -d --name your-app-name --restart unless-stopped -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 ghcr.io/your-github-username/your-app-name ⚠️ Change your-github-username and your-app-name to real values. Check if the app container is running. docker ps docker logs -f --tail your-app-name P.S. To restart the app. docker stop your-app-name docker rm your-app-name docker run -d --name your-app-name --restart unless-stopped -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 ghcr.io/your-github-username/your-app-name Use Nginx as a Reverse Proxy Install Nginx. sudo apt -y install nginx sudo systemctl enable --now nginx Turn off the default config. sudo rm -f /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx Create a new config for the app. sudo nano /etc/nginx/sites-available/your-app-name ⚠️ Change your-app-domain.com to the real value. server { listen 80 ; server_name your-app-domain.com www.your-app-domain.com ; client_max_body_size 25m ; location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000 ; proxy_http_version 1.1 ; proxy_set_header Host $host ; proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr ; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for ; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme ; proxy_read_timeout 60s ; } } Let's enable the config. sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/your-app-name /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/your-app-name sudo nginx -t sudo systemctl reload nginx Set up the DNS A Record This is necessary so that the domain knows which IP address it should be linked to. Log in to your domain registrar's admin panel. Add the A record. Enter the IP address of your server. Add HTTPS with Let's Encrypt Install Certbot. sudo apt -y install certbot python3-certbot-nginx Create the certificate. sudo certbot --nginx -d your-app-domain.com -d www.your-app-domain.com That's it. The app is live now! 🥳 Credits Photo by Kevin Ache on Unsplash

title: Senate panel clears NGE president, 15 others for NHRC governing board
body:
The Senate Committee on Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters screened and cleared 16 nominees, including the President of the Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE), Eze Anaba, for appointment to the governing board of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) on Tuesday.
The committee, chaired by Adeniyi Adegbonmire (APC, Ondo Central), screened the nominees at the National Assembly about five months after President Bola Tinubu nominated them.
The committee nominated Salamatu Suleiman as chairperson-designate, while Anthony Ojukwu, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), was nominated to retain his position as executive secretary.
Other nominees are Maupe Ogun-Yusuf of Channels Television; Ayo Adewuyi of the Nigerian Television Authority; Chinonye Obiaku, SAN; Roseline Tasha; Ambassador Adam Yubak Baku; retired Assistant Controller-General of Corrections, Felix Lawrence; Edmund Chinonye; Oluwakemi Asiwaju Okere-Odo; Adedeji Ogunji; Kingsley Chidozie; Mohammed Adelodu; Francis Meshioye; Patience Patrick; and Hawwa Ibrahim.
The committee will present its report to the Senate plenary for consideration, after which lawmakers will decide on confirming the nominees.
During the screening exercise, lawmakers urged the nominees to demonstrate integrity, patriotism, and a strong commitment to the national interest as they discharge their responsibilities.
Peter Jiya (APC, Niger South) stressed that nominees should place the country’s interests above their personal convictions as they prepare to assume responsibilities in a public institution.
Mr Jiya expressed confidence that the commission could make meaningful contributions to human rights protection if its governing board approached its responsibilities with integrity and a strong sense of public service.
He also commended the nominees’ professional and personal qualities, urging them to balance their individual beliefs with the institutional obligations of their appointments.
The senator congratulated the nominees on their nominations and expressed optimism that they would contribute positively to the commission’s work.
The committee chair clarified that the NHRC governing board comprises 16 members, including representatives of the Federal Ministries of Justice, Interior and Foreign Affairs.
Mr Adegbonmire explained that the law did not subject the representatives of the three ministries to individual screening because it specifies the offices or ranks to be represented rather than the names of particular nominees.
“The law says there should be 16 members. Three of the members are nominees of the Federal Ministry of Justice, Interior, and Foreign Affairs. But because they are not specific as to persons, we don’t screen them,” he said.
Mr Anaba, also the editor of Vanguard Newspapers, said the nomination gave him an opportunity to sustain his commitment to human rights protection, which he described as integral to his journalism career.
The NGE president expressed satisfaction with the committee’s decision but cautioned against treating the screening clearance as final confirmation by the Senate.
“We’ve just been screened. We’ve just been confirmed. So don’t let us jump the gun. That’s number one. I’m happy to be approved at least by this screening committee. So until confirmation,” he said.
Explaining his background in human rights advocacy, Mr Anaba said his professional experience had consistently brought him into contact with issues relating to the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms.
“I’ve done this human rights thing all my life. It has gone together with my journalism job. So it’s going to be a continuation of what I’ve been doing,” he said.
Mr Anaba also said he had been involved in the NHRC’s activities before his nomination to its governing board.
He expressed optimism that the incoming board’s diverse professional expertise would improve the commission’s performance and strengthen its contribution to human rights protection in Nigeria.
“I’ve been part of Nigeria’s Human Rights Commission for a while, not at this level. But I can assure you that with the members we have in this council, Nigeria will benefit from a very good National Human Rights Commission,” he said.
The Senate’s consideration of the committee’s report will determine the next stage of the nominees’ confirmation process.

title: Continued pretraining vs fine-tuning: which do you need?
body: Use continued pretraining when the model lacks knowledge or vocabulary from your domain, and use fine-tuning when it knows enough but behaves wrong for your task. Nodus runs both from one managed runtime, nodus/sft , and in our October 2026 pilots it produced byte-identical weights to Modal at 42.5% lower charges for continued pretraining and 67% lower for fine-tuning. Most teams need fine-tuning only; continued pretraining pays off when you hold a large body of domain text the base model has rarely seen. What is the difference between continued pretraining and fine-tuning? The difference is the data and what the model learns from it. Continued pretraining keeps the original next-token objective and feeds the model raw, unlabeled text: contracts, papers, internal docs, a codebase. The model absorbs vocabulary, style and facts from that corpus. Fine-tuning trains on labeled examples: prompt and completion pairs, chat transcripts, or chosen and rejected answers for preference methods. It teaches the model how to respond, in what format, and when to refuse. What you want Method Data you need Domain vocabulary and facts Continued pretraining Raw text A fixed output format or tone Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) Prompt/completion pairs Better instruction following on your task SFT Chat examples Answers people prefer DPO, ORPO or KTO Chosen/rejected pairs or labels Start from the data you actually have: raw text points to pretraining, examples point to fine-tuning. When does continued pretraining pay off? It pays off when the base model keeps misreading your domain, not when it merely answers in the wrong shape. The strongest evidence is Gururangan et al., "Don't Stop Pretraining" (ACL 2020) . Across four domains (biomedical papers, computer science papers, news and reviews) and eight classification tasks, a second pretraining phase on in-domain text improved results in both high- and low-resource settings. Our decision rule has three checks: The base model mangles your terms, abbreviations or code conventions even with good prompts. You have far more raw domain text than labeled examples, typically hundreds of millions of tokens or more. The knowledge is stable. Facts that change weekly belong in retrieval, not in weights. If all three hold, continued pretraining is worth the compute. If only the first holds, try fine-tuning on a few thousand examples first and measure. Continued pretraining can also erode general skills, so keep a held-out general benchmark next to your domain test. Our post on catastrophic forgetting after fine-tuning shows how to measure that. When is fine-tuning enough? Fine-tuning is enough when the model already understands the material and you need consistent behavior. Typical cases are a JSON schema it must always follow, a support tone, a classification label set, or tool calls in your format. It needs much less data than people expect. Zhou et al. fine-tuned a 65B model on 1,000 curated examples in "LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment" and reported strong instruction following. Quality and coverage of the examples matter more than raw count. LoRA and QLoRA train a small adapter instead of every weight, which cuts memory enough to fit larger models on one GPU (see how much VRAM a 70B model needs ). How much more does continued pretraining cost? Cost grows with the tokens you train on, so continued pretraining usually costs tens of times more than fine-tuning. Here is the math for a 7B model, full-weight training on one NVIDIA H100, listed at $2.60/hr on the Nodus pricing page (price checked October 27, 2026). Training compute is roughly 6 x parameters x tokens floating-point operations, the standard estimate from Kaplan et al. (2020) . NVIDIA lists the H100 SXM at 1,979 BF16 teraFLOPS with sparsity , about 990 without it. We assume 40% utilization, so about 396 teraFLOPS of useful work. That utilization is an assumption, not a measurement; your real number depends on sequence length, kernels and batch size. Continued pretraining on 1 billion tokens: 6 x 7B x 1B = 4.2 x 10^19 FLOPs. At 396 teraFLOPS that is 106,000 seconds, about 29.5 hours, or about $77. Fine-tuning on 50,000 examples of about 500 tokens (25 million tokens): 1.05 x 10^18 FLOPs, about 0.74 hours, or about $1.92. The ratio is 40 to 1 because the token count is 40 to 1. Change the assumed utilization and both numbers move together, so the ratio holds. LoRA lowers the fine-tuning side further because frozen weights need no weight gradients or optimizer state. Same model, same GPU, same rate: the 40x gap comes entirely from tokens trained. How did Nodus compare with Modal on both jobs? We ran the same continued-pretraining and fine-tuning recipes on Nodus and on Modal with Qwen2.5-0.5B on one NVIDIA L4. In both pilots the exported weights matched byte for byte, so the only difference was the bill. Pilot Nodus charge Modal charge Nodus share of Modal Supervised fine-tuning $0.048696 $0.14746756 33.0% Continued pretraining $0.121164 $0.21090282 57.5% Recorded charges for successful attempts before credits, October 2026 pilots, one seed and one accepted run per platform. The pilots used standalone Nodus Jobs, not TrainingJobs. In the chart, Modal's charge is the 100.0% baseline. Identical weights in both pilots, so the lower charge bought the same model. Two caveats from those posts. The fine-tuning pilot also had one failed Nodus attempt; counting it, Nodus cost 24.7% less than Modal instead of 67%. And a 0.5B model on one L4 says nothing certain about a 70B run, so treat the ratio as evidence for this job size only. How do you run continued pretraining on Nodus? Use the nodus/sft runtime with task: Pretrain on the spec, and point it at a Volume of text rows. The default initialization: Continued starts from the model's existing weights, and method: Full trains every weight rather than an adapter. apiVersion : nodus.dev/v1beta1 kind : TrainingJob metadata : name : domain-pretrain spec : runtime : nodus/sft task : Pretrain model : uri : hf://Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B@c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca data : volume : domain-corpus path : corpus.jsonl format : JSONL parameters : steps : 5000 initialization : Continued method : Full packing : true appendEOS : false maxCostUSD : " 50.00" Set appendEOS: false when your rows are chunks or paragraphs rather than whole documents, so the trainer does not insert an end-of-sequence token after every row. Packing fills each training block with text instead of padding. Price it before it runs: $ pip install nodus-compute $ nodus login $ nodus apply -f pretrain.yaml --dry-run -o yaml $ nodus apply -f pretrain.yaml The dry run returns a cost estimate, and maxCostUSD stops the run at the cap. Long pretraining runs checkpoint with optimizer state, so a lost GPU resumes the run instead of restarting it. How do you run fine-tuning on Nodus? Same runtime, no task field, and a columns map onto your prompt and completion fields. The lora block makes it an adapter run; leave it out for full fine-tuning. apiVersion : nodus.dev/v1beta1 kind : TrainingJob metadata : name : support-sft spec : runtime : nodus/sft model : uri : hf://Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B@c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca data : volume : support-chats path : chats.jsonl format : JSONL columns : { prompt : question , completion : answer } parameters : steps : 2000 lora : { r : 16 , alpha : 32 } maxCostUSD : " 20.00" The Training (Beta) guide covers validation-based checkpoint selection and preference tuning. A model you trained earlier can be the input of the next TrainingJob, which is how you chain the two methods. Should you do both, and in what order? Do both only when you have both kinds of data, and always pretrain first. Gururangan et al. found that adapting to the task's own unlabeled text helped even after domain-adaptive pretraining, so the stages stack. A sequence that works: continued pretraining on the domain corpus, then SFT on labeled examples, then preference tuning if you have chosen and rejected answers. Each stage starts from the previous stage's exported model. Evaluate after every stage on the same held-out set, plus a general benchmark, so you can see which stage helped and which one cost you general skill. FAQ What is the difference between pretraining and fine-tuning? Pretraining teaches a model language and facts from huge amounts of raw text with a next-token objective. Fine-tuning adjusts an already pretrained model with labeled examples so it behaves a certain way. Continued pretraining sits between them: more raw-text pretraining, but on your domain. Can continued pretraining replace retrieval (RAG)? Not for facts that change. Weights are a snapshot, and retraining every time a document changes is slow and expensive. Teams often pretrain for vocabulary and reasoning style, then use retrieval for current facts. What learning rate should continued pretraining use? Lower than the original pretraining peak, with a warmup, because a high rate on a narrow corpus speeds up forgetting. Run a short sweep on a small slice and keep the setting whose held-out general score drops least. How do you know continued pretraining worked? Measure perplexity on held-out domain text before and after, then check a general benchmark for forgetting. In our continued-pretraining pilot, held-out perplexity fell 21.8%, from 21.0 to 16.4, on both Nodus and Modal. Which is cheaper on Nodus? Fine-tuning, by roughly the ratio of tokens trained. Both run at the same listed GPU rates on the pricing page , and the dry run shows the estimate before anything is charged. Originally published on the Nodus blog .

title: Israel's voter turnout soars as Netanyahu faces a tight election
body:
A video wall displays images of Benjamin Netanyahu with President Trump at a Likud party event before the release of the first exit poll results in Israel's general election, in Jerusalem, on Tuesday. David Goldman/AP hide caption
Israeli voters turned out in their highest numbers in more than two decades in a tense national election on Tuesday to decide whether to stick with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right coalition or change course.
Netanyahu was in a tight race with his top rival, Gadi Eisenkot, a center-right former military chief of staff, as exit polls appeared to swing slightly in one and then the other candidate's favor.
Still, the final vote tallies may take some time. And even when they're complete, if no bloc wins a majority, it could take days or weeks to decide who will be Israel's next prime minister, as party leaders try to assemble a governing coalition.
Israelis consider this one of their most consequential votes in history — the first parliamentary election since the October 2023 Hamas-led attack and the start of the wars in Gaza and elsewhere in the Middle East .
The Central Elections Committee said 77.7% of voters cast ballots as of 10 p.m. — calling it the highest turnout since 1999.
Enthusiasm was high among voters seeking to replace Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, with almost two decades in office across multiple tenures.
" Important is an underestimation, because it's much more than important. It's crucial," voter Naama Aaronsohn said of the election. "I'm worried. ... What's going to become of our country if there's not a major change?"
Another voter, Itamar Ariel, cast his ballot for Netanyahu. He said there are problems in Israel but no one can replace him. It's a matter of security for Israel.
But many Israelis question Netanyahu's ability to keep them safe after the deadly Oct. 7, 2023, attack. They have been reeling from reports that the government had repeated warnings from countries in the region that Hamas was planning a major assault on Israel.
Israel's subsequent wars in Gaza and the region, and its policies in the occupied West Bank, have badly strained its relations with many international governments, and public support for Israel in the United States has plummeted, worrying many Israeli voters.
Citizens in majority-Arab areas also took the opportunity to make their voices heard.
"This government it's not good for us and ... not good for anyone," said Nur Abu Na, a 30-year-old nurse. There are two predominantly Arab blocs in the elections.
Netanyahu voiced alarm throughout the day, in multiple social media posts , alerting followers to the high number of Arab citizens of Israel who were voting. He urged his right-wing supporters to get out and vote too.
Gadi Eisenkot, leader of Yashar party and former military chief of staff, delivers a speech at the party headquarters in Tel Aviv, Israel, following the release of exit polls after Tuesday's election. Nir Keidar/Anadolu via Getty Images hide caption
The early exit polls suggested Netanyahu's Likud Party won the most seats, with Eisenkot's Yashar party coming second. No party won a majority in the 120-seat parliament, known as the Knesset.
The final results will depend on the math and negotiations among broader alliances.
Opposition leaders quickly reacted to the preliminary results, saying they suggested voters dealt a blow to Netanyahu's coalition .
Shira Efron, an Israeli policy analyst at the Rand Corp. think tank, told NPR it was a "very good outcome for Eisenkot" and his recently formed party.
At an election party in Tel Aviv, Eisenkot's supporters cheered as the first exit polls were announced after voting closed at 10 p.m. local time.
""We made history! The public has voted for change," Eisenkot said in a speech.
But votes will continue to be counted on Wednesday, and the electoral map could shift. Eisenkot's bloc could lose, or have difficult political negotiations ahead if he is chosen to form a government.
"I'm anxious. Listen, the results are good, but they're complex. It takes time before we have a full picture," said opposition supporter Ophelie Namiech.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu gestures to his supporters at the election night rally after the first exit polls were announced Tuesday, in Jerusalem. Jalaa Marey/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
At the Likud election night party in Jerusalem, giant screens played Hollywood-style videos of soldiers marching, airstrikes blowing up buildings and other destruction. Some clips appeared to show massive explosions of villages in Lebanon, where Israeli destruction of civilian infrastructure has drawn condemnation from human rights groups as potential war crimes, which Netanyahu's government denies.
The videos also repeatedly showed President Trump shaking hands with and endorsing Netanyahu . The two leaders plan to potentially launch major attacks against Iran after the Israeli and U.S. midterm elections. Trump urged Israeli voters to reelect Netanyahu to "finish the job that we started."
Netanyahu's supporters were confident that their candidate, a master political survivor , would pull through.
" I've been here many times at different campaigns where at the first hour, that's what the exit polls show, and then you wait a little bit. And Prime Minister Netanyahu has had a knack of getting over the top when he needed it," said Netanyahu supporter Elie Pieprz.
He said in the end, he believes that Israelis will stand by their current leadership at a time of war.
"Right now we're in a war ... as unattractive as that may be to sound internationally, that's the reality," he said. "I think it is much more likely that they [Israeli voters] will understand that Prime Minister Netanyahu needs to lead this war against Iran, particularly with President Trump, and will come together because they, we need to have a certain amount of unity."
In the early hours of Wednesday, Netanyahu addressed supporters at the event. "Israel faces a singular historical opportunity, together with our partner President Trump, to remove the existential threat of Iran once and for all," he said .
Netanyahu celebrated that Likud was voted to be the largest party in the Knesset, and said the party awaited final results, but vowed to form "a strong right-wing, national government."
Daniel Estrin reported from Tel Aviv, Israel. Ruth Sherlock reported from Jerusalem. Samantha Balaban, Itay Stern, Shir David and Alon Avital contributed reporting in Israel.
NPR does not offer or accept money for coverage or interviews. Anyone who makes such an offer or request is not an NPR employee and does not represent NPR.

title: SEO AI Anxiety Is Rising. A Lean-Team GEO Playbook
body: AI is creating a capacity problem for many SEO professionals, not simply a job-security problem. In an SEOjobs.com survey of 279 respondents, 43.7% said they were more concerned about AI than a year earlier. The leading concerns were smaller teams, keeping up with AI, and tougher competition. That distinction matters for businesses and agencies planning their search strategy. A lean team cannot respond by pursuing every new AI-search tactic. It needs a repeatable way to improve how its core pages, products, services, and brand information can be understood across conventional search and AI-generated discovery. What the SEOjobs survey found SEOjobs' survey report collected 279 responses between October 6 and October 24, 2026. It was published on October 26 and updated on October 27. Respondents included in-house SEOs, agency professionals, consultants, owners, and people looking for work. The results show meaningful anxiety, but they also clarify what respondents see as the source of pressure. Of the 279 respondents, 92 people, or 33.0%, described themselves as very or extremely concerned about AI. The survey's question about change over the previous year drew an even clearer result: 122 respondents, or 43.7%, said they were more concerned. Reported concern Respondents Share of 279 respondents Smaller teams 127 45.5% Keeping up with AI 125 44.8% Tougher competition 123 44.1% Skills losing value 93 33.3% Pay or rates falling 84 30.1% Role elimination 68 24.4% This makes the survey more useful than a simple claim that AI will replace SEO roles. Smaller teams and the pace of change were more commonly cited worries than role elimination. The operational question is how to focus limited time on work that keeps a site understandable, reliable, and discoverable as search interfaces evolve. The survey is a signal, not an industry census SEOjobs notes important limitations. The survey used non-random sampling and was distributed through social media and email lists, so it is self-selected and not representative of the entire SEO profession. It also included 87 open-ended responses, which add context but do not turn the results into population-level estimates. The country results should be read with the same care. The United States supplied 154 responses, while the United Kingdom had 38, Canada 23, Germany 21, India 17, and Spain too few to chart. Germany's 21 respondents showed 71.4% both very or extremely concerned and more concerned than the year before, but that is a small country sample rather than evidence of a national industry rate. One notable segment was job seekers: 11 of 18 respondents, or 61.1%, said they were more concerned. This may reflect particular uncertainty for people seeking roles, but the small group means it should not be overgeneralized. Why this points to a focused GEO workflow Generative Engine Optimization, or GEO, is not a shortcut for earning an AI-generated answer or citation. AI systems can change their responses, sources, and presentation, and visibility in an answer does not itself establish clicks, leads, or revenue. For lean teams, however, GEO provides a useful prioritization lens. Its best practices overlap with durable SEO work: making important information easy to crawl, interpret, validate, and keep current. Rather than creating broad volumes of generic AI-focused content, teams can concentrate on the pages and signals most closely tied to their business. Start with the pages that carry commercial and informational weight Identify the limited set of pages that explain what the organization sells, whom it serves, where it operates, and why it is a credible choice . For a publisher, these may be cornerstone guides and author pages. For an ecommerce site, they may include category pages, product detail pages, policies, and support content. For a service business, they may be core service, location, and proof pages. These pages should provide direct answers to real questions while retaining the detail needed for a user to evaluate the offer. A page that is vague, outdated, or inconsistent with other parts of a site is difficult for search systems and AI systems to interpret confidently. Make entity and factual signals consistent Entity-based optimization means being explicit and consistent about the people, organization, products, places, and concepts a site represents. Lean teams can audit whether names, descriptions, dates, authorship, product attributes, service areas, and contact information align across their priority pages. Appropriate structured data can help express those relationships in machine-readable form. It should accurately reflect the visible page, not be treated as a way to manufacture rich results or AI visibility. Clear internal links and descriptive page architecture serve a similar purpose by showing how key topics and offerings relate. Build an update cycle before expanding production Keeping up with AI does not require rewriting every URL. A stronger operating model is to assign an owner, review cadence, and evidence standard to priority content. Update pages when a material fact changes, when search demand reveals a recurring unanswered question, or when the page no longer explains the topic clearly. This protects teams from the common trap of using AI to publish more content than they can verify and maintain. The capacity saved by avoiding low-value production can be used to improve accuracy, source quality, internal linking, and conversion paths on pages that matter. Separate visibility observations from business outcomes AI answer appearances, brand mentions, and citations can be useful observations, but they are not interchangeable with organic traffic or commercial performance. A practical scorecard should keep these measures separate: Indexing and technical accessibility for priority pages. Rankings, impressions, and clicks in conventional search reporting. Referral traffic and conversions where analytics can identify them. Changes in branded search demand and qualified leads, interpreted with care. Observed AI-answer or citation presence for a defined set of relevant queries. The goal is not to prove that every change produced a result. It is to create a consistent record of what was changed, what visibility signals moved, and whether measurable business outcomes followed . For teams feeling the capacity pressure reflected in the survey, create a GEO Search Leads account to begin assessing your website's GEO readiness and identify optimization opportunities around the pages that matter most. A structured baseline can help focus discussions on content clarity, entity signals, and technical accessibility instead of treating every AI-search development as an equally urgent project. Frequently Asked Questions What did the SEOjobs AI survey measure? The SEOjobs survey gathered 279 responses from SEO and search professionals between October 6 and October 24, 2026. It measured respondents' concern about AI, how that concern had changed over the prior year, and the pressures they associated with AI. What was the top AI concern among respondents? Smaller teams were the most commonly cited concern, selected by 127 of 279 respondents, or 45.5%. Keeping up with AI was close behind at 44.8%, followed by tougher competition at 44.1%. Does the survey prove that AI is reducing SEO jobs? No. The survey reports respondents' concerns, not verified employment outcomes. Role elimination was selected by 68 respondents, or 24.4%, while smaller teams, keeping up with AI, and competition were more frequently cited concerns. What should a lean SEO team prioritize for GEO? Prioritize accurate, useful core pages; consistent facts about the organization and its offerings; suitable structured data; clear internal relationships between topics; and a manageable content review cycle. Measure AI visibility observations separately from traffic, conversions, and other business outcomes. Conclusion The SEOjobs findings show that AI anxiety is closely tied to resourcing and competitive pressure. For lean teams, the constructive response is not to chase every new feature. It is to strengthen the accuracy, structure, accessibility, and measurement of the website assets most important to discovery and business performance.

title: Ashiru: I didn’t blame El-Rufai for insecurity
body: The Kaduna State gubernatorial candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Rt. Hon. Isa Mohammed Ashiru, has denied blaming the immediate past Governor of Kaduna State, Mallam Nasir Ahmad El-Rufai, for escalated insecurity in the state. In a statement which Abdulwaheed Olayinka Adubi, his Chief Press Secretary, issued on his behalf, Ashiru described the report as misleading and a misrepresentation of his position, stressing that his comments during a television interview had been misconstrued and presented in a manner that did not reflect what he actually said. He maintained that the report attributed to him did not accurately reflect his position on the former governor or the security challenges confronting the state. Ashiru expressed confidence that the necessary steps would be taken to ensure that the published report accurately reflected the content and context of the interview. He urged media organisations to ensure that reports of interviews and other public engagements accurately reflect the views expressed by those involved, noting that misleading reports can distort public understanding and undermine constructive democratic discourse. The ADC candidate reaffirmed his respect for the media and its critical role in promoting accountability, strengthening democracy and keeping citizens informed. He, however, called on media practitioners to uphold the highest standards of professionalism, accuracy and due diligence, especially when reporting politically sensitive issues.

title: Benjamin Larweh: Ghana’s cocoa farms must not become casualties of the gold rush
body: Ghana’s fight against illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, has reached a critical juncture. As the government explores ways to formalise eligible artisanal and small-scale miners, a fundamental principle must remain non-negotiable: no economic activity should be permitted to destroy the agricultural assets, livelihoods and ecosystems upon which the country’s long-term prosperity depends. The Ghana Cocoa Board Act, 2026 (Act 1182), provides an important legal foundation for defending one of Ghana’s most valuable agricultural resources. By according cocoa farms protected status and establishing safeguards against mining and other prohibited extractive activities, including a reported 500-metre restriction around protected farms, the law reinforces a principle that should guide national development: the pursuit of mineral wealth must not come at the expense of agricultural sustainability. The challenge now is to translate that principle into effective enforcement. Protecting more than cocoa trees Cocoa is far more than an export commodity. It sustains hundreds of thousands of farming households, supports rural economies and contributes to Ghana’s international economic standing. Behind every productive cocoa farm lies years of labour, investment and accumulated agricultural knowledge. When illegal mining destroys such a farm, the loss extends beyond uprooted trees. It can deprive families of their principal source of income, degrade productive soil, threaten water resources and undermine the economic prospects of future generations. The damage may also extend beyond the immediate mining site. Excavation, erosion, altered drainage and potential contamination can affect neighbouring farms and communities. For Ghana, therefore, protecting cocoa farms is not simply an agricultural responsibility. It is an economic, environmental and social imperative. Act 1182 must mean what it says The enactment of Act 1182 creates an opportunity to strengthen the protection of cocoa farms against destructive activities. Its effectiveness, however, will depend on the clarity of its implementation and the consistency with which the law is enforced. The reported 500-metre restriction is particularly significant because the risks associated with mining are not always confined to the precise location of excavation. Activities close to cocoa farms can compromise their productivity and threaten surrounding ecosystems. To make this protection effective, the relevant authorities must establish reliable farm maps, clearly identify protected areas and ensure that proposed mining sites are screened against applicable restrictions before authorisations are granted. The Ghana Cocoa Board, mining regulators, environmental authorities, land administration institutions and local government must work together to prevent conflicting decisions and close enforcement gaps. A protected farm must not exist only on paper. Its protection must be visible in the security of the farmer, the integrity of the land and the continued productivity of the crop. Formalisation is not a licence to break the law Recent public debate surrounding comments by Ghana Gold Board Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi has renewed attention to the government’s approach to unlicensed mining. There is a legitimate case for formalising eligible artisanal miners. Proper licensing, registration, environmental standards and regulatory oversight can improve accountability, support livelihoods and help move mining into the lawful economy. But formalisation must never be confused with permission to mine wherever an operator chooses. An unlicensed operation does not become lawful simply because it is economically beneficial or located outside a forest reserve or water body. Its eligibility for formalisation must be assessed under the applicable legal framework, including restrictions governing protected cocoa farms. A miner who qualifies for formalisation must still comply with every applicable law governing where mining may take place. This distinction is essential. Formalisation should create a pathway towards lawful mining, not an avenue for circumventing environmental safeguards or statutory prohibitions. Where mining is prohibited to protect cocoa farms, no administrative arrangement or economic justification should be used to override that restriction. The objective is not to demonise miners or dismiss the economic pressures facing mining communities. It is to ensure that legitimate economic opportunities are pursued within the law and without transferring unacceptable costs to farmers and the wider public. From legislation to enforcement Three priorities should guide implementation. First, with the already existing Cocoa Management System (CMS), Ghana can develop an authoritative, georeferenced register of protected cocoa farms to help regulators identify prohibited areas and verify compliance with the prescribed buffer. Second, enforcement must be consistent and evidence-based. Those responsible for illegal mining should be investigated and held accountable in accordance with the law, regardless of their political connections, financial influence or position in society. Third, COCOBOD can further strengthen the economic viability of cocoa farming through improved access to agricultural inputs, extension services, farm rehabilitation and effective support for farmers. Protecting cocoa farms requires both enforcement against unlawful destruction and sustained investment in the livelihoods that make farming worthwhile. These measures should complement a transparent formalisation programme that directs eligible miners towards lawful sites and requires compliance with environmental and licensing obligations. A national interest beyond partisan politics The protection of cocoa farms should not become another casualty of political disagreement. The government’s anti-galamsey policy must be assessed against clear standards: compliance with the law, effective environmental protection and measurable results for affected communities. Ghana must demonstrate that its commitment to responsible mining is compatible with its responsibility to protect agriculture. It must also assure international cocoa buyers, processors and development partners that the country is serious about safeguarding the land and communities that sustain its cocoa industry. The choice is not between gold and cocoa. It is between a development model that respects the limits of lawful economic activity and one that allows immediate commercial gains to undermine long-term national prosperity. Act 1182 provides an important foundation. The real test lies in its implementation. Ghana’s cocoa farms represent generations of investment and a vital source of rural livelihoods. Their destruction in the pursuit of gold would impose costs far greater than the value of the minerals recovered. The gold beneath Ghana’s soil may be valuable, but it must never become an excuse to destroy the cocoa farms that help sustain the nation.

title: GhostShell: A Haunted Terminal Powered by Open-Source AI 👻
body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine . What I Built Meet GhostShell , a haunted terminal assistant that brings a little supernatural personality to everyday software development. What if your terminal could talk back? What if, after running a command, your computer responded like an ancient digital spirit that had been trapped inside your repository for years? GhostShell combines a spooky terminal experience with a locally running open-weight language model. It can react to developer commands, comment on Git activity, and explain errors while staying in character as a mysterious AI haunting your machine. Instead of connecting to a proprietary AI API, GhostShell uses a model running locally on the developer's computer. The result is a small experiment in making local AI both useful and fun. The interaction above is an illustrative example. Code The project includes the terminal interface, AI inference layer, personality configuration, and command-processing logic. How I Built It GhostShell is built around local AI inference. The initial stack consists of: Python: Core application and terminal interaction. Ollama: Runs the language model locally. Qwen2.5 3B: An open-weight model used for generating responses, subject to its model license. Rich: Provides formatted terminal output. Git: Supplies real repository context for development-related interactions. The application collects the relevant command and output, constructs a prompt, and passes it to the locally running model. The generated response is then displayed in the terminal. The model's personality is controlled through a system prompt, allowing it to behave like a spooky digital entity without sacrificing its usefulness as a coding assistant. Why Does Open Innovation Matter? For GhostShell, open innovation is not just a technology choice. It changes where the application runs, where its data goes, and how much control its users have. 1. Local inference and privacy Terminal output can contain sensitive paths, environment details, and other information developers may not want to send to an external service. Running the model locally gives users more control over their development data. 2. Offline capability After the model and required dependencies have been downloaded, GhostShell can generate responses without requiring an internet connection. That means the experience doesn't have to disappear when the network does. 3. Freedom to experiment The model is not permanently tied to one hosted AI provider. Developers can experiment with compatible models, change prompts, adjust the personality, and modify the inference pipeline. 4. Lower running costs Local inference avoids per-request API charges. The trade-off is that users supply their own computing resources, and running a model still consumes electricity. For a small developer tool, that trade-off can be worthwhile. Open innovation makes GhostShell something developers can inspect, modify, and extend rather than simply consume as a hosted service. My Agent Session The Spirit of It Halloween is usually associated with ghosts, haunted houses, and things hiding in the dark. For developers, there are other kinds of ghosts. Abandoned repositories. Forgotten commits. Dependencies that nobody remembers adding. Bugs that return just when everything seems to be working. GhostShell gives those familiar experiences a playful personality. But beneath the horror aesthetic is a practical idea: AI does not always need to live in a remote service. Sometimes, it can live right on your own machine, where you can inspect it, experiment with it, and decide how it behaves. The machine isn't haunted. It just finally has something to say. Prize Categories Built with Python, local inference, and a little Halloween spirit. 👻

title: What I learned integrating 25 review platforms into one API
body: Every review platform looks the same from the outside: a star rating, a text, an author, maybe a reply. Getting at that data looks nothing alike. I spent the last months building Prisma Reviews , a single REST API for reviews, and these are the notes I wish I'd had on day one. 1. There are four kinds of "review API" Once you've done a few platforms, every one falls into one of four kinds: Kind Examples How you connect Can you reply? OAuth, business-owner API Google Business Profile, Trustpilot The owner approves your app Yes Keys from a developer console App Store Connect, Google Play The owner creates a key and gives it to you Yes Shop-app tokens Judge.me, Trusted Shops, eKomi, Okendo An API token from the platform's admin Sometimes No owner API at all Yelp, Tripadvisor, Booking.com Only the public listing URL No: link to the platform Each kind needs its own onboarding UI, its own error handling and its own way to refresh credentials. If you design for only one, the next one won't fit. 2. Access is the real bottleneck, not code The code for a connector is usually a day or two. Getting permission takes far longer: Google Business Profile needs an access application. It's reviewed by hand, and the default quota is very low until you're approved. Trustpilot sells API access as a paid add-on to the business, not to you. eBay and Etsy need a developer app per integrator, with their own review of your use case. Apple and Google Play are the easy ones: the owner creates a key in their console (an App Store Connect .p8 key, a Play service account) and you can start right away. The lesson: ship the platforms with self-serve keys first, apply for the gated ones on day one, and be honest in your UI about which ones are still waiting. 3. Normalise early, and keep the original Every platform has its own field names ( starRating: "FOUR" , rating: 4 , stars: "4.0" ), dates (ISO, Unix seconds, "2026-10-19 12:41:07 +00:00" ) and ideas of what an "author" is. We map everything into one shape: { "id" : "rev_01KJ8Q2M4T7HX3VB9CWD6NRZ5E" , "platform" : "app_store" , "rating" : 4 , "title" : "Great, one bug" , "text" : "Love the app, the widget crashes on iOS 19." , "author" : "marta_g" , "language" : "en" , "created_at" : "2026-10-19T12:41:07.000Z" , "reply" : { "text" : "Thanks! Fixed in 3.2." , "status" : "published" } } Two rules that saved us later: Ratings are integers 1–5 or null . Some platforms allow reviews with no rating, so a missing rating is null , never 0 . Prefer the original text over the translation. Several sources auto-translate reviews to the reader's language. Store what the customer actually wrote and its language. 4. Polling is fine if you're honest about cost Most platforms have no webhooks, so you poll. That's fine for official APIs, where calls are free and rate limits are generous. It's not fine when every read costs you money (scraped sources charge per review). What worked for us: Poll official APIs often (every 15–60 minutes). Poll paid sources rarely (every 6–24 hours), always ask for "newest first", and stop at the first review you've already seen. Reserve a budget before every paid job and cap the job at that budget, so a bug can't spend a month's margin in an hour. Expose one webhook ( review.created , review.updated ) to your users, whatever the platform does underneath. 5. Replies are a queue, not a request Publishing a reply can take seconds (Apple), fail because the review was deleted, or be rate-limited. So POST /reviews/{id}/reply returns at once with status: "queued" , a worker publishes it, and a reply.published or reply.failed webhook tells you how it went. Idempotency keys stop a retry from posting the same reply twice, and a customer reading the review a second later sees a queued reply instead of none. 6. Make it testable without a real account The biggest friction for a developer trying a reviews API is "I need a real business with real reviews first". Test keys ( pk_test_… ) that return realistic sample data for every platform let someone build the whole integration before connecting anything real. They're also what we use in our own test suite. 7. Agents are users too A surprising share of our early traffic was AI agents reading docs. Three cheap things helped: Every docs page is also available as Markdown (add .md to the URL), and there's an llms.txt file. GET /v1/platforms returns, for each platform, which fields to send, the steps the owner follows and an example body. An agent can connect a platform without reading the docs. Error responses include required_fields and an example , so the next request can fix itself. Wrapping up If you're integrating reviews from more than two platforms, the time goes into access, normalisation and cost control, not HTTP calls. That's the work we packaged into Prisma Reviews . It's free for 2 locations, with test keys for every platform. If you'd rather build it yourself, I hope the notes above save you a few weeks. Questions about a specific platform's API? Ask in the comments. I've probably hit the same wall.

title: Early third-quarter earnings show a 'resilient' U.S. consumer, with signs of strain
body:
One word keeps appearing in third-quarter earnings reports: "resilient."
That's the early read on U.S. consumers from various companies that released their results this week. Many businesses say Americans are still spending despite inflationary pressures, though not every company has enjoyed the same success.
The commentary comes amid fears that diesel fuel prices, which hit an all-time high of $6.52 per gallon in September, would drive up prices on consumer products . Economists also worried that more expensive regular gas, combined with high borrowing costs and continued tension between the U.S. and Iran, would spur a pullback in consumer spending.
Retail sales rose 0.8% in September, following a jump of 1.3% in August. Sales in September were boosted by rising gas station spending. Despite all those challenges, some corporate executives say the headwinds aren't yet affecting sales.
"There's been a lot of noise in the market this year. There's a lot of geopolitical stuff," Royal Caribbean Chairman and CEO Jason Liberty said on the company's earnings call on Tuesday. "But I look at our business [and our results], and I think that really talks to the resilience of the business, the resilience of the consumer."
Royal Caribbean reported an increase in bookings during its third quarter, while Sherwin-Williams' CEO said the quarter was evidence of the company's strength.
Here's how companies are reading the consumer in the most recent three-month period:
The food and beverage company beat analysts' expectations for third-quarter earnings and revenue despite what CEO Henrique Braun called an "uneven environment."
Coca-Cola reported that North America unit case volume was flat, indicating demand was steady in the face of higher prices. The company's overall unit case volume was helped by higher demand outside of North America.
"The underlying momentum remains quite strong," Chief Financial Officer John Murphy told CNBC. "Consumer sentiment is largely unchanged in the sense that, wherever you are on the income scale, you're looking for value, and I think our system here has done a good job interpreting that."
The company increased its full-year forecast and now expects its comparable earnings per share to grow at least 11%, up from a prior forecast of growth between 9% and 10%.
The cruise company beat Wall Street's expectations for earnings per share and narrowly missed on revenue.
"Our third quarter results reflect continued strong consumer demand for our vacation experiences and the accelerated momentum across our industry leading brands," CEO Liberty said in the release .
The company reported that the number of guests served in the third quarter increased 9% year over year to 2.7 million vacationers and said booking volumes for 2027 were already "up in the high teens," pacing ahead of historical levels and indicating high travel demand.
"It's not that we don't see points of challenges, but really what we've seen is that even in those points of challenges, the consumer comes roaring back as relates to the vacation experiences," Liberty told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" following the report.
Royal Caribbean shares closed up more than 5% on Tuesday.
Sherwin-Williams beat analysts' expectations for revenue but fell short of expected earnings per share.
Sherwin-Williams CEO Heidi Petz said in the company's earnings release that the paint retailer's performance demonstrated "the resilience of our Company and the strength of our strategy in a challenging demand environment."
"Despite muted underlying market volumes, we continued to win new customers, increase share-of-wallet and deliver sales growth across all three reportable segments," she said.
Net sales increased 7.9% from the same period last year. The company attributed the gain to higher selling prices, but the benefits to profits were partially offset by increased costs of raw materials and supply-chain related expenses.
And the company maintained full-year guidance, saying "customer sentiment and the leading indicators we track point to muted demand over the remainder of the year and into 2027."
UPS beat Wall Street expectations for both earnings per share and revenue in the third quarter.
Revenue in the U.S. rose 4.5% during the period to $14.86 billion.
CEO Carol Tomé told investors on the company's earnings call that consumers remain "resilient" ahead of the holiday season, the company's busiest period. She said the company expects that average daily shipping volume will grow next quarter at a rate consistent with last year. However, fourth-quarter domestic average daily volume will likely fall due to reducing deliveries with Amazon, she said.
UPS has been in the midst of unwinding its partnership with Amazon at the same time it's executing a broad turnaround effort to operate more leanly.
The company raised its full-year forecast for the second quarter in a row, projecting consolidated revenue of approximately $92.6 billion, up from its previous expectations of $91.2 billion.
Shares closed up more than 5% on Tuesday.
Not every company is seeing the same spending trends, however.
Appliance maker Whirlpool missed on both the top and bottom lines for its third quarter and cut its full-year revenue guidance.
Net sales in North America fell more than 8% year over year during the period ending on Sept. 30.
Even still, the company cited its own read on "resilience."
"Through disciplined working capital management, we are protecting our year end free cash flow and our balance sheet resilience to navigate challenging market conditions," CFO Roxanne Warner said in the earnings release .
Shares closed up more than 3% on Tuesday.
— CNBC's Amelia Lucas and Laya Neelakandan contributed to this report.

title: Robinhood Misses Q3 Earnings as Crypto Revenue Rises and Prediction Market Bets Grow
body:
Robinhood, the trading app where more than 28 million people keep money to buy stocks and crypto and now bet on sports and elections, reported third-quarter revenue of $1.42 billion billion on Tuesday, missing the roughly $1.43 billion Wall Street expected
Earnings came in at $0.51 per share, missing the $0.55 analysts projected and down from $0.61 a year ago. Earnings per share is profit divided by the number of shares outstanding, and it is the figure investors use to call a quarter a beat or a miss.
Robinhood is the app that brought commission-free trading to a generation of first-time investors, which makes its quarterly report one of the clearest readings of what ordinary people are doing with their money. When customers trade more, deposit more or pile into new products, the shift shows up in these numbers.
Net income was $476 million, down 14% from $556 million a year earlier and 17% from $573 million in the second quarter. The quarter included a $67 million unrealized loss, meaning a drop in value on paper, on Robinhood Ventures Fund I, which cost $0.07 per share. Adjusted earnings per share, which exclude certain items, came to $0.60, down 3% from a year ago.
Event contracts, the yes-or-no bets that pay out $1 if a game, an election or an economic report goes a certain way, brought in $173 million, up from $156 million in the second quarter, when they overtook crypto revenue for the first time. Customers traded a record 16.4 billion of them, more than seven times a year earlier.
“I believe we’re at the very beginning of a prediction market supercycle,” CEO Vlad Tenev said in December last year, when Robinhood added NFL player contracts and parlay-style combos that pay only if every outcome hits.
Crypto trading revenue rose to $120 million from $100 million in the second quarter, but remained down 55% from the $268 million Robinhood earned in the third quarter of 2025. Customers traded $50 billion in crypto during the quarter, down 38% from a year earlier, with $21 billion on the Robinhood app and $29 billion through Bitstamp, the crypto exchange it acquired
Robinhood Chain went live on July 1 as a layer-2 network, meaning a blockchain that runs on top of Ethereum to make transactions cheaper and faster. Its first weeks were driven by meme coins , joke-themed tokens, rather than the tokenized stocks it was built for, which are digital versions of company shares that trade on a blockchain.
By the end of August the chain had earned about $3.13 million in fees over 30 days, more than Ethereum and Base , which came in at $2.47 million and $2.89 million.
Hours before the report, Robinhood announced a deal with Ripple that brings RLUSD, a stablecoin (a crypto token designed to stay worth one dollar), to Robinhood Chain and Bitstamp, with an in-app rollout planned later this year. RLUSD has a market value above $2.5 billion, and Ripple will also supply Robinhood’s treasury software and lending for Bitstamp traders.
Robinhood shares closed Tuesday at about $94.61 and slipped in after-hours trading- The stock is down roughly 18% this year and about 37% below its 52-week high of $150.47.
Robinhood narrowed its 2026 outlook for adjusted operating expenses and stock-based pay to $2.675 billion to $2.75 billion, trimming the top of the $2.675 billion to $2.775 billion range it set in July.

title: Halifax council puts off decision on bike network alternatives
body:
Halifax Regional Council has deferred action on alternatives to the all ages and abilities (AAA) bike network because councillors say they want to gather more feedback on the proposed plans.
Cycling advocates say they appreciate this step but the mayor is concerned the decision will only create more delays and increase costs.
“Those committees open the door to redesign, which opened the door to increase costs, which open the doors to delay,” said Mayor Andy Fillmore.
“Today, we had a clear path to get that section down and to help to complete the bike network. And we stepped off that path into a bit of a swirl.”
The deferral was based on a motion put forth by Coun. Sean Cleary at Tuesday’s regional council meeting.
The motion called for the two transportation committees to hear a report on alternatives to the network before council decides on a direction. Staff completed the report after Coun. Tony Mancini and Mayor Fillmore asked them to consider alternative routes to save money.
“I cannot imagine we can make an informed decision on any of these without feedback from the people who are actually going to be using it,” said Cleary.
The network would consist of protected bike lanes, multi-use pathways and local street bikeways as part of the municipality’s Integrated Mobility Plan. AAA design guidelines focus on safe infrastructure for riders of all ages, and use physical separation from motor vehicles, as well as traffic calming methods.
As of this past January, the project is expected to cost $85 million . The project was initially pegged at $25 million.
Staff have identified seven alternative routes in the report, but noted that while the alternatives may reduce costs, they likely won’t accommodate all ages and abilities.
“I have a real problem with that because the whole point of the minimum grid and expanding our protected cycling infrastructure, and other active transportation infrastructure, is to achieve a mode shift to more sustainable modes of transportation,” said Cleary.
Cyclists were in council chambers Tuesday to silently protest the report and the suggested alternatives.
“We need to get it built properly because we know if you build it improperly, they’ll use that as an argument not to improve it,” said Halifax Cycling Coalition Chair David Trueman.
Trueman adds that cyclists don’t need raised or separated lanes necessarily, but that lanes on roads with concrete dividers are sufficient.
“We don’t need the most expensive options. We just need adequate safe options,” he said.
Since work isn’t expected until 2028, reviewing the report in the committees is not expected to delay the project.

title: Sokoto Assembly okays establishment of state police
body: The Sokoto State House of Assembly unanimously adopted the Sixth Alteration Bill, which seeks to provide a constitutional framework for establishing state police services in Nigeria. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the Deputy Majority Leader of the House, Mustapha Abdullahi (APC-Sokoto South II), moved the motionduring plenary in Sokoto on Tuesday. Presenting the bill, Abdullahi said it sought to amend the 1999 Constitution, as altered, to establish state police services while retaining the Nigeria Police Force as the federal police service. He said the executive transmitted the bill, the Senate considered it on June 24, the House of Representatives on July 23, andthe Sokoto Assembly on September 22. According to him, the proposed framework will delineate the responsibilities of federal and state police services to ensure effective policing and address security challenges across the country. He explained that the federal police would handle interstate and international crimes, terrorism, cybercrime, border security, policing of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) and protection of federal assets. “Conversely, state police services would be responsible for law enforcement, maintenance of public order and safety, protection of lives and property, and investigation of local crimes. “Therefore, the federal police and state police will function side-by-side in every state,” Abdullahi said. The lawmaker added that the federal police could intervene in state policing matters at the request of a state governor or where there was a breakdown of law and order that the state police could not contain. He said the head of a state police service would be known as the State Commander of Police and appointed by the governor on the recommendation of the National Police Council, subject to confirmation by the State House of Assembly. Abdullahi further explained that the bill proposed the establishment of a State Police Service Commission as an executive body responsible for the appointment, promotion and discipline of state police personnel, except the State Commander. On funding, the lawmaker said the proposed framework would provide for the State Police Service Commission to receive funds directly from the state’s Consolidated Revenue Fund to ensure financial autonomy. He added that the Nigeria Police Force would continue to operate in every state until the state’s police service commenced operations. Abdullahi cited Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which provides that a constitutional alteration must be approved by resolutions of the houses of assembly of not less than two-thirds of all the states. Contributing to the debate, several lawmakers supported the bill, describing state policing as a necessary measure to address the security challenges confronting states across the country. The Speaker, Alhaji Tukur Bala, who presided over the plenary, subsequently put the motion to a voice vote and the lawmakers unanimously adopted it. The post Sokoto Assembly okays establishment of state police appeared first on Vanguard News .
