title: Yealink: 110,802 titles against 35,421 fingerprints, and the provisioning file behind both
body: Yealink: 110,802 titles against 35,421 fingerprints, and the provisioning file behind both Two ZoomEye queries were run against the same corpus on 28 October 2026. title="Yealink" returned 110,802 matches. app="Yealink" returned 35,421. The gap is about three to one, and it says something about how desk phones announce themselves. Yealink builds IP desk phones, conference units and Teams-certified video devices. Those devices sit on the same access VLAN as laptops, they hold a SIP registration and, in most deployments, they fetch their entire configuration from a server on every boot. What the two queries select title="Yealink" matches the HTML title of the device web interface. Almost every desk phone ships with a local admin page, and most leave it enabled because the installer needs it once. That page is what the title query finds: a device that answers HTTPS (or plain HTTP) with a login form. app="Yealink" matches protocol-level product recognition rather than the page title. The number is smaller because a device behind a reverse proxy, a device with the web server disabled, and a device whose page was rewritten by a custom template will not match. Both counts refer to the same product family; neither is a count of exposed phones in total. The three-to-one ratio is the useful part. Roughly two-thirds of the hosts that present a Yealink page are not being classified as Yealink at the application layer. For an asset inventory that depends on fingerprints, that two-thirds is invisible. Provisioning is the interface that matters A Yealink phone does very little out of the box. On boot it looks for a provisioning server, typically over HTTPS, and downloads a configuration tree: network settings, SIP accounts, line keys, firmware references, and sometimes a phonebook. The location is set by DHCP option 66, by a redirection service keyed on the device MAC, or by hand. Three consequences follow. The provisioning server configures everything, including trust. If the certificate on that server is not validated, an attacker on the path can hand the phone a config with their own SIP registrar. Whether validation happens is a device setting, and on older firmware it is often a checkbox that ships unchecked. The MAC address is the credential. Redirection services identify a device by its MAC rather than by a secret. A MAC is visible on the local segment and, in some deployments, in the web interface itself. The local admin page is a configuration editor. Default credentials on these devices are documented and widely unchanged. Once authenticated, the page can read the SIP password, the provisioning URL, and the phonebook, and it can point the device at a different server. A work list that starts with your own inventory Query your own ranges, not the internet: title="Yealink" && ip="10.0.0.0/8" in ZoomEye, or the equivalent in your scanner. The 110,802 figure is context; your phones are the task. On each phone, confirm the admin password is not the factory value. This is a manual or scripted check, and it is the single highest-value item on the list. Confirm the provisioning URL uses HTTPS and that the device validates the certificate. Where the platform supports it, pin the provisioning host. Disable the web interface where the platform allows it after provisioning, or restrict it to a management VLAN. Treat a phone as a credential holder: the SIP account on it can place calls, and on many systems that account can also read voicemail. Put phones on their own VLAN with an explicit rule set toward the call server and the provisioning server, and nothing else. Why the number is not the finding A desk phone with a login page is not a vulnerability. It is a device doing what its manual describes. The finding is the combination: a page that is reachable from a network segment with more hosts on it than the phone expects, a factory password, and a provisioning channel that can redirect the device to a different server without the phone noticing. The 110,802 and 35,421 counts describe how much of the voice estate is visible to a title-based query versus an application-based one. The number an organisation should care about is how many of its own phones still accept the password printed in the box. Sources ZoomEye AI SDK queries title="Yealink" (110,802 matches) and app="Yealink" (35,421 matches), page size 1, sub_type all, executed 28 October 2026 Beijing time. Yealink device administration documentation covering auto-provisioning, DHCP option 66 and the local web interface.

title: GPT-6.1 Terra is GA in GitHub Copilot: what engineers should know
body: GitHub has made GPT-6.1 Terra, a new OpenAI model, generally available in Copilot. The announcement is short, but it points to a trend worth noticing: model choice inside coding assistants is becoming a cost-and-fit decision rather than a "pick the biggest one" decision. Here is what GitHub has said, what it hasn't, and how I'd evaluate it. What happened On 26 October 2026, GitHub announced through its changelog, X and LinkedIn that GPT-6.1 Terra, from OpenAI, is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. According to GitHub, the model is aimed at everyday agentic coding and terminal work, and it costs less than GPT-6.1 Sol, another model in the same family. GitHub says you can use it in the Copilot app, the Copilot CLI and Visual Studio Code. GitHub also shared a few observations from its early testing: GPT-6.1 Terra solved noticeably more terminal and C# coding tasks than GPT-5.6 Terra. It tends to work in focused, consolidated steps when the task is well-scoped. The sources I reviewed do not include benchmark scores, task counts, the evaluation methodology, pricing figures, premium request multipliers, context window sizes or a breakdown of which Copilot plans get access. I won't guess at any of those. The changelog excerpt I saw was also truncated, so there may be more detail on the original page. Why it matters It is a cost tier, not just a new version. GitHub frames Terra as the lower-cost option next to Sol. If you use Copilot heavily, especially in agentic or CLI workflows where a single task can trigger many model calls, the price difference between models adds up. A cheaper model that handles routine work well is useful. The details of how the cost differs matter, and they aren't in the announcement. The reported gains are in specific areas. GitHub names terminal tasks and C#. That is a narrow claim, and it is more useful than a vague "better at coding". If your daily work is shell scripting, build tooling, CI debugging or .NET services, those are the areas where GitHub says it saw improvement over GPT-5.6 Terra. If you work mostly in other languages, the announcement tells you nothing either way. "Focused, consolidated steps" is a behavioral claim. Agentic tools can be tiring when the model takes many small steps, rewrites files it didn't need to touch, or wanders off the task. GitHub's description suggests Terra tries to do less, more deliberately, on tasks with clear boundaries. The qualifier matters: "well-scoped". The description doesn't say how it handles vague, large or cross-cutting work, and that is where you would likely still consider Sol or a different approach. That part is my inference, not something GitHub claims. These are vendor-run early tests. GitHub ships Copilot and has an interest in presenting its model lineup well. That doesn't make the results wrong, but a statement like "solved noticeably more tasks" without numbers can't be compared against your own experience. Your repository, your test suite and your conventions are the real benchmark. What you should do There is nothing to patch here and no security angle. This is an evaluate-and-decide item. Find it. Check the model picker in the Copilot app, CLI or VS Code. If your organization manages Copilot centrally and you don't see it, check with your admins whether model access needs to be enabled. The sources don't describe the rollout for managed plans, so confirm that locally. Run a small, honest comparison. Pick five to ten recent tasks from your own backlog, ideally a mix of terminal-heavy chores and C# changes if that's your stack. Run them with Terra and with whichever model you use now. Compare: whether the result passes your tests on the first try how many iterations or corrections it needed how large and how clean the diff is how much of your usage quota or budget it used Write tighter tasks. Since GitHub highlights well-scoped work, give the model a clear goal, the relevant files, the constraints and a definition of done. This tends to help with any model, and it costs you little. Route by task, not by habit. If Terra holds up on routine work, you can reserve Sol for harder, more open-ended problems. That only makes sense if your own tests show a real difference, so measure before you change team defaults. Keep normal review discipline. Agentic output still needs code review, tests and a look at what commands it ran in your terminal, especially for anything that touches infrastructure, credentials or deployment. A model that is more efficient is not a model that is always right. The short version: this is a reasonable thing to try this week, particularly if cost or terminal and C# work matter to you. Don't change team-wide defaults based on a single vendor announcement without running your own comparison first. Sources https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-26-gpt-6-1-terra-in-github-copilot https://x.com/github/status/2114799272634007801 https://www.linkedin.com/posts/github_gpt-61-terra-in-github-copilot-github-activity-7520565094611619840-vR2O

title: Robinhood shares fall 5% as crypto slump weighs on profits, offsetting gains in new businesses
body:
Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.
Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:
Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.
Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.
Robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly important sources of transaction revenue, while the company has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.
Transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.
Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.
Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.
Net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

title: PANDEF demands 50% derivation allocation for oil-producing states
body:
The Pan Niger Delta Forum ( PANDEF ) has called on the National Assembly and the federal government to increase the derivation allocation to oil-producing states from the current minimum of 13 per cent to 50 per cent.
PANDEF said the increase would enable oil-producing states and communities to address environmental degradation, health hazards and developmental challenges associated with oil and gas exploration and production.
The group made the demand in a communiqué read by Godknows Igali, the national chairman of its National Executive Committee, after the committee and the Board of Trustees met virtually on Tuesday.
The meeting brought together former governors, former ministers, first-class traditional rulers, political leaders, opinion leaders and other stakeholders from the six South-south states: Akwa Ibom, Bayelsa, Cross River, Delta, Edo and Rivers.
Mr Igali said the current minimum derivation allocation, provided for under Section 162(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, has remained unchanged for more than two decades despite the environmental and developmental burdens oil-producing communities in the Niger Delta bear.
He said the region continued to face environmental damage and the social and economic consequences of petroleum exploration and production, making an increase in the allocation necessary.
“PANDEF therefore calls for an increase in the derivation allocation from the current minimum of 13% to a minimum of 50%, to enable oil-producing communities and states to address the longstanding developmental deficits, environmental damage, health hazards and social and economic consequences of oil and gas exploration and production,” he said.
The group urged the National Assembly, the federal government and other relevant authorities to review the existing revenue-sharing arrangement to enable oil-producing states to tackle persistent developmental deficits and the effects of oil and gas activities on their communities.
PANDEF also called for the abolition of the onshore/offshore dichotomy in revenue allocation, urging the National Assembly, the federal government and the Revenue Mobilisation, Allocation and Fiscal Commission (RMAFC) to initiate the necessary constitutional and legislative measures.
“The meeting further calls on the federal government, the Revenue Mobilisation, Allocation and Fiscal Commission (RMAFC), and the National Assembly to urgently address the longstanding and contentious issue of the onshore/offshore dichotomy in revenue allocation,” Mr Igali said.
The onshore/offshore dichotomy refers to the distinction between oil revenues from onshore and offshore production when applying derivation principles.
PANDEF argued that offshore petroleum operations could also affect coastal communities whose livelihoods depend on marine ecosystems and fishing grounds.
It said oil spills and other incidents associated with offshore oil and gas activities could damage marine ecosystems, disrupt fishing and undermine the economic well-being of coastal populations, regardless of where the petroleum resources are located.
The group maintained that coastal communities should not be excluded from the benefits of derivation because oil and gas resources are located offshore, given the potential environmental and economic consequences of such operations.
It urged the National Assembly to work with the federal government and RMAFC to address the issue through appropriate constitutional and legislative reforms.
Nigeria’s 11 oil-producing states are Abia, Akwa Ibom, Anambra, Bayelsa, Delta, Edo, Enugu, Imo, Kogi, Ondo, and Rivers.
The Petroleum Industry Act (PIA), signed into law in August 2021, established a framework for the development of communities affected by petroleum operations. Under Section 240(2), oil and gas companies are required to contribute an amount equivalent to three per cent of their actual annual operating expenditure in the preceding financial year to the Host Communities Development Trust Fund for communities affected by their operations.
The fund is intended to support development projects in host communities, including infrastructure, education, healthcare, economic empowerment and environmental protection. The three per cent contribution is calculated from the operating expenditure of the relevant companies, not from the 13 per cent derivation allocation paid to oil-producing states.
The 13 per cent derivation allocation, meanwhile, is guaranteed by Section 162(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which stipulates that the principle of derivation must account for not less than 13 per cent of revenue accruing directly to the Federation Account from natural resources.
PANDEF is demanding that this minimum be increased to 50 per cent, arguing that oil-producing states need more resources to address environmental degradation, health risks and developmental challenges associated with petroleum operations.
PANDEF also expressed concern about the state of the nation, stressing the need for peace, security, national cohesion and responsible governance as Nigeria approaches the 2027 general elections.
The group urged people in the South-south to vote according to their conscience and elect candidates at all levels whose programmes, commitments and demonstrated capacity align with the region’s aspirations.
It said voters should support candidates who could contribute meaningfully to peace, progress and development in the Niger Delta.

title: US, Cuban officials engage in shouting match during UN debate over economic embargo
body:
U.S. and Cuban officials have engaged in a stunning shouting match on the floor of the United Nations General Assembly
U.S. and Cuban officials engaged in a stunning shouting match on the floor of the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday, the latest in a series of public spats between the longtime adversaries over Washington's escalating economic campaign against Havana.
The interaction began shortly after U.S. Ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz took the podium to argue against supporting the annual resolution this week condemning the U.S.' decades-long economic embargo against the island country.
As Waltz was detailing years of alleged corruption by the socialist government, members of the Cuban delegation, including Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez, began to slam on their designated table and yell for a point of order.
Then, as U.N. officials sought to tone down the outbursts, Rodríguez walked down the aisle to the head of the General Assembly and yelled to Waltz, “You are a liar!"
Waltz responded: “You understand who you’re dealing with? This is America. Back up.”
While the moment represented a shocking break from diplomatic decorum traditional to the U.N., it perfectly captured the heightened tensions between Cuba and the U.S. as President Donald Trump's administration seeks to force changes to Cuba’s political system by increasing its already punishing economic campaign.
The Caribbean country — already facing the dire impact of longtime economic and financial troubles — is now being pushed to a breaking point after Trump, a Republican, announced in late January that he would impose tariffs on any country that sells or provides oil to Cuba. The warning has effectively cut off fuel to the island , leading to widespread power outages that affect basic activities such as cooking, the water supply and internet and telephone services.
Cuban officials have also repeatedly stressed that as U.S. officials demand that Cuba open up to private investment, Washington keeps piling on sanctions that stymie the very economic opening it has sought for decades.
The outbursts Tuesday come a week after a similar interaction between Waltz and his Cuban counterpart, Ernesto Soberón Guzmán, outside a U.S.-hosted panel with Cuban dissidents and former prisoners that sought to highlight allegations of the oppressive behavior of the island’s government.
Waltz and other U.S. officials have been using these public events and gatherings at the world body to try to persuade U.N. member states to vote on Wednesday against the annual resolution, which is aimed at calling out the U.S. government’s “maximum pressure policy” against Cuba.
For the past 34 years, the resolution has received overwhelming support. Last year, the vote was 165-7, with 12 abstentions. Argentina, Ukraine and Hungary opposed the measure for the first time.
While such resolutions are not legally binding, they do reflect world opinion.

title: Russia, Equatorial Guinea have potential for mutual supply increase — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Russia and Equatorial Guinea have a substantial potential to increase mutual supplies of marketable products and implement joint investment projects, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at a meeting with the Central African country’s leader, Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo.
"I’d also like to note that our countries have a considerable potential both toward the growth of mutual supplies of marketable goods and the implementation of promising investment projects, mostly in energy and mining," the Russian head of state said.
The field of trade and economic cooperation between the two countries is "somewhat lagging," Putin noted. "A certain decline has even been reported. We expect that establishing an intergovernmental commission could improve the situation," the Russian president added.

title: ‘What Are You Doing With The Money?’ Umeh Questions Tinubu’s Fresh Loan Request
body: The Senator representing Anambra Central, Victor Umeh, has questioned how the Federal Government has spent funds from previous borrowings, asking why budgetary obligations remain unmet despite repeated approvals for loans. Umeh spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Tuesday while reacting to President Bola Tinubu’s request to the National Assembly for approval to borrow an additional $20.5 billion and €1.45 billion. The senator argued that previous borrowing requests were justified on the grounds that the funds would finance government budgets, yet contractors were still owed for capital projects. “The truth is that we have approved so much funds to be borrowed in the past, and on each occasion we’ve been told that this borrowing would be able to fund the budgets and these budgets have remained unfunded up till this day,” Umeh said. ﻿ He noted that three budgets were running concurrently, while the government had yet to meet its obligations to contractors handling capital projects. “Three budgets are running concurrently and the government is not meeting its obligations to contractors on capital projects and so on and so forth. So if you borrow to finance a budget and you are not able to finance that budget, where has the money gone to? That is the question in the lips of everybody,” he said. Umeh also suggested that the latest loan request would eventually receive legislative approval, arguing that opposition lawmakers would be outvoted by members of the ruling party. President Tinubu has written to the National Assembly seeking approval for the Federal Government’s 2026–2027 supplementary external borrowing plan, valued at $20.5 billion and €1.45 billion. The government says the proposed loans would fund critical infrastructure, agriculture, education and other key sectors of the economy in line with the administration’s development priorities. The request has added to the debate over the government’s borrowing plans and Nigeria’s rising debt burden. The post ‘What Are You Doing With The Money?’ Umeh Questions Tinubu’s Fresh Loan Request appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Quantum fears already limiting Bitcoin’s growth, Stacks founder says
body:
Speaking on Cointelegraph’s Chain Reaction podcast, Muneeb Ali warned that uncertainty over Bitcoin’s quantum security could deter institutional investors.
Concerns about quantum computing are slowing institutional investment in Bitcoin, according to Stacks founder Muneeb Ali, who warned that the network needs a credible roadmap for security upgrades to restore investor confidence.
“There is already a ceiling on the growth of Bitcoin because of quantum fears,” Ali said during an interview on Cointelegraph’s Chain Reaction podcast. He argued that uncertainty could lead risk-averse institutional investors to delay large Bitcoin purchases until developers establish a credible path toward quantum-resistant security.
Stacks is a Bitcoin layer-2 network designed to bring smart contracts and decentralized applications to Bitcoin. Ali co-founded the project, which uses Bitcoin as its underlying settlement layer.
Chain Reaction Podcast. Source: Cointelegraph
Ali warned that Bitcoin could enter a riskier period if developers fail to make meaningful progress toward quantum-resistant security by 2028. He said upgrades typically take years to implement, with additional time needed for users to move their holdings to new addresses.
Ali pointed to 2030 as a target for transitioning to quantum-resistant security, citing guidance from the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). He suggested advances in artificial intelligence could accelerate the development of quantum computers, potentially bringing that timeline forward to 2029.
Ali acknowledged that some Bitcoin proponents believe the quantum computing threat remains distant and concerns are overblown. He argued, however, that disagreements over the urgency of the threat could themselves undermine investor confidence, particularly without a credible upgrade roadmap.
Related: Justin Sun says Tron’s post-quantum cryptography has gone live on testnet
Despite his concerns, Ali said a sufficiently powerful quantum computer would more likely emerge from a major research laboratory than an unknown attacker. He suggested companies such as Google or Microsoft would have little incentive to use the technology to steal Bitcoin, given the potential legal consequences.
Ali also said a quantum security threat to Bitcoin would affect the broader cryptocurrency industry, even projects developing their own protections. “If Bitcoin gets hit, everyone gets hit downstream as well,” he said.
Meanwhile, developers are exploring ways to protect Bitcoin against quantum attacks. In September, StarkWare reported that researchers had reduced the estimated computing cost of preparing an experimental quantum-resistant Bitcoin transaction by 79%, following a weeklong optimization challenge.
The approach requires no changes to Bitcoin’s consensus rules, but the latest cost reductions have been demonstrated only in benchmark tests. StarkWare has described the technology as a last-resort measure and continues to advocate for a protocol-level upgrade as a longer-term solution.

title: South-East monarchs renew demand for Nnamdi Kanu’s release
body: — Insist on leadership rotation to Abia, urge massive voter turnout By Steve Oko The South-East Traditional Rulers Council has renewed its demand for the unconditional release of detained Indigenous People of Biafra, IPOB, leader, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, lamenting that previous appeals to the Federal Government have failed to yield the desired outcome. The monarchs also reaffirmed their position that the council’s leadership should rotate to Abia State, with HRM Eze Sir Dr Linus Nto Mbah assuming the chairmanship in accordance with the council’s constitution. These resolutions were contained in a communiqué issued after the council’s quarterly delegates meeting held on October 23, 2026, at the Parliament of Ndi Eze, Owerri, Imo State. On the political front, the traditional rulers expressed concern over the scheduled dates for the forthcoming national elections, which they said could pose challenges for the South-East. They nevertheless urged eligible voters across the region to return to their respective registration areas and participate massively in the elections. The council also called on traditional rulers and community leaders to suspend festivals and ceremonies during the election period to enable eligible voters to exercise their civic responsibilities. On traditional leadership in the South, the monarchs reaffirmed their support for the rotational chairmanship of the Southern Traditional Rulers Council among the South-East, South-West and South-South geopolitical zones. They rejected any arrangement that would confer permanent chairmanship on one zone, insisting that the position should rotate among the three zones for two-year terms, in line with the decision of the Southern Governors Forum reached in Ogun State in 2025. The council further called for the reconstitution of the Southern Traditional Rulers Council’s leadership to reflect recognised traditional rulers from member states and conform to the leadership template of the Southern Governors Forum. The communiqué was signed by the chairman of the South-East Traditional Rulers Council and chairman of the Abia State Council of Traditional Rulers, HRM Eze Dr Linus Nto Mbah; the Obi of Onitsha, HRM Igwe Nnaemeka Achebe; and other traditional rulers from the five South-East states. The monarchs expressed appreciation to Imo State Governor, Senator Hope Uzodimma, for hosting the meeting, as well as the Imo State Council of Traditional Rulers and the people of the state for their hospitality. They also acknowledged the support and encouragement of governors across the South-East. The post South-East monarchs renew demand for Nnamdi Kanu’s release appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Boeing says it won't significantly ramp up 737 Max production until late 2027
body:
Boeing doesn't expect to significantly ramp up output of its best-selling 737 Max aircraft until the second half of 2027 as it grapples with a slower-than-expected pace of wing production.
CEO Kelly Ortberg said Tuesday on the company's quarterly earnings call that Boeing is targeting a production rate of 52 planes a month in the second half of 2027. It has been manufacturing about 47 of its 737 Max planes a month.
Ortberg had told investors last month that the production stabilize was taking a "little bit longer" than expected because of the wings production pace.
Boeing stock fell 10% in trading Tuesday.
"I know everybody wants us to go faster, but we're going to do it right," Ortberg told CNBC's Phil LeBeau in an interview Tuesday.
Ortberg reiterated the company's priority in stabilizing production on Tuesday.
"Looking ahead, expectations are rising, and they should," Ortberg said in a note to staff on Tuesday. "That means elevating our performance through lean, productivity and efficiency improvements in our day-to-day work while upholding our high levels of safety and quality."
Aircraft production and deliveries are key to Boeing's recovery since the bulk of an aircraft's price is paid when the customer receives it.
The company also reported Tuesday that it narrowed its losses in the third quarter, thanks to a boost from its defense unit.
For the three months ended Sept. 30, Boeing reported a net loss of $116 million, or 26 cents a share, compared with a $5.34 billion loss, or $7.14 per share, a year earlier. Adjusting for one-time items, the company posted a loss of 34 cents a share. A year earlier, Boeing had taken a nearly $5 billion charge on its long-delayed 777X aircraft program.
Revenue climbed 4% on the year to $24.19 billion. Free cash flow rose to $464 million from $238 million in the third quarter of 2025.
The company's defense unit revenue jumped 15% in the third quarter from a year earlier to $7.94 billion.
Here's what Boeing reported for the third quarter compared with what Wall Street analysts expected, according to consensus estimates from LSEG:
Boeing delivered 161 commercial airplanes in the third quarter, one more jet than a year earlier.
Revenue in the all-important commercial aircraft business fell 3% to $10.72 billion. The unit had a negative operating margin of 6.5% because of a "less favorable delivery mix, higher projected costs associated with future production rate adjustments and higher estimated supply chain costs," Boeing said.
Ortberg told staff in a memo that the manufacturer has "more work to do."
The manufacturer had some wins lately. The U.S. Navy tapped Boeing to develop its next-generation fighter jet.
And the Federal Aviation Administration last week signed off on the 737 Max 10 , the largest in the Max family. That followed the approval of the 737 Max 7 in August and marked the final certifications for the aircraft line.

title: Re:Build, which spun out Slate Auto, raises $2.1B
body:
Re:Build, the Massachusetts-based manufacturing accelerator that spun out EV startup Slate Auto in 2023, has raised $2.1 billion
The company said Tuesday that it will use the funding to “expand Re:Build’s capacity to manufacture hard tech products and launch new industrial startups,” which will “ensure the most innovative products can be made in America for generations to come.” The investment was led by General Catalyst and JPMorganChase’s Strategic Investment Group. Other investors weren’t disclosed.
The funding round comes as increasing attention and capital is flowing to the idea of building up manufacturing and supply chains in the United States, especially as a hedge away from China.
“We started Re:Build because the deindustrialization of America is an economic failure and national security risk,” Re:Build co-founder Jeff Wilke said in a statement. “This capital allows Re:Build to go faster and further than would otherwise be possible, and build a great manufacturing business and a platform for American industrial leadership. The products and companies emerging from our ecosystem prove we can help restore America’s industrial might.”
General Catalyst’s CEO Hemant Taneja echoed those sentiments in a statement, saying, “General Catalyst has long believed that rebuilding American industrial capacity is one of the most important economic and national security imperatives of our time.”
Taneja added: “To compete with China, re-industrialize the U.S., and revitalize the towns and jobs that have been left behind, we need platform companies that can operate at genuine scale — and we need our innovation ecosystem to learn how to build hardware again.”
Founded in 2020, Re:Build bills itself as “America’s answer to Shenzhen,” and it has numerous ties to Amazon. It was co-founded by Wilke, who was Amazon’s former commercial CEO. Wei Gao, a longtime Amazon VP and technical adviser to Bezos, is Re:Build’s chief digital and product officer. Multiple other Re:Build executives also worked for the e-commerce giant.
Re:Build claims to have “launched hundreds of products and production systems” over its six-year existence. The company tends to operate two ways: It enters partnerships with industrial companies to “design, engineer, and manufacture products at scale across verticals including aerospace and defense,” and it incubates startups in “critical, underserved markets.”
Re:Build says its network of companies employs more than 2,100 people in the U.S. and houses more than 2.4 million square feet of manufacturing capacity.
Wilke and his co-founder Miles Arnone came up with the idea of Slate Auto in 2022 and decided to spin it out in order to help it attract more capital. The company has since gone on to raise at least $1.4 billion, including funding from Bezos’ family office, in an attempt to build an ultra-low-cost, bare-bones pickup that can be customized to a customer’s liking.

title: US military’s drug boat strikes have now killed at least 240 people
body: The U.S. military killed five people Tuesday aboard what Southern Command described as a “go-fast vessel” associated with “narco-terrorists” in the eastern Pacific Ocean, bringing the death toll from its campaign against suspected drug traffickers to at least 240 since September 2025. U.S. Southern Command said Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere carried out the Oct. 27 strike against a speedboat traveling along known drug-trafficking routes. The command said intelligence confirmed the vessel’s involvement in narcotics trafficking but did not publicly provide evidence supporting that assessment, with the majority of these killings occurring at sea . Video released by U.S. Southern Command on X appears to show the vessel sitting nearly motionless in the water before a large explosion engulfs it. The footage does not establish whether the vessel was anchored or disabled. The attack was at least the third deadly strike carried out by SOUTHCOM this month . On Oct. 4, U.S. forces killed four people aboard another suspected drug-trafficking vessel. News Space Force wants to embed more guardians into the joint force By Nicholas Slayton News US expands alcohol restrictions for troops in Japan By Nicholas Slayton News Air Force special ops trainees are graduating months faster in revised pipeline By Patty Nieberg Over the previous months, these strikes have gained mounting legal scrutiny, domestically and internationally. In September, the United Nations found reasonable grounds to believe the killings constituted murder under international law and warned that the broader campaign could amount to crimes against humanity. The organization rejected the Trump administration’s argument that the United States is engaged in an armed conflict with designated terrorist organizations, finding that suspected drug trafficking does not constitute an armed attack justifying military force in self-defense. The families of two men killed in an October 2025 strike have also sued the U.S. government, alleging wrongful death and extrajudicial killing . The lawsuit, filed with assistance from the American Civil Liberties Union and Center for Constitutional Rights, concerns Chad Joseph, 26, and Rishi Samaroo, 41, both from Trinidad and Tobago. Their families say the men had been fishing and working in Venezuela and were returning home when the military struck their boat. The lawsuit seeks damages and a finding that their deaths were unlawful. The Trump administration has maintained that the strikes are lawful. SOUTHCOM previously told Task & Purpose that all military operations had complied with the law of armed conflict and that every person killed was a confirmed member of a designated terrorist organization. The post US military’s drug boat strikes have now killed at least 240 people appeared first on Task & Purpose .

title: 2027: How we will curb election violence – INEC
body: .Vows to hunt down anyone who threatens ad-hoc staff, corps members .Set to hold National Election Security Confab By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has unveiled an intelligence-led security framework to curb violence ahead of the 2027 General Election, vowing to hunt down anyone who threatens its ad-hoc staff, National Youth Service Corps NYSC members or permanent personnel. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, disclosed this in Gombe on Tuesday while declaring open the North-East Zonal Interactive Meeting with Staff and Readiness Assessment for the 2027 General Election. The Commission in its daily bulletin said it was shifting from reactive, election-day deployments to a framework designed to protect voters, personnel and electoral materials before any ballot paper is moved. INEC said its collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps NSCDC, the Department of State Services DSS, the Armed Forces and other paramilitary agencies under the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security ICCES has, according to him, been fundamentally restructured. The new framework, which the Commission terms the “ICCES Tentacle,” extends inter-agency security coordination from national and state headquarters directly down to the most remote Local Government Areas and Registration Area Centres. Amupitan told the gathering that no election, however well planned administratively, could be deemed credible if voters, election personnel and observers operate under physical threat or fear of violence. He explained that the framework rests on three pillars, the first being “Map and Mitigate.” Under it, the Commission will use Electoral Risk Management (ERM) tools to identify security flashpoints, seasonal threat factors and local vulnerabilities early, so that security agencies can deploy proactive measures long before ballot papers arrive. The second pillar, “Ensure Safety,” provides a protective umbrella over all electoral personnel, technological assets, including Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices and server infrastructure, and, most importantly, the voter. The third pillar, “Guarantee Access,” is aimed at ensuring that each of the 176,846 polling units nationwide remains a safe, peaceful and dignified space for the exercise of democratic rights, regardless of geographical remoteness or historical security challenges. According to him, the collaboration among the agencies had already produced concrete results. He disclosed that joint operations led by the DSS recently uncovered a covert plot by criminal kingpins targeting the Commission’s ad-hoc staff and Youth Corps members. Amupitan said swift, intelligence-led intervention neutralised the threat, and the principal orchestrators were arrested and are currently undergoing prosecution. “Let me send a clear message from Gombe,” Amupitan said, warning that anyone who attempts to threaten, intimidate or harm ad-hoc staff, NYSC members or permanent personnel of the Commission would be hunted down and brought to justice under the full weight of the law. He disclosed that the Commission would shortly convene a National Election Security Conference in Abuja, where state-specific security protocols for high-risk zones would be finalised. Amupitan acknowledged that the North-East presents distinct operational challenges, including vast desert terrains, riverine stretches along the Benue trough, remote agrarian communities and expansive landmasses. He noted, however, that the zone had demonstrated remarkable resilience and civic determination. The zone has 13,965,475 registered voters, representing 13.51 per cent of the national register of over 103 million. Bauchi State has the highest number with 3,012,547 voters, followed by Borno with 2,765,165, Adamawa with 2,431,146, Taraba with 2,254,380, Gombe with 1,768,566 and Yobe with 1,733,671. The Chairman said the 2027 General Election would be a simultaneous national undertaking across 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). The Presidential and National Assembly Elections are scheduled for Saturday, 16th January 2027, while the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly Elections will hold on Saturday, 6th February 2027. Earlier, the host Resident Electoral Commissioner REC for Gombe State, Alhaji Umar Muktar Gajiram, speaking on behalf of all North-East RECs, assured the Chairman that the zone was fully prepared, loyal and committed to ensuring that not a single voter out of the 13.96 million in the zone is disenfranchised. Gajiram said all directives on voter register display, logistics audit and technological testing would be executed to the letter. Amupitan assured staff and stakeholders across the North-East that INEC was not working in isolation, describing security as “the bedrock of electoral integrity.” “Insecurity may pose a challenge, but our collective constitutional resolve is far stronger,” he said. The post 2027: How we will curb election violence – INEC appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: How ONSA under Dasuki paid out security funds received from CBN, accountant general – EFCC witness
body:
A bank official on Tuesday gave details of security funds the Sambo Dasuki-led Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) received from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and the Office of the Accountant General of the Federation in 2015, and how the funds were transferred to various beneficiaries.
Arhyel Mshelia, a compliance officer with Access Bank, testified before the FCT High Court in Maitama as the third prosecution witness in an over-a-decade-long N4.6 billion arms procurement fraud trial case involving Mr Dasuki.
Mr Mshelia narrated how the security funds made their ways into the accounts of Jabbama Ada Global Services, Jawas Multipurpose Ventures and Onile Nigeria Limited in 2015.
Mr Dasuki has been standing trial in the case since 2015 alongside former Sokoto State Governor Attahiru Bafarawa, his son Sagir Bafarawa, former Minister of State for Finance Bashir Yuguda, and Dalhatu Investment Limited.
Mr Dasuki and his co-defendants are facing 25 counts of misappropriation, criminal breach of trust and receiving stolen property.
The charges accuse them of diverting N4.6 billion from the NSA office’s account. The money was said to be meant for procurement of arms to firm up the offensive against Boko Haram terrorists during former President Goodluck Jonathan administration, between 2014 and 2015.
Going through the statement of the ONSA’s account on Tuesday, the witness informed the court that the former NSA, Mr Dasuki, and one Salisu Abdulmalik Shaibu used to be signatories to the account with Access Bank.
Arhyel said on 16 March 2015, there was an inflow credit of N500 million from the CBN; the amount was disbursed on 25 March, 2015.
Similarly, the account was credited with N5 billion on 10 April 2015. On 16 April 2015, N27 million and N400 million were sent to Jabbama Ada Global Limited.
The signatory to Jabbama Ada was Salisu Umar Garu, the witness said.
He also said Jabbama Ada received N500 million on 5 February 2015 and N1 billion on 16 April 2015 from the ONSA’s office.
From the Federation Allocation Account Committee’s (FAAC’s) account with the OAGF, the company received N38 million and N25 million on 6 and 7 January 2015, respectively and N55 million on 5 February 2015.
According to the witness, Onile Nigeria Limited, whose signatory is Tom Ikimi, received N200 million and N100 million from ONSA on 9 and 18 February 2015. Jawas Multipurpose Ventures also received N2 billion, he said.
During cross-examination by the defence, the witness said he did not know the purpose of the transactions. He also disclosed that Jabbama Ada was involved in general contracts, oil and gas, purchase and resale of lands and transport.
He also noted transfers to defence headquarters.
Fielding questions from Mr Yuguda and Dalhatu Investment Limited’s lawyer, James Olatoke, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), the witness said he did not know of any relationship between Jabbama Ada and his clients.
He also noted transfers from other individuals and companies aside from the ONSA and CBN.
Thereafter, the judge adjourned the case to 17 November.
The first prosecution witness, Hamza Abdullahi, who served as the second-in-command of the EFCC’s Special Task Force that investigated the alleged arms procurement fraud in the NSA office, had testified that N4.633 billion was traced to Dalhatu Investment Limited. He said Mr Sagir, the son of the former Sokoto governor, is the company’s sole account signatory.
The second prosecution witness, Mr Yusuf, had also testified that funds were released from the NSA office for the supply of security equipment but that the contracts were not executed.
He said that during the investigation, Mr Sagir brought a list showing how the funds were used.
The witness said the funds were used to sponsor pilgrimage to Mecca and partly used for the 2015 political campaigns of the then-ruling party, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).
He listed the recipients of the funds to include Sheikh AbdurRahman Al-Sudais Foundation (N500 million), belonging to former Governor Bafarawa, and 2015 Sokoto PDP governorship candidate, Abdallah Wali, who allegedly received N580 million through a company.
The case is one of the twin arms procurement fraud matters filed against Mr Dasuki and his co-defendants over the streams of funds he released from NSA office accounts between 2014 and 2015.
In the other trial, the EFCC is prosecuting Mr Dasuki, a retired colonel, alongside a former General Manager at the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC), Aminu Baba-Kusa; Acacia Holdings Limited; and Reliance Referral Hospital Limited on 32 counts of fraud involving diversion of N33.2 billion arms funds entrusted to the NSA office.
In March, the EFCC re-arraigned the defendants on criminal breach of trust, among other charges, following the reassignment of the case that started in 2015 to a new judge, Charles Agbaza.
The defendants denied all charges as they did when they were first arraigned in 2015.
The two cases suffered multiple adjournments in their early years, largely due to the State Security Services (SSS) refusing to release Mr Dasuki on bail despite multiple court orders.
Mr Dasuki served as NSA between 2012 and 2015, at the height of Boko Haram attacks in Nigeria’s North-east, during the administration of then-President Goodluck Jonathan.
An audit panel set up by the administration of President Muhammadu Buhari, who came to office after defeating Mr Jonathan in the 2015 presidential election, revealed that about $2 billion entrusted to the office of the NSA, then led by Mr Dasuki, for procurement of arms could not be accounted for.
The EFCC, which instituted multiple charges against diverse persons who received funds from the NSA office, alleged that the arms funds were doled out to friends, relatives, political allies, particularly members of the PDP, for purposes unrelated to the purchase of arms.

title: Walmart says AI training is boosting confidence with the technology among its 2.1 million associates
body:
To join the CNBC Workforce Executive Council, apply at cnbccouncils.com/wec .
As enterprise AI investment continues to grow, companies of all sizes are trying to figure out how employees feel about the technology in the workplace.
Walmart , the biggest private employer in the world, asked its 2.1 million associates in June that exact question for the first time, trying to get a sense of how one of the most diverse workforces is experiencing AI.
What it found, based on more than 1.7 million survey responses, is that while workers have different levels of familiarity and comfort with AI, training and experience with the technology matters.
Seventy-seven percent of Walmart's office-based associates said are excited about AI's potential to improve their work, Walmart Chief People Officer for Associate Experience and Digital Maren Waggoner told CNBC's Leslie Picker at the 2026 CNBC Workforce Executive Council Summit in New York City.
And as for Walmart's U.S. frontline associates, 84% said they are confident using digital tools, a reflection of the AI-powered tools that many of them are now using in their roles, she said.
"We've given them certificates, we've given them training programs and tools, and so they're using it in their day-to-day," Waggoner said.
In the last 13 months, Walmart has partnered with both Google and OpenAI around learning and AI certification programs for associates at no cost. Waggoner said that associates who went through OpenAI training said they had a 27% confidence gain using AI.
That has helped Walmart buck some of the larger trends around AI across the country. While about 52% of U.S. adults say they are more concerned than excited about AI, according to an August 2026 Pew Research Center poll, Walmart associates report greater comfort and excitement, Walmart data showed.
"Providing the tools, providing the training; they feel more confident," Waggoner said.
While AI is perhaps the biggest technological revolution that Walmart has gone through over its 64-year history, Waggoner said the company's approach to transformation has remained the same.
"We have a pretty bold mission statement around being a people-led, tech-powered omni-channel retailer that is ultimately dedicated to helping save money," she said. "The people-led and tech-powered piece has been around for a while."
Many workers across the economy say they are afraid of AI replacing their jobs. While Waggoner said Walmart is finding ways to use AI to automate processes in fulfillment centers, for example, the retailer's efforts with the technology are to "reduce some of that friction and use robotics to help, and then really focus the work on human judgement."
In fact, Waggoner said, at the company's innovation lab in Dallas, Texas, automated efforts to reduce the physical tasks previously performed by humans have instead created more quality assurance-type roles as opposed to broader job losses.
And on the front lines of stores, Waggoner said Walmart has found that its customers "actually like talking to a human at checkout."
That has allowed associates to focus their efforts on using AI to solve customer challenges.
Waggoner pointed to a store manager in Mexico that she met earlier this year who built his own AI agent to look at reports and drive fresh produce sales.
"He's using the tool, but he's still running the store," she said. "The store manager job is still there. He's using the tools and technology to drive his business. And by the way, his fresh sales are through the roof."

title: Speaker Mike Johnson calls election-transfer concerns ‘absurd’
body:
U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson , R-La., committed Tuesday to a peaceful postelection transfer of power, calling concerns that President Donald Trump and congressional Republicans could contest the results if Democrats win control of Congress "absurd."
"We're going to follow the Constitution," Johnson said in Orangeburg, New York during a campaign stop with Republican Rep. Mike Lawler one week before the Nov. 3 midterm election . "The Constitution says when a state certifies the election of members of Congress, then they're administered the oath. That's what I'll be doing on Jan. 3 to everybody who's there," Johnson said in response to a question from MS NOW.
"I may not like some of those outcomes, but that's our system," he said. "And for anybody to suggest otherwise is absurd."
Democrats and voting rights advocates are bracing for potential challenges if control of the House flips, as is widely projected to happen , or control changes in the Senate, which is more closely contested . Republicans have a majority in both chambers of Congress.
Trump, who has continued to falsely claim that widespread fraud cost him the 2020 election , has fueled those fears by calling to "nationalize" elections earlier this year and repeatedly questioning the security of mail voting, while also suggesting noncitizens could vote in large enough numbers to skew results. His administration sued California on Oct. 15 in a fight over noncitizens voting.
The Department of Justice also sued Alaska on Oct. 22 to block the certification of its results in the event of voter confusion. GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan will appear on the ballot beside Daniel J. Sullivan, a retired teacher whom Republicans have said is on the ballot only as a spoiler candidate.
Johnson, who in the wake of the 2020 election was a key congressional ally of Trump's in his quest to overturn results, on Tuesday said questions about a peaceful transfer were "a little silly."
"Of course we'll have a peaceful transfer of power. But it will not be transferring, because we are going to keep the majority and I'm going to be the speaker of the House and I will keep steady hands at the wheel," Johnson told reporters.

title: Ukraine intercepts nearly 60% of Russia’s Geran-4 jet drones, General Staff says, as Kyiv races to counter evolving threat
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukraine’s air defenses have been intercepting nearly 60% of Russian Geran-4 jet-powered attack drones over the past three months, with the interception rate reaching 80% during some attacks, Ukraine’s General Staff said. Russia has increasingly used jet-powered drones in its attacks on Ukraine, adding a faster-moving threat to the Shahed-type drones Moscow deploys against Ukrainian cities and infrastructure. Ukraine is working to improve interception rates while reducing the cost of countering these aerial threats amid shortages of surface-to-air missiles. The General Staff’s update did not mention interception rates for Russia’s more advanced Geran-5 jet-powered drone. F-16s, Mirage jets help intercept Russian drones According to the General Staff , tactical aviation plays a significant role in destroying Russian jet-powered drones. Ukraine uses F-16s, French Mirage aircraft, and MiG-29 fighters to intercept them. The military is also strengthening what it calls “short-range air defense” as Ukraine faces a shortage of guided anti-aircraft missiles. These systems include Gepard and Shilka anti-aircraft guns, newer Skynex, Skyranger, and Terrahawk Paladin systems, interceptor drones, and mobile fire groups deployed by different branches of Ukraine’s Defense Forces. Mobile fire groups are equipped not only with machine guns and supporting equipment but also with man-portable air-defense systems (MANPADS). Ukrainian troops have been successfully using these missiles to shoot down Russian jet-powered drones, the General Staff said. A Ukrainian soldier with an LMM Martlet MANPADS. Screenshot: Ukrainian Air Assault Forces, via Militarnyi. Explore further Denmark rushes 50,000 cannon rounds to Ukraine to help F-16s hunt Russia’s advanced jet drones Ukraine tests cheaper drone interceptors Ukraine is also seeking to lower the cost of countering Russian aerial attacks by testing new interceptor drones. According to the General Staff, some models have already downed dozens of Russian Geran jet-powered drones. The military did not provide further details about the interceptor models or the number of drones destroyed. The rising interception rate reflects Ukraine’s efforts to adapt its air defenses to Russia’s evolving drone campaign while preserving scarce and expensive air-defense missiles for threats that require them. title: PM Koretskyi discusses EU integration support, energy assistance for Ukraine with Lithuanian Seimas Speaker
body:
Koretskyi said this in a Facebook post , Ukrinform reports.
According to him, the sides paid particular attention to the work of the IBAR Task Force, a special working group established jointly with the European Commission to prepare a positive report on Ukraine’s progress in meeting the interim criteria for EU accession. Ukraine co-chairs the group together with European Commissioner Marta Kos.
“Lithuania will hold the presidency of the Council of the EU in the first half of 2027. We have ambitious goals for this period,” Koretskyi said.
The Prime Minister also asked the Lithuanian side to make additional contributions to the Energy Support Fund. According to him, Ukraine is ready to exchange experience with Lithuania on protecting energy facilities and the work of emergency repair crews.
The sides also discussed strengthening railway infrastructure and using the port of Klaipėda to import liquefied gas and export Ukrainian cargo.
Koretskyi thanked Lithuania for its support for Ukraine’s defense sector, including its annual allocation of 0.25% of GDP in assistance to Ukraine.
As reported by Ukrinform, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelensky and Speaker of the Seimas of the Republic of Lithuania Juozas Olekas discussed Ukraine’s European integration prospects and the priorities of Lithuania’s presidency of the Council of the EU in the first half of 2027.

title: Trump weighs lifting sanctions on Russian fund once described by U.S. Treasury as Putin’s ‘slush fund,’ NYT reports
body: President Donald Trump’s administration is considering lifting sanctions on the Russian Direct Investment Fund (RDIF), sources familiar with talks between Russia and the United States told The New York Times. Russia is pressing for sanctions relief for RDIF so the fund can take part in sup plying Russian diesel fuel to the United States, the sources told the Times. The U.S. Treasury Department is reviewing the fund’s application for sanctions relief under its standard procedures, one source said. RDIF will have to prove that the reasons it was sanctioned no longer apply. RDIF is headed by Kirill Dmitriev, a key participant in the talks between Russia and the United States. He is leading the Kremlin’s push for possible joint business ventures between the two countries. RDIF was established in 2011 to attract foreign investment to Russia. The best-known project it helped develop was Russia’s Sputnik V coronavirus vaccine. Dmitriev and his wife, Natalya Popova, are believed to be close to Russian President Vladimir Putin’s younger daughter, Katerina Tikhonova. President Joe Biden’s administration imposed sanctions on RDIF on February 28, 2022, four days after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. “While officially a sovereign wealth fund, RDIF is widely considered a slush fund for President Vladimir Putin and is emblematic of Russia’s broader kleptocracy,” the U.S. Treasury Department said at the time. title: ‘Are they crazy? We'll die’: Netanyahu shouts at ultra-Orthodox activist in recorded call
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu berated Itche Dzalovsky, the operator of an ultra-Orthodox information hotline, on Tuesday evening. In a recorded phone call, Netanyahu can be heard demanding to know whether ultra-Orthodox Jews were going out to vote. "What's happening with the Haredim?" the prime minister asked.  Dzalovsky replied: "What's happening is that they're very angry that, to this day, all the promises about conscription and the ultra-Orthodox community..." Netanyahu interrupted him, shouting: "Tell me, are they crazy? Do they want a left-wing government? Are they crazy? We'll die."   Dzalovsky, a member of the Ger Hasidic community, tried to explain: "They want a government that will deliver on what it has repeatedly promised." Netanyahu continued shouting angrily: "Do they want to die? They want to destroy the Torah world, and they're not coming out? That's what I want to know." The ultra-Orthodox activist replied: "They want ultra-Orthodox Jews to be able to observe the Torah and its commandments to the depths of their souls, without having their religion trampled." The prime minister continued: "So, in short, they're not coming out to vote. That's what I'm asking. They're not coming out. Is that the point?" Dzalovsky replied: "They want to come out, but after seeing those promises honored over time." Netanyahu responded: "What do you mean, promises being honored? In another hour and a half, they're going to establish a government of Mansour Abbas, who says he's going to destroy the Torah world." Netanyahu was referring to the leader of the Arab Islamist Ra'am party.   "But they've had four years of promises being broken consistently," Dzalovsky said. Netanyahu replied: "Fine, but that's not the question right now. Are they going out to vote or not? That's what I'm asking." The ultra-Orthodox activist responded: "They're not convinced there's anyone who will keep his word." "What? What?" Netanyahu asked. "They're not convinced there's anyone who will keep his word," Dzalovsky repeated. "So that means they're not going out. That's what you're telling me," Netanyahu replied. The information hotline operator continued along the same lines: "I get the impression that it's very difficult to convince people who received promises that weren't kept." The prime minister asked: "So they're not going out, okay. Is there anything we can do about it now, with an hour and a half left?" Dzalovsky replied: "I think if you call and promise to provide guarantees to the leading rabbis, members of the Council of Torah Sages and other rabbinic authorities..." Netanyahu interrupted: "I'm going to give them guarantees now, with an hour and a half left, tell me?" "What hasn't been done for four years is certainly very difficult to do now," Dzalovsky replied. At the end of the call, Netanyahu made one final attempt to appeal to the ultra-Orthodox activist: "So, in short, you're telling me there's nothing to be done, right?" "That's what I think. I think it's really, really impossible," Dzalovsky answered. "Thank you, Itche. Goodbye," Netanyahu said.

title: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware affects most servers on planet Earth
body: Defenders across the world face the burden of responding to yet another botched code-execution vulnerability, this time in boot-time firmware used by most of the world’s server vendors and data centers. The vulnerability, with a severity rating of 9.5 out of 10, resides in the TianoCore EDK II , an open source codebase that hardware makers and cloud providers use to create the UEFI firmware that runs during the boot-up sequence. Last year, a representative of the UEFI Forum called EDK2 the "preeminent solution / implementation of the UEFI specifications." Virtually all UEFI suppliers (sometimes still called IBVs or independent BIOS vendors), including AMI, Insyde, and Phoenix, use the reference code extensively. Project Mu, Microsoft's hardened EDK2 fork, used the code containing the vulnerable component as well. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-97631, is a memory-corruption flaw in an ICMP component that attackers can exploit to execute malicious code that runs before the operating system and firmware can implement defenses like Secure Boot , which establishes a chain of trust for all code, including the Trusted Platform Module (TPM), loaded during boot. While final payloads delivered by CVE-2026-97631 have no persistence—meaning they run only once—they can give attackers a wide opening to install other payloads that also run each time early in the boot process.
