title: Arab voter turnout surges as parties projected to nearly double their seats
body: Amid historic voter turnout in Israel's 26th Knesset election, large numbers of Arab citizens turned out to cast their ballots Tuesday. According to television exit polls, the Joint List and Ra'am are projected to win a combined 16 to 18 seats, up from just 10 in the outgoing Knesset. As of 8 p.m., nationwide voter turnout stood at 74.3%, with particularly high participation recorded in many Arab communities, including Bedouin towns and villages. In the village of al-Aryan in Wadi Ara, turnout reached 90.7%, followed by Sakhnin at 83.5%, Kafr Qasim at 81.3%, Rahat at 79.8%, Kuseife at 78.6%, Bir al-Maksur at 77.6%, Tira at 77.5% and Hura at 76.3%.   However, turnout in several Arab communities remained below the national average. In Shefa-Amr, 72.5% of eligible voters had cast ballots, compared with 70.1% in Umm al-Fahm, 70% in Nazareth and 73% in Tel Sheva. In Tayibe, turnout stood at 74.3%, matching the national average. Among Bedouin communities, turnout reached 87.3% in Bir Hadaj, 85.2% in the Abu Qrenat tribal community, 84.2% in Kabu'a and 71.3% in Ar'ara in the Negev. In the Galilee, the Bedouin village of Dmeideh recorded 87.9% turnout, while Shibli-Umm al-Ghanam, at the foot of Mount Tabor, recorded 74.3%. By comparison, turnout in Arab communities was considerably lower during the previous Knesset election in 2022. In Sakhnin, 68.4% of eligible voters participated, compared with 66.88% in Kafr Qasim, 60.6% in Rahat, 57.7% in Tayibe, 51.5% in Shefa-Amr, 49% in Hura and 48.3% in Nazareth.   The most dramatic increase was recorded in Umm al-Fahm, where turnout reached 70.1% by 8 p.m. Tuesday, compared with just 38.3% in 2022, nearly doubling. One possible factor behind the sharp increase is that Joint List chairman Professor Yousef Jabareen is a resident of the city. Most Arab voters support the Arab parties, the Joint List and Ra'am, which could play a significant role in determining the composition of the next government. According to the exit polls, the opposition bloc may need the support of these parties to advance measures against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc, including legislation that would bar a politician under criminal indictment from serving as prime minister, replacing Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana and potentially establishing a government dependent on their support. However, Gadi Eisenkot, chairman of the Yashar! party, who appears positioned to receive the first mandate to form the next government, has already declared that he would establish a coalition only on the basis of a Zionist majority. The Joint List and Ra'am: From 10 seats to a possible 18 The Joint List is an alliance of three Arab parties: Hadash, Ta'al and Balad. Hadash is headed by Yousef Jabareen, who succeeded Ayman Odeh. Ta'al has been led since 1995 by Ahmad Tibi, who has served continuously in the Knesset since 1999. Balad is led by Sami Abu Shehadeh, although he will not enter the Knesset after the Central Elections Committee disqualified his candidacy.   During a hearing on an appeal against the disqualification, the Supreme Court recommended that Abu Shehadeh consider withdrawing his candidacy to avoid the need for a ruling. The Balad chairman subsequently withdrew. At its peak in 2020, the Joint List won 15 Knesset seats, although all the major Arab parties, including Ra'am, were running together at the time. A year later, when the Joint List ran with the same three-party composition as today, it secured just six seats. Ra'am has been headed by Mansour Abbas since 2019. The party is considered the political arm of the southern branch of the Islamic Movement in Israel. In the two previous elections, Ra'am ran independently, winning four seats in 2021 and five in 2022. Following the election to the 24th Knesset, and after also holding coalition negotiations with Likud, Abbas and Ra'am backed the so-called change government, the coalition that replaced Netanyahu. That decision prompted fierce attacks from Netanyahu and Likud, which continued throughout the current election campaign. Netanyahu's central campaign slogan was "Right or Palestine." This time, for the first time, Abbas placed a Jewish candidate on Ra'am's electoral list: former deputy public security minister and retired police major general Yoav Segalovitz, who was ranked second.

title: INEC speaks on suspicious photos in voter register
body:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) said it is investigating suspicious photographs, including those suspected to be AI-generated, that appeared in the preliminary voter register it recently published on its website.
In a statement by its spokesperson, Mohammed Haruna, INEC said it had identified and flagged some questionable registration records during the physical display of the preliminary register at Registration Areas nationwide from 9 to 15 October.
The commission said it had begun reviewing the records and taking corrective action in line with established procedures.
The statement followed public concerns and social media reports about suspected AI-generated photographs in the register published online on 26 October.
INEC said the online register was the same preliminary register displayed physically across the country during the Display, Claims and Objections exercise. It explained that the online version did not reflect all ongoing data-cleanup activities.
“The commission is also examining the circumstances surrounding the suspicious photographs, including possible technical or procedural lapses, and will take appropriate action based on verified findings,” the statement said.
The commission emphasised that the preliminary register was not the final certified register, adding that the display exercise was designed to allow members of the public to scrutinise the records, identify inaccuracies and irregularities, and facilitate corrections before certification.
INEC said it appreciated citizens and stakeholders who drew attention to suspected irregularities, describing public scrutiny as important to improving the voter register’s accuracy and integrity.
The commission assured Nigerians that verified irregularities would be addressed through the applicable procedures and that it would provide further updates as the review progressed.
It said the verification, adjudication and data-cleanup processes would be completed ahead of the scheduled certification of the final register of voters on 15 December 2026.
The publication of the preliminary register is part of INEC’s preparations for the 2027 general election. The exercise allows registered voters and other stakeholders to review the records and flag errors or questionable entries before the commission certifies the final register.

title: Cameroon suspends opposition party
body: Authorities have suspended the Cameroon National Salvation Front (FSNC) of opposition figure Issa Tchiroma Bakary, in Gambian exile, for three months, the minister for territorial administration announced Tuesday. Bakary, a former minister, had rallied young people seeking change during the presidential election of a year ago, won by 93-year-old Paul Biya, who has been in power since 1982. Territorial administration minister Paul Atanga Nji suspended the party, according to a statement, on grounds of “incitement to insurrection” and “serious disturbance of public order,” saying this had occurred “before, during and after the presidential election of October 12, 2025.” The statement warned the party could face legal challenge if it did not accept the sanction. After declaring himself the winner of the election, Bakary repeatedly called on supporters to defend his “victory”, triggering protests in major cities that were brutally suppressed, resulting in a number of deaths with the government yet to provide a toll. Thereafter Bakary went into exile in Gambia. The temporary suspension of the party, which has two members of parliament, comes ahead of local and parliamentary elections, scheduled for early 2027 after multiple postponements. The post Cameroon suspends opposition party appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ukrainian startup, GomSpace test satellite for future communications network
body:
WASHINGTON — A Ukrainian defense technology company and a Danish satellite manufacturer have begun operating an experimental communications satellite in orbit.
Ukrainian startup Himera and Denmark’s GomSpace said Oct. 27 that their Obria Nano satellite, launched Oct. 1 aboard the SpaceX Transporter-18 rideshare mission, is undergoing tests. The companies plan to design a constellation that would provide communications coverage across Ukraine.
The project is one of at least two European-backed initiatives aimed at giving Ukraine greater control over satellite communications, following disruptions this month to SpaceX’s Starlink and Starshield services that affected Ukrainian military operations.
The announcement comes five days after Finnish satellite manufacturer Iceye and telecommunications equipment maker Nokia signed a letter of intent with Ukraine’s Defense Ministry to explore developing a sovereign broadband satellite communications network.
Ukraine has relied heavily on SpaceX’s satellite services for battlefield communications since Russia’s invasion in 2022. The services have become essential to military command networks, drone operations and communications in areas where terrestrial infrastructure has been destroyed or disrupted.
But restrictions imposed in mid-October limited satellite connectivity, interfering with Ukrainian drone operations, including efforts to intercept Russian attack drones.
Ukraine said Oct. 24 that Starlink and Starshield services had returned to normal operating speeds. The disruptions prompted a dispute over responsibility, with SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk and U.S. officials offering conflicting explanations about who had authorized the limits.
Himera and GomSpace said the Obria Nano project is intended to establish a communications system under Ukrainian control, with plans eventually to manufacture satellites and ground terminals domestically.
“For us, this project is about more than launching a satellite. It is an opportunity to lay the foundation for an independent communications network for Ukraine,” said Misha Rudominski, Himera’s co-founder and chief executive.
“We are starting by testing technologies in orbit, while our long-term goal is to develop capabilities that will strengthen the country’s strategic security and reduce dependence on external communications providers,” he said.
Himera, founded in 2022, develops secure tactical radio systems for military forces, including equipment designed to operate in environments affected by electronic warfare.
GomSpace, headquartered in Aalborg, Denmark, manufactures small satellites, communications payloads and spacecraft subsystems.
The companies said Obria Nano is operating in orbit and undergoing testing that will inform the design of a constellation. They did not disclose the satellite’s specifications, communications capacity, project financing or the number of satellites envisioned for the network.
Neither European initiative is expected to replace Starlink’s extensive global network. Smaller national constellations could provide dedicated communications for selected military operations while supplementing commercial services.
Sandra Erwin writes about military space programs, policy, technology and the industry that supports this sector. She has covered the military, the Pentagon, Congress and the defense industry for nearly two decades as editor of NDIA’s National Defense... More by Sandra Erwin

title: Netanyahu vs. Eisenkot: What Israel's election exit polls mean
body: An especially dramatic night lies ahead for Israel's party leaders and voters. Exceptionally high turnout, strong participation in liberal strongholds, a surge in voting among Arab citizens and renewed mobilization in Likud strongholds have created a complex political picture that remains difficult to predict even after the release of the television exit polls. With the exception of Channel 14 and i24NEWS, the polls give an advantage to the bloc seeking to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, although it remains dependent on Arab parties. Polling stations across Israel closed at exactly 10 p.m. Tuesday, ending a dramatic election day marked by exceptionally high and unprecedented turnout. From early in the morning, it was clear that this was no ordinary election. Record participation was reported in liberal strongholds and among Israelis who returned from abroad specifically to vote, but there was also a surprising surge in areas traditionally loyal to Netanyahu. While most of the final pre-election polls had placed Likud as the second-largest party, exit polls suggest Netanyahu managed to mobilize his supporters and could emerge with the largest party in the Knesset, Israel's parliament.   In that sense, Netanyahu may find himself in a stronger starting position in the battle that will begin Wednesday morning over who receives the mandate from Israel's president to form the next government. Israeli law does not require the president to give the mandate to the leader of the largest party, but rather to the candidate considered most likely to form a government, giving the president broad discretion in making that decision. Therefore, if Likud emerges as a larger party than Eisenkot's Yashar!, Netanyahu is likely to wage a fierce public campaign, using every means available to persuade the president to give him the first opportunity. Securing the first mandate carries enormous significance for the candidates. The initial period allotted to form a government is 28 days, after which the candidate can request an additional 14 days from the president. This is a critical window for the parties, because the faction whose leader receives the first mandate also gains control of the Knesset's Arrangements Committee, a powerful body responsible for managing parliamentary affairs until permanent committees are established. Whoever chairs the committee can advance legislative initiatives while working to replace the Knesset speaker or, in Likud's case, keep the position in the party's hands. This would allow the party to establish facts on the ground before the mandate is transferred to the opposing side or a government is formed. Another dramatic factor is the performance of the Arab parties, whose communities have recorded a significant and unprecedented increase in voter turnout. Both the television exit polls and party officials point to a combined result that could surpass the Joint List's previous record of 15 Knesset seats. In such a scenario, both rival blocs would find themselves further from the 61 seats needed for a parliamentary majority, making it difficult for either to form a government. Likud officials are pointing Tuesday evening to pollster Shlomo Filber's exit poll on Channel 14, which they say indicates a tie between the blocs, and are already looking toward their next objective. At the same time, they stress that the night will be tense and dramatic, and that until the very end, it will be impossible to know which bloc has gained the advantage.

title: Reps seek transparent framework for EV, CNG vehicle imports
body:
The House of Representatives has urged the federal government to establish a transparent framework for the importation of electric vehicles (EVs), compressed natural gas (CNG) vehicles and other clean mobility equipment into Nigeria.
The call followed a motion moved by Ademorin Kuye (APC, Lagos) during Tuesday’s plenary in Abuja.
Moving the motion, Mr Kuye said Nigeria has adopted policies that promote the transition to EVs, CNG vehicles, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) vehicles, and other clean transportation technologies as part of its energy transition and economic diversification agenda.
He said the government had introduced fiscal incentives, including import duty and tax reliefs, to encourage investment in clean mobility technologies and expand charging infrastructure and CNG refuelling stations.
He said the policy’s success would also depend on the availability of maintenance centres, spare parts, technical expertise, and after-sales support.
Mr Kuye said Nigeria could use the import incentives to encourage local investment, technology transfer, employment generation and domestic value addition by linking the incentives to measurable investments in infrastructure and technical capacity.
“Nigeria has the opportunity to encourage local investment, technology transfer, employment generation, and domestic value addition by linking import incentives to measurable investments in infrastructure and technical capacity,” he said.
He urged the federal government to establish a transparent licensing and approval framework for the commercial importation of EVs, CNG vehicles and related clean mobility equipment.
He also urged the National Automotive Design and Development Council (NADDC), in collaboration with the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP), Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON), Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) and other relevant agencies, to develop objective criteria for approving importers.
Under the proposed framework, companies seeking approval would, where applicable, be required to establish certified service and maintenance centres in Nigeria, provide genuine spare parts and warranty support, and employ and train qualified Nigerian technical personnel.
They would also be required to invest in EV charging infrastructure or CNG refuelling facilities, comply with Nigerian safety, environmental and technical standards, and submit consumer protection and after-sales service plans.
The lawmaker further urged the NADDC to maintain a public register of approved importers and infrastructure providers to promote transparency and consumer confidence.
He said the approval process must remain open, competitive, and non-discriminatory, allowing any company that meets the prescribed standards to obtain approval without undue preference.
He also urged the government to align tax incentives, import duty concessions, and other fiscal benefits with the proposed regulatory framework to encourage sustained investment in local infrastructure.
The motion was seconded by Makki Yalleman (APC, Jigawa).
Contributing to the debate, Dominic Okafor (APGA, Anambra) supported the motion, saying importers should be required to provide after-sales support, maintenance centres and spare parts to protect consumers.
Adedeji Olajide (APM, Oyo) said greenhouse gas emissions contribute to global warming and argued that an appropriate framework for electric mobility would help Nigeria develop a more environmentally friendly transport system and contribute to global efforts to address climate change.
Sada Soli (APC, Katsina) said legislation was required to provide clear guidelines for implementing the policy.
The House unanimously adopted the motion after Speaker Abbas Tajudeen subjected it to a voice vote.
It then asked the NADDC, BPP, SON, NCS, and other relevant agencies to develop objective qualification criteria for approving the importation of EVs, CNG vehicles, and related clean mobility equipment.
The House Committees on Industry, Commerce, Gas Resources, Environment and Legislative Compliance were also mandated to monitor implementation and report back within four weeks for further legislative action.
CNG is natural gas compressed to high pressure and used as vehicle fuel. It is generally considered a cleaner-burning alternative to petrol and diesel because it produces lower levels of some pollutants and greenhouse gas emissions.

title: Robinhood Taps Ripple's Stablecoin, Treasury Software and Trading Loans
body:
Robinhood, the trading app with 28.6 million funded customers , is adding a digital dollar built by Ripple, the company whose founders created the XRP cryptocurrency. Ripple's RLUSD token went live Tuesday on Robinhood's own blockchain and on its Bitstamp exchange, and is expected to reach the main Robinhood app later this year, according to Ripple's announcement .
RLUSD is a stablecoin, a crypto token designed to always be worth one U.S. dollar, which lets money move across a blockchain without waiting for banks to open. It launched in December 2024, and Ripple said its market capitalization, meaning the combined value of every token in circulation, now tops $2.5 billion.
Robinhood will also run its global treasury operations on Ripple Treasury, software that manages a company's cash, from payments to cash-flow forecasts and risk. That includes intercompany netting, which offsets what a company's own divisions owe one another so fewer payments have to move.
Ripple Prime, a prime broker that lends money and clears trades for hedge funds and other large institutions, already provides Bitstamp with lending and margin financing, meaning borrowed money for trading, across roughly 20 digital assets. Ripple paid $1.25 billion for the firm in a deal announced in April 2025, when it was still called Hidden Road.
Ripple Prime clients also get access to spot trading on Bitstamp, which means buying at the current market price, and later this year Prime will support perpetual futures there, contracts that bet on a coin's future price and never expire. Robinhood closed its purchase of Bitstamp, one of the world's longest-running crypto exchanges, in June 2025 for about $200 million, and most of the exchange's volume comes from institutions.
Robinhood will use RLUSD on the XRP Ledger, the blockchain behind XRP, for institutional settlement, the step where a large trade is finalized and paid for, across Bitstamp's institutional business.
“Utility is what moves stablecoins forward. Working with Ripple, Bitstamp and Robinhood will have access to RLUSD for institutional settlement, Ripple Treasury for our operations, and Ripple Prime for financing,” said Johann Kerbrat, senior vice president and general manager of Robinhood Crypto and International. “That is what a connected, global financial system looks like.”
Robinhood, which pared back its crypto listings during the SEC crackdown on Ripple and other crypto companies, added XRP for U.S. customers in November 2024. Now Ripple's software will help run Robinhood's own treasury department.
Robinhood cut about 10% of its staff in June, after revenue fell 34% in its crypto transaction business in the first quarter to $134 million. It will report its third-quarter results after the market closes on Tuesday, the first report to cover a full quarter since the July 1 launch of Robinhood Chain.

title: Russia Says Northern Sea Route Transit Cargo to Nearly Double in 2026
body:
Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe.
Nuclear icebreaker Arkitka escorting commercial shipping along the Northern Sea Route. (Source: Atomflot via Telegram)
Russia expects cargo transits along the Northern Sea Route (NSR) to more than double in 2026, marking a substantial increase in Arctic shipping despite Western sanctions, although volumes remain far below Moscow’s original ambitions for the route.
Transit cargo will exceed 7 million tonnes this year, Vladimir Panov, head of the Arctic Directorate at state nuclear corporation Rosatom, said on Oct. 27. Total cargo traffic along the route is expected to surpass 40 million tonnes, also a record, he said.
“The Northern Sea Route has two competitive advantages – efficiency and security,” Panov said, adding that the summer-fall route between Asia and Europe is 30% shorter than the passage through the Suez Canal.
“Businesses are already voting for the NSR with tonnes,” he said.
Transit cargo, which excludes commodities extracted in the Russian Arctic, is a small but growing component of overall traffic. Russia’s forecast of more than 7 million tonnes would nearly double the previous year’s volume, Panov said.
Independent tracking by Norway’s Centre for High North Logistics (CHNL) offers a more conservative assessment. By Sept. 30, researchers had identified 104 confirmed transits, already exceeding the 103 recorded during the entire 2025 navigation season. Estimated cargo carried stood at 3.7 million tonnes, compared with 3.2 million tonnes for all of 2025.
CHNL estimated that the season could approach 150 transits and exceed 4.5 million tonnes of cargo if most of the voyages already underway at the end of September were completed. The organization’s figures are preliminary estimates based on vessel tracking and available cargo information, rather than official statistics.
Oil shipments have been a major driver of this year’s surge. In an unprecedented Arctic operation in August, a convoy of at least 15 vessels, including eight oil tankers, sailed north of the Severnaya Zemlya archipelago to bypass difficult ice conditions in the Vilkitsky Strait . The detour took the ships above 81.5 degrees north, along a route nearly 1,000 kilometers longer than the conventional passage. Russian oil shipments through the NSR had reached approximately 20 million barrels between the start of navigation in July and mid-October, nearly 50% above the previous year’s total.
The longer-term picture is equally striking. Total NSR cargo traffic has risen from about 3.7 million tonnes in 2014 to more than 37 million tonnes in each of the past two years, driven overwhelmingly by Russian oil, liquefied natural gas and other resource exports.
Yet the growth has fallen well short of the Kremlin’s original targets. President Vladimir Putin had set an 80-million-tonne goal for 2024, before later projecting that annual traffic could reach 70 million to 100 million tonnes by 2030. Russia carried approximately 38 million tonnes in 2024.
Western sanctions have delayed or complicated several major Arctic oil and gas developments, limiting the expansion of cargo volumes. Nevertheless, the latest figures demonstrate that Moscow continues to develop the route and redirect trade toward Asian markets, albeit at a slower pace than originally envisioned. It also increasingly relies on sanctioned or shadow fleet vessels to carry goods across the Arctic.
Further growth could come from Rosneft’s Vostok Oil project, a major planned oil development on Russia’s Taymyr Peninsula. Increased crude shipments through the Arctic could add substantially to traffic if production and export infrastructure ramp up as planned.
Novatek’s LNG exports could also contribute to the shift. The European Union’s planned prohibition on Russian LNG imports under its phaseout schedule, beginning Jan. 1, 2027, is likely to increase pressure on Russian producers to find alternative markets in Asia. The extent to which this translates into additional NSR shipments will depend on production, shipping capacity, ice conditions and available receiving infrastructure.
Container shipping is also expanding , although it remains a small part of the route’s overall business. Panov said the number of transit container voyages would rise to 46 this year from 23 in 2025, with international containerized transit cargo expected to exceed 600,000 tonnes. However, those figures have not been independently verified and sit well above what the CHNL observed, which reported just 13 voyages by the end of September.
The NSR remains primarily an export corridor for Russian Arctic resources rather than a major alternative to established global shipping lanes. This year’s record figures nevertheless show that sanctions have not halted Russia’s Arctic ambitions.
