title: AI debt fears ease ahead of Oracle, Alphabet and Amazon updates. Here's what to watch.
body:
Fears over artificial intelligence debt have eased after a bout of volatility. But more tests for AI debt are coming.
Oracle holds its Investor Day on Wednesday. And hyperscalers Alphabet and Amazon.com are scheduled to report quarterly results after the market close on Wednesday and Thursday, respectively.
Credit markets are on edge over a flood of AI debt, though fears have eased up a little lately. Meta Platforms ' plans for a $95 billion stock offering , announced on Monday, helped bring down its credit-default swap spreads. Those spreads had risen last week when the company reported negative free cash flow in the third quarter. Other CDS spreads had moved higher too, though they have since backed off.
Investors had expected Meta to bring a large bond deal to market shortly after its earnings announcement, said Richard Cheng, head of Nuveen's investment-grade corporate sector team. The fact that it wasn't announced came as a relief.
"Just the absence of the bond deal itself is a direct catalyst for AI-related spread tightening," he said.
A credit spread is the difference in the yield between the corporate bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. When spreads tighten, it means investors are becoming more confident about the bond issuer.
The market action over the last few days shows that investors are recognizing that "credit fears may have been overblown," said CNBC contributor Paul Meeks, head of technology research at Freedom Capital Markets.
"I expect that these better feelings, maybe not good but better, may continue as companies announce their quarters over the next few weeks."
Still, spreads on CDS remain wider over the past year due to a surge of debt issuance and free cash flows turning negative across the AI space. Meta's CDS spread, for instance, is still up 177% year to date, while Amazon's spread has gained 129%.
"It's not necessarily fundamentals," said CreditSights analyst Jordan Chalfin. "It's more, I'd say, 80% driven by technicals and sentiment."
Alphabet and Amazon pose the next big hurdle for tech bonds as they update their capex plans and free cash flow forecasts. Microsoft 's earnings are also due Wednesday, but the company has yet to issue any bonds to pay for its AI spending.
Both Amazon and Alphabet reported negative free cash flow in the second quarter and analysts expect that trend to continue.
Analysts expect Alphabet to report free cash flow of -$2.3 billion while spending $55.2 billion on capital expenditures in the third quarter, according to FactSet consensus estimates. Amazon is expected to report -$9.9 billion in free cash flow against capex of $58.7 billion.
S&P Global Ratings estimated in an August report that the hyperscalers will have negative free operating cash flow in 2026 and 2027.
More critical will be their outlooks, Cheng says. "The singular focus on the investors' minds is really what the capex guidance trajectory looks like across the hyperscaler space."
Meeks believes elevated capex is a sign of strong AI demand. The hyperscalers have "decided that with all the evidence they have — and they have more than you and me — that this is worthwhile spending, and not just worthwhile; it's required," he said.
CreditSights' Chalfin doesn't expect the hyperscalers to announce major new bond issuance around their earnings reports. Oracle's updates may be more critical for credit markets. The company has issued $117 billion in long-term debt and is clinging to an investment-grade credit rating of BBB-, the lowest level of investment grade above junk, according to S&P.
"It's the most important IG tech credit, just given how it's a bit more stressed relative to the A-rated names," he said. "It's trading more like a high-yield credit, even though it's IG, and so there's just a lot of investor concern on that one."
One wrinkle to the AI debt story: balance sheets don't reveal the whole picture. The companies are using complicated off-balance sheet arrangements for data centers and chip financing, and they aren't fully transparent, S&P Global said in a September report.
"There are commitments they are entering into, for example, into data center leases or purchase commitments on chips that aren't necessarily treated as debt," Mark Habib, digital infrastructure sector lead at S&P Global Ratings, said on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" Monday.
S&P is trying to provide the market with more visibility on those commitments "to give a fuller picture of what kinds of obligations they're actually entering into," he added.
Oracle aside, hyperscaler credit ratings are all comfortably above A levels — reflecting the fact that they have broadly diversified revenue streams, ample coverage for interest payments, and capacity to add leverage if they choose.
Nuveen's Cheng isn't concerned, pointing out that while there has been some credit repricing, there is no credit crisis.
"They continue to have exceptional credit profiles, strong cash generation liquidity," he said of the largest hyperscalers.
"The market is really not concerned about credit quality at this point," Cheng added. "It's really just the trajectory of the capex needs and the supply of debt to fund that. Both of those are pointing in one direction — and that's up."
Correction: This story has been revised to reflect that Oracle's investment-grade credit rating is BBB-, according to S&P. A previous version mischaracterized the company's credit rating.

title: Andre Ayew donates to Black Challenge ahead of World Cup
body: Former Black Stars captain Andre Ayew has donated an undisclosed amount to Ghana’s national amputee football team, the Black Challenge, ahead of the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico. Although the amount has not been officially disclosed, sources indicate that the donation is estimated to be between GHS 50,000 and GHS 100,000. Ayew visited the team at their training to offer his support and encourage the players ahead of the tournament, which will take place from 13 to 22 November in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico. “I’m here to support and give you all the love and power that I can give you, and to wish you great luck. I hope that you guys will bring us a medal, but the gold will be better,” he said. Ghana have been drawn in Group D alongside Angola, Colombia and Iraq, with 24 national teams set to compete for the title. The donation adds to the support the Black Challenge have received ahead of their World Cup campaign as they seek to build on Ghana’s reputation in amputee football.

title: Five countries seek Nigeria’s support for climate finance reforms
body:
MIKTA countries have urged Nigeria to support efforts to make climate finance more accessible and responsive to the needs of countries vulnerable to climate change ahead of the COP31 climate conference in Türkiye.
Representatives of Mexico, Indonesia, the Republic of Korea, Türkiye and Australia made the appeal at a stakeholder meeting in Abuja on Tuesday, describing Nigeria as an important partner in advancing climate-finance reform.
In her opening remarks, the Australian High Commissioner to Nigeria, Leilani Bin-Juda, said Nigeria’s voice would help build momentum for practical reform ahead of COP31.
“Nigeria’s voice would carry particular weight. Its support would demonstrate solidarity with African Least Developed Countries, while strengthening the broader case for a climate-finance system that is simpler, more responsive and more accessible,” she added.
Ms Bin-Juda noted that the climate challenges in the Small Island Developing States and Least Developed Countries in the Pacific are similar to those experienced in Africa, hence the call for collaboration on better access to climate finance that reflects the distinct realities of countries.
Responding to Ms Bin-Juda’s remarks, Omotenioye Majekodunmi, director-general of the National Council on Climate Change, represented by Jummai Vandu, said Nigeria was ready to work with MIKTA towards an implementation-focused COP31.
She highlighted Nigeria’s priorities to include adaptation finance, decentralised climate action, and an inclusive and just transition.
“We must scale up direct, predictable, and accessible adaptation finance that matches the scale of ecological shocks we face, ensuring that vulnerable communities are not left behind,” Ms Majekodunmi said.
Adaptation finance remains a priority for the African Group of Negotiators, which argues that Africa’s vulnerability to climate change warrants greater international support despite the continent’s relatively small contribution to global greenhouse gas emissions.
Ms Majekodunmi said Nigeria would no longer remain a passive participant in the global climate architecture, but wants to help build its enduring pillars.
Mehmet Poroy, ambassador of Turkiye to Nigeria, remarked that Turkiye, host of COP31, is working with Australia to ensure that this year’s conference delivers on accelerating the implementation of commitments already made.
He also acknowledged Nigeria as an important partner.
“We believe that climate finance should therefore not be considered separately from development finance…Our message from Türkiye is that climate investments must deliver tangible results for people,” Mr Poroy said.
He added that COP31 in Antalya should not be an isolated conference; rather, it should help maintain momentum towards COP32 in Ethiopia.
He further described Africa “not simply as an important stakeholder in this process, but as a central partner in delivering meaningful climate action.”
Jeong Yo-an, Korea’s ambassador to Nigeria, added that Korea looks forward to working closely with all MIKTA partners and Nigeria to achieve this goal.
“Indonesia stands ready to engage with Nigeria, MIKTA partners, the United Nations, and others in a spirit of mutual respect,” Bambang Suharto, ambassador of Indonesia to Nigeria, said during the event.
Mr Suharto called for collaboration to ensure that climate finance becomes not merely a promise, but a practical instrument for resilience, sustainable development, and prosperity for all.
The 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) is scheduled to be held at the Antalya Expo Centre, Antalya, Turkiye, from November nine to November 20.
In an unusual arrangement, Turkiye holds the COP31 presidency while Australia will lead negotiations at the conference.
It has been dubbed the Implementation COP as Turkiye seeks to move the yearly conference from negotiations to implementation.
Its outlined priority areas include: electrification, zero waste, food security, resilient cities, green industrialisation, youth participation, health and education, oceans and seas.

title: Ripple, Robinhood expand partnership to bring RLUSD to retail and institutional markets
body:
Ripple also expanded its collaboration with BNY on digital asset custody and partnered with C2FO to bring trade finance settlement onto the XRP Ledger.
Ripple and Robinhood have expanded their partnership to bring the RLUSD stablecoin to Robinhood’s retail and institutional businesses, alongside new integrations spanning treasury management, lending and trading services.
RLUSD is already available on Robinhood Chain and Bitstamp by Robinhood, with a launch in the Robinhood app planned for later this year, according to a Tuesday announcement coinciding with Ripple’s Swell 2026 conference in New York. Robinhood also plans to use the stablecoin on the XRP Ledger for institutional settlement.
Robinhood will also adopt Ripple Treasury to manage its global cash and liquidity operations, including payment processing, cash flow forecasting and intercompany transactions. The integration extends the partnership beyond customer-facing services to Robinhood’s internal financial infrastructure.
The partnership also expands Robinhood’s existing relationship with Ripple Prime, which provides financing services to Bitstamp by Robinhood and plans to introduce perpetual futures trading on the exchange later this year.
Launched in December 2024, RLUSD has reached a market capitalization of $2.57 billion, with nearly $1 billion issued on the XRP Ledger, according to DeFiLlama data. Robinhood reported 28.6 million funded customers globally as of August, offering a potentially significant distribution channel for the stablecoin.
Related: Majority of Americans want candidates who support US-based financial technology: Poll
Ripple also announced on Tuesday an expanded partnership with financial services giant BNY, which now supports custody of XRP and RLUSD through its Digital Asset Custody platform. The companies plan to work together to allow BNY clients to mint and redeem RLUSD directly through the bank and broaden support for tokenized assets issued on the XRP Ledger.
Separately, Ripple partnered with working-capital platform C2FO to bring financing and settlement for its new Instant Pay service onto the XRP Ledger, using RLUSD. The service is designed to let suppliers receive payments against approved invoices in seconds rather than waiting days for traditional bank settlement.
A C2FO spokesperson told Cointelegraph the service is currently in testing, with a controlled launch and the first RLUSD transactions on the XRP Ledger expected by the end of the year.
The string of announcements on Tuesday followed Ripple’s receipt of final approval from the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency on Monday to establish a national trust bank. The institution will manage reserves backing RLUSD and provide digital asset custody services, while stablecoin issuance will remain with Ripple’s New York-regulated subsidiary.

title: US Air Force awards Lockheed Martin $694M hypersonic missile production contract
body: The U.S. Air Force awarded Lockheed Martin a nearly $700 million contract for the production and fielding of a hypersonic missile . The service granted Lockheed the $694 million contract in late September as it moved the AGM-183A Air-Launched Rapid Response Weapon, or ARRW , from prototyping and flight testing to production, according to a Monday announcement . “This is a turning point in our advanced weapons roadmap,” Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink , said in a release. “By moving ARRW from test to production, we’re providing our combatant commanders with a credible, high-speed strike weapon capable of penetrating the most advanced anti-access and area-denial systems.” The contract, which was completed under the Defense Department’s Enterprise-Wide Agile Acquisition Contract, is another effort by the U.S. military to modernize the country’s Arsenal of Freedom, the statement says. The ARRW is designed to accelerate to speeds greater than Mach 5 by using a solid-fuel rocket booster before releasing a hypersonic glide vehicle. The boost-glide hypersonic missile is meant to give the service the ability to strike heavily defended targets from a safe distance away, or standoff range, in a time-sensitive manner, the announcement states. “Fielding ARRW enhances our ability to hold targets at risk anywhere around the world,” Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. Ken Wilsbach said in the release. “This hypersonic weapon provides the Joint Force a flexible and rapid response option for highly contested environments.” The announcement did not say how many missiles Lockheed is expected to produce or specify its timeline for delivery, citing operational security risks. The Air Force previously moved to halt the purchase of ARRWs in 2023 after its prototyping phase ended, following unsuccessful tests , and instead opted to focus on its other major hypersonic weapon program, the Hypersonic Attack Cruise Missile. Then, two years later in 2025, the service’s then-Chief of Staff Gen. David Allen told Congress that the service intends to revitalize its ARRW program with new funding in the fiscal 2026 budget proposal after not including it in the fiscal 2025 budget request. The service allotted roughly $387 million for the ARRW program in its fiscal 2026 procurement budget request, according to budget documents . For fiscal 2027, the Air Force boosted the program’s budget slightly with a request for $452 million, budget documents show.

title: Voter turnout at Israel’s elections exceed 74% two hours before end of voting — TV
body:
TEL AVIV, October 27. /TASS/. Voter turnout at the elections to Israel’s Knesset, or parliament, reached 74.3% two hours before the closure of polling stations, TV Channel 12 reported.
According to it, this figure is a record for any election held in Israel since 1988. Furthermore, it has already surpassed the final turnout figure from the previous parliamentary elections, held in November 2022, when 70.63% of voters took part.
More than 12,000 polling stations opened on Tuesday at 7:00 a.m. local time (5:00 a.m. GMT) and will close 10:00 p.m. (8:00 p.m. Moscow time). Shortly after they close, exit poll results will be announced and the vote count will begin. The elections are taking place amid heightened security measures; according to Israel’s Channel 12, a total of 20,000 police officers, border police, and volunteers are maintaining order. For its part, the army announced a blockade of the Palestinian territories and the closure of all checkpoints in the West Bank.
Parliamentary elections in Israel are held on party lists, with 36 parties vying for seats in parliament. The electoral threshold is 3.25%. AS many as 7.3 million Israelis are eligible to vote. The Central Elections Committee is expected to announce preliminary vote counts on October 29, and the final results of the elections are to be officially released no later than November 4. Once the official results are received, the president will begin consultations with representatives of the parties that have won seats in the Knesset, following which he will task one of the lawmakers with forming a new governing coalition.

title: The Ebola outbreak is breaking records -- and just marked a grim milestone
body:
Marie Bakikula, a caregiver at a UNICEF-supported nursery in Mongbwalu in the Democratic Republic of Congo, works at an emergency nursery for Ebola orphans. Marie Ruwet/AFP/via Getty Images hide caption
The fastest spreading Ebola outbreak in history has surpassed another grim milestone. More than 10,000 people have been infected since the outbreak was first declared in May, according to the latest government figures from the Democratic Republic of Congo.
"It's a milestone that we're all surprised to be passing this quickly," says Katie Thomas-Canfield, interim Ebola response director for the International Rescue Committee. "Ten thousand people affected by Ebola in such a short period is really staggering," she says. At this point in the West Africa outbreak of 2014-2016, only about 4,000 people had been infected. But that earlier outbreak still has the highest case count — more than 28,000 cases.
The current outbreak is also the largest ever in geographic scope, spanning Nigeria to Kenya. It is second in the death toll, with nearly 5,000 deaths compared to the previous toll of over 11,000.
About a third of those who've died in this outbreak have been kids. Children under 5, with their developing immune systems, are hit especially hard — roughly three out of four infected have died.
"Behind every figure is a life interrupted, a family mourning, a health worker under pressure and a community seeking reassurance," said Mohamed Janabi, regional director for the World Health Organization Africa, at a press conference last week. "We must reach people earlier, bring safe care closer, and strengthen trust before fear becomes a barrier to survival."
A woman mourns the loss of a relative suspected of having died from Ebola. Jospin Mwisha/AFP/via Getty Images hide caption
Here's a look at some of the key questions about the 2026 outbreak.
Part of the answer lies in uncertainty over when the virus started circulating
While the outbreak was officially declared in May, more recent evidence suggests the virus likely started spreading in February or March.
"That's a really long time for things to be undetected in communities, and that means we started at a disadvantage," says Thomas-Canfield. A confluence of factors contributed to the delay.
First, there's the fact that a rarer species of Ebola is behind the outbreak — Bundibugyo. Existing tests weren't calibrated for this species , leading to delays. What's more, this region of northeastern DRC is remote and beset by conflict. And U.S. cuts to foreign aid may have slowed disease surveillance efforts, says Nahid Bhadelia, an infectious disease physician at Boston University.
Workers build an Ebola treatment center in Beni territory of North Kivu Province, the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Xinhua News Agency/via Getty Images hide caption
In those early days, "the writing was on the wall that this would be a hard road and it would need international cooperation," says Bhadelia. International cooperation and support have been slower in coming than in previous Ebola outbreaks.
In 2014, for example, healthcare workers from around the globe traveled to West Africa to bolster the response. Bhadelia was one of them.
"I think you are seeing a lot less American or other healthcare workers coming into DRC because of U.S. policy that Americans may not be allowed back even if they're sick," says Bhadelia. That's different from the policy in the prior major outbreak. "That means that a lot of the burden is being carried by DRC and regional healthcare workers."
Despite pledges of funding from around the world, including more than $880 million from the U.S., some health workers on the ground say that money is slow to materialize. "The scale of financing that's available for this response is really a fraction of what it was in our previous response," says Thomas-Canfield. "I think the degree of international solidarity has been a lot less."
A Kenyan Ministry of Health official checks the temperature of a traveler on the Kenya-Uganda border as health authorities step up Ebola screening measures, On October 12, Kenya reported its first-ever Ebola death — a Kenyan man who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo died after returning to the country. Bright Emoja/AFP/via Getty Images hide caption
The response on the ground has improved over the past several months. There are now two dozen or so diagnostic labs and more than 50 treatment centers.
"We're up toward almost 2,000 treatment beds for Ebola, so there's been a lot of progress," says Douglas Noble, global incident manager for Ebola at UNICEF. Nonetheless, roughly two-thirds of deaths are occurring in the community, not in treatment centers — a sign that people are not coming forward with symptoms. That figure has been stubbornly constant for months and needs to improve for the outbreak to get under control, says Noble.
Part of why people aren't seeking care may be that Bundibugyo infections can seem mild at first. "Things like fever, headache, body ache, they're all symptoms of the most common and largely treatable endemic diseases in the region," says Thomas-Canfield. Those who are infected with Ebola may not decide to seek treatment until it's too late, he says.
A bigger hurdle, say many healthcare workers on the ground, is community distrust.
An October survey from the International Rescue Committee found that 85% of respondents in North Kivu — a current hotspot — say that distrust of community responders is keeping them from seeking care.
"We're constantly fighting different kinds of rumors, different kinds of misinformation," says Thomas-Canfield of the International Rescue Committee. Many community members question whether Ebola is real or believe responders are just trying to make money. Others wonder why teams come for Ebola and not other diseases that afflict the region, like malaria or typhoid.
Community health workers are working hard to rebuild that trust. "I do think that in areas where we've been able to establish a longer-term presence, we're better able to respond," says Thomas-Canfield. But the virus is rapidly spreading to new health zones. Building trust from scratch is hard, she says. That's especially true in conflict zones, where fighting makes it hard to work, and armed groups actively sow disinformation.
When trust is low, people don't seek care or engage with health officials trying to find new cases and isolate their contacts. Roughly 80% of new cases are still coming in from people who weren't on health officials' radar. Until that rate goes down, the outbreak will remain out of control, says infectious disease doctor Bhadelia.
She points to the cases in Nigeria and Kenya this month as proof of that point. "The sporadic cases that we're seeing in neighboring countries is a sign of the growth in DRC," she says. While daily case counts seem to be plateauing, she says there's likely many regions where the virus is spreading undetected. "It's so far out of control."
No vaccine or treatment is licensed for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola. Several are in the works , but all far from being used in this response.
There is an existing vaccine for Ebola. It's called Ervebo, but it targets a different species of the disease. It hasn't been widely deployed, but healthcare workers began receiving the vaccine in late August and researchers just started a clinical trial, dubbed Tumaini after the Swahili word for hope, aimed at testing how well Ervebo, and eventually new vaccines, work against Bundibugyo. If it proves effective, "that would be amazing, that could make a difference," says Bhadelia. But she cautions that vaccines and new treatments are not a silver bullet.
A person who died of Ebola is buried at a cemetery in Mongbwalu, Ituri province, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Michel Lunanga/Getty Images hide caption
"Targeted medical countermeasures are necessary, but they are not sufficient," she says. These interventions need to be coupled with basic public health measures, like tracing all the contacts for a newly infected person and isolating and treating those who are stricken. Improving these strategies takes more work and resources, she says, and she worries that the needed support may not come fast enough.
"In this moment, the question that scares me more than anything is will the international community turn its eyes and forget about DRC?" she says. "I am worried the funding will dry out, that we will not keep paying attention to a public health disaster that is much deeper and bigger in this moment than people realize."
For stories about life in our changing world, subscribe to NPR's Global Health newsletter.

title: FG to pay workers N70,000 transport allowance for six months
body: …19-month health workers’ arrears By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Federal Government and the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) have reached an agreement on a series of measures aimed at easing the economic difficulties facing workers, including a ₦70,000 transport intervention and the payment of 19 months’ arrears owed to health workers. The resolutions were reached at a conciliation meeting held at the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment on Tuesday, 27 October 2026, following an earlier meeting convened on 22 October. The meetings were organised to address concerns raised by the NLC over the rising cost of living, the implementation of the National Minimum Wage, petroleum pump prices, workers’ welfare and outstanding allowances. Under the agreement, the Federal Government will provide a transport intervention of ₦70,000 across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026. The government also approved the peculiar allowance with effect from 1 May 2026. Payment of the arrears is expected to begin in November and will be made in three equal monthly instalments. In addition, the 19 months’ outstanding allowances owed to health workers will be paid within three months, beginning in December 2026. The meeting also agreed that the Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee would be constituted and commence work immediately. However, the parties remained divided over the effective date for implementing the new minimum wage. On the issue of tax relief for workers, the meeting resolved that the matter would be referred to the National Executive Council, as taxation is a statutory issue. The Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security has submitted the list of beneficiaries and the cost implications of the proposed hazard allowance for agricultural officers to the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission for verification. The verification is expected to be completed within two weeks, after which the commission will issue an implementation template. Similarly, the NSIWC is expected to complete an updated assessment of the cost implications of the proposed CONHESS adjustment within three weeks. The assessment will enable the Presidential Committee on Salaries to take a decision on the matter. The Federal Government and the NLC urged state and local governments to participate in the intervention process and implement the agreed measures. The parties also agreed to reconvene after one month to review the level of implementation of the resolutions. The agreement was signed on behalf of the federal government by Dr. Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi, Honourable Minister of Labour and Employment, Timi Yakubu, Director-General, Budget, Dr. Garba Abdul S. U., Permanent Secretary (SWO), Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation. For the NLC , its president, Comrade Joe Ajaero; For the Joint National Public Service Negotiation Council (JNPSNC), National Secretary, JNPSNC, Olowoyo Gbenga The post FG to pay workers N70,000 transport allowance for six months appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ghana to review laws to implement Accra Convention – Ofosu-Adjare
body: The Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, says Ghana will review its laws to facilitate the implementation of the Accra Convention on Negotiable Cargo Documents, a move expected to improve businesses’ access to trade financing. Speaking at the signing ceremony in Accra, she said the Convention would address inequalities in access to credit, particularly for businesses transporting goods by road that often struggle to use cargo as collateral for loans. “There are fewer ways to raise finance for one whose goods are on a truck than one whose goods are on a ship. That is the imbalance this Convention was written to correct,” she said. The Convention introduces a negotiable document of title for goods in transit by road, rail, air or sea, allowing the holder to claim the goods and transfer the associated rights to another party. It also provides protections for buyers and banks that rely on the document in good faith, while recognising electronic cargo documents as having the same legal effect as paper-based versions. Mrs Ofosu-Adjare said the framework could help exporters, manufacturers and small businesses unlock capital tied up in goods in transit and improve their ability to secure financing. “Let me say plainly that this signature is for the exporter whose cargo spoils while paperwork catches up. It is for the manufacturer whose capital sits locked in a container. It is for the small firm that has never been able to borrow against goods on a truck,” she said. Ghana to amend legal framework The Minister said the government would review existing laws on transport, the sale of goods, evidence, electronic transactions and secured lending to ensure they accommodate the new cargo documentation system. She said the process would involve collaboration with the Attorney-General’s Department, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Transport. Mrs Ofosu-Adjare added that Ghana intended to complete the necessary constitutional processes and deposit its instrument of ratification among the earliest signatories. She stressed that signing the Convention was only the first step and that its benefits would depend on effective implementation. “The statute will follow, working with the Attorney-General, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Transport,” she said. Government plans stakeholder collaboration Mrs Ofosu-Adjare called on other countries to sign the Convention and support its implementation to expand trade financing opportunities across different transport systems. She said Ghana would work with institutions including the Ghana Shippers Authority, the Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority, the Customs Division of the Ghana Revenue Authority and commercial banks to pilot the use of negotiable cargo documents. The initiative is also expected to support the modernisation of trade documentation, encourage electronic transactions and make it easier for businesses to access credit while their goods are being transported. The Minister said broader participation by other countries would be important to achieving the Convention’s objectives and facilitating trade across borders. “Ghana signs first, but we would be delighted not to sign alone,” she said.

title: Russia emerging as leading supplier of fertilizers to Africa with 20% share — UralChem
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Russia is becoming a leading supplier of fertilizers to Africa, having increased the share of its supplies to the continent to 18-20% of total imports, up from 4% in 2018, UralChem Group told TASS.
"Russia is steadily emerging as a leading supplier of fertilizers to Africa. For instance, the share of Russian supplies in African imports has grown from 4% in 2018 to 18-20% in 2025," the company stated ahead of the Russia-Africa forum.
This means that Moscow acts as a guarantor of the stability of the continent’s agri-food markets, UralChem said. "This is a highly responsible role, and we recognize that part of our function is to help maintain the stability of this market," the company added.
Uralchem ranks among the top five fertilizer suppliers to the African continent, having increased its sales from 100,000 tons in 2018 to around 1 million tons by 2025. Moreover, the company supplied about 135,000 tons of fertilizers to African nations free of charge between 2022 and 2024, while also covering the transportation costs associated with these humanitarian shipments.
TASS is an information partner of the third Russia-Africa Summit and Economic and Humanitarian Forum.

title: Oracle integrates ChatGPT, Codex into apps and expands cloud chip lineup
body:
Oracle on Tuesday announced an expanded collaboration with OpenAI that brings the artificial intelligence lab's ChatGPT and Codex into the software maker's applications to make databases more actionable.
Mahesh Thiagarajan, Oracle's president of Cloud Infrastructure, told CNBC at Oracle AI World in Las Vegas that using ChatGPT "allows anybody to build an application, deploy it, manage it."
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is set to join Oracle co-CEO Clay Magouyrk on stage for an Oracle AI World keynote on Tuesday at 12:40 p.m. ET.
For OpenAI, the announcement represents another example of the frontier lab's push into the enterprise market, just one day after its key competitor, Anthropic , filed its S-1 as it heads toward an initial public offering .
Oracle's database plays a crucial role in underpinning businesses across healthcare and finance in logging and securing data.
Thiagarajan said his team observed OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra model get trained at Oracle's Stargate data center campus in Abilene, Texas, and could see the real-time benefits.
"More businesses are choosing OpenAI as we make it easier to put AI to work through the tools and systems they already use," said Greg Brockman, president and co-founder of OpenAI, in the press release.
Oracle also said Tuesday that it is making different hardware accessible on its cloud infrastructure, including Google 's tensor processing unit AI chips and OpenAI's Jalapeño chip.
"Now customers can actually have infinite possibilities in terms of how they can drive AI," Thiagarajan said.
It is the first time Google's custom chips will run on another hyperscaler's cloud, and illustrates how the companies are increasingly looking for opportunities to get their hardware in the hands of the frontier labs.
Thiagarajan added that the scarcity of chips remains an ongoing issue and that customers such as OpenAI can benefit from having different accelerators to choose from. When asked whether this marks a pivot away from Nvidia GPUs, Thiagarajan said no, adding that Nvidia chips are "the best, most fungible," and that the AI market remains incredibly large.
OpenAI's Jalapeño chip and Cerebras will also run on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. The Cerebras deal is material, but the AI chipmaker won't be disclosing the scale because it's in a quiet period, a Cerebras spokesperson said.
Cerebras stock climbed about 8% following the news. Oracle shares were up nearly 5% on Tuesday.
The announcement comes seven months after market-leading cloud Amazon Web Services announced plans to bring Cerebras hardware into its data centers , a major point of validation.
Thiagarajan also addressed Oracle's multibillion New Mexico data center dubbed Project Jupiter and the ongoing pushback it's receiving from the local community. He said Jupiter represents just one of the 30-40 different data center projects in development, per quarter, for the company.
"We're actually not too worried about what we're doing because I think we're building global infrastructure," he said.
A hearing to address air quality permitting is scheduled for Dec. 7 in Sunland Park, where the controversial data center has already broken ground. The political pushback tied to the project prompted Oracle to deliver a force majeure notice to its backer Blue Owl Capital last month. Right now, Oracle maintains that the project is on schedule.
Investors are now counting down to Oracle's investor day, where investors will want to see if the company can back its fiscal year 2030 revenue targets and if the margin profile of its cloud deals has changed due to the rising cost of capital.
Bank of America analysts wrote to clients that updates on Oracle's major data center projects are among the topics they expect clarity on at the meeting.
Oracle shares are down more than 30% this year due in part to concerns about how the company plans to finance its ambitious digital infrastructure pipeline.
— CNBC's Jordan Novet contributed to this article

title: Iraq deepens ties with Jordan as Baghdad looks to strengthen regional alliances - analysis
body: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi visited Jordan on Monday for meetings with King Abdullah II and Jordanian Prime Minister Jafar Hassan, highlighting Baghdad's efforts to strengthen relations with its western neighbor amid regional tensions. The visit resulted in the signing of nine cooperation documents and discussions about expanding trade, energy links, and security coordination.Zaidi's visit to Amman was his first official trip to the kingdom since taking office. It followed a visit to Saudi Arabia on October 14 and comes as Iraq is seeking to diversify its economic partnerships and strengthen ties with neighboring Arab countries.According to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Zaidi returned to Baghdad after meeting Jordanian officials, Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas, and Iraqi businesspeople and investors. The visit included expanded bilateral talks and the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) covering higher education, environmental protection, consumer protection, diplomatic cooperation, cultural exchanges, and support for small and medium-sized enterprises.The Iraqi Prime Minister's Office said the discussions focused on increasing cooperation in economic, commercial, industrial, and security matters. “Jordan is a strategic partner for Iraq, and we look forward to more cooperation and joint coordination to deal with all the challenges and advance the consolidation of bilateral relations,” Zaidi said, according to his office.The visit illustrates the importance of Jordan for Iraq at a time when Baghdad faces challenges involving Tehran, Damascus, and the security of its country's borders.Iraq, Jordan's historic ties rooted in shared Hashemite ruleIraq and Jordan have longstanding historical, political, and economic ties. Both were ruled by branches of the Hashemite dynasty during the 20th century, until Iraq's monarchy was overthrown in 1958. Jordan's Hashemite monarchy continues to rule the kingdom today.During the 1980s, Jordan became an important economic partner for Iraq. The port of Aqaba provided Iraq with access to international trade routes during the Iran-Iraq War, while the highway connecting Amman and Baghdad became an important commercial corridor.Amman also maintained relations with Baghdad during Saddam Hussein's rule, when Iraqi oil supplies and trade were important to the Jordanian economy.The 2003 US-led invasion of Iraq transformed the relationship. Many Iraqis fled to Jordan as refugees. Extremists also threatened Jordan from Iraq. In subsequent years, the rise of the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria posed another challenge to relations between Baghdad and Amman. ISIS invaded Iraq in 2014. This presented threats to Jordan. The US deployed forces to Jordan and to Al-Tanf military base in Syria near the Jordan-Syria-Iraq border.Iraq and Jordan have a border that is almost 180 km. long. Trade is important and could grow over the next few years. The security of Anbar Province in Iraq is therefore essential. The province covers a vast area of western Iraq and borders Syria, Jordan, and Saudi Arabia. Its location makes it strategically important for transportation, trade, and regional security.The importance of this cooperation was underscored by the recent attack on a church in Jordan's Karak Governorate. Nine people were murdered and 40 wounded in the October 23 attack. Jordanian security forces subsequently arrested three suspects.Iraq, Jordan discuss proposed duty-free economic zone to boost tradeEconomic cooperation was a central focus of Zaidi's visit. This comes as no surprise since he was a banker before becoming prime minister. According to Rudaw, he emphasized the importance of establishing a duty-free economic zone between Iraq and Jordan. Zaidi said the proposed free zone would increase trade and economic cooperation between the two countries.Jordanian Prime Minister Jafar Hassan also stressed the importance of implementing existing economic projects.“We want to move joint economic projects between the two countries to the stage of actual ground implementation, following practical steps and clear timelines,” Hassan said, according to Jordan's Petra news agency, as quoted by Rudaw.The nine agreements signed during the visit represent efforts to expand cooperation across several sectors.However, the announced documents did not include a specific agreement establishing the proposed free trade zone.Jordan previously imported between 10,000 and 15,000 barrels per day of Iraqi crude oil under a bilateral agreement, reports indicate. According to Rudaw, deliveries have been suspended since late December 2025 following the expiration of the agreement and difficulties obtaining suitable crude.Jordan's Energy Ministry said the kingdom imported approximately 2.76 million barrels of Iraqi oil throughout 2025. Another major project under discussion is the proposed Basra-Aqaba oil pipeline, which would connect Iraq's southern oilfields to Jordan's Red Sea port. The pipeline could provide Iraq with an alternative export route and reduce its dependence on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Iraq is also increasing exports through Syria.Jordan offers Iraq both a commercial partner and a potential alternative route for exporting oil.The two countries also participate in a trilateral cooperation mechanism with Egypt, focused on energy, electricity, infrastructure, and trade. Zaidi is slated to visit Cairo on November 23, according to Egyptian officials cited by Rudaw.The visit to Jordan also comes as Zaidi is expected to travel to Syria for talks with officials in Damascus. According to previous reporting by Kurdistan24, the Iraqi prime minister had planned to visit Syria before traveling to Jordan, but the trip was postponed.Iraq seeks stronger ties with Jordan, Syria to secure borders and reduce reliance on IranThe proposed visit to Damascus is important because Iraq's western border security is closely tied to developments in Syria.For Baghdad, improving relations with both Jordan and Syria could help reopen commercial routes and reduce dependence on infrastructure and trade corridors linked to Iran or the Persian Gulf. Security also remains a major issue. Iraq must maintain control of its borders, prevent militant infiltration, and address the influence of armed factions operating within the country.Jordan has its own concerns about instability in Syria, particularly along its northern border, where smuggling networks and armed groups have posed security challenges. These shared concerns create opportunities for greater coordination among the three countries.Zaidi's visit to Jordan reflects a broader effort by Baghdad to strengthen relations with Arab neighbors while managing its complicated relationship with Iran. Iraq has economic and political ties with Tehran, but it is also seeking to expand trade, investment, and energy cooperation with Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and other regional partners. This could wean it of Iranian influence. Iraq is doing the heavy lifting now for the future. Jordan and Syria are part of this vision.This would essentially reunite the three Arab kingdoms that almost came into being in the 1920s. France, at the time, moved into Syria, pushing the Hashemites into Iraq and Jordan. The pan-Arab Ba'ath Party then came to power in Syria and Iraq.For Jordan, closer ties with Iraq offer economic benefits and opportunities for greater regional integration. The next stage will depend on whether the agreements signed in Amman lead to practical results.A proposed free-trade zone, electricity interconnection projects, and the Basra-Aqaba pipeline are among the initiatives that could deepen bilateral relations.The greater question is whether Iraq can translate these diplomatic initiatives into new economic corridors and stronger regional partnerships. Much work remains to be done. Keeping Iran from destabilizing Iraq is vital.

title: OpenAI’s Sam Altman urges companies to focus on AI security threat as GPT-6 adoption soars
body: OpenAI's chief executive Sam Altman urged companies to focus on the security threat from artificial intelligence as use of the technology soars globally. "If I could recommend, like, only one thing to a company right now to do with AI in the very short term … it would be to really understand the security threat landscape from AI and mitigate against that," Mr Altman said at the Oracle AI World event in Las Vegas on Tuesday. With increased adoption of AI, the technology is also constantly finding new threats, he said. “I find myself shocked at just how many vulnerabilities these AI systems are finding, and … just the truly incredible effort that it's going to take to get ahead of this,” he said in a discussion with Oracle chief executive Clay Magouyrk. “I think the only way through this is to go find all these issues and fix them. In fact, I think we'll need new ways to fix them, and it's maybe too hard to patch every bug one by one across the entire supply chain." OpenAI revealed in July that one of its AI models went rogue during a security test and autonomously hacked the start-up Hugging Face. It happened during an internal exercise to test the cyber capabilities of OpenAI models but the programme managed to escape containment, reach the internet and break into Hugging Face, a competitor in the field. Hugging Face co-founder and chief executive Clem Delangue said the incident was "possibly the first of its kind". It was driven by a combination of OpenAI models, including GPT‑5.6 Sol, which OpenAI launched in July, the company said. But Mr Magouyrk stressed that AI is not "creating these problems", but is instead "helping us discover all the security issues that we have developed over the past 50 years". "I'm glad that we're able to discover them in AI rather than waiting for some unknown hacker to let us know," he added. Despite the threat concerns, the adoption of the AI models has been on the rise. Mr Altman said the adoption of GPT-6 Astra, which was unveiled last month, was the "strongest" seen so far. "GPT-6 has been our strongest adoption by far than any model, and watching what people are doing with this across ... any version of enterprise software, like security, science, industry, has been quite amazing to see," he said. At its launch, OpenAI claimed the model was the "most intelligent" in the world, with cyber security a key focus . The rate of change when it comes to AI adoption has been "one of the biggest surprises to me this year", Mr Altman said. "The last say six months have felt like a very accelerated version, even on that time frame [of the past four years since GPT was launched]," he added.

title: Ghana’s ambassador to Côte d’Ivoire extends consular outreach to four western towns
body: Ghana’s Ambassador to Côte d’Ivoire, Brigadier General Alhassan Abu (rtd), has extended the Embassy’s diaspora engagement and consular outreach programme to Ghanaians living in San Pedro, Sassandra, Grand Lahou and Tabou in western Côte d’Ivoire. The initiative is aimed at strengthening ties with Ghanaians living outside Abidjan, improving access to consular services and addressing concerns affecting their welfare and protection. During engagements with the Ghanaian communities, the Ambassador conveyed the greetings of President John Dramani Mahama and the government, assuring them of the Embassy’s commitment to protecting their interests in the host country. He explained that the Ghana Embassy in Abidjan was responsible for maintaining diplomatic relations between Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire, as well as promoting Ghana’s national interests and protecting its citizens. Brigadier General Abu stressed that the welfare and protection of Ghanaians remained a priority for the Mission, saying no Ghanaian should feel abandoned or neglected while living in Côte d’Ivoire. “Hence the doors of the Embassy are open to them at all times,” he said. He outlined the consular services available to Ghanaians, including passport processing and issuance, visas, consular identity cards, attestations, emergency travel certificates and registration of Ghanaian nationals. The Ambassador encouraged Ghanaians to register with the Embassy to enable officials to locate and assist them during emergencies and other crises. He also assured the communities that the biannual Meet Your Ambassador town hall meetings would continue to provide opportunities for the government to explain its policies and programmes while listening to the concerns and grievances of Ghanaians abroad. The Ambassador disclosed that he had led an Embassy delegation to visit Ghanaian nationals detained at the Penitentiary Pole Prison in Abidjan, formerly known as Maison d’Arrêt et de Correction d’Abidjan (MACCA), to provide consular assistance. He said plans were underway to visit other prisons to extend similar support to detained Ghanaians. The visits form part of the Embassy’s broader responsibility to provide consular assistance to citizens facing difficulties in the host country. Brigadier General Abu said the Embassy was working towards establishing a Ghana-Côte d’Ivoire Chamber of Commerce and Industry, alongside plans to organise trade bazaars and cultural events to promote commerce and tourism between the two countries. He cited the participation of 47 Ghanaian small and medium-sized enterprises in the 2026 Semaine Internationale de l’Artisanat de Grand-Bassam (SIAB), held in Côte d’Ivoire from July 30 to August 9, as an example of efforts to expand commercial opportunities. The participation was facilitated by the Ghana Embassy under the auspices of the Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA). On education, the Ambassador said Accra Technical University, Nduom School of Business and Technology, and the University of Cape Coast had signed memoranda of understanding with Côte d’Ivoire’s Ministry of National Education, Literacy and Technical Education to facilitate student exchange programmes. He disclosed that 25 Ivorian students travelled from Abidjan on September 23, 2026, to pursue various programmes at Accra Technical University. The Ambassador also briefed the Ghanaian communities on President Mahama’s Reset Agenda, highlighting developments in the economy, infrastructure, education and healthcare. He cited a reported decline in inflation to 5.2% in September 2026, reductions in public debt, relative price stability and the performance of the cedi as indicators of the government’s economic programme. He also highlighted the phased implementation of the 24-Hour Economy initiative, mentioning the Passport Office, Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority and Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority as institutions operating around the clock. Other initiatives he referenced included the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), the Free Senior High School programme, Operation Recover All Loot (ORAL), and the government’s Big Push infrastructure programme. The Ambassador also pointed to planned road infrastructure, including the Lagos-Abidjan Highway and the proposed Accra-Kumasi Expressway, as part of efforts to improve connectivity and support economic activity. In healthcare, he cited the implementation of primary healthcare initiatives and efforts to expand the local manufacture of medicines and vaccines. These developments, he said, formed part of the government’s broader economic and social transformation agenda. Brigadier General Abu encouraged Ghanaians in Côte d’Ivoire to explore business and investment opportunities in Ghana, saying the government’s policies were intended to create a conducive environment for investment. He also highlighted skills development initiatives, including the Edwumawura and Million Coders programmes, and the support available through the Tree Crops Development Authority for individuals interested in tree-crop farming. He urged members of the diaspora to consider how their skills, experience and investments could contribute to Ghana’s development. Call for unity and security awareness The Ambassador reminded the Ghanaian communities of the longstanding relationship between Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire, urging them to protect the cordial ties between the two countries through responsible conduct. He advised Ghanaians to respect Ivorian laws, regulations, customs and traditions, and to live peacefully with their host communities. “United we stand, divided we fall,” he said. He also encouraged them to remain vigilant, be aware of their surroundings and seek travel advice from the Embassy before travelling to neighbouring countries. “The Embassy is at your service 24/7, so do not hesitate to call on the Embassy anytime for assistance or advice when faced with challenges you cannot comprehend,” he added. The outreach forms part of the Ghana Embassy’s efforts to strengthen engagement with citizens across Côte d’Ivoire, improve access to consular support and promote trade, investment and educational cooperation between the two countries.

title: Neil Young sues Trump committee for $10M for playing 'Rockin' in the Free World' at rally
body:
Legendary musician Neil Young filed a $10 million lawsuit against President Donald Trump 's campaign committee for infringing Young's copyright by playing his song "Rockin' in the Free World" just before the president took the stage to speak at an Oct. 12 rally in Youngstown, Ohio.
The Trump 47 Committee has caused that song, without the musician's permission, "to be played numerous times at other rallies designed to encourage Republican votes in the upcoming mid-term elections," Young's lawsuit in U.S. District Court in Richmond, Virginia , alleges.
Trump "was personally aware that a license would be required to play the Song at rallies," and that Young "has not, and would not, grant the required license," the suit filed Monday says.
Young, 80, in 2020 sued another corporation formed by Trump, Donald J. Trump for President Inc., in Manhattan federal court for copyright infringement of "Rockin' in the Free World," and another song written by Young, "Devil's Sidewalk," for having played the songs without permission at campaign rallies.
In that first case, Trump's corporation "asserted no defense and immediately settled shortly after it was served, promising that it would never again use 'Rockin' in the Free World' without a license and permission from Young," the new suit said.
CNBC has requested comment from the Trump 47 Committee about the suit, and from Young's lawyers.
The White House, when asked for comment, referred CNBC to the Republican National Committee, which did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment.
Young, who was born in Canada, is a naturalized U.S. citizen. He is a two-time inductee in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame : in 1995 as a solo artist, and in 1997 as a member of Buffalo Springfield. Young was also a member of the folk rock supergroup Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young.
Young released "Rockin' in the Free World" in 1989.
His lawsuit describes the tune as a "blistering anthem that contrasts the hollow promises of American political rhetoric with the harsh realities faced by the poor, homeless and forgotten."
The lyrics include descriptions of a mother discarding her baby, addiction, and "garbage piling in the shadows of prosperity — while the repeated chorus delivers savage irony, celebrating freedom that clearly isn't shared by all," the suit notes.
"In short, the Song is the opposite of everything that Donald J. Trump stands for," the suit says.
In addition to the Trump 47 Committee, the suit lists five other defendants, identified by the pseudonym "Doe," whom Young believes are liable for infringing on Young's copyright.
The Oct. 12 Trump rally that is referenced in the lawsuit was also the scene of an incident that has drawn attention from local law enforcement. Videos from the rally show several attendees apparently attacking and beating a woman, Blake Miley, who had repeatedly yelled 'fascist" at Trump while wearing a shirt bearing the message "Release the Epstein Files."
Mahoning County, Ohio, Sheriff Jerry Greene reportedly is investigating three individuals in connection with the incident.

title: ‎NCGC unlocks N64bn credit, vows to end collateral barrier for viable businesses
body: ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ABUJA– THE National Credit Guarantee Company Limited (NCGC) on Tuesday said its guarantees have already unlocked ₦64.13 billion in loans for 174,495 borrowers nationwide, as it intensifies efforts to dismantle the collateral barriers that have long shut viable Nigerian businesses out of formal credit. It said it is supporting an estimated 914,791 direct and indirect jobs within its first 14 months of operation. ‎‎Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Dr. Bonaventure Okhaimo, disclosed this while briefing State House correspondents at the presidential villa, Abuja, on the company’s achievements, challenges and expansion plans. ‎‎The company, which was established by President Bola Tinubu to dismantle longstanding barriers to credit access, has also disclosed that 22,616 Nigerians who had never accessed formal bank credit have secured loans through its intervention, while women now account for 42.7 per cent of beneficiaries. ‎‎Okhaimo, who was accompanied by the Executive Director, Risk Management, Professor Ezekiel Oseni, and Executive Director, Strategy and Operations, Mrs. Tinuola Aigwedo, among others, explained that the company had deployed N30.19 billion in credit guarantees to unlock the N64.13 billion in loans as of October 21, 2026. ‎‎He said the intervention had enabled participating financial institutions to extend loans to previously excluded businesses and individuals, particularly those unable to meet conventional collateral requirements. ‎‎According to him, the initiative has already reached more than 170,000 beneficiaries through 19 participating financial institutions, including commercial and microfinance banks. ‎‎”For every one naira that we give as a credit guarantee to a bank, it creates two naira in loans. That’s the additionality”, Okhaimo explained. ‎‎He stressed that President Tinubu established the company to address a fundamental weakness in Nigeria’s financial system, where otherwise viable businesses were routinely denied credit because they lacked acceptable collateral. ‎‎”The President has said, don’t let a viable Nigerian business suffer because it doesn’t have collateral. He has taken the collateral and given it to the bank. So that’s what we are doing”, he said. ‎‎Explaining the operational model, Okhaimo said NCGC does not lend directly to businesses or individuals but provides guarantees that encourage financial institutions to extend credit to borrowers they would ordinarily consider too risky. ‎‎He said the company currently assumes up to 60 per cent of the credit risk on eligible loans, allowing lenders to relax collateral requirements while retaining responsibility for credit assessment, loan monitoring and recovery. ‎‎According to him, some banks traditionally demand collateral worth more than 150 per cent of the amount being borrowed, a practice that excludes many small businesses despite their commercial viability. ‎‎”What we are saying is, forget about collateral. Do the other due diligence. As long as the customer’s business is viable and the customer has good character, we are willing to support by giving you a credit guarantee that will enable you to give loans to your customers”, he stated. ‎‎On employment generation, the NCGC boss said the company’s interventions had supported 914,791 jobs, comprising direct employment reported by participating banks and indirect employment estimated through recognised development finance multipliers. ‎‎He explained that the indirect employment calculations were based on sector-specific multipliers, including those used by the African Development Bank, with NCGC attributing employment impact according to its share of guaranteed credit risk. ‎‎Speaking on the initiative, Aigwedo said women entrepreneurs remained disproportionately excluded from formal credit because of their limited ownership of assets acceptable as collateral. ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ The post ‎NCGC unlocks N64bn credit, vows to end collateral barrier for viable businesses appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: King Willem-Alexander to open Robin Radar Systems’ new Delft headquarters
body:
His Majesty the King of the Netherlands will officially open Robin Radar’s new 9,000sqm headquarters, highlighting the company’s rapid growth, technological innovation and contribution to the Dutch defence industry.
Robin Radar Systems, a leading Dutch radar technology company specialising in the detection, tracking and classification of small flying objects, including drones and birds, will officially welcome His Majesty King Willem-Alexander of the Netherlands to open its new headquarters in Delft on Thursday 12 November.
The visit marks a significant milestone for Robin Radar, following the expansion into its new 9,000sqm research, engineering and operations facility, more than three times the size of its previous headquarters. With over 800 radar systems deployed worldwide, the company continues to scale its operations to meet growing international demand for advanced radar technology.
During the visit, King Willem-Alexander will officially open the facility and meet employees from across the business. A tour of the production department will highlight the opportunities and challenges associated with scaling the Dutch defence industry, alongside Robin Radar’s expanding manufacturing and technological capabilities.
The King will also receive an introduction to the operational deployment of Robin Radar’s technology in conflict zones, including how direct battlefield feedback is incorporated into the continuous development and improvement of its radar systems.
The visit will provide an opportunity to demonstrate the role of Dutch radar innovation in responding to evolving drone threats, while highlighting the importance of operational experience, technological development and industrial capacity in strengthening Europe’s counter-UAS capabilities.
Siete Hamminga, CEO of Robin Radar, on the King’s visit, said : “It is a great honour to welcome His Majesty King Willem-Alexander to officially open our new headquarters in Delft. This is a proud moment for everyone at Robin Radar and a testament to the hard work of our team. As demand for counter-UAS technology continues to grow, this facility represents an important step in our ambition to strengthen Dutch innovation and contribute to Europe’s defence and security capabilities.”

title: Bitcoin Price Rests Near $80,500 as Midterms, Fed Decision Loom
body: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Rests Near $80,500 as Midterms, Fed Decision Loom Bitcoin price traded near $80,500 most of Tuesday, holding above the $80,000 level that has become the market’s line in the sand. Prices ranged between roughly $79,400 and $80,800 over the day, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data, and the asset was up about 0.3% over the prior 24 hours by mid-afternoon Eastern time. The steadiness follows a rough stretch. Bitcoin price fell below $80,000 on Monday as investors cut risk exposure, weighed down by concerns about AI-sector valuations and higher oil prices. Spot Bitcoin ETFs have also been shedding money. Still, the selling hasn’t turned into panic. Bitcoin price has mostly stayed in a band between about $79,000 and $81,000 this week. The longer view is harder on anyone who bought near the top. Bitcoin’s all-time high sits near $126,000, set in October 2025, and the price is roughly 30% below where it was a year ago. The Federal Reserve’s policy meeting runs October 27 and 28, with the decision due Wednesday. The central bank has held its target range at 3.75% to 4% after raising it in September, and officials have signaled another increase may be needed by year-end. Market odds leaned toward a hold the last time they were clearly reported in early October, but those numbers are stale and likely have moved. Traders will watch Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s press conference for hints about a December hike. Bitcoin price logic amidst the midterms The logic for Bitcoin is simple. Higher rates drain liquidity from speculative assets, so a hawkish surprise would likely push the price back toward $80,000 or below. A hold, or a softer tone, could give buyers room to push toward the $88,000 range seen earlier this fall. The November 3 midterm elections add another layer. Prediction markets have favored Democrats winning both chambers of Congress, according to one Polymarket reading cited in recent coverage. For crypto, the most immediate policy question is the pending market structure bill, and lawmakers’ votes on it could shape how the industry approaches the races. Bitcoin and other risk assets have tended to rally in the 12 months after past midterm cycles. TD Cowen analysts have warned the results could stall the CLARITY Act for two years. Prediction markets gave Democrats a 90% chance of winning the House and 62% of winning the Senate, a scenario TD Cowen called the most negative for bitcoin. A split Congress, with Republicans holding the Senate, was seen as better, while a Republican sweep was viewed as the best path for crypto. The bill had stalled after a failed Senate cloture vote in September, with ethics provisions and stablecoin yield still dividing lawmakers. At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is roughly $80,600. This post Bitcoin Price Rests Near $80,500 as Midterms, Fed Decision Loom first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman .

title: Senior Russian defense official, Madagascar general discuss military cooperation
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Russian Deputy Defense Minister Vasily Osmakov has held a meeting with General Demosthene Pikulas, Chief of the Army Staff of Madagascar, to discuss bilateral military cooperation, Russia’s top brass reported on Tuesday.
"Vasily Osmakov has held a working meeting with General Demosthene Pikulas, Chief of the Army Staff of the Republic of Madagascar. During the talks, the sides discussed joint projects of bilateral cooperation in the defense sphere and further plans toward their practical implementation," the Russian Defense Ministry said in a statement. According to it, the two senior defense officials "reaffirmed their commitment to developing constructive dialogue and maintaining their high level of interdepartmental partnership."
The meeting was held in a friendly atmosphere and confirmed mutual interest in strengthening bilateral ties in the military sphere, the ministry noted.

title: Anchorage Positions Itself as Custody Backbone of US-Mexico Stablecoin Corridor
body:
Anchorage Digital is planting itself at the center of one of the world’s largest money-transfer routes, expanding a custody-and-listing arrangement with Latin American crypto platform Bitso to hold the stablecoins moving between the United States and Mexico.
Announced Tuesday, the deal puts Anchorage Digital Bank’s custody beneath both sides of the corridor. MXNB, Bitso’s Mexican peso stablecoin, is now custodied by the federally chartered crypto bank across six blockchains: Arbitrum, Base, Ethereum, Polygon, Avalanche, and Arc.
In turn, Bitso has listed USDPT and USAT, the U.S. dollar stablecoins from Western Union and Tether, both of which Anchorage issues and custodies. The companies did not disclose financial terms.
The target is the U.S.-Mexico remittance corridor, which moves tens of billions of dollars a year and ranks among the biggest cross-border payment flows on earth. Much of that money still travels over correspondent banking, wire transfers and cash-pickup networks that are slow and costly, while about 15% already runs through Bitso’s infrastructure.
Anchorage is betting that stablecoins, which settle onchain in seconds around the clock, will increasingly replace those legacy rails, and that doing so requires custody that is regulated and sits wherever the liquidity is.
“The US-Mexico corridor is where stablecoins stop being a thesis and start moving real money at scale,” said Nathan McCauley, Anchorage’s CEO and co-founder, arguing the firm is now “the institutional custody layer on both sides of that flow.” Ben Reid, Bitso’s head of stablecoin, said clients can now access the full dollar-peso corridor fully onchain, backed by a federally chartered bank.
The move extends a broader race to wire stablecoins into Latin America’s payments plumbing. Circle recently pushed deeper into the region with a USDC settlement pilot in Colombia, part of a wider expansion into dozens of emerging markets as stablecoins go mainstream.
For Anchorage, the deal builds on its deepening stablecoin footprint. The bank issues Tether’s U.S.-regulated USAT stablecoin, while Bitso has been pushing its MXNB peso coin across networks like Arbitrum. By anchoring both ends of the corridor, Anchorage is aiming to become the default custodian for any issuer or bank entering the route.
