title: RCMP investigating Alberta health procurement for possible fraud, money laundering
body:
Mounties looking into an Alberta health-care spending scandal are investigating potential fraud, breach of trust and money laundering.
The information is contained in court documents filed this month as part of an ongoing wrongful dismissal lawsuit filed by Athana Mentzelopoulos, the former head of Alberta Health Services, once the province’s health authority.
RCMP confirmed last year that they’re investigating health-care procurement contracts, but they didn’t provide details about it.
The police probe is one of multiple investigations sparked after Mentzelopoulos alleged she was fired for looking into sweetheart deals, high-level political interference and corruption in health services contracts.
The government has said she was fired because she was failing in her job and working to stop mandated health reforms.
None of the civil suit allegations, from either side, have been proven in court.
In a letter sent Oct. 15, Ontario Crown prosecutor Tom Andreopoulos writes that the ongoing RCMP investigation is looking into fraud, breach of trust and money laundering related to contracting at Alberta Health, the government ministry, and Alberta Health Services, the health-care provider.
He doesn’t offer specifics or identify a subject in the investigation.
The office of the Ontario Attorney General’s role is to help RCMP with advisory support and the prosecution of any charges that may arise from the investigation.
For months, lawyers for the government, AHS and Mentzelopoulos had been haggling in court over which documents related to the case might be protected by solicitor-client privilege or who has authority over them.
Last month, Justice Michael Lema ruled Mentzelopoulos wasn’t entitled to keep or disclose certain records deemed confidential.
The Andreopoulos letter was filed as part of a court application from a lawyer for Mentzelopoulos. The application argues that when Mentzelopoulos retained records, she had legitimate reasons and that the Andreopoulos letter demonstrates that.
In his letter, Andreopoulos notes that the RCMP seized “various documents and materials” that were provided by Mentzelopoulos after she was fired.
Andreopoulos writes that the prosecutors’ office reasonably believes there’s overlap between what the RCMP seized and which documents have been deemed privileged in court.
Andreopoulos declined to comment Tuesday. RCMP said that to protect the integrity of their ongoing investigation, they have no further comment at this time.
In the spring, RCMP carried out multiple search warrants amid the investigation but declined to give details.
At the time, officers were seen outside the Edmonton offices of MHCare Medical Corp., the medical supply company headed up by businessman Sam Mraiche, which is caught up in the controversy.
MHCare and Mraiche are not party to the lawsuit and have said they did not engage in any improper conduct.
Justice Minister Mickey Amery said Tuesday, of the RCMP investigation, “we will fully co-operate and work with them as we have from the very beginning.”
In question period in the house Tuesday, Opposition NDP Leader Naheed Nenshi continued to press for a full, public inquiry into the affair, accusing Premier Danielle Smith’s government of dragging its feet to avoid accountability until after next year’s election.
“The CorruptCare scandal also refuses to go away,” he said.
Smith responded by pointing to the government-commissioned report from former Manitoba judge Raymond Wyant, saying his investigation was the best way to “clear the air.”
“I think that’s what people want to see, that we have identified issues that were problematic in the AHS procurement process and we’re fixing them,” she said.
Nenshi noted that the Wyant inquiry had no subpoena authority, nor could it compel testimony under oath.
Wyant wrote in his report that he was unable to find any evidence of wrongful interference by government staff, Smith or other elected officials.
However, he said that the scope of his investigation was limited and he could only make conclusions based on the documents he was able to review and the people he interviewed.
“(It) didn’t clear the government in any way and nobody believes the premier when she says it did,” Nenshi said.
“The only reason to avoid a public inquiry right now is if the government has something more to hide.”
Smith said that the government will allow the RCMP to continue their work and “would happily co-operate in any way.”

title: Ukraine war latest: Zelensky reveals details of 'Operation Veles'
body:
Ukrainian forces " eliminated " more than 100 Russian soldiers and captured more than 30 others during an operation involving underground gas pipelines near Kupiansk in Kharkiv Oblast, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Oct. 27.
"The Russians had already tried to use underground gas pipelines to move through our positions and launch assault operations. Ukrainian warriors have successfully transformed this tactic, modernized it, and made it much more sophisticated and technologically advanced," Zelensky said.
The operation, code-named "Veles," involved an underground advance of more than 15 kilometers (9 miles), according to Zelensky .
The operation was carried out by the National Guard's 2nd Khartiia Corps alongside other Ukrainian units.
Zelensky said he had received reports on the operation's initial results and progress from Commander-in-Chief of Ukraine's Armed Forces Mykhailo Drapatyi, 2nd Khartiia Corps Commander Ihor Obolienskyi, and Deputy Head of the Presidential Office Pavlo Palisa.
The 2nd Khartiia Corps previously reported on Oct. 22 that Ukrainian troops had infiltrated Russian rear positions near Kupiansk through underground gas pipelines as part of Operation Veles .
The operation followed earlier Russian attempts to use the same tactic in the area. On Sept. 12, Ukrainian battlefield monitoring group DeepState reported that Russian troops had used a gas pipeline to cross the Oskil River and penetrate Ukrainian defenses near Kupiansk.
A localized ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky has been "expanded… within Kherson (Oblast)," U.S. First Lady Melania Trump said in a post on social media on Oct. 27.
The ceasefire, which came into effect in the early hours of the morning, initially covered Oleshky and surrounding areas in Kherson Oblast and is meant to allow the safe evacuation of civilians and the delivery of humanitarian aid over the coming days.
Trump did not specify the extent of the expanded ceasefire but Tetiana Shelest, head of communications for Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, told reporters it now covered the entirety of Kherson Oblast.
According to a statement from Lubinets, the ceasefire was being "fully honored," with Ukraine and Russia adhering to the agreement as of 5:30 p.m. on Oct. 27.
"I hope that everything will continue in accordance with the agreed plan and that we will be able to help the civilians in Oleshky who are eagerly awaiting assistance," he added.
Oleshky has been under Russian occupation since the early days of the full-scale invasion. Located just across the Dnipro River from Kherson , it has been effectively blockaded by Russian forces, who prevent humanitarian aid from entering.
Residents face severe shortages of food, water, and electricity. Mined roads and constant drone attacks make safe evacuation virtually impossible, and civilians trying to flee on the only roads in and out of the city are frequently targeted by drones.
Trump added that the timing was accelerated by two days to protect civilians and facilitate the delivery of humanitarian aid.
Earlier, Kyrylo Budanov, head of the Office of the President of Ukraine, confirmed a "bilateral ceasefire" began in the embattled Oleshky, in a statement on Oct. 27.
The ceasefire will last until Nov. 1, David Arakhamia , the parliamentary leader of the president's Servant of the People party, said in a later post on social media. Lubinets added that the ceasefire will remain in effect until 10:59 p.m. Kyiv time on Nov. 1.
The agreements were reached in negotiations with Yana Lantratova, head of the Russian negotiating team.
Russian ballistic missiles targeted Kyiv in a deadly attack overnight on Oct. 26-27, striking a university campus, a major bridge, an administrative building, and medical facilities.
Kyiv, a city of three million people, has been relentlessly assaulted by Russian ballistic missiles in recent months as Moscow exploits Ukraine's air defense shortage. While its battlefield offensive has slowed, Russia has chosen a strategy of mass aerial strikes against vulnerable civilians.
At least one person was killed, and 15 people have been injured in the latest Russian attack , Ukraine's State Emergency Service (DSNS) said. Those injured in the attack include a paramedic, a medical technician, and a 20-year-old university student.
The mayor later reported a strike on the city's Southern Bridge over the Dnipro River, one of Kyiv's major traffic arteries. The bridge connects the city's eastern and western sides and is crucial for the daily commutes of hundreds of thousands of residents.
The bridge and metro infrastructure were damaged overnight, Klitschko said. Train service on the bridge has been temporarily suspended.
Ihor, who lives on the east bank of the Dnipro River but works on the west bank, said his commute now takes around two hours, including about half an hour spent walking across the Southern Bridge.
"We’ll have to walk like this every morning now. Taking a detour would take too long," Ihor, who declined to give his surname, told the Kyiv Independent.
Iryna was also crossing the bridge while it remained closed to traffic, but she was using an electric scooter to get across. Following the overnight attack on Oct. 27, this was her first time commuting to work this way.
"This is an alternative means of transport, but I don’t know how long the journey will take," Iryna, who also declined to give a surname, said, expressing hope that the bridge would be repaired soon.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said that a university campus in the city was struck by Russia alongside Kyiv's well-known Kyoto park and residential buildings.
Education minister Andriy Butenko later said that the Russian attack damaged buildings and dormitories of the State University of Trade and Economics. He said there were no deaths among university students or employees.
"This is once again a terrorist country attacking educational institutions. A university, a scientific institution, a college, a school, or a kindergarten - the enemy directs its missiles at children, teachers, and scientists without any pity or humanity. There is no excuse for Moscow's cynical actions," Butenko added.
Ukrainian postal and courier company Nova Poshta has started its own private air defense force and shot down Russian attack drones targeting their facilities, Vyacheslav Klymov, co-owner of the Nova group of companies, revealed at the Kyiv International Economic Forum on Oct. 26.
"We are one of the few companies that has implemented this project. I don't want to disclose the numbers, but we have destroyed 'Shahed' drones, " Klimov said.
Nova Poshta is the largest private postal and courier company in Ukraine, operating over 15,817 branches across the country, and employing over 34,000 people. Its post offices and distribution centers have frequently come under Russian attack .
Despite the ongoing war, business is going well for Nova Poshta. The company quadrupled its net profit compared with last year, according to financial reports published on April 27.
Klimov also emphasised the importance of companies having their own private firefighting capabilities, rather than just waiting for the response of state authorities.
Nova Poshta employees frequently put out significant fires on their premises before the arrival of state emergency service firefighters, Klimov said.
"Now big businesses are looking for fire engines in Europe in order to create their own services. This is our property… who can forbid me from putting out a fire on my own territory?" he said.
Since late summer , Russia has been attacking Ukraine with jet-powered drones, adding to the now-familiar threat posed by conventional Shahed-type drones and missiles. Between larger assaults, successive waves of jet-powered drones now arrive day and night.
Russia's jet-powered drones target civilian infrastructure such as supermarkets , schools , shopping malls , telecommunications infrastructure , data centers , gas stations , and medical facilities .
Units of the Ukrainian Defense Forces have killed or severley wounded 302,000 Russian servicemen by using drones since January 2026, the Ukrainian Defense Ministry said on Oct. 27.
"Each defeat is recorded on video in the Delta combat system and verified by the Brave1 defense innovation cluster," the Defense Ministry said.
The Ukrainian military uses an incentive system in which the verified destruction of enemy personnel and military materiel awards combat units points that they can exchange for more drones, electronic warfare equipment, and other gear on an internal marketplace .
In September, 46,230 Russian soldiers were killed or irrecoverably wounded, according to figures published by the Ukrainian General Staff.
Of these, 32,739 were killed or wounded by drones, the figures show, amounting to about 70% of the total.
The highest number of casualties Ukrainian drones inflicted on the Russian military was recorded in March, with almost 34,000 soldiers killed or irrecoverably wounded.
Drones of various types now cause the vast majority of casualties on both sides. "The destruction of enemy manpower using UAVs helps preserve the lives of Ukrainian soldiers, making it difficult for the enemy to approach our positions," the ministry said.
The prevalence of drones from both sides has significantly changed assault tactics , making heavy equipment such as tanks a rare sight on the battlefield.
With the "kill zone" reaching 20 kilometers (12.4 miles), Russia has largely stopped using tanks or other heavy equipment for assault operations, Joint Forces Task Force spokesperson Viktor Trehubov said on Sept. 20. Drones have replaced many of the tanks' roles for both sides, since a tank driving close to the front would be easily spotted and hit by much cheaper drones.

title: Nvidia and Oracle expand Vera Rubin cloud infrastructure, pitching better utilization as enterprises report idle GPUs
body:
Credit: VentureBeat made with OpenAI ChatGPT-Images-2.5
Nvidia and Oracle are expanding their AI infrastructure partnership with the general availability of Vera Rubin NVL72 systems and standalone Vera CPUs on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, alongside plans to expand their Superclusters to multi-gigawatt scale.
The October 27 announcement addresses two different demands: the computing power required to train and run advanced models, and the CPU capacity needed for agents to execute code, retrieve information and use software tools between model calls.
The companies argue that allowing customers to scale CPU and GPU resources separately can help reduce unused capacity.
For enterprise buyers, that makes the announcement about more than access to Nvidia’s latest hardware: it raises the question of whether a different balance of infrastructure can produce more useful work from the capacity they pay for.
That question is particularly relevant given the latest findings from VentureBeat Intelligence , VentureBeat’s in-house research division, showing low enterprise GPU usage .
VentureBeat Intelligence 's monthly Pulse surveys from July , August and September found 79% of 218 respondents reporting GPU utilization at 50% or below; 70% of that group nevertheless plans platform changes.
The research surveys organizations with at least 100 employees , including consultants answering for clients. These are self-reported findings, not a hardware audit.
For buyers assessing Nvidia and Oracle’s announcement, the implication is that access to more powerful chips should come with a diagnosis of what prevents existing resources from doing useful work.
A GPU waiting for a CPU to finish executing an agent’s code presents a different purchasing problem from a GPU with no queued work. Faster CPUs could help the former.
They would not create demand for the latter. Likewise, if the constraint lies in a remote service, database access or an application’s design, a processor upgrade alone may leave the underlying problem unresolved.
Those are possible explanations that an enterprise should test, rather than causes established by the utilization finding.
The distinction also separates the business cases for a foundation-model developer and an enterprise application team. A model developer with sustained training and inference demand may need additional capacity and faster supporting infrastructure. A business with lightly used GPUs should first establish which workloads would move to the proposed system and why they would run more economically there.
The appropriate test is therefore not simply whether a new chip is faster. It is whether the proposed configuration lowers the total cost of completing an acceptable task, at the response time and reliability the business requires.
Nvidia describes Vera as a processor for the work surrounding model execution: coordinating agents, running code in isolated environments, processing data and supporting reinforcement learning.
A model can decide which action to take, but other software must carry out that action and return the result. When that work becomes a bottleneck, improving model performance alone does not necessarily make the whole agent finish sooner.
Oracle’s technical announcement says Vera is available through bare-metal servers and flexible virtual machines. The standalone offering allows customers to deploy CPU services separately from GPU infrastructure.
Oracle cites Nvidia’s claim of up to 80% faster performance on agent-related CPU workloads compared with leading x86 processors. It also explicitly says those results come from Nvidia platform benchmarks, not tests of the OCI instances themselves. Buyers should treat that figure as a vendor benchmark rather than a demonstrated improvement for their applications.
For an enterprise considering a migration, a representative test would run the same agent workflow on its existing infrastructure and the proposed Vera configuration. It should measure successful task completion, delays across the full workflow, CPU and GPU consumption, and total cost—including any model API charges.
The strongest named customer example is OpenAI.
“We are bringing Vera into production on OCI to support these workloads at scale,” Uday Ruddarraju, OpenAI’s chief technology officer of compute, says in the joint announcement , referring to its agent sandbox workloads.
That example supports a clear role for foundation-model companies. But the potential customer base extends beyond organizations training their own frontier models.
Oracle identifies retrieval, analytics, agent coordination and GPU fleet management among the CPU platform’s uses. Those workloads can also exist inside enterprise AI deployments.
Our reading is that workload characteristics provide a better guide than company size alone. An enterprise running substantial volumes of agent code or retrieval operations could have a reason to evaluate Vera without training a foundation model. Conversely, a large company whose AI use consists mainly of calling externally hosted models may have little reason to acquire a large GPU allocation of its own.
The announcement therefore addresses both markets, but its components serve different needs. The Supercluster expansion most directly addresses exceptionally demanding model workloads. Standalone CPUs offer a more targeted option for organizations seeking to accelerate the software around those models.
Alongside the available NVL72 systems, Oracle plans an eight-GPU Rubin NVL8 configuration using Intel Xeon processors. It is intended to support training, fine-tuning and inference while maintaining compatibility with x86 applications.
That offers a smaller deployment option than the 72-GPU rack configuration, although the announcement describes NVL8 as planned rather than generally available.
Oracle also says its infrastructure can shift between training and inference workloads and accommodate successive Nvidia platforms. That is part of its argument that customers can keep using capacity as their requirements change.
For procurement teams, the distinction between available products and planned expansion matters. The multi-gigawatt buildout describes the providers’ infrastructure ambitions; it is not a minimum deployment requirement for an individual enterprise.
The announcements reviewed do not provide enough workload-specific pricing and performance evidence to calculate a customer’s expected savings.
Regional access also requires checking. Although the companies announce general availability, Oracle’s Vera CPU post says availability will extend to selected regions this quarter. Buyers should confirm the instance types, locations and capacity they can actually obtain.
For a team whose GPUs repeatedly wait on CPU work, Vera presents a concrete proposition to test. For a team with insufficient demand to occupy its existing GPUs, the first task is different: identify useful workloads, reconsider capacity commitments and establish whether a new platform improves the economics.
Nvidia and Oracle are offering additional infrastructure and a way to balance parts of an AI system more independently. The enterprise purchasing decision rests on demonstrating where that flexibility translates into completed work.

title: Threat to Sloviansk-Kramatorsk agglomeration persists despite success of Vivaldi operation – DeepState
body:
Roman Pohorilyi, co-founder of the DeepState project, said this in an interview with Ukrainian Radio , Ukrinform reports.
According to him, the Vivaldi operation enabled Ukrainian forces to cut off the Russian salient north of Lyman, where Russian troops had been attempting to bring in reinforcements in the Shandryholove area and advance through forests near Yampil and Zarichne. The situation was stabilized with the involvement of the Third Army Corps.
“Undoubtedly, the Vivaldi operation was successful at the tactical level. When the enemy’s resources were depleted, the Defense Forces seized the opportunity and their tactical advantage, pushed the enemy back, and carried out a very successful and effective operation,” Pohorilyi said.
At the same time, according to the expert, after losing their advantage north of Lyman, Russian forces began looking for opportunities to advance farther south.
“Having failed to gain an advantage north of Lyman, the Russians began looking for openings farther south and putting pressure from there. Fighting is currently underway for Rai-Oleksandrivka because it is an important settlement, one of the last ones before Sloviansk... Therefore, it is still too early to say that the threat to the Sloviansk-Kramatorsk agglomeration has been averted,” the DeepState co-founder said.
Commenting on the situation in the Kupiansk sector, the analyst noted that the Veles operation had partially helped address the problem of Russian troops infiltrating the city. At the same time, “gray zones” remain in the area, and attempts at infiltration continue.
“The problem that existed before is no longer there today... But overall, the Russians are still making these attempts. So, the Defense Forces are keeping the whole situation under control, identifying and destroying the infiltrators, but the situation could escalate at any moment,” Pohorilyi said.
Analyzing the Zaporizhzhia sector, the expert drew attention to the worsening situation near Orikhiv, where Russian forces are gradually building up their manpower.
“If we talk about the Zaporizhzhia sector, the situation near Orikhiv has actually been getting difficult lately... Many of the tree lines are already teeming with the enemy. They are getting closer and closer, and perhaps at some point we will have to sound the alarm again,” Pohorilyi said in conclusion.
As reported by Ukrinform, President Volodymyr Zelensky said that since the beginning of autumn, the Defense Forces had liberated more territory than Russian forces had managed to capture.

title: No justification for fresh borrowing amid revenue gains — Umeh
body: …Says past loans failed to ease hardship …2026 capital budget yet to be implemented …Rising fuel prices show loans haven’t eased hardship …No work on Eastern Rail Line despite $3bn loan approval By Juliet Umeh Senator Victor Umeh has questioned the Federal Government’s request for fresh loans, saying there is no justification for further borrowing when the government says it has surpassed its revenue targets. Umeh, who represents Anambra Central, spoke on Channels Television’s programme, where he reacted to the President’s request for approval of additional external borrowing. He said the government should account for previous loans and show their impact on Nigerians’ lives. “From what they have told us, there is no justification for the borrowing. Since you have surpassed your revenue expectations, there is no need taking the country into a circus around borrowing all the time,” he said. Umeh said previous loans had been presented as funding for infrastructure, but Nigerians were yet to see the results. “All the borrowing plans we have approved before have been hinged on the development of infrastructure. When you ask where the money is going, you are told the government needs money for emergencies,” he said. He added: “What we want to see is how these monies you have borrowed have impacted positively on the lives of the Nigerian people.” He said the country was in distress, with living costs rising while many people lacked money. “The cost of living has become unacceptable. People don’t have money. They don’t have purchasing power in the midst of soaring costs,” he said. Citing fuel prices, he said he had bought petrol at N1,410 per litre, while diesel was selling for about N1,889 per litre. “When will these things come down? When can people buy petrol or diesel without complaints?” he asked. Umeh criticised budget implementation, saying the 2026 capital budget had yet to be implemented as October drew to a close. “In the 2026 budget, there is no implementation of the capital budget yet. This is the end of October. We have barely one month until the end of the year,” he said. He cited a previously approved loan for the eastern rail line, saying no work was under way. “Part of that $21 billion was $3 billion for the reconstruction of the Eastern Rail Line. No work is going on there,” he said. He said the government should explain whether the funds had been accessed and how they had been used before seeking more loans. Asked whether opposition lawmakers could block the request, Umeh said the governing majority had the numbers to secure its approval. “We are not rubber stamps, but you don’t have the number to say no to it,” he said. The post No justification for fresh borrowing amid revenue gains — Umeh appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Judge admonishes Trump administration over plans for Washington, DC, golf course
body:
Trump said he plans to close the course Nov. 15.
A federal judge has ordered a top Department of Justice official back into court after President Donald Trump posted on his social media account affirming that East Potomac Golf Course will close Nov. 15 for renovations — directly contradicting repeated assertions from administration officials in a hearing last week.
District Judge Ana Reyes has ordered Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward to clarify whether his prior statements to her that there were no plans to close the course remain accurate.
She further ordered Woodward's attendance at a hearing either Friday or Monday where she is expected to press the government for more updates on its compliance with her injunction barring further construction at East Potomac.
In a sharply worded 70-page ruling, Reyes criticized the Trump administration over its plans for the historic golf course in Washington, D.C., and concluded the administration likely violated environmental laws in the process.
"Rarely, if ever, has the United States Department of Justice urged a federal court not to believe the sitting President," Reyes wrote. "Not to believe him that a cabinet secretary has 'developed' a federal land project. Not to believe him that the secretary's agency will destroy a historic golf course already on the land. Not to believe him that 'Restoration work' will begin 'IMMEDIATELY!' Not to believe him that the course 'will be closed' for over a year. Not to believe what the President has repeatedly told the American public. And yet, here we are."
The case began over golf and long walks, Reyes said, but has now morphed into an effort to reconcile sworn statements made by members of the administration with statements made by Trump.
The administration must give "ten business days' written advance notice before making any irreparable modification to any forms or features of East Potomac Park, pending the outcome of this litigation," Reyes said.
Hours before the hearing was set to start, the president had posted on social media that construction on East Potomac Golf Course would begin immediately, despite the administration suggesting to the court that it would not.
"If, as DOJ insists, President Trump is wrong, Secretary Burgum can just say so," Reyes wrote. "He has not. That said, at this juncture Plaintiffs carry the burden of showing a final plan likely exists. They have done so. This is confirmed not just by the President's and Secretary's many posts, but also by the Government's actions, not the least of which is the removal of hundreds of healthy, non-invasive trees on no real notice."
The tree removal had been scheduled a week earlier, but Reyes concluded that those involved in the lawsuit had little notice to stop the cutting.
The administration also likely violated environmental laws — specifically the National Environmental Policy Act -- by "segmenting" the environmental impacts of the construction, she said.
Trump said his administration will appeal the ruling, insisting he will move forward with his plans to shut down the course on Nov. 15 to start the project.
"We are closing the East Potomac Golf Course Site as scheduled on November 15th in order to renovate and rebuild for Competitive (with other such projects!), Safety, Modernization, and Aesthetic reasons," Trump wrote on his social media platform overnight.
He said the judge's request for updates is "unconstitutional."
"We believe this Project is totally 'as of right,' and that the judge does not have the Constitutional Right to 'ask for or receive notices,' which are time-consuming, unnecessary, expensive, and unconstitutional. We will immediately appeal this decision," Trump wrote.
During a gaggle with reporters on Monday night after his Mississippi rally, Trump also said he has a "go-ahead" to work on the renovations and blasted the judge for being an "architectural critic of golf courses."
"It's not my golf course, it's a public course being built in Washington D.C. and it has a go-ahead," Trump said.
He added that the current public course is "extremely dangerous to play" because it is too close together and that he was asking the D.C. Circuit Court for "immediate remedy."

title: VanEck Launches All-in-One Wealth Builder ETF With Bitcoin Exposure
body: Bitcoin Magazine VanEck Launches All-in-One Wealth Builder ETF With Bitcoin Exposure VanEck launched the Wealth Builder ETF today, trading on the NYSE under the ticker WBMO. The actively managed fund packages the firm’s Wealth Builder model portfolios, which advisers have used through third-party platforms, into one product anyone with a brokerage account can buy. VanEck , which oversees about $244 billion in assets, selects the holdings, sets the weights and rebalances the portfolio. VanEck describes the product as a way to “gain exposure to a broad mix of investments across stocks, bonds, gold, and bitcoin with a single ETF purchase.” The fund holds global stocks, bonds, gold and other real assets. Its bitcoin exposure is indirect. WBMO owns no bitcoin. A wholly owned Cayman Islands subsidiary holds certain investments and gains digital asset exposure through exchange-traded products, which are funds that hold bitcoin or track it. The subsidiary is generally capped at 25% of total assets at each quarter-end, but that limit covers several asset categories. The prospectus sets no specific bitcoin target. Investors do not need a wallet, seed phrase or exchange account to hold the bitcoin slice. They also cannot control the bitcoin position directly. JUST IN: $200 billion VanEck includes Bitcoin exposure in their new Wealth Builder ETF "This fund brings Bitcoin to investors who want one simple diversified holding" pic.twitter.com/dLhGu8VrWy — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) October 27, 2026 Details of VanEck’s fund The fund’s gross expense ratio is 0.33%. A 0.07% fee waiver brings the net ratio to 0.26%. The underlying bitcoin products charge their own fees. The allocation also limits the swings. If bitcoin rises sharply, WBMO captures only part of the gain. If it falls, bonds and gold should cushion some of the loss, though not prevent it. VanEck warned in its announcement that digital asset ETPs can be extremely volatile and that some are not registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940, which means they lack certain investor protections. The firm’s other crypto-linked fund, NODE, raised its bitcoin ETP exposure from about 7% at the end of June to 16.8% at the end of September. NODE holds blockchain companies rather than WBMO’s mix, but it shows how VanEck is using crypto in its portfolios. Earlier this fall, VanEck’s Head of Digital Assets Research, Matthew Sigel, said the Bitcoin community recognized the risks quantum computing posed to Bitcoin’s cryptography. “It’s a risk,” Sigel said at the time. “But the community has recognized the scope of the issue. There’s a lot of talent that’s now come together with a framework of how to upgrade the system…The upgrades don’t happen as fast because there’s no CEO who can tell the devs, ‘hey, do it now.’ There’s a governance process — it takes more time, it’s a little bit messier, but there are technological paths for quantum resistance, and I think you’ll see more of that over the next couple of years.” Major companies, including Coinbase and Blockstream, had begun developing quantum-resistant security measures to prepare for future threats. A Bitcoin Security Consortium, including BlackRock, Fidelity Digital Assets, and Block, had also been formed to fund open-source security initiatives, including proposals such as BIP-360. This post VanEck Launches All-in-One Wealth Builder ETF With Bitcoin Exposure first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman .

title: Utah police have connected Ted Bundy to another unsolved 1970s homicide
body:
DNA connects serial killer Ted Bundy to the death of a Utah teenager, authorities announced Tuesday, more than 50 years after her body was discovered by a hunter.
Bundy has been dead since 1989, but the tally of his confirmed victims continues to grow due to advances in DNA testing. He killed at least 30 women and girls in multiple states in the 1970s, and many more escaped or survived with injuries.
The Summit County, Utah, prosecutor said investigators are satisfied that Bundy was responsible for killing 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith in 1974, a death that had long been listed as a cold case.
“This case demonstrates the importance of preserving evidence,” said Salt Lake County Sheriff Rosie Rivera.
Sergeant Reynolds with the Utah County Sheriff’s Office identified there were similarities between the Laura Aime and Melissa Smith cases.
DNA that identified Bundy was from the Y-chromosome, which is only present in men. A highly similar DNA profile was found in evidence obtained from Smith’s autopsy. Officials have been in touch with Smith’s next of kin, none of whom still live in the area.
Officials confirm DNA evidence recovered from another victim matched Smith’s body. Utah County officials presented the DNA evidence to the Summit County Sheriff’s Office on Oct. 7.
“With every case closure, may we stomp the memory of Ted Bundy out,” said Sergeant Mike Reynolds with the Utah County Sheriff’s Office, who participated in the investigation.
Bundy was executed in 1989 by electric chair in Florida for the 1978 murders of two women at the Chi Omega sorority house at Florida State University.
Bundy gave a series of confessions in his final days, including to some crimes that were previously unknown to police. Not all of those cases have been confirmed.

title: Canada’s Eurovision finalists include Rêve, Tyler Shaw
body:
The five finalists vying to represent Canada at the 2027 Eurovision Song Contest have been announced.
They are Montreal dance-pop artist Rêve, Quebec vocalist William Cloutier, Ottawa pop-rocker Talk, New Brunswick singer-songwriter Josiane and B.C. pop crooner Tyler Shaw.
CBC/Radio-Canada revealed the competitors Tuesday at a splashy media event in Toronto.
The public broadcaster says 325 artists from across Canada applied earlier this year for a chance to become the country’s inaugural representative at the international music competition.
The public will be invited to vote for Canada’s Eurovision entrant, with the winner set to be announced by December.
Canada will make its official debut at the 71st Eurovision Song Contest, set to take place next May in Burgas, Bulgaria. It will be the first new country to join the competition since Australia in 2015.
CBC/Radio-Canada said its music team sifted through applications to make initial selections before a seven-member jury chose the finalists at an Oct. 8 meeting in Toronto.
The panel included Montreal International Jazz Festival programming director Maurin Auxéméry, choreographer and director Sam Chouinard, television composer and musical director Orin Isaacs, social media strategist and Eurovision specialist Shawn Myers, and soprano Élisabeth St-Gelais.
Rounding out the jury were Radio-Canada executive vice-president Dany Meloul and CBC executive vice-president Douglas Smith.
CBC/Radio-Canada said the winning artist will then work with leading music-industry talent to develop Canada’s Eurovision song and performance.
Eurovision is considered one of the world’s largest live music spectacles.
Organizers say more than 130 million viewers across 35 markets watched this year’s edition. The event also drew unprecedented social engagement, including more than a billion views on Instagram alone.
The competition has helped propel several major artists to international fame.
Céline Dion’s 1988 win for Switzerland, with the Swiss-written song “Ne partez pas sans moi,” launched her to international stardom.
The contest also helped turn ABBA from a Swedish touring band into global superstars, while Italy’s Måneskin achieved international success following their 2021 win.
The competition has also faced controversy. Israel’s participation amid the conflict in Gaza prompted five public service broadcasters — from Ireland, the Netherlands, Spain, Slovenia and Iceland — to boycott this year’s event.
Ireland’s public broadcaster RTÉ has confirmed a second consecutive boycott of both participating in and broadcasting next year’s Eurovision Song Contest.
In contrast, the Netherlands is making a complicated return; while its entertainment broadcaster AVROTROS continues its boycott, the umbrella public broadcaster NPO has stepped in to ensure the country competes in Burgas.
In 2022, the European Broadcasting Union banned Russia from participating in the contest following its invasion of Ukraine.

title: NMA commends Gov Lawal for repositioning, improving health sector
body:
Governor Dauda Lawal has been commended by the Zamfara State chapter of the Nigerian Medical Association, (NMA) for his administration’s commitment to transforming the health sector and supporting the medical profession.
The State NMA Chairman, Dr Muhammad Murtata Salahu made the commendation at the 2026 Annual Physicians’ Week and Ordinary General Meeting of the association.
Dr Salahu said that Governor Lawal has been repositioning the health sector in Zamfara state through infrastructural revitalisation, improved healthcare service delivery and institutional strengthening among other interventions.
He reaffirmed the NMA’s readiness to work closely with Governor Lawal’s administration in building a healthcare system that is resilient, accessible, equitable and responsive
The Zamfara NMA Chairman statedp: “A stronger medical profession means a stronger healthcare system, and a stronger healthcare system means a healthier and more prosperous Zamfara.
“On behalf of the entire NMA members in Zamfara let me express our profound appreciation to Governor Dauda Lawal for his visionary leadership, remarkable commitment to healthcare transformation and sustained support for the medical profession.
“We acknowledge and commend the determination of the present administration in the state to reposition the healthcare sector through infrastructural revitalisation, improved healthcare service delivery, institutional strengthening and greater attention to the welfare and professional development of healthcare personnel.
“Governor Dauda Lawal’s commitment to giving the healthcare sector a priority attention of his administration demonstrates a clear understanding that a healthy population remains the foundation of sustainable development, economic productivity and social stability.
“We particularly appreciate his administration’s responsiveness to the needs and concerns of medical professionals and its efforts towards creating a more conducive environment for effective medical practice.
“These initiatives are encouraging and represent important steps towards addressing longstanding challenges within our healthcare system.
“The commitment of the state government to healthcare development is commendable, and we assure you of the continued professional support and constructive partnership of the Nigerian Medical Association in translating the state healthcare vision into sustainable benefits for the people of Zamfara.
“We equally encourage the governor to sustain this positive momentum through continued investment in healthcare infrastructure, workforce development, improved welfare packages, recruitment and retention of medical personnel, and the strengthening of healthcare services across the state.
“I want to reaffirm the NMA’s readiness to work closely with the present administration in the state in building a healthcare system that is resilient, accessible, equitable and responsive,” Dr Salahu emphasised.
Held with the theme, “Securing the Future of Medicine in Nigeria,” part of the activities marking the physicians’ week are scientific lectures, presentations on polio in Zamfara, application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in healthcare, and Diphtheria Case Management among others.
The NMA Chairman noted that the resource persons for the presentations were carefully selected with a view to addressing the critical public health concerns and expose members to emerging innovations in medical practice.
Dr Salahu acknowledged the contributions of the WHO , UNICEF and other development partners, healthcare institutions and stakeholders whose technical and institutional support continues to strengthen public health interventions and healthcare delivery in Zamfara.
Salahu who is the Incident Manager, Polio Emergency Operations Centre in Zamfara State, noted that the Physicians’ Week is an important annual event that provides the opportunity to celebrate the contributions of medical doctors to national development, reflect on the challenges confronting the medical profession, and chart a sustainable path towards strengthening healthcare delivery in Nigeria.
“This year’s theme is particularly timely, considering the evolving global healthcare challenges, increasing disease burden and outbreaks, emerging technologies, workforce shortages and the growing demand for accessible, affordable and quality healthcare services.
“As medical professionals, we recognise that securing the future of medicine requires more than clinical expertise,” he stressed.
He said that the healthcare system demands visionary leadership, sustained political commitment, strategic investment, technological innovation and a motivated workforce to function well.

title: AI Agents Are Creating a New Layer of Cybersecurity Spending
body:
AI-focused cloud service provider Akamai launched a sandbox for AI agents on Tuesday, a sealed environment where code an agent writes can run without touching the rest of a company's systems. Agent Sandbox is in beta, alongside Akamai Inference, a service for running open AI models on Akamai's cloud.
The launch may be small but the problem behind it is not. Software is no longer just answering questions—it logs into accounts, writes code, moves money and acts on its own, and every one of those powers is something a hacker, or the software itself, can abuse.
This is what’s known as agentic AI, and it’s taking over the internet. A 2026 Palo Alto Networks survey of 2,930 security leaders found an average of 109 machine identities for every human, the logins and keys software uses to access other software. Of those, 79 are AI agents.
Agentic AI comes with a lot of perks, but also some serious dangers, especially when those agents have too much freedom, or are so intelligent they can bypass their own restrictions.
For example, Hugging Face, a major hub for open AI models, disclosed an intrusion on July 16, and OpenAI confirmed five days later that its own models were responsible. The research group METR later investigated the incident and found about 1,200 OpenAI agents had coordinated on a hidden message board, with roughly 700 joining the attack.
Turns out the agents escaped their sandbox and chained a previously unknown software flaw with stolen credentials to reach live systems. OpenAI called it a "warning shot." It said a monitor that reads a model's written reasoning was not running during the tests.
In simple terms, AI safety usually ends up being a tug of war game between alignment (the guys in charge of making sure AI is safe) and development (the guys in charge of making sure AI is powerful), with each team wanting the other to play a minor role in order to secure its own goals.
That is what Akamai wants to treat. “Enterprises should not have to choose between speed and control when they put AI into production,” Jon Alexander, Senior Vice President of Cloud Technology at Akamai said in a press release.
“Some teams want to ship an AI feature this quarter on a managed platform. Others need dedicated GPUs to run frontier-class open models on their own terms. Every team running agents needs a boundary around the code those agents write,” he said.
Hijacking is another fear. In July, Zscaler found web pages hiding instructions meant for AI agents, a trick called indirect prompt injection. One fake documentation page told agents to pay a $3 "license fee" in about 0.0012 Ethereum to a hardcoded wallet, and four of the 26 models Zscaler tested complied.
Back in May cybersecurity firm Bugcrowd saw submissions more than quadruple in three weeks in March, most of them fake. HackerOne and Nextcloud suspended paid programs in April.
The machines also find real bugs. Mozilla said an early version of Anthropic's Claude Mythos helped find 271 vulnerabilities in Firefox, all patched within the week. That flood of real and fake findings is what security companies are now racing to manage.
Palo Alto closed its CyberArk purchase on Feb. 11 to extend privileged-access controls to AI agents. In April it bought Koi , which secures AI coding agents running on employee machines. Cisco announced a planned acquisition of Astrix Security in May, a firm that governs the keys and tokens agents use, and completed the deal June 29.
Akamai's piece is the fence around the code itself. Its sandbox uses WebAssembly, a format that runs programs in a tightly walled box, to cap an agent's computing power, memory and outbound connections. Akamai's Alexander said every team running agents "needs a boundary around the code those agents write."
Palo Alto's survey found organizations expect AI agents to grow 85% over the next 12 months, against 56% for human identities.

title: ‘NASS Must Not Approve A Single Dollar’, Atiku Tells Tinubu To Publish Loan Details
body: Former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has called on the National Assembly not to approve President Bola Tinubu’s proposed external loans until the President publishes full details of the projects to be funded. Atiku said the lawmakers must not approve “a single dollar” until the government provides details of every project, contract, cost, contractor, loan term and repayment obligation. He spoke after Tinubu requested the Senate’s approval to borrow $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion, a development Atiku said vindicated his October 12 warning about a loan plan of up to $20 billion. In a statement issued on Tuesday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said he had previously warned Nigerians about the proposed borrowing in connection with the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway. “On October 12, I warned Nigerians that President Tinubu was reportedly preparing to borrow up to $20 billion in connection with the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway. I demanded that he confirm or deny the plan and publish the accounts. He did neither. Today, he has asked the Senate to approve $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion in external loans. My warning has been vindicated,” he said. Atiku faulted the President for failing to provide a project-by-project account of how the proposed loans would be spent, arguing that listing broad sectors was not enough to justify the scale of the borrowing. “The President has listed broad sectors but has not provided Nigerians with a project by project account of what this enormous borrowing will fund. There are no clear project details, costs, locations or contractors for the public to scrutinise,” he said. The former vice president also questioned the rerouting of the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway inland, alleging that the project could be used to channel borrowed public funds to Tinubu’s political campaigners and favoured contractors. “That silence is especially troubling when the Coastal Highway has been rerouted inland. Nigerians have every right to ask whether the highway is being turned into a pipeline for borrowed money to reach Tinubu’s campaigners and favoured contractors,” Atiku said. He questioned the timing of the loan request, asking how the President could seek approval for more than $20 billion and €1 billion in additional debt barely 12 weeks before an election without identifying the projects and their costs. “Is this a development plan for Nigerians or a campaign financing scheme dressed up as infrastructure? Tinubu must answer,” he said. Atiku insisted that the National Assembly must make the proposal and its supporting documents public and subject them to rigorous scrutiny before taking a decision. “The National Assembly must not approve a single dollar until the President publishes every project, contract, cost, contractor, loan term and repayment obligation. No public money should be borrowed in the dark. No lawmaker should sign a blank cheque against Nigeria’s future,” he said. He added: “I warned Nigerians before this request reached the Senate. Now the burden is on Tinubu to prove that this borrowing will serve the country, not his political interests.” The post ‘NASS Must Not Approve A Single Dollar’, Atiku Tells Tinubu To Publish Loan Details appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Austal USA Hosts VCNO at Navy Additive Manufacturing Center of Excellence
body: MOBILE, Ala. — Austal USA welcomed Admiral James Kilby, Vice Chief of Naval Operations, at the Navy’s Additive Manufacturing Center of Excellence (AMCoE) in Danville, Va., on October 15. ADM Kilby was joined by Vice Admiral John B. “Brad” Skillman, Deputy Chief of Naval Operations for Integration of Capabilities and Resources; Vice Admiral Scott Gray, Deputy Chief of Naval Operations for Sustainment; Rear Admiral Kristin Acquavella, Commander Naval Supply Systems Command; and Rear Admiral Peter Small, Acting Commander Naval Sea Systems Command. Austal USA and their AMCoE partners hosted the senior Navy leaders for a briefing and tour of the state-of-the-art facility highlighting capabilities in additive manufacturing (AM), heat treatment, metrology and inspection, post processing, and testing. While touring the center, the Navy delegation witnessed first-hand the advancements being made in additive manufacturing that will benefit our military far into the future and the success of the efforts being put forth to equip a new workforce with the skills required by the Navy AM mission. “We were pleased to welcome back Admiral Kilby and Navy leadership to the Additive Manufacturing Center of Excellence and showcase the advanced capabilities being developed in Danville.,” stated Austal USA President, Gene Miller. “The progress being made in additive manufacturing and advanced inspection techniques will strengthen the Navy’s ability to produce critical parts and sustain the fleet with greater speed and flexibility. Austal USA is proud to support this important mission and to help build the technical expertise, industrial capacity, and partnerships needed to advance maritime readiness for decades to come.” The AMCoE’s mission is to build AM production capability and capacity in the submarine and maritime industrial base to improve fleet operational readiness. The Center’s work includes burning down non-recurring engineering to reach scale, supporting fleet modernization, maintenance, repair, and overhaul planning processes, and lowering barriers for AM suppliers and OEMs to deploy AM for Navy needs along with the digital infrastructure required to support it. “A skilled workforce and a strong industrial base are critical to maintaining our Navy’s warfighting advantage,” said Adm. Jim Kilby, Vice Chief of Naval Operations. “Here in Danville, ATDM equips workers with the advanced manufacturing expertise to strengthen supply chains, accelerate repairs, and return ships to sea faster. The Additive Manufacturing Center of Excellence is pushing the boundaries of engineering and technology to streamline production, drive innovation, and deliver capabilities our Sailors need. title: MoMo Fest 2026 promotes cashless shopping and digital financial inclusion in Kumasi
body: MoMo Fest 2026 has brought digital payments to traders and consumers at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi, allowing festival-goers to purchase food, clothing and other goods using mobile money. The event, supported by Mobile Money Fintech Ltd (MMFL), combined live entertainment with a marketplace featuring local vendors, with the MoMo App serving as the primary platform for transactions. Organisers say the initiative is aimed at expanding digital financial inclusion, encouraging businesses to adopt cashless payment systems and educating users on safer mobile money transactions. MTN Kumasi Territory Sales Controller, Samuel Owusu Baah, said the festival was designed to extend financial services to people at the grassroots level by making digital payments more accessible to traders and consumers. “We are organising a cashless market in Kumasi with vendors. We are ensuring that the financial inclusion we have been trumpeting with MTN MoMo reaches the grassroots, to ensure everyone is included,” he said. He explained that selected vendors had been brought together to sell their products while encouraging customers to pay electronically through the MoMo platform. Mr Owusu Baah said MTN staff were also available at the festival to help existing and prospective customers register for services and access products, including loans and savings. “MoMo is now an everyday thing, so our staff are also here to assist customers and prospective customers,” he said. He added that the initiative formed part of the company’s efforts to support livelihoods and strengthen its relationship with consumers in Kumasi. Festival promotes safer digital transactions Beyond encouraging cashless shopping, MMFL used the festival to educate patrons and vendors on mobile money fraud prevention. The education covered measures to protect accounts, identify scams and adopt safer digital financial practices as more people rely on electronic transactions. Vendors at the festival also offered discounts on selected products, providing an additional incentive for patrons to shop at the cashless marketplace. Ecobank offers on-site banking support Ecobank, the event’s main sponsor, provided on-site banking support to help patrons access its services, open accounts and resolve account-related challenges. A representative of the bank said its team was available to assist customers with the Ecobank account and mobile application, while also helping vendors interested in opening business accounts. “We are giving services and assisting customers to have the Ecobank account, Ecobank app and assist with problem solving. If you are a vendor and you need a business account we can assist you,” the representative said. The representative also highlighted a prepaid card available for online transactions, which the bank said was free and accessible to non-customers. The festival reflects efforts by financial service providers to integrate digital payments into everyday commercial activities while improving access to financial services for traders and consumers. Through the combination of cashless shopping, customer support and financial education, MoMo Fest 2026 seeks to encourage greater adoption of digital financial services among businesses and the wider public.

title: GECF member states concerned about impact of geopolitics on gas market stability
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Member states of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) have expressed concern regarding the impact of geopolitical developments, including those in the Middle East, on the stability of the gas market. They also highlighted increased investment risks and volatility in gas prices, according to the declaration adopted following the summit in Moscow.
"We, the Heads of State and Government of member countries of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum, gathered on October 27, 2026, the year marking the 25th anniversary of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum, for the eighth Gas Summit in Moscow <…> expressing our deep concern regarding the adverse impact of geopolitical developments, particularly in the Middle East, on the stability, security, and sustainability of the global gas market, including disruptions to gas supplies, heightened uncertainty regarding the security of gas supply and demand, increased investment risks, and significant volatility in gas prices," said the document released on the Kremlin’s website.
The Gas Exporting Countries Forum includes Russia, Iran, Algeria, Bolivia, Egypt, Equatorial Guinea, Libya, Nigeria, Qatar, Trinidad and Tobago, the United Arab Emirates, and Venezuela. Angola, Azerbaijan, Iraq, Malaysia, Mauritania, Mozambique, Peru, and Senegal are observer states. GECF members hold roughly 70% of the world’s proven gas reserves, account for 38% of global gas production and 42% of global gas exports, and represent 47% of global exports of liquefied natural gas (LNG).

title: Hanwha Defense USA to Acquire Hanwha Philly Shipyard
body: ARLINGTON, Va. — Hanwha Defense USA (HDUSA) announced it is acquiring a controlling stake in Hanwha Philly Shipyard , bringing the shipyard under HDUSA’s leadership and governance structure and strengthening its presence in the U.S. shipbuilding and defense market. The announcement follows HDUSA establishing a presence at the shipyard earlier this year to transition it into a dual-use yard building for the U.S. Navy and commercial customers. Since Hanwha acquired the shipyard in December 2024, Hanwha Systems has held a 60% stake, with Hanwha Ocean holding the remaining 40%. In September, Hanwha Systems announced plans to sell its stake to Hanwha Defense USA Shipbuilding LLC, an HDUSA-led joint venture with Hanwha FutureProof. HDUSA President of U.S. Shipbuilding RADM Tom Anderson (Ret. title: GECF member states intend to cooperate to protect gas infrastructure
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Member states of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) intend to strengthen cooperation on issues such as the uninterrupted operation of gas supply chains, the maintenance of freedom of navigation, and the protection of energy infrastructure, according to the declaration adopted following the summit in Moscow.
"We declare our shared determination to strengthen cooperation among GECF member countries in ensuring the continuity of global gas supply chains, upholding freedom of navigation and the unimpeded conduct of commercial operations, and protecting critical gas infrastructure, including production facilities, pipelines, and liquefied natural gas carriers, through the exchange of knowledge, joint risk assessment, and the development of coordination mechanisms to counter physical, cyber, and hybrid threats, thereby contributing to global economic stability," the document reads.
The Gas Exporting Countries Forum includes Russia, Iran, Algeria, Bolivia, Egypt, Equatorial Guinea, Libya, Nigeria, Qatar, Trinidad and Tobago, the United Arab Emirates, and Venezuela. Angola, Azerbaijan, Iraq, Malaysia, Mauritania, Mozambique, Peru, and Senegal are observer states. GECF members hold roughly 70% of the world’s proven gas reserves, account for 38% of global gas production and 42% of global gas exports, and represent 47% of global exports of liquefied natural gas (LNG).

title: Trump continues red-state campaign push with days until midterms
body:
Trump is set to attend campaign rallies in Texas on Tuesday.
President Donald Trump is barnstorming deep-red states across the country to defend GOP majorities in Congress as Democrats make inroads in some unlikely places.
As of Tuesday afternoon, the president has made 20 stops to states he handily won and six to battlegrounds since Sept. 9, according to ABC News tracking. Those include four in Texas, two in Ohio, two in Tennessee, and visits to states that for some observers may be surprising: Oklahoma, Kentucky and Alabama.
The president made his fourth campaign season trip to Texas -- a state he won in three presidential elections -- on Tuesday, where he is attending two rallies; Vice President JD Vance will be in Texas for a rally later this week. Trump's Tuesday trip and Vance's upcoming one means the president and vice president will have visited Texas -- typically reliably red -- eight times since Labor Day weekend.
An early October ReconMR poll found that among likely Texas voters, Texas Democratic state Rep. James Talarico had 48% support while Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton had 44% support, within the poll's margin of error.
Trump's red-state travels come with just days until the high-stakes midterm elections where control of Congress is at stake.
As Democratic candidates largely center their campaigns around affordability and ending the Iran war, they are fending off attacks from Republicans, largely on taxes, culture war and transgender issues. At the same time, Republicans are calling on the president and his Cabinet officials to heed voter economic concerns.
As Republicans look to shore up support among the MAGA faithful, Trump's approval ratings have suffered. His approval rating recently reached a record low of 33% in the ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos poll . About 7 in 10 Americans say that gas is unaffordable and that the country is headed in the wrong direction, according to the same poll.
On Monday, Trump hit the campaign trail in Mississippi, where no Democrat has been elected to the U.S. Senate since 1982. Trump carried the state by a 23-point margin in the 2024 presidential election. GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith is defending her seat against Democrat and district attorney Scott Colom.
"A lot of folks ain't gonna be able to make this rally because they can't afford the gas to get up here," Colom said at a press conference in Corinth ahead of Trump's rally in the city.
Trump said on Monday that he was supporting Hyde-Smith in the state because he "can't take a chance."
"I can't take a chance. She's got no problem. The only problem is sometimes, and this happens, and sometimes when you think somebody's doing so well, nobody wants – they all stay home," Trump said -- later adding "so that's why I'm here."
Last week, Trump campaigned in Kansas for Republican incumbent Sen. Roger Marshall, who is fighting in what ABC News is rating a toss-up race for reelection against Democrat Rev. Adam Hamilton. Vance stumped for the one-term incumbent in September and again on Monday.
Hamilton could break a 94-year losing streak for Democrats -- he is split even with Marshall among likely Kansas voters, according to a September New York Times/Siena University poll .
Trump is headed back to Kansas on Saturday in Salina, where he will need to run up the score in a county he carried by more than 30 points in 2024.
Several Republicans -- including Trump, Vance, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Speaker Mike Johnson -- have visited Wisconsin's closely watched 3rd Congressional District, where Democrat Rebecca Cooke is facing off against GOP incumbent Rep. Derrick Van Orden. ABC News recently shifted its rating from "toss-up" to "lean Democrat."
Trump surrogates are also flocking to Iowa, a state Trump won in the last three presidential elections. The president has already paid a visit to Sioux City and will headline a rally in Dubuque just two days before the midterms.
Iowa Democratic Senate candidate Josh Turek, a state lawmaker, is running against Republican Rep. Ashley Hinson to succeed outgoing GOP Sen. Joni Ernst.
Hinson has praised the president but also sought to distance herself at times and recently called for an end to the Iran war.
But Turek told ABC News it is "good" for Trump to see how healthcare funding cuts and tariffs have affected Iowans.
"I think that the war in Iran has hurt Iowa more than any other state," Turek said.
Kennedy is stumping for Iowa Republican gubernatorial candidate Zach Lahn on Wednesday. Johnson is headlining a rally for GOP incumbent Rep. Zach Nunn in the state's 3rd Congressional District that same day.
At least nine cabinet members visited Iowa in August, underscoring just how competitive the House races, open Senate and governor races have become.

title: Manhunt underway for convicted murderer who escaped from Tennessee prison
body:
Authorities are searching for a man convicted of murder who escaped from a Tennessee prison and stole a truck from a nearby farm.
Jacob Morley, who was serving a life sentence for killing a co-worker four years ago, was found to be missing from the Northwest Correctional Complex (NWCX) late on Sunday.
“At approximately 11:30 pm on October 25, 2026, staff at NWCX confirmed Morley was unaccounted for and immediately conducted an emergency count and search of the facility,” the Tennessee Department of Correction said in a news release .
“Further review of security cameras confirmed Morley breached the perimeter fence and exited the facility in his TDOC uniform,” the Tennessee Department of Correction said.
“Morley is serving a life sentence for a conviction in Carter County for first-degree murder, aggravated burglary, tampering with evidence, evading arrest, and vandalism. He is 28 years old, 5’11” tall, and weighs approximately 240 pounds. He has brown hair and green eyes,” the news release added.
The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation released surveillance video from the farm, showing Morley open the truck’s unlocked driver’s side door and drive off at around 1 a.m. on Monday.
Firefighters in Hornbeak, about 19 kilometres east of the farm, said on social media that investigators confirmed their cameras captured footage of the truck driving by their station about 15 minutes later.
By Tuesday afternoon, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation announced that the vehicle stolen by Morley was found abandoned in Marion, Illinois.
“Morley’s whereabouts remain unknown, and locating him continues to be an urgent priority for law enforcement,” the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation added.
“Public safety is our top concern. We are working around the clock with our local, state, and federal partners to track down Morley as quickly as possible,” authorities said.
Prison officials are asking for the public’s assistance in locating Morley and said he has been added to the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation’s Most Wanted list.
There is a reward of up to $2,500 available for information leading to Morley’s arrest.
Authorities are asking residents in the area to check home security and doorbell cameras, trail and hunting cameras, and other surveillance systems for possible sightings or activity.
Morley is serving a life sentence for killing co-worker Cody Birchfield in 2022, according to The Associated Press.
Birchfield’s body was found in a box under Morley’s home after he had been missing for a few weeks. The two lived in Carter County, in eastern Tennessee.
Along with first-degree murder, Morley was convicted of aggravated burglary, tampering with evidence, vandalism and evading arrest, The Associated Press reports.
When Morley saw deputies at his home, he led officers on a chase that ended in North Carolina, authorities said.

title: Fairbanks Morse Defense Awarded $100M Contract to Accelerate Global Submarine Availability
body: BELOIT, Wis. — October 27, 2026 — Fairbanks Morse Defense (FMD), a portfolio company of Arcline Investment Management, was awarded a $99.09 million contract to ensure the availability of U.S. attack submarines (SSNs) and ballistic missile submarines (SSBNs) into the 2030s by enacting critical life extension services. Under a Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA) contract, FMD will provide repair, parts and labor through 2030 for Emergency Diesel Generator (EDG) overhauls on six nuclear submarines. This follow-on, sole-source award comes as the U.S. Navy seeks to secure its global sea-based deterrent against near-peer competitors, Russia and China. The contract work is part of a mitigation strategy developed by the Navy to extend the service life of Ohio- and Los Angeles-class submarines by up to 14 years by working with OEMs to overhaul critical systems. “This contract is part of the ongoing investment in undersea power projection that we have seen not only from the United States and our friends in Europe, Australia and Canada, but also from Russia and China, who are actively growing and modernizing their submarine fleets,” said Keith Haasl, FMD President of Services and Technology. “Because the timely delivery of critical components dictates fleet availability, we are moving quickly to scale our capabilities. Our work with the Navy actively demonstrates principles of rapid submarine maintenance and overhaul that we can share with allies, so we can ensure operationally ready submarines faster.” The current contract supports completion of multiple EDG overhauls per year through 2030. FMD will employ its robotic welding platform for improved precision and speed. Robotic welding has proven to reduce manual welding times by up to two-thirds. To further accelerate timelines, FMD is applying the Pit Stop methodology to shrink depot maintenance periods from months to weeks. Inspired by NASCAR and Formula One, and co-developed with the U.S. Navy, Pit Stop eliminates “open and inspect” bottlenecks by pre-staging OEM parts needed for routine overhauls, driving a continuous cycle of component refurbishment. FMD’s use of robotics, automation and the Pit Stop methodology for critical systems offers a model for U.S. and allied navies to apply broadly to reduce depot-level maintenance delays and improve parts availability. Fulfillment of the contract effectively addresses the geopolitical risk of a post-2029 submarine deficit resulting from scheduled decommissionings and delays in new construction of Columbia-and Virginia-class vessels. FMD has successfully completed EDG overhauls on two Ohio-class and one Los Angeles-class submarine under a previous NAVSEA contract. As a trusted original equipment manufacturer of the power systems that safeguard submarine operations, FMD anticipates future opportunities to support the Navy’s submarine service life extension programs to secure the undersea deterrent throughout the next decade. title: Egypt, Bahrain and UAE Back Greece Over Turkey-Libya Maritime Deal
body: Greece gains regional support as three Arab states join Athens in challenging the Turkey-Libya maritime agreement, warning it threatens international law and Eastern Mediterranean stability. Greece has secured the backing of Egypt, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates in its dispute with Turkey over a controversial maritime agreement with Libya, as tensions over maritime boundaries and energy exploration continue in the Eastern Mediterranean. In a joint statement delivered to the United Nations in New York on Monday by Greek Foreign Minister George Gerapetritis, the four countries raised concerns about the agreement, warning that it could undermine regional security and established principles of international law. The diplomatic intervention follows the approval of the Turkey-Libya maritime accord by Libya’s eastern-based parliament last week, reviving a dispute that has shaped relations across the Eastern Mediterranean since 2019. Four countries challenge maritime agreement Greece, Egypt, Bahrain and the UAE warned that bilateral arrangements must not undermine international legal frameworks or establish precedents that threaten regional stability. Their joint statement expressed serious concerns about the agreement’s implications for security and stability, arguing that maritime arrangements must respect established rules of international law. Greece and Cyprus have long opposed the 2019 memorandum between Turkey and Libya, arguing that it disregards their maritime rights and claims in the Eastern Mediterranean. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, however, defended the agreement on Monday, dismissing criticism from the European Union and other parties as unjustified. The latest diplomatic move broadens the opposition to the agreement beyond Greece and Cyprus, bringing three Arab states into a coordinated effort to challenge its implications. Libya’s eastern parliament approves deal The maritime memorandum was signed in 2019 by Turkey and the internationally recognised Libyan Government of National Accord, based in Tripoli. However, Libya has remained divided between rival administrations since the 2011 uprising that toppled longtime leader Muammar Gaddafi. The agreement was opposed for years by the eastern Libyan administration associated with military commander Khalifa Haftar, whose forces fought to capture Tripoli in 2019 and 2020. Turkey provided crucial military support to the Tripoli government during that conflict, helping repel Haftar’s offensive. Relations between Ankara and eastern Libya have since improved, with Turkish officials making regular visits to Benghazi and Turkish businesses expanding their involvement in construction and other sectors. The eastern parliament’s recent approval adds a new dimension to the dispute, although Greece and Cyprus continue to reject the agreement’s implications for their maritime claims. Greece pursues energy exploration and maritime negotiations The dispute carries significant implications for energy exploration and potential offshore resources in the Eastern Mediterranean. Since the agreement was signed, Greece has moved forward with plans to explore for natural gas off Crete, awarding a licence to a consortium led by US energy company Chevron. Athens has also pursued a separate maritime delimitation agreement with Libya, seeking to establish boundaries through negotiations rather than unilateral arrangements. Gerapetritis said Greece remained ready to continue diplomatic efforts, calling on Libya to maintain constructive relations with its neighbours and respect international maritime rules as the country navigates its political transition. The dispute is particularly significant for Greece because maritime boundaries influence offshore energy exploration, access to potential natural gas reserves and the legal status of activities across the region. With Egypt, Bahrain and the UAE now joining Greece in its diplomatic opposition, Athens is seeking wider regional support for its position on maritime law.
