title: Oleshky humanitarian mission could be extended to other communities – Lubinets
body:
Parliamentary Human Rights Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets said this during a televised broadcast, Ukrinform reports.
“There is a preliminary agreement that the humanitarian mission in Oleshky could automatically be extended to other communities, because Oleshky is not the only place facing a humanitarian catastrophe. The Oleshky territorial community comprises several settlements, and thousands of civilians are affected,” Lubinets said.
The initial focus would be on settlements in the Kherson region, Lubinets said, adding, “…and then we are ready to move forward”.
As previously reported, US First Lady Melania Trump said she had secured a localized ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine covering only Oleshky, a town in the Russian-occupied part of the Kherson region.
According to the White House press office, the parties had agreed to temporarily halt all military activities in Oleshky to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and prepare for the evacuation of civilians through an agreed safe corridor.
On the morning of October 27, Head of the Presidential Office Kyrylo Budanov announced the launch of the humanitarian mission in Oleshky . A bilateral ceasefire was declared in the area where the mission is being conducted.
According to David Arakhamia, head of the parliamentary faction of the Servant of the People party, the ceasefire under US First Lady Melania Trump’s initiative to unblock Oleshky began at 3:00 a.m. Kyiv time on October 27 and will remain in effect until 10:59 p.m. on November 1 .

title: Corps Members’ Kidnap: Court Admits Evidence DSS Tendered Against Suspects
body: A High Court of Imo State, on Tuesday, resumed trial of five persons accused of kidnapping 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps members on Independence Day, admitted the evidence tendered against them by the Department of State Services (DSS). At the resumed sitting, the Court heard a continuation of the evidence of Ikem Emmanuel, the first principal witness, who testified that the defendants made confessional statements admitting to the crime of conspiracy, hostage-taking and unlawful possession of firearms. The witness tendered an audio visual recording of the confessions of the defendants. He also tendered their written statements, the recovered firearms and money in cash, recovered recovered from them. The Presiding Judge, Justice Emeka Orafu, in admitting the exhibits, ruled that the arms and money be kept in the custody of the DSS. The principal witness maintained that the defendants statements were obtained in the presence of their legal representatives and DSS legal officers. In a related matter involving two other kidnap suspects, the DSS officer also gave evidence on the investigation, stating that their confessional statements were taken under caution in the presence of their lawyers and DSS legal officers. He also tendered the audio visual recording of their statements, written statements money recovered in Naira, but for want of time, could not tender his report. At the conclusion of proceedings, the trial judge, Justice Orafu adjourned both matters to October 28th, 29th and 30th for continuation of hearing. He ordered that all the five defendants remain in custody of the DSS.

title: Show HN: I built flightdeck – Observability and control plane for AI agents
body:
Self-hosted · Apache 2.0 · Production and coding agents
Every LLM call, MCP event, and tool call your agents make streams to the dashboard as it happens, surfaced as a per-agent timeline and as a live fleet-wide feed. Set token budgets, MCP allow/block rules, and live directives on your production agents.
Coding agents attach via the Claude Code plugin .
Production agents add the flightdeck-sensor Python package to their entrypoint: init() + patch() , no other code changes.
One row per agent, sub-agents nested under their parents, events plotted as they arrive. Hover any event to inspect it; hovering pauses the stream.
Every agent on a shared timeline: LLM calls, embeddings, tool uses, MCP events, and structured errors, streamed as they happen. Click any event to inspect it.
Central token budgets per flavor, enforced in-process. Warn at 80%, swap to a cheaper model at 90%, block at 100%. Defaults, all configurable, every decision a structured event.
Stop one agent or an entire flavor from the dashboard; the signal delivers on the agent's next call. Register custom directives in Python and invoke them remotely.
Allowlist or blocklist the MCP servers your agents may talk to, per flavor. Misconfigured or unrecognized servers warn or block before the call leaves the process.
Multi-agent runs render as a tree: orchestrator parent, one child session per sub-agent, linked and labeled by role. Claude Code tasks, CrewAI agents, LangGraph nodes.
Token consumption, latency, model distribution, policy volume, and estimated cost, grouped by flavor, model, framework, host, team, or role.
Not a proxy. The sensor wraps SDK clients inside your agent's own process: init() + patch() , no other code changes, and calls go straight to the provider. Prompt capture is off by default in the sensor; the Claude Code plugin captures your own session by default and can be turned off.
The live fleet feed. Agents, events, run boundaries, and policy decisions on one shared clock.
Every agent with token, latency, error, and cost trends, plus a per-agent drawer and swimlane.
Filter every event by agent, type, framework, model, or MCP server. Click through to the run.
Inside Claude Code, install the plugin from the repo's marketplace:
Add the sensor to your entrypoint. Nothing else changes:
Run the stack itself with git clone https://github.com/flightdeckhq/flightdeck && cd flightdeck && make dev , dashboard on localhost:4000 . Docker Compose and a Helm chart cover production. Full walkthrough in the README .

title: Jalud families still unable to return to burned homes despite High Court order
body: The state acknowledged a sense of “shame and failure” before the High Court of Justice on Monday over an operation to return a Palestinian family to its home in Jalud that ended with its evacuation under attack, as the justices questioned why the residents remained displaced and their homes had burned despite an order intended to protect them.The Monday hearing returned to the case of three Palestinian petitioners whose homes near the West Bank village, south of Nablus, had been taken over by Israeli extremists. Seven weeks after the court ordered authorities to secure their return, the discussion concerned how to protect workers repairing the damaged houses before the residents could live in them again.“Sometimes, even when time is needed, there is no time,” Justice Dafna Barak-Erez told the deputy commander of the IDF's Judea and Samaria Division, pointing to the residents' inability to live in their homes and the destruction of their property.Supreme Court President Isaac Amit and Justice Yechiel Kasher also sat on the panel.Attorney Ghiath Nasser, representing the petitioners, said the case had begun before the houses burned and had now reached a worse position. His clients still wanted to return, he said, and the destruction had not changed that demand.High Court orders state to secure Palestinian families' return and restore access to homesOn September 6, the court ordered authorities to coordinate the petitioners' return within 14 days, provide security, and allow in equipment and supplies needed to repair the homes and restore water and electricity. It also required the state to explain why it should not restore access to the homes and remove roadblocks.The attempted return took place on the night of September 28-29. More than 100 Israeli extremists attacked security forces and prevented the Tubasi family from remaining at home. Three Border Police officers were wounded, and the family's two houses were burned.In their account filed with the court, the petitioners described arriving to find broken windows and doors and damaged electrical connections. Within minutes, a crowd began attacking the house with stones. Soldiers gathered the family in a corner to protect them before evacuating them in an armored vehicle under continued stone-throwing.The state's October 8 response described Border Police officers shielding the residents with their bodies after exhausting crowd-control ammunition. It said Israelis entered the houses while the family was inside, and the brigade commander ordered the residents evacuated for their protection.At Monday's hearing, state attorney Avi Milikovsky acknowledged the operation had ended in failure but rejected the suggestion that this reflected indifference to the court's order. Officers had risked themselves to protect the residents, he said.The homes were now burned and unsuitable for an immediate return, Milikovsky told the court.Dispute over damage assessment delays repairs to Palestinian homes in JaludNasser said his request to bring in engineers to assess the damage had gone unanswered. Milikovsky said coordination was being handled through the military's local liaison office, which had conducted a damage-assessment visit.Amit distinguished a brief inspection from the protection needed for sustained repairs. Workers would need to remain at the houses over a period of time, he said. Barak-Erez said that protection was an integral part of allowing the residents to return.The justices also sought an explanation for Nasser's allegation that the September fire burned for seven hours without being extinguished.“If soldiers can be there, fire engines can be there too,” Barak-Erez said after the deputy division commander referred to the difficulty of bringing Israeli fire engines into Area B, where the houses are located.The officer said he needed to check what happened in this specific incident rather than give an improvised answer. Milikovsky proposed providing a supplementary written response.Kasher also asked how the third petitioner's house had subsequently burned. Nasser had informed the court that Tawfiq Shweiki's home caught fire on October 24, after settlers had been staying there. Responsibility for that fire remained disputed; Nasser told the justices he did not know who had burned the house.The deputy division commander, identified as Col. A., said the army was bound by the law and responsible for creating conditions for the families' safe return. The outposts in the relevant Area B sector should not exist, he said.He cited arrests, search warrants, vehicle seizures and repeated operations against the outposts, while describing competing demands arising from attacks elsewhere, the olive harvest and the election period. A lasting return required preparation, intelligence and forces to protect both the repairs and the families, he said.Barak-Erez also challenged the failure to meet the original deadline.“If it is 14 days, it is not 15 or 16,” she said, adding that an extension should have been sought in advance. “That is not the biggest problem in this case; it is only the symptom.”Petitioners seek NIS 50,000 daily fine as state disputes contempt sanctionsThe petitioners have sought enforcement through contempt proceedings, including a daily NIS 50,000 fine. The state opposes that request, arguing that it acted to carry out the order and that the failed operation does not justify contempt sanctions.Asked to give a timeframe for the preparations, the officer estimated up to 30 days, while stressing that operational circumstances could affect it. His estimate was not a new court deadline.Amit closed the hearing by saying a decision would follow.Yonah Jeremy Bob contributed to this report.

title: Three TLS Bugs in GoAhead
body:
GoAhead is used in hundreds of millions of IoT, Firewall, OT, and Military devices including those from Palo Alto Networks, Comcast, D-Link, HP, Canon, Honeywell, GE, Oracle, Siemens, Rockwell, Digi, Lockheed Martin, Boeing, and more.
Three independent bugs in GoAhead's TLS integrations can leave revoked client certificates accepted, encrypted sessions recoverable to an observer or a configured chain-depth limit unenforced. Exposure depends on the TLS library and the verification settings built into the device:
OpenSSL-compatible backend - Critical, CVSS 9.1 - CRL loaded but not enforced, revoked client certificates are silently accepted. GOAHEAD-SA-2026-0006.
LibreSSL legacy verifier - High, CVSS 7.4 - An over-depth client chain is accepted when client certificates are required but issuer checking is disabled. This bypasses the chain-depth restriction. GOAHEAD-SA-2026-0004.
Mbed TLS - Medium, CVSS 5.9 - A buffer-length typo reduces a 2048-bit DH modulus to one byte. TLS 1.2 DHE_RSA sessions are decryptable when the client accepts the broken parameters. GOAHEAD-SA-2026-0005.
mTLS enabled with a CRL configured. Revoked client certificates remain accepted even with issuer verification enabled.
TLS 1.2 DHE_RSA negotiated with a client that accepts the broken DH parameters.
Upgrade to 6.1.1 or later , disable finite-field DHE suites, or use the OpenSSL backend.
LibreSSL legacy verifier â 3.2.x or 3.3.2â3.3.6
VERIFY_PEER=1 and VERIFY_ISSUER=0 . An over-depth client chain is accepted.
Enable VERIFY_ISSUER=1 with a trusted CA bundle, or use OpenSSL / LibreSSL 4.x.
GoAhead is an embedded web server used for device management: routers, switches, printers, gateways, and industrial controls and is deployed in hundreds of millions of devices.
Each finding below affects a specific subset of those deployments, depending on the build and configuration.
GoAhead supports two TLS backends: OpenSSL, the default, and MbedTLS. The OpenSSL backend also works with compatible libraries such as LibreSSL.
GoAhead takes a compile-time approach regarding certain configurations:
- ME_GOAHEAD_SSL_VERIFY_PEER=1 requires a client certificate.
- ME_GOAHEAD_SSL_AUTHORITY points at a PEM bundle of trusted CAs.
- ME_GOAHEAD_SSL_VERIFY_ISSUER=1 requires the certificate chain to establish issuer trust against that bundle.
- ME_GOAHEAD_SSL_REVOKE points at a PEM-encoded Certificate Revocation List.
- The OpenSSL backend sets a chain-depth limit of 10 ( VERIFY_DEPTH ).
GoAhead's OpenSSL backend loads the configured CRL into the certificate store but never enables revocation checking. Revoked client certificates can therefore complete the mTLS handshake even when issuer verification is enabled.
OpenSSL requires X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK to enable CRL checking. Loading the file into the store does not set that flag. Without CRL or OCSP checking enabled, check_revocation() returns success before checking revocation status:
GoAhead never sets either CRL flag. OpenSSL returns success without checking the loaded list. The application's callback would reject error 23, X509_V_ERR_CERT_REVOKED , through its default: branch, but the verifier never generates that error.
On GoAhead 6.1.0 with OpenSSL 3.6.2, a revoked CA-signed client certificate completed the mTLS handshake with issuer verification enabled. The verification callback reported error 0 throughout the chain:
X509_STORE_load_locations() succeeds, so startup produces no warning that CRL enforcement is inactive.
Affected: GoAhead 3.4.5 through 6.1.0 using the OpenSSL-compatible backend with a CRL configured. The security impact is clearest with VERIFY_PEER=1 , a trusted CA bundle, and VERIFY_ISSUER=1 : a previously trusted but revoked identity retains access. When issuer checking is disabled, the CRL defect remains but unknown issuers are already accepted by policy.
Fix : 6.1.1 now checks after loading the CRL:
GoAhead's mbed TLS backend configures the RFC 3526 2048-bit DH group through mbedtls_ssl_conf_dh_param_bin() . The modulus length passed to that function is taken from the generator buffer:
The size arguments tell mbed TLS how many bytes to read from each buffer. The call uses sizeof(dhm_g) for both, even though dhm_g is only one byte long. The length for dhm_p should be sizeof(dhm_p) , or 256 bytes.
As a result, mbed TLS reads only the first byte of dhm_p : 0xFF (255). The remaining 255 bytes are discarded. It accepts this value and sends it to the client during the TLS 1.2 DHE_RSA handshake:
In ServerKeyExchange, 00 01 ff identifies a one-byte DH parameter with the value 255. It should contain the full 256-byte value.
The broken parameters leave just eight possible shared-secret values : 01 , 02 , 04 , 08 , 10 , 20 , 40 and 80 in hex. An observer can try each candidate and identify the correct one by checking whether it decrypts the captured traffic successfully.
In the attached PoC, I managed to reproduce the shared secret after five attempts. It matched the client's secret, confirming that the same TLS session keys could be derived to decrypt the HTTP exchange.
A passive observer can decrypt captured sessions using the recorded handshake and encrypted application records completely out of band.
Exploitation requires a client that accepts the broken DH parameters. The tested OpenSSL client rejected them with DH_check_params_ex: modulus too small . Permissive clients, including custom or embedded implementations without a minimum-size check, can complete a decryptable session. ECDHE sessions and TLS 1.3 are unaffected by this configured finite-field group.
Affected: GoAhead 4.0.2 through 6.1.0 using the mbed TLS backend with TLS 1.2 DHE_RSA suites, where the client accepts the parameters. The typo entered in 2018 during migration to the binary-parameter API and survived the April 2024 TLS refactor. Mbed TLS 4.x removed the TLS_DHE_* suites, so this DHE path isn't impacted.
If you see any of these suites in the JA4S logs of your environment, you might be impacted (eg. t120100_009f_1ca028f07214 )
A sample query you might want to run (in Splunk or other) would look like:
replacing 0014 with the curves listed above.
Essentially, an attacker can present a certificate chain longer than GoAheadâs limit and still complete the mTLS handshake on an affected build. LibreSSL reports an issuer error instead of a depth error. GoAhead accepts that issuer error when issuer checking is disabled.
GoAhead 6.1.0 sets a chain-depth limit of 10 using SSL_CTX_set_verify_depth(sslctx, VERIFY_DEPTH) . Its verification callback also checks the depth:
That check only assigns a depth error when ok is true, the reported depth exceeds the limit, and no error is already present. The callback then classifies the error:
Error 20, UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY , is tolerated when issuer checking is disabled. Error 22, CERT_CHAIN_TOO_LONG , is rejected.
LibreSSL 3.2.x and 3.3.2â3.3.6 use the legacy X.509 verifier by default for peer verification. Its chain-building loop contains a FIXME comment (which is what prompted a look at GoAhead in the first place):
The loop stops building the chain without recording the depth error. The failure later reaches GoAhead as error 20. With VERIFY_ISSUER=0 , the callback accepts it.
On GoAhead 6.1.0 linked against LibreSSL 3.3.6, a 17-certificate chain rooted in an attacker-controlled, self-signed CA produced the following callback trace:
The handshake completed and the resource behind the client-certificate requirement returned HTTP 200. The same GoAhead source built against LibreSSL 4.3.1 received error 22 at depth 10 and rejected the chain.
With VERIFY_ISSUER=0 , ordinary self-signed certificates are already allowed. The over-depth chain bypasses the separate chain-depth restriction because the verifier reports a tolerated issuer error. Deployments requiring a trusted client CA reject it.
Demonstrated configuration: GoAhead 6.1.0 with the LibreSSL legacy verifier, ME_GOAHEAD_SSL_VERIFY_PEER=1 , and ME_GOAHEAD_SSL_VERIFY_ISSUER=0 . Enabling issuer trust rejects error 20. OpenSSL, BoringSSL, AWS-LC, and LibreSSL 4.x builds are not exposed to this legacy-verifier trigger.
All three findings affect GoAhead's integration with its TLS libraries. CRL enforcement depends on a verification flag, DH parameters depend on the supplied buffer lengths, and chain-depth enforcement depends on how verification errors are handled. None of these defects prevents the affected handshake from completing.
The backend and build configuration determine which defects apply. LibreSSL builds can inherit both the CRL defect in the OpenSSL-compatible backend and the legacy verifier's depth issue. The mbed TLS backend uses a separate verification path but is affected by the DH truncation when a client accepts the parameters.
To find impacted publicly facing servers in your fleet, here are the JA4Scan-TLS fingerprints that map to the different backends:

LibreSSL 4.3.1 (depth bypass unaffected)

title: Sheikh Khaled attends dinner hosted by Canada's PM during official visit
body: Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed , Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, has attended a dinner hosted by Prime Minister Mark Carney during his official visit to Canada. Mr Carney welcomed Sheikh Khaled and expressed hope that the visit would further strengthen friendship and co-operation between the UAE and Canada. Sheikh Khaled thanked Mr Carney for the warm welcome and generous hospitality extended to him and the accompanying delegation. During the dinner, discussions included UAE-Canada relations and ways to elevate them to new levels of co-operation. Several issues of mutual interest were also discussed with a shared focus on deepening the strategic partnership between the two nations. The high-level UAE delegation includes Dr Sultan Al Jaber, Minister of Industry and Advanced Technology; Reem Al Hashimy, Minister of State for International Co-operation; Dr Thani Al Zeyoudi, Minister of Foreign Trade; and Mohamed Alsuwaidi, Minister of Investment. Sheikh Khaled's visit comes weeks after President Sheikh Mohamed spoke by phone with Mr Carney to explore efforts to deepen partnerships, with a focus on the economy, investment and advanced technology. The Abu Dhabi Crown Prince's visit to Canada reflects the UAE's broader diplomatic efforts to deepen partnerships with key global allies. In July, the UAE finalised a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement ( Cepa ) with Canada , which aims to reduce trade barriers for goods, services and investment. Sheikh Khaled's trip to Canada comes just days after he completed an official visit to Greece, where he met Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis . The two countries strengthened their growing relations during the visit, with the UAE agreeing to invest a further €15 billion ($16.8 billion) in Greece as part of a joint initiative. Sheikh Khaled also represented the UAE at the Brics Summit in India last month and met Xi Jinping, President of China, during an official visit to the country in April.

title: Omoluorogbo Grammar School at 50: Aiyedatiwa to Inaugurate Administrative Block, Flag Off Classroom Projects
body: Preparations for the golden jubilee celebration of Omoluorogbo Grammar School, Akure, Ondo State, have reached an advanced stage, with Governor Lucky Orimisan Aiyedatiwa expected to inaugurate a completed ultra-modern administrative block and perform the groundbreaking ceremony for two new four-classroom block projects initiated by the school’s alumni. The events, scheduled for Saturday, form part of activities marking the institution’s 50th anniversary and underscore the alumni community’s commitment to improving educational infrastructure and securing a brighter future for the school. The completed administrative block and proposed classroom projects form part of a legacy infrastructure initiative comprising four four-classroom blocks planned for the school. The initiative is designed to address the institution’s infrastructural needs, enhance the learning environment and provide a more conducive atmosphere for teaching and learning. The projects, championed by the alumni, reflect a collective determination to translate the golden jubilee celebration into tangible development that will benefit current students and generations to come. The anniversary, themed “Celebrating Our Legacy, Shaping the Future,” with the motto “Five Decades of Excellence and Impact,” is expected to attract former students, government representatives, traditional rulers, religious leaders, members of the school community and other distinguished guests. The Chairman of the OGSA 50th Anniversary Planning and Implementation Committee, Hon. Kayode Akinmade, said alumni sets across different graduating years were intensifying preparations to ensure a successful and memorable celebration. He said the various sets were mobilising members, coordinating reunion activities and supporting programmes designed to commemorate the school’s five decades of educational service. Akinmade also disclosed that encouraging indications had been received from alumni groups in the diaspora, including members in the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada and parts of Asia, particularly China and Japan, who had expressed their intention to participate in the historic reunion. Their anticipated participation, he said, would add an international dimension to the celebration while strengthening the bonds among former students across geographical boundaries. The three-day celebration will commence on Thursday, October 29, with an interdenominational thanksgiving service, alumni reunion, mentorship and networking activities. Friday, October 30, will feature inter-house sports and social engagements involving former students and members of the school community. The grand finale will hold on Saturday, October 31, at the school premises in Akure, beginning at 10:00 a.m. Activities for the day will include the commissioning of the completed administrative block, the groundbreaking ceremony for the two four-classroom block projects, goodwill messages from invited dignitaries and stakeholders, and the presentation and launch of the golden jubilee legacy project. A keynote address will be delivered by Dr. Mogaji Stephen Alaba of the Federal University Oye-Ekiti on the topic, “The Past, the Present and the Future.” The programme will also feature a discussion on “The Future of Omoluorogbo Grammar School, Akure: Challenges and Solutions,” alongside cultural presentations and other anniversary activities. Akinmade said the golden jubilee was more than an occasion to celebrate the institution’s history, describing it as an opportunity for alumni and other stakeholders to renew their commitment to the school’s development. He noted that the classroom projects represented a practical demonstration of the alumni’s resolve to invest in the institution and create a lasting legacy for present and future students. The planning committee has called on alumni, parents, corporate organisations, philanthropists, government agencies and well-meaning individuals to support the school’s development initiatives and participate actively in the anniversary celebration. As Omoluorogbo Grammar School marks 50 years of educational heritage, the golden jubilee offers an opportunity for reflection, reunion, gratitude and renewed commitment to academic excellence and institutional growth.

title: Emir of Qatar says Doha proud of scale of its investment in Russian companies
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Qatar takes pride in the scale of its investments in Russian companies and plans to expand economic cooperation with Russia, Emir of Qatar Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani said at a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
"Relations between the Russian Federation and Qatar are strong, solid, and historic. <...> We take pride in the volume of Qatari investment in Russian companies," he said.
Bilateral relations have developed actively in the economic and investment fields over the past ten years, he noted, adding that the parties are closely monitoring the implementation of joint projects through the intergovernmental commission.

title: Countries take first step toward global crackdown on environmental crime
body: Negotiations are set to begin on the world’s first international protocol to fight environmental crime, including wildlife trafficking, illegal deforestation, and illicit waste smuggling. The protocol, to be drafted over the next two years, aims to make it easier to investigate, prosecute, and adjudicate these crimes. The negotiations will take place under the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime (UNTOC), a global treaty established in 2003 to combat international criminal networks, money laundering, and corruption. The resolution to begin drafting the protocol was approved Oct. 23 at the treaty’s 13th biennial gathering. “This is a landmark moment in the global fight against environmental crime,” Alice Pasqualato, global policy specialist for environmental crime at U.S.-based NGO Wildlife Conservation Society, said in a press release. The proposal was put forward by 12 countries — eight from Latin America and four from Africa — led by Brazil. It secured more than the required two-thirds majority: Of the 112 parties physically or electronically present and cast a vote, 83 voted in favor and 12 against. The latter included the U.S. and Japan. Another 27 countries abstained. The decision “sends a powerful message that governments recognize the scale, seriousness and interconnected nature of environmental crime,” Mark Jones, head of policy at U.K-based NGO Born Free, said in a press release. “We commend the States that developed, tabled and supported this resolution and look forward to engaging constructively in the negotiations ahead.” The draft protocol will be discussed at the next UNTOC gathering in two…This article was originally published on Mongabay

title: Northrop Grumman CEO says Sentinel missile on track for first flight in 2027
body: Warden said Northrop completed the first full vertical assembly of an inert missile at Vandenberg Space Force Base during the third quarter. Speaking to analysts on October 20, she said the program was progressing as planned through testing and development milestones. The missile will undergo further integration and a rigorous test campaign, while design work continues on launch facilities, including silos and command centers. Northrop is also developing the command-and-control systems needed to integrate the equipment and enable the government to operate it. Warden said all three development efforts would continue over the next several years, leading into an integrated test campaign. Toward the end of the decade, the company expects to look at increasing production across both the missile and infrastructure portions of the program. “Toward the end of the decade, we will begin looking at ramping production on all aspects of the program,” Warden said. She stressed that the company’s immediate task remained completing development. “And yet our focus in these next several years will be on completing the development program,” she said. Warden expects Sentinel to contribute to Northrop’s growth through the 2030s as work shifts from development into production. Chief Financial Officer John Greene said Northrop recorded an additional $2 billion in Sentinel awards during the quarter. Increased activity on the program, together with higher tactical solid rocket motor volumes, helped drive a 12% increase in Defense Systems sales to $2.3 billion. Asked how Sentinel would contribute before production expands, Warden said the program had been growing modestly faster than Northrop overall. She expects its growth to remain around the company’s rate or slightly above it over the coming years.

title: Brazil’s Flávio Bolsonaro misses passport handover, compliance unclear
body:
A deadline for defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro to surrender his regular and diplomatic passports expired at noon Tuesday, but it remained unclear whether he had complied.
Bolsonaro, 45, was served with the order Monday, a day after his stunning loss to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Bolsonaro said he received it outside the home where his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, is under house arrest serving out a 27-year sentence for attempting a coup following his 2022 election loss to Lula.
The sealed Supreme Court order, viewed by The Associated Press, was issued Sunday. Bolsonaro has refused to concede defeat and has made unsubstantiated allegations of election fraud.
Bolsonaro’s whereabouts Tuesday were unclear, and a spokesperson did not respond to an AP request for comment. It is also unclear whether Bolsonaro’s passports had been turned over.
Bolsonaro initially asked for the election results to be annulled after an evening of chaos at some polling places that prompted authorities to extend voting by two hours. On Monday, he urged the electoral court to investigate alleged election fraud and nullify Lula’s and Vice President Geraldo Alckmin’s candidacies, which it has never done before.
To overturn the result, Bolsonaro would have to present evidence of fraud affecting Lula’s 4.4 million-vote margin and convince the eight-member electoral court before the results are certified on Dec. 18.
Lula, who turned 81 on Tuesday, received more than 64 million votes, compared with fewer than 60 million for Bolsonaro, a margin of nearly four per cent.
Bolsonaro said in a video posted Monday on his social media channels that he had no plans to leave Brazil and instead was attempting to organize opposition among his congressional colleagues to the election results. His eight-year term as a senator expires Jan. 31, 2027, which will also cause him to lose special jurisdiction at the country’s Supreme Court.
Bolsonaro is under investigation by Brazil’s Supreme Court for alleged corruption, money laundering and tax evasion in two cases. In one, he’s accused of using a sports betting company to launder fraudulent deductions from government pensions to senior citizens. In the other, he is accused of accepting millions of dollars from a disgraced banker.
He has denied any wrongdoing in both cases.
Prosecutors suspect the funds from the banker were used to pay his brother Eduardo Bolsonaro’s expenses and to promote Flávio Bolsonaro’s political agenda with the Trump administration, documents show.
Brazilians had earlier taken to social media to ask where Bolsonaro was. Reporters gathered outside his home in the capital, Brasilia, but he did not appear.
A spokesperson for the Ministry of Security of Argentina denied reports the Brazilian senator had entered the country. Brazilian media outlets reported that many Bolsonaro allies had been unable to reach him.
Paulo Figueiredo, a close ally of Bolsonaro’s who lives in the United States, was asked about the senator’s whereabouts and did not answer directly.
“At this moment — following months of intense work that were unfairly thwarted — I have no desire to speak with the press. I kindly ask that you do not persist. Should I have a statement to make on any matter, I will reach out,” Figueiredo said.

title: Russia’s Crude Exports Set to Fall as Diesel Production Rises
body:
Goldman Sachs Raises December Brent Oil Price Forecast to $105
Julianne Geiger is a veteran energy journalist and market analyst with more than a decade of experience covering the global oil and gas sector. Her…
Russia's crude exports from its western ports could fall by as much as 200,000 barrels per day in November as refiners increase diesel production under Moscow's new agreement with Washington, according to preliminary loading schedules cited by Reuters on Tuesday.
Two traders expect shipments from Russia's Baltic and Black Sea ports to decline by 100,000 to 200,000 bpd from October. The estimates include Kazakh crude transported through Russian pipelines.
Russian refineries have increased processing since the October 9 diesel agreement between Presidents Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, helped by the return of facilities from maintenance. Moscow has issued new diesel export quotas after restricting shipments earlier this year to address domestic fuel shortages, while Washington has eased sanctions on Russian fuel exports.
The arrangement gives Russia an opportunity to increase diesel sales during a global fuel shortage, although its refineries will need more crude to sustain higher processing rates. Russian oil production, however, has been declining for months.
OPEC secondary-source estimates put September production at 8.64 million bpd, the lowest since mid-2020 and the tenth consecutive monthly decline. Moscow also lowered its 2026 production forecast in September to a 17-year low.
Russia's seaborne crude exports were already struggling in October. Shipments averaged 3.59 million bpd in the four weeks through October 18, down 110,000 bpd from the previous period. Weekly exports fell to 3.13 million bpd, their lowest since March, following a temporary suspension of loading at Primorsk.
At Novorossiysk, crude loadings are facing delays of nearly three weeks, according to the traders, with threats to shipping in the Black Sea limiting exports. Further Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries could also derail plans to increase diesel production in November, leaving more crude available for export than currently expected.
Less Urals crude is also expected to move through the Northern Sea Route as Arctic navigation winds down for the season.
Russia's ability to increase diesel exports will depend on refinery availability and sufficient crude supply, both of which remain constrained after months of Ukrainian attacks and declining domestic production.

title: Nasa astronaut stranded on ISS for nine months praises UAE's space ambitions
body: Indian-American astronaut Sunita Williams has hailed the UAE 's commitment to space exploration as she revealed what it was like to be stranded on the International Space Station for nine months. “The UAE is already committed to having astronauts fly in space,” Ms Williams said at an event in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday. The nation's ambition to become a leading spacefaring nation was clear, she added, as was its intention to work collaboratively with other countries to make scientific discoveries. During her 27-year-career, the 61-year-old has spent 608 days in space, providing her with a unique insight into the sector. What was meant to be an eight-day-long test flight in 2024 ended up with Ms Williams calling the ISS home for 286 days after her crew's Boeing Starliner encountered technical failures and was sent back unmanned. “Getting used to gravity is tough. This time, I was about 10 years older than when I flew last time and it took quite an adjustment,” Ms Williams told The National . Recovery from that trip took longer too – almost two years rather than the one year it took following her previous space mission. “I could definitely tell this time it took a little bit of a toll on me, but I'm finally feeling like I'm getting the speed. I'm back, I can't escape gravity,” she said at the UAE Space Biotech and LEO (Low Earth Orbit) Commercialisation Symposium in Masdar City. “This is a new chapter,” said Ms Williams, who now works as an astronaut adviser at commercial space flight firm Vast. “Of course, I'd like to fly again. But that's not my role right now. My role is to help start these companies up and get things going.” Vast, a US space infrastructure company founded in 2021, hopes to provide commercial alternatives for the international space station, which is due to be phased out in 2030 or 2031. The company's first space station, Haven-1, will launch in early 2027. Final frontier The UAE's impact on the space sector is only going to grow with the advances made by commercial companies, said one expert. “As commercial stations emerge, the UAE has an opportunity to help shape the future of research,” said Salem Al Qubaisi, director general of the UAE Space Agency. “Our strategy promotes international partnership, reciprocal access to facilities and joint missions. Our focus must remain on clear solutions for Earth, not only space.” Space exploration requires global collaboration, said Mohammed Al Mulla, a former Dubai Police pilot selected in 2021 to join the UAE's astronaut programme. “We learnt that we need to go to space together. It's never been someone or a country by itself,” Mr Al Mulla said at the event. “It's all about collaboration … and nowadays, [the] private sector is doing a great job pushing space technology even further and faster so that it will be a huge collaboration in the future.” The UAE's National Space Strategy 2031 aims to bring together research, industry and investment to enable national companies to contribute to developing and manufacturing advanced space technologies. The country also has ambitions to be one of the world’s 10 leading space economies by 2031. The first commercial satellite to be built entirely in the UAE was launched this month in what has been hailed as a major leap forward in the nation's quest to be a global leader in the space sector. Altair-1, designed, assembled and tested in Abu Dhabi, blasted off from Vandenburg Space Force Base in California aboard the Transporter-18 ride-share mission. In May, Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence, unveiled a Dh1 billion ($272.2 million) strategy to advance the UAE's role in the space sector. Sheikh Hamdan said the launch of the International Space Co-operation Programme would support the country's mission to cement its growing status as a major player in the booming industry.

title: CFTC Again Probes Polymarket Over Whether It Let Americans Trade
body: Bitcoin Magazine CFTC Again Probes Polymarket Over Whether It Let Americans Trade The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is investigating whether Polymarket broke a 2022 enforcement settlement, according to Reuters reporting earlier today. The probe revives an inquiry the agency closed in 2025 without filing charges. For a platform that has tried to fit prediction markets inside US law, the question strikes at its core. Polymarket settled with the CFTC in January 2022 and paid a $1.4 million penalty for offering event-based binary options without registration. The company agreed to block American users from its offshore exchange. Geofencing tools followed, but regulators and critics pointed to traders who reached the site through VPNs. The platform has also courted crypto natives, adding bitcoin deposits in October 2025 as part of a broader push to fund accounts with digital assets. According to the sources, investigators are examining three areas: the adequacy of Polymarket’s location controls, its advertising inside the United States, and the onboarding and customer protections on its US platform, which launched late last year. The company is headquartered in New York and runs its offshore exchange through a Panama-registered entity. A probe is an inquiry, not a finding, and many investigations end without enforcement. Polymarket’s mounting regulatory scrutiny The inquiry sits inside a wider effort. In June, the Wall Street Journal reported that Polymarket paid individuals to produce videos of fictitious winning bets, and senators Adam Schiff and John Curtis urged the agency to open a probe. Bloomberg reported that investigators were examining the company’s social media activity. CFTC Chairman Michael Selig has framed prediction markets as tools for hedging and information discovery, and he has argued that federal regulators, not states, should oversee them. Enforcement director David Miller has pledged tough policing of the sector. Enforcement pressure has a test case. In April, prosecutors charged a US soldier, Gannon Ken Van Dyke, with making $400,000 from insider bets on the offshore platform. The indictment says he used a VPN and an “exit mode” that appeared to sit in a foreign country. Van Dyke has denied the charges, and Polymarket says it referred the matter to authorities. Scale raises the stakes. Intercontinental Exchange, the parent of the NYSE, agreed in October 2025 to invest roughly $2 billion, and Bloomberg counted founder Shayne Coplan, 27, among the youngest self-made billionaires. The bigger the platform, the more its geographic walls matter. Earlier this year, Polymarket’s five-minute Bitcoin up/down contract was exploited by a small group of traders who pushed Binance’s price in the final seconds before each close, according to a study. Just 821 wallets, about one in 300 traders, took $8.2 million in the pushed cycles, and 93% of the losses fell on retail bettors. The authors of the study found no manipulation in the fifteen-minute contract, since a longer window dilutes a fixed push, a lesson that matters now that Nasdaq and Cboe have filed to list similar binary contracts on equity indices. This post CFTC Again Probes Polymarket Over Whether It Let Americans Trade first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman .

title: Ghana developing first National Action Plan on Youth, Peace and Security – Osman Ayariga
body: Ghana is developing its first National Action Plan on Youth, Peace and Security to strengthen young people’s participation in conflict prevention, peacebuilding and national security, Chief Executive Officer of the National Youth Authority (NYA), Osman Ayariga, has announced. Speaking on behalf of the Minister for Youth Development and Empowerment at the ECOWAS Ministerial Consultation on Youth, Peace and Security in Accra on Tuesday, October 27, Mr Ayariga said the initiative reflects Ghana’s commitment to giving young people a meaningful role in shaping peace and security policies. He said young people must be recognised not only as beneficiaries of peace and security interventions but also as partners in developing and implementing solutions to challenges confronting their communities and the sub-region. Mr Ayariga said the proposed action plan would provide a framework for strengthening youth participation in peacebuilding and conflict prevention, while supporting efforts to promote stability and security across West Africa.

title: Russia values emir of Qatar’s efforts to advance ties, Putin says
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Russia appreciates the personal contribution of Qatar's Emir Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani to the promotion of friendly relations between the two countries, President Vladimir Putin told the emir.
"We appreciate, Your Highness, your personal attention and contribution to the promotion of friendly and mutually beneficial relations between Russia and Qatar," Putin said, thanking Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani for coming to Moscow for the summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum.
"Bilateral cooperation is steadily developing, a meaningful political dialogue has been established, and the Russian-Qatari intergovernmental commission is operating, headed by First Deputy Prime Minister of the Russian government, Mr. Manturov, on the Russian side," Putin added.

title: Sharjah announces women-only clock tower in Kalba and care complex on Khor Fakkan Road
body: Sheikh Dr Sultan bin Muhammad Al Qasimi, Ruler of Sharjah , has announced a new clock tower dedicated to women, to be built near Kalba University, opposite the existing clock tower. Construction of the new tower is under way, the emirate's media office said. Sheikh Dr Sultan hoped the new tower would bring people joy. Sheikh Dr Sultan spoke about the new tower during a phone-in on Direct Line , a popular daily radio and television programme. Talking about launching projects, he recalled happy childhood memories of the inauguration of Al Islah Al Qasimia School. He said the existing clock tower is for men, while a second tower is being built primarily for women at the opposite end of the university grounds. The new tower features an attractive design and scenic views of the surrounding area. Its location was carefully chosen to keep it far enough from nearby homes to preserve residents’ privacy. The tower has the university to the west, and the co-operative society, Kalba Creek and the island to the east. Behind it lies a spacious public park that extends to the cemetery wall. The park features a large, air-conditioned indoor hall equipped with a variety of games, making it a recreational space for the community. Sheikh Dr Sultan said the park was the first of its kind developed in Kalba and a gift to its residents, adding that similar parks are planned for other areas. The new women’s tower is intended to provide a private and comfortable environment where women can gather and enjoy their leisure time. Construction is under way, and the project's engineer has prepared the architectural designs. The project will add a new architectural feature to Kalba, near the existing clock tower at the junction of Al Wahda Street and Al Corniche Street. The announcement did not specify the tower's expected opening date. The existing clock tower was inaugurated by Sheikh Dr Sultan on March 17, 2022. The 60-metre landmark has seven floors and features elegant Islamic architectural designs, crowned by a five-metre clock and a dome adorned with gilded mosaics. Surrounded by 12 main fountains representing the hours and 60 smaller fountains representing the minutes, the tower combines timekeeping with a distinctive water display. It also features two observation decks, including a restaurant, offering panoramic views of Kalba’s lake, university, mangrove reserve and surrounding mountains. Sheikh Dr Sultan has also approved an integrated care complex for men and women on Khor Fakkan Road, the media office said. The complex will include two nursing homes, physiotherapy centres, two counselling centres, two childcare homes, a women's protection centre, a community centre, and 390 parking spaces for visitors, residents and staff. The integrated care city is planned as a comprehensive setting for care, rehabilitation, family support and community activities. Gardens, a mosque, and an event square will also provide spaces for recreation, worship, and social interaction alongside the specialised facilities.

title: 1,447 emoji? We'll do it live
body:
One of the things you get to do after being laid off is a lot of reflection, but also to revisit all the old projects you used to contribute to.
One of them was Pidgin : “the universal chat client” .
I designed the original emoticon set for version 2 and helped redesign the user interface when the project was renamed from Gaim after a legal dispute .
Meanwhile, after a huge rewrite , Pidgin 3 is making progress towards a first release and I’ve been helping out here and there with a new app icon and some status symbols for the development releases.
I’ve been meaning to start live streaming my weekly app icon work to share a look in the kitchen of the icon design process, but once I gathered the courage to start a test run, the experience wasn’t amazing.
I need something I can return to consistently without needing a new plan every time…
So why not create a base set of 1,447 emoji for Pidgin in GNOME -style exclusively live on stream ? What could go wrong?
Here’s the design file to keep me accountable, so I can’t sneakily make progress offline!
I’ll be chipping away at it a few times a week. Follow me on Twitch to get a notification when I go live. We’ll grab a cup of tea, put on some music, and get through the winter.
If you want to support my design work for Free and Open Source projects, I’m always looking for more sponsors .
Or a “ sub ” as the kids call it these days.

title: Tinubu orders intensified probe into Katsina cleric’s killing amid Ansaru claim
body:
President Bola Tinubu has directed security agencies to intensify investigations into the killing of Islamic preacher Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka and his friend, Adamu Abubakar, in Dutsin-Ma Local Government Area of Katsina State.
The directive comes as the terrorist group Ansaru claims responsibility for the Monday evening attack, in which gunmen shot the two men outside the cleric’s residence.
In a statement issued on Tuesday by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, the president condemned the killings and directed the police and other security agencies to intensify efforts to identify and arrest those responsible.
Mr Tinubu described the attack as heinous and an assault on peace and the sanctity of human life.
He also extended his condolences to the families of the deceased, their followers and the people of Katsina State.
Earlier on Tuesday, PREMIUM TIMES reported that Ansaru, formally known as Jama’atu Ansarul Muslimina Fi Biladis Sudan, had claimed responsibility for the killing in a four-minute video obtained by the newspaper.
The group cited the cleric’s religious positions and advocacy for peaceful coexistence among people of different faiths as reasons for targeting him.
The claim has not been independently established as proof that Ansaru carried out the attack, and the police have yet to publicly confirm the group’s involvement.
The Katsina State Police Command had earlier said the shooting occurred at about 7.30 p.m. on Monday, when two gunmen riding a motorcycle opened fire on the victims.
The police said tactical teams had been deployed to track down the attackers.

title: No extension for manufacturers: EPA on January 1, 2027 styrofoam and single-use plastics ban
body: The Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) has rejected calls by local manufacturers and importers for an extension of the January 1, 2027 deadline for the nationwide ban on polystyrene foam (styrofoam) products and selected single-use plastics. Speaking at a stakeholder engagement session in Wa, the EPA’s Chief Executive Officer, Professor Nana Ama Browne Klutse, said the policy would be enforced as scheduled despite concerns from businesses about investments made in machinery, equipment and raw materials. “We have engaged producers, manufacturers, and importers of styrofoam products. Their concern is that they want some extension of time so that they can recoup some of the investment they have made in their machines, equipment, or raw materials,” Prof. Klutse said. “However, we have informed them that we cannot. They are making their profits at the expense of the environment, our health, and our properties,” she added. The ban follows an announcement by President John Dramani Mahama during the 2025 World Environment Day observance. It targets products including takeaway food packs, foam mattresses, ceiling panels and roofing insulation. Prof. Klutse urged Ghanaians to adopt sustainable alternatives, including carrying personal food containers, using reusable plates and wrapping traditional meals such as waakye and tuo zaafi (TZ) in plantain or banana leaves. Providing further details on the scope of the ban, the EPA’s Director of Sustainable and Circular Economy, Larry Kotoe, said polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastic bottles would be excluded from the immediate ban because of their distinct polymer structure and recycling potential. He said the Authority would, however, target single-use thin polythene bags commonly known as “coco rubbers” as part of its efforts to eliminate single-use plastics. “Once you serve food in a coco rubber, you can’t use it again; the next thing is it gets thrown away,” Mr Kotoe said. He added that the bags would be banned from next year as part of the single-use plastics elimination strategy. Mr Kotoe also warned food vendors against wrapping hot food items such as kenkey in thin plastic film before boiling or wrapping them in leaves. He said environmental officers would confiscate materials that do not comply with the policy. To support implementation, EPA management is working on a reward system to encourage compliance at the district level. The Authority is also developing a structured take-back collection system to channel recyclable PET plastics to specialised processing plants. The EPA said the nationwide campaign was being funded through its internally generated funds (IGF). The Authority’s Director of Risk and Strategic Management, Sydney Kwaku Danso, said the prohibition of imported styrofoam materials was already being enforced at key entry points in collaboration with the Ghana Revenue Authority’s Customs Division. Speaking on behalf of DSP Abdul-Rahman, Sergeant Gabriel Akornor said security personnel were prepared to enforce compliance when the deadline takes effect. “We will be at the borders with Immigration. If you say you haven’t heard and you try to bring it out, police officers will meet you in the middle of town,” Sgt. Akornor cautioned. “We are there to protect lives and property, and if you refuse to protect your own life, we will force you to protect it. We urge our rich importers: stop importing these items and start bringing in healthy alternatives,” he added. The Deputy Director of the Upper West Regional Coordinating Council (RCC), Tonsuglo Alhassan, who delivered a speech on behalf of the Regional Minister, Charles Lwanga Puozuing, pledged the region’s support for the policy. “Protecting our environment is a shared responsibility and an essential condition for sustainable development. The convenience of styrofoam comes with environmental costs that require urgent action,” Mr Alhassan said. He added that the RCC, together with municipal and district assemblies, would support the implementation of the ban and public education efforts. Mr Alhassan also described the phase-out as an economic opportunity for young Ghanaian entrepreneurs to develop alternatives such as paper-based packaging, bamboo products, glass bowls and sugarcane-bagasse tableware. The Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) also expressed support for the ban, with Juliana K. Toboyee, an officer of the Ministry’s Plant Protection and Regulatory Services Directorate (PPRSD), highlighting the harmful effects of plastic pollution on agriculture. Ms Toboyee said MoFA would use its agricultural extension networks to educate farmers on the ban and the proper disposal of agrochemical containers to promote a safer agricultural environment. As the January 1, 2027 deadline approaches, the EPA is expected to continue its nationwide public education campaign, urging citizens, traders and institutions to adopt environmentally friendly packaging alternatives.

title: 2027: INEC flags questionable voter registration, probes AI-generated photo claims
body: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC on Tuesday said it flagged a number of questionable registration records during the physical display of the preliminary register of voters, and has begun reviewing them. It added that currently investigating reports of suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs in the register published on its website. In a statement issued on Tuesday night, the Chairman of its Information and Voter Education Committee, Malam Mohammed Kudu Haruna, said the Commission “has noted public concerns and reports circulating on social media regarding suspected AI-generated photographs appearing in the Preliminary Register of Voters recently published on its website.” The Commission said the online register was not a new or altered document. “The register published online on 26 October 2026 is the same preliminary register physically displayed at Registration Areas (RAs) nationwide from 9th to 15th October 2026 as part of the Display, Claims and Objections exercise,” the statement said. It explained that the questionable records had already been picked up at that stage. “During the physical display, a number of questionable registration records were identified and flagged for further examination. The Commission commenced the process of reviewing these records and taking appropriate corrective action in accordance with established procedures,” it stated. INEC added that what Nigerians can see online is the version before any of those corrections. “The online publication represents the original preliminary register and does not reflect all ongoing data-cleanup activities,” the Commission said. It stressed that the document was never meant to be the final word on who is eligible to vote. “It is important to emphasize that the preliminary register is not the final certified register. The Display, Claims and Objections exercise is specifically intended to facilitate public scrutiny, identify inaccuracies and irregularities, and enable appropriate corrections before certification,” the statement said. On the suspicious photographs, the Commission said it was looking into how they got into the register in the first place. “The Commission is also examining the circumstances surrounding the suspicious photographs, including possible technical or procedural lapses, and will take appropriate action based on verified findings,” it said. INEC also acknowledged the citizens and stakeholders who raised the alarm. “The Commission appreciates the vigilance of citizens and stakeholders who have brought these concerns to public attention. Such scrutiny contributes to the process of improving the accuracy and integrity of the register,” the statement read. It assured the public that proven irregularities would not be swept aside. “The Commission assures Nigerians that verified irregularities will be addressed through the applicable procedures,” it said. The Commission said the work would be completed before the final register is certified. “INEC remains committed to completing the necessary verification, adjudication, and data-cleanup processes ahead of the scheduled certification of the final Register of Voters on 15th December 2026,” Haruna said.
