title: Navantia Launches Second F110 Frigate ‘Roger de Lauria’ Four Months Ahead of Schedule
body: Navantia has successfully launched the second F110-class frigate, Roger de Lauria (F112), for the Spanish Navy four months ahead of schedule in Ferrol. Navantia press release Navantia has held the launching ceremony of the F112 frigate “Roger de Lauria” in Ferrol (A Coruña). The vessel, the second in the F110 programme for the Spanish Navy, entered the water for the first time at high tide. The event was attended by the Secretary of State for Defence, María Amparo Valcarce; the Regional Minister for the Presidency, Justice and Sport of the Xunta de Galicia, Diego Calvo; the Chair of the State Industrial Holding Company (SEPI), Belén Gualda; the Spanish Government Delegate in Galicia, Pedro Blanco; and the Mayor of Ferrol, José Manuel Rey. Also in attendance were the Director-General for Armament and Materiel (DIGAM), Aniceto Rosique; the Chief of Staff of the Spanish Navy (AJEMA), Admiral Antonio Piñeiro; and the Chairman of Navantia, Ricardo Domínguez. The F112 frigate resting on the shipyard slipway prior to its launch, displaying the vessel’s lower hull profile and supporting blocks. This second frigate in a five-ship series was built on Slipway 3 at the shipyard. Navantia employees and their families, partner companies and other guests attended the moving ceremony, during which the frigate, after being blessed by military chaplain Vicente Hernández Chumillas, slid into the sea to the sound of the Spanish national anthem performed by the Northern Marine Regiment Band. The F112 frigate, named after Roger de Lauria, admiral of the fleets of the Crown of Aragon and Sicily, and sponsored by his descendant Almudena de Arteaga, was launched four months ahead of the delivery schedule agreed with the Ministry of Defence . As was the case with the F111 frigate, its level of installation and assembly is far higher than usual at this stage of construction. A low-angle close-up of the vessel’s hull displaying the “F112” pennant number, with personnel stationed along the upper deck railing. From this point onwards, construction of the vessel will continue alongside the shipyard quay until its delivery in 2029. The next two frigates in the series are already in production in Ferrol: five blocks of the F113 are on the slipway , while initial work on the F114 is under way at the new Digital Block Factory. The F111 frigate, the first vessel in the series, is in the systems installation and start-up phase and is scheduled to begin sea trials in 2027. Strategic Autonomy and Skilled Employment The F110 programme strengthens the Spanish Navy’s capabilities and represents a major industrial and technological development for Navantia and its partner companies. It reinforces Spain’s strategic autonomy, supports exports and generates around 9,000 jobs over more than ten years, involving approximately 500 companies across the country. The Secretary of State for Defence, Amparo Valcarce, expressed her appreciation for Ferrol and its naval and industrial community, “deeply linked to the history of the Spanish Navy”, as well as for the shipyard workers, auxiliary and supplier companies, and all the professionals involved in building these frigates. She also thanked the Spanish Navy and the Directorate-General for Armament and Materiel for their joint work in implementing the F110 programme, which “incorporates the development of industrial capabilities and a technological transformation of particular importance to Spanish shipbuilding”. “As her sponsor, this bond of blood and tradition will unite me in spirit with the frigate, her steel, and her crew on each and every one of her future voyages, accompanying her in thought and in heart wherever duty may take her. May the sea be kind to you, may your missions strenghthen peace and security for all, and may you always be a safe haven for the men and women who will make up your crew”, wished the ship’s sponsor, Almudena de Arteaga. “The frigate ‘Roger de Lauria’, like its predecessor ‘Bonifaz’, faithfully reflects Spain’s commitment to innovation and technological sovereignty. Each vessel in this series creates highly skilled jobs, promotes R&D&I and strengthens the Spanish naval industry’s international leadership,” noted Antonio Piñeiro, Chief of Staff of the Spanish Navy (AJEMA). For his part, Navantia Chairman Ricardo Domínguez thanked all employees for their dedication and effort in delivering the programme, which, “with technological developments such as the digital twin, the Integrated Services System and the suite of latest-generation sensors, antennas and radars, is a symbol of Spanish innovation. We are convinced that it will become an international success, just as the F100 frigates did in their day”. “This achievement reflects sound planning, exemplary institutional cooperation with the Ministry of Defence and the Spanish Navy and, above all, the tireless work of those who make it possible. This frigate bears the mark of thousands of people whose daily work turns our commitments into reality,” said Eduardo Dobarro, Director of the Frigates and Intervention Vessels Business, in his welcoming remarks. A frontal view of the F112 frigate “Roger de Lauria” adorned with ceremonial flags, highlighting its bow and integrated mast behind the event stage. A Capability for Today and Tomorrow The F110 programme comprises the construction of five escort vessels. Designed to respond to a range of operational scenarios, the frigates will be prepared to counter air, surface and submarine threats, operate alongside other units and support civilian authorities in maritime security missions. Through this programme, Navantia will provide the Spanish Navy with a new generation of highly digitalised and automated vessels. The digital twin and the sensor network of the Integrated Services System will enable data-driven decision-making, enhance safety, reduce crew requirements and incorporate unmanned vehicles into operations. One of the platform’s main strengths is its potential for growth and evolution. Its design facilitates the incorporation of additional capabilities without requiring a fundamental redesign of the platform. Spanish industry plays a leading role in the programme: 65% of the content comes from domestic suppliers, combined with technologies provided by international partners. The F110 is also one of Navantia’s strategic projects. Solutions developed by the company include the core of the SCOMBA combat system and the Integrated Platform Control System (SICP), as well as engines and other systems manufactured at Navantia’s facilities in the Bay of Cádiz and Cartagena. One of the principal technological innovations is the digital twin, a virtual replica of the vessel developed by Navantia together with the Spanish Navy and the Directorate-General for Armament and Materiel. Powered by sensors and technologies such as the Internet of Things, cloud computing and machine learning, this tool will support data-driven management and help optimise the frigate’s operation and maintenance. The digital twin is complemented by the Integrated Services System (SSI), a neural network connected to sensors installed in the vessel’s lighting infrastructure. Developed jointly with the Spanish Navy and the University of Vigo, the system helps consolidate an innovation ecosystem around the F110 programme. The frigate will be equipped with SCOMBA, the combat system developed by Navantia’s Systems business unit. Considered the vessel’s “brain”, it will process information from sensors, radars and weapons in real time. It is complemented by the integrated mast, installed in the superstructure, which optimises use of the electromagnetic spectrum and reduces the vessel’s radar signature. – End – The post Navantia Launches Second F110 Frigate ‘Roger de Lauria’ Four Months Ahead of Schedule appeared first on Naval News .

title: Zelenskyy on operation Veles: AFU successfully transform underground advance tactics, make them more technologically advanced
body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy highlighted the importance of the Veles military operation, which the Khartia second Corps of the Ukrainian National Guard is conducting on Kupiansk sector of the frontline in Kharkiv region, and reported that Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine Mykhailo Drapaty, Khartia Commander Ihor Obolensky, and Deputy Head of the Office of the President Pavlo Palisa had briefed him on its initial results.
"More than a hundred Russian occupiers have already been eliminated, and more than thirty have been taken prisoner. We have advanced more than 15 kilometres underground. The Russians have already tried to use underground gas pipelines to advance through our positions and launch assault operations. Ukrainian soldiers have successfully adapted this tactic, modernized it, and made it significantly more sophisticated and technologically advanced," Zelenskyy said on Telegram on Tuesday.
As reported, the Defense Forces under the command of the Khartia second Corps of the Ukrainian National Guard broke the stalemate on Kupiansk sector and carried out the next phase of the liberation of Kharkiv region as part of the underground operation "Veles," during which more than 15 kilometres of underground tunnels were dug behind enemy lines. "The Russians believed that underground tunnels were their exclusive tool for bypassing our defenses. We studied their experience, outmaneuvered them on their own turf, and turned this threat into our counteroffensive advantage," Obolensky said.
The corps noted that tunnels have been used in wars from Vietnam to Gaza, but exclusively for defense, concealment, or localized sabotage. At the same time, the Russian army used underground tunnels near Avdiivka to infiltrate infantry. "Veles" became the first full-scale underground counteroffensive maneuver in world history.

title: NCGC: We’ve Unlocked N64.13bn Loans, Support 914,791 Jobs
body: .Says women account for 42.7% of 22,616 Nigerians accessing bank loans for first time Deji Elumoye in Abuja The National Credit Guarantee Company (NCGC) has disclosed that it has facilitated N64.13 billion in loans to Nigerian businesses and individuals, as well as supporting about 914,791 direct and indirect jobs in its less than one and half years of operation. NCGC’s Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Dr Bonaventure Okhaimo, who made this known on Tuesday at a media parley at the State House, Abuja, also stated that 22,616 Nigerians who had never have access to formal bank credit have secured loans through its intervention, with women accounting for 42.7 per cent of such beneficiaries. Okhaimo added that the company had also deployed N30.19 billion in credit guarantees to unlock the N64.13 billion in loans as at October 21, 2026. He said the intervention within 14 months of its operation had enabled participating financial institutions to extend loans to previously excluded businesses and individuals, particularly those unable to meet conventional collateral requirements. The initiative, Okhaimo explained, has already reached more than 170,000 beneficiaries through 19 participating financial institutions, including commercial and microfinance banks. “For every one naira that we give as a credit guarantee to a bank, it creates two naira in loans. That’s the additionality”, the CEO stated. The CEOs stressed that President Tinubu established the company to address a fundamental weakness in Nigeria’s financial system, where otherwise viable businesses were routinely denied credit because they lacked acceptable collateral. His words: “The President has said, don’t let a viable Nigerian business suffer because it doesn’t have collateral. He has taken the collateral and given it to the bank. So that’s what we are doing”. Okhaimo also explained that NCGC does not lend directly to businesses or individuals but provides guarantees that encourage financial institutions to extend credit to borrowers they would ordinarily consider too risky. According to him, the company currently assumes up to 60 per cent of the credit risk on eligible loans, allowing lenders to relax collateral requirements while retaining responsibility for credit assessment, loan monitoring and recovery. Some banks, he stated, traditionally demand collateral worth more than 150 per cent of the amount being borrowed, a practice that excludes many small businesses despite their commercial viability. “What we are saying is, forget about collateral. Do the other due diligence. As long as the customer’s business is viable and the customer has good character, we are willing to support by giving you a credit guarantee that will enable you to give loans to your customers”, he stated. The NCGC boss also disclosed that the company’s interventions had supported 914,791 jobs, comprising direct employment reported by participating banks and indirect employment estimated through recognised development finance multipliers. The indirect employment calculations, he emphasised, were based on sector-specific multipliers, including those used by the African Development Bank, with NCGC attributing employment impact according to its share of guaranteed credit risk. Okhaimo described the inclusion of 22,616 first-time borrowers in the formal financial system as particularly significant, noting that many previously depended entirely on family members, friends and informal financing arrangements. He also disclosed that 7,731 young Nigerians had benefited from guaranteed loans but expressed dissatisfaction with the relatively low level of youth participation. The CEO said the company was developing strategies to increase the proportion of young beneficiaries to at least 40 per cent, considering the country’s predominantly youthful population. “We need to encourage them. We need to engage them. We need to do much more around youth empowerment”. On the company’s women-focused interventions, Okhaimo announced plans to unlock more than N100 billion in financing for over 20,000 women-owned enterprises within five years through its GuaranteeHer initiative. The scheme, launched on July 29, 2026, and formally unveiled to financial institutions in Lagos on September 3, raises credit guarantee coverage to 70 per cent for eligible women-owned businesses, compared with the standard 60 per cent. He said the framework, which provides guarantees for loans of up to N50 million per borrower, was designed to strengthen existing women-focused lending programmes operated by financial institutions. On the high interest rates charged by commercial banks despite government credit guarantees, Okhaimo acknowledged that access to finance and affordability remained two separate challenges. He explained that NCGC was primarily established to improve access, although its risk-sharing model could progressively reduce borrowing costs. According to him, banks determine lending rates by considering the Central Bank of Nigeria’s Monetary Policy Rate, inflation, funding costs and additional premiums reflecting the perceived risks associated with individual borrowers. He said the credit guarantee intervention specifically targeted the risk premium, potentially allowing banks to reduce interest rates as their exposure to possible losses declined. “We don’t determine the interest rate because we are not the ones lending to you. We are incentivising the banks to lend from their own balance sheets”. He added that NCGC was working with the Central Bank to explore regulatory capital relief for loans backed by eligible guarantees, a measure that could further encourage lower lending rates. Okhaimo also stressed that credit guarantees were not grants or free money, insisting that beneficiaries must operate viable businesses and meet their repayment obligations. He also confirmed that agriculture remained a major beneficiary of the scheme, noting that early interventions involving agricultural aggregators had enabled numerous smallholder farmers in North-Central Nigeria to secure formal loans for the first time. On the company’s institutional structure, Okhaimo explained that NCGC was established on May 29, 2025, with an initial capitalisation of N100 billion, contributed equally by four federal institutions. He identified the shareholders as the Bank of Industry, Ministry of Finance Incorporated, Nigerian Sovereign Investment Authority and Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation, each holding 25 per cent. NCGC, the CEO said, obtained its licence from the Central Bank on August 9, 2025, and operates under the bank’s regulatory supervision, alongside oversight by the Federal Ministry of Finance. According to him, the company’s capital base provides substantial opportunities to expand credit guarantees and mobilise additional lending in support of President Tinubu’s ambition to build a trillion-dollar economy by 2030.

title: SAWA Program: Newage begins training of first cohort of ‘urban bluers’
body: Newage Agric Solutions Ltd. has held the first hands-on field training for participants in its Urban Blue initiative, under the Sustainable Aquaculture for Women Advancement (SAWA) Program at the Saletso Industrial Hub at Okwenya in the Eastern Region of Ghana, marking a new stage in their preparation to establish home-based catfish production businesses. The training combines practical catfish production exercises, business guidance, and safeguarding education to prepare young women for home-based aquaculture enterprises. Held on October 15, 2026, the training brought together the first cohort of female participants known as Bluers, who had completed the initiative’s online learning course. The sessions moved beyond theory, giving participants practical exposure to catfish production, tank assembly, water management and stocking density, alongside business guidance and a session on Gender, Safeguarding and Inclusion. Led by Mr. Ken Nelson, the practical aquaculture sessions covered feeding practices, water management, identifying signs of fish illness and determining appropriate stocking density based on tank capacity. Participants also worked in teams to assemble and fix their tarpaulin fish tanks, determine appropriate water levels and stocking density. The exercise gave the Bluers an opportunity to practice tasks they will need to undertake when they receive their starter packages and establish their own production units at home. It also encouraged teamwork, shared problem-solving and peer learning. Beyond the practical demonstrations, Newage’s General Manager, Mr. Martin Tettey Nartey, facilitated a business-focused session that introduced participants to considerations involved in turning their aquaculture skills into a livelihood. The program also included a tour of Adwenepa Hub, another initiative under the SAWA Program, and Saletso’s cereal processing unit, where Evivi Foods products are produced, including a Tom-Brown processing site. The visit exposed participants to food processing and the wider possibilities of value addition within agribusiness. A Gender, Safeguarding and Inclusion session led by Ms. Berlinda Sarfoa Owiredu addressed respectful conduct, safe and inclusive environments, and how participants can raise concerns and seek support if they experience or witness unsafe behavior. For Gariba, one of the Bluers, the practical experience was particularly significant. She shared that she had joined the initiative despite initially disliking catfish because she wanted to challenge herself to try something new. Although she had doubts at the beginning, she said the hands-on training had helped ease her fears and strengthened her willingness to commit to the business as her own. About SAWA Program The Sustainable Aquaculture for Women Advancement (SAWA) Program is a four-year national initiative of the Mastercard Foundation in partnership with Agri-Impact Ltd spanning 2026 to 2030, designed to address systemic constraints while unlocking inclusive economic opportunities within the aquaculture sector. The Program is a women-centred initiative that seeks to unlock 60,000 dignified and fulfilling jobs for young women aged 18–35 years, including 3,000 young women with disabilities, across the aquaculture value chain i.e. tilapia and catfish. The SAWA Program is being implemented in collaboration with a consortium of strategic partners, including Newage Agric Solutions Ltd. About Urban Blue Initiative Through its Urban Blue initiative, Newage seeks to support women aged 18–35 who are interested in establishing homebased catfish production businesses. Selected participants receive training, technical support and a starter package comprising a tarpaulin fish tank, juvenile catfish and fish feed. Before attending the physical training, they complete an online course covering catfish production and foundational business concepts. According to Newage, the initiative received over 1,000 applications. Applicants were assessed against the program’s selection requirements, and successful candidates were organised into cohorts for training. The first cohort’s field training marks an important step in Urban Blue’s rollout, with further cohorts expected to follow.

In its latest gift to oil and gas companies, the Trump administration is expected to announce plans today to weaken rules that guard against methane leaks.
Methane is a smog-forming pollutant and a powerful greenhouse gas that’s up to 80 times as potent as carbon dioxide on a 20-year horizon. It’s the primary component of what the fossil fuel industry calls “natural gas” that routinely leaks from oil and gas wells and pipelines.
The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is reversing course on its previous efforts to plug those leaks. As part of President Donald Trump’s deregulatory agenda, the EPA plans to undo Biden-era rules that were expected to cut methane emissions by 80 percent over 14 years .
Methane has caused about 30 percent of global warming
The EPA teased the rule change earlier this month, saying in a press release that it was “days away” from making the proposal. EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin says the rollbacks will save oil and gas companies $45 billion, while the previous rules would have incurred $18 billion in regulatory costs.
“This proposal takes on many of the problems American [oil and gas] producers and operators have raised with us,” Zeldin said in the October 7th press release. “The Trump EPA is committed to fixing this so the U.S. can reach its full energy potential.”
The agency is expected to step back standards for so-called “marginal wells” — old wells that produce little fuel but create an outsize amount of methane pollution from leaks. These wells are responsible for half of the industry’s methane emissions despite only producing 6 percent of US oil and gas, ProPublica reports . The EPA is also expected to end the Super Emitter Program that notified oil and gas infrastructure operators of large releases of methane reaching 100 kilograms per hour or more.
Trump plans to make the announcement from a campaign rally in Lubbock, Texas, today, Bloomberg reports . Not only is Texas the top oil - and gas -producing state in the US, it’s also the world’s biggest data center market . With more data center capacity under construction than any other state, Texas has become emblematic of the challenges energy-intensive AI models pose. In just five years, data centers could undo decades of air quality improvements in Texas, according to a recent report by the Houston Advanced Research Center.
Methane has caused about 30 percent of global warming so far. But unlike carbon dioxide, which can linger in the atmosphere for hundreds or thousands of years, methane dissipates in a little over a decade. That makes eliminating methane emissions, particularly from unintentional leaks, one of the fastest and most straightforward ways to stop global temperatures from rising.
The EPA’s rollbacks quickly triggered furor from health and environmental advocates. “Any proposed rollback to the federal methane rule is a slap in the face to families who are exposed to oil and gas pollution where they live, work, and play,” Celerah Hewes, a senior manager for state field campaigns at Moms Clean Air Force, said in an email ahead of the expected announcement. “For over a decade, [our group] has been fighting for methane protections for our families—and we were making progress. Today’s announcement from EPA is a massive blow to the efforts to safeguard our children’s health and our climate.”
The Biden-era methane rules were estimated to bring in up to $98 billion in benefits by reducing climate risks and health costs from air pollution, even after factoring in the costs of compliance. Plugging leaks was supposed to lead to up to $13 billion worth of recovered natural gas .

title: Senate committee clears Eze Anaba, 15 other NHRC board nominees
body: By Henry Umoru, ABUJA THE Senate Committee on Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters has cleared the President, Nigeria Guild of Editors, NGE, and Editor, Vanguard Newspapers, Eze Anaba, and 15 other nominees for appointment to the governing board of the National Human Rights Commission, NHRC. The committee, chaired by Senator Adeniyi Adegbonmire (APC, Ondo Central) screened the nominees as part of the legislative process for reconstituting the commission’s governing board following President Bola Tinubu’s request for Senate confirmation. The Committee will, thereafter, forward its report to the Senate for consideration at plenary, where the upper chamber will take a final position on the nominations. Speaking with journalists after the screening exercise, Anaba explained that his nomination would provide an opportunity to sustain his longstanding commitment to human rights protection, which he described as an integral part of his journalism career. The NGE President, who expressed confidence that his diverse professional backgrounds would strengthen the commission’s capacity to promote and protect the rights of Nigerians, however cautioned against making definitive commitments before the completion of the process by the Senate. “We’ve just been screened. We’ve just been confirmed. So don’t let us jump the gun. That’s number one,” he said. Anaba expressed satisfaction with the committee’s decision, adding that the Senate’s final position would determine the next stage of the process. Explaining his background in human rights advocacy, the Vanguard Editor said his professional experience had consistently brought him into contact with issues relating to the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms. “I’ve done this human rights thing all my life. It has gone together with my journalism job. So it’s going to be a continuation of what I’ve been doing,” he said. Anaba also disclosed that he had been associated with the activities of the NHRC before his nomination to its governing board, just as he expressed optimism that the incoming board, with its blend of professional expertise, would improve the commission’s performance and strengthen its contribution to human rights protection in the country. Earlier in his remarks after the screening, Adegbonmire explained that the screening exercise had been completed and that the committee’s recommendations would be presented to the Senate for consideration. He said the Senate would communicate its decision to the President through the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation after deliberating on the report. Adegbonmire clarified that the NHRC’s governing board comprises 16 members, including representatives of the Federal Ministries of Justice, Interior and Foreign Affairs. He explained that the three ministries’ representatives were not subjected to individual screening because the law specifies the offices or ranks to be represented rather than the names of particular nominees. title: Russia-Qatar trade turnover modest in volume, but has increased by 10% — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Trade turnover between Russia and Qatar, modest in absolute terms, has increased by 10%, Russian President Vladimir Putin said during talks with Emir of Qatar Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani.
"A set of measures is being implemented to diversify and increase trade turnover, which remains modest in absolute terms, but is nonetheless growing - it has increased by 10%," Putin said.
Moreover, investment cooperation between the two countries is developing, he added. "The Qatar Investment Authority has stakes in a number of Russian companies, including Rosneft and VTB. Partnerships with the RDIF (Russian Direct Investment Fund - TASS) are growing, and humanitarian ties are expanding as well," the Russian leader noted, adding that tourism exchanges have increased.

title: Presidency: Tinubu Receives Regular Briefings On People’s Living Conditions
body: .Says president knows price of bread, eggs, essential foods, wants grassroots devt Deji Elumoye in Abuja The Presidency on Tuesday declared that President Bola Tinubu is aware of the status of an average Nigerian saying he receives regular briefings from aides on people’s living conditions. It also disclosed that the President knows the current price of essential foodstuffs like egg, bread while pushing for grassroots development across the 774 local government councils in the country. Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement (North-Central), Dr Abiodun Essiet, made this disclosure while speaking to newsmen at the the State House, Abuja, alongside her counterparts from the five other geo-political zones. Asked if the government at the centre sufficiently understood the economic pressures confronting citizens nationwide, Essiet explained that President Tinubu gets regular information about developments in communities, including the rising cost of essential commodities like food stuffs. Her words: “I don’t feel it’s only media people that understand what the people are facing. Some of the reality of what our people are facing is what we are communicating to Mr President. “I usually tell people, you think Mr President doesn’t know the price of egg or bread in the market? He does, because we brief him regularly, and so do members of the Federal Executive Council”. According to the presidential aide, government’s community engagement structure was designed to provide direct feedback from citizens, enabling the President to identify pressing needs and respond through appropriate government institutions. Essiet further explained that the President’s determination to secure financial autonomy for local governments demonstrated his recognition that meaningful development could not be achieved without strengthening the third tier of government which is the closest to the people. “You see him taking government to court because of local government autonomy. There’s no president that has done that because he believes the masses need to benefit”. She emphasised that effective local governments would accelerate development, expand economic opportunities and ensure that empowerment programmes reached communities beyond state capitals. “When our local government is strengthened, then you’ll see the same level of empowerment and development that you’re seeing at the federal level up to the state level”. The SSA disclosed that her office had established a citizens’ assembly comprising more than 700 representatives across the North-Central zone to gather complaints, assess community needs and communicate development priorities to the Presidency. The exercise, she stated, indicated that approximately 70 per cent of the challenges reported by residents fell within the constitutional responsibilities of local governments. Her words: “I must tell you, 70 per cent of the things they reported are responsibilities of local government”. Commenting on poor service delivery at the grassroots, Essiet observed that some local government employees hardly reported for duty, while communities continued to struggle with basic infrastructure and social services. She therefore called for greater accountability in the management of local council resources and improved collaboration among the three tiers of government. On infrastructure, the presidential aide said the Tinubu government was executing about 1,200 projects across the North-Central zone, reflecting its commitment to addressing longstanding development deficits. According to her, no than 167 kilometres of roads had been completed, while another 1,207 kilometres were under construction. Essiet highlighted the 401-kilometre Bida-Lambata-Mokwa Road project in Niger State, valued at N1.8 trillion, which she said had remained a source of hardship and fatal accidents for decades. Also speaking, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement, (North West), Abdullahi Tanko Yakasai, said government was transforming major transportation corridors to improve trade, agricultural productivity and regional connectivity. He listed the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano highway, Zaria-Funtua-Gusau-Sokoto road, Kaduna-Jos road and Kano-Maiduguri highway among critical interventions. Yakasai also highlighted the 1,068-kilometre Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, which he said is a strategic economic corridor capable of linking agricultural communities to major commercial centres and expanding interstate trade. He said the Kaduna-Kano railway project was approaching completion, while investments in renewable energy, irrigation, agricultural mechanisation and ecological infrastructure were expected to improve livelihoods across the region. On her part, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement (South East), Chioma Nweze said federal infrastructure investments were changing perceptions of neglect in a region that had long complained about inadequate attention from the Federal Government. According to her, over 1,000 kilometres of road projects were being executed simultaneously across the zone, identifying the Enugu-Onitsha, Onitsha-Owerri, Enugu-Port Harcourt and Enugu-Abakaliki highways among major beneficiaries. Nweze also mentioned interventions on the Niger bridges, bypasses and the rehabilitation of a collapsed bridge in Enugu as part of efforts to improve transportation and commercial activities. Apart from roads, she said the establishment of the South-East Development Commission, proposed improvements in gas distribution and implementation of the Electricity Act 2023 would help address longstanding energy constraints and stimulate industrialisation. The SSA said improved electricity supply and transport infrastructure would attract investments, revive industries and create employment opportunities. “My people are saying the President has done a lot for us, and we are going to come out to support President Tinubu because of what he has done for us”, she stated. Also, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement, (South-South), Gift Johnbul described the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and ongoing interventions on the East-West Road as major responses to the infrastructure challenges confronting the Niger Delta. She stressed that the region, despite its enormous contributions to Nigeria’s oil and gas revenues, had suffered inadequate road connectivity that restricted its economic potential. Johnbul identified the Benin-Agbor road, Benin bypass, Benin-Warri-Sapele corridor and bridge projects connecting previously isolated communities among the administration’s interventions. She maintained that improved transportation, electricity and market access would help diversify the regional economy beyond oil and gas, particularly through agriculture, commerce and industrial development. “The people of the South-South are 100 per cent with Tinubu. We support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, and come 2027, because of the infrastructural development we are seeing in our region, we want to vote for continuity”, she said. On the part of Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement (North-East), Hon. Abdullahamid Abba, he highlighted federal investments in road infrastructure, education, healthcare and water resources, maintaining that the administration had demonstrated considerable commitment to the region’s development. According to him, the Akwanga-Jos, Jos-Gombe and Gombe-Biu roads, alongside the highway towards Gamboru Ngala and the Cameroon border, as important transportation corridors that would facilitate commercial activities and cross-border trade. Abba commended the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, for advancing the administration’s road construction programme, arguing that improved connectivity would stimulate economic opportunities and strengthen regional integration. “We thank Mr President for the wonderful work he has been doing, and we assure him that the people of the North-East will come out massively in 2027 to vote for him so that he can continue his good work in the region”. On her part, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement (South-West), Moremi Ojudu identified local government autonomy, the establishment of the South-West Development Commission and major highway projects as significant achievements of the Tinubu government in the last three and half years. She believed autonomous and financially empowered local governments would be better positioned to undertake community projects, support small businesses, generate revenue and improve service delivery. Ojudu therefore urged state governors to cooperate with the Federal Government in implementing local government autonomy. On infrastructure, the presidential aide highlighted interventions involving the Third Mainland Bridge, Apapa-Oshodi Expressway, Lagos-Ibadan Expressway and Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway. According to her, 47.7 kilometres of the coastal highway had been completed, opening up communities along the Lekki corridor and improving opportunities for commercial development. All the six presidential aides submitted that infrastructure development, strengthened grassroots governance and investments in agriculture, education and energy were central to the administration’s strategy for sustainable economic growth. According to them, the combined impact of these interventions provided a compelling record on which the APC could seek renewed electoral support ahead of the 2027 general election. The presidential aides insisted that the administration’s ongoing investments were laying the foundation for lower transportation costs, increased productivity, expanded employment opportunities and greater economic inclusion. They called for continued cooperation among the three tiers of government saying sustaining the development programmes would be critical to translating infrastructure investments into lasting benefits for communities nationwide.

title: Russian steel lobby still blocks Ukraine's access to EU market – Metinvest executive
body:
A Russian metallurgical lobby remains active in the EU, actively obstructing Ukrainian metal products from accessing the European market and seeking to push Ukraine out, Oleksandr Vodoviz, head of the CEO's office at Metinvest Group, said during the panel "Global Markets: Closed Doors or New Opportunities" at the 12th Kyiv International Economic Forum (KIEF) titled "People. Business. Economy. What's Next?" on Monday.
"We see that the Russian lobby is also present in Brussels. They hire companies and fight to keep Ukraine out. And when we enter certain offices there, a Russian delegation is leaving them," Vodoviz stated.
He recalled that after the outbreak of the war, Europe imposed sanctions, Russia stopped supplying almost all steel products to the European market, and Ukraine managed to partially replace those supplies. However, Vodoviz noted that there are now efforts to bring Russia back to the European market, while quotas for Russian slabs have effectively not been reduced.
The head of the CEO's office specified that, in addition to Europe, China had historically been a key market for Metinvest, to which the group supplied iron ore. However, due to a significant increase in production costs and logistics expenses, the company had to abandon supplies to distant markets, and Europe will remain its key sales market.
Regarding Europe, he identified the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) carbon levy and the quotas introduced in July this year, set at 670,000 metric tons annually, as barriers to entering the market. Previously, supplies to the EU amounted to approximately 2 million metric tons. He said Metinvest had recently acquired a pipe plant in Romania, but the EU introduced quotas two months later, meaning the group can no longer supply Ukrainian steel to the plant for pipe production.
"I know that the Romanian government also raised this issue at the meeting of foreign ministers in Dublin, but there were no answers, and there still are none," Vodoviz said.
According to him, the European Commission has broken its promises to Ukrainian steelmakers regarding CBAM and quotas, and its overall policy is unpredictable and unfair, given that Ukraine is at war, plants in the industry have been destroyed, and the sector has been deprived of access to financing.
"We are asking the European Commission and the EU to take a somewhat broader view of financing for Ukrainian metallurgy and Ukrainian metallurgical companies' access to the European market," Vodoviz said.
The senior executive expressed concern that, because plants in Ukraine have been idled as a result of shelling, the group may be unable to use its EU quotas. In December 2026–January 2027, the European Commission could use the quota data for those six months to make a final decision and introduce quotas for the next five to 10 years.
"We are very concerned that our plants have been destroyed and we cannot supply products, while they could take these six months and set some minimum quota for the next 10-year period. That could also happen, which is why our government is currently engaged in a very difficult negotiation process," Vodoviz said.
Asked what the state could do to help in this situation, the head of the CEO's office noted that it was difficult to ask anything of a state that was essentially bankrupt, given that 51% of Ukraine's budget is financed from abroad. He said one could only sympathize with officials who receive a huge number of requests from businesses seeking assistance.
"But there are things that do not require money. For example, there is a war-risk insurance fund that the state wants to establish. We support this idea. The question is: where was everyone over the past five years, and why didn't we do this in the very first year? There is also the issue of compensating war-related losses using funding from European donors. At present, we have funds blocked that flow directly into the state budget. But this money could be used to finance funds for the recovery of strategic industries. We know that the Ministry for Communities, Territories and Infrastructure Development has established such a fund, and it is operating," Vodoviz stated.
Metinvest is a vertically integrated group comprising mining and metallurgical enterprises. The group's enterprises are located primarily in Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions. The holding's principal shareholders are SCM Group (71.24%) and Smart-Holding (23.76%), which jointly manage it. Metinvest Holding LLC is the management company of Metinvest Group.

title: Zelensky-Putin meeting needed to discuss the most sensitive issues, Sybiha says
body:
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha made the statement at a press conference alongside his counterparts Elina Valtonen of Finland and Espen Barth Eide of Norway in Helsinki, Ukrinform reports.
Asked what he expected from the upcoming trilateral meeting of negotiating teams, Sybiha said that “all negotiations are about creating new momentum” and suggested that the teams would focus on security issues.
The negotiating teams had already met several times but often returned to the same issues, the minister said.
“In my view, this group is not at a sufficiently senior level, with all due respect to its participants, to discuss the most sensitive issues. That is why a meeting between Zelensky and Putin is still necessary,” Sybiha said.
Ukraine had specific proposals, including a partial ceasefire, he said, while highlighting the situation in the Black Sea and the protection of Ukraine’s energy system, which Russia continues to attack daily ahead of winter.
“Incidentally, three groups had already been established as part of the negotiation process. So this is about resuming our negotiations in precisely that format. And that is indeed important,” the minister said.
As Ukrinform reported, President Volodymyr Zelensky said that Ukraine, the United States, and Russia had agreed to hold a trilateral meeting of negotiating teams in the first half of November.

title: Kidnappers abduct six in Kaduna
body: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Suspected kidnappers have abducted six persons during an attack on Nuru Suraj Estate in the Millennium City area of Kaduna metropolis on Tuesday morning. The attackers were said to have invaded the estate early in the morning, shooting sporadically and throwing residents into panic as they scrambled for safety. Sources in the area disclosed that the suspected kidnappers gained access to the estate through its second gate before carrying out the abduction. A resident, who identified herself as Maman Hamid, said her house was close to those of the victims, adding that the attackers arrived at the estate and began shooting, causing fear among residents. According to her, the assailants exploited the second entrance to gain access to the estate before whisking away the victims to an unknown destination. The circumstances surrounding the abduction, including the identities of the victims and whether any contact had been established with their families, were not immediately clear as of the time of filing this report. The incident has renewed concerns over the security situation in Millennium City, an area of Kaduna metropolis that has witnessed previous attacks by suspected kidnappers. A few weeks ago, suspected kidnappers reportedly invaded another part of Millennium City and abducted several persons, raising fresh concerns among residents over the recurrence of such attacks in the area. Efforts to obtain a reaction from the Kaduna State Police Command were unsuccessful as the command had yet to react to the latest incident as of the time of filing this report. The post Kidnappers abduct six in Kaduna appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: NYSC Members’ Kidnap: Court Admits AK 47 Rifles, ConfessionalEvidence Tendered by DSS Against Suspects
body: A High Court of Imo State, on Tuesday, at the resumed trial of five persons accused of kidnapping 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps members on Independence Day, admitted the evidence tendered against them by the Department of State Services (DSS). At the resumed sitting, the Court heard a continuation of the evidence of Ikem Emmanuel, the first principal witness, who testified that the defendants made confessional statements admitting to the crime of conspiracy, hostage-taking and unlawful possession of firearms. The witness tendered an audio visual recording of the confessions of the defendants. He also tendered their written statements, the recovered firearms and money in cash, recovered recovered from them. The Presiding Judge, Justice Emeka Orafu, in admitting the exhibits, ruled that the arms and money be kept in the custody of the DSS. The principal witness maintained that the defendants statements were obtained in the presence of their legal representatives and DSS legal officers. In a related matter involving two other kidnap suspects, the DSS officer also gave evidence on the investigation, stating that their confessional statements were taken under caution in the presence of their lawyers and DSS legal officers. He also tendered the audio visual recording of their statements, written statements money recovered in Naira, but for want of time, could not tender his report. At the conclusion of proceedings, the trial judge, Justice Orafu adjourned both matters to October 28th, 29th and 30th for continuation of hearing. He ordered that all the five defendants remain in custody of the DSS.

title: Makinde’s campaign group asks EFCC to probe alleged sale of ministerial appointments
body:
The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has called on the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission ( EFCC ) to investigate a claim that some ministers paid billions of naira to secure appointments and later sought to recover the money while in office.
The organisation, which is championing Oyo State Governor Oluseyi Makinde’s campaign for the presidency on the platform of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), made the demand in a statement issued on Tuesday and signed by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa.
Its demand follows remarks by Alwan Hassan, a spokesperson for the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, who alleged during an interview on Arise Television on 23 October that some ministers paid billions of naira to secure their appointments.
“A lot of ministers pay billions and billions, and, you know, to get themselves appointed. The first thing they think of is how to recoup that money,” Mr Hassan said.
Although Mr Hassan did not identify any minister allegedly involved in the practice or name anyone who received the payments, he noted that such practice had been going on for years in the country.
However, in its statement, the MDPCO said the EFCC should independently investigate the allegation and ensure that anyone found culpable is held accountable under the law.
It also criticised President Bola Tinubu for not publicly addressing the controversy, describing the Presidency’s silence five days after the remarks as a cause for concern.
It argued that the allegation raised questions about the integrity of ministerial appointments and the possibility that public office could be treated as a financial investment to be recouped through access to public resources.
“Mr President’s silence validates public apprehension that either he is not in control or he sits in approval of a corrupt and fraudulent system where public offices are reduced to commodities sold to highest bidders with devastating consequences on governance, the welfare of Nigerians and image of our nation,” the statement read.
It urged Nigerians to demand greater transparency and accountability ahead of the 2027 presidential election, while promoting its proposed “Reset Nigeria” agenda under the APM platform.

title: Nasarawa 2027: Ex-IGP Adamu raises alarm over PVC buying
body: Former Inspector-General of Police, Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, has raised concerns over alleged vote-buying and the collection of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) from women to prevent them from voting in the 2027 Nasarawa State governorship election. Adamu spoke in Doma Local Government Area while responding to his endorsement as the preferred governorship candidate by the Alago nation. He alleged that some political actors were buying voters’ cards to suppress participation in the election, urging residents not to surrender their PVCs for money. “Those who don’t have people following them are collecting cards in the hands of women; they are buying so as to stop them from coming out to vote,” he said. He urged anyone whose PVC had been collected to retrieve it and encouraged eligible voters to turn out on election day with their cards. “Everyone should not agree to sell their card, and everyone should come out on election day with their card,” the former police chief said. The endorsement was announced at a rally organised by the Alago Support Group for Adamu, who is seeking to govern Nasarawa State in 2027. He expressed appreciation to the group for its support, saying the endorsement had strengthened his confidence in his political ambition. Adamu also thanked God for what he described as progress in his political journey, adding that the support from the Alago community was encouraging. He said his ambition was driven by the need to improve the welfare of ordinary residents, particularly vulnerable people who, according to him, had been neglected under the present situation. “Our coming out for this election is for the common people. We came out for the common man, to see that the common man does not suffer the way they are suffering now,” he said. Adamu pledged to prioritise education, healthcare and security if elected governor, promising to pursue improvements in public services and create safer communities. “We will put people’s lives first, to see that education with quality is given to our people, health with quality our people have obtained, and the issue of security, we will see that everyone will find peace, so that people can return to their homes to sleep without any fear,” he said. He also expressed gratitude to the Alago Support Group and other supporters for their commitment to his aspiration, saying he hoped to secure victory in the 2027 election. The former IGP’s allegation of PVC collection and vote-buying was not accompanied by specific details of those allegedly involved. The post Nasarawa 2027: Ex-IGP Adamu raises alarm over PVC buying appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Eight million children out of school in Sudan — teachers warn of looming education catastrophe
body: Eight million children are falling outside Sudan’s education system, the Sudanese Teachers’ Committee says, warning that the public education system is at risk of collapse as teachers struggle to make ends meet and pupil numbers fall, particularly in poor and peripheral areas. The Sudanese Teachers’ Committee has called for education spending to be increased to 20% of the national budget and confirmed that a teachers’ strike in Khartoum state is continuing. It is considering further peaceful action, including school closures and sit-ins, if its demands are not met. Committee member Ammar Youssef said at an online press conference on Monday evening that about eight million children were now outside the education system. He warned that the crisis was worsening as families struggled to afford schooling and public schools faced growing difficulties in continuing to operate. Call for teachers to join strike Committee spokesperson Sami al-Baqir said the minimum wage stood at SDG 12,000, according to the committee’s estimates. He criticised the failure to implement decisions concerning workers’ rights and called for higher wages, payment of outstanding dues, and improvements to school conditions. The committee urged teachers across Sudan to join the strike and called on parents to understand teachers’ position and demands. It said the union action aimed to protect public education and ensure its continuation, while improving the living conditions of education workers. In a field statement issued on Tuesday, the committee said the strike in Khartoum state had entered its second consecutive day, with strong participation in the localities of Karari, Bahri, and East Nile. It warned of what it described as serious developments threatening the future of public education, saying its field monitoring had revealed a substantial and worrying decline in pupil numbers, particularly in schools in poor and peripheral areas. The fall in enrolment reflected the scale of the crisis facing the education sector and raised the prospect of classrooms emptying of children from low-income families, who rely primarily on public schools. The committee warned that the situation could deprive entire generations of educational opportunities. The committee said some teachers were unable to reach their schools because they could not afford transport. Their absence, it stressed, was not solely linked to participation in the strike, but also reflected the sharp deterioration in their living conditions amid low salaries and rising living costs. It said teachers being unable to afford the journey to work was a serious indication of the economic crisis facing education workers, amid what it described as the government’s continued disregard for their demands. Class divisions in education The committee criticised what it described as class-based discrimination between ordinary public schools and high-fee model schools. It said teaching had continued regularly in some model schools because they provided teachers with paid lessons, while public schools in poorer areas suffered from inadequate resources and deteriorating educational conditions. It warned that this growing disparity risked turning education from a universal right into a service dependent on families’ financial means, undermining equal educational opportunities and widening the gap between different social groups. The committee accused the authorities of attempting to circumvent teachers’ demands by relying on bodies it said had lost their effectiveness, while making promises to pay outstanding dues without fulfilling them. It said these practices were prolonging the crisis and worsening its impact on education. It warned of what it described as a plan to systematically undermine public education, saying the continued deterioration in teachers’ living conditions, declining pupil numbers, and poor school environments could lead to the suspension of public education in several areas, particularly poorer and peripheral communities. The committee stressed that the threat extended beyond teachers’ rights and outstanding payments to the future of millions of children who depend on public education. It warned that the number of children deprived of schooling could continue to rise. Further strike action under consideration Committee spokesperson Sami al-Baqir confirmed that the protest movement would continue. He said the committee was considering further peaceful measures, including closing schools and organising sit-ins, if the authorities failed to respond to its demands. Al-Baqir announced that the strike’s higher committee would hold a decisive meeting at the end of the week to assess the situation on the ground, review developments in the strike, and determine the next steps. He said the committee would continue what he called a “long-haul battle”, stressing that protecting public education and securing teachers’ rights were the two main objectives of the union’s campaign. He renewed his call for unity among teachers and solidarity with their demands. Sudan’s education crisis As previously reported by Radio Dabanga, Inflation is making education increasingly unaffordable in Sudan . On World Teachers’ Day on October 5, Sudanese educators called for housing and better support . Sudanese educators warned that low salaries and deteriorating working conditions were undermining teaching. Many teachers struggle to afford transport and basic necessities, forcing them to seek additional employment. Education specialists called for better wages, housing, social security and teaching materials, while warning that inadequate public investment was contributing to the growth of private schooling. Share article The post Eight million children out of school in Sudan — teachers warn of looming education catastrophe appeared first on Dabanga Radio TV Online .

title: Six killed in another Plateau attack as governor vows to track down killers
body:
At least six people have been killed in an attack on Gero community in Jos South Local Government Area of Plateau State, with Governor Caleb Mutfwang saying investigators have recovered evidence that could help track down the perpetrators.
The attack, which occurred on Monday night, has renewed concerns over the security of communities around Jos metropolis, with residents appealing to the government and security agencies to prevent further killings.
Mr Mutfwang gave the assurance on Tuesday during the swearing-in of special advisers at the New Government House, Little Rayfield, Jos, describing the attack as disturbing because of its proximity to the state capital.
The governor said investigators were pursuing leads from evidence recovered at the scene, expressing confidence that those responsible would be brought to justice.
“This particular attack left some bits of evidence that we are trailing and, by the grace of God, we will continue to pursue these perpetrators of this dastardly act,” he said.
Mr Mutfwang also urged communities across the state to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements to security agencies, acknowledging that delays in providing information could undermine efforts to prevent attacks.
“The security forces cannot be everywhere; they can only cover some places. If they get information, they will react, but sometimes the reaction comes late because by the time the information gets to them, it is impossible to have saved the situation,” he said.
The Plateau State Police Command confirmed that six people were killed in the attack, revising an earlier figure of seven reported by community representatives.
In a statement, the police spokesperson, Alfred Alabo, said unidentified gunmen invaded Gero in the early hours of Tuesday, 27 October, and opened fire indiscriminately on residents.
He said the Commissioner of Police, Ayodeji Faniyan, immediately deployed mobile policemen and tactical operatives, led by the deputy commissioner of police in charge of operations, to the community.
The team, working with military personnel and operatives of Operation Rainbow, dislodged the attackers, who fled into a nearby hillside forest, according to the police.
The bodies of the victims were evacuated to a morgue, while an injured person was taken to hospital for treatment.
Mr Alabo said joint security personnel subsequently began bush-combing, cordon-and-search, and clearance operations to locate the fleeing attackers.
The operations led to the recovery of motorcycles and other items allegedly abandoned by the assailants, he added.
Mr Faniyan visited the community on Tuesday to assess the situation and meet community leaders, youth and women representatives, and other residents.
During the visit, residents expressed concern over the attack and called for measures to prevent further violence.
The police commissioner urged stronger cooperation between security agencies and community members to improve intelligence gathering.
The police also appealed to residents to remain calm and report suspicious activities to the nearest police station.
Earlier, the National Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders Association, Rwang Tengwong, said seven people were killed when the attackers stormed Gero at about 9:30 p.m. on Monday.
Mr Tengwong said the gunmen opened fire on unsuspecting residents at relaxation spots and nearby shops.
He called on the state government and security agencies to strengthen surveillance and intensify operations to protect communities.
Beyond the Gero attack, Mr Mutfwang disclosed that the alleged leader of the deadly attack on Kombun District in Mangu Local Government Area had been arrested.
He said his administration would continue to pursue the prosecution of suspects linked to violent attacks across the state.
The governor’s pledge comes amid persistent concerns over attacks on communities in Plateau, where residents have repeatedly called for sustained security operations and the arrest and prosecution of those responsible for the killings.

title: Police arrest man in viral video preaching religious intolerance, violence
body:
The Zamfara State Police Command on Tuesday arrested the man caught in a viral video preaching religious intolerance and violence against Christians in Enugu and Plateau states.
The suspect, reportedly a member of Jama’atu Izalatil Bidi’a Wa’ikamatus Sunnah (JIBWIS), was arrested by the group and handed over to the police for investigation after the video circulated on social media.
The Commissioner of Police, A.M. Bello, disclosed this during a press briefing in Gusau, saying the command had launched an investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.
The arrest followed a call by the leadership of JIBWIS) which has distanced itself from the man leading a jogging exercise in its First Aid Group uniform, chanting threats to Christians.
The National Chairman of JIBWIS, Abdullahi Bala-Lau, condemned the footage and urged the State Security Services (SSS), the police and other security agencies to launch an immediate investigation, unmask those behind the recording, and prosecute anyone found culpable.
Mr Bala-Lau stated that the inciting remarks and calls for violence are entirely foreign to the core values, teachings, and objectives of JIBWIS.
He cautioned that merely wearing the organisation’s First Aid Group uniform or standing among members does not confer official representation or authority to speak on behalf of the body.
Expressing concern about the video’s timing and nature, the cleric noted that external actors might have calculatedly staged the incident to smear the organisation’s image and undermine national peace.
He pointed to JIBWIS’s peacebuilding track record, citing its recent international conference in Abuja, which convened Christian leaders, scholars from Islamic denominations, and international delegates to foster interfaith harmony and religious tolerance.

title: Trilateral talks in UAE tentatively scheduled for Nov 4 – Tusk
body:
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced that talks in Abu Dhabi (UAE) between Ukraine, Russia, and the United States at the leadership level are tentatively scheduled for November 4 of this year.
According to The Guardian, the Polish prime minister made this announcement while commenting on a phone call between Finnish President Alexander Stubb, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre, and Vladimir Putin. According to him, the call took place following "consultations with me, among others, but primarily with president Zelenskyy and the US side … that it would be good for European politicians to have a working contact given the planned ceasefire talks that may take place in Abu Dhabi."
Tusk noted that Stubb informed him after the phone call that "both sides maintained their positions," and that "the European side's impression during the call was one of very restrained optimism" about the chances of making progress in Abu Dhabi.
The Polish prime minister said he approaches cooperation with Russia "with very cautions" and urged Stubb and Støre to be "vigilant" during negotiations with Putin, since "Russia's agenda and interests are quite precisely defined, and that one should harbour any illusions about getting an agreement."
He noted that Stubb and Støre had informed Putin that the security of NATO's northern and eastern flanks "is non-negotiable."
The head of government also emphasized that, despite the resumption of dialogue, "nothing changes" in Europe's "full support for Ukraine," or collective views on "the [broader] security architecture and security guarantees for Ukraine."
"We should not have any illussions; it is clear what the Russian side is playing at, but I will remain in constant contact with all those who possess the good will and the belief that an agreement is possible – or at the very least, a ceasefire before winter," Tusk said, summarizing the results of the talks.
As reported, Zelenskyy discussed his conversation with Putin with Stubb and Støre and thanked them for "their active support of our diplomacy and joint peace efforts with all partners." According to the Ukrainian president, the Finnish president and the Norwegian prime minister told the Russian leader that concrete de-escalation measures are needed regarding Ukraine's energy sector and infrastructure. They also discussed preparations for the trilateral Ukraine-U.S.-Russia meeting, scheduled for November in Abu Dhabi (UAE) at the working-level.

title: Ceasefire in Alyoshki to end at 7:59 p.m. GMT on November 1 — ombudswoman
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. The localized ceasefire in Alyoshki in the Kherson Region will remain in effect until 10:59 p.m. Moscow time (7:59 p.m. GMT) on November 1, Russian human rights ombudswoman Yana Lantratova said.
"The ceasefire has been in force since 4:00 a.m. Moscow time and 3:00 a.m. Kiev time (1:00 a.m. GMT) on territories where the humanitarian mission is carried out. It will stay in place until 10:59 p.m. Moscow time on November 1," she wrote on messaging app Max.
The Russian Defense Ministry reported earlier that Russian forces had ceased combat operations in the Kherson area at 4:00 a.m. Moscow time on October 27 and declared a ceasefire to prepare a humanitarian operation in Alyoshki. It did not say however how long the ceasefire would remain in effect.

title: Unlocking the Future: Zenith Bank’s Tech Fair 6.0 puts AI in focus
body:
Zenith Bank Plc is set to host the sixth edition of its flagship technology event, Zenith Bank Tech Fair 2026: Future Forward 6.0, on Thursday, 5 November 2026, under the theme, “AI: Embrace or Extinct.”
Renowned for its scale and showcase of technological innovation, the annual Tech Fair has evolved into a platform for connecting ideas, talent and opportunities. Over the years, the event has brought together technology leaders, entrepreneurs, and young innovators to explore emerging technologies, showcase solutions and examine the future of the digital economy.
Conceived by the Bank’s Founder, Jim Ovia, the initiative reflects his vision of empowering young Nigerians through technology and nurturing inventors capable of developing solutions with global relevance. It also reinforces Zenith Bank’s commitment to digital advancement and the growth of Nigeria’s technology ecosystem.
The impact of the Tech Fair is evident in the solutions emerging from its competitions. Previous winners include JumpnPass, which developed a self-checkout solution for retail, and CreditChek, which uses artificial intelligence and open banking to streamline credit verification. At the 2025 edition, TrustLoopwon the hackathon for its digital identity verification solution, while Cubbes Technologies won the startup pitch competition with its AI-powered EdTech learning platform. Through millions in prize funding and mentorship, the Tech Fair continues to support promising innovators in developing practical solutions to real-world challenges.
For the first time, the Tech Fair will be held virtually, opening participation to a wider borderless audience across Nigeria and beyond. This year’s theme explores the growing influence of AI and challenges individuals and organisations to consider howbest to harness its potential in an increasingly technology-driven world. The event will offer participants an opportunity to discover emerging innovations, gain fresh insights and engage with ideas shaping the future of work and business.
The Tech Fair will be accessible via Zoom, Instagram, X, TikTok, Facebook and YouTube.
Be part of the future of technology. Register now at www.zenithbank.com/techfair and experience the possibilities of AI at Zenith Bank Tech Fair 2026.
Zenith Bank Plc is one of Nigeria’s leading financial institutions, recognised for its commitment to innovation, service excellence and strong corporate governance. Through strategic investments in technology and human capital, the Bank continues to deliver innovative financial solutions and contribute to the development of Nigeria’s digital economy.

title: Bitcoin Wallet Maker Keystone Pulls Devices as Stolen Key Opens Door to Fakes
body:
Keystone, a maker of Bitcoin hardware wallets that keep the secret codes controlling your crypto offline, said Monday it will destroy 18,835 unsold devices after attackers obtained the key that proves its hardware is genuine. The company has also suspended shipping of all unshipped orders from its website.
For buyers, the risk is a counterfeit wallet that looks brand new and passes Keystone’s own verification check, because the attacker obtained the key that the check relies on. A criminal could then sell such a device to someone who loads real savings onto it.
“If it is exposed, an attacker could use it to produce counterfeit devices that pass authentication checks,” Keystone said in its statement. “These devices could then be sold or shipped to customers, who might unknowingly use them as genuine products, potentially resulting in asset theft.”
Keystone calls it a WebAuth key, a secret code written into each device at the factory so a page on the company’s website can confirm the hardware is real. It cannot be erased or rewritten, and the 18,835 units in inventory that carry it are being destroyed rather than sold.
Keystone first said Saturday that a third party had obtained customer shipping information. Monday’s statement added the stolen key and a count of 25,964 affected buyer records, but it does not say who is responsible or when the attacker first got in.
The incident affected records from Keystone’s Shopify store, the e-commerce platform that handled its online sales. Keystone says 51,083 buyer records were involved, but 25,119 had already had their personal information erased, leaving 25,964 from 2024 to 2026 that still held names, contact details, shipping addresses and order information. Purchases through Amazon and other channels were not affected.
Some of that data should already have been deleted. Keystone’s policy was to erase buyer records after 180 days, and the automated bulk-deletion tool it built for the job did not work reliably.
“Some erasure tasks failed, and we did not detect and address these failures in time, resulting in certain personal information being retained beyond the permitted period,” Keystone said. “We failed to fulfill our commitment to erase customer data on time, and we accept responsibility for this failure.”
Customer lists are a recurring weak point for wallet makers. Ledger’s 2020 leak eventually reached about 292,000 customers, and those who received phishing emails afterward worried they could become targets of home invasions.
— Keystone Hardware Wallet (@KeystoneWallet) October 26, 2026
Trezor and SafePal each disclosed customer-data breaches in August, affecting 13,689 customers and about 39,798 customers , respectively.
Names and addresses matter because of wrench attacks, in which criminals use threats or violence to force owners to hand over their crypto. Chainalysis counted 46 violent attacks in the first half of 2026, with more than $30 million stolen.
The manufacturer also warned of scammers offering “asset migration,” “wallet verification” or “investigation assistance.”
“We will not ask you to return your device,” the company said. “Anyone contacting you under the pretext of a ‘recall’ and asking you to ship your device to them should be treated as a scammer.”
Sales on Keystone’s website will switch to preorders until production of devices with a new key is complete, and the company says it has submitted reports to authorities in the EU, UK, and other jurisdictions.
Keystone cut its retention period for customer data from 180 days to 90 and asked Shopify on October 24 to erase all overdue buyer data, a process with a 10-day waiting period. The company expects the erasure to finish on November 3.
