title: BC Ferries CEO Nicolas Jimenez fired amid ‘revitalization review’
body:
There has been a major shakeout at BC Ferries after the organization announced it has fired its CEO Nicolas Jimenez.
The BC Ferries board is not releasing many details about why Jimenez was dismissed, but the chair did say that this is a leadership transition and a “revitalization review” to ensure the ferry service is optimized for growing demand.
The board also said it is working with the incoming provincial Conservative government to ensure the system is reliable, safe and sustainable.
Jimenez was hired as CEO in March 2023 and was paid more than $550,000 a year between his salary and other benefits.
According to the BC Ferries executive compensation statement, Jimenez is entitled to 24 months’ severance.
BC Ferries vice-president of strategy and planning Brian Anderson will serve as interim CEO and the search to find a new permanent CEO will follow that review, the board said.
The BC Ferry and Marine Workers Union said it is not surprised by the decision.
“Whoever takes over needs to listen to frontline workers,” president Eric McNeely said.
“They need to work constructively with the union, which I think has been a challenge in the last couple of years. We’re, you know, one year without a collective agreement, 15 months in negotiations.
“Labour peace and stability matters in a ferry system that is struggling with investments in its workers, investments in the infrastructure, like the terminals, as well as the vessels. So I think there’s an opportunity to reset some of those relationships and to make sure that the ferries system is safe, it’s reliable and I think what people most want, affordable.”
On the campaign trail, the BC Conservatives pledged to establish a charter that would set the standards for performance, capacity and affordability.
Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson said he acknowledges Jimenez’s firing, but said his focus is on ensuring that the ferry service in B.C. is improving.

title: Those Listed in Osun Presidential Campaign Council Are Not Our Representatives, Says IPAC
body: Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo The Osun State chapter of the Inter-Party Advisory Council, IPAC, has disowned those listed as representatives of political parties in the Osun Presidential Campaign Council by the state coordinator, Governor Ademola Adeleke. IPAC said the individuals paraded as its members in the Presidential Campaign Council, PCC, are on their own and were never authorised to represent it. The council made this known in a press statement signed by leaders of some political parties in the state on Tuesday. The political parties include Action Alliance, National Rescue Movement, Action Democratic Party, Nigeria Democratic Congress, Social Democratic Party and National Democratic Party. Others are Democratic Leadership Alliance, African Action Congress, Labour Party, Zenith Labour Party, All Progressives Grand Alliance and others. It could be recalled that an advertorial signed by Adeleke, who is the coordinator of Tinubu Presidential Campaign Council in Osun, in one of the national dailies, named Odeleye Titus, Faribido Benson, Enorch Olalekan, Adetunji Olubunmi, Prince Adesoji Adeleke and Rev. Olatunji Popoola as IPAC representatives. However, the statement by Osun IPAC noted that the inclusion of the names in the PCC list is misleading and capable of creating confusion. “We wish to state categorically and for the record, that the persons whose names were paraded as IPAC members in the said council are not our representatives, nor were they, at any point in time, nominated or authorised by the council to represent us in any capacity. “IPAC is a structured body with duly recognised leadership and member political parties, and any representation must follow due process and official communication from our secretariat,” the statement noted. The council said it dissociates itself completely from the list, stressing that IPAC should not be used to score political points or create a false impression of broad-based acceptance. IPAC also urged President Bola Ahmed Tinubu not to recognise those listed as its representatives in the Osun PCC, insisting that members with strong grassroots presence across all local governments are the legitimate stakeholders. “We are the majority members of IPAC in Osun State with strong grassroots presence across all local governments, and any engagement with IPAC in the state should be through us,” the statement added.

title: Finland, Norway do not intend to mediate Ukraine conflict settlement
body:
STOCKHOLM, October 27. /TASS/. Finland and Norway do not seek to mediate a settlement to the conflict in Ukraine but support the idea of a trilateral meeting in Abu Dhabi, Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide said.
"We do not want to be mediators, but we believe we can make a certain contribution to the process," he said at a news conference in Helsinki attended by his Finnish and Ukrainian counterparts, Elina Valtonen and Andrey Sibiga. The Finnish newspaper Iltalehti reported their remarks.
Finland supports the US-led peace process and does not plan to restore relations with Russia, Finnish Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen said. She added Finland is not seeking to mediate the conflict and is committed to supporting Ukraine.

title: Nigeria records 43,000 snakebites, 2,500 deaths yearly
body: Experts have urged residents to avoid handling snakes and seek prompt medical attention for snakebites, as Nigeria records an estimated 43,000 cases annually. The ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌‌‍‍⁠‌​‌‌​cases reportedly result in between 1,099 and 2,500 deaths yearly. The experts gave the advice at a national training workshop on snakebite handling, treatment and management at the Lekki Conservation Centre, Lagos, on Tuesday. A medical expert, Abubakar Ballah, described snakebite as a neglected tropical disease, identifying the carpet viper as responsible for about 66 per cent of snakebite deaths in Nigeria. Ballah cited the World Health Organisation estimates of 5.4 million snakebites globally each year, resulting in 81,000 to 138,000 deaths and about 400,000 cases of permanent disability. He identified Gombe, Plateau, Bauchi, Benue and Taraba as major snakebite-endemic states, particularly within the Niger-Benue trough and Sudan Savanna. According to him, farmers, herders, children and hunters are among the most vulnerable, with cases often peaking during farming, rainy and harvest seasons. Ballah identified the carpet viper, puff adder and black-necked spitting cobra as Nigeria’s three medically important snakes. He said their venom could cause severe bleeding, tissue destruction, kidney injury, neurological complications and respiratory paralysis. He warned that delayed hospital presentation and harmful first aid could worsen patients’ conditions. He said such practices include applying tight tourniquets, cutting bite wounds, using animal dung and resorting to traditional remedies. Citing clinical cases, Ballah said some patients died following delayed treatment and harmful first aid, while others recovered after early hospital presentation and appropriate care. He identified the high cost of antivenom, poor healthcare access, bad roads and inadequate blood bank services as factors contributing to snakebite deaths. According to him, antivenom costs between ₦170,000 and ₦250,000 per vial. Ballah stressed that trained healthcare personnel should administer antivenom when clinically indicated and monitor patients for allergic reactions and other complications. He called for quality antivenom supplies, proper storage, improved referral systems and community education to reduce snakebite-related deaths. In a separate presentation titled “Dangerous Snakes of Lagos State, Nigeria,” wildlife conservation expert, Dr Mark Ofua, advised residents against attempting to catch, kill or handle snakes. Ofua said snake encounters could occur in mangroves, swamps, farms, gardens, building sites, drains, compounds and stores. He urged residents to exercise caution in such environments and leave snake handling to trained personnel equipped with appropriate tools. He identified the puff adder, black-necked spitting cobra, forest cobra, green mamba and Gaboon viper among species requiring particular attention in Lagos. Ofua also discussed the boomslang and carpet viper, noting that the presence of some species, particularly the carpet viper, required confirmation through local records. He cautioned residents against identifying dangerous snakes solely by their head shape, pupils, colour or size. He noted that some venomous species could be difficult to recognise and that protective equipment did not eliminate the risk of bites. Ofua advised suspected snakebite victims to remain calm and still, immobilise the affected limb, remove tight items and seek immediate medical attention. He warned against cutting or sucking bite wounds, applying tourniquets, using traditional remedies or attempting to chase and kill the snake. For venom spat into the eyes, he recommended immediate and prolonged irrigation with water. Both experts emphasised public awareness, prompt hospital treatment and safer interactions with wildlife as essential measures to reduce snakebite injuries and deaths. Earlier, the Director-General of NCF, Dr Joseph Onoja, said snakes played important roles in biodiversity and ecosystem balance. Onoja said snakes help control rodent populations, warning that unchecked rodent increases could heighten the risk of infections such as Lassa fever. “It becomes important that we learn to live as one in harmony with nature and more specifically snakes,” he said. The two-day national training workshop, scheduled for Oct. 27 and 28, focuses on improving snakebite handling, treatment and management. title: AHSAG calls for stronger accountability in Free Primary Healthcare implementation
body: The Association of Health Service Administrators, Ghana (AHSAG), has called for stronger administrative coordination, accountability and resource management to ensure the successful implementation of the government’s Free Primary Healthcare programme. The Association says the initiative’s success will depend not only on policy and funding but also on effective planning, logistics, maintenance and supervision at health facilities. It has also raised concerns about staff discipline, financial management systems and the sustainable funding of the Ghana Medical Trust Fund. The concerns were outlined during AHSAG’s 49th Annual General Conference and Continuing Professional Education programme, in Tamale, Northern Region. The Association of Health Service Administrators, Ghana (AHSAG), Rev. Ezekiel Amadu Daribi, said health service administrators must be actively involved in planning and implementing healthcare policies to improve service delivery. “Involve Health Service Administrators in programme planning, implementation, resource allocation and relevant decision-making structures. Implementing facilities should receive the administrative capacity and operational resources needed to deliver the programme. AHSAG stands ready to contribute its expertise in administration, transport, estates, supply chain and technical support services,” he said. AHSAG seeks role in Free Primary Healthcare implementation AHSAG commended the government for introducing the Free Primary Healthcare (FPHC) programme, describing it as an important step towards improving access to essential healthcare and advancing Universal Health Coverage. However, the Association cautioned that the programme’s effectiveness would depend on the capacity of health facilities to manage resources, coordinate services and maintain the infrastructure required for quality healthcare delivery. It called on the Ministry of Health, the Ghana Health Service, development partners and other stakeholders to involve health service administrators in programme planning, implementation, resource allocation and relevant decision-making processes. The Association said its members had the expertise to support the programme in areas including administration, transport, estates management, supply chain operations and technical services. Calls for stronger staff discipline The Association also expressed concern about misconduct among some healthcare workers, warning that negligence, absenteeism, lateness, abandonment of duty and breaches of patient confidentiality could undermine public confidence in health institutions. It urged health service administrators, hospital administrators, facility heads and other managers to strengthen supervision, attendance monitoring, duty-roster compliance and staff performance management. AHSAG further called for regular staff education on professional ethics, confidentiality, patient rights and customer care. It stressed that alleged breaches should be addressed consistently and fairly, in accordance with applicable rules and due process. Rev. Amadu said maintaining discipline and professionalism was essential to protecting patients and improving the quality of healthcare services. Concerns over GIFMIS role assignments The Association also called on the Ministry of Health, the Ghana Health Service and the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department to review role assignments under the Ghana Integrated Financial Management Information System (GIFMIS). According to the association, some health service administrators and pharmacists have reportedly not been assigned system roles that correspond with their approved responsibilities. AHSAG warned that incomplete or unclear role configurations could disrupt established workflows and weaken coordination within health institutions. “AHSAG calls on the MoH, GHS and the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department to review the relevant GIFMIS role configurations against approved responsibilities and financial controls. The review should identify the specific functions affected and ensure that authorised officers have the access needed to perform their duties, subject to segregation of duties, approval limits and applicable financial management requirements” he said.

title: Congressmen launch bipartisan military range, test facility caucus
body: A bipartisan group of U.S. representatives launched a caucus focusing on educating Congress and the public on military ranges and test facilities in an effort to further encourage the federal government to invest in its associated infrastructure, land and workforce. The Congressional Military Range and Test Facility Caucus was formed with the purpose of highlighting the role military ranges and test facilities play in advancing research, technology development and test missions for the military, according to a Tuesday announcement . “America’s military ranges and test facilities are where our nation’s warfighters get their edge, and I am proud to represent some of the most critical in the world,” Rep. Vince Fong, R-Calif., who launched the caucus, said in the release. “This caucus will ensure that Members of Congress understand what is at stake, fight for the resources these facilities need, and protect the missions that keep America ahead of our adversaries,” he continued. The caucus was formed by Fong alongside co-chairs Reps. Ken Calvert, R-Calif., George Whitesides, D-Calif., and Gabe Vasquez, D-N.M. Other members include Reps. Jay Obernolte, R-Calif., Julia Brownley, D-Calif., and Mike Haridopolos, R-Fla., per the statement. The caucus news comes after the Army announced earlier this year that it is opening five of its test ranges to private industry, aiming to quicken the development and testing of drones, counter-drone systems, long-range fires and cheap interceptors. The Army isn’t the only service that eyed opening up its ranges to approved companies. Earlier this month, Air Force leaders said they were working with the Army to understand how they could also apply the concept. Although the Air Force has yet to open any ranges, Brig. Gen. Mark Massaro, the commander of the Air Force Test Center, said at an October Mitchell Institute for Aerospace Studies forum that in a previous posting he worked with officials and contractors to coordinate smaller-scale test range access for specific tests, which gave him insight into how opening the ranges to industry could work.

title: Russia to share experience in restoring refineries with countries on Arabian Peninsula
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Russia has established its own chain for production of oil refinery equipment and is prepared to share its expertise with other countries regarding the restoration of such facilities, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said.
"For various reasons, we now have extensive experience not only with routine, scheduled maintenance, but also in handling situations with core equipment taken out of service. Therefore, our enterprises are currently working very quickly to restore oil refinery units that had gone out of service. We are prepared to provide support, including through technologies and equipment," told reporters on the sidelines of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) summit.
Virtually the entire range of oil and gas equipment, especially that required for oil refineries, is manufactured in Russia now, Novak said. "Therefore, should such assistance be needed, our specialists can provide it," he said when asked whether Russia possesses the expertise required to restore oil refineries in countries on the Arabian Peninsula.
Industry and Trade Minister Anton Alikhanov said earlier that Russia had offered assistance to countries on the Arabian Peninsula in restoring their damaged oil refineries.

title: New settlement outposts opening in Hebron Hills in response to Yehuda Junction attack
body: Eight new outposts are being established in the Hebron Hills in response to Friday's attack at Yehuda Junction, the Mount Hebron Regional Council announced on Sunday.St.-Sgt. Ron Yonatan Roytman, 23, and Sgt. Yuval Shai Svilem, 20, were killed in the shooting on Friday when two terrorists driving with an M4 machine gun and a pistol opened fire.The attackers had originally intended to pass the junction and carry out a larger attack on the heavily traveled Route 35, IDF sources said, before realizing they would not get through the checkpoint.“Out of the deep grief and pain over the terrible attack at Yehuda Junction in which soldiers Ron Yonatan and Yuval Shai were murdered, we choose to continue the construction and growth of settlement in the Yehuda region by establishing eight new points,” the council said, adding that it was fundraising to purchase security for the new outposts.Simcha Raz, an Israeli journalist for the national-religious weekly magazine Olam Katan, reported that the outposts would comprise six farms and two settlementsMount Hebron Foundation raises over NIS 158,000 for new outposts, vows to expand settlements in memory of slain IDF soldiersBy Sunday, the Mount Hebron Foundation had raised more than NIS 158,000 of its NIS 500,000 goal.“In the face of those who seek to sow fear and expel us from the heights of our homeland, we stand firm and deepen our grip on the land. In their memory and in their name, we embark on a large-scale settlement movement,” the foundation said in a statement.“This is the deepest Zionist, moral, and Jewish response: to turn loss into momentum for growth, preserving the land and building the future of future generations. In the place where they tried to cut off lives: We plant roots.”Ariella Roitman contributed to this report.

title: Flavio Bolsonaro vanishes after Brazil election defeat, reportedly flees to US
body: Two days after his crushing presidential election defeat, Brazil was left wondering Tuesday evening where Flavio Bolsonaro had disappeared to. The far-right candidate, who had led in the polls but lost to incumbent left-wing President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, has refused to recognize his defeat. On Monday, Brazil's Supreme Court ordered him to surrender his passports over fears he might flee the country while under investigation for corruption.  But by Tuesday evening, after the deadline had passed, Brazilian authorities announced that he had failed to comply and that his passports had been canceled. Shortly afterward, Brazilian media outlets, citing sources including people close to Bolsonaro, reported that he had left for the United States. A U.S. official subsequently told Reuters that Bolsonaro was on his way to the country.   The reports that Bolsonaro had left for the United States came after Brazilian Federal Police officials said earlier Tuesday that they were trying to locate him. Amid speculation and reports that he might have attempted to flee overland into Argentina, where his political ally, right-wing President Javier Milei, is in power, Argentine authorities said they had no record of Bolsonaro entering the country. Bolsonaro's aides, meanwhile, either declined to say where he was or said they did not know. Brazilians can enter neighboring Argentina using only a national identity card, without a passport. The Argentine government's statement followed local media reports earlier Tuesday that a private aircraft had landed at Iguazu International Airport, near the Argentina-Brazil border. Authorities inspected the aircraft and its crew but found no flight plan listing members of the Bolsonaro family. A spokesperson for Milei, who has yet to congratulate Lula on his victory, said that "there is no asylum request," declining to provide further details. A senior Brazilian Federal Police official said Bolsonaro had not left the country through any official border crossing.   Paulo Figueiredo, a right-wing social media influencer who serves as an unofficial spokesperson for the Bolsonaro family, declined Tuesday afternoon to answer questions about the politician's whereabouts. In a statement, he wrote: "After months of intense work that has been unfairly thwarted, I am not in the mood to speak to the press. If I have any comments to make on any matter, I will get in touch." Another source close to Bolsonaro said he had been unable to reach him. "I tried to talk to Flavio this morning by phone," the source said. "It rang and it rang, but he didn't pick up." A film, $12 million and a missed 24-hour deadline Bolsonaro had been considered the favorite to win Sunday's decisive second round of Brazil's presidential election, leading Lula by 1 to 2 percentage points in opinion polls. But when the votes were counted, he had lost by more than 3.5 percentage points, receiving 48.21% of the vote against Lula's 51.79%.  The count began late following a decision to extend voting by two hours, prompting Bolsonaro to allege irregularities and announce that he would not recognize the results, just as his father, Jair Bolsonaro, had done after narrowly losing to Lula in the 2022 presidential election. On Monday, however, the younger Bolsonaro's party announced that it recognized Lula's victory.   On Monday, the Supreme Court gave Flavio Bolsonaro 24 hours to surrender his passports amid several ongoing investigations against him, including a complex corruption, money laundering and tax evasion case in which he acknowledged seeking around $12 million from former banker Daniel Vorcaro to finance a film about his father's life. The younger Bolsonaro denies any wrongdoing and promised to hand over his passports, but by Tuesday evening it emerged that he had failed to do so, prompting authorities to cancel them. The order requiring him to surrender his passports, making it more difficult for him to leave Brazil, came amid fears that he might follow in the footsteps of his father, Jair, who flew to the United States after refusing to concede defeat four years ago and remained there for an extended period. The elder Bolsonaro eventually returned to Brazil, where he was later arrested and sentenced to 27 years in prison for plotting a coup. The demand to confiscate Flavio Bolsonaro's passports also followed a statement by his younger brother, Eduardo Bolsonaro, who lives in the United States and said that an election defeat would require Flavio to leave Brazil. "If my brother does not win, I'm in favor that he would leave the country," Eduardo told podcaster Steven Crowder on October 23. On Monday, after the election defeat and the order to surrender his passports, Flavio Bolsonaro said in an Instagram video: "I never thought about leaving the country. I will hand over my passports and defend myself against this outrage, which is clearly an attempt to intimidate me, but no one will silence me."   U.S. President Donald Trump, an ally of the Bolsonaro family, also weighed in on Brazil's election Monday, joining efforts to cast doubt on the results and claiming without evidence that the vote had been rigged. "It looked terrible to me," Trump told reporters before boarding Air Force One. "I didn't take sides, but it looked like another rigged election, frankly." He added that elections should be beyond dispute and that the Brazilian vote had looked very bad to him. Throughout his campaign, Flavio Bolsonaro had promised to strengthen ties with the United States if elected. His defeat this week dealt a blow to Trump's ambitions to further expand his influence in Latin America, where Brazil is the largest country by both area and population, following a series of victories by right-wing politicians in the region, including Chile, Peru and Colombia. Lula, who has taken strongly critical positions toward Israel, frequently clashes with Trump and has accused him of improperly interfering in Brazil's election. In his victory speech Sunday, Lula delivered a pointed message to the American president, promising that under his leadership, "Brazil is nobody's backyard."

title: Uganda Airlines begins scheduled flights to Accra
body: Uganda Airlines has commenced scheduled commercial flights to Accra, introducing a new travel option between West and East Africa and raising prospects for improved regional connectivity, trade, investment and tourism. The Ugandan national carrier began operations at the Accra International Airport on October 27, 2026, with four-times-weekly services linking Entebbe, Lagos and Accra. The new route is expected to provide travellers with an additional option in a market served by established airlines, while potentially intensifying competition on airfares between the two African regions. Speaking at the inaugural flight ceremony, Managing Director of the Ghana Airports Company Limited, Yvonne Nana Afriyie Opare, said the airline’s entry into Ghana’s aviation market demonstrates the country’s growing appeal as a destination for aviation investments. “The arrival of Ugandan airlines in Ghana represents a significant milestone in the growing relationship between the two countries. Beyond expanding travel options for passengers, this new service is expected to enhance connectivity, stimulate tourism and culture, facilitate trade and strengthen economic cooperation between Ghana and Uganda”, she said. She noted that the development reinforces Ghana’s position as a strategic gateway for regional and international air travel. Chief Executive of Uganda Airlines, Girma Wake, said the airline’s operations in Ghana would strengthen air connectivity between West and East Africa, making travel between the regions more accessible. The service is also expected to facilitate business travel and create opportunities for stronger commercial relationships between Ghana, Uganda and other markets along the route. Transport Minister Joseph Bukari Nikpe reaffirmed government’s commitment to investing in aviation infrastructure to strengthen Ghana’s position as a preferred destination for international travel. He said continued infrastructure development would be important in supporting growth in the aviation sector and improving the country’s competitiveness as an aviation hub. Uganda Airlines’ entry into Ghana comes amid broader efforts by African aviation stakeholders to improve intra-continental connectivity and reduce reliance on indirect journeys through European and Middle Eastern hubs. Limited direct air links between African countries have long been identified as a constraint on regional trade, tourism and business integration. The new service adds to the available connections between West and East Africa, with the potential to improve travel convenience and expand opportunities for businesses and travelers. The launch marks another development in Ghana’s efforts to attract aviation investment and strengthen its role in connecting African markets to one another and the rest of the world.

title: Majority of Americans want candidates who support US-based financial technology: Poll
body:
The September survey offered a possible window into US voters who could consider fintech and digital asset policies on Election Day.
A new poll from the DeFi Education Fund and Ipsos found that 72% of people surveyed said it was “somewhat” to “extremely” important for politicians to be supportive of policies encouraging financial technology built in the US.
On Tuesday, Ipsos released the results of a poll of 1,545 people conducted in September, showing that 35% of respondents said it was “very” or “extremely” important for political candidates to support the idea of “ensuring that those who are building the next generation of financial technology are encouraged to do so in the United States.” An additional 37% of those surveyed said that the fintech policy was “somewhat important.”
Notably, only 9% of the Ipsos poll respondents said that they were familiar with crypto, and 5% with stablecoins. A majority, 87%, said that they had not held any digital assets in the previous 12 months. Only 13% said it was “very” or “extremely” important for a political candidate to encourage growth in blockchain, crypto, and DeFi.
“Ownership of crypto and openness to DeFi are largely consistent with 2025, and interest looks consistent across party lines,” said Ipsos.
The poll was conducted about two months before Americans were set to vote on the next session of Congress in the 2026 midterm elections, in which crypto policies and laws could be a factor at the polling stations. Political action committees backed by crypto companies have already spent tens of millions of dollars in an attempt to influence voters in key races.

title: Ukraine is teaching the world to fight drones and use them in combat, Netanyahu says
body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu made the remarks at a pre-election meeting with media representatives, responding to a question from journalist Shimon Briman about lessons from Russia’s war against Ukraine and the threat Iranian drones pose to Israel, Ukrinform reports.
“What Ukraine has learned, and what the whole world is analyzing, is both how to fight against drones and how to fight using drones. This is the biggest change and the most significant impact of the war in Ukraine on the global arena. People do not fully understand this, but here in Israel, we are investing enormous sums in this area,” Netanyahu said.
He noted that drones had become one of the most significant technological developments in modern warfare. According to Netanyahu, Israel is developing new solutions to counter various types of drones, drawing on leading scientists, military experts, and technology companies.
Netanyahu also said that Iran’s transfer of such systems to Russia runs counter to Israel’s interests.
“But I believe our path forward lies in a tremendous breakthrough by our defense industries, including startups. There are numerous interconnected areas in which we are investing, and I believe we will provide the world with solutions both for drones themselves and for protection against them,” the Israeli prime minister said.
As previously reported, according to the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, the average interception rate for Russian Geran-4 jet-powered attack drones has stood at nearly 60% over the past three months.

title: GRASAG president joins World Bank-backed Africa development conference in Italy
body: The World Bank Group has invited the President of the Graduate Students Association of Ghana (GRASAG), Richard Class-Peters, to participate in an international conference in Italy focused on skills development, job creation and Africa’s economic growth. Mr Class-Peters is expected to join the second edition of the Africa Growth and Opportunity – Research in Action (AGORA) conference, scheduled for October 26 to 27, 2026, in Palermo, Italy. The invitation was extended by Nancy Lozano Gracia, Head of the World Bank Group’s Rome Center. The conference, held under the theme “Building Skills for Africa’s Home-Grown Development,” will bring together policymakers, researchers, think tanks, private-sector leaders and development partners to explore how research can inform policies that expand employment and economic opportunities across the continent. Discussions will focus on the mismatch between the skills acquired through education and training and those required by employers, an issue that continues to affect graduate employment and workforce development across Africa. According to the World Bank, many businesses struggle to find workers with the technical, digital and management skills they need, while graduates face difficulties securing jobs that match their qualifications and competencies. Mr Class-Peters’ participation could provide an opportunity for graduate students’ perspectives to feature in discussions on how African countries can better align tertiary education with labour-market demands. The conference will also examine ways to expand employment opportunities in sectors such as energy and agribusiness while preparing young people for changes in the workplace driven by artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies. Focus on skills and job creation The World Bank says Africa’s working-age population is projected to increase by more than 450 million by 2040, placing greater urgency on efforts to create jobs and equip young people with relevant skills. Against this backdrop, AGORA seeks to bridge the gap between research, policymaking and implementation by bringing together stakeholders to identify practical approaches to Africa’s development challenges. The discussions are expected to explore how governments and businesses can translate investments in education, skills training and economic development into productive employment. For Ghana, the conference could offer an opportunity to highlight challenges facing postgraduate students and young graduates, including the transition from university to employment and the need for stronger links between academic training and industry. It could also provide opportunities for exchanges with policymakers, researchers and development partners on approaches to entrepreneurship, workforce development and job creation adopted in other African countries. The two-day conference will take place at the historic Palazzo dei Normanni in Palermo, bringing together participants from across Africa and beyond. Mr Class-Peters’ participation would place graduate representation within broader discussions about the future of work and the policies needed to ensure that Africa’s growing workforce can contribute to and benefit from the continent’s economic transformation.

title: Ukraine's 'Veles' pipeline operation near Kupiansk 'eliminates' over 100 Russian troops, Zelensky says
body:
Ukrainian forces "eliminated" more than 100 Russian soldiers and captured more than 30 others during an operation involving underground gas pipelines near Kupiansk in Kharkiv Oblast, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Oct. 27.
"The Russians had already tried to use underground gas pipelines to move through our positions and launch assault operations. Ukrainian warriors have successfully transformed this tactic, modernized it, and made it much more sophisticated and technologically advanced," Zelensky said.
The operation, code-named "Veles," involved an underground advance of more than 15 kilometers (9 miles), according to Zelensky .
The operation was carried out by the National Guard's 2nd Khartiia Corps alongside other Ukrainian units.
Zelensky said he had received reports on the operation's initial results and progress from Commander-in-Chief of Ukraine's Armed Forces Mykhailo Drapatyi, 2nd Khartiia Corps Commander Ihor Obolienskyi, and Deputy Head of the Presidential Office Pavlo Palisa.
The 2nd Khartiia Corps previously reported on Oct. 22 that Ukrainian troops had infiltrated Russian rear positions near Kupiansk through underground gas pipelines as part of Operation Veles .
The operation followed earlier Russian attempts to use the same tactic in the area. On Sept. 12, Ukrainian battlefield monitoring group DeepState reported that Russian troops had used a gas pipeline to cross the Oskil River and penetrate Ukrainian defenses near Kupiansk.

title: “Gossip, myths and manipulation” – fifth day of hearings on banning opposition parties held in Georgia
body: Georgia opposition ban trial On 27 October, Georgia’s Constitutional Court held the fifth day of hearings on the merits of a lawsuit filed by the ruling Georgian Dream party seeking to ban five opposition parties. At this stage, the court is hearing arguments from the parties involved in the case. The lawsuit names the United National Movement, Coalition for Change, Lelo – Strong Georgia, Gakharia for Georgia and the Federalists. Georgian Dream argues that these parties have violated Article 23 of the Constitution, which prohibits political parties whose aims include overthrowing or forcibly changing the country’s constitutional order. One of the arguments is that the parties refuse to recognise the legitimacy of the current authorities. The lawsuit also accuses them of organising attempts to overthrow the government. The United National Movement faces additional accusations of undermining Georgia’s independence and violating its territorial integrity. The lawsuit holds the party responsible for the August 2008 war with Russia over South Ossetia, when it was in power. All five opposition parties reject the accusations. Hearings are scheduled to continue through 30 October. The court must deliver its final ruling by 24 June 2027. At the 27 October hearing, three representatives of the United National Movement appeared before the court: Ana Tsitlidze, Levan Bezhashvili and Alika Kuprava. Ana Tsitlidze spoke for the longest time. She criticised the legal grounds for the lawsuit and the evidence presented, and questioned the judges’ impartiality. She argued that the case was politically motivated and that banning the parties would restrict political pluralism. Proposed ban on five opposition parties in Georgia: what’s happening and why Billionaire Ivanishvili won’t testify in Georgia opposition ban case. Constitutional Court, day four “ Don’t like it? Too bad”: third day of Constitutional Court hearings on opposition ban in Georgia Tsitlidze spoke at length about high-profile criminal cases from the period when the United National Movement was in power in Georgia. She also addressed corruption allegations, relations with international partners and the events of the August 2008 war. Whenever she mentioned a particular official by name, the presiding judge urged her to be more restrained and interrupted her speech. With these statements, one of the parties defending itself in the case, the United National Movement, concluded its presentation to the court. At the end of their speeches, none of the party’s representatives used the standard legal phrase: “I ask the court to dismiss the claim.” Instead, each speaker ended by appealing to the judges’ conscience. The judges seemed to find it extremely difficult to hide their irritation at this unusual conclusion. On 28 October, the Constitutional Court will begin hearing arguments from representatives of the Coalition for Change. They have announced in advance that they have prepared an extensive set of documents and will need a full day to present their case. Below are the main points from the 27 October hearing. Opinion: If Georgia’s Constitutional Court bans opposition parties, Russia will use it against Georgia According to the Lelo party leader, a ban on five opposition parties would harm the country more than the parties themselves. Ana Tsitlidze: “Political gossip, myths and manipulation” Ana Tsitlidze said the court must draw a clear line between the state’s legitimate powers and the use of constitutional procedures to target political opponents. In her view, the lawsuit filed by the ruling Georgian Dream party lacks legal grounds and amounts to nothing more than “political gossip, myths and manipulation”. Tsitlidze said she was not trying to shield the United National Movement from responsibility for its political or legal record. On the contrary, she was ready to discuss every decision the party had made in the past, including those that were difficult to defend. However, she argued that Georgian Dream’s lawsuit had no legal basis and relied on a selective interpretation of historical events. “ If maintaining a critical attitude towards the government and questioning the legitimacy of elections can become grounds for banning a party, then political pluralism in Georgia is over and the country has become a one-party dictatorship .” Judge interrupts Tsitlidze: “How can you say that a man was killed?” When the discussion turned to the circumstances surrounding the death of Nugzar Putkaradze , a Batumi City Council member who died in November 2021, presiding judge Revaz Nadaraia interrupted Ana Tsitlidze. Putkaradze represented the United National Movement in Batumi City Council, in the Ajara region. He died of a heart attack. A few days before his death, his party said that representatives of the ruling party had been putting him under “unbearable pressure”. “ There is concrete evidence that Georgian Dream put pressure on him. This evidence has been made public. Nugzar Putkaradze was offered $100,000 to betray the National Movement and switch sides to Georgian Dream. In the end, he suffered a heart attack and died ,” Tsitlidze said. “ How can you say such a thing? Think about your words! This is a very serious allegation. How can you make such statements from the podium in a courtroom? On what grounds are you claiming that a man was killed? ” Judge Nadaraia asked. “ But the entire argument put forward by the parliamentary investigative commission, which prepared a report for this court, was based precisely on the claim that the National Movement had allegedly killed people as part of systematic crimes, ” Tsitlidze replied. Opinion from Tbilisi: 'Everything is in place for Prime Minister Kobakhidze's resignation' Political analyst Gia Khukhashvili predicts that Georgian Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze could resign soon. Tsitlidze on controversial actions by the United National Movement in power and double standards Ana Tsitlidze recalled several high-profile cases from the previous government’s time in office, including the Aprasidze family case, the case of Roin Shavadze, the murder of Sandro Girgvliani and the death of Yuri Vazagashvili. She argued that the possible crimes of individuals should not automatically be grounds for banning an entire political party. Speaking about the case of Roin Shavadze, Tsitlidze said she also had questions about it. Shavadze was a former military officer who fought in the August 2008 war with Russia. He was arrested in Batumi on 24 August 2008, shortly after the war, and later killed. The case involved allegations of torture and extrajudicial killing. The circumstances remain the subject of political and legal disputes. “The Roin Shavadze case was a problem for the United National Movement. I myself support reopening the investigation. “ But how can this case be used as grounds for banning the National Movement when the lead investigator was Resan Kontselidze, who later became a Georgian Dream MP? Moreover, the deputy prosecutor at the time was Vasil Roinishvili, who is now a Constitutional Court judge ,” Tsitlidze said. Turning to the Sandro Girgvliani case, Tsitlidze pointed out that the presiding judge was Levan Murusidze, who was later appointed as a judge for life by Georgian Dream. In January 2006, when the United National Movement was in power, Sandro Girgvliani, a young man, and his friend were abducted and brutally beaten by people linked to senior Interior Ministry officials following a dispute at a cafe in Tbilisi. Girgvliani later died from his injuries. Four former senior officials were convicted in the case. However, their subsequent pardons and early releases sparked public outrage. “ Georgian Dream divides the careers of judges Murusidze and Chinchaladze into two periods. Their work before 2012, when Georgian Dream came to power, is portrayed as criminal because it helps build the case for banning the opposition. Yet the same judges’ work after 2012 is presented as a model of integrity and independence. This is a double standard, and such double standards undermine the very concept of justice ,” Tsitlidze said. In her view, Georgian Dream’s use of past misconduct within the judicial system as grounds for banning a political party is contradictory, especially since people who continue to work within that same system are not being held to the same standard. Tsitlidze on Zurab Adeishvili and former officials from his circle now sitting in judgment on the opposition Ana Tsitlidze noted that Zurab Adeishvili, a senior official under the United National Movement government, is mentioned 25 times in Georgian Dream’s constitutional lawsuit. Adeishvili was an influential figure in President Mikheil Saakashvili’s administration. He served as Georgia’s chief prosecutor from 2004 to 2008 and as justice minister from 2008 to 2012. The plaintiffs argue that his actions were so systematic and unconstitutional that the entire party should be banned. Tsitlidze said she had never met Adeishvili in person. However, Constitutional Court judge Vasil Roinishvili knew him well: when Adeishvili was justice minister, Roinishvili served as deputy chief prosecutor. Tsitlidze challenged the judges with the following question: “ How can someone be banned from political activity on the basis of the actions of a person they have never even met, while a former senior official from that very same system is now allowed to sit on the court and take part in constitutional justice? ” Tsitlidze on fake prison videos, planted drugs and weapons, and violations of privacy Ana Tsitlidze cited criminal cases from the period when Georgian Dream was already in power. These included staged prison videos and cases involving drugs and weapons allegedly planted on people. She noted that well-known figures Tamaz Elizbarashvili and Lado Bedukadze had spoken about prison footage being staged. On the issue of drugs and weapons being planted, she recalled the December 2024 arrest of Giorgi Akhobadze, an active participant in pro-European protests. Akhobadze was charged with acquiring and possessing drugs. He was later acquitted, and the court ordered his immediate release in the courtroom. Tsitlidze also raised the issue of violations of privacy. One of the arguments in the lawsuit is that the United National Movement committed systematic crimes by distributing recordings of people’s private lives while in power. Tsitlidze argued that those responsible for publishing private recordings of journalists and politicians during Georgian Dream’s time in office should also be held accountable. Tsitlidze: UNM accused of corruption as Georgian Dream officials jailed for corruption Ana Tsitlidze noted that the plaintiffs accuse the United National Movement of corruption, despite serious questions surrounding senior officials from the ruling Georgian Dream party itself. She cited the cases of former Prime Minister Irakli Garibashvili, former State Security Service chief Grigol Liluashvili and former Defence Minister Juansher Burchuladze , all of whom have been convicted of corruption. Given these cases involving members of their own party, Tsitlidze said, it was unclear why the plaintiffs believed the United National Movement should be banned over individual cases of corruption within its ranks. 14 years in power: how experts assess Georgian Dream's rule Assessments differ sharply from those given just five years ago Georgia’s international partners and sanctions Tsitlidze criticised the argument that the opposition had worked with international partners to persuade them to impose sanctions on Georgia’s current authorities. She said that engaging with international partners was a normal part of political activity, while decisions on sanctions were made by the partners themselves. Tsitlidze’s closing words to the judges “The choice of which path to take is yours” “ I am not asking you to dismiss this lawsuit. Georgia’s history has never been one-dimensional. We have had people like Antsukhelidze and Sergo Ordzhonikidze, Ilia and Berbichashvili. The choice of which path to take is yours ,” Ana Tsitlidze concluded. “ Would it not have been better to simply state, instead of making rhetorical remarks …” the presiding judge began, cutting himself off mid-sentence as he tried to hide his irritation. “ You are asking the court to dismiss the lawsuit, are you not? ” “ We are not asking for anything ” Tsitlidze replied. Levan Bezhashvili “The rule of law must not fall with those in power” The speeches by the two other United National Movement representatives, Levan Bezhashvili and Alika Kuprava, were relatively brief. “ Today, you are deciding not only the fate of political parties, but also whether the Constitution will remain a check on government power in Georgia or become entirely dependent on the will of those who hold that power ,” Levan Bezhashvili told the Constitutional Court judges. “ History does not remember who held more power at any given moment. It remembers what people did with that power. Your decision will be judged by whether you defended the rule of law at the moment when it was most difficult to do so. A party may be defeated, a politician may leave office, but the rule of law must not fall with those in power ,” Bezhashvili stressed. Reactions to the hearing Badri Japaridze, one of the leaders of Lelo – Strong Georgia, told journalists that when it was his party’s turn to speak, its representatives would use every legal means available to expose what he called Georgian Dream’s real aim: to eliminate the opposition in the country. Maia Kopaleishvili, a member of the Coalition for Change, told journalists that Georgian Dream had presented nothing but hearsay in its lawsuit. “The hearings of the parliamentary temporary investigative commission, which form the basis of the lawsuit, are built on gossip and cannot provide sufficient grounds to accuse a political party of unconstitutional activity,” Kopaleishvili said. Representatives of the United National Movement who addressed the court. Photo: Batumelebi, 27 October, Batumi. News in Georgia Georgia opposition ban trial

title: House Moves to Institutionalise Use of Strategic Research Findings in National Policy Formulation
body: The House of Representatives has moved to institutionalise the consideration and utilisation of strategic research findings in national policy formulation, development planning and governance. The move followed a motion sponsored by the Deputy Minority Leader, Rep. Abdussamad Dasuki, who represents Kebbe/Tambuwal Federal Constituency. The motion seeks to establish a coordinated framework for the systematic review, referral and monitoring of strategic research recommendations produced by key national institutions, including the National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies (NIPSS), Kuru; the National Defence College (NDC), Abuja; and the National Institute for Security Studies (NISS). The lawmakers noted that the Federal Government had over the years established and sustained these institutions to undertake research, develop strategic leadership capacity and provide informed policy recommendations to address Nigeria’s economic, security, governance and developmental challenges. The House further noted that the institutions regularly produce comprehensive reports and policy recommendations through their executive courses, studies programmes and research activities, drawing on the expertise of senior public servants, military and security officers, academics, policymakers and other professionals. The House also acknowledged the statutory mandate of NIPSS under Section 3 of the National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies Act to conduct interdisciplinary research into Nigeria’s social, economic, political and security challenges and present practical policy options to support national policy formulation and implementation. It cited Sections 13 and 18 of the Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2007, which provide for institutional consultation in the preparation of the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) and establish the framework as the basis for annual budget preparation. According to the motion, these provisions offer an existing legal framework through which strategic research findings can contribute to national economic planning and expenditure priorities. The lawmakers observed that although research reports and policy recommendations from the institutions are periodically presented to the Presidency and other relevant authorities, there is a need for a more systematic and coordinated mechanism to ensure their formal consideration, referral to responsible Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs), and follow-up on decisions arising from their recommendations. The House expressed concern that the absence of a clearly defined, government-wide framework requiring relevant MDAs to formally review and respond to strategic research recommendations could limit the effective utilisation of public investments in research. The motion also warned that without an established process linking strategic research findings to national development plans, medium-term fiscal planning, sectoral policies and programme implementation, the government could overlook practical policy options for addressing recurring national challenges and improving public expenditure. To address the concerns, the House expressed the conviction that institutionalising a formal Government Response to Strategic Research Recommendations mechanism would strengthen evidence-based governance, promote accountability and ensure greater value from publicly funded strategic research. Under the proposed mechanism, relevant MDAs would be required to document whether recommendations referred to them were accepted, accepted with modification, deferred or rejected, alongside reasons for their decisions and proposed implementation measures where applicable. The motion urged the Federal Government, through the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (OSGF), in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning and other relevant authorities, to establish a coordinated framework for receiving, reviewing, referring and monitoring strategic research recommendations from NIPSS, NDC and NISS. It also called on the government to integrate consideration of research recommendations into existing national development planning and budgetary processes, including the MTEF, Fiscal Strategy Paper (FSP), Medium-Term Sector Strategy (MTSS) and annual budget preparation. In addition, the motion urged the Office of the National Security Adviser, in collaboration with relevant defence, intelligence and security authorities, to establish procedures for the secure consideration and utilisation of strategic research findings from NDC and NISS, while safeguarding classified information and national security interests. The lawmakers further called for a periodic reporting mechanism, through existing administrative and performance-monitoring structures, to track the consideration and implementation of strategic research recommendations, with appropriate summaries made available for accountability and policy evaluation, subject to applicable confidentiality requirements. The motion also mandated the Committees on National Planning, National Security and Intelligence, Defence and Special Duties to engage the concerned institutions, monitor the establishment and implementation of the proposed framework, and report back to the House within four weeks. The proposed measures are aimed at creating a more structured link between publicly funded strategic research and government decision-making, with the objective of improving policy coordination, institutional learning and the implementation of national development priorities.

title: AWS named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contact Center as a Service
body: I’m proud to share that Amazon Web Services (AWS) has been named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) for Amazon Connect for the fourth consecutive year. We believe this recognition reflects years of work pushing on what’s possible in customer experience. When we launched Amazon Connect Customer, we set out to evolve how businesses serve their customers: to make personalized, intelligent experiences possible without giving up efficiency, flexibility, or control. That belief still drives how we build today. Customer expectations have shifted. People expect you to recognize them, understand what they need, and stay consistent across every channel. They don’t want to repeat themselves. They don’t want to navigate disconnected systems to solve a simple problem. They want interactions that feel natural, relevant, and genuinely helpful. Meeting that takes more than traditional contact center technology, it takes a comprehensive solution that brings together customer context, AI, and the flexibility to adapt. That’s what we’re building with Amazon Connect Customer. Customer experience without compromise What matters most to your customers hasn’t changed: they want to be known, they want their problems fully resolved, and they want to trust you in the moments that matter. Read the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant to know why we are recognized. Experiences that start with knowing the customer. Connect Customer builds a living picture of every customer: who they are, what they’ve been through, what they need next. Every touchpoint draws on that intelligence. Your customer feels known before a single word is exchanged. That’s what personal actually looks like. Resolution that carries all the way through. Most of the industry is still optimizing for deflection: getting customers away from humans as fast as possible. We took a different path. Connect Customer is built for the hard things: the disputed claim, the renegotiated mortgage, the disrupted itinerary that needs real action and can’t go wrong. We carry those interactions all the way through to resolution, and we make them feel natural and personal. Generative and agentic AI push this further: understanding what a customer needs and acting on it. Every action is auditable. Humans step in when the moment calls for it. You get enterprise scale and the confidence that nothing slips through the cracks. Building for what’s next The companies that win the next decade of customer experience won’t be the ones with the most channels or the fastest bot. They’ll be the ones whose customers feel known, whose problems actually get resolved, and whose trust is earned in the moments that matter most. Connect Customer exists to make that real for businesses of every size. I’m proud of the Connect Customer team for receiving this recognition for the fourth year in a row. Our engineers, product teams, partners, and customers shaped what we’ve built. This is a moment to celebrate how far we’ve come, and a signal of what’s ahead. Every customer is unique. title: CDC's deputy director resigns after being hired in April
body:
Dr. Jennifer Shuford's last day will be Nov. 12.
Dr. Jennifer Shuford, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's deputy director, has resigned, the agency said in a statement on Tuesday.
Shuford, who also served as chief medical officer, was hired for the role in April. Her last day will be Nov. 12, the CDC said.
"I am leaving to spend more time with my family," Shuford said in a statement. "I am so thankful to President Trump and Secretary Kennedy for giving me the opportunity to help lead CDC. It has been an amazing experience and I will be forever grateful for it."
In a separate statement, Dr. Erica Schwartz, the CDC's director, thanked Shuford for her time at the federal health agency.
"I am deeply grateful for Dr. Shuford's outstanding leadership and commitment to CDC and public health, especially as she has navigated an exceptionally demanding, high-profile and constantly evolving environment over the past several months," Schwartz said.
In the interim, Satish Pillai will serve as acting CDC chief medical officer and deputy director.
Shuford is board-certified in internal medicine and infectious diseases and received her medical degree from the University of Texas Southwestern Medical School, according to her bio on the CDC website .
Before joining the CDC, Shuford served as Texas' chief state epidemiologist, later becoming commissioner of the Texas Department of State Health Services.
"In this role, Dr. Shuford oversaw statewide public health programs, including infectious disease response, health promotion, epidemiology and emergency preparedness," her bio reads.
Shuford was appointed in April with two others at the same time Schwartz was nominated by President Donald Trump to serve as the next CDC director.
"These Highly Respected Doctors of Medicine have the knowledge, experience, and TOP degrees to restore the GOLD STANDARD OF SCIENCE at the CDC," Trump wrote in a social media post at the time.
Shuford has been a vocal supporter of vaccination, saying areas with declining measles vaccination rates are at an increased risk of outbreaks.
In February 2025, when a measles outbreak was spreading in western Texas, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said measles outbreaks were "not unusual," adding that they happen every year.
But in an appearance on CNN the same month, Shuford described Texas' measles outbreak as "unusual" for the state.
"We haven't had this sort of an outbreak since the early 1990s and it's seriously impacting the population in that region," she said. "This community has had some falling vaccine coverage rates in recent years and so we're trying to correct that, trying to get vaccines out there to protect our population and to try to get rid of this measles outbreak that's affecting them right now."
Additionally, during the COVID-19 pandemic, while still in her role as chief state epidemiologist, Shuford appeared in a video posted on Facebook explaining how COVID-19 vaccines work, including efficacy and side effects.

title: Some 75% of Jewish employees find workplace DEI approaches inconsistent on antisemitism - study
body: A new workplace study published on Tuesday has revealed that 75.5% of Jewish employees feel that Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) approaches within their organizations fail to respond consistently to antisemitism.The research report titled Yes, But... Antisemitism and the Limits of Workplace Inclusion was published by Pearn Kandola, a business psychology firm co-founded by Professor Binna Kandola. Pearn Kandola is a UK-based occupational psychology consultancy that specializes in diversity, inclusion, and unconscious bias training for corporate and public sector organizations.The study follows the organization's 2024 research on workplace antisemitism and Islamophobia, which tracked a nearly 50% increase in antisemitic incidents following the October 7, 2023 massacre.Following a series of webinars held during Antisemitism at Work Week in June, researchers noted that Jewish attendees repeatedly described a lack of responsiveness from diversity teams regarding antisemitism, prompting a broader investigation into whether these experiences reflected an isolated trend or a systemic pattern.The research combined a national survey of 1,002 Jewish employees across the UK with qualitative interviews involving participants from various sectors and organizational levels. The interviews included individuals directly involved in diversity and inclusion roles, with some working for large US multinationals and describing interactions with American diversity teams.Majority of Jewish respondents have misgivings over practical application of corporate commitments to equalityAccording to the survey findings, while the vast majority of Jewish respondents acknowledged public corporate commitments to equality, major misgivings emerged regarding their practical application. Specifically, 87% of respondents agreed that their organization expressed a clear commitment to tackling racism and discrimination, and 83% agreed that the diversity function was visibly active on these issues. However, 75.5% agreed that their organization's diversity approach was not consistent in its response to antisemitism, 72.7% noticed a gap between public commitments and actual responses, and 60.5% agreed that antisemitism receives less attention than other forms of racism.The survey findings also highlighted a severe chilling effect on employee reporting and confidence. Only 15.9% of respondents said they felt able to raise concerns about antisemitism in the workplace. Furthermore, 70.8% of respondents agreed that they had avoided raising concerns because they were unsure how those reports would be received. The report analyzed this low reporting not as an indicator of low prevalence, but as a cycle of futility where employees conclude that speaking up will not yield understanding or action.The study pointed to organizational listening as a central challenge. The report claimed that providing formal reporting channels or communication pathways is insufficient if institutions lack the capability and motivation to properly receive, interpret, and act upon employee feedback. When concerns are routinely minimized or misread, employees tend to withdraw, creating a dangerous paradox where a low number of complaints mistakenly bolsters corporate confidence that no underlying problem exists.Problem goes beyond lack of understanding Kandola tells 'Post'Professor Binna Kandola OBE told The Jerusalem Post: “Our research raises serious questions about the way Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion functions operate. We found that many Jewish employees feel overlooked by the very people whose responsibility it is to promote inclusion.”Kandola added, “The problem goes beyond a lack of understanding of antisemitism. It concerns the assumptions and frameworks that some DEI practitioners use to understand discrimination. Jews are often stereotyped as wealthy, powerful, influential, and privileged. Because many are white, they do not fit comfortably into models of discrimination that see racism primarily through the lens of power and privilege. As a result, antisemitism can be minimized, explained away, or simply ignored.”Through in-depth interviews, the research examined how diversity functions can fail to address antisemitism, identifying several recurring rhetorical devices and organizational responses. Among these, denial manifested directly or through silence and omission, such as when Holocaust Memorial Day events omitted references to Jews or when organizations remained silent following October 7. Reversal occurred when individuals raising antisemitism were repositioned as the wrongdoers or accused of self-interest. Liberal arguments regarding merit and fairness were also identified, where perceived Jewish success, wealth, or representation was used to imply that Jewish people do not experience racism or require inclusion support.Deracialization emerged when antisemitism was reframed as a generic religious matter, an international political issue, or an interpersonal disagreement rather than a form of racial exclusion. Other identified mechanisms included distancing through inaction or framing incidents as isolated anomalies rather than systemic issues, positive self-presentation where inclusion credentials masked operational gaps, trivialization of Jewish safety by making it low priority, and empathizing primarily with perpetrators over targets.Additional themes from the interviews explored the complexities of Jewish identity, which participants noted encompasses ethnicity, culture, ancestry, and peoplehood rather than religion alone. Interviewees also discussed the distinction between legitimate criticism of Israeli government policy and antisemitism, noting that difficulties arose when diversity teams viewed all Jewish concerns exclusively through the lens of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Employee resource groups, while intended to offer support, were occasionally reported by interviewees as having been utilized by diversity teams to block action or contain antisemitism as a niche issue relevant only to Jewish networks. Furthermore, participants described heightened fear, visibility concerns, and the heavy emotional burden of acting as educators or public advocates for their community.The report concluded by outlining several core findings regarding the limitations of current diversity practices. The report emphasized that diversity frameworks centered rigidly on power, privilege, and oppression can inadvertently obscure Jewish vulnerability due to persistent stereotypes surrounding influence and success. The report stressed that psychological safety remains ineffective without active organizational listening, and that professional expertise in antisemitism and prejudice cannot be assumed simply through a general commitment to equality or membership in affinity groups.Professor Kandola told the Post, “Organizations need to take a critical look at their DEI functions. They should examine the assumptions that underpin their work, the evidence supporting their approaches, and whether they are applying the same standards of fairness to everyone. Importantly, these reviews should not be led by the DEI functions themselves.”Professor Kandola further noted, “We also need to professionalize DEI. A commitment to equality, however sincere, is not a substitute for expertise in the psychology of prejudice, stereotyping and discrimination. Practitioners must be prepared to recognize and challenge their own biases, not just those of others.”Based on these conclusions, the report provided six key recommendations for organizational leaders: reappraise the purpose and practice of diversity functions through independent review; redefine professional expertise by ensuring practitioners understand the distinct history and contemporary manifestations of antisemitism; separate representation metrics from inclusion experiences; clarify the role of employee resource groups so they do not act as expert advisory bodies or veto mechanisms; build genuine organizational listening capabilities into reporting structures; and introduce reflexive practice so that inclusion teams routinely examine their own underlying assumptions and potential biases.“Our findings are not an argument for abandoning DEI. They are an argument for fundamentally rethinking how it operates. An approach to inclusion that fails to recognize discrimination because the people experiencing it do not fit a particular model is failing in its most basic purpose,” Professor Kandola told the Post.

title: Meet 5 Nigerians in the diaspora appointed to global positions in 2026
body: Nigerians in the diaspora have continued to secure leadership positions in global companies, academic institutions and healthcare organisations, strengthening the country’s representation in global decision-making. In 2026, several Nigerian professionals received appointments spanning corporate strategy, medicine, law, public health and academic leadership, placing them in positions to influence organisational growth, healthcare policy and international cooperation. Their appointments highlight the contributions of Nigerian professionals working across different countries and industries. Here are five Nigerians in the diaspora appointed to prominent positions in 2026. 1. Ugwechi Amadi — Chief Strategy Officer, McDonald’s Nigerian-born executive Ugwechi Amadi was appointed Senior Vice President and Chief Strategy Officer of McDonald’s in July 2026, joining the American multinational fast-food company after holding senior positions in sports, retail and management consulting. Her appointment was announced on July 15, 2026, following a statement by McDonald’s Chief Financial Officer, Ian Borden. Before joining McDonald’s, Amadi served as Executive Vice President and Head of Corporate Strategy and Development at LIV Golf, where she oversaw strategic planning and business development. She previously worked at Nike as Vice President of Global Operations Strategy, contributing to initiatives involving technology, supply chain management and organisational transformation. Earlier in her career, she worked at Boston Consulting Group, advising multinational companies on corporate strategy and business performance. Amadi holds a bachelor’s degree in Brain and Cognitive Sciences from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and a doctorate in Clinical Neuroscience from the University of Oxford. Her appointment places her in a senior position overseeing strategic priorities and supporting the company’s long-term growth. 2. Professor Ibrahim Abubakar — CEO-designate, Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations Nigerian-born epidemiologist Professor Ibrahim Abubakar was appointed Chief Executive Officer-designate of the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations in August 2026. The appointment was announced on August 14, with Abubakar scheduled to join the organisation in March 2027 and formally assume leadership in April 2027. He is expected to succeed Richard Hatchett, who has led CEPI since its establishment in 2017. Abubakar is currently Vice-Provost for Health and Professor of Infectious Disease Epidemiology at University College London. He previously directed UCL’s Institute for Global Health, contributing to research and policy development in infectious diseases, migration health and public health systems. His academic work includes research on tuberculosis, epidemiology and global disease prevention. CEPI is an international partnership that finances and coordinates vaccine development against emerging infectious diseases and potential pandemic threats. In his new role, Abubakar is expected to oversee international vaccine research partnerships and initiatives aimed at strengthening pandemic preparedness. 3. Ibironke Odumosu-Ayanu — Dean, University of Saskatchewan College of Law Nigerian-born legal scholar Ibironke Odumosu-Ayanu was appointed Dean of the University of Saskatchewan College of Law in Canada, effective October 1, 2026. Her appointment was announced on September 1 for a five-year tenure, succeeding Professor Martin Phillipson. Born and raised in Lagos, Odumosu-Ayanu obtained her law degree from the University of Lagos before moving to Canada for postgraduate studies. She holds a Master of Laws degree from the University of Calgary and a doctorate from the University of British Columbia. She joined the University of Saskatchewan in 2008 and previously served as a professor and Associate Dean of Research and Graduate Studies. Her research focuses on international investment law, business and human rights, natural resource governance and community development. She has also received recognition for her teaching and academic mentorship. As dean, Odumosu-Ayanu is responsible for providing academic leadership, advancing research and supporting the strategic development of the Canadian law school. 4. Bolu Ogunyemi — President, Canadian Medical Association Nigerian-born physician Dr Bolu Ogunyemi assumed office as President of the Canadian Medical Association on May 29, 2026, becoming the first Black person to lead the organisation. His inauguration took place during the association’s annual general meeting, marking a milestone for representation in Canada’s medical profession. Ogunyemi is a dermatologist based in St. John’s, Newfoundland and Labrador, with experience in clinical medicine, medical education and healthcare advocacy. The Canadian Medical Association is a national professional organisation that represents physicians and advocates improvements in healthcare delivery. As president, Ogunyemi has focused on issues including access to primary healthcare, reducing administrative burdens on physicians and supporting innovations that improve patient outcomes. He has also highlighted the importance of healthcare systems that reflect Canada’s diverse population. His appointment places him at the forefront of national discussions on healthcare policy, physician welfare and the future of medical practice in Canada. 5. Dr Zainab Shinkafi-Bagudu — President, Union for International Cancer Control Nigerian paediatrician and cancer advocate Dr Zainab Shinkafi-Bagudu assumed the presidency of the Union for International Cancer Control, a Geneva-based organisation working to reduce the global cancer burden and improve access to cancer care. She is the founder of the Medicaid Cancer Foundation, a Nigerian nonprofit organisation focused on cancer awareness, screening, prevention and patient support. Shinkafi-Bagudu previously served as First Lady of Kebbi State from 2015 to 2023, during which she championed healthcare interventions, particularly cancer prevention and treatment for women and children. Her work has involved collaboration with international health organisations, policymakers and advocacy groups to improve cancer care in underserved communities. As UICC president, she leads the organisation’s board in promoting international cooperation, equitable access to cancer treatment and stronger cancer-control policies. Her appointment places a Nigerian healthcare professional at the helm of an international organisation working with partners across the global cancer-control community.
