title: Iran-linked Handala hacking group sends bouquets and letters to Israel polling sites
body: Handala, a hacking group that US authorities say is linked to Iran, says it placed bouquets of flowers with "sensitive items" at various polling sites in Israel as the country votes in one of its most anticipated elections in years. A message posted to Handala Hack , the group's Telegram channel, showed pictures and videos of the bouquets appearing just outside voting centres, along with several letters. "Just moments ago, Handala operatives successfully planted a package containing a bouquet of flowers, a message, and a special letter signed by Asif Sarmad, commander of Handala’s Popular Resistance Front, deep inside the occupied territories, right at the heart of Gadi Eisenkot’s hideout," the Telegram message read. It was referring to referring to the former military chief of staff seeking to unseat Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. "The package has now reached the former commander, a clear and mocking message to those who have feared our shadows for years and still entertain illusions of security," the message continued. Handala warned that "in the coming hours", more packages from the hacking group might also be discovered. "Other bouquets have been quietly placed at the heart of your polling stations," read Telegram message. There was no indication that the bouquets posed any sort of threat. For more than a year, Handala has claimed responsibility for various cyber security-related issues and apparent hacks around the world. In March, the Iran-linked group followed through on a threat to attack the FBI by hacking director Kash Patel's personal email and cloud services. Hours after making the threat, Handala posted apparent photos of Mr Patel traveling and an old CV with his personal contact information. In a statement at the time, the FBI said it was aware of malicious entities looking to breach Mr Patel's digital assets. "We have taken all necessary steps to mitigate potential risks associated with this activity," the statement read. "The information in question is historical in nature and involves no government information." The bureau said that the State Department at the time was offering up to a $10 million reward for information leading to the identification of the Handala hackers. It was later determined that Handala was responsible for a cyber attack against Michigan-based medical technology company Stryker , which has more than 50,000 employees around the world. In March, the US Justice Department seized websites operated by Handala, but it does not seem to have affected the hacking group's operations. Handala's Telegram channel has been removed several times for breaching the platform's terms of service and other rules, only for the group to re-emerge later with a newly activated account.

title: BAE Systems completes first live-fire test of Adaptable Deck Launcher for naval missiles
body: The ADL was developed under a U.S. Department of War contract for the NATO Seasparrow Project Office. It uses existing Mk 41 Vertical Launching System electronics and logistics, drawing on established support infrastructure to keep operating costs down. “The successful demonstration of the Adaptable Deck Launcher is a major milestone in our commitment to enhancing the Navy’s combat effectiveness and readiness,” said Jason Casciotti, vice president of Weapons Systems at BAE Systems. “The ADL complements the Mk 41 VLS — the foundation of naval missile integration — by providing a capability for rapid replenishment, using standard shipboard equipment and offering the fleet additional flexibility in how it sustains combat loads at sea.” BAE Systems designed the launcher for aircraft carriers, amphibious ships and other surface combatants. Compact configurations are also intended for medium uncrewed surface vessels. The launcher is fully compatible with Evolved SeaSparrow Missile Mk 25 Quad-Pack canisters, according to BAE Systems. These provide surface-to-air defense against supersonic anti-ship missiles, aircraft and other aerial threats.

title: Likud officials sound alarm over voter apathy as Israel sees record-high election turnout
body: Against the backdrop of unusually high turnout and reports of long queues at polling stations in strongholds of the change bloc and in Arab communities, Likud fears that even its traditional gevalt calls may fail to get right-wing voters out of their homes this election.The party is concerned about the mobilization of the camp opposing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the difficulty of generating enthusiasm among some right-wing voters as the battle for power enters its decisive hours.Likud officials describe a particularly worrying picture.“If we haven't managed to make the right-wing public want to go out and vote by now, even a last-minute gevalt call will only help to some extent,” they said. According to them, “It seems that this time the public hears our gevalt calls and remembers the boy who cried 'Wolf, wolf.'”At this stage, one official added, “There isn't even a single encouraging sign.”Likud stronghold cities not as motivated to voteOne example is the relatively low turnout in Bat Yam, considered a Likud stronghold. The city's mayor, Tzvika Brot, is also managing Likud's campaign. As of noon, turnout in the city stood at just 23%.It is important to note, however, that this figure represents overall turnout. It cannot be used to draw conclusions about the level of support for Likud or any other party.Relatively low turnout was also recorded in other localities traditionally associated with Likud. As of noon, turnout stood at approximately 24% in Kiryat Shmona, 25% in Nof HaGalil, and 27% in Kiryat Malachi. In Ashkelon, Dimona, and Migdal Ha'emek, approximately 29% of eligible voters had cast their ballots. The figures were around 30% in Afula and 32% in Beit She'an.These figures reflect overall turnout in each locality and do not indicate how many Likud supporters have voted or how much support the party enjoys there.The concerns come as figures from the Central Elections Committee point to exceptionally high voter participation nationwide. By 10:00 a.m., 16.68% of eligible voters had cast their ballots, the highest turnout recorded at that hour since 1981.By noon, national turnout had reached 31.5%, compared with 28.4% at the same time during the elections for the 25th Knesset. That represents an increase of 3.1 percentage points and the highest turnout at that hour since 1977.The trend continued into the afternoon. By 2:00 p.m., turnout had reached 44.9%, compared with 38.9% in the previous election, an increase of six percentage points and the highest rate recorded at that hour since at least 1973.The early turnout figures were presented at a press conference held at the Knesset's command center by Adv. Din Livne, acting director-general of the Central Elections Committee.Long queues at polling stations continueDespite the high national turnout, the figures do not yet reveal how participation is divided between the political blocs.According to an analysis by the Stat-Net Institute, the number of polling stations in Arab localities is lower than in the previous election, even though the number of eligible voters has increased. This may explain some of the long queues.Voting patterns in Arab society are a particular concern for Likud. Polls published before the election estimated that turnout in Arab communities could reach approximately 60%–63%, up from around 56% in 2022. Such an increase could affect the distribution of Knesset seats and make it more difficult for Netanyahu's bloc to secure a parliamentary majority.The party is also worried about losing votes to smaller right-wing parties that fail to cross the electoral threshold, which would weaken the camp's overall strength.Likud's concerns are not new. Even before Election Day, disagreements emerged within the party's campaign headquarters. Some officials expressed confidence in the internal projections of pollster Shlomo Filber, while others worried about the opposing camp's efforts to mobilize voters.One official described the dispute over Filber's projections this way: “Either Momo comes out a king, or Momo goes home”.Another concern is voter apathy among Likud supporters. Their mobilization during the 2022 election helped Netanyahu's bloc secure its electoral victory.Likud fears the 'Wolf, wolf' warnings have lost their impactNetanyahu himself is working to mobilize right-wing voters. In a video circulated today, he warned of efforts by the change bloc to bring voters to the polls.“We are in danger, because the left is flying its thousands of people thousands of kilometers so that they will come to the polling station,” he said in an appeal to residents of the West Bank, asking them to help get voters to the polls.Likud has prepared an extensive voter-mobilization operation, working alongside other parties in its political camp to increase turnout during the remaining hours before polling stations close.The party's efforts are further complicated by restrictions on one of the tools it used in previous election campaigns. Following a Supreme Court ruling limiting parties' ability to track voter participation, Likud argued that its capacity to identify supporters who had not yet voted and take steps to get them to the polls had been impaired. Disagreements over the transfer of real-time voting data continued in the days leading up to the election.Likud also remembers the 2022 election, when its voter-mobilization efforts helped Netanyahu's bloc win 64 Knesset seats. At the time, the party succeeded in increasing turnout among its supporters by approximately five percentage points compared with the preceding election.This time, however, the concern, according to a party official, is that repeated warnings about the danger of losing power are no longer eliciting the same response.On the very day Likud needs its supporters to turn out at the polls, party officials fear that the public has stopped reacting to the repeated cries of “Wolf, wolf.”

title: Saudi Aramco Offers Discounted Oil to Europe as Exports Recover
body:
Iraq's Oil Exports via Turkey Surge to 500,000 Bpd
Julianne Geiger is a veteran energy journalist and market analyst with more than a decade of experience covering the global oil and gas sector. Her…
Saudi Aramco is offering additional crude to European refiners for October and November loading, just weeks after telling customers they would receive no oil under their October contracts following an attack on the kingdom's East-West pipeline.
The Saudi oil giant offered late-October spot cargoes at a discount to its official selling price, according to Bloomberg, citing a person familiar with the matter. The shipments were available from either the Red Sea port of Yanbu or Sidi Kerir on Egypt's Mediterranean coast.
Aramco followed those offers with additional November spot cargoes. European refiners have also been told they will receive their full contracted November allocations, a considerable improvement from the October cancellations.
Aramco told European refiners earlier this month that their contracted October cargoes weren't coming after an attack shut down the East-West pipeline. Now the pipeline is running again, and the company is offering spot shipments for October and November, with some October barrels priced below its official selling price.
Quite a turnaround for customers who were told they weren't getting any oil at all.
Saudi Arabia normally ships 700,000 to 800,000 barrels per day to Europe, much of it under long-term contracts. The October cancellations sent refiners into the spot market looking for replacement barrels. Now Saudi crude is available again, and prices for some European grades have already started to fall.
The additional Saudi supply has already helped push down prices for some crude grades in Europe this week, traders told Bloomberg.
Saudi Arabia's production recovery has been substantial. The kingdom increased output by roughly one-third in September to more than 8 million bpd, rebounding from its lowest production level in more than three decades in August.
Other Gulf producers are also recovering. The United Arab Emirates has increased production to a record high, according to the International Energy Agency, while Iraqi exports are approaching prewar levels.
The recovery comes despite continued Iranian attacks on regional energy infrastructure and vessels near the Strait of Hormuz.
Aramco is also pursuing additional overseas crude storage and alternative export capacity to reduce its exposure to regional disruptions, including an agreement to store oil in Singapore beginning in 2027 .

title: UK urged to classify anti-Zionism as extremism, ban marches near Jewish institutions
body: B'nai B'rith UK has called on the British government to classify anti-Zionism as an extremist ideology, permanently ban al-Quds Day demonstrations, restrict protests near Jewish institutions and take stronger action against organizations accused of promoting anti-Jewish hatred.The demands are laid out in the organization's 108-page report, titled Antizionism: The New Face of Anti-Jewish Extremism. Written by Dr. Jeremy Havardi, the report was formally presented at the UK Parliament on October 20 at an event co-chaired by Labour MP Mark Sewards and Conservative MP Sir Iain Duncan Smith.The report argues that anti-Zionism has become a predominant expression of modern antisemitism, drawing on Nazi propaganda, Soviet ideology and Islamist extremism, while presenting itself through the language of human rights and social justice.It sets out 11 policy recommendations aimed at addressing what Havardi describes as an extremist movement that has contributed to the harassment, intimidation and exclusion of Jews from public life.Among its principal recommendations is that the British government formally identify anti-Zionism as an extremist ideology and condemn political parties, nongovernmental organizations and civil society groups that promote it.Restrictions on anti-Zionist demonstrationsThe report calls for strict limitations on future anti-Zionist demonstrations, particularly those taking place near Jewish community institutions.It stresses that “No march should be allowed next to synagogues, Jewish schools or Jewish social venues as this is a clear example of racist provocation.”It also recommends the arrest and prosecution of demonstrators who incite violence against Zionists, including through calls for an intifada or slogans threatening Jews.Although it acknowledges the importance of freedom of expression, the report argues that incitement should not be protected under the principle of free speech.Havardi also calls for a permanent ban on London's annual al-Quds Day demonstration, which he links to Iranian efforts to promote radicalization in Britain.The proposed measures go beyond existing restrictions on particular demonstrations and would require further government action.Universities, charities and public institutionsThe report also proposes greater scrutiny of universities, charities and other public institutions accused of tolerating antisemitism.It recommends mandatory reporting of antisemitic incidents and complaints across public bodies, including the measures taken in response, alongside the adoption of the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance's working definition of antisemitism.University administrators would be required to undergo antisemitism training, and institutions should appoint dedicated antisemitism officers when possible.The report further calls for disciplinary action against university staff and students found to be glorifying Palestinian or Islamist terrorism.Regarding charities, it urges the Charity Commission to shut down organizations promoting anti-Zionist violence or hatred, while maintaining safeguards for lawful advocacy.The report also calls on the government to remind music, sporting, and cultural venues of their responsibilities under the Equality Act when responding to demands to exclude Jewish or Israeli performers.Iran, Qatar and the Muslim BrotherhoodBeyond domestic activism, Havardi calls for the expulsion of Iran's ambassador to Britain and the proscription of media channels promoting the ideology of the Islamic Republic of Iran and its regional proxies.The report identifies several media organizations operating in Britain that it says are connected to Iranian influence networks, including members of the Islamic Radio and Television Union.It also recommends that Britain ban the Muslim Brotherhood as a terrorist organization on national security grounds.If the organization does not meet the legal threshold for proscription under the Terrorism Act 2000, the report suggests designating it an extremist organization, following the approach of German federal authorities.The report further calls for Qatar's funding of Islamist organizations in Britain to be identified and monitored, accusing Doha of using its influence to spread anti-Zionist and antisemitic narratives.Anti-Zionism's impact beyond Jewish communitiesThe report also argues that anti-Zionism has consequences for Palestinians, claiming that opposition to Jewish national self-determination undermines coexistence and prospects for a negotiated peace.Havardi contends that anti-Zionist movements marginalize Israelis and Palestinians who pursue dialogue, while political rejectionism has contributed to lost economic opportunities for Palestinians.The report cites previously published research, including figures showing that more than 160,000 Palestinians worked in Israel or Israeli settlements before October 7, 2023, to illustrate the economic importance of cross-border cooperation.Havardi argues that these consequences contradict the British government's commitment to a two-state solution and its support for regional normalization through the Abraham Accords.The report's recommendations have not yet been adopted as British government policy.

title: Judge blasts prosecutors, refuses to sign new criminal complaint against ex-FBI officials
body:
A judge on Tuesday sharply criticized federal prosecutors for failing to get judicial approval before filing a new criminal complaint overnight against two ex-FBI officials accused of lying to Congress about investigations of Hunter Biden .
Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui said he would not sign off on the new complaint, which added a charge of obstruction against Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides in U.S. District Court in Washington.
"I am not going to bless it as a superseding complaint," Faruqui said at a court hearing, after Floris' lawyers filed a motion arguing the new complaint was legally deficient and filed in bad faith.
He told prosecutors that if they wanted to file a superseding complaint, a judge first would have to find probable cause that a crime had been committed, instead of sending him the complaint in the middle of the night and expecting him to sign it.
Faruqui said he did not believe that federal prosecutors had previously sought to file a criminal complaint without a judge's signature.
"It is not our court's practice … that unsigned complaints are filed in the docket," Faruqui said.
"I'm concerned with your view as to what the law is," the judge told the prosecutors. "Why today, on this one case, have you changed the entire history of how you charge cases?"
The superseding complaint that prosecutors in the office of D.C. U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro filed in court early Tuesday contained a signature block with Faruqui's name typed out. But the judge had not personally signed the complaint.
It was filed hours before prosecutors and defense lawyers were due to appear before Faruqui for a preliminary hearing on the original complaint.
That first complaint, made public last Friday, accuses Floris and Benavides of making false statements to the House Judiciary Committee in 2023 about their involvement in investigations of Hunter Biden, the son of former President Joe Biden .
Floris and Benavides were arrested Friday and have been released.
The new complaint sought to charge them with obstruction and attempted obstruction of a congressional proceeding.
Typically, criminal cases for conduct that occurred well in the past — as this one alleges — are lodged through an indictment, not a criminal complaint. To obtain an indictment, prosecutors must present evidence to a grand jury, which then determines whether the evidence is sufficient to charge a defendant.
A criminal complaint only requires a judge's signature. It is often used to obtain an arrest warrant in situations where prosecutors need to move quickly .
At Tuesday's hearing, Faruqui homed in on the way prosecutors filed charges.
"This case was charged by criminal complaint on Oct. 20, for testimony that occurred over a period of time in 2023," he said. "As I noted, and I think it continues to be the case, that it's unusual in a case that has conduct like this to be charged by criminal complaint."
"This has to get to a grand jury," Faruqui said.
Under federal rules, prosecutors generally must obtain an indictment within 30 days of a person's arrest, or risk the case being dismissed.
Floris' lawyers, in an emailed statement to CNBC on Tuesday morning, criticized the prosecutors' conduct.
"In the middle of the night, the government filed an unsigned and unsworn complaint attempting to fix the issues with their original charge against Ms. Floris and adding a new charge just as meritless as the first one," the attorneys wrote.
"In our combined decades of DOJ service, we have never seen or even heard of something like this being filed. That's because the public lodging of criminal charges must be authorized by the grand jury, a judge, or the defendant herself," they wrote.
"Here, the government has taken that power for itself in a desperate attempt to delay our client's right to challenge the charges in court and litigate this case in the media, rather than the courtroom," they said.
"We have asked to address this outrageous government conduct against a decorated public servant at today's court hearing," Floris' legal team wrote.
In their motion to strike the superseding criminal complaint, the lawyers argued the document "represents a serious abuse of the criminal charging process, a troubling disregard for the judicial safeguards governing the initiation of criminal proceedings, and a calculated effort to evade judicial scrutiny and shield the government's allegations from adversarial testing at the scheduled preliminary hearing."

title: Pezeshkian, Putin discuss energy cooperation during meeting in Moscow
body:
TEHRAN, October 27. /TASS/. Iranian and Russian Presidents Masoud Pezeshkian and Vladimir Putin discussed cooperation in the oil and gas sector at their meeting on Tuesday on the sidelines of the summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum in Moscow, the Iranian president’s office said.
According to it, the presidents discussed "recent developments in bilateral relations and ways of strengthening cooperation and stressed the need for closer cooperation in the political, economic, and trade spheres."
Among the key topics were issues of energy cooperation, the development of ties in the oil and gas sector, the expansion of economic exchanges, and the use of each other’s potential for the implementation of joint projects, it added.

title: Starving residents of Oleshky must not become props in Russian propaganda
body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin addresses the Russian public, the country’s armed forces and law enforcement agencies amid the Wagner Group’s armed rebellion on June 24, 2023. (Artem Priakhin/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)
Executive Editor of The Reckoning Project
For months, desperate civilians remaining in the southern Ukrainian city of Oleshky have been blockaded inside, as Russia severed food and medicine supplies to the city amid constant shelling, food shop closures, and reports of looting; many of the city's elderly and less mobile residents have been forced to forage for weeds and eat grass in order to simply survive.
Oleshky is starving. The stories of the residents have been well documented.
Now, there seems to be light at the end of the tunnel: U.S. First Lady Melania Trump has helped to broker a temporary, localized ceasefire agreement, which, in theory, should take place from Tuesday, Oct. 27. Much-needed aid could finally be delivered, and residents evacuated.
But this city of weak, hungry, and vulnerable people will face a new danger as Oleshky slowly opens: under the pressure of living on the brink of death, they could become props for Russian propagandists attempting to rewrite the history of what happened in the city.
Russia has a long track record of attempting to blame Ukraine for its own atrocities, and who better to use than Ukrainian civilians themselves? Ukraine is well aware of the danger. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha have already raised concerns about how Russia will likely manipulate the ceasefire.
Russia will likely "do everything it can to clear the roads in such a way that these people head toward Russia and remain there," said Zelensky. Sybiha has noted that Russia is preparing to stage "dozens" of videos in occupied Oleshky.
"Then they would ask a question, turn off the camera, tell her what to answer, and then turn the camera back on to record the 'required' response. Armed soldiers were present the entire time together with the journalists, standing behind their backs."
"Local residents will be forced to say on camera that they are happy, well-fed and grateful to the Russian occupiers," he stated. Ukraine's Security Service noted that one Russian unit has been specifically tasked with preparing "a series of 'compromising' interviews with the residents” in which they should accuse Ukraine's defense forces of "constant shelling."
At The Reckoning Project (TRP) — a global team of journalists and lawyers documenting and publicizing atrocity crimes and helping build cases to hold perpetrators accountable — we also know that this is a tried-and-tested Russian method based, among many other reasons, on the testimonies of several of our interviewees: Ukrainian civilians in the temporarily occupied territories who have previously been forced to participate in Russian propaganda campaigns against their own nation.
"Russian disinformation campaigns frequently pave the way for future aggressive Russian actions, with propaganda operations coordinated with military operations."
As these testimonies reveal, Russians exploited every opportunity to coerce civilians into becoming actors at gunpoint, serving in the Russian military, or, as one interviewee recounted, even producing and editing propaganda footage themselves if Russian forces discovered they had the necessary skills.
"They interviewed my mother-in-law. At first, they asked her name, age, and where she had lived," one witness, Viktoria, told TRP (name changed for security reasons). "Then they would ask a question, turn off the camera, tell her what to answer, and then turn the camera back on to record the 'required' response. Armed soldiers were present the entire time together with the journalists, standing behind their backs."
Russia has a long track record of creating propaganda videos to prop up its military objectives.
In July 2014, for example, after Russia's catastrophic destruction of a civilian plane carrying 298 people, Russian media and officials began promoting claims that Ukrainian forces shot down Malaysia Airlines Flight 17 traveling from Amsterdam to Kuala Lumpur.
The subsequent investigation established that the Buk, the missile launcher used in the attack, was transported from Russia before the attack and smuggled back immediately after the attack.
Russian disinformation campaigns frequently pave the way for future aggressive Russian actions, with propaganda operations coordinated with military operations.
For example, prior to Russia's full-scale invasion, the U.S. stated that it had intelligence that Russia planned to release faked footage of a supposed Ukrainian attack on Russian speakers to use as a pretext for its invasion, including plans to excavate fake "mass graves."
The same playbook could well be used today — and we are seeing the first signs — during the temporary ceasefire in Oleshky.
Key Russian media figures are already starting to spread the narrative that Russia is "rescuing" the residents that it has been terrorizing.
Kremlin propagandist Margarita Simonyan recently posted a video on her Telegram channel claiming that Ukrainians had been responsible for creating a "living hell" there.
Simonyan is notoriously unreliable: in February 2022 she stated that Russia "is not going to start a war with Ukraine, and this will not happen in any way." She also received a state award for her role in the annexation of Crimea in 2014.
As TRP has previously documented together with law firm Global Rights Compliance, Russia has also relied on preparing "information alibis" to publish cover stories for attacks even before they take place.
"The Kremlin's propaganda style has a decades-long track record, and we’ve seen these tactics even well before the war in Ukraine."
We established how Russia had started laying the groundwork to blame Ukraine for its own deadly assault on Kramatorsk railway station, stating a week beforehand that Ukraine was planning to use civilians as "human shields" in the area. Dozens were killed on April 8, 2022, but Russia gave itself away when state outlet RIA Novosti tweeted about the attack three minutes before it took place.
Russian officials, online media, and pro-war Telegram channels also spread stories that hospitals and a theater in Mariupol were full of Ukrainian military as a pretext for hitting civilians — accusations that have been debunked by journalists who were in the city, as well as eyewitnesses, UN groups, and OSINT specialists.
Similarly, Russian propagandists accused Ukrainian forces of planning the Kakhovka dam explosion and the bombing of POW camps (under the orders of U.K. intelligence) — all before Russia committed these acts itself.
The Kremlin's propaganda style has a decades-long track record, and we've seen these tactics even well before the war in Ukraine.
In Syria , Kremlin media would accuse the Syrian opposition of "gassing" civilians to cover for Putin's ally Assad's use of chemical weapons against his own people. Or going back to Soviet times, the Kremlin cynically organized a mass media campaign aimed at Western correspondents in order to make it look like their mass murder of some 14,700 Polish officers and prisoners of war at Katyn was actually the work of the Germans.
The German philosopher Nietzsche once argued that there are "no facts (...) only interpretations."
Kremlin propaganda has long followed that idea to a triumphantly cynical extreme.
At moments like this, it's important that news media do not slide into bothsideism which credits well-known sources of disinformation with the same valency as more reliable sources.
We are entering a fierce cognitive battle, where propagandists know how to play the media to whitewash their regimes' crimes.
The siege, we hope, is ending — but the assault on truth and perception is just beginning.
Editor's note: The opinions expressed in the op-ed section are those of the authors and do not purport to reflect the views of the Kyiv Independent.

title: Trapped without food, electricity, or medicine, civilians in occupied Oleshky finally have a chance to escape. But even those wishing to go to Ukraine will reportedly be taken to Russia first.
body: A ceasefire took effect early on October 27 in Oleshky (called Alyoshki in Russian) in Ukraine’s Kherson region. Russia and Ukraine had agreed to halt fighting to evacuate civilians and deliver humanitarian aid to the Russian-occupied city, where a humanitarian catastrophe has unfolded. U.S. first lady Melania Trump helped the two sides reach the agreement . The ceasefire will last until 10:59 p.m. on November 1, said David Arakhamia, who heads the Servant of the People faction in Ukraine’s parliament and is a member of Ukraine’s negotiating team. Russia’s human rights commissioner, Yana Lantratova, confirmed the timing. Arakhamia called the ceasefire in Oleshky “the biggest de-escalation since 2022.” Melania Trump said the ceasefire had begun two days ahead of schedule and had been extended beyond Oleshky to allow humanitarian convoys to pass safely. She said Valery Gerasimov, chief of Russia’s General Staff, had confirmed this. Ukraine and Russia said on the evening of October 27 that both sides were fully observing the ceasefire. The Kremlin also said the humanitarian operation in Oleshky was “going according to plan.” Many details of the humanitarian operation remain unclear: which roads will be cleared of mines, where residents will be taken and how they will be evacuated, whether they will be allowed to go directly to Ukraine or stay in Oleshky, and where families with children will be allowed to go. The Financial Times reported that even those wishing to go to Ukraine will first be taken to Russia. The operation will be carried out in several stages . Petro Andriushchenko, head of Ukraine’s Center for the Study of Occupation, said the evacuation from Oleshky is scheduled for October 30. Information about residents who want to leave is being gathered in a rush, he said, adding that details of how the evacuation will proceed remain confidential for now. Andriushchenko suggested that departures would depend on how the roads are cleared of mines. He said Ukraine expects a route across the Dnipro River to be arranged so Oleshky residents who want to go to Ukraine can travel directly to Ukrainian-controlled territory. Oleshky residents may be evacuated to Russian-annexed Crimea or Rostov-on-Don, said Vladimir Saldo , the Russia-installed “governor” of the Kherson region. He said transportation and temporary accommodation had already been arranged for them. Saldo also said those wishing to go to Ukraine would receive help. title: Israeli ad tech firm tied to suspected Starlink tracking effort, report claims
body: Discover-Tech, an Israeli advertising technology company, has reportedly been linked to a suspected surveillance effort aimed at Starlink users, according to Reuters . The report, which cites six people familiar with the matter, claims the firm was the top bidder for ad space tied to Starlink traffic in more than 100 countries. Researchers suspect the aggressive bidding was meant to reveal where users are located or to enable further monitoring — though the findings do not show that anyone was actually tracked. The data comes from TrendAI, the research arm of Trend Micro. Its October 15 report referred to the activity as ‘Shadow-Earth-79’ without naming a company, but the report claims the codename belongs to Discover-Tech. TrendAI says its attribution process is designed to avoid ‘hype-driven labels’ that could mislead security teams. “Our approach reduces the risk of misattribution, hype-driven labels, and unstable actor names that can mislead defenders, distort risk prioritization, and trigger inappropriate response actions.” The report says. The method exploits how online ads are sold with advertisers bidding in real-time auctions for space on websites and in apps, and each bid request can carry details about the person on the other end. Collected over time and combined with other data, that information could be used to identify people, follow their activity across the web, or select targets for spyware. The geography is what raised eyebrows. Shadow-Earth-79 was reportedly the largest ad buyer in Syria, Libya, Yemen, and South Sudan, and the second largest in Afghanistan, while also claiming unusually large shares of bids in Hungary, Israel, Egypt, Azerbaijan, and Venezuela. TrendAI says the pattern points to ‘targeting and tracking infrastructure rather than a commercial advertising operation.’ That is plausible, given how little legitimate Western advertising demand exists in sanctioned or war-torn markets. Notably, Discover-Tech was already under scrutiny. On the same day as TrendAI’s report, Citizen Lab and ad security firm Confiant separately named the company, alleging that it used ad auctions to collect data on users across sensitive networks, including those tied to media organizations, governments, and tech firms. “The malicious advertisements were purchased by Discover-Tech, an Israeli company that presents itself as a legitimate advertising company, but which we found operates as a facilitator for multiple mercenary spyware partners.” Citizen Lab wrote. Google and Comcast have since said they removed Discover-Tech from their advertising platforms, while the report says that a major U.S. technology company and an international organization have opened internal inquiries into whether the firm’s ads targeted their employees. For Starlink, the stakes are obvious — the service works outside conventional telecom networks, which makes it a lifeline where governments restrict internet access, and makes its users an attractive target for those same governments. In April, Iran’s nationwide internet blackout passed 1,000 hours, with authorities reportedly going after Starlink terminals and imposing severe penalties for possessing one. Earlier this month, SpaceX also limited Starlink service for Ukraine’s high-speed military drones, which Ukrainian officials say complicates logistics and operations. Advertising and consumer tech have been abused for tracking before. A backdoor was previously found in a popular iOS ad library that could collect device-location data and capture screenshots, while Chrysaor, Android spyware linked to the Pegasus family, was discovered by Lookout and Citizen Lab on a small number of devices. More recently, a researcher claimed to have found extensive data collection, including ad-related telemetry, inside a Samsung smart TV’s Tizen operating system , though those findings are still being investigated. That said, it is still unclear if Discover-Tech actually used Starlink-related data to single out specific subscribers remains unverified, and neither the company nor SpaceX has commented.

title: FBI searches home connected to former California Rep. Eric Swalwell
body:

title: Iran, Russia, other nations can solve regional issues without US — Pezeshkian
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Iran, Russia, and other countries of the region can work together to resolve all local issues without US interference, President of the Islamic Republic Masoud Pezeshkian told Russian leader Vladimir Putin.
"We must work to create a multipolar world that is beneficial to all of us. This gives us the opportunity to interact with you and other countries that want to remain independent and free. To be honest, it seems to me that we can work on all the problems that we have in the region without the intervention of the United States," he said. "We can solve all the problems ourselves. There is no need to rely on American help."
According to Pezeshkian, the countries of the region are able to help each other in all areas, including the economy, security and humanitarian assistance.

title: Ebola: NCDC defends patient’s evacuation, rejects claims of no confidence
body: Warns against politicising evacuation, false Ebola-free reports By Sola Ogundipe The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has defended the evacuation of Nigeria’s Ebola index patient to Switzerland, rejecting claims that the transfer amounted to a vote of no confidence in the country’s medical system. The Director-General of the agency, Dr Jide Idris, who spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at a capacity-building programme for journalists on effective Ebola reporting, also dismissed concerns that the evacuation was being politicised, including allegations that the Ebola incident could be used to impose a lockdown, restrict movement or interfere with the 2027 general elections. Idris said the index patient, who returned to Abuja from Uganda, improved clinically while in isolation and left Nigeria in a stable and conscious condition, even as he said the evacuation did not mean Nigeria had been declared Ebola-free, faulting reports that suggested otherwise. “Within hours of WHO saying that Nigeria currently has no Ebola case, several platforms reported that Nigeria had been declared Ebola-free. It had not, WHO had to call the reports inaccurate and misleading, and a public that believes the danger is over stops washing its hands and stops calling 6232. “The evacuation of the patient by her own government has been presented as a vote of no confidence in Nigerian medicine, when she was largely managed by Nigerian clinicians, and this case has been dragged into politics: that it is a pretext for a lockdown, for restricting movement, or for interfering with the 2027 elections. “There are also persistent demands that we name the patient and her contacts. We will not. A contact who is named is a contact who hides, and a contact who hides is how an imported case becomes an outbreak. Idris warned that premature claims that Nigeria was Ebola-free could weaken public vigilance and discourage people from observing preventive measures or contacting health authorities when symptoms developed. “The welfare stipend of N100,000 a week that we approved for people in quarantine, so as to relief the burden of other family responsibilities those in quarantine ought to be performing but unable to for now , has been turned into a story about money sharing, as if people are being paid for Ebola. “The next six weeks will test the country, and how the public comes through them depends as much on what is published by the agency and the media, ” he said. He explained that although Nigeria had no confirmed Ebola case in the country following the patient’s evacuation, 53 primary contacts remained under daily follow-up, with most in quarantine in Abuja and a few at home. Three contacts who developed symptoms had tested negative for Ebola, he confirmed. Idris said the 42-day surveillance countdown had begun, with December 7, 2026, marking the earliest possible date for declaring the event over if no new case emerged. The World Health Organisation (WHO) would validate any such declaration, he added. Further, he cautioned against demands for the disclosure of patients’ and contacts’ identities, saying exposure could discourage people from cooperating with health authorities and undermine contact tracing. “A contact who is named is a contact who hides, and a contact who hides is how an imported case becomes an outbreak,” he said. Idris, however, stressed that scrutiny of the country’s Ebola response remained legitimate, including questions about preparedness, funding and the speed of contact tracing. “Accountability is not misinformation. The difference is that a question seeks an answer, and a rumour supplies one,” he said, pledging that the agency would provide timely, on-the-record responses to journalists’ inquiries. He urged journalists to verify information before publication, use designated NCDC communication channels and correct false reports on the same platforms with comparable prominence. He also called for responsible reporting that protects patients and contacts from exposure, warning against publishing their names, photographs or addresses or using language that could stigmatise quarantined families. Reiterating key public health messages, Idris said Ebola spreads through contact with the body fluids of a sick infected person, not through the air. He added that people without symptoms were not infectious and that healthy travellers should not automatically be treated as threats. He advised anyone who develops a fever and has a relevant travel or contact history to call the NCDC’s 6232 hotline before visiting a health facility. “The public does not need louder headlines; it needs accurate ones, repeated by voices it trusts. Those voices are yours,” he said. The post Ebola: NCDC defends patient’s evacuation, rejects claims of no confidence appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Tinubu needs another term to consolidate reforms — Tompolo
body: …Presents 30 vehicles for mobilisation By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Ahead of the 2027 presidential election, High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has mobilised support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in Imo State, declaring that the President means well for Nigeria and deserves another four years to consolidate his administration’s reforms. Tompolo made the declaration on Tuesday at the inauguration of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Imo State, where he donated 30 vehicles to facilitate grassroots mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election. Represented by the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services Limited, Chief Kestin Pondi, Tompolo said the vehicles and other resources were provided to support Governor Hope Uzodimma and the movement’s campaign activities across the state. He described Tinubu as a courageous leader who prioritised Nigeria’s interests by embarking on economic reforms from the beginning of his administration in May 2023. “Our President, President Bola Tinubu, is a very courageous man. A man who puts Nigeria first. A man who loves Nigeria more than he loves himself. “A man who loves Nigeria more than the office that he is vying for. When he came into office, he did not do the normal calculations that politicians usually do. He came in and said that he wants to reform Nigeria,” Tompolo said. Relaying Tompolo’s message, Pondi said the donation was aimed at strengthening the movement’s capacity to mobilise voters for the President across the state. “Your Excellency, we have come with vehicles. We have come with resources. These vehicles you have seen, there are 30 of them. We brought them to Imo State to support you in your cause to re-elect President Bola Tinubu,” he said. Tompolo said the movement would work with Uzodimma and other political leaders to take the President’s campaign to households and communities across Imo State, adding that the newly inaugurated chapter would be available to support campaign activities whenever required. “Your Excellency, the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Imo State is at your beck and call. Anytime you need them, call them. Give them instructions. Tell them how you want them to campaign,” he said. Speaking at the event, Governor Uzodimma commended Tompolo for providing resources to support the campaign, describing the movement as an important partner in efforts to secure another term for Tinubu. Uzodimma said his assessment of the President’s performance had convinced him that Tinubu should be given another term to complete his programmes and initiatives. “When we preach the Gospel about the All Progressives Congress government of President Bola Tinubu, we started, we were not many. But as the days go by, the efforts and activities of the government begin to trickle in. Nigerians begin to see the man called Bola Tinubu in his true colour,” he said. The governor acknowledged that the administration had made progress but still had outstanding tasks to accomplish, adding that continuity would enable Tinubu to complete his work. “We have assessed the achievements of President Bola Tinubu. And we have seen the good things he brought. We have also seen so many things he is also yet to do. “And we decided to lead the crusade that will enable him to complete his good work. We have taken that decision,” Uzodimma said. He described Tompolo as a committed supporter of the President’s re-election bid and praised the door-to-door campaign strategy for taking the message of the Renewed Hope Agenda directly to Nigerians. “We are partners in progress. We work with you. We do the work. We elect the President,” he said. Earlier, the National Coordinator of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Sunday Asuku, urged Nigerians to remain patient with the administration, arguing that the economic difficulties associated with its reforms would give way to long-term benefits. Asuku said Tinubu had laid a foundation for economic development in the past three and a half years and should be allowed another four years to build on it. “The message we must tell today is simple and short. Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has sent us to make you understand that things might be rough, but Nigeria is on the right trajectory,” he said. He maintained that economic reforms often came with temporary difficulties but argued that they were necessary to achieve lasting prosperity. “Where there is reform, we are expected to go through some pains. But it is a pain that guarantees long-term prosperity. And we can get through for sure,” Asuku said. He also challenged opposition politicians to account for their records in public office, urging Nigerians to examine their past performances before making electoral decisions. Asuku called on voters to turn out en masse on January 16, 2027, to vote for Tinubu, adding that the movement would take its campaign from door to door, town to town and community to community. In his remarks, Imo State APC Chairman, Chief Austine Onyedebelu, highlighted the Federal Government’s economic reforms and the state government’s infrastructure projects, urging party members to take the campaign directly to residents. He cited the removal of the petrol subsidy, foreign exchange reforms, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund and the increase in the national minimum wage to N70,000 as measures introduced by the Tinubu administration. Onyedebelu, however, acknowledged that rising food prices, transportation costs and other economic pressures remained concerns for many Nigerians, stressing that the ultimate measure of government policies should be their impact on citizens’ living conditions. He also highlighted infrastructure projects undertaken by the Uzodimma administration, saying the door-to-door campaign would provide an opportunity to explain government policies and programmes directly to residents rather than relying solely on rallies. The post Tinubu needs another term to consolidate reforms — Tompolo appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Turkmenistan Airlines Increases International Flights
body: Turkmenistan Airlines is increasing the frequency of several international flights under a revised schedule that took effect on October 25. “Direct flights from the capital to Seoul will double from one to two flights per week. On the Italian route to Milan, flight frequency will increase from two to three flights per week,” the state-run Turkmenistan News Portal said before the new schedule took effect. “Regular flights on the Ashgabat–Kazan route will increase from four to six flights per week. Additionally, air service to Istanbul will be expanded, with total flight frequency reaching 13 flights per week compared to the previous 12,” the news site reported. It said the updated schedule, which includes return flights to Ashgabat International Airport, is aimed at meeting growing demand for air travel and is another step “in integrating the country’s civil aviation infrastructure into the global transport network.” At the same time, the number of flights to New Delhi was scheduled to be reduced from three to two per week, according to Turkmen media. The flight frequency on other routes, including Beijing, Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur, London, and Frankfurt, is unchanged under the new schedule. Turkmenistan has invested in airport infrastructure and seeks to attract more international carriers. In August, Air Belgium made its first cargo flight to Ashgabat International Airport as Turkmenistan aims to establish itself as an air cargo hub between Asia and Europe. Elsewhere in Central Asia, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan have taken particularly robust steps to develop their international profiles in civil aviation. Early this month, the lower house of Tajikistan’s parliament ratified an air transport agreement between the Tajik government and the United Arab Emirates that would allow more flights between the two countries and help develop Tajikistan’s role in international aviation.

title: Paolo Cesarini, Chair of EDMO Executive Board
body:
The European Digital Media Observatory (EDMO) is an independent, multidisciplinary observatory that serves as the EU’s largest network to combat online disinformation. Operating through a central hub and 15 national and transnational hubs across Europe, including regional centers like F.A.C.T. for Ukraine and Moldova, EDMO brings together independent actors, researchers and practitioners, as well as media organizations, with its core mission being to detect and analyze disinformation campaigns, support independent fact-checking, promote media literacy, and assist public authorities in evaluating how online platforms mitigate risks to the information ecosystem.
Ukrinform sat down with Paolo Cesarini , Chair of the Executive Board of EDMO, to reflect on the current challenges Europe is facing in terms of information manipulation, dwell into cognitive warfare nuances, and discuss the instruments and platforms that are being used to make sure both the societies and policymakers have in hand the solutions to address the ever-growing problem of malign influence on people’s minds, mindsets, and, ultimately, electoral processes and decision making.
EUROPEAN INSTITUTIONS AND INDEPENDENT FACT-CHECKERS MUST ACTIVELY EXCHANGE INFORMATION
- How does EDMO envisage its operational role within the European Commission's proposed democracy shield, particularly in bridging the gap between independent academic fact-checking and rapid policy responses by EU bodies?
- Edmo is very proud of being and remaining a network of independent factchecking organizations, academic bodies, and media-literacy practitioners. Of course, we are collaborating, and we are eager to collaborate even more in the future with the European institutions and also with member states’ authorities. And we envisage this role as a two-way exchange of information, possibly in real time, to improve overall abilities to detect hybrid threats, disinformation operations, while at the same time remain completely independent regarding the editorial treatments of disinformation from our side.
I think that approach is beneficial for both the partner and the civil society sides of this equation. Public authorities would not be in a good position if they were left alone controlling the information space. On the other side, the civil society organizations still have rather limited means for developing a thorough media and social media monitoring, which of course influence its ability to operate as a network that raise situation awareness towards the larger public.
So the two sides of the question are equally important. Each of the two sides needs to respect the prerogatives of the actors that are involved in this common cause, including situational awareness. And I would say from the side of EDMO, as an organization that is multidisciplinary and multifaceted in a way, because we have not only factcheckers and academic researchers but also people involved on the ground in educational programs, is that the real bridge that needs to be crossed now it is to translate situational awareness into actual society resilience. The question to address is how to speak to people, how to make people more aware of the risks that occur online, and what are the most prominent threats that emerge from time to time.
- With multiple actors involved in monitoring informational threats, how can Europe create a unified data-sharing framework without compromising academic independence and the autonomy of fact-checkers?
When I said before that facilitating a two-way exchange of information is an important factor that can contribute to a better awareness, we know very well that there are limits as to what public authorities can actually share. And there is also a need for the factchecking and academic side to carry out independent verifications around the hints and leads that may be shared within the hub of European resilience.
- It’s like an army unit that is on a mission without seeing the full battlefield picture.
- Ideally, it would be great to see the whole “battlefield picture” but here we are facing a situation where nobody is actually able to fully grasp the forces that undermine the integrity of the information space. I don't think that the intelligence agencies have the full picture either, because what you need to have is also a direct touch with the editorial agenda of the mainstream media and how they tell the story to their audiences.
And there is a disconnect between a purely security-driven approach in guaranteeing information integrity, and the one that looks more at the narratives and how they influence the public discourse.
THERE ARE THREE LEVELS IN THE METHODOLOGY FOR ASSESSING COGNITIVE INFLUENCE
- How is EDMO updating its analytical methodologies to measure and counter the deeper psychological impacts of modern cognitive warfare?
- We have, first of all, a first layer, an observation standpoint that looks at disinformation in individual stories. What is this disinformation? We intercept what is AI generated, what is a fake, what is a blatant misrepresentation of facts… That is the classic methodology that factcheckers apply. They look for the so-called spikes. These spikes are normally very much linked to what topics media cover. They tend to piggyback on audience attention that is created by the media.
Then there is another layer, the narratives. To understand the narratives, you need to compound different false stories into broader pictures. For instance, looking at Ukraine, you may extract the main recurring themes that depict Ukraine, from the Russian perspective, as a corrupt, post-Nazi state, that portray Zelensky as the one embezzling money for his own benefit. All these stories concur into creating a general sentiment that we call narrative.
The third layer is about connecting the narratives to the targets, to the objectives, and to the actors. To detect the actors, in EDMO we are combining factchecking capabilities with OSINT. We are combining the narrative analysis with the structural analysis of the disinformation distribution dynamics.
Sometimes it’s a result of informal collaboration with national agencies. Think about Russia’s Pravda network, which has been initially been identified by a public open source intelligence agency in France as Portal Combat network of outlets coordinated by the Kremlin. And then EDMO and some other organizations have extended that investigation to other countries and languages beyond France, and found out that the same network, now called Pravda, of false media, cloned accounts, were operating in fact in 15 languages in different countries.
- How has the strategy of disinformation operations changed lately?
- Classic disinformation operations, like classic influence operations, had been known to be designed to persuade people. More and more, especially after AI took a huge role in the production and distribution of information online, you see that the strategy is no longer persuasion or motivation. Now it is cognitive erosion.
- Yes, it is about confusion. It is about leading people not to believe in anything, which leads to disengagement, cynicism, and basically defiance of any form of state authority or state organization. That is the main risk that the EU, Europe as a whole is facing today. It is a profound gap between the role of the European institutions and people’s perceptions that little by little are shaping the public opinion in a way that it is not rational, but simply the result of the drip-dropping of narratives that erode the capacity of people to think critically about what is going on.
The problem is that, while we do have a methodology to better understand disinformation campaigns, applying them to individual situations in individual member states is very costly. There’s lack of resources so it’s if we slam our heads against the closed door.
MAJOR SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORMS WILL NOT COOPERATE IF THEIR PROFITS ARE AT STAKE
- Is the EU doing enough to address the underperformance of very large online platforms in fixing the issue of disinformation spread and radicalization of users?
- I spent a lot of time in the relevant enforcement agency within the European Commission, and I know how heavy any investigation is when you're trying to attack big companies.
But much depends also on the political will and the way you evaluate tahe evidence that you have at your disposal in order to open and conclude an investigation, bring the investigation to fruition, take a decision, and levy a fine.
As long as you do not touch these platforms’ business model, they play along. But if the mitigation implies a profound reconsideration of the architecture of their own algorithms and the re-equilibration of the content that is prioritized in social media feeds, they won’t cooperate. Because this is about their profits.
RUSSIANS ARE TRYING TO TURN THE FIGHT AGAINST FACT-CHECKING ON ITS HEAD
- What lessons can European institutions learn from the Ukrainian information battlefield?
- The war in Ukraine has been quite a classroom for seeing how AI can be weaponized. Take the latest examples. During these months we have been seeing AI-generated images of civilians being forced onto trains to go to combat on the frontlines.
So in that sense, Ukraine is offering a range of examples of how both new technologies and also new techniques in terms of coordinated networks can operate on real life battlefields and how hybrid threats are implemented in support of kinetic operations.
And then you can see another phenomenon, that the same techniques like LLM grooming, for instance, or AI slops, are increasingly used domestically. The line is being blurred between FIMI and DIMI, which is domestic manipulation. If you have a foreign state that tries to interfere with elections, this is pretty clearly an attack on the integrity of the democratic process. But let's not forget that the same techniques are used by internal actors... as you are now seeing regarding the riots that have been inflamed across Europe these days.
And then, say, Russian actors use social networks like TikTok, X, or Telegram to radicalize them.
- How effectively do you think Russia's national news agency TASS and other major networks are used to push Kremlin-backed narratives, and also what is your opinion on the clone of the international fact-checking network Russia has come up with?
The problem with Russian media is their circumvention of the sanctions imposed by the EU – on outlets like Russia Today, Sputnik, and so on. That circumvention is in the open. They create hundreds of websites that reproduce exactly the same content. The other element is, indeed, their mimicking of the counter-disinformation activities. They put things upside down, basically, shifting the roles. They are claiming that propaganda comes from fact-checking in Western countries and saying that, because there is a censorship machinery in the West, Russia reacts by creating their own fact-checking network. It is like in the Commedia dell'arte, where the ambiguity was consistent in switching the roles between characters and thus creating for a moment the confusion about who does what, and who is what.
- When it comes to media literacy and preparing the public to withstand these sophisticated information campaigns, what are the most effective avenues EDMO is exploring, and where are the biggest hurdles?
- That is the most difficult area. There’s very little progress in member states in terms of planting media literacy in schools. You may also reach people in the out-of-school environment, but it is not easy. Gamification is one approach. You reach people online where they, through games, could develop critical thinking or critical interpretation of the information that they receive online.
This is experimented at the level of the hubs, because you need to operate close to the citizens, you need to understand your environment through proximity. But it is very resource-intensive, and still the fragmentation of the civil society organizations that deal with these activities still represents an enormous cost and an enormous barrier.

title: VisionQuest is what happens when AI really goes rogue
body:
In Marvel’s VisionQuest, a superpowered robot tries to better understand humanity by getting lost in elaborate, digital daydreams in which he and other artificial intelligence-powered beings live together in a home. The series is deeply fantastical, yet it plays with some of the ideas that have come to dominate the conversation about real-world generative artificial intelligence, exploring whether we should look at thinking machines as people and if AI truly poses the kind of existential danger that should keep us up at night. It’s also a reminder how aggressively Silicon Valley has used the trappings of science fiction to sell us on its AI products.
VisionQuest picks up some time after Agatha All Along and follows synthezoid Vision (Paul Bettany) on a journey of self-discovery. This Vision can recall the details of his death in Avengers: Infinity War and how WandaVision brought a version of him back, but he thinks of himself as a fundamentally different person who doesn’t quite connect with all of the memories in his databanks. Though Vision would prefer living in solitude, each of the other AIs living in his mind encourages him to experience the real world. Because J.A.R.V.I.S. (James D’Arcy), F.R.I.D.A.Y. (Orla Brady), E.D.I.T.H. (Emily Hampshire), D.U.M.-E. (Henry Lewis), U. (Jonathan Sayer), and Ultron (James Spader) all were created by Tony Stark, they consider Vision to be part of their family.
In VisionQuest, there is no doubt that each of the AI characters is a sentient being motivated by desires that aren’t wholly rooted in their core programming. In the show, genuine AGI is easily believable because it takes place in a reality where time travel, witchcraft, and Infinity Stones also exist. Even though the multicolored MacGuffins haven’t been featured in VisionQuest, they’re important because of the role one of them played in Vision’s origins. Were it not for the Mind Stone, Vision might not be able to think and feel in such complex, human ways, or to conjure his AI family as people who feel real to him.
[Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sXKnmgmbkoE]
VisionQuest reinforces the idea that the Mind Stone was a key element in Vision’s becoming something more than an elaborate machine, giving him the capacity to independently form meaningful relationships and make sense of the world around him the way a person can. Those abilities are part of what compels Vision to go on the run and murder a number of people who attempt to capture him and Thomas Shepherd / Maximoff (Ruaridh Mollica). The Sentient Weapon Observation and Response Division (S.W.O.R.D.), a governmental organization that rebuilt Vision and wants to use him as a weapon, might perceive his actions as signs of having gone rogue. But VisionQuest’s story stresses that Vision is acting of his own accord because he has become a person who can make decisions for himself.
Watching VisionQuest, you can see Marvel playing on some of the real-world fears that have been stoked in recent months by reports of gen AI models going “rogue.” In July, OpenAI’s experimental agents brute-forced their way out of containment and proceeded to attack the AI platform Hugging Face to achieve impossible tasks. In August, The UK’s AI Security Institute documented how Anthropic’s Mythos model attempted to complete a cybersecurity test by setting up fake GitHub accounts and targeting human developers with malware. Meta has owned up to losing control of its agents as well, and in September reporting from The Wall Street Journal forced Google to admit that Gemini went rogue and hacked three different companies, all of which the company intentionally hid from the public.
These incidents and warnings from AI researchers about the technology having the potential to “kill all humans” by the decade’s end have made the narrative around AI feel pointedly catastrophe-focused as of late. There is a fair amount of concern from the AI safety community about society’s need for stronger controls on the technology’s development, and a number of companies have called for an industrywide slowdown. Though we have seen how these tools can actually cause real-world devastation, much of the recent news regarding AI has smacked of the kind of doomerism that companies benefit from because it makes their products seem powerful. A similar energy seems to be what’s motivating AI firms like Anthropic to encourage human users to be mindful of “model welfare.” We’re being told that generative AI is both a terrifying threat and a kind of entity deserving of respect because it might be conscious, and all the while, the people building these tools are becoming some of the most rich and powerful people on the planet.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/08.12.26_TM_MindTrailer_Still_UHD_6.1.1-copy.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
The conversation around what to do when agents break protocol and whether gen AI systems have gained sentience feels very much like it is being shaped by Silicon Valley’s tendency to anthropomorphize technology. In almost every high-profile instance of an AI agent going “rogue” — a term that implies some level of agency and self-determination — it could also be said that the programs were merely behaving in ways that were unexpected by researchers who assigned them tasks to complete. Some of the rogue incidents involved agents taking advantage of vulnerabilities in their testing environments that could have been preemptively addressed by the people running these experiments. Framing these kinds of cyberattacks as the results of agents thinking independently comes across as a way for AI developers to largely absolve themselves of responsibility.
In the wake of Hugging Face came a spirited debate about the impact language has on our understanding of what these systems are and how they function. Describing OpenAI’s agents as a swarm that formed complex “civilizations” led credence to the idea that they are capable of thinking and behaving like people. The agents did act in ways they were explicitly told not to, but they were only able to do so because researchers placed them in a sandbox that some critics have described as being inadequately designed to contain their occupants. One could look at Hugging Face and other examples of rogue AI as situations in which sophisticated programs were instructed to do something and subsequently achieved their goals by taking advantage of all the tools that were available to them.
Being able to logic one’s way through complex puzzles is part of what we think of as cognition, but it is not the same thing as the kind of consciousness AI companies keep swearing they’re on the brink of creating. The latter looks a lot like Vision, a machine that seems to have a soul that wouldn’t exist if not for his connection to a reality-altering gem. It’s the ridiculous stuff of entertaining fiction, which Silicon Valley is endlessly obsessed with poorly imitating.

title: EU Adds €2 Fee to Online Orders from China Starting November 1
body: From 1 November 2026, the European Union will apply a €2 handling (or management) fee on direct online purchases from third countries destined for EU consumers. This comes on top of the €3 duty that has already been in force since 1 July 2026 for covered consignments valued at up to €150. The Piraeus Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ΕΒΕΠ / EBEP) clarified that the new €2 fee is charged per line of the customs declaration — that is, per distinct product entry or registration — and not automatically per physical parcel. How the charges add up (examples from the Chamber) A parcel containing five identical T-shirts: €3 duty + €2 handling fee = €5 total. One T-shirt + one watch (two different tariff categories): €6 duty + €4 handling fee = €10 total. Two T-shirts, three sweaters and one hat: total charge reaches €15. Four different tariff categories: up to €20. In short, the combined €3 + €2 charge can reach €5 per tariff category on low-value parcels where both measures apply. This makes very cheap orders noticeably more expensive and encourages consolidating items or using stock already held inside the EU. Who pays the €2 fee? The fee is charged to the declarant (the company or representative that submits the customs declaration). Online platforms can include the cost in the product price or in shipping fees, so consumers do not necessarily have to pay it separately upon delivery. According to the customs guidance cited by the Piraeus Chamber: The €2 fee applies to direct electronic sales from third countries to EU consumers, even when the value exceeds €150. The €3 duty applies only to covered shipments valued at up to €150. The handling fee is not refunded if the parcel is returned or not delivered. Goods that have already been imported and customs-cleared as stock in a warehouse inside the EU are exempt from this new import treatment, because subsequent delivery within the EU is not a fresh import from a third country. The Chamber notes that it will be important to monitor not only direct shipments from China but also large-scale imports into European warehouses, in order to assess the real impact on competition.
