title: Proposed gas pipeline will cut costs, boost South-East economy — Tinubu
body: By Chinedu Adonu ENUGU – President Bola Tinubu has said the proposed South-East Gas Distribution Pipeline Project will reduce energy costs, boost industrialisation and create jobs across the five states of the region. Tinubu, represented by Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, spoke yesterday at the South-East Gas Infrastructure Investment and Project Development Ceremony in Enugu. The proposed $100 million project, being developed by Gas Sync Limited in partnership with NNPC Gas Marketing Limited and other stakeholders, seeks to connect gas resources to industrial and commercial centres in Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu and Imo states. The President said reliable and affordable energy was critical to unlocking the region’s industrial potential, lamenting that manufacturers had continued to spend heavily on alternative power. “There is a sound familiar to every manufacturer in Aba, Nnewi, Onitsha, Enugu and across the South-East. It is the sound of a generator,” he said. “Our manufacturers should not have to spend more on generating electricity than on expanding production.” Tinubu said the project would strengthen manufacturing, encourage agro-processing and attract new investments, adding that the benefits of the region’s gas resources should be measured by the industries they power and the jobs they create. “The true value of our gas is in the factories it powers, the jobs it creates and the prosperity it brings to our people,” he said. He commended the South-East Development Commission (SEDC) for committing $3 million to the initiative, stressing that the project required cooperation between federal and state governments, private investors and financial institutions. However, he cautioned that the ceremony was only an investment and project-development milestone, with financing, regulatory approvals and construction still ahead. “We are not investing in pipelines for their own sake. We are investing in the industries, businesses and jobs those pipelines will make possible,” Tinubu said. Earlier, SEDC Managing Director, Mark Okoye, disclosed that the commission had completed technical, financial and legal due diligence before making its $3 million investment. Okoye said the commission was targeting up to $30 million in aggregate regional investment participation, including its contribution, with additional funds expected from state governments and private investors. “This is not merely an expression of interest or a promise of future investment. The commission has made an actual financial investment towards advancing this regional infrastructure initiative,” he said. He explained that the project would initially draw on gas resources associated with the Assa North–Ohaji South development in Imo State. Okoye said the initiative formed part of SEDC’s broader industrialisation programme aimed at addressing infrastructure constraints facing manufacturers and businesses across the region. “Our philosophy is simple: Plan. Prepare. Partner,” he said, adding that the commission would work with state governments and private-sector operators to mobilise investment for regional development. Also speaking, SEDC Chairman, Dr Emeka Wogu, said affordable and dependable energy was essential for improving productivity, attracting investments and creating employment. He urged investors and energy companies to support the project, stressing that its success should be measured by its economic impact. “The ultimate purpose of infrastructure development is to improve lives,” Wogu said. He called for transparency, environmental responsibility, community engagement and strict adherence to safety standards in the development and operation of the proposed pipeline. The initiative however aligns with Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah’s call for a high-pressure gas pipeline linking major cities across the South-East to accelerate industrial development. Mbah had argued that reliable access to piped gas would ease energy constraints, lower production costs and improve the competitiveness of industries in the region. Earlier, South-East governors pledged their support for the project, describing energy access as a major challenge facing businesses in the region. They assured that the states would provide the necessary support to ensure the pipeline became a reality. “We will do everything required of us to make sure that the project succeeds. We are happy that the project is here in the South-East because the major problem of the region is energy,” the representative said. “With this project, every company will be able to produce at a lower cost of energy, while more people will have opportunities to work and contribute to the economy,” the representative added. The post Proposed gas pipeline will cut costs, boost South-East economy — Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Jigawa Assembly approves constitutional amendment for state police
body: ‎By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Jigawa State House of Assembly has approved the proposed constitutional amendment seeking the establishment of state police in Nigeria. The Speaker of the House, Haruna Aliyu Dangyatin, announced the approval during plenary, saying the move was aimed at strengthening community policing and improving security across the country. He explained that the proposed amendment was transmitted to the state Assembly for consideration after its passage by the Senate and the House of Representatives. ‎According to him, the establishment of state police would help address security challenges at the grassroots by giving state governments greater responsibility for protecting lives and property. The approval is part of ongoing efforts to decentralise Nigeria’s policing system and strengthen the capacity of states to respond to security threats within their jurisdictions. The development comes after the National Assembly gave state Houses of Assembly a 30-day deadline to communicate their positions on the proposed constitutional amendment. State legislatures were directed to indicate whether they supported or opposed the bill as part of the constitutional amendment process. The post Jigawa Assembly approves constitutional amendment for state police appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Kremlin aide echoes Putin's calls that Zelensky welcome in Moscow for talks
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Vladimir Zelensky is welcome to come to Moscow for talks if he so desires, Kremlin Aide Yury Ushakov told Vesti following Russian President Vladimir Putin’s phone call today with Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store and Finnish President Alexander Stubb.
The Norwegian head of government and the Finnish leader conveyed "Zelensky’s active interest in holding a one-on-one" with Putin to the Russian president, Ushakov said.
"Our leader reiterated that if Zelensky really wants to talk face-to-face, let him come to Moscow where he will be provided with all necessary precautions, including in terms of security," Ushakov shared.

title: ‘Toluwanisings should be buried in his home, not cemetery’ – Grandma
body: By Adegboyega Adeleye The paternal grandmother of late gospel singer Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, has alleged that he rarely supported her financially before his death while opposing plans to bury him in a cemetery. The elderly woman, identified as Sabitiyu Olayemi, made the claims in a trending social media interview with journalist Dunmininu in Osun. The interview was conducted in Yoruba. She said Toluwanisings was born in Kano and also narrated how she helped care for the singer and his mother before he moved to Lagos, but had not seen him for more than five years. “Sodiq was born in Kano, that was where his naming cermony was conducted. We have been taking care of Sodiq (Toluwanisings) and his mother even before he went to Lagos. He attended Arabic schools. When he was in grammar school, I would visit him” she said, in Yoruba language. The grandmother also revealed that she knew he was a musician but did not know he had built a house or held a housewarming ceremony. She recalled that he once visited her with his wife and first child, but alleged that they had been out of touch for years. “I just knew he is a musician. I am not aware he built a house; I was not aware of a housewarming. Even if I want to call him, they will say I shouldn’t. It’s been a long time I saw him. It has been over five years I set my eyes on him,” the grandmother said. She said she eventually asked someone in the village to help her call him. “So I called and told him it was me. He responded, ‘Ahh, Mummy.’ I told him that you cannot even check up on me. He said it is work that has been a hindrance,” she recounted. According to her, Toluwanisings sent her ₦10,000 on about three occasions after that conversation, but did not send money again. She also alleged that when her phone was damaged and she sought help contacting him about a replacement, his elder sibling told her not to call him. Asked whether he sent her medication or money for medical expenses, she replied: “There is nothing Sodiq (Toluwanisings) sends to me.” Despite her allegations, she said his death deeply affected her as she broke down in tears during the interview. “When I heard that he had died, I felt so sad. Whether I benefited from him or not, he is still my child. I have accepted my fate. I wish God had taken me so I would not have had to witness this tragedy,” she said, breaking down in tears. The grandmother also objected to burying the singer in a cemetery, saying he should be laid to rest at his home. “I do not agree that Toluwanisings should be buried in a cemetery. They should bury him at his house. They should not come and bury him close to his mother,” she said. Toluwanisings’ family announced that the singer died in the early hours of October 14, 2026 at the age of 41, but did not disclose the cause of death. Vanguard reported that his personal assistant said the singer was taken to between seven and eight hospitals in Ibadan after he slumped, but efforts to secure medical attention were unsuccessful. The family has not publicly confirmed a cause of death. The post ‘Toluwanisings should be buried in his home, not cemetery’ – Grandma appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Trump admin demands Washington set aside 400 ballots it says are from noncitizens
body:
Washington's secretary of state expressed skepticism about the request's timing.
The Justice Department is asking election officials in Washington state to set aside hundreds of ballots it says may belong to noncitizen voters, the latest move by the Trump administration to intervene in a state-run election just days before the midterms.
The move sparked backlash from state officials who said the Justice Department’s intention in publicizing these allegations so close to an election was to create "unfounded suspicion."
Federal prosecutors in Washington state claimed in a statement Monday that the more than 400 individuals on the list represented “only the tip of the iceberg.” The statement accompanied a letter sent by the state’s two U.S. attorneys demanding that election officials set aside any ballots belonging to individuals on the list. ABC News has not seen the letter.
The Justice Department’s messaging in Washington on Monday echoes steps it took ahead of a lawsuit it filed last week against California, where it has sued to prevent the state from counting more than 20,000 ballots it claims may belong to noncitizen voters.
The Trump administration has promoted a number isolated cases of alleged noncitizen voting in recent weeks as evidence of rampant election fraud. But all available evidence suggests voter fraud and noncitizen voting remains exceedingly rare , and certainly not widespread enough to alter the outcome of any election.
A federal appeals court declined to intervene in that matter and said that the "emergency" the DOJ claimed was in part "self-constructed."
Local officials in Los Angeles said a sampling of the 20,000 ballots surveyed showed a "high percentage" of people who say they were born in the U.S.
"We saw what happened in California and don't want Washingtonians to be harassed," Secretary of State Steve Hobbs said in a statement on Monday responding to the Justice Department's letter.
Hobbs wrote in his response that at least one of the individuals on the Justice Department’s list dates back to 1994. Since then, 113.5 million primary and general election ballots have been cast in Washington, according to the secretary of state’s office.
"The timing of this request -- one week before the General Election -- is no doubt intended to cast unfounded suspicion on the results," Hobbs added. "We are carefully reviewing the request and assessing the information sought to ensure that our response complies with applicable state and federal laws."

title: Israel election turnout hits 74.3% by 8 p.m., highest since 1988
body: Israel's parliamentary election recorded its highest voter turnout at 8 p.m. since 1988, with 74.3% of eligible voters having cast their ballots Tuesday, according to the Central Elections Committee. The figure represents a surge of eight percentage points compared with the same hour in the November 2022 election, when turnout stood at 66.3%. More than 5.4 million Israelis had voted, with two hours remaining before most polling stations were scheduled to close.   Acting Central Elections Committee Director-General Dean Livne announced the latest figures, continuing a day of unusually high participation that had already broken records at several earlier reporting intervals. By 6 p.m., turnout had reached 66.7%, compared with 57.7% at the same hour in 2022. The nine-percentage-point difference represented a relative increase of 15.6% over the previous election's pace. At that point, 4,892,186 Israelis had already cast their ballots.   "By 6 p.m., we have surpassed the number of people who voted by 10 p.m. in the previous election," Livne said, referring to the number of ordinary ballots cast, excluding special double-envelope votes. Earlier, turnout reached 55.7% by 4 p.m., compared with 47.5% in 2022, and 44.9% by 2 p.m., compared with 38.9% four years ago. Each milestone reflected the unusually strong participation throughout Election Day. The latest turnout also exceeded the previous election's final participation rate of 70.63%, with two hours still remaining before the scheduled closing time. Long lines and heavy demand at polling stations The surge in participation brought long lines to polling stations in several cities, including Ra'anana and Ramat Gan, with some voters reporting unusually lengthy waits. Election officials urged the public to remain patient as the number of voters continued to climb. Central Elections Committee Chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg said waits at some polling stations had reached 15 to 20 minutes. Officials stressed that anyone arriving before the scheduled closing time would be allowed to cast a ballot, even if the line continued moving afterward.   Participation was also high among military personnel. According to the IDF, 68% of eligible service members had voted by 5 p.m., compared with 65% at the same hour during the previous election. At the Jalame military base south of Afula, unusually heavy demand forced the IDF to deploy an additional polling station after soldiers reportedly waited more than two hours to vote. Other soldiers reported waits of approximately 90 minutes at a base in central Israel. The military said it had prepared for high turnout by operating more than 850 fixed polling stations, alongside mobile voting stations serving troops in the field, and was deploying additional facilities where necessary. Where is turnout highest? Some communities surpass 90% Figures published by the Central Elections Committee earlier in the evening revealed striking differences between communities and major cities across the country. The highest turnout among regular polling stations was recorded in Timorim, a community near Kiryat Malakhi in southern Israel, where 91.6% of eligible voters had already cast their ballots. Close behind was Yuval, near the Lebanese border, with 91.5%, followed by Shorashim in northern Israel at 90.1%. Other communities reporting exceptionally high participation included Bat Hen at 87.7%, Hazon and Shavei Darom at 87% each, Nataf at 86.4%, Netiv HaLamed-Heh at 86.2%, Yesodot at 85.3% and HaBonim at 85.2%.   Among larger cities, Modi'in-Maccabim-Re'ut stood out with a turnout rate of 70.1%, one of the highest among the major urban centers included in the committee's earlier update. Tel Aviv recorded 58.6%, Jerusalem 55.3% and Haifa 54.5%. Rishon LeZion reached 61.3%, Petah Tikva 63.1%, Ashdod 59.4% and Netanya 50.6%. In the south, Be'er Sheva recorded 55.8% and Ashkelon 58.8%. Holon reached 58%, while Ramat Gan recorded 61.9%, Bnei Brak 64.3% and Rehovot 63.8%. Herzliya recorded 63.1%, while Bat Yam stood at 47.6%, one of the lowest turnout rates among the major cities included in the update. The local figures reflect voting at regular polling stations as of the earlier reporting period and should not be confused with the updated nationwide turnout figure for 8 p.m. Election committee rejects bid to extend voting hours Israel's Central Elections Committee rejected a request Tuesday to extend voting beyond the scheduled 10 p.m. closing time, following a political dispute between coalition and opposition parties amid record voter turnout and long lines at polling stations. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party had submitted a formal request to extend voting hours, citing heavy turnout and lengthy waits. The proposal gained support from the far-right Otzma Yehudit party, led by National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, and the ultra-Orthodox Shas party, headed by Aryeh Deri.   Ofer Winter's Amcha Yisrael party also supported the proposal, calling for an additional hour of voting. Opposition parties rejected the request. Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar! party, Naftali Bennett's Beyahad party and the Democrats, led by Yair Golan, all opposed extending voting beyond the scheduled closing time. Yashar! said it "strongly opposes" Likud's request, arguing that no exceptional circumstances justified changing the voting hours. "No exceptional incident has occurred that would justify approving the request, which is intended to lay the groundwork for claims against the integrity of the election, following the lies Netanyahu has been spreading since this morning," the party said in a statement. Following a meeting of the committee's presidium, chaired by Justice Sohlberg, officials concluded that there was no justification for a nationwide extension. "The high national voter turnout across all sectors reflects the public's strong engagement in the democratic process, and under these circumstances, no need was found to extend voting hours," the committee said.   Under the decision, most polling stations will close at 10 p.m. as originally scheduled. However, anyone who arrives before closing time will still be allowed to vote, even if they remain in line after 10 p.m. The committee separately approved extending voting in Hebron until 10 p.m. because of a power outage that had disrupted the voting process. Why the final results could take until Friday A total of 7,331,981 Israelis are eligible to vote in the election for the 26th Knesset, with 12,018 polling stations operating nationwide. Most are scheduled to close at 10 p.m., when television networks traditionally release their exit polls. However, the final results could remain uncertain for several days. More than 650,000 special double-envelope ballots are expected from soldiers, diplomats, displaced residents, voters with disabilities and others voting away from their registered polling stations. These ballots require separate verification and counting. Livne warned that the number of special ballots could be higher than originally anticipated and that counting might not be completed by Thursday evening, potentially continuing into Friday morning. "It is possible that the number of double envelopes will be higher, and it is possible that we will not finish counting them by Thursday evening," he said, adding that the count would be broadcast live. The unusually high turnout could also have significant political consequences, particularly for smaller parties attempting to cross Israel's 3.25% electoral threshold. The threshold itself remains fixed, but as the total number of valid votes increases, so does the absolute number of votes a party needs to enter the Knesset. With several parties potentially finishing close to that threshold, special ballots could alter the final distribution of seats and change the balance between rival political blocs. The record turnout has already transformed the scale of Israel's election. Whether it will also transform the political balance will become clear only when the final ballots are counted.

title: Qatar says Iran needs to show good intentions for mediation efforts to succeed
body: Iran needs to show good intentions for mediation efforts to succeed, mediator Qatar said on Tuesday, after a delegation from the Gulf Arab country visited Tehran earlier this week in an effort to de-escalate regional tensions in coordination with the United States.A spokesperson for the Qatari Foreign Ministry told a press briefing that Iran should stop threats against Arab Gulf states and open the Strait of Hormuz to show good intentions.Qatar, along with Pakistan, has been mediating between Washington and Tehran in an effort to end the US-Israeli war on Iran that has disrupted global shipping and oil supplies, and spilled over across other parts of the Middle East.Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan hold talks with Iran amid renewed Houthi attacksTop officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan also met Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday in an effort to de-escalate the conflict, as Yemen's Houthis launched new attacks on Saudi Arabia and Egypt approved defense support for the Gulf kingdom.Tensions between Washington and Tehran have sharpened recently, with President Donald Trump saying on Friday the US may strike Iran again. Iranian security officials told Reuters Tehran had drawn up detailed plans to attack Gulf undersea cables if the US and Israel attack again.

title: Russian Geran-4 jet-powered attack drones have nearly 60% interception rate – General Staff says
body:
This is according to a Facebook report by the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, seen by Ukrinform.
“The interception rate for enemy jet-powered attack drones is gradually increasing. Overall, an analysis of the past three months shows that the average interception rate for Geran-4 UAVs is nearly 60%. During some individual attacks, the interception rate for jet-powered UAVs can reach 80%,” the General Staff said.
Tactical aviation, including F-16s, Mirage aircraft, and MiG-29s, currently plays a significant role in destroying jet-powered UAVs.
“At the same time, strengthening our short-range air defenses is a key priority amid a shortage of surface-to-air guided missiles, and considerable attention is being devoted to this issue. Short-range air defenses include anti-aircraft systems such as the Gepard and Shilka, newer systems such as Skynex, Skyranger, and Terrahawk Paladin, interceptor drones, and mobile air defense groups from all components of Ukraine’s Defense Forces,” the General Staff said.
The mobile air defense groups are equipped not only with machine guns and associated equipment but also with man-portable air defense systems (MANPADS). Ukrainian troops are using MANPADS to intercept jet-powered drones with considerable success.
“Meanwhile, work is ongoing to reduce the cost of countering such aerial threats. Trials of new interceptors are underway. Some models have already been used to shoot down dozens of Russian Geran jet-powered drones,” the General Staff said.
As previously reported, Ukrainian air defenses neutralized two ballistic missiles and 255 drones launched by Russian forces against Ukraine since the evening of October 26.

title: Quebec premier accuses Ottawa of censoring him at EU Summit
body:
Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon is planning to boycott the upcoming Canada-European Union summit in Montreal, accusing Ottawa of muzzling Quebec by denying him an opportunity to address European leaders.
The federal government has said St-Pierre Plamondon is invited to a dinner with EU representatives, but the premier will not speak at the summit, which takes place Thursday and Friday.
The dispute comes just one week after St-Pierre Plamondon was sworn in as Quebec’s 34th premier and two days after he did not participate in a meeting between the federal government, provincial premiers and First Nations.
Bloc Québécois Leader Yves-François Blanchet challenged Prime Minister Mark Carney over St-Pierre Plamondon’s role at the summit.
“How does the prime minister justify silencing the premier of Quebec?” Blanchet asked.
Carney was not in the House of Commons to answer the question directly, but told reporters that the federal government had held three consultations with Quebec’s delegation.
He said it was St-Pierre Plamondon’s decision not to attend.
In a social media post, the Quebec premier blasted Carney over the situation.
“This is not only a serious lack of respect, but, more importantly, a significant setback for Quebec’s ability to act autonomously and to defend its own interests,” St-Pierre Plamondon wrote.
He also accused Ottawa of seeking to impose economic decisions on Quebec without allowing the province a seat at the negotiating table.
Federal Industry Minister Mélanie Joly said in Ottawa that geopolitics, including the summit, fall under federal jurisdiction.
The Parti Québécois government also says Ottawa denied Quebec’s request to host a reception on the sidelines of the summit. The request was submitted by former premier Christine Fréchette in September.
A party spokesperson said the EU routinely holds a forum for economic leaders during such summits, which Quebec could have hosted or co-hosted.
The PQ also says there is precedent for Quebec to be included, pointing to provincial representatives’ participation in negotiations for the Canada-European Union Free Trade Agreement.
Quebec Liberal Leader Charles Milliard said he understands why the premier wants to speak at the summit but argued a boycott is not the answer.
“We agree to disagree on that issue,” Milliard told reporters.
Québec solidaire co-spokesperson Sol Zanetti also said St-Pierre Plamondon should attend.
“He should be allowed to speak to everybody and say whatever he wants,” Zanetti said.
The dispute unfolded on the same day U.S. President Donald Trump posted a message on Truth Social congratulating St-Pierre Plamondon on his election victory.
Trump’s post included a link to an Irish Times article with the headline, “Separatists win Quebec provincial election in blow to Mark Carney. Result may hamper Canadian prime minister’s efforts to maintain national unity against Trump.”
Daniel Béland, a political scientist and head of the McGill Institute for the Study of Canada, noted Trump has previously made much stronger comments about the country.
“He has written much more dramatic things about Canada, much more negative things,” Béland said.
Béland also said the Canada-EU summit is fundamentally a meeting involving the federal government rather than provincial leaders.
“Strictly speaking this is a meeting between the government of Canada and the European Union,” he told Global News on Tuesday.
The growing tension between Ottawa and Quebec City follows St-Pierre Plamondon’s absence from Monday’s meeting between the federal government, provincial premiers and First Nations.
The Quebec premier also spoke with French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday.

title: Nearly 10, 000 Iranian students enrolled at Russian universities — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. There are some 10,000 Iranian students currently enrolled at Russian universities, President Vladimir Putin told Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.
"We also cooperate in the humanitarian sphere. The number of Iranian students in our universities has hit nearly the 10,000 mark," the Russian leader said.
Putin drew attention to the fact that in late September and early October, as part of the festival of Iranian culture, a series of vibrant events were held in different cities of Russia - in Moscow, Kazan, and Astrakhan.

title: Kernel yields: wheat up 9%, sunflower up 18%, rapeseed up 48%, corn down 13%
body:
Net wheat and sunflower yields at Kernel's agricultural operations increased by 9% and 18%, respectively, year over year, reaching 6.4 tonnes per hectare and 3.1 tonnes per hectare, the company said in a stock exchange filing last week.
"The Group's total acreage under operations increased by 48% y-o-y to 530,000 hectares, following the expansion and optimization of its farming footprint during FY2026," Kernel said.
The company specified that wheat acreage increased by 13%, to 106,000 hectares, while sunflower acreage rose by 90%, to 88,000 hectares. This is expected to translate into increases in their respective harvests of 22.3%, to 678,400 tonnes, and 2.2 times, to 272,800 tonnes.
At the same time, the company noted that sunflower harvesting remains to be completed on 4% of the area allocated to the crop.
As for corn, harvesting has so far been completed on 28% of the planted area. Taking this into account, the net yield is expected to reach 8.1 tonnes per hectare, down 13% from last year, "primarily reflecting the impact of summer heatwaves and insufficient rainfall during key stages of crop development, which severely affected corn yields in one of the Group's clusters," Kernel explained.
However, given that corn acreage increased by 48% this year, to 254,000 hectares, the harvest is expected to rise by 28.6%, to 2 million 57,400 tonnes.
In addition, Kernel increased its rapeseed acreage from 3,000 hectares to 43,000 hectares. Combined with an increase in yield from 2.4 tonnes per hectare to 3.5 tonnes per hectare, this resulted in a 20.9-fold increase in the rapeseed harvest, to 150,500 tonnes.
The company also allocated 39,000 hectares to other crops, compared with 43,000 hectares last year.
Before the war, Kernel ranked first globally in sunflower oil production, accounting for about 7% of worldwide output, and exports, with a share of around 12%. It is one of Ukraine's largest producers and sellers of bottled sunflower oil. The company also grows and sells agricultural products.
In FY2026 (July 2025-June 2026), Kernel increased EBITDA by 20%, to $558 million, and net profit by 35%, to $322 million, while revenue rose 7%, to $4.404 billion.

title: Four men arrested after violent altercation breaks out at Rahat polling center
body: Four men were arrested after a violent altercation broke out at a polling station in the Bedouin city of Rahat in southern Israel on Tuesday. Video of the Election Day incident showed a number of men fighting, holding chairs, and one man lying on the ground seemingly unconscious.The fight was reportedly not election-related but broke out when members of rival families arrived to vote at the same location at the same time. Unusual footage: Violence near a polling station in Rahat. https://t.co/M9Q4223Z3m— Amit Segal (@AmitSegal) October 27, 2026Also in Rahat, masked individuals riding on horses and camels through the city were seen waving political flags and playing loud music.Residents in the area alleged that Border Police officers were present at polling sites across various localities to ensure order as people arrived to vote.Additional claims suggest that polling station staff are intentionally prolonging the voting process for individual voters by taking too much time to examine the identification cards presented to them.ובינתיים ברהט... צילום: וליד אלעוברה https://t.co/zAdiw38Ujt— ilana curiel (@ilanacuriel) October 27, 2026Arab voter turnout surgesMeanwhile, in Rahat, voter turnout reached 72.2% by 6 p.m., up 12.66% when compared to 2022 - the largest increase seen across four of Israel's Arab-majority cities.Increases in turnout have been seen in other Arab-majority cities including Umm al-Fahm, Kafr Qasim, and Nazareth, which all experienced an increase of 3-4 percentage points compared to the previous electionRecord voter turnout across the country shows a similar trend, reaching 74.3% by 8 p.m., up 8 points compared to the same time in the 2022 election.At the same time, haredi (ultra-Orthodox) majority cities across Israel recorded turnout figures that remained substantially below their final 2022 totals.Shir Perets contributed to this report.

title: 'Call me': Israeli right-wing candidates go door to door pleading for votes
body: Israel’s election on Tuesday descended into a frantic plea by right-wing parties for supporters to get out and vote by any means possible, amid a surge in turnout that could indicate their defeat. Senior officials in the governing coalition warned of a high Palestinian-Israeli turnout that could tip the balance in favour of the opposition and bring down the ruling coalition. “Do you have a friend or sister who’s hesitating? Talk to me. Send me their number. I’m available now by phone,” Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich pleaded in a post on X, followed by a phone number. Itamar Ben-Gvir, Minister of National Security, went door to door urging people to vote. He posted a video of himself knocking on a door, writing: “We went to wake up the Bat Yam residents in their homes. Go out and vote.” Voter turnout surged to a record 55.7 per cent by 4pm on Tuesday, compared with 47.5 per cent at the same hour in the previous election, the Central Elections Committee announced. The figure is the highest turnout recorded at that stage of Election Day since comparable records began in 1973. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, whose long career has been marred by corruption charges and wars, has issued more than 20 calls for his supporters to vote since the polls opened. “This is an emergency,” he wrote on X, adding siren emojis. In another post, he published photos of women in black veils and abayas and warned that the Muslim Brotherhood could be stealing the election. “Higher-than-usual voter turnout in the Arab sector compared to the low turnout of right-wing voters,” Mr Netanyahu said. His Likud party announced that it had submitted a formal request to extend voting hours, as its leader continued to warn supporters that the vote was being stolen. Other candidates, even from opposition parties, complained of slow ID checks, especially in Palestinian Israeli areas. In what is being called one of the most consequential elections in Israel’s history, some say the state’s future is at stake. But all agree the central issue is Mr Netanyahu’s long rule. The vote could mark the end of a long and complicated career, marred by corruption charges and a contested wartime strategy, if voters decide he should pay the price for the October 7, 2023, security failures. Polls show the Netanyahu camp could fall well short of the 61 seats needed to form a government, forcing it into tortuous coalition talks or a second election.

title: Lavrov says US open to dialogue with Russia, Europe refused contacts until last moment
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. The administration of US President Donald Trump immediately advocated developing dialogue with Russia, while Europe refused to engage until the last moment, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said at a meeting with editors-in-chief of African media outlets.
"The Trump administration in the United States, despite supporting Ukraine by supplying weapons to European countries and providing satellite intelligence, is open to dialogue with Russia," Lavrov noted. "The Trump administration openly advocates developing and deepening this dialogue and covering as many areas as possible."
"Europe, by contrast, categorically refused to engage in any contacts with Russia until literally the last moment," he added.

title: ‘Selling Sunset’ star Chrishell Stause announces split from G Flip
body:
Selling Sunset star Chrishell Stause and her partner Australian musician G Flip have split.
The 45-year-old reality star announced the news on Monday and said that she had a “humbling” update to share with her followers.
“G and I are no longer together and we have agreed to treat this public separation with love and respect for each other,” Stause said in a video shared to Instagram .
“That’s not hard for me because I am in love with this person and I don’t have all the information or the reasons. I’m sure — just like always — with time, you get the lessons you’re meant to get,” she continued.
Stause said that she’s going “to heal” and that “everything is going to be fine.”
“I’m definitely never doing this again. But I just felt like you guys deserved a little bit more than a cold, written statement because you have been so supportive and loving,” Stause added.
The Traitors star told her followers that she feels like “a little bit of a failure.”
“There’s nothing you could say about me that would be worse than what I say to myself,” she said as she began to tear up. “I just have to kind of heal and figure this out. It’s hard. It’s painful. I’m a lover girl.”
“I swing big. I miss. Maybe you don’t miss. Maybe these are the lives and seasons you’re meant to have with people, and I had an amazing over four years with G,” she concluded her video.
G Flip posted a statement on their Instagram page that read, “After 4+ years Chrishell and I are no longer together. I will always love her, we will always share a special connection and I cherish our memories together deeply.”
“My head & heart are feeling very heavy right now and I’m not able to talk but I want to thank you all for your support and appreciate you respecting our privacy at this time,” G Flip added.
The 33-year-old singer previously told Vogue Australia that they met Stause at a Halloween party in 2021.
Stause confirmed her relationship with the Australian musician during a Selling Sunset reunion in May 2022.
“I recently have been spending a lot of time with someone that’s very important to me. Their name is G Flip. They’re non-binary, so they go by they/them. And they are an extremely talented musician,” she said during the episode.
The pair tied the knot in May 2023 with Stause announcing the news in an Instagram post .
“Love doesn’t always go as planned,” she wrote at the time. “Sometimes it’s immeasurably better.”
Stause was previously married to This Is Us actor Justin Hartley for two years until their split in 2019 .
Hartley cited “irreconcilable differences” as the reason for the couple’s split, according to E! News .
Hartley began dating the Days of Our Lives star in 2014 only a couple of years after separating from his first wife, Lindsay Korman.
The pair announced their engagement in July 2016 before marrying on Oct. 28, 2017.
—With files from Global News’ Adam Wallis

title: Frontier AI labs say their models refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis. What does that mean?
body:
OpenAI released solutions to three blockbuster math problems that have long vexed researchers. One was a surprise rejection of the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), a durable assumption in computer science that plays a large role in how we understand what is difficult to compute.
As with previous proof-drops from the frontier lab, scientific communities responded with a mixture of thrill and dismay. Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge suggested that OpenAI was basing its solutions on pre-existing work, and hours later, Anthropic subsequently released its own refutation of ETH.
However, OpenAI’s process is evolving. This time, the lab structured its releases differently for each of the three disciplines involved: Mathematicians got the work dropped on GitHub; the computer scientists formed a working group, asked for the proofs to be shared publicly and OpenAI to fund a conference to discuss them; the physicists formed a working group that will determine how their result will be released.
MIT professor Ryan Williams is the computer scientist who is organizing his field’s response to the new finding. Williams, whose work focuses on these questions of computational complexity, has criticized OpenAI’s approach in the past, calling its proof dump earlier this October a “DDOS attack on mathematicians.”
However, he agreed to collaborate with the frontier labs in order to help shepherd ideas that are vital to the field, he told TechCrunch. The lab asked him to help interpret the solution, along with UC San Diego computer scientists Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi, who first published the ETH in 1999.
Their first step was to release an open letter calling for feedback from scientists interested in these problems and a discussion of the norms around AI contributions to their work.
“Some parts [of OpenAI’s proof] are, maybe you could say routine, but then yes, there are two or three alien-looking parts, and it’s exactly these parts that I saw that made me think, wow, this is something that the whole community needs to work on together,” Williams told TechCrunch.
The ETH is part of a broader class of problems known as P versus NP, which has animated computer science and many other fields for decades. Reductively, researchers are trying to understand if any problem whose solution can be easily verified (NP) can also be easily solved (P).
A simple example is the game Sodoku: Once a solution to a puzzle is in place, it can be quickly verified, but finding the solution is time-consuming. That dynamic is true across a range of important problems, and the insight underpins cryptographic systems: When you have the key to an encoded message, you can reveal it, but actually cracking an effective code takes too long to be useful.
However, scientists have yet to prove whether that is always true. “P = NP is saying that, not only can you verify Sudoku solutions when they exist, you can just generate them,” Williams said. “P = NP is asserting that this is true for every single problem you can verify quickly — if you can verify it quickly, you can solve it quickly. So this just seems too good to be true.”
That’s why most scientists assume that P ≠ NP. ETH provided evidence for that. It basically says that even the fastest computer algorithm needs exponentially more time to find a solution as the number of variables grow in a specific class of tricky logic puzzle.
The claims from OpenAI and Anthropic is that their models have come up with algorithms that solve those puzzles in “sub-exponential” time, meaning faster than the speeds previously thought possible. If true, they may have proven the EFT to be false — refuted it, in scientific terms — and maybe opened up a path for algorithms that generally perform P = NP.
“Every computer scientist should probably put a little more weight on the plausibility of P = NP, but one’s weight may vary,” Williams said. “I do think that it kind of calls into question a lot of the intuitions that we thought we had about … how tractable [hard NP problems] are. I also think that this is probably not the final answer either. I don’t think that OpenAI’s algorithm could possibly be the best algorithm you can get.”
The durability of ETH has lead to it being included in many scientific papers over the past decade that will need to be revisited if the AI labs claims that they’ve proven it wrong holds up, Williams said.
“This is partly why I was asking or pushing OpenAI to support a conference on this — it’s going to affect many researchers’ works, and we need to figure out, okay, what happens next besides understanding the algorithms. We need to understand, how should the foundations change compared to what we had before?” he said. Before scientific concerns, there are cybersecurity questions. Williams said that an improved algorithm could imply that cryptographic systems relying on certain key sizes could be considered broken. So one of the first questions he asked OpenAI science lead Dan Roberts “was if they had checked that this affects any crypto systems … is anything insecure now? And apparently, they checked, and they were reasonably confident that this didn’t … imply any breaks.”
This new AI paradigm of scientific discovery is still a work in progress, but Williams says he is optimistic despite real concerns, particularly about training the next generation of scientists. Being a computer scientist who does high level math has perhaps made the adjustment easier for him than for pure mathematicians.
Still, he says AI is “forcing people to be a little more ambitious about the kind of work that they do, and to think more deeply about, okay, if all the things I used to work on are now low-hanging fruit for AI, how can I raise the bar for the kind of scientific questions I want to ask?”

title: Ebola: WHO expresses hope as cases surpass 10,000, deaths near 5,000 in DRC
body:
The World Health Organisation (WHO) has expressed hope that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) can be contained, despite confirmed cases of Bundibugyo virus disease surpassing 10,000.
The optimism comes as data released by the DRC’s Ministry of Public Health on Tuesday put confirmed cases at 10,060, with 4,887 deaths, according to a report by Al Jazeera.
The outbreak, declared on 15 May, is the largest and deadliest Ebola epidemic recorded in the DRC.
It is also the second-largest and second-deadliest Ebola outbreak globally, behind the 2014–2016 West African epidemic, which recorded about 28,600 cases and more than 11,000 deaths.
In a post on his official X account on Tuesday, Mohammed Janabi, the WHO Regional Director for Africa, said the rising figures reflected the toll the outbreak had taken on families and communities but noted that progress in recovery, research and response efforts offered reasons for hope.
Mr Janabi said more than 2,600 people had recovered, while new vaccine and treatment candidates were advancing through clinical trials.
He added that laboratory testing, treatment capacity, infection prevention and control, community engagement and surveillance were being strengthened to help contain the outbreak.
“Our teams are on the ground, working side by side with the government and partners to stop transmission and save lives,” he said, calling for sustained commitment, community trust and solidarity, as well as safe access to affected communities.
The rising figures come amid growing concerns about the spread of the virus beyond the DRC, with Kenya and Nigeria reporting infections linked to the wider outbreak.
PREMIUM TIMES reported last week that Kenya had recorded nine confirmed cases, including two deaths, after the virus was introduced by a traveller who arrived from the DRC through Uganda.
Nigeria also confirmed its first Ebola case in more than a decade on 20 October, after a woman who had travelled from Uganda tested positive in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).
In a subsequent report , PREMIUM TIMES reported that the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) was investigating a possible link between the Nigerian case and the infection recorded in Kenya.
Both patients travelled through Entebbe International Airport in Uganda on 3 October, prompting investigations into whether they had shared equipment or had other contact. However, health officials have stressed that a direct connection between the infections has not been established.
Nigeria’s health minister, Muhammad Pate, later said genomic sequencing showed that the viruses detected in Nigeria and Kenya differed by only one mutation. He cautioned, however, that the finding did not establish where the Nigerian patient contracted the virus.
According to the Al Jazeera report, about 80 per cent of new cases in the DRC are occurring outside the known chains of transmission being monitored by health authorities.
This means many infections are being detected among people whose exposure to previously confirmed cases has not been established, complicating efforts to identify contacts and interrupt further transmission.
The Africa CDC has said at least 95 per cent of cases must be linked to known contacts of infected people for an outbreak to be considered under control.
The absence of an approved vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain remains another major challenge in the response.
PREMIUM TIMES reported on Friday that the World Health Organisation (WHO) had announced the commencement of the Tumaini clinical trial in Bunia, eastern DRC, to assess potential vaccines against the strain.
The trial began with the vaccination of its first participants on 23 October and is expected to evaluate several vaccine candidates, including Ervebo, which is licensed against a different Ebola virus species, as well as experimental candidates being developed by Moderna and the University of Oxford in collaboration with the Serum Institute of India.
The trial is intended to establish whether the candidates can safely generate an immune response and protect against the Bundibugyo virus. Their effectiveness against the strain has not yet been established.
The development follows an earlier WHO recommendation, reported by PREMIUM TIMES in August, that Ervebo be prioritised for a clinical trial after preliminary animal studies suggested it might offer some cross-protection against Bundibugyo virus disease.

title: US Marine indicted over suspected murder, robbery of woman in Okinawa
body: Japanese prosecutors indicted the U.S. Marine suspected of murdering and robbing a local woman Oct. 4. Lance Cpl. Devin Jacob Ballard , 20, assigned to the III Marine Expeditionary Force headquartered at Camp Courtney in Okinawa, Japan, was indicted on Sunday for the murder and robbery of Anna Yagi, a 39-year-old Naha resident, at a hotel in the city. Earlier this month, local authorities arrested Ballard for allegedly murdering and robbing Yagi at a hotel in the city. Prosecutors allege that Ballard strangled Yagi with a phone cord at the hotel and then stole her backpack with her wallet and other belongings inside, according to a copy of the indictment provided to Japan’s public broadcaster, NHK, by the Naha District Public Prosecutors Office. The Naha District Public Prosecutors Office declined to give Military Times a copy of the indictment, saying only those registered locally with the office could receive one. An investigation of the body found that Yagi died from suffocation. Hotel security footage shows a person with hair and tattoos resembling Ballard’s entering a hotel room with a woman and leaving with items. The murder and subsequent arrest reignited concerns among Okinawa residents over the large American troop presence on the island, causing U.S. officials to implement new restrictions for service members in an effort to show goodwill. Japanese officials have lodged what Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi described as a “strong protest” against the U.S. while demanding full cooperation with local authorities in the investigation. Days after Ballard’s arrest, U.S. officials directed a 48-hour operational pause for all service members on Okinawa for a Period of Training. Commanders and senior enlisted leaders trained all service members on standards, discipline and troops’ responsibilities as members of the local community. Directly after the training, personnel transitioned to a 30-day Period of Reflection, which is slated to end on Nov. 8, to implement restrictions on liberty, such as enhanced supervision at installations’ gates and new curfews. More recently, Kadena Air Base instructed junior enlisted personnel from E-1 to E-4 to cease alcohol consumption for the rest of the Period of Reflection, as well as adhere to a curfew from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. The new restrictions on Kadena follow the base implementing an Emergency Off-Limits Order of a local establishment that was found to be serving alcohol to military personnel during curfew hours and allowing them to stay past curfew, in violation of the Period of Reflection directive. “The demonstration of this establishment to allow members to openly violate the 30-Day Period of Reflection endangers the already strained relationship between the people of Okinawa and U.S. military personnel,” the off-limits order reads.

title: Lockheed Martin, U.S. Government say Poland will host European PAC-3 missile maintenance hub
body: The U.S. government announced the selection on the sidelines of NATO’s Conference of National Armaments Directors meeting. Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden will have key supply-chain roles, building on an agreement signed with the United States and Poland. Lockheed Martin plans to integrate the facility into Poland’s defense industry, creating skilled jobs and work for local suppliers. The Department of War said maintenance capacity within Europe would strengthen supply lines and help allied forces respond to increased demand during a crisis. “For more than 75 years, Lockheed Martin has been a trusted partner to Europe— strengthening regional sustainment, expanding production capacity and accelerating the delivery of critical missile defense capabilities. The PAC-3 MMF represents the next evolution of that partnership, bringing essential sustainment support to our European allies and ensuring these advanced defense systems remain available when and where they are needed most,” said Tim Cahill, president of Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control. The project expands regional support for a growing number of NATO countries operating PAC-3 interceptors. It accompanies efforts to increase production, including a $58.62 billion U.S. government award this year that Lockheed Martin said would accelerate PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement output. “Today’s announcement puts partnership into action,” said Michael P. Duffey, under secretary of war for acquisition and sustainment. “By investing national resources to establish this critical sustainment capability on NATO’s Eastern Front, Allies are sending a clear message: the Alliance is united, serious about deterrence, and ready to back our words with action.” Jay Pitman, president of Lockheed Martin International, said the facility would deepen partnerships in Poland, Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden. He said it would also expand opportunities for American and European suppliers and strengthen supply-chain resilience on both sides of the Atlantic. The Department of War linked the initiative to defense industrial commitments made at the July 2026 Ankara Summit under the “NATO 3.0” framework. The announcements did not disclose the site within Poland, opening date, investment value or planned annual maintenance capacity.
