title: IRGC dispmantles two terror teams in southeast Iran
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 27 (MNA) – IRGC Quds Base stationed in southeast Iran said Tuesday that two terrorist teams were identified and apprehended in the Saravan and Iranshahr counties.
The Public Relations office of the IRGC Ground Force’s Quds Base stated that, as part of a series of successive blows dealt to terrorist groups in the southeastern region—facilitated by intelligence oversight and preemptive action by the intelligence community—two terrorist teams were identified in the Saravan and Iranshahr areas, and their members were arrested at dawn today.
The IRGC base also said that the dismantled teams intended to carry out several terrorist operations in Iranshahr and Saravan; however, their plans were thwarted by the decisive action of intelligence agencies.
While expressing gratitude for the patience, forbearance, and cooperation shown by the valiant local population during the execution of this operation, the Quds Base of the IRGC Ground Force issued a warning to the mercenaries of the United States and the Zionist regime: the ultimate fate of serving as a mercenary for the enemy is destruction and annihilation.

title: 2027: Mbah leads the charge as Enugu APC unveils campaign council
body:
The Enugu State Chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) on Monday unveiled the party’s Campaign Council ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The Council, which is chaired by the Governor of Enugu State, Dr Peter Mbah, is also headlined by an Advisory Council comprising former President of the Senate, Ken Nnamani; former governor of old Anambra State, Senator Jim Nwobodo; former military governor of old Anambra State and Chief of Naval Staff, Rear Admiral Allison Madueke.
Others with advisory role are former Minister of Power, Professor Barth Nnaji; former Minister of Information and governorship candidate of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) in the 2023 governorship election in the state, Mr Frank Nweke Jr.; business mogul, Prince Arthur Eze; Senator Chuka Utazi; and former deputy governors Mrs Cecilia Ezeilo, Bishop Ralph Nwoye, Dr Sunday Onyebuchi, and Chief Okechukwu Itanyi, among other high-profile personalities.
The Campaign Council, comprising 51 Directorates, is chaired by the Governor of the state, Dr Peter Mbah, while the Deputy Governor, Ifeanyi Ossai; Deputy National Chairman, APC (South); Speaker, Enugu State House of Assembly, Hon Uchenna Ugwu; Chairman of the party in the state, Dr Martin Chukwunweike; and the Secretary to the State Government, Professor Chidiebere Onyia are Vice Chairmen.
The list signed by Chukwunweike and the Secretary of Enugu APC, Hon Chukwudi Nnadozie, also has Chief Charlie Mbah as the Director-General of the Campaign Organisation and Dr Eric Oluedo as the Secretary-General.
Senator Osita Ngwu, Senator Ikeje Asogwa, and Senator Kelvin Chukwu are Coordinators of the Campaign Council in Enugu West, Enugu North, and Enugu East, respectively.
Deacon Okey Ogbodo, Dr Dan Shere, and Hon S K E Udeh-Okoye are Deputy Campaign DGs for Enugu East Senatorial District, Enugu North Senatorial District, and Enugu West Senatorial District, respectively.
Steve Oruruo is the Campaign Spokesperson and Director of the Public Communication Committee, with Dr Austin Okolie as co-spokesperson and Dr. Malachy Agbo as Secretary.
Mazi Uche Anichukwu and Dan Nwomeh, both drawn from the Governor’s media team, head the Directorate of New Media and Strategic Communication and the Directorate of Mainstream Media, respectively. Dr Collins Ogbu is the Secretary of the former, while Dr Reuben Onyishi is the Secretary of the latter.
Victor Udeh leads the Administration Directorate, while Dr Ben Nwoye and Uche Nwatu are the Director and Co-Director of the Fundraising Committee, respectively.
Former Chief of Naval Staff, Vice Admiral Ikechukwu Ogalla (Rtd.), chairs the Security Directorate, while former Inspector General of Police, Ogbono Onovo (Rtd.), is the Secretary.
The Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr Kingsley Udeh, SAN, is in charge of the Directorate of Government Appointees Coordination (Federal and State), with Professor Chidiebere Onyia as Secretary, while former Speaker of the Enugu State House of Assembly, Hon Eugene Odoh, heads Inter-Party Affairs.
APC State Woman Leader, Mrs Esther Edeh, is at the helm of the Women Mobilisation Directorate, with the APC South East Woman Leader, Dr Oby Ajih, as Co-Director and Commissioner for Children, Gender Affairs and Social Development, Mrs Ngozi Enih, as Secretary.
Senator Chuka Utazi heads the Directorate of Parliamentary Mobilisation, with former Deputy Minority Leader, Hon Toby Okechukwu, as Secretary, while Senator Ben Collins Ndu is the Director of Contact and Mobilisation, with Peter Okonkwo as Co-Director and Mrs Lovelyn Obioma Nweze appointed as Secretary.
Commissioner for Culture and Tourism, Dame Ugochi Madueke, leads the Directorate of Welfare, which has Mrs Amaka Alinta as Secretary, while Dame Rita Mbah is the Director of Event Management, with Ifeoma Azike as Secretary.
Commissioner for Chieftaincy Affairs, Chief Charles Egumgbe, leads the Directorate of Monitoring, which has former Speaker of the Enugu State House of Assembly, Hon Edward Ubosi, as Secretary.
Uchenna Nwobodo is in charge of the Directorate of Works and Venue with Christian Enebe as Secretary. Hon USA Igweshi returned to his 2023 role as the Director, Directorate of Support Groups, while DrChiedozie Nwafor will serve as the Secretary.
Nollywood star Rachael Okonkwo, popularly known as Nkoli Nwa Nsukka, is the Director of the Directorate of Creativity and Entertainment, while the General Manager of the Enugu State Community and Social Development Agency (CSDA), Monday Diamond, heads the Directorate’s secretariat.
The Town Unions Coordination Directorate is headed by Chief Arinze Ogbodo, while the secretariat will be manned by Hon Charles Chime.
Meanwhile, in their co-signed statement, Chukwunweike and Nnadozie said the size of the Campaign Council was a reflection of “the conviction that every community, ward, local government area, professional group, support organisation, youth body, women’s group, elder, party faithful and person of goodwill must be seen, heard and meaningfully engaged.”
“Appointment into the campaign structure is therefore not merely an honour; it is a call to duty, accountability and measurable contribution,” they stated.
The Council was scheduled to be inaugurated at the International Conference Centre, Enugu, later on Tuesday, 27 October 2026.

title: Makinde camp asks EFCC to probe alleged payments for ministerial appointments
body: By Luminous Jannamike The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation has called on the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to investigate allegations that serving ministers paid billions of naira to secure appointments in President Bola Tinubu’s administration. The organisation, which is campaigning for Seyi Makinde under the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), said the President’s silence five days after Tinubu campaign spokesperson Alwan Hassan reportedly made the revelation on national television had raised concerns about possible high-level complicity. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, the campaign organisation accused the President of failing to address an allegation it said raised fundamental questions about the integrity of ministerial appointments and the conduct of his administration. “Mr. President’s silence validates public apprehension that either he is not in control or he sits in approval of a corrupt and fraudulent system where public offices are reduced to commodities sold to highest bidders,” the statement said. The organisation further alleged that a cabal of APC leaders in the National Assembly, senior presidential aides and individuals close to Tinubu had usurped government responsibilities, paving the way for the appointment of people it described as incompetent and corrupt. It blamed the administration for worsening insecurity and economic hardship, warning that alleged diversion of public resources could further undermine efforts to address Nigeria’s infrastructure deficit. “The EFCC must identify all those involved in this bribe for appointment scandal and ensure that anyone found culpable is held accountable in accordance with the law,” the organisation said. It urged Nigerians not to lose faith in the country ahead of the 2027 presidential election, promising that a Makinde-Daura government would prioritise transparency, accountability, service delivery and citizens’ welfare under its proposed four-year ‘Reset Nigeria’ agenda. The post Makinde camp asks EFCC to probe alleged payments for ministerial appointments appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Oil Markets Brace for a New Iran Escalation After U.S. Midterms
body: Brent holds near $115 as Iran war tensions and escalating Saudi-Houthi hostilities keep oil markets on edge ahead of U.S. midterms.      Hormuz Becomes Even More Dangerous  and More Expensive    - October has seen the most acute escalation in maritime attacks since the US-Iran war started eight months ago, with already more than 30 incidents recorded in the Strait of Hormuz and surrounding waterways, up from 14 in September.   - The most recent addition to the list of maritime targets is a crude tanker in Iraq's exclusive economic zone, signaling that it is not only tankers seeking to surreptitiously transit the Hormuz that get targeted by Iran.   - VLCCs, the largest crude tankers available, account for 28% of all drone and missile attacks in the Persian Gulf, with the 32 impacted ships representing almost 4% of the global VLCC fleet.  - Freight rates from the Gulf remain elevated with a Saudi Arabia-China voyage still costing around $33 per barrel, whilst regional demurrage rates have been rising since mid-August to their current level of $1,000,000/day.  - UKMTO, a provider of maritime security alerts, recently admitted that it is becoming increasingly more difficult to report on strikes as transiting ships prefer to sail unnoticed and charterers are wary of pushing freight rates even higher. Market Movers  - US gas producer EQT NYSEEQT has agreed to buy Range Resources NYSERRC in a $13 billion all-stock deal to create the largest US gas company, with the combined Appalachian-focused company having a net output of more than 9 bcf/d.  - US energy firm Ovintiv NYSEOVV will acquire Canada's Logan Energy in an all-cash deal valued at $0.9 billion, adding around 20,000 boe/d of production and 266,000 net acres across the Montney shale play.  - UK oil major BP NYSEBP has started the second phase of exploration in Venezuela's offshore Loran gas field, using the research and survey vessel Fugro Brasilis to perform final seabed studies.   - US oil giant ExxonMobil NYSEXOM reported a commercial discovery with its Rockhead-1 exploration well offshore Guyana, its first drilling success since the 2024 Hatchetfish find with a resource estimate of 500-600 million barrels.   - Italian oil major ENI BITENI has launched the construction of its 3 TCf Cronos project offshore Cyprus, aiming for first gas in the first half of 2028, to be exported via Egypt's Damietta LNG terminal. Tuesday, October 27, 2026  The oil markets are counting down the days until the November 3 midterm elections in the US, with expectations of impending hostilities rising into next month. Last-minute efforts to negotiate some form of de-escalation are ongoing, with both Qatar and Pakistan seeking to mediate between the Trump administration and Tehran, temporarily capping the upside for ICE Brent at $115 per barrel. Simultaneously to Hormuz tensions, the Saudi-Houthi conflict appears to be gaining self-sustaining momentum.  OPEC Holds the Fort on Supply Hikes. OPEC is expected to hold December output targets steady at its Sunday's meeting, with seven core members focusing on 2027 production quotas instead after they've completed the roll-back of 1.65 million b/d voluntary cuts, disrupted by the Hormuz crisis.  US Moves China Shipping Fees into 2027. The US is considering extending its truce with China on port charges for Chinese-linked ships by two months to January 9, preserving a suspension of tit-for-tat fees that previously imposed millions of dollars per port call and raised freight costs.  Houthis Hit Saudi Arabia's Largest Refinery. Yemen's Houthis claimed a ballistic missile strike hit Saudi Arabia's 550,000 b/d Ras Tanura refinery, causing a fire and disrupting operations at the Middle Eastern kingdom's largest plant, with an earlier March attack shutting it for three months.  Refining Boom Derails GalpMoeve Merger. Portugal's Galp and Spain's Moeve have abandoned plans for a potential downstream merger that would've combined 700,000 b/d of refining capacity and 3,500 service stations, claiming that 2026 bumper profits made it harder to agree M&A terms.  Brussels Builds a European Wall Against China. The European Union may introduce quotas or tariffs on Chinese chemicals, furniture and machinery from early 2027, seeking to replicate its recent import caps on hybrid vehicles as it struggles to narrow its 360 billion trade deficit.  Singapore Launches First LNG Term Tender. Singapore's state gas buyer GasCo launched its first ever LNG term supply tender after neighbouring Indonesia had announced it would slash pipeline gas exports by 15% to 31 MMCf/d, just as the government plans to add 5 new gas-powered plants.  East Timor Buys Out Its Untapped Offshore Gem. Australia's major Woodside ASXWDS has agreed to sell its stakes in the Greater Sunrise fields offshore East Timor for $200 million to the island nation, leaving state oil firm Timor gap as the only stakeholder of the untapped 5.3 TCf field.  Alberta Pushes for Scrapping of Tanker Ban. The province of Alberta called on the Carney government to repeal Canada's 2019 West Coast tanker ban that bars vessels carrying over 12,500 tonnes from loading at British Columbia ports, backing a proposed 250,000 b/d crude-by-rail route.  Indonesia Gives Up on Market-Based Imports. Indonesia plans to replace tender-based crude oil and refined product imports with government-to-government G2G and government-to-business G2B agreements to secure supplies, courting India and China for long-term supply deals.  Dangote Considers Third African Refinery. Nigeria's Dangote conglomerate is considering building a third 700,000 b/d refinery in Africa, alongside the existing plant in Lekki and the upcoming Kenyan refinery in Lamu, whilst simultaneously investing into refined product pipelines in West Africa.  Malaysia Doubles Down on Coal. The Malaysia government has proposed extending the lifespan of its existing coal-fuelled power plants despite an earlier pledge to retire coal by 2044, with coal accounting for 56% of current generation as JKM prices jumped to $33 per MMBtu this week.  Iron Ore Plunges Again on China Demand Fears. Iron ore prices fell to their lowest since September 2024 as weak Chinese demand and wafer-thin margins are expected to curb Q4 steel consumption, sending the Dalian iron ore futures to 662 per tonne, below the $100 per tonne threshold. White House to Ease Methane Emission Rules. The Trump administration is planning to relax rules on methane emissions from oil and gas operations, including exemptions for wells producing up to 15 boe/d, projecting incremental output of 210 million barrels for older and depleted wells.  Bahri Orders Three New VLCCs to Expand Tanker Fleet. Saudi national shipping company Bahri has ordered three VLCCs from domestic shipbuilder International Maritime Industries for $451 million, with deliveries scheduled in 2029-30 and marking the first attempt at exclusively Saudi shipbuilding.  UK Considers Fast-Track Approvals for Tiebacks. The UK's Burnham government is considering the fast-tracking of a small number of oil and gas tiebacks before pending legislation creates Transitional Energy Certificates that extend existing fields but preserve the country's exploration ban.  By Tom Kool for Oilprice.com

title: Janus Henderson, Centrifuge launch tokenized Nasdaq-100 fund on Stellar
body:
The blockchain-based fund offers eligible non-US investors exposure to the Nasdaq-100 as Janus Henderson expands its institutional tokenization business.
Asset manager Janus Henderson and tokenization platform Centrifuge have launched a blockchain-based fund tracking the Nasdaq-100 Index on Stellar, offering eligible investors outside the United States exposure to the benchmark.
Called JQQQ, the fund uses Centrifuge’s tokenization infrastructure and seeks to track the Nasdaq-100 under a licensing agreement with the exchange, according to a Tuesday announcement.
The launch expands Janus Henderson’s onchain investment offerings beyond US Treasurys and structured credit into equity-index exposure. The asset manager said its institutional onchain strategies now exceed $1 billion.
JQQQ is structured as a segregated portfolio of a British Virgin Islands investment company and provides indirect exposure to the Nasdaq-100 rather than ownership of the underlying stocks. The fund targets eligible professional investors outside the US, according to the Wall Street Journal, which reported a minimum investment of $100,000.
The launch follows Nasdaq’s decision in April to expand licensing of its Nasdaq-100 Index to additional asset managers, including BlackRock and State Street, while maintaining its longstanding partnership with Invesco, which operates the $499 billion market cap Invesco QQQ Trust exchange-traded fund.
Related: US Bank tests proprietary stablecoin in cross-border Stellar transaction
The Janus Henderson launch expands Stellar’s growing tokenization business. The Layer-1 blockchain currently ranks fourth among blockchains by distributed real-world asset value, with approximately $3.8 billion in tokenized assets, behind Ethereum, BNB Chain and Solana, according to RWA.xyz.
The network hosts tokenized assets from major issuers including Spiko, Franklin Templeton and Ondo. In July, tokenization platform Tradable announced plans to bring up to $1 billion in private credit assets to Stellar, with $500 million expected at launch.
Stellar is also part of a planned expansion by the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), which announced in May that it would connect its tokenization service to the network. DTCC-tokenized assets are expected to become available in the first half of 2027, potentially including US Treasurys, major index ETFs and Russell 1000 stocks.
Despite the expansion of Stellar’s tokenized asset market, its native token, XLM, has fallen about 16% year to date, trading near $0.17 on Tuesday, according to CoinGecko data .

title: 2027 Presidential Poll: Court reserves judgment in SDP’s suit against INEC
body: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Federal High Court in Abuja has reserved judgment in a suit the Social Democratic Party (SDP) filed against the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) for publishing the name of Adewole Adebayo as its candidate for the 2027 presidential election. The party filed the suit alongside its National Organising Secretary, Dr Chukwuma Ogbonna, as the 2nd plaintiff. They accused the electoral body of failing to recognise its duly nominated candidate. According to the plaintiffs, the SDP conducted its presidential primary election and national convention on May 20, 2026, in Abuja, under the leadership of its national chairman, Alhaji Shehu Musa Gabam. The plaintiffs told the court that the primary election was observed by INEC, which issued a Certified True Copy of its monitoring report. Following the outcome of the exercise, the SDP said it submitted the name and personal particulars of the winner, Hon. Abimbola Akeem Atanda, to INEC as its presidential candidate. However, the plaintiffs alleged that INEC published Adebayo’s name as the party’s candidate instead of that of the winner of the primary election monitored by the commission. They argued that INEC’s action was inconsistent with provisions of the Electoral Act, 2026, and asked the court to intervene. Among other reliefs, the plaintiffs are seeking an order directing INEC to stop recognising, accepting or publishing the name of any person other than their validly nominated candidate as the SDP’s presidential candidate for the 2027 election. They also want the court to set aside the purported publication of Adebayo’s name and restrain INEC from placing his name on the ballot as the party’s presidential candidate, on the ground that, according to them, he was not properly nominated by the party. The plaintiffs further urged the court to order the electoral body to recognise and publish the name of the candidate who emerged as winner of the presidential primary election it monitored. Justice Salim Ibrahim reserved judgment in the case after the parties adopted their final briefs of argument. title: Atiku to Tinubu: $20.5bn loan plan vindicates my warning
body: By Luminous Jannamike Former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has said President Bola Tinubu’s request for approval to borrow $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion vindicates his earlier warning about a proposed $20 billion loan, accusing the administration of failing to disclose the specific projects the funds would finance. Atiku said the absence of project-by-project details raises questions about transparency and the possibility of public funds being channelled to political allies and favoured contractors, particularly through the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway project, which he alleged had been rerouted inland. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku recalled that he had warned on October 12 about the reported borrowing plan and challenged Tinubu to confirm or deny it and publish the relevant accounts. “Today, he has asked the Senate to approve $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion in external loans. My warning has been vindicated,” he said. Atiku faulted the President for failing to provide details of the projects, their costs, locations and contractors, insisting that Nigerians should not be asked to shoulder such a huge debt without knowing how the money would be spent. He questioned whether the highway project could become a conduit for directing borrowed funds to political allies, especially with an election approaching. “Is this a development plan for Nigerians or a campaign financing scheme dressed up as infrastructure?” he asked. The ADC candidate warned that he would scrutinise loans obtained during the final year of Tinubu’s administration if elected President, vowing to challenge any borrowing found to have breached constitutional, statutory or due process requirements. “I put local and international lenders on notice: any loan granted to this winding-down administration must meet all constitutional, statutory and due process requirements,” he said. He urged the National Assembly to withhold approval until the President publishes the projects, contracts, costs, contractors, loan terms and repayment obligations attached to the borrowing plan. “No public money should be borrowed in the dark, and no lawmaker should sign a blank cheque against Nigeria’s future,” Atiku said. He said the burden of proof rested on Tinubu to demonstrate that the loans would serve the national interest rather than political interests, warning that Nigerians struggling with the cost of living should not be made to pay for debts incurred without adequate public disclosure. Atiku said the controversy could further shape the political contest, with voters having an opportunity to hold the administration accountable for its borrowing decisions. title: Ripple strikes deal with Robinhood to expand its RLUSD digital dollar
body:
Ripple has struck a deal with Robinhood to expand the reach of its digital dollar, RLUSD , strengthening trading and financing links between their institutional businesses and improving Robinhood's internal money management.
The partnership involves using RLUSD to settle institutional trades, automate Robinhood's treasury operations and expand access to digital asset trading and financing through Ripple Prime and Bitstamp, the global crypto exchange acquired by Robinhood last year .
It also helps meet Robinhood's ambition of becoming a global financial superapp, centralizing its customers' financial lives while expanding the underlying infrastructure that can serve both retail and institutional clients.
"Utility is what moves stablecoins forward. Working with Ripple, Bitstamp and Robinhood will have access to RLUSD for institutional settlement, Ripple Treasury for our operations and Ripple Prime for financing," Robinhood Crypto General Manager Johann Kerbrat said in a statement shared with CNBC. "That is what a connected, global financial system looks like."
Stablecoins have long been a workhorse of the crypto world, giving traders a way to move money among exchanges, buy and sell crypto assets, and park funds between trades without having to convert back into traditional currency. But as the crypto industry evolves beyond trading and markets move toward 24/7 liquidity, stablecoins are becoming essential financial infrastructure because of their ability to enable near-instant settlement and move dollar-denominated value at any time, regardless of traditional banking hours.
As firms look to do more with stablecoins beyond simply listing them on exchanges, stablecoin issuers are betting they'll favor a one-stop-shop approach that bundles the technology and services needed to move money, settle trades and manage cash.
"Stablecoins have evolved from a crypto trading tool into a critical piece of financial infrastructure," Ripple President Monica Long told CNBC. "The clearest evidence of this is where they're now being embedded — from corporate payments to capital markets. Our partnership with Robinhood reflects that evolution."
"This is about much more than trading," she added. "It's about fundamentally changing how money moves and is managed — giving institutions the ability to operate 24/7/365, unlocking liquidity and putting capital to work more efficiently."
Circle Internet Group, a Ripple competitor, is positioning itself for a similar future, where winning platforms, in addition to issuing stablecoins, also provide the infrastructure to put them to work. Earlier this year, for example, it launched the Circle Payments Network, connecting financial institutions and payment providers using its flagship USDC stablecoin and other digital assets for cross-border payments.
The network is Circle's answer to the 8-year-old Ripple Payments business, a service that helps businesses move money across borders, using any of several assets moving through that system, including USDC, Ripple-created XRP and, as of its debut in December 2024, RLUSD.
RLUSD's market cap has grown to more than $2.5 billion . Tether's USDT and Circle's USDC still dominate the total stablecoin market, which now exceeds $300 billion .
RLUSD will also be listed on Robinhood's trading platform, and is currently available to traders on Bitstamp as well as Robinhood Chain, the company's home-grown blockchain for tokenized stocks and other assets.
Robinhood, which reports third-quarter results for the three months ended in September after the market closes, rose about 2.5% in early trading Tuesday, snapping a three-day decline.

title: Labour shortage hurts West Lake Gold output
body: West Red Lake Gold Mines (TSXV: WRLG; US-OTC: WRLGF) reduced its annual production target by about a quarter as labour shortages and difficult mining slowed its Madsen gold operation in Ontario. The stock plunged. The Vancouver-based company now expects 27,000 to 32,000 oz. this year, down from 35,000 to 45,000 oz., it said Tuesday. The northwestern Ontario mine is about 260 km east-northeast of Winnipeg. “In addition, the extraction of certain remnant pillars proved more challenging than anticipated as mining activities remained concentrated in previously mined areas,” CEO Shane Williams said in a news release. The setback tests the company’s ability to turn Madsen into a reliable producer after declaring commercial production in January. West Red Lake is planning to use the existing mill to process ore from nearby deposits, but first needs to establish consistent output at the operation already running. West Red Lake shares fell 12% to 61¢ by midday in Toronto, giving the company a market value of about C$253 million ($180 million). They’ve traded between 56¢ and C$1.49 over the past year. Production optimism Before Tuesday’s cut, Cantor Fitzgerald analyst Matthew O’Keefe expected Madsen to meet annual guidance as production increased in the second half, according to an Aug. 28 note. His assessment linked a potential improvement in the company’s valuation to establishing and meeting production and cost targets through 2027. That optimism followed a 51% increase in second-quarter gold output from the first quarter. All-in sustaining costs fell 30% to $3,284 per oz. sold. The improvement showed how higher volumes could spread the operation’s costs across more gold sales. West Red Lake’s Madsen mine enters commercial production Third-quarter production fell 8.4% to 7,859 oz. from 8,576 oz. in the previous quarter. The company added specialist contractors and commissioned a secondary crusher. Mining the remaining rock in previously worked areas requires more selective extraction and extra ground support, the company said. Difficult operation West Red Lake acquired Madsen through Pure Gold’s creditor-protection proceedings in June 2023. The site’s existing mill, shaft and underground access offered infrastructure to reuse, but the current shortfall illustrates the challenges of mining around old workings. The forthcoming prefeasibility study would bring Madsen and the neighbouring Rowan project into one production plan, with Rowan feeding the existing mill. The company’s third-quarter financial results are due Nov. 27.

title: Russia strikes publishing house warehouse in Kharkiv on Ukrainian Language Day, adding to a campaign against Ukrainian literature and culture
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Russian forces struck a warehouse belonging to Ukrainian publishing house KSD in Kharkiv on 27 October, disrupting the publisher’s planned November releases. No employees were injured, but the company is still assessing the damage and losses. The attack came on the Day of Ukrainian Writing and Language, a national holiday celebrating Ukraine’s language and literary heritage. It adds to a series of Russian strikes on Ukrainian publishing houses, printing facilities, and book warehouses that have destroyed millions of books and disrupted the country’s publishing industry. KSD announced the strike on social media, saying it had planned to greet readers on the holiday and reveal its November releases but instead had to deal with the attack. The publisher said strikes in the area were continuing, preventing it from determining the full extent of the damage. The company had planned to begin releasing its new books on 5 November. It has now postponed the announcements while it assesses the situation and determines how to proceed. “We really want to show you the new releases we had prepared for November,” KSD said. “But for now, as we clarify the details, we cannot yet assess the scale of the destruction and understand how we will work going forward.” The publisher said it would share updates as more information became available. Russian forces struck a warehouse building in Kharkiv’s Slobidskyi District with a drone, as Moscow continues targeting civilian and industrial infrastructure across Ukraine. Ukraine’s State Emergency Service pic.twitter.com/F6Ee7VybbI — Euromaidan Press (@EuromaidanPress) October 27, 2026 Russia’s attacks devastate Ukraine’s book industry KSD’s warehouse is the latest publishing facility affected by Russia’s campaign against Ukraine’s book industry. In July and August alone, Russian attacks destroyed around 13 million books, nearly a third of the number Ukrainian publishers printed in all of 2025, according to the Ukrainian publishing industry. On 1 August, a Russian strike on a warehouse used by the Ranok publishing group in Kharkiv destroyed around 8 million books, including hundreds of thousands of school textbooks. A separate attack on a printing facility in July destroyed print runs and book materials belonging to numerous Ukrainian publishers. In October, Russian strikes also damaged a Kyiv warehouse belonging to publisher Knyholav, destroying tens of thousands of books, including titles and reprints that had replaced stock lost in an earlier attack. Explore further Russia has burned millions of Ukrainian books, striking at the infrastructure of Ukrainian culture These strikes threaten more than publishers’ finances. Destroyed print runs and damaged warehouses delay new releases, deprive readers of Ukrainian-language books, and force publishers to spend scarce resources replacing titles instead of developing new ones. KSD has not yet disclosed its losses or announced a revised release schedule for its November books. title: US arrests Nigerian man who fled to Nigeria in 2019 over money laundering
body: A 34-year-old Nigerian man, Adetunji Abudu, has been arrested in the United States over an alleged money laundering conspiracy involving millions of dollars obtained through fraud schemes targeting elderly Americans. Abudu, from Lagos, Nigeria, was arrested on Monday night at Logan Airport in Boston, Massachusetts, while attempting to re-enter the United States from Istanbul, Turkey. According to a statement from US authorities, he appeared before the US District Court in Rhode Island on October 21, 2026, and was ordered detained pending trial. He is one of six defendants charged in a superseding indictment returned by a federal grand jury in Providence over an alleged conspiracy to launder proceeds from multiple fraud schemes operated from Nigeria. The schemes allegedly targeted elderly US residents through online romance scams, fraudulent sweepstakes, false rental listings and sham online shipping transactions. According to the indictment, money obtained from victims was allegedly channelled through bank accounts and businesses in Rhode Island, Idaho and other locations, with significant proceeds ultimately transferred to Nigeria. Members of the alleged conspiracy were also accused of purchasing vehicles with illicit proceeds and shipping them overseas. US authorities said Abudu fled the country to Nigeria in 2019 after the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) executed a court-authorised search of his residence in North Providence. Five of his co-defendants — Dotun Olawale Alonge, Oluwaseyi Akintol, Samson Ikotun, Olabode Shaba and Oladipup Shodipu — have since pleaded guilty to money laundering conspiracy. They received sentences ranging from time served to 42 months’ imprisonment, according to the statement. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant US Attorney John P. McAdams. The FBI investigated the matter with assistance from the US Postal Inspection Service and the Tallmadge Police Department in Ohio and the Moscow Police Department in Idaho. The allegations against Abudu remain unproven in court. He is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty. title: Core Systems Now Offers 25GbE Ultra-Low-Latency Networking as a Solution for the ATMOS2 Rugged Computing Platform
body:
SAN DIEGO, Calif. Core Systems, a designer and manufacturer of rugged computing solutions for defense and industrial customers, today announced that it is integrating high-performance 25 Gigabit Ethernet networking into its ATMOS2 rugged computing platform.
The new ATMOS2 configuration will incorporate the AMD Solarflare X2522-25G-PLUS dual-port 25GbE network adapter, bringing the adapter’s ultra-low-latency performance and hardware acceleration to demanding, mission-critical environments. The configuration is planned for availability in the first quarter of 2027.
PURPOSE-BUILT NETWORKING FOR MISSION-CRITICAL SYSTEMS
Unlike conventional network cards, the X2522-25G-PLUS is engineered for environments where speed, precision and reliability are non-negotiable. Core Systems engineers selected the adapter and are integrating it so that ATMOS2 can move large volumes of sensor, video and command data without becoming the bottleneck in a larger system.
The goal is rapid data processing, reduced CPU overhead and consistent, high-throughput communications. Those qualities make the adapter an ideal fit for the ATMOS platform and the operators who depend on it.
■D ual-port 25GbE: Two 10/25GbE SFP28 ports will provide bandwidth headroom for data-intensive workloads and support redundant or segregated network paths.
■ Ultra-low latency: The adapter supports kernel-bypass acceleration, which shortens the path between the network and the application so time-sensitive data can arrive faster and more predictably.
■ Hardware acceleration: The adapter offloads network processing from the host, which is designed to free CPU cycles for mission applications such as signal processing, analytics and AI inference.
■ Precision timing: Hardware timestamping on the adapter supports accurate time synchronization across distributed sensors and systems.
■ Consistent throughput: The X2522-25G-PLUS is built for steady performance under sustained load, helping keep communications stable when the mission depends on them.
For defense programs, faster networking translates directly into faster decisions. ATMOS2 with 25GbE networking is designed for C5ISR, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR), sensor fusion and edge processing applications, where data must be captured, moved and acted on in real time.
By reducing latency and CPU overhead at the network layer, ATMOS2 will give integration more processing capacity for mission software within the same rugged footprint. That will help programs field more capability without adding size, weight or power.

title: Elon Musk argues that the threat of Russian anti-satellite attacks is a reason to restrict Starlink’s military use in Ukraine
body: Starlink service for Ukraine’s armed forces was restricted over fears that Russia would shoot down the company’s satellites, a post on X by SpaceX chief Elon Musk suggests. Musk was responding to a post about Russia’s ability to blow up satellites in space. “This is indeed one of the main reasons that Starlink must remain a civilian operation,” Musk tweeted. “It can be used for infrastructure that is military, but it cannot be used for unequivocally offensive strikes that make it fair game to be struck back. An adversary blowing up Starlink satellites would create a domino effect of destruction that would generate a vast field of debris making space unusable.” In mid-October, Ukraine’s armed forces encountered restrictions on their Starlink satellite terminals, specifically the military version, Starshield. Connections cut out when drones flew faster than 160 kilometers per hour (about 100 mph). Western media reported that Musk himself had initiated the restrictions on Starlink service for the Ukrainian military. He later accused Ukraine of using Starlink for “offensive” drone strikes. Ukraine’s armed forces responded that this was “technically impossible,” since Starlink does not work over Russian territory. title: Same Tax, Collected When You Pay: Bringing fairness to VAT on foreign digital services
body: Over the past week, many Ghanaians have asked a fair question: will paying for a streaming subscription, cloud storage, or an online game soon cost more because of the introduction of a collection and monitoring system? I understand why people are concerned. Digital services are now part of how we work, learn, run businesses and unwind, and household budgets are carefully managed. The answer deserves to be stated plainly. This is not a new tax, and the rate has not changed. It is the same VAT, now collected when you pay. VAT on digital services sold to Ghanaians by companies based abroad has been part of Ghana’s VAT law since 2022, following the amendment of the Value Added Tax Act, 2013 (Act 870) by the Value Added Tax (Amendment) Act, 2022 (Act 1082), and the Authority has been collecting it since then. The combined rate remains 20 per cent: 15 per cent VAT, plus 2.5 per cent each for the National Health Insurance Levy and the GETFund Levy. It is worth recalling that this rate came down, not up, effective January 2026, following the passage of the Value Added Tax Act, 2025 (Act 1151), which reduced the effective VAT rate from 21.9 per cent to 20 per cent. Nothing is being added to it now. What is changing is how the tax is collected. Until now, the Authority has relied largely on the foreign companies themselves to declare their sales in Ghana and pass the VAT on to us. About 92 of them are registered and paying. About 100 more have been identified as selling to Ghanaian customers without charging or paying the VAT the law already requires. Enforcing compliance through self-declaration alone, against companies with no physical presence in Ghana, is slow and uncertain. In view of these challenges, Parliament in July 2026 approved the implementation by GRA of a system that will efficiently collect VAT, beginning with digital services supplied by cross-border entities. Under the new arrangement, run through GRA’s Sentinal® system, the VAT will be collected at the point the consumer pays, by the bank, mobile money operator or other licensed payment company handling the payment, and passed on to GRA. Connecting to GRA’s system is mandatory for those institutions. For the customer, very little changes. There is no form to fill and no extra step. You continue to pay for and enjoy your services as usual, and each time you make a payment, you will receive an SMS or email confirming the transaction, so you can see exactly what you have been charged, including VAT. There are, however, two things people will notice, and I would rather explain them now than have them discovered on a bank statement. First, registered providers will now display prices without VAT, with the VAT added when you pay. A subscription may therefore show a lower listed price and a separate VAT amount at checkout. This is the same VAT that used to sit inside the price, now shown openly. It is not an extra 20 per cent on top. Second, customers of providers that were not charging VAT may now see it deducted for the first time. I will not pretend otherwise. But that is not a new tax. It is the existing law being applied evenly. No one who is already paying VAT should pay it twice. Where VAT is wrongly charged, it will be refunded automatically. If it is not, the customer should notify the bank or mobile money provider from which the payment was made, keeping the SMS or email notification as a record. Where the matter is still not resolved, GRA’s official channels remain open. The scope is deliberately narrow. VAT is collected at payment only when three conditions are met together: the payment is made with a Ghana-issued debit or credit card, mobile money account or digital wallet; the business selling the service is based outside Ghana; and the service is delivered online, such as streaming, cloud computing and online gaming. Sending mobile money to family is not a payment to a foreign digital service and is not affected. Physical goods bought from abroad remain under Customs procedures. Why does this matter? The first reason is fairness. A Ghanaian software developer, streaming platform or digital advertising agency must charge VAT on its services. When a foreign company offering the same service to the same customer charges nothing, our own businesses compete on uneven ground. The same rules should apply to every business selling into the Ghanaian market, wherever it is based. The second reason is the public purse. The Minister for Finance told Parliament this year that Ghana loses an estimated 60 per cent of its potential VAT revenue through non-compliance, and that sustainable revenue growth must come from stronger compliance and smarter administration rather than higher tax rates. Collecting VAT on foreign digital services at the point of payment is a direct application of that principle. It asks those who are already obliged to pay to do so, rather than placing more weight on those who already comply. Every cedi of tax already due that is properly collected is a cedi that does not have to be raised through new taxes or additional borrowing. Collecting VAT at payment does not relieve the companies concerned of their obligations. Registered providers must still file their periodic VAT returns. The return accounts for what has been collected; it does not add a second tax. This reform is one part of a wider modernisation of tax administration, alongside the Integrated Tax Administration System, the Publican AI Trade Solution at our ports and the Fiscal Electronic Device now being piloted. The aim throughout is the same: that tax due under the law is collected on time, accurately and transparently, with every taxpayer treated consistently. Public trust in the tax system depends on people understanding what they pay and why. So let me close where I began. This is not a new tax, and the rate has not changed. You do not need to do anything differently. It is the same VAT, collected when you pay, so that it is collected fairly from every provider, local and foreign alike. For further information, please rely on official GRA channels (020 926 7047/8, 055 299 0000, info@gra.gov.gh, www.gra.gov.gh) and your bank or mobile money provider. – By: Anthony Akwasi Sarpong, Commissioner General, Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA).

title: Ukraine’s StarGate Drone Now Evacuating Wounded Soldiers
body: Ukraine’s 475th Separate Assault Regiment, known as CODE 9.2, says it has used the StarGate uncrewed aerial platform to evacuate two seriously wounded soldiers from the battlefield in the span of a week. Reportedly, this is the first time the specialized drone has been used for an operation of this kind. It is not, however, the first instance of Ukraine using an aerial rescue drone on the battlefield, with the more extemporized heavy hexacopter also having been used recently, as you can read about here . Taken together, the missions underscore Ukraine’s efforts to develop alternative casualty evacuation capabilities as Russian drone threats, electronic warfare, and harsh terrain increasingly complicate conventional recovery operations, including those using uncrewed ground vehicles (UGVs). According to CODE 9.2, on its Facebook page, the regiment’s personnel carried out two complex evacuation missions using StarGate, a platform developed and manufactured by Ukrainian company SkyFall. The two wounded servicemen were 25-year-old Yevhen, callsign “Izyum,” and 24-year-old Artem, callsign “Kolobok.” Both belonged to adjacent units and had suffered severe limb injuries while occupying positions in a so-called gray zone approximately three miles from the Russian border. Difficult terrain, including water obstacles, and the threat posed by Russian first-person-view (FPV) drones prevented ground vehicles from reaching the casualties, the regiment said. Air evacuation was the only available option. Drone operators watch as two soldiers carry their injured comrade to the SkyFall drone for evacuation. CODE 9.2/screencap The missions were planned and executed by CODE 9.2 personnel with support from SkyFall. They required coordination among multiple units, additional forces and equipment, and dedicated fire support — much like a more traditional casualty evacuation effort involving crewed helicopters . Vampire heavy strike drones were employed to suppress enemy positions during the operations. “The injury tore off half of my foot, so a lot of blood was lost already,” Izyum said in a video interview from his hospital room. “I think if that incredible little bird hadn’t flown in, well, getting out from there would have been unrealistic.” During one of the missions, StarGate reportedly flew nearly 20 miles to reach the casualty before covering approximately the same distance on the return leg with the wounded serviceman aboard. CODE 9.2 said Russian electronic warfare systems were actively attempting to suppress satellite navigation signals in the area. An injured soldier is helped out of the drone after recovery to a safe area. CODE 9.2/screencap Despite the reported interference, the platform completed the mission using its onboard artificial intelligence-based navigation system, according to the regiment. The statement did not specify the navigation technologies involved. StarGate was designed specifically for casualty evacuation, or CASEVAC, when conventional ground transportation cannot reach wounded personnel or would expose them to unacceptable risks. Its stated specifications include a payload capacity of up to 330 pounds and a maximum speed of approximately 65 miles per hour. The evacuation module is based on a covered, medical-grade stretcher. StarGate on the ground. SkyFall Oleksandr Nastenko, commander of CODE 9.2, callsign “Flint,” said the regiment intends to use the experience gained from the two missions to train crews and make aerial evacuation a more established capability. The regiment also plans to set up a dedicated aerial medical evacuation unit within its medical company. The StarGate missions follow a separate reported operation involving the 92nd Assault Brigade, which says its personnel helped evacuate a wounded soldier using a heavy-lift hexacopter drone, produced by Gurzuf Defense, with the casualty suspended beneath it, as seen in the video below: This drone was reportedly an Audag-6 model , which is said to be capable of carrying a 200-pound payload over a distance of up to 15 miles. In that incident, the soldier had been wounded while holding his position. Once again, aerial extraction was judged the only suitable option; in this case, due to the presence of mines and intense Russian drone activity. This was a more improvised approach, which the brigade described as the world’s first frontline aerial drone evacuation of a wounded soldier. Compared to Stargate, the Gurzuf drone brings some drawbacks with it, including casualty stability, exposure to the elements, the risk of swinging during flight, and the difficulty of safely lifting and lowering a severely injured person. It subsequently emerged that the soldier involved, Kostiantyn Vlasenko, had been forced to amputate his own foot as part of a 491-day ordeal on a frontline position. A soldier clipped to the underside of a Gurzuf drone via a harness is flown to safety. 92nd Assault Brigade/YouTube screencap This was not the first time that Ukrainian forces have adapted existing drone technology to effect battlefield evacuations. TWZ also previously reported on a Ukrainian soldier who managed to escape from the Russians that surrounded him after an electric bike was dropped to him by a large aerial drone. As a purpose-built platform, StarGate offers a more standardized way to secure and transport casualties, and to transport them protected from the elements, in a secure, prone position. However, StarGate still faces the challenges of flying in contested airspace and navigating under electronic warfare conditions. Once again, depending on the degree of injuries, the casualty may need assistance being put on the stretcher and, regardless of the degree of medical care that can be provided, StarGate is only an option if already available in proximity to the victim. Close-up view of the StarGate stretcher. SkyFall The fact that the StarGate missions also needed strike drones for fire support underscores that casualty recovery, whatever the platform being used, typically requires coordination across multiple combat elements. Despite the limitations, CODE 9.2’s plan to create a dedicated medical aviation element indicates it wants to move beyond one-off missions toward a repeatable capability. StarGate in flight. SkyFall As with other emerging technologies from the war in Ukraine, this is likely to be studied by other armed forces, too. The U.S. military, for example, has long looked at the potential of uncrewed aerial systems to effect casualty evacuation missions, as you can read about here . Meanwhile, the challenges of that conflict mean that Ukrainian troops continue to explore different ways to recover wounded troops from positions that more conventional evacuation methods can no longer safely reach.
