title: Amazon Is Gutting Its AI Division After Sustained Failure
body:
Can’t-miss innovations from the bleeding edge of science and tech
By now, you’d be hard pressed to find anyone who isn’t broadly familiar with the AI heavyweights and their flagship models. OpenAI has ChatGPT, Anthropic has Claude, Google has Gemini. But what does Amazon have?
Not a whole lot, it turns out. Unlike its competitors in the tech megacorp scene, Amazon’s standout AI model — organized under the name “Nova” — is about the farthest thing from a household name. And that’s not likely to change anytime soon, because the ecommerce giant is now gutting its in-house AI labs, Bloomberg reports .
Per the outlet, Amazon is scaling back the ambitions of most of its Nova AI models and reorganizing its AI development teams as part of an effort to narrow its focus on “highest priority” goals, after its power-hungry large language models turned out to be a bust.
Accordingly, the company has put most of its AI models on ice, Amazon insiders told Bloomberg . This includes its text-based Nova models, as well as video- and image-generating models, all of which have been placed in a state of “keep the lights on,” meaning they’re technically still supported, but only receive the bare minimum resources needed to sustain them.
Instead, labor and computing power are being diverted toward a singular “frontier-model effort” led by Pieter Abbeel, director of the Berkeley Robot Learning Lab whose robotics company Covariant was hoovered up by Amazon in 2024. At the time Abbeel joined the tech giant, Covariant’s founders were working on AI models for robots, which lines up pretty well with Amazon’s push to automate everything it possibly can.
News of the shift in Amazon’s strategic focus comes a week after it closed one of its key AI offices in San Francisco, an 80-person site specializing in research on artificial general intelligence, the supposed next-level of AI development where the tech obtains human-level intelligence and reasoning skills.
With urgent questions swirling over whether LLMs can ever usher in a return on investment — let alone AGI — it may be that Amazon is jumping out of the AI hype cycle while it still can.
More on Amazon: Amazon’s AI-Generated Animated Series Canceled After Relentless Derision

I’m a tech and labor correspondent for Futurism, where my beat includes the role of emerging technologies in governance, surveillance, and labor.

title: Rising Sea Levels Could Threaten Lagos by 2050, Majekodunmi Warns
body: Funmi Ogundare Environmental activist and Chairman of the Lekki State Urban Forest and Animal Shelter Initiative (LUFASI), Dr. Desmond Majekodunmi, Tuesday warned that rising sea levels and the growing effects of climate change could threaten parts of Lagos by 2050, urging Nigerians to embrace sustainable environmental practices to avert an ecological crisis. He stated that continued greenhouse gas emissions, deforestation, pollution and the destruction of biodiversity were worsening the climate crisis and putting communities at risk. Majekodunmi made this known at the three-day international conference of Society for Environmental Toxicology and Pollution Mitigation (SETPOM), themed: ‘Driving Environmental Security, Innovation, and Resilience through AI, Research, Industry, and Regulation for Global Livelihoods,’ held at the University of Lagos. He stressed the need for urgent collective action to protect the environment, warning that prioritising profit over people and the planet could have devastating consequences for future generations. According to him, “The earth remains uniquely habitable because of its atmosphere, but human activities are increasingly threatening the natural systems that sustain life.” He identified industrial activities, fossil fuel consumption, mining, deforestation, agricultural practices, waste disposal and transportation among the major contributors to environmental degradation and global warming. Majekodunmi explained that rising global temperatures were intensifying the water cycle, contributing to heavier rainfall, flooding and other extreme weather events. He cited the effects of coastal erosion and rising sea levels as particular concerns for Lagos, a coastal city vulnerable to the consequences of climate change. He warned that continued emissions could worsen the situation, with potentially devastating implications for communities, infrastructure and institutions, including the University of Lagos. The environmentalist called for greater public awareness and stronger commitment to sustainable development, saying: “Individuals, institutions, industries and governments must take responsibility for protecting the environment.” He, however, expressed optimism that the climate crisis could be addressed through the adoption of renewable energy, improved waste management, recycling, scientific research, technological innovation and effective environmental regulation. He identified solar, wind and water-based energy as potential sources of cleaner power, stressing that sustainable alternatives were available but required stronger commitment and investment. Speaking with journalists, the President of the Society for Environmental Toxicology and Pollution Mitigation (SETPOM), Dr. Idowu Aneyo, stated that Nigerians must embrace behavioural change and leverage Artificial Intelligence (AI) to protect the ecosystem and promote environmental sustainability. Aneyo, a lecturer in the Department of Zoology at the University of Lagos (UNILAG), said although regulations were in place, particularly in Lagos State, effective environmental protection required greater public cooperation and a deliberate commitment to sustainable practices. She commended the state government for its efforts in enforcing environmental regulations, noting that the major challenge was getting people to accept and adapt to the changes needed to protect the environment. “There are regulations, especially in Lagos State. I want to say that the Lagos State Government is really trying to enforce them. It is just we humans that need to accept this change,” she said. According to her, behavioural change remains difficult for many people, but individuals must be intentional about protecting the ecosystem. She stressed the need for Nigerians to take personal responsibility for environmental preservation, adding that effective regulation must be complemented by public awareness and a willingness to adopt environmentally responsible practices. Aneyo also emphasised the potential of AI and machine learning in addressing environmental challenges, noting that the technologies could help predict environmental risks, control damage and support sustainable ecosystem management. “In the era of artificial intelligence, there is a lot that it can actually help to do. We need to use machine learning and AI to predict and also control some damage, and bring about sustainability of the ecosystem,” she stated. The conference witnessed a debate competition among secondary school students, titled, ‘Harnessing Innovation and Artificial Intelligence for Environmental Sustainability Investments’. It produced winners in the junior and senior categories who were rewarded with cash gifts and certificates.

title: PHP2Shell, LiteLLM, GitLab: Find What You Need to Patch
body:
Between October 16 and 23, 2026, PHP, Node.js, GitLab, LiteLLM, OpenCode and the eMudhra certificate authority all had serious security incidents. PHP, Node.js and GitLab shipped fixes on October 21, the same day the bad LiteLLM release went out. Every advisory ended with some version of upgrade, rebuild or rotate.
Doing the upgrade is the easy part. What takes time is working out, for your own accounts, where the affected thing runs, who owns it, and what it can reach. If you have an inventory you trust, that’s an afternoon. If you don’t, it’s a week of Slack threads, and this week didn’t give anyone a week. Amazon’s MadPot honeypots logged a PHP2Shell exploit attempt four days before the bugs were disclosed .
Nothing on that list is obscure. Two are runtimes that a large share of the web sits on, one is the source-control server plenty of companies still host themselves, and one is the AI gateway a lot of teams adopted in a hurry to route LLM traffic. If you run a reasonably sized estate on AWS or Azure, at least one of these was probably yours to deal with.
Mandiant tracks how long attackers take to exploit a vulnerability after disclosure. Its time-to-exploit analysis put the average at 63 days in 2018–2019, 44 days in 2020–2021 and 32 days in 2021–2022. In 2023 it was five days, and 70% of the exploited vulnerabilities Mandiant tracked that year were zero-days, exploited before a patch existed.
Drew Silcock’s post Is this the new cyber normal? , which reached the front page of Hacker News on October 23, argues that LLMs have compressed this further, so the gap between a bad RCE becoming public and automated attacks against it is now hours rather than weeks. PHP2Shell fits. The bugs were found with help from an AI model , patched binaries appeared before the advisory after an embargo dispute, and exploit attempts started before most people could install the fix.
Your exposure window is the time to find what’s affected plus the time to fix it. Most teams have spent years shrinking the second number with CI/CD, managed runtimes and automatic patching. The first number is still a spreadsheet, a Slack thread, and whoever remembers how the old GitLab box was set up.
This is why the frameworks put inventory first. The CIS Controls make inventory of enterprise assets and inventory of software Controls 1 and 2; vulnerability management doesn’t show up until Control 7. CISA’s BOD 23-01 requires US federal agencies to run automated asset discovery every seven days and vulnerability enumeration every 14. If you don’t know a server exists, you won’t patch it.
Here is how I’d answer each of those questions with what AWS and Azure give you out of the box, using this week’s incidents as examples. Every command below is read-only.
Start with Node.js. On Lambda, supported managed runtimes get runtime updates automatically by default, so most functions on a current Node.js runtime pick up the fix without a redeploy. Two groups don’t. Functions on the deprecated nodejs20.x runtime stopped getting security patches when Node.js 20 reached end of life in April 2026. Functions deployed as container images carry whatever Node.js was baked into the image. So what you actually need is the list of functions on an old runtime or packaged as an image:
Image-based functions are in that output because the Lambda API can’t tell you what’s inside them. For those you need your image scanner, or a rebuild.
For PHP2Shell on Azure, App Service records each Linux app’s runtime stack, and Azure Resource Graph can search it across every subscription you can read:
Anything on PHP 8.1 or older gets no regular upstream fix, so put it at the top of the list.
VMs and containers are harder, because the cloud control plane doesn’t know what’s installed on them. That’s what AWS Systems Manager Inventory, Amazon Inspector and Microsoft Defender for Cloud are for, and each one only sees the machines it’s enabled on. That coverage gap is the one that hurts most, and I’ll come back to it.
GitLab patched GitLab.com itself. Self-managed instances are on you, and short of upgrading there’s no workaround. The one that worries me is rarely the GitLab the platform team runs. It’s the one some team stood up in 2019, or the one that came along with an acquisition, still answering on 443.
Search by name and tag first, then look at exposure:
In Azure, az vm list -d --query "[?contains(name, 'gitlab')].{name:name, rg:resourceGroup, ips:publicIps}" -o table gets you the same first pass.
Be careful with what this tells you. A name filter only finds servers someone named honestly, and an instance with no public IP can still be reachable through a public load balancer. Both make this hard to answer from the console in the middle of an incident. It’s much easier if you already have an inventory that holds the relationships.
Once you’ve found the server, somebody has to approve the downtime, and ideally that person knows how it was installed. Tags are the first place to look. If there aren’t any, CloudTrail can tell you who created the resource:
Event history only goes back 90 days, and the same is true of the Azure Activity Log. For a server from 2019 you need your trail in S3 and an Athena query, which Who Created This AWS Resource? walks through. Even then the creator may have left. In one case we looked at , 89 idle Azure VMs came from an acquisition and nobody on the current team could say what they were for. Resources like that are exactly where an unpatched GitLab ends up living.
LiteLLM shows why a package finding is only the start. According to Microsoft’s analysis , the malicious release went after AWS, Azure and Google Cloud credential caches, Kubernetes service-account files, Docker configuration and mounted secrets. It also tried to pull credentials from the AWS and GCP metadata services, and on proxy hosts it read provider keys out of LiteLLM’s own database.
The bad package is what the scanner reports. What you actually have to respond to is the identity the host ran as. For every environment that installed 1.107.0, find the role it had and what that role is allowed to do:
On ECS the identity is the task role in the task definition. On EKS it’s the role mapped to the pod’s service account. Microsoft’s guidance is to investigate from a clean machine, rebuild from verified artifacts, rotate every reachable credential, and pin container images by digest instead of floating tags like latest . I’d underline the clean-machine part: their analysis says the payload runs when Python starts, so running pip inside a suspect environment to check for the package can trigger it.
OpenCode told users to revoke and reissue the exposed keys. Revoking takes a click. Working out what breaks when you do is the real job, because AI provider keys end up in Secrets Manager or Key Vault, in Lambda and App Service settings, in CI variables and in developers’ .env files. On AWS, Secrets Manager at least records when each secret was last read and last rotated, and CloudTrail’s GetSecretValue events show which roles read it:
eMudhra raises the same problem for certificates. With a private key that small, anyone could compute it and sign certificates that browsers would have trusted until the intermediates were blocked. Two checks are worth running. First, search the certificates you’ve imported for eMudhra or emSign issuers. ACM is regional, and certificates used by CloudFront live in us-east-1, so run this in every region you use, us-east-1 included:
In Azure, Resource Graph covers App Service certificates across subscriptions:
Second, software with its own trust store keeps trusting a CA until that store is updated. Old AMIs, base images and runtimes that bundle their own CA list are where a blocked chain keeps working long after browsers have dropped it.
Amazon Inspector and Defender for Cloud are good at telling you whether a package version on a given machine is vulnerable. The AWS and Azure consoles are good at telling you what’s in one account in one region. Neither is what you need the morning an advisory lands.
The first problem is coverage. A scanner sees the accounts, subscriptions and machines it’s been enabled on, and the GitLab server from the acquisition is usually sitting in the account nobody onboarded. The second is ownership. Findings land in a shared queue where nobody has the authority to restart someone else’s server, so they sit there. A finding with no owner attached is just one more alert. The third is context. The scanner says the package is bad. It doesn’t say the host’s role can read every S3 bucket in the account, or that three other teams’ services call it. With LiteLLM, that context was most of the incident.
What fills those gaps is an inventory that stays current and records what exists, who owns it and how it connects to everything else. That’s the thing we’re building Cloud Sleuth to be.
Cloud Sleuth maps your AWS and Azure resources, assigns an owner to each one whether it’s tagged or not, and keeps both up to date. Here’s the GitLab question asked the way Cloud Sleuth is designed to answer it.
Illustrative example - commands and output not final:
That one result covers exposure, ownership and reach: the server, the path from the internet to it, the team to page along with the evidence for that answer, and what the server’s role can touch. Without it you’d be in four consoles and a CloudTrail search, and you’d be doing it again for every account, including the one from the acquisition.
Inventory search puts AWS and Azure resources in one schema you can query with SQL or plain English, so the region-by-region Lambda loop above becomes a single query across both clouds with owners already attached:
Illustrative example - schema not final:
The cloud map draws network paths, load balancer targets, attachments and IAM relationships from your real accounts, which is how you see what sits in front of a forgotten server and what its role can reach before you start rotating. The ownership model infers owners from CloudTrail and the Azure Activity Log, IaC state, naming and account structure, and shows a confidence score and the evidence behind it. Guardrails flag unowned, untagged and orphaned resources, and in Cloud Sleuth Cloud findings can be routed to the owning team in Slack or Jira, with custom policies like “no function on a deprecated runtime” running continuously. There’s also a read-only MCP server , so you can ask an agent like Claude or Cursor “which of our functions run Node.js 20, and who owns them?” during an incident.
Given that this week included a vendor console leaking keys customers had stored in it and a popular package shipping a credential stealer, the trust model matters. The Cloud Sleuth CLI is read-only by default, installs nothing on your servers, and runs on your machine or in your VPC. If you want to try it, join the early-access list .
Pick one of this week’s advisories and time how long it takes your team to do the following. List every place Node.js and PHP run, including Lambda runtimes, App Service stacks, container images and VMs. Find every self-managed GitLab, and any other self-hosted developer tool, and check whether the internet can reach it. Put an owner’s name next to each one. For any environment that installed LiteLLM 1.107.0, list the roles it ran as and rotate everything those roles could reach. Write down where your AI provider keys are stored and which workloads use them. Search your certificates for eMudhra or emSign issuers.
If that took more than an hour, expect the next advisory to take about as long.
One more landed that week. On October 22, TianoCore disclosed CVE-2026-97631 , a pre-boot code execution bug in the PXE driver most UEFI firmware is built from. It asks the same questions about the hardware you run yourself.
Only code that decompresses Brotli data from untrusted sources with node:zlib is exposed. Lambda rolls out runtime updates to supported managed runtimes automatically by default, and the INIT_START line in a function’s logs shows the runtime version it’s running. Functions on the deprecated nodejs20.x runtime no longer get security patches, and container-image functions carry whatever Node.js version is in the image, so upgrade or rebuild those.
GitLab patches GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated itself, and coverage of the release says both were already running fixed versions. Self-managed GitLab Community and Enterprise Edition instances need to upgrade to a patched release. There’s no workaround.
Treat it as compromised. Investigate from a clean machine, rebuild from a verified version, confirm that cook.pth , cook.py and sitecustomize.py are gone from the Python library path, and rotate every credential the environment could reach: cloud roles, CI/CD secrets, SSH keys and model provider keys. Microsoft’s analysis lists the indicators to search for.
It answers the questions that decide how fast you can respond: which of your AWS and Azure resources are in scope, which ones the internet can reach, who owns each one, and what each one can reach. Owners come with the evidence behind them, so the fix goes to a team that can actually make it. The CLI runs read-only on your machine, and you can join the early-access list now.

title: Lockheed Martin Invests $10M in AI for RCAF CC-130J Fleet
body: Lockheed Martin is investing $10M CAD in Canadian-developed artificial intelligence technology to help modernize maintenance, training and workforce readiness for the Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF)’s CC-130J Hercules Fleet. The investment supports the development of the Intelligent Maintenance, Asset, Personnel and Learning Environment (iMAPLE)—an AI competency management platform being developed through a joint initiative between Lockheed Martin Canada, the RCAF and Contextere. Contextere develops AI-powered workforce solutions that transform institutional knowledge into actionable intelligence for the people who maintain, sustain, and operate mission-critical assets. READ: Lockheed Martin Acquires Ultra Maritime, Expanding ASW Sonar This investment contributes to the fulfillment of Lockheed Martin’s economic impact commitments associated with the CC-130J In Service Support program, while advancing technology that will support the fleet for decades to come. Why It Matters This unique collaboration brings together Canada’s defence industry, AI sector and the RCAF to deliver benefits aligned to Canada’s defence industrial strategy: modernizing how workforce competencies are matched to tasks, enabling AI-driven sustainment decisions that help improve aircraft availability, maintenance efficiency and overall fleet readiness, and advancing potential for broader applications and export opportunities. Beyond its financial commitment, Lockheed Martin will also serve as a consultative Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning partner across all project phases, delivering validated machine-learning methodologies, quality reviews and knowledge transfer, as well as advising on designing, testing and optimizing AI components. Supporting Canada’s National Artificial Intelligence Strategy: AI for All , iMAPLE integrates human expertise, cutting-edge Canadian innovation and Lockheed Martin Canada’s deep understanding of the defence landscape to improve readiness, grow Canadian sovereign AI capability and meet Canada’s aerospace sustainment needs long into the future. Expert Pespectives “Today’s announcement demonstrates meaningful results for Canadians through Canada’s Industrial and Technological Benefits Policy. This partnership invests in a Canadian-developed artificial intelligence solution that supports the Royal Canadian Air Force’s CC-130J Hercules fleet. It is strengthening Canada’s defence capabilities, creating opportunities for Canadian workers, and helping grow a sovereign AI ecosystem with export potential. Canada’s government will continue to support Canadian innovation by building our domestic defence capabilities,” said the Honourable Stephen Fuhr, Secretary of State for Defence Procurement. “Lockheed Martin’s investment in iMAPLE reflects a shared belief that the future of sustainment depends on connecting people, knowledge, and technology,” said Gabriel Batstone, CEO & Co-Founder, Contextere. “Together, we are building on Canadian intellectual property that supports our armed forces, strengthens our industrial base, creates opportunities for skilled trades, and showcases how Canadian AI can deliver value on the global stage.” “This collaboration with the Royal Canadian Air Force and Contextere offers something truly special,” said Kristen Leroux, Vice President & Regional Executive for Canada and Latin America, Lockheed Martin. “We’re proud to be a part of the development of iMAPLE and to work alongside Contextere in support of our air force and the CC-130J fleet, demonstrating how Canadian innovation can build a sovereign defence and dual-use ecosystem right here at home.” Additional Context For decades CC-130 and CC-130J Hercules aircraft have been the workhorse for the Royal Canadian Air Force. Through Canada’s Industrial and Technological Benefits Policy, over $4.7 billion CAD in economic benefits has been delivered to Canada by Lockheed Martin, as a result of Canada’s purchase and associated In-Service Support of 17 CC-130J Super Hercules aircraft. Aligned with Canada’s Defence Industrial Strategy and Industrial and Technological Benefits policy, this investment delivers long-term economic benefit, building on Lockheed Martin Canada’s measurable impact in Canada. Over the past 5 years, Lockheed Martin Canada has contributed $3.6 billion CAD to Canada’s gross domestic product and supported an average of 4,561 jobs annually. Canada Sells Retired CC-130H Hercules to Coulson for Aerial Firefighting Lockheed Martin Acquires Ultra Maritime, Expanding ASW Sonar The post Lockheed Martin Invests $10M in AI for RCAF CC-130J Fleet appeared first on Canadian Defence Review .

title: GTCO posts 12% drop in nine-month profit amid soaring costs
body:
Guaranty Trust Holding Company (GTCO) reported a 12.2 per cent decline in net profit for the nine months to September, compared to the corresponding period of last year, as mounting costs strained earnings, its unaudited accounts issued on Tuesday showed.
The financial services group posted an improvement in interest income, its major source of revenue, but faced increased pressure from interest expense, which jumped 27.7 per cent year on year.
Interest expense as a percentage of interest income stood at 27.6 per cent, relative to 22.6 per cent a year ago.
Consequently, net interest income, which implies the difference between the cash generated by banks and financial institutions on interest-bearing assets and what they pay out to depositors, fell to N935.9 billion from N952.1 billion.
The banking group set aside N29 billion as provision for bad debt, marking a 58.4 per cent drop.
Net fee and commission income slightly dropped by 0.4 per cent to N182.4 billion, despite a higher gross fee and commission income amid escalating costs.
Depreciation and amortisation jumped 41 per cent to N82.5 billion, following a notable increase in depreciation of property equipment, while other operating expenses rose 6.5 per cent to N228.8 billion, eroding pre-tax profit.
Other income fell 12.9 per cent to N74.8 billion, driven by unrealised fair value loss on financial instruments and a much weaker unrealised foreign exchange revaluation gain.
Profit before tax decreased to N879.9 billion from N900.8 billion
GTCO recorded a 31.9 per cent surge in income tax spending, weakening profit after tax, which slid to N614.6 billion from N699.6 billion.
Last July, the banking group completed the secondary listing of its shares on the main market of the London Stock Exchange, replacing years of trading through global depositary receipts, a financial instrument that enables investors to hold shares in a foreign company and trade in them on the stock exchanges of their own countries.
The stock has been up by 37.9 per cent so far this year.

title: Ceasefire in Oleshky being fully observed, Lubinets says
body:
Lubinets announced this in a Telegram post, Ukrinform reports.
“The ceasefire in Oleshky is being fully observed. As of 5:30 p.m. on October 27, Ukraine and Russia are adhering to the ceasefire arrangements in designated areas related to the humanitarian mission. The ceasefire took effect today at 3:00 a.m. Kyiv time and 4:00 a.m. Moscow time,” Lubinets wrote.
The ceasefire will remain in effect until 10:59 p.m. on November 1. Neither side has reported any ceasefire violations.
“We are carrying out the humanitarian mission jointly with Yana Lantratova, Russia’s human rights commissioner, with the mediation and coordination of U.S. First Lady Melania Trump. I hope the operation will proceed according to the agreed plan and that we will be able to help the civilians in Oleshky who are waiting for assistance,” Lubinets said.
As previously reported, the ceasefire in the Oleshky area is scheduled to remain in effect from October 27 until 10:59 p.m. on Sunday, November 1.

title: Northern youths demands Justice over killing of Sheikh Masusuka
body: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The Northern Youth Council of Nigeria (NYCN) has called on the Federal Government and the Katsina State Government to ensure a thorough investigation into the killing of Islamic scholar, Sheikh Yahaya Ibrahim Masusuka, and bring those responsible to justice. The council, in a statement issued on Monday by its president, Comrade Isah Abubakar, condemned the killing of the cleric, describing it as a grave attack on Islamic scholarship and the moral fabric of Northern Nigeria. According to reports, Sheikh Masusuka was shot dead at about 7:30 p.m. on Monday in front of his residence in Dutsin-Ma Local Government Area of Katsina State by gunmen riding on a motorcycle. His friend, identified as Adamu Abubakar, was also killed in the attack. Both men were reportedly taken to a hospital but were pronounced dead on arrival. The Katsina State Police Command said an investigation had commenced, while efforts were being made to apprehend the assailants. The identities of the attackers and the motive for the killings had yet to be established in the reports available. Reacting to the incident, the NYCN described the late cleric as a revered scholar and mentor whose teachings of the Holy Qur’an had inspired many people, particularly youths in the North. The council said the killing went beyond the loss of an individual, arguing that it represented an attack on religious scholarship, truth and the values that sustain society. It also expressed concern over what it described as the persistent problem of impunity surrounding high-profile killings in the country, urging the authorities to demonstrate their commitment to protecting citizens and ensuring accountability. The council called for a transparent and comprehensive investigation into the circumstances surrounding the assassination, including any possible security lapses and the existence of a wider conspiracy, if established by evidence. It further urged the authorities to look beyond the immediate perpetrators and investigate any individuals who may have financed, planned or facilitated the crime. According to the statement, justice would not be served by arresting only those who directly carried out the attack if further investigations established the involvement of other persons. “The era of empty promises, superficial condolence messages and decorative investigative committees is over,” the council said, insisting that the authorities must demonstrate the political will to ensure that those responsible are brought to justice. The NYCN said it would continue to monitor the investigation and called on the governments at both federal and state levels to ensure that the case was not abandoned. The council also prayed for the repose of the soul of the deceased cleric and asked Almighty Allah to comfort his family, associates and followers. It urged the security agencies to act swiftly and professionally to establish the circumstances surrounding the killing and prevent similar attacks on religious leaders and other citizens. The post Northern youths demands Justice over killing of Sheikh Masusuka appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Israel supplying offshore patrol vessel with advanced naval systems to Cyprus
body:
NICOSIA, Cyprus. Israel and Cyprus signed an agreement for a new offshore patrol vessel (OPV) built by Israel Shipyards and equipped with Rafael naval systems, while systems aboard Cyprus’s existing Israel Shipyards-built OPV IOANNIDES will also be upgraded, the Israel Ministry of Defense announced in a statement.
The agreement was led by the Israel Ministry of Defense’s International Defense Cooperation Directorate and the Cyprus Ministry of Defence’s Armaments & Defence Capabilities Development Directorate. The release does not identify the specific Rafael systems that will be installed on the new vessel or upgraded aboard IOANNIDES.
The new OPV and upgraded vessel are intended to support patrol, surveillance, and search-and-rescue missions for the Cyprus Naval Command. The agreement was signed by Israel Ministry of Defense Director General Maj. Gen. (Res.) Amir Baram and Cyprus Ministry of Defence Acting Permanent Secretary Stelios Kountouris.

title: Ceasefire in Oleshky being fully observed – Lubinets
body:
As of 17:30 on October 27, Ukraine and Russia are complying with the agreements on a ceasefire in designated areas related to the humanitarian mission. It began today at 03:00 Kyiv time and 04:00 Moscow time, according to Verkhovna Rada's Commissioner for Human Rights Dmytro Lubinets.
"The ceasefire will last until 22:59 on November 1. No violations of the ceasefire have been recorded by either side. (…) I hope that everything will continue according to the agreed-upon plan and that we will be able to help the civilians in Oleshky who are so eagerly awaiting assistance," Lubinets said on his Telegram channel.
He added that the humanitarian mission is being carried out jointly with Russia's Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova through the mediation and coordination of U.S. First Lady Melania Trump.
Oleshky is located on the left bank of the Dnipro River in Kherson region, across from Kherson. The city has been under temporary Russian occupation since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.
After Kakhovka Hydroelectric Power Plant was blown up in June 2023, Oleshky was among the settlements that suffered widespread flooding. Due to the fighting and the occupation, access to the town is difficult, and the civilian population suffers from a lack of humanitarian aid and the danger of shelling.
On October 23, 2026, U.S. First Lady Melania Trump said that an agreement had been reached between Ukraine and Russia on a ceasefire in Oleshky area to allow for a humanitarian operation. According to Ukrainian Ombudsman Lubinets, the agreement provides for the delivery of humanitarian aid, technical demining, and the free movement of civilians.
Lubinets said that a ceasefire in Kherson region was declared at 03:00 on October 27.
The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine also reported that a ceasefire was implemented in Oleshky on October 27 to facilitate a humanitarian operation.

title: Pope to meet with clergy abuse survivors during Latin America visit: Vatican
body:
Pope Leo XIV will meet with survivors of clergy sexual abuse during his upcoming trip to Latin America, which will take the American pope to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, the Vatican said Tuesday.
The Vatican statement didn’t say when the encounters would take place or where, but said “several meetings are planned,” suggesting more than one encounter. The Nov. 6-17 trip is going ahead as planned despite Leo’s Oct. 13 lung cancer surgery which had put the trip in question.
Continuing the practice of his two recent predecessors, Leo met with abuse survivors in June in Spain and most recently in France. Ahead of the French trip, the Vatican confirmed the meeting ahead of time rather than after it took place, as had been the previous practice.
“These meetings reflect the pope’s desire to express his solidarity with those who have suffered and continue to suffer as a result of this violence, to work with them to build paths to healing that are accessible to anyone in need, and to ensure that the church is a safe and spiritually healthy place that lives out and communicates the Gospel,” according to a Vatican statement Tuesday.
Leo spent two decades as a missionary priest in Peru, and he saw first-hand the effects of abuse on victims. He was the designated bishop in the Peruvian bishops conference to hear from victims of an influential but abusive movement, the Sodalitium Christianae Vitae.
The former Cardinal Robert Prevost then was instrumental in Pope Francis’ decision in 2025 to suppress the movement.
Francis’ native Argentina, for its part, has had a wretched reckoning with abuse and victims there have been demanding action from the Vatican, including to address cases in which Francis was personally involved.

title: Tinubu: South-east Must Move From Promises to Realities
body: Gideon Arinze in Enugu President Bola Tinubu has reaffirmed his commitment to industrialising the South-east, declaring that the region must move beyond promises to tangible economic development. Tinubu spoke on Tuesday in Enugu at the launch of the South-east Gas Distribution Pipeline Infrastructure Project, an initiative of the South East Development Commission (SEDC), through the Southeast Investment Company (SEIC). The project, launched in partnership with Gas Sync and NNPC Gas Marketing Limited (NNPC NGML), proposes a 400-kilometre pipeline network connecting the ANOH Gas Processing Plant in Imo State to major industrial and commercial centres across the five South-east states. The pipeline is expected to improve energy access, attract investments and stimulate regional economic growth. Represented by the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, the president said the project responded to the need for reliable energy infrastructure to support businesses and manufacturing in the region. He called on investors, industrialists and manufacturers to explore the South-east’s economic opportunities, noting that energy security remained a key commitment of his administration under the Renewed Hope Agenda. “Energy infrastructure will reduce costs, create jobs and expand opportunities. Nigeria has substantial gas resources, and the South-east has its fair share, but we must use them to create jobs and prosperity for our people,” he said. Tinubu said manufacturers should not have to spend more on generating electricity than expanding their businesses, stressing the need for infrastructure that supports enterprise and industrial production. “The prosperity of the region is inseparable from the prosperity of the entire country. We cannot achieve our full economic potential when any region operates below its economic potential,” he said. In his address, Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah, said inadequate energy supply and poor connectivity had remained major challenges to industrial development in the South-east. According to him, unreliable energy increases production costs, limits business expansion and weakens the competitiveness of enterprises across the region. Mbah said the proposed pipeline would provide opportunities for young people to build businesses and secure employment within the region rather than travel elsewhere in search of jobs. “Enugu State alone has more than 20 tertiary institutions graduating young people annually,” he said. Reliable energy would help them turn their ideas into viable enterprises.” “Enugu alone has four gas fields that remain unexploited. This shows the massive opportunities we have, and we also have reserves in other states. We cannot wait to see the project become a reality,” Mbah said. The governor commended Tinubu for supporting the establishment of the SEDC, describing the commission as an important step towards addressing the region’s industrial development needs. Earlier, the Managing Director of the SEDC, Mark Okoye, said the commission was committed to promoting inclusive prosperity and creating economic development opportunities across the region. Okoye also proposed the establishment of a South-east Oil and Gas Week to bring stakeholders together to discuss investment opportunities and challenges in the sector. The Deputy Governors of Ebonyi, Anambra and Imo States, Princess Patricia Onyemaechi, Dr Gilbert Ibezim and Chinyere Ihuoma, respectively, commended the SEDC for initiating the project. They pledged their states’ cooperation to ensure its successful implementation.

title: China Gold restarts CSH mine after five-month shutdown
body: China Gold International Resources (TSX: CGG) (HKEX: 2099) has resumed open-pit mining operations at its Chang Shan Hao (CSH) gold mine in Inner Mongolia after a nearly five-month shutdown caused by slope instability, keeping its 2026 production guidance unchanged. Operations resumed in early October after the company completed remediation work and regulatory filings, according to a company statement . China Gold expects CSH to produce between 70,732 and 83,592 oz. of gold this year. The restart follows a localized slope instability incident that forced the company to halt open pit operations on May 22, 2026. No casualties or equipment losses were reported. Slope remediation China Gold International commissioned geotechnical assessments after the incident to develop remediation plans, which were completed by the end of September. They included road system restoration, removal of loose material and rocks, reinforcing the landslide body, establishing drainage systems and ongoing slope monitoring. The mine met safety standards needed to restart normal operations after the remediation was completed and the company finished the filing process with the emergency management authorities. The processing plant kept operating using existing low-grade ore stockpiles, which will assist the company in achieving its production guideline for 2026, estimated to be between 70,732 ounces and 83,592 ounces of gold. Now that mining operations are back to normal, the plan is to blend fresh mined ore with stockpiled ore to maintain stable delivery volumes and processing grades while implementing safety risk control measures to support efficient production scheduling for the rest of 2026. The CSH mine in Inner Mongolia produced 96,816 ounces of gold in 2025. China Gold International also has operations at the Jiama copper-gold polymetallic mine in Tibet that produced 70,883 tonnes of copper and 61,218 ounces of gold in 2025. Shares in China Gold International were up 2.4% to C$33.03 apiece by mid-day Tuesday in Toronto, valuing the company at C$13 billion ($9.2 billion).

title: International Stammering Awareness Day: ‘Shades of stammering – What’s yours?’
body: Every year on the 22nd of October, the world comes together to observe International Stammering Awareness Day, a day dedicated to increasing public understanding of stammering, celebrating the voices of people who stammer and calling on communities to do better. This year’s theme “Shades of Stammering — What’s Yours?” reminds us that stammering looks and feels different for every person who lives with it. Some repeat sounds. Some get stuck mid-sentence. Some hide it so well you would never know, but at a great personal cost. Every shade of stammering deserves to be seen, heard, and respected. What is Stammering? Stammering is a speech condition that disrupts the flow of speech through repetitions, prolongations or blocks. It is not caused by nervousness, low intelligence, poor upbringing or spiritual problems. It is a neurological condition. Approximately 1 in 100 adults stammer, meaning hundreds of thousands of Ghanaians stammer. It cannot be cured, but with support from a speech and language therapist, people who stammer can manage it and communicate with confidence. The Hidden Cost: Career Entrapment What many people do not see is the daily emotional burden of stammering. Many people who stammer experience anxiety, shame and low self-esteem. Some avoid speaking altogether, in classrooms, job interviews, social gatherings, not because they have nothing to say, but because they fear how they will be received. This fear has a name: career entrapment . Many gifted Ghanaians quietly abandon dreams of becoming lawyers, teachers, doctors, politicians or broadcasters, not because they lack ability, but because stammering makes those spaces feel closed to them. This is a silent injustice that robs individuals of their potential and robs our society of their contributions. To Comedians Comedy is a gift. But using stammering as a punchline is not comedy. It is cruelty with a microphone. Somewhere in your audience is a child who stammers, watching the crowd laugh at the way they speak. We ask Ghana’s comedians to choose differently. There is no shortage of material in our rich culture. Stammering does not need to be one of them. To Teachers and Lecturers The classroom can be a place of growth or daily dread for a student who stammers and you decide which. Do not laugh at, mimic or single out a student for how they speak. Do not tell them to slow down or start again. Simply give them time, maintain eye contact and listen to what they are saying, not how they are saying it. Your patience can change a student’s life. Our Call to Action This year, the Speech Therapists and Audiologists’ Association of Ghana (STAAG), in collaboration with the Ghana Stammering Association, is calling on all Ghanaians to help build a more inclusive society. Here is what you can do: Give people who stammer time to finish speaking Never finish their sentences for them Do not laugh, mimic, or mock stammering Speak up when you witness others doing so If your child stammers, seek help from a speech and language therapist early Every voice matters. Every shade counts. Let us build a Ghana where no one is held back by how they speak. Dr. Josephine Ohenewa Bampoe President, Speech Therapists and Audiologists’ Association of Ghana (STAAG) Lecturer, University of Ghana Contact STAAG: jobamp@hotmail.com

title: Nasarawa Guber: Ex-IG Adamu Pledges to Prioritize Security As Ethnic Group Endorses Him
body: Igbawase Ukumba in Lafia A former Inspector General of Police (IGP) and gubernatorial candidate of the social Democratic party (SDP) in Nasarawa State, Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, has said his aspiration to govern Nasarawa State in 2027 is driven by the desire to uplift the common man. Adamu stated this Tuesday in Doma, while responding to his endorsement as the preferred governorship candidate by the Alago ethnic nationality for the 2027 election. The endorsement was announced during a rally organised by the Alago Support Group for IGP Adamu. The former police boss first thanked God for the success recorded so far in his political journey, saying no success would have been possible without divine intervention. He expressed appreciation to the Alago Support Group for the support and for agreeing to include them in his campaign, noting that the people have shown they will vote for him and, God willing, he will win the election. “Because yesterday, the people gathered and the progressives as a whole came out and endorsed our candidate for governor. Also, the major tribe that is prominent here endorsed our candidate. We are grateful for the strong assurance they gave us that we will not face any hardship on election day,” he said. Adamu said his decision to contest is for the common people who are suffering under the present situation, where mothers, children and youths are neglected while government focuses on things that do not concern their lives. “Our coming out for this election is for the common people. We came out for the common man, to see that the common man does not suffer the way they are suffering now,” he stated. He promised to prioritize the lives of the people if elected, with focus on quality education, quality healthcare and security. “We will put people’s lives first, to see that education with quality is given to our people, health with quality our people have obtained, and the issue of security, we will see that everyone will find peace, so that people can return to their homes to sleep without any fear,” Adamu said. He also raised the alarm over alleged vote-buying and collection of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) from women to stop them from voting. “Those who don’t have people following them are collecting cards in the hands of women; they are buying so as to stop them from coming out to vote. Therefore, anyone who collected a card, let them go and collect their card. Everyone should not agree to sell their card, and everyone should come out on election day with their card,” he urged. Earlier in his address, the leader of the conveners, Danjuma Joseph, said the historic movement was conceived when they resolved that Alago could not remain on the sidelines while the future of Nasarawa State is being shaped. Joseph said after thorough political and moral interrogation, they found in him a man of proven integrity, impeccable track record and uncommon patriotism who served Nigeria meritoriously to the pinnacle of his career. He noted that Adamu is not a stranger to Alago land, as he shares deep historical and blood affinity with the people, having schooled with many prominent sons and daughters of Alago in Obi, and having maternal ties with Alago. “We have resolved that we will no longer be onlookers or fence-sitters while the political destiny of our dear state is being decided. The time to participate, to take a stand and to take our destiny in our own hands is now,” Joseph declared. He said there should be no acrimony over who Alago should support, citing Section 40 of the 1999 Constitution which guarantees freedom of association, and stressed that their constitutional and political choice remains IGP Adamu. He added that the current political era is that of ‘Rainbow Coalition’, where one can remain in his party and still support any candidate of his choice, hence their action is not exceptional but a political alliance for the good of Alago and Nasarawa State. “Your Excellency, this programme today is organised on the sacred sand of Alago ancestral land, in the name of Alago and in the interest of Alago. It is a political covenant, a bond of trust between you and Alago nation. By the grace of God, when you ascend as governor, do not forget Alago people,” he told Adamu. Joseph said the group will traverse all Alago electoral wards in Nasarawa South and extend mobilisation to Nasarawa North and West Senatorial Districts to deliver Adamu.

title: PenCom urges SMEs to remit workers’ pensions, plan for retirement
body:
The National Pension Commission (PenCom) has urged small business owners to remit workers’ pension contributions as required by law and make retirement planning a priority rather than depend solely on their businesses for income in old age.
Samuel Uwandu, PenCom’s commissioner for inspectorate, gave the advice on Tuesday at an engagement with small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and informal sector operators in Lagos, on the second day of the 2026 National Pension Week.
The 2026 National Pension Week is scheduled to run from 26 to 30 October planning and encouraging wider participation in Nigeria’s pension system.
At the event, Mr Uwandu said timely remittance of pension contributions was both a legal obligation and a responsibility employers owed workers whose efforts contributed to the success of their businesses.
“Pension contributions deducted from employees’ salaries must be treated with the seriousness they deserve and remitted in accordance with the laws of the Federal Government of Nigeria,” he said.
He warned that delayed or unremitted contributions could undermine workers’ retirement security and weaken public confidence in the pension system.
“Compliance with pension obligations is not merely a regulatory requirement; it is an expectation and responsibility of business leadership, and respect for the people who help make the business succeed,” he said.
The commissioner said employees’ knowledge, skills and commitment were essential to business growth, adding that employers should recognise their contributions by meeting their statutory obligations, paying salaries when due and providing safe working conditions.
“Employees are not simply a cost of doing business. They are partners in building the enterprise,” he said.
Mr Uwandu also urged entrepreneurs to prepare financially for retirement instead of assuming their businesses would continue generating income indefinitely.
He said many business owners devoted their most productive years to building their enterprises, reinvesting earnings and supporting their families but paid little attention to their own retirement.
According to him, business owners should consider how they would sustain themselves when age, illness, economic difficulties or other circumstances made it difficult to continue working.
“As your business grows, you should also begin to prepare for your financial future and retirement,” he said.
He advised entrepreneurs to cultivate a savings culture, set aside retirement funds separately from their business working capital and explore appropriate long-term savings arrangements.
Mr Uwandu said the Personal Pension Plan (PPP) under Nigeria’s contributory pension framework provides a retirement savings option for eligible self-employed Nigerians and people working in the informal sector.
He urged business owners to seek guidance from licensed pension fund administrators and PenCom on the arrangements applicable to them.
“The central message here is simple: retirement planning should not begin only when a person is approaching retirement age.
“It should be gained when there is still time to save money, contribute, benefit from long-term accumulation, and build financial resilience,” he said.
He added that entrepreneurs should aim to retire with dignity rather than remain entirely dependent on their businesses or financial support from their families.
Beyond pension compliance, Mr Uwandu urged small business owners to strengthen their financial management practices to improve the sustainability of their enterprises.
He advised them to maintain proper financial records, separate personal finances from business accounts, manage income and expenditure responsibly, and reinvest a reasonable portion of their profits into their businesses.
He said reinvestment could help business owners acquire better equipment, improve technology, expand inventory, train employees and reach new markets through advertising.
“Where profits are consumed entirely by immediate personal needs, the business may struggle to expand or withstand unexpected challenges,” he said.
However, he stressed the need to balance reinvestment with personal financial needs, noting that sustainable businesses should support both growth and the long-term security of their owners.
Mr Uwandu also called on the government to provide an enabling environment for businesses, noting that SMEs contribute to employment, skills development, local production and economic activities across communities.
He encouraged participants to use the engagement to share experiences, identify practical solutions and commit to actions that would improve the prospects of Nigerian businesses and the welfare of their employees.

title: Jailed Russian political scientist Alexander Kynev faces new ‘foreign agent’ allegation as broken leg leaves him unable to use cell toilet
body: Political scientist Alexander Kynev, who was arrested for allegedly attempting to sell drugs, has been cited for violating “foreign agent” regulations. It is unclear what prompted the citation, which was filed with Moscow’s Perovsky District Court on October 27. No hearing has been scheduled. Kynev has been in pretrial detention since September 25. He denies the drug allegations. The Slovo Zashchite project reported that Kynev was beaten so severely during his arrest that his leg was broken. Political scientist Ekaterina Schulmann said the beating was an attempt to force Kynev to confess to treason. On October 26, reports emerged that Kynev had stopped eating in pretrial detention because his broken leg prevented him from using the toilet in his cell. Kynev himself said the injury left him unable to move around properly. Alexander Kynev is one of the most respected experts on Russian regional politics and elections. Russian authorities designated him a “foreign agent” in February 2026. More on Russian politics Russian elections expert Alexander Kynev stayed in the country to keep studying its politics. After criticizing the latest vote, he was arrested on drug charges. Russia’s FSB security service publishes dramatic videos of political arrests. A human rights group says roughly a quarter of the arrest scenes it examined were staged. title: One week out, prediction markets see Democrats as favored to sweep Congress
body:
The 2026 U.S. midterm election will be held a week from Tuesday, with the Republican Party looking to defend majorities in both the House and Senate , though Democrats are seen as two-to-one favorites to flip both chambers blue on prediction markets .
Speculators on platform Kalshi place a 63% chance that Democrats win control of both the House and Senate. Those odds have stayed relatively stable since the beginning of October. Meanwhile, there's just under a 10% chance that Republicans sweep both chambers, and a 29% chance Democrats win the House while the GOP maintains its majority in the Senate.
Contracts on the market are resolved using official data from the U.S. Congress.
Odds and gambling platforms do not use methodologies used by traditional political polling, and therefore are not substitutes for political polls.
On Sunday, prediction markets gave high odds to right-wing candidate Flavio Bolsonaro to win in the Brazil presidential election before polls closed, though the incumbent left-wing president Lula da Silva was re-elected . Some markets in Democratic primaries this election cycle also drew criticism for giving sky-high odds to some candidates winning who ultimately only narrowly won or lost.
Platforms, however, say that odds traders place often end up happening that exact percentage of the time . That means, essentially, that a candidate with a 20% chance to win on an event contract exchange pulls out an "upset" win 20% of the time.
Before early September, Democrats had less than a 50% chance to sweep both chambers of Congress, though their odds have risen from around 30% earlier in the year before the start of the U.S.-Iran war and higher gas prices that have hit consumers .
On Polymarket, Democrats have a 65% chance to sweep both houses.
Polls broadly show Democrats favored in the national popular vote for the House, and competitive in a series of red-state Senate races that will decide control of the upper chamber. Though House Speaker Mike Johnson , R-La., has cast doubt on those findings.
"We've been from coast to coast," he said in an appearance on Fox News Monday , "and I'm telling you, the polling is inaccurate."

title: GES sets November 16 deadline for payment of outstanding 2025 promotion arrears
body: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has announced that outstanding promotion arrears for staff promoted in 2025 will be paid on November 16, 2026. In a statement on Tuesday, October 27, the GES said it was working with the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department to ensure that all affected personnel receive their outstanding payments by the stated date. The Service explained that the Controller and Accountant-General’s payment system had been closed to allow for the processing of October salaries at a time when the necessary inputs for the promotion arrears were expected to be made. According to the GES, the payment system is scheduled to reopen on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, to enable the required inputs to be processed and facilitate payment to affected staff by November 16. The Service also assured staff that discrepancies identified in payments made on October 16, 2026, would be rectified accordingly. Management expressed regret over the delay and the inconvenience caused to affected staff. Regional Directors have been requested to communicate the information to all staff awaiting their promotion arrears. This statement comes barely few hours after the Minister of Education told JoyNews that he had called teacher unions to a meeting to notify them about the challenge in paying some 28,000 teachers their promotion arrears, although some 52,000 had received theirs. title: AbdulRazaq Constitutes New Governing Councils of Eight Tertiary Institutions in Kwara
body: Hammed Shittu in Ilorin Kwara State Governor, Alhaji AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, has approved the constitution of new governing councils for eight state-owned tertiary institutions and nine government agencies in the state. A statement issued in Ilorin on Tuesday signed by the Deputy Chief Press Secretary to Governor AbdulRazaq, Alhaji Mashood Abdulrafiu Agboola, stated that: “The appointment, which took effect from October 16, 2026, is aimed at strengthening professionalism and service delivery.” The statement said that the affected institutions are Kwara State Scholarship Board; International Vocational, Technical and Entrepreneurship College (IVTEC), Ajase-Ipo; Kwara State Polytechnic, Ilorin; International Aviation College, Ilorin; College of Nursing Sciences, Ilorin; College of Education, Oro; College of Education, Ilorin; College of Nursing Sciences, Oke-Ode; and the Kwara State Agency for Mass Literacy. Others are Kwara State Primary Health Care Development Board, Kwara State Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Agency (RUWASSA), Kwara State Road Traffic Management Authority (KWARTMA), Kwara State Rural Electrification Board, Kwara State Social Investment Programme (KWASSIP), Kwara State Housing Corporation, Kwara State Environmental Protection Agency (KWEPA), and Kwara State Signage and Advertisement Agency (KWASAA). Under the new arrangement, according to the statement, former presidential candidate, Gani Galadima, will chair the seven-member IVTEC council, while Dr Ahmed Ameen Funsho will chair the 17-member Scholarship Board. Musa Yeketi was named Chairman of the Kwara State Polytechnic council, while Nigeria’s first Professor of Aviation Law, Prof. Adua Ismail Mustapha, will chair the council of the International Aviation College, Ilorin. Both councils have six members each. Amudipe Christiana Titilayo will chair the College of Nursing Sciences, Ilorin; Gezinde Adedeji Amosa will head College of Education, Oro; and Muhammadu Suno Gofe will chair College of Education, Ilorin. Dr. Afusat Ameen will lead the College of Nursing Sciences, Oke-Ode, while Hajia Riskat Lawal was appointed to chair the Agency for Mass Literacy. Similarly, Ayinmode Sunday Samuel was named Chairman of the Primary Healthcare Board; Alhaji Muhammed Sakwa for RUWASSA; Hon. Olasunkanmi Ere-oye for KWARTMA, and Sikirullah Abdulkareem Oladimeji for the Rural Electrification Board. Hon. Memud Azeez Alonge will chair KWASSIP, Hon. Abdulazeez Oluwanilo will head the Housing Corporation, Femi Aina will lead KWEPA, while Dr. Laaro Oba Abdulkadir was appointed Chairman of KWASAA. title: CAN Demands Probe Of Video Showing Boys Chanting Threats Against Christians
body: The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) has called on security agencies to investigate a viral video showing a young man leading a group of boys in chants advocating attacks on Christians in Enugu and Jos during Sunday worship. The association described the chants as “chilling and utterly unacceptable,” demanding that those behind the threats be identified and prosecuted if found culpable. In a statement signed by its President, Archbishop Daniel Okoh, on behalf of the national leadership, CAN said Nigerians must be able to practise their faith without fear of attacks or intimidation. The association warned against dismissing the chants as youthful exuberance, insisting that the threats required urgent investigation and decisive action. It also expressed concern over the involvement of children and young people in the video, warning that exposing them to messages promoting religious hatred and violence could have serious consequences. CAN urged the Department of State Services (DSS), the Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies to establish when and where the video was recorded, identify those involved and determine who organised or facilitated the activity. It further called for an investigation into whether any individuals or groups financed or encouraged the threats, insisting that anyone found responsible must face the law. The association also urged security agencies to assess potential threats arising from the video and take appropriate measures to protect Christian communities and places of worship in Enugu, Jos and other parts of the country. While acknowledging the reported disavowal of the video by the leadership of Jama’atu Izalatil Bid’ah Wa Iqamatis Sunnah (JIBWIS), CAN maintained that the position of the organisation should not replace an independent investigation. It also called on religious leaders across the country to condemn messages promoting hostility against people of other faiths and teach young people to respect human life and the rights of fellow citizens. “Religious leaders across Nigeria also have a responsibility to reject, unequivocally, any teaching, slogan or activity that promotes hatred or violence against people of another faith,” the association said. CAN warned that Nigeria could not afford to treat threats of religious violence lightly, given the country’s history of bloodshed and religious tensions. It said failure to investigate the incident could create the impression that threats against citizens on religious grounds would go unpunished. The association, however, urged Christians to remain calm, vigilant and law-abiding while the authorities investigate the video, cautioning against retaliation that could worsen religious and social tensions. “CAN stands for justice, religious freedom and peaceful coexistence,” Okoh said, stressing that every Nigerian was entitled to equal protection under the law, regardless of religious affiliation. The association called on the government to investigate the incident thoroughly and ensure that anyone found responsible was held accountable, adding that the safety of Nigerians and their freedom to worship must remain non-negotiable. The post CAN Demands Probe Of Video Showing Boys Chanting Threats Against Christians appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Warri Wolves appeal NPFL sanctions over referee assault
body:
Warri Wolves have announced plans to appeal the sanctions imposed on them by the Nigeria Premier Football League (NPFL) following the assault of a match official after their fixture against Kano Pillars.
The club said it would seek leniency, citing efforts to identify the suspect, video evidence showing its attempts to caution the individual, and the subsequent arrest.
In a statement to supporters, Warri Wolves acknowledged the seriousness of the incident and said it respected the league’s disciplinary process, while remaining hopeful that its appeal would receive favourable consideration.
“Following the league’s decision, an appeal will be filed, appealing for leniency in view of the efforts made by the club to apprehend the suspect, the available video evidence showing the club’s caution to the individual, and the subsequent arrest of the suspect,” the club said.
The club urged supporters to remain calm and united while awaiting the outcome of the appeal.
The NPFL sanctioned Warri Wolves after finding the club guilty of breaching the 2026/27 NPFL Framework and Rules for inadequate security and unauthorised access to restricted areas.
The incident occurred after the club’s fixture against Kano Pillars on Sunday, when a supporter allegedly assaulted the appointed match officials. The second assistant referee reportedly sustained a nose injury and was left bleeding.
The league imposed a total fine of ₦4.25 million on Warri Wolves, comprising ₦2 million for failing to provide adequate security, ₦2 million for assaulting a match official, and ₦250,000 in compensation to the affected assistant referee for medical treatment.
The sanctions also include a deduction of three points and three goals from the club’s accrued tally. In addition, Warri Wolves were ordered to play their next three home matches behind closed doors.
The league further directed the club to identify and produce the alleged assailant, and to provide evidence of his prosecution, within seven days. The NPFL also gave the club 48 hours from the date of notification of the sanctions to lodge an appeal.
Warri Wolves said the points deduction would have significant implications for their league campaign if it remains in force.
“If the points deduction stands, Warri Wolves will drop from 12 points to nine points and fall from 14th to 17th position on the league table,” the club said.
Such a drop would increase the pressure on the Seasiders as they seek to improve their position in the 2026/27 season.
While expressing regret over the difficult situation, Warri Wolves maintained that the club’s identity and reputation must remain above the actions of any individual.
“This is undoubtedly a difficult moment for the club, but we urge our supporters to remain calm, united and steadfast in their support. Warri Wolves is bigger than any individual, administration, coach or player. It is a legacy we must all protect,” the statement said.
The club also expressed hope that the league would consider its appeal fairly, citing the steps taken to apprehend the suspect after the incident.
The appeal, if successful, could affect the sporting consequences of the sanctions, although the outcome will depend on the league’s review.
Warri Wolves concluded by urging supporters to continue backing the team while the process runs its course.
“As we await the outcome of the appeal, let us continue to stand behind Warri Wolves — The Seasiders,” the club said.
Warri Wolves’ case comes amid a series of disciplinary actions by the NPFL during the 2026/27 season. Just last week, Doma United were sanctioned following incidents during their Matchday Nine fixture at Pantami Stadium in Gombe on 17 October.
On 1 October, Ranchers Bees were fined ₦5 million over security failures, misconduct by players and bench officials, supporters’ behaviour and the reported detention of match officials after their Matchday Six fixture against Rivers United.
Four days later, Inter Lagos received a ₦5 million fine and a three-point deduction following incidents involving match officials during their 1-1 draw with Katsina United.
Tunde Eludini is a graduate of the Obafemi Awolowo University Ile-Ife, Nigeria where he studied International Relations. He is a Senior Correspondent coordinating the sports section for PREMIUM TIMES. Twitter : @tundeyeludini

Mozilla is updating Smart Window — Firefox’s AI-powered browsing experience — with a new feature that can help you fill out online forms based on your open tabs. As an example, Mozilla says Smart Window can pull information from your online portfolio or LinkedIn page to paste your work history into a job application.
You can try out this feature by clicking into a form with at least four text fields. From there, you’ll see an option to “Fill from sources,” which will show all of the tabs Firefox will draw from. You can then select or deselect tabs that you want Firefox to use, and the browser will generate suggestions based on the information in them. This feature currently supports text fields on web forms, but Mozilla is working to add support for dropdown menus and PDFs. Mozilla notes that data from your source pages is shared with Google’s Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, the AI model that generates the text suggestions.
Along with this update, you can now ask Firefox’s Smart Window to watch a certain webpage for sales, new job listings, and other updates. You can set up a task by typing “/watch” in the Smart Window chat, describing what you’re looking for, and adding the webpages you want to watch. Firefox can then check for updates on a daily or weekly basis, but only when the browser is open.
When Firefox detects the change you’re looking for, it will send you a notification through the Tasks button on the toolbar, or on your desktop (if you have desktop notifications enabled). Firefox will pause watching for updates if it doesn’t detect a change after 60 days, before stopping them completely after 90 days.
These two features are rolling out to the Smart Window beta on desktop in the US and Canada. They’ll be available in other countries in the “coming months.”
