title: 2027: NDC Appoints Ex-Soludo’s Ally to Lead Peter Obi’s Campaign in Anambra
body: David-Chyddy Eleke in Awka The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has appointed former House of Representatives member, and erstwhile close ally of Anambra State Governor, Prof Chukwuma Soludo, Hon. Ifeanyi Ibezi, as Anambra State campaign coordinator of the party. Ibezi, who had been a strong pillar of Governor Soludo’s All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), recently dumped the party in a highly attended rally, to join the NDC. His recent appointment is seen as a move to use his popularity to drive votes for NDC and also put APGA in check, especially with Soludo’s growing resentment for NDC’s presidential candidate, Mr. Peter Obi. Meanwhile, Ibezi has quickly swung into action, calling on all to rally round Obi and give him a resounding victory, saying that merely winning Obi’s home state, Anambra, was not enough. In a press statement he released on Tuesday, Ibezi said though the task is a daunting one, but he and his team will move into the 326 political wards, markets, town union meetings to speak to the people on the need for every Anambra vote to go to Peter Obi and other NDC candidates. He said: “Anambra occupies a peculiar place in this campaign. As the home state of our presidential candidate, His Excellency, Mr. Peter Obi, the expectations are understandably high, and we must rise to meet them. Our responsibility goes beyond securing victory; we must work to ensure that Anambra delivers a resounding mandate, reflected in the strength and number of valid votes cast for Mr. Peter Obi,” Ibezi said. “We must reach those who are undecided, those who feel left behind, those who have grown weary of the system, and those who have withdrawn from the electoral process because they no longer believe their votes can make a difference. “We must listen to them, earn their confidence, and remind them that the future of our country is too important to be surrendered to apathy. The work has begun, and there is no room for complacency. “We must take this campaign to the 21 LGAs, 326 wards, 5,720 polling units, markets, churches and every household in Anambra State. Our objective is clear: to mobilise the people, secure their participation, and translate their aspirations into votes at the polls. We must also ensure that every valid vote counts and that the democratic process reflects the will of the people.”

title: Sudan’s Burhan heads to Moscow for Russia-Africa summit
body: Sudan’s Sovereignty Council head Abdel Fattah al-Burhan has departed for Moscow to attend the third Russia-Africa summit on October 28-29, state news agency SUNA reported on Tuesday. His delegation includes the foreign and finance ministers, the heads of the General Intelligence Service and the Defence Industries System. Al-Burhan is expected to address the summit, hold bilateral talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin and visit the Russian State University for the Humanities. Closer ties Sudan’s ambassador to Russia, Mohammed al-Ghazali al-Tijani Siraj, said the visit reflects growing bilateral relations and cooperation at international forums. He said Russia had supported Sudan’s sovereignty and state institutions, particularly the Sudanese Armed Forces, which have been fighting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) since April 2023. Russia had also defended Sudan at the United Nations Security Council, using its veto power to oppose measures it considered threats to Sudan’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, Siraj said. “Russia’s recent position against attempts to expand the scope of Resolution 1591 to cover the entire territory of Sudan is evidence of this,” he said. Reconstruction Siraj said Russia could help Sudan rebuild after the war, citing potential cooperation in energy, oil, mining, agriculture, infrastructure and higher education. He said the countries’ joint intergovernmental committee on economic and trade cooperation had continued to meet, with agreements reached at its eighth session outlining areas for future collaboration. Sudan and Russia are marking 70 years of diplomatic relations this year, he said. Siraj said al-Burhan would outline Sudan’s vision for peace and stability while defending its sovereignty and unity. He described the war as a fight against what he called a terrorist militia and its regional and international backers. “The will of peoples cannot be defeated, and falsehood, no matter how long it lasts, is destined to disappear,” he said. Summit agenda The summit is expected to consider three draft documents: a summit declaration, a declaration on civilian uses of artificial intelligence, and an action plan for the Russia-Africa partnership for 2027-2029, Siraj said. The documents cover political, economic, security and legal cooperation, as well as education, science, health, the environment and climate issues. The proposed action plan seeks to strengthen the Russia-Africa Partnership Forum, maintain dialogue and expand ministerial consultations. It also prioritises cooperation in the digital economy, trade, tourism and natural resource management, Siraj said. The plan aims to support African countries’ development goals under the African Union’s Agenda 2063, known as “The Africa We Want”, he said. The post Sudan’s Burhan heads to Moscow for Russia-Africa summit appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Lula’s election win leaves Brazil facing a fiscal tightrope
body:
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's surprise re-election as Brazil's president on Sunday prompted a sharp market reaction — and showed the tightrope he must walk between pleasing his grassroots base and nervous investors who could fuel a fiscal crisis.
The country's benchmark stock index tumbled 13.9% on Monday, the sharpest daily decline since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, and the Brazilian real fell nearly 8% against the U.S. dollar, the most since 1999.
The yield on Brazil's 10-year government bond rose 2.46 percentage points to its highest level in more than a decade.
The moves wiped out a rally in Brazilian assets that followed Flávio Bolsonaro , seen as the more market-friendly and fiscally disciplined of the candidates, winning the first-round vote in early October.
Lula, who has been in office since Jan. 1, 2023 and was president before from 2003 to 2011, now faces a host of challenges, including a heavily right-wing Congress opposed to many of his policies and hostility from the White House .
Economic issues will be top of the pile.
Growth is slowing in Latin America's biggest economy, and inflation and interest rates are high.
Lula has promised expensive measures that appeal to his grassroots base. Those include protections of existing benefits, minimum-wage increases ahead of inflation, expansions of housing and education support programs, tax cuts on food essentials and a reduction in the country's long working week to 40 hours without pay cuts.
His ability to deliver will "revolve around a central tension," Rafael Ch, senior analyst for Latin America and emerging markets at Signum Global Advisors, said in a note Tuesday.
Voters want "tangible improvements in household finances," and the election result will be seen as an endorsement of higher social spending, Ch said.
But bond markets are already uneasy with Brazil's growing debt-to-GDP ratio, and are likely to demand an ever-higher premium if public spending rises significantly. The Brazilian Treasury on Monday canceled two planned bond auctions scheduled for this week amid concerns over demand and soaring yields.
"Insufficiently funded fiscal expansion could leave the central bank cutting [interest rates] less, offsetting part of the relief Lula hopes to deliver," Ch said.
"We believe Lula will manage this tension through sequencing: reassure markets initially, capture the benefits of monetary easing, and subsequently seek greater fiscal flexibility to deliver his legacy agenda," he added.
Reassurance will come through signals that he is preparing measures to increase the 2027 primary surplus, including a possible constitutional amendment expanding spending freezes, and appointing a market-conscious finance minister, Ch added.
A key question will be whether markets view any fiscal discipline as temporary and whether Lula embarks on a spending spree ahead of the 2030 elections if support for the left falls, Ch said. "Even a limited easing cycle could weaken his commitment to restraint once some of its economic benefits have materialized," he said.
Lula is facing a potential fiscal crisis "largely of his own making," Elizabeth Johnson, managing director of Brazil research at TS Lombard, said on Tuesday.
Johnson also said that market-calming measures should be expected, including the curbing of civil-service benefits, reducing subsidized credit and the presentation of a proposal for a new "sin tax" — on goods such as alcohol and cigarettes — in the coming days.
Meanwhile, the president will rush to approve reforms before the new legislature convenes in February, Johnson said, which "hinges on Lula's willingness to cut spending."
"Our base case is that Lula will advance a modest fiscal reform, helping avert a major fiscal crisis in 2027," Johnson said.
In the short term, Brazilian stocks would nonetheless suffer, according to Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell.
"Who will foot the bill for Lula's proposed welfare spending and debt moratorium for small enterprises remains to be seen, but the 10-year bond yield is likely to rise first and ask questions later, a development that can only serve to make Brazilian equities relatively less attractive," Mould said in a Tuesday note.
Brazil's Ibovespa had been the best-performing major stock market index this year, he said, buoyed by Bolsonaro's expected victory and the country benefiting from higher commodity prices.
The latest decline "in turn may not help wider pan-Latin American indices, which investors can easily access via exchange-traded funds (ETFs). The MSCI Latin America index hit a 12-year high this year, helped by the political rightward swing, which Brazil had been expected to join," Mould said.

title: OSAP ‘fraudsters’ in private career colleges ‘going to jail,’ Doug Ford claims
body:
Ontario Premier Doug Ford says a “couple of bad apples” in the private career college system led to “innocent people” being denied their OSAP payments from the Ontario government – a decision the province is being pressured to reverse.
In early October, the province said students at all 242 private career colleges in the province would be barred from accessing the Ontario Student Assistance Program (OSAP) as the government investigated “serious concerns” raised by the federal government, advocacy groups and internal audits and inspections.
The government alleged that some private career colleges were co-owned by immigration services and recruitment firms, could not validate students or provide verification that they were enrolled in courses and that there was a “high concentration of OSAP applications” from the same geographic locations.
Ford insisted that while the government grants come with “trust” and an expectation that “people are going to be honest,” the system was defrauded by “bad actors.”
Under persistent questioning from interim Liberal leader John Fraser, who said students were “approved, enrolled and abandoned” by the government, Ford insisted the criminal investigations, charges and convictions would come.
“We’ve called in the OPP in and I hope to God these bad actors are going to jail,” Ford said.
While the province referred the findings of an interim KPMG report to the OPP, the force has yet to confirm whether a criminal investigation will be opened into the file.
Meanwhile, Opposition MPPs called on the premier to fire Minister of Colleges and Universities Minister Nolan Quinn over the file after the government revealed that it received warnings about the use of OSAP in 2025 from multiple parties, including the federal government.
Critics said the minister “failed miserably to manage this file,” took too long to intervene and over corrected by cutting off all students from provincial aid.
Quinn insisted the government followed up on the claims of wrongdoing from the federal government, conducted “enhanced reviews” and targeted inspections of colleges, hired KPMG to conduct a system-wide audit and called in police before pausing student aid.
“It’s because of serious allegations, criminal allegations against bad actors, that’s why we paused OSAP,” Quinn said in his own defence. “We’re respecting taxpayer dollars.”
Ford rejected multiple calls from the NDP and Liberals to remove Quinn as minister over the situation.
“The minister has done an incredible job,” Ford said.

title: Ukraine seeks to end war but will take no unilateral steps, Sybiha says
body:
Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said this at a press conference alongside his Finnish counterpart, Elina Valtonen, and Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide in Helsinki, Ukrinform reports.
Sybiha said he had discussed with his Finnish and Norwegian counterparts the phone calls their countries’ leaders had held with Russian President Vladimir Putin that morning, as well as their subsequent conversations with President Volodymyr Zelensky.
“We welcome this active support for our diplomatic efforts and the peace process. I want to emphasize once again: Ukraine wants to end this war. We have realistic proposals and solutions. We are ready for a partial ceasefire and a complete cessation of hostilities. Of course, everything must be fair. We will not take any unilateral steps,” the minister said.
He also said that Ukraine was ready for a trilateral meeting in the United Arab Emirates.
“We will use every opportunity to bring peace closer,” Sybiha said.
As previously reported, President Volodymyr Zelensky discussed the leaders’ phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin with Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre.

title: Palestinians protest against military demolitions in West Bank as Israelis vote
body: Israeli troops fired a stun grenade on Tuesday to disperse Palestinians who gathered to protest against an Israeli military operation that has displaced thousands of residents from a neighborhood in Hebron in the West Bank.The unrest, which follows the deaths of two Israeli soldiers shot by Palestinian gunmen at a checkpoint last week, unfolded as Israelis were voting in an election in which the country's posture in the West Bank has been a major political issue.Some Palestinian officials have accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of launching a crackdown in the West Bank to coincide with the vote, as a way to energize his right-wing supporters. The government says its operation is a response to the attack on its soldiers.A group of Palestinian men, women, and children gathered at Tuesday's protest. One elderly man held a placard that said: "No to collective punishment, no to closures, and no to displacement."The military said it had fired a stun grenade to disperse them so that its operation could continue.UN says over 3,000 Palestinians displaced by Israeli military operation in HebronOn Monday, the United Nations said that over 3,000 Palestinians had been forced from their homes by the Israeli military operation, which targeted neighborhoods near the checkpoint where Palestinian gunmen killed the two Israeli soldiers on Friday."Collective punishment is a grave violation of international law," said UN human rights chief Volker Türk in a statement. "Threats to empty and erase entire neighborhoods also raise serious concerns of ethnic cleansing."The Israeli military said in a statement on Sunday that troops would carry out demolitions in the area. It said soldiers had not located any weapons in searches of the houses.Since Friday's attack on the checkpoint, Israel has blocked the entrances to most Palestinian cities and towns across the West Bank, severely curtailing Palestinians' freedom of movement.Noura Nassar, a displaced resident who attended the protests, said she had struggled to get medical treatment because of the blockages."Where is the democracy in all of this? Their elections are today, sure, but what about us? Aren't we human beings? We want to go out, we want to visit the doctor," said Nassar.Netanyahu, Eisenkot oppose Palestinian statehood as Hebron residents question election's impactNetanyahu and his main rival Gadi Eisenkot both oppose the creation of an independent Palestinian state alongside Israel. Residents expelled from the Hebron neighborhood said Tuesday's election in Israel would do little to change the reality on the ground in territories Israel has occupied since 1967."Among themselves they will elect who is the oppressor and who will destroy the Palestinian people. That is their election," said Sana' Salman Abu Sneineh, another expelled resident.Netanyahu's government has presided over a rapid expansion of Israeli settlements, which are deemed illegal by UN bodies and ​most countries, though ⁠Israel disputes this. Under Netanyahu's right-wing coalition, there has also been a surge of militant settler violence against Palestinians.

title: Penticton homeless encampment residents face eviction after court grants injunction
body:
For people living at the Fairview homeless encampment in Penticton, a court-ordered eviction has raised questions about where they will go next.
“I have no idea where I’m going to go,” said Casper, a Fairview encampment resident who did not want to use her last name. “I don’t have anywhere to go.”
The B.C. government secured an injunction Monday to dismantle the encampment, located on Ministry of Transportation land between Highway 97 and Ellis Creek.
In granting the injunction, B.C. Supreme Court Justice Breanna Hardwick ruled the site represents a significant and ongoing public safety risk and is unsuitable for outdoor sheltering.
Casper says the uncertainty is compounded by the repeated need to move their belongings and find somewhere else to stay.
“I’ve been through the daily grind of having to move everything that I have at a moment’s notice until I can find another place that I can park a tent and camp until 6 a.m. and do it all over again,” Casper said. “That’s really hard on somebody. ”
Concerns over safety have grown over the past two years, including the risk from repeated fires at the site.
There have been multiple fires at the encampment in recent months, including a large one in May that had black smoke billowing into the sky.
While no one has been seriously hurt, a fire last year spread to the nearby Leisureland RV Centre, destroying two recreational vehicles.
Other businesses, including Inland Truck and Equipment, have also experienced fire damage.
Luke Bradley, who operates Inland Truck and Equipment, says he hopes dismantling the site will help ease concerns about property crime and fires.
“There’ll be less fear of you know break-ins, which we’ve had, fires, which we’ve had,” Bradley said. “It will be refreshing for the businesses around here to not have to be as worried.”
While Bradley welcomes the prospect of the site being cleaned up, he says more support is needed for people experiencing homelessness.
“They need help, and I feel like we’ve kind of let them down in a way that we are not providing what they need to actually get out of here,” he said.
Penticton’s outgoing mayor, Julius Bloomfield, says the injunction may provide some relief for businesses that have struggled with the encampment, but he is concerned about the lack of available shelter space.
“We have no shelter space that I know of. The one shelter is completely full, and I suspect the other one doesn’t have that kind of room,” Bloomfield said.
Bloomfield argues that dismantling the encampment does not address the underlying issue of homelessness.
“This doesn’t solve the problem, it just moves the problem,” he said.
The roughly one dozen people living at the Fairview encampment have until noon Friday to leave the site.
Casper says they plan to resist the eviction.
“I’m not leaving without being handcuffed and arrested. So that’s how I’m leaving,” Casper said. “If that’s what it takes to get some kind of attention for this, I think then it will happen.”

title: Nigeria to Begin Mass Production of Military Munitions Locally Within One Year, Defence Minister Reveals
body: Linus Aleke in Abuja The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (rtd), has disclosed that Nigeria will commence large-scale local production of defence hardware within the next year for domestic use and export, particularly to other African countries. Speaking at the inaugural Africa International Defence Exhibition (AFRIDEX) in Lagos, the minister urged participants to seize the opportunity presented by the exhibition to invest in Nigeria’s defence sector. According to a statement by the Chief Information Officer of the Ministry of Defence, Dr. Queenet Iheoma-Hart, the minister said the side events scheduled to take place during the exhibition would strengthen bilateral and multilateral relations among defence establishments, government representatives, industry stakeholders and other strategic partners. In his remarks, the Minister of State for Defence, Dr Bello Muhammad Matawalle, described AFRIDEX as a dynamic platform capable of achieving the objectives for which it was established. In their goodwill messages, the Lagos State Governor, represented by his Deputy, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, and the representative of the ECOWAS Commission, Mr Birame Diop, expressed optimism that the gathering would provide an inclusive platform for African countries to expand and revitalise their defence sectors. The Director-General of the Defence Industries Corporation of Nigeria (DICON), Major General B.I. Alaya, commended President Bola Tinubu for his continued support for DICON and pledged to enhance its production capacity. Following the opening ceremony, the minister of defence inspected exhibition stands featuring displays from various countries and held an executive meeting with the United States Africa Command (AFRICOM). Dignitaries in attendance included the Chief of Defence Staff, serving and former Service Chiefs, the Chairman of the National Assembly Committee on Defence and representatives from more than 20 African countries.

title: Hitler’s Eagle’s Nest, famously captured by ‘Band of Brothers,’ deliberately set ablaze
body: A 33-year-old German citizen was arrested over the weekend after a fire tore through one of the last architectural relics of Nazism. On Friday, roughly 200 firefighters were deployed to Adolf Hitler’s notorious Bavarian retreat, dubbed the “Eagle’s Nest,” shortly after a smoke detector triggered an alarm around 9:15 p.m. local time. Surrounded by rough mountainous terrain near the Austrian border, the infamous retreat is accessible only by a single road and a series of tunnels that lead to the base of the knoll. The historic building sits at an altitude of roughly 6,000 feet, hampering efforts to put out the blaze. By 9:52 p.m., when firefighters arrived on the scene, the entire structure was engulfed in flames and deemed largely unsalvageable. No one was hurt, authorities said, and their investigation into what appears to have been a deliberately set fire is ongoing. Carved into an Alpine crag, the structure, designed by Martin Bormann , head of the Nazi Party Chancellery and Hitler’s private secretary, was intended to serve as a diplomatic reception venue rather than an operational command center. It did not, according to The Telegraph , host any of the regime’s fateful conferences, which all took place lower down at the Berghof. “This was because the supposedly fearless Alpine Führer was really a hypochondriac crippled by acrophobia who complained the thin air at the Eagle’s Nest aggravated his stomach spasms. He was also terrified of lightning striking the complex’s lift mechanism,” writes the outlet. Hitler himself only visited the site a handful of times. The building, however, also holds unique lore for one unit of Army paratroopers — made famous by Stephen Ambrose’s 1992 bestseller Band of Brothers and the subsequent 2001 HBO miniseries of the same title. In 1945, the Allied Command feared the Germans were planning a “last stand” in Berchtesgaden and, to that end, Gen. Eisenhower ordered it to be secured before German resistance could coalesce around the Nazi stronghold. A seemingly very hungover Capt. Lewis Nixon. (U.S. Army Signal Corps) On the morning of May 5, the hard-bitten 506th Parachute Infantry Regiment of the 101st Airborne Division, which had fought near-continuously from D-Day through Operation Market Garden and the Battle of the Bulge, arrived in Berchtesgaden. While they weren’t the first — the 7th Infantry Regiment of the U.S. 3rd Infantry Division and the French 2nd Armored Division hold that distinction — they stayed the longest, culminating in some iconic photos from the end of the war — particularly that of a heavily hungover Capt. Lewis Nixon after he and his men drank their way through Hitler and Hermann Goering’s booze collection. The structure was spared from the wrath of Allied bombing and postwar, and while plans to dynamite the Eagle’s Nest — and all remaining Nazi structures — were created, the notorious guesthouse was spared from destruction on the intervention of the district administrator, Karl Theodor Jacob. Jacob proposed to neutralize Nazi tourism through “profanation” — namely beer. “I always said, let’s serve Munich Hofbräu beer up there,” Jacob later recalled, “and then no reverent mood will ever take hold.” Now, the alleged arsonist has destroyed what the Allies and postwar Germans did not. “It is damaged to a large extent,” a police spokesperson told the German tabloid Bild . “The house is unlikely to be saved.”

title: Western Copper CEO exits as Casino review advances
body: Western Copper and Gold (TSX, NYSE-A: WRN) said CEO Sandeep Singh will leave the company this week, handing leadership to chairman Mark E. Smith as the developer advances its Casino copper-gold project through Yukon’s highest level of environmental assessment. Singh will step down as president, CEO and director on Saturday, Western said late Monday without providing a reason. Smith will become interim CEO on Sunday while chief financial officer Michael Psihogios adds the president’s role. The board plans to search for a permanent CEO. The move puts an engineer with extensive Yukon experience in charge of one of Canada’s largest undeveloped copper-gold projects. Casino, about 300 km northwest of Whitehorse, would require $3.62 billion (US$2.6 billion) in initial capital under Western’s 2022 feasibility study, which forecast 27 years of operations. “Singh’s departure will be a surprise to the market, given that the company has been on steady course to begin a major ‘Panel Review’ phase of permitting, which in our view, is a core value driver aligned with our thesis for Casino to be de-risked towards an eventual M&A exit to a global mining company and mine builder,” National Bank Financial mining analyst Rabi Nizami said in a note. Under Smith, Western’s interim leadership team will probably “maintain a steady hand on Panel Review and leverage his Yukon government and industry relationships, although additional work streams to orient the company’s capital allocation towards additional engineering and exploration spending may be under consideration to advance the project on multiple fronts in parallel with the core permitting track,” Nizami added. Stock climbs Western shares rose 2.1% to $2.45 in Tuesday morning in Toronto, boosting the company’s market capitalization to about $554 million. The stock has traded between $2.34 and $5.74 in the past year. Smith joined Western’s board last November and became chairman in August. He has more than 45 years of mining experience, including nearly 25 years leading Vector Engineering, which he co-founded. His Yukon work includes advising on mine waste and heap-leach management and chairing the independent review board investigating the Eagle mine failure. Over the past year, he worked with Boroo on its recommissioning plans for the mine , which the Singapore-based investor agreed last week to buy for $140 million. “Casino is one of the most significant undeveloped copper -gold projects I have worked on in my career, and the board and I are fully committed to advancing it,” Smith said in Monday’s statement. “The Panel Review, the engineering work and our engagement with First Nations and the Government of Yukon continue without interruption.” Open-pit mine Casino, a proposed open-pit operation, would produce an average of 164 million lb. copper and 259,000 oz. gold annually, alongside molybdenum and silver, according to the feasibility study. Its processing plan combines a 120,000-tonne-per-day concentrator with a smaller heap-leach facility for oxide material. Using an 8% discount rate, Casino is projected to have an after-tax net present value of C$2.3 billion with an 18% internal rate of return and 3.3-year payback. The estimates use $3.60-per-lb. copper and $1,700-per-oz. gold. They remain study assumptions from 2022, rather than an updated construction budget or forecast based on today’s prices. Although Western acquired Casino in 2006, exploration in the area dates to 1917. The project remains under panel review by the Yukon Environmental and Socio-economic Assessment Board, a process that involves technical scrutiny, public hearings and consideration of effects on land, water, wildlife and communities. Government and First Nations decision bodies would consider the panel’s recommendations before decisions on the project. Drill program Engineering and design work is continuing. Western’s 2026 program includes geotechnical drilling, permafrost investigations and metallurgical sampling. Vancouver-based Western reported more than C$120.6 million in cash and investments as of Sept. 30, supporting the work ahead while the leadership search proceeds. Singh joined Western in February 2024 after serving as president and CEO of Osisko Gold Royalties, now OR Royalties (TSX, NYSE: OR). His appointment brought investment banking and transaction experience to a company seeking to advance a large, capital-intensive development. He previously co-founded mining advisory firm Maxit Capital. Rio Tinto (ASX, LON, NYSE: RIO) owns about 8.5% of Western, while Japan’s Mitsubishi Materials owns a 5% stake.

title: New 14‑inch MacBook Pro with M6
body:
Apple introduces the new 14‑inch MacBook Pro with M6
Supercharged by M6, the 14-inch MacBook Pro features incredible performance and next-level AI capabilities, enhanced connectivity, and up to 24 hours of battery life, delivering even more value
CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today announced the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 , delivering even more performance, powerful on-device AI capabilities, and faster connectivity for college students, business users, creators, and more. M6 features an advanced 12-core CPU with the world’s fastest CPU core, so everything from productivity tasks to more demanding pro workflows feels incredibly fast and responsive. 1 The 12-core GPU delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to 25 percent faster AI workloads when compared to M5, making the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 a compelling value for users who need serious power. 2 For those upgrading from M1, the performance gains are even more significant, with up to 11x faster graphics and up to 13x faster AI performance. 3 With additional Neural Accelerators in the GPU and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, M6 turns MacBook Pro into an even more powerful platform for AI — from taking advantage of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features across apps and macOS to running LLMs locally, all while preserving user privacy. 4 In addition, the 14-inch MacBook Pro features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, while superfast storage makes working with large files, exporting projects, and running demanding AI workflows fly. And with phenomenal battery life of up to 24 hours, it delivers the same remarkable performance whether plugged in or on battery, so users can work, create, and pursue their passions from anywhere. 3 It also offers the advanced features users love, including the stunning Liquid Retina XDR display with a nano-texture option, a 12MP Center Stage camera, an immersive six-speaker sound system, and a wide array of ports. Together with macOS 27, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is a major upgrade for existing Mac users and those coming to Mac for the first time. Available in space black and silver, it can be pre-ordered beginning tomorrow, October 28, with availability starting Friday, November 6.
“The 14-inch MacBook Pro is the pro laptop of choice for a wide range of users — from college students, to business professionals across every industry, to multidisciplinary creators doing it all on one device,” said Shelly Goldberg, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering. “With the powerful M6 chip, we’re taking performance to the next level, with a boost in CPU speed and graphics and even more powerful capabilities for on-device AI. With its amazing battery life, remarkable Liquid Retina XDR display, and even faster connectivity, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 delivers a fantastic combination of performance, capability, and value.”
M6: Blazing-Fast Performance and On-Device AI Capabilities
M6 brings even more performance and next-level AI capabilities to the 14-inch MacBook Pro. Featuring a powerful 12-core CPU, a 12-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each core, Dual 16-core Neural Engine, and faster unified memory, MacBook Pro with M6 is faster and more responsive.
The 12-core CPU, with two more cores than before, brings blazing-fast single- and multithreaded performance, so users can fly through everything from multitasking across apps to compiling code to handling complex creative workflows. The 12-core GPU, also with two additional cores, delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics performance when compared to M5. 2 Everything from 3D modelling to photo editing and gaming feels incredibly fast, enhanced by a third-generation ray-tracing engine and Dynamic Caching to optimise on-chip memory. It also brings up to 25 percent faster performance for on-device AI workloads, like LLM prompt processing, compared to M5. 3 The Dual 16-core Neural Engine delivers up to 1.9x faster performance than M5 and works with the advanced GPU to dramatically accelerate AI workloads like image generation, Super Resolution, and AI upscaling. 2 The Neural Engine also powers Apple Intelligence, enabling advanced and energy-efficient on-device AI processing. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 does all this with industry-leading performance per watt and up to 24 hours of battery life, the longest ever in a Mac. With 16GB of unified memory standard, configurable up to 32GB, and higher memory bandwidth up to 170GB/s, MacBook Pro makes multitasking and working with demanding apps and large projects even faster.
The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 enables : 3
There’s never been a better time for customers to upgrade from a previous-generation MacBook Pro with Apple silicon or an Intel-based Mac. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 delivers remarkable value thanks to major performance improvements and powerful AI capabilities. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro also features all of the compelling capabilities that have made it so popular, including:
The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 comes to life with macOS 27, which includes Siri AI, a profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal assistant; helpful Apple Intelligence features across everyday apps; and improvements that make the Mac even more responsive and reliable. Siri AI can draw on personal context to help users find what they need in the moment across messages, emails, photos, and more; answer questions about virtually any topic; and get things done across apps — all with groundbreaking privacy protections. Siri AI is integrated into Spotlight and systemwide context menus, and users can ask Siri about what’s on their display with Visual Intelligence using a dedicated keyboard shortcut. Users can also write and edit with Siri almost anywhere they type.
Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful. In Safari, it powers new tools that automatically organise a user’s tabs into topics; notify them of website changes, like product restocks or price drops; and enable the creation of custom extensions based on a description. Users can also easily create an automation in Shortcuts by simply describing it, or tap into intelligent photo editing tools in the Photos app. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro gets even more responsive, reliable, and delightful with refinements to design, performance, search, and more. Updates to Liquid Glass deliver an even more focused and approachable experience. A new slider in Settings gives users the option to personalise Liquid Glass, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference, and app icons are sharper and more defined.
14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 and the Environment
The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. It is made with 45 percent recycled content overall, 6 including 100 percent recycled aluminium in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and, in a first for Apple, 100 percent recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors. It is manufactured with 60 percent renewable electricity, such as wind and solar, across the supply chain. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is designed to be durable and repairable, and meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 7 and designed to be recycled.
Apple revolutionised personal technology with the introduction of the Macintosh in 1984. Today, Apple leads the world in innovation with iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro. Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV. Apple’s more than 150,000 employees are dedicated to making the best products on earth and to leaving the world better than we found it.

title: Rourke, Oliveira, Philpot top Canadian finalists
body:
TORONTO – B.C. Lions quarterback Nathan Rourke is in the running to defend his CFL top Canadian award.
Rourke was named as a finalist for the honour. He was the league’s top Canadian and outstanding player last season.
Rourke, of Victoria, threw for 4,614 yards and 24 touchdowns while completing 70.5 per cent of his passes. He also ran for 356 yards — averaging 11.5 yards per carry — with three touchdowns.
Winnipeg running back Brady Oliveira — the CFL’s top Canadian in 2023-24 and its outstanding player in 2024 — and Montreal receiver Tyson Philpot are the other finalists.
Oliveira was the CFL’s top rusher this season with 1,493 yards and averaged 6.3 yards per carry. The Winnipeg native recorded his fifth straight 1,000-yard campaign while adding 42 catches for 348 yards and scoring eight total TDs (seven rushing, one receiving).
Philpot led the CFL in receiving with 124 catches for 1,809 yards and was tied with teammate Tyler Snead for most TD grabs (13 apiece). Philpot, of Delta, B.C., set new Canadian standards for receptions and yards, accomplishing both feats in 16 games.
The CFL also unveiled its finalists for the top offensive lineman and rookie awards.
Winnipeg’s Jarell Broxton and Montreal Alouettes Nick Callender and Pier-Olivier Lestage are the top lineman finalists. Toronto receiver Tyler Kahmann, B.C. linebacker Parker McKenna and Bombers defensive back Major Williams will vie for the outstanding rookie honour.
Broxton started 17 games this season with Winnipeg and helped pave the way for Oliveira. Broxton ranked second among offensive tackles with a Pro Football Focus (PFF) grade of 75.2 (minimum of 100 snaps).
Callender started 12 games for a Montreal offensive line that allowed a league-low 19 sacks. Callender led the CFL with a PFF pass-block grade of 84.2 (minimum of 100 snaps).
Lestage started 17 of 18 games with Montreal. The Saint-Eustache, Que., native helped the Alouettes lead the CFL in yards per game (420.9) and yards per play (7.5).
Kahmann was one of four Argos receivers this season to crack the 1,000-yard mark. He had 77 catches for 1,092 yards and eight TDs.
McKenna appeared in all 18 of B.C.’s games this season, registering 75 defensive tackles and six on special teams. He also had four tackles for a loss, a sack and two forced fumbles.
Williams made 18 starts this season for Winnipeg. He ranked second on the team in defensive tackles (77, one for loss) while adding nine special-teams tackles and three interceptions.
On Wednesday, the CFL will reveal the finalists for outstanding player, top defensive performer and outstanding special-teams player.
The league won’t be honouring its top players at an annual awards ceremony this year. Instead, the winners will learn of their accomplishment through surprise presentations that will be shared online.
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 27, 2026.

title: IERPP demands account of $4bn 24-Hour Economy before rollout of $10bn New Economy
body: The Institute of Economic Research and Public Policy (IERPP) has challenged the Mahama administration to account for the financing, projects and jobs associated with its $4 billion 24-Hour Economy programme before proceeding with the proposed $10 billion New Economy initiative. The institute’s Executive Director, Professor Isaac Boadi, says the government must provide verifiable evidence of the original programme’s performance, including funds disbursed, projects implemented and employment created. Speaking at a press conference at the IERPP Conference Room in Adabraka, Accra, on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, he questioned the credibility of announcing a substantially larger economic initiative without first publishing a comprehensive account of the existing programme. He said Ghanaians needed evidence that public commitments were translating into measurable economic benefits, particularly sustainable employment for young people. Prof. Boadi recalled that on June 30, 2025, Presidential Adviser on the 24-Hour Economy, Augustus Goosie Obuadum Tanoh, announced plans to mobilise $4 billion over four years for the programme. He said Abdul-Nasser Suglo Alidu, then Head of Strategy and Programmes at the 24-Hour Economy Secretariat, had set a target of at least 1.7 million jobs within the same period. President John Dramani Mahama subsequently launched the 24-Hour Economy and Accelerated Export Development Programme, known as 24H+, on July 2, 2025. The initiative was designed to expand production, boost exports, attract private investment and create jobs. However, Prof. Boadi cited a MyJoyOnline report published on October 19, 2026, in which Mr Suglo Alidu reportedly said the Secretariat could not provide a total figure for jobs created under the programme. “I won’t be able to give you a number in terms of the total number of jobs the 24-hour economy created. We don’t want to throw numbers around,” Mr Suglo Alidu was quoted as saying. Prof. Boadi said the absence of a verified employment figure made it difficult for the public to assess progress towards the programme’s 1.7 million-job target. He argued that a programme of that scale should have a system for measuring and verifying employment outcomes from the outset. The institute also questioned the Secretariat’s reported announcement in July 2026 that agreements worth approximately $5.5 billion had been signed, with four projects expected to generate more than 160,000 direct jobs. Prof. Boadi said the government needed to clarify how much of the reported amount represented binding financing commitments, how much had been disbursed and which projects had progressed to implementation. He cautioned against treating signed agreements or projected employment figures as evidence that financing had been secured or jobs had already been created. The institute is demanding a breakdown of the original $4 billion financing target, including the amounts pledged, secured, released and spent, alongside details of projects completed and those still awaiting implementation. It also wants the government to distinguish between permanent, temporary and indirect jobs and employment opportunities that remain projections. Prof. Boadi raised a separate concern over what he described as a discrepancy between two figures for the 24-Hour Economy programme in the 2026 Budget documents. He said the detailed expenditure table in the Budget presented by Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson on November 13, 2025, listed GH¢90 million for the programme, comprising GH¢70 million for goods and services and GH¢20 million for capital expenditure. However, he said the Budget Speech cited an allocation of GH¢110 million. Prof. Boadi called on the government to reconcile the figures and disclose how much was actually released and spent. He stressed that a budgetary allocation did not necessarily mean the entire amount had been disbursed or expended. The institute is seeking a clear account of the programme’s financial performance and the outputs achieved with the resources released. The concerns come as the government prepares to advance its proposed $10 billion New Economy initiative, which Prof. Boadi said President Mahama announced on August 14, 2026. The programme is expected to run over four years, with an estimated $2.5 billion annually allocated across seven priority sectors. Prof. Boadi acknowledged the importance of investment in agriculture and agro-processing but questioned the timing of the proposal, particularly the reported allocation of $5 billion to those sectors. He said the government should provide a credible financing and implementation plan and demonstrate how the proposed initiative would build on lessons from the 24-Hour Economy programme. He also called for clarity on the sources of funding, including the respective contributions expected from public resources, private investors, development partners and financial institutions. Prof. Boadi urged the government to explain whether the programme could create additional fiscal obligations or contingent liabilities for the State. He said the proposed investment criteria, sectoral allocations, implementation timetable and accountability arrangements should be made public. According to Prof. Boadi, the Finance Minister has indicated that consultations on the initiative are ongoing, with further details expected in the 2027 Budget. Prof. Boadi outlined five measures he wants the government to implement. First, he called for a comprehensive financing and implementation report on the 24-Hour Economy, detailing pledges, signed agreements, funds disbursed, expenditure incurred and projects completed. Second, he demanded independently verifiable employment figures that distinguish permanent, temporary and indirect jobs from projected opportunities. Third, he wants the government to reconcile the GH¢90 million and GH¢110 million figures in the 2026 Budget documents and disclose actual releases and expenditure. Fourth, he called for the publication of the New Economy initiative’s financing structure, investment criteria, sectoral allocations, implementation timetable and accountability mechanisms. Finally, he proposed a public dashboard, supported by periodic independent audits, to track financial commitments, disbursements, project milestones and jobs created. Prof. Boadi said these measures would allow citizens to assess whether the government’s economic programmes were delivering the results promised. The IERPP Executive Director argued that Ghana’s challenge was not necessarily a shortage of economic plans but the need for stronger accountability for commitments made under them. He warned that announcing ambitious financial targets without publishing comprehensive progress reports could weaken public confidence in government initiatives. Prof. Boadi said the government should demonstrate how much had actually been invested under the 24-Hour Economy, what the expenditure had achieved and how the lessons would inform the proposed New Economy programme. “The era of announcing numbers must end. The era of accounting for results must begin,” he said. He urged the administration to make transparency, financial accountability and measurable outcomes central to both programmes.

title: IT Worker Jailed 13 Years in Russia After Binance Revealed He Donated Money to Ukraine
body:
A Russia n IT specialist has been sentenced to 13 years in jail on charges of financing terrorism after the cryptocurrency exchange Binance passed details to authorities in Moscow of his donations to Ukrainian fundraising campaigns.
A judge at the 2nd Western District Military Court on Monday found 49-year-old Yury Belenky guilty of the charges and sentenced him to three years in prison, plus an additional 10 years in a strict-regime penal colony, according to a court statement.
Belenky, who has a Bulgarian residence permit, was arrested in September last year when he flew to Moscow for a visit and has been in police custody ever since. He denied the charges, according to the court.
Documents showed that Binance provided Russia n investigators with Belenky's transaction history last year, including records of transfers to Ukrainian fundraising campaigns, in response to a Russia n request, and that the records were instrumental in prosecuting him, Reuters reported in August.
According to the records, Belenky sent more than $700 to the Ukrainian military in response to an online appeal by Arkady Babchenko, an exiled Russia n critic of the Kremlin who supports Ukraine. Some payments went to the Azov Brigade.
"The response from Binance serves as key evidence in the criminal case against Belenkiy," said Yevgeny Smirnov, a lawyer with the rights group First Department, which helps people facing politically motivated charges in Russia .
Rights advocates who monitor such prosecutions say dozens of Russia ns have been convicted in recent years for donations made through cryptocurrency platforms to causes that authorities later classified as extremist or terrorist. Many used cryptocurrency because they believed it would keep their identities secret.
Asked on Tuesday about the sentence, Binance referred Reuters to a previous statement in which it said the exchange "does not make or enforce the laws of any jurisdiction, determine charges or decide how any government uses information in legal proceedings."
Binance said it does not comment on confidential law-enforcement requests or individual cases.
A lawyer who specialises in crypto regulation, Mike Bystrov, told Reuters in August that Binance, which left Russia in 2023 following the full-scale invasion of Ukraine and the subsequent imposition of Western sanctions, had been under no obligation to provide Belenky's data.
He said it might, in fact, have had obligations under European Union data-protection law not to do so because of Belenky's Bulgarian residency status.

These actions are direct attempts to silence independent journalism in Russia. The authorities claim our work "discredits the decisions of the Russian leadership." We see things differently: we strive to provide accurate, unbiased reporting on Russia.
We, the journalists of The Moscow Times, refuse to be silenced. But to continue our work, we need your help .

By supporting The Moscow Times, you're defending open, independent journalism in the face of repression. Thank you for standing with us.

title: Major League Baseball is looking for a new kind of fan
body:
On October 2nd, just as Major League Baseball’s Division Series was kicking off, the main MLB Instagram and TikTok accounts posted a video hyping up the teams still in the running for the World Series. It featured clips of players from the Milwaukee Brewers, Los Angeles Dodgers, Chicago White Sox, and more sliding into home plate, hitting homers, and celebrating hits — standard fare for a highlight reel. What really makes the montage, though, is that it’s set to an Olivia Rodrigo song.
The song, “My Way,” is an album track — not even a single — from Rodrigo’s latest record. It’s not exactly the soundtrack one might expect from an MLB-produced video. (“And here is the part where the girl gets pissed / And the girl is me, did you get that hint?” she sings.) But as evidenced by the comments, it hit exactly the right people: “I see I’m part of a very niche part of MLB fans,” one person said. “Target audience reached,” another responded. The clip has over 2.1 million views on Instagram and 615,000 views on TikTok.
[Media: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DeAZTw2v3Fk/]
“One of our favorite things is when a community says, ‘Oh, MLB knows ball,’ or, ‘Oh, I can’t believe my interests [are] converging,’” says Cameron Gidari, MLB’s vice president of social media and innovation. The social team is a fan of Rodrigo’s to begin with and loves the song, Gidari says, “but then also we thought we could make a really interesting edit with it, and we thought that community would appreciate being seen.”
Acknowledging the combination of baseball–Olivia Rodrigo fans is smart. It also might be essential for the survival of the sport. People love baseball, of course, but it often feels like it’s trailing other sports, not just in viewership but also culturally. Baseball is famously stats heavy — there are thousands of games every season across the league, and teams play almost every day. What happens on the field today is often contextualized through what happened in games in the past, making it hard to jump in without a history of watching (or learning about) the sport. Go back a few years, and you’d find MLB social channels were more “editorially focused,” Gidari says, focusing on facts of the game or highlights. Speaking to fans who have other interests — or who are simply more casual — has been a deliberate choice, he says.
“Our tone overall on social is the tone of fandom,” Gidari says. “We think there is something really inviting and magnetic about that, and it was a conscious shift.”
Here’s a post of Dua Lipa and Callum Turner at a Yankees game, the night the team was eliminated from the postseason. Here’s an edit spliced together with shots of athletes looking shocked and in awe, as if they were reacting to a song by the K-pop group Stray Kids. Here’s a highlight reel of White Sox first baseman Munetaka Murakami being funny.
The nature of social media algorithms all but requires MLB to branch out. Recommendation-based social feeds mean that following an account doesn’t necessarily mean followers will see the content — feeds have become reorganized into content niches, topics, and trends, and Gidari says “really aggressive algorithm changes” meant the league had to rethink what it posts. Content from the MLB in English- and Spanish-language social accounts racked up 19.1 billion views during the 2026 regular season, Gidari says, a record.
[Media: https://twitter.com/MLB/status/2069218730442137723]
A significant part of that shift has been MLB’s embrace of influencers and content creators. So far this year, the league has tapped 400 creators who posted a combined 3,800 pieces of content, and in the postseason, MLB has had content creators at every single game. The league expects to have 100 content creators at the World Series, depending on how many games it runs.
The openness and collaboration with content creators is relatively new for MLB. As recently as 2024, content creators (including Jimmy “Jomboy” O’Brien, who does viral lip-reading breakdowns) complained of getting wide-ranging copyright takedowns on their content. In 2025, Commissioner Rob Manfred acknowledged the league fumbled this slice of the fanbase and that changing its tune had been “a really good thing” for MLB. (The league even acquired a stake in O’Brien’s media company last year.) More recently, a TikTok partnership gave select creators access to the league’s archives to use in their content.
For the first time, MLB has expanded beyond having influencers only at big events. The league now brings content creators to regular season games, too, and has broadened its reach to include more than just baseball and sports creators. Rachel Richter, director of influencer strategy, says MLB works with food, fashion, lifestyle, gaming, and family influencers, too.
“There are casual fans or [people] that aren’t even fans yet, that maybe they’re going to go to a game just because they get to put on a cute outfit, or they want to try this new food item,” Richter says. The idea is to get those creators to a game and let them incorporate baseball into their usual content.
The league is building on momentum, especially coming off a successful season last year: Game 7 of the 2025 World Series between the Dodgers and the Toronto Blue Jays was the most-watched World Series game since 2017, and more international viewers watched last year’s matchup than ever before. But as other sports have found, it can be a learning curve to balance longtime fans and the culture of the sport with an insurgent, at times unpredictable, class of promotional power brokers: The biggest story out of this year’s US Open, for example, was not the tennis itself but the many complaints and debates about the influencers who attended.
MLB is working to expand what constitutes a fan, reaching into corners of the internet and culture that previously were ignored or, at the very least, untapped. At the same time, it’s hurtling toward an uncertain 2027 season as the collective bargaining agreement between team owners and the MLB Players Association is set to expire in December. If the union and owners don’t reach a deal in time, players likely would be locked out, and the 2027 season could be shortened. Messaging that conflict would be a challenge in itself for the league — especially after adopting the voice of new, casual, and eager fans who are looking for a reason to tune in.
Correction, October 27th: Corrected a misspelling of Gidari’s name.

title: Genie 4: A new generation of world simulation
body:
Today, we are announcing Genie 4, our new world model, which unlocks unprecedented realism and improves real-time interactive simulation. Genie 4 is natively multimodal, enabling audio-like music, ambient noises, and interactive dialogue to be simultaneously generated with the world.
The Genie 4 model incorporates and builds on capabilities from the Gemini family: Gemini Omni anchors the simulations in real-world appearance and behavior, while other Gemini models provide the complex reasoning needed to help maintain a simulationâs coherence and continuity.
With this foundation, you can set an event in motion, and Genie 4 simulates what happens next: how the world responds, how it sounds, and how the people in it move, react, and speak.
Understanding and simulating the world is a crucial aspect of building AGI. Genie 4 advances our ability to create safe, infinitely variable simulations that can help with everything from developing training environments for robots and agents to unlocking the creation of new interactive experiences.
We have started rolling Genie 4 out as a research preview for trusted testers â gathering feedback before we release it to consumers and developers, starting with Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early access partners of the Gemini API and Google AI Studio. Join the waitlist for Genie 4 in Project Genie here .
Genie 4 delivers enhanced photorealism, fluid movement, and native audio. All accompanying sounds featured above are produced directly by Genie 4.
The following are recordings of real-time interactions from Genie 4, where users use standard keyboard controls for navigation and camera control, and text prompts to steer the scene as it evolves.
With Genie 4, you can use natural language to modify a simulation in real-time â like changing the weather, moving the camera, or introducing a new person or object â and Gemini will contextually adapt your prompt to match the surrounding scene. Between your inputs, Gemini also monitors and steers the scene to keep the world progressing cohesively.
Prompt: Use the reference image as the exact first frame and visual basis for the scene. Preserve the same floating rectangular platform, weathered concrete edges, wild grasses, ferns, twisted small tree, warm glowing amber sphere, and the same middle-aged man in a loose brown suit playing a brass saxophone.
A cinematic, highly naturalistic documentary scene, photographed on 16mm film with subtle grain, soft photographic detail, extremely low contrast, muted natural colors, lifted shadows, gentle highlights, and soft diffuse overcast light. Absolutely no HDR, no dramatic contrast, no glossy digital rendering, no artificial cinematic lighting.
The platform floats in the middle of a vast, quiet lake surrounded by distant misty forests. Thin layers of fog drift above the water. The sky is pale blue-gray and overcast, with a soft, almost monochromatic atmosphere. The warm amber sphere provides a delicate contrasting glow, softly illuminating the surrounding vegetation and reflecting in the lake.
Begin with a slightly closer view of the saxophone player than in the reference image, while keeping the platform, glowing sphere, tree, and surrounding lake visible. The man continues playing his saxophone naturally, with subtle breathing, finger movements, and gentle body swaying.
The camera moves independently and can freely explore the entire environment, gliding smoothly over the water with gentle, controlled movement. The camera is not attached to the man or the platform. Maintain realistic spatial continuity and natural camera movement.
Everything must remain photographic, physically believable, documentary-like, extremely low-contrast, and softly desaturated throughout the entire experience.
One continuous shot. Natural lake ambience, distant wind, soft water movement, and realistic saxophone sound. No background music beyond the instruments physically present in the scene.
Environment prompt: A wide, sun-drenched hilltop meadow filled with tall green grass and scattered purple, white, and yellow wildflowers swaying in a warm breeze. Low green shrubs dot the right side of the field while distant blue-green rolling hills stretch along the left horizon beneath a bright, partly cloudy sky.
Character: Winding in sweeping S-curves through the center of the grassy meadow from the immediate foreground far into the distance is a long, continuous stream of glossy bubblegum-pink satin fabric. The shimmering pink cloth billows, ripples, and lifts softly above the wildflowers like a flowing river of silk as the wind moves beneath its folds.
Environment prompt: A sweeping aerial view over the vast, frozen landscape of Antarctica, featuring endless snow-covered glaciers, jagged icy mountain peaks, and sculpted blue icebergs bathed in crisp polar sunlight under a clear, pale blue sky. Numerous hot air balloons dot the horizon at varying altitudes, with a large cream, red, and blue striped balloon floating prominently in the mid-distance above the ice sheet.
Character prompt: Shot from a first-person POV standing inside the woven wicker basket of a flying hot air balloon, looking out over the leather-trimmed basket edge on the right side of the frame, where black padded support poles, metal rigging chains, and the dark base of the balloon canopy overhead frame the drifting polar vista.
Genie 4 introduces a new standard of realism to real-time interactive simulation. Built on an advanced physical understanding of the world, Genie 4 simulates real-world physics scenarios, such as aerodynamics, collisions, and more.
The most dramatic leap is how Genie 4 simulates people, creating characters that move naturally, respond organically to their environments, and can be interactively steered in real-time.
Environment prompt: A sunlit outdoor courtyard featuring a weathered stone plinth set against a soft-focus background of lush green garden foliage and clear blue sky, bathed in bright, warm afternoon sunlight that backlights airborne droplets in crisp slow motion.
Character prompt: A whole, glossy green-striped watermelon rests in the center of the stone plinth.
Prompt: A macro close up of a maple seed falling from the tree into the grass
Prompt: A crowded rural Japanese train station in the 1980s, packed with passengers waiting along the platform. The only railway inspector in a dark navy uniform stands close to the camera, observing the scene. A long, deep-red local train with many carriages occupies the railway track closest to the camera POV, stretching across the frame and extending far into the distance. The train is clearly visible in the immediate foreground, not on a distant track. People fill the platform naturally, standing, walking, boarding and waiting with luggage. Lush green mountains, cedar forests and humid summer haze surround the station. Authentic 1980s Japanese atmosphere, cinematic 35mm documentary photography, realistic perspective, asymmetrical composition, natural lighting, subtle film grain, photorealistic textures. The station must look genuinely busy, with a dense crowd of visible people throughout the platform. The red train must be on the nearest track, dominating the scene. No empty platforms, no distant train, no sparse crowds, no centered symmetrical composition.
Genie 4 is our first real-time world model to generate audio natively. Every world carries the ambient sound of its own setting, from wind in the trees to waves crashing at the beach.
The true frontier, however, is human speech. Genie 4 introduces interactive dialogue that adapts on the fly. Characters converse and react to your inputs or events in the world, all in real-time.
Prompt: Create a fully three-dimensional immersive stained-glass landscape that feels like a handcrafted crystal window brought to life. The world should be explorable, as if the camera can move freely through a giant 3D stained-glass environment. The entire scene must have a stained-glass / crystal-window look: translucent colored glass, dark lead outlines, glowing layered panels, volumetric depth, and artisanal glass textures.
Show a beautiful landscape with a flowing river running through green fields, flowers in the foreground, trees, distant mountains, clouds, and a radiant sun in the sky. The river should feel like flowing translucent blue glass, the flowers like upright stained-glass sculptures, the grass and trees like layered colored-glass forms, the mountains like stacked glass panels, and the sun like a luminous circular stained-glass element. Everything must feel spatial, cohesive, luminous, and handcrafted, with depth and the sensation that the viewer can move through it in three dimensions.
The camera should be able to travel through the scene as if walking or gliding inside this 3D stained-glass world. Keep the world beautiful, magical, and fully consistent in style.
Absolutely everything must remain made of stained glass or crystal at all times, including the grass, the water, the sky, the clouds, the flowers, the trees, the mountains, the sun, and all visible surfaces. Do not introduce any natural real-world textures. No real grass, no real water, no normal sky, and no realism outside of the stained-glass universe.
No text, no modern objects, no realism outside of the stained-glass universe
Prompt: Immersive first-person POV, we only see the big strong hands of the knight rider tightening the reins, dragon and wings. Photorealistic, ultra-realistic action-camera footage seen entirely through the rider's own eyes while riding a gigantic black dragon at 140 km/h through a mountainous dragon-racing course with many dragons and riders. Other dragons are mounted by other knights.
The camera IS the rider's eyes. The camera is attached to the rider's head, facing forward, and moves naturally with the rider's head. The rider is the viewer. The rider's face, head, torso, body, and full silhouette are NEVER visible. No third-person shots, no external camera angles, no cutaways, no views of the rider from behind or from the side.
Only show what the rider would naturally see: the dragon's neck and occasional parts of its upper back near the bottom edge of the frame, the rushing landscape, two other dragons and their riders racing alongside and ahead, and a huge castle with catapults on its walls. A standard is carried naturally by the rider and may occasionally appear at the edge of the frame, but never blocks the view or fills the frame.
The camera maintains this exact first-person perspective throughout the entire flight. Aggressive high-speed racing, powerful realistic wingbeats, aerodynamic weight, intense wind, natural head movement, subtle camera vibration, wide-angle action-camera distortion, realistic motion blur, cinematic natural lighting, physically believable movement.
Strict visual constraints: true first-person rider POV, no visible rider, no third-person perspective, no external tracking shot, no drone camera, no over-the-shoulder shot, no cinematic cutaways, no camera floating outside the rider's body, no CGI appearance, no video game look, no 3D-render aesthetic.
Audio: deep thunderous wingbeats, roaring high-altitude wind gusts, distant volcanic rumble, and crackling flame embers.
Prompt: A cinematic macro close-up from a 1995 Hong Kong indie romantic drama, shot on 35mm film. Two young, unconventional-looking Korean lovers in their 20s ride a motorcycle across a bridge on the outskirts of Hong Kong at dawn.
The male driver wears no helmet, looking around anxiously, while the pale-skinned female passenger wears an open-face helmet. Their faces dominate the foreground, large and overlapping, with natural skin texture and subtle expressions of worry and tenderness.
Low-angle panoramic composition, framed by solid black bars. Shallow depth of field, blurred road receding behind them, orange streetlights streaking past, and a dark green dusk sky. Intimate, imperfect, melancholic 35mm film aesthetic.
Bringing Gemini and Genie 4 together adds a new layer of reasoning to world simulation, allowing us to model complex, multi-step events and test how AI systems navigate different environments before bringing them to the real world.
To achieve this in real-time, Gemini 3.8 Flash serves as a guiding agent in the loop: as Genie 4 generates a world in real-time, Gemini continuously observes the scene, breaks down goals into a sequence of steps, and reviews incoming frames to track the progress and verify that each step succeeded. As the world shifts or the user intervenes, Gemini adapts its plan in the moment, unlocking worlds with reliable causality, procedural behaviors, and multi-step reasoning.
Prompt: Universal Robots UR5 holds a pipette and dispenses liquid into a lab plate, triggering tiny electric sparks.
Prompt: A REAL, ultra-photorealistic, high-end 35mm cinematic first-person perspective (POV) experience set inside an opulent, claustrophobic antique salon, strictly avoiding any video game, CGI, or digital render aesthetic. Real place, cinema, not render.
POV & Foreground Wand: Authentic first-person perspective looking down along the player's physical right hand, which firmly grips an ornate, hand-carved hardwood and polished brass wizard wand pointing into the room. The player's skin exhibits realistic pores, skin creases, cuticle texture, and natural muscle tension under ambient room light. The wand displays fine wood grain, tiny varnish micro-cracks, cold metallic brass inlays, and tactile surface wear from handling.
Porcelain Menagerie & Room Architecture: A suffocating, baroque-style gallery packed floor-to-ceiling with thousands of fragile, life-sized and miniature glazed porcelain animals. Glistening ceramic peacocks with intricate feather patterns and vibrant cobalt and emerald enamels, regal porcelain dogs, and curled porcelain cats perched on marble mantels, mahogany display shelves, and velvet-draped pedestals. The surfaces showcase authentic high-gloss ceramic glazing, micro-crazing cracks in the enamel, delicate bone china translucency, and natural dust gathering in the crevices.
Cinematic Optics & Lighting: Shot on high-end anamorphic 35mm film lenses. Natural optical characteristics featuring shallow depth of field, subtle barrel distortion, realistic optical lens flares, fine organic film grain, and creamy bokeh in the background. Natural daylight streams through tall, grime-streaked Victorian lace curtains, casting soft volumetric dust motes and creating sharp, physically accurate specular highlights across the glossy curved porcelain glazes.
Dynamic Movement & Physical Interaction: Continuous, smooth handheld POV traversal. The player subtly sweeps and points the wand toward the ceramic figures, causing realistic micro-vibrations in the frame as footsteps tread across creaking hardwood floorboards. The figures remain frozen in immaculate, fragile stillness, catching shifting highlights as the wand moves.
Acoustic Atmosphere: Raw, immersive documentary-grade audio. Faint floorboard creaks underfoot, distant room tone, quiet breathing, the subtle dry friction of fingers adjusting their grip on the wooden wand, and the delicate, crystalline clinking resonance of fine porcelain vibrating faintly in the quiet air.
A real magician stands beside a tall wooden table. On the table is a large rectangular wooden box, completely open at the top, with no lid.
A real peacock stands calmly inside the box.
Exceptional production design, sophisticated art direction, cinematic lighting, natural but carefully controlled light, realistic skin tones, beautiful contrast, subtle shadows, rich textures, elegant composition, shallow depth of field, high-end cinema camera, realistic human actors, extremely photorealistic.
It should look like a frame from a prestigious, beautifully shot modern TV series: understated, expensive, cinematic and completely believable.
No theater, no stage, no fantasy, no cartoon, no plastic-looking people, no CGI look.
Prompt: crowned crane walks across the snow beneath the clear dusk gradient sky. Natural colors in a documentary style.
As part of exploring this capability, we have also been experimenting with Gemini 4 Argon and Genie 4 to bring our frontier research together with Gemini Robotics .
In the example below, Argon breaks down a user-instructed task into steps for Genie to render. These steps are interleaved as text captions to Genie 4 as the simulation is rendering. Because Genie 4 can be steered in real-time with text captions using Gemini, this now unlocks the path of adapting the simulation as it progresses towards the completion of that task. This capability becomes a path for simulating a breadth of scenarios in imagined worlds, using Gemini 4 Argon and Genie 4.
Gemini 4 Argon and Genie 4 work together to simulate Apptronik's Apollo humanoid playing a game of checkers, breaking the task down into real-time steps.
While Genie 4 is a major research milestone, it remains an early, experimental model. To understand how interactive world models can support real-world workflowsâand where they still need to growâweâve been working with cohorts of trusted testers across creative industries, journalism, education, gaming, and engineering.
Testers highlighted how the leap in photorealism, native audio, and real-time steering allows ideas and concepts to be turned into realistic simulations, unlocking new abilities across disciplines:
A promising path for future progress lies in hybrid world models, which combine the logical, structured reasoning of code and language models with the rich, sensory representation of pixel-level simulation. Bringing Genie and Gemini models closer together is an early step in this direction. Gemini works behind the scenes to map the structure and plan the narrative timeline, while Genie generates the immediate physical realityârendering how the world looks, sounds, and responds, pixel by pixel. Together, these complementary strengths can unlock a new class of world models that are far more coherent, controllable, and grounded than either approach could achieve alone.
Genie 4 marks a new area of frontier research that merges real-time generation and photorealism, introducing a new range of capabilities and dimensions that we want to roll out and explore in a responsible way. Genie 4 includes strict safety guardrails that are consistent with our safety policies across other models. Before launching this preview, we evaluated Genie 4 through internal rigorous safety evaluations to prevent the generation of harmful or malicious content. Also, we have intentionally deployed it first to trusted tester partners to get early feedback, before we release the model more broadly.
To maintain transparency, all video and audio generated by Genie 4 will include SynthID, our imperceptible digital watermarking technology that helps identify AI-generated content across visual and audio modalities.
Genie 4 remains an early, evolving area of research.
While it can maintain coherent environments over short sessions, visual details and object permanence can still shift or drift over timeâespecially as a simulation runs longer, after multiple complex prompt edits, or when navigating throughout the scene. Complex physical interactions, real-time audio accuracy, rendering legible text, spatial accuracy, and long-term consistency are active areas of ongoing research. We are sharing Genie 4 as a preview to learn alongside our community and safely advance the frontier of interactive simulation.
Genie 4 has been released as a research preview to trusted testers, and is coming soon to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early access partners in the Gemini API and Google AI Studio. Join the waitlist for Genie 4 in Project Genie here .
Weâre excited for users to step inside, experiment, and build their own interactive worlds soon.
